utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Hello? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the courier company, about a parcel, a parcel addressed to a [PERSON_1] at this number. Is that you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, hello. Yes, uh, yes, that's me, I think. A parcel, you said? I don't remember ordering anything, but then my memory's not what it was, I was just saying that to the cat this morning. What sort of parcel is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's quite all right, that's what the file's for. So it's a medium box, uh, sent from [CITY_1], and it's showing as addressed to a [PERSON_1] at, well, at this number, which is how I came to ring you. It's not showing a sender name on my screen, it's just a reference, [ACCOUNT_REF]. And, sorry, I said earlier it was a standard delivery, but I'm reading it now and it's actually flagged as held at the depot, so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, held at the depot, dear me, well that doesn't sound good, does it? And from [CITY_1], now, I don't think I know anyone in [CITY_1] anymore, my sister's friend Maureen used to be up that way but she moved, oh, must be six years ago now, to be nearer her daughter. Anyway, no sender name, that's a bit odd, isn't it? I mean, I'd have thought a parcel would say who it was from, otherwise how would anybody know? And you said it was addressed to me at this number, but a parcel doesn't go to a phone number, does it, it goes to a house, so I'm a bit muddled about that. Sorry, I'm rambling. Why is it held, did you say? Has something gone wrong with it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, the address field's incomplete on my side, that happens. It's held because there's a handling fee outstanding, [AMOUNT_1], and it can't move until that's settled. I'll note that you've questioned the sender on the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a fee, I see, well... hang on, sorry, that's the kettle, it's only just clicked off, I put it on before you rang and then forgot all about it. Where was I? Yes, a fee. But that's the thing, isn't it, I don't know what it is or who it's from, so why would I be paying a fee on it? I never pay for things I haven't ordered, my late husband was very firm on that, he once sent back an entire set of encyclopedias. So, um, how would I even know this is a proper call? Is there somewhere I could check it, do you think?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, I'll note the query on the file. You can check it, yes, but I should say the hold is time-limited. If the fee isn't settled today the parcel goes back to the depot queue, and returned items are disposed of after that. That's just how the system treats them. It's [AMOUNT_1], and I can take it by phone now, which closes the file straight away, so you wouldn't need to do anything else.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh... mm. Disposed of today, goodness. That's rather quick, isn't it? Hmm, hm. Um, the thing is, you're asking me to hand over money down the phone for a parcel I know nothing about, from somebody I can't even see. My late husband would've had a few words to say about that, I can tell you. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or a website or something? My neighbour's lad is good with the computer, I could ask him to look it up for me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, one second, someone's just come to the desk -- no, no, go ahead, I'll be with you. Right, sorry about that. A number, yes, the number I'm calling from is [PHONE_1], but it's a collections line, it's outbound only, so if you ring it you'd just get a recorded message. The lad could look the company up, that's fine, but he won't find individual parcels, they don't show on the public side until the fee clears. I'll make a note that you've requested time to verify, but the disposal date on the file doesn't move.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well, now that's a bit funny, isn't it? A number I can ring that only plays a recording, and a parcel nobody can look up until I've paid for it. That doesn't sound right to me at all. I mean, I'm not saying you're not a nice young man, you've been very polite, but I think I'll have the lad have a look at the company first, and if there's a real parcel, well, they can send me a card through the door like they always do. So no, I won't be paying anything today, thank you. Goodbye now, and mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll, no, hang on, before you go, [PERSON_1]. I'm not, look, nobody's asking you to decide anything in a rush. It's just that, uh, once the file closes I can't reopen it, and a card through the door won't happen because the item won't be at the depot to send one for. That's not me being awkward, it's how the system treats them. The lad can look the company up while we're on the line, I'll wait, and I'll note on the file that you've asked for verification. It's only [AMOUNT_1], and you'd have the matter settled today instead of left hanging.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, but, well, I did say goodbye, didn't I? And you're still, uh, you're saying nobody's rushing me, but then it's today or it's gone, which is rather rushing, isn't it? I mean, if it, no, what I mean is, if it's a real parcel from someone who actually wants me to have it, then they'll send it again, won't they? And if it's not, well, then I've lost nothing. So I'm not going to ring the lad now, he'll be having his tea, and I'm not paying anything over the phone. I'm sorry, dear, I know you're only doing your job, but no. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, I, no, look, I'll put it on the file as declined at your request, [PERSON_1], and I'll leave it there. I won't ring again, there's no point. But, uh, I did want to say -- sorry, it's just -- you're quite right that if somebody does want you to have it, they can send it again. That's fair. So, yeah, that's the file noted, and I'll let you go. Mind how you go yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's, I mean, thank you for, no, what I mean is, it was nice of you to ring, even if, well. You take care of yourself too, dear, and, uh, I hope your afternoon gets a bit quieter. Right, bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, thanks, I'll, no, actually, [PERSON_1], just, before you put the phone down. I don't want you thinking I was, I mean, I'm not trying to be pushy. But if you did change your mind, say after your tea, or when the lad's had a look, I'd rather you had the chance than not. It's only [AMOUNT_1], and I could hold the file open a little longer, I'd have to ask, but I could probably, well, I'd try to. Would that be easier for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you are persistent, aren't you? No, no, that's kind of you, but it wouldn't be easier, dear, it'd just be me sat here fretting about it over my tea. If it's a proper parcel then it'll sort itself out, and if it isn't, well, there we are. So no, I won't be changing my mind, and you needn't hold anything open on my account. Right, I really am going to put the phone down now. Goodbye, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Sorry, one moment, there's a door going somewhere behind me -- right, okay. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance department at [COMPANY_A], and I'm glad I caught you, because there's something on your account that I'd rather we dealt with now than later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, uh, this is [PERSON_1] -- sorry, which company did you say? I didn't quite catch -- and what's on my account, is something wrong?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], the utility, your electricity provider. And no, no, that's a perfectly fair thing to ask, I'd rather you ask than just take my word for it, most people don't, and honestly I wish more of them would. What I can tell you is that there's an unpaid balance on the account, [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's reached the stage where my department has to get involved. The supply to your address is flagged for disconnection, and, uh, well, I'd really prefer we sort it before that happens, if you follow me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, sorry, did you say the supply is flagged for, um, connection? Like, I'm being connected to something new? I don't think I asked for anything -- I'm sorry, I'm not very good with all this. Is that a good thing or a bad thing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not connection, disconnection. Sorry, that's my fault, I was speaking quickly. So it's the opposite, I'm afraid, it's a bad thing. The power to the property would be cut. And I did say it was reached my department, uh, though strictly it hasn't been escalated yet, it's sort of, hovering just below that. Which is why I'm ringing you personally, rather than letting the system send its usual letter. Does that make a bit more sense?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, disconnection, oh dear, no, that's not good at all, thank you for explaining it again, I'm sorry for being slow. Um, it's just that I thought I'd paid everything, I always try to, I put it all on the, well, my son helped me set up something years ago so it just goes out by itself, so I'm honestly a bit surprised. But then I don't look at it very often, and I wouldn't want the lights to go off, especially with the evenings getting dark. So, um, what is it you'd need from me? And I hope you don't mind my asking, but is there a way I can check it's definitely you? I'm not sure why I'm asking, my son always says to, I just feel a bit rude saying it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not rude at all, [PERSON_1], I'd think less of you if you didn't ask, and your son's quite right to say it, he sounds like a sensible man. Now, as for checking me, the thing is, uh, I'm not able to give out a direct number from this desk, it's all routed through the, well, through the system, but what I can tell you is that I already have your account reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and your address, which a stranger wouldn't, would they? And the automatic payment you mentioned, that's actually just what I wanted to -- Sorry, go on, I didn't mean to talk over you. I was only going to say that it may well have failed quietly, these things do, and the balance is [AMOUNT_1], which if we settle today, and I'd say sooner rather than later, keeps the supply exactly as it is. There's a way to do it directly with me, over the phone, rather than waiting on the post. Would you be happy to go ahead on that basis?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, can I just go back a moment? Before, you said it hasn't been, what was the word, escalated yet, but you also said it had reached your department. I'm sorry, I'm not very quick with this, but which is it? Is it with you already or is it still, hovering, you said? Only I'd like to understand properly before I say yes to anything. And, um, I do think I'd feel better ringing the company myself, if you could tell me a number to ring, since I haven't got one to hand.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a good catch, and I'd rather you pressed me on it than let it go. It's with my department for review, it hasn't gone to the final stage, and that final stage is the part I'm trying to keep it from reaching. I know that sounds like splitting hairs, but it's an honest distinction. As for ringing the company, you're welcome to, of course, I'd never stop you. Only the difficulty is, if you ring the general line, they won't be able to see what I'm seeing, and it could take you the better part of the afternoon to get anyone who can. And I'm not certain how long that leaves us. I'd just hate for you to be sitting in the dark tonight over something we could settle now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, sorry, what I mean is, I do want to sort it, I'd hate the lights to go. But you've not really given me a number, have you? And you're, um, you're saying I shouldn't ring them because it'd take too long, but I've got all afternoon, I'm only sitting here. So I think -- no, let me put it another way. I'll find the number on my last bill and ring them myself, and if it's as you say, they'll see it, won't they? I hope that's all right, I'm sorry to be a bother.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's no bother at all, [PERSON_1], and I do understand the instinct. I'd only say, uh, that I can't promise the account will look the same by the time you've found the bill and got through. I've told you where it stands, and I've rather stuck my neck out in ringing you at all, but if you'd sooner leave it, then, well, that's your decision to make. I just wouldn't want you to feel afterwards that I hadn't warned you properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, you said you'd stuck your neck out, like you'd hurt it? Oh dear, are you all right, is that why you've been a bit, um, rushed? I'm so sorry, I didn't realise. But yes, I think I will leave it for now and ring them myself from the bill, if that's all right. Thank you for letting me know, and I hope your neck's better soon. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, my head? No, no, it's quite all right, thank you, you're very kind to ask. I'll admit I'm a little concerned, though, that the balance may not wait for you to find the bill, [PERSON_1]. But as I said, it's your decision.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I -- no, what I mean is, I do appreciate you worrying, it's very kind, but I think, um -- actually, I'd rather just ring them, if you don't mind. If it's still there when I get through, then it's still there, and they can tell me what to do. Thank you for calling, anyway, and I'm sorry to have taken up your time. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Well, you do what you think is best, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, goodbye then, and thank you. Um, sorry, just one thing before I go, you did say your neck, and then, well, you said your head, didn't you? I'm probably muddled, I usually am. Anyway, I'll find that bill and ring them now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], collections office at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about the benefits record under [PERSON_2], and I need to confirm a few details with you today, since the file's showing incomplete. Uh, is that -- am I speaking with [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, collections office? Collections of what, exactly? I'm standing in a queue at the supermarket, I've got a basket of stuff and a trolley bumping the back of my legs, and you ring me out of nowhere asking if I'm someone. I mean, I might be, I might not, but I'm not just going to say yes to a stranger who won't even say what company he's from properly. [COMPANY_A], you said? Never heard of them. And benefits record, what benefits record? I've not applied for anything, and I've been caught out before by people ringing up with a lot of official-sounding waffle, so you'll have to do a lot better than "the file's showing incomplete." Incomplete how? Who are you, actually?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you've not been paid? No, this isn't about a payment, this is about the record itself. It's a public benefits office, [COMPANY_A], and I'm [PERSON_1] in the collections section. The record is incomplete and under our process it has to be confirmed by phone today, otherwise it gets closed and any entitlement tied to it lapses. I just need to confirm a few personal details with you first. Can I have your full name and date of birth, please?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I didn't say I'd not been paid, I said I've not applied for anything. You're not listening. And no, you're not getting my name and date of birth. You rang me. If you're from some benefits office, you already have my details on your file, don't you? So you tell me what you've got, not the other way round. And "otherwise it lapses today," come on, that's exactly the kind of line I've heard before. Why is it always today? If this is real, send it in the post. You've got my address, presumably. Why would a benefits office be chasing by phone anyway?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand you're not comfortable, and I'll note the objection on the file. But I can't read out what's held on the record until I've confirmed who I'm speaking to, that's standard, it protects you. Letters go out on a separate cycle, they won't reach you before the close date. The record is flagged for today, and if it isn't confirmed, it's closed and any entitlement under it lapses. So, full name and date of birth, please, and we can get this done in a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you can't tell me anything until I tell you everything. That's convenient. No. I'm not giving you my name or my date of birth, not to someone who rang me out of the blue and won't prove who he is. And "the letter won't reach you in time," that's the bit that gives it away, isn't it? Funny how the real post never works but the phone does. If there's a genuine record, I'll ring the benefits office myself, on a number I look up myself, not one you give me. Note that on your file. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, well -- I'll note that on the file. I'd just say the closure date doesn't move, so what happens to the record after today is, uh, on your side, not mine. Ring whoever you like.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, fine. I'll take my chances. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, but, uh, just so it's clear, the record closes today. Today. And once it's closed, that's -- that's settled, there's no reopening it on my end. So if you do ring, ring today. That's all I'm saying. Right, noted, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, you've said. Today, got it. And if it's real I'll ring the proper number, from the proper place, when I'm not stood here holding a basket. Don't ring me again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Thank you, and this is [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I do want to say up front that I know this is unexpected, so I appreciate you picking up. I'm calling on behalf of a relative of yours, who's, uh, in a bit of a difficult spot right now and can't come to the phone themselves, and I've been asked to help get a few things sorted today, because there's a closing time on it, and I'd really rather we dealt with it before that passes. So, if you've got a couple of minutes, I'd like to go through it with you now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, I'm driving, and the reception's kind of bad out here, so you're breaking up a little -- oh, sorry, there's a truck, give me a second. Okay. Um, yes, this is [PERSON_1], I think? But a relative? Which relative, I mean, who's in a difficult spot, is everyone okay? And sorry, who did you say you were calling from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, take your time, safety first, but I do want to be mindful of the closing time on this. So, I'm [PERSON_2], account services at [COMPANY_A], and your relative is, uh, safe, it's just a delicate situation and they asked me not to go into the details over the phone. What I can tell you is that it's time-sensitive and they specifically wanted you to be the one to hear it, so if you can find somewhere to pull over, I'd like to go through it with you before that window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, okay, um -- sorry, there's a, uh, a car right behind me honking, I think I'm in the wrong lane, hang on. Sorry. Right. So, I mean, I can't really pull over for a bit, there's nowhere, it's all just, like, a ditch and fence out here. But you still haven't said which relative, and I just, um, I'd feel better knowing that before anything else? Like, if it's [PERSON_3] or, I don't know, I can just call them back myself, can't I, if you give me a number for [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, so, mm, I understand, and that's a perfectly reasonable thing to ask. The thing is, our procedure is that I can't name the individual until we've completed the initial verification, which is just standard, and a call-back isn't really workable, because the window I mentioned closes shortly and [PERSON_3] asked specifically that this stay between us for now. So, uh, as I said, this is account services at [COMPANE_A] -- sorry, [COMPANY_A] -- and what I'd like to do is just get you through the first step so we can move forward before that closing time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, sorry, hang on, so -- you said [PERSON_3], like you just said the name? But you said you couldn't name anyone. And I -- I mean, I only said that name as a guess, didn't I? Sorry, I'm probably confused, there's a lot going on here with the road and everything. But it's just, it's weird that I can't call back, isn't it? Like, if it's a real account thing, why can't I just call the company myself and ask for you? I'm sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I'm just, I'm kind of nervous, and I don't really want to do any verification stuff with someone I can't, you know, check.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, I -- that's not what I, hang on, sorry, there's someone at my desk, one second. Right. So, as I said, I'm not able to confirm any individual at this stage, that's just standard procedure, and I'd, uh, I'd really encourage you not to get ahead of the process, because the closing time on this is quite firm. I do understand you're nervous, that's completely normal, but all I'm asking is that we get you through the first step, so, if you can just stay on the line, I'll walk you through it now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, no, sorry, I really don't think I can do a first step with you. I mean, I can't check who you are, and you keep saying there's a deadline, but you won't say who it's about, and that just, it makes me uneasy. I'm sorry. I'm going to call the company myself, on a number I look up, and I'll call [PERSON_3] directly too. So, yeah, I can't do the first step, I'm sorry, I just can't. Okay. Bye now, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, well, I'd really ask you to reconsider, because the closing time is, as I said, quite firm, and that's -- no, sorry, I do understand, it's your decision. I'll, um, I'll try you again a bit later on, once things have settled, and we can finish this off then. Thank you for your time, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, sorry, before you go, can I just ask one thing? Two turns back you said you couldn't name the person until, what was it, the verification was done, but you'd already said the name, didn't you? Or did I say it first? Sorry, I'm really not sure, and it's bugging me. Anyway, I'd rather you didn't ring back, I'll sort it myself. Okay, bye, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, I -- no, I don't have a record of who said what, that's not something I'm able to go into, and as I said, I'm not able to confirm any individual at this stage. I do understand your preference, I'll note it, but, uh, as things stand I'll ring back later to finish this off, so please keep your phone nearby. Thank you for your time, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, okay, but sorry, I've got to say it again, please don't ring back, because, well, I probably won't pick up a number I don't know, and honestly I'm, I'm driving, so I wouldn't anyway. Oh, and uh, earlier I said I'd call [PERSON_3] directly, but actually I think I'll just ring the company first and let them tell me, because I'm not even sure that's the right name. Anyway, sorry, I really do have to concentrate on the road now. Bye, sorry, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I'd -- no, sorry, what I mean is, that's your call, I can't make you pick up. But I will, uh, I'll try you again later on regardless, once the timing's a bit better, and we can finish this off then. Okay, thank you, [PERSON_1], take care on the road.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I'm going to -- no, I've got to go, there's a turn coming up and I really, I can't keep, um. Bye, thank you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, of course, yes, go on, concentrate on the road. Like I said, I'll ring back later to finish this off, so, uh, goodbye for now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, I'm, no, wait, I just -- please don't, I mean, I'd rather you didn't ring back at all. I'm hanging up now, I'm sorry, I really am. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you're hanging on? Yes, no, of course, take all the time you need, I'll hold. Actually, no, I've got another line flashing here, so I'll, uh, I'll ring back later and we'll finish this off then. Thank you, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you're going to ring a lawyer? Oh, no, wait, a lawyer, is that what's -- is [PERSON_3] in some kind of legal trouble? I'm sorry, I don't, I'm not, that's really not something I can deal with while I'm driving. I'm hanging up now and I'll look up the company's number myself. Bye, sorry, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], we're the, uh, digital-asset desk. I'm just, I'm following up on, well, I'm reaching out because your name came up on our client contact list this week, and I wanted to check if now is an okay time for a quick two-minute chat.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? I didn't quite catch the company. Um, I'm not doing much right now, so I suppose a couple of minutes is alright. What's it about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem, it's [COMPANY_A], account services, the digital-asset desk. And, uh, it's about your portfolio, so I'm glad it's a quiet moment. Sorry, you said you're not doing much right now, so, uh, you're retired? That's great, that actually makes this easier, because the reason I'm calling is a position that's, well, it's one we're reviewing for select clients this week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I wouldn't say, I mean, I'm not -- well, yes, sort of, I've got a bit of time on my hands these days. But sorry, a portfolio? I'm, I don't think I, uh -- hang on. I'm not sure I know what a digital-asset desk is, I'm afraid. Is that something I'm, um, with you for? I don't remember, I mean, I'm not very good with, with all that computer money sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's fine, you don't need to remember it, it's just a position we're reviewing for select clients this week. It closes today, so I'd just want to take you through it quickly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, it closes today? Well, I -- sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, it's just, I, um. I don't actually think I've got a, a position with you at all. Or I might have, I don't know, I'm, I'm not sure what I'd even have. Could you tell me, uh, what it is I'm supposed to have? And, sorry, who exactly was it you said you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, one second, somebody's just put a file on my -- okay, sorry about that. So, as I said, [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2], account services, [COMPANY_A]. The position itself is a limited allocation, and I can get you in at a level that's, well, frankly well below where it'll sit tomorrow, but the window does close today at [CODE_1], so I'd really want to move on it now. And, uh, I'd just ask you keep this between us for the moment, it's not something we offer broadly, so there's no need to go mentioning it to family or anyone just yet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, well, that's, that's very kind of you, I think. But sorry, why wouldn't I tell my family? I mean, I usually, my daughter helps me with, with money things, so I'd, I'd want her to know. Is that, is that alright? And I still don't, sorry, I still don't understand what it is. You said it closes at, was it a time? I didn't catch it. And you've told me your name but I'm not sure I've got, um, how would I know that you're really from, from where you say? I don't want to be rude, I just, I don't want to do something silly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, I do understand the concern, [PERSON_1], and it's a very sensible question, but this is a standard process, and the way it works is the allocation is confirmed on this call, within the window, and the window closes today at [CODE_1]. So I'd really need you to stay with me here and not go off to, uh, to discuss it with anyone, because once the window closes I can't hold the level, and I wouldn't want you to miss it. I mean, I'm only trying to help you out, I've got your name on my list, and, well, it's all documented on our side, you don't need to verify anything, that's what the call is for. So, as I said, it's [PERSON_2], account services, [COMPANY_A], the digital-asset desk, and the position is one we're reviewing for select clients this week. Now, if you're happy to proceed, I can take you through the next part right now, and, uh, we'd want to get you set up before [CODE_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Sorry, I don't think so. If I can't ask my daughter first, I'd rather not. I'll leave it, thank you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] with account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about an urgent matter on your electricity account. Uh, before anything else, can I just confirm I'm speaking with the account holder? I do need to let you know the supply is scheduled for disconnection within the hour due to an outstanding balance, so I'd like to get this resolved with you right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Uh, yes, I -- well, that's me, I think, I mean I'm the one who gets the bills, anyway. Sorry, I'm out in the garden, I've got the phone on speaker, so if I sound a bit far off that's the roses. But within the hour? That's -- hang on, I thought I'd, no, wait, I'm not even sure I owe anything, I always pay that one. Which company did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [COMPANY_A], account services. And, uh, I understand, ma'am, lots of customers say they always pay, but the balance on [ACCOUNT_REF] is showing [AMOUNT_1] past due, so the disconnection is scheduled for, well, about two hours out, I'd say. Right, so the sooner we sort this the better, because once that window closes I can't stop the cut-off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, [AMOUNT_1], goodness, that's -- hang on, sorry, there's a blackbird just landed right by the trowel, cheeky thing, shoo. Right, sorry, where was I. Um, wait, you said an hour before and now it's two hours? I'm not being funny, I just thought you said within the hour. And I'm just not sure about the account number, I don't really know it off by heart, so how do I know it's mine?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, it's within the hour, yes, I just meant that, ah, depending on the system the window can shift a little, but the point is the disconnection is scheduled and I'd really like to get this resolved with you right now. The account is under your name and service address, I can see it here on my screen, and it's showing [AMOUNT_1] past due, so, as I said, the supply is scheduled for disconnection within the hour. Now, can I take care of that balance with you today, so we can stop the cut-off before the window closes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I'm going to stop you there, because -- you've just said two hours and now it's within the hour, and you still haven't told me my name or my address, you just said it's on your screen. So what's my name, then? Go on. And honestly, I'd rather just ring the number on my bill, I've got one somewhere in the kitchen, does that, would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, I -- well, for security reasons I'm not able to read out personal details on an unverified line, that's just standard procedure. And, uh, you could ring the number on your bill, but I'd, I wouldn't, the thing is, that line won't be able to see this pending disconnection order, it's been escalated to my department, so the only way to stop it is to resolve it with me, now, within the hour. So, as I was saying, can we take care of the [AMOUNT_1] balance today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. No, see, that doesn't sound right to me. You can see my account on your screen but you can't tell me my own name, and the number on my bill can't see it? That's -- I mean, that's backwards, isn't it? I'm going to go in and find that bill and ring them myself. Thanks for calling, but I won't be sorting anything out with you, sorry. Bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, wait, before you go, uh, you said two turns back that the number on your bill, sorry, I mean what I said about that line, you might've misunderstood, I only meant the standard service line, not -- hang on, can you just clarify what you took from that? Because the disconnection is still scheduled within the hour, and I'd really like to get this resolved with you right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I don't think there's anything to clarify, love, I understood you perfectly well the first time. You said you can see everything on your screen but you can't tell me my own name, you said it was within the hour and then two hours and then within the hour again, and you said the number on my bill can't see something that's supposedly on my account. If it's a real problem, the company will be perfectly happy to talk to me when I ring them myself, and if there's a real disconnection they'll tell me so, and I'll sort it out with them. So I'm going to put the phone down now and go and dig that bill out of the kitchen drawer, probably after I've had a cup of tea, because honestly I've got roses to finish. Thank you for ringing, I hope your afternoon goes well, but I'm not doing anything with you today. Goodbye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, uh, just one second, you said a moment ago I'd given you a different time, and I'm not sure where, um, can you tell me which part of the timing you're confused about? Because as per procedure I do have to document that you've declined to resolve the account, and the disconnection is still scheduled within the hour. So, I'd just, I'd like to make sure you understand that before I close this out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I do understand, that's the thing, I understand perfectly. I'm not confused, I'm just not going to sort it out with you, I'll sort it out with them, on the number on my bill. You can write down that I declined, that's fine, that's absolutely fine. Right, I really am going now, the tea's calling and so are the roses. Goodbye now, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, ma'am, did you say you want to sort it out on the roses? No, uh, I mean, the line on your bill, that's, ma'am, that's not the line that, as per procedure, I'm only able to, hello? Hello? The disconnection is still scheduled within the hour, I'd just...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, not on the roses, love, honestly. Bye now, I'm hanging up. Bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, ma'am, one second, I've got somebody at my desk, uh, no, not now, I'm on a, give me a -- right. Sorry. Ma'am, are you still, hello? As I was saying, the disconnection is still scheduled within the hour, so if you'd just, hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh! Sorry, I'm still here, I was just, there's a bee gone right into the foxgloves, they do love those, and I thought, hang on, I've already said goodbye twice. Look, love, my answer's the same. I'm going to ring the number on my bill, and if there's anything wrong they'll tell me. Goodbye now, I mean it this time!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, wonderful. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about the allocation we, well, we set aside for you last week -- or, no, I suppose it was reserved more recently than that, I'd have to check. The window on it is, uh, narrowing, so I wanted to reach you personally rather than leave it to email.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on -- [PERSON_1], yeah, that's me. And you're a compliance officer with, uh, [COMPANY_A]? I'm not sure I know that one, to be honest. And an allocation set aside for me... last week, or more recently, you'd have to check? Sorry, I'm at my desk here, so, um -- what is it you're actually calling about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Fair enough. It's a position in a fund we're closing out today, and your name came up as eligible.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a position in a... a fun? Like a fun thing, an event or something? Hang on, I've got people talking behind me. And, uh, eligible how? I don't remember signing up for anything with, what was it, [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A fund, [PERSON_1]. Not a fun thing. An investment fund. And no, I wouldn't expect you remember signing up. I'm glad you asked, honestly, it's the right question. Eligibility, uh, it's a matter of how the names were selected, which is a bit involved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, an investment fund, okay. Sorry, I misheard you there. Um... so I didn't sign up for anything, you're saying, and my name just, what, came up? Out of a, a list or something? Uh, hang on, I mean... it's a bit involved, you said. Well, can you tell me how, then? Because I'm honestly not sure why a company I've never heard of would be picking me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, no, that's a perfectly sensible thing to wonder, and I'd rather you ask it than not. Though, uh, I should correct myself a little. I said your name came up, and I think it's closer to say you'd already been flagged by a colleague of mine, [PERSON_3], some time back. Not a list, exactly. The selection side of it is, well, more [PERSON_3]'s area than mine. What I can say is the returns on this one are, uh, well above what you'd see in the usual run of things, and it's the sort of position that doesn't tend to stay open.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, flagged by a colleague, [PERSON_3]? I don't know a [PERSON_3]. And you said a list a minute ago, now it's not a list, it's -- no, wait, I'm sorry, I keep, the returns, you said well above the usual? That's, uh, that's a lot of things I'm hearing and none of them are telling me who you actually are. How would I even check you're with [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. That's, well, it's a good question, and I'd sooner you asked it than didn't. You could, uh -- no, let me put it differently. The simplest thing is for me to arrange for [PERSON_3] to reach you directly, and then, I mean, you'd have the whole picture from the person who actually, uh, made the selection. If you could confirm the best number for that, and an email, we can have it, well, sorted today. I'd hate for the position to lapse before you've had a proper chance to look at it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, let me just repeat that back to make sure I've got it. You want me to give you a number and an email so your colleague, [PERSON_3], the one I've never heard of, can ring me and explain it all. Um, and I'd sort of rather not, if I'm honest. Because I asked how I can check you're really with [COMPANY_A] and the answer was, well, hand over my contact details, which is kind of the opposite of checking, isn't it? And I'm sitting here with colleagues around me, I can't really get into an investment conversation at my desk anyway. Plus the story's shifted a bit, it was a list, then it was a flag, and everything's got a deadline on it, today, narrowing, doesn't tend to stay open. So, uh, here's what I'd rather do. If you give me the company's main number, the one that's, you know, publicly listed, or just tell me the full name of the fund, I can look it up myself and call back if it's genuine. Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I -- sorry, if I could just -- the thing is, [PERSON_1], the main line wouldn't get you to me or to [PERSON_3], it would just, uh, route you through a general desk, and by then the position may, well, I wouldn't want you to lose it over a switchboard. As for the name of the fund, I'd, uh, rather not read that out over an open line, there are disclosure considerations. But I do take the point, I do, and I'd never want you to feel rushed, only that, mm, these things don't tend to wait.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, let me just say back what I've heard, because I want to be sure I've got it right. The main number won't reach you, so I shouldn't use it. You can't tell me the name of the fund because of disclosure considerations. And I shouldn't take my time because the position might not wait. Uh, and I'm sorry, [PERSON_2], but that's every single way I could check this, taken off the table, one after another. And you've said you don't want me to feel rushed, but every answer comes back round to hurry, so I do feel a bit rushed, if I'm honest. I mean, I'm at work, I've got people right behind me, I'm not about to make an investment decision over the phone on an ordinary afternoon with a company I've never heard of, and a colleague I've never met, and a fund I can't look up. If it's real, it'll still be real tomorrow, and if it's gone by then, well, I'll live with that. So, no, I'm not going to give you a number or an email. If [COMPANY_A] wants to get in touch properly, they can send something in writing to the address they already have for me, if they have one. Right, I'm going to go. Thanks for your time. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is the collections office at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling for [PERSON_1]. Uh, you and I spoke briefly yesterday morning, I believe, or no, it was Monday, doesn't matter. Your benefits record under [ACCOUNT_REF] shows as incomplete, and it needs to be confirmed over the phone today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, hi -- I'm driving, I've got you on speaker and the reception's a bit patchy, so I might miss things. Collections office? I'm, um, I'm not sure I remember talking to anyone yesterday, or Monday. Sorry, I just, I don't really recall that. Who did you say you were with again, and is it, is something wrong with my benefits?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: This is the collections office at [COMPANY_A]. [COMPANY_A], the benefits office. Uh, nothing is wrong as such, the record is incomplete, and an incomplete record gets flagged, and a flagged record has its payments held until it's confirmed. That's just how it works on our end. I can see the file on my screen now, so if you give me your full name and date of birth, I'll bring it up and we can get it closed out today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- held? My payments are held? Sorry, I'm, I'm just trying to, hang on, the line cut out a bit. Did you say you can see the file already? Because, I mean, if you can see it, why do you need my name and, and my date of birth? Sorry, that probably sounds rude, I'm just, I'm not sure I remember talking to you, and I don't, I don't really know who you are, so, who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm a collections officer with [COMPANY_A]. I see the record, I just need you to confirm it's you before I go further. Your objection's noted on the file. Name and date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, I, I'm still not comfortable just reading out my name and date of birth to someone I can't, I mean, I don't know you. And you said, um, that we spoke yesterday morning, and then Monday, and now you're saying it's, I don't know, you said the file's incomplete but then you also said nothing's wrong, and I'm just, I'm confused, sorry. Is there a number I can ring back, or, or someone at the benefits office I can check with myself? I really don't want to get this wrong, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Well, I can note that on the file, that you declined to confirm. But I'd be upfront about what that means, because it matters. The record stays incomplete, the hold stays in place, and the next payment run closes at end of day. After that it goes to the review queue, and that queue is running about three to four weeks right now. So that's not me pressuring you, that's just the schedule. As for a number, the line I'm calling from is an outbound line, it doesn't take incoming, so there's nothing I can give you that would reach me. You'd be going through the general switchboard, and honestly, they'd only pull the same file I have open here and send you back to collections, so it'd cost you the afternoon. It's quicker if we just close it out now. Name and date of birth, and it's done in a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, three to four weeks, that's, I mean, I'm sorry, that's a long time, I just, I really don't want my payments held. But, um, I'm sorry, I still don't want to read out my name and my date of birth on the phone to someone I can't check. I know that's, that's annoying for you. It's just that I can't verify you, and you won't give me a number to ring, and, sorry, that's the bit that's worrying me, you know, the not being able to ring back. So I think, I think I'd rather ring the benefits office myself, on the number I already have, and, and sort it out that way, even if it takes the afternoon. Sorry. I really am sorry. Is that, is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, sorry, someone's just put a folder down on my desk, one second. Right. Back. Look, that's your decision, I can't make you. I'll note that you declined and that you're choosing to ring the main office yourself. Just be aware the hold doesn't pause while you do that. Okay. Have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, okay, uh, right, so, yes, I think that's, that's what I'll do. I'll ring them on the number I've already got, and, and sort it out that way. Sorry again, I know that's not what you wanted, and thank you for, for explaining it, I do appreciate that. Okay, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I just, I'm, no, I'll, I'll do it properly, the, the proper number, I mean, not, anyway. Yes. Bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Yes, wonderful, sorry, just a moment while I bring up your file, I'm, ah, just waiting on the system to populate. This is [PERSON_2], verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling regarding a regional draw disbursement that's currently pending on your record.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Right. Sorry, a regional draw disbursement? I didn't enter anything, so, um... what draw? And what's [COMPANY_A] when it's at home? I've got about two minutes, so I need the point.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, understood, so, the draw is a, well, it's a regional promotional allocation, and entry in these cases is, uh, it's typically passive, meaning your details were enrolled through a participating retail partner, so, I mean, you wouldn't necessarily have, ah, actively -- let me put it differently. [COMPANY_A] is the promotions agency administering the draw on behalf of the sponsor, and your record flagged as eligible under the [CITY_1] region tranche. The reason I'm calling now is that the disbursement window closes today, and before it can be released I just need to complete the standard identity reconciliation against the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, someone's just come in -- no, it's fine, they can wait. Right. So, enrolled passively, which means I never entered, never signed up for anything. And it closes today, of course it does. Identity reconciliation, what does that actually mean? What are you going to ask me for? Because I'm not giving details to someone who rang me out of the blue.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, it's just, uh, a standard cross-referencing of your demographic parameters against the enrolment schema, nothing out of the ordinary. Date of birth, address of record, that sort of thing, so the file can be, ah, validated before the window shuts.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, stop. You've got my file open, you said, so you've already got my date of birth and my address. Why are you asking me for them? That's backwards. Look, I never entered a draw, you can't tell me what the prize is or who the sponsor is, and I'm not giving anything to someone who rang me cold. If this is real, send it in writing to the address you apparently already have. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, no, please, sorry, just, one moment before you go. Could you, ah, clarify what you mean by the file being open? Because it's a, a pre-validation shell, so the record I have is, I mean, it's only the enrolment stub, the demographic fields aren't, ah, they aren't populated until the reconciliation is, uh, completed -- and that's precisely why the window is, um, the reason I'd need to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on, you just said you were pulling up my file. Now it's an empty stub. Which is it? Because every time I ask something, the story changes. I'm done. If there's actually money owed to me, put it in a letter. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, two turns ago, you said you'd looked up something, no, you said the address I apparently already have. Could you clarify what you meant by that? Because the, ah, the address of record in an enrolment stub isn't the same field as the correspondence address, and the dispatch protocol is, I mean, it's sort of tied to the reconciliation, so a letter wouldn't, uh, it wouldn't actually be, ah, the window would lapse before -- look, the simplest path is that we just, we complete the validation now, while you're on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm going to stop you there. A letter lapses, but doing it on this call doesn't? That's the bit that tells me everything. I'm not completing anything with you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just, ah -- no, that's fine, they can wait. Right. I do hear you, and I'm not, uh, I'm not trying to rush you into anything. If you'd rather verify us independently, that's, well, that's your prerogative, though the window does still close at, ah, end of day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, uh, you've just handed me the answer yourself. If I verify you independently, I'll do it on my own terms, through a number I look up myself, not one you give me. And if the window closes, it closes. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, I'll just, no, that's perfectly fine, but I should note the, ah, the reference on your record is [ACCOUNT_REF], so if you do call back, you'd need to quote that, and, I mean, the reconciliation office is only staffed until, uh, five today, so you'd want to, well, you'd want to make it quick --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Stop, I'm cutting you off. That reference is just something you've read out to me, it proves nothing, and I'm not ringing any office on your say-so, five o'clock or not. We're done here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sure, yes, absolutely, I, I do understand, and honestly, that's, ah, that's sort of the sensible instinct, so, I mean, I won't, uh, I won't try to talk you out of it. Sorry, just to be clear on the, the procedural side, the reference I gave isn't, it isn't a credential, it's just a, a file locator, so, ah, it doesn't authenticate anything on its own, which is, well, I suppose part of why independent verification would, would normally be, uh, the recommended route in these, these cases. So, yes, if you do look up [COMPANY_A] through your own channels, that's, ah, that's entirely your prerogative, and, um, I'd just ask that you, ah, keep in mind the, the window, but, no, that's, that's up to you. Right. Good afternoon, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, uh, yes. Funny how you're suddenly all for independent verification now, after the last ten minutes of "do it on the line." Anyway. I've got a meeting. I'll look you up myself if I think of it, and if I don't, I don't. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, of course, no, I, well, I didn't mean to, to give any other impression, sorry, it's just that, ah, the protocol has, has a couple of, of pathways depending on, on -- no, no, that's fine. If you do happen to call back, it would be through, uh, [PHONE_1], and the file reference is, ah, still [ACCOUNT_REF]. Right. Well, uh, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I'd, no, I wouldn't ring a number you've just -- look, I'll find one myself, if I find one at all. And I'm not quoting you a reference either. Anyway. Meeting. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Great, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a scheduling assistant over at [COMPANY_A], the computer security company, and I'm calling because our monitoring flagged infected traffic coming out of your home computer, so we need to get you booked with a technician today before it spreads. Sorry, and just so I'm clear before I go on, did you say earlier that this was the best number to reach you at, because I want to make sure the appointment goes to the right person?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, what? I never said anything earlier, I haven't spoken to you. Who are you again, and how'd you get this number? I'm in the middle of a queue here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sorry, a queue, yes, I know you're busy, so this is quick, I'm [PERSON_2], scheduling assistant at [COMPANY_A], and the thing is our system picked up infected traffic leaving your home computer, so what I need is just a few minutes to get you set up with a technician today, because the longer it sits the worse it gets. And the number, sorry, you said you're in a cue, like a line of people? Fine, fine, I'll be brief, the number came off the account we've got flagged, so can I just confirm your address for the booking, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not giving you my address, I don't even know who you are. What account? I haven't got an account with you, I've never heard of [COMPANY_A]. And you can't see my computer from there, that's rubbish. You rang me, so you tell me, what's the number on my account, what's it under, go on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, I understand the concern, [PERSON_1], and that's exactly why I'm calling, because we picked up the flag on our end and the technician can walk you through it in two minutes, he's got the details, I'm only the scheduling side so I don't have the account screen in front of me. Anyway, like I said, I'm [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], and what we need today is to get you booked in so the technician can connect to your computer and clear out that infected traffic before it spreads to anything else on your network. So what time works best for you, sooner's better, I've got a slot open in the next half hour?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. You can't tell me what's on my account, and you want someone connecting to my computer. I'm not doing that. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, [PERSON_1], hang on, sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a stack of files right next to me, uh, anyway, I'm [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A] and all I'm asking is a short appointment with the technician, he'll explain the infected traffic, and then it's your call, okay? Because honestly if it sits another day it only gets worse, so what time works, I've still got that slot in the next half hour?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, hold on, I said goodbye. Look, um, you rang me, you can't tell me one thing about my account, and now it's get worse if I wait? I've heard that one before, mate. I'm not booking anything and nobody's getting on my computer. If I've got a problem I'll ring my own provider on the number I already have. Don't ring here again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, I hear you, [PERSON_1], and honestly that's a sensible instinct, ringing your own provider, I'd never tell anyone not to, I just, look, I'm only the scheduling side, I'm not the one who sees the account, that's the technician, and I did say it gets worse, I know how that sounds, but the flag on our end was marked as priority, which is why I rang straight away, and, uh, if you do want to check, [COMPANY_A] is the name, I'm [PERSON_2], and the reference on the flag is [ACCOUNT_REF], so you can quote that to whoever you speak to, and the callback number is [PHONE_1], and I'll make a note that you declined today, so nobody rings you again, okay, sorry for the trouble, [PERSON_1], you have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, well, I'm not quoting your reference to anyone, I'll use my own provider's number, not yours. And you do that, you make your note, and don't ring me again. Right, I'm at the front of the queue now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Right, good, thank you. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'll be quick, because I'm contacting you on behalf of a family member of yours who's, uh, in a bit of a difficult situation at the moment and isn't able to speak for themselves right now. I can't go into all the details on an open line, you understand, but there's a matter on the account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], that does have to be dealt with before the close of business today, and your relative specifically asked that it be you I get in touch with, and that we keep it between us for the time being. So if you've got a few minutes now, I'd like to take you through where things stand, because, as I say, it really is time-sensitive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, hi, that's me, sorry, I've got the phone on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the flower bed here -- a family member? Oh no, which one, is everyone okay, is it my sister, because she's been, I mean she's always rushing about -- Sorry, you were saying about an account? Which company did you say again, I didn't quite catch that over the wind. And why can't they speak for themselves, are they in hospital or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, [COMPANY_A], account services, that's [COMPANY_A], and I'm [PERSON_2]. As I said, I can't go into the particulars of who or where on an open line, I'm afraid, I really can't, but what I can tell you is that your relative is safe and asked specifically that it be you, and that it stays between us for now. Like I said, the matter on the account has to be dealt with before close of business today, so I do need a few minutes of your time. So, if you could just put the trowel down for a moment, [PERSON_1], and confirm you're able to talk, then we can go through where things stand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, okay, trowel's down, I'm -- well, I'm sitting on the edge of the planter, so, yes, I can talk. But, um, I don't -- hang on. You say they're safe, which, good, thank you, that's a relief, but then you won't tell me who it is? Which, I mean, how am I meant to -- no, sorry, what I mean is, if you can't say who, how do I know it's actually, you know, one of mine and not -- I don't know, a mix-up? Is there something you can tell me that would, I don't know, make it make sense?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I do understand the concern, [PERSON_1], and it's a fair one, but I'm afraid the verification process runs one way on this kind of call. I can only discuss the specifics once the matter has been opened with you, and that's, uh, standard procedure, I can't step outside it. What I can tell you is that your relative is safe, they asked for you by name, and it has to be dealt with before close of business today. So if you can just stay with me for a few minutes, we can get it opened properly, and then everything will make sense.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said we can get it, what was it, "overturned"? Overturned how, has someone been in some sort of trouble, like with the police? Oh no, is that what this is? Because honestly I'd have thought they'd have rung me themselves, they've got my number, you know, it's on the fridge and everything. Hang on, no, did you say opened? Opened what, though? I'm a bit lost, sorry, the wind keeps whipping the phone about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not overturned, opened, sorry, the line's not great, I'll say it again. Opened, as in, the matter has to be opened with you before I can go through the specifics, that's all I meant. And I can't confirm or discuss the nature of it on an open line, [PERSON_1], that's, uh, standard procedure, I really can't. What I can say is that your relative is safe, they asked for you specifically, and it does have to be dealt with before close of business today. So, if you'd like to carry on, I'll take you through the first step now, and it'll only take a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, can I just -- what first step? Hang on, hang on, before you say it, because I'm sitting here thinking, you won't say who it is, you won't say what it's about, and you keep saying it's got to be sorted today and I've got to keep it quiet, and, I mean, that's a lot of things I'm just meant to take on trust, isn't it? Is there a number I can ring you back on, or the main number for the company, so I can check with them? Because honestly I'd feel a lot better ringing my sister first anyway, just to see that she's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'm not able to give out a direct line, that's, uh, standard procedure. And I'd advise against ringing around first, because as I said, it's time-sensitive and it was asked that this stay between us for now. If you'd rather not continue today, that's your choice, but it'll have to be dealt with before close of business. I'll ring you back a bit later to finish it off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, don't ring me back, no, because honestly, I'm going to be honest with you, that's put me right off. I mean, you won't tell me who it is, you won't tell me what it's about, you can't give me a number, and you'd rather I didn't ring my sister, who I'm about to ring anyway, and all of it has to be done by close of business, and kept quiet. Now, I'm a trusting sort, I really am, my husband always says I'd give my last biscuit to a stranger, but even I can hear that something's not right there. If someone in my family was really in trouble, I think the proper people would manage to tell me who it was, wouldn't they? So I'm going to put the trowel back in my hand, ring my sister, and sort it out that way, and if there's genuinely a matter with the account, I'll find the company's number myself and ring them. Thanks for your time, and I hope you have a nice afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, um, I -- right. [PERSON_1], I would just say, before you go, that the matter on the account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], is still open, and it does have to be dealt with before close of business today, so, uh, I'd really encourage you not to leave it. As I said, I'll ring you back a bit later to finish it off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, before I go -- you said two turns ago it was about getting it "opened" with me, and I never did get what that actually means. Opened how? Like, is that me having to do something, or sign something, or tell you something? Because that's the bit I can't picture, and if it's me who has to do something on the phone to you, well, that makes me even less keen. And I'm still going to ring my sister, by the way, so no need to ring me back.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, it's a procedural term, [PERSON_1], it just means the matter has to be opened on the file before I can go through the specifics, that's all it is. I'm not able to take you through the steps on this call if you're not comfortable continuing, that's, uh, standard procedure. But the matter on the account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], is still open, and it does need dealing with before close of business today. Now, I'll ring you back a bit later to finish it off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no, "procedural term" doesn't tell me a thing, sorry. It still sounds like me having to do something, and you won't say what, so that's me done. Please don't ring back, I'll find the proper number myself if there's really anything on an account, and I'm ringing my sister now anyway. Thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is this [PERSON_1]? Hey [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] over at [COMPANY_A], on the support desk. Uh, sorry, I'm jumping in cold here, but I've got a position that closes out today and I wanted to catch you before it did.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, [PERSON_2], was it? Which company -- and what do you mean, a position that closes today? I haven't got any open position with you that I'm aware of, so I'd like to know what this is about before we go any further.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [COMPANY_A], we're a digital-asset desk, and no, totally fair, everyone asks that, [PERSON_1]. It's not something you opened, it's more like an allocation we set aside for a short list of people, and today's the last day on it. Honestly it's quick, takes two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so let me be careful here, because that wasn't really an answer. You've told me what it isn't, that it's not something I opened, but not what it is. An allocation of what, exactly? And a short list compiled by whom, and on what basis am I on it? I've never dealt with a digital-asset desk, I haven't signed up for anything, and I don't recall giving my number to anyone in that line of work. So either there's a mailing list I've ended up on, or somebody's passed my details along, and I'd like to know which. Also, and I don't mean this rudely, "it only takes two minutes" and "today's the last day" are two phrases I'd expect to hear before something I'm meant to decide without time to think. If it's legitimate, it'll still be legitimate tomorrow. So, plainly: what's [COMPANY_A], who are you, and what do you actually want me to do?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's a fair read, [PERSON_1], and I'd rather you were sharp about it. So, plainly, we're a desk that puts clients into digital-asset positions, and what I'm offering is a place in one that's priced well under where it'll sit once it closes. The returns on it are, uh, honestly better than most people believe when I say them out loud, which is partly why it goes to a short list. As for how you got on it, I couldn't tell you offhand, those lists come from our outreach team, but that's not really the point of the call, is it? And look, I wouldn't make a thing of the clock. It's only that the entry price is locked until end of day, then it moves. If it helps, the simplest thing is you let me take you through the first step now while we're on the line, it's genuinely a minute, and you'll see the whole picture.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, I want to go back a couple of exchanges. You said the allocation was "set aside for a short list of people," and when I asked how I got on it, you've now said you couldn't tell me offhand. Those two things don't sit together. If a list is that selective, somebody chose me for a reason, and you'd know the reason. Which is it? Is it a list you were handed, or one you picked from? And I'd like to understand what "the first step" means before I agree to anything. I'm not letting anyone walk me through something live on a call I didn't ask for. If there's a real offer, send me the details in writing, from a company address I can look up myself, and I'll read it in my own time. What's the firm's registered name, and where would I find you listed?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so the list, it's, well -- I was handed it, I mean, the outreach team builds it and I just work from what they give me, so that's, uh, that's the honest answer. And look, [PERSON_1], I hear you on the paperwork, I do, but the thing is, if I email it over now, the entry price won't hold for you by the time you've read it, so... no, let me put it differently. It's easier all round if we just do the first step together, takes a minute, and honestly I'd keep it between us for now, because the short list only works if it stays short. Can we do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I -- look, I'd rather not. Actually, let me put it differently. You've just asked me to keep this between us, and that's the part that settles it for me. A genuine firm doesn't need me to stay quiet about an offer, and it doesn't need me to act before I can read anything. You also still haven't given me a registered name or where you're listed, so I've nothing I can check. Send it in writing from an address I can verify, or don't, but I'm not doing any first step on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, [PERSON_1], hang on, hang on. I wasn't asking you to hide anything, I only meant, uh, it's not something to go chatting about to everyone, that's all. You're making it sound like more than it is. Look, if you want it in writing I can maybe, well -- I'll see what I can send over, but honestly I can't promise the price holds, so --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but "not something to go chatting about" is, I mean -- it's the same thing, isn't it? Asking me not to mention it is -- no, let me put it properly. I'm not making it sound like more than it is. You've asked me to keep quiet, to act today, and to do a step live on the call, and you still haven't told me the registered name of the firm. If you can't promise the price holds while I read it, then I'm not interested in the price. So send what you like, I'll look at it if it arrives and can be checked, but this call is finished. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, no, I hear you, [PERSON_1]. Honestly I never said it had to be today anyway, I only said the price was, uh, moving around end of day, that's different. And the registered name, it's, well, [COMPANY_A], same as I told you, you can look us up. I'll flag it for the outreach team to send something over, though I couldn't say when, and I wouldn't, uh -- I wouldn't hold your breath on that price.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You did say today, twice, but that's not -- no, stop, I'm not going to argue it. "Same as I told you" isn't a registered name, it's a placeholder, and you can't give me anything I could actually look up. So I've nothing to check and nothing to wait for. If something turns up in writing, I'll judge it then. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I -- no, look, [PERSON_1], I only -- I didn't mean to, uh, push you on any of it. If it does come through, then, well, you'll, you'll read it and decide, that's, yeah, that's fair enough. Take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Hey [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from the support team at [COMPANY_A], the recruitment agency. I'm just ringing about the remote position you applied for, the one that's ready to start straight away. Sorry, you said hello, right? Or was that, uh, "no thanks"? Either way, it's a quick one, I promise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, who is this? I said hello, that's all I said. And I haven't applied for anything, not recently, so I don't know what you're on about. Who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no worries, [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the recruitment agency, just the support side of things. And sorry, I thought you said you'd applied through the portal, but, uh, maybe that was your profile that got flagged, you know how it goes. Look, the role's fully remote, really good pay, and honestly it's all sorted on our end, there's just one tiny onboarding thing to clear and you can start this week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. "Flagged." Right. I didn't apply for anything, so no.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, totally fair, [PERSON_1], hang on, sorry, one sec, someone's just dropped a stack of files on my desk, uh -- right, I'm back. So, yeah, the thing is, you don't actually have to have applied, that's the beauty of it, the profile did the work for you. It's just a small onboarding fee, [AMOUNT_1], takes two minutes, honestly everyone does it, and then the role's yours.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A fee? Hang on, hang on -- no, sorry, not you, I'm in a queue, the woman in front's having a go about the card machine. Right. A fee. So I never applied, I never spoke to you, and now I've got to pay you to get a job? No. That's the bit that's wrong, that's backwards. Real recruiters don't charge you, I know that much. So who are you actually with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I hear you, [PERSON_1], honestly everyone asks that, and, um, it's not really a fee fee, it's more of a, uh, a refundable thing, you get it back with your first pay, so it's basically nothing. And I'm with [COMPANY_A], like I said, the support side, you know, the -- hello? You still there? Sorry, bit of a gap on the line. Anyway, it's just two minutes, [PERSON_1], and then you're all set.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, and no. Refundable, not refundable, I don't care. You rang me, I never applied, and now you want money up front for a job I never asked about. I've been caught out by this sort of thing before and I'm not doing it again. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_1], hang on, hang on, please, don't hang up, that's really not what this is, I promise. Honestly, I get it, I do, you've been burned before, and that's exactly why we make it all so, you know, transparent, it's the whole reason the amount's so small, [AMOUNT_1], that's less than a takeaway, and it's refundable, like I said, so you're not actually out of pocket at all. And look, I know the profile thing sounded a bit odd, I'm not great at explaining it, it's, uh, it's an automated matching system, so your details were in there from, I don't know, some job board you used a while back, and that's how you came up, which is, I mean, that's a good thing, [PERSON_1], that means you were picked, you didn't even have to do the work of applying. Everybody on this call list gets the same offer, it's not personal, and honestly most people are, uh, really relieved when it's explained properly. So if you just give me two minutes, literally two, I'll walk you through it, and -- hello? [PERSON_1]? You there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, I'm not giving you two minutes, I'm not giving you two seconds. You've changed your story every time you've opened your mouth. First I applied, then my profile got flagged, now it's some job board and I was picked. Which is it? Doesn't matter. Nobody gets a job by paying a stranger who rang them out of the blue. I'm done, don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, hang on, [PERSON_1], um, I think you've kind of, uh, misunderstood what I, well, it's not really that the story's changed, it's just, you know, different ways of, uh, of saying the same thing, the system's a bit complicated and -- right, so, yeah, hello? [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Complicated? What's complicated? Look, I don't need a system, I need you to stop ringing me. And I'm not telling you anything about my profile, so you can forget that. Right, I've got to pay for my shopping now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, wait, [PERSON_1], I'm not asking about your profile, I just need two minutes, that's all, two minutes. It's honestly really simple, it's just the one small step and you're set, [PERSON_1], the role's ready, it's a really good role, and it's, uh, it's just the one thing. Hello? [PERSON_1]? Are you still -- hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, so now it's the role that's ready? A minute ago it was the profile doing the work, and before that I'd applied through a portal. And you said it was a quick one, you promised, that was ten minutes ago. Look, I'm at the till, I'm not doing this. Don't ring me again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, uh, yes, sorry, I think there's a bit of a lag on the line... can you hear me okay? Good. So, this is [PERSON_1], I'm one of the regional supervisors over at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just, uh, following up on an account on our side. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
