utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan going. Um, you said a lag, yes, I can hear you. But what was it you said before that -- regional what? And which company again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Regional supervisor, sorry, at [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, you'd have bought through us at some point, I mean it's just a routine -- oh, no, no, go on, finish your pan, I don't want to burn your dinner. It's just a quick account matter, nothing to worry about. Can I just confirm I've got [PERSON_2] on the line?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, let me just turn this down. Right. Sorry, software retailer? I don't, um, I don't really remember buying anything. And you haven't said what the account thing is yet. Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair enough, it's [PERSON_1], I'm a supervisor at [COMPANY_A], and honestly most people don't remember it, it's a subscription, not a one-off purchase, so it just sort of ticks along in the background. That's actually why I'm ringing, it looks like it got billed twice. Oh, and sorry, I said regional supervisor earlier, I'm more on the, uh, accounts side, but same department really. Anyway, it's [AMOUNT_1] that's come out twice on your account, and I'd rather sort the refund while I've got you than have you chasing us later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a refund? I don't, I don't remember any subscription.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, and that's really common, honestly, these things get set up through a free trial and people forget. But it doesn't change the fact that [AMOUNT_1] went out twice, and under our procedure a double-billing has to be flagged and put right on a live call, otherwise it drops into a queue and you could be waiting weeks. Look, I'm trying to help you here, so if you could just bear with me for a couple of minutes, that'd be great.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I really don't remember any subscription. I don't remember signing up for anything. Um, and you said regional supervisor, and then accounts, and I'm, I'm just a bit lost. What is it you actually need from me? Because I don't remember any subscription, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, I'll just -- no, hang on, let me cut in, because I think I'm making this more confusing than it needs to be. I don't need anything from you, not really. What I need is two minutes for you to confirm it's your account so I can authorise the refund, and honestly the supervisor, accounts thing, it's the same desk, I'm not sure why that's a sticking point. I mean, I'm the one trying to give you money back here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a desk? What desk? Oh, you mean the, um, the cash desk? I haven't been in to any shop. Hang on. And you said giving me money back, but I haven't paid anything, have I? I don't know what you want me to confirm. Confirm what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not a cash desk, it's, uh, the department, accounts and supervision sit together, that's all I meant. And you have paid, that's the whole point, [AMOUNT_1] came off twice, I can see both entries in front of me under [ACCOUNT_REF]. All I need is for you to confirm you're [PERSON_2] and that you're happy to proceed, and I can get the refund moving while we're talking. I mean, I'd have thought you'd be pleased, it's not often someone rings to give money back, and I'm getting the sense you think I'm trying something on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't think that, I mean, I don't know. I don't know you, do I? Um. You keep changing what you are, supervisor, then accounts. And you've still not said what I'm supposed to confirm. Hang on, I've got to stir this. Sorry. Look, if it's really my account, can't I just ring the company myself? Is there a number for you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ringing the company, no, look, that's just going to put you in a queue, and then the reference -- listen, if you ring the main line they can't even see the flag I've put on it, so you'd be starting from scratch and the refund window closes today. I'm not asking for anything strange, I just need a couple of minutes at your computer so I can show you the duplicate on screen and sort it live, and honestly I'd have thought after all this you'd trust me by now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, my computer? No, no, I'm not going to do that. I'm cooking, and I don't, I don't even really use it much. And you said the window closes today, but you only just said that, didn't you? Before it was weeks in a queue. I don't, I don't like this. If it's a real refund then it can wait while I ring them myself. I'm going to go now. Sorry. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, hang on, please, don't hang up, because I think we've got our wires crossed and that's on me, not you. Look, the weeks in a queue and the window closing today, those are the same thing, honestly, the queue is what happens after the window shuts, so I wasn't contradicting myself, I just explained it badly because I was trying to rush you off to your dinner. And the supervisor, accounts business, that's me being sloppy, I wear a couple of hats, it happens, but it doesn't change what's on the screen in front of me. I'll tell you what, we don't need your computer, I'm not even fussed about the computer, forget I said it. All I need is for you to say yes, that you're happy for me to go ahead and process it, and that's it, I put it through, you get the money back, you carry on stirring your pan. I mean, you've been very patient, and I'd hate for you to lose [AMOUNT_1] just because we got off on the wrong foot, so, can I go ahead?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? No, hang on. You said you didn't want anything from me, and now you want me to say yes to something. Yes to what? I don't even know what I'd be agreeing to. And you said, um, it was just two minutes at the start, and then my computer, and now it's not the computer. I'm not saying yes. I'm going to ring the company myself, on whatever number's on, um, on a bill or something. Sorry. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, just listen a second, because you're not hearing me, and I'll say it one more time, it's only a yes to the refund, that's it, a yes to the refund. I'm not asking for anything else, not the computer, nothing, and I honestly don't understand why that's such a problem. I'm the one doing you a favour here, and it's a bit much to be treated like I'm up to something just because I'm trying to put your money back. So, a yes to the refund, that's all, and then we're done and you can get back to your dinner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Sorry, no. You keep saying it's just a yes, but I don't know what I'm saying yes to, and you've changed your story about three times now. I'm not agreeing to anything. If there's really money owed to me, the company can sort it when I ring them. I've got to go, my dinner's catching. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yes, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm just -- I'm calling from the regional office at [COMPANY_A], and I only need a minute of your time, it's about your--

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Which company did you say? I didn't catch that, I've got -- hang on, [PERSON_1], hang on, just put that down for a second -- sorry. Who is this, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, take your time. It's [COMPANY_A], the bank, I'm a regional supervisor over on the fraud side. Sorry, did you say you were putting down a pen? No, no, you don't need to write anything down, this is just a quick courtesy call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said put something down, it's, it's a kid thing, never mind. Sorry, a courtesy call about what? Because I haven't, I didn't ask the bank for anything, and you still haven't said what this is actually, so what's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, kids, I get it, I've got two myself. Okay, so, uh, it's just that our monitoring picked up a charge attempt on your account earlier today, [AMOUNT_1], and it was flagged for review. Nothing's gone through, that's the point of the call, I just need to confirm a couple of things with you before it's released or declined.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said it was a courtesy call, and now there's a charge, and it's about to be released or declined? That's not really a courtesy, is it. And you said nothing's gone through, but if it's flagged, wouldn't it just be stopped already? Why do you need me for it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, it's, look, it's both, it's a courtesy and a review, that's just how the procedure works, the system holds it and then it needs a human to confirm it. I mean, I did say nothing's gone through, it's on hold, it's sitting on hold, and it stays on hold only until we speak to the account holder. So I just need to verify a couple of details with you and we can get it closed out today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Verify what details, exactly? Because you rang me, so shouldn't you be the one who already has them? And you still haven't actually said which bank. You just said the bank. Which one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, [PERSON_1], I'm going to be straight with you, because I'd rather not spend this whole call going in circles. I did say [COMPANY_A], twice now, and honestly I'm a little surprised I'm being asked to prove myself when I'm the one trying to stop money leaving your account. As for the details, no, we don't hold everything on screen, and that's by design. The system only shows me partial information so that nothing sensitive sits in front of a supervisor, so what I do is confirm a few things with the account holder directly, like your full name, your date of birth, and the last few digits of the card, and then I can release or decline the hold. Look, the window on this review closes fairly soon, and if it lapses the charge gets pushed through automatically, so I'd honestly rather not be the one explaining to you afterwards why it went through. So if we could just get on with it, that would really help us both.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Right, so, I'm supposed to hand over my date of birth and card digits to someone who rang me, and who's now telling me it gets pushed through if I take too long? Doesn't that, I mean doesn't that seem backwards to you? Why would a bank let a charge go through just because a phone call ran late? And no, I'm not saying any of that. If it's really the bank, I'll ring the number on the back of my card and ask for the fraud team myself. That's, yeah, that's what I'll do. Sorry, I've got a kid here, I need to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, [PERSON_1], hold on a second, I'd really rather you didn't hang up on a live review. If you ring the front line, they won't have any of this in front of them, you'll be queuing for, uh, half an hour, and by then the hold will have lapsed. I mean, it's your account, it's your call, but I'm not going to take it personally if-- Look, what's the branch I'd tell them you were speaking to? Or, no, never mind, I've got other accounts to get to. Just, if anything goes through, that's on file as you declining to verify. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right, well, um -- yeah. Declining to verify, okay. Fine, that's, I'll take that. If it's real, the bank'll have my number and they can ring back, and I'll ring them first anyway. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], I'm telling you, it's a live review, it's a live review and it's running right now, so if you could just stay on for one second -- no. You know what, I can't, I can't give you a direct line, it doesn't work like that, the number goes through the system. So that's, yeah, that's all from me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, one thing. You said it was just a courtesy call, and then you said it was a live review that was about to lapse, and now there's no direct line. That doesn't add up for me. So no, I'm hanging up and I'll ring the number on the back of my card. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Two turns ago, uh, what did I say two turns ago? That it went through the system? Look, I don't have time to go back over every word, I've got a queue of accounts here, and frankly I don't appreciate being cross-examined by someone I'm trying to help. That's it from me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sweetheart, not now, put that down, I'm on the phone -- sorry. What? No, I'm not cross-examining anyone, I just asked a few questions. Anyway, I'm done. I'll ring the bank myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, so, right, I mean, that's, that's your choice, [PERSON_1], and I'm not going to, uh, chase you. Just make a note of the time you rang off, that's all I'll say. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, a note of the time I rang off? I thought you rang me. And a couple of turns back you said the number goes through the system, what did you mean by that? Through what system? Never mind, I'm not going to get a straight answer, am I. I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, hello. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the power company, and I, I really hate to be the one doing this, but your electricity is going to be cut off within the hour. There's an unpaid balance on the account, and, well, I just didn't want you to get caught off guard.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi, yeah, this is, uh, [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, hang on, I've got you on loudspeaker, I'm elbow-deep in the tomato bed and there's a blackbird going absolutely nuts at me, he thinks I'm after his worms, ha. Anyway, cut off within the hour? Gosh, that's, I mean, I thought I paid everything, I'm usually pretty on top of it. Which company did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, [COMPANY_A]. Yes. I'm, uh, I'm not actually with them myself, I'm sort of passing along a message from a person there, so it's a bit... anyway. And I'm sure you did pay, [PERSON_1], I'm sure you're very careful, it's just that the balance is showing as [AMOUNT_1], and, I mean, I'd hate for your lights to go out, especially, uh, with the day getting on. Actually, sorry, I said within the hour, didn't I? It might be a little less than that, I'm not totally sure, but it's soon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, bless you for letting me know, that's kind. Hang on, sorry, the dog's just got hold of my glove again, drop it, Biscuit, drop it! Ha, no, he's got the whole thing, never mind. Right, where was I. Sorry, so you're passing along a message from someone there, but you're not actually with them? That's, um, a bit odd, isn't it? And it's "within the hour" and then "a bit less," so, I mean, how soon is soon? Because honestly I'd feel better if I just rang them myself, you know, on the number on my bill. Would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, well, I, I wouldn't, uh, I don't think there's time for that, [PERSON_1]. By the time you're on hold with the main line, it could already be, well, you'd be sitting in the dark. And I'm, I'm only trying to help here, I went out of my way to call you. Honestly, the quickest thing would be to settle it with me now, over the phone, I can, uh, give you the details on how, and then it's done and you can go back to your tomatoes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, but I could just, sorry, go on, no, you go -- no, sorry, I was only going to say I've got the bill right here in the shed, it's on the shelf with the twine, so ringing them would take two minutes, honestly. And hang on, settle it with you? Over the phone? But you just told me you're not even with them. That's, hmm, that's a bit of a funny way to pay a power bill, isn't it? I'd much rather do it with the actual company, so, um, no, I think I'll ring the number on the bill. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, I mean... right, so... look, I'm, I'm not trying to be funny about it, [PERSON_1]. I'm just, I'm really not the one who makes the rules here, it's, it's how they asked me to do it, so, um, I'd be careful, because if you ring the main line and they can't even see that I called, well, that's not on me, is it? I just, I really don't think you should risk your power over, over a phone call you could have skipped.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Yeah, no, I don't think that's right, sorry. If the real company can't see you rang me, well, that's sort of the point, isn't it? And a power company wouldn't mind me ringing them to check, they'd be glad of it. Honestly, if the lights go off, they go off, and I'll sort it out with them in the morning. I'm going to go and find that bill and ring the number on it myself, okay? Thanks for the call, though, and, um, mind how you go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], please, don't hang up. Um, you said, a second ago, that the, that the company can't see that I called, and that's not, I didn't mean it like that, I only meant that, well, it might take them a while to, to find the note, and I, I really don't see why you'd think I was, that I'd do something, that's a bit hurtful, honestly, I took the time to call you. And, and it's not just the lights, is it, if it gets cut there's a reconnection fee on top, and that's, that's worse, so if you could just, uh, stay on with me a minute, please, and we, we can sort it out right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm sorry, I don't mean to be hurtful, honestly, you've been very nice about it. But I'm going to ring the number on my bill, that's all. I'll ring the number on the bill, and if there's a fee, there's a fee, and I'll sort it out with them. I really don't want to stay on and sort it out with you, because you did say you're not actually with them, and that's, well, that's what's stuck with me. So I'm going now, all right? Thanks again, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, [PERSON_1], sorry, just, you said I told you I'm not with them, and I, I did say it, but what I meant was, um, I'm not on the, the main desk, I'm, I'm sort of attached to them, there's a difference, and, and I don't think you really understood what I... could you just tell me what you think I said? Because I don't want you leaving this thinking I, I was being dishonest with you, that, that really isn't fair, I was only trying to look out for you, and if you hang up now and the power goes, I'd, I'd feel just awful about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you'd feel what? Oh, "awful," right, no, I thought you said "offal," and I was thinking, what's that got to do with anything, ha. Anyway, no, please don't feel awful, it's not on you, honestly. I'm not saying you're a bad person, I just, I'm going to ring the number on the bill and that's that. Right, I'm hanging up now, take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um... uh, well, I, right, so... [PERSON_1], please, one more second, I just, I don't see why you won't, I mean, I called you in good faith, and now it's like you think I'm, that I'm lying, and that's, that really stings, you know? And, uh, and I'm telling you the time is running out, so if you just stay on, just for a minute, and let me, let me help you sort the [AMOUNT_1] before it's, before it's too late, then nobody has to feel awful, do they?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you're not lying, I never said you were lying, I just said I'd ring the number on my bill. And that's, well, I've said it three times now, ha. Sorry, Biscuit's got the glove again. Anyway, the other thing, you said it was about this much, [AMOUNT_1], but earlier I think you said it was less than that? Or no, hang on, it was the time that kept changing, wasn't it, an hour, then less. Whatever. I'm not staying on, love, I'm going to find the bill in the shed and ring them, so, bye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, hang on, I never said the amount was different, it's [AMOUNT_1], it's always been [AMOUNT_1], and the time, well, it's, it's soon, that's all I've ever, I mean, I'm not trying to trick you, [PERSON_1], I'm just, I'm trying to help, and it really hurts that you'd think, that you'd... look, please, if you ring the main line you'll lose the window, and then the lights go out, and that's on you, not me, so, so please, just stay on and let me sort the balance with you now, before it's too late.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, sorry, love, I really am going now. The lights can go out if they like, I've got candles somewhere, ha. And I did notice you said it'd be on me if I rang them, and honestly a real power company wouldn't mind that, so, um, that's that. I'm going to find the bill and ring them myself. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, [PERSON_1], hold on, I never said it'd be on you, I said, well, I said it wouldn't be on me, that's different, and I, I only said an hour, I never said less, whatever you think you heard, and, and it's, it's soon, it's really soon, so please, I'm begging you, just stay on the line and settle it with me now, because if you ring them you'll, you'll lose the, the window, and that's not a threat, it's just, it's how it works, and I'd, I'd feel terrible, I really would...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a window? Oh, I thought you said "widow," and I was thinking, well, I'm not a widow, I've got a husband, he's up the ladder doing the gutters, ha. Oh, a window, right, the window to pay. Mm. I don't think I believe in that window, love, to be honest. Look, I'm going to find the bill and ring the number on it. You take care now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Right. It's, uh, I'm calling from the collections office at [COMPANY_A], and it's regarding a matter that, well, it concerns your relative, [PERSON_2]. They can't come to the phone right now, so I'm, I'm the one handling it on their behalf.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Collections? Who is this? I'm just, I've got a pan on, hang on. Sorry, who did you say you were calling about? [PERSON_2]? What do you mean, they can't come to the phone? Sorry, who are you again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_2], that's the name on the file. And it's, uh, not a pan, no, I said they can't come to the phone, because of the situation they're in. I'm with the collections office at [COMPANY_A], that's who I am, and there's an outstanding figure of [AMOUNT_1] that's been sitting there, and that's now at the stage where it has to be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? No, the pan's mine, I'm cooking, I said I've got a pan on. Hang on. What situation? What do you mean, the situation they're in? Is [PERSON_2] all right? Sorry, I just, I don't understand, why are you ringing me about money? Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sorry, the pan, understood. Hang on one second, there's someone at my desk, uh -- no, it's fine, carry on. So, [PERSON_2] is, I mean, they're not in a good place at the moment, and I'd rather not go into all of it, it's not really mine to say. What I can tell you is the balance is [AMOUNT_1], and if it isn't settled today, the account goes to the next stage, and that isn't something that can be reversed after. I'd ask you not to ring around the family about it, it would only make things harder for [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, hold on. Not ring round the family? Why would you say that? That's -- no, sorry, what? Is [PERSON_2] in trouble? What's the matter with them? And you still haven't said who you actually are, you just said collections. Sorry, which company? I can't, I've got dinner on, I can't be doing with this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, there's a, uh, a colleague asking me something -- right, I'm back. [COMPANY_A], that's the name, collections department. I can note on the file that you'd like more detail on who I am, that's fine, but it doesn't change the balance, which is [AMOUNT_1]. As for [PERSON_2], I've said what I can say, they're not in a position to talk and it's better kept between us for now, because if it gets round, it gets worse for them, that's just how it goes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, that's not on. You won't tell me who you are, you won't tell me what's wrong with [PERSON_2], and you want me to keep quiet about it? That's, no. I'm going to ring [PERSON_2] myself, on the number I've got, and sort this out. And I'm not paying anything to anyone I don't know. Sorry, I've got to turn my pan off now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, I'll note that on the file, that you're declining, that's fine. Sorry, hang on, someone's just put a folder on my desk, uh -- no, it's fine. But I'd say, ringing [PERSON_2] at this stage, I mean, that isn't going to get an answer, and the balance of [AMOUNT_1] stays where it is. I'll try you again later this evening.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, don't ring me again. And hang on, why wouldn't [PERSON_2] answer? You just said that like you know something, and you still haven't told me one thing about who you are or what's gone on. If somebody's really in trouble you don't ring their family and tell them to keep quiet, I don't think. So I'm ringing [PERSON_2] myself, and if I can't get hold of them I'll ring someone else in the family, whatever you've said about it. I'm not paying anything today, not to you, not over the phone. If there's a real bill, they can send it in the post like anybody else. Right, I've got to see to my dinner. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, if I could just -- no, listen, I'm only saying that because, uh -- right, I'll note all of that, the post, the refusal, ringing round the family, it's all going on the file. Whatever you decide, the balance of [AMOUNT_1] stays as it is and the next stage still goes ahead, I can't change that from this end. I'll leave you to your dinner and ring you back later to finish this off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, you're not ringing me back. I said, don't ring me again. I'm not paying anything, not over the phone, send it in the post. And I'm ringing [PERSON_2] myself, I said that, I'm ringing them tonight. I don't know who you are, that's the whole thing, you never said. So, no. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you'll pay it tonight? Right, good, that's, uh, that's sensible, I'll make a note of that on the file. No, hang on, I've -- yes, ring [PERSON_2] if you like, I can't stop you, that's up to you. But I'll still try you again later to finish this off, so, uh, have your dinner and I'll be in touch.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I never said I'd pay, I said -- no. I said I'm ringing [PERSON_2]. That's all. I'm not, I'm not paying anything tonight, or, I mean, not ever, not on the phone. Don't write that down, that's not what I said. And don't ring me later, I mean it. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a phone going off behind me, uh -- right, that's stopped. No, understood, I've got you down as declining, I'll amend the note. That doesn't change the balance, though, and it doesn't change the stage the account's at, those are settled on this side. I'll leave you to your dinner and, uh, I'll ring back later to finish this off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, stop, listen. I've said goodbye about four times now and you keep going. I don't know who you are. You said collections, you said [COMPANY_A], that's all you've said, and then it's been nothing about [PERSON_2], just that they're in a bad place and I mustn't tell anyone. Well, I'm going to tell everyone. That's what you do when someone's in trouble, you ring round, you don't keep it quiet. And I've got a pan on the hob and it's catching, I can smell it, so I haven't got time for this. If there's a real bill, post it. If [PERSON_2]'s really in trouble, I'll hear it from them or from the family, not from you. So no, I'm not paying, I'm not having you ring me back, and I'm putting the phone down now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Noted. I'll ring back later to finish it off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. You're not ringing back, I've told you. I'm going to put the phone down now, and if you ring again I just won't pick up. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yes, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Great, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant there, and I'm only calling because you're showing as approved for the remote position, the one you applied for through the, uh, the portal, and we've got a start slot open this week but it closes, so I just need two minutes of your time to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi! Yes, this is, uh -- yeah, that's me. Sorry, give me a sec, I've got dirt all over my hands, you're on speaker. Um, the remote position -- I mean, I did apply for a few things, so I'm, well, which one was this again? Sorry, I don't, I just want to make sure I know which one you mean, because I've sent off a bunch of those lately.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, that's fine, take your time, so it's the remote position, the remote one, you're approved for it, and it's a really good package, flexible hours, [AMOUNT_1] a week to start, no experience gap, none, which is why the slot closes so fast, so as I was saying, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A] to get you scheduled for this week. And which one it was, honestly, it's all under your approval on my screen, so that's not a problem, we just need to get you booked in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Okay, but you still haven't said which job it is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you haven't got the cost? No, no, that's the whole point, there's barely any cost, it's just the one-off onboarding fee, [AMOUNT_2], and that gets cleared before your start date, and then you're in, [AMOUNT_1] a week, so the fee's really the only thing standing between you and the slot, and honestly it's the same for everyone we onboard, so, yeah, shall we get you booked in?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, shoot, hang on, there's a bee going absolutely mad around the lavender, sorry, I'm just -- okay, it's off. Um, wait, a fee? I didn't say anything about the cost, I asked which job it was, and you've sort of skipped past that twice now. And a fee to start a job is, I mean, that's a bit backwards, isn't it? I thought the company paid me, not the other way round. So what's the actual job, and who exactly are you with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: So, um, [COMPANY_A], that's us, recruitment, and I hear you, I do, I get that question a lot, but it's not you paying the company, it's more of a, a cost that's reimbursed, it comes back to you, and the role itself is the remote administrative one, the flexible one, so that's all, uh, that's all in your approval, and the slot's open until end of day, so what I can do is pencil you in right now and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but -- no, wait. If it comes back to me, then why do I, why would I have to pay it first? That's, hm. And "remote administrative" is, well, that's not really a job, is it, that's just a type of job. I mean, I'm happy to hear it out, I really am, but I'm not putting any money down for something when I can't even find out which one it is, or, or look you up myself. Can I ring you back through the company's main number or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ring back, sure, you can, of course, but the thing is the main line won't have your approval on screen, that's all with me, with scheduling, so you'd be starting from scratch and the slot, the slot closes end of day. So it's [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A], scheduling, remote administrative, flexible, [AMOUNT_1] a week, and the fee's just the, the one-off onboarding fee, and it comes back to you, that's all it is, so shall I pencil you in?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the main line won't have my, my what, my "approval" on screen? No, wait, I thought you said "provincial"? The provincial line? Is there a different office, is that what you mean? Hang on, I've got the secateurs here, let me just put these down. Okay, but honestly, if I'm ringing the main number anyway it'd be starting from scratch, fine, that doesn't scare me. If it's a real approval they'll have a record of it somewhere, won't they? So I think I'll just ring them myself and ask. And no pencilling in, thanks, not with a fee in the picture. Anyway, lovely chatting, you take care, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, the secateurs, yes, no, there's no sending anything, just the, the Thursday slot, so Thursday works, I've got you down for Thursday, and there's nothing to do on your end today except, uh, you're approved, [PERSON_1], that's the main thing, so I'll pencil Thursday and we'll go from --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, wait, I'm not, I didn't say Thursday, I said I'd -- sorry, I'm not booking anything. Don't put me down for Thursday. I said I'd ring the company myself and ask, that's, that's all. If there's a real approval they'll find it. Anyway, thanks for the call, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Well, the slot's still there till end of day if you change your mind.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I won't be changing my mind, sorry. Like I said, I'll ring the company myself and ask them, and if there's really an approval sitting there, they'll find it, and if they don't, well, then that tells me something too, doesn't it? So, no Thursday, no fee, I'm just going to get on with my lavender. Thanks for ringing, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this, uh -- am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I always -- I mean, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, you sound like you might've just walked in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... yes, speaking. Who's calling, please? And, no, I haven't just walked in, I've been home a while.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, good, good, [PERSON_1], lovely, so you're home, that's -- that's perfect. It's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], customer care side of things, nothing to worry about, I promise. And I'm sorry, I did say hi, didn't I, I'm just -- I'm always the one who forgets to say who I am, my manager's forever telling me off for it. How's your day been so far, anything nice planned, or is it one of those just-stay-in kind of afternoons?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. Sorry, but I want to go back a moment. You said it's nothing to worry about, and you said you promise. What exactly is there that I might have worried about? You haven't actually told me what the call is regarding.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, you're right, that's fair, I do waffle, my husband says the same thing. It's nothing to worry about, [PERSON_1], really, it's just -- nothing to worry about, it's a routine thing, but, okay, so, there was a charge, a card charge that came through on your account earlier, for [AMOUNT_1], and our system flagged it as, you know, a bit unusual. So I just need to confirm a couple of things with you, and honestly the sooner we do, the better, because it's still sitting there pending.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, a moment ago you said there was nothing to worry about, and now it's a flagged unusual charge that's still pending and getting more urgent by the minute. Those two don't really sit together. Which account is this, exactly? You haven't named it, and [COMPANY_A] on its own doesn't tell me which of my providers you mean. And what are the couple of things you need me to confirm?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, okay, you've got me there, I'm being a bit all over the place, aren't I? It's your current account with us, the one ending in [ACCOUNT_REF], and the confirming is just, you know, quick bits, your full name and date of birth, and the address we have on file, so I can pull up the right record. I mean, I'd love to leave it, I really would, but if the charge goes through while we're chatting about it, that's a real headache for you, and nobody wants that on a Friday.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on. First you said it was a card charge, and now it's my current account. Those aren't the same thing, so which is it? And you're asking me for my name, date of birth and address so you can pull up the right record, but you rang me. If you're the bank, you already have all of that in front of you. I'm not giving you any of it. If there's a genuine problem, I'll ring the number on the back of my card myself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, it's the same thing, [PERSON_1], the card's tied to the current account, I just said it a bit loosely, that's all. And look, I could ring back, of course, but honestly the line you'd get on that number this time of day is a nightmare, and -- well, I'd hate for that charge to go through while you're sat on hold, and then it's your account that's, you know, frozen while we sort it out. Anyway, how long have you been with [COMPANY_A], out of interest? Because I've got a note here that says -- hang on, sorry, I've lost my place.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I said I'm not giving you my details, and I'll say it once more, I'm not giving you any of it. How long I've been a customer isn't something I'll discuss either, because you've lost your place, and that's rather the point. You've changed the story three times in a few minutes, and you've now told me that ringing the bank is the risky option. I'll ring the number on my card, and if there's a real charge, they'll tell me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Wonderful. My name is [PERSON_2], and I'm calling from the compliance office at [COMPANY_A], the charity you've supported in the past. Now, I do want to say right away that this isn't a, a complaint or anything of that sort, it's really a thank-you call, because our records show you were a monthly donor with us for quite some time, and, well, that monthly gift stopped a while back, and I wanted to, I mean, I felt it was right to reach out personally and ask whether that was intentional, or whether it simply slipped through, because those things do happen, cards expire, people move, and it would be a shame, a real shame, if a lapse like that went unnoticed on our end and, you know, wasn't ever properly looked at.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Compliance office? For a charity? Look, I'm in a queue here, so get to the point. Are you asking me for money or not?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, fair question, and I'm glad you asked it straight out, because you should always ask it straight out, with any organisation that calls you. The honest answer is, uh, yes, in a sense. I'm asking whether you'd consider renewing your monthly gift to [COMPANY_A], the one that lapsed. That's all this call is. I'm not asking you to pay anything today, and I'm not asking for card details over the phone, not on this call. As for the title, compliance office, I know that sounds rather formal for a charity, and I do see why it made you pause. It simply means my team looks after donor records and how supporters want to be contacted, so I'm the person who notices when a regular gift goes quiet. Now, I'd say it would be, well, better for the record if the lapse were resolved sooner rather than later, but that's only tidiness on our side, and it's entirely your decision. And if you'd rather not hear from us, just say so, and I'll take you off the calling list right now, no questions, no persuading.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, what's wrong with the record? You said something's been, what, flagged? Because nobody's flagging anything of mine. And "better for the record," that's a funny thing to say to someone who gave you a few quid once. Look, if you want to be taken off the list, then do it, I'm not stopping you. But I'm not renewing anything over the phone to a bloke I've never heard of. Which charity did you say it was again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, nothing's flagged, and, uh, I'm sorry, that was clumsy wording on my part. There's no problem with your record, nothing's wrong, I just put it badly. It's [COMPANY_A], the charity, that's the name. And I'll take you off the calling list now, as you've asked. You won't hear from us by phone again, and I'm sorry to have taken your time while you're in a queue. If you ever do want to look us up, you'd find us at [URL_1], but there's no obligation at all. Thank you for what you gave in the past, truly, and, uh, take care of yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Take me off the list. Off the list, yeah? Not "we'll see," off. And I'm not looking anything up, I've got my own way of finding a charity if I want one, thanks. But hang on, you said "better for the record" and you said "compliance" and now you say nothing's wrong, which is it? Never mind. I'm not renewing anything, not today, not over the phone. Right, I'm at the front now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Off the list, yes, properly off, no "we'll see." It's done as of this call. And you're right to press me on the wording, I wasn't clear, so, uh, to be plain: nothing's wrong, nothing's outstanding, and nothing needs doing from you. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], I hope the queue moves quickly. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well. I'll believe it when the phone stops ringing, because I've been told "you're off the list" before and then it was three more calls the following week. So if I get another one from you lot, I'm not being polite about it, I'll just put the phone down. And I'll say this, and I'm not having a go at you personally, but you did ring up and say compliance and records and lapse and "properly looked at," and none of that sounds like a thank-you call. It sounds like someone trying to make me feel I'd done something wrong, when I'd just stopped giving. People are allowed to stop giving. That's not a problem on anyone's record. Anyway. Nothing's outstanding, you said, so that's that. I'm not writing anything down, I'm not looking anything up, and I'm not ringing anyone back. Cheers. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, you're right, and I'd rather agree with you than argue. People are allowed to stop giving. It's not a problem on anyone's record, and, well, I shouldn't have framed it the way I did, with the lapse and the properly looked at, that was poor wording and I do apologise for it. I've marked you down as no further contact, so there shouldn't be any more calls, and if one does come, you've every right to put the phone down. Thank you for hearing me out, [PERSON_1], and, um, all the best. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, fine. Hang on, no, I'm not buying a bag, thanks, just the one thing. Sorry, what was I -- right. Good. No further contact, that's what I wanted. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] from the customs desk at [COMPANY_A]. Sorry, long day over here, but I've got a parcel of yours sitting with us.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Who is this, again? Customs desk at what -- [COMPANY_A]? I didn't, uh, I'm not expecting a parcel. Hang on, [PERSON_2] from where, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, not a pardon, a parcel, from [COMPANY_A], the courier. Though honestly, I'd take a pardon myself after the morning I've had. Anyway, it's the package that came in from overseas, the one with the tracking number you'd have on your confirmation email, and it's just got a small import charge on it before we can send it out to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said parcel, I heard you, I just -- I'm not expecting a parcel. Overseas? From who? I haven't ordered anything. And I don't have a confirmation email, so what tracking number are you talking about? Who's it even from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, right, so, uh, let me just -- sorry, bit of a pause there while I pull it up, bear with me. Look, it could be a gift, or something a friend sent, so it might've been a surprise to you, which is fair enough. The reference on the label is [CODE_1], and if you've got a text or email from us, or you look us up on our official tracking page, you'll see that same number sitting there. And honestly, there's no rush on my end, you don't need to pay anything on this call, it all goes through that tracking page, whenever you're ready.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- no, put that down, we don't throw that. Sorry. Uh, right, so a gift, from who? You still haven't said who it's from. And I don't have a text or an email from you, so why would I look at a page I don't know? You rang me, so how'd you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, sounds like you've got a busy house over there, no worries. So, fair questions, and I'd ask the same. I don't have the sender's name in front of me, just the origin and the parcel details, and the number on the shipment is the one the sender or the shop gave us for delivery, that's all I can see. Look, if you're not expecting anything, don't take my word for it. Go to the courier's own website, the one you'd find yourself, not anything I send, and put in [CODE_1] to see whether it's yours. If it's not, no harm done, you just ignore all this, and I'll note it as a wrong number on my end. Anyway, I've kept you long enough, you take care and sort out whatever got thrown, yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, wait. Two minutes ago you said there was an import charge on it, a small one. So is there a charge or isn't there? Because now you're saying it might be a wrong number, and that doesn't sound like the same call. And you don't know who it's from, but you know it's got a charge on it? How's that work?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair catch, I did make that sound muddled. So, there is a charge on the parcel, that part's real, it's [AMOUNT_1], and it's on the tracking page next to [CODE_1]. What I can't tell you is who sent it, because that's not on my screen, and that's why I said check it yourself. If the page shows nothing under your name, then it's a wrong number and you can forget I called. If it does show up, the charge sits there, you pay it through that page when you're ready, not on the phone, and nothing happens to the parcel today either way. Anyway, I'll let you get back to the house, thanks for putting up with me, [PERSON_1], you take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, wait, you don't know who sent it but you know it's [AMOUNT_1]? That's -- no. I'm not looking anything up because you told me to. If there's really a parcel, you can post me a card or email me, I'm not doing it off a phone call I didn't ask for. So, yeah, no, I'm done with this. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Um, is this [PERSON_1]? Right, good. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm the compliance officer at [COMPANY_A], the shop on the high street in [CITY_1] -- and before you say anything, I do realise a call like this can sound a bit, well, unexpected, so please take your time with it. The reason I'm ringing is that you entered our prize draw at the community event a few weeks back, and your entry was one of the ones drawn, and, uh, it's only a minor prize, nothing grand, but our process is that I confirm the details with the winner personally before anything is set aside, and I'd rather do that properly than just leave you a message, if that makes sense.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, one sec -- [muffled, turning away] yeah, I'll be right there, just give me a minute. Sorry, um, so you're, uh, the compliance officer at a shop, and I won a prize draw? I mean, I don't really remember entering anything, a few weeks back, at a community event? Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, that's a perfectly fair question, and I'd much rather you asked it than just took my word for anything. So, [PERSON_2], compliance officer, [COMPANY_A], the shop on the high street in [CITY_1]. And the event was the community fair, uh, the one at the [CITY_1] hall on the, well, I can give you the exact date, it was a Saturday, and entry was a little paper slip you'd have filled in at our table, name and a phone number, that's all it would have been. Now, um, you said you don't remember entering, and that's quite common honestly, people drop a slip in a bowl while they're chatting and forget about it, but I wouldn't want to presume, so if you'd like to think back, take a moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, a paper slip, name and phone number, at a table at the fair. Hm. I mean, I might have, I go to that thing most years, but I honestly can't say I remember a shop table. And, uh, why does a prize draw need a compliance officer? That's a bit of an odd job title for handing out a minor prize, isn't it? What is it exactly you need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, uh, a "noble" prize? No, no, ha, nothing quite so grand, it's a minor one, I did say. Sorry, I'm wondering if the line's a bit crackly, I'm sure you said something else. But the title, yes, I welcome that, honestly, it's a fair thing to wonder about. It's a bit grand for a small shop, I'll grant you, but I'm the one who looks after how we run draws and handle entries, which, well, it covers a good deal of ground, and I like to keep it by the book. What I need from you is, um, really just to confirm the entry is yours, so that the prize can be put by with your name on it, and, ah, I'd rather not rush that, though these things do tend to want settling reasonably soon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I said minor, not noble, I didn't say anything like that. Anyway, "confirm the entry is yours" -- confirm how, exactly? And why does it need settling soon?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, yes, minor, you're quite right, I misheard you, I'm sorry about that, that's my mistake and not yours. Now, confirm how, and I'm glad you're asking, because it's the right question and I'd think less of anyone who didn't. Really it's very small. Your name, which I have, the phone number on the slip, which is obviously this one, and, um, perhaps your address, so that I can match you against the entry. But I want to be clear that none of it is a condition of anything, and you don't owe us a thing. There's nothing to pay, nothing to send, no card, no account, no fee of any kind, and if I ever said otherwise you should put the phone down on me. The prize itself is collected in person, at the shop, over the counter, and you'd bring nothing but yourself. And if you'd rather not give me an address over the phone, which, honestly, I wouldn't blame you for, we can skip it entirely and you simply come in and we sort it out face to face. As for the settling soon, I may have made it sound firmer than it is. It's only that we like to tidy the draw up and put the prizes on the shelf at some point, so, well, sooner is simpler than later, though I'm not holding a clock over you. And, uh, the date of the fair, since you

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, you cut off there at the end, something about the date of the fair? Um, but actually, can I go back a second? Two turns ago you said you needed to confirm the entry's mine so the prize can be "put by" with my name on it. Put by where? And if you've already got my name and this number off the slip, what is there left for me to confirm?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, yes, sorry, I trailed off there, I do that. The date of the fair, I was going to say I can give it to you, it was a Saturday, and, um, now "put by," that's a bit of shop talk, I do apologise. It just means set aside, on a shelf behind the counter, with a note on it, nothing more mysterious than that. Now, what's left for you to confirm, well, honestly, very little, and I think I made it sound like more than it is. What I have is a name and a number off a paper slip, and what I'm asking is only whether those are yours, which, you've sort of half said already, so, uh, there may be nothing else I need from you at all. Actually, you mentioned a "hurry," just then, and I want to be clear I'm not in one, nor should you be.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I didn't say hurry, I said soon, but fine. Look, if there's a prize, it's collected at the shop, so I'll just pop in sometime and ask. I'm at work, so I'll leave it there. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, no, you're quite right, soon, not hurry, I keep putting words in your mouth, and I'm sorry. And popping in is exactly what I'd suggest, honestly. Though, um, I did say a Saturday earlier, and I think I may have muddled that, it might have been the Sunday of that weekend, I'll check my notes. Which is rather another reason it'd be easier if I rang you back at a better time, when you're not at work, and I'll have the exact date in front of me. Would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you don't need to ring back. I'll come into the shop if I want the prize, and you can check your notes before then. So Saturday or Sunday, you've gone back and forth on it, and that's all the more reason I'm not giving anything out over the phone. Thanks for calling. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Oh, hi, um -- is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm calling from, well, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier, and I -- I don't want to alarm you, but it's about an overdue balance on your account, and I did want you to hear it from us before anything happened. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm still here. Sorry, hang on -- [PERSON_1] is, well, who's asking? And before anything happens, what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, that's -- yes, it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A]. I'm a case handler there, and I'm only calling because there's an overdue balance of [AMOUNT_1] on the account, and if it isn't dealt with, supply would be interrupted on the [CODE_1]... I mean, sorry, I'm not meant to say that's going to happen, it's just that the date on the notice is the [CODE_1]. I'd really like to stop it getting that far, for your sake. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I'm sorry, you're a case handler, and you haven't actually said whether you're talking to [PERSON_1] yet, have you? I mean, if it was overdue, wouldn't I have had a letter or something first?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, I'm sorry, I should have asked first. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? And on the letter, yes, there should have been reminders sent before today, so if nothing's reached you, that's worth knowing, and I'm sorry about that. Um, and if it helps, your last bill showed an account balance of [AMOUNT_2] against reference [ACCOUNT_REF], so you can check what I'm saying against that. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on a sec -- no, put that down, not on the sofa, please -- sorry. Um. So you're asking if I'm [PERSON_1], but you rang me. Shouldn't you already know who you've called? And you've read me a reference and an amount off my own bill, which, I mean, anyone could have those, couldn't they? How would I know you're actually from them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, that's a fair thing to say, and I'm sorry. Um, I did ring the number on the account, I just like to check I've got the right person before I say anything about it, but I can see how that sounds backwards. And, uh, you're right, I don't want you to just take my word for it. So please don't. If you log into your own online account, or ring the number printed on your bill, you'll see the balance and the date there, and I'm not asking you to pay anything on this call, nothing at all. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, I'm here. Sorry, it's just -- so you're saying I should ring the number on my bill, not you. Right? The number on the bill. And you're not asking me for anything today, nothing? Because, I mean, that's not usually how these calls go, is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, well -- yes, the number on your bill, not one I give you. And no, I'm not asking for anything today, no payment, no details, nothing. I just, I mean, if you did want to sort it out, there's a payment plan we can set up, so it doesn't have to be the whole [AMOUNT_1] at once, but that's something you'd do through your own account, not with me on the phone. I'd only hate for the [CODE_1] to come round and you hadn't heard. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here, sorry, I've got my little one on the other side of the room and she's, uh, she's got a pen near the wall, so I'm half watching that. Right. So, let me just say it back, because I want to be sure I've got it. You rang me, you've told me there's a balance, you've told me there's a date, and what you want me to do is go and check it myself, through my own account or the number on my bill, and not through you. Which, I mean, that's sensible, that's what I'd do anyway, so why does it feel like I'm being nudged toward something? Maybe that's just me. A relative of mine got caught out last year, so I'm probably a bit jumpy about all of it. But I still don't know why I'd be hearing about this from a phone call before a letter, and you did say there'd been reminders, and I haven't had any, not that I remember. So here's what I think I'll do. I'll check the account myself, later, when she's in bed and I can actually concentrate. And if there's something there, I'll ring the number on the bill. Is that, uh, is that all right with you? Is there anything else you actually need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's, yes, that's all right, that's more than all right. And no, there's nothing else I need from you, truly. Sorry, you said your relative got caught out, and I'm sorry to hear that, it's horrible when that happens. And, um, the pen on the wall, I hope that's, well, I hope it comes off. Just, if you do check it later, the date on the notice is the [CODE_1], so it's worth having a look before then, that's all, only so it doesn't catch you out. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. I'll check it later, like I said. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, thank you for your time, and sorry again for the worry. Bye now, [PERSON_1] -- take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry to trouble you, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A] -- I'm one of the case handlers there. I just wanted to say thank you, really, for the monthly gift you used to give us, I think it was [AMOUNT_1] a month, or, no, sorry, [AMOUNT_2], I've got two records open here and I'm mixing them up. Are you still there? I know a call out of the blue can feel a bit much.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Who is -- hang on, I've got a pan on, hold on a sec. Yes, yes, this is [PERSON_1], but who did you say you were again? A gift, you said? I used to give --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, go and see to your pan, I'll wait, there's no rush at all. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the charity. Sorry, I did say a gift, but it wasn't a one-off, it was a monthly one, and it's actually lapsed, so nothing's wrong, I just wanted to thank you for it. And, uh, I said I was a case handler, but really I'm more on the supporter care side, I'm sorry, I always get that wrong. Are you still there, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, I'm here, I'm here. Uh, just -- turning the heat down. Right. So, a charity, you said? And I used to give, um, every month? Sorry, what was it called again? I give to a few things, you see, I can't always -- hang on, what's it you want, exactly? You said nothing's wrong.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, nothing's wrong, I promise, it's just -- sorry, I'm [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], and what I wanted was to ask whether you'd think about starting your monthly gift again, only if you want to, and -- Oh, sorry, I've talked over you, I do that when I'm nervous. You said you give to a few places, of course you do, it's easy to lose track. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm still here, sorry, it's just, I've got the onions going and they'll catch if I'm not careful. Um. So you want me to start giving again? Every month? Sorry, what, I really don't remember if I gave to you, that's the thing. I do give to a couple of the bigger ones, the animal one and the one for the, oh, what is it, the hospital one, but I couldn't tell you if yours was ever on my statement. Do you have it written down, when it stopped? Or how much? You said two different amounts, didn't you, and I don't know which was mine. And, hang on, how did you get my number? Not that I'm accusing you of anything, sorry, I just, I'd want to check it's really you before I said yes to anything, if that makes sense. Is there a number I could ring you back on? Or I could look you up, if you tell me how to spell it again. Sorry, I'm all over the place, it's a bad time, I've got the dinner on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that makes complete sense, and honestly I'd want to check too, so please do. Ring the main supporter line for [COMPANY_A], it's on the website, [URL_1], and it'll be on any letter we've sent you, and that way you know it's us and not just a voice on the phone. I'd rather you were careful with your own details, I do worry about people who aren't. And, sorry, I should tidy something up, because I've muddled you. I said both amounts came off my screen, but really only one of them's yours, and I can't tell you which until you've confirmed who you are with us, so I shouldn't have read either out. That's my mistake. As for how we've got your number, it was from when you set up the gift, it's on your supporter record. I'll be honest, I don't want you to feel pushed, especially with the onions going. If you'd rather not be called again, just say, and I'll take you off our list right now. Are you still there, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, still here, sorry. Um, can I go back a bit? Earlier you said you were a case handler, and then you said no, you were more supporter care. What's the difference, sorry? Only it's a bit odd, isn't it, you saying one thing and then the other. And you said you'd read out an amount but you shouldn't have. Sorry, I'm not good with all this. Which job is it, really?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair thing to pick up on, and I'm sorry, I did muddle it. The job title on my badge is case handler, but the work I actually do all day is supporter care, so thanking people and checking in on lapsed gifts, and I should have just said that plainly the first time. Oh, sorry, someone's just dropped a stack of folders behind me, give me one second -- right, sorry, I'm back. It's an open-plan office and it's never quiet. Anyway, you don't need to take my word for any of it, please ring the supporter line and ask for me by name, [PERSON_2], and if they can't find me, that tells you something. And honestly, if you'd rather I just took you off our calling list, I'll do that now, no more calls. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I'm here, sorry. Um, well, uh, hang on, let me just -- there. Right. Sorry, I'm just, I'm thinking, you know. So, ring the number on the website and ask for you. Yes. I think I'd rather do that, actually, if that's all right? Because I don't really know you, do I, and the dinner's, well, it's all going. So I'll look it up myself, not from anything you've said, and if it's right I'll ring them. And no, I'd not go taking me off any list just yet, I'll see what they say. Sorry. Thank you for ringing, I suppose. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Um, hi, sorry, is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling on behalf of, uh, the customs desk at [COMPANY_A] -- the courier, I mean. It's about a parcel you're expecting, and, well, there's a charge on it that I need to, uh, explain to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm in a queue. What parcel? I'm not expecting anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, okay, sorry, I know that sounds -- I mean, I'd think the same thing, honestly. It's a parcel sent to you from [COMPANY_B], I think it's coming through [CITY_1], and it's been held at our customs desk since, uh, yesterday, or maybe the day before, sorry, I'd have to check that. I'm sorry, I know you're busy in a queue and everything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but I just said I'm not expecting anything. And you don't even know when it got there, "yesterday or maybe the day before." That's not a lot of detail for someone who's got my parcel sat on a desk. What's the tracking number? And who's it from, actually from? "[COMPANY_B], I think" isn't an answer. I've been caught out with this sort of thing before, so, no. If there's really a parcel, I'll deal with it through the courier's own site, not over the phone to someone who rang me out of nowhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh -- no, that's, that's fair, honestly, and I'm sorry, I did fumble the date. It came in two days ago, I've got it here now, sorry. Um, and the tracking reference is [CODE_1], that's the one you'd see on your own tracking page, so you don't have to take my word for any of it. And, uh, you said you've been caught out before, and I'm sorry about that, I don't want to be one more person who -- never mind. You're right about the site, really, that's the best way. The charge shows on that page, you can pay it there, in your own time, and I'm not asking for anything on this call, I promise. It's just, it'd feel awful if it got sent back before you even knew it was there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well, uh... that's, yeah, that's what I said, so. Look, that's the first thing you've said that makes sense, but it doesn't change that I never ordered anything and I still don't know who it's from. And if it's not asking me for anything, why ring me at all? Why's a customs desk chasing me on the phone instead of just sending a card through the door?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, yeah, so -- we did send a card, I think, or, no, sorry, that's not right, the card goes out when nobody's home for a delivery, this is a customs hold, so it's an email notice, and I don't actually know if yours went to the right address. That's, uh, partly why I'm ringing, to make sure you know. And the sender, I did say [COMPANY_B], and that's what's on my screen, but it could be a gift, or something someone ordered for you, which I know doesn't help much. Honestly, if you don't recognise it, that's fine, you can leave it, nobody's going to chase you, but the hold does run out in a few days, and I'd hate for you to find out too late.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you rang to make sure I knew, but you can't tell me who it's from, and you're not sure if the email went to the right address, and I can just leave it if I don't recognise it. That's a lot of "I don't know" for a call that's supposed to be about my parcel. And the "few days, don't miss it" bit, I've heard that one before. I'm not paying anything on the strength of this call, and I'm not clicking anything you send me either. If there's a real parcel, the courier can post a card or the email'll turn up. I'm going to go, I'm at the front of the queue. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh -- okay, no, that's, that's fine, really. I'm not asking you to pay anything now, I just -- the reference is [CODE_1], it's on the courier's tracking page, you can look it up yourself, and nothing's due on this call, nothing at all. I mean, I'm only trying to help, I wasn't trying to, to catch you out or anything, it's just, I'd hate for it to go back. But, yeah, you're right, if it's real, the email'll turn up, or you can check the page whenever you like. Sorry to take your time. Bye now, and, uh, good luck with the queue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Right. If it's real, I'll find it myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah, thank you, and, uh, sorry again for the bother. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, well. Look, I'm not having a go at you personally, but you can see why I'd be short, can't you? Somebody rings out of nowhere, I'm stood here with a basket of shopping and a woman behind me tutting, and I'm told there's a parcel I never ordered, from somewhere you can't pin down, that I've got to sort out before some deadline. That's, I mean, that's exactly how it went last time, and I'm still sore about it, so I'm not going to take it on trust. If there's a real parcel, fine, it'll turn up on the courier's own site or in an email and I'll look at it properly, in my own time, on my own phone. And if it's not real, well, then you've wasted both our afternoons. Anyway, I've got to pay now, so. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I do see, I really do, and I'm sorry, I'd be sore about it too, honestly. Like I said, the reference is [CODE_1], it's on the courier's own tracking page, so you can look it up in your own time, on your own phone, just like you said. And nothing's due on this call, nothing at all, I'm not asking you for anything, I just, I didn't want you to find out too late. But you're right, it's your call, so, um, go and pay for your shopping. Sorry about the woman tutting. Bye now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Right. And I never gave you my name, by the way, so how'd you know to say it? Doesn't matter. I'm done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello? Sorry, hang on one second, we've got a delivery van reversing outside the shop and it's -- there, sorry about that. Um, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler at [COMPANY_A], and I'm, uh, I'm calling about the prize draw you entered at the [CITY_1] open day a few weeks back. Are you still there?

utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, sorry -- someone's just walked past with a trolley, hang on. Right. Who did you say you were with? And what prize draw? I don't really remember entering anything, so you'll need to get to the point.

utterances.speaker: caller

You'd have filled in a slip with your name and number, I think, which is how we've got you. Hello? Are you still with me?

utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here. But I'm not sure I went to that, and I definitely don't remember a fishbowl. What's the call actually about? Did I win something, or are you after something from me? I've got about two minutes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not after anything, I promise, I'd hate for you to think that. Um, you did win, it's a small one, a [AMOUNT_1] voucher for the shop, and there's nothing to pay and nothing for me to take down from you today. Sorry, I know it sounds a bit too good to be true. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, someone's just stuck their head round the door -- no, it's fine, tell them five minutes. Sorry. Right. So you've got my number off a slip I don't remember filling in, and you're telling me I've won something I don't remember entering. That's two things I can't check. Which shop is it, exactly? Give me the actual name, and a number I can ring back on, not one you read out to me now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fair, sorry. It's [COMPANY_A] on the high street, and the number's on the shop's own website, [URL_1], so you can look it up yourself and ring us there. Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, I'm here. Right, but you said something a minute ago, "for your own protection." Protection from what? It's a voucher. Why would it need protecting, and who else would it go to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, that was just a clumsy way of putting it, uh, I only meant it'd go back in the pot if nobody collects it. It's nothing sinister, honestly. Um, hello? utterances.text: Uh... yeah, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? And, hm, what was that about a scheduled interruption? Because I've not had anything from my supplier about a balance, so I'm, um, a bit lost here.

utterances.text: Of course, [PERSON_1], I understand, it's a lot to take in on a call you weren't expecting. I'm with [COMPANY_A], the supplier named on your bills, and the matter is that the arrears recorded against your account have passed the statutory notice window, which means supply would be subject to interruption on the scheduled date unless the balance is reconciled or an arrangement is lodged. utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, fair question. The date on our notice is the [DATE_1], so that's, um, about ten days out, though I did say earlier it was past the notice window, and I should be more precise, it's the, uh, second reminder stage, not the final notice. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So, a couple of things there. You rang me, so "inbound-style call" doesn't really make sense. And you won't read out the address, but you're happy to tell me a balance. That's, uh, the wrong way round, isn't it? Also you said past the notice window, and now it's only the second reminder. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right on all three, and I'm sorry, I muddied it. It's an outbound call, I phrased that badly, and quoting the address would have been the more sensible way round. The stage is the second reminder, not the final notice, so nothing happens before [DATE_1], and "past the notice window" was loose wording on my part. Look, I don't need anything from you on this call. Please don't take my word for it. Log in to your own online account, or ring the number printed on your bill, and you'll see the balance and the date there. I can also note the account for a payment plan so you've got time to look at it properly.

So what's [COMPANY_A] going to see on my side if I do ring them, a note saying you called, or what? Have you got a reference I can quote?

utterances.text: That's a reasonable thing to ask. Yes, the call will be logged against the account, so whoever you reach should be able to see a note that I rang today. The reference to quote is [CODE_1], and the account reference I mentioned at the start is [ACCOUNT_REF], which should match the one printed on your bill. If the number on your bill doesn't show a note of this call, then treat it with suspicion and tell them so. I'd sooner you checked it properly than took my word.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, I'm -- sorry, but I'll stop you there, because that's more or less what I was going to say. I'll ring the number on my bill and see if there's a note. And if there isn't, well, you've just told me what to think about that. So, uh, that's me done, I'll sort it that way. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's entirely sensible. Thank you for your time, [PERSON_1], and, um, I do apologise for the confusion on my part. Goodbye.

utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, did you say apologise for the confusion on my part? No, no, I wasn't confused, I just wanted the reference. Anyway. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you weren't confused at all, that was my phrasing, I meant the confusion I caused. You asked sensible questions. Right, so the reference is [CODE_1], and if they've no note of it, tell them so. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, got it. I'll ring the number on the bill and see what they've got. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, good, that's -- well, no, I mean, that's exactly what I'd do. Sorry, I'll not keep you, [PERSON_1]. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Goodbye, [PERSON_1]. And, uh, if there's -- no, never mind. Take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: Oh, hello, hi -- sorry, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from the IT helpdesk at [COMPANY_A], I'm following up on the ticket you opened this morning about your laptop, the one that keeps dropping off the network. Sorry, you're, you're still there?
