It's only so your machine's protected and stops cutting out on you, that's all it's for. Sorry, you're still with me? So I think the portal's the right way, if you'd rather -- you can find your ticket there under [ACCOUNT_REF], and [PERSON_3]'s name is on the escalation note, so you can check it's all genuine before you book a time with me. Would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, yes, that's, that's good, thank you. So the portal, and I check the ticket, and [PERSON_3]'s name on it, right, and then I book a time with you. Portal, ticket, check the name, book a time, and if it doesn't match, ring the helpdesk the normal way. Right. Thank you for not rushing me, and sorry again for being, you know, a bit of a faff on the phone. I'll sort it when I'm parked. Bye now, thanks, bye.

utterances.text: Oh, that's perfect, and you weren't a faff at all, honestly. Sorry, one second, someone's just put a delivery down on my desk -- right, sorry, I'm back. So, drive safe, [PERSON_1], and thank you for bearing with me. Bye now, bye.

utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, deliveries happen, sorry, I'm still just, yes. Thanks again, and I will, drive safe, I mean I'm driving safe, sorry, you know what I mean. Okay, bye, bye now.

Thank you, [PERSON_1], bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: Yes, I'm, I'm fine, thank you, it was just, I mean, it's, sorry, it's all fine now. Okay, so I'll, I'll check the, no, I'll look at the portal when I'm parked and, yes, that's, that's it. Thank you again, bye now, bye.

utterances.text: No no, that's fine, take your time with the pan, I'm [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the charity, and our records show a monthly gift under your name that ran for a good while and then stopped, so I'm just -- sorry, did you say you never set one up? utterances.text: Sorry, a smaller what? A smaller account? No, I've only got the one account, I think. Oh, sorry, hang on, did you say renewing? Like, renewing a licence? I don't drive anymore, so I don't, um, I don't think that's me.

utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], we're the maintenance contractor, the boiler service is under your name. Look, if you're driving, don't worry about it, that's fine. I only need to give you a morning or afternoon slot, that's all, nothing you need to do right now. I can ring back whenever suits, or you can call the office on [PHONE_1] and quote your booking reference, whichever's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the office is, um, closed? Because I can't really, I mean I can't be going to an office at the moment, I'm miles from, hang on, sorry. Oh, you said ring the office, right, okay, sorry, the line keeps cutting out. Um, a booking reference, I don't actually have that on me, it'd be in an email somewhere, I think? Is it, could you maybe just ring me back later when I've stopped driving? I'm sorry, I know that's a nuisance.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, I didn't say the office was closed, I said you can ring the office, on [PHONE_1], that's all, there's no going anywhere. And look, you don't need the booking reference for me, it's on my system, I only mentioned it in case you wanted to call in yourself. Ringing back is fine, I just thought it'd save us both a bit of time, that's all. When are you likely to be stopped, about an hour, or...?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, sorry, I misheard. Yeah, an hour, maybe a bit more, I'm sorry. I'll probably just look for the email and ring the office myself, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, that's fine, ring the office, though I'll be honest, it'd be quicker if I just ran through the slots with you now. Sorry, one thing though, you said a minute ago you weren't sure you'd even booked with us, so what exactly do you think you booked? Because it's on our system under your name, and I'd rather we sorted that out than have you hunting through emails for something that's already here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh gosh, sorry, I probably sounded really muddled there, it's just the driving and the signal and, um, I'm a bit anxious on motorways anyway. So, what I meant was, I do think I booked a boiler service, I mean someone did, maybe me, maybe it was through the landlord, I honestly can't remember which company it was. And I'm not saying you're wrong, I really don't want to be rude, it's just that I can't actually say yes, that's you, because I don't know that it is. So I'd feel better looking up the email and ringing the office number on whatever it says there, if that's okay? Sorry, I know that's the long way round. And honestly, I don't think I can pick a slot right now anyway, my diary's all at home. So, um, yeah. I'll ring you back, or the office, whichever, once I've found it. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that's, I mean, it's up to you, but I'll say it's a bit odd to doubt a call about a booking that's on our system. Sorry, can I just check one thing, you said earlier "ring the office" and then something about the office being closed, and I never said that. Did you mean the number I gave you, [PHONE_1], or were you thinking of a different one? Because I don't want you ringing the wrong place and then blaming us when nothing's sorted.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, that was me mishearing, the line cut out and I thought you'd said closed, my fault entirely. Um, and the number you gave, I'm sorry, I didn't catch it properly, I was swerving round a bend or something. Is that [PHONE_1], did you say? Because I'd actually rather not use a number you read me over a bad line, I'd sooner use whatever's on the email, if I can find it. I'm sorry, that probably sounds awful. Would that be okay? I don't want to blame anyone, I just don't want to ring the wrong place.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, it's [PHONE_1], that's the number, [PHONE_1], and that's the one I gave you. But look, if you'd rather use the number on your email, that's fine, that's absolutely fine, I'm not going to argue with you over it. I'll just say I've been quite straightforward with you this whole call, and I'm not sure what more I could've done. Anyway, ring whichever office you like when you've found it, and we'll get you a slot then. Right, I'll leave it there, take care on the road.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, you've been perfectly nice, honestly, I'm sorry if I made it sound like you weren't. It's just me being nervy. Um, and sorry, one more thing, you said you'd ring me back in an hour, didn't you? Actually no, I think that was me saying an hour, wasn't it, sorry. Anyway, don't ring me, I'll ring the office myself once I've found the email and I'm parked up. Thanks for calling, and sorry again for being such a muddle. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, this is [PERSON_1], regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A] -- just calling about a repeat prescription that's ready for collection.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, hello. Sorry, I'm not sure I caught that properly -- who did you say you were with again? And a prescription, did you say? I'm sorry, I'm not very good with this sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem. It's [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy. Uh, actually, sorry, I'm one of the supervisors there, not the only one, I mean -- anyway, it's just a repeat prescription, it's ready, so whenever suits you to pop in and collect it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, the pharmacy, I see. Um, well, that's very kind of you to ring. Uh, it's just -- I'm trying to think, I do have a repeat one, I think, but I wasn't sure it was due yet. Is it, um, is it under my name, do you have it there? Sorry, I'm probably being daft.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not being daft, it's a perfectly fair question. Uh, so the way it works, and this is standard procedure across all our branches, is the repeat requests come through either from your surgery or from you directly, and then the pharmacy team dispenses it and flags it as ready. We don't generally flag anything until it's been through the checks, so if I'm ringing, it's because it's sitting on the shelf with your details on the bag. As for whether it's due, I can't see the schedule from where I am, that's something the branch team would confirm when you're in. But honestly, there's nothing you need to do over the phone, no need to read anything out or confirm anything to me. You just come in, show some ID at the counter like normal, and they'll hand it over and talk you through it. I mean, it's only a courtesy call really, we do them as part of the collection reminder process, and I'd have thought that was straightforward enough.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, that's all very helpful, thank you. Um, sorry, can I just go back a bit? Earlier you said you were the regional supervisor, and then you said you were one of the supervisors, not the only one. I wasn't sure if I'd got that right. Is it the regional one, or at a particular branch? Only I don't know which branch you mean, you see, and I'd hate to turn up at the wrong one.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, regional, I cover several branches, that's the role. The one thing I tripped over earlier was saying I'm the only one, because we've got a few of us across the area. It's hardly a mystery. As for which branch, it's whichever one you normally use, [CITY_1] I'd assume, that's where the bag is with your details on it. Honestly, I'm not sure what else you want me to say here, I've told you there's nothing to confirm and nothing to hand over. If it helps, ring the branch yourself on the number you've always used, [PHONE_1] if you've got it handy, and they'll tell you if there's anything waiting. I just thought a courtesy call was the helpful thing to do.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I don't mean to be awkward, I just -- oh, that's a good idea actually, ringing the branch myself. I think I'll do that, if that's all right. I've got the number somewhere, and they can tell me if there's anything waiting. Thank you ever so much for ringing, that was very kind. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, yes, that's fine. Uh, I did say that's the sensible thing to do, so. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, thank you, bye bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, just so I've got it straight on my end -- when you said earlier you'd have to check the branch about which one, did you mean you'd ring the one in [CITY_1], or you weren't sure which branch you use? Only if there's a mix-up I'd rather flag it now. Not that it matters hugely.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, I think that might've been you who said the branch bit, wasn't it? I just said I'd ring the one I normally use, on the number I've got. So I'll just do that, [CITY_1] I suppose, whichever it is, and they can tell me. Thank you again, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], we're doing a short consumer survey today -- do you have five minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um... a survey. Yeah, I suppose so. I've not got much on today.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wonderful, thank you, that's great. So the survey line closes at the end of today's session, so we do want to get you through nice and quick. It's just a handful of questions about your household shopping habits, and there's no sales element at all, I just need your first-name basis answers, uh, I mean, just your honest answers, nothing to prepare. Shall we begin with question one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh well, yes, go on then, I've not got much on, like I said. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? [COMPANY_A], was it? I didn't quite catch it. My hearing's not what it was. I do like a chat, you know, it's been very quiet here today, just me and the telly. Anyway, what's the first question?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and my name's [PERSON_1]. No need to apologise at all. So, uh, as I said, today's session closes shortly, so if we could just crack on, question one is: roughly how many times a week would you say you do a main food shop? Take your time, there's no wrong answer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, how many times a week... hang on, sorry, there's a pigeon on the windowsill, he's a cheeky one, comes every afternoon. Shoo, go on. Sorry, where was I? Oh, the shop. Well, I'd say once, really, maybe twice if I run out of milk or something. I used to go every day when Harold was, well, never mind. Is that the sort of thing you want?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's exactly the sort of thing we want, thank you, so that's once or twice a week, lovely. And I'm sorry to hear about Harold. Now, as I mentioned, the line does close at the end of today's session, so if we can move along, question two is: when you shop, do you tend to go to one main store, or do you split it between a few different ones? Whenever you're ready.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you, Harold was, well, he's been gone three years now, but anyway -- oh, the stores, yes, mostly just the one, the one down by the -- sorry, you were saying something about the line closing? Why does it close, dear? It's only a few questions, isn't it? I don't see why it should be in such a hurry, I mean, nobody's rushing me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're quite right, dear, there's no need to rush at all, and I'm sorry if I made it sound that way. It's just the, uh, the survey line closes at the end of today's session, that's just the standard procedure on our end, the session closes at the end of today. But honestly, there's no hurry on your side, you take as long as you like. So, the stores, you said mostly just the one? Which kind would that be, a big supermarket, or a smaller local shop?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hm, standard procedure, I see. Um... it's, uh, well, it's one of the big ones, the supermarket, you know, with the car park and the little cafe where they do the scones. Harold liked the scones. Oh, but, um, hang on, sorry, I do ramble. Is that the sort of answer you want, the big one, or...? And er, how did you get my number, dear, if you don't mind me asking? I'm not sure I ever put it down for anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, a big supermarket, that's perfect, thank you. And, uh, fair question. The numbers come from a randomly generated list, it's just a computer picking numbers in your area, so you didn't put it down anywhere. It's nothing personal, I promise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a computer picked it, well, isn't that something, I never know how they do all that. A random list, you say. Funny, though, isn't it, that it picked me. Sorry, I'm going on. So, um, the big supermarket, with the scones, that's the one I go to, yes. Like I said, the big one. And you're with, what was it again, [COMPANY_A]? It's just, my hearing, I keep losing the name. Is it a, what do they call it, a research agency? Can you say it once more, dear?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, it's [COMPANY_A], and that's a research agency, that's right. If you'd rather not carry on, that's fine, I can take you off the list.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, no, I don't mind carrying on, I'm enjoying the company, really. Though, hm, you said at the start it was five minutes, and then the line was closing, and now it's a list and you'd take me off it, I'm a bit muddled which it is. Never mind, never mind. Ask me the next one, dear. I do like the scones at that little cafe, but I suppose that's not on your list. Where was I? Oh yes, question three.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I -- no, it's, let me put it plainly. It's five minutes, I just kept going on about the line closing, which, uh, I shouldn't have, that's only a scheduling thing on our side and it's no reason for you to feel rushed. And the list is just how we pick who to ring. That's all it is. Now, I think you've been so helpful already, and I've got what I need for today, so I'll let you get back to your pigeon. Thank you ever so much for your time, and I hope the scones are good.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, is that it? Well, that was quick, I'd only just got going. Thank you for being so patient with me, dear, I do go on. And thank you for asking, it's nice to be asked, nobody much does these days. I'll go and see if that pigeon's still about. You mind how you go, and, um, you have a lovely rest of your afternoon. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good morning, this is account services at [COMPANY_A], the school office, I'm calling about -- sorry, did I catch you mid-sentence? Anyway, I'm ringing regarding [PERSON_1], who was marked absent this morning, and we do need to close off the register before, uh, eleven, so I'll be quick.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Who is this, the school? Which school?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, no rush, take your time, I'll just, uh, hold on, um -- it's [COMPANY_A], the school office, account services, and I'm calling about [PERSON_1], who's down as absent this morning. Like I said, we do close the register at eleven, so if you could just confirm whether [PERSON_1] is poorly or whether there's been some sort of mix-up, that would be great.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Absent? Hang on, let me turn this down. Right. Which child is this, who did you say? Because I didn't catch a name, you just said, um, the school office. And account services? That's an odd sort of -- sorry, who exactly am I speaking to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, it's [PERSON_1], that's the pupil, [PERSON_1], marked absent this morning, and you're through to account services at [COMPANY_A], the school office. I'm [PERSON_2], and it's just a quick check on the absence, that's all, nothing to worry about. Like I said, we do close the register at eleven, so if you could just let me know whether [PERSON_1] is poorly or whether it's a mix-up, that would be great.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? I'm still not, um -- I can't hear a name. You keep saying [PERSON_1] but, I mean, is that my child? Because I'm sure he went in this morning. I walked him to the gate. So I don't, I don't understand how he's absent. Is this the main office? Why's it account services?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, no, that's a fair question, and I do apologise, because I should have said that more clearly at the start. So [PERSON_1] is the pupil, your son, and what's happened is he's been marked absent on this morning's register, which is exactly why I'm ringing, because if he was walked to the gate, then he may well have been marked wrongly, or he came in late and the entry wasn't updated, and that happens more than you'd think. As for the account services bit, that's just the name of the team that handles attendance queries and, uh, the records side of things, so I'm calling from the school office, the same building, and if you'd rather, you can ring the main number, [PHONE_1], and ask for me, [PERSON_2], by name. We do close the register at eleven, so the sooner I can note down that he's definitely in school, the sooner I can correct the mark and nobody gets an automated absence message sent home. I won't need anything from you except a yes or no on whether he's in today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right, sorry, I'm a bit -- I've got dinner on and I'm not thinking straight. Yes, he's in. I definitely took him in this morning, I walked him to the gate myself. Um, but hang on, you still haven't said his name, you just keep saying [PERSON_1]. And the number you gave, I didn't catch it. Is it the same one that's on the letters from school? Because I think I'd feel better just ringing them back, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely fine, and you're quite right to -- sorry, to cut in, but yes, [PHONE_1] is the number on the school letters, the main office line, so please do ring back and ask for [PERSON_2] in account services. Now, as I said, we do close the register at eleven, so if you could just ring before then, I'll have it corrected and no absence message goes home. And thank you for confirming he's in, that's really all I needed, so I'll note that down now, and, uh, I'll let you get back to your dinner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right. Okay, so I'll just -- no, hang on, I'll ring the school, yes. I'll do that, I'd rather. Sorry, it's nothing against you, it's just, I'm in the middle of the, um -- I'm not really, I don't know who you are, do I? So I'll ring them and they can sort the register. Right. Thank you, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fine, and honestly that's the right thing to do, so no apology needed. Do ring the main office before eleven and they'll get the register sorted. Thanks for your time, and sorry again for catching you mid-dinner. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I'll -- no, sorry, I'll ring them, I'll look up the number on the letter. Not the one you said, I mean, the one I've got. Anyway. Bye, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's -- sorry, to cut in, but that's perfect, use the number on your letter, that's what I'd do. Ring before eleven and they'll have it sorted. Thanks again, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Right. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is the account services team at [COMPANY_A], am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a stack of folders behind me -- okay, back. I'm calling to arrange a window for your boiler service visit, the one you already booked, and I do need to get that confirmed before we close the day's scheduling at four.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, who's speaking, sorry? You said [COMPANY_A], but I'm not sure that's a company I've got a boiler service with, so could you tell me which one that is, exactly? And when you say I already booked it, when was that, and through what, a phone call, a website? I'd just like to know what I'm supposed to have booked before I confirm anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's fair. So I'm an account services agent with [COMPANY_A], we're the maintenance contractor that carries out the boiler servicing, and the booking would've come through whoever you arranged the service with, so it's under reference [ACCOUNT_REF] on our system. I don't have the exact date in front of me, I'd have to pull the full record, but I'm only calling to arrange the visit window, and as I said, we do close scheduling at four today, so, uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you've called me, so you ought to already know who you've reached. I'm not going to confirm my name to someone who rang me out of the blue. And I'd like to be clear that you haven't actually told me anything I can check. You can't give me a date, you can't say who I booked through, and the only thing I've got is a reference that I can't see from here. Who's the service provider on your records, as in the company I'm supposed to have the contract with, and what address have you got the boiler at?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, as I said, I'm calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm only here to arrange the window for the visit you booked. I understand the concern, I do, but I can't read out the address or the provider details until I've verified who I'm speaking with, that's just our procedure, it protects your information. And, uh, the scheduling closes at four, so if I could just have you confirm your name -- sorry, I know you've said you'd rather not.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on a second, sorry, the dog's just started going at the front door. Right, it's the postman, never mind. Where was I. So you need me to prove who I am, but I'm not allowed to hear a single detail about the booking first? That's backwards, isn't it? You rang me. If I've genuinely got a boiler service booked, then whoever I booked it with has my details and can tell me about it, so I'll contact them myself, using a number I already hold, not one you give me. And I'd still like a straight answer, which company is the contract actually with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's, uh, that's perfectly reasonable, and I'm not going to argue with it. I'm calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and the only thing I was here to do was arrange the window, but if you'd rather go back through whoever you booked with, using a number you already hold, that's entirely your call. I'll note on the record that you've declined to schedule today, and the visit can be arranged another time. Thanks for your time, and, uh, enjoy the rest of your afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Yes, please do note that. And just so it's clear, I haven't declined any service, I've declined to confirm anything over a call I didn't expect. If there's a genuine booking, I'll find it through the provider I actually dealt with. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, and, uh, sorry, I did put that wrong, you haven't declined anything, I'll note it as unable to confirm on this call. And the, the four o'clock cut-off I mentioned, forget that, it's more of a soft cut-off really, so there's no rush at all. Thanks for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, thank you for correcting that, though I did notice the four o'clock deadline went from a hard cut-off to a soft one rather quickly. I'm not saying that to be difficult, it's just that a deadline that disappears the moment I push back isn't much of a deadline. And to be fair to you, if there is a genuine booking, nothing is lost. I'll look through my own records, find whoever I arranged the servicing with, and ring them on a number I already have. If they've got a visit pencilled in, they'll tell me, and I'll sort out a window with them directly. I'd also suggest, for next time, that whoever is making these calls be able to say which provider the contract is with, and when it was booked, before asking anyone to confirm their name. Most people would find that a good deal more reassuring. Anyway, I appreciate you being straightforward at the end there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's -- I mean, the cut-off, that's, well, it's the, no, you're right, it was a bit of a stock line, I shouldn't have leaned on it. And that's fair feedback about the provider and the booking date, I'll, uh, pass that along to the team, because I take the point. So, if you do find the booking, they'll sort the window with you directly, and, yeah, thanks for your patience. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, thank you. I appreciate you being upfront about the cut-off. Like I said, I'll go through my own records and contact the provider directly, so there's nothing more needed from your side. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy, collections desk. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? Right, so I'm ringing about your repeat prescription, it's ready to collect, uh, under reference [ACCOUNT_REF].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, [pause] no, no, put that down, sweetheart. Uh, sorry. Who is this again? And, um, you said collections desk -- is that the pharmacy or is that something else?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, it's the pharmacy. [COMPANY_A]. Collections is just the desk that handles prescriptions ready for pick-up, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Except "collections" usually means somebody's chasing money, doesn't it? So, uh, which pharmacy is it, exactly? Because I've got one I use, and I didn't think I had anything waiting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, I get that, it's just the name of the desk, there's no debt on the file. It's the [COMPANY_A] branch in [CITY_1], the repeat for [PERSON_2] was put through on the system and it's showing ready, that's all I've got in front of me. If you use a different pharmacy then I'd just -- sorry, go on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, that's the thing, I haven't ordered anything. So who put it through? Like, which medication is it supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. I can't read the medication name out over the phone, not before I've confirmed who I'm speaking to, that's just how we do it here. What I can see is it's a repeat item, and it's showing as requested through your surgery, not through us. If it's not something you recognise, I'll note that on the file, and, uh, it stays on the shelf for seven days either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the shelf? No -- wait, did you say a charge? Is there something to pay on it? Because you said it's not a debt, but then you're saying seven days, so is it seven days till it, what, goes to somebody?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no charge, I didn't say that. Seven days is just how long we hold it, after that it goes back into stock and the request closes. Nothing's owed, nothing goes to anybody. Sorry, one sec, [PERSON_3], can you -- yeah, just leave it on the side, thanks. Right, sorry, where was I. After seven days it's returned and, uh, if you still need it, the surgery would have to put it through again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but I still haven't ordered anything, that's what I keep coming back to. I didn't order anything. So if it's the surgery that put it through, then I'd ring the surgery, wouldn't I? Or just go into the shop myself, the one I actually use. Why would I need to go through you for that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fair, you don't need to go through me. If you'd rather check with the surgery first, or ask at the shop you normally use, that's completely fine. I'm just the one who rings when an item's flagged as ready. I'll put your query on the file, that you don't recall requesting it, and the shelf hold stays at seven days regardless. Is there a better time for us to call you back, or would you rather we just leave it with the surgery?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Earlier you said you couldn't tell me anything till you'd confirmed who I was, and now you've got my query on file, and a call back. So what have you actually confirmed? I haven't told you a thing. Look, I'll ring the surgery myself. And I'll go into the shop, the one I actually use, if it comes to that. No need to call me back. Right, I've got to go, my little one's, uh -- yeah. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, that's fine, and you're correct on the first point, I haven't confirmed anything with you. The only thing I've got is the name and reference on the system, and that's why I wouldn't read out the medication. So you've given nothing away, there's nothing to undo. Ringing the surgery is the sensible route anyway, they'll tell you straight away whether they sent it through, and if they didn't, the branch will see it flagged and sort it on their side. I've noted that you don't recall requesting it, so that's on the file either way. I'll leave the callback off, as you've asked, and uh, if you do end up at the shop, just quote the reference and they can pull it up. Go on, sort your little one out. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, right. [pause] No, not on the sofa, love, we've talked about this -- sorry. Yeah. I'll ring the surgery. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no bother. Oh, and just so you know, it's seven days, sorry, I think the system actually says ten on this one, but the surgery'll sort that out. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, wait, now it's ten? You said seven, twice. And, um, two turns back you said you've noted I don't recall requesting it, and that's on the file. What file, exactly? You haven't got anything from me. Right, no, I'm going. I'll ring the surgery. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair, I should've checked before I said it, it's seven on the screen, ten was me misreading the line below. And the file's just the note against the reference, that you don't recall asking for it. It's not anything you've given me, it's what you said on this call, that's all. Right, you've got the surgery to ring, so I'll let you go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a note against the reference, like a, what, a reference for the, uh, the surgery? No, wait -- you said what I said on this call, so you're writing down what I say? Right. Well, that's -- I'm not giving you anything else. I'll ring the surgery, like I said. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, hello? Hi, um, yes -- sorry, is this, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm, um, I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and I was just, uh, wondering if you might have, like, five minutes for a short consumer survey?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is, uh, yes, that's me. A survey, you said? Well, I suppose I've got a few minutes, I'm just sitting here, the kettle's not even on yet. What's it about, dear? Only I'm not very good with, you know, the technical things, but I don't mind a chat.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's, that's lovely, thank you, and please, no, there's nothing technical at all, it's just, um, questions about everyday shopping, like what you buy, where you tend to go, whether you've, uh, noticed prices changing at the supermarket, that sort of thing. There aren't any right or wrong answers, I mean, it's really just your opinion, and it, it only takes about five minutes, maybe a little more if you're, if you're chatty, which honestly is, is fine by me, I'm not, I'm not very good at these calls myself, I only started doing them recently. And, um, I should say, I'm not asking for any money or bank details or anything like that, I just, uh, I just really need to get a few of these finished today, so it, it would mean a lot, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, you sound a bit nervous yourself, love, so don't worry, I'll go gently on you. Prices, goodness, yes, I've noticed those, my eggs have gone right up. Though you said earlier it was a consumer survey, and now it's the supermarket, which I suppose is the same thing, isn't it? Hang on, no, you said five minutes, and then a little more. Anyway, I don't mind. It's lovely to have someone to talk to, honestly, I was only going to watch the telly. Where was I? Oh yes, I usually go to the shop on the corner, not the big one, because my knees aren't what they were.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, that's all right, you're not, you're not going wrong at all. And you're right, it's, um, the supermarket is just one part of the consumer survey, so it's the same thing, yes. And it is five minutes, or, I mean, maybe a few more if we chat, like I said. So, the shop on the corner, that's, that's really helpful, thank you, and I'm sorry about your knees. Um, so, just, just so I get it down right, do you go there most days, or, uh, just once or twice a week? And, sorry, one other thing before we go on, I should say, I'm only the, the person making the call, the survey itself is for someone at [COMPANY_A], I'm sort of, um, passing it along for them, if that makes sense.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, most days, I'd say, just for a loaf and a bit of -- hang on, "passing it along," you said? Passing it along to who, exactly? Only I didn't quite catch, who's it for? Sorry, dear, I'm not being funny, it's just, you said a company and I didn't hear the name properly. Anyway, the shop, yes, they do a lovely bit of ham there, but go on, who did you say it was?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, no, that's, that's fair, I should've said it clearer. It's [COMPANY_A], the research agency, and the, the person I'm doing it for there is [PERSON_2]. Um, and it's, sorry, I know you said you didn't quite catch it, and actually, back a bit, you asked what it was about, and I said everyday shopping, but I think I, I made it sound smaller than it is, it's, it's a few sections, the shopping's just the first one. I'm not, I'm not trying to be sneaky, honestly, I'm just, I'm not very good at explaining it. Um, so, the ham, that's, that's nice, most days then, for the loaf and the ham, yes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, the loaf and the ham, that's right. But hang on, you said a minute ago you'd made it sound smaller than it is, and I didn't quite follow that. A few sections, you said? What are the other sections? Only you said five minutes and I'm not sure that's what we're doing now. And that name, [PERSON_2], I'm not sure I know them. Sorry, dear, I'm not trying to be difficult, I'm just a bit lost. It's not about the ham, is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, it's not about the ham, please don't think that, I'm, I'm so sorry, I've made a muddle of it. Um, it really is just about shopping, I promise. The first section's the one we're doing, where you shop and how often, and then there's a short bit on prices, whether you've noticed them going up, like your eggs, and then, uh, a last bit on what matters to you when you choose a shop, like, is it being close, or the price, or the, the staff, that sort of thing. So three bits, and I, I said five minutes at the start and that's, that's still about right, maybe seven if you're telling me about the ham, which I don't mind at all. And, um, you wouldn't know [PERSON_2], no, that's, that's not a person you'd have met, they're just the one at the agency who set the survey up, I'm only, I'm only ringing on their behalf. Oh, and I should say, I got a bit, a bit flustered earlier, I think I told you I'd only started doing these calls recently, and that's, that's true, but I've actually been with the agency a couple of months now, so I'm, I'm not completely new, just, um, still not good on the phone. I'm sorry, that was a lot, I'm, I'm babbling. Is that, does

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, there's no need to be sorry, dear, you're not babbling, well, a bit, but so do I, my daughter says I could talk the hind leg off a donkey. Right, so three bits, shop, prices, and what matters when I pick a shop, that's not so bad. I can do that. It's just, you did say a couple of different things about how long you'd been doing it, and I got a little muddled, that's all. Anyway, what matters to me is that it's close, because of the knees, and then the ham, I suppose, and the lady on the till is very nice, she always asks after my cat. Did you want to carry on with the prices bit, or was there something else you were about to ask me, you sort of trailed off there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, the cat, that's lovely, what's the cat called? Sorry, no, I shouldn't, that's not on the, hang on, someone's just come past my desk, sorry, uh, where was I -- yes, the prices. And, um, you're right, I did say two different things about how long I've been doing this, I'm sorry, I got mixed up, it's been a couple of months, that's the true one. If you'd rather check I'm who I say I am before we go on, I'd understand, honestly. You could ring [COMPANY_A] yourself and ask for [PERSON_2], that wouldn't, I wouldn't mind that at all. Or, um, I could tell you something only the agency would know, like the reference on the letter we posted out, [CODE_1], if you got one? Some people did.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very good of you to say, dear, about me ringing them myself, though I wouldn't know where to start, I've never been much good with finding numbers, and my glasses are in the other room anyway. And a letter, hmm, a reference on a letter, now I don't remember getting one, but I get such a lot of post, my daughter says I should throw half of it out, and it all piles up on the little table by the door, with the catalogues and the one from the council about the bins. Which, honestly, they changed the bin day and nobody told me, I put it out on the wrong morning twice. So I couldn't tell you if a letter came or not, and I wouldn't want to say yes just to be polite, because then you'd think I had it, wouldn't you? Anyway, the cat's called Biscuit, since you asked, she's ginger and very bossy. But I'll say this, you're very honest about getting your times muddled, and I do like that in a person. So, the prices, go on, what did you want to know? Have I noticed them going up? Well, yes, the eggs, and the butter, and even the ham, a bit, though I try not to look at the little labels too closely.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, Biscuit, that's a lovely name, and bossy, ha, they always are. And, um, no, you're quite right, don't say yes to the letter just to be polite, that, that wouldn't help me at all, and it doesn't matter if you didn't get one. Sorry, I think I, I heard you say something about the bin, the council, and I'm not from the council, I should've said, that's, that's nothing to do with us, the survey's only the shopping. Um, so, prices, yes, the eggs and the butter and the ham, that's, that's very helpful, thank you. So, would you say they've gone up a little, or, uh, quite a lot, since, say, the spring?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the bins, yes, no, I know you're not the council, dear, I just, well, it popped into my head. Since the spring, now, hmm, let me think. Well, um, uh, let me see, it's, it's, hmm. Quite a lot, I'd say, the eggs especially, they were, oh, what was it, nearly double, or it felt like it anyway. And I'm only going on what I remember, mind, I don't write it down. Is that the sort of thing you wanted? Only you've been very patient with me wandering off, and I'd hate to be giving you the wrong sort of answer.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's, that's exactly the sort of thing, thank you, and there's no wrong answer, honestly. Um, sorry, did you say the eggs were nearly doubled, or, or nearly doubtful? No, sorry, that doesn't make sense, I, I think I heard double, I'm, I'm so sorry, my line's gone a bit crackly, hang on. Right, double, yes, I'll put quite a lot, and that it felt like double, which is, that's, that's useful, it's your impression and that's, that's what we want. And, um, I know you couldn't check the letter reference, which is fine, but is there, is there anything else I can do so you feel comfortable carrying on? I'd hate for you to, to answer all this and then wonder who you'd been talking to.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, double, yes, that's what I said, nearly double, though now I think about it, it might have been the butter that went up most, not the eggs. Or both, I don't know, you'll have to put down quite a lot and leave it at that. And that's kind of you, dear, but I feel perfectly comfortable, honestly, you've been very nice. Though, hang on, didn't you say right at the start that it was five minutes, and then I think you said seven? We must be well past that now. Not that I mind, mind you, Biscuit's asleep on the sofa and I've nothing on till the telly. So what's the last bit again, what matters when I choose a shop? I already told you that one, didn't I, the knees and the ham?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, you did, you told me all of it already, the knees, and the ham, and, uh, the lady on the till, so, so that's that bit done, honestly. And you're right, we're well past seven minutes, I'm sorry, that was my fault for, for getting in a muddle. Um, so, so there's, there's nothing left, really, you've answered all three sections, and I, I can put down butter and eggs both, that, that's fine, that's, that's what you said. So, uh, thank you, [PERSON_1], that's, that's very kind of you, and I'll let you, um, go and put the kettle on, and, and say hello to Biscuit for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's it, is it? Well, that wasn't so bad, was it, and the kettle's still waiting, I'd forgotten all about it. I'll say hello to Biscuit, she'll ignore you, mind. Now, before you go, dear, two turns back, what was it you said about the letter, the reference one? I didn't catch whether I was meant to do something with it or not, and you did say it didn't matter, but I'd hate to leave it lying on that table if it's something I should've sent back.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, good morning, is this [PERSON_1]? It's, um, [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A] -- I'm on the claims side, sort of assessing, but I'm ringing about your boiler service, the visit you booked. Sorry, just let me pull it up -- yeah, so I wanted to arrange the window for the engineer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is -- well, yes, speaking. Sorry, did you say the boiler survey? Because I haven't had anyone round about the, the roof, I don't think, although actually my neighbour had that chap in last spring, lovely man, fixed her gutter in about ten minutes. Uh, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, not the roof, the boiler. Service, not survey. I'm with [COMPANY_A], the maintenance contractor, um, [PERSON_2], on the claims side.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the boiler, right, right. And you said claims -- sorry, did you say clay? Because I did have a man about the clay, out the back, the flowerbeds go all claggy in winter, but that was ages ago and he wasn't from any company, just somebody's nephew. Is that what this is about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not the clay, claims. Uh, the boiler service you booked, that's all it is. I just need to sort a time window for the engineer to come out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, claims, yes, sorry, my hearing's not what it was on this phone. Now, I don't remember booking a boiler service, I really don't, though my memory's a bit of a sieve these days. Who would I have booked it with? Only the boiler's been fine, it makes that little tick when it comes on but it's always done that. Is it the same company as, um, [COMPANY_A], is that who you said?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], that's -- no wait, it's -- sorry, let me just check the screen. Yeah, [COMPANY_A], that's right. So the booking, it should be under your address, I'd have to, um, look at who actually took it, and I can't see that bit from here. But the little tick is, I mean, that's normal, the engineer would look at that anyway.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, I still don't remember booking it, dear. Can you tell me who it was that took the booking?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, I'd have to check that, I can't see who took it from this screen. Look, if you're not sure, that's fine, honestly. You could ring [COMPANY_A] yourself on a number you look up, not one I give you, and they can confirm the booking and sort the window with you directly. I mean, that's probably the simplest way, yeah.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very decent of you, I'll do that then. Now, sorry, can I just go back a bit -- you said at the start you were on the, the claims side, and then you said you were the maintenance people. Which is it? I got a bit muddled there, what with the clay and everything. Only I'd like to know what to say when I ring them.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon... uh, I'm hoping I have the right number. This is [PERSON_1], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and, well, I'm calling to ask whether you might have, say, five minutes for a short consumer survey. Um... no rush at all, of course, I realise I've caught you out of the blue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, you have caught me out of the blue, I'm standing in a queue at the supermarket with a basket cutting into my arm. And a compliance officer doing a survey? That's, I mean, that's an odd job title for someone ringing round asking about, what, biscuits? Compliance is the bit where somebody checks the rules are being followed, isn't it, not the bit where somebody rings me up. Anyway, who is [COMPANY_A] when they're at home, and how did you get this number? Because I've had some right rubbish phone calls over the years, and I'm still properly cross about the last one, so you'll forgive me if I don't just say yes to five minutes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't blame you at all, and I'm glad you asked, because it's a fair question, and honestly the title does sound odd out of context. Uh, in our line of work the compliance side is the part that makes sure the survey calls are made properly, so that people are asked whether they want to take part, that nobody is pressured, that participation is voluntary, and that sort of thing... and part of the job, now and then, is to make some of the calls myself, so I can hear how they actually go. So, yes, you've put your finger on it, it is a bit of a hybrid role. As for who [COMPANY_A] is, we're a research agency, we gather opinions for other organisations, and... um, I'd rather not say who the survey is for until you've agreed to take part, because it can colour the answers. And as for how we got your number, it came from a sample drawn for this particular study, I believe, and, well, I'd want to be careful about saying more than that on a call, but if you wanted it looked into properly, that's something you could ask us to do. Now, I can hear you're mid-queue, so please don't feel obliged to settle anything this second... although, uh, I'd rather not leave it too long before we're able to fit you in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, so let me get this straight, because you've said a lot there and I'm not sure any of it was an answer. You won't tell me who the survey's for, you won't really tell me where you got my number, and now you'd rather not leave it too long before you "fit me in"? That's not no rush at all, is it, that's a bit of a nudge. And the colouring the answers business, I've heard that one before, or something very like it. Honestly it's a bit rich, ringing me up out of nowhere and then being the one who's careful about what to say on a call. I'm the one who should be careful, I'm the one who picked up. If you're a proper research agency then you've got a proper name, a proper website, a number I can look up and ring you back on, and you can give me all that without it spoiling anybody's answers about, I don't know, washing powder. So go on, what's the actual name, and what's the number I'd ring? Not the survey's client, I don't care about that bit, just yours. And the trolley in front of me has stopped moving, so I'm not in the best mood for dancing about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's fair, and you're right about the nudge. I shouldn't have said that, because there isn't a deadline you need to worry about, and I'm sorry for putting it that way. The name is [COMPANY_A], and the number to ring is [PHONE_1], and you'll find us under that name at [URL_1], so please do look us up. And honestly, I'd much prefer you check than take my word for it... I'd rather you rang us than said yes to someone you can't verify. I'll say plainly, too, that I've no reason to keep the client back from you for any reason but the usual one, so if you decide to take part, I'll tell you who it's for before we begin. And, uh, since you're stuck in a queue with a basket cutting into your arm, this clearly isn't the moment, so I won't ask for your five minutes now. Would it help if I rang back at a better time?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't ring back. If I want to take part I'll look you up and ring you. Right, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's entirely reasonable, and I won't ring again. Uh, the name is [COMPANY_A], the number is [PHONE_1], so if you do decide to, you'll know where to find us. Thank you for being so direct with me, and I hope the queue picks up... goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, well, you've backed off now, I'll give you that. But I'll be honest, I'm not going to look you up. I've got a basket cutting into my arm and a trolley that's only just started moving, and I've had enough of people ringing out of the blue for one afternoon, so I'm not going to spend my evening checking out a name I never asked to be given. If you're genuine, fine, no harm done, and if you're not, well, you've had nothing out of me, have you? And I do mean nothing. I'm still cross about the last time, and I'm not going to go over it with a stranger in a queue. Right, I'm at the till, so that's me. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's perfectly fine, and you're quite right, you've given me nothing, and there's no obligation on you to do anything further. Uh, I'm sorry about the last call, whoever it was, and I'm sorry to have added to it. I won't keep you from the till... thank you for your time, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Fine. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye now... oh, sorry, hang on, somebody's just put a file down on my desk, uh, never mind. Yes. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said you wouldn't ring me back and then you're still sat there fiddling with files. And earlier you told me you'd tell me who the survey was for before we started, but then it was a no-go on that too, wasn't it? Doesn't matter. I'm done, I'm at the till, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, well, that's... I mean, I'm only still on because I thought you might want a word more, and no, I'm not going to ring you back, I said that and I meant it. And on the client, what I said was I'd tell you before we began, if you took part, so, um, it was never a no-go, it just never got as far as the start. But you're at the till, so, yes. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, that's a tidy bit of explaining, isn't it, but it doesn't change anything. It never got as far as the start because I wasn't going to get as far as the start, was I, not with somebody who wouldn't say where my number came from and wouldn't say who it was for until I'd already said yes. That's the wrong way round. A proper one tells you first and lets you decide, it doesn't ask you to agree and then promises to tell you later. And I've said goodbye about four times now and you're still going, which is exactly what gets me, because it's always the one more word, the one more little point, and I've got a cashier looking at me and a bag I haven't even opened. So no, I don't need a word more. I'm not cross with you personally, I'm just not doing this today. Goodbye, and I mean it this time.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the vehicle warranty provider. I'm calling about your vehicle's warranty coverage, it's about to lapse, and we do need to confirm the renewal today. Hello? Can you hear me okay? Yeah, so, your warranty coverage, it's set to lapse and the renewal has to be confirmed today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you. I'm in a queue. I didn't ask for a call about my car.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, understood, and I appreciate you taking the call, I do. So this is just a courtesy notification, it's part of our standard account services outreach, we reach out to every customer on file before coverage lapses, that's all this is. And the reason I'm calling now rather than, say, next week, is that our renewal window for your account closes at the end of today, so after that point the coverage drops and any repairs would be out of pocket. Now I know you're busy, you said you're in a queue, so I'll keep it brief, it's a quick confirmation, couple of minutes, and then you're done and the coverage continues without a gap. Like I said, the renewal does need to be confirmed today, so if we could just go ahead and get that squared away, that would be ideal.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. Which car? You haven't said which car, you haven't said my name, and you've told me three times it's today. Why's it always today? I've had this before, so no, I'm not just confirming anything. Who are you actually with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, and I hear the concern, I do, that's a fair question. So, I'm with account services at [COMPANY_A], and per our verification procedure, I can only go into the vehicle details once the account holder has been confirmed on the line, that's for your protection, it's so no one else can access your file. Which is why I haven't read out the make or model, because that's standard, that's how every one of our agents handles it. And as for the timing, I'm not pushing you, it's simply that the renewal window is a fixed window, it's set by the system, I don't control the closing time, and it does close at the end of today. So what I'd suggest, just to keep this moving, is that we get you verified, then I can bring up the vehicle, walk you through the coverage, and you'll see exactly what's lapsing. Now, like I said, the window closes today, so if we could go ahead and begin the verification, that would be the best way to protect your coverage.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Verification? You want me to verify myself to you, when you rang me? No. That's backwards. And you said company, which company? Because you said [COMPANY_A], that's not a name, that's like a, a letter. Look, if you've got my file, you tell me something about it first. What car, what's my name? Go on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, I understand, but per procedure I can't release any file details until the account holder is verified, that's, that's for your protection. It's standard, it's how every agent handles it. And I am with [COMPANY_A], account services, the vehicle warranty provider, that's the name on the account. Now, the renewal window does close at the end of today, so if we could just go ahead and begin the verification, that really is the quickest way to protect your coverage. I mean, it's just a couple of minutes and then you're done.

utterances.speaker: receiver

So, yes, take your time, nothing's gone anywhere. Thanks for being careful about it, [PERSON_1]. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I've got it -- I'll ask them about the compliance review, but I'm not taking the question from you, I'll just ask them what's on the ticket and see what they say. Anyway. Portal, [PERSON_3], my own number. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Oh, hi, sorry, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the vehicle warranty people, I'm just -- sorry, can you hear me alright? It's about your vehicle's cover, it's due to lapse and I'd hate for you to be left unprotected, so I just need a quick moment to confirm the renewal with you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh hi, yeah, I can hear you fine, I've just got you on speaker 'cause I'm up to my elbows in the flower beds here. Sorry, did you say my vehicle's cover is due to... what was it, a lapse? Oh, I thought you said collapse, like it's falling apart, which, I mean, the old thing does make a noise on the hills, ha. But wait, which vehicle is this about, and who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, sorry, lapse, not collapse, though I do hope it's not that, ha. It's the warranty on the car, the cover itself is running out, and I'd only be thinking of your protection here, because if it's not renewed today there'd be nothing behind you if something went wrong. And that's [COMPANY_A], sorry, [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler there. Are you still there? I thought I'd lost you for a second.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, I'm here, I'm here, just got a trowel in one hand, but hang on, you still haven't said which car, because I've actually got the two, well, the van and my daughter's little hatchback that I sort of look after, and I don't even remember signing up for a warranty on either, so how would I, oh sorry, you were going to say something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you go on, sorry. It's, uh, it's the one that's showing on the file, and I'd want to read it back to you properly rather than guess, so if I could just confirm a couple of details with you, that would let me keep the cover in place. And please don't worry that you don't remember signing up, these things do get set up through the dealer sometimes, it's very common. It's really only for your protection, [PERSON_1], I'd just hate for it to run out today. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, still with you, just brushing the dirt off my knees. But hang on a sec, you said you'd read it back to me from the file, and you still haven't actually told me which car it is, or the company name properly either. I only heard something like [COMPANY_A], which, sorry, doesn't ring any bells. Could you just tell me what's on the file, like the make or whatever, before I go confirming anything? Because if I didn't sign up for it through a dealer I'd remember, I think, I mean I'm not great with paperwork, but still.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, of course, that's completely fair, I'm so sorry. The thing is, the full vehicle details come up on the second screen, and it only opens once I've confirmed who I'm speaking with, so I'd just need you to confirm a couple of things first and then I can read it all back to you. I know it's a bit backwards, sorry. And if you'd rather check with someone, or ring the office yourself, I'm afraid the line I'm on is internal, so I can't give you a direct number, but I'd be happy to call you back a bit later. It's only that the renewal does need confirming today, so I'd hate for it to slip. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, I'm here, sorry, just putting my gloves down. But that does sound a bit backwards, you know? You're asking me to confirm things before you'll tell me which car it even is, and you can't give me a number to ring, and it's got to be today. I mean, I'm sure you're lovely, but if I did sign up for something there'd be a letter or an email or a policy number somewhere, wouldn't there? I think I'd rather look it all up myself, in the house, and ring whoever it says on the paperwork, if there is any. So I'll leave it for now, but thanks for ringing, and you have a good afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I understand, I really do, and I'm sorry if I -- well, it's only that I'd hate to think of you -- no, you're quite right to want the paperwork in front of you, that's sensible. But, um, if you do find nothing, then the cover really would be gone by tonight, so I'll ring you back a bit later on and we can finish it off then, all right? Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, honestly, don't ring back, I'll sort it myself. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], the events venue, I'm one of the verification specialists on our bookings desk. Uh, I'm calling in regards to a private function booking, a, a retirement dinner, and I'd like to confirm the, the attendee provisioning with you. Sorry, can you hear me alright? It's a retirement dinner, for a colleague of yours.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, yeah I can hear you, sorry, just, hang on, um -- so you're from an events venue, and it's a retirement dinner, for a colleague of mine? Which colleague, sorry, I'm, I'm at my desk and I'm not sure I know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, of course, so, uh, the booking was placed under the guest-of-honour protocol, which is why you wouldn't have seen any, any correspondence on your end. The colleague in question is [PERSON_2], and the function is a surprise, so, I mean, the organiser, [PERSON_3], has asked that [PERSON_2] not be made aware of the booking. That's really the only party it's confidential from, everyone else is fine. And, uh, just so we're clear, I'm not asking you for any payment or personal details today, it's purely a, a courtesy confirmation of your invitation status.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, "guest-of-honour protocol"? I've, I've never heard of that -- and you said you're not asking for payment or anything, okay, but I didn't ask that, so why are you telling me? And, uh, how'd you even get my number? If [PERSON_3] booked it, why isn't [PERSON_3] just telling me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, you said how did I get your *name*? Right, so the name came from the organiser's invitee list, uh, [PERSON_3] supplied it as part of the, the attendee manifest. And look, you're right, "guest-of-honour protocol" is just our internal term, it's not a thing you'd know. I mean, it simply means the booking is flagged confidential from [PERSON_2]. Honestly, the best thing is you don't take my word for any of it. The venue is [COMPANY_A], the booking contact is [PERSON_3], and you can reach the bookings desk on [PHONE_1] and confirm directly. I'm not after anything from you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, I said how did you get my -- my number, not my name. But okay, so [PERSON_3] gave you my details, that's -- hang on, I mean, it's odd, because if [PERSON_3] wanted me to come, why wouldn't, why isn't [PERSON_3] just walking over to my desk? We're in the same building. And, so you're saying I should call [PHONE_1] to check, but, uh, that's a number you just gave me, isn't it? I'd sort of rather just ask [PERSON_3] directly. What is it you actually need from me, though?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, yes, number, not name, sorry, my mistake, uh, hang on one second, someone's just dropped a stack of folders over here, bit of a clatter, sorry. Right. The number would have come off the same manifest, [PERSON_3] supplied it with the guest list, I don't have it from anywhere else. And that's fair about [PHONE_1], you're quite right, it's a number I've just read out to you, so don't use it on my say-so. Look it up yourself, or, honestly, ask [PERSON_3] in person, that's probably simplest. As for what I need, it's only whether you're, uh, available on the evening, a yes-or-no on attendance for the headcount, that's all. And the only person to keep it from is [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, let me just, let me get this straight. You want a yes or no on whether I'm free that evening, and you're telling me to go ask [PERSON_3] in person, and not ring [PHONE_1]. Which, uh, honestly sounds sensible, but it also makes me wonder why you're ringing me at all if you'd rather I go and check with [PERSON_3] first. I haven't even been told the date. I think I'll just do that. I'll talk to [PERSON_3] and if it's real, someone can tell me the date and I'll say yes then. I'm not going to give you an answer on the phone, sorry. Thanks for the call, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's entirely fair, and, uh, you've actually got the right instinct, I'd do the same. To clarify, I didn't mean don't ring [PHONE_1], ring it by all means, just find it yourself rather than taking it from me. And you needn't give me anything on the phone, I haven't even got the date to hand, which, I mean, is a bit of a failing on my side. If it's easier, I can ring back at a better time, say once you've spoken to [PERSON_3], and you can tell me then whether you'd like to attend. Would that suit, or would you rather [PERSON_3] just handles the headcount directly?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, I'd say don't ring back, honestly. Let me just, let me repeat that so I've got it right -- you'd call me again after I've spoken to [PERSON_3], and I'd give you the yes or no then. But if [PERSON_3] is the organiser and it's all real, then [PERSON_3] can do the headcount directly, can't they? That's what I'd rather. I mean, I've got no way of knowing who you are from this call, and you've said yourself you don't even have the date, so it just feels backwards that you'd be chasing me for an answer before I've heard anything from the person who's supposedly throwing this thing. And I've got people sat around me and I'm, I'm kind of in the middle of something, so I'm not going to start chasing up venue numbers on the strength of a call out of nowhere. If [PERSON_3] wants me there, [PERSON_3] knows where my desk is. So, no, no call back, thanks. Anyway, I'm going to go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, understood, and honestly, that's the sensible way round, so, uh, I won't ring you back. [PERSON_3] can handle the headcount directly, and if you do hear from [PERSON_3], then you'll have the date and everything from the source. I'm sorry for the, the muddle on the call, I did make it sound more convoluted than it needed to be. And, uh, just the one thing to bear in mind, if it does turn out to be real, [PERSON_2] is the only person it's being kept from. Right, I'll leave you to get on. Thanks for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, so you won't ring back, and, and [PERSON_3] does the headcount. Fine. I'll, uh -- no, actually, I'll just have a quiet word with [PERSON_3] later, see if there's anything in it. If there is, I'll hear it from them. Okay. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, and, uh, thank you for being so patient with me, I do appreciate that. A quiet word with [PERSON_3] is exactly the right course, because then everything comes to you from the organiser, with the date and the time and whatever else they've planned, and the venue's side of it, the booking and the headcount, is all squared away between us and [PERSON_3] regardless. I mean, I'd only add, and I think I said this already, that if [PERSON_3] does confirm it, the one thing [PERSON_3] will ask is that [PERSON_2] doesn't get wind of it, and that's the only person it's being kept from, nobody else in the building needs to be kept in the dark. And if it turns out [PERSON_3] knows nothing about it, well, then I'd very much like to hear that too, because it would mean something's gone wrong with our records on this end. So, uh, apologies again for the interruption, and thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, so, uh, you'd like to hear back if [PERSON_3] knows nothing about it. But hang on, you said earlier you wouldn't ring back, and now you want to hear from me? And you also said nobody apart from [PERSON_2] needs to be kept in the dark, but a minute ago it was only [PERSON_2] it was being kept from, so, I mean, which is it? Anyway. I've said what I'm doing. I'll talk to [PERSON_3] and if there's anything in it, they'll take it from there. I'm not calling anyone back about this. Right, I've really got to get on. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, so, right, yes, those two things are the same thing, really, I just said it clumsily, it's only [PERSON_2] it's being kept from, that's all I meant, and I did say I wouldn't ring you, that's still the case, no call back from me, and no need to call me either, I only meant, if it turns out, uh, well, um, sorry, I'm, I'm rambling, aren't I. Look, you've made your plan, it's a sound one, so speak to [PERSON_3], let [PERSON_3] sort it from there, and, uh, I'll leave you to your afternoon. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, um, okay. So no call back from you, and no call from me, and [PERSON_3] sorts it. Right, well, that's, that's what I'm doing anyway. Um, so. Yeah. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, um, sorry to bother you... this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], the public library. Is that, uh, is that [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, one second -- the kettle's just clicked off, I'll, uh... right. Sorry. Yes, that's me, speaking. And this is about, what, a library book? I'm just, I don't recall having anything out at the moment.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, nothing overdue, sorry -- it's a book you reserved last week, it's come in. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still here. Uh, it's just -- I don't think I reserved anything last week. Which book are you referring to, exactly? The title, I mean.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, sorry, that's a fair question. Um, I don't have the title right in front of me on this screen, I've just got the reservation slip with your name on it and the date it came in, but if you pop in or ring the front desk on the number on your library card, they'll be able to look it up and tell you exactly which book it is. I'm only ringing because we like to let people know it's arrived, and it'll be held at the front desk for ten days, so there's no rush at all, honestly. And if it turns out it wasn't you, that's absolutely fine too, sometimes a name gets mixed up, and I'd rather you heard from us than missed something you'd asked for. Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, still here, I'm just, um... thinking. So you've got a reservation slip with my name on it, but no title in front of you. That's, well, that's a bit odd, isn't it? Usually the title's the whole point of the slip. And I'd like to be clear about one thing: you've rung me, so what is it you actually need from me today? Because it sounds like all I need to do is call the number on my card, which, uh, I'd do from my own end anyway.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, sorry, you're right, that does sound odd. And I need nothing from you today, honestly, nothing at all, it's only a courtesy ring. Um, I did say I'd no title, but the system does show it, it's just on another screen and I've not, uh, I didn't want to keep you on while I went hunting for it. That's probably the muddle, I'm sorry. But the book's there for ten days either way, and ringing the number on your card is exactly the right thing to do. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, right. Except a minute ago you said you only had the slip, and that you didn't have the title. Now it's on another screen. Which is it? And you also said you've got my name, but you've only ever asked me to confirm it, I haven't actually told you anything. So, sorry, I'll ring the library on the number on my card, from my own phone, and if there's a book, there's a book. Thanks for the call, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, of course, sorry, that's completely fair, I did muddle that, and I'm sorry for the confusion. Ringing the number on your card is exactly the right thing to do. Um, there's no need to do anything today, the book's there for ten days. Thank you for your time, and sorry again to have bothered you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. I'll ring the front desk later on. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, thank you, sorry again. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, goodbye. And, uh, just to say again, I'll ring the front desk myself, on the number on my card. Not today necessarily, but I will. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, sorry, yes. Um, just before you go, you asked earlier whether it was a book you'd reserved last week, and I think I said it was on another screen, and I'm sorry, that did come out muddled. All I meant was the title's in the system, it just isn't on the slip I was looking at. Is that, um, is that clear enough? Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm still here, but that's not quite what you said earlier. You said you had the slip with my name on it and the date, but no title, and then it was on another screen. Now it's not on the slip but it's in the system. Those aren't quite the same thing. Anyway, it doesn't matter. I'll sort it out with the front desk myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, um, did you say the front desk's closed? No, no, it's open, it's open all week, I think, but that's... sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... no, I didn't say the front desk was closed. I said I'd ring them myself. Look, I'm going to hang up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, hello, yes, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? I'm, um, I'm calling on behalf of [PERSON_2] at the [COMPANY_A] foundation, and I'm sorry to catch you out of the blue like this, it's just that, well, there's a pledge from the event last month that really does need to be sorted out, and it's, uh, rather time-sensitive now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, hang on, I've got a pan on. Sorry, what? Who's calling? A pledge? From what event? I'm, I'm not sure I -- sorry, can you say that again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, of course, please, take your time, I didn't mean to interrupt your cooking, that's, uh, that's awful timing on my part.
