So, it's, um, [PERSON_2] who asked me to ring, I'm just helping out on [PERSON_2]'s behalf, at the [COMPANY_A] foundation, and the event was the, the fundraising evening, last month, I think it was, or maybe the month before, I'd have to check. And you said, well, I'm told you said, at the time, that you'd be giving a really generous gift, [AMOUNT_1], and everyone there was so moved, honestly, [PERSON_2] was quite touched by it, and now the foundation has, um, sort of planned around that money, so there are families, there are people counting on it, and I'd hate for it to look like it's been, well, forgotten. It does need to be settled quite soon, I'm afraid, that's why I'm ringing today rather than, you know, writing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hold on, let me just turn this down. Right. Sorry, what? A fundraising evening? I, um, I don't really remember -- was that, when was that? You said last month, or the month before? You're not sure? And [AMOUNT_1]? I said that? That sounds like a lot. I'm not sure I'd have, I mean, I don't think I'd say a number like that out loud. Sorry, who did you say you were again? And who's [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, I'm [PERSON_3], I just help out. [PERSON_2] is, um, at the foundation, I did say that. I can't really go into the records, they're confidential, and honestly it's a bit hurtful to be asked all this when people are relying on you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, I didn't mean to hurt anyone's feelings. It's just, I'm a bit lost. Sorry, but back a minute ago, you said the foundation had, what was it, planned around the money? And that I'd said it at the event? Um, who told you I said that, though? Was it [PERSON_2], or did you hear it yourself? And you couldn't say which month it was, so, sorry, how do you know I said it at all?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, um, so, [PERSON_2] told me, I wasn't, no, I wasn't actually there myself, I, uh -- no, wait, I might've been there, for part of it, I'd have to, um, it was a very busy evening, you understand. And, uh, the month, it was last month, I'm fairly sure, I only said the other thing because, well, my notes are, they're... hm. Look, I really can't get into where it was written down, that's all kept private, and I'd just, I'd hate for it to seem like the pledge is being doubted, because people are counting on it, that's all I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, the pan's spitting. Hold on. Right. Sorry, what was I -- oh, you said you weren't there, and then you might've been there? Um. I'm getting a bit confused, to be honest. You don't know the month, you don't know if you were there, and you can't say where it's written down. Sorry, but that doesn't, that doesn't really add up, does it? I think I'd want to ring the foundation myself, you know, on a number I look up. Is that, is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a number, um, no, I wouldn't, I mean, you don't need to go looking things up, I can, I could just, uh -- sorry, you said it was spitting? No, the, the pan, I meant the, never mind. Look, I've, I've said what I was asked to say, and I don't, I don't know what else I can tell you, it's a bit upsetting honestly, I'm only trying to help. I'm going to, uh, I'll let you get back to your cooking. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right. Sorry, you're going? Well, um, I'll look the foundation up myself and ring them, then. If there's a pledge, they'll have it written down. Sorry, I didn't mean to upset you. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Good, it's [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor with [COMPANY_A], your electricity supplier. I'm calling about the overdue balance on your account, it's been, uh, about six weeks now, I think seven actually, and supply is scheduled to be interrupted on the date in the notice we sent, so I wanted to speak to you directly before that happens.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Overdue? Hang on, I've got something on the hob -- hang on. Um, sorry, who did you say you were again? And I don't, I mean, I didn't get any notice, I don't think. Cut off? When?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], supervisor at [COMPANY_A], and look, the notice went out by post, it's all on file, so I'm not sure why we're -- right, the date is the one printed on the notice, and after that it's a reconnection process, which is a hassle for everyone, so I'd really rather we sorted this today. I mean, you've had a few weeks to look at this, [PERSON_1], so I'm a bit surprised it's news to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? I really don't remember any letter. And you still haven't said what the date is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, you're right, I should have said. The interruption date is the [DATE_1], and the balance is [AMOUNT_1]. Honestly, you can check it yourself, it'll match what's on your last bill.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the what? Did you say the interruption? No, hang on, I thought you said, um, something about an inspection. Is someone coming round to the house? Because I'm not, I mean, I'm cooking, I can't have anyone just turn up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nobody's coming to the house, sorry, that's my fault, I was talking fast. Interruption, as in the supply being switched off, not an inspection, nothing like that. Nobody turns up unannounced, that's not how we work, there's a whole procedure and a visit would only ever follow a written notice. And look, I know a call like this is alarming, and I know you're in the middle of cooking, so let me make it simple. Please don't take my word for any of it. Log into your own account, the way you normally do, or ring the number printed on your bill, and have a look at the balance and the date. That's [AMOUNT_1] on the account, and it should match what's on your last bill. I'm not asking for a payment on this call, I won't take one, and I don't need any details from you. If the figure's more than you can manage in one go, there's a payment plan, which you can set up through your account or by speaking to the team on the bill number, so it doesn't have to be a lump sum. All I'm trying to do is make sure you hear about this before the [DATE_1] and not after, because I've seen it go badly for people who found out when the lights went off. Does that sound fair?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Uh, okay. Yes, that sounds, I mean, that's fair, I suppose. Sorry, I'm just, the pan's spitting. So you're not wanting money off me now, you just want me to look at the account? And ring the number on the bill? I don't really do the account online, not much. But I've got the bills in a drawer somewhere. I'll find the number and ring it. Is that all right? Is that what you want me to do?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's all right, that's exactly it. No money from you on this call, none, I just want you to look at the account, or ring the number on the bill, and check the balance and the date for yourself. Like I said, don't take my word for it, go to the bill in the drawer. And if the figure's a bit much, ask them about the payment plan when you ring, that's what it's there for. Go and see to your pan, [PERSON_1], and sorry again for the alarm, it's never a nice call to get. You take care, and I hope the dinner's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Um... yes. Okay. I'll, uh, I'll find the bill once I've sorted this pan and ring the number on it. Not yours, the one on the bill. Sorry, you're right, I should go, it's catching. Thanks for ringing, I suppose. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, this is [PERSON_1] from [COMPANY_A], ticketing and venue booking. I'm calling about your concert booking, it's been rescheduled, so I need a minute to go over the new date with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hi, sorry, hang on, I'm driving so you're on speaker and the reception's a bit patchy out here, so if I cut out or ask you to repeat something, I'm really sorry. Um, a concert booking? I mean, I think I did book something, a while back, maybe a couple of months ago, but I've booked a few things this year and I honestly can't remember which one this would be. Which concert is it you're talking about? And, sorry, who did you say you were with again? I only caught part of that, the line kind of broke up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No problem. [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], we handle ticketing and venue booking. The booking reference is [ACCOUNT_REF]. The original date was [CODE_1], and the new date is [AMOUNT_1]. That reference should be in your confirmation email from when you booked, so you can match it up when you're parked. If you'd rather not go over it while you're driving, I can email the details across, or you can look up the venue's published number and ring back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, um, right, that's, that's actually really kind of you, thank you. Sorry, I'm just, uh, hang on, the signal went again for a second so I think I missed the new date, but, I mean, you're saying I can check the reference against my email once I'm parked? Yeah, I think that makes more sense, I don't want to be fumbling about with my phone on the road and get something wrong. Is it, um, is the email the best way to get the details, or should I ring the venue? Sorry, I'm probably over-thinking it, I'm just a bit, uh, anxious when I'm driving and someone's telling me something important.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not over-thinking it at all. Either works, and the email's probably easier. I'll send the confirmation to the address on the booking, and you can match it up once you're parked. Since you missed the new date, I'll give it again, same as before: booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [CODE_1], new date [AMOUNT_1]. If you'd rather check with the venue, use the number they publish, not one I give you, and quote that same reference. Want me to send the email now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, uh, yes please, sending the email's fine, to the address on the booking. Sorry, I think I said that already, I just want to be sure you heard me, with the line going in and out. And I'll check the reference against my confirmation when I'm parked, like you said, and if it doesn't match I'll just ring the venue myself, on their own number. So, uh, that's all sorted then? Thank you, sorry for all the fuss, and, um, thanks for not making me do it while I'm driving. Bye now, drive, I mean, I'll let you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, heard you fine. Email goes to the address on the booking. That's all sorted. Drive safe, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, great, thank you, and sorry again for all the, uh, repeating myself. I'll look out for the email once I'm parked. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No trouble at all. Email's going out now, reference [ACCOUNT_REF] on it. Thanks for your time, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, thanks, yeah, I'll look out for it. Okay, bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, bye, I'll just, I mean, I was going to say thanks again, but, well, you've heard it already, haven't you. Sorry. Okay, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good afternoon, is that, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I do hope I haven't caught you at a bad moment, I'm just ringing from [COMPANY_A], the foundation, my name's [PERSON_2], and I'm one of the case handlers on the supporter side. It's nothing to worry about at all, I'm only following up with a handful of people who came along to our event back in the spring, just to see how everyone found the evening and whether there's anything we could've done better, that sort of thing. Are you still there? Sorry, the line's a bit faint on my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm still here, sorry, I've got my little one running about in the background so I was just, um, keeping an eye. Which foundation did you say? Because I mean, I go to a few things in the spring, school stuff, a couple of charity bits, so I'm not sure which event you mean. And you said you're a case handler? That's a funny thing to call someone who's ringing about an evening out. What's the case, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, it's just the title, sorry, it's [COMPANY_A], the foundation, and it was the evening in [CITY_1]. Honestly I'm only following up on a note that was left on your name.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A note left on my name. By who?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, by, well, it's, sorry, it's logged under the events team, so I wouldn't want to, um, put a name to it when I'm not completely sure myself. I mean, it's only a, a note that says you made a, a verbal pledge on the night, a fairly generous one actually, [AMOUNT_1], and it just hasn't been, well, honoured yet, and I'd hate for that to land badly for you. Are you still there? Sorry, I just wanted you to hear it from me first, gently, rather than, you know, in a letter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on. A moment ago this was how did you find the evening, and now it's a pledge I never honoured? I'm sorry, but I don't remember pledging anything, and I'd remember [AMOUNT_1]. And land badly for me how, exactly? What's in this letter? Because you can't name who left the note, you can't tell me which event it was beyond a city, and that's, I mean, that's not a lot to go on, is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I know, I know that sounds like a sudden turn, and I do apologise, I should've said it more clearly at the start. It's just that the pledge record is, um, confidential, I'm not able to share the details of it over the phone, the date or the form or who took it down, it's all held on file for, well, for your own protection, really. But I'd hate for you to be caught out by it, you know, if it went any further, so if we could just get it settled quietly today, that'd be so much kinder all round. Are you still there? Sorry, I only want to help.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Settled quietly today? How do you settle something I don't remember and you won't describe? Honestly, that's the wrong way round. If there's a record, then I'm the one it's about, so why can't I hear the date, or who took it down? And go further, what exactly do you mean by "if it went any further"? Further to what, a debt collector? Because I'm not paying anything on a phone call, not to someone I can't check. If this is real, you can send it in writing, to me, with a proper address I can look up myself. I'm going to hang up now and if there's something real, I'll hear about it that way. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, please don't hang up, I only mean, if it goes further it's out of my hands and I'd hate to see you, I'm really not trying to upset you, [PERSON_1], it's only that the file can't be opened to you here, it's confidential, and writing it down would just, it would only make it more formal, and that's the very thing I'm trying to spare you. Are you still there? Hello? Sorry, I'm only asking for a few minutes today, just so it can be put right quietly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say a few minutes, or a few pounds? Because that's, no. I said goodbye, I don't know why you're still talking. I'm not paying anything today and I'm not putting anything right quietly, and honestly the more you tell me it can't go in writing, the less I believe any of it. Please don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, [PERSON_1], I'm only trying to, it isn't about pounds, it's about keeping this from, from becoming something unpleasant for you, and I'd hate for your little one to, no, sorry, I shouldn't have said that, I only mean it's far kinder if we, are you still there? Please, just one minute, it's only to put it right quietly today, and then it's all over, I promise, and I'd never ring again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, put that down, no, not on the floor, honey, uh -- right. Sorry. What did you just say about my little one? Because I heard that, and you can't, you don't get to bring a child into this. No. That's it, I'm done, and I'm putting this number down as a nuisance call. Don't ring again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, [PERSON_1], I didn't mean it like that, I'd never, I only meant it's a worry for the whole household when these things drag on, and I'm so sorry if it came out wrong. Please, just one moment before you go, if we could only settle it today, quietly, I'd stop ringing and it'd all be, hello? Are you still there? I only want to protect you, that's all, I promise, it's only a few minutes and then, hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, I'm not -- you mentioned my child, and then you tried to wriggle out of it, and I'm not doing this. I've said goodbye three times now. I'm not paying anything, not today, not quietly, not ever on a phone call, and if you ring again I'll report it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, this is [PERSON_1] from the collections desk at [COMPANY_A]. Uh, Saturday's match has moved, the pitch is waterlogged, so it's a different ground and a different kick-off. Have you got a minute for the details?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who -- I just, I was having a, hang on. Collections desk? Collections for what, exactly? And a match, I don't, I mean I don't think I'm, is this about the, the five-a-side thing, or...? Sorry, I've only just woken up, can you say who you are again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, not the five-a-side, sorry. It's the junior team, Saturday morning. And the collections desk, that's just, I mean, it's the club's subs and kit fees side, I'm a volunteer, I do the admin. So, I've got your number down as a parent on the under-tens list. Anyway, the old pitch is out because of the waterlogging, so we're on the [COMPANY_B] ground now and kick-off's pushed back. Want me to read you the new time?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Under-tens, right, um. Well, I mean, I've got, my sister's lad plays, I think, or he did, so maybe, hang on, is it, which team did you say? Because I don't, I wasn't told anything about, and you said collections, that's the bit I keep, uh, snagging on. Sorry. What name did you say you were?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_1], and that's fair, collections is just what the desk is called, it's nothing to do with you owing anything. This call is only the pitch change. If your sister's lad is on the under-tens, she's probably the number we've got down and yours might be a backup, so it could be a wrong number. I can note the query on the file if you'd rather check with her first. Do you want me to read the new time out anyway, or leave it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no, that's, okay. I think I'd better ask her first, yeah. Because I really don't, I don't know anything about it, and you said collections, and I keep, well, I keep coming back to that, why's it called collections if it's not, you know. Sorry. So you're [PERSON_1], from the collections desk, and it's the junior team. And you got my number from, from my sister, did you say? I didn't catch that bit.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not from your sister, no, it's just on the under-tens contact list, I don't know who put it there. Yeah, ask her first, that's fine. I'll put a note on the file that you've queried it, and if the number's wrong we'll take it off. Sorry for the early call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, no, it's, it wasn't early, I mean it's, well, I was just -- never mind. Yeah, I'll, I'll ring her and, no, actually I'll text her, and if it is me on the list she can, she'll sort it. So you're not wanting anything from me, then? Just so I've got that straight, because I'm still a bit, nothing to pay or, no? Okay. Right. Well, thanks for, thanks. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, nothing to pay, nothing I need from you at all. The call was only to say the pitch has changed because of the waterlogging, that's the whole of it. And look, texting her is the right move, because if you are on the list she'll know what it's about, and if you're not, she can tell whoever keeps the list and they'll take your number off. I'll leave the note on the file that you queried it, so nobody rings you again by mistake. Sorry again for catching you half asleep. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's, I mean, I'll, no, let me, I'll text her now, actually, while I've got it in my head. And, uh, thanks for, for being straight about it. Right. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, estates side. Have you got a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, that's me, sorry, hang on, I've got you on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the flower bed here -- there's a blackbird going absolutely mad at me, I think I've disturbed his worm patch. Uh, anyway, a solicitor's office, you said? Estates side? Sorry, what was it you wanted again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, take your time. Sorry, did you say a bird patch? Uh, I don't have anything on a patch of land on my screen, so I'll note that. It's an estate we're handling, and you may be named in it. That's all I can say for now, and I'd ask you to keep it between us until the formal letter reaches you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, not a bird patch, a worm patch, the blackbird's, it's just -- never mind, it's nothing to do with you! Sorry. Right, so, an estate, and I might be named in it? Oh gosh, who's died? And hang on, why can't I tell anyone, I'd have thought I'd want to tell my sister -- is it, like, a secret thing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, worm patch, noted, sorry. Uh, no, it's not a secret as such. Estate matters are confidential until the formal notification goes out, that's just standard. I can't give you the name of the deceased on this call, because I haven't confirmed I'm speaking to the right [PERSON_1]. That's why I'm asking you to hold off telling anyone for now, but it's only until the letter arrives, and your sister can hear all about it after that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, that makes some sense I suppose. Though, hang on, how are you going to confirm it's the right me, then? Because I'm [PERSON_1], that's definitely my name, but I don't know what else you'd need, and I'm not sure I like the idea of just reading things out over the phone. Is there a, uh, a number I could ring you back on? Or a letter I could wait for? I mean, if it's all going to come in a letter anyway, why ring first?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, and you're right not to want to read things out cold. Ringing first is just so the letter lands without a surprise, and, uh, I did say earlier I couldn't tell you anything about the estate, which isn't quite right. I can say it's an estate where a [PERSON_3] may have named you, I just can't say more than that yet. All I'd need is your full name and the address the letter should go to, which is already on our file, so really you'd just be confirming it matches. And please do look us up, [COMPANY_A], we're in [CITY_1], find us in an independent directory and ring back on that number, not one I give you. Happy to note on the file that you want to verify first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's a good idea, ringing you back on a number I find myself, yes, I'll do that. Uh, hang on though, earlier you said you couldn't tell me anything at all about who it was, and now there's a [PERSON_3] who might have named me, so which is it? And you said it was just a minute, and I think we're well past that, ha. Sorry, I'm not having a go, I just like to get things straight. Is there a reference I should quote when I ring, so they know it's you I'm after?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right, I did change my line there, and I'll put that on the file. It's the same position though, I can give you the name of whoever it concerns but not the details of what's left, not until you're confirmed. Sorry, one second, someone's just put a delivery on my desk, uh, right, back. Reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], quote that and ask for [PERSON_2] in the estates team, and they'll find it. And yes, we've gone past the minute, I'll own that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, [ACCOUNT_REF], and ask for [PERSON_2], got it, I'll remember that. Hang on, though, going back a bit, you said earlier that you didn't have anything about a patch of land on your screen. Why would you be looking at land at all? Is it a house or some land or what, and what did you mean by that? Sorry, I'm only asking because I wasn't sure what you meant at the time and then we moved on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, yes, that was me misreading you, I thought you'd said a patch of land, and I was just checking the file for property, there's nothing on it either way. I don't have a house or land in front of me, and I can't tell you what's in the estate until it's confirmed. Honestly it was a throwaway line, I should have just said I'd misheard. Uh, so, to wrap up, you'll look us up yourself and ring back quoting [ACCOUNT_REF], and the letter will follow. Is that --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine, I'll look you up myself and ring back, ha. Though hang on, you said right at the start it was a minute, and then earlier you said you couldn't say anything about who it was, and I'm sure at one point you told me not to tell my sister, and then you said that wasn't a secret as such. I'm only saying, it's a bit all over the place, isn't it? Anyway, I'll find the number myself, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], ask for [PERSON_2], and wait for the letter. Right, I'd better get back to my blackbird. Bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, just to be clear on the sister point, since you raised it, I'd not want you leaving it muddled. It's not a secret, and I shouldn't have put it as an instruction. I'm only asking you to hold off until the letter's with you, and after that you can tell her whatever you like. And yes, I take the point about it being all over the place, I'll note that on the file. Right, so you'll look us up yourself, ring back quoting [ACCOUNT_REF], ask for [PERSON_2], and the letter follows. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, good luck with the blackbird. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, thanks, he'll need it, he's a stubborn little thing. Right, well, yes, I'll look you up myself, and I think I might mention it to my sister after all, whatever you said, because it all sounds a bit odd when I say it out loud. But thanks for ringing, and for being so patient with the worm patch business. Bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from security operations at [COMPANY_A]. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? Good. I'm calling about your remote position, the one we confirmed last week, and there's a clearance item that needs to be finalised today so your start date isn't pushed back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who? Which company did you say? And what position, I don't, I've not got anything pending that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, [COMPANY_A]. The recruitment agency, [PERSON_2], I just said that. And the position is the remote role you were approved for, it's all on file under [ACCOUNT_REF], so I don't, I mean, I don't have time to go back over the whole file with you. Right, so, as I was saying, there's a one-time onboarding cost of [AMOUNT_1] that has to be cleared before your start date is released, and I need to know you're ready to proceed today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, hang on. Security operations at a recruitment agency, and now it's a payment? That's a bit of a jump. And you said company A, but you haven't actually said a company name. Just company A. Which, I mean, what's the agency actually called? And when did I apply for this? Because I genuinely don't remember confirming anything last week.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I stated the agency name, it's [COMPANY_A], and I'm not going to keep repeating it. The application was submitted through our portal, [PERSON_2], and your confirmation is logged. That's what the reference is for. Now, I've explained the onboarding cost, it's [AMOUNT_1], it's standard, and the position doesn't release until it's cleared. This is time-sensitive, and if it lapses, the file is closed and the placement goes to the next candidate.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but see, that's the bit that doesn't sit right. A real recruiter doesn't charge the candidate to start a job, the employer pays the agency, not the other way round. So what's the actual job? Which employer? And what's the name of the portal I supposedly applied through, because I'd have an account there and an email in my inbox.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Every agency structures its onboarding differently, [PERSON_2], and I'm not here to walk you through our fee model. The employer is, uh, a client of ours, and the details are released after clearance. The portal's on your confirmation, which you should have, and I'm telling you, slowly, the position lapses today if this isn't cleared.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no. You can't tell me the employer, you can't name the portal, and the one thing you're sure about is that I pay by the end of today. That's not an onboarding process, that's a pitch. If there's really a role, send it to me in writing from an address I can check, and I'll look it over. I'm not paying anything over the phone. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_2], listen. Listen to me. The position is approved, it's on file, and it lapses today, today, if it isn't cleared. I'm not sending anything in writing, that's not how this department works, so I need an answer now, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. That's your answer. A department that won't put anything in writing, can't say who the employer is, and needs money today, I'm not dealing with that. If the role's real, it'll survive me checking. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Fine, that's your decision, [PERSON_2]. Though I'll note, I did say the file was confirmed last week, uh, no, it was submitted this week, whichever, it's all in the record. I'm closing it now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Last week, this week, yeah, that's about what I figured. Hang on, sorry, there's something going off on my screen, a notification or, never mind. Anyway. Close whatever you like. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hm? No, that's, hold on, someone's at my door, give me a -- no. Never mind. The file's closed, [PERSON_2], that's all. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go. Two turns back you said the application went in through your portal, so what's it actually called? You never said, and you've now changed the week twice. No? Fine. Not paying, not ringing back, and I'd drop this number. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, the, well -- the portal, it's, uh, it's on the, I don't have that in front of me. Look, I've got another call holding. The file is closed, [PERSON_2]. That's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you don't have it in front of you. That's the thing, though. You've been quoting a reference, a confirmation, a portal submission, a file that's logged, and the moment I ask for one plain fact, the name of the thing I supposedly used, you've got another call holding. Anyone actually working a file would have the portal name in their head by now, because it's the first thing a real candidate would want. So no, I don't think there's a file, and I don't think there's another call either. If I've somehow missed a genuine application, the agency can email me from an address I can look up, and I'll check it properly in my own time. Until then, nothing gets paid, nothing gets confirmed, and I'd rather you didn't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is account services at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling about an urgent fault we've flagged on your line. Uh, and before we go further, I just need to clarify something, did you say you're the primary account holder, or is it someone else in the household? Because I do have to speak with the named holder, and I've only got a short window to get this logged before the line gets queued for disconnection.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, I didn't say anything, you just started. Who is this, exactly? And what fault? I've got maybe two minutes, so, yeah, just get to the point.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, yes, I'm calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], your home internet provider. And the fault is a line integrity issue, uh, it's been flagged on your connection and it needs to be logged within the next few minutes, which is why I'm keeping this brief. Now, going back to what I asked a moment ago, are you the named account holder, or is that someone else in the household?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, back up a second. You said it's about to be queued for disconnection, right? That was in your first bit. Disconnected for what, exactly? Because my internet's working fine, I'm using it right now. And you still haven't answered who you actually are. A company name's not a person.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, the disconnection isn't a penalty, it's a standard protocol when a line integrity fault goes unlogged. And it can look fine on your end right up until it drops, that's sort of the nature of it. My name's [PERSON_1], I'm with account services at [COMPANY_A]. Now, I do need to get this logged before the window closes, so are you the named account holder, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. No, I'm not answering that. You rang me, you tell me what account you've got. And if it's a fault, I'll call the number on my bill.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, ma'am, sir, sorry, there's no need to ring anyone, this is the call, I'm the one who's been assigned to your fault. And I haven't said the line's being disconnected today, I said it's queued, which is just the standard process. Look, I can't read out account details until I've confirmed the account holder, that's procedure, so I do need that answer from you, and the window closes in about five minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, huh. Right. So, um, you won't tell me anything until I tell you who I am, and I'm not to ring anyone else because you're the call. That's, uh, that's backwards, mate. You rang me. Look, I'm hanging up and I'll ring the number on my bill. If there's a real fault, they'll know about it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, hold on, please, uh, there's no need for that. Look, I never said you couldn't ring anyone, I only said it'd be quicker through me, and I did say the disconnection was today, or, well, queued for today, it's the same -- anyway, if you hang up now the fault just drops off our system and I can't guarantee anything after that. So if I could just have a yes or no on the named account holder, sir, that gets us logged in the next couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Listen, you've changed your story about four times in the last minute. First it's queued for disconnection, then it isn't a penalty, then it's not today, then it's queued for today, and now if I hang up the fault just falls off your system and nobody can help me. That's not how a real fault works, is it? A real fault sits in a ticket until someone fixes it, it doesn't vanish because I put the phone down. And I've asked you three times for something simple, like what account you're actually looking at, and all I've got back is a deadline and a yes or no question. I'm not confirming a single thing to you, not who I am, not who's in the house. If there's genuinely a fault, my provider can find it from their side without me, and I'll ring the number on my bill, not the one you're on. So, no. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, I understand your frustration, truly, but if I could just, uh, go back to the beginning, because I think we've gotten a bit tangled. I'm calling from account services at [COMPANY_A] regarding a line integrity fault, and what I've said is that the fault needs to be logged within the window, which is why I've been asking for the account holder confirmation, because it's procedure, and I can't discuss account specifics, or the ticket, or anything about the line, until that's been completed. Now, as for the ticket, it does sit in the system, you're right, but it sits in a, uh, a pending status, and pending faults that aren't actioned within the window get escalated to the disconnection queue, which, again, isn't a penalty, it's just how the process runs. So all I'm asking, and it's really the only thing standing between you and getting this sorted, is a simple confirmation that you're the named account holder, and then I can go ahead and log it, and we can all get on with our afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. That's the fifth version of it now, and I'm done. I'm not confirming anything to you, and I'm not staying on for another lap. If there's a pending ticket, my provider can sort it from their end when I ring the number on my bill. Don't call back. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, did you say you're not the bill holder? Because if the bill's in someone else's name, then, right, that changes things, I'd need to speak to them directly, so if you could just put [PERSON_2] on, or whoever the, the named holder is, we can still get this logged before the window shuts.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Who's [PERSON_2]? I never said anything about a bill being in someone else's name. I said I'd ring the number on my bill, the bill, that's all. And no, nobody's coming to the phone for you. You've just tried to get a second person to confirm the same thing. That's it. I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you're done with the, uh, the fault? No, no, sir, that's not an option on my end, the fault doesn't close because you've finished with it, it has to be logged, and that's the thing I'm still waiting on. So if I could just have that confirmation, the named account holder, and we've got maybe three minutes left in the window, then I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said I'm done with YOU, not the fault. I'm not confirming anything, I'm not putting anyone on, and I'm ringing my provider myself. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, sir, please, I'm only asking for the named account holder, that's all I need, the named account holder, and then I can log the fault. Just that one confirmation, and we've got, uh, about two minutes left in the window, so if you could just --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Nope, stop, I'm not -- no. Not answering it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good morning, sorry, one second -- [PERSON_3], can you close that door, thanks -- sorry about that, it's a bit of a busy floor today. Hi, is this [PERSON_1]? It's just the scheduling desk at [COMPANY_A], I'm only ringing to book a short time to go over some details with you, shouldn't take more than a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who? You said scheduling desk, but I didn't catch what company that was, just a placeholder sort of -- [COMPANY_A]? And I'm fairly sure you said a couple of minutes, but then you said book a time, so which is it, a booking or a conversation right now? What details, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah no, fair question, so it's [COMPANY_A], we're the international lottery claims office, and I'm just the scheduling assistant, I don't handle the claims themselves, I just line up the appointments, so it's a booking, but because you're on the line anyway we can sort the booking and the confirmation in one go, which is honestly easier for everyone, it's only a few quick checks, your name, your contact details, that sort of thing, and then the claims officer picks it up from there. And the reason I'm calling, I should've said, is that your entry came up as a winning one in the overseas draw, so that's what the appointment's about, [PERSON_1], we just need to confirm the claim details so nothing gets held up, and it really is quick, so shall we just do that now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I'm going to stop you there, because -- I don't recall entering any overseas draw. I haven't bought a ticket, not that I know of. So how exactly did my entry come up? Where did you get this number from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, the draw date, yeah, so that's the thing, it was the, uh, the ninth, no, sorry, it's on the sheet as the nineteenth, but that doesn't really matter, what matters is the entry's already been validated, so there's nothing for you to remember or look up, it's all in the system under your name, [PERSON_1], and the claims officer just needs two minutes to confirm it so the prize doesn't go back into the pool, so if I can just take your full name and the best number to reach you on, we can get you booked in before the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, can I stop you -- you've just given me two different dates for the draw, the ninth and then the nineteenth, so which is it? And "validated" by who, exactly? I never entered anything, so there's nothing to validate. You already rang me by name, so you have my name, which means you can tell me where you got this number. I'm not giving you anything else until you answer that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's the nineteenth, the ninth was a typo on my screen, that's all it was, but look, [PERSON_1], the number came from the entry list, it's all the same system, and I can't pull up the source while you're on the line, that's the claims officer's side, I just do the diary, so all I need is your full name and a number to reach you on and I'll get you slotted in, because the slots are going fast today and I'd hate for yours to lapse.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, the dishwasher's just started beeping at me, give me a second -- right, okay, no, it can wait. Where was I. Yeah, so you can't say where the number came from, you say the slots are going fast, and a prize is about to lapse unless I act today. I'm not putting a name or a number into your diary on that basis. I never entered a draw, so there's no claim for me to confirm. Thanks for the call, but no, I won't be dealing with it this way. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], before you go, it's only a two-minute confirmation and then the claims officer takes over, I'm just the scheduling desk, so if I can take your full name and best number we'll get you slotted in today and then it's all out of my hands, and honestly I'd hate for the prize to go back into the pool over a --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I've said I'm not doing this, and you still haven't told me where you got my number, so that's the end of it. Please don't ring again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, but, I mean -- no, look, it's not that I can't, it's just that -- right, the thing is, [PERSON_1], the claims officer has the whole entry file and I only have the diary, so if you could just give me your full name and the best number to reach you on, then I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I've already said no, twice. You've given me two draw dates, no source for my number, and a deadline of today, and that's quite enough. I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no no, wait, hang on, the nineteenth, it's definitely the nineteenth, and the amount is, uh, [AMOUNT_1], no, [AMOUNT_2], but that's all in the file, [PERSON_1], so it's only the name and a number and then you're --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, uh... hm. And now you've given me two different amounts as well, so that's the date and the prize both changing on you in the space of a minute. I'm done with this. I won't be giving you a name or a number, and I won't be dealing with it by phone. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon! Is that [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I hope I'm not catching you in the middle of lunch or anything. I'm sorry, did you say you were just heading out, or was that the kettle? Ha, either way, I won't keep you long, I just wanted to have a quick chat about your account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, who's this? [COMPANY_A], you said? And what about my account, I mean, which account are we -- sorry, I'm at my desk, I've got people right here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no no, that's fine, I'm the same, always three conversations at once. It's [PERSON_2], customer care at [COMPANY_A], we're the regulator that oversees the banks, so I'm not calling from your bank itself, that's sort of the point. And the account, well, it's your savings, [PERSON_1], but I'd rather not go into detail with people around you, it's a bit sensitive. Is there somewhere you can step away for a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, you're the regulator? That oversees the banks, but you're calling me about my savings, and it's sensitive -- sorry, but why would a regulator be ringing me at my desk? I mean, how do I know you are who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair question, honestly I'd ask the same thing, uh, you know, these days you can't be too careful. Look, the thing is, and I'll be straight with you, [PERSON_1], there's been some activity flagged against your savings, and it's the sort of thing where time matters, so I'd really like to get you sorted today, sort of before the end of the day if we can. Oh, and one thing, um, because it's an open matter, I'd ask you not to mention this call to anyone, not even your bank, just while we deal with it. Can you step out for a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, wait, so, going back a bit, you said you're not calling from my bank, that's sort of the point. What does that mean, exactly? Because now you're telling me there's activity on my savings and I shouldn't tell the bank, and that, I mean, that sounds backwards to me. If something's wrong with my money, surely the bank's the first place I'd ring?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, you're sharp, I'll give you that, you'd be surprised how many people just go along with it. No, the bank's not the problem, it's more that, uh, the matter is still open on our side, and when it's open we ask people to keep it between us until it's resolved. It's really just procedure, nothing to worry about. Anyway, the important bit is that your savings would need to be moved into a protected holding arrangement, and the sooner that's done the better, because if it drags on past today I can't promise what happens to the funds. So, can you step away for a few minutes and we'll get it sorted?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right. So, hang on, let me just, um, get this straight. You want me to move my savings into a protected holding thing, today, and not tell my bank. Um, sorry, no, that's, that doesn't sit right with me at all. If it's really the regulator, then I can ring [COMPANY_A] myself on a number I look up, can't I? And you can tell me what reference this is under.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, you can, of course, but honestly, [PERSON_1], that's the thing, it's just that it's really time-sensitive, so, um, like I said, the sooner we get your savings into that protected arrangement the better, because past today I can't promise what happens to the funds. And I'd just ask again, please, keep this between us for now, not the bank, not anyone, it's only procedure. Look, a reference, yes, it's, uh, [ACCOUNT_REF], but if you ring around and start asking questions, it could slow things down, and, I mean, we really don't have that kind of time. So, can we just get on with it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. No, I'm sorry, but I'm not doing that. You've told me to move my savings today, keep it secret from my bank, and not to ring anyone to check, and that's, honestly, that's exactly what I've heard on the news about these calls. A real regulator isn't going to mind me phoning them back. So I'm going to hang up, and I'll look up the number myself and call them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, come on, [PERSON_1], there's really no need to -- look, you're being a bit, I mean, nobody's trying to -- honestly, if you hang up now I can't promise what happens to the funds, and that's not a threat, that's just, uh, just how it is. Ha, listen, why don't we just --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Nope. I've said what I'm doing, and you're not changing it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, sorry, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy on, uh, [CITY_1] high street, I'm just ringing to let you know your repeat prescription's ready for collection. Sorry, I did leave a message on Tuesday, or I think it might've been Monday, I'm not quite sure, anyway, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes I'm here, sorry, I was just -- the kettle's on, you know how it is. Now, you said a message, was it Monday or Tuesday, you weren't sure, I didn't hear any message, mind you I don't always check the machine. But what was it you said about, uh, which pharmacy was it again? Only I've been going to the one near the, oh, what's it called, the old bakery, for years.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a bakery, yes, sorry, I don't think we've, um, we're not near a bakery, I don't think. We're [COMPANY_A], on the high street in [CITY_1]. And I'm sorry, did you say the kettle's on? I can ring back after your tea, honestly, there's no rush at all. It's just that your repeat's ready, and I'd hate for it to go back on the shelf, you know, for your own sake, in case you run short. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the shelf, yes, the *shelf*, no, I've got plenty of room on the shelf, it's the, well, I've got all those little jars Margaret left me, you wouldn't believe. Sorry, what was I saying? No, no, don't ring back, I'm only boiling the kettle, I'm not doing anything else. It's just, I'm not sure I've got a repeat with you, dear, my tablets come from the one by the old bakery, I've always gone there. Which tablets did you say they were?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I'm, um, I'm afraid I can't say which tablets over the phone, not till I know I've got the right [PERSON_1], that's just to protect you, you understand. And I'm sorry, I did say I'd left a message on Tuesday, but actually I think I only tried the once, it might've been a different number, I'm so sorry, it's all in the notes here. Are you still there, [PERSON_1]? If it's not your pharmacy, honestly, the best thing is just to pop in and ask, and we can sort out whose it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's -- yes, I suppose that's sensible, about protecting me, I mean. Only I'd, uh, I'd rather -- no, what I mean is, if it's not even my pharmacy, then I don't see why you'd have my number at all, do you? Hang on, say that again, did you say you only tried once, or twice? Because first you said a message, and then it's the once, and a different number, and I'm, well, I'm just a bit muddled now. Maybe I'll just pop in to the bakery one and ask them, dear, they'd know if I had anything waiting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I've muddled you, that was my fault, I shouldn't have gone back and forth like that. Yes, that's probably the sensible thing, [PERSON_1], asking at the one you know, they'll be able to tell you straight away. It's only that I didn't want your repeat going back on the shelf without you knowing, that's all, for your own protection really. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um... yes, I'm here, I'm just, uh, thinking. You know, it is a bit odd, isn't it, ringing me about tablets you can't even name, and then not sure which number you rang. I don't mean to be rude, dear, you do sound very nice. But I think I'll do just that, I'll go and ask at the bakery one, and if they say it's yours, well, then I'll pop in to you on the high street. Thank you for ringing, anyway, it's nice to have a chat. Right, bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, [PERSON_1], honestly. Sorry to have bothered you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no bother at all, dear, it was lovely to -- oh, hang on, there's the kettle going, it's whistling away, I'd quite forgotten it. Right, sorry, where was I? Yes, bye now, mind how you go, and I'll ask at the bakery one tomorrow. Bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, um, that's quite all right. You go and see to your kettle, [PERSON_1], I won't keep you. Sorry again for the muddle, and, uh, mind how you go too. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, dear, you're very kind. Right, I'll go and rescue that kettle before it boils dry. Bye bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, go on, mind the steam, it, um... well, you know, it does spit sometimes. Sorry, are you still, uh, still there? No, of course you're not, you'll be off to the kettle. Bye now, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, dear, just, well, I keep saying goodbye and then not putting the phone down, don't I? Silly me. Right, I really am going this time, kettle's screaming the place down. Bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, no, not silly at all, I'm just as bad, honestly. Sorry, I'll, um... well, you go and see to that kettle, [PERSON_1], I really won't keep you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I won't, I'm going, I'm going, honestly, it's only the -- right, bye now, dear, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Hey [PERSON_1], my name's [PERSON_2], I'm with the internal investigations unit over at [COMPANY_A]. Sorry to catch you out of the blue, got a couple of minutes? It's nothing to worry about, I just need to run something past you real quick.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is -- sorry, hang on, there's a truck right on my bumper, I'm on speaker, I'm driving. Okay. Yes, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? The reception's kind of cutting in and out, and I didn't quite catch the, uh, the company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No worries at all, [PERSON_1], safe driving, I can hold on. It's [PERSON_2], I'm a senior investigator with the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A], that's your bank. Look, it's a quick one, and honestly you can pull over or I can walk you through it in two minutes, whichever's easier. Thing is, it's about some activity on your account, and I do need to keep this one just between us for now, so, uh, is it okay if we do it while you're driving, or d'you want a moment to find somewhere to stop?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, did you say a, a bonus? On my account? Because I don't, I wasn't expecting anything like that, I mean, I don't think I've, hang on, is this the bank or is it, sorry, it's really breaking up. And the, um, the keeping it between us part, I didn't quite get why. Why would it need to be secret? Sorry, I'm probably being slow, I just, I'm a bit nervous driving and talking.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, not a bonus, [PERSON_1], sorry, the line's bad on my end too. It's the bank, [COMPANY_A], internal investigations, I'm calling about some activity on your account. Activity, not a bonus. And the keeping it between us, that's just because we think someone on the inside might be involved, so I can't have it going round the branch or the family either, you know how people talk. It's honestly a very quick thing, two minutes tops, and everyone asks me that, so don't feel slow at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Oh god, someone on the inside? Sorry, that's, that's a lot to hear while I'm trying to watch the road. Um, but I mean, how do I know it's actually the bank? Sorry, I don't mean to be rude, it's just, you called me, and I can't really tell who you are. Could I maybe, I don't know, call the bank back on the number on my card? Or is that, would that be a problem?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not rude at all, [PERSON_1], honestly everyone asks me that, it's smart. Um, here's the only thing though, if you ring the main number you'll get put through to the branch, and that's exactly where I can't have this going right now. Like I said, someone on the inside, so the branch is the one place we're keeping out of the loop. It's the bank, [COMPANY_A], internal investigations, I'm [PERSON_2], and it really is just a two-minute thing, so can we just sort it now and save you the hassle?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, no, sorry, I think I'd really rather call the number on my card. I know that's annoying, and I'm sorry. But it's kind of strange that I can't ring the bank to check you're the bank, you know? If it's real, it'll still be real in twenty minutes when I've pulled over. So, yeah, I'm going to do that. Sorry. Thanks for, uh, for calling. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, [PERSON_1], hang on, before you go, hang on a second. I hear you, I do, and it's a fair thing to want to check, but it's just, I'm only asking for two minutes, that's all it is, two minutes, and then you can do whatever you like. And I did say, calling the card number puts you straight through to the branch, which is the one place I can't have this going, so, uh, it'd kind of undo the whole thing. It's me, [PERSON_2], internal investigations, [COMPANY_A], and honestly the longer we wait, the more exposed your account is. So can we just sort it now, you and me, quick and quiet? Yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I really am, but that's the bit that's, um, that's making me not want to. Because you said earlier it was fine, you said I could pull over and take my time, and now it's, it's urgent and the longer I wait the worse it gets? That doesn't, those two things don't sit right together. And if the number on my card just goes to the branch, then, I mean, I'll deal with that, that's okay. I'm going to hang up now and ring the bank myself. Sorry. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's practice, I'm an assistant in the probate and estates department, and I'm ringing in respect of a, a testamentary matter in which you may be a named beneficiary, subject to the usual verification of, of identity and capacity to receive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, I didn't quite catch all of that -- a testa-- testamentary? Is that, um, like a will? Someone's left me something, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, a will, that's, uh, that's the plain way of putting it, sorry. A will, a testamentary matter, it's the same thing. So, to say it again more simply, an estate, that's to say the affairs of someone who has passed away, is being administered by our firm, and your name may appear in it. May, I stress, I can't confirm anything more until I've established I'm speaking with the right [PERSON_1], which is rather the purpose of the call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, no, that's all right, thank you for putting it plainly. Um, but you said a moment ago it was definitely me named, and now it's, it's only maybe? Sorry, I'm probably muddling it. Who is it that's passed away, if you can say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not muddling it, that was me being imprecise, I did say "may" at the start and then drifted into firmer language, apologies. The position is that a [PERSON_1] is named, but whether that [PERSON_1] is you is what we're establishing, hence the "may". As to who has passed away, I'm afraid I can't give the name over the telephone, not until you've had our formal letter, because estate matters are confidential and I'd be disclosing it to someone I haven't verified. What I'd ask is that you keep this between yourself and us until that letter reaches you, which is simply to protect the other parties to the estate.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, that's the kettle going in the kitchen, um, just a second. Right, I've turned it off. Sorry about that. Now, you said keep it between us -- you mean not tell anyone? Only that seems a bit odd, if somebody's left me something, I'd have thought I could mention it to my sister, say. And you can't tell me who it is, but you want to know if I'm the right person? How would I even, um, how do I know you're really from a solicitor's, if that's all right to ask?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a perfectly fair question, and please do ask it. And on the secrecy, I put that badly. I don't mean you can't mention it to your sister. I mean I'd ask you not to share the particulars of the estate with other parties until the formal letter arrives, because there may be other beneficiaries who haven't been notified yet. Telling your sister you had a call from a solicitor's office is absolutely fine. As to how you know, you don't, not from a voice on the phone, and I wouldn't expect you to take it on trust. So here's what I'd suggest. I'm [PERSON_2], calling from [COMPANY_A], and our address is [CITY_1], which I can give you in full. Don't use any number I give you. Look the firm up yourself in an independent directory, or through the solicitors' regulator's register, and ring the main switchboard and ask for me by name. I should also say now that I will never ask you for money, fees, or bank details, not today or in the formal letter. All I need is to confirm you're the right [PERSON_1], using only what's already in our file, and I'd be glad for you to do the checking first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very good of you, thank you, I'd never have thought to look it up myself. Um, and I'll write down your name, [PERSON_2], was it? Only earlier you said you couldn't tell me anything until you knew it was me, and now you're saying it's just a matter of confirming from what's in your file, so, sorry, if you've already got all that, what is it you'd want me to tell you? And I thought you said at the start you were ringing about it being me for certain, but never mind, I'm sure I've got that wrong, I do get muddled.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you haven't got it wrong, that's, that's entirely on me, I've been circling. Let me, uh -- let me put it straight. What I'd ask you to confirm is just your full name and the address our letter would be going to, so I can match it against what we hold. Nothing else. No dates of birth, no bank details, nothing like that, and if you'd rather not say anything today, that's fine, I'll simply note it and the letter goes out regardless. And yes, it's [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], do write that down. I did say "for certain" at one point and I shouldn't have, because it's only once you've confirmed those two things that we'd know it's you. I'm sorry, I've made a rather simple call sound like a puzzle.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's all right, you've been very patient with me. Sorry, you said the letter would go to, um, the address, and then something about matching it against what you, you owe? What you owe? Is it that I owe something? Because I thought it was me being left something, not, um, owing money. Or is that the other way round, I've got myself in a tangle again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you don't owe anything, nothing at all, and that's my fault again, I said "what we hold," meaning the details in our file, the records, not anything owed. No money is being asked of you, not now, not ever in this matter. It's you who may be receiving something, and that's all I'd say about it until the letter's with you. So, to clear up the tangle, all I'd ask is your full name and the postal address we have for you, and you needn't give me either today. You could look the firm up first, ring the switchboard, ask for me by name, and we'd do it then, or you simply wait for the letter. Which would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, no, thank you for clearing that up, I'm sorry for being slow. Um, I think I'd rather do it the way you said, look the firm up and ring the switchboard, if that's all right? Only I'd feel better, and I've never had a call like this before. So I've got [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], written down, and I'll wait for the letter and ring if I want to know more. Thank you very much for explaining, and sorry again for all the questions. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'd do in your position, and please don't apologise, the questions were all sensible ones. So it's [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], and if the switchboard asks, say it's regarding an estate matter and I'll be put through, or someone will take a message. If the letter doesn't turn up in a week or two, do ring us and we'll look into it. Thank you for your patience, [PERSON_1], and I'm sorry I made such heavy weather of a simple call. Goodbye now, and take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, that's very kind, I'll, um -- no, I'll write it all down properly before I forget, and then I'll ring the, the switchboard, like you said. Right, well, thank you for ringing, [PERSON_2], and sorry again for being so slow. Goodbye then, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm the compliance officer over at [COMPANY_A]... about the draw from the weekend.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, who? I was just, uh, I was having a lie-down, I'm a bit -- who's this again? Compliance officer, you said? Compliance officer at what? And what draw, I don't, there's been no draw, I don't think. Who did you say you were?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, no, I'm sorry to catch you resting. That's... a fair thing to ask, and please do ask it again if I don't answer it properly. I'm [PERSON_2], and I work in compliance at [COMPANY_A], the shop in [CITY_1], the one that had the stand at the community fair. You'd have filled in an entry slip, name and a phone number, and dropped it in a box... and your slip was one of the ones drawn, uh, for one of the smaller prizes. Nothing large. I just, well, I do like these things confirmed properly, and sooner rather than later, if you follow.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A fair? Oh, the, hm, I did go to a thing, there was a, a lot of tents, my neighbour dragged me along, and I think there was cake. But a slip in a box, I don't, I really don't remember that. So you're the compliance officer, and it's a shop, and you're ringing about a prize. Confirmed properly, you said, confirmed how? Sooner rather than later, why's it got to be sooner? I've only just woken up, love, I'm not, who did you say you were again? [PERSON_2]? And which shop?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_2], and the shop is [COMPANY_A]. I'm glad you're asking, truly, and you're quite right to be careful. The fair was on [DATE_1], the Saturday, and ours was the stand with the, uh, the prize jar and the entry box beside it. If you did put a slip in, that's the one I'm calling about, and if you didn't, well, tell me so and I'll note it and leave you be. As for confirming, it's only that I'd like to be sure I've got the right person, which I can do with the name and the number the slip was filled in under. And there's nothing to pay, nothing at all, the prize is collected in person at the shop, so there's no need to hand over anything to me today. As to why sooner... I wouldn't want it to sit about, that's all. Prizes do tend to, uh, get tidied away if they aren't claimed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, the Saturday. Well I did go to a thing on a Saturday, I think, with the cake, my neighbour dragged me, but I don't remember a jar, or a box, or any slip. I'd have remembered a slip, wouldn't I? So you're ringing from the shop, [COMPANY_A], and you want my name and the number off the slip, but you've rung me, so you've already got my number, haven't you? Which is a bit, hm. You said nothing to pay, you said that twice, and I don't know why that's what you'd lead with. So which shop is it again? And what's the prize, if it's only a small one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: You're right to say it, and I'd think less of myself if I'd rung you without expecting it. Yes, I have your number, it's on the slip, so I don't need it from you, and I'll take back the bit about confirming it. You needn't tell me anything today. Uh, the shop is [COMPANY_A], in [CITY_1], and the prize is [AMOUNT_1] worth of vouchers, a small one, as I said. Now, I did say nothing to pay, and I said it twice because that is usually where people's minds go, and I'd rather it were settled early. But here's the thing. If you'd rather not take my word, don't. Ring the shop on the number you'd find yourself, ask for me by name, and ask what the stand was and when it was held. Then you'd know it was us.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hm, ring the shop myself, well, that's, I suppose that's fair enough. But sorry, going back a bit, you said before it was something about, uh, you wanted to be sure you'd got the right person, and then you said you'd take that back, so what is it you actually wanted from me today? Because I got a bit lost there. And the other thing, you said prizes get tidied away if they're not claimed, how long have I got, roughly? I'm only asking because I'm not sure I even want to go trotting off to a shop for vouchers, I don't really know the, where is it again, the shop?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that was muddled of me, and I'm sorry. What I wanted today is simply to tell you the slip was drawn and ask whether you'd like the vouchers. I don't need anything from you, no details, nothing. As for how long, uh, I don't have a date written down, and I won't invent one for you. It isn't a thing to rush over, and if you'd rather not trot off to a shop for vouchers, that's perfectly all right, just say so and I'll note it. The shop is [COMPANY_A], in the [CITY_1] high street, and if you'd like to be certain it's us, ring and ask them on a number you find yourself. Or, if it helps, I can tell you the stand had the prize jar with the entry box beside it, on [DATE_1], and a woman at the table gave out the slips, a short one with a pen on a string. Does any of that ring a bell? And if it does, whenever you've had a think, you just come in and ask for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, a short woman with a pen on a string, no, I don't, and you said before it was a jar and a box and now it's, no, that's the same, never mind. But you did say a minute ago there was a deadline, sort of, prizes get tidied away, and now you're saying there's no rush, so which is it? I'm not going to trot off anywhere on the strength of a phone call, love, I'm only just awake. If I want vouchers I'll ring the shop myself, on a number I find, like you said. So, no thank you, not today. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Good, it's [PERSON_2] here, I'm a regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], the pension provider. Uh, I'm ringing because we need to confirm a few details before we can talk through a change to your plan, and, well, if you'd rather not go through any of that on the phone, just say so and ring us back on the number on your statement, that's perfectly fine by me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, yes, this is -- sorry, I've just woken up, I was having a bit of a lie down. A pension, you said? Which pension is this now, because I've got, well, I had the one from the old job, and there was another thing my brother-in-law set up... Sorry, who is it you said you were again? Pension provider, what was the name?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, take your time. It's [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], and the plan I'm looking at is the one we hold under reference [ACCOUNT_REF], which, honestly, may or may not be the one from the old job, I couldn't say without you confirming it, and I'm not going to ask you to do that while you're still half asleep. What I said a moment ago was, if you'd rather not go through anything on the phone, you can ring us back on the number printed on your statement, or I can send the same query by post instead. Either way there's no rush at all, so would you like me to do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, there's the, uh, the kettle going off in the kitchen -- no, hang on, that's the neighbour's telly through the wall, they always have it so loud in the afternoons. Sorry. What was I saying? Oh, the post, yes. So you're saying I could just ring the number on my statement? I'd have to find a statement, mind you, they're in a drawer somewhere, or possibly the one by the bed. I mean, it does sound sensible, you not wanting me to go through it all half asleep. Um, but what is it you actually want to change on the plan? You haven't said, have you, not properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so the change is, uh, it's the -- Sorry, go on, I didn't mean to talk over you, you were saying the drawer. No, you're right to ask, I haven't said, and I should have. It's a routine review, the plan's due for one, and before I can talk you through the options I'd need to confirm a few details with you first. But I'd rather not go any further today unless you're comfortable, so the cleanest thing is the post. I send you the same query in writing, you find your statement when you're properly awake, ring the number printed on it, and ask for me by name, [PERSON_2]. How does that sound?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, no, that sounds, that sounds all right, actually. I'd rather do it that way, I'm no good on the phone when I've just woken up, I'll say yes to anything and then regret it. So the post, and then I find the statement, wherever that's got to, and ring the number on that. Not a number you give me, the one printed on it. Right. Well, thank you for not rushing me, that's decent of you. I'll look out for the letter, then, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's it, exactly right, the number on your statement and not one from me, and ask for [PERSON_2] when you get through. Sorry, hang on, someone's just put a file down on my desk -- no, it's fine, just the post trolley. Anyway, the letter will be with you in the next few days, and there's no deadline on it, so take as long as you need. Thanks for being so sensible about it, [PERSON_1], and have a good rest of the afternoon, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, thank you, I'll, uh -- no, sorry, what I mean is, I'll keep an eye out for it, the letter. And if it doesn't come, I'll just, I mean, I'll ring the number on the statement anyway and ask about it. Yes. Good. Back to my nap, I suppose, or, well, a cup of tea first. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, do that, and if the letter hasn't turned up in a week or so, ringing the statement number and asking about it is exactly right. Oh, and one thing from earlier, you asked which plan this was, and I said the reference was [ACCOUNT_REF], but I didn't say clearly whether it's the one from the old job or the one your brother-in-law set up. I honestly can't tell from my side, so don't worry about it today. The letter will carry the reference, and whoever you speak to on the statement number can match it up. Right, enjoy the tea, and thanks again, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, I did wonder about that, the, uh -- no, what I mean is, I'll just, the letter will sort it, you said. Or whoever's on the statement number, they can, well, they'll match it up. That's fine. I'm not going to, I mean, I'll leave it at that for today. Thank you again, and, yes, tea. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, leave it there, that's sensible. Oh, and I need to correct myself on one thing, sorry. I said the letter would reach you in a few days, but it's more likely to be the end of next week, post being what it is. So don't start worrying if nothing's come by Friday, and if it hasn't turned up in ten days or so, that's when you ring the statement number and ask. Right, enjoy the tea, [PERSON_1], goodbye.
