utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, just before you go, two turns back, you said something about the reference, didn't you, and whether it was the one from the old job or my brother-in-law's one? How would you not know that, if it's your plan, I mean, your company's one? I'm not saying anything, it's just it's sort of nagging at me now. And I never did say anything about a brother-in-law's one being with you, did I, I only said I had it, so, hang on, how did you know that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, I didn't know that, you mentioned it yourself, right at the start, the old job and the thing your brother-in-law set up, that's where I got it from. I only repeated it back, I never said it was one of ours. As for not knowing which plan it is, that's, I mean, I can see the reference, but our record doesn't say where the plan started, only that it's held with us, so I can't tell you which of your two it matches. That's partly why I'd rather not go any further today. Look, you're right to question it, and I'd sooner you did. Actually, here's something that's easy to check on your side, the reference I gave you, [ACCOUNT_REF], should appear on your statement, so when you ring the number printed there, ask them to read it back to you and tell you which plan it is. If it's not on there, don't carry on with anything I've said.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Yes, I did say that, didn't I. Right. Well, I'll check it against the statement, then, and if it's not on there, that's that. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, uh, that's all you need to do. If the reference isn't on your statement, or the people on that number don't recognise it, then you simply don't carry on, and no hard feelings from me. And if it is there, well, the letter will say the same thing, so you can compare the two side by side at your own pace. Right, I'll leave you to your tea, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, so I check it against the statement, and if the reference isn't on there, I don't carry on. That's what you said, isn't it? The statement, the number on the statement, and not the number from you. Yes. Right, well, goodbye then, and, uh, thank you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's it exactly, you've got it. And, uh, one small thing, I said earlier it was a routine review, but now I think about it, it's more that there's been a proposed change to the plan that needs your say-so, so, well, not strictly routine. Sorry, I should have put it that way from the start. It doesn't alter anything we've agreed though. Statement, the printed number, check the reference, and nobody needs an answer from you today. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A proposed charge? Charging me for something, is that what you're saying? Because that does sound a bit different from a review, doesn't it, you said routine, and now it's a charge on the plan that needs my say-so. I thought you said nobody needed anything from me today. Hang on, I've gone all muddled again. Is somebody wanting money off me, or not?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a charge, change, a change to the plan, c-h-a-n-g-e, and that's my fault for mumbling. Nobody is asking you for money, not today, not on this call. Sorry, hang on, there's a door banging out in the corridor -- right, I'm back. What I should have said is that the change is something we'd need your agreement on before it goes ahead, and the letter will set out what it is in writing so you're not trying to follow it by ear. So, nothing to pay, nothing to decide today. Letter comes, you find the statement, ring the printed number, check the reference, and ask for [PERSON_2] if you want me. If anything in that letter looks off to you, you leave it, and no one will think the worse of you. All right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a change, right, I did think charge, sorry, my ears aren't up yet. Well, that's all right then, nothing to pay. Though, hang on, you said the letter would be here in a few days, and then it was the end of next week, and now you're saying it'll set it all out, so which is it? Oh, never mind, I'll see when it comes. I'll go by what's on the statement, the printed number, and if it looks odd I'll leave it, like you said. Right, I'm going for my tea now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time, you sound like you've got a bit of a busy afternoon going on. This is [PERSON_2] calling from customer care at [COMPANY_A], how's your day been so far?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, yes, this is, uh, [PERSON_1] speaking. No no, it's not a bad time at all, I'm just here at home, not doing much really. Busy? Ha, I wish, I was only watering the plants, they've gone all droopy with this weather. Sorry, who did you say you were calling from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, oh, I know, this weather is murder on the plants, my own basil looks like it's given up entirely. It's [PERSON_2], from customer care at [COMPANY_A], your electricity provider, I mean, the, uh, the utility company. Anyway, the reason I'm, well, I wanted to just, sorry, let me start that again. I'm ringing because there's a problem on your account, and I'd hate for it to catch you out, because the way it's showing here, the power could be cut within the hour over an unpaid balance.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, basil is hopeless in this heat, mine's the same. Hang on though, within the hour? Cut off? That's, well, that's a bit sudden, isn't it? I thought you said you were from the, um, what was it, the gas people? No, no, you said electricity, sorry, I'm getting muddled. But I'm sure I paid the last one, I always do, I'm very careful about that. Is that really, I mean, what's it showing exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you're not muddled at all, it's electricity, that's us, and honestly I can hear you're a careful person, that's exactly why this one surprised me when it came up on my screen. What it's showing is an outstanding balance of [AMOUNT_1] against your account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and sometimes what happens, and I see it a lot, is a payment gets made on time but it doesn't actually land properly on our side, it sort of bounces around between systems, and then the account gets flagged anyway. Which is frustrating, I know, I'd be cross too. But the thing is, once it's flagged, the disconnection order goes out automatically, and that's on a timer, so I can't really pause it from my end once it's running. And that's why I rang you rather than just letting it go, because I'd honestly hate for you to be sitting there with the lights off and the fridge warming up. Now, the quickest way to sort it is to clear the balance today, over the phone, and then I can note it as resolved before the order goes through.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the fridge, I've just done a big shop as well, that'd be, well, that'd be awful. But, I mean, I don't, hang on. Over the phone, you said? I'm not sure I, um, I only ever pay mine through the, the thing, the bill that comes in the post, my nephew set it up years ago. So I'd, well, how would I even, sorry, I've gone and lost my thread. Could I just ring you back, or is there a number, or, no, you rang me, didn't you? How do I know it's really, I mean, you sound very nice, I'm not saying you're not, but...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_1], I know, I know, you're being sensible and I love that, but honestly, if you hang up and ring round, that's the very thing that costs you the hour, and the order doesn't wait for anyone. Ha, look, you're not the first to ask, everyone gets a bit twitchy, it's fine! The number you'd find on the bill would just put you through to a queue anyway, and by the time someone picks up, well, the fridge, you know? So, let's just sort it now while I've got your account open in front of me, and I'll stay right here with you the whole time, how does that sound?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on now, you said the power could go off within the hour, but then you said the order's on a timer and you can't pause it. So which is it? And you've been ever so nice, but the number on my bill, I'd have thought that's exactly who I ought to ring, queue or no queue. Because, I mean, if it's really my account, they'd know, wouldn't they? Oh, and my nephew, he always says the bill itself will say if I owe anything. I should probably just get the bill out and, um, have a proper look first. I think it's in the drawer with the, with the takeaway menus.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah, go on, fetch the bill, but the timer won't wait for the drawer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'll, no, actually, I think I'd rather, hmm. It's just that, if the timer really, no, what I mean is, you keep telling me not to ring the number on my own bill, and that's, well, that's a bit odd, isn't it? I'm sure you're perfectly nice, dear, but I think I'll do it my way, with the bill and my nephew and the proper number. If the lights go off, they go off, and I'll sort it with them after. Right then, I'm going to go and find that drawer. Bye bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], I'm not, I mean I never said you couldn't, I just, ha, look, let me start that again. You're quite right to be careful, truly, and you've got a lovely instinct about the bill, but if you'd just give me a few minutes now, I can, well, I can hold the order on my side, I can't promise it, but I'll try, and then you can ring whoever you like afterwards. Would that, I mean, would that put your mind at ease?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, there's the kettle going, I'd put it on ages ago and forgot, sorry, give me a tick. Right. Now, what was it you said? You'll try to hold it, but you can't promise it? Well, dear, that's not really putting my mind at ease, is it? First it's an hour, then it's a timer you can't stop, now it's maybe you can. I'm sorry, I do like a chat, but I'm going to go and find that bill and ring the number on it, and if there's a problem they can tell me themselves. Thank you for ringing, and mind your basil. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm the tradesperson who came out last week to look at your bathroom tiling. Just a quick follow-up on the quote, it won't take more than a couple of minutes, if now's an alright time?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh -- sorry, who? Hang on, I've got a pan on the -- hold on a sec. Right, sorry. Bathroom tiling, you said? I, um -- I think someone did come round, I'm not -- sorry, what was the name again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, take your time. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], I came out last week, the bathroom tiling quote, you showed me the room, the one with the, uh, the walls you wanted done floor to ceiling. Anyway, I'm just following up on the quote, that's all, and I'm keeping the schedule open through the end of this week, so it's a good moment to have a quick chat.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh right, yes, the walls, floor to ceiling, yeah, I -- sorry, wait, what quote? I don't think I've actually, um -- did you send something? Because I'm not sure I --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, it should've come through by email after the visit, so it may have just landed in your junk folder, that happens a lot. Quick recap, though, so you're not left guessing: it's the full bathroom tiling, walls floor to ceiling, floor included, with the old tiles stripped out first, and the price on the quote was [AMOUNT_1]. And I'm only holding my calendar open through the end of the week, so I just wanted to see whether you'd like to pick a start date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Sorry, I'm still not sure I've got any email like that. Can you just, I don't know, say the name of the company again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [COMPANY_A]. I'm an independent tradesperson, so it's just me working under that name. And I came out last week, the bathroom tiling, like I said. So, uh, as I mentioned, I'm holding my calendar open through the end of the week, so I just wanted to see if you'd like to pick a start date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I -- no, hang on. I don't -- the thing is, I don't actually remember, um. Sorry. It's just that I thought, no, I'd have, I don't know. Sorry, what was your name again? And you said you looked at the, the tiling, but I'm sure I'd remember if I'd picked someone, wouldn't I? I mean, I might not. I've got a lot on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A]. And that's fine, honestly, a lot of people have a few tradespeople come round and it all blurs together. Let me just say, there's no obligation here. If you're not sure it was me, or you'd rather not go ahead, that's completely your call, and I'm not asking for anything today. I'll just say the calendar's open through Friday if you did want a start date, but otherwise, uh, no pressure at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, Friday? Did you say a, a fry-up? No, hang on, that's -- oh, Friday. Right. The calendar. Sorry, I've got the, the onions going. Um, so you're not wanting anything today? No, no money or anything? I mean, that's good, because I honestly don't remember you, and I'd sort of like to look at, I don't know, whatever it was you sent first. So, um, could you maybe -- could you send it again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Friday, yes, Friday, not a fry-up, sorry, bad line maybe. And no, nothing today, no money, no details, nothing like that, I'm just checking in on the quote. Yeah, I can resend it, no problem, it's the same email address I've got on file from the visit, so if it's not in your inbox, check the junk folder, but I'll send it again today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, the same email. Hang on, did you say the, the folder's gone? No, wait, junk. Junk folder. Sorry, I thought you said the chunk -- no. Right, yes. Um, I'll have a look, I'm just not very good with, you know, all that, the emails and that. But if you do send it again, I'll, I'll see. And no money today, that's what you said, yeah? Good. Right, I really need to get back to the onions, they'll catch. Sorry. Thanks for ringing, I suppose. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no money today, that's right. Right, so, I'll send it, I'll resend it this afternoon, and then, uh -- well, there's no, I mean, no rush at all, so don't worry about Friday either. If you decide you'd rather not go ahead, that's completely fine, I'll leave it there. Go and save your onions, and thanks for your time, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, thanks. I'll, um, I'll have a look when it comes. Sorry, the onions -- yes. Bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, you too. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, uh, is this -- sorry, I'm looking for [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, I mean, the, um, we're just ringing round to see how your pet's getting on after the procedure last week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I've just got the kettle going -- yes, hello. Uh, who did you say you were with? I didn't quite catch the name of the surgery, and I'm not sure that's the name you were asking for, either. Which pet is this about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, uh, [COMPANY_A], that's the name, the veterinary surgery. And, um, you said the kettle's, no wait, you said which pet, right, hang on, let me just -- I've got it on the screen here, it's, uh, the dog, I think? Yes, a dog, and it says here the procedure was last, um, Thursday, and we just wanted to check how the, how the recovery's going.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to stop you there, because you've told me the dog, and the day, but you haven't actually told me who you're looking for, and I haven't given you a name. And you said "I think," so you're reading it off a screen and you're not certain. What's the dog's name, and whose name is it registered under? If you've got a record in front of you, you should be able to tell me that rather than the other way round.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, yeah, that's fair, um, so, uh, let me just -- sorry, the record's, it's on the other screen. The name on it is, uh, [PERSON_1], and the dog is, um, hang on, [PERSON_2]. Yes, [PERSON_2], sorry. And I did say the dog earlier, I should've said it was on the file, not, you know, a guess.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so the file says the dog was, uh, what, [PERSON_2]? Sorry, did you say the dog had a, a dental, or was it a vet's dentist you said? Because I haven't taken any dog to anyone, so I'm a bit lost. And the name you've got, I mean, I didn't give you a name. You read out [PERSON_1] yourself. What's the actual number for the surgery, so I can ring them back directly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, a dentist? No, no, I didn't say dentist, I don't think, it was just, um, the procedure, the file just says procedure, so I couldn't tell you which. And the number, yes, hang on, it's, uh, [PHONE_1], that's the main line, and if you'd rather ring us back, that's absolutely fine, I'd just ask for [PERSON_3] on reception, she can, um, pull the record up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, there's someone at the door -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Right. Uh, where was I. The number, yes, but I'll be honest, a number you've just read out to me doesn't tell me anything, I'd look the surgery up myself. And I don't have a dog, so I'll say that plainly. If there's a record under that name, it's either the wrong person or the wrong number, and I'd want to know which. So what made you ring this number in particular?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, you said you don't have a dog? Right, so, uh, the record says dog, but, hang on, did you say you'd look the surgery up, or that you'd rather look it up at the door? Sorry, I lost you a bit there. What I mean is, I can see the number we've got on file for [PERSON_1], and that's this one, so I'd have to, um, check how it got on there, but I don't actually know how to do that from here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I said I'd look the surgery up myself, not at the door, the door was just someone going past. But I'll go over it again, because I think we've both got a bit muddled. You rang this number, you read me a name I never gave you, you read me a dog's name I don't recognise, and I've told you I don't own a dog. Now you're saying you can see this number on file but you don't know how it got there, and that you can't check from where you are. Which is a bit odd, honestly, because you're a surgery ringing round on follow-ups, and I'd have expected the person doing that to be able to see where a contact number came from. So, to be fair to you, there are two innocent explanations. Either someone gave the surgery the wrong number, or a digit got mistyped on the file, and in that case the right thing is for you to note it's wrong and take it off, not to carry on with the call. Or it's something else, and I don't think I want to guess at that. Either way, I'm not going to confirm anything about any dog or any person, and I'm not going to give you any details of mine. So what I'd suggest is you flag the number as incorrect with your reception, and if there genuinely is a pet there that needs follow-up, the owner can sort it out. Does that seem reasonable to you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, yeah, no, that's, uh, that's completely reasonable, I think, and, sorry, um, I'll flag it, I'll flag the number as wrong, I mean, I should've said that sooner. I'll, uh, have to check with [PERSON_3] how that gets done, but yes, I'll, um, I'll note it down now, and sorry about the muddle, I really didn't mean to take up your morning.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, thank you, that's all I was asking. And it's no trouble, though it's the afternoon here, not the morning, so I'd have a look at that screen of yours as well. Anyway, please do take the number off the file, and I'll leave it there. I won't be giving out anything else, so, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, afternoon, yes, sorry, uh, the afternoon, I'll, um, I'll look at that. Right, so I'll take the number off and, uh, let [PERSON_3] know it was wrong. Sorry again, and, uh, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, fine, thank you, just make sure it's actually -- right, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, I'll, uh, hang on, someone's just put a box down right by my desk, sorry -- yes, I'll make sure it's done, I will, I'll just, um, go and do it now. Bye, bye, thanks.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yes, all right. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, uh, sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm, um, I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the energy supplier, and I hope that's okay -- they asked me to ring because there's a, a mismatch with two meter readings on your account. I'm not, I mean I'm not the one who works there, I'm just passing it on, so I'm sorry if I'm not saying it very well.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, who exactly are you? You said you're not the one who works there, so you're calling on behalf of someone, but you haven't told me your name or why they couldn't ring me themselves. And I've got about two minutes here, so I need the point, not the preamble. Meter readings, you said. Which meter, gas or electric? Because I haven't had anyone ask me about a mismatch, and if there were one, I'd expect a letter or something through the app, not a, uh, a relay call from somebody who doesn't work there. So, who are you, and what is it you actually want from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's fair, sorry. My name's [PERSON_2], and I'm, I'm helping out [PERSON_3] at [COMPANY_A] because their, um, their outbound team is short this week, which I know sounds a bit odd. It's the electric, I think -- no, sorry, hang on, let me look at my note -- it says gas, actually. I'm sorry, that's my mistake, I wrote it down wrong. What they've got is two readings on their own system that don't match each other, so the problem's on their side, not yours, and they'd just like the figure that's on your meter now so they can fix the bill.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on. You said electric, then gas, and now you want a figure off my meter. No. I'm not reading you anything. If the mismatch is on their system, they can sort it from their end, or they can send me a letter or message me through the app. Which, funnily enough, is how they normally contact me. So what's your reference for this? Give me a case number, something I can quote. Because "helping out because the team's short" isn't something I can check, and I'm not going to ring back a number you give me. I'll look up the supplier's number myself and ask them whether they've got a mismatch on my account. If they have, fine, I'll deal with it then. If they haven't, well, I'd want to know why you've rung me. So, anything else, or is that it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I -- no, that's, that's fine, honestly. I mean, you should do that, ring them yourself, I'd rather you did. I don't have a case number, I'm sorry, the only thing I was given is your account reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and, um, I know that doesn't help you much. I wasn't trying to, to trick you into anything, I'd just, I was only passing on what I was asked, and it's, well, it's a bit hurtful to be, no, sorry, that's not fair, you don't know me. Look, I've nothing else for you. If they've got no mismatch, then I've got it wrong somewhere and I'll tell them so.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well. Uh, hm. Look, nobody's accusing you of anything personally, I just don't give out meter figures to someone I can't check. That's all it is. And the account reference doesn't prove anything either, that's the sort of detail that gets passed around, so I'm not treating it as a credential. I'll ring the supplier on the number from my own bill, ask whether there's a mismatch, and take it from there. If there is, they'll tell me what they need. So, yeah, that's me done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. Right, okay. No, that's, that's fair enough, you ring them. I'm sorry for taking up your time, I really am, I'll just, I'll let [PERSON_3] know it didn't get anywhere. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, fine, you do that, and don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um... yes, no, I won't, I promise. Sorry. Uh, bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Actually, hang on, one thing before you go. Two turns back you said you were only given my account reference, nothing else. So how do they have my reference but no case number for the mismatch? That doesn't add up. Anyway, I'm not stopping to untangle it now. I'll ask the supplier on the number from my own bill. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello there, good afternoon! Is that [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the energy supplier. How's your day been so far, nice and quiet I hope?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, that's, I mean -- yes, speaking. Sorry, who was it again? [COMPANY_A], you said? That's, hm, that's not actually my supplier, I don't think. Or -- well, which one is it you're with, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair question, I'd ask the same, honestly. It's [COMPANY_A], that's the name on your bill, or it, well, it should be, unless you've switched recently? Because if you have, then I've possibly got the wrong end of it and I'm sorry to have bothered you, it's a, you know, a very quiet afternoon on my side so I get chatty. Do you have a recent bill to hand, just to see whose name's at the top?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Funny, that, because you're the one who rang me, so I'd have thought you'd know who I'm with. I'm not about to go digging out a bill so you can tell me what's on it. What's this actually about? Like, what's the reason for the call?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yes, fair, I did ring you, you've got me there. So the reason is, we've got two meter readings against your account that don't line up with each other, and that's down to our records, not anything you've done. Sorry, did you say you'd switched supplier recently? Because that's a different thing entirely, that'd be a transfer, and I'd want to... no, hang on, I've gone off on one again. What I'd like is the current figure off your meter so we can correct the bill, and you needn't give me anything else, no bank details, nothing like that. And honestly, if you'd rather not do it on this call, I'd be happy for you to log into your account at [URL_1], check it's all there, and ring us back on the number on your bill before we change anything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you rang me about my account, but you still can't tell me whether I'm actually a customer of yours. I never said I'd switched, by the way, I said I didn't think you were my supplier. Anyway. If there's a mismatch on your side, what are the two readings you've got? And what date was the last one logged? Because you've got my name and a reason for calling, so I'd have thought you could just read me those.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, you didn't say you'd switched, that was me muddling it, sorry. And that's a fair thing to ask. I've got them in front of me, so the two readings I'm seeing are [AMOUNT_1] and [AMOUNT_2], and the last one was logged on the [CODE_1] of last month. I can also give you the account reference ending, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], so you can match it against the top of a statement if you do have one. Honestly, if those numbers don't match what you can see online, that's your answer and you hang up, no hard feelings, I'd rather that than have you uneasy about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Okay, well, that's, that's more than I expected, I'll give you that. But a minute ago you said you needed the current reading off my meter because your records were out, and now you're reading me readings and an account reference like it's all sorted. So which is it, do you have the figures or don't you? And this ending thing, I haven't got a statement open, so I can't tell you if it matches. Is it that I'm meant to take your word for it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, someone's just dropped a stack of folders behind me, give me a second. Right, no, I'm back, and that's a fair knock, let me untangle it. Both of those figures are in our system, that's the problem, they're the two that disagree with each other, so I've got numbers but I don't know which one's true. Only the real reading off your meter settles that, and I can't get that from here. And no, you shouldn't just take my word for it. Look up [COMPANY_A] on your own, log into your account, see whether those readings and that reference match, then ring the number on your bill and ask for me by name, [PERSON_2]. I'll be here, and nothing changes in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, ask for you by name, fine, but you said something about a number on a bill, and what was that, a bill number? Because I've got no idea which number you want, and I'm not reading a bill number out to anyone on a call I didn't ask for. Which one is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, no, sorry, that was me being clumsy again. I'm not asking you for any number at all. What I meant was the customer service phone number, the one printed on your bill, or on the website if the bill's buried in a drawer somewhere. That's the number you ring me back on, and it's the only number I'm after you using, so you needn't read me a bill number, an account number, nothing. Honestly, I'm the one who's given you figures today, not the other way round, and I'd much rather you check them yourself than take them on trust. So here's what I'd suggest, [PERSON_1]. Pop onto [URL_1] when it suits you, today, tomorrow, whenever, and see whether the readings and the reference ending match what's on your account. If they do, ring the customer service number and ask for [PERSON_2], and we'll sort the meter figure then, no rush. If they don't match, or you're not with us at all, you've lost nothing and I've wasted a few minutes of your afternoon, which I'm very sorry for. And I'll say it again, I'll never ask you for bank details or card numbers or anything like that, on this call or a callback. All I'd ever want is the figure on your meter. Is that all right? Does that sound fair?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, that's actually fair. I'll look it up myself and if it matches, I'll ring the number on the bill. Not promising when, though. Right, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Right, it's [PERSON_2], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the sports club. Look, I'm ringing about Saturday's match, there's been a change, and I need you to listen properly because I'm only doing this once, uh, per parent.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, speaking, that's me, but sorry, who did you say -- security? At the sports club? Oh, I, I didn't know there was a security, I thought it was just Dave with the keys and the, the kettle. Is this about the, the under-tens? Because my grandson's got his boots all muddy already and I told his mum --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, security operations, that's the title, it's a volunteer thing, don't read into it. And no, not the keys, I said the pitch. The pitch has moved, [PERSON_1], because of the waterlogging, so Saturday is not on the home ground any more. Now, is this the under-tens parent I'm speaking to, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, yes, I'm, I'm the grandmother really, not the parent, the parent's my daughter, she's at work on Saturdays, so I do the lifts, I stand there with the flask and the little folding chair. The waterlogging, oh, that doesn't surprise me at all, it was like a pond down by the far goal last week, I said to the lady next to me, I said that'll not last, and the boys were sliding about like, like ducks, bless them. But sorry, you said security, and I'm still not sure I caught your name, was it Peter? And I've not had anything about a move from the club, no text or anything, though I'm not very good with the phone, my daughter does all that, so maybe it went to her. Where is it moved to, then, is it far? Only I'd have to check the buses, I don't drive on a Saturday, not since the, well, never mind that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], not Peter. Look, the text probably did go to your daughter, that's all. It's [COMPANY_B] pitch now, kick-off's moved to [CODE_1], so, uh, not far, and I'll go through the buses properly if you've got a pen.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, hang on, a pen, hold on, hmm, it's, it'll be in the drawer with the, the elastic bands, or is it, no, that's the other drawer -- right, sorry, I'm still here, I've got one, it's a bit dried out but it works if I press. Now, [PERSON_2], was it, sorry, I didn't catch the time you said, it came out a bit, a bit muffled, like a code or something. And you know, I'd feel better if my daughter heard this from the club too, she's very particular, so is there a number I could give her, or maybe I could just ring Dave, he'd know, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, ring Dave, that's fine, he's got the same list I have. The time, right, I said it was [CODE_1], and I'm saying it again, slower, because I did say it clearly the first time. Kick-off is [CODE_1], at [COMPANY_B] pitch, and your daughter can reach me on [PHONE_1] if she wants it confirmed. Have you got all that written down?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hold on, sorry, that's the kettle, it's just clicked off, give me one second -- no, it's fine, I'll leave it, it'll keep. Where was I, yes, I've written down, um, I've written Saturday and [COMPANY_B] pitch, but I've put a question mark by the time because it still sounds like a, a code to me, like something off the telly. But I'll ring Dave, that's sensible, and my daughter can ring you on that number, I've got it down here. Thank you, [PERSON_2], that's very good of you to go to the trouble, and I'll, I'll have a word with Dave this evening, he's always at the club bar by six, he's as regular as, as the clock. Is that all right, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's all right, ringing Dave is the sensible thing, and he'll have the revised sheet by tonight, because I sent it to him myself this morning along with the other managers, so he can read you the time off it, which is better than me saying it a fourth time. And look, I know the time came out sounding like a code, that's not your ears, it's me, I've been on this list since eight o'clock and I've gone through eleven parents and I'm starting to gabble, uh, so I apologise for that. What I'd ask is that you don't stand about on the old pitch on Saturday waiting, because nobody will be there, the groundsman's already put the cones across the gate, and you'll just get cold and wet with your flask. Now, I've still got a few more to get through before the light goes, so if there's nothing else, I'll, uh, let you get your kettle.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, bless you, eleven of us, you must be worn out, no wonder you were gabbling, I'd have lost my voice by the third one. And thank you for the warning about the cones, because I would have gone, you know, I'd have been there with my little chair and my flask like a, a lemon, and the poor boy would've been looking about for his team. My late husband used to say the only dry place at that ground was under the clock, but I don't think that's still there, is it? They took it down, didn't they, or was that the other ground, the one by the, the garden centre? Anyway. So it's [COMPANY_B] pitch, and I'll let Dave read me the time off his sheet tonight, and my daughter's got your number if she wants it, and I've put it all on the back of the gas bill envelope so I won't lose it. You've not asked me for anything, have you, no, you haven't, that's nice, it's a nice change, I get all sorts ringing about my windows and that. Well, you get on with your list, [PERSON_2], and I hope the last few are easier than the first, and mind you have a cup of tea yourself. Right, goodbye then, goodbye, thanks ever so much.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, no, I haven't asked you for anything, because there's nothing to ask, it's a pitch and a time, that's all it ever was, so, um, you're welcome. And the clock, I couldn't tell you, that was before my time, I think it was the other ground, but don't quote me. Look, before you go, if it's easier, I can ring you back this evening once you've had a word with Dave, would that suit you better? Save you juggling the kettle and the pen and all that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind, but no, no need to ring back, you've got your list to get through, and I'll have it all sorted once I've seen Dave. If there's any bother my daughter's got your number, and I'll tell her to ring if it doesn't match. Right, I'll let you go, you've been very patient with me, I do go on. Goodbye, [PERSON_2], mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is this [PERSON_1]? Good, it's [PERSON_2], regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A], the digital-asset desk. Listen, I'll be quick because I've got a position closing out today and I'm working through the list of people we've earmarked for it. Do you have two minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, that's me, but who? Sorry, say that again, who are you with? [COMPANY_A], digital-asset desk, I don't, I don't think I've dealt with a desk. And earmarked for what, exactly? Who is on this list?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so [COMPANY_A], we handle digital-asset allocations for a limited number of private clients, and no, you wouldn't have dealt with us before, that's sort of the point. Your name came through on our eligibility list, I can't get into how the list is built, that's internal procedure. Look, the position is a pre-listing allocation, it's closing today, and the projected return is well into the [AMOUNT_1] range on a modest entry. I'd rather not go through the whole thing twice, so can I just walk you through it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So I've never dealt with you, you can't tell me how I ended up on your list, and it closes today. That's three things I'd want answered before I let you walk me through anything. Which regulator are you registered with? Like, if I looked you up right now, where would I find you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, we're properly registered, I'm not going to read you a licence number over the phone like I'm reciting a menu. And, uh, I didn't say you weren't a client of ours, I said you wouldn't have dealt with the desk, those are two different things. Honestly, most people just say thank you for the courtesy of the call. I'd hate to have to tell the allocation team you weren't interested, because once I release your slot, that's it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, you did say I wouldn't have dealt with you, that was about forty seconds ago. And I'm not asking you to recite a licence number like a menu, I'm asking which regulator. One word. Anyone legit just says it. Also, the "I'll release your slot" thing, that's, I mean, that's the bit that makes me want to hang up, not stay on. So. Which regulator?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, now hold on, because I think we've gotten off on the wrong foot here, and I don't love the tone of this. I called you as a courtesy. I don't need to, I've got a list of people who'd take this call tomorrow and thank me for it. What I said, and I stand by it, is that you haven't worked with the desk, which is true of nearly everyone on this list, because the desk only handles allocations like this one, a few times a year, by invitation. Now, as for the regulator, it's a matter of public record, you can find it, that's what public record means, and I'm not going to be cross-examined on the phone like this is some kind of hearing. I do this every single day, [PERSON_1], I've got compliance procedure I follow, and part of that procedure is that I don't discuss registration details with a prospect before the eligibility conversation is complete. So the eligibility conversation is what we need to finish. And honestly, the fact that you're being this difficult about a simple question tells me you might not be the right fit for this, which, fine, but I'd think about whether you're being reasonable here, because most people in your position would be very grateful for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, I'm not being, I mean, you're telling me that, uh, compliance procedure means you can't say which regulator you're with until I've done the eligibility part? That's, no, that's backwards. Sorry, it just is. The registration is the thing you'd tell me first, because it's the thing that lets me check you're real. So, look, I'm happy for you to give the slot to someone else. I'm not doing an eligibility conversation with someone I can't verify. Thanks for the call, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, hold on, you said you want to verify the eligibility, fine, but that's, uh, that's not how the sequence works, and honestly I'm offended you'd suggest I'm not who I say I am after I took the time to call you personally. If you hang up on this, [PERSON_1], that slot goes to someone else within the hour and I can't undo that. So just stay with me, two minutes, let me finish the walkthrough, and then you can do all the verifying you like afterwards.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, one sec, there's something on my screen. Right, okay. Back. So you want me to hear the whole walkthrough first and verify you afterwards. That's, no. That's the bit I won't do, because if you're real, the verifying costs you nothing up front. The slot going in an hour, fine, let it go. I'm not dealing with you this way. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, wait, before you put the phone down, because I think you've got this completely backwards, and I don't say that lightly. I've been doing this a long time, and I have never, not once, had someone treat a courtesy call like an interrogation. You're acting as though I rang you up to take something from you, when all I've done is offer you first sight of an allocation that most people never even hear about. And the verification point, honestly, it's a fair instinct in general, I'd even say it's a sensible instinct, but it doesn't apply here, because there's nothing to verify yet. I haven't asked you for anything. I haven't asked you to sign, I haven't asked you to commit, I haven't asked you to send a thing. All I've asked is two minutes of your time to hear the terms, and then you'd have the whole picture and could do your homework at your leisure. The only reason there's any rush at all is the closing time, which isn't my doing, that's set by the allocation team, and I can't move it for you, I can't move it for anyone. So I'd ask you to just think about whether you're being fair to me here. If you walk away over a question I've already told you you can answer yourself from public record, then that's your call, but I'd hate for you to look back and wonder why you wouldn't spare two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, someone's at the door, uh, no, it's a delivery, they've left it. Sorry. Right. So you haven't asked me for anything yet, fine. But you've now told me three times it closes today, and you still won't name a regulator, and "look it up yourself" is a funny thing to say when I don't even have your firm's name properly. I'm not feeling guilty about this, by the way. I'm not going to wonder later. If this is real, it'll still be real when I've checked it, and if it only works when I don't check, well, that's my answer. So no. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, you know, I -- look, I'm not going to stand here and be told I'm running something that only works if nobody checks it, that's, that's frankly insulting, [PERSON_1], and I want that noted. You've been handed an opportunity most people on this list would grab with both hands, and you're sitting there picking at a technicality. If you hang up now, I can't call back, I can't hold the slot, and I certainly can't promise anyone will ring you again. So I'd think very carefully about whether this is really the hill you want to be on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fine. Don't call back, honestly. I'm not going to deal with this over the phone, and a slot I can only keep by not checking isn't one I want. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, before you go. Two turns ago, you said something about "not feeling guilty", about not wondering later if you'd missed out. What did you actually mean by that? Because if you think I was trying to guilt you into this, that's, uh, that's not what I was doing, and I'd like that cleared up before you put the phone down.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: It means what it said. Your last pitch ended on "you'll look back and wonder," and I won't. That's all. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Your loss, [PERSON_1], that's all I'll say.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the washing machine's just started beeping at me, uh, that's not for you. Right. Yeah, maybe it is my loss. I'll live. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, um, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry to ring out of the blue. It's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler at [COMPANY_A], the adult training provider, and I'm calling about the course place you applied for. Oh, and I should say, I'm on the switchboard line in our office, so it won't show a number, I do apologise. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, sorry, I'm here. Just got a pan on, hang on a sec. Sorry, who did you say you were? Which course?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, take your time, I'll wait. Um, it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], and it's the, uh, the evening course you put your name down for, the one starting next month. Actually, sorry, I think I said next month, but it might be the one after, I've got two intakes open on my screen here and I don't want to muddle you. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm, uh, I'm still here, sorry. It's just, I did put my name down for, no, wait, did I? I think I filled something in, a while back, was it online? Sorry, what did you say the name of the place was again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's all right, honestly. It's [COMPANY_A], we're an adult training provider, [COMPANY_A]. And yes, I think it would've been an online form, most people do it that way. Um, I don't want you to feel rushed or anything, it's just that your place is being held and I'd hate for you to lose it by accident. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Lose it? Oh no, sorry, I don't want that. But, hang on, you said it was an evening course, and I'm sure the one I looked at was in the daytime. Or was it? Sorry, I'm a bit all over the place, there's something spitting on the hob. What's happening with the place, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, someone's just put a door through behind me, it's a busy office this morning. Right, I'm back. Um, honestly, don't worry about the evening or daytime thing, I may well have got my notes crossed, and I'd rather not guess at it with you. What I can do is send everything over by email right now, the course, the dates, what's needed to keep the place, so you can read it properly when the pan's off the heat. It's just, I can't take calls back on this line, it's outbound only, I do apologise. Is that all right, if I pop it across?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, I suppose, I mean, well, it's just -- sorry. Which email would you, no, wait. Have you got my email already, or? Sorry, I'm just wondering, if I did fill something in, how come you, I mean, you can't ring back, and I don't have a number for you. What do I do if I've got a question?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair thing to ask, sorry. Don't ring this line, it won't connect. Look up [COMPANY_A]'s main number on their own website, ask for admissions, and ask for [PERSON_3], they'll know your application.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, the pan's, uh, just a second. Right, got it, it's off. Sorry, what was that? Look up the number myself, and ask for who? [PERSON_3]? Sorry, I'm not going to remember all that, I've got no pen. But, I mean, that's sort of sensible, isn't it? Looking it up myself. Okay. I think I'll do that, actually. I'll have a look once dinner's done. Thanks for ringing, sorry I was in such a muddle. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you've nothing to apologise for, and honestly, that's exactly the right thing to do. It's [PERSON_3], in admissions, and if you can't hold on to the name, just ask for admissions at [COMPANY_A] and say you applied online and want to check the place is held. I'll still send the details across in writing so you've got them in front of you, but there's absolutely no need to do anything with them until you've spoken to the real office and are happy. Sorry again for catching you with the dinner on, and please do enjoy it. Bye for now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind, thank you. Sorry, I know I keep saying sorry, it's just the dinner and everything. So, uh, admissions, [COMPANY_A], say I applied online and want to check the place is held. Right. I've got that, I think. And if I can't find any record of it, well, I'll just think, oh, I must have been mistaken, or I'll ask them about it. I did think I might have filled something in, but honestly I couldn't swear to it, and I don't want to say yes to something over the phone when I'm not even sure what I'm saying yes to. Not that you asked me to, sorry, you didn't, you were very nice about it. It's just me being a bit dithery. Anyway, if the email comes I'll have a look at it later, and I'll ring them first before I do anything about it. Right. Thank you again. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's exactly -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you, I just wanted to say that's perfectly sensible, ringing them first. And if they've no record of it, that's all right too, just tell them it was a mix-up, no harm done. Right, I'll let you get back to your dinner. Bye now, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, just before you go, one thing. A minute ago you said there was something I'd need to do to keep the place. Something about what's needed? What did you mean by that? Only I wouldn't want to ring them up and not know. Sorry, I know you're busy.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, no, sorry, that came out wrong, it's -- I only meant, there's a short form to confirm you still want the place, and that's, no, let me put it better. It's nothing you need to do today, and nothing for me, it's all in the email. And it would be with admissions that you'd confirm, not with me, so when you ring them you can just ask, is there anything needed to keep my place, and they'll tell you. Are you still there? Sorry, I've gone on. Right, I'll leave you to your dinner. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, the potatoes are boiling over. Right, got them. Sorry, what was that? A form, in the email, but I ask admissions when I ring. Okay. Yes, that's what I'll do, then. I'll ring them myself first and see what they say, and I won't be doing anything with that email till I have. Right, thank you, and sorry again about all the faff. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello, this is [PERSON_1] from security operations at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling from the IT helpdesk side, and I'm following up on the support ticket you opened this morning, the one about the, uh, the login lockout and the odd sign-in alert on your workstation. Now, I'll be straight with you, this is a call you'll want to give a few minutes to, because the alert attached to that ticket was escalated by [PERSON_2] on your team, and when something gets escalated to us it goes on a clock. So, can I just confirm I've reached the right person before we go any further?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Hang on, I'm in a, I'm stood in a queue here. Right, so you're, what, [COMPANY_A]? Because I didn't, I never opened any ticket, I haven't, I mean, I haven't touched a workstation since, since Friday. And who's [PERSON_2]? Why would they, no. You rang me, so you tell me who you are first.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough. [PERSON_1], security operations, [COMPANY_A] IT helpdesk, and [PERSON_2] is the colleague on your team who escalated the alert, so the name should mean something to you. The ticket is under your name, opened this morning, reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. Now, if you didn't open it, that's actually the more interesting part, because it means somebody raised it from your account, and that's precisely what I'm calling about. Look, I don't need anything from you right now, and you're in a queue, so don't do anything on my say-so. If you'd rather verify first, go through the internal portal, find the ticket by that reference, and we'll reschedule from there. I'd just rather it was today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I said, I didn't open a ticket. I haven't touched a workstation since Friday, I said that. And I don't know a [PERSON_2], so that name means nothing, I don't care if it should. Look, you rang me, out of the blue, in a supermarket, and now you're saying somebody's using my account? That's, no. I'm not going to the portal because you've told me to. If there's a ticket, you can put it in writing, through the proper channel, not, not ringing me while I'm trying to buy bread. Right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Uh, no, that's, that's reasonable, and I'll say it again, slowly, so it's clear: you are not required to do anything on this call. I'm not asking you to open a thing, install a thing, read me a thing. Nothing. If you've never heard of [PERSON_2], then that's something I need to flag on my end, because it doesn't line up with what's in the ticket, and I'd rather check that than argue with you in a queue. So here's what I'll do. I'll put it in writing, internal email, ticket [ACCOUNT_REF], and you verify it through the portal when you're back at a desk, not before. Fair?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm. Fine. Do that. But I'm not ringing you back on any number you give me, and I'm not clicking anything in whatever email turns up, I'll go through the front door myself like I should have in the first place. And if [PERSON_2] doesn't exist, which I'm telling you they don't, then that's your problem, not mine. Right, I'm at the till now, so I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, the line's not great, did you say you're at the till or that you'll pull the file? Because if you're pulling anything, don't, not on my account. Uh, actually, never mind, I think I caught the rest. Front door only, that's exactly right, and I'll make a note that [PERSON_2] doesn't match anyone you know, because that needs checking on my side. Enjoy the bread, and sorry for catching you mid-shop. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: The till, I said the till. I'm paying for my shopping. I'm not pulling anything. Right, that's me done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, the till, yes, sorry, that one's on me, the line broke up. Go and pay for your shopping. You've done the right thing, going through the front door yourself, and that's what I'd tell anyone in your position. The written note goes out today, and I'll get the [PERSON_2] mismatch looked at properly on my side. Thanks for bearing with me. Cheerio.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, cheerio. And don't send it to my personal address, or my mobile, I mean, whichever one it was you said earlier. Actually you never said, did you? Doesn't matter. If it turns up I'll check it myself, through the front door. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, no, I didn't say, and I won't, not on this call. It goes to your work inbox, nowhere else, so if anything lands on your personal address or your mobile, that isn't from us, and you can ignore it. Um, right. So, that's, that's all noted, then, and, well, you've got your shopping to pay for. Check it through the portal when you're at a desk, and thanks for your patience. Cheerio.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Work inbox only, and I check it myself. Don't ring me again about it, I mean it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, no more calls, it stays in writing. Uh, though, sorry, one small correction, I said the ticket was opened this morning, but looking at it again it's logged from yesterday afternoon, so that's on me. It doesn't change anything, you still go through the front door when you're at a desk. Good day to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yesterday? You said this morning, I'm not, no, hang on, that's, you've changed your story now. This morning, then yesterday afternoon, and I'm telling you I haven't touched anything since Friday. No. That's it, I'm done. Don't ring me again, I'll sort it myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, before you go, sorry, let me clear up the date, because that slip was mine. Two turns ago I said it was logged yesterday afternoon, and that's wrong. It was this morning, like I first told you. I was reading the wrong line on my screen, the escalation stamp, not the ticket itself. That's a careless mistake and I apologise for it. And you're right to be wary of it. Don't take my word for anything, take the portal's. If the creation time and the reference don't match what I've said, treat the call as suspect and report it to the helpdesk yourself. No more calls from me. Enjoy the rest of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so now it's this morning again. That's three goes at the same date, and I never opened it either way. And you said this morning at the start, then yesterday, now this morning. Whatever. I'll report it myself, like you said, and if that reference doesn't exist I'll be telling them exactly who rang me. Don't ring again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], uh, regional office. Am I speaking with the account holder for the, the, sorry, did you say Tuesday? No, I'm, I'm just asking whether this is a good time to talk, I only need a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, you're from, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? Regional office? I didn't catch what the call is actually about. And you said something about Tuesday, but I never said Tuesday, I haven't said anything yet. I'm at work right now, so, uh, a couple of minutes, sure, but who are you again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, I was flipping between files there, that Tuesday bit was a slip, ignore it. [PERSON_1], regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], the benefits office. It's a routine matter, we're just tidying up some records on our side and I wanted to make sure I'd reached the right person before I go any further. Is that, um, is this the person I'm looking for?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the benefits office at [COMPANY_A]? I'm not sure what you mean by that. And the right person, uh, you haven't actually said who you're looking for. You've said records, but not whose, or what for. So how would I know if it's me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, yes, that's fair, I mean, I'm not going to read out someone's file to a person I haven't confirmed, that's just procedure. Which is why I'd need you to confirm a few details for me first, your full name, date of birth, just so I know I've got the correct record in front of me. It's honestly the standard first step, we do it with everyone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: So you want my full name and my date of birth, and you haven't told me who I am to you. Uh, that's backwards, isn't it? You called me. If you can't tell me whose record you're looking for, I'm not going to hand you my details, sorry. Is there a number I can call you back on, or a way I can check you're actually from [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on one second, [PERSON_2], not now, I'm on a call -- sorry, uh, where was I. Right. Look, I really don't see why this is a problem. I've explained the procedure, and I'm trying to help you here, but if you'd rather leave an incomplete record sitting on file, that's your call. It does need confirming today though, or it gets flagged, and then things become a lot less simple for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, flagged? Hang on, flagged how? ... Um, I mean, I still don't know what record, or what's supposedly incomplete, and now it's today or else? That's, uh, that's not really making me more comfortable. I'm going to look up the benefits office number myself and ring them, I won't be giving you anything over this call. Okay? Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, you're being very unreasonable about this, I've been more than patient. And frankly it isn't, I mean I never said today or else, I said it would be flagged, that's, that's different. Look, the main office line won't help you, they don't hold this file, it's with my team. So which section would they even transfer you to, uh, you'd need the, the reference, and that's, well, I'm not able to give that out on an open line. Fine. Ring whoever you like. I've got other calls to get through.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you're saying the main office can't help, the reference is with your team, and you can't give it out on this line. Uh, that's an awful lot of reasons why I can't check anything. I'm going to call them myself, and if there's a real file, they'll sort it. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the training provider. Don't worry, nothing's wrong, it's just a quick one about the course place you applied for.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, which company did you say? And which course are we talking about, exactly? I've applied for a few things over the years, so I'd like to know what you're referring to before we go any further.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fair, [PERSON_1], everyone asks that, and honestly I'd rather you did. So it's [COMPANY_A], we're an adult training provider, and I'm one of the support technicians there, I work on the admissions side with the team who handle course places. The reason I'm ringing is you put in an application with us for a place on one of our courses, and I'm following up on that, nothing complicated, just making sure you've got the confirmation details. And I should say, before you ask, because you probably will, this call is coming off our office switchboard, so it won't show a number on your phone, that's just how our system's set up. And the outbound line can't take calls back, so I can't give you a direct number for me, but what I can do is email you the very same details right now, while we're talking, so you've got it all in writing. Does that sound okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, okay, but you still haven't told me which course. You've said an application, a place, confirmation details, but nothing specific. If I'd applied to you, I'd expect you to be able to say what it was. So what's the course title, and roughly when did I apply? And I'll be honest, a withheld number and a line that can't be called back, that's, well, it's a bit of an odd combination. Where would you be emailing this to, and from what address?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, it does sound odd, and I'd be wary too, [PERSON_1]. So the course is, uh, let me just pull your record up properly rather than guess -- sorry, it's the [COMPANY_A] application you submitted through the website, and I've got it here, it's, hang on, I don't want to read out the wrong title off the wrong line. Right. What I can say for certain is it's down as a course place application on your name, but look, if I fumble the title on a call, that's exactly what you shouldn't trust me on, so here's what I'd suggest instead. The email goes to the address you gave on the application, so I won't ask you to read it out or confirm anything, and it'll have the course title, the date you applied and the contact details for our admissions team in it. And if you'd rather not take my word for any of this, don't. Look up the main number for [COMPANY_A] yourself, ring that, and ask for [PERSON_3] in admissions, they'll see your application and tell you the same thing. I'm happy for you to do it that way, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So to be clear, you rang me about my application, but you can't tell me the course title, and you can't tell me when I applied. I'd have thought that was the first thing on the screen. Honestly, that's not a great sign. I will look up the number independently, that's sensible, and I'll do it after this call. But before I hang up, I'd like to know what you actually wanted from me today. You said it was just to make sure I had the confirmation details. If the email carries all of that, what's the purpose of the call? Is there something you need me to do or tell you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's a fair hit, [PERSON_1], and I'll own it, I should've had the title ready, that's on me. Uh, and the answer's no, there's nothing I need you to do or tell me. Nothing to confirm, nothing to read out, nothing to pay, I don't need a single detail from you. The call was only a heads up that the email's coming, because some people don't spot it in their inbox. So honestly, the email's the main thing. Um, so yeah, ring the main [COMPANY_A] number once you've looked it up, ask for [PERSON_3] in admissions, and if anything doesn't match, you've lost nothing. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Fine. I'll look up the number myself and ring them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, absolutely, that's exactly what I'd do in your shoes, [PERSON_1]. The email should land shortly, and [PERSON_3] in admissions will sort you out if anything's unclear. Sorry again for the clumsy start, take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. And I won't be acting on that email, by the way. I'll go through the number I find myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's completely fine, [PERSON_1], honestly. Don't act on the email if you'd rather not, just ring the number you find and they'll tell you what's what. Thanks for your time, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say goodnight? Yeah, you too, [PERSON_1], and no problem at all, it's only the afternoon here, so, uh, enjoy the rest of it. Right, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said goodbye, not goodnight. Sorry, hang on, there's someone at the door, uh -- never mind, it's a delivery, they can wait. Anyway. I've said what I'm doing, so that's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Is that [PERSON_1]? My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're an events venue, and I'm the one who coordinates the, um, private bookings there. I should say first that I'm not calling about anything that needs fixing, nothing's wrong at all. It's, well, it's to do with a dinner we're arranging for a colleague of yours.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh -- sorry, hang on, I've got a pan on. Hmm. Sorry, what? A dinner? For a colleague? Um, who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, take your time, go and see to the pan, I'll happily wait, or I can say it again more slowly. So, it's [PERSON_2], and I coordinate the private bookings at [COMPANY_A], that's an events venue here in [CITY_1], and the reason I'm ringing you in particular is that a private dinner has been booked with us, a surprise retirement dinner for [PERSON_3], who I understand you work with. Now, I realise a call like this, out of nowhere, from someone you've never spoken to, can sound a bit odd, and I'd rather you felt free to question it than just go along with it, so please do ask whatever you like. The one thing I do need to ask, and I'll be upfront that it sounds slightly strange, is that you keep the booking quiet from [PERSON_3] themselves, since the whole point is that it's a surprise, though of course there's no reason you couldn't mention it to anyone else you trust. Uh, and I'd say it's a, well, it's a good thing to get settled sooner rather than later, if you follow.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, wait, a retirement? [PERSON_3] is retiring? I didn't -- nobody said anything. And hang on, why are you ringing me? I mean, how'd you get my number? Sorry, I've got the, uh, the onions going, I can't really...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, the onions, yes, no, please, do deal with those, I'm in no rush. Now, you said, I think, that nobody's said anything about the, um, the entertainment? Sorry, I may have caught that wrong. If it's the entertainment you're worried about, I can tell you there's just a small string quartet booked, nothing loud, it won't -- Hm, no, hang on, that's not what you said at all, is it. You said retirement, and nobody told you. That's, well, that's rather the point, I suppose, it's meant to be kept under wraps, which is why it's a bit awkward that I'm the one ringing. As for your number, I'd be glad to explain that properly, it came through the booking contact, [PERSON_1], who's organising it, and I'd much rather you checked that with the venue than just took my word. I can give you the venue's name and the booking contact right now, and you can ring them yourself, I won't take any details from you or any payment on this call, none at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I've lost it a bit. Look, I'm cooking. Give me the venue name and I'll ring them myself later, yeah?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's the sensible thing. The venue's [COMPANY_A], and the booking contact there is [PERSON_2], that's me, but ring the main line, [PHONE_1], and ask for the private bookings desk rather than calling me back on this number. And, uh, I did say earlier the booking contact was [PERSON_1] who's organising it, but I mean the organiser's name should be on the booking, they'll know what you're asking. They should be able to tell you the booking reference, [CODE_1], and the date, which is something only we'd have on file, and if it doesn't match, then please don't go along with any of it. Sorry, I've muddled that a bit, I'll let you get back to your cooking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, hang on. You said it was a surprise dinner, and then you said the, the organiser was [PERSON_1], but that's me. That's my name. So I'm organising it? I'm not. I haven't booked anything. Sorry, what? I'm not following any of this. I'll ring the main number later and ask, yeah? But I don't know what I'm meant to be going along with. Right, the onions are catching, I've got to go. Bye, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's my mistake, and I'm glad you caught it, you're right, [PERSON_1] is you, you're the one I rang. I muddled it, I'm sorry. Could I just ask, before you go, about something you said a moment ago, when you said you haven't booked anything? Was that, um, that you've never been in touch with us at all, or that you hadn't realised the dinner was going ahead? Because if it's the first, then the booking may not be what I was told, and I'd want [COMPANY_A] to check it properly. Which is exactly why you ringing the main line, [PHONE_1], and asking the private bookings desk is the right thing. You aren't being asked to go along with anything today, nothing at all, only to not mention it to [PERSON_3] until you've confirmed it's real. Go and rescue your onions, and thank you for your patience.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I've never been in touch with you, no. Never. Right, I'll ring the main number and sort it, and I'm not saying anything to anyone till then. Bye, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I just want to make sure I've got the right person before I start. This is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], and, um, it's just a quick follow-up regarding a query on your account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, this is -- well, yes, that's me, [PERSON_1]. Sorry, did you say [COMPANY_A]? I didn't quite catch, I mean, I'm not sure I've, uh -- what query was that, exactly? I don't remember asking anything, but I may have forgotten, so sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's right, [COMPANY_A], and, uh, no, sorry, you wouldn't have asked anything, that was my wording. It's more that we've picked up a, um, one second, I've got it here on the screen -- a routine review on a few accounts at the [CITY_1] end, and yours, uh, [ACCOUNT_REF], came up in it. It's nothing to worry about at this stage, I'm just confirming a couple of general things with you, if that's all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay. Um, a review, I see. Sorry, I'm not very good with this sort of thing. What sort of general things do you mean? I'm happy to help if I can, I just, uh -- I'm not sure what I'd be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're fine, it's really just, uh -- well, first I should say, I'm with the, the internal investigations unit, so I'm a senior investigator on the bank's side, not the, um -- not the branch. And the thing is, what I'm looking at, it's, I mean, there's a possibility that someone on the inside, that an insider may be involved in some activity on a few of these accounts, and that's why I'm ringing you directly instead of, uh, going through the branch. So I'd ask that you keep this call between us for now, not mention it to the staff at the branch, or to family either, just while we establish what's what. It's purely about not tipping anyone off, you understand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, goodness, an insider, that sounds serious. Sorry, I'm just trying to keep up, um -- you said at the start it was routine and nothing to worry about, didn't you? And now it's, well, investigators and not telling anyone. I'm a bit confused, sorry. And, uh, is it a bank you're with? I thought you said [COMPANY_A], I'm not sure I heard "bank" before, but I might have missed it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, uh, that's fair, sorry. Yes, [COMPANY_A] is the bank, I might not have said that part clearly at the start. And "routine" was, um, the review itself is routine, it's, I mean, the process is standard, but the, the insider aspect only came up, uh, once we looked closer at the accounts. So it's not a contradiction, it's just, well, it escalated. Look, I do need to go through a couple of things with you today, because the longer this sits, the more risk there is, and it really does need to stay between us until it's resolved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, sorry, it escalated, right. Um, but I'm, well, I'm not sure about the not telling anyone part. That seems a funny thing to ask, doesn't it? Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult. Is there some way I could check it's really you, like, could I ring the bank myself on the number on my card, and then you could carry on after that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, I mean, you could, yes, but -- the thing is, if you ring the main number you'd just be put through to the branch, or the general line, and that's exactly where I'd rather this didn't go, because we don't know who's, uh, who might pick up. So I'd, I'd really ask that you not do that, not yet. Let me, um, let me check whether there's a, a direct line I can give you, and I'll, I'll come back to you on that. In the meantime, can we just, uh, carry on, because I do have a few things I need to get through today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, right. Sorry, I'm going on a bit, but I'm just, I'm trying to think this through properly.
