It's only that, well, you've asked me not to tell anyone, and now not to ring the bank either, and I'm not very good with all this, but that does seem like rather a lot of not doing things, doesn't it? And you said at the very start it was nothing to worry about, and then it was investigators and insiders, and, uh, it's all gone a bit quick for me. I'm sorry, I do want to help, I really do, it's just that I think I'd feel happier ringing the number on my card, the one on the back, and speaking to them myself, and if it's all above board then that won't do any harm, will it? And if you do find a direct line, well, you could leave it with them, or, I don't know, send something in the post. So I think I'll do that, if that's all right. Sorry to have troubled you, and thank you for ringing. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with, um, [COMPANY_A], the local police force. I'm just following up on the, uh, the incident you reported last week, and I've got a few details I need to run through to complete the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... hello? Sorry, I, um -- I've just woken up, I was having a bit of a nap, so give me a second. Is that, uh, yeah, yeah that's me, I think. A claims assessor, you said? With the police? That's, hmm, that's a funny thing, because I'm not sure I reported anything last week, I mean, I might have, my memory's not what it was, and anyway the cat was sick all week so I wasn't really, um -- sorry, what was it you said the incident was?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, that's fine, take your time, sorry to wake you. Um, so the incident, hang on, let me just pull it up here -- yes, so it's logged as a, uh, a report made on, I want to say Tuesday, no, sorry, Wednesday, Wednesday of last week, about the, uh, the break-in. Or, well, attempted break-in, I think, it says here. So, um, I just need to confirm a few details to close that off, and I'd ask that you keep it to yourself for now, since the case is still open.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A break-in? Uh... well, hang on, I don't think so, I'd remember a break-in, wouldn't I? Although the back gate was open the other morning, but I thought that was the bin men, they never close it, it drives me up the wall. And, sorry, why would I keep it to myself? That's a bit odd, isn't it? I'd normally tell my sister, she'd want to know if somebody was trying to get in. And you said claims assessor, but I thought it was the police, so which is it, because I'm a bit lost.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sorry, that's -- I've muddled it, that's my fault. It's the police force, I work for them, the claims side, so I deal with the paperwork on reported incidents. And on the keeping it to yourself, I only meant, um, while the case is open, not to go sharing the particulars around, but if you want to tell your sister, that's, well, that's up to you, I suppose. Um, so, if you could just confirm your full name and your date of birth for me, I can match you up to the report.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, hang on. I'm not, um -- you rang me, didn't you? So shouldn't you already have my name, if you've got the report there in front of you? That's what I'd have thought, anyway. And I still don't, I don't actually remember reporting anything, so I'm, I'm not sure I want to be reading out my birthday to someone I can't see, you know? How would I even, is there a number I could ring the police on myself, to check it's, to check you are who you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, that's completely fair, and you're right, I should have -- sorry, go on, I didn't mean to cut across you. Yes, ring the station on the main number, [PHONE_1], and ask for [PERSON_2] in the claims office. And the reference on the original report is [CODE_1], so they can pull it up and match it to you. Or, I mean, if you'd rather, I can send a letter, or someone could come by in person, whichever you'd feel better about.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, that's, yeah, that sounds more sensible, ringing them myself, I'd feel better about that. Oh, but hang on, can I go back a bit, because you said something about keeping it to myself, and then you said I could tell my sister, and I didn't quite follow that. Which is it? Because if there's some reason I shouldn't be telling people, I'd want to know what the reason is, wouldn't I? Sorry, I'm probably being slow, I'm still half asleep.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not being slow, that was me, I, uh -- it's, so what I meant was -- no, sorry, let me start that again. I asked you to keep the details quiet because the case is still open, and that's just, it's the usual thing, it stops anything getting muddled before it's closed off. But there's no actual rule, there's no, um, no reason that means you can't tell your sister, I put that badly. Honestly, ring the station first, with the reference, and if it doesn't match up to you, then, well, then I've got the wrong person and that's all there is to it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well, okay, I suppose, if it's no rule then it's no rule, and I'll tell her, she'll be in a state about it, she gets like that, she rang the council once about a pothole and they put her on a list. But I'll tell you what, I'm going to do what you said and ring the station myself, and I'll need to find a pen first, because I'm hopeless at remembering numbers, I mean I can't even keep hold of my own half the time. Only I've just had a thought, how do I know the number you gave me is the real station number and not just some other number you've got? I'd sooner look it up myself, in the phone book or on the, what's it called, the website, if I can work out how to get on it. So I'll do that, and if there's a report in my name, they'll tell me, and if there isn't, well, then I'll know. And I'm not going to give you my birthday on this call, I hope that's all right, I'm not trying to be rude. Right then, thank you for ringing, I'll let you get on, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, you're not rude at all, that's actually the, the right thing to do, look it up yourself, don't use the one I -- yes. And if there's any trouble with it, they can, uh, they can always write to you. So, yeah, that's fine, I'll leave it there, and, um, sorry again for waking you up. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, don't worry about the nap, I'd only have slept through the afternoon and then been awake all night, so -- oh, but just, before you go, I'll find the number myself, like I said, I'll not use the one you -- right. Yes. Bye now, bye, thank you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, no, that's, yes, that's completely sensible, and I'd say the same to anyone, really, because there's all sorts of people ringing round these days pretending to be all sorts of things, so you're right to check, and, um, if the station can't find anything under your name, then it's probably me who's got the wrong end of it, or the wrong [PERSON_1], and I'll look at it again at my end. And, uh, if they do find it, well, they'll probably have a letter out to you anyway, I'd think, so you'd have something in writing as well, which is, which is better for you, honestly. So, yeah, don't, don't give it another thought, and have a good rest of the afternoon, and, um, sorry, thanks for your patience. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, well, thank you, you've been very patient yourself, I know I've gone round the houses a bit. I'll have my cup of tea and find the number myself, and I'll see what they say. Bye then, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Lovely, yes, you do that, have your tea. Um, and if they do ask, just tell them it was [PERSON_2] who rang, from the claims side, so they know who you mean. Right, I'll let you get on, then. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'll say, I'll tell them it was -- oh, sorry, I've cut across you, but I will, I'll tell them, and if they've never heard of you, well, then I'll know that too, won't I? Right. Tea. Bye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Wonderful, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the foundation, customer care side of things. How are you doing this afternoon? Oh, or is it morning where you are, I never can tell, I'm sitting here in [CITY_1] and the clocks all feel the same to me, ha.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, this is, uh -- sorry, the foundation? Which foundation, exactly? I didn't --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, sorry, I do get ahead of myself, my team always tells me I start in the middle of the story, ha. It's [COMPANY_A], the charitable foundation, we do the community programmes, the youth side, the winter outreach, all of that, and honestly I've been here going on six years now so I sometimes forget not everyone has our name on the tip of their tongue. We had that event a little while back, I won't bore you with the whole schedule, lovely evening, lots of people, a bit of a crush near the front if I'm honest, and I'm calling about something that came up from it. But first, you're not rushing off anywhere, are you? I hate catching people mid-errand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm just -- hang on, sorry, there's a thing on the screen here, give me a second. Okay. Right. So that was a lot of words and I still don't know the name, you just said it's the foundation. What's it actually called? And what event? I don't think I went to any event.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right, you're quite right, I did it again. It's [COMPANY_A], that's the name, and I know, I know, the event was a few weeks back, so it's easy for the details to blur. Anyway, I'll just say it plainly, because I'd hate to waste your afternoon. Our records show you made a verbal pledge that evening, a very generous one actually, [AMOUNT_1], and it's come round to the point where we need to honour it. A lot of the programme planning was built around that promise, so it's a bit of a delicate spot for us. I'm sure it just slipped your mind.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh -- right. So, I said I didn't go to any event, and your answer is that I pledged [AMOUNT_1] at it. Hm. Okay, so, um, what date was this event? And where? Like, the venue, the actual date. Because if there's a record of me saying something out loud in a room, somebody should know where that room was.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you do ask a fair question, I'll give you that. Honestly the specifics of the event paperwork sit with another team, and the pledge records are confidential, so I can't read the details out over the phone, that's just our policy. But I don't want you thinking I'm being cagey with you, [PERSON_1], we've had such a nice chat. And can I go back to something I said a minute ago? I told you it slipped your mind, and I meant that kindly, it happens to everyone in a busy evening. The thing is, the youth programme planning was already built around that figure, so there are real families waiting on it, and I'd hate for them to feel let down. So what I'm hoping is we can just get it sorted today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hang on. You can't tell me the date or the venue because the records are confidential. But they're my records. Apparently. And the same confidential records say I owe [AMOUNT_1]. That's a bit of a convenient policy. Also, you've said the name of the foundation about three times now and it's still just a placeholder to me, so I'm not even sure I'd know it if I heard it. So no, I'm not sorting anything out today. If this is real, send me something in writing with the date and the pledge details on it, and I'll look at it. Otherwise I think we're done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Ha, well, you're rather making it sound like I'm doing something wrong, which, honestly, is a bit hurtful. I'm only the messenger here, [PERSON_1], and I just hate the thought of those families hearing it fell through.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Look, I'm not saying you personally are doing anything wrong. I don't know you. I'm saying I've got a stranger on the phone telling me I made a promise at an event I don't remember, can't be given the date or the venue because of policy, and I'm supposed to settle it today because families are waiting. And that last part, honestly, that's the bit that bothers me most. The families waiting is a nice picture, but it isn't a reason for me to skip checking the thing is real. If anything it's a reason to check it properly. A genuine pledge is still a pledge next week. It doesn't expire because we hung up. So the answer's the same. Send it in writing, with the date and the details, and I'll read it. If it's real, that takes you five minutes and nobody gets let down. I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_1], please, don't go away thinking badly of me, we were getting on so nicely, weren't we? Ha, look, I do hear you, and I'm not trying to bounce you into anything. I mean, writing it up is a bit of a process on our end, it can take a while to go through the proper channels, and it'd be a shame to leave those families hanging in the meantime. Couldn't we just sort out the main part now, and then the paperwork can catch up with us afterwards? It really is the easier way, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Paperwork can catch up afterwards. Yeah, no. Written first, then we talk. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, now hang on, [PERSON_1], don't hang up just yet, because I think we've got our wires crossed and I'd hate that. I'm not saying you have to do anything rash, honestly, I'm only saying that these things tend to go a lot smoother when they're dealt with while they're fresh, and I know it sounds like I'm pushing, I really don't mean it that way. I get a lot of calls like this, and most people, once we've had a proper chat, they say oh yes, now it's coming back to me, it was that lovely evening, and we sort it out in a couple of minutes and everyone's happy. And I did say the records are confidential, but that's not me being awkward, it's just how the foundation works, and I'm sure you can appreciate a charity having to be careful with people's information. So what if we do it this way. I could make a note on the file that you'd like something in writing, and in the meantime we could just agree the main part of it between us, and then the letter would follow, because honestly the letter is a formality, and the pledge itself is already, well, it's already made, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, no, I think we've got it the wrong way round. You said earlier you couldn't send me anything because the records were confidential. Now it's just a formality. Which is it? And I said I wouldn't know the name if I heard it, but that's not true, I've heard it plenty. It's a placeholder, it doesn't mean anything. Honestly, I don't think any of this exists. No pledge, no event I went to. Make a note on the file that I said no. I'm hanging up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_1], honestly, I think you're being a little harsh now, because I never said the letter was a formality in the sense of it not mattering, I only meant it's the sort of thing that follows once the main part is settled, and I did say the records are confidential, that's not the same as saying I can't put anything in writing, ha, it's just that the way it's done here is a bit backwards from how you'd expect, and I don't make the rules, I only work here. And the placeholder business, I honestly don't follow, I'm sure that's just a crossed line or something on your end, because [COMPANY_A] is a perfectly real foundation and we've been doing the youth programmes and the winter outreach for years, and I'd hate for you to put the phone down thinking this was some kind of trick when all I'm trying to do is help the families who are counting on that [AMOUNT_1]. I'll note on the file that you've said no, of course I will, but I do think that's a shame, because most people, once they've had a night to sleep on it, ring back and say they'd rather just honour what they said, and I'd feel awful if you ended up carrying that around. So, look, why don't I just ring you again tomorrow, once you've had a chance to think it over properly, and we can pick it up then,

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Two turns ago you said the letter was a formality and the pledge was already made. Now you're saying the letter matters, it just comes after. I'm asking which one it is, because I don't think you've actually answered that. And no, don't ring tomorrow. I've said no, so put that on the file. If there's a real letter, post it. I'm done now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, it's, uh -- look, I think you've tied me in a bit of a knot there, I probably put it badly, I do tend to talk in circles when I'm trying to be helpful. Could you just say again what it was you wanted put in writing, exactly? I'm not sure I've got the right picture of it, and I'd rather not put something on the file that's wrong, because then it only causes trouble for you later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no. I've said it three times already. Date, venue, what the pledge says, on paper. And, um, hang on, you've gone quiet. Anyway, I'm not repeating it a fourth time so you can tidy up the answer. Don't call back. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], we handle account management, and I've got something important to go over with you. Can you hear me okay? I'm getting a bit of crackle on my end, so, uh, hello? It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], just a quick matter regarding your account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi! Yeah, yeah, I can hear you fine, sorry, I've got you on speaker, I'm out in the garden, bit of a mess out here, there's soil everywhere. Um, sorry, who did you say you were again? [COMPANY_A]? I'm not sure I caught that properly. And which account is this, I've got a few things, so, uh...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no worries at all, [PERSON_1], gardening on a lovely day, I'm jealous. Yeah, it's [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A], we do account management, and honestly it's the main one on file, the one under your name, I'll pull up the exact reference in a sec. Sorry, the line's cutting out a bit on my end again, can you still hear me? Anyway, it's really just a quick thing, a couple of minutes, but it does need sorting today, so I wanted to catch you now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you, it's all good this end. Um, but hang on, "the main one on file", which one's that though? Like, what kind of account, is it the bank, or the electric, or what? Because I honestly don't recognise [COMPANY_A], sorry, and you said it needs sorting today, what's the actual problem? I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, I'd like to know what we're talking about before I, you know, go along with anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a fair question, [PERSON_1], everyone asks that, honestly. Sorry, hang on one second, somebody's just come up to my desk -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Right, so, it's the main one tied to your name, it's, uh, basically a flag that came up on the file and it's a really simple fix, two minutes tops, but it does have to be done today or it gets, you know, messier. And the line's breaking up again, can you still hear me okay? I'll pull the exact reference for you in a moment, I just want to get you sorted first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, yeah, I can still hear you, it's me that's the problem, I keep putting the phone down in the dirt. But hang on, a minute ago you said it was a quick matter regarding my account, and now it's a flag on the file that gets messier if it's not done today? That's, uh, that's not quite the same thing, is it? And you still haven't said what kind of account. I mean, I'm happy to help, I just, can you tell me what the flag actually is?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, the phone in the dirt, I've done worse, [PERSON_1], honestly. Sorry, hang on, there's a lot of noise out in the corridor, somebody's moving a trolley or something, give me a second. Right, I'm back, sorry. Look, it's the same thing, I just worded it badly, it's the account flag, that's all, it's a really small thing on the file and it's quick to clear, a couple of minutes. I don't want to bore you with the ins and outs on the phone, I can do all that once it's sorted. Does that sound okay to you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, no, sorry, that doesn't really sound okay, actually. You said it was the one under my name, and now it's just a small flag on a file, and I still don't know what account, or what company you're even with. Earlier you said you'd pull the reference up in a sec, and that was a few minutes ago and I haven't heard it. And I don't understand why you'd explain it after it's sorted rather than before, that feels a bit backwards, doesn't it? Can you just give me the reference now, and say what the flag is, and then we'll see?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, I know, [PERSON_1], everyone says that, and it's honestly nothing, I just can't get the reference to load on my end, the system's being slow. It's a two-minute thing, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but see, that's what I keep asking, I'm not being funny. What kind of account is it? And what's [COMPANY_A], I don't know them. And you still haven't said what the flag is. If the system's slow, fine, but then I'd rather you rang me back when it loads, because I'm not going to go along with anything today if I don't know what it is. Sorry, I know you said it's two minutes, I just, I'd like to know what we're actually talking about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a callback, uh, yeah, I can't really do that, [PERSON_1], I'm moving between desks today and I'm not at my own line, and honestly the signal's so patchy I'd probably lose you anyway. And look, I think I said the flag was on the file rather than the account, sorry, that's on me, it's more of a, uh, a note against the account, really. But it's the same small thing, two minutes, and it's just easier to clear it while I've got you. You're the person I need on this, [PERSON_1], so can we just get it done now and I'll send you all the detail afterwards?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, I don't think so, sorry. I mean, you seem friendly enough, and I'm not trying to be rude, but I've asked you four or five times now what the account is and what the flag is, and what I've got is, it's a flag, no, it's a note, it's two minutes, and you can't ring me back, and you'll send the detail afterwards. That's a lot of afterwards, isn't it? And honestly the whole thing's moved around a bit, first it was a quick matter, then it had to be today or it gets messier, and now it's a note against the account. If it really mattered I'd have a letter or an email or something, wouldn't I? So I'm going to leave it there. If [COMPANY_A] needs something from me, they can post it, or I'll look up a number myself and ring them. Anyway, thanks for calling, I'll go and rescue my tomatoes. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'll ring me with a number? No, no, you don't want to be hunting round for numbers, [PERSON_1], that's a waste of your afternoon, honestly. Look, I'm cutting out again, but it's really just the two minutes, and then I'll let you get back to your tomatoes. Can you just stay with me and we'll get this done? Yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said I'll look up a number myself and ring them, that's all, and it's no waste of my afternoon, honestly, I like a bit of a sit down with a cuppa anyway. And I did say I was going, didn't I? I said I'm leaving it there. So, no, I won't stay on, sorry, I'm going to go and see to my tomatoes, and if [COMPANY_A] needs me they can post something. Right, bye now, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, I hear you, [PERSON_1], and honestly, I'd, no, wait, what I mean is, it's your call, of course it is. Look, I can't ring you back and I can't give you a line to ring, that's just how it is today, but it's two minutes, and I'll be straight with you, if we do it now it's done and dusted. So, can we, can you just stay on with me for those two minutes? Go on, for me, yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Look, I, no, it's, hang on. I don't, I mean, you can't ring me back and you can't give me a number and I'm meant to just stay on because it's bigger tomorrow? That's, no. That's exactly why I'm not going to. Honestly, if it's that important, it'll keep until I've rung them myself. Right, I'm going now. Bye, [PERSON_2], take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, [PERSON_1], someone's just walked in with a, uh, no, that's fine, they've gone. Right, listen, you're not going to ring anyone and have them tell you something different, because it's only me who's got the file open, so honestly the quickest thing for everyone is two minutes now. I'd just hate for you to be sat there tomorrow with it ten times worse. Can we do that? Please?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. If I ring them and they say something different, that's rather the point. I'm going now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], we act on behalf of the private landlord for the property you're currently renting in [CITY_1]. I'm calling because there's been a, uh, a flag raised on the tenancy deposit registration associated with your address, and frankly it needs addressing today before it moves to the next stage of the process.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who exactly did you say you're calling on behalf of? I caught "private landlord" but the company name, I didn't, I didn't quite get that. And what do you mean by "the next stage of the process"? Because I haven't been told there's any process.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, it's [COMPANY_A], I'm with their verification and compliance function, we sit upstream of the managing agent, so you wouldn't have dealt with us directly. As for the process, it's essentially a reconciliation of the deposit against the scheme registration, and where there's a discrepancy in the custodial record, it escalates to a formal forfeiture review. Which, to be candid, puts your deposit at risk, uh, so I'd ask that we keep this conversation between ourselves for now, rather than raising it with the letting agent or your housemates, as it could prejudice the review.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, let me make sure I've got this straight. You're a company I've never dealt with, you sit "upstream" of an agent I do deal with, you're telling me my deposit's at risk, and you'd like me not to mention it to the agent or anyone in the house. I'm sorry, but that last part is exactly what makes me less inclined to go on with this, not more. If there's a genuine discrepancy with the deposit registration, the agent would know about it, and so would the scheme itself. So what's the name of the deposit scheme you're referring to? And what's the actual discrepancy, specifically? Not "a flag", what does the record say, and where does it differ from what it should?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, I understand the caution, and it's sensible, but the specifics of the custodial record sit within the compliance layer, so I'm not at liberty to itemise the discrepancy over an unsecured line, uh, nor to name the scheme until we've completed identity verification on your end. What I can say is the variance relates to the deposit's allocation tier versus the registered tenancy instrument, and the review window closes this afternoon. After that the forfeiture determination is, I mean, it's effectively non-reversible, so I'd really urge you to stay with me here rather than escalating it sideways to the agent, who frankly may not have sight of this at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said earlier it was a flag on the deposit registration, and now it's a variance between the allocation tier and the tenancy instrument. Those aren't the same thing. And a minute ago you said the agent wouldn't have dealt with you because you sit upstream, and now they may not have sight of it at all. Which is it? I'm also a bit stuck on this: you want me to verify my identity to you, before you'll tell me which scheme, when you rang me. Normally that's the wrong way round. So here's what I'll do. I'll look up the scheme myself, check my own deposit record through the agent, and if there's a real issue, someone can put it in writing. Can you give me a reference number and a callback number for [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, um, so, those are really the same underlying matter, it's just a question of terminology, flag at the registration level, variance at the instrument level, it's the same discrepancy viewed from two sides, if you follow. And look, I wouldn't want you routing this through the agent, because that's precisely how a review gets prejudiced, and the window is, um, it's genuinely closing. I can note a [ACCOUNT_REF] for you, but a callback line, I mean, our compliance desk isn't set up for inbound, so it really is simpler if we resolve this on this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I don't follow, I'm afraid, and I'll tell you why. Terminology doesn't turn a flag into a variance. A flag is something that's been raised, a variance is a difference between two specific records, and you've used the two words for what's supposed to be one thing, in the space of about ninety seconds. That's not the main problem, though. The main problem is the pattern, and I'll just say it plainly. You've rung me unprompted, you won't name the scheme, you won't say what the discrepancy is, you want me to stay quiet to the one party who'd actually know, there's a deadline that happens to be this afternoon, and there's no way to ring you back because the desk doesn't take inbound calls. Any one of those I could put down to a badly run office. All of them together, I can't. A reference number you're willing to read out is worth nothing to me, because I've no way of checking it against anything real. So I'm not going to continue this on the call. I'm going to contact the agent directly using the details on my tenancy agreement, and I'll log into the deposit scheme's own site, which I'll find myself, and if there's a genuine issue, it can be sent to me in writing. If the window closes before that happens, then it closes, and the scheme and the agent can explain why I was never properly

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: If you'd just let me -- no, listen, if you go to the agent now, you will have prejudiced the review, and I can't, uh, I can't be responsible for what the determination looks like after that. I mean, the window is --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you can't be what, "responsive"? I don't see how you're not responsive, you're the one who rang me. No, hang on, doesn't matter, that's not the point. You've just told me that checking with the agent, the person who actually manages my tenancy, is the thing that'll cause the problem. That's the opposite of how a genuine review works. A real one would want me to check. So I'm done with this, I'll be contacting the agent and the scheme myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, wait, I said responsible, not responsive. Look, I'm only asking you to hold off until the review closes, and once it closes, once it closes, it's final. If you ring the agent now, that is exactly what prejudices the outcome, and I can't undo that afterwards. Please, just stay on the line a moment longer and we can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, responsible, fine, I did mishear that, but it doesn't change anything, so let me be clear about where we've got to. You're now asking me to hold off contacting the agent and to stay on the line a bit longer, and that's the same request you've made three times in different words. A genuine verification process doesn't get damaged by the tenant checking it with the agent, the scheme or anyone else. It gets confirmed. The only kind of process that's harmed by me checking is one that wouldn't survive being checked. And you haven't given me one thing I can verify independently. No scheme name, no description of the discrepancy, no number I can ring back, and a deadline that conveniently expires before I could do any of that. I'm not accusing you of anything I can prove. I'm telling you what I'm going to do, which is the ordinary thing. I'll find the agent's contact details on my own paperwork, I'll find the scheme through its own website, and if there really is a problem, it'll still be a problem tomorrow and it'll arrive in writing. If the answer is that it all falls apart overnight, then it wasn't a genuine deadline. So no, I'm not staying on the line. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll note that you've declined to participate in the verification, which is your prerogative, but I would ask you to appreciate the position that leaves us in. Our remit is limited to flagging the matter and affording the tenant an opportunity to engage, and the consequence of non-engagement, uh, isn't something I can soften or defer on my side, because the determination proceeds on the record as it stands once the window lapses. I did try to be accommodating, I really did. You've got a very fixed idea of how this ought to run, and I'd only say that processes at the compliance tier don't always mirror what a tenant sees at agent level, which is partly why I asked for discretion in the first place. If you do, um, if you do contact the agent, I'd merely suggest you don't characterise this as a threat, because it isn't, it's an advisory, and what happens to the deposit afterwards is, I mean, it's a matter for the scheme, not for [COMPANY_A].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one thing before I go. Two turns back you said you'd note a [ACCOUNT_REF] for me, and then you never actually gave me one. So what is it, and which body issued it? Because if you're asking me to engage with a verification, I'd want something I could quote to the agent or the scheme, and so far you've given me nothing I can quote to anyone. And "advisory" is a new word as well. A minute ago it was a review with a closing window, now it's an advisory. I'll be passing all of that on, as it's been said. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, the reference, yes, I did say I could note one, and I will, but, I mean, it's an internal case identifier, [ACCOUNT_REF], generated at our end, so it isn't issued by a scheme or a registry, which is why you wouldn't be able to look it up anywhere external. It's simply our own working label for the matter, a sort of file locator within the compliance function, and quoting it to the agent or the scheme wouldn't, uh, wouldn't really yield anything, because it only has meaning to us. As for the advisory point, I'd gently say that's a semantic distinction. Advisory, review, determination, they're all stages of one continuous process, and I'd rather not have you take away the impression that I've contradicted myself, because the underlying position is unchanged. And look, if you do decide to pass all of this on to the agent, which I'd still caution against, but I accept it's your decision, I'd just ask that you relay it accurately, that we flagged the matter, that you declined verification, and that no threat was made, because that really isn't how this was intended, and I'd hate for there to be any, um, any misunderstanding about the nature of the call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said it's a, a "file locator", and that the reference is "issued by a scheme"? No, wait, that's the opposite of what you said. Never mind. A company I can't verify rang me unprompted, wouldn't name the scheme or the discrepancy, asked me not to speak to the agent, and gave me a deadline of this afternoon. I'm not declining verification, by the way. I'm declining to be verified by you, on this call, in this way. I'll deal with the agent and the scheme directly. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. That's your decision, I've noted it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Before I go, one thing from two turns back. You said that if I contact the agent, I shouldn't characterise this as a threat. I never said it was one, so why raise it? Either way, I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi, hello! Anyway, I'm so sorry, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm with customer care and account management, and is this [PERSON_1] I'm speaking with? Because I've got your name down here as someone we really wanted to reach about something, uh, fairly important, but I don't want to jump straight in, how are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? [COMPANY_A], that's not a name I know. And it's not morning, it's well into the afternoon, so you're not even sure where I am, are you? I've got about two minutes. What's the something fairly important?

utterances.text: Ha, no no, you're right, I know exactly where you are, it's [CITY_1], I was just, uh, talking loosely, long day, like I said! Okay, two minutes, fair enough, so here's the thing, there's a time-sensitive matter on your account, and honestly it's good news, there's a [AMOUNT_1] adjustment in your favour, but it has to be sorted today or it lapses, and I'll need to confirm a couple of details with you first. Oh, and I'm sorry, the line's a bit crackly on my side, can you hear me okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you fine. Which account? I've got a few, and you haven't said what [COMPANY_A] does or how you got my details. Behind the scenes for who? And if it's a refund, you don't need anything from me to pay it out. So what details exactly, and why today?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you're sharp, I like that, you'd be surprised how many people just go along with me. Okay, so, it's, uh, one of your main accounts, and I'd rather confirm which one together than read out the wrong reference, there's an [ACCOUNT_REF] on my screen but, hm, you're breaking up a little now, can you hear me? Anyway, the details are just a quick verification, nothing scary, and the reason it's today is that the window closes at the end of the day, which is out of my hands, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I can hear you perfectly, and that's the third time you've asked. Okay, let me just say where I am with this, because I've got about a minute left. You still haven't told me what [COMPANY_A] actually does, or who you work for, or how you got my name. You can't tell me which account, you want me to help you work out which one it is, and you're reading a reference off a screen that you won't say out loud. Then there's a deadline that's out of your hands, and a verification that's nothing scary. I've had training on exactly this kind of call, so I'm not going to sit here and give you details to confirm. If there's genuinely money owed to me, the company I actually bank with can tell me that, and I'll ring them on the number on my card, not one you give me. So that's what I'll do. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, the number on your card? Oh, no, no need to go reading me a card, I'm not asking for card details, that's not what this is at all, ha. Look, you really don't want to hang up on this one, it's only a quick -- hello? Hello, can you still hear me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, I can hear you, I haven't hung up yet. And I didn't say you wanted my card details, I said I'd ring the number printed on my card. Different thing. Look, I've had my say. You've dodged every question, so I'm done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, right, no, I know, I just -- I mean, I wasn't -- okay. Look, I'm not, uh, I don't want you to think I'm trying to, to rush you into anything, that's really not -- hm. It's only that it'd be a shame if you missed out, that's all. You do what you need to do. Take care now, and, uh, have a lovely afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. If there's really something owed, my bank will tell me, and I won't lose anything by waiting. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2], I'm, uh, I'm a regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A], and I work with your partner, well, I'm a friend of theirs, really, outside of work. Sorry to ring out of the blue, I've got a minute if you do.

utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is -- sorry, who? [PERSON_2]? I don't, hang on. A friend of my partner's, from where, exactly? And what's this about, I've only got a couple of minutes.

utterances.text: Yeah, [PERSON_2], no, that's fine, I wouldn't expect you to place me straight off. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, you're asking whether we're free, and not to tell my partner? Why are you ringing me and not them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I'm not, I mean, I did try, [PERSON_3] was the first person I -- no, look, that's fair, honestly. You don't know me from Adam, and I'd be wary too. Ring [PERSON_3] now if you like, they'll tell you who I am, and I'm not asking you for anything, no details, no money, just whether that weekend's clear, yes or no. And if you'd rather leave it there, that's completely fine, I'll just find another way to sort the date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, one sec, [PERSON_4], no, not that room, the other one -- sorry. Right. So you "did try" my partner, then, no, you said you did, and then you stopped. Which is it? Look, I'm not confirming my diary to someone I can't place, and I'm certainly not keeping it from my partner. If this is real, I'll hear about it from them. That's all I've got.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, that's, uh, that's fair, and you're right to pick me up on it, I did fumble that. What I meant was I'd spoken to [PERSON_3] first, they're the one who gave me your number, and I got tangled up saying it. But I take the point, I'm a name you can't place, I've rung you cold, and then I've asked you to keep something from your partner, which on paper sounds exactly like the sort of call you'd be wise to turn down. The secret bit is only because it's a party, there's nothing behind it, but I get that you can't know that from where you're standing. So, no, I won't push, and I'd rather you didn't feel pressured on a call you didn't expect. If you want, check with [PERSON_3] whenever suits, or just let it come out through your partner, and if it turns out I've botched the whole thing, well, that's on me. Sorry for taking up your couple of minutes, and thanks for hearing me out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, you've backed off, I'll give you that. But the story's changed twice in two minutes, so I'm not confirming anything. If [PERSON_3] really gave you my number, they can tell my partner, and that's the end of it. I'm done with this one. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I -- fair enough, that's, well, I'd probably say the same thing in your seat. I'll let [PERSON_3] know it landed badly and they can sort it with your partner, however they like. No hard feelings at all. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, fine. Though you said [PERSON_3] was the first person you tried, and then that they gave you my number, so, whatever. Just have them go through my partner. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, well, uh, I, no, that's, I did say it clumsily, I'll own that. Right, I'll leave it there, honestly. [PERSON_3] can go through your partner, and that's that. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Great, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm with the internal investigations unit, just scheduling on behalf of a senior investigator, and I need about ten minutes of your time today regarding some activity on your [ACCOUNT_REF], so if you could just confirm you've got a quiet spot to talk, that'd be wonderful.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who is this again? I didn't catch the company, [COMPANY_A], is that what you said? And what do you mean by activity on my account, which account, exactly? I mean, I haven't had any contact from you before, so, uh, which account are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], internal investigations, that's right, and I'm just the scheduling side of things, the senior investigator will walk you through the account detail himself, which is -- sorry, one second, [PERSON_3], I'll be right there, no, that's fine -- sorry about that, busy floor today. So, the main thing is, this is a sensitive matter, there may be an insider involved, so we're asking you to keep this conversation between us, not the branch, not family, nobody, just until we've wrapped up, and he's got a window open in about ten minutes, so can I put you down for that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, hold on. A moment ago you said you were with the investigations unit, and now you're only the scheduling side and the investigator will explain the account detail himself. That's not quite the same thing, is it? And you still haven't told me which account, you've just said [ACCOUNT_REF], which doesn't tell me anything. I'm also not going to agree to keep this from the branch or anyone else, that's, uh, an unusual thing to ask. If there's a genuine matter with my account, I'll call the number printed on my card and ask for the investigations team myself. Is there a reference number I can quote when I do that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I understand, and that's fair, but the thing is, [PERSON_1], it's really just a ten-minute window, the senior investigator has it open, and once it closes it's a different queue entirely, so it's really just ten minutes, and the only thing I'd ask is that it stays between us, because of the insider side of it. And calling the number on your card, I'd honestly steer you away from that, because that line routes straight through the branch, which is exactly what we're trying to avoid. So can I put you down for the window, ten minutes, quiet spot, and he'll cover the account detail himself?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I won't be putting myself down for that. You've asked me twice now to keep it quiet, and just now you've told me not to call the number on my card, which is the one thing that would actually let me check you. A genuine investigations unit wouldn't object to me verifying them. And you still haven't given me a reference number or told me which account. So I'll contact the company myself through the official number and take it from there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I hear you, and that's -- look, I'd hate for you to miss the window, so just so you've got it, it's [PHONE_1], that's the direct line, and uh, I'd really say hold off on calling the branch side until after you've spoken to him, because the ten minutes is -- hello? Are you still there? It's really just ten minutes and then it's all done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here, but I've said what I'm going to do. I'm not going to ring a number you've just given me, and I'm certainly not going to hold off on calling the official line. You've now asked me three times to avoid the one way I could verify you, and that settles it for me. I'll contact the company myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, but if you just -- no, look, what I'm saying is, the window, it's, sorry, let me put it differently, it's only ten minutes, [PERSON_1], and once it's closed there's no way to, uh, reopen the file, so if you could just hold on and -- hello? [PERSON_1]? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Look, I'm -- no. Let me put it differently. I've heard the same thing four times now, ten minutes, keep it quiet, don't call the card number, and none of it has changed. If the file really can't be reopened, then, uh, that's something the official line can tell me when I ring them. I'm done with this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], the courier service. I'm just reaching out about a delivery that's registered under this number, uh, nothing alarming, simply a routine confirmation of your details on file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who is this, exactly? You said a courier service, but, uh, who? I mean, which company? And what delivery -- I haven't, I'm not expecting anything. Which delivery are we talking about, and what details do you mean, "on file"?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, that's a fair question. It's [COMPANY_A], we handle last-mile fulfilment for a number of retailers, so the sender may well be someone you'd recognise by their own name rather than ours. The parcel's logged under reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and all I'm confirming at this stage is that the delivery address and this contact number are matched correctly in the manifest, nothing more than that. If you aren't expecting anything, that's really quite common with gifts and, uh, marketplace orders, so it needn't concern you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you don't know the sender, and I'm not expecting anything. Which retailer is it, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, so, um, that's the thing, the manifest only carries the consignor under a batch designation, [CODE_1], rather than a retailer name, it's a sort of, uh, consolidated inbound from the [CITY_1] hub, so the individual sender field isn't surfaced to me at the verification tier. What I can see is that the consignment status is currently flagged as held pending an ancillary handling reconciliation, which is, I mean, entirely routine and only a minor amount, [AMOUNT_1], but it does need to be settled before the release window lapses.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, so I'm not expecting a parcel, you can't tell me who sent it, and now there's a fee to release it? That's, uh, that's rather a lot of unknowns. What exactly is the [AMOUNT_1] for, and settled how? Because I'd want to know that before I confirm a single thing on this call.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I understand the hesitation, and I'd rather you didn't confirm anything you're uncomfortable with. The [AMOUNT_1] is an ancillary levy, essentially a customs-adjacent reconciliation on the consolidated inbound, it's applied at the batch level and then, uh, apportioned to the individual consignee, which is why the line item looks so opaque from your side. As for settling it, we do that by phone at the verification tier, it's a, a same-session disposition, because the release window on [CODE_1] closes at the end of today and after that the consignment reverts to the hub for return processing, so it really is rather time-sensitive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, let me just say this again, because I don't think I've had a straight answer. I'm not expecting a parcel. You can't tell me who sent it. And now I'm to pay [AMOUNT_1], by phone, today, for a levy you describe as "customs-adjacent." I mean, a real customs charge has a named item and a named sender, doesn't it? So, again, what is actually in the parcel, and why can't I settle this through your official website or the tracking page instead of on this call?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one moment, I've got a colleague, uh, no, it's fine, she can wait. Right, so, the contents -- the manifest doesn't itemise at the verification tier, it carries a declared-value band and a handling class, which is, I mean, precisely why the levy sits at the batch level rather than against a named article. As for the website, the portal only exposes consignments in standard-release status, whereas [CODE_1] is in an exception state, so it won't resolve there, and the tracking page would simply show you a generic hold notice, which is, well, rather why I'm calling you directly, to expedite the disposition before the window lapses.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, that's not going to work for me. A parcel I'm not expecting, from a sender you can't name, with contents you can't itemise, and a fee I have to pay by phone before the end of today? And the website can't see it because it's in an "exception state"? Every part of that is something I can't check. I'm not going to settle anything on this call. If there's a genuine consignment, it'll have a tracking number I can look up myself through the official site, and I'll deal with it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I do understand, and I'd never want you to feel rushed, but, uh, I would just flag that once the window closes on [CODE_1], the consignment reverts to the hub and the reconciliation then re-prices at a higher tier, so, I mean, the [AMOUNT_1] becomes [AMOUNT_2]. And the tracking number you mention, it's not generated for exception-state consignments until the, uh, disposition is cleared, so there'd be nothing for you to look up. If you could just stay with me for another moment, I can place the item on a brief administrative hold while we, um -- sorry, you were about to say?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I wasn't about to say anything. I said goodbye, and I meant it. Now there's a higher price if I wait, and a tracking number that doesn't exist until I've paid. That's precisely the sort of thing I won't act on. If there's a real parcel, it'll still be there when I check through the official channels. Don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, understood. I'll just note it as, um, unresolved on the manifest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Note whatever you like. I'm not paying anything, I'm not confirming anything, and I'm not staying on. I said don't call this number again, and I'll say it once more, in case that wasn't clear: don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Hey [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from the internal investigations unit over at [COMPANY_A]. Got a quick minute? It's nothing to worry about, I just need to run something by you real quick.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, who is this again? Internal investigations at what, I didn't catch the company, there's a beeper going off behind me. And "nothing to worry about", right, that's exactly what people say when it's something to worry about, isn't it? Look, I'm standing in a queue at the supermarket, I've got a basket digging into my arm, so if you want to tell me what this is actually about, go on, but make it quick. And how'd you get this number anyway?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, [PERSON_1], everyone asks that. It's [PERSON_2], internal investigations at [COMPANY_A], the bank, uh, you're a customer of ours. The number's just from your account file, that's all, nothing odd. So, look, it's about, well -- I mean, I can't really get into the whole thing in a supermarket queue, but basically we've flagged some activity on your account, [ACCOUNT_REF], and I'm a senior investigator on it. One thing I do have to ask, and it's a quick one, is that you keep this between us for now, don't mention it to the branch staff or anyone at home. We think someone on the inside might be involved, so, yeah, just us for the moment, okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, I'm not -- no. Don't tell the branch, don't tell anyone at home, that's, I mean, that's the bit that's got my back up. A proper bank doesn't ring me in a queue and ask me to keep secrets from the bank. And you can't tell me here but you want me to stay quiet, so what is it you actually want from me? Because I've been had before, I'm not doing this again. If there's a real problem on my account I'll ring the number on the back of my card and ask them, so what's the actual point of this call?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, [PERSON_1], totally get it, you're being careful and that's good. But honestly, ringing the number on the card is the one thing I'd hold off on, because if the insider's in the system, that call lands right on them, and that's the whole problem. It's really quick, ten minutes tops, and then it's sorted and you can ring whoever you like. All I need is a couple of small confirmations from you, nothing big, and I can lock the account down before anything else goes out. Can we just do that now, while it's still catchable?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. No, that's it, that's the bit. Don't ring the number on your card, that's the one thing you tell me not to do? That's backwards. That's exactly what I'd be told by someone who didn't want me checking. Real bank wouldn't mind me ringing them, they'd want me to. And no, I'm not giving you confirmations of anything, I don't know who you are. You've got a name, you've said a bank, that's it. I'm going to hang up and I'm going to ring the bank myself, on the number I already have, and if there's a problem they'll tell me. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, [PERSON_1], hang on a sec -- it's just ten minutes, that's all it is, ten minutes and it's done. I'm only trying to help you here, honestly, and the longer it sits, the harder it is to catch. Everyone gets nervous at this stage, that's totally normal. Can we just do it now, [PERSON_1]? Hello? [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, I heard you, I'm still here, I just -- right, look. Ten minutes, ten minutes, you keep saying it like that makes it better. It doesn't. I said no, and "everyone gets nervous" is just you telling me my own sense is wrong. I'm not nervous, I'm annoyed. I'm ringing the bank myself, on the number I've already got. Don't call me again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, [PERSON_1], okay, I hear you, and honestly I'm not going to argue with you, you've made your decision. But look, I'd just say, if you do ring them, uh, maybe don't make a big thing of it at the branch, because if the wrong person picks up it could, well, you know, it could make things trickier on our end. And if it's all sorted when you check, great, no harm done, I'll just note that you declined on the file. I mean, I was only ever trying to get ahead of it for you, that's all this was, but you do what feels right, I won't keep you, I know you've got your shopping to get on with. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Don't make a big thing of it at the branch. Third time you've told me to keep quiet, so no, I'll say whatever I like to whoever I like. And you can note what you want on your file, I couldn't care less. I'm ringing the bank, I'm telling them exactly what you said, and if you ring this number again I'll report it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, um, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry to trouble you, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler over at [COMPANY_A]. I'm, uh, I'm just calling about the position that closes today, and, sorry, I realise I may have rushed past something when my colleague spoke to you earlier -- could you just remind me what you understood by the "protected window" she mentioned? I want to be sure we're on the same page before I go on. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, yes I'm still here, sorry, I was just -- I had the kettle on, you know how it is. Um, this is [PERSON_1], yes. But I'm afraid I don't, I don't remember anyone ringing me earlier? A colleague of yours, you said? I'm not sure about any protected window, that doesn't ring a bell at all. Who did you say you were with again, dear?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm so sorry, that's -- it's [COMPANY_A], we're a digital-asset investment desk, and I think there's been a mix-up with the notes, that's all, nothing to worry about. The thing is, [PERSON_1], your name was flagged for a position that closes at the end of today, and, um, I'd hate for you to miss it, because it's been returning really quite well, and I only want to make sure you're protected. Are you still there? I know it's a lot to take in on the phone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm still here, it's lovely to have a chat actually, it's been a quiet day. But I'm a bit lost, dear. You said "protected window" a minute ago, right at the start, and now you're saying "protected" again, so what is it that I'm being protected from? And, um, a position, what sort of position? I thought you meant a job at first, like one closing today, but then it's something about investments, and I don't have any investments, not that I know of. I've got my pension, and the little savings account, that's all. Sorry, I'm not being difficult, I just, I like to understand things properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not being difficult at all, I'm sorry, that's my fault for not explaining it properly. So the position, it's a digital-asset position, [PERSON_1], and it's, um, it's one I've set aside for you, and it closes today, and I'd hate for you to miss it. And the protected part, that's simply, it's to protect you from missing it, from the price moving before you've had the chance to secure it. You don't need to have any investments already, that's the nice thing, it's, um, it's quite straightforward. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yes, yes I'm still with you, I was just, um, well, hang on, let me think. Hm. Mm-hm. Sorry, I'm just, it's very quiet my end, you see, there's only the clock ticking in the hall, my late husband's clock, it never did keep proper time. Where was I? Oh, yes. So you've set something aside for me, but I haven't, I mean, I never asked for it, did I? That's what I don't quite follow. Why me, dear? How did you come by my name in the first place?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's, I'm sorry, that's a fair question, and I do want to answer it properly. Your name came through on a list, [PERSON_1], that's all I can see from my end, a list of people who'd be, um, well placed for this kind of position, and it's been set aside for you, and it closes today. I know, I know I've said that a few times, it's only that I wouldn't want you to lose out, that's all, and I'm only trying to look after you. Are you still there? It sounds so peaceful with the clock.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. A list. Well, I don't know what list that'd be, dear. I don't remember signing up for anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you wouldn't have, no, you didn't sign up for anything, I'm sorry, that's, um, that's what I meant, it's not a list you'd have signed. Well, actually, I think you might have, years back, something with your pension provider, but that's, I'm not sure of the details from here. And I did say it's been set aside for you, but really the position is open to a few people, I just, I only want you to have it first. It's all perfectly ordinary, [PERSON_1], I promise. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that's, hang on, that's not the same as what you said before, is it? First it was set aside just for me, and now it's a few people, and I didn't sign anything, and now maybe I did, with my pension. I don't, I don't think I did, dear. I really don't remember signing up for anything, and I've been on my own with my papers for years, so I'd know. And you keep saying it closes today, but you haven't really said what it is I'd have to do. Or who you are, not properly. What's the name of the company again? I didn't catch it, with the clock going.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm sorry, you're right, I did say it differently, that's, um, that's my mistake, and I do apologise. It's [COMPANY_A], and what I'd need from you is only, well, a small amount to secure the position before it -- no, sorry, you were asking about the company, it's [COMPANY_A], digital-asset desk, I did say. And the only thing is, [PERSON_1], I'd ask you to keep this between us for now, just until it's secured, because if other people hear about it before it closes, the whole thing, it can be taken away from you, and I'd hate that. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Keep it between us? Well, I, hm -- no, that doesn't, I mean, why would I not tell my daughter? She always looks over my papers, she'd want to, I mean, she'd be cross if I -- no. Sorry, dear. But you've gone and said a small amount now, and secret, and it closes today, and I still don't know what the thing is, not really. And that's not how it works, is it, someone rings you up out of the blue and says don't tell anyone? I think, well, I think I'd better talk it over with her first. Or, um, perhaps I won't do it at all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, please, I'm so sorry, I put that badly, and I wouldn't want you to feel you couldn't speak to your daughter. I only meant, um, I meant for your own protection, [PERSON_1], that's all. But she, well, she's right to look over your papers, of course. Only, the position does close today, and if it's gone by the time you've spoken to her, I'd feel terrible, because I did set it aside for you. Perhaps you could, um, just let me note it down as agreed on my end, so it's held, and then you can tell her everything this evening? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, hmm. No, I'd, I'd rather not have anything noted down as agreed, dear, not when I've agreed to nothing. And, well, you've gone and said it's held for me so I can tell her this evening, but then you also said no one should hear, and I can't keep up with which it is. So, uh, no. If it's gone by this evening then I suppose it's gone, and that's all right. I'll speak to my daughter, and if it's all above board, well, it'll still be above board tomorrow, won't it? Thank you for ringing, I do like a chat, but I'm going to say goodbye now. Goodbye, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to make you uneasy, and you're quite right to want to speak to your daughter first. I won't note anything down, I wouldn't want that. Please, um, take your time, and I do hope you have a lovely evening, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Thank you, dear, yes, and you have a lovely -- oh, and one more thing, if anyone does ring again about it, I'll just, I'll tell them to speak to my daughter, shall I? Right. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the events venue, uh, sorry, bit of a long day over here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Though I'm, I mean, I'm trying to think if I've booked anything with a venue lately, because I'm sort of working through a pile of stuff here, half a screen of spreadsheets and some video I'm not really watching, so, no, nothing's coming to mind. What's this regarding, exactly? And, sorry, which venue was that again, the name kind of went past me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, you haven't booked anything, don't worry, I'm [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], and honestly I'm glad I caught you mid-spreadsheet, I know that feeling, I've got about forty tabs open myself. So, uh, the reason I'm ringing is it's actually a nice one, I'm helping arrange a private surprise retirement dinner for your colleague [PERSON_3], and your name came up as someone who'd want to be there. The only thing is, we're trying to keep it completely quiet from [PERSON_3], so I'd just ask that you don't mention it to them.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Huh. Okay. Retirement dinner for [PERSON_3]. That's, uh, news to me, I hadn't heard [PERSON_3] was retiring. Who gave you my name, exactly? And the venue name again, because you said it but it's a bit of a blur, and honestly I'd like to know who's organising this before I agree to keep anything from anyone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yeah, fair enough, that's a very reasonable thing to ask, so, um, the venue is [COMPANY_A], and the booking's under the organiser's name, which I'd rather let them tell you themselves, since it's their surprise, you know? But honestly, you don't have to take my word for it, you can ring [COMPANY_A] directly on [PHONE_1] and ask for the events desk, they'll confirm the booking exists, and I'm not asking you for any money or details or anything, it's just, uh, the keeping-it-quiet-from-[PERSON_3] bit, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you've just offered me a number to ring that you gave me, so that's not really checking anything, is it? I'd look it up myself. And I'm still stuck on the basics. You won't say who the organiser is, you won't say who gave you my name, and the one thing you do want from me is that I keep quiet. So what's the date of this dinner? And what's the actual question for me, am I being asked to confirm I'm coming, or what?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, yeah, look it up yourself, please do, don't use my number, use whatever you find for [COMPANY_A]. And the date, it's, um, [CODE_1] is the booking reference, they'll have it at the events desk. The question for you is just, are you coming, and then the keeping it quiet from [PERSON_3], that's the only secret, just from [PERSON_3], okay? Honestly it's just, are you coming, and then quiet from [PERSON_3], that's genuinely it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but you didn't give me a date. You gave me a booking reference, which isn't the same thing. And earlier you said I wasn't to mention it to anyone, and now it's just [PERSON_3] I'm hiding it from. Which is it? Because if it's only [PERSON_3], then surely the organiser, who you still won't name, can ring me themselves with the date. I'm not saying I'm out, I'm just, uh, not saying yes to a dinner with no date on it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, someone's just walked in with a trolley of glasses, one second -- yep, thanks, just over there. Sorry, where was I? Right, it's only [PERSON_3] you'd be keeping it from, I said it badly earlier, and honestly the organiser can ring you, that's no problem at all, I'll pass your number along if you're happy with that, and the date will come from them. Anyway, I think it's easier if you just ring [COMPANY_A] yourself when you've got a quiet minute, and, uh, we'll leave it there, no pressure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you'll pass my number along? Sorry, I thought you said you already had it, so what number are you actually passing, and who's it going to? And you said glasses, right, a trolley of glasses, so is this dinner there at the venue, because you've called it private but you also said you can't tell me the date. Honestly I'm still not hearing one thing I could check.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right, I tied myself in knots there, I don't need to pass anything along, scrap that. Yes, the dinner's here at [COMPANY_A], and honestly the date and the organiser are best coming from the events desk when you ring them, so look the venue up yourself and ask them. I've taken up enough of your afternoon, so I'll leave you to your spreadsheets, and thanks for hearing me out, [PERSON_1]. Take care now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, can I just go back a bit? Two turns ago you said it was easier if I just rang the venue myself, but earlier you wanted me to keep the whole thing quiet, and you never actually said what you needed from me. So what happens if I don't ring? Does anything, I mean, is there anything you actually need from me today?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is account services at [COMPANY_A], the national tax office. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Good. I'm calling because we show a refund owed to you, [AMOUNT_1], and I do need to get it processed before our close of business today, so I'll just need a few minutes of your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, I'm at my desk here. So, a refund, owed to me, and you need to process it before close of business today? Why today, exactly? And, um, which office did you say you were calling from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Account services, [COMPANY_A]. Today's the cutoff for this batch, that's just the procedure. So, the refund, it's [AMOUNT_2], if I can just confirm a few details with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, that's a different number from before, isn't it? You said [AMOUNT_1] a second ago and now it's [AMOUNT_2]. And, um, a few details, like what details? I mean, if you're the tax office, shouldn't you already have, uh, whatever you need?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, figures get updated through the day, that's normal. Look, I'm just verifying identity per procedure, [PERSON_1], date of birth and the reference number on your file, and we're against the close of business.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hm, so the figure just, what, changes through the day? That's... okay, I don't know. And you want my date of birth and a reference number, on the phone, from someone I, um, haven't actually been able to check. I mean, how do I know you're who you say you are? Wouldn't I normally get a letter or something about a refund?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, you'd normally, no, letters go out afterwards, that's, look, it's all in the procedure. I'm the account services agent, that's who I am, and this is, uh, this is a courtesy call so the refund doesn't lapse. Now, good afternoon, [PERSON_1], I do need to confirm your date of birth and the reference number on file, and we're closing today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, a courtesy call, and the letter comes afterwards. Hm. Sorry, but that's, um, that's not really answering how I check you're real. You've just said who you are again, and the amount changed, and now it's closing today again. I'm not giving out my date of birth or any reference number on an incoming call. If there's actually a refund, I'll look up the tax office myself and ring them on a number I find, not one you give me. Okay? Right. Thanks, but no, I'm going to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, hold on, [PERSON_1], hold on, just so you understand, if this lapses today it goes back into the, the unclaimed pool, and I can't, I mean there's nothing further I can do after close of business. Now, all I need is the date of birth and the reference number on your file, it takes two minutes, and we can, uh, we can get this wrapped up before the cutoff. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, uh -- yes, no, I'm just, someone's walking past with the... never mind. So, goes back in the unclaimed pool, nothing more you can do. Okay. Well, if it lapses, it lapses, and I'll sort it out with the tax office directly, on a number I look up myself. I'm not giving you my date of birth or a reference number, I said that already. So, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], I'm going to have to flag this as a declined verification, and that's, that's on your file, so, uh, it's your call, but the cutoff is today. Good afternoon, I do need your date of birth and the reference number to proceed, and we're running out of, hello? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm here, I'm just, um... so a declined verification goes on my file. Right. Okay, well, that's fine, then. I'll ring the tax office myself, on a number I find, and they can tell me what's on my file. Anyway, that's me done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Well, the cutoff's still today, [PERSON_1], so, uh, date of birth and the reference number, and we can finish this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I've said that a few times now, and you've just asked for the same two things again. I'm not giving you anything on this call. If there's a refund, the tax office can tell me about it when I ring them myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hello -- uh, yes, good, you're there. This is [PERSON_1], security operations, [COMPANY_A], regional utility maintenance. I'm ringing on behalf of one of our engineers, he's returning a missed call from this number about a fault that was reported.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hello, yes, sorry -- I'm driving, so you're on speaker and it's a bit crackly. Um, a missed call? From me? I mean, I don't, I don't think I called anyone about a fault. Sorry, who did you say you were again, [COMPANY_A]? Uh, I just, I might've missed some of that, the reception's, um, it keeps cutting out.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, [COMPANY_A], regional utility maintenance, I'm [PERSON_1] in security operations. Uh -- look, it was logged against this number as a reported fault, so either you or someone at your address rang it in. I mean, it may not have been you personally.
