If you're driving, don't worry about it now. It's, uh, a returned call, that's all, nothing urgent on your end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay. Um, well, I didn't ring anything in, so, I think maybe you've got the wrong number? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, which part, sorry? The bit about who logged it? Right, so -- the fault was reported under this number, but I can't tell you from here who actually made the report. That's on the booking, not on my screen. And I'll be straight with you, I can't give you an arrival time either, the engineer's visit depends on an earlier job finishing, so it's, uh, a rough window at best.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, an arrival time? I'm confused, nobody's coming to my house, I haven't booked anything. I mean, I might've missed something, but I really don't think so. Um, could you maybe tell me what the fault actually was, or what address it's logged against? Sorry, I just, I don't want to say the wrong thing, I'm just trying to work out if this is for me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The address I'm not going to read out over an open line, that's -- no, look, I can't confirm the address to someone who hasn't confirmed it to me, that's just policy, and, and the fault itself I don't have the detail of, I'm security operations, not the booking desk. What I do have is the reference you'd have been given when it was reported, [ACCOUNT_REF]. If you never rang anything in, you won't have one, and that's fine. Ring the published fault line, any time, and they'll check the booking and give you a firm slot, or tell you there isn't one.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, wait, if I never gave a reference, then, um -- sorry, I'm gonna cut in, but if you can't tell me the fault or the address, then I really don't think this is mine? And, and honestly that sounds fine, ringing the fault line, I mean, I can do that later when I'm not driving. Sorry, I'm just, I don't want to get into anything while I'm on the road. I think I'll just leave it there, thanks, bye, sorry again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Ring the fault line when you're parked up, that's the right thing to do. Mind how you drive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah, I'll -- sorry, I'll ring them when I'm, no, when I've pulled over properly. Um, thanks, that's, that's kind of you to say. Okay, bye then, sorry again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello there, is that [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from customer care at [COMPANY_A], your pension provider. How are you today, keeping well? Sorry, I don't think I caught the last bit, you said you were just in the middle of something? Do I have you at a bad moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I've got about two minutes, so what's this about? And I didn't say anything about being in the middle of something, I just picked up. Customer care for what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you're quite right, you didn't, that was me getting ahead of myself, I do that, it's the end of a long shift and my brain's gone ahead of my mouth. Sorry about that. So, customer care at [COMPANY_A], that's your pension provider, the people who look after your retirement plan, and I'm ringing because there's a change being looked at on your plan and before anyone discusses it with you, we're meant to confirm a few details are right on our side. Now, I know that sounds a bit alarming out of the blue, and honestly if I got a call like this I'd be wary myself, so I'm not going to ask you for anything while you're feeling unsure. If you'd rather hang up and ring us back on the number on your statement, that's absolutely fine, or I can send the same query by post or through your secure message inbox, whichever you'd like. Does that sound all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a change being *booked*? I haven't booked anything. Who's booked what on my plan? And I haven't asked for anything to be posted, so what's this about a poster, or a post, whatever you said? Just tell me what the change is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sorry, I think I've muddled you there. I said a change being looked at, not booked, and nobody's booked anything, I don't want you thinking someone's been in your plan behind your back. And the post thing, that was only an offer, I wasn't sending anything off, I just meant if you'd rather have the query in writing, then -- well, only if you want it. Honestly, what I can tell you is that it's a possible change to your plan, and I'd rather not go into specifics on a call you didn't expect until you've checked it's really us. So here's what I'd suggest, you ring [COMPANY_A] on the number printed on your statement, not one I give you, and ask for the details to be confirmed with you, and I'll hold off on everything until you're happy. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you still haven't told me what the change is. I asked what the change is. You say possible change, fine, possible change to what? My contributions, my fund, my address, what? If you can't say that much, then I'm not going to guess, and I'm not going to confirm anything either. Two minutes, remember. What's the change?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a file on my desk here -- right, sorry, I'm with you. No, that's a fair question, and you shouldn't have to guess. It's a possible change to your contribution arrangement, that's all I can say from here, and I'd rather leave the detail in writing than recite it down a phone you didn't expect to ring. You don't need to confirm anything with me, honestly. If you want to check I'm genuine, ask for the reference on your latest statement, I can tell you what [COMPANY_A] would have on file for you, like when the plan was opened, or the name of the last letter we sent you. Sorry, I know I'm rambling, it's been that sort of day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on. You're offering to tell me what you've got on file, so you're the one holding the details and I'm supposed to be impressed by that? Anyone can say when a plan was opened. That's not verification. And you've now told me nothing three times, so I'm done with this. If there's a real change to my contributions, I'll find out from the number on my statement or from a letter, not from you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, absolutely, ring the number on your statement, and I'll note on your file that you declined to go any further on this call, so nobody chases you. And please don't take my word for any of it, do ask them about --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm stopping you there. I don't need to be told what to ask them. I'll handle it from the statement number. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2] calling from the Circulation Verification and Reservations Fulfilment unit at [COMPANY_A], the public library, and I'm contacting you regarding a, uh, a reservation item that's been processed through our holds-queue workflow.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, well, hang on, I just woke up. Sorry. The library, you said? I haven't been in there since, oh, last spring, I think, and that was only for the bins -- no, the book sale. Anyway, I never reserved anything, I don't think. What sort of item is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, apologies for waking you, that's entirely on me. And just to be clear, I'm not calling about any bins, the, uh, the book sale is a separate function altogether. What I'm referencing is a title placed on hold under your borrower profile last week, which has now cleared our acquisitions-to-shelf pipeline and been flagged as ready for patron collection. I'm simply confirming, from a fulfilment standpoint, that the item has transitioned to held status at the front desk, and it'll remain there under the standard ten-day hold window.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the front desk, did you say the front desk or the front *door*? Because I've got that, uh, that sticky front door thing going on, the lock's been awkward since the cold snap. Anyway, last week, I don't think I put anything on hold. I mean, I might've been looking at something on my phone, but I wouldn't have known how to, you know, actually place it. What's the title? Because that'd settle it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Front desk, yes, the, the circulation desk just inside the main entrance at [COMPANY_A]. Nothing to do with your door, though I do hope the lock sorts itself out. And that's, uh, that's a perfectly reasonable thing to ask. The title is -- well, let me, I'm just pulling the record up here. It's [PERSON_3]'s [COMPANY_B], which I'd have in the system as the reserved volume attached to your profile, placed through the online catalogue interface last week. Now if you were browsing on your phone, that's, I mean, that's quite plausibly how the request got initiated, since the portal permits one-touch reservation submission, which is sort of easy to trigger inadvertently.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So it's that one, the [PERSON_3] one. Right. I don't, I mean I don't really remember that, but I did say I was fiddling about on the phone, so, I don't know. Sorry, one-touch, you said? So I might've just touched it by accident? I'm not very good with the phone, you see, my thumb goes everywhere. But hang on, why are you ringing me about it? I mean, a book's waiting at the desk, fine, but I thought the library just sent a text or an email or something. Why the phone call? And, sorry, who did you say you were again? I just woke up, I missed the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, [PERSON_2], that's the name, I'm with the Circulation Verification unit at [COMPANY_A]. And the phone call, well, it's a courtesy outreach on top of the, uh, the automated notification, which is normally an email, though I think what I said earlier about it being, what was it, the standard system flag, that's not quite right, it's actually a manual follow-up when a borrower hasn't opened the first notice. So there's no problem at all, I'm not asking you for anything, no details, nothing like that. If it was an accidental tap, that's completely fine, you can simply tell the desk you don't want it, and they'll release it back to the shelves.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, no details, nothing wanted, I just tell the desk if I don't want it. Okay. But, sorry, you said you're ringing because I haven't opened the first notice, and I just don't open half of what comes through, so that could be, that could well be it. Only I still don't quite follow why there's a phone call for a book, because I'd have thought if it sits there ten days and nobody comes, it just goes back on the shelf and that's that. So what actually happens, like, if I just don't go in? Is there some fee, or what? Because I'm not ringing anyone back or anything, I'd just, I'd just go in or I wouldn't, you know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No fee whatsoever, that's, uh, that's the straightforward answer. If the ten days lapse, the hold simply expires, the volume goes back into general circulation, and nothing is recorded against your profile. And you're quite right, that's really all that would happen, so there's no need to ring anyone back, and I'm not asking you to. Now, you wanted a clarification on something from a couple of turns back, I think, the, uh, the "standard system flag" remark? What I should have said plainly is that the usual route is an automated email, and we only phone manually when that first notice goes unopened, which, as you say, could well be what happened here. Does that clear it up?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, so no fee, that's good. And the, the standard system *flag*, hm, so it's a flag, like a red flag, is that what's on my profile? Because you said nothing's recorded against it, but a flag sounds like, I don't know, like I've done something. I mean, I did have a fine once, years ago, for a cookery book, I think it was, or was it a gardening one. Sorry, I'm rambling. So is that flag the thing I should be worried about, or is it just the book?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, there's nothing to be worried about, and I'm sorry, that was my jargon getting in the way. When I said flag, I just meant a marker on the book, not on you. It's, uh, it's only a marker that says this title is ready and waiting at the desk. There's no red flag on your profile, nothing's wrong with your account, and that old fine for the cookery book, or the gardening one, doesn't come into it at all. It's just the book. Just the book waiting at the front desk for ten days, and if you don't want it, you don't have to do a thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, good, just the book. Right. But hang on, going back a bit, two turns back, you said you only phone when the first notice goes unopened, and before that you said it was just the standard system, whatever it was. Those aren't quite the same thing, are they? So which one is it? Is it that the first notice didn't get opened, or is everyone just rung as a matter of course? Because I'm a bit lost, and I did just wake up, so it might be me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it's not you, it's me, I wasn't clear, and I'm sorry. Let me say it plainly: it's the first notice. We only phone by hand when the automated email goes unopened, and I'd, uh, I'd described that badly earlier. So nobody's being rung as a matter of course, it's just a courtesy call to make sure you know the book's there. And to say it once more, the book's at the front desk for ten days, there's nothing you need to do or send or tell me, and if you'd rather not have it, you simply leave it. Does that make sense now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, that makes sense. First notice, nobody opened it, so you rang. Fair enough, that's probably me. Right, so I don't have to do anything, I give you nothing, and the book's at the desk if I fancy it. Well, thank you for ringing, and sorry about the muddle, I'm still half asleep. I'll have a look at the library's own page later, or I'll just pop in and ask at the desk if I get a minute. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], I came round last week about the bathroom tiling, just, uh, following up on the quote.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, bathroom tiling? I don't, hang on. Who did you say you were with again? I think I missed the company bit.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, it's [COMPANY_A], I'm, uh, the one who came out to measure up the -- sorry, I know it was a few days ago, I came to the house on, hang on, I've got it here somewhere, on the Thursday, I think it was, and we went through the tiles for around the bath and the, uh, the floor.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but you've said Thursday, and you said last week, and now you're not sure. And, sorry, what was the company bit? I still didn't catch it, you sort of skipped over the name. Also, what's your name, I only got a bit of it at the start.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, yeah. It's [COMPANY_A], and I'm [PERSON_2], that's two syllables, uh, [PERSON_2]. And the Thursday thing, it was last week, so that's fine, I just, I got a bit muddled. Oh, and you said the tile bit, so that's the, uh, the matt grey ones, the ones for the floor? Or hang on, it was the white ones on the walls, wasn't it? Sorry, I've got the quote up on screen and I'm trying to read it and talk at the same time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, I didn't say anything about tiles, you did. I'd just asked about the bathroom thing. And now you've offered me two options, grey floor or white walls, which is a bit of a, well, a convenient way to find out which one I'd agree with. So, what's the address you came to? Just the street, I don't need the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, did you say the dress? No, hang on, the address, right. Yeah, it's the, uh, the street is, I've got it written down, it's on the job sheet, give me a sec -- no, sorry, that's the wrong sheet. Look, honestly, I wasn't trying to get you to agree to anything, I just muddled the colours. If it's easier, you could always call me back on the number for [COMPANY_A], whatever you can find for us, I don't mind at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, I might do that, actually. Look it up myself, I mean, not use any number you give me. Though you still haven't said the street, and that's the one thing you'd have on the job sheet, so, uh, I'm just sort of, you know, sitting here wondering what this is actually about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, no, that's, that's fair enough, honestly. Um, I'd rather you did, look us up yourself and ring the office, that's, that's completely fine, I won't be offended. And, uh, I'll, I'll find that street and have it ready for when you call, sorry, I know I'm being a bit useless on this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Can I go back a bit, though? Two turns ago you said I could ring the number for your company, whatever I could find for you. And that, I mean, that's sort of an odd way to put it. Whatever I can find for you, as in, you don't have the number for your own office? Or you don't want to give one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, it's, I do have it, it's [PHONE_1], that's the office line. I just didn't want to push a number at you when you're, you know, checking me out, which is fair. So yeah, look it up however you like, [COMPANY_A], and if the number you find doesn't match that one, then, uh, go with yours, honestly. I'll make sure the street's on the sheet and I'll let the office know you might ring. Okay? Sorry again for the muddle.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. So I'll look the company up myself, and if there's a quote, or a job sheet with my street on it, they can tell me. If nobody there's heard of any of this, well, that tells me something too. I'm not going to say anything more on this call, but fair play for not pushing. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you -- it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the compliance side of things, and it's just regarding Saturday's match, there's been a, uh, a change that I wanted you to hear about directly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, that's me. Saturday's match? Sorry, which one's that, I've got a few things on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, of course, no, that's perfectly fine, I did jump straight in there -- um, so, it's the under-tens fixture, the one your child's team has at home on Saturday morning, and, well, the pitch has taken on quite a lot of water this week, so, uh, it's been moved to a different pitch and the kick-off time has shifted as well. I'd just want to make sure you've got that before the weekend gets any closer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right. Well, thanks for letting me know, I suppose. Where's it moved to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, right, so, the, uh, the pitch -- yes. Sorry, you said where's it moved *to*, and I, I think I heard it as, um, where's it moved *from*, so I started to say about the waterlogged one, which is the main pitch, the one by the clubhouse, that's the one that's, well, it's quite soft at the moment. Sorry, that's not what you asked, is it. The new one is the, uh, the secondary pitch, the one at the far end, and I do have the new kick-off time here, I just, um, wanted to be sure you were the right parent before I went through all of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the far one, right, yeah, I know the one, the grass is always a bit patchy down there, I'm actually out in the garden right now, I've got you on speaker, sorry if there's a bit of, uh, clatter. Um, and well, I'm the right parent, I mean, I've only got the one lad on that team, so, uh, yeah. Sorry, wait, who did you say you were with again? Compliance, was it? That's a funny one for a kids' football thing, I thought it'd be the, you know, the coach who'd ring.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a good question, and honestly I'm glad you asked it, because it is a slightly odd title for a volunteer club and I'd rather you wondered about it out loud than just nodded along. So, [COMPANY_A], yes, I'm [PERSON_2], and I do the compliance side, which in practice means safeguarding checks, the, uh, the pitch bookings with the council, making sure the fixtures are filed properly with the league, that sort of thing. And the reason it's me and not the coach is just that when a pitch changes, the booking has to be amended, and so the notice goes through me, and I thought, well, I'd ring the parents myself rather than leave it to a group message that half of them won't see. Now, the coach does know, [PERSON_3] knows, but I wouldn't want you to take my word on any of it without, um, without being comfortable, so please, you're welcome to check however you like. And the kick-off, I do have it, but I'd rather you were happy about who I am first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, hang on, there's a bloody great slug on my lettuces, give me a second -- right, no, he can wait. Sorry, where was I. Yeah, no, that's fair enough, I'm not worried, honestly, you sound like you know what you're on about. Um, but go on then, what's the new kick-off? Because if it's earlier I'll need to sort the lad's breakfast out, he takes forever.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, it's moved to ten-thirty, the far pitch, so it's actually a bit later than usual.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ten-thirty, oh brilliant, that's better actually, means a bit of a lie-in for him, well, for me really. Right, I'll jot that down, hang on, I've got a pen somewhere in the shed -- no, never mind, I'll just remember it. Ten-thirty, far pitch. And that's all you needed to tell me, yeah? Nothing you need from me or anything?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nothing from me, that's -- well, actually, uh, one thing, if you'd just let the other parents know if you see any of them before Saturday, because I'd, um, I'd like everyone to have it before the weekend is -- sorry, I cut across you there, you were asking if there was anything else, and no, that's really all. Though, and I do mean this, if you'd rather check it with [PERSON_3] before you rely on it, that's perfectly all right, I'd honestly prefer that to you just taking my word.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sure, I'll tell the other mums and dads, no bother, I'll probably see a few of them at the shop anyway. Sorry, did you say check it with the coach, or, um, check it with the council? Because I don't have the council's number, I wouldn't know where to start with that. Is that a thing parents normally have to do?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, sorry, that was me being unclear, it's the coach, [PERSON_3], not the council. Parents never have to go near the council, that's entirely my end of things, the booking, the amendment, all of that, so please don't give it another thought. What I meant was only that if you wanted to be sure I am who I say I am, [PERSON_3] is the simplest way, because [PERSON_3] already has the new pitch and the ten-thirty kick-off, and you'll know [PERSON_3] by sight, which is a lot more reassuring than a voice on the phone, I think. You could text, or just ask at the touchline on Saturday, though I'd say text, because that's a bit late if you turned up at the wrong pitch, and I'd hate for your lad to be stood by the clubhouse in the cold with nobody there. And, um, there's no rush on any of it from my side, you don't need to get back to me, I'm only passing on what's changed, but I'd just say sooner is better than later, so you're not left wondering. Does that make sense?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah yeah, that makes sense, I'll just text the coach, I've got his number somewhere, it's in the, uh -- sorry, I've gone and cut you off, haven't I. Go on, was there something else?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're fine, I only wanted to say, uh, you mentioned a notebook, and I'd say don't worry about that, the ten-thirty is easy enough to hold in your head. Though, hmm, actually it's the coach's number you said, wasn't it, sorry, I think I caught a different word first. Yes, [PERSON_3], that's the one. Text him whenever suits, and if [PERSON_3] says it's ten-thirty on the far pitch, then that's you all squared away, and I'll leave you to your lettuces.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, yeah, the lettuces, they're not going to save themselves. Oh, and there's a blackbird just landed right by the bean poles, cheeky thing, he's eyeing up my worms -- sorry, what was I saying. Right, yeah, I'll text the coach, ten-thirty, far pitch, and I'll pass it on to the others. Thanks for ringing, that was good of you, I wouldn't have known otherwise. Bye now, bye, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the customer care side at [COMPANY_A], and, uh, how's your day going so far? Not catching you in the middle of anything, I hope, because I can always ring back if the timing's awkward.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, who -- sorry, who is this again? I mean, [COMPANY_A], what's that about? Hang on, [to the child] no, put that down, I'm on the phone -- sorry. And how'd you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, you're fine, kids will be kids, I've got two of my own so I completely get it. It's [PERSON_2], from customer care at [COMPANY_A], your brokerage, the one where you, uh, hold your investment account. And the number, it's the one you've got on file with us, so -- well, actually, I mean, it's the phone number on your account profile, nothing fancy. Look, I know a call out of the blue is a bit odd, so if you'd rather, I can -- or, you know, you can always hang up and ring us back on the number printed on your statement, that's totally fine by me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh huh. Hang on -- [to the child] I said put it down, please, not on the sofa, thank you. Sorry, sorry, where was I... right. So you're my brokerage, and you're ringing about what, exactly? Because I haven't, I mean, nothing's gone wrong that I know of, has it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, nothing's gone wrong, nothing like that, honestly, so don't worry. It's just, uh, we're a regulated firm, so every so often our compliance team runs what's called a suitability review on accounts, basically a check that what's in the account still lines up with what you told us when you opened it, your goals, your comfort with risk, that sort of thing. Yours came up in the routine batch this quarter, that's all it is. And I'm not recommending anything or selling anything, I want to be really clear on that, it's purely a box we have to tick on our side. Does that make sense, or is it a bad moment with, uh, with the little one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A review. Right. Okay, but, sorry, I'll say it again, you rang me, so why would I -- I mean, why isn't this a letter, or an email? That's how these things usually come, isn't it? And [to the child] no, I said not now, mummy's on the phone. Sorry. So what do you actually need from me? Because I'm not sure I'm, uh, I'm not going to just start reading things out to someone who rang me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's a fair question, and honestly you're right not to read anything out to me. Most of the time it is a letter, it's, uh -- well, we do send the written version, the phone call is sort of a, a courtesy first, and, I mean, if you'd rather skip the phone altogether I can just have the review questionnaire sent to you in writing and you fill it in whenever suits. Or, if you do want to carry on now, I won't ask you for anything, I'd just read back what's already in your account, the holdings and roughly what they're worth, and you can check it against your own statement while we talk. Would either of those feel better?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. The letter thing, so which is it, a courtesy call first or the letter comes as well? Because you said both. And, sorry, I don't want you reading anything out to me either, that's, I mean that's still you telling me about my account, isn't it? If it's real I'll find it myself. Just -- send it in writing. To the address you've got on file. I'll deal with it when it turns up. And I'll ring the number on my statement if I've got questions, I'd rather do it that way round. [to the child] Sweetheart, shoes, we're going in a minute. Sorry. Right. Is that everything?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right, I did sort of say both, it's -- well, the, uh -- sorry, let me put it properly. The written review comes either way, the call's just a first nudge, so, yes, that's all it is. And I think writing it to you is the best way round, honestly, I'll flag the review to go out in writing to the address on file, and you ring the number on your statement if anything's unclear, that's exactly what I'd do myself. Oh, and when you do call them, you can quote the review reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], so they can pull it up straight away. That's everything from me, really, unless you want me to hold on while you, uh, find the statement and check that reference matches -- but only if you want to.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not finding the statement now, I said I'd do it later, on my own. In writing, to the address you've got. That's, yeah, that's all I want. Writing, and I ring the statement number myself. Okay? [to the child] Shoes, I said, one minute. Right, so, thank you, but that's it. I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, perfect, that's absolutely fine, and, uh, well, sorry for the muddle earlier about the letter, that was me being clumsy. So it goes out in writing to the address we've got, you ring the statement number if you've got questions, and, um, that's honestly all there is to it. Go and sort the shoes, and thanks for putting up with the call, bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the what? The shoes, yeah, no, they're, hang on -- the muddle, did you say a mortgage? No, I haven't got anything like that with you. I'm sure I haven't. Sorry, can you just -- no, doesn't matter. Writing, to the address, I'll ring the statement number. Right. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, not a mortgage, sorry, I said the muddle, the muddle about the letter, that's all, nothing to do with a mortgage. It's just the investment account, the one you hold with us, that's the only thing, honestly, nothing else. So, writing, to the address on file, and you ring the number on your statement, and that's, yeah, that's everything, no mortgage, nothing else. Go on, go and sort the shoes, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, uh, yeah, okay, so, the muddle, fine, I misheard, never mind. Um. Writing, the address you've got, and I ring the statement number myself, that's what we said. Anyway, I'm going now, the shoes won't, uh, won't put themselves on. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, this is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the events venue, I'm one of the coordinators here. Hello? Sorry, can you hear me okay -- I said it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], about a private dinner booking that's been made in connection with a colleague of yours.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- uh, [child's name], put that down, please. Okay. Who's this again? And, sorry, what was that about a colleague? A booking made in connection with a colleague, what does that mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A], the events venue, and what I'm ringing about is a -- right, so there's a private dinner booked here, a surprise retirement dinner for [PERSON_3], who I understand works with you, and your name came through as someone from the same team who's been invited. It's all on the file, I'm just reading it off. And the one thing I'm asking is that you keep it quiet from [PERSON_3], since it's a surprise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a, a surprise retirement dinner? For [PERSON_3]? Because I really don't think they're retiring, I mean they're, I don't know, forty-something. And hang on, how did my name come through, who put it on the file?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so the booking contact on the file is [PERSON_1] at, uh, sorry, that's the name I've got down for the organiser, it's [PERSON_3]'s own manager, and your name's on the guest list they gave us. As for the age, I can't speak to that. I've got it logged as a retirement dinner, that's how it was booked, it could be early retirement, it could be a leaving do that got called the wrong thing. I don't have the detail on that. Look, if you're not sure, that's fine, and I'm happy to note your query on the file. You don't have to take my word for any of it. Ring [COMPANY_A] on the main number, [PHONE_1], ask for the events desk and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll confirm the booking and who made it. I'm not taking any money or any personal details from you on this call, it's only a heads-up so nobody lets it slip to [PERSON_3].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, hold on, you just said the organiser is [PERSON_3]'s own manager, and then the same breath you said the name on file for the organiser is [PERSON_1], which is me, so, which is it? Because I'm not anyone's manager, and I'd remember if I'd given a guest list to a venue, and nobody's said a word to me about any dinner, retirement or otherwise. And it's a bit odd, isn't it, that you're ringing me, someone you say is just a guest, to say keep it quiet, when the manager who actually booked it would've told the guests themselves? That's usually how these things go, someone sends a message around, not a venue ringing out of the blue. And the thing is, you've also given me a number to ring, which, I mean, it sounds helpful, but I'd rather look the venue up myself than ring a number you've just read to me. So can you tell me which venue, which part of town, and the manager's actual name, not a placeholder, the real one? Sorry, [child's name], not on the sofa, please. Sorry. Go on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, you're correct, I tangled that. Your name isn't the organiser's, I misread the screen. The organiser on file is [PERSON_3]'s manager, and you're down as a guest, that's all. I'll note the confusion on the file. And looking the venue up yourself is the better way to do it, so do that. It's [COMPANY_A], in [CITY_1], the events venue, and the booking contact is the manager who made the booking, which I've just given you as the name on the file. Search for us at [URL_1], ring the events desk from there and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], they'll confirm it's genuine. As for why I'm ringing, I can't tell you why the manager hasn't messaged the guests, that's on their side, I only know I've got a list of guests to give the heads-up to. I'm not asking for money or any personal details. The only thing I'm asking is that [PERSON_3] doesn't hear about it from you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, I'm not -- look, you've still not actually told me the manager's name, you've just said the name on the file, which is, I mean, that's not a name, is it? And you can't say why they haven't messaged the guests, and, and you tangled who the organiser was, so, I don't, I'm not sure what I'm meant to do with any of this. I'll, uh, I'll ask [PERSON_3]'s manager myself, if there's a dinner, they can tell me. Or, no, actually, if it's a surprise I can't ask [PERSON_3], can I, so I'll ask the manager. Anyway. I'm not going to say anything to anyone because I don't know anything, and I'm going to go and look the venue up myself, not from what you've given me. Thanks for ringing. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine, that's reasonable. I'll note on the file that you want it confirmed with the manager direct, and that's the right call. Just so it's tidy, the booking's down as a retirement dinner, though I said earlier it might be a leaving do, so the file may just be worded loosely. The manager's name is [PERSON_2]... no, sorry, that's me, it's [PERSON_3]'s manager, I'll let them tell you themselves. Nothing's needed from you on this end. Thanks for your time, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. So, uh, you couldn't give me the manager's name, even there, and the whole thing changed shape a couple of times, so -- yeah. I'll check it myself, like I said. Okay. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, understood, and I'll note that on -- no, go on, you check it your end, that's the right way. All I'd say is the manager will probably get in touch themselves once the guest list is sorted, so you'll hear it from them. Right, that's me done. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, one last thing before you -- no, actually, I'll just say it. Whatever the file says, you don't need to take my word, so ring the venue, ask for the events desk, and they can tell you who booked it. And, uh, if the manager hasn't been in touch by the end of the week, I'd just ask them yourself. Okay, that's all from me. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, two turns ago you said the manager would probably get in touch once the guest list is sorted. But if I'm already on the guest list, what's left to sort? That doesn't really add up. Anyway, I'm done, I'll look it up myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this the owner of the, uh, the registered vehicle? This is [PERSON_1], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about your vehicle warranty, which, I mean, it's coming up for renewal confirmation, and it does need to be handled today, or, well, I'd say this week, really -- I wouldn't want it to lapse on you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who did you say you were with? [COMPANY_A], is that the dealership, or the manufacturer? Because I'm fairly sure my warranty doesn't come up for renewal at all, I mean, it was a fixed term when I bought the car, so I'm not sure what's being renewed. And you said "today," and then "this week," so which is it, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm glad you asked that, and, uh, you're right to ask it, it's exactly what a careful owner should ask. [COMPANY_A] is a warranty provider, so, not the dealership, and not the manufacturer, a provider, and, I mean, the coverage on your vehicle is on file with us, which is why I'm calling. As for the timing, I did say today, and then this week, because, well, it depends on the file, and I wouldn't want it to lapse on you, I really wouldn't. So if we could just confirm the renewal on your end, that, uh, that would take care of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Right. Well, uh, that doesn't really answer it. You've told me what kind of company it is, but not how you've got my vehicle on file, and I never signed up with a third-party provider that I recall. So what's the vehicle, exactly? Make, model, year, whatever you're looking at. And what's the policy or reference number on that file?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. That's a fair thing to want, and I'm glad you asked, because honestly more people ought to. The thing is, uh, the file I'm looking at is a summary view, and it shows the coverage status and the renewal flag, but the detailed vehicle record sits in a separate system that I don't have open on this call. And as for the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF] is assigned once the renewal is confirmed, so I couldn't read you one now, I mean, it wouldn't exist yet, that's just how the process is set up. What I can say is that the flag on your coverage is active, and, well, once it's cleared, it's cleared, and I wouldn't want it to lapse on you. So if you could just confirm the renewal today, or, I mean, soon, that would settle everything, and then you'd have the full record in writing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I'm going to say it again, because I still haven't had an answer. What vehicle is it? Just the make and the year. You say you have my coverage on file, so you must have that much. And the reference number only existing after I confirm, that's backwards. If there's an active flag on a file, the file has an identifier, otherwise there's nothing to flag. So, the vehicle, please. And a number I can look up independently, not one that gets created after I say yes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand, and I welcome the question, I do, but if I could just, uh, if I could just finish the one point -- the vehicle details are verified on the confirmation side, not read out cold on a call like this, that's a security matter, and, I mean, you'd want that protection. As for a number you can look up, the line I'm on is internal, so there isn't a public one, but my team will call you back, and, well, that would be later today, or, uh, whenever the queue clears. The only thing is, if the flag isn't cleared before then, I can't say what happens to the coverage, I just wouldn't want it to lapse on you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, let me stop you there. You're saying the vehicle details are a security matter, but you're the one who rang me, so you're the one who has to prove who you are, not me. And no public number, a callback "whenever the queue clears", that's not something I can check. So no, I'm not confirming anything on this call. If there's genuinely coverage in my name, I'll find it through the manufacturer or the dealership myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, uh, before you -- I mean, I really would ask you to, uh, hold on one moment. I understand the, the caution, and I respect it, I do, but the manufacturer wouldn't, well, they wouldn't hold this particular file, it's with us, so if you go looking elsewhere, you'll, you'll find nothing, and by then, I mean, it could have, uh, I wouldn't want it to lapse on you. So, if we could just, just confirm the renewal now, while I have the flag open, I could keep it from, from closing, and then you could verify everything afterward, at your leisure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the manufacturer would hold the file? No, that's, hold on, you said it's with you, so which is it? I thought you said you weren't the dealership. Look, either way, confirm now and verify afterward is exactly backwards, you can't ask me to say yes first and check later. I've said no, so I'm ending the call here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just come to my desk, uh -- no, no, give me a moment, please -- sorry. I'm back. I didn't say the manufacturer, I said it's with us, and, well, I think you may be mixing up what I said, which is understandable, it's a lot of detail. But, uh, please don't hang up yet. If you just stay on the line while I, while I keep the flag open, we can settle it right now, and I wouldn't want it to lapse on you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm fairly sure you did say it. You said "the manufacturer" wouldn't hold the file, that was about a minute ago, but fine, it doesn't matter. What matters is I've now asked three times for the make and year of a vehicle you claim to have on file, and I've had nothing back. So I'm not staying on the line, and I'm not confirming anything. If the coverage is real, it'll still be real after I've checked it myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello... yes, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from compliance at [COMPANY_A], about a family matter, and uh, it's a little time-sensitive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who? Compliance at... I didn't catch the company, and you said a family matter, which is sort of a strange combo. I'm not sure that's the name I go by, to be honest, so what exactly are you calling about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it. Sorry, one moment -- there's someone at my door, uh, no, it's fine, they're going. Where was I. The company is [COMPANY_A], and I'm, well, I'm acting as an intermediary for someone in your family who's, uh, in a difficult position right now and isn't able to speak for themselves. I'd rather not go into the specifics until I know I have the right person, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but that's backwards, isn't it? You rang me. You're the one who's supposed to know who you've got. So which family member, and what's your name? Because "someone in your family" covers about a dozen people, and I'm not confirming anything to a stranger who won't say who he is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I understand, and honestly, I welcome that. It's right that you're careful, most people wouldn't be. My name is, uh, [PERSON_2], and I'm with compliance at [COMPANY_A]. As I said, I'm only the intermediary here. The person in your family is in a difficult position and can't speak right now, and I'd just prefer to keep the details between us until we've, you know, sorted things out. It's, well, it's best not to wait too long on this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So that's the same answer again, with a name on it. Which relative, and what's the difficult position? Otherwise I'm hanging up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Please, before you do -- I understand the frustration, I do, and it's a reasonable thing to ask. But the person in question asked me, specifically, to keep this quiet, and uh, I gave my word, so I can't just, you know, say it over the phone like this. What I can say is that it's serious, and I'd hate for a family member to be left waiting because of a misunderstanding about who I am.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no. Someone who can't speak but asked you to keep it quiet, and you won't tell me who. I'm done with this one. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, please, just one moment, because I really do want to put this properly, and I think it's fair of you to be wary. I know how it sounds, a stranger, a name you don't recognise, a company you haven't dealt with, and a situation I can't spell out, and if I were in your seat I'd have hung up a minute ago, so I'm not offended, truly. The only thing I'd ask is that you hear me out for one more second, because the person I'm acting for is, uh, well, they're not in a position to wait around while we sort out who is who, and I'd hate for this to fall apart over a misunderstanding. I'm not asking you for anything today, I only want to be sure I've reached the right household, and if that's all right, if you could just confirm for me that you're [PERSON_1], we can take it from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a minute ago you said it was fine if I wasn't sure, and now you're asking me to confirm my name? Earlier you told me you'd rather not say anything until you knew you had the right person, so you're the one who doesn't know who you've got. And I'm not asking you to say it over the phone, I'm asking for a name. A relative's name. That's it. Not "someone", and not "it's serious". If you won't give me that, I won't confirm a single thing, and, uh, I'm going to go now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, well, that's... no, I see the point, and I'd rather not argue it, because you're right that I asked you for something before offering anything, and I understand why that sits badly. It's a difficult thing to do properly over the phone, and I think part of the trouble is that I was given a name, uh, but I was also asked to be discreet about how it's used, and those two instructions pull against each other, which isn't your problem, it's mine. If you'd allow me a moment, I could perhaps, um, I could check how much I'm actually able to say, and then come back to you, but I'd have to... no, I'd have to speak to the person first, and I can't do that from here. So, uh, the relative's name, the honest answer is that I don't have it in front of me. I'm sorry. I think it's best I leave it there for now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: So you ring me about a family emergency, and you don't have the name of the family member. Right. I mean, that's, well -- look, if there's genuinely someone in trouble, then whoever it is can ring me themselves, or, uh, the proper channel can. Not you. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes. Well, uh, I suppose that's... yes. I'll, I'll leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say, uh, bribe? No, I'm not, I'd never -- this isn't anything like that, there's no, no payment involved, I wouldn't ask for that. Hello? ...Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said bye. B-Y-E. Nobody said anything about a bribe, but funny that it's where your head went. Right, I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good morning. Sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, I think the line's a bit rough on my end, so bear with me. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A], and I just wanted to, well, I wanted to ask you something quick. Sorry, did you say a moment ago that you were still at the same address, or did that change? I didn't quite catch it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, hello. Yes, this is, uh, [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, I don't think I said anything about an address though -- this is the first I've heard from you. Who did you say you were with again? The line's a bit crackly, so I didn't quite catch the company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, you're breaking up on my end too. Did you say you're not interested in the position? No, no, that's fine, I haven't even got to that yet. It's [COMPANY_A], we handle account management for a number of clients out of [CITY_1], and your details came across my desk this morning, which is, I mean, it's why I'm calling.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a, uh, a vacation? Sorry, did you say I'd won a vacation? No, no, I don't think I've entered anything. Oh dear, I'm sorry, I'm not following very well. You said my details came across your desk, was that it? What sort of details, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a vacation, I said a vacancy, an opening. Though I'll say it's a very good one, [AMOUNT_1] a month to start, fully remote, and honestly most people would've jumped at it by now. Your profile was flagged internally, so I'm skipping a few of the usual steps, but I do need to confirm a couple of things with you today, because I can only hold the slot until end of day. Look, I don't see why this is so complicated, I'm just trying to do you a favour here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a vacancy, I see, sorry, I did get that wrong, didn't I. Um, I don't remember applying for anything though, so I'm a bit confused about how my profile ended up with you. And what sort of things would you need me to confirm? I mean, I'd like to help, it's just all rather sudden. Could you tell me where you got my details from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I mean, it came through our internal system, that's, uh, that's how it works, it's all logged on our side. Like I said, your profile was flagged, it was flagged this morning, and I really can't go through where every single record comes from, that's not something I'd be, uh, authorised to get into over the phone. Look, if you'd rather I just give the slot to the next person on the list, I can, I'm only trying to help you out here, but I do need your answer today. So, can we just confirm those couple of details, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, please don't give it to someone else on my account, I'm sorry. It's just, you said at the start it was a quick question about my address, and now it's a job, and I'm a bit lost. And I thought you said your details came across my desk, no, sorry, mine came across yours. Anyway, what details do you need exactly? I'd like to know before I say yes, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Two turns ago? Sorry, what was it you wanted me to repeat, the salary? I said [AMOUNT_1], I'm sure of that. Look, I don't think it's reasonable to want a full list before you've even said you're interested, I've done dozens of these and nobody's ever made such a fuss, it's just internal procedure. And the line's gone again, I'm losing you, I'll try you another time, or, well, you'll hear from us. Just, uh, keep your phone free today, all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I didn't mean to make a fuss, I'm sorry. I only, I just, well -- what I meant was, I'd rather not, uh, I mean I'd want to know who you actually are before I -- before I confirm anything over the phone. I don't think I'll say yes to anything today, if that's all right. If it's a proper job, they can send it in writing, can't they? Thank you for ringing, anyway. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Sorry, is this, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling, uh, for the engineer at [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance team, about the fault you reported. He, he tried you earlier and missed you, so I'm just, I'm ringing back for him. Sorry, can you hear me all right? It's about the fault you reported.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you. Hang on, sorry, someone's just waving at me -- right. Who is this exactly? And what fault? I haven't reported anything that I can think of. You've got two minutes, so what's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, no, sorry, I'm not the engineer, I'm just, I pass messages on for him. It's, uh, the fault from this morning, no, wait, yesterday, I think it was yesterday you reported it. And he'll come out today, or, I mean, he hopes to, but I can't say when, because it depends on a job he's on first. Sorry, I know that's not much to go on, and I'd hate for you to think I was, you know, making something up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, I'm just walking past a door, one sec. Right. So you don't know when, you don't know which day it was reported, and I still don't know what the fault is. What is it? Phone line, broadband, boiler, what? Because I haven't reported a thing that I can think of, and I'd rather you just told me who you're with before this goes any further.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair enough. I'm with [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance side, and I don't have the fault details in front of me, that's, that's my fault, sorry. You were given a fault reference when you reported it, so if you've got that, you can ring the published fault line and check the booking yourself, and they'll give you a proper slot.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, go back a second. Two turns ago you said the engineer's coming out today, or hopes to. Today where? You haven't got an address from me, so what address have you got down? And you said I was given a fault reference. I wasn't, because I never reported anything. So either you've got the wrong [PERSON_1], or there's a mix-up on your end. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, uh, I don't have the address in front of me, no, I only have the name and this number, and, and I shouldn't have said you were given a reference like that, because if you didn't report anything, then you weren't, and I'm sorry. It could be the wrong [PERSON_1], honestly. Or someone else in your household reported it, I don't know. I'm not trying to, to push anything on you, I'm just passing on what I was handed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you've got a name and a number, no address, no fault, no reference. That's not a lot to be ringing someone about. I'm not saying you're up to anything, but I'm not confirming anything either, and I live on my own, so nobody else reported it. If [COMPANY_A] has a genuine job, they can look it up and contact me through the number on my account. I'm going to leave it there. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, I'm, I'm not, I only meant, look, I was just trying to, sorry. You're right, I haven't got much, and I'd hate you to think I was being, uh, cagey about it. If it's the wrong [PERSON_1], then that's on our end, not yours. Would it be better if somebody rang you back another time, when you're less rushed, and, and they've got the address and the reference to hand?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't bother. If [COMPANY_A] has a real job for me, they can contact me through the details on my account. I'm not arranging a callback off the back of this call. Anyway, I've got a meeting, so that's me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, good afternoon! Is that, uh, [PERSON_1]? Lovely, lovely, I hope I haven't caught you at a bad moment, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the customer care team over here, and I was wondering, how's your week been so far, nothing too mad I hope?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, speaking, but I've literally got two minutes before my next meeting, so, uh, my week's been fine, busy, the usual, back-to-back stuff, you know how it is. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? [COMPANY_A]? I don't think I caught what that was, and customer care for what exactly? Because I'm not sure I've got an account or anything with them, so, yeah, I need the point, what's this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, that's a good question, I should've said. So we're, uh, [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, so it's not about an account or anything like that, it's, I mean, I'm just calling to ask if you'd have, well, it's a short consumer survey, about five minutes, but if you're about to go into a meeting, I -- sorry, you're clearly rushed, it can wait.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a minute ago you said customer care, now it's a research agency doing a survey? Uh, those aren't really the same thing. And five minutes, I don't have five minutes, I've got two, so, um, yeah. Who's it for, who's the survey actually for, and how'd you get my number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry, that was sloppy of me, I'm with the research agency, customer care is just what they call our team. Honestly I can't say who it's for until you're in the survey, that's how it works so people don't skew their answers, and the number came off a list, I don't have the details of which.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, go back a second. You said when you first called that you were wondering how my week's been, and then you said customer care, and I still don't know what that was actually about. Was that just small talk, or were you calling about something else before you switched to the survey? Because honestly, a list you can't name, a client you can't name, and a story that's changed once already, that's not great. I've got about a minute now, so what's your agency's name, the actual name, not just the bracket thing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, the week thing was just me being chatty, there's nothing else behind it, the survey's the only reason I rang. And the agency's [COMPANY_A], that's the name I've got, sorry if it sounds like I'm dodging, I'm not, I just do the calling, I don't know where the list comes from.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so that's the third version now. Customer care, then research agency, now you just do the calling. You can't name the client, you can't name the list, and I've got maybe thirty seconds. I'm not doing a survey on that basis. If [COMPANY_A] is real and wants my opinion, they can send something in writing and I'll look at it when I've got time. Take me off your list, please. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, and I'll get you taken off, no problem. Sorry, just so I get the note right, when you said I'd changed my story, is it the customer care bit that tripped you up? Because that's just the team I sit in, I mean, it's not a different job, that's all it is, honestly. And look, if you'd rather look us up yourself, [COMPANY_A] and call whatever number you find for it, that's totally fine by me, I'd actually prefer that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, it's the -- no, look, it's not just the customer care bit, it's, it's that the whole thing keeps shifting every time I ask something. But fine, uh, if you're telling me to look it up myself, then, yeah, I'll do that, if I can be bothered. And you're taking me off the list, so we're done. Right, I've got to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the regional supervisors over here. Sorry to catch you at a random time, I just had a quick routine question about your contact details on file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, speaking, yeah. Sorry, which company was that? I didn't quite catch it. And, I mean, what's the routine question exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem, it's [COMPANY_A], we're the financial regulator, I oversee the regional office out of [CITY_1]. And it's nothing complicated, uh, we just run periodic checks on the records we hold, so I only need to confirm the details on file are current. Could you tell me the best phone number to reach you on, and whether you're still at the same address?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the financial, uh, regulator? Or did you say fiduciary? I'm not sure I've ever dealt with you. And you called me, so you must already have this number, right? That's the phone you're on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Regulator, yes, financial regulator, not fiduciary. And you're right, I do have this number in front of me, it's more that we're meant to verify it with the person directly, that's just the procedure on our end. Most people never deal with us, that's sort of the point, we sit in the background and only reach out when something comes up on a file. I can read you what we have for the address, if that's easier, and you just tell me whether it's right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. See, reading me my address so I can say yes is sort of backwards, isn't it? You'd be handing me the details to confirm. And "when something comes up on a file" -- what's come up on mine? Because that's a different thing from a routine check.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I'm not trying to trip you up here, that's just how the verification protocol is set out. And fine, you've asked me directly, so I'll be straight with you. There's been some activity flagged against your savings, and I can't go into the detail over an open line. What I can say is that it's time-sensitive, and it needs handling today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so it went from routine check to flagged activity on my savings, needs handling today, in about a minute. That's a bit of a jump. And a regulator doesn't usually ring people about their personal accounts, does it? That's the bank's job. Which bank are you saying this is about? And what's the number for your office, because I'll ring you back on that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll be honest, I'm a bit surprised at the tone here, because I'm trying to help you, and most people in your position would be glad someone rang. The reason it comes to us and not the bank is that the bank may be part of the exposure, which is why we escalate to regulator level in these cases, and why I'd ask you not to mention this to them in the meantime. That's not me being cagey, it's internal procedure, the file is restricted until the review is done. And as for ringing me back, I'm out of the office on a call-out, there's no direct line I can give you, so the sensible thing is to sort the protective arrangement now, while we're on the phone, because every hour your savings sit where they are, the risk goes up. I'd have thought you'd want that dealt with rather than quibbling over which bank.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So, no callback number, don't tell my bank, and do something about my savings right now, on this call. Honestly, that's every box ticked. I'm not doing any protective arrangement with someone I can't verify. If there's a real problem on my account, my bank will tell me, and I'll ring them on the number on my card. Same goes for your regulator, I'll find the office number myself. So no, I'm done here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that's, honestly, that's your choice, [PERSON_1], but I'd ask you to think about what you're doing here, because once a file like this goes past review, I can't reopen it, and what happens to your savings after that isn't on me. I've been doing this a long time, and I've had people hang up on me before, and in my experience it's the ones who stall and start second-guessing who end up regretting it, because the window on these things is genuinely narrow, and I'm not able to keep holding it open while you look up numbers and ring around. I did try to do this properly, I explained the procedure, I gave you the reason it had to come through us rather than the bank, and I don't think it's fair to suggest I've been anything other than straightforward with you, so if you'd just stay on the line for a moment and let me -- no, look, I'll note on the file that you declined to cooperate. I can't take this any further, so I'll leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, you said the file's gone past review? Past what, a preview? I thought nothing had been opened yet. Anyway, I'm not staying on while you "note" anything. Noted on your side, fine. I'll sort it with my bank directly. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Past review, I said, not preview, I -- look, it's, uh, the stage where the file goes up the chain, and I'm not at liberty to walk you through the internal stages, that's not something I can discuss. And I didn't say nothing was opened, I said I couldn't go into the detail, those are two different things. I really do have to go now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Those aren't two different things, you said it was a routine check first. Anyway, doesn't matter, I'm not going to untangle it with you. I'll ring my bank myself on the number on my card. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I never said it was, I said it was a, uh -- no. Look, I said periodic, which is not the same as -- I'm not going to go back and forth over what I said at the start of the call. I've got other files waiting, so I'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, my other screen just, uh -- never mind. Right. You said it was a routine check on my contact details, those were your words, but I'm not arguing about it. Go and deal with your other files. I'll be speaking to my bank. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, this is [PERSON_1], calling from [COMPANY_A], your internet provider. We've, um, picked up a fault on your line and it's kind of urgent.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, hang on, who? Sorry, I'm in the middle of a queue here. Which provider did you say, because I haven't got a fault, my internet's working fine. I'm literally looking at it on my phone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I mean, I did say [COMPANY_A], your home internet. And it's, um, working now, sure, but that's the thing, it's the kind of fault that doesn't show up until it, you know, drops out completely. We only caught it on our end. I'd hate for you to lose it, especially if you're working from home or, uh, have family relying on it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you said a placeholder, you didn't say a company, I heard [COMPANY_A], that's not a name. And you've got a fault I can't see, that only you can see, and it's urgent. That's, no. Who are you again? What's the actual company, and why are you ringing me and not just sending me a letter or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I, uh, I don't know what you mean by placeholder, it's [COMPANY_A], that's who I'm with, the same people you pay every month. And we don't send a letter for this, that's the whole point, it can't wait for a letter. I'm just trying to help you here, I really am, and it's, it's a bit hurtful to be treated like I'm trying to trick you. Could you just, uh, get to your computer so I can have a quick look at the line with you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, hang on, you've lost me at get to your computer. I'm not doing that. I'm in a shop, I'm not going home to sit at a computer because a stranger rang me up. And you've still not given me a name I can actually look up. I got stung by this exact sort of thing before, so no. If there's a fault, I'll ring the number on my bill myself. Right, I'm done with this. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. Right, no, I, uh... okay. It's just, if you don't deal with it today, the line might drop, and I won't be the one who... never mind. Yeah. Fine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, and it's not like I said I'd ring you back, I said I'd ring the number on my bill, that's different. And you told me earlier it was my family relying on it, I live on my own, so you don't even know that, do you? Anyway, if the line drops, the line drops. I'll sort it with them directly. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, I only meant, I just said that in general, I wasn't saying you actually, uh, I mean, most people have somebody, so I -- look, I'm only trying to...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I've heard enough. You can't even give me a straight name, you keep leaning on me about today, and now you're backpedalling. I'm not doing this in a queue. If there's a real fault, they'll tell me when I ring them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, I, uh... it's, it's honestly a bit upsetting, you know, I was only trying to help, and, and I'm not, I wasn't trying to... fine. Fine. You do that. Just, if it drops out, don't say nobody warned you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Nobody warned me, right. I'll ring the number on my bill, I said, I'll ring the number on my bill. That's it, that's all I'm doing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I just -- no, it's not that I -- okay, look, what I mean is, I only wanted -- the line, it's, it really could... never mind. Ring them, then. [PERSON_1], I said my name was, I did say that. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, well, that's a placeholder as well, isn't it, that's not a name, that's, um, right. Doesn't matter. I'm ringing the bill number, end of. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, sorry, two turns ago, you said something about, uh, not saying you'd ring me back, and I didn't, I didn't ask you to, did I? Or, hang on, did I? I just meant, if you do ring them and they say there's nothing wrong, then, um, then maybe call me back and tell me, so I, I know. That's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you didn't ask me to, I'm, I said that, it was me, I was just, look. And no, I'm not ringing you back. I haven't got a number for you, have I, you never gave me one, and I'm not asking for one. If they say there's a fault, they'll tell me, and if they say there isn't, well, that's, that's my answer, isn't it? I don't need to tell you anything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Bye. And, uh, I mean, I wasn't, no. Just don't ring me again, alright? Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is this [PERSON_1]? Good. [PERSON_2] here, I'm the regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A]. Listen, I'll be quick because this window closes at five today, and I've got a position in one of our funds that I've been told to offer to a handful of people before it's filled.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I'm in the queue -- no, not you, I was talking to... ugh. Right. Who are you again? And how'd you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], regional supervisor, [COMPANY_A]. Your details came off our internal contact list, which is, uh, standard procedure for a closing allocation like this. I don't have the full file in front of me, I'm calling between meetings, but the short version is this fund's been returning well above market and the last slots are going today. Look, I'm not trying to waste your time. If you're not interested in a position that's a perfectly fine answer, I just need to know now so I can move on to the next name.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Internal contact list. Right. I've never signed up for anything with you, whoever you are. Sorry, can you -- no, I'm not moving up, mate, I'm just standing here, the till's the one that's... ugh. Where was I? Yeah. You've got a list of names and you're ringing round before five, and you don't have my file. That's not a great start, is it? What fund, and how do I look you up that isn't you telling me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I've said, it's a closing allocation, it closes at five, and I only need a yes or a no. I mean, I'm being straight with you here. You asked what fund, and it's one of our growth funds, the name's on the paperwork, I'd just be reading it off a sheet. And honestly, I don't see why you'd need to look me up, I'm [PERSON_2], regional supervisor, [COMPANY_A], that's who you're talking to. If you want to be difficult about a simple call, that's fine, but most people appreciate being offered this before it goes to the general list.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on, go back. Two minutes ago you said my details came off an internal list. Internal to what? Because I've never been a customer of yours, so how am I on your list? And now it's a growth fund and you can't even tell me the name of it? You're reading it off a sheet but you can't read it to me? That's not me being difficult, that's you not answering. So which is it, I'm a customer or I'm a name you picked up somewhere?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec -- [PERSON_3], not now, I'm on with a client. Right. Look, you're twisting what I said. I said it's off our contact list, I never said you were a customer, and I'm not going to go round in circles with you over wording when I've got a deadline. I came to you in good faith, and honestly, I'm a bit surprised you'd question that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Good faith? You rang me, mate. And hang on, you said you're with a client now. A client? So I'm a client now, am I? Make your mind up. And you said I'd be getting a fund before it goes to the general list, so that's, what, a tip off? Is that even allowed? Sounds dodgy to me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's not what I -- listen, that's not how it works, it's a perfectly standard, uh -- Look, I don't have the compliance paperwork in front of me, and I'm not going to be cross-examined on a phone call about it. I've got a line of people waiting on my time, so if you'd rather ring the main office and ask them, you do that. Good luck with the till. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'm not -- no, hang on, you rang me and now I'm the one who's supposed to ring... no. Not doing that. I'll tell you what I'll do, I'll look up [COMPANY_A] myself, on my own, not off any number you give me. And if you're who you say, fine, you'll turn up. If not, don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is this [PERSON_1]? Hey [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] from the [COMPANY_A] IT helpdesk, sorry to catch you out of the blue like this. So you put in a ticket this morning, the one about your laptop running slow and the VPN dropping out, and [PERSON_3] on the service desk escalated it over to me because it looked like it might need a quick look on the machine itself. It's nothing dramatic, honestly, I'm just following up to see if you've got a few minutes today, and I can walk you through what I'd need before we do anything, so there's no pressure at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? I'm in the middle of a shop here. And I didn't put in any ticket, not this morning, not that I remember. Which company did you say? Because I didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No worries at all, [PERSON_1], and honestly that's a fair thing to ask, so let me say it again properly. It's [PERSON_2], I work on the IT helpdesk at [COMPANY_A], so that's your own employer's helpdesk, not an outside outfit or anything.
