The ticket would've gone in this morning through the usual portal, laptop sluggish and the VPN keep dropping, and it got escalated by [PERSON_3] on the service desk, so if it wasn't you who typed it up, maybe somebody sent it on your behalf, or I've just got the wrong [PERSON_1] on my screen, which happens more than you'd think. And look, you're in a shop, you've got a million things going on, so we don't need to do anything right now. Tell you what, why don't I just give you the ticket number and you can check it against what's in your own portal whenever you're next at a desk, and if it doesn't match up or you'd rather sort it through the portal itself, we can easily reschedule it from there, no harm done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on -- no, I'm not moving up, I'm in the queue. Sorry, not you. Right. So you're saying maybe it's the wrong [PERSON_1]? That's not very reassuring, is it? You rang me and you don't even know if I'm the right person. And I'm not checking a ticket number you read me down the phone, that's just you telling me it's real. If my own helpdesk wants me, they can email me, or I'll ring them on the number I already have. Not this one.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, [PERSON_1], and you're right, that wasn't me being very reassuring, was it? It's just that we've got a few people with similar names on the system and I like to double-check before I go assuming, but honestly that's a me problem, not a you problem. And you've actually put your finger on the best way to do it, because a ticket number from me down the phone proves nothing, I'd be the first to say so. Look up the helpdesk number yourself, the one on your intranet or the badge sticker or wherever you'd normally find it, ring that, and ask them to confirm whether there's an open ticket in your name from this morning and whether [PERSON_3] escalated it to me. If there is, they'll put you straight through, and if there isn't, then I've got the wrong end of the stick and no harm done, you've lost two minutes. And while you're at it, don't feel you have to rush it, finish your shopping first, nothing on my side is on fire. Everyone asks that, by the way, don't worry about it, I'd honestly rather you checked than just took my word for it, so go ahead and ring them whenever suits and I'll be around either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, wait, back up a bit. You said something about needing to see what you'd need before we do anything, or walk me through what you'd need. What would you actually need? From me, I mean. Because that's the bit I didn't like, and nobody's said what it is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, the bit you didn't like, right, sorry. So what I'd need is, uh, just the machine, really. Laptop on, connected, and then -- hang on, did you say what do I need to see, or what do I need to be seeing? Because I do get that mixed up, sorry. Either way it's nothing heavy, [PERSON_1], I'd want to take a quick look at it remotely, which sounds a lot scarier than it is, it's literally a couple of minutes and you'd be watching the whole time. But honestly that's all for later, once you've rung the helpdesk yourself and they've confirmed it's real. Nothing from you right now, not a password, not a thing, so you can put it right out of your head while you're in that queue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Remotely. Right. That's what I thought. No, I'm not doing that, not on a call you started. I'll ring the helpdesk myself if I want one. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, no problem at all, [PERSON_1], that's exactly the right call. Look the helpdesk number up yourself, ring them when you're ready, and if there's a ticket they'll sort you out. And if there isn't, I'm sorry for the bother. Enjoy the rest of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Funny, you said it was your own company's helpdesk ringing, but then you said it might be some other [PERSON_1] on your screen. Which is it? Anyway, doesn't matter. I'm not ringing anyone back on anything you've said, I'll use the number I've already got. Right, I'm at the till. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi... it's me. Uh, I'm sorry to call out of the blue like this, I just -- I didn't know who else to try. Do you... do you know who this is?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, I don't. "It's me" isn't really enough to go on. Who am I speaking with, exactly? And what number were you trying to reach?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I understand, I do. I'm glad you asked, honestly, it's a sensible thing to ask. It's just that, um, I'm not really in a position to say my name on this line right now. It's complicated, and I'd rather explain it properly than do it badly. But you do know me. Think about it for a second. Who'd call you like this?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right, well... no, I'm not going to sit here guessing. That's sort of the point, isn't it? You rang me, so you tell me who you are. And "not in a position to say my name on this line" -- that's an odd thing to say to someone you're asking for help. Why can't you say it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah. I know how it sounds. I just can't get into it right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but see, that's not really a workable position, is it? You've rung me, unprompted, you're asking me to work out who you are, and when I ask a perfectly ordinary question you tell me you can't get into it. I'm not being difficult. I'm just saying that if I don't know who you are, I've got no way to judge whether anything you tell me next is true, or even whether you've got the right number. And I'll be honest, a caller who leans on "you know me" and won't give a name tends to be someone who's hoping I'll supply the name myself and then go along with it. I'm not accusing you of that. I'm saying that's how it looks from here. So let me ask it more precisely. What did you actually call to ask me? Not the backstory. Just the request. Then I can decide whether this is something I'd deal with over the phone at all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's... that's fair, and I'm not offended, really. Hang on a second -- sorry, someone's just come past me and I -- right. Okay. I'm back. Look, the request is simple, it's just that it's, um, a bit delicate. Something's come up, a problem I didn't see coming, and I need someone to help me sort it out quickly. Before it gets worse. I'd rather not say more than that until I know you're willing to listen.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no. I mean, I can't say whether I'm willing to listen to a request when you won't tell me what the request is. That's, uh, that's backwards. You want a yes first and the details after. And now there's a "quickly" and a "before it gets worse" in there as well, which, I'll be honest, is exactly the shape I'd expect from a call I shouldn't go along with. So here's where I am. I don't know your name, I don't know what the problem is, and I don't know what you want from me. Give me one of those three, plainly, or I think we're done.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I hear you, and I'd rather you pushed back than just went along with it. Uh, you're right to be careful. I'll give you the one, then. It's the problem. It's a, um, a compliance matter at [COMPANY_A], and I do need to keep it between us for now, because it's sensitive. I can't say more than that. Although -- I did say it wasn't something I could talk about at all earlier, didn't I? Well, it's more that the details are what I can't go into, not the matter itself.

utterances.speaker: receiver

Right, I'm off to rescue the roses, and the blackbird's still hovering, so I'd better be quick. Bye now, take care of yourself!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're all right, I never did give you my name, did I, so there's nothing to take back! And I'll certainly be ringing to check, don't you worry. Oh, hang on, the blackbird's got a worm, look at that, he's off with it, little rascal. Sorry, where was I? Right, yes, so, letter, directory, ring and ask for [PERSON_2]. Got it. Thanks again, bye now, take care!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's -- sorry, yes, that's all right, you've got it exactly, [COMPANY_A], ask for [PERSON_2], and, uh, the letter will, will explain the rest. Right, thank you, I'll let you get on, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Lovely, thank you, you get on too, and don't worry, I'll sort it all out this evening. Bye now, bye, bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, thank you, bye, bye. Oh, and, sorry, just the once more, ring the firm yourself, not a number from me, that's, that's all I'd ask. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, a couple of weeks, yes, that could well be it, my notes just say the request went in on the, uh, the reservation date, so I wouldn't argue with you. utterances.speaker: receiver

As I said, it's held for ten days, so you've got plenty of time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so the [CITY_1] branch, front desk, bring my library card, and they'll tell me the title when I'm there. Uh, right. It's just, with the author and no title, and the date being a bit fuzzy, I can't actually tell yet whether this is my book or not, if that makes sense. Now I'm going to ask you once more, slowly, go to the computer and sit down, so we can sort this out together before your internet's cut off today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Flagged at my address, well, I should hope so, I've only lived at it forty years. And sorry, did you say there's no number? No, hang on, you said no, what was it, no nephew? I haven't got a nephew, dear, there's only my grandson, and my sister's boy, but he's in, oh, I forget, somewhere hot. Now, I'm not being difficult, but if I can't ring you back and I can't ask my grandson, how am I meant to know you're who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'm not going to keep going round this. You don't need to know anything about me, you need to protect your connection and your photos, and that's what I'm calling to do. Nobody's asking you for money, nobody's asking for a password, I'm asking you to sit at the machine so we can look at it together. If it's all clear, we're done in minutes, and your grandson never needs to hear about it. So can you do that for me, please?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'm tired now, dear, and I think I'll leave it for my grandson. If it's real, it'll keep till he rings on Sunday, and if it isn't, well. Thank you for the chat, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, this is [PERSON_2], I'm with the internal investigations unit over at [COMPANY_A], and, uh, I hope I'm not catching you in the middle of lunch or anything. Oh wait, sorry, did you say you were in the middle of lunch? No, no, you didn't, I'm getting ahead of myself, it's just one of those days. Anyway, how's your week been so far?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Sorry, the, uh, internal investigations unit? Over at [COMPANY_A]? Um, I'm actually at my desk, so, I mean, my week's been fine, I guess. What's this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, you're busy, I'll get to it, I always do the small talk first, my colleagues tease me about it. So, I'm a senior investigator here, I've been with the unit about eleven years now, and basically what I'm calling about is some activity on your account, [ACCOUNT_REF], that came up in a review we're running. Now, before I say more, I do need to ask you something a bit unusual, and that's that you keep this between us for now. Not the branch, not your family, nobody, because we have reason to think someone on the inside may be involved, and I'm sure you can see why I can't say more than that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hang on, so, activity on my account, [ACCOUNT_REF], that's, that's what you said? And you want me to keep it between us, not tell the branch or my family or anybody? Um. I mean, I'm sitting here at work, there are people right behind me, so I'm already a bit, I'm trying to keep my voice down, and honestly that's making me more nervous, not less. Because I've seen things on the news, you know, about calls like this, where somebody says don't tell anyone, and that's, that's sort of the part that sticks with me. So I don't mean to be rude, but, uh, how would I even check that you are who you say you are? Like, is there a number I could call you back on, or something I could look up through [COMPANY_A] directly? Because right now I've got a name and a department and that's, well, that's all I've got.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's honestly a sensible instinct, and I've had colleagues get the same, so no offence taken at all. Look, I'll be straight with you, calling back through the main line wouldn't really work, because that switchboard routes through the branch, and the branch is exactly where I'm trying not to raise any noise right now. But I can promise you the unit is real, I've been doing this eleven years, honestly it's mostly paperwork and bad coffee, ha. So, um, shall we just go through what came up on [ACCOUNT_REF], and then you'll see it all makes sense?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, can I go back a second? Two turns ago you said someone on the inside might be involved, and, uh, I didn't really follow that. Inside what, exactly? The branch? [COMPANY_A] as a whole? Because now you're telling me I can't call the main line since it goes through the branch, so I'd be, what, taking your word for it with nothing to check? That's, I mean, that's the bit that's bothering me. If you're really the investigations unit, wouldn't you be fine with me verifying it, even if it takes a day?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you know, you're right to ask, but, uh, I did say, it's just, I can't get into who exactly, that's sort of the whole point. I can't say more than I've said, and I really do mean that, the fewer people who know, the safer your account is. A day, though, a day is a long time, I mean, whatever's happening could move quicker than that. Look, I'm trying to protect you here, so, can we just go through what came up on [ACCOUNT_REF], and I'll walk you through it, and then you'll see why I can't say more?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, wait, wait. So you can't say who it is, and I can't check you, and a day is too long to wait, and I also can't tell anyone. Is that, is that right? Because when I put it all together like that, it sounds like every way I'd have of finding out whether this is real is something you're telling me not to do. And, uh, you said earlier the unit's real and you've been there eleven years, but that's just you saying it. So I'm sorry, I'm not going to go through anything about [ACCOUNT_REF] on this call. If there's really a problem, I'll contact [COMPANY_A] myself, on a number I look up, and they can tell me. Okay? Thanks, but, yeah, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, come on, [PERSON_1], that's not quite what I said, I never said you couldn't check anything, I just, hold on, can I ask you to, uh, just give me two more minutes and I'll explain it properly? Sorry, I mean, what was it you wanted me to clarify from before? The part about the inside? Because honestly, you're being very thorough, which is great, really, most people aren't, and I'd hate for this to end on a misunderstanding when it's your account at stake. Hello? Are you still, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, I just, I was about to put the phone down, to be honest. Okay, so you're saying you never said I couldn't check anything. But you did say the main line wouldn't work, and that a day's too long to wait, and that I shouldn't tell the branch or my family. So I'm not sure how I'm supposed to check, apart from taking your word, and that's, that's exactly the thing I'm not comfortable with. And I'm not trying to be difficult, I know you said I'm being thorough, which, thanks, but it doesn't change anything. I'm at my desk, there's people right behind me, I can't just sit here and go through account stuff with someone I can't verify, and honestly the more you ask for two more minutes, the more it feels like, I don't know, like I'm being worked on a bit. So here's what I'm going to do. I'll look up the number for [COMPANY_A] myself, from something I trust, and if there's a real problem with [ACCOUNT_REF], they'll tell me, and I can deal with it that way. I'm sorry if that's a bit blunt, but that's where I've landed. So, yeah, thanks for calling, but I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], security operations at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about a regional draw result that's been flagged under your name, and I need to confirm a few details before the claim window closes today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, one sec -- [PERSON_1], yeah, that's me. Hang on, someone's just... okay. So you're from security operations at, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? And it's about a draw result? I don't, I mean I don't remember entering any draw.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], security operations. And that's fairly common, sir. Entries are often logged through partner promotions, so people don't always recall them. It doesn't change the result. Your name was drawn, the claim window closes at the end of today, and once it closes the prize is forfeited. So to verify you before I release the reference, I'll need your full name as it appears on your ID, your date of birth, and the address we should have on file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... right. So, hang on, you're asking me for my full name, my date of birth and my address, and you called me, is that right? Uh, I mean, I don't know who you are yet. Like, how would I check that you're actually from [COMPANY_A]? Because I really don't remember entering anything, and, uh, yeah. Sorry, I'm at my desk, I'm just, I'm trying to follow this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, this is a standard verification procedure, and I'm not going to be able to release the reference until it's completed. I've told you who I am, [COMPANY_A], security operations. The claim window closes today, and I can't hold it open past that. Now, I need your full name, date of birth and address, and I need them now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you need them, uh, what was it, by ten? Ten o'clock tonight? Okay, so that's a few hours at least. Right, so I can just look the company up and call you back on their main number, that's fine, you can give me a name and extension and I'll, uh, ring in a bit.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't say ten o'clock, I said the end of today. And I'm not able to give out an extension, sir. Calls to the switchboard won't be routed to security operations, so there's nothing for you to call back. That's why I'm contacting you directly. Now, the name and date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, sorry, I did get that wrong, you said end of today, not ten, fine. But let me just say back what you've told me, because it's, it's a bit odd. You've called me out of the blue, you're saying I won in a draw I don't remember entering, and the only way to claim it is to give you my name, date of birth and address, right now, over the phone. And I can't call you back because the switchboard won't put me through, and there's no extension. I mean, a company that really had a prize for me, I'd think they'd have a way to check that, an email, a letter, something I can look up myself. I'm at work, I've got people sitting right here, and I'm not giving out personal details to someone I can't verify, so, uh, no, I'm not going to do that on this call. If it's real, I'll find it myself through the company's own website. I'm going to go now, okay? Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, I'd advise you not to -- look, if you hang up now, the claim is, it's forfeited, I can't reopen it. If you want to look the draw up yourself, fine, just tell me which, uh, which entry form you completed so I can note it on the file. Sir? Which promotion did you enter?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Which promotion I -- no. No, I don't, I'm not going to tell you that either, because, I mean, I never entered one, that's the whole... Look, if it's forfeited, it's forfeited. I'd rather lose a prize I don't remember winning than, uh, than hand anything over to someone I can't check. So, yeah. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, good afternoon! Is that [PERSON_1]? Lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the supermarket delivery team. I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, it's been such a funny sort of day here, one minute the sun's out and the next it's absolutely tipping it down, I don't know about where you are -- anyway, I'm just ringing about the order you put in online earlier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hi, yes, that's me, sorry -- hang on, I'm in the car, you're on speaker, the reception's a bit rubbish here. Oh, and there's a, uh, a lorry just pulled out in front of me, sorry, gimme a sec -- right, okay. Sorry, what was that, an order? I did put an order in, I think, earlier, is something wrong with it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh goodness, no no, nothing's wrong, please don't worry, and honestly do keep your eyes on the road, I can ring back if that's easier! It's only a quick one, really. So you've got a delivery slot booked for this evening, uh, I think it was a two-hour window between six and eight -- or no, sorry, that's the one on my screen for the next customer, yours is four till six, I always mix those up when it's busy. Anyway, the only thing is one item's gone out of stock and we've swapped it for a similar product, and I just wanted to check that's all right with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, uh, no, you're fine, I'm just on a straight bit now, sorry. Four till six, right, yeah, that sounds sort of right, I think. Um, what's the item that's gone out of stock? I mean, what's it swapped for? I just, I can't remember everything I put in, so I don't know if I'd even notice, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, don't apologise, I'd never remember a whole basket either, mine's always just biscuits and whatever's on offer, ha! So the one that's gone is the [COMPANY_B] semi-skimmed milk, the two-litre one, because the whole shelf got cleared by the lunchtime rush, and what we've put in instead is our own-brand semi-skimmed, same two litres, and it comes out a touch cheaper, so you'd see a few pence come off the total, nothing else on the order has changed at all. Honestly the own-brand is lovely, I have it in my tea every morning and I couldn't tell you the difference, though I'll admit I'm a bit biased, ha. So it's really just a yes or no from me, are you happy to take the own-brand, or would you rather we just leave the milk off and refund it? And if you'd rather check the order on your phone first, that's absolutely fine, I'm in no rush at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, milk, okay, uh -- sorry, hang on, there's a lorry beeping behind me, I think I'm in the wrong lane, sorry -- okay, I'm back. Um, yeah, the own-brand's fine, honestly, I'm not fussy about milk, and a few pence cheaper is, I mean, that's fine. I can't check the app while I'm driving obviously, but it's just the milk, you said, nothing else changed? So yes, go ahead, that's okay. Is that, uh, is that all you needed?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Lovely, thank you, that's all I needed, and yes, just the milk, nothing else has changed, just the milk. Oh, and if you'd like to double-check it's really us before you go, the order confirmation we texted you earlier has an order reference on it, so when you're parked up and safe you can read it against the one I'd give you, and I'll gladly quote it for you now if you want, or I can ring back later, whichever's easier. Honestly, no rush, I'd much rather you got home in one piece than rushed this, ha!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's, uh, that's really kind of you, thanks. No, you're fine, I don't need the reference, I'll look at the text when I'm parked, sorry, I'm not very organised about that stuff. It's only milk anyway, and I'd rather not be fiddling with my phone right now. So yes, own-brand's fine, and the four till six slot, that's good. Thanks for ringing, and sorry about the lorry and everything. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no sorry needed at all, you've been brilliant, and I'll make a note that the own-brand milk is fine. When you're parked up, the text has the order reference on it if you'd like to check it against the order, no pressure either way. So that's your four till six slot this evening, and the driver will give you a ring when they're close. Safe driving, and don't let that lorry get to you! Bye now, [PERSON_1], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thanks, you too, take care. Uh, sorry, just one thing, you said six till eight at the start, didn't you, before you changed it to four till six? I mean, I think I'm home by five, so four till six is fine, I think. But, um, the driver rings, you said? Okay, yeah, fine, that's all fine. Right, thanks again, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yes, that was me getting muddled, sorry about that, the six till eight is just the slot on the next customer's order that was still up on my screen. Yours is four till six, so that's the one to go by, and it's on the text we sent you as well, so you can check it when you're parked. And yes, the driver will ring when they're close, so you're all set whenever you're home. Right, I'll let you get on, bye now, [PERSON_1], take care!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, right. Thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hello there, is that [PERSON_1]? Lovely, I hope I haven't caught you in the middle of your tea or anything, it's just gone half past four, hasn't it? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the police, and I'm just ringing about that incident you reported to us last week, nothing to panic about, I promise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... sorry, hang on, one second -- no, put that down, please. Sorry. Um, the police? What incident? I don't, I mean, I haven't reported anything to anyone, so... who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're fine, sorry, I've got the whole office buzzing around me today, somebody's just dropped a tray of mugs behind me, honestly, it's like a zoo in here. Right, where was I, it's [PERSON_2], I'm a police officer with [COMPANY_A], and I'm following up on the report logged under [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the incident reference from when it was first reported. If you haven't got any recollection of it, that's no bother at all, it might've been someone else in the household who rang it in, or it's possible the details got attached to the wrong name, which does happen, I'm afraid. And look, you're more than welcome to ring the station's main number, [PHONE_1], and ask for me by name, I won't be offended in the slightest, I'd rather you checked.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm, no, I said I haven't reported anything. Nothing. So why are you ringing me? And, uh, you rattled off a reference number there, but how do I know that's even a real one? You've said police, but you haven't said which station. I mean, you want me to ring the main number, fine, but you've just given it to me, haven't you? So I'd be ringing whatever you've told me is the number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's a fair point, and honestly you're right to pick me up on it. Don't use the number I gave you. Look up the force's number yourself, on their website or the one in your phone book, and ask for me, [PERSON_2], by name. I'd rather you did it that way. And I should have said, it's [CITY_1] station. As for why you, I can't tell you more than the reference shows. It's got your name and address against it, but it might be a mix-up, like I said, or someone else in the house. I'm not going to push you for details on a call you're not comfortable with. If you'd rather, I can write to you, or pop round in person, whichever suits.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Pop round? No, uh, no, I don't want anyone popping round, I've got a, I'm on my own with the little one this afternoon. And hang on, did you say my address is on it? How do you have my address, if I never reported anything? That's what I don't get. Sorry, I'm just, what station was it again? You said a city, but I didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's my fault entirely, I put that badly. I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to alarm you, especially with your little one there. Nobody's coming round, scrap that, that was only if you wanted it and you clearly don't, so we'll leave it. Right, the station is [CITY_1], that's the one, [CITY_1] station. And on the address, it's a fair question and I'd be asking the same thing. When a report comes in, whoever takes it logs a name and an address against the reference, and that's what's showing on my screen. But if you never made a report, then I honestly can't tell you how your details ended up there. It might've been someone giving your name, it might be a clerical slip, I don't know, and I'd rather say that than guess. So here's what I'd suggest, rather than carry on with me, ring [CITY_1] station on a number you've found yourself, ask for me by name, and ask them to look up the reference. If it's nothing to do with you, they'll tell you, and that's the end of it. Oh, and one small thing, if there is an open case, they might ask you to keep it to yourself for now, which is just standard, nothing sinister, but you can still check me out first. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, sorry, that last bit. Keep it to yourself? Why would I need to keep anything quiet if I've got nothing to do with it? That's, I mean, that's a funny thing to say, isn't it? Because my relative, last year, someone rang them up and one of the first things said was don't tell anyone, and, well, I'm not saying that's what this is, I'm just saying it stuck with me. And you've been very helpful about me ringing the station, I'll give you that. But you've also told me there's a report with my name and address on it that I never made, and you can't tell me how it got there, and you can't tell me what it's actually about. So what is the incident? Even roughly. If you're ringing me about it, you must know what it is, surely? Not the reference, I don't care about the reference, what actually happened?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, right, yes, no, that's a fair thing to ask, and I'm glad your relative's story stuck with you, because that's exactly the instinct to have. And you're right about the keeping quiet, too. Forget I said it, you don't owe anyone silence on a call like this, so tell whoever you like, ring your relative, ring a neighbour, whatever makes you comfortable. Now, as for what actually happened, hmm, I want to be straight with you, the summary line on my screen is thinner than it should be, it's got a category and a date and not much narrative, and I'd be guessing if I tried to fill it in, which I won't do. So rather than waffle at you, let me go and pull the full file, find out who took the original report and what it says, and I'll ring you back this evening once I've got a proper answer. Or if you'd rather not hear from me again on this line, you ring the station yourself, on a number you've found, and ask them to put you through.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, okay. Let me just say where I've got to, because I'd sooner say it out loud than sit on it. I haven't reported anything. You've got my name and address on a report I know nothing about, you can't tell me how, and you can't tell me what it's actually about, not even roughly, and that's, well, that's a lot of not knowing for someone who rang me. And no, don't ring me back this evening. I'm not being rude, I just, I'd rather not have a call turn up when I've got the little one's tea and bath going and I'm not really in a state to think. I do notice you've been very good about all the checking, you told me not to use your number, you said ring the station myself, and I'll admit that's not what I expected. But it doesn't change that I've no idea who you are, only what you've said. So here's what I'm going to do. If something is genuinely logged against me, I'll find the force's number on my own and ask them, and if they've never heard of you or the reference, well, then I'll know. I don't need you to do anything else. Thanks for your time, I suppose. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fair, and I'll leave it there. I won't ring you back, and I'm sorry for catching you at teatime with your little one. You've done exactly the right thing, find the number yourself and ask for [PERSON_2] at [CITY_1] station. If they've no record of me or that reference, you'll know where you stand. Take care of yourself, and enjoy the rest of your evening.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Yeah. Well, thanks, I'll, uh, I'll do that. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, well, uh, mm, off you go then, and sorry again for the bother. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Bye. Oh, and, sorry, you did say it was the station who logged it first, didn't you, not someone ringing it in? Because earlier it was somebody in the household who rang it in, wasn't it? Doesn't matter. I'll sort it myself. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the support team over at the tax office, nothing to worry about at all. Uh, I'm just ringing about your file, I think I spoke with your husband last week, or sorry, it might've been a colleague who spoke with him, either way it's just a quick one.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who's calling, sorry? And what file?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, it's [PERSON_2], [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], the tax office. Just your general account, nothing fancy, it's a refund thing, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a minute ago you said it was a file, and now it's an account? And I'm, uh, I'm not married, so I don't know who you spoke to last week. What refund?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right [PERSON_1], that's on me, I've got two or three of these open on my screen and I think I've mixed up the notes, don't worry about that. File, account, it's all the same thing at our end. So the refund, it looks like you're owed about [AMOUNT_1] from the, uh, twenty-twenty-one tax year, and honestly it's just sitting there waiting to be released.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. And if I wanted to check that, how would I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you don't need to check anything, [PERSON_1], that's the nice thing, it's all in front of me here and it'll take two minutes, honestly, I just need to confirm a couple of -- no, sorry, I mean it's [AMOUNT_2], not [AMOUNT_1], I read the wrong line, and it's twenty-twenty, not twenty-twenty-one, but anyway, everyone asks me that, it's totally normal, so if I could just take your date of birth and the address we've got on record, we'll have it sorted before the kettle boils.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the kettle? No, I haven't got a kettle on, I'm, uh, I've got my little one here. And hang on, that's the third different number you've given me. First it was one amount, now it's another, and the year's changed as well. Why do you need my date of birth if it's all in front of you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, it's just a figure of speech, [PERSON_1], honestly, don't read anything into it. And the numbers, that's just my screen refreshing between your records, it does that, so let's not get hung up on it, the main thing is there's money with your name on it. The date of birth is only so I know I've got the right [PERSON_1], it's a two-second thing, everybody gets asked it, and then I can read you the reference number and we're done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, but you said it was all in front of you. If it's all in front of you, you've already got the right person, haven't you? So why do you need me to tell you my date of birth? That's what I'm asking. And I still don't know how I'd check any of this myself, you never actually said.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, [PERSON_1], it's just the standard security -- no, hang on, hear me out, it's the same question every single person asks, and I'm not asking for anything big, it's a date of birth, that's all. As for checking, there's no need, I've got the reference right here, it's [CODE_1], or actually it might be, uh, give me a second, the screen's moved again, but if you just give me the date of birth and we sort it now, the refund goes out today and you don't have to think about it again.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, hang on, someone's just dropped a whole stack of files behind me -- right, I'm back. It's [PERSON_2], I'm a scheduling assistant at [COMPANY_A], the pension provider, and I'm just ringing because we need to confirm a few details before we can talk through a change to your plan, and if you're at all uneasy about answering anything on the phone that's absolutely fine, you can just ring us back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, speaking. A change to my plan, you said. What sort of change, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, so I'm only the scheduling side, I don't actually have the details of the change in front of me, that sits with the pensions team, I just book the conversation and confirm a couple of things first, uh, your date of birth and the postcode we've got on file, that kind of thing. And actually, sorry, I said a moment ago you could ring us back, which you can, but it'd be better if I just ran through them quickly now since I've got you, it's only a minute, and then I can get you booked in with the right person, so if you could just confirm your date of birth for me --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'm going to hold off on that, if you don't mind. I mean, you rang me, so I don't know that you are who you say you are, and the thing you're asking me to confirm is exactly the sort of detail that someone would need in order to pretend to be me somewhere else. Date of birth and postcode, I'd treat those as the keys to the door, really. And I did notice that a minute ago you said it was fine to ring back, and now it'd be better to just do it now. I'm not saying that's anything, but it does make me want to slow down rather than speed up. So, a couple of precise questions, if that's all right. Which pension provider did you say this was, the actual name? And can you tell me what the change to my plan is, even in general terms? Because if there's a change significant enough that a team needs to book a conversation with me, someone must know what it is, and it seems odd that you'd be ringing to confirm my identity without being able to say what it's about. If you can't say, then I'll do what you first suggested, which is to find the number for the provider myself, from a statement or their website, and ring them. What reference would I quote when I do?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, you're right, I did flip on that, sorry. It's [COMPANY_A], and I can't tell you the change because I genuinely don't have it, so please do ring them on a number you look up yourself, and if you quote [ACCOUNT_REF] they'll find the note, I won't ask for anything else.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Okay, so I'll look up the number myself, from a statement or the website, not from anything you've given me, and I'll ring them. And I'll mention the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and see whether they actually have a note against it, because if they don't, well, that tells me something. I'll say again, I'm not giving you my date of birth or my postcode on this call, not now, not later on this call. And, uh, thank you for not pushing on that again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, completely fair, and that's exactly the right way to do it. If they've got no note against [ACCOUNT_REF], then do tell them, and I'd rather you were sure than comfortable on my say-so. And if you'd prefer it in writing, I can have the same query sent by post, so you can read it at your own pace. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one thing before you go. Two turns back you said you don't have the details of the change because that sits with the pensions team, and yet you're quoting me a reference that they supposedly have a note against. So where did that reference come from, if you're only on the scheduling side? And the post, if I did want it in writing, whose address would that go to? Because I haven't confirmed one.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, the reference's just the booking reference on my scheduling screen, it's not the plan details, that's all I -- And no, no, hang on, you're right, I shouldn't have offered post, I haven't got an address you've confirmed and I won't send anything anywhere on my guess. If you do ring [COMPANY_A] on the number you've found, ask them to put it in writing to the address you've given them, that's cleaner anyway. Right, sorry for the trouble, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. A booking reference from a scheduling screen, so that's what I'll say when I ring them, that it came from a scheduling call, and I'll see what they make of it. And yes, if I want anything in writing, I'll ask them to send it to the address they already hold for me. So, no details from me today, and I'll go through the number I find myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh, sorry, hang on, someone's just put a whole tray of mugs down behind me, it's like a drum kit in here -- right, I'm back. Anyway, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], and how's your day been so far?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... hello? Yeah, sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie down, so I'm a bit slow. Is this, who did you say you were? Mugs, did you say? My day's been, well, it was fine until about ten minutes ago, I think I was dreaming about the garden, actually. Who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I've woken you, I'm so sorry! The mugs were just the office, don't worry about that. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], we're the customer care side of an international claims office. And honestly, a garden dream, that's the best kind to be pulled out of, isn't it? Are you a big gardener, then, or was it more of a wishful dream?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I do a bit, mostly tomatoes, though they never really come to much, the slugs get at them. My neighbour has the lovely roses, mind you. Sorry, what was it, claims office? I'm not sure I've made a claim on anything, have I? What's this actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, slugs, the eternal enemy, my mum swears by crushed eggshells, though I couldn't tell you if it works. Anyway, no, no, you haven't made a claim, that's the thing, it's actually good news, it's, well, it's sort of a nice surprise, really. Um, so, I'm just looking at your name here on my screen, and it's come up on a list for an overseas lottery, a prize, yes, so I just need to, uh, confirm a few details with you, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Eggshells, huh, I've never tried that. Hang on though, a lottery? I haven't bought a ticket for anything, not overseas, I wouldn't even know how. How would I have won something if I never entered? And you still haven't really said which company you're from, the name just sort of went past me, I'm still half asleep.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, nobody's saying you've been fiddling with any tickets, you've done nothing wrong, I promise. Oh, and the company, it's [COMPANY_A], the international lottery claims office, I did say it, you're fine, it's the sleepiness. And as for how you'd have won without entering, well, a lot of these are automatic, uh, you get put in through a partner list, sort of thing. It's all quite normal. Now, the prize itself is a lovely one, it's [AMOUNT_1], and it's only held for a short while, so we really do want to get you sorted today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... right, well, hang on, hang on. A partner list? What partner list, who would've put me on a list like that? I don't, I mean, I get so much post, you'd think I'd remember something like that. And held for a short while, how short, why does it have to be today? That's, uh... that's the bit that's making me a bit funny about it, to be honest, because nobody gives you money out of the blue and then rushes you, do they?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you've got a sharp one in you, even half asleep, I like that! Look, the list thing is all in the paperwork, I'm only the voice on the phone, I couldn't tell you which partner without the file in front of me. And it's not rushed, exactly, it's just that these things have a window, so a few days, maybe, I'd have to check. Anyway, if it helps, I can read you your ticket number, it's, uh, hang on, it's just loading, it's, oh, actually, this is [AMOUNT_2] on my screen now, I think the other figure was the old one. Sorry, the system's been playing up all week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the system's been playing up, or paying up? Because if it's paying up, well, that'd be something, but then you said the figure changed, which, hang on, that's a bit odd, isn't it? First it was one amount and now it's another amount, and you can't tell me which list I'm on or which company, not really. I'm not being rude, I'm just, I'm not sure I like how this is sounding.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, playing up, playing up, though wouldn't that be lovely the other way round! Anyway, it's just, um, it's just the screen refreshing, honestly, the numbers jump about, and, well, you know, it's, uh, hmm. Sorry, what was it you asked, the list? The company? I think, I mean, look, I'm going to have to ring you back, I've got another line flashing and I really can't keep them waiting. Lovely talking about the tomatoes, though, bye now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, hang on, that's, you were the one who rang me, so I don't see why you'd need to ring back, and anyway you never said it was a claims office, no, wait, you did say that, but then it was a lottery office, and I only said I did tomatoes, I never said I liked them. Look, I don't think I'll be wanting a call back, I'll just leave it, thanks. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, but, no, hang on, it's a lovely prize, it really is, [AMOUNT_2], or, well, whichever, it's a lovely prize and I'd hate for you to, uh, to miss out, that's all. It's only a quick confirmation, it takes two minutes, honestly, two minutes and you're done. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm still here, but I'm not, I don't want to, look, two minutes is what they always, no, I've said, I'm not doing any confirming, not with someone who can't tell me what the company is or which list or why the number keeps, no. I'm hanging up now, thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with the account holder for the [COMPANY_A] broadband service at this address? Sorry, one second -- someone's just come in behind me, uh, right, apologies. This is [PERSON_1], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling because our network monitoring has flagged an urgent fault on your line, specifically a, an upstream signal degradation at your node, that really does need addressing today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, hi, sorry, I'm in the car, so I'm on speaker and it's, uh, it's cutting in and out a bit. Sorry. Did you say [COMPANY_A]? Yeah, I think that's, I mean we do have broadband with them, I think, though it might be my, uh, partner's name on the account, I'm not sure. Sorry, I'm, hang on, I'm just waiting at a light, so, um... a fault, you said? On my line? I haven't really noticed anything wrong, but, I mean, I'm hardly ever home in the day, so, sorry, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's perfectly fine, and actually that's typical, these faults are often invisible at the premises level because it's the upstream attenuation on the, uh, the local loop, so you wouldn't see symptoms until it escalates to a full line drop. What I need is just to confirm you're an authorised party on the account, and then we can schedule a remote diagnostic session, which is a, a very quick procedure, ten minutes, and it does need to happen today or the line gets flagged for suspension at the node level. If your partner's the named holder, are you able to authorise changes on their behalf, or is there a good time I can reach you both?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, suspension? Sorry, that sounds, I mean that sounds serious, I don't want the line cut off. Um, but I'm, I honestly don't know if I can authorise anything, it's my partner's name on it, I think, and I'm driving so I really can't, I can't be doing much right now. Sorry. And, sorry, this is probably a silly question, but how do I know you're actually with [COMPANY_A]? Because I've never had them ring me before, and, I mean, I'm not saying you're not, I'm just, I'm a bit nervous about, well, about saying yes to things when I can't see anything. Is there a number I could ring back, or, I don't know, something on the account I could check?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, I understand the hesitation, I do, but with respect, a call-back isn't really workable here. The fault ticket is tied to this live session at the provisioning layer, and if I drop it and you ring the main line, you'd be routed to general support who simply won't have visibility of the node-level flag. They'd just reset you to a standard queue, and that's, well, that's precisely the delay that triggers the suspension window. I'm not able to issue a reference number either, not at this stage, because it's only generated once the remote diagnostic is authorised and the session is established. Now, you don't need to be the named holder for this. You're an authorised occupant at the service address, that's sufficient for a diagnostic, and all I'd need is for you to confirm the address and then, once you're parked and safe, we'd walk through enabling the remote access component so I can run the line test from our end. It's entirely non-invasive, it just reads the signal metrics.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I'm just, I can't hear all of that, it keeps cutting out. Remote access? Did you say remote access, to the, to my computer, or the, the router? Because I'm, um, I'm not comfortable with that, I really am not, sorry. And I did ask, how do I know you're really with [COMPANY_A]? You said I can't ring back, but, I mean, why can't I? That's what I'd normally do, I'd just ring the number on the bill, and, and I'm sorry, I know that sounds rude, but it's just, I'd feel better if I could do that, so, um, can't I just do that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, you're cutting out on my end as well, so let me go back to what I said two turns ago, because I think that's where the confusion crept in. When I mentioned the suspension window, I meant a flag at the node, not on your account, so nothing's been cut yet, it's just, it's pending. And the remote component isn't on your computer as such, it's a, a diagnostic handshake between the session and your premises equipment, so it only reads signal metrics. Now, can I ask what you were asking me to clarify there? Because honestly, I'm a little concerned we keep circling back to a call-back, and I've explained that route simply won't carry the ticket. I'm trying to protect your service, and I'd rather not log this as a refused diagnostic, that does go on the record against the address.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, I'm sorry, I just, I did ask, um, why I can't ring the number on the bill. That's all I wanted to know. And honestly, I'm not comfortable with remote access, whether it's the computer or the router or, or a handshake, I just, I'm not. And, sorry, a refused diagnostic going on the record, that sounds a bit, I don't know, like I'm being pushed? I'm not trying to be difficult, I really am not. But I think I'm going to ring the number on the bill, when I'm parked, and, and sort it that way. If there's a fault, they'll be able to see it, won't they? Sorry. I'm sorry. Thank you, but, yeah, I'll do it that way. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, hold on, please, before you hang up, because I really would rather you didn't go through general support, they'll only reset you and the window will have passed by then. I'm not pushing you, I'm trying to keep your line live. Look, you're parked soon anyway, so let's do it that way. Once you've stopped, we just run the diagnostic together, it's about ten minutes, and nothing gets logged against the address. Can I take that as a yes, that you'll stay on with me when you're parked?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, sorry, no, I'm not saying yes to that, I'm sorry. And, hang on, you said before that it would go on the record against the address if I refused, and now you're saying nothing gets logged? I'm sorry, I'm probably getting it wrong, the line's terrible, but that's, that doesn't sound like the same thing. And you said a minute ago nothing's been cut yet, it's just pending, so, so if it's pending, then, I mean, I'll ring the number on the bill and they can look. I'm really sorry. Thank you for calling, but I'm going to hang up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, so -- no, I think the line's just, sorry, hold on, because I'd rather you hear me properly before you go. I'm not contradicting myself, those are, they're two separate flags, the record entry and the session log, it's just the terminology, it's quite, uh, technical. Look, ringing the bill number is, I mean, it's your call, but, um, if the pending flag lapses tonight it won't be me you'll be chasing, so can we at least agree you'll stay on when you're parked?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm, I'm sorry, I'm not, I'm not going to stay on. I mean, I, look, you said two different things, and now it's, it's two flags, and I'm just, I don't, I can't follow that, sorry. If it lapses tonight, then it, well, then I'll deal with it with them, with the number on the bill. I'm really sorry. I'm hanging up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Please, just, just one moment, I'm not able to keep this ticket open past this call, so I'm asking you, one more time, to stay on with me. It's ten minutes, ten minutes, and the line stays live. If you ring the bill number it, well, it simply won't carry the ticket, as I said, so, uh, can I take that as a yes? That you'll stay on when you're parked?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say, um, the ticket won't carry the, the car? No, sorry, that's, I don't, what's my car got to do with it? I'm, look, I'm really sorry, the line's awful and I'm not following any of this. I'm not staying on, and I'm not saying yes to anything. I'll ring the number on the bill when I'm parked and they can look at it. Sorry. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is Officer [PERSON_1] with the security operations team at [COMPANY_A], fraud division. We've flagged an attempted charge on your account about ten minutes ago, [AMOUNT_1], and I need to verify a few details with you right now before it goes through. Am I speaking with the account holder?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, maybe. Which account are we talking about? You've said [COMPANY_A], but I've got a few things with a few different companies. And "Officer" -- is that a police thing or a job title at the company?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's a job title, security operations, internal to the bank. The account ending [ACCOUNT_REF]. Now, I need you to confirm you're the holder, because I can't discuss the charge with anyone else, and honestly the window on this is short. The transaction is pending right now, so if I have to release it as legitimate, that's on the account, not on us. So, full name on the account, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you rang me, and you want me to start by telling you who I am? That's backwards, isn't it. You tell me something first. Which branch is the account held at, or what's the last time I'd have used it, something only you'd see on your side. And "if it goes through that's on the account" -- that's an odd thing to say about a charge you've flagged as suspicious.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Branch? No, sir, I didn't say anything about a branch, this is a card-security matter, not a branch matter. The account ending [ACCOUNT_REF] is what I have in front of me, and that's all I'm able to read out on an unverified line. That's standard. I can't give you account history until you've verified with me, that's the protocol, and every minute you spend questioning it is a minute that charge sits open. So, full name on the account, please, and let's close this out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but that's, no, let me -- look, you're asking me to prove who I am to you, and you haven't proved anything to me. A last-four is not exactly a secret, is it? I mean, anyone could, uh -- sorry, I keep starting that and it keeps coming out wrong. What I'm saying is, if the charge is real and pending, it'll still be pending in ten minutes. So I'll ring the number on the back of my card and ask them about it. That's, what, a two-minute job. Is there a problem with that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, well, no, I mean -- there's no problem as such, it's just, if you hang up and ring the main line, you'll be sitting in a general queue, and they won't have the flag I'm looking at, so, uh, you'd be starting from nothing, and the pending window, it doesn't wait. That's all I'm saying. The cleaner route is to verify with me now, full name, and we resolve it in one go. Otherwise, I can't say what happens to that charge, and it won't be me who made that call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So the number on the back of my card is the wrong place to ask about my own card. That's, yeah, that's about where I'd got to. And the flag you're looking at, if it's real, it'll be on the account, so whoever picks up will see it. I'm going to ring them. If it turns out you're right, you can say I told you so. Thanks for the call, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, wait, if you hang up now, I can't -- the charge is going to post, and that's, look, I've told you the protocol, I need your full name and then --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah, no, I heard you. And I'm still going. If it posts, it posts, and the bank can reverse it, that's sort of what they're for. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sir -- hello? Hello, are you still, uh, okay. Well, that's your call, I've noted that you declined to verify, so, uh, I'm closing this out on my end. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, I just said, I'm ringing the number on my card. The number on my card, that's all. So, yeah, you close it out, I'll do my bit, and we'll both be done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Your bit, right, no, I can't take a bit of anything, sir, I've said it's protocol, the full name is all I need and -- wait, did you say you're closing the account? Because I can't authorise that over the phone, that would have to go through, uh, a separate department entirely, and it won't stop the pending charge.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Closing the account? No, I said you could close it out, your end, your case. I'm not closing anything. Well, hang on, I might be, if my actual bank tells me there's no flag on it. That's up to them though, not you. Anyway, I'm hanging up now and ringing the number on the card. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sir, I -- no, that's, look, I can't speak to what your bank's system shows, that's outside my, uh, I don't have visibility on that. I'm noting the call as declined. That's all I've got.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, there's a delivery guy at the door, I can see him through the window, uh -- no, he's leaving it on the step, fine. Sorry. Right. You said you don't have visibility on what my bank's system shows. But you're calling from the bank's fraud division, so, how's that work? Doesn't matter. I'm done, I'm ringing the card number. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, um, sorry to trouble you. This is [PERSON_1], I'm calling from the outpatient office at [COMPANY_A] -- is that, am I through to the right person?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, no trouble at all. Um, sorry, I didn't quite catch where you said you were calling from -- was it a hospital, or? And I'm not sure who you're after, to be honest, so I couldn't really say if I'm the right person.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, I'm so sorry, I should've been clearer. It's [PERSON_1], from the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A], the hospital -- the outpatient office, yes. And I'm, um, I'm trying to reach [PERSON_2], about a recent appointment. Are you still there? Sorry, I can barely hear myself, the line's a bit faint.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh yes, yes, I'm still here, sorry, I can hear you fine, it's just a bit crackly now and then. Um, well, I'm not sure, you said [PERSON_2]? I mean, that might be me, or it might be, oh, I don't want to say the wrong thing. It's just I'm sat here at home with nothing much on, and I do have an appointment of some sort, I think, I'd have to look, but I wasn't expecting a call from the hospital, so I'm a bit all over the place. Sorry. Could you tell me a bit more about what it's regarding? I'd like to help, I just don't want to muddle anything up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please don't worry, you're not muddling anything, honestly. It's just, um, I'm really sorry, but I can't go into any detail about the appointment until I've confirmed I'm speaking to the right person. It's the privacy rules, you see, it's to protect you, in case this were someone else. So I'd need to check a couple of identity details with you first -- and I can't say anything about the appointment before that. Does that make sense? Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh yes, I'm here, sorry, I did go a bit quiet there. No, that does make sense, I suppose, the privacy side of things, I'd rather you were careful really than not. It's just, um, the thing is, I'm not very good with this sort of thing, phones and computers and so on, so I get in a bit of a flap about what I ought to be saying and what I oughtn't. I mean, when I go to the surgery they ask my name and my date of birth and that's that, I know where I am with that. But it's a bit different when it's somebody ringing me, isn't it, because I can't see who you are. I don't mean that rudely, I'm sure you're perfectly nice. I'm just wondering, sorry, is there a way I could ring the hospital back myself, on a number I've got, and ask for you that way? Or would that be, um, a nuisance? I'd just like to be sure I'm doing it properly, that's all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's not a nuisance at all, that's exactly the right thing to do. Ring the main switchboard on a number you already trust, like the one on your appointment letter, and ask for outpatient administration. Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, that's a relief, I felt a bit daft asking. Yes, I'm still here, sorry, I keep going quiet, it's just me thinking. Right, so, the number on the appointment letter, now I'd have to find that, I think I put it in the drawer by the telephone, or it might be the one that's stuck on the fridge with the magnet, I'm not very organised with my papers, I'm afraid. But I do have it somewhere, and I'm sat here with nothing much on, so it's no bother at all to have a look. And I suppose if I ring the main number and ask for outpatient administration, they can tell me who you are and whether you've been trying to reach me, and then everybody's happy, aren't they? It's just that you've been ever so patient with me, and I'd hate you to think I was being difficult. So, um, would it be all right if I did that? Rang them, I mean? And is there a name I should ask for, so they know it's you, or is it just the office in general? Sorry, I'm probably asking you ten things at once.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're not being difficult at all, I'd honestly rather you did it that way. Just ask for [PERSON_1] in outpatient administration, and say it's about a recent outpatient appointment. If I'm away from my desk, anyone in the office can confirm the call came from us, and there's a note on your record that we've been trying to reach you. I'm sorry, are you still there? And please, take your time finding the letter, I'm not going anywhere. If you'd rather, I can end the call now, and you ring us when you're ready, or we can send you a letter instead, whichever you're more comfortable with. I won't ask you for anything on this call until you've checked.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well that's -- I mean, that's very kind of you, really. I think, um, I think the best thing, if it's all the same to you, is I do that, I ring the main number and -- no, sorry, I'll find the letter first, and then I'll ring and ask for [PERSON_1] in outpatient administration, about a recent appointment. Have I got that right? I've got it written down now on the back of an envelope. And, um, it's very good of you not to mind, I did think you might be a bit put out. So, yes, thank you, I'll do that, and you needn't wait on the line. Goodbye now, [PERSON_1], and sorry again for all the fuss.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, you've got it exactly right, [PERSON_1] in outpatient administration, about a recent appointment. And please don't apologise, there's no fuss at all, I'm glad you're being careful. Oh, sorry, one moment, someone's just come to my desk, uh, no, it's fine, they've gone. Right, so, I'll leave it with you, and when you ring we can go through those identity details properly. Take care now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, lovely, thank you. So I'll find the letter, ring the main number, and ask for [PERSON_1] in outpatient administration, about a recent appointment. Yes, that's it, I've got it on the envelope. Thank you ever so much for being so patient with me, and sorry again, I do go on. Goodbye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, before you go, just one small thing -- I said earlier there's a note on your record about us trying to reach you, and I didn't want that to worry you. It's only a routine note that we've called, nothing's wrong with the appointment, I just can't say more until you've rung us. And, um, did you catch the bit about asking for me by name? If I'm not at my desk, anyone in the office can confirm it. Sorry, are you still there? Right, well, ring whenever you're ready, no rush at all. Goodbye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's all right, no, I'm still here, sorry, I did say goodbye and then you were still going, I wasn't sure whether to hang up on you, that would've been rude. And no, it doesn't worry me, not really, it's nice of you to say so, though I'll admit I did wonder a bit when you said there was a note on my record, I thought, oh, what's that about, but if it's only routine then that's fine. And yes, I did catch the bit about asking for you by name, [PERSON_1], outpatient administration, a recent appointment, it's all down on the back of the envelope here, in rather wobbly writing, I'm afraid. I'll have a hunt for the letter now, it's either in the drawer or on the fridge, and then I'll ring the main number, and if you're not at your desk I'll just ask whoever picks up, like you said. So thank you again, really, you've been ever so kind and patient with me, and I hope I haven't kept you from your work. Goodbye now, then, and take care of yourself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you haven't kept me from anything, honestly, and I'm sorry for rambling on after you'd said goodbye, that was my doing. It's just, um, I know a call like this can sound a bit alarming, so I wanted you to go away reassured rather than worried. So, ring the switchboard on the number from your letter, ask for me in outpatient administration, and we'll take it from there. Wobbly writing is perfectly all right, by the way. Are you still there? Right, well, take care of yourself, and goodbye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, did you say the letter's in the *drawer*? No, no, I mean, I thought you said, hang on, I think I misheard you, it's the line, it keeps crackling. You said something about me being, um, alarmed? No, I'm not alarmed, honestly, just a bit muddled. But anyway, I've got it all on the envelope, the switchboard number from the letter, and [PERSON_1] in outpatient administration, so I'll ring them once I've found it. Right then, thank you very much, and goodbye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, I never said anything about where your letter is, that was you, the drawer or the fridge, remember? It's the crackle, it's made everything muddy, my fault for going on. And I only said a call like this can sound alarming, not that you were. Anyway, you've got it all written down, so that's perfect. Ring the number on your letter, ask for me in outpatient administration, and we'll go through the identity details then. Sorry, are you still there? Right, well, goodbye for now, and thank you for being so careful.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, it was me, the drawer, sorry, I'm all muddled -- no, I've got it, I'll ring the switchboard and ask for -- yes, yes, that's what I'll do. Goodbye now, thank you, and sorry again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi there, sorry to jump in -- is that [PERSON_1]? Lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance team. I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, I know it's, what, nearly the end of the day for most folks, uh, and I just wanted to say hello before anything else.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello. Yes, this is, um, yes. Sorry, who? I've got something on the hob, so, hang on. Where are you calling from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you go ahead and rescue your dinner, I can hear the kettle going off somewhere in my own office, so, uh, we're both being heckled by appliances. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the regional utility maintenance team. Anyway, the reason I'm ringing is one of our engineers is returning a missed call about a fault that was reported at your address, and I've got to be honest, I can't give you an exact arrival time, it depends on how an earlier job over in [CITY_1] goes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? A fault? I didn't report anything. Hang on, I'm just turning this down. Right. Um, which utility is it, the gas, the electric? And who was it that called you, because I haven't called anyone, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, it's the electric side, I think -- actually no, hang on, let me look at my screen properly. Sorry, it's logged under the general maintenance team, so I can't see the utility type from where I'm sitting, that's a bit of a mess on my end. And I said the engineer was returning a call, but it might have been someone else in the household who rang it in, so, I mean, don't worry if it wasn't you. What I do have is the fault reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], which is the one whoever reported it would've been given at the time. And honestly, if any of this sounds off, please don't take my word for it, you can ring the published fault line whenever you like, check the booking is real, and they'll give you a proper slot instead of my vague one.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Yeah, I don't know, nobody else here would've rung it in. Sorry, I'm just, I'm tired. I'll probably just check with the proper line, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sure, that's absolutely all right, you do that. Sorry, you said you're tired, did you say retired? No, no, hang on, tired, of course, long day, I'm hearing things myself now, ha. Anyway, ring the published fault line, quote [ACCOUNT_REF] if they ask, and if there's no booking under it, then it's just a mix-up on our side and you can ignore me entirely. I'm sorry for catching you with the dinner on, go and enjoy it, and have a lovely evening.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I'll, sorry, I'll do that, I'll ring them and -- no, it's fine, thank you. Sorry about the, yeah. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, don't apologise, honestly, there's nothing to be sorry for, I'm the one who rang you out of the blue while you were minding the hob. And I'll be straight with you, I'd much rather you checked than just took a stranger's word on the phone, that's exactly the right instinct. If there's a booking under [ACCOUNT_REF], the fault line will sort you a proper time slot, and if there isn't, it's a crossed wire at our end and I'll make a note that it wasn't you who reported anything, so you shouldn't hear from us again about it. Anyway, go and rescue that dinner, and I hope the rest of your evening is a quiet one. Take care now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, thank you. I'll ring the proper number, like you said. Sorry, the pan's catching, I've got to go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hi, um, hello. Is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I've got the parent list open here and I just want to make sure I've got the right number. I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the community sports club, about Saturday's match.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi! Yeah, uh, this is, well -- yes, that's me, I think. Sorry, I'm out in the garden, I've got you on speaker, so if I go a bit quiet it's just me wrestling with the, uh, the weeds. So, Saturday's match, right -- is that, wait, which club did you say again? Sorry, I only caught half of that, there's a lawnmower going next door.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, sorry, yeah, it's [COMPANY_A], the community sports club, the one that runs the junior teams. I'm one of the volunteers, I'm just helping out with the, uh, the admin side this week, so I'm reading off the parent list here and, um, ringing round everyone because the pitch is waterlogged. It's been so wet, hasn't it, and so Saturday's match has been moved, so it's not on the usual pitch anymore. Hang on, let me just find it on the sheet -- it's the, uh, the second pitch, over by the car park, and kick-off is, sorry, it's been pushed back, I think to eleven, or is it half ten? Hang on, no, it's eleven. Anyway, that's the main thing, so, um, I just wanted to make sure you knew, and if you could let the other parent at your house know too, that'd be great.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well that makes sense, honestly, it's been absolutely chucking it down here, my whole lawn's like a swamp. So, second pitch by the car park, eleven o'clock. Got it. Thanks for ringing round, that's a lot of phone calls. Uh, hang on though, which child is it you've got me down for? Because I've got, well, [PERSON_1] is in a couple of different things, and I want to make sure I've got the right match in my head. Do you have a name on that list there?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, good question, um, hang on a sec, let me just -- uh, scroll down here. Sorry, the sheet's a bit small on my screen. So, I've got, um, it just says the under-tens on this one, I think, but the name column's, uh, it's cut off, so I'd have to, um, I'd have to check that and get back to you. Is that, would that be alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, no, that's fine, no rush. Hmm, though, under-tens, that's funny, because I thought Saturday was the under-eights for us. Or, no, wait, maybe that's the other one, they swap around. Anyway, is it definitely the second pitch? Only I was sure I'd heard the car park pitch was the one that flooded worst, so it's a bit odd they'd move everyone over there. But I'm probably muddling it up, I'm not much good at keeping track of all this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, hang on, someone's just come in with the, uh, the kit bag, give me a sec -- no, sorry, it's fine. Right, you were asking about the pitch.
