Hmm, now you say that, I, uh, I might have that wrong, because I'm only reading off what [PERSON_3] sent round, and I'm not totally sure which pitch it said. Tell you what, don't go on my word, check the club page, [URL_1], or ring the club number, [PHONE_1], and they'll have the proper pitch and the right age group for you. Sorry, I know that's not much help, I'm still getting the hang of this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's fine, honestly, that's probably the safest thing, I'd rather check than turn up at the wrong pitch with a soggy kid. So I'll look at the club page, and, hmm, the number you said, I didn't catch it properly with the mower going, but I've got the club's number saved somewhere anyway, I'll ring that. And you were going to get back to me about which child it was, weren't you? Don't worry about it, I'll just sort it with the club directly. Thanks for ringing round though, bit of a thankless job, that. Right, I'd better get back to these weeds before it chucks it down again. Bye now, take care!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's absolutely fine, honestly, probably best you do. Sorry again about the muddle, I'll, um, I'll have a proper look at the list and make sure whoever's next gets the right details. And, uh, actually, hang on, I said it was the second pitch earlier, but I think that might be the one that's flooded, so definitely check before you go. Right, yeah, okay, sorry for taking up your time. Enjoy the garden, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're fine, honestly, it's all a bit of a muddle with this weather, isn't it? Uh, well, um, thanks again, and good luck with the rest of your list, hope the next lot are a bit quicker on the uptake than me. Right, bye now, take care!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? I'm calling on behalf of, uh, [PERSON_2], at the customs desk at [COMPANY_A] -- it's about a parcel you've got coming, there's a charge on it, an import, uh, import charge. Sorry, I'm not very good at these calls.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who's this? Customs desk at, um -- hang on, I've got people around me. So you're saying there's a parcel, and there's an import charge on it? I'm, uh, I'm not really expecting anything. Who did you say you were calling for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, I'm calling for [PERSON_2], at the customs desk, at [COMPANY_A] -- no wait, I said that already. Uh, it's a parcel from, um, [COMPANY_B], I think? Or maybe it's a different sender, I've got it written down here somewhere. And it's, uh, it's the clearance on it that's held up, the charge is [AMOUNT_1], and I really don't want it getting sent back because, I mean, someone's waiting on it, you know?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec -- [muffled] no, yeah, just put it on my desk, thanks. Sorry, um. So you don't actually know who the parcel's from? You said [COMPANY_B], then maybe someone else. That's, I mean, that's a bit odd. And you want me to pay [AMOUNT_1] or it gets sent back? How do I know this is real?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I -- that's fair, I'm sorry, I'm not explaining it well. I do have a reference, it's [CODE_1], that's the tracking reference, and you can look it up yourself, it should be on the, uh, the courier's tracking page, you'd see the charge on there too. The reference, [CODE_1], that's the one. And I don't want you paying anything on this call, honestly, I'd, I'd rather you didn't. Check the page first, and then the payment goes through there, on the page, not through me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but -- sorry, can I just -- so I look it up myself, on the courier's page, and pay there, not to you. Right. Which courier, though? You still haven't said, you keep saying maybe this one, maybe that one. And I'm not expecting a parcel at all, so why would I even have a reference? I mean, if I'm not waiting on anything, I'd probably just ring the actual courier, or, uh, check my own orders first.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, no, you're right, that's, that's what I'd do too, honestly. The courier is [COMPANY_A], that's who I'm with, I said [COMPANY_B] earlier but that's, uh, that's just the sender, I think. Or maybe it was the other way round, sorry, I've got my notes in a muddle. It's just that if it sits there much longer it goes back, and, I mean, someone made an effort sending it, so it'd be a shame.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, you said the customs desk at [COMPANY_A] earlier and now it's the courier, and the sender's [COMPANY_B], or the other way round -- I mean, you don't know your own notes. I'm not expecting anything, so I'm going to check my own orders and ring the courier myself, on a number I've looked up. Okay? Thanks for the call, but I'll leave it there. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, wait, I -- okay, yeah, that's fine. That's fair, you do that, ring them on a number you found yourself, I'd want that too. I'm sorry I, uh, muddled it, I really did want to get it right. Take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah. Thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], we spoke briefly last week, or, uh, I think it was the week before -- anyway, I'm following up on the application you put in through our site.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, who? Sorry, hang on -- I'm in a queue here. Application for what? I don't remember speaking to anyone, and you don't even sound sure yourself, "last week, or the week before." What's this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, that's fine, I'll be quick -- it's [COMPANY_A], we're a recruitment agency, and you submitted a CV through our portal for the remote administration role, the, uh, flexible hours one. I'm just confirming a couple of things on the file, so, is this still a good number for you, or, hang on, should I try you later when you're out of the queue?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I didn't apply for anything. Not with you, not through any portal. Where'd you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's on the file, [PERSON_1], I can see the submission right here. Look, if you'd rather not proceed, I'll note it down.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, uh -- "it's on the file." That's not an answer, is it? I asked where you got my number. And I'm not confirming anything, not my name, not my address, nothing, until I know who you actually are. What's the company again? And how do I check you're who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm a security operations officer at [COMPANY_A], and I've already told you that. Verification isn't something we do over the phone, we have protocols. The submission is on file under this number, that's all I'm able to say. Now, the position is fully remote, [AMOUNT_1] a week, and it can start immediately, but there's a one-off onboarding cost that has to be cleared first, so, are you interested or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. First you're a recruitment agency, now you're a security operations officer? Which is it? And I never applied, so there's no job I'm interested in. And a cost I have to pay before I start? No. No, that's not how a real job works. I've had this one tried on me before, I'm not doing it again. I'm done, I'm not paying anyone anything and I'm not confirming a single detail. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Listen to me, [PERSON_1]. I said the cost is a standard requirement, it's on the file, and if you hang up now the position goes to the next candidate and I can't reopen it. Is that what you want? Hello? Hello, are you still --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I heard you. I said I'm done. I said don't ring this number again. I'm not paying anything, I never applied, so the next candidate can have it, I couldn't care less. Don't ring again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Your choice. It's noted on the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, note whatever you like. Take me off your list. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Whatever. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, before you -- just one more thing, [PERSON_1], the file shows the clearance window closes today, so if you'd just let me --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I've said goodbye three times now, so I'm not doing this again. There's no window, there's no file, I never applied for a thing, and you've changed what you are halfway through the call, recruitment agency, then security operations officer, and then you want money up front. I've been caught by this sort of thing before and I'm still angry about it, so no, I'm not going to be hurried by a deadline you've just made up. If there's genuinely something real here, put it in writing to the address you already claim to have on file, and I'll look at it in my own time. Until then, I'm not discussing it, I'm not confirming anything, and I'm putting the phone down. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1] from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], your home internet provider. Um, I'm calling about a fault on your line, and it's... it's fairly urgent, so I'd rather not take much of your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, hello? Sorry, I just woke up, I was having a little lie down. A fault on my line, you said? Compliance team... I thought compliance was the, uh, paperwork people, not the fault people. Who did you say you were again, the compliance team at, sorry, which company? A fault on my line, so, the internet's been fine, I think, I mean I haven't really looked.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it. Compliance does sit a bit apart from the engineers, but when a fault touches a customer's account, we're the ones who make sure it's handled properly. It's [COMPANY_A], your home internet provider, and I'm [PERSON_1]. The thing is, a line can look perfectly fine from your side and still be showing a fault on ours, and those tend to get worse the longer they're left. So if you could just get to your computer for me, I'd like to take a look at it together.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Get to my computer? Oh, I don't know, it's in the other room, I haven't turned it on since, hm, Tuesday maybe. And I'm not really good with that sort of thing, my nephew usually sets it all up. Look at it together how, exactly? Because I never actually, I mean you said it's [COMPANY_A], but I pay my bill to, hang on, is it the same one? I'd have to look at the letter. What is it you want me to do on the computer?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so it's nothing complicated, and I'd walk you through it slowly. There's a small program that lets me see what your line is doing from my end, and I'd just need you to open the computer so we can set that up. And please don't worry about the letter, [COMPANY_A] is your provider, I wouldn't be calling otherwise. It's only that the longer the fault sits there, the harder it gets to put right, so it would help to do it while we're on the phone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A program? Oh, I don't know about that. See, my nephew, he's always telling me never to put anything on the computer unless he's looked at it first, he had a whole speech about it last Christmas, something to do with my sister's neighbour and her bank, I never got the whole story. And I don't love that you won't let me check the letter, because if you were really my provider I'd think you'd just say, oh, go and check, take your time. It's not that I think you're up to anything, I'm just, I've only been awake about five minutes, and now there's a program and a fault and it's urgent, and I can't tell which bit is the actual problem. If there's really something wrong with the line, can't you just send an engineer round? Or I could ring the number on the bill, that seems the sensible thing, doesn't it? Then it wouldn't matter whether it was you or not.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I'd say your nephew gave you very sound advice, and I'm glad he did, because more people ought to be that careful, and I wouldn't want you doing anything you're not comfortable with. And you're right that checking the letter is perfectly reasonable, I'm not stopping you from doing that. It's just that if you ring the general number on the bill, you'll be put through to the customer line, and they won't have the fault notes in front of them, they'll only be able to open a new query, which takes time, and I'd hate for this to sit there while that happens. As for an engineer, uh, that isn't really how this stage works, the engineer visit only gets booked once the fault has been checked remotely, so it does rather start with the computer. I'm not trying to rush you, I'd just... I'd prefer to keep this moving while the fault is still showing on my screen.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well, um, hang on, I'm just, I'm thinking. Let me think about that for a second, because that's, uh, that's a lot of pieces. So the number on the bill can't see your notes, but you can see my line, and the engineer only comes after the computer thing, and it all has to be now, while we're talking. Which is, I mean, it's very tidy, isn't it? Everything points back to me turning the computer on. And you still haven't said what the fault actually is, have you? Not really. Just that it's a fault. I think I'll do what my nephew would do, and ring the number on the bill, and if there's really a note on my account they can find it. Thanks for the call, I suppose, but I'm not doing the computer today. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, I wouldn't say it's quite as tidy as that, it's more that, um, the fault is of a type that's... I mean, I'd have to pull the exact classification up, and, uh, that isn't something I have in front of me on this screen just now. It's, it's a line-level matter, if that helps. Look, I'll, I'll note on the account that you declined, and I can't say what that means for the fault. Good day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, you said it was a fault on my line, that's what I heard, and now it's a line-level matter you can't even pull up, and earlier you said it was all in front of you on your screen. And you said you wouldn't want me doing anything I'm not comfortable with, but now it's what that means for the fault, which sounds a bit like a telling-off, doesn't it? Anyway. I'm ringing the number on the bill. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, someone's just come in, I'm, um... no, it's fine. I didn't mean it as a telling-off, that isn't, I just, I can't speak to what the fault will do, that's all I was saying. I, uh, I really do have to go, I've got another call waiting. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Another cough waiting? Oh, you poor thing, is it a bad one, because my sister had one of those last winter that went on for weeks, honey and lemon didn't touch it. No, wait, you said call, didn't you? Another call. Right. Well, anyway, I've said what I'm going to do, I'm ringing the number on the bill, and you carry on with your other call, or your cough, whichever. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's a call, not a cough, though I do appreciate you asking, and I'm sorry to hear about your sister, that sounds like it was a miserable winter for her. I, uh, I should say I think you're being very sensible, ringing the number on the bill, and I'd never want to talk anyone out of that, and if you do speak to them, then, well, they may or may not have the notes, it does depend on which department you get and what time of day it is and whether the fault has been logged against the account yet, which, I mean, I couldn't promise either way. And if they ask who rang you, you could just say it was [PERSON_1] from the compliance side, although I'd, I'd understand if that doesn't mean much to them. Right. I really must go. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. I'll ring the number on the bill. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, two turns back, when you said I'd told you it was all in front of me on my screen, I, uh, I'm not sure I put it quite like that, I think I said the fault was still showing, which is a slightly different... no. Hm. Look, I really do need to... Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I mean, you did say it was showing on your screen, but fine, never mind, and you also said the computer's where it started, so it's the same thing really. And you know, I think I was wrong about Tuesday, it might have been Wednesday I last turned it on, but that's by the by. I'm ringing the number on the bill, that's all I'm going to do. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, uh, is this -- is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I said, is this [PERSON_1] I'm speaking to? I'm just calling about the account, the one with [COMPANY_A], the electric, um, the electricity account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, I just woke up, I was having a bit of a lie-down. Who -- who is this, did you say? You said something about an account, and then, uh, something before that, about the name, and I didn't catch what company you said. It's the electric, is it? I mean, I've got an electric bill, obviously, everyone has, but I'm not sure which one you mean.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, I didn't mean to wake you, I -- yes, it's the electric, it's [COMPANY_A], that's the one, and I'm, um, I'm not actually with them, I'm just, I'm helping someone there who -- sorry, I mean, they asked me to ring around about some of the accounts, so it's just a quick -- is this [PERSON_1], though? I just want to be sure I've got the right person before I go on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, now you've lost me a bit. You're not with them, but you're helping someone there, and they asked you to ring round? Um... that's -- sorry, I'm still sort of waking up here, give me a second -- that doesn't really sound like... I mean, who is it you're actually with? And why would you need to know if I'm [PERSON_1] before you've even said who you are? I don't know, I've got a kettle I was meant to put on, it's all a bit...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a kettle, no, no, I'm not selling anything, I swear, it's not that kind of -- I'm not with a ketchup company, I mean, a kettle company, I'm sorry, I'm just, I'm doing this badly. It's the electric. It's about your balance, there's an unpaid balance, [AMOUNT_1], and I, um, I really didn't want to ring and worry you, but they told me the power could be cut off within the hour, and I felt awful, I thought somebody should just tell you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Cut off within the hour? Oh, hang on, that's -- no, that doesn't sound right. If it was that bad I'd have had a letter, wouldn't I, or an email, I don't know, my daughter sets up the emails. And you still haven't told me who you actually are, you keep saying you're helping someone and ringing round, but who's the someone? Is it a person at [COMPANY_A], or are you, like, a separate company that does it for them? I mean, I'm not saying you're lying, I'm just, I'm a bit muddled, I've only just got up, but that's a funny way to be told.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not a funny way, I'm just, I'm trying to help you here, and honestly it's a bit hurtful to be, I'm not lying, I'm really not -- the letters, they, they send those out and sometimes they just don't, and there's not time now anyway, it's the hour, so if you could just sort it today, with the, um, the payment, then it's all fine and I don't have to ring back and, I mean, I'd hate for you to be sat there in the dark, it's the cold as well, isn't it, this time of year, and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, can we go back a bit? A minute ago you said you were helping someone there, that they asked you to ring round, and you never said who. That's what I was after, who the someone is, and you've gone straight on to the dark and the cold. And, uh, I'm not trying to hurt your feelings, love, I'm just tired and I don't understand it. If you're not with [COMPANY_A], why would they have you ringing me about the bill? I'd sooner ring them myself, to be honest, on the number on the, the bill. Or my daughter would.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, don't, please don't ring them, there's no time, they'd just put you in a queue and by then it's, it's done, the power's off. I really can't, I'm not able to give you a name, they just said to, um -- it's quicker if it goes through me, and it would have to be, uh, a voucher, or something like that, not the normal way, because the normal way takes days to, to show up on their end, and I --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on. A voucher? Not the normal way? And I'm not to ring them, and you can't even give me a name? Now, I'm not the sharpest first thing after a nap, but that's three things in a row that sound backwards to me. If the electric company wanted paying they'd take it the normal way, wouldn't they, they wouldn't send some stranger round the houses for vouchers. No, I'm not doing that. I'm going to put the phone down and ring them on the number on my bill, and if the power's really going off in an hour, well, they can tell me themselves. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, no, please, I'm only trying to -- it's not even an hour, I mean, it's sooner, it's more like a couple of hours, I think they said, or, no, an hour, I don't -- look, I'm not a stranger, I'm just, I can't really say more than that, I'm sorry, I have to go, I've got another one to ring.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: An hour, a couple of hours, you can't even keep that straight. No. I've heard enough, love. I'm ringing the electric myself, on the number on the bill, and you go and ring your other one. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I -- that's not fair, I was only trying to help, I wasn't -- oh, never mind. Never mind. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say fair? Oh, the fair, no, I haven't been to the fair in years, my knees can't take the walking. Anyway, I'm off to ring the proper number now, and put that kettle on. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I said fair, not -- never mind, it doesn't matter. I've got to go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you said fair, not -- no, hang on, I think I -- well, it doesn't matter, you said so yourself. I'm not, I don't mean to be unkind, I just, if it's -- no. No, I'll ring the proper number and sort it out with them, that's all. Right then, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um... right. Well, uh... yeah. Okay, I'll, I'll let you go, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, well, off you go. And, uh, I did say before that I'd leave the kettle, but it's the first thing I'm doing, so, never mind, that's not your worry. Right, I'm ringing the number on the bill. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, um, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry to trouble you -- it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier. Are you able to talk for a minute? It's about your account, and it's, well, a bit time-sensitive, which is why I'm ringing rather than just writing again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, "writing again"? I haven't had a first letter from anyone, so I'm not sure what you're following up on. And, um, which supplier did you say? I'm fairly sure I'm with somebody else, so you'll have to tell me what the account actually is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, that's fair. I'm with [COMPANY_A], and the account ending [ACCOUNT_REF] shows [AMOUNT_1] overdue, with supply due to be interrupted on the date in the reminder. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here. But you've just told me an account ending in something that's, um, apparently a placeholder, and I never got a reminder with a date on it, so I can't check any of this. Honestly, if supply was about to be cut off at my address, I'd expect the company I actually pay to have mentioned it. So what's the address you've got on file? Just the first line is fine.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm sorry, I shouldn't be the one reading your address out to you, that's the wrong way round, it's -- well, you should be the one to tell me, and, I mean, I'd rather not ask you for it on a call you didn't expect. Um, what I can do is give you the figure from your last bill, [AMOUNT_2], that's the balance it showed, and if that doesn't match what you remember, then please, don't take my word for any of it. Are you still there? I'm only ringing because I'd hate for the supply to be cut off without you knowing, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here. I don't have a last bill from you, though, so there's nothing to match it against. I'll look up the supplier's number myself and ring them. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, that's, that's completely fine, I'd do the same. Um, if you do ring, it's the number on your own bill or your online account, [URL_1], not one I give you, and there's no payment needed on this call, none at all. And if there is a balance, they can set up a payment plan, so it doesn't need to be a worry. Are you still there? I just, I really hope it gets sorted, that's all I wanted.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm still here, I just... um, hang on, I'd already said bye, hadn't I? Look, you're telling me to ring the number on my own bill, which is fine, that's what I'll do. But I don't have a bill from you, so there's nothing to ring about. Right, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, you did, I'm sorry, I should have, I mean -- well, if you're not a customer of ours, then it may be that I've got the wrong, um, the wrong person on my list, and that's my mistake, not yours. I'll note it down so nobody rings you again. Sorry to have bothered you, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh, sorry, the, uh, the dog's just found something it shouldn't have. Right. Yeah, wrong person, fine, no harm done. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I think there's a bit of a delay on the line, bear with me a second. Right, yeah, it's [PERSON_2] here, I'm a support technician with [COMPANY_A], the local police, and I'm just following up on that incident you reported last week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, I -- who is this again? A support technician with the, uh, the local police? And you're following up on an incident I reported last week? I mean, I'm at work right now, and I don't, I'm not sure I even -- what incident are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, totally fair, [PERSON_1], and sorry for catching you at work, that's on me. It's [PERSON_2], I'm a support technician with [COMPANY_A], the local police force, and I help the officers get their case files tidied up. Basically, last week you got in touch to report something, I won't go into the ins and outs over the phone while you're at your desk, but it's the one you reported to us, and the file's just missing a couple of small bits, nothing major, honestly it's about two minutes. And look, there's no pressure at all, if now's a bad time I can ring back, but I'd just ask that you keep the details of the case to yourself for now, as it's still open. Everyone I ring says the same thing, they weren't expecting the call, so you're not being daft at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, so you're saying I reported something to you last week, but you can't tell me what it was? Because that's, I mean, that's a bit odd, isn't it? And you want me to keep it to myself, it's an open case, right, but I still don't know which case you mean. Can you just tell me what it was about, or who the officer was, or -- I don't know, a reference number or something? Because I honestly can't think of anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right to ask, [PERSON_1], that's a fair question, so let me give you something solid. The reference on the original report is [CODE_1], and that should match whatever you were given when you rang it in. The officer who took it is [PERSON_3], and you don't have to take my word for any of it. Ring the station's main number, [PHONE_1], ask for [PERSON_3] by name, and check I'm who I say I am before you tell me a single thing. Oh, and sorry, I said you got in touch with us last week, but actually, hang on, let me look at the file, it might've been the week before. Sorry, I've got a few of these open at once. Honestly, if you'd rather skip the phone altogether, I can have the officer come see you in person or send a letter, whichever's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, [CODE_1] and the officer's [PERSON_3], and I can ring the station on [PHONE_1] and ask for them by name, right? Hm. Sorry, I'm just, I'm trying to sort of take that in with people next to me at their desks. It's good that you're not pushing me to stay on the line, I'll give you that. But the thing that's bugging me is, a minute ago it was last week, and now it might've been the week before, and I still can't think of anything I reported to the police, not last week, not the week before, not this year really. So either I've forgotten something quite big, which I doubt, or the file's got the wrong person on it, or, I don't know, something else is going on. And you still haven't said what it's actually about, even roughly. Is it a theft, a, a break-in, something online? Because if you can't give me even that much, I think I'd rather do what you said, ring the station myself on a number I look up, not the one you read out, and ask them if there's a file under my name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, honestly, that's the best way to do it, [PERSON_1]. Look the station up yourself, don't use the number I gave you, and ask for [PERSON_3] or whoever's on the front desk and quote [CODE_1]. And no, you haven't done anything wrong, you're not in any trouble, it's just a follow-up. As for what it's about, I'm only seeing the admin side of the file here, so the notes just say a vehicle-related report, I think, or, hang on, no, that might be the other one, it could've been something to do with a phone. Sorry, that's me being sloppy, and I know it doesn't help. I don't have the full details in front of me, so let me find out exactly what's on the file and who logged it, and I'll call you back once I've got a proper answer for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, so a vehicle, or a phone, or, I mean... you don't actually know which? Right. Hm. And you'll ring me back, okay, but I don't think I want that, to be honest. No offence, but I'll just look the station up myself and ask about [CODE_1], and if there's really a file under my name they can tell me. So, yeah, I'm going to go and do that now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No offence taken at all, [PERSON_1], that's exactly what I'd do in your shoes. Look the station up yourself, quote [CODE_1], and if there's nothing under your name, then it's on us and I'm sorry for the bother. And hey, if you do want a proper answer on what's on the file, [PERSON_3] can sort that out directly, or I can find out and have it come to you in a letter instead. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, so, just so I've got it straight, I look the station up myself, quote [CODE_1], and if there's nothing under my name then it's a mix-up on your end. Yeah, I think that's what I'll do, and I'd rather it was a letter than another phone call, honestly, because it's hard to think properly with people sat right next to me here. I did sort of expect you to push a bit harder, so thanks for not doing that, but I'll be honest, I'm still not sure what this was. I'll check, and if there's a file somewhere I'll hear about it the proper way. Anyway, thanks for being straight about the details being a bit hazy. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right, [PERSON_1], you've got it exactly. Look the station up yourself, quote [CODE_1], and if there's nothing under your name, then it's a mix-up on our end, and that's on us. And a letter's no bother at all, I'll make a note on the file that you'd rather have it in writing, so nobody rings you at your desk again. Like I say, I'm sorry about the hazy bits, I'd sooner admit that than guess at it, so I'll find out what's actually on the file and get it sent to you properly. Take care now, [PERSON_1], and thanks for your patience.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, I'll -- well, actually, hang on, there's one thing. If you're sending a letter, you'll already have my, my address, so there's no need for me to give you anything else, right? Because I don't want to, I mean, I'm not going to, not on this call. Anyway, I'll look the station up myself and see what they say. Bye now, thanks.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you don't need to give me anything else, [PERSON_1], not today and not on this call. Whatever's on the file will have your address already, so a letter goes to that, and you can ring the station on a number you've looked up yourself to check it. Oh, and one other thing, you asked two turns back about what I meant by it being a mix-up on our end, and just so that's clear, I mean if the station says there's no file under your name, then I've got the wrong person and I'll drop it, no letter, nothing more from me. That's honestly the better way round, so please do check first. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so if the station says there's no file, you drop it, and no letter, no -- sorry, I mean, that's, okay. That's fair, I suppose. I just, I'd still rather you didn't contact me at all until I've, no, let me put it another way, I'll check first, and if there is something, they'll know how to reach me. Okay. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, [PERSON_1], I'll hold off contacting you until you've -- sorry, didn't mean to cut across you. Yeah, no, you check first, and if there's a file, the station'll know how to reach you, so I'll leave it with them. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Yeah. Uh, yeah, that's, that's all right, I suppose. So, you leave it with the station and I'll ring them myself. Okay. Right. I think that's, yeah, that's everything. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, that's, no, that's everything from me too. I'll leave it with the station, and I'll, well, if they've got nothing under your name, then that's the end of it and, sorry, I mean I'll just make a note that you'd rather they dealt with you directly. Thanks for your patience, [PERSON_1], and sorry again for the bother. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. Right. So I ring the station, and you're not contacting me. Yeah. Thanks. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Yeah, it's me, it's -- no, listen, just listen. I need you to know who this is, okay? Come on, you know my voice.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, hang on -- I don't, sorry, I'm not sure I do know your voice? Like, you're saying it's you, but, um, who's "me"? I'm at my desk right now, there's people around, so -- can you just tell me your name?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not doing the name thing, I shouldn't have to. Look, two minutes ago I said you know my voice, and I meant that, I'm not repeating myself. Just take a guess, [PERSON_1] or [PERSON_2], whichever, and we can skip all this. I don't have time for twenty questions, okay? Something's happened and it needs sorting today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec -- no, Dave, that's fine, leave it on my desk -- uh, sorry, what? You want me to guess? I'm not going to guess who you are, that's, I mean that's kind of weird. If something's happened and it's urgent, then just tell me who you are and what it is. So you're saying it's urgent, and it's got to be sorted today, but I still don't know who I'm talking to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I've said this twice now. I'm not going to say it a third time, slower, so listen. It's family, it's a problem, and it can't wait, and every minute you spend on this is a minute it gets worse. I work security at [COMPANY_A], I deal with this kind of thing all day, so believe me when I say I'm not wasting your time. Now, are you going to help me or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Family, a problem, can't wait... right. And I still don't know who you are. I'm not helping with anything until you tell me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Fine. I'm telling you, this is not something I want to say over the phone, and I'd appreciate it if you kept it to yourself, okay? Don't call anyone, don't go asking around, because that's exactly how it gets worse. I just need you to say you'll help me. That's all. Say it, and I'll explain the rest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, you still haven't told me your name, and now I'm supposed to promise to help before I know what it is, and not tell anyone? No. I'm not saying that. That's, honestly, that sounds like exactly the kind of thing you hear about on the news. If it's family, it's family, but I'm not agreeing to anything blind. So, I'm going to hang up now, and if you really are who you say, you can call back and tell me your actual name. Okay? Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait -- no, don't hang up, you're making a mistake here. I said not to go asking around and you're about to -- look, it's a serious situation and I'm telling you, if you walk away from this, that's on you, not me. Hello? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, see, that -- that's on me now? I'm done. I've asked you three times who you are and you won't say, so I'm not doing this. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, hello, is this -- sorry, am I speaking to [PERSON_1]? It's about the, the draw you put your name in at the [COMPANY_A] event, I'm calling because you've, um, you've won something, and I -- oh, sorry, did you say something?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, I didn't -- that was my kid in the background. Who is this, exactly? And what draw? I don't remember putting my name in anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you, uh, you don't remember the kid -- sorry, no, that's not what I -- the draw. Sorry. I'm [PERSON_2], I'm just, I'm helping out for [COMPANY_A], the shop, I'm not, I don't normally do calls like this. It was the little prize draw at the, um, the weekend event, there was a bowl with the entry slips, and your name was drawn. It's nothing big, I just, I really didn't want it to go to waste.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said a minute ago I'd put my name in, and now it's slips in a bowl at a weekend thing. Which is it? Because I honestly don't remember a bowl, and I don't think I was at any event last weekend -- I was here with the kids. And you still haven't said what I've supposedly won.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's the same thing, you put a slip in the bowl, that's what I meant by -- oh, hang on, sorry, someone's just come in the back with a, never mind. Sorry. And, uh, it wasn't last weekend, I got that wrong, it was the one before, the [DATE_1] one, the [COMPANY_A] open day, I've got the date written down here somewhere. I'm, honestly, I'm a bit hurt, I'm only trying to do something nice for you. It's, it's a small hamper, nothing more, and there's nothing to pay, you just come by the shop and pick it up. Could you just, um, confirm your full address so I can put it on the, the collection slip?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, so, the date's changed now too. First it was last weekend, then the one before, and you've got it written down somewhere but you can't, I mean... Sorry, can you hear that? That's, uh, hold on, [PERSON_1], put that down, please. Right. And my address? You rang me, so you've got my name, you've got my number, and you've still not told me which [COMPANY_A] shop, or where it is. Why would you need my address if I'm only collecting it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. No, you're right, you don't need to give me your address, I shouldn't have asked that, that was daft of me. Forget it. I don't need it at all, you just walk in and give your name at the counter. Um, the shop's the [COMPANY_A] one on [STREET_1] in [CITY_1], and the open day was the [DATE_1] one, I had the date wrong earlier, I got muddled, I'm sorry. I'm, I'm not very good at this. They asked me to ring round because they'd run out of time. If you'd rather, don't take my word for it, ring the shop yourself on [PHONE_1] and ask them, they'll tell you there's a hamper under your name. Or just don't bother, honestly, that's fine too. I only thought it'd be a nice surprise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'll find the shop's number myself, not use the one you've just given me. If there's a hamper, it'll still be there. Thanks for ringing, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. Okay. No, that's, that's fair, that's actually the sensible thing to do, and I'm sorry I made such a mess of it. I should've just said the shop and the date straight off instead of, instead of tripping over myself. You look the number up yourself and ask for [PERSON_3], she's the one who ran the draw, she'll know about the hamper. And there's no rush, they'll hold it for a couple of weeks at least. It really is only a little thing, a few bits and pieces from the shop, nothing to pay, nothing to sign up for. I only rang because I hate the idea of a prize sitting there and nobody coming for it. Sorry again for the muddle, and for asking for your address, that wasn't right of me. Thank you for being patient with me, and, um, sorry about the noise at your end, I hope the little one settles. Bye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, I'll -- no, I've got it, I'll look it up myself, thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Great, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the support desk at [COMPANY_A], we're the promotions agency, and I've got some genuinely good news for you today. You've been selected as a winner in our regional prize draw, and I just need a couple of minutes to get you set up so we can get it released.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- no, put that down, not on the sofa -- sorry. Uh, a prize draw? I don't remember entering anything. Which company did you say it was?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No worries at all, [PERSON_1], sounds like you've got your hands full! It's [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency, so we run these regional draws on behalf of a bunch of different brands. And honestly, that's really common, a lot of people don't remember entering, it'll have been a sign-up form or an online entry sometime back, you tick a box and forget about it. Anyway, the good part is there's nothing complicated on your end, I just need to confirm a few details so the prize can be released, it'll take two minutes, tops.

utterances.speaker: receiver
