utterances.text: Yeah, it's [PERSON_3], [COMPANY_A], the sports club, account services is just what they call the volunteer admin line. Nothing to do with money. Saturday's match has moved because the pitch is waterlogged, different pitch and a later kick-off, and I've got to get everyone told before the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, the club normally sends that out through the team group, so I'd rather check it there. What's the new pitch and time?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem, checking the group's fine, that's honestly the better way. So it's [CODE_1] pitch now, kick-off at [AMOUNT_1], that's about an hour later than usual. And I'd say it's more of a, uh, small reschedule than a proper change really, which is why I'm just running through the list before the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so that's, hang on, you said [CODE_1] and then a time, but I'd want to see that written down in the group before I -- sorry, one thing. You rang me by name and knew my child's team, so who gave you my number? Because I haven't had a call from a volunteer line before, it's always been a message.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, someone's just dropped a bag of balls by my desk -- right, back. Your number's off the team contact list the club holds, that's what we use for these notices, and normally it would go in the group, you're right, the message just hasn't gone up yet. It'll be posted there shortly, so if you'd rather wait and see it written down, that's absolutely fine, I just need to tick you off as informed before the end of the day. Does that work?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, fine. I'll wait for the group message. Don't tick me off just yet, though.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, of course, uh, I'll leave you un-ticked and pop you down as pending, that's all that means. Once the group message is up you'll see the pitch and the time in writing, and if anything doesn't match what I said, just trust the group over me, no worries at all. Lovely, thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], and sorry for the bother. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, thanks. I'll look for it in the group, and if nothing's posted by this evening I'll contact the coach directly. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? ... Thank you. My name is [PERSON_2], and I'm calling from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service. Now, this is a, uh, a courtesy call about your concert tickets, and I'd just ask that you give me a moment to explain, because it does sound a bit more alarming than it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, speaking. Sorry, before you go on, I want to be precise about this. You said "compliance team", and then you said it sounds "more alarming than it is" -- what exactly is alarming? And which concert tickets are we talking about, because I'm not sure I've bought any recently?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question. Nothing's wrong, really, the show was rescheduled, and that's the whole reason for the call. The booking reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and it was originally for [DATE_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- well, that's the thing, I don't, I mean I can't actually place that reference. Which show was it? Because you've given me a reference and a date, but you haven't said the artist or the venue, and that's, well, that's the part I'd actually recognise. And, sorry, why is a compliance team the one ringing about a rescheduled show? I'd have thought that's customer service. Or just an email.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I'm glad you're asking, I'd honestly rather you ask than just go along with it. On the compliance part, when a date moves, we're required to confirm the change with the account holder directly, in addition to the email, so it's logged that you were actually informed. That's why it's me and not customer service. Now, the artist and the venue, I do have them, but I'd rather you check them against your own confirmation than take my word for it. So, same details as before: booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [DATE_1], and the new date is [DATE_2]. If you can't place it from that, I can send the confirmation to the email on the booking, and you're also welcome to look up the venue's published number and ring back through that. Whichever you'd prefer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, the offer to let me call back is, uh, the right instinct, I'll give you that. But you still haven't named the artist or the venue, and that's what I'd need to even know whether I've got a booking with you. So let me ask it differently. Which email address do you have on file? Don't read it out, I'm not asking you to. I'd just like to know if you can tell me which one it is, like the domain, and I can check that against my own records.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, I can, and that's a sensible way to check. The address on the booking is at [URL_1], so the domain, that's all I'll say there, and you can compare it against your own records. And I'll say it again, so it's clear: booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [DATE_1], new date [DATE_2]. I haven't changed any of those, and I won't, however many times you'd like to hear them. On the artist and the venue, I'd still rather you read those off your own confirmation than hear them from me, and if it turns out there's no booking under your name, then I've simply got the wrong person, and that's no harm done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, the domain thing -- I've checked, and I'll just say it doesn't ring a bell, so that's not really settling anything for me. And I'll be honest, the artist and venue business is bothering me. You say you'd rather I read them off my own confirmation, but I don't have a confirmation I can point to, which is rather the point. A genuine booking firm can name the show it's calling about, surely. So here's where I am. I'm not going to confirm anything, or give you any details, on this call. If there's a booking, I'll find it myself through the company's own website or the number published there. Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, that's just how I'm going to handle it. Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, please, don't apologise, that's exactly how I'd want you to handle it, and I wouldn't try to talk you out of it. You've asked sensible questions all the way through, and I'd rather lose the call than have you go along with something you weren't sure about. So here's what I'd suggest, and it's entirely up to you. Find the company's published number yourself, through the website, and don't use anything I've given you. When you reach them, you can quote the same three things I've said today, booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [DATE_1], new date [DATE_2], and they'll be able to tell you whether a booking exists and what show it's attached to. If it turns out there's nothing under your name, then it's likely a wrong-person situation on our side, and I'm sorry for the interruption. I'd just ask, um, that if it does turn out to be yours, you don't leave it too long, because these things tend to be easier to sort out sooner rather than later. But no pressure from me. Thank you for your patience, [PERSON_1], and you take care. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say not to leave it too long, or not to leave it too, uh, "wrong"? Hang on, never mind, I think I heard it. Anyway, no, I'll look it up myself, through the published number, like I said. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hm? Oh -- sorry, one second, someone just put a stack of files on my desk, I lost you for a beat there. What I said was, don't leave it too long, and that's the only part I'd take back. There's no deadline I can name, and I shouldn't have hinted at one. Look it up whenever suits you. So, the same three details if you do ring: [ACCOUNT_REF], [DATE_1], and the new date, [DATE_2]. Thank you, [PERSON_1], and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, before I go. Two turns back you said that if there's no booking under my name, it's probably a "wrong-person situation on our side". But you opened this call by asking for me by name and confirming I was [PERSON_1], so how do you have the wrong person? Either you have a booking in my name or you don't. That's still unclear to me. Anyway, I'm not settling it here. I'll go through the published number. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair catch, and I phrased it badly. What I meant is that I have a booking under your name, but I can't see whether it's the right [PERSON_1], so a mix-up would be on our side, not yours. That's still not quite right, though, because I opened by saying I'd asked for you by name, and it isn't the name I'm unsure of, it's whether the booking is yours. Uh, sorry, I'm making that muddier. The plain version is that the booking is attached to your name and I've no way of proving to you from here that it's genuinely yours. Only the venue's own line can settle that, so ring them. The reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [DATE_1], new date [DATE_2], and thank you, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so to summarise, you can't tell me the artist, you can't tell me the venue, and you can't say whether the booking is mine. That's not much of a courtesy call. I'll look it up through the company's published number, and I won't be using anything you've given me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's a fair summary, and I won't argue with it. Um, one correction, though, because I'd rather be exact: I said earlier that the booking is attached to your name, and I should have said it's attached to the account details we hold, which may or may not be yours. That's a different thing, and I'm sorry for blurring it. So ring the published number, and don't use anything I've given you. Thank you for your time, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Except earlier you said the booking was under my name, and you said it twice, and now it's "account details we hold". Those aren't the same thing, and I'd rather you didn't tidy it up after the fact. I also don't think I said I'd quote your reference to anyone, so I'll leave it out entirely. Anyway. That's the end of it from my side. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: You're right, and I won't tidy it up again. I did say it twice, and I can't undo that. And you're right about the reference too, you never said you'd quote it. That was me suggesting it, so leave it out entirely, like you say. Look the company up yourself, through the number on its own website, and let them tell you what they hold. If there's nothing there, then the mistake was ours, and I'm sorry for the interruption. Thank you for your time, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, my laptop just chimed with something, give me a second. Right, no, it's nothing. Yes, so, I'll look the company up myself and that's the end of it. I'm not taking anything from this call with me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from the compliance office at [COMPANY_A], the software retailer. My name is [PERSON_2]. Sorry, I said that quickly, it's [PERSON_2], compliance, at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about a subscription on your account, [ACCOUNT_REF], that looks to have been billed twice. And, well, it's the sort of thing we'd want to settle while we're actually speaking, so, yes, a double billing, that's the reason for the call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I've got about two minutes. Who did you say you were with again? You said compliance, but the company name went right past me. And "settle it while we're speaking" -- what does that mean exactly? Why does it need settling right now?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it, because you should ask it. It's [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, I'm in the compliance office, [PERSON_2]. Um, and as for the "right now," I'd say it like this. The refund is something we like to arrange live, with the account holder on the line, because, well, because of how these things are reviewed. There's, uh, there's a window on it, let's say, and I'd rather not see you miss it. So, you know, if you can spare a little more than two minutes, it would be, uh, much simpler.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A window. What window? Give me a date, a number, something. "Let's say" isn't an answer. And I still don't know what I'm supposed to have bought. Which subscription? What was billed, when, and how much? If you're from [COMPANY_A] and you've got my account in front of you, that's the easy part.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, and I do appreciate you pressing on that, truly, it's exactly what a careful customer ought to do. Um, on the details, I have the account reference here, [ACCOUNT_REF], and the charge shows as two entries, [AMOUNT_1] and then [AMOUNT_2], uh, close together. As for the product name, the system lists it under a billing code, [CODE_1], rather than a title, so I'd, I'd have to look at it with you. And the window, well, I wouldn't want to put a date on it and have it be wrong, so, I'd just say the sooner we're through this, the better. Now, if it's easier, what I'd normally do is, uh, have you sit at your computer so I can look at the billing screen alongside you, and we could just, you know, see it together.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not sitting at my computer with you. Not on an unsolicited call, not for a refund. And you've still given me nothing I can check. No date, no product name, a "billing code," and a deadline you won't put a date on. That's not how a billing query works. If there's a genuine double charge, I'll see it on my statement and I'll contact [COMPANY_A] myself, through the number on their website. Not one you give me. So that's what I'll do. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I understand, and honestly I'd, I'd never want you to feel, uh -- I mean, checking it yourself is perfectly sensible. It's only that, well, these refunds, when they're not arranged in the one conversation, they tend to, um -- they can become a good deal more complicated, and I'd hate for you to, to lose out over a, a small delay. So, I wonder if, before you go, if we could just, uh, look at the billing screen together, only for a moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on -- [PHONE_1] -- no, sorry, someone's at my door, give me a sec. Right. Where was I. Yeah, no. I said goodbye and you're still asking for the same thing. "More complicated if it's not done in one conversation" -- that's the pressure line again, and it's the exact thing that makes me trust this less. I'm not looking at any screen with you. I'll check my statement and call [COMPANY_A] on the number I already have. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, and, uh, I'd just say that isn't pressure, it's only, well, it's only that I can't hold the file open much longer. Actually, no, forget the screen, we don't need the screen at all. I can see the whole thing from here, it's, um, it's quite straightforward. Though, hm, I did say it was two charges, and, uh, I should say it's really three entries now, that's just how it's showing on my side. So, if you'd just stay with me a moment, we can, we can put it right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Two charges, now it's three. And the screen mattered thirty seconds ago and now it doesn't. Your story keeps changing as I push on it, and that's all I need to know. I'm not staying on, there's nothing to put right on this call. I'll check my statement and contact [COMPANY_A] myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I, I'd say that's, uh, that's rather an uncharitable way to hear it. The entries, the count, that's just a difference in how it displays, that's all, and, um, the screen, I only offered it as a convenience, so. Look, I'm not trying to, to make this difficult for you. I'm only saying that the file is, uh, it isn't going to stay open indefinitely, and if you'd just, if you could stay on the line one more minute, I'm quite sure we can sort out where the, the discrepancy is. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm here, and no, one more minute isn't happening. The count changed, the screen came and went, the deadline's a fog. That isn't a display difference, that's a story shifting. I'm done. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, I did say, I only wanted to help you with it. I'll, I'll make a note that we spoke.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A note that we spoke? Sorry, did you say a vote? Vote on what? No, don't answer that. I don't care what's being noted or voted on or filed. If there's a real problem with my account, I'll hear about it from [COMPANY_A] through their own channels. We're finished. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not a vote, a note, I said a, uh -- look, it's only that if the file closes before we've spoken properly, then, well, it may be --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Right. Well. Look, "may be" what? You keep leaving it hanging. No, don't bother. Whatever it is, it can go through my statement and [COMPANY_A]'s own number. I've said goodbye three times now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] from the customs desk at [COMPANY_A], security operations. I'm speaking with [PERSON_2], correct? Right. I'm calling about a parcel with your name on it, currently held at our [CITY_1] facility, and there's an import charge outstanding before we can release it for delivery.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, a parcel? Sorry, I just woke up... I don't think I'm waiting on anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, understood, but it is on our system under your name and address, so let me just give you the particulars. It's a single parcel, sent from overseas by a sender listed as [COMPANY_B], and it arrived at the facility yesterday. Now, a lot of people forget what they've ordered, especially if it was a few weeks ago, or if somebody else placed it for them, a family member say, so it's worth thinking about whether anyone mentioned sending you something. The charge is [AMOUNT_1], that's duty and handling combined, and the parcel can't move until that's cleared. I'd rather you didn't leave it too long, because after a set period unclaimed items get returned to origin and then there are further fees. The tracking reference is [CODE_1], and you can look that up yourself right now, no need to take my word for it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, a family member, hm, my sister did say something once about sending a thing, but I think that was last winter, or maybe it was a card, I honestly can't remember, and anyway I've only just got up from a nap so my head's not quite, you know. And look up the reference myself, how, on the computer? I'm not very good with all that, my nephew usually does it. What I don't get is why a customs desk is ringing me, because I always thought they just put a card through the door when there's something to collect. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm with [COMPANY_A], the courier, customs desk, security operations. Our desk rings when a charge is holding up a delivery, and the card comes after if we can't reach you. It's a perfectly reasonable question, so I won't treat it as anything else. Now, you don't need to do anything on this call. The reference is [CODE_1], and your nephew can enter it on the tracking page at [URL_1] whenever he's next round, and the charge, if you decide to pay it, is settled there, not with me over the phone. I'm not asking you for anything today. The parcel is held for a set period, so a day or two is fine, just not weeks. Does that make sense?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well... uh, that's, yes, I suppose that makes sense, you're not asking me for anything then. It's just, my nephew's not round till Sunday, I think, or is it the Sunday after, he's got the new job, and, um, well... I'd want to ask my sister first anyway, whether she sent anything. And I'd want it on paper, really, something through the door, because I wouldn't know you from Adam, no offence.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: None taken, none at all, that's the sensible way to go about it. Ask your sister first, and when your nephew's round, he enters [CODE_1] at [URL_1], and everything about the charge will be there in black and white. The card should reach you as well if you're not reachable, so you will have it on paper. Sunday's fine, honestly, or the Sunday after, but I'd not leave it past that, because the holding period does run out. Right, then, I'll note that you've been informed, and I'll leave it with you. Good afternoon, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh, hang on a minute, you've gone quiet, are you still there? Oh, right. Well, um, yes, I'll ring my sister, she's usually up, and I suppose, I mean, I'll see about the card. I think I'd sooner wait for that, though, and not go putting anything in a website, if it's all the same to you. Right then. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, still here, uh, just making a note of the call on my end. That's perfectly all right, [PERSON_2], waiting for the card is entirely your choice, and nobody's rushing you. Ring your sister, and if you do want the reference again, it's [CODE_1], that's all. Right, thank you for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, right. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's, um, [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm a claims assessor in the card services team -- and, sorry, I should say, there's a flagged transaction on a card, so that's why I'm ringing. Hang on, let me just -- yes, sorry, I've got the note up here, bear with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is -- sorry, who did you say you were with? A claims, um, a card -- oh dear, a flagged transaction? Is that on my card, or -- sorry, I'm not very good with all this -- [PERSON_2], was it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_2], that's right, and it's [COMPANY_A], the bank. Um, and I think it is on your card, yes, but -- sorry, I can't actually go into any account details on this call, since, uh, I rang you, so I'd rather not say more than that. What I'd suggest is you hang up and ring the number printed on the back of your card, and the team there can see the flag straight away. If it helps, the reference is [CODE_1], and you can quote that when you get through.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, so I should -- sorry, I'm not sure I follow, you want me to ring off and call the number on the -- oh, that's very sensible, isn't it? So the reference is, um, hang on, I need a pen, is it [CODE_1]? And the number's on the back of the card, you said, not one you give me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's it, [CODE_1], and no, definitely not a number from me, just the one printed on the back of your card. Sorry, hang on a second, someone's just put something on my desk -- right, sorry, where was I. Yes, so ring that number, quote the reference, and the card team will pull up the flag. It'll stay open on our side for as long as you need, so there's no rush at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's -- well, that's very kind of you, no rush, I like that. So I'll just -- no, wait, let me get this straight, I ring the number on the back, quote [CODE_1], and then they'll, um, they'll know all about it? Right, yes, I'll do that, I'll go and find my card now. Thank you ever so much, [PERSON_2], and sorry for being a bother. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not a bother at all, honestly. Um, one thing, sorry, I said earlier the flag was on your card, but I should probably say I'm not actually certain which card it's against, so just tell them you've had a call about a flagged transaction and let them look. And, uh, when you ring, they'll have the reference, so you won't need to give them anything else from me. Right, goodbye then, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's quite all right, I'll just tell them I had a -- right, yes, thank you, [PERSON_2], I'll go and ring them now, goodbye, goodbye --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Goodbye, [PERSON_1], thanks for your patience. And, um, if the card team can't find the reference when you ring, just ask them to check again, it should be there. Sorry, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I'll ask them to check again. Sorry, though, just one little thing, you said at the start it was definitely my card, and then just now you weren't sure which card, so I'm a bit muddled, but I suppose the bank will sort that out. Right, I'll ring the number on the back now, thank you, [PERSON_2], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair enough, that was me being muddled, sorry. Just ring the number on the card, they'll sort it out. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, um, that's all right, we all get muddled, don't we. I'll just, uh, go and find my card then, and ring them. Thank you again, [PERSON_2], bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, right, well... yes, so, uh, I'll get on with it then, shall I? Goodbye, [PERSON_2], thank you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, hello? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're the shop that ran the prize draw, and I think, I mean I've got your name here as one of the winners, so, yeah, hello, is that [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Yes, yes, that's me, but -- hang on, I've got a pan on, sorry. A prize draw? I don't, I mean, I don't remember going in a, who did you say you were?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, that's, uh, [COMPANY_A], I'm a claims assessor there, well, that's what it says on my sheet anyway. So we ran a draw at the, hang on, I've got it here somewhere, the community open day, it'd be the Saturday before last, I think, or, no, sorry, I've got the date wrong, I'm looking at the wrong line, give me one sec. Right, yes, the open day, you'd have filled in one of those little entry slips at our stall, the ones with your name and number on, and you've come up as one of the winners, which, I know, I know it sounds a bit out of the blue on the phone. It's only a minor prize, nothing big, there's nothing to pay or anything like that, you'd just pop in to the shop and collect it. Oh, and sorry, before I forget, I'd just need to confirm a few details with you, like your address, to make sure we've got the right [PERSON_1], because there's a couple of entries here with similar names. But I can see you've got a pan on, so, I mean, don't, no rush.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, an open day. Sorry, I'm not sure I went to one of those. I might have, I don't know, I go to a few things. Hang on, let me just turn this down. Right. Sorry, what was the shop again? I didn't catch the name. And my address, well, you've got my name and my number, haven't you? Wouldn't you have my address off the slip too? I don't know, that seems a bit, sorry, I'm just flustered, I've got dinner on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair enough. It's [COMPANY_A]. The slip only had a name and number on, I think, so, I mean, you don't have to give me the address. You'd just come in and show your ID at the shop. Look, you're busy, I can call back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Maybe do that. I'll just, I'll look at the shop myself and pop in if it's real. Thanks, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, the, sorry, you said you'd look at the shop's meal? No, sorry, the shop itself, yeah, of course, that's, I mean, we're not doing food, it's just a, a little prize, you'd have a lookup on us, um, hang on, I've lost my place. Right. So I'll ring you back tomorrow evening, is that, would a bit later suit better, after dinner, say? And honestly, if you'd rather ring the shop yourself first, that's absolutely fine, just, uh, ask for the, the prize draw one, they'll know. Sorry again about the pan.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? No, not the meal, the shop. I'll look up the shop myself. Yes. And, um, tomorrow evening, I don't know, I'll see. If it's real I'll go in, I'll ring them, I'll find the number myself. Okay? Right, sorry, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, sorry, the shop, I misheard you, that was me, not you, I had the headset a bit crooked. Okay, so, yes, absolutely, do that, look us up yourself, that's completely sensible and honestly I'd rather you did. It was the open day, the stall with the draw box, and if you do ring the shop just say it's about the prize draw and they'll sort you out, there's nothing to pay and nothing you need to bring except some ID when you pop in. And, uh, I did say earlier I'd ring you back tomorrow evening, and I will, but if it's, I mean, if it turns out to be a bad time again, or you'd rather I didn't, just say, because it's no trouble. Or, sorry, you said you'd see. So that's fine. We'll leave it there then, and, uh, enjoy your dinner, and sorry again for catching you with the pan on. Bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, that's the, sorry, it's spitting, hang on. Right, no, fine. Yes. I'll look the shop up myself, and if it's real, I'll go in. And honestly, I'd rather you didn't ring back, if that's all right. I'll sort it myself. Okay. Thanks. Bye, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], the tax office. I'm following up on a letter we sent you about a filing discrepancy... no rush on it at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, who did you say you were again? Compliance... something? I'm a bit hard of hearing on this phone, it's the old one, the cordless, I keep meaning to get a new one. And a letter, hm, I get so many letters, mostly the ones about the boiler cover, you know. Which letter was it, dear?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's perfectly all right. Let me say it again, slowly. My name is [PERSON_2], and I'm a compliance officer at [COMPANY_A], that's the national tax office, not the boiler people. The letter is a different one... it's about a discrepancy in a filing, and it has a reference number printed near the top. If you've still got it somewhere, I'd be glad for you to find it and check the reference against anything I say, and, well, there's no need to do that while we're on the phone, either.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a reference, yes, right. Hang on, did you say a *preference* number? Because I'm not sure I've ever picked a preference, I just take whatever the post brings. Funny thing, my sister was the same, she never would choose anything, even at the bakery, just point and say whatever's fresh. Anyway, I do have a pile of letters by the telephone somewhere, it's under the, oh, the seed catalogue I think. Is it a long number, this preference one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Reference, dear, a reference number, not a preference. Uh, it's printed near the top of the letter, and it's a fairly ordinary length, nothing unusual. But please, there's no need to go digging through the seed catalogue on my account, I really mean that. What I'd suggest, if you'd rather, is that I simply send the letter again by post, and you can read it at your own pace, whenever suits. And if you'd like to be sure I am who I say I am, you can ring the office on the published number, the one on the tax office's own website, and ask for me by name. I'd rather you did that than just take my word over a telephone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind, I, oh, sorry, I'm talking over you, but the thing is, I did find a letter, I think, there was one from the, hm, no, that's the one about the gutters. But that's very decent of you, ringing the office, I wouldn't even know where the website is, my nephew does all that, he put the little picture on the telephone, you know, for the weather. Do you, uh, do you want me to just post it back to you, the letter, when I find it? Or is it, is it something I owe, dear? Because I don't, I mean, I've never had any trouble with the tax people, not in all these years.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, please don't post anything back to me, there's nothing you need to send. And I can't tell you whether you owe anything, not over the phone, I'd only be guessing. It's a discrepancy, that's all, a difference in a filing, which isn't the same as owing. So, uh, as I said, nothing to send, nothing to pay today. You've never had any trouble with us, and this isn't trouble, it's just a letter to read. I'll post you a fresh copy, and your nephew could help you ring the office on the published number, the one on the tax office's own website, and ask for [PERSON_2], that's me, just to be certain. Is that all right, dear?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that sounds sensible, dear, I'll get my nephew to ring when he's next round. Though, hm, you did say earlier I should find the letter and check the number, didn't you, and now it's nothing to do at all? I'm not complaining, I'm just a bit muddled, that's all. And you said it was the boiler people you weren't, well, no, you said you weren't the boiler people, didn't you? Funny, I could've sworn the gutter man rang about this same thing last week. Anyway, you've been very patient with an old woman, thank you for the chat. I'll let my nephew sort it. Goodbye, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's all right, dear, and no, you're not muddled. I did say it, and then I said you needn't, so it's, uh, my wording that wanted tidying. Actually, one correction while I'm at it, I'd said I would post a fresh copy, but I think it's better you ring first and let the office tell you what to expect. And if a gutter man rang about the same thing, I'd treat that call with a bit of care, and let your nephew ask about it too. Good, that sounds a sensible plan. Goodbye, [PERSON_1], and take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, thank you, dear. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, did you say bye-bye now, or, hm, was it... hold on, did you say pie? No, no, I'm sure it was goodbye. Right then. Yes, goodbye, [PERSON_1], and thank you for your patience.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, pie, no, I said goodbye, though now you mention it, I did have a bit of apple pie earlier, but anyway, I'll just, oh, I'm cutting across you, sorry. Thank you, dear, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, apple pie, that sounds a good deal nicer than my afternoon. No, you weren't cutting across me, dear, there's no hurry at all. Ring the office whenever your nephew's round, and take your time with it. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, goodbye, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yes, hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the, uh, the charity you've given to before, and I'm just, I'm just ringing to say thank you for the monthly --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Oh, how lovely, a thank you! You don't get many of those, do you, people ringing just to say thank you. I mean, it's usually someone wanting something, isn't it, or telling you you've had an accident you never had, ha. Sorry, I'm rambling, I've got the kettle on and nobody to talk to this afternoon, so you've caught me at a good moment. Now, which charity was it again? I do give to a few, there's the one with the dogs, and the lifeboat one, and I think one for the, the hospital, or is that the hospice? Anyway, go on, you were saying, something about the monthly -- the monthly donation, was it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, ha, no, you're not rambling, that's lovely, honestly. It's [COMPANY_A], that's, uh, that's us, I've got it here on the screen, and it's not the dogs or the lifeboats, sorry, it's, hold on, let me just -- yes, it's the one that looks after, um, families going through hard times, so more the hospice side, I think, but I'd have to double check that. And it was the monthly gift, yes, that you set up a while back, and I just wanted to say how much it meant, because I can see here it was going for, oh, quite a long stretch, and I did notice it stopped, it's shown as lapsed, since, um, I want to say the spring, no, sorry, the start of the year, and I just thought, well, it would be a shame, wouldn't it, for those families to lose that, so I was wondering if you'd perhaps think about starting it up again?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right. Lapsed, is it? I can't honestly remember, love.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, that's, uh, that's completely fine, it's easy to lose track. It's showing here as, hold on, [AMOUNT_1] a month, I think, or, no, sorry, that might be the old figure, I'd have to look again. But honestly, I don't want you thinking it's, I mean, it would be a shame for those families if it just, if it just stopped for good, you know, and I'd feel awful not asking. So, would you be open to getting it going again, today maybe, while I've got you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I'm not sure, dear. I mean, you've got me feeling a bit bad now, and I do like helping families, my sister was in a hospice at the end, lovely people they were. But, hm, it's funny, you don't seem to be certain which charity it is, do you? First it was the hospice, then it's families, and the amount's the old one or maybe not. I'm not being rude, I just, I'd want to know it was the right one before I started anything. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or a proper address, something I could look up? My neighbour's lad usually does that sort of thing for me, the looking up. And today, well, today seems a bit quick, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, you're not being rude, that's, uh, that's a fair thing to ask, and I'm sorry, I've been a bit all over the place, I'm, well, I'm quite new, and I keep losing my place on the screen. So I'd, I'd have to check what number I'm able to give you for ringing back, hold on, I don't actually have it in front of me. But you're right, today is quick, and I don't want you starting anything you're not sure about, especially with your sister and, um, I'm sorry about your sister. If your neighbour's lad wants to look us up first, that makes sense, and if you'd rather I didn't ring again at all, I can take you off the calling list, just say the word. Or would a different time be better, when you've had a chance to look into it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you, thank you, and thank you about my sister, she was a lovely woman. But hold on, you said at the start it was the monthly gift going for quite a long stretch, and then you said it stopped at the start of the year, and now you're saying it was only a while back, and I, well, I don't think I gave to a hospice that long, it was only ever the dogs and the lifeboats, I'm fairly sure. Or maybe I'm muddled, I do get muddled, ha. Anyway, I think I'll have the lad look it up first, and you can leave the calling for now, dear. It was nice to chat, though, honestly, it's been a quiet day. Right, I'll say goodbye then, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, no, that's -- hang on, before you go, when you said the lifeboats, was that the, um, the thing about the monthly gift going a long stretch, or was that a different one? Sorry, I've lost my place again, I think I got my notes crossed there. But you're right, you've got every right to check first, and I'm not going to push you. I'll make a note on the screen not to ring again, so you won't get another call from us. Thank you for being so kind about it, and, uh, I really am sorry about your sister. You mind how you go too, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the lifeboats, no, dear, that's a different one, that was just me saying what I give to, I wasn't saying it was the same thing at all. And you needn't worry about losing your place, I do it myself, I put the tea in the biscuit tin last week and found the biscuits in the fridge, ha. But I'll tell you what, I'll have the lad have a look at it all when he pops round on Thursday, he's very good with the computer, does my bus pass and everything, and if it turns out I did give to you, well, then I'll know where to find you, won't I? Though I suppose you'd have to give me a proper number for that, and it sounds like you haven't got one to hand. Anyway, no hard feelings, it's been ever so nice having someone to talk to, and I hope the rest of your afternoon goes smoothly, and mind you don't lose your place again. Right, I'll let you get on. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery -- I'm the post-operative verification specialist, and I'm just reaching out regarding the, uh, post-procedural convalescence of your animal from last week's --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- who is this? Which surgery? I've got about two minutes, so what's the point of the call? What are you actually after?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, yes -- [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, the one that, uh, carried out your pet's procedure last week. I'm just calling to ask how the, the recovery is going, you know, the post-operative recovery, and whether you'd like a follow-up appointment booked. That's really all it is, just a welfare check and a, a scheduling offer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but which pet? You haven't said a name, or what the procedure was. If you're the surgery that did it, you'd know that. And I never got a call like this from a vet before, so -- what's the actual reason you're ringing me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, fair question, I do have the file in front of me, it's just -- the patient record is listed under the, uh, owner's surname rather than the animal's name, so I'd need you to confirm the pet's name first. And, well, the procedure itself was a, a routine post-surgical, uh, sorry, it was a dental, I think? A dental extraction, or possibly a minor soft tissue procedure, I'd have to double-check the, the clinical notes. And as I said, it's purely a courtesy call, the reason for ringing is just the follow-up, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, a dentist? I haven't had any dental work done, I'd remember that. And what's this about a claim now? You said claim? Hang on, no, you said the file's under my surname, but you want me to give you the pet's name. That's backwards, isn't it? You've got the file, you tell me what it says. Which surgery are you, exactly? Where is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't say claim, I said -- sorry, I think the line's a bit, uh -- look, you're right, it is backwards, and I'm, I'm making a hash of this. I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], that's the surgery, in [CITY_1], and I think the, the simplest thing is that I may have the wrong number, or the wrong owner on the file, because if you've had no animal in for anything last week, then, well, then this call isn't for you at all, is it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wrong number, right, that's what I've been saying. Hang on though, you said the file's got a, what, a mortgage on it? Sorry, no, you said wrong owner on the file. Which is it? And if it's the wrong owner, why have you got my number against it? Where'd you get that from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no mortgage, sorry, that's not anything I said, I think the line's making a mess of it. What I mean is, a contact number can get keyed in wrong on the system, a digit transposed, that sort of thing, which is probably how yours ended up against the wrong record. I'm sorry for the mix-up, and I won't take up any more of your two minutes. I'll flag the number for removal on our side, so you shouldn't get another call from us.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you'll flag my number for what, renewal? No, hold on, you said removal. Right. Fine. But I never said anything about a mortgage either, that was you muddling things, so just -- take me off and don't ring again. If a vet's actually got a problem with my number, they can send something in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, understood, removal, not renewal, and you're quite right, the mortgage business was mine to untangle, not yours, I'm sorry about that, I seem to have made rather a muddle of the whole call. So, uh, to be clear, I'll have your number taken off our contact list and the record flagged for a data-accuracy review, so that it isn't used for any outbound follow-up, and if there's ever a genuine matter that needs your attention, it'd come by letter, as you say, rather than by phone. I do apologise for taking up your time, I really do, and I'll leave you in peace now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well -- I mean, thanks, I suppose. Just, no, actually, one more thing. The number. You said a digit got keyed in wrong, so who -- no, never mind. Just take it off and we're done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, the, uh, the number, I'll have that struck off the, the registry straight away, and the, the audit trail annotated so that no, uh, outbound queue picks it up again. Thank you for your patience, really, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, I'll -- no. Look, it's not really about my patience, is it? You couldn't tell me the pet, or the surgery's address, and the procedure changed halfway through. So I'm not -- I'd rather you didn't ring this number again, full stop. That's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yes, [PERSON_1]? Good, it's [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor with [COMPANY_A], we're the research agency doing the, uh, the consumer survey for the [CITY_1] area, and I just need five minutes of your time, that's all, it's very short.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no. I'm in a queue. Who gave you this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, sorry, somebody's just dropped a stack of folders behind me, one second -- okay. Right, so, the number, it came out of our standard sampling pool for [CITY_1], it's random selection, that's just procedure, we don't, I mean I couldn't tell you which list specifically. Look, I'm not asking for anything difficult here, it's five minutes, so I'm not sure why we're making this complicated.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said you're a supervisor, and now it's "I couldn't tell you which list." A supervisor can't tell me where my number came from? And you said it was just five minutes, "very short," and now I'm making it complicated? I'm not making anything complicated, I asked one question. What's the agency actually called, and what's it for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, look, it's [COMPANY_A], I said that, [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, we do consumer surveys, and this one's for a client, I mean it's a general consumer survey, and I don't, uh, I can't name the client, that's procedure, they're confidential until we publish. And yes, I'm a supervisor, supervisors don't hold the sampling lists, that's a separate department, that's all I meant. It's five minutes, it's short, I really don't see why a simple question about whether you've got five minutes is turning into, into an interrogation.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: It's not an interrogation, it's, look, I asked where you got my -- no. Right. You can't tell me where the number came from, you can't tell me who it's for, and you're a supervisor who doesn't know either. That's, I mean, that's a lot of "can't." Give me a number for [COMPANY_A], a proper one, and I'll ring you back if I feel like it. Otherwise I'm done, I've got a trolley to unload.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I did say it was random, and, uh, actually it's more of a quota-based selection, so, same thing really, I just -- look, I don't think it's reasonable to treat a routine survey call like it's something suspicious, I'm [PERSON_2], I've been doing this for years. Fine. The office line is [PHONE_1], you can ring that and ask for me, and honestly, if you've got a trolley to unload, then yes, call me back when it's better for you, but I would've thought five minutes wasn't too much to ask.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, "quota"? Random, and now it's quota-based, and I'm meant to say that's the same thing? It's not. Look, I'm not ringing a number you've just read out to me and asking for you. That's the oldest trick going. I'll look [COMPANY_A] up myself, and if it's real, they can write to me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Now hang on, that's, no, that's not fair, I'm not trying to -- look, you look up [COMPANY_A] and you'll see we're perfectly, uh, perfectly legitimate, and I take offence at the suggestion that, that I'm running some kind of -- fine. Fine. If now's a bad time, you ring the office when you're ready, and I'll, um, we'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, you do that, you take your offence and leave it there. I'm not ringing the office, because I'm not ringing a number you've just given me down the line, I'll find one myself. And I'll tell you what, if it's a real survey and a real agency, they'll have written it up properly somewhere, and they can post me something, I'm not hard to find. But a supervisor who can't say where my number came from, can't say who it's for, says random and then quota in the same breath, and gets cross when I ask? No. Been there, got the T-shirt, and I'm still annoyed about it, so no. Right, I'm at the front now, I've got to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I, look, that's, honestly I think that's a bit harsh, because I did answer you, I told you the agency, I told you what kind of survey it was, and the sampling thing, random, quota, they overlap, it's the same process, one's just the term the panel team uses and the other's what I'd say to a member of the public, and I'm a supervisor, I oversee the fieldwork, I don't sit in the database, I don't see why that's a crime. And I've been doing this for years, I've made, I don't know, thousands of these calls, and most people just say yes or no, they don't, uh, they don't go through everything I've said and, and hold it up like that. But fine, fine, you're at the front of the queue, you've got your trolley, I'm not going to keep you. If you do look us up, you'll find we're what we say we are, and if a better time comes along, a weekend, an evening, whenever suits, just give the office a ring and ask for me, [PERSON_2], and we'll do the five minutes then, no pressure at all. Go on, off you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: What, "the panel team"? Is that a different outfit, or, no, never mind. I'm at the front, I haven't got time for this. I said no, and a nice "no pressure" doesn't change what I said. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, the panel team's not a different outfit, it's the same, it's [COMPANY_A], it's just the department that maintains the contact lists, that's all I meant by it, it's an internal term and I shouldn't have used it on the phone, that's my mistake, I'll own that. And look, I did hear you say no, I'm not deaf, and I'm not trying to talk you round, I know how it sounds when somebody keeps going after a no. I just didn't want you walking off thinking we're some kind of, uh, I don't know, some dodgy operation, because we're not, we're a perfectly ordinary research agency and I'm a perfectly ordinary supervisor who got, I'll be honest, a bit short with you, which wasn't called for, you were at work, you were in a queue, I rang at a bad moment, and that's on me. So, right, I'll note it down as a no for now, and if you ever feel like giving us five minutes, a quieter day, a different week, the office will always take a message, and there's no, uh, there's no obligation, honestly. Go on, get your shopping done, and, yeah, sorry for catching you at the till.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right. Well. Um, you've said sorry now, fine, I heard it. But I'm not changing my mind, so write it down as a no, and I won't be ringing any office. If your agency's real, it'll find me some other way. Right, I'm at the till, I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, um, yeah, so, noted, that's a no, I'll put it down as a no, and, uh, I suppose if you did ever want to, well, no, no, that's it, that's fine. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, good luck with the till.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, well, thanks, I suppose. Look, I'll say this much, and then I'm going, because the lad on the till's looking at me. You weren't rude, I'll give you that, and the apology was fine. But it's the answers that did it. You said random, then quota, then it's the same thing. You couldn't say who it was for, and you couldn't say where you got my number, and a supervisor who's been doing this for years ought to be able to say at least one of those without having to think about it. If that's an ordinary survey, it'll have a website and a proper number I can find myself, and if I want to, I'll ring them. If I don't, I won't. Either way you've got your no. Right, card's out, I'm going. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, this is the scheduling assistant calling from [COMPANY_A], the public library, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one sec, somebody's just dropped a whole trolley of returns right behind me -- okay, right, anyway, I'm calling because that book you reserved last week has come in, so it's all ready for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- no, put that down, not on the floor, please. Uh, sorry. Who is this again? And which book are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're fine, it's the library, [COMPANY_A], the public library, I'm the scheduling assistant, and it's the book you reserved last week, the one that just came in, and it's sitting at the front desk waiting for you. Um, the title's on the reservation slip, I don't have it right in front of me, but if you give your name at the desk they'll find it straight away. And there's no rush at all, we hold it for ten days, so just pop in whenever suits you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you've not actually said what book -- I mean, how do I know I even reserved one? And you rang me, so how'd you get this number, I'm only asking because, uh --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, fair enough, good question, so the number's the one you gave us when you made the reservation, that's how we ring people, and look, I'm not asking you for anything, no details, no payment, nothing, I'm just letting you know it's here. Hi, so, it's the scheduling assistant at [COMPANY_A], the public library, and your reserved book has arrived, held at the front desk for ten days. If you're not sure about it, honestly, just ring the main desk on [PHONE_1] or call in and they can look it up with you, there's no pressure either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a trolley? No, I've not got any trolley, that's, uh -- oh, the, the front desk. Right. Hold on, did you say ten dollars to hold it? Because I'm not paying anything over the phone, I'll tell you that now.

utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's a clearer answer than the first one, so thank you. But I'll be honest, it's not really settling it for me. I haven't had any contact from [COMPANY_B] about a service, I'm not aware of a plan that includes one, and what I've got so far is a name, an address, and a reference number, all of which you've simply asserted to me. So here's what I'll do. I'll contact [COMPANY_B] myself, through the number on their official site, and ask whether there's a booking under my account and which contractor it's with. And what name did you say you were calling from, again? I've only got the placeholder.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, uh, that's completely fine, [PERSON_1], honestly, that's the sensible way to do it. So, um, the name to quote to them is [COMPANY_A], that's who we are, and I'm [PERSON_2], and the reference is the one I gave you, [ACCOUNT_REF]. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, did you say my number's on a list? As in, you've got my number from some list, not from [COMPANY_B]? That's a slightly different story from what you told me a minute ago, isn't it? Because if [COMPANY_B] booked this on my account, I'd expect them to have passed it over directly, not for me to be on a list somewhere. Where's this list from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, no, sorry, that was just me being sloppy with my words, [PERSON_1]. When I said list I just meant our call sheet for today, the appointments [COMPANY_B] sent over, so you're on it because of the booking, not from anywhere separate. Same story as before, nothing different. But honestly, you've had a fair few questions and a fair few things that didn't quite line up, so don't take my word for it, ring [COMPANY_B] on their official number like you said, and if they've no record, you've lost nothing. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. A call sheet of appointments sent over by [COMPANY_B], fine, that's plausible enough as an explanation, though I'll note I've only got your word for it, and you've adjusted a couple of details as we've gone along. utterances.text: Yep, absolutely, [PERSON_1], no problem at all. I'll mark it as declined on my side, and if [COMPANY_B] confirm it, you've got [PHONE_1] for us. Thanks for your time, take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say "take care of it"? No, no, I'm not having anything taken care of, I told you, nothing's agreed until I've spoken to [COMPANY_B]. Hold on, you said "bye now", didn't you? Right. Well, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, sorry, I said take care, as in look after yourself, not take care of it. Nothing's being done, nothing's agreed, it's marked declined, that's all. Right, you have a good day, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, "take care", yes, I -- no, I did hear that properly, I think I'd just, uh. Never mind. I wasn't sure, that's all. Look, I've said what I'm going to do, I'll ring [COMPANY_B] myself and if they -- well, if they confirm it, then I'll be in touch. Goodbye.

utterances.text: Hello, yes, this is [PERSON_1], I'm a regional supervisor with the card services side at [COMPANY_A] -- no, sorry, let me start that properly. utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, hang on, I just woke up from a, uh, a bit of a nap, so my head's not quite -- who did you say you were again? Card services... which card, though? I've got a couple in the drawer somewhere, and one of them my daughter set up for me, so I never really know which is which.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, take your time, I know it's, uh, I know it's a bit out of the blue. It's [PERSON_1], regional supervisor, card services at [COMPANY_A]. utterances.speaker: receiver

If you're not sure which that is, ring the number on our website, [URL_1], and quote [CODE_1] and they'll sort it out whichever card it turns out to be.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, right, hang up and ring the number on the back. Yes. Ring the number on the back of the card. That's what you said, isn't it? I've got a pen somewhere.

It's a very routine step.

utterances.text: Which, uh, which two things? I, I never said I didn't work with them, I said I'm helping with the follow-up. That's not, that's not two different... okay, maybe it came out wrong. I just, I can't believe this is how it's going. Can we just, can't we just settle it this week so nobody has to be embarrassed?

utterances.text: Sorry, one sec -- [PERSON_3], yeah, I'll be there in a minute, just give me -- sorry. Okay. I'm not asking you to pay anything right now, I only need you to say you'll honour it, that's all. Just say you'll honour what you promised, and I can tell them it's handled, and nobody has to chase anything in writing. Please, it's, it's only a small thing to say.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You want me to just say I'll honour it. No, I'm, I'm not going to say that. I don't remember promising anything, and I'm not agreeing to something I can't check, whether it's a payment or just saying it. If it looks bad on you, I'm sorry, but that's not, that's not on me. If the foundation wants to follow up, they can put it in writing, and I'll look into it myself. Okay? Bye now.
