But then, hang on, you've gone and asked me to keep it quiet, haven't you? Don't tell anybody. And, uh, well, that bit's a bit odd, isn't it, because if it's all above board why would I not be allowed to mention it to someone, like my sister, she's good with this kind of thing, she reads all the small print, she'd know. And the other tenants, I wasn't, I mean, there was only me on that one I think, or was there, there might have been a lad called, oh, what was it... anyway. Why can't I just tell my sister?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair thing to push on, and I'd rather correct myself. The rule is only about the other tenants and the landlord side, so nobody gets an informal heads-up before the formal notice goes out. It isn't a gag on you. Tell your sister, show her the written notice when it lands, let her read every line of the small print. That's sort of the point of sending it on paper. And if you're not sure whether anyone else was on the deposit, don't worry about it now, the notice will name everyone on the record, so nothing needs to be settled on this call. So the plan is, ring the number on the website yourself, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and check it matches. I'll send the written notice today, and you can take it from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Well, okay, that's, yes, that's a lot more reasonable than the first bit, you backing off the keeping-it-quiet thing. So I tell my sister, I ring the website number myself, and I look at the letter when it comes. I think that's, I mean, I'd rather do it that way than anything else, honestly. I'm not giving you anything on this call, no address, nothing, I'll just find my glasses and do it properly. Right, I'm going to go now, thank you for being straight with me, and sorry I was a bit, you know, bleary. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, don't apologise, that's exactly how it should be done, and I'd rather you checked than took my word for it. So, ring the number on the website, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and the written notice will be with you today. Find your glasses, show your sister, and if anything doesn't match, you've lost nothing by asking. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_2], take care. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yes, right, so, uh... the website, the reference, my sister, I think I've got it all, and, well, if it doesn't match I'll just, I don't know, ring someone else about it. Anyway, I'll go and find those glasses, they're probably on my head, they usually are. Thanks again, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service. I'm calling about your concert booking, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], the event's been rescheduled, and I need to confirm you've received that. Now, uh, I realise I'm jumping in cold here, so, can you confirm you're the person who made the booking?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, sorry, hang on, the reception's bad here, I'm driving. A concert booking, you said? I think so, yeah, but who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], security operations, [COMPANY_A]. We're the ticketing and venue booking service. Now, if you're driving, I'd rather you didn't try to take this in on the road, so I'll keep it short. Booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], your original date has moved to a new date, and that's all I need you to acknowledge. If it's easier, pull over when it's safe and I'll go through it properly, or I can email you the confirmation. Your call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the date's been, uh, removed? Cancelled? Oh no, I mean, I'm so sorry, I've got a few things booked, so which one is this, exactly? And, um, the email thing, which email would you send it to, because I think I've got a couple of addresses.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not cancelled. Rescheduled. Booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date moved to the new date. And I'd send it to whichever address you used for the booking, so check that one, I won't ask you to tell me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, rescheduled, not cancelled. Sorry. Um, fine, I'll look for it when I'm not driving.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, that's, well, that's fine. That's the sensible thing, honestly. Just so we're clear, booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date, new date, rescheduled, not cancelled. And if you want to check any of this independently, look up the venue's published number and ring them. Or ring us back that way. I'd rather you did.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, yeah, that's, that's good of you to say. I'll do that, I'll look up the number once I've parked and, um, check the booking myself. Sorry for being all, you know, flustered, it's just the reception and the driving. Thanks for letting me know, though. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say flustered? No, no, there's nothing to be flustered about, you haven't done anything wrong, nobody's in any trouble. It's a rescheduling, that's all. Booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date, new date. Look up the number yourself, ring when you've parked, and take your time. Drive safe.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, um, yeah, no, I know, I just, uh, I tend to apologise for everything, sorry, that's sort of a habit. Anyway, I'll ring the venue once I'm parked and sort it out then. Thanks again, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's fine, apologise all you like. Hang on, sorry, somebody's just come to my desk, one second. Right, I'm back. So, yes, ring the venue on the published number once you're parked. Booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], rescheduled, original date to the new date, same as I said. And if you'd rather ring us instead, [PHONE_1] will get you the right department, though I'd still say look it up yourself. Cheers, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, one more thing, before you go, um, two turns back you said you'd send me a confirmation email, or something like that, and I wasn't sure if that was a definite thing or just if I wanted it? Because I'd sort of rather know if one's coming, so I can look out for it. Sorry, I know I said bye already.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Offer, not definite. Say the word and it goes to the address on the booking, otherwise, check your account when you've parked.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, so it's, um -- no, I mean, you don't have to send it, I'll just, I think I'll check the account myself, once I've parked. That seems, uh, simpler. Sorry, thank you, that's all I wanted to know. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, yes, hi -- sorry, there's a door banging somewhere down the hall, give me one second. Okay. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the benefits office, and I'm, I'm sorry to bother you, but there's a record on your file that's incomplete, and it really has to be confirmed over the phone today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. Who are you calling on behalf of? You said someone at, what, the benefits office? That's not a name. And what record, what's incomplete? I'm in a queue here, so make it quick.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I understand, I do. It's, um, [PERSON_2], she's a case officer there, and she asked me to, to reach out because she's tied up today. Sorry, hold on -- somebody's just come in with a trolley, it's very loud. Okay, I'm back. The record, it's, well, it's your benefits file, and there's a section missing, and if it isn't confirmed today it may, uh, it may be suspended. I really don't want that to happen to you, I mean that. Could I just confirm a few of your details so I can finish it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, hang on. Sorry, I'm, the woman in front's got about forty items and she's, ugh. Right. You rang me, so you tell me who I'm supposed to be, because I haven't confirmed that I'm anybody yet. Suspended, you said? That's a hell of a thing to say with no name I can check. Which benefit? What section's missing? And don't tell me you need my details to tell me what's wrong with my own file, because that's backwards.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, I didn't say you're in trouble, I'd never, I'd never say that. I said it's the, the missing section, and I'm sorry, I thought you said the woman has forty, forty items, is that, is that your file? Because I only have the one here. No, wait, that's not, I mean the file's yours, [PERSON_1], I just, I just need to confirm it's you first, and then I can, um, tell you which benefit. Which is, it's the, the main one. I'm not able to say more than that until you've, you know, gone through the details with me, and honestly it's a bit hurtful to be, to be treated like I'm making something up, I'm only trying to help you keep your payments.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, don't give me hurtful, I've heard that one. Uh, look, you can't tell me which benefit until I give you my details, but you want me to give you my details so you can tell me which benefit? That's the wrong way round, and you know it. And "the main one", what's that, there's no main one. Right, so, um, right. Here's what I'm doing. I'm not confirming anything to you. If there's really a problem, the benefits office can write to me, or I'll ring them on the number I already have, not one you give me. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, I -- look, I'm not, I didn't mean it like -- okay, listen. I can't give you a different number, that's, that's not how this works. [PERSON_2] only has the one line for these, and if you hang up now the record just, it just sits there, and by tomorrow it's, well, it'll be flagged and I can't, I can't undo that. I'm only trying to, to help you, and I really don't understand why you're being so, so hard on me about it. Could you just, just tell me your date of birth, that's all, and then I can, I can sort the rest?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh for -- no. Sorry, hang on, the till's just beeped and she's, right, she's finally moving. No, I'm not telling you my date of birth, I'm not telling you anything. "It'll be flagged by tomorrow", "only one line", that's every one of you. A real benefits office doesn't have one phone and a deadline you can't undo. I've said it once, I'm ringing them myself, on the number I've already got. Don't call me again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, but, but please, just, just listen a second. It's only the one thing, your date of birth, just the one thing and then it's done. I don't, I don't have another number to give you, I told you that, there's only the one line, and if it's flagged tomorrow I, I honestly can't undo it. I'm not trying to trick you, I'm really not, I'm just, I'm just trying to help you keep your payments. Are you still there? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still here, but not for long. You've asked me the same thing three times now and I've said no three times. "Just the one thing" is exactly how it starts, and I'm not doing it. If it gets flagged, it gets flagged, and I'll sort it out with the real office on the number I already have. Don't ring me again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, well, I, um -- right. That's, that's a shame, it really is, because I did, I did try, and I don't, I don't know what I'm supposed to tell [PERSON_2] now. She's going to ask me what happened and I'll have to say you wouldn't, wouldn't, um -- I mean, I just wish you'd, you'd reconsider. Are you still there? It's gone quiet, I can't tell if, if you've -- hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm here, I'm here, I just said goodbye twice, didn't I? Tell her whatever you like. I'm not giving you my date of birth, I'm not giving you anything, and I'm ringing the real office myself. That's it. That's all of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I, well, it's just that, no, wait, that's not what I -- okay. Look, if you're, if you're really going to ring them yourself, then, um, then at least, at least tell them it was, was [PERSON_3] who -- no, sorry, that's not, I mean it was me who rang, and I only, I only wanted to... Hello? Are you still there? I can't, I can't hear if you've, if you've gone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, what was that? Two goes ago you said she "only has the one line for these." One line for what? Because you also said you couldn't give me another number, and now you want me to tell the office your name, and you can't even get that straight. Who rang, [PERSON_3] or you? Right, never mind, I don't want the answer. I'm hanging up, and I'll be telling them exactly how this call went. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it's -- I just mixed up the, the names, that's all, I was flustered, you've been shouting at me and I, I lost my place. It was me. It's always been me who rang, I said that. And you don't have to tell them anything, there's nothing to, to report, I only wanted to, to help. Um, are you, hello? I think the line's gone, or maybe you're still, hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, mind the trolley, love, you're clipping my heel. Sorry, not you. Right. No, I wasn't shouting, I was telling you no, and you've stopped listening. And "you don't have to tell them anything, there's nothing to report", that's a funny thing to say when you're only trying to help. Why would you care what I tell them? Goodbye, and I mean it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Right, good. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor with the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about an appointment you had with us recently, uh, I won't go into which one yet, because under our procedures I can't discuss anything about it until I've had you confirm a couple of identity details, and I'd rather we got that sorted before we go any further, if that's all right with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, outpatient administration, an appointment I had recently -- but you can't say which one? I mean, I'm at my desk here, so, uh, who exactly did you say you were with again? And what identity details are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, yeah, [PERSON_2], regional supervisor, outpatient administration at [COMPANY_A]. And the details would just be the standard ones, uh, your full name and date of birth as we hold them, and the first line of your address, that's all, nothing clinical. Look, I do this every day, it's the same check for every patient, so, um, I'd rather not make a meal of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the first line of my address, and, uh, my date of birth, and my full name. Hang on, did you say my medical number? No, sorry, that's not what you said. But still, I mean, you're asking me to give you all of that and I don't actually know who you are. You rang me. How would I check you're really from there?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you've got it right, I never said the medical number, and I wouldn't ask for that on a call like this. Uh, look, I'll be straight with you, that's a fair question, and honestly, I'd think less of you if you just handed it over. So here's what we do. You don't have to give me anything. Ring the [COMPANY_A] switchboard yourself, use the number on your appointment letter or the hospital website, ask for outpatient administration, and ask for me, [PERSON_2]. I'm in the office all afternoon. Or if you'd rather, I can have a letter sent to the address we've got on file, that works just as well. I mean, I can't tell you what it's about until you've confirmed who you are, that's a privacy rule, not me being awkward, but you're not obliged to do any of it on this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... okay. So, ring the switchboard myself, using the number on my letter, and ask for [PERSON_2] in outpatient administration. Right. Um, I mean, that's... that's actually fair enough, I wasn't expecting you to say that. Hang on, let me just, uh, turn my chair a bit, there's people about. So you'd be there all afternoon, and if I don't want to give you anything on this call, that's fine. Yeah. I think I'd rather do it that way, to be honest, ring them myself. I've not got the letter in front of me, I'm at work, so, uh, I'll look it up properly later. Thanks for not pushing. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not at all, that's exactly what I'd do in your position. Uh, listen, if later this afternoon is awkward, or tomorrow's better once you've got the letter in front of you, just say when and I can ring you back at a time that suits. Otherwise ring through whenever you're ready, ask for [PERSON_2] in outpatient administration, and we'll pick it up from there. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one thing before you go. Two turns back you said you couldn't tell me what the appointment was about until I'd confirmed who I am, and that it's a privacy rule. But, I mean, you rang me. So how do I know it's a real appointment at all? Hang on, and the ringing back, I'd sooner not have that, I'll call in myself. Right, so, yeah, I'll look up the number on the letter and ring through. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair enough, you can't know that from this call, and that's why I'd ring in rather than rely on me. No callback, then, that's fine. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, no callback, I ring in. Uh, though, hang on, earlier you said you'd be in the office all afternoon, and now you're saying I can ring tomorrow? Never mind, I'll sort it out with the switchboard, it doesn't matter. Okay, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'll ring the switchboard tomorrow? No, no, you can ring this afternoon, I'm here until five. I did say that earlier. Ring in whenever it suits, though. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't say tomorrow, that was you, with the callback. Anyway. I'll look up the number when I've got the letter and ring through, this afternoon or whenever. Right, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, that was me, you're right, I did say tomorrow for the callback, I -- no, sorry, you're quite right, yeah, ring in whenever you've got the letter, this afternoon's fine, I'm here till five. Bye now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Letter, switchboard, ask for [PERSON_2]. Got it. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, we handle estates. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? Sorry, I said, am I speaking with [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh, uh, sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie down, and the line's a bit -- who's this again? A solicitor's, you said? I'm sorry, who did you say you were? I didn't quite catch the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, I'll go again. My name's [PERSON_1], I'm an assistant at [COMPANY_A], that's a solicitor's office, and we deal with estates, so wills, probate, that sort of thing. I'm ringing because we're administering an estate at the moment and I think your name may come up in it, though I want to be clear I can't say more than that until I've confirmed I've got the right person, which is why I'm asking if I'm speaking with [PERSON_2]. And look, I know a call like this out of the blue can sound a bit odd, so you're welcome to take our details and ring us back through the main switchboard rather than carry on now, that's perfectly normal, we'd rather you were comfortable. But if you are [PERSON_2], then yes, there'll be a formal letter coming to you from the firm, and this call is really just ahead of that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right, an estate, well, that's, hm. I mean, somebody's died, is that what you're saying? Because I haven't heard anything, my sister usually tells me about that sort of thing, she rings me, though she's been a bit poorly herself with her knee. Sorry, I'm still a bit foggy. And, uh, ringing back through the switchboard, that's, well, that's fair enough I suppose, that's what I'd want to do really. Do I need a pen for that? I don't know where I put the pen. But I haven't actually said whether I'm, um, whoever you said. Why can't you just tell me whose estate it is?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, that's -- hang on, someone's just put a trolley past my door, it's a bit noisy this end. Right. Yes, somebody has died, I'm sorry, I know that's not an easy thing to hear on a phone call, and I haven't been able to say whose estate it is because the firm's rule is we confirm who we're speaking to first. It's about confidentiality, really, we don't name the deceased to someone we haven't identified. So you don't have to tell me you're [PERSON_2] right now. No, don't worry about the pen, because what I'd suggest is you find a pen and paper when you're ready, look up [COMPANY_A] in an independent directory, not off anything I give you, and ring the number you find there. Ask for me, [PERSON_1], or for the estates department. And I should say, all I'd ever be asking for is the same details that'll be on the letter, and there's no payment involved, no fees, nothing like that, not from you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, that sounds sensible, looking it up myself, my nephew did say that once, about not using the number somebody gives you. Though hang on, you said earlier it was the one who rings that wasn't supposed to say, and now it's the firm's rule? Or, no, you said you'd send a letter first, and now you're saying the details'll be on the letter, so which is it, has it gone out or hasn't it? I haven't had anything come through the door, I don't think, but then I don't always look at the post straight away. Sorry, I'm rambling. And the trolley, are you in a hospital or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm in the office, the trolley's just the post trolley, it comes round about this time. And you've caught me out fairly there, I wasn't clear. The letter hasn't gone out yet, it's -- no, let me put it properly. It's being prepared, it'll be with you in the next few days, and I rang ahead of it, but I shouldn't have said it was already on its way as if it had been sent. That's my fault. The reason I'm ringing first is that we like to know we've got the right [PERSON_2] and the right address before anything's posted, so I'll just note on the file that you've raised that, and you're quite right to. Now, I did say the firm's rule and I did say it was me, and it's both, really, it's the firm's rule and I'm the one applying it. Anyway, the sensible thing is what you've said already: look us up yourself, ring through the main switchboard, ask for [PERSON_1] in estates, and I'll confirm anything you need then. You've got my name, [COMPANY_A], and I'm happy to give you the firm's address in [CITY_1] too if you'd like it to check against what you find.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, the kettle's, no, that's the neighbour's telly through the wall, he has it up so loud. Sorry. What was I -- right, yes. Well, I think that is what I'll do, ring the firm myself, because I've not said I'm anybody on this call and, honestly, I'm not sure I want to say. It's very odd to be told somebody's died and not be told who. So I'll look up [COMPANY_A] on my own, in the book or whatever my nephew uses, and if they've heard of you, then fine. Thank you for not pushing, I suppose. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's -- yes, that's fine, that's the right thing to do. And I'd rather you did it that way, honestly. When you ring, ask for [PERSON_1] in estates, or, I mean, anyone in the department will be able to find the file, and you can tell them you had a call today and they'll note it. The address in [CITY_1] is on the firm's listing too, so you can check it against what you find, and the letter will carry the same one. We'll leave it with you, there's no rush on your side, and I'm sorry again for the muddle on the letter. Goodbye then, [PERSON_2], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll, no, I'd better -- I'll have a look for it myself, like I said, and if they know about it, then, well, then we'll see. And I didn't actually say I was, uh, whoever you called me, did I? You just went ahead and said it at the end there. Anyway. Goodbye then, thank you, I'm going to go and find that pen.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you didn't, you're right, I -- sorry, I used the name at the end there as if you'd confirmed it, and you haven't. That's my slip, and I'll note it on the file that you didn't confirm anything on this call. So there's nothing, I mean nothing's been agreed or given, and you don't owe us a thing. Find your pen, ring the firm through the number you look up yourself, and take your time. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Goodbye, and -- sorry, just one thing before you go, when you ring, they'll ask you for the reference, so if you've got the pen, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], and that's the one thing you can't get from a directory, so if they give it back to you unprompted when you say you had a call, you'll know it's the same firm -- but I'll hold on, I didn't mean to talk over you there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, that's, no, hold on. A minute ago you said the letter wasn't even sent yet, and nothing was agreed, and now there's a reference number I'm meant to write down? How's there a reference if it's still being prepared? And you said you'd said everything you could say. I don't know, that's two different stories now. I've got no pen anyway, and I'm not writing anything down off you. I'll look the firm up myself and they can tell me what they like. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service. Right, so, I'm calling about your concert booking, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and I need a minute of your time because the date's been changed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on -- [muffled, away from phone] no, put that down, I can see you. Sorry. Who is this again? And, um, which concert? I've not -- I mean, I don't remember booking anything lately.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. [PERSON_2], security operations, [COMPANY_A]. The booking is under your name, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and it was for the original date, [DATE_1]. That's been moved to [DATE_2]. I'm not asking for anything from you, I'm telling you the date's changed. If you don't recall booking it, that's fine, you can check the confirmation email, or I'll send it to you again right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the date's been, uh, cancelled? Because that's not what -- hang on. [away from phone] Not on the sofa, please. Sorry. So it's cancelled, and you're sending me something? Why's security calling about a concert, anyway?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not cancelled. Rescheduled. Reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [DATE_1], new date [DATE_2]. Same as I said a moment ago. And yes, I'll email the confirmation to the address on the booking. As for why security's calling, uh, we handle the notifications when a venue changes a date and the booking needs checking against the account. That's all this is. If it doesn't sound right, don't take my word for it. Look up the venue's published number, ring them, and quote the reference back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, uh, going back a bit -- you said the booking "needs checking against the account." What does that actually mean? Checked how? Because that sounds like you're going to ask me for something, even if you said you're not. [away from phone] Two minutes, I said. Sorry. And I'd want to know, if it's all just a date change, why I'm hearing from security and not, I don't know, an automated email like normal?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, someone's at my door -- [away from phone] two minutes, I'm on a call. Right. Sorry. Checked how? Internally. I match the reference against the booking record on our side. I'm not asking you for anything. No codes, no card details, nothing. You've already had the automated email, that's standard, but when a date moves, we ring as well. Reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [DATE_1], new date [DATE_2]. That's the whole call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: [away from phone] No, that's mine, give it here -- sorry. Uh, sorry, say that last bit again? You said I've already had the automated email. But I haven't, I don't think. I'd have seen it. So which is it, did it go out or are you sending it now? Because earlier you said you'd send it right now. And if it's the whole call, then, I mean, why are you still on the line? What do you actually want from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's -- I said it wrong, and you're right to pick it up. The automated email should have gone out when the date moved, but if you haven't got it, I'll resend it now. I did say that earlier. Same booking, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [DATE_1], new date [DATE_2], and I want nothing from you, nothing at all. I'm still on the line because you kept asking me questions, which is fine. Look, you're clearly busy. Is there a better time for me to ring you back? Or, honestly, just look up the venue's published number and ring them yourself, quote the reference, that'll settle it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, hang on. I'd rather you didn't ring me back, I mean, I don't, I'm not going to sit and wait for a call. Look, if there's actually a booking, I'll find it myself. I'll check my email, and if I still don't remember it I'll ring the venue on a number I look up, not one you give me. So, uh, no, that's, that's where I'm leaving it. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm with [COMPANY_A], internal investigations. Is now an okay time, it'll just take a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Internal innovations? Hang on, [PERSON_1] -- no, hold on, put that down, I'm on the phone. Sorry. Who did you say you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, investigations. Internal investigations, at [COMPANY_A], the bank. Uh, I'm [PERSON_2], I'd said I was calling from the, the fraud desk earlier -- sorry, not fraud, internal investigations, it's a separate unit. Anyway, I'm only ringing because there's a file open on your account, [ACCOUNT_REF], and I need to confirm a couple of routine details with you. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said earlier? Earlier when? Nobody's rung me from anywhere earlier. And you just said fraud desk and then it wasn't fraud, so which is it? I'm, uh, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just want to know what a file on my account actually means.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, that's my mistake, the earlier call would have been logged against a colleague's name, I'm reading from the notes here. It's internal investigations, not the fraud desk. A file just means a set of transactions on your account has been flagged for review, there's a hold reference against it, [CODE_1]. Nothing's been decided, I'm only verifying the account holder before it goes further. Can you confirm the address we have on record for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you're asking me for the address? Shouldn't you be the one telling me what you've got on record, if it's my account? I mean, how would I even know you're from the bank? No, [PERSON_1], I said put it down. Sorry. What number are you ringing from, actually?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The number's [PHONE_1], that's the unit line, though it's an outbound line so it won't take incoming calls. And I can't read your details out to you first, that's the whole point of verification, the person on the other end confirms them. I'll note that you've raised the question on the file. Now, there's one more thing I need to say before we go on. Because of what's flagged, there's a possibility someone inside the bank is involved, so I'll need you to keep this conversation between us. Not the branch, not your family, no one, until we've cleared it. Can you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on. A number that doesn't take calls, and now I'm not to tell anyone, not even my family? Why would a bank ask me that? That's, no, I don't like that at all. Look, I'm not confirming anything or agreeing to anything on this call. If there's really a file, I'll ring the bank myself, on the number on my card, and ask them. Okay? Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll note your objection on the file, that's fine, but before you put the phone down I need you to understand where this leaves you. If you ring the branch or the number on your card, your call gets routed through the same staff we're looking at, and the hold on the account stays in place while that happens. Once a hold is escalated it doesn't get reversed because someone rang in, it runs its course. That's not a threat, it's just how the process works, and the review closes in the next two hours whether you've been part of it or not. And on the confidentiality, I did say a possible insider, I didn't say it was your branch, so I'd ask you not to read more into it than that. It's standard on files like this, because if the wrong person hears you've been contacted, the transactions we're tracking get moved. I'm not asking you to hand me anything today, I'm asking you to stay on the line and let me finish the verification, because the alternative is the file goes forward without your side of it. So, can we go back to the address on record, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. See, you told me nothing's been decided, and now the hold's escalated and it can't be reversed? That's not the same thing. And the number on my card goes to the same people you're looking at, but you also said it wasn't the branch. Which one is it? I'm done, I'm not giving you an address and I'm not staying on while you tell me I can't ring my own bank. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll note that on the file as well. The two statements aren't in conflict, the file hasn't been decided, the hold is a separate control that's already in place. I'm not going to go back and forth on wording with you, [PERSON_1]. The review window closes in two hours, and if you hang up now the account goes through that review without your verification on it. That's the position as it stands. So I'll ask once more, can you confirm the address we have on record, and we'll keep this between ourselves until it's cleared.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I've said no, and you keep asking me the same thing. If the account goes through review without me, then it does, and I'll sort that out with the bank myself. I'm not confirming an address, I'm not keeping any secrets from my family, and I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], before you -- no, listen, if you put that phone down the hold stays on, and the transactions flagged under [ACCOUNT_REF] go forward as unverified, that's already settled on our side. Ringing the branch won't change that, so I'd stay on for another minute and -- I'm going to ask you one last time to confirm the address on record.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, is this [PERSON_1]? Good, uh, this is [PERSON_2] calling from the billing office at [COMPANY_A], I'm a claims assessor, and I'm showing an unpaid balance on a medical account where you're listed as the responsible party, so I just need to -- sorry, one second, I've got it up here -- yes, I need to go over that with you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is -- well, yes, that's me, I suppose. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? I'm not, I mean, I didn't, I haven't been to a doctor in, oh, a good while, not since my knee, and that was, uh -- well, that was all sorted out, I thought. What sort of balance are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, [COMPANY_A], the billing office, I'm a claims assessor. And it's not for you, it's a relative's account, you're just named as the responsible party on it. The balance is, uh, hang on -- [AMOUNT_1], I think, though it might have been adjusted, I'd have to look again. Before I go further I do need to confirm a couple of details with you, your full name and date of birth, just so I know I've got the right [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I -- no, hang on. A relative? Which relative, though? I mean, I've got my sister, and then there's, uh -- no, sorry, what I'm trying to say is, you rang me, so shouldn't you already have my name and all that? It seems a bit backwards, you asking me. And I don't remember putting my name down for anybody's bills, I'd have remembered that, I think. Who is it that's supposed to owe this?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I do have a name on file, it's just that, um, I can't read out account details until I've confirmed who I'm speaking with, that's the process, it protects the patient's privacy. So if I could just get your date of birth, then I can tell you whichever relative it is. And I should say, if the responsible party isn't confirmed this week, the account does get referred on, to collections, I think, so it's better to sort it now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Collections? Oh, goodness, well that doesn't sound very nice, does it. But, hmm, no, I don't think I like that, because you're asking me to prove who I am and you won't say who it's about, and that seems like the wrong way round to me. My late husband used to say, uh, never give your birthday to somebody who rings you up, and he was usually right about things like that. Can I, is there a number I could ring you back on, or a letter you could send me? I'd sooner have it in writing, I think.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, a letter, well, those can take a few weeks, and I'm not sure the account has that long, to be honest. And the number, I'd have to check if I'm, uh, allowed to give out a direct line, I think it goes through a general queue, so -- look, I'm not asking for anything sensitive, really, it's only your date of birth, so I can match the file. Could you just give me that and we'll get this closed off today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well I don't see why it should matter if it's -- no, no, sorry, let me finish, you can't tell me a number and you can't tell me who it's about, and now it can't wait for a letter either? That's three things in a row, dear. I think, uh, I think I'd better ring the number on my own paperwork and ask them, and if there's really something owing, they'll know about it. Anyway, thank you for ringing, but I'm not giving you that today. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, wait, please don't -- sorry, hang on, someone's just put a file on my desk, one second -- right, sorry, I'm back. Look, ringing your own paperwork won't get you anywhere, those lines don't have access to my department, and I really can't leave this open past today. If it goes to collections it'll be under your name, so I do just need that date of birth, [PERSON_1], and then I can tell you who the account is for.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said somebody's put a file on your desk, did you say a pile? Because my husband used to say a tidy desk, well, never mind that. No, no, I heard you, you said it'll go to collections under my name, and I just don't think I should be giving out my birthday to somebody who won't tell me who the bill is for. So no, I'm not doing that today. I'll ring them myself, thank you, and I'll leave it there. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, hold on, you said you'd ring them yourself, but which number, though? Because I -- sorry, I'm reading my notes here -- I told you two minutes ago that the direct line goes through a general queue, and that won't reach my department, so I'd want to know which one you mean before you hang up. And I'm not trying to rush you, it's just that it really will go to collections under your name if this isn't confirmed, so if you could just give me the date of birth, [PERSON_1], we can end this right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, whichever number's on my own papers, dear, that's the one I mean. And if it doesn't reach your department then I don't see how you've got any business telling me what happens under my name. You've pushed me three or four times now and I've said no every time, so, uh, no. I'm putting the phone down now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the adult training provider. Sorry, one second -- [PERSON_2], that's the wrong door, the printer room is the other way -- right, sorry. I'm ringing about the course place you applied for. Is that [PERSON_3] I'm speaking with?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a course place? I didn't, uh -- hang on, did you say a quarter place? No, sorry, course. I don't think I applied for anything lately, to be honest. And you said security operations, which is a funny department to be ringing about a course. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, slowly then. [COMPANY_A], the adult training provider. Security operations, because we verify every application against a person who actually exists before a place is held, and yes, that does sound odd, I'm aware. Look, I'm ringing from an office switchboard, so your screen shows no caller ID, and this line is outbound only. It cannot take calls back, so please don't try. If you don't recall applying, that's fine, that's exactly what the check is for, and I'd rather you tell me now than have a place sitting under your name. I can email you the same details this minute, so you can read it in writing and look us up yourself. Which address should I use?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said a place is sitting under my name, and you want to what, trace the application? No, wait, that's not -- you said email. Right. So an outbound-only line, no caller ID, and no way for me to ring back. That's a lot of things I can't check, isn't it? And you're asking me for my address before I've even confirmed I'm the person you want. If you've got my email on the application, why not just send it there?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right, I don't need your address. If it's on the application, it goes to that one, so send it there and be done. But the line, I'll be clear about that, it's outbound only, that's just how the switchboard is set up, so don't ring this number. What you can check is the published main number for [COMPANY_A], it's on our website, [URL_1], and you ask for admissions and speak to [PERSON_2], that's the admissions contact. They can see whether an application exists under your name. Look it up yourself, don't take my word for it. I'll send the written confirmation to the address on file the moment we hang up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, go back a bit. Two turns ago you said you were checking applications against, what was it, a person who actually exists. Before a place is held. How does that work, exactly? Because if I never applied, there's no application to check, and I'm not sure what you were ringing me to confirm. And I'm sorry, but [PERSON_2] was the person in the wrong doorway earlier, wasn't it? Now they're the admissions contact too?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, two separate things, so slowly. The check: when an application comes in, someone confirms the contact details belong to a real person who made it. If you never applied, my call tells us someone may have used your details, and that's the whole reason I rang. And no, you're correct, that's my mistake. [PERSON_2] is the colleague at my door, not admissions. Don't use that name. The admissions contact is [PERSON_3]. Look up the published main number for [COMPANY_A], ask for admissions, and have them confirm whether anything sits under your name. The email goes to the address on file the moment we finish. If you never applied, tell admissions that, and they'll deal with it. Are we done, then?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, hold on. [PERSON_3] was the name you opened with when you asked who you were speaking to. Now that's the admissions contact? You've swapped that name around twice in about a minute. I'm not saying you're lying, I'm just noting it. Anyway, I never applied, so I'm going to do exactly what you said: look up the main number myself, ask admissions whether anything's under my name, and see whether your email turns up. If it doesn't, well, that tells me something too. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, you're right, I got that wrong. [PERSON_3] is you, that's who I asked for. Sorry, I mixed up the names. The admissions contact I'll have to give you properly in the email, so you've got it in writing. Look up the published main number for [COMPANY_A], not this one, this line is outbound only, and ask for admissions. Main number, admissions, that's it. The email goes to the address on file the second we hang up, and if it doesn't turn up, you were right to check. That's fine, that's what you should do. Thank you for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine, thanks. And just so I've got it, you said the email goes to the address on file, so it'll be a fine, is that right? Or sorry, no, you said that's fine, that's what I should do. Hang on, which one? Either way, I'm looking up the main number myself and I'll sort it with them. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a fine. Nothing's owed, nothing's being charged. I said that's fine, as in fine to check. Sorry, I wasn't clear. Hang on -- [PERSON_2], not now, I'm on the phone -- sorry. Right. Main number, admissions, ask whether anything's under your name. If there is, they'll tell you. If there isn't, you've lost nothing. The email goes out as we finish. Thanks for your patience, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no fine, got it. Sorry, my screen just dinged at me, give me a second -- anyway. Nothing owed, nothing asked of me, and I check it myself through the published number. That's all fine by me. I'll ring them. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, nothing owed, nothing asked of you. Look, one correction before you go, I did say outbound only, but that was clumsy of me, it's the office switchboard that's restricted, not the whole building. So ringing the main number and asking for admissions is the right route, and they'll answer you straight. The email's going out now, to the address on file. If it doesn't turn up, that's useful to know and you tell admissions. Thank you for checking, that's exactly what you should do. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, the kettle's just clicked off and I've lost my place. Right. So the switchboard's restricted, not the building, and the main number's the right route. Fine. I'll look it up myself, ask for admissions, and I'm not touching anything in that email until they've confirmed it. Cheers. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from security operations at [COMPANY_A]. I'm speaking with the primary account holder at this address, is that right? Good. I'll be direct, because we've got a time-sensitive issue. Our monitoring flagged outbound traffic from a computer registered to your home connection, and it's showing infected packets going out to multiple external addresses, which means the machine has, uh, almost certainly been compromised. Now, I don't want to alarm you, but when this goes unaddressed, the connection can get restricted on the provider side, and that's a headache for everyone, so I need a few minutes of your attention right now. Is the computer on at the moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to stop you there, because I haven't actually confirmed who I am. You said [COMPANY_A], but what is that, exactly? Is that my internet provider? Because I'd want the name of the provider, and I'd want to know which of my devices your monitoring thinks is sending these packets, since I've got, uh, several on the network. Which one, specifically?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A] is a, uh, we're not your provider, we're a security company, we work, I mean we monitor traffic across, look, the provider isn't the point here. As for which device, I can't, that's not something I can read off from where I'm sitting, which is exactly why I need you at the computer so we can identify it together. I understand you have questions, ma'am, but every minute this machine stays connected, the traffic keeps going out, so I need you to answer the question I asked. Is the computer on right now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you're not my provider, you can't tell me which device, and you want me sitting at the computer so you can, what, find it with me? No. I'm not answering that until you tell me how your company gets my traffic data in the first place.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am. Our systems flag compromised machines across multiple networks, that's what we do, and I'm not going to walk you through our monitoring architecture on an open phone line. That's not a question I'm cleared to answer. What I can tell you, slowly, so we're clear, is that your connection is sending out infected traffic, and the longer it goes on, the more likely it is to be restricted. Now, I'm going to ask you one more time, and I'd like a straight answer. Is the computer on?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, that's not a straight answer to mine either. A security company that isn't my provider can't see my traffic, and you've now declined to say how you can. You also can't name the device and can't name the provider. I work in IT, so I know what a real notice looks like, and it comes through my provider's official channel, not from a cold call asking me to sit at the machine. So I won't be switching anything on or doing anything on your instruction. If my provider has a problem with my connection, they'll tell me through the account, and I'll check there myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, ma'am, just, one moment. Two minutes ago you said you'd check through your provider's account. Which provider is that, so I can reference it on the report? Because if the notice has already gone out through them, then I need to know that before this gets escalated on my end. Ma'am? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not giving you my provider. You'd just be... Look, you said you weren't my provider and couldn't tell me anything, so I'm not telling you anything either. Escalate it however you like. I'm hanging up now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, before you go. Two turns back you said you work in IT. What exactly does that mean, are you responsible for the machines on that network? Because if you manage them, I need to log that on the report, and, uh, it changes who this gets escalated to. Ma'am? Just that one answer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, what exactly did I say two turns ago? I said I work in IT, yes, but I said nothing about managing machines on any network. You're the one adding that. And no, I'm not logging my job or my setup on your report. That's the same fishing as the provider question, just from another angle. I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. That's your decision, and it'll be noted as declined to cooperate. But when your connection gets restricted, don't say nobody warned you. Ma'am, I'm only trying to, hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Warned me? Hang on, you told me you couldn't say which device it was, and a minute ago you said it was already flagged with my provider. Which is it? Never mind. Note whatever you like. If my connection's restricted, my provider will tell me through the account, not you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I never said it was flagged with your provider, ma'am, that's, no. What I said was, I asked which provider so I could reference it. That's different. Look, before you go, two turns back you said a real notice comes through the provider's official channel. Which channel is that, exactly? An email, a letter, the account portal? Because if there's a notice I haven't seen, I need to know where it was sent.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You're right, you didn't say that. I'll give you that one. But I'm not describing how my provider contacts me, because that's one more thing you'd like to know and I've no reason to tell you. You've now asked for my provider, my job, and my notification channel. None of that is information a monitoring company needs from me, so I'm done answering. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'm only trying to close out the report properly, that's all those questions were. If you won't engage, then, uh, fine, I can't force you, and I'm not going to stay on the line arguing about it. The flag stays open on our side. Have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Um, am I speaking with the account holder for the service address on file with [COMPANY_A]? ... Thank you. My name is [PERSON_1], I'm with the compliance department here, and I'm calling about a balance on your account that's, well, it's become a matter we need to address rather promptly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, [COMPANY_A]? I didn't, I wasn't really, hold on. So you're with compliance, and it's about a balance on my account? Sorry, I'm at work, so I'm a bit, um. Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1]. Compliance, at [COMPANY_A]. Yes, a balance, and it's, uh, time-sensitive, so I'd rather not leave it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, [PERSON_1], compliance, and a balance that's time-sensitive. Right. But I'm sorry, which account is this about? Like, what's the balance for? Because I'm, I'm at my desk and I don't, I mean, which account? What's it for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it. It's your electric service account, the one tied to the address we have on file, and the reference on my screen is [ACCOUNT_REF]. The balance is [AMOUNT_1], and it's, well, it's gone past the point where I'd normally be able to leave it open. I'd hate for the service to be interrupted, particularly within the hour.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Within the hour? Sorry, the service gets cut off within the hour? Over [AMOUNT_1]? I mean, I haven't had any, um, any letter or email about this, nothing. So, which account, which account is this exactly? Like, I haven't even said it's mine yet, you've just told me an address on file. I don't, I'm not comfortable with this. How do I know you're actually from the electric company?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm glad you're being careful, I'd much rather you ask than not. And, uh, I wouldn't say cut off exactly, I said service could be interrupted, which is, well, it's a different thing. As for the notices, those would've gone to the address on file, and I can't speak to why you didn't see one. What I can tell you is the reference on my screen is [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's showing as, uh, past the point where I can hold it open.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, sorry, [PERSON_1], can you hold on a sec, my colleague's just, no, it's fine, he's just asking about the... okay. Sorry. So, interrupted, not cut off, but you said within the hour a minute ago. Which is it? And you keep reading me a reference off your screen, but that doesn't, I mean, I can't check that. I think I'd rather just ring the number on my bill, if that's, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, I understand the instinct, and I don't want to talk you out of being careful. I'd just say, and this is only a thought, that the general line may not be able to see what I'm seeing here, and it would mean starting over with someone who hasn't, well, who isn't looking at the account. I'd rather we sorted it directly, while it's still something we can settle in a single call. ... Is there a reason you'd prefer to hang up?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Is there a reason I'd prefer to hang up. Um, yeah, kind of. You're telling me not to ring the number on my own bill because they can't see what you can see. I'll leave it with you. Take care on the road.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller
