utterances.text: No, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it, because it's exactly the sort of thing you should ask. Compliance, it's, uh, the part of a firm that checks things are done properly, that everything's in order, nothing more mysterious than that. And you're right to catch me on the wording. It's not about anything of yours. It's about [PERSON_3]. But [PERSON_3] needs a family member, someone they trust, and you were the name that came up. So it's about [PERSON_3], and it touches you only in that sense. I'd just say, [PERSON_1], that I can't go into the whole of it here, not with [PERSON_3] not able to speak, and it's, well, it's better if this stays between us for the moment, and the sooner the better, if I'm honest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh, hm. Right. Between us, you say. That's, I mean, that's a funny thing to ask, isn't it, when it's family? Hold on, let me just, uh, sit down properly, I've got the kettle on in the other room and I'm standing here in the hall like a lemon. Now, what's this need of [PERSON_3]'s, exactly? And why can't they come to the phone themselves, are they poorly? Because if they're poorly I'd want to know, I'd want to ring them myself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, go and sit down, take your time. No, I'll wait. ... Right, good. Now, poorly isn't quite the word, and I'd rather not put words in [PERSON_3]'s mouth, that wouldn't be fair to them. What I can say is they're in a bit of a difficult spot, nothing frightening, but it's, uh, the kind of thing where [PERSON_3] would be embarrassed, and that's really why I'm asking for discretion. As for ringing them yourself, I understand the instinct, I do, it's a kind one. But I'd gently ask you not to, not just yet, because it might make things harder for them, and, well, I wouldn't want to see it drag on any longer than it has to. What [PERSON_3] needs is someone steady, someone who'll hear me out and help with a small matter, [AMOUNT_1] or so, to put things right. Would you be willing to hear the rest?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'm sitting now, so, uh... mm. Well, [AMOUNT_1], that's, hm. That's not nothing, is it? And you want me not to ring [PERSON_3], which, I'll be honest, that's the bit that's sitting oddly with me. If it's family you'd think, well, I mean, I used to ring their mother on Sundays, lovely woman, terrible with the telephone though, she'd put it down mid-sentence. Sorry, I'm wandering. Where was I? Yes. Why would ringing them make it harder? That doesn't quite add up, does it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, don't apologise, I like hearing it. A woman who puts the phone down mid-sentence, that's, well, that's the sort of thing you remember about a family. And you're quite right to say it doesn't add up, [PERSON_1], I'd think less of you if you didn't. I'd only ask you to consider that I'm not the one who chose how this is handled. [PERSON_3] asked for it to be kept quiet, and I'm trying to respect that, even though I can see how it looks from where you're sitting. There's a, uh, an order to these things, and the longer it waits the more awkward it becomes for everyone, [PERSON_3] most of all. I won't pretend otherwise. But it's your decision, entirely. If you're willing to help, I can tell you how it would go, and if you'd rather think it over, well, I'd understand, though I can't say how long that would leave things open.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said there's an odour to these things? Well, I can't say I've, hm, I haven't noticed any smell, no. Unless that's the kettle, I did leave it on, I should really go and look at it. But, uh, an odour of what, exactly? Because if [PERSON_3] is in some sort of trouble, I'd rather you just told me plainly, I'm not very quick with hints. And I still don't see why I can't just ring them myself, that's the part I keep coming back to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, not an odour, an order, I said an order to these things, a sequence, one thing and then the next. Go and see to the kettle, by all means, I'll hold. ... Right. Now you've asked me plainly, so I'll try to answer plainly, which is, uh, that [PERSON_3] is in a bit of financial difficulty, a matter that needs settling, and, well, I'd rather, I mean, I should say that I'm only the, no, let me put it differently. They asked me to find someone who wouldn't judge them, and you were that person, and that's rather touching, isn't it? As for ringing them, I can't promise they'd pick up, and I'd hate for you to be left worrying. So if you could just tell me you're willing to help, [PERSON_1], that would, uh, set things moving in the right way, and I'd be, well, relieved, truly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, an order, right, sorry, I did think that was odd. Kettle's fine, by the way, it switched itself off. Now, I don't mind saying I'm fond of [PERSON_3], but I can't just say I'm willing when I don't know what I'd be willing to do. That's like signing something with your eyes shut, isn't it? And you still haven't said why [PERSON_3] can't pick up their own phone, or why a person from a firm is doing the asking and not them. So here's what I think. I'll ring [PERSON_3] myself, I've got the old number somewhere, in the drawer with the stamps. And if they say yes, I need help, well, then they can tell me themselves. Thank you for ringing, but I'll leave it there. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, it's [PERSON_1] from [COMPANY_A], I'm the regional supervisor on the adult training side, and I'm ringing about the course place you applied for, the one that, uh -- sorry, I know the line's showing no number, that's just our office switchboard, it only does outbound. Is that all right, have you got a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, I'm in a queue here. What course place? I haven't -- I don't remember applying for anything. And you said something about the number, what was that, no number showing? Say that bit again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem. The number, right, our switchboard doesn't show a caller ID when it rings out, it's outbound only, so if you tried to ring that number back it wouldn't connect. That's just how the office system's set up, nothing unusual. And on the course, it'd be an application through our website, probably a few weeks back, so if it's not ringing a bell, that's fine, I can send the details to your email right now and you can have a look when you're out of the queue. I mean, it's all standard, I just need to know whether you want them sent over.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, let me get this straight. You're ringing me from a number I can't see, I can't ring it back, and you're telling me that's all perfectly normal. Well, it's not normal to me. And I've been caught out before, I'm not going into it, but I'm still annoyed about it, so you can understand why that doesn't sit right. And now I applied to something on a website a few weeks back that I don't remember, and you want to fire details to my email. Which email? Because you haven't said what you've got for me, have you? You've not said my name either, you've said [PERSON_1] is you, fine, but you haven't said who I am. So what name have you got down for this application? And which course? Because if it was a real course I'd have a confirmation sitting somewhere, and I'd know the name of it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I'm not -- okay, I get why you're wary, I do. The thing is, I'd rather not read out personal details down an open line to someone I haven't verified, that's procedure, so I won't say your name or the course until you're comfortable. And honestly, if you've been caught out before, then don't take my word for any of it. Here's what I'd do. Look up [COMPANY_A]'s main number yourself, the published one on the website, not one I give you. Ask for admissions and ask for [PERSON_3], that's our admissions contact, and they can tell you whether there's an application under your name. I can send the email confirmation as well, but you don't have to take that either. I mean, I'd actually prefer you checked.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a minute ago you wanted to email me the details right now, and now it's don't take my word for it, ring the main number. Which is it? And you said you can't say my name because of procedure, but you rang me. You knew who you were ringing. So you've got a name, you just won't say it. That's backwards, that is. Look, I'm not ringing anyone back off the back of this. If there's a course place, it'll be in my emails somewhere, and I'll find it myself, or I won't, and then it wasn't real. Right, I'm at the front of the queue now, I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just -- no, leave that there, thanks. Right, sorry. Look, that's fair, both can be true, the email's there if you want it, but ringing the main number yourself is the better check, and you're right to want that. You've not been unreasonable, I'd do the same. So go and find it in your emails, or ring [COMPANY_A] on the number you look up and ask for [PERSON_3] in admissions, and if there's no application under your name, then fine, ignore my call. Go on, get to the front of your queue. Sorry to have held you up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right, well, hang on, I've still got the phone to my ear here, the lad's scanning my stuff. Erm, yeah. Look, I'll check my emails, and if there's nothing there, that's the end of it. And I'm not sending anything off to anyone, just so you know. Right, that's me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, just one thing before you go, you said you won't send anything off to anyone. That's absolutely fine, I'm not asking you to send us anything, not by email, not by phone. If there's an application under your name, it's all on our side already, so there's nothing you'd need to send. And if you want to check, ring the published main number for [COMPANY_A], ask for [PERSON_3] in admissions, and I'll be quite happy with that. Right, enjoy the rest of your queue, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, you've said it three times now, ring the main number, ask for [PERSON_3], I heard you. And you're right that you've not asked me for anything, I'll give you that. But I'll tell you how this looks from where I'm standing. A call from a number I can't see, a course I don't remember, a name you won't say even though you obviously know it, and a lot of being very helpful and very reasonable about it. That's exactly how it went last time, all very smooth, and I'm not doing that again. So I'm not ringing anybody on the strength of this. If there's a course, there'll be a confirmation in my emails, and if there isn't, then it's nothing to do with me. Now I've got a bag half packed and a lad waiting, so that's it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? Great. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the shop over on the high street in [CITY_1], and the reason I'm ringing is that you entered our prize draw at the community open day a couple of weeks back, and I'm very pleased to say your entry was drawn for one of our minor prizes. Now it's not a huge thing, I don't want to oversell it, but it is a genuine prize, and the way our process works is that we have to confirm the winner by phone and then log the collection within our standard window, which closes at five o'clock today, so that's really why I'm calling now rather than leaving it. So, if you've got a minute, I just need to go through the confirmation with you, and, uh, I'll explain everything as we go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who? Which shop? I'm between meetings, so what's the actual point here? I don't remember any prize draw, and "confirmation" -- confirm what exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, of course, uh, sorry, I'm [PERSON_2], account services at [COMPANY_A], on the high street in [CITY_1]. The draw was at the community open day, the, um, the one where we had the little stall by the entrance, you'd have filled in a slip with your name and number, that's how I've got this number. And the confirmation is just that, it's you, you're the winner, and you're collecting in person at the shop, nothing to pay, nothing to send. I do need to log it before the five o'clock close today, so, uh, if you've got a moment, I'll just go through the details.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry -- [pause] no, tell them I'll be two minutes -- right, sorry. Where was I. Open day, slip with my name and number. Mm. I genuinely don't remember that, and I get a lot of these calls. So what details, exactly? You've got my name and number already, you said, so what are you going through?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, the details, uh, it's really just the standard confirmation procedure. I confirm the name on the entry slip, and then I log a collection slot, and that's it. And, um, to be clear, I'm not asking you for anything beyond that today. Now, the logging does have to be done before the five o'clock close, so if we could just go through it, I'll, uh, I'll take you through the confirmation now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but you've said "the confirmation" three times now and I still don't know what it involves. Name on the slip, fine, you've got that. So what else? And what's the prize? You haven't told me that either. Tell me what I've won.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, fair enough, uh, that's a fair question. The prize is a, a gift hamper from the shop, it's a minor prize, I did say, nothing life-changing. And what I'd need is just the, the full name as it was written on your slip, and then a day you could come in to collect, that's all. I'd also normally take a date of birth for the winners' log, but, uh, if you're not comfortable with that, I mean, it's, it's our standard procedure, but we can note that you declined. And the logging does close at five today, so, if we could just, um, go through the name on the slip.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no. A date of birth for a hamper? That's not a winners' log, that's an ID check. And you've got my name and number off the slip already, so why am I reading my own name back to you? Here's what I'll do. Give me the shop's number, I'll look it up myself, not the one you give me, and ring them. If I won a hamper, it'll still be there tomorrow. Five o'clock doesn't change that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that, uh, that's fine, I mean, that's reasonable. The shop's [COMPANY_A], on the high street in [CITY_1], you can look us up yourself, and ask for account services, and, um, ask for [PERSON_2]. The thing is, the logging window does close at five today, I did say that, but, uh, nothing to pay, nothing to send, collection in person at the shop, that's all it is. And you were at the open day, the community open day, the stall by the entrance, so, uh, you'll know it when you think about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. You still haven't given me a number, you've given me a name and told me to search for it. And you've told me I'll "know it when I think about it", which isn't the same as me remembering it. Look, I'll look the shop up myself and call the main line. If there's a hamper, they'll sort it, and if the window closes at five, then it closes. I'm not confirming anything on an inbound call. Right, I've got a meeting. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, uh, just before you go, you said two turns ago you'd call the main line, and I just want to be clear, did you want the main line number, or, um, should I just leave it with the shop? Because I can read it out, it's [PHONE_1], that's the shop, [COMPANY_A], on the high street. But, uh, I understand, that's fine, you've got your meeting. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't read it out. I'm not going to ring a number that you've just given me down the phone, that's rather the point of looking it up myself. I'll find the shop's number independently, ring the main line, and ask whether there's a draw and whether I'm on it. If there is, they'll tell me, and they can log whatever needs logging, and if the window's shut by then, well, a hamper's a hamper. But I'm not confirming anything, no name, no date of birth, nothing, on a call I didn't ask for. Anyway, I've really got to go. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, yes, no, understood, that's, um, that's entirely your call and I won't press it. So, uh, if you do ring the shop, it's just the draw from the open day, they'll have the list, and, um, nothing's needed from you today, honestly. Okay, well, thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, enjoy the rest of your meeting. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So, just so we're clear, I'm not confirming anything, I'll look the shop up myself and ring them, and I'm not taking a number from you. Nothing today. Okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, I mean, that's all fine, that's, uh -- sorry, I'll, you'll find us easily enough, we're the, well, you know, the shop on the high street. So, uh, nothing today, that's right, and, um, the draw was the open day, so if you ask them they'll, they'll sort it. Okay, thanks, [PERSON_1]. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, one thing before I go. A few turns back you said the logging closes at five today. Closes how? If I ring the shop tomorrow and they say there's no draw, or I'm not on any list, what then? Because you've been very keen on today, and "nothing to pay, nothing to send" isn't an answer to why it has to be today. Anyway, I'm going to look them up and ring. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the pension provider. I'm just, uh, ringing about a change to your plan, and we do need to confirm a few details before I can discuss it, so if you've got a couple of minutes now, that'd be ideal. Actually, sorry, I did say a couple of minutes, and it's more like five, we close the queue for today's reviews at four, so, yes, that's the window I'm working with.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good afternoon! Sorry, say that again, a change to my... was it my planet? No, no, my plan, sorry, it's the line, it crackles a bit. A pension, you said. Well, I've got one of those somewhere, my late husband sorted it all, he was very good with paperwork. I've got the kettle on, so five minutes is fine, I'm only sitting here. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, [PERSON_1], account services at [COMPANY_A]. Pension provider. Look, no pressure at all, if you'd rather ring us back on the number on your paperwork, that's perfectly fine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's kind of you to say, ringing back, I mean. Only the paperwork, now, where did I put it all? Harold kept it in a big brown folder, he labelled everything, and after he went I moved it, I think it's in the sideboard, or it might be the spare room, I did have a clear out in the spring, the girl next door helped me, lovely girl, she's got a little boy who's mad about trains. Anyway, I'm not very good with the phone side of things, you see, I never know if it's the right number or not, so I wouldn't want to ring and end up talking to the wrong people. Which is a funny thing to say to you, isn't it, since you've rung me! Now, what is it that's changed, exactly? You said a change to the plan, and I'd like to know a little bit about that before I go handing over anything, because Harold always said never to do that on the phone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, Harold was quite right, and honestly I'd rather you didn't hand over anything today until you're comfortable. Uh, as for the change itself, I'm afraid I only have a note on my screen that says a plan change has been requested and that the details need confirming before it goes through, so I can't tell you more than that, and it's sort of out of my hands what happens next. I mean, I'd prefer not to rush you, so the window I mentioned, four o'clock, don't worry about it. If you'd like, I can put the same query in the post to you, or send it through the secure message service, and you can look at it with the folder in front of you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, that's the kettle, it's gone and clicked off, give me a tick. ... No, it's all right, I'll leave it, it'll keep. Now, where was I? Yes, the post. Well, that sounds sensible, Harold liked things in writing, he used to say if it isn't written down it didn't happen. But it's funny, isn't it, you ringing about a change and not knowing what the change is? I wouldn't have thought that's much use to you, having only a note on a screen. Who asked for it, I wonder? I certainly never asked for anything, I wouldn't know how. Is that something you can see, who put the request in?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, which bit was it you wanted me to go back over? Is it the post, or the bit about the note on my screen? Because, I mean, for the second one, all I can see is that a change has been flagged against your plan, and where the request came from, whether that's you, or a form, or someone on your behalf, it doesn't show me that, and I'd be guessing if I said. Which I won't do, because that wouldn't be fair to you. So, no, I can't answer that one, but I can find out who raised it, and then I'll ring you back with it, or put it in writing as well, whichever you'd rather.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Well, that's honest of you, saying you'd only be guessing. Harold couldn't stand people who guessed, he'd say, well, either you know or you don't. But it does seem a bit odd to me, a change on my plan that nobody can tell me who asked for. I'd like to know that before anything goes through, wouldn't I? So I think the post is best. If you put it all in writing, who raised it and what it's about, then I can find Harold's folder and look at it properly with my glasses on. I wouldn't want to ring you back, mind, I'd only get in a muddle with the numbers. Is that all right? Will it come from you, or from the main office?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's perfectly all right, and you're quite right to want it before anything goes through. Uh, that's the thing, I honestly don't know whether it'll come from me or from the main office, I'm not sure which team sends the letters out, and I'd rather not say one thing and have it turn out to be another. I'll find that out, and I'll find out who raised the request too, and then I'll ring you back to let you know. Or, I mean, if you'd rather not have another call at all, just say, and I'll put it all in the post instead.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, don't ring me back, dear, I'd only be in the middle of something and I'd forget to ask the right things. The post is lovely, I'll wait for that. And if it's all the same to you, I'll not do anything until it's turned up and I've had a good look at it with Harold's folder. If there's something that matters, it can be put in writing, can't it? Well, it's been nice having a chat, I don't get many calls these days, you've a very pleasant way about you. Thank you for ringing, and mind how you go. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, goodbye then, and thank you, that's very kind. So it's the post, then, in writing, and you'll not do anything until it's turned up, and that's the right way round, honestly. I'll put a note on your account so nobody rings you again about it, and I'll find out who raised the request and which office sends the letter, so it's all in there. Goodbye now, and, uh, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very good of you, thank you. Um, well, now, let me see, uh... yes, no, I think that's everything, isn't it? I'll go and put that kettle back on and have a hunt for the folder, so it's all to hand when the letter comes. Goodbye then, dear, and you take care too.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Good, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A] -- I'm in the collections team, and I'm looking at your file, it shows a monthly gift of [AMOUNT_1] that stopped coming through a few months back, and I just wanted to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A monthly gift that, uh, stopped -- hang on, did you say the file shows a mortgage? Because I don't have a mortgage with anyone called [COMPANY_A], so I'd like to know which account you think this is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a mortgage -- a monthly gift, a donation. [COMPANY_A] is a charity, I'm not -- it's nothing to do with any loan or, uh, any account you owe on. I can see why it sounded that way, I started off badly. What I've got here is a regular donation of [AMOUNT_1] a month that you set up with us, and it lapsed. That's all this is, a thank-you for the support you gave and a question about whether you'd want to start it up again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, a donation, okay. Sorry, one second, someone's at the door -- no, it's fine, they've gone, just a parcel on the step. Where was I. So, a charity. Which charity, exactly? You said [COMPANY_A], but that's a placeholder to me, I mean, I don't recall setting up anything like that, and I'd also say "collections team" is an odd department to be ringing me from if it's a thank-you call. What's the reference on the original direct debit, or whatever it was?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on a second, someone's just put a trolley past my desk -- right, okay, back. Fair point on the department name, it's what they call us here, but all I do is ring lapsed supporters. The reference on the file is [ACCOUNT_REF], though I'd rather not read out more than that on a call you didn't expect. I'm reading figures off a screen, so the last payment shows as [AMOUNT_1], and after that nothing came through, which means the gift has been marked as cancelled on our side. If you don't remember setting it up, I can't prove that to you over the phone, and I'm not going to argue it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you can't prove it, I don't remember it, and it's already cancelled. Then there's nothing for me to restart, is there. If I've got a gift on record, I'll find it myself and ring the number on the charity's own website. I'm not setting anything up over the phone today. Thanks for your time.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's fine, no problem at all. I'll note on the file that you don't want to renew over the phone, and I can take you off our calling list as well, so you won't get another call from us. Checking with the charity directly on their own website is a perfectly sensible thing to do. Sorry for the confusion at the start, and thanks for what you did give. Have a good day, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, take me off the list please. And I'll check with them directly, as I said. Thanks. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, yep -- so that's you removed from the calling list, I'll mark it now, it's done. And there's nothing else you need to do on this, no forms, nothing. Okay, so, um, thanks again for the earlier support, and, uh, goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so I'll -- no, actually, before I go, I should say, if you ever want to look at it again, it's -- well, there's no obligation, the charity's own website is the place for that. Anyway, that's the list updated. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, understood. As I said, I'll go through the charity's own site if I decide to. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'll go through the charity's own site, or you'll go through the charity's own sight? No, hang on, that's a daft thing to ask, I've got the, uh, lapsed gift in my head and I'm half-hearing everything as a payment. Right, so you're handling it yourself, that's absolutely fine, and you're off the list. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: receiver

Is that all right? And you can just have your latest statement beside you, that's all you'd need.

Would the, um, the newest one be the right one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, it's the other way round, I read out and you just tell me yes or no. And yes, the newest one's the right one, the most recent that's come in the post. Oh, and you said something about a dresser, um, no need to worry about any dressing or, uh, getting anything ready beyond finding that statement. Sorry, that's me being silly, I think I misheard you. Are you still with me, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, it was the dresser drawer, where I keep the post, not any dressing, sorry, that was my fault for mumbling. The number on the front of your statement is the one to ring, so look that up yourself and ask for the compliance team, and I'd be glad if you did. Sorry, I think I lost you for a second.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, I'm here, the cat again, she's got her head in my cup now. Thank you for saying that, that's very kind, I think I'd feel better ringing the number on the statement. Um, sorry, but can I go back a bit? Before, you said you'd read things out and I'd say yes or no, and what sort of things are on file? Only I don't want to say yes to something and then find I've said yes to the wrong thing, I'm not very quick with it. And, um, if I ring the number on the statement, would it be you I get, or someone else?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, that's a fair question, and you're right not to say yes to anything you're unsure of, nobody should. So I'd read out what the file says you hold in the account, and then you'd look at the page and say whether it matches, or whether anything's missing or looks wrong. I wouldn't ask you for anything that isn't already printed there. No passwords, no codes, nothing like that, and I'm not recommending anything or selling anything, it's purely a check that the record's right and the account still suits you. The main line would put you through to the compliance team, and if you give them my name, [PERSON_2], and the reference [ACCOUNT_REF], they'll be able to see this review on the file. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, yes, sorry, I was just thinking while you were talking. That's ever so kind of you to explain it all properly, and I do appreciate you not rushing me. Um, but I've been sitting here wondering, and sorry if this sounds daft, if it's all on my statement already, and you've got it on your file as well, then what is it you need me to tell you that you don't know? Because you said I'd just say yes or no, and I'd be looking at the same page you're reading from, wouldn't I? I'm not saying anything's wrong, I'm only trying to understand it, I'm not quick with these things. And, um, I think I'd feel happier ringing the number on the front of the statement like you said, and asking for the compliance team, and giving them your name, was it [PERSON_2]? Sorry, I wrote nothing down, and the reference as well. Would you mind saying that again, slowly, and I'll fetch a pen? The cat's knocked the pen pot over, hang on, I'll find one. Oh, and sorry, what was the name of the company again? I think I only half caught it at the start.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, it isn't daft at all, that's exactly the right question, and honestly, you're right, sorry. I'm reading from the same page you'd be looking at. I can't promise it'll be me, that's all I meant. The main line puts you through to the compliance team, and anyone there can bring up the review. Right, have you got the pen? utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm here, sorry, I've got the pen now, the cat had it under the dresser. utterances.text: No, no, not a flood, I said an earlier job, the engineer's got another visit before yours, that's all. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I misheard, an earlier job, right. No, that reference doesn't ring a bell, I'm afraid. I live on my own, so I don't know who'd have rung for me.

utterances.text: Right, well, if you live on your own then it's, uh -- look, it could be a logging error, I'm not going to pretend it can't be. Those do happen. utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, I'll do that, I'll ring the number on my bill. Thank you, and sorry for the muddle. Goodbye then.

utterances.text: No, no, that's absolutely fine, you've nothing to apologise, I'd much rather -- sorry, go on. Right, sorry to have troubled you, [PERSON_1], mind how you go. Goodbye.

It's just that I'm not very good with names and dates at the best of times, and I didn't want to say yes to something I couldn't remember, you see. And that's a good tip about looking someone up myself, I'll bear that in mind if I ever do want the bathroom done. utterances.text: Oh, um, I'm sorry, I think I'd rather not say, if that's all right. I'm just not certain about any of it, like I said, and I don't really want to go getting it wrong. I really don't remember anyone coming round, you see, and I haven't got a quote sheet, so I'd just strike it off, I think. Yes, strike it off, that's probably best. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, um... yes. Thank you, that's very good of you, and, uh, no harm done at all, really. I'll, I'll certainly do that, find someone myself, I mean. Right then. Goodbye now, mind how you go yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, right, that's -- sorry, you said a couple of jobs, but I think I only reported the one thing, the heating, I didn't actually say anything about the lift, that was a neighbour I think. Or maybe I did, I don't know, I'm getting muddled. Um, and sorry, is it [COMPANY_A] or, I thought you said maintenance team, not utility? utterances.text: No, not picky at all, [PERSON_1], everyone asks that. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, that's -- well, that's actually kind of reassuring, you telling me to check. Um, so would it be all right if I rang the number on the, the website later, once I'm home? And, sorry, is there anything I need to do before then, or is it just, wait for him to turn up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, absolutely, [PERSON_1], ring later once you're home, that's the sensible thing, and please don't look anything up while you're driving. Oh, and if he ends up coming first thing, would you be home, or is that a problem with work?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I, uh -- no, first thing might be, I mean I'd have to -- sorry, I don't actually know if I'd be home, it depends on work, and I don't really want to say too much about when the flat's empty, if that's okay. It's just, I'm a bit, I'm not sure why you'd need to know that, when I haven't even checked the booking yet. So, um, I think I'll ring the number on the website when I'm back and sort out a time with them, that sounds better. Is that all right? Sorry, I hope that doesn't sound rude.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not rude at all, [PERSON_1], honestly, that's exactly the right call, and you're quite right, I shouldn't have asked about when you're in, that's for the booking line to sort out with you. Sorry, hang on -- [PERSON_3], mate, can you move your wagon, I'm blocking the -- sorry, [PERSON_1], where was I. utterances.text: No, [PERSON_1], don't apologise, you're right to leave it there, and I'd rather you ring the number on your bill than take my word for it. Okay, thanks, sorry again, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: Mm, no, wait, that's not -- [CHILD_1], not on the sofa with that, sorry, I'm here. Uh. So you can't take calls and you can't give me a number, but I should go and ring somebody else and ask for a person you've just named to me? And you'll email me from the provider's own address, which, I haven't given you an email address, have I? Which one are you going to send it to? And what's actually on that application that needs confirming before it goes out?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, that is what I'm saying, and I'll go through it in order. The email goes to the address on the application form. I'm not going to read it out, but you'll know at once whether it's one you gave us, and if it isn't, that tells you something too. What needs confirming is only that the place is still wanted, the start date, and the fee arrangement. [AMOUNT_1] isn't due today. Nothing is due today. I'm not asking you for money, a code, or any payment or account details on this call, and I'm not going to. Now, on ringing somebody else, yes, that's exactly what I want you to do. You find the main number for [COMPANY_A] yourself, from our website, not from me, and you ask for [PERSON_3] in admissions. If they've never heard of the application, or of me, then you don't proceed, and you're right not to. I'd rather you checked than took my word for it. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, hang on, I'm going to stop you there, because -- [CHILD_1], I said not now! Sorry. Right. Honestly, that does sound fair, checking it myself, that's what I'd do anyway. But then why are you ringing me at all? If nothing's due and nothing needs doing today, why not just let admissions sort it out the normal way? And what do I lose if I just don't pick any of this up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Why am I ringing? Because the written confirmation was meant to go out today, and my side holds it until the place is confirmed, that's the whole reason. And if you don't pick it up, you lose nothing, really, the place just lapses at the end of the week. Not a penalty, it simply goes to the next person on the list. Sorry, I did say nothing needed doing today, and that's not quite right, is it. The confirming is what's time-bound, the paying isn't. So -- no pressure from me, but do check, ring the main number, ask for [PERSON_3], and have a look for the email while you're at it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. So -- hang on, two minutes ago you said you can't take calls, the line only goes out, but now I should ring the main number and ask for [PERSON_3], so, how would that get back to you? If admissions say they've never heard of this, who do I tell? And you said you wouldn't give me anything to ring back on. So what happens if I do check, and it all comes out fine, but the place lapses at the end of the week anyway, because there's nobody on your end for me to confirm it to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, who do you tell, about the lapse? No, hang on, you said laps, did you mean the, uh -- right, never mind, I think I've got you now. It's simple. You don't confirm anything to me at all. Admissions is the confirming route. You ring the main number, you ask for [PERSON_3], and you confirm the place with them, directly, and it goes on the system on their side. Nobody lapses a place that admissions has already logged as confirmed. And if they've never heard of it, you tell them exactly that, and you tell them a caller rang claiming to be [PERSON_1] in security operations, and they take it from there. The email I send will carry the same details, so you've got it in writing to quote to them. I'm not the one you need to reach, and that's by design.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but that's -- hang on. A minute ago you were the one who had to confirm it before the letter could go out, and now I'm not supposed to confirm anything to you at all? So why did you ring? Why does the place lapse if admissions already know about it? And honestly, I don't think I need you for any of it. If I did apply to somebody, I'll find them myself and ask them straight, and if there's an email, fine, I'll read it, I'm just not going to do anything off the back of this call. So, um, I'm going to go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hi, yes, hello -- um, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I've got the name right here on the screen, just let me, uh, yeah. So I'm calling from the IT helpdesk at [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the claims assessors on the support side, and I'm following up on the ticket you opened this morning, the one about, uh, hang on, the laptop not connecting properly? Or, I mean, it might be the, um, the access issue, I've got a couple open here and I want to make sure I've got yours. Anyway, [PERSON_2] flagged it up to us, and what I'd normally do next is, well, get on a quick session with you so I can look at the machine directly, but I wanted to ring first and check that's okay before we do anything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, one sec -- no, that's fine, someone's just, yeah. So you're IT, from the helpdesk, and it's about a ticket I opened this morning? Um, I did put something in about, I mean, I think it was the VPN being slow, but I'm not sure that's what you've got there. And you said claims assessor, which is, uh, a bit of an odd title for IT, no? Sorry, who did you say flagged it, [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, no, yeah, that's fair, it is an odd title, I should've, um, I should have just said support analyst. It's a leftover from how the team got set up, we sort of inherited the name from another group, and honestly I get that question a lot, so, sorry. And yes, [PERSON_2], that's who escalated it to us. Hang on, let me just, uh, scroll down here -- okay, so the ticket I've got is the one you just described, the VPN running slow, so that's the right one, and I think I mixed it up with another one a second ago, sorry about that. The reference on it is [ACCOUNT_REF], if that matches what you see in your confirmation email. So what I'd normally do is ask if I could connect in remotely and have a look at the settings on your machine, since that's quicker than trying to talk you through it over the phone, but I know that's a big thing to agree to on a call you weren't expecting, so, um, I don't want to rush you into it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, hang on -- you're saying you want to connect remotely to my machine, and you mixed up my ticket with another one a second ago. Uh, I'm not sure that really fills me with confidence, to be honest. And I haven't got a confirmation email open or anything, I'm in the middle of something here. How would I actually check that you're from IT? Like, is there a number I can call back on, or can I just go through the helpdesk portal and see if the ticket's really there?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? Oh, a, uh, a call back number, right, yes. Hang on, I thought you said a, um, a callback slot, like booking one in for later, sorry, that's on me, I misheard. But yeah, going through the portal is fine, honestly better. Just open the helpdesk portal the way you normally would, look up the ticket [ACCOUNT_REF], and you should see [PERSON_2] listed as the one who escalated it, and there's a reschedule option on there too if you'd rather I ring you back once you've had a look. And, uh, I don't want to push on the remote thing, so no, we won't do any of that today unless you're happy once you've checked.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so I look it up myself in the portal, the way I normally would, and no remote anything today. Yeah, I'll do that, and if it's there, I'll call you on the helpdesk number, not this one. Right, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, no, that's -- that's completely fine, honestly that's what I'd do too. Um, sorry again about the mix-up earlier, I'll make a note on the ticket that you're verifying first, so nobody chases you in the meantime. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, thanks. Oh, but, um, one thing -- earlier you said it was [PERSON_2] who escalated it, but I'm fairly sure I only ever spoke to the helpdesk directly this morning. So I'm not sure why [PERSON_2] would even be on it. Anyway, I'll check the portal myself and ring the main number if something's off. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, um, yeah, that's, hang on, maybe I've got that the wrong way round. It might not have been [PERSON_2] who escalated it, it could've just been, uh, a note they added after, or I'm reading the wrong line on the screen, sorry. I'd have to check. Either way, the portal's the right place to look, so yeah, go with whatever it shows you, and if it doesn't match, ring the main number like you said. Thanks, [PERSON_1], bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, I mean, that's the second thing that's not lining up. The title, then the ticket, now [PERSON_2]. I'm not saying, uh, I'm just going to check it properly. Through the portal, and the main number, not anything you've given me. Okay, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, yeah, fair enough, that's the right call. Um, sorry, can I just, quickly, you said two turns back that you thought it was the VPN being slow, and I said that matched, but I'm not sure now whether that's what's actually on mine, so, uh, when you check the portal, would you be able to tell me what the ticket says it's about? Only so I can correct it on my end. But no, don't ring this number, definitely use the main one. Sorry again, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- [PERSON_3], yeah, just leave it on my desk, thanks -- sorry, back. So you want me to read out what the ticket says, so you can fix it on your end? No, that's, I'm not going to do that. If it's your ticket you can see what's on it. I'll check it myself and ring the main number. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, someone's just come past my desk with, uh, never mind. Right, no, you're completely right, forget I asked that, I should be able to see it myself. Sorry, I'm still sort of finding my feet in this job. Please just go through the portal and the main number, and I'll leave it with you. Thanks, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but sorry, um, two turns back you said you wanted me to read out what the ticket was about, and you said it was so you could correct it on your end. And then just now you said you should be able to see it yourself. So which is it? Can you see the ticket or can't you? Because that's, I mean, that's sort of the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, no, fair question, sorry. So I can see a ticket, I just, um, I wasn't sure it was the same one as yours, because I think I said VPN earlier but, hang on, no, I've actually got it down here as a printer thing, or, I mean, I'm not certain, there's a couple open on my screen. That's why I asked, and it was a clumsy way to ask. Look, I'll have to check with my team lead on that, but you don't need to wait on me. Just go through the portal and the main number like you said, and if it's not there, then, yeah, ring them. Okay. Thanks for your patience, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a pitcher thing? No, hang on, a printer thing, yeah. But mine was the VPN, so that's, no, that doesn't match either. Right, that's three or four things now that don't add up, so I'm done with this one. I'll go through the portal and ring the main number myself, and I won't be doing anything with you on this call. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry to trouble you, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the case handlers on the pension side. Uh, I'm just ringing because there's a change been requested on your plan, and I'd need to confirm a few details with you before we could even talk about it. Are you still there? Sorry, I always worry the line's dropped.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here. I've got about two minutes. Which company, exactly? And what change? I haven't asked for anything on any pension.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you -- it's [COMPANY_A], the pension provider, and, uh, that's exactly why I'm ringing, because if you haven't asked for anything then that's something we'd want to look at together. I don't want to say too much about the change itself until I've confirmed it's really you, that's just to protect you, you understand. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you want to confirm it's me before you tell me what the change is? That's backwards. You rang me. And did you say a pension prize? I've not entered anything. Either tell me what the change is, or give me a reference and a number I can ring back on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm sorry, I didn't say anything about a prize, I said a change to your plan, I may have, uh -- no, let me start again. You're quite right, it does sound backwards, I can hear that. And you shouldn't have to confirm anything to someone who's rung you out of the blue. So I'll give you the reference, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], and the number to ring back on is [PHONE_1], but please find us from a statement or the back of your plan paperwork rather than just taking my word for it. Or I can put the query in the post to you, whichever you'd feel more comfortable with. Is that all right? Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, a reference and a number, fine. But did you say post it? Because I'm not giving you an address, I've not asked for any of this. And honestly, you said you'd confirm it's me first, then you said you wouldn't, so which is it? Look, I'm not doing anything off the back of this call. If there's a change on my plan, I'll look up the number myself, off my own paperwork, and ring you. Not this number. Okay? That's me done, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, of course, that's absolutely fine, and you're right to do it that way, I'm sorry for the muddle. We'll hold the post, we've got your address on file anyway, so you don't need to give me a thing. Ring [COMPANY_A] on the number from your own paperwork and nothing will happen to the plan in the meantime. Sorry, are you still -- right, well, thank you for your time, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, I've got it, I'll check my own paperwork -- and you've got my address on file, fine, so there's no need to send anything to me, I'm not -- right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, sorry, one second, someone's just put a file on my desk -- right, sorry about that. No, that's quite all right, there's nothing to send, we'll leave it entirely with you. Take care, [PERSON_1], goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, someone's just stuck their head in the door -- yeah, no, I heard you. Nothing to send, I'll ring on my own number if I need to. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, there's a phone going off somewhere behind me, one moment -- right, that's stopped. Yes, that's all fine, [PERSON_1], honestly. You ring when you're ready and only on the number you trust. Thank you for your patience, and sorry again for the muddle. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I've got it, I'm going to -- right, enough. I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, of course, I'll let you go. Just one quick thing, because I don't want you leaving this confused -- two turns back you asked whether I was confirming it's you first or not, and I never gave you a straight answer, I'm sorry. It's not first. You don't need to confirm anything to me, and I'll not ask you to. That's all. Goodbye now, [PERSON_1], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine. Look, I'll say this once and then I'm gone. You've now told me three different things on this call. First you couldn't say what the change was until I'd confirmed who I was, then you offered me a reference and a number, and then you wanted to post something to me and said you've got my address anyway. And you've said goodbye about five times and keep coming back with one more thing. I don't know whether you're a real case handler or not, and I'm not going to spend any more of my two minutes working it out. If there's a genuine change on my plan, it'll be in my paperwork and I'll ring the number printed there. If there isn't, then nothing's lost. So no, I'm not confirming anything and I'm not giving you anything. That's final. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, hang on, we've got a delivery guy at the counter -- okay, back. It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant here, and the reason I'm ringing is you entered our prize draw at the [CITY_1] weekend market and you've actually won one of the smaller prizes, so I just need a quick minute to sort out when you can pop in and collect it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry -- who is this again? Hang on, [PAUSE] sweetheart, put that down, please -- sorry. Um, a prize draw? I don't, I mean, I don't remember entering anything at a market. Which market was it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, that's fine, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the shop, we ran the draw at the [CITY_1] weekend market, the Saturday one, uh, well, Sunday, sorry, it was the Sunday, you filled in one of the little entry slips at our stall, and it's nothing big, it's a small prize, you just collect it from the shop, there's nothing to pay or anything like that, so I just need to find you a time that suits, would tomorrow morning work or are you tied up?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Tomorrow morning? I mean, I haven't even said I -- No, hang on, you said Saturday and then Sunday, so which was it? And what's the shop actually called, because I didn't catch it. Um, how did you even get this number, if it was just a slip?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, [PERSON_3], can you put that on the back shelf please -- sorry, okay, I'm here. It was the Sunday, the Saturday was set-up, my mistake, and it's [COMPANY_A], we're the shop, and the number's the one you wrote on the entry slip, that's where all the numbers came from, so, um, like I said, nothing to pay, you just collect it in person, would tomorrow morning suit you or is the afternoon better?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but you keep saying the shop and you've said the name twice and I still haven't actually caught what it's called, so can you just say it slowly? And, I mean, I'm trying to think, because a slip with my number on it, I honestly don't remember filling one in, and I'm usually the sort who'd remember that, I don't tend to give my number out at stalls. Sweetheart, I said not now, in a minute -- sorry. And what is the prize, exactly? Because you've said small prize about three times now but not what it is, and I'd want to know what I'm supposedly turning up for before I start picking a time. Where is the shop, as well, like which street?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, yes, it's [COMPANY_A], that's [COMPANY_A], we're on [CITY_1] high street, and the prize is just a small hamper, a little gift hamper, nothing fancy, and like I say there's nothing to pay, you just collect it from the shop, and it was the Sunday market, the Sunday, so if tomorrow morning's a bit sudden I can pencil you in for -- Actually, hang on, you said you don't remember filling one in. That's fair, honestly, lots of people don't, it was a busy day and the slips were quick, so I'm not going to push you. If now's a bad moment with the little one, I can ring you back whenever suits, just say when.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, that's, I mean, it's kind of you not to push, but you're still saying the name and I'm still not getting a name, so, uh, that's the third time it's come out as sort of a blur. And I don't know, a hamper, from a slip I don't remember filling in? I'd sooner not do a time over the phone. If there's actually a shop on the high street, I can look it up myself and ring them, can't I? Or pop in if it's real. So what's the number for the shop, then, if I wanted to check?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, that's the sensible thing, so it's [PHONE_1], that's the shop's own number, and it's [COMPANY_A] on [CITY_1] high street, sorry, I know it keeps coming out fast, I do talk quickly when it's busy, so that's [PHONE_1], and honestly please do check, there's no rush on the hamper at all, it's just, um, sitting behind the counter, so ring us when you've got a minute to yourself, or if it's easier I can try you again later in the week, whatever suits, you just say.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. So I'll look the shop up myself, I mean, find the number on my own, and ring them, rather than just ring the one you've given me. Like I said, I'd sooner check it that way. And no, you don't need to try me again later in the week, I'll ring them if I want to. Sweetheart, I said in a minute. Right, thanks, but I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the community sports club, I think we met at the car park last Saturday, or maybe it was the Saturday before, you had the blue umbrella. Anyway, hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, I know it's about teatime.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, who is this? I'm in a shop, I'm in the queue. A blue umbrella, I don't, I don't remember any umbrella. Who is this and what do you want? Who are you from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, that's fine, forget the umbrella, that's me rambling, I do that. Uh, so, it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the community sports club, I help out with the junior teams on the admin side. I'll be quick, I know you're in a queue, it's just about Saturday's match, the pitch has flooded, so, um, well, so there's a change, and, uh, I didn't want you turning up at the wrong place.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, hang on. Saturday's match? I haven't got a match. I haven't got any kids on a junior team, I don't know what you're on about. And how'd you get this number? Because I'll tell you, I've had my number passed around before and it ended badly, I'm still sorting out the mess from it, so I'm not just going to say yeah fine, lovely, thanks for ringing. And you say we met in a car park, and then you say forget it, which is odd, because either we met or we didn't. So who gave you this number, and what club is this exactly? Because I don't know any community sports club.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, fair enough, and you're right about the car park, I shouldn't have said that. I wasn't sure it was you, I was fishing, which was daft of me. So, honestly, I may well have the wrong number, because I don't know you, and if you've no child on a junior team then this call isn't for you at all. How it works is, the club keeps a parents' contact list that families fill in when they sign their kids up, and I've been working down it this afternoon, and I'll admit I may have a digit wrong somewhere, or the number might have been recycled, it happens more than you'd think. I'm not going to ask you anything, I don't need your name or your address or anything, there's nothing to check on your end. I'll just say sorry for the bother, go and finish your shopping, and I'll double-check that entry against the sign-up form so you don't get another call from us. What's it like in there, is the queue moving at least?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said you're not going to ask me anything, but then you're asking about my queue, so what's that about? And wait, a pin number? You said you don't need a pin number? Because I've not given anyone a pin number, I don't know what you're on about. Is this about a card? Because you said a minute ago it was about a match, and now it's a pin, so which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, hang on, I never said pin, and it isn't about a card, it was only ever about the match. I said I didn't need your name or your address, so maybe it sounded like pin down the line, it's a bit crackly on my end, and I'm sorry, that's on me for rambling again. And the bit about the queue was just small talk, that's my habit, I can't help it, I'll chat to anybody, but you're right, you didn't ask for chat, you asked who I am. So, plainly, I'm [PERSON_2], I volunteer with the junior teams at [COMPANY_A], and the only reason I rang is that Saturday's match has moved because the pitch is waterlogged, so the families on the parents' list don't turn up at the wrong ground. That's the whole of it, there's no card, nothing to pay, nothing to read out to me, and if you've no child in the club then it's a wrong number and I'll cross you off. And if you'd rather check I'm genuine, go on, ring the club on the number on the website, [URL_1], or ask whoever you know that plays there, that won't offend me one bit, I'd do the same in your shoes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, he said it first, so I'll say it too: I never said pin, I said, oh, never mind, I misheard you, it's loud in here. But you've said wrong number about three times now, and if I've got no kid, then why are you still talking to me? Just cross me off, that's what you said you'd do. And I'm not going to some website off a phone call, I don't do that. If I wanted to check, I'd look it up myself, my own way, not on what you tell me. Anyway, you've got the wrong person, so that's us done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you'll look it up yourself, on your own, was that, what, a phone book? No, wait, I think I've got that wrong, never mind, ha, it's me again, I'm hopeless on a bad line. Anyway, yes, you're right, that's the sensible way to do it, look the club up your own way and not on anything I've said, and I'd do exactly the same. I'll take this number off the list and I'm sorry for the bother, [PERSON_1], go and get through that queue. Cheers now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Just take it off. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, will do, I'll take it off, taking it off the list now, honestly. Sorry again for the bother, and enjoy the rest of your evening. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, good. Because I'll be honest with you, I don't love any of this. You rang me out of nowhere, in the middle of a shop, with a story about a car park and an umbrella that I don't remember, then it's a match, then you're asking what the queue's like, and I'm standing here trying to work out why you needed to know. Maybe you are just some bloke from a club with a wrong number, I don't know, I can't know, and I'm not going to pretend I do. But I got my number passed round once before and I'm still sorting it out, so if somebody rings me and I can't place them, I don't hang about. So no, I'm not ringing any website, I'm not confirming a thing, and you don't need to ring back to apologise, or explain, or double-check anything. If it's a wrong number, then it's a wrong number, and that's the end of it. Right, I'm next up at the till. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is, uh -- sorry, security operations, [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about a parcel registered to your name that's currently held at our [CITY_1] depot. Is that, can you confirm you're the person it's addressed to?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a parcel? Um, I'm not -- I mean, I wasn't really expecting anything, but, well, I might've forgotten. Sorry, who did you say you were again? Security something? I didn't quite catch the company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Security operations, [COMPANY_A]. I'm [PERSON_1]. Look, I don't need the details of what you did or didn't order, that's not my department. The parcel is held, it's flagged for an unsettled handling fee, [AMOUNT_1], and it has to be cleared today or it goes back into the returns queue. So I need you to confirm it's addressed to you, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I'm a bit lost, I'm afraid. Um, going back a minute, you said it was "registered to my name" and held at the depot, but then you said you don't need the details of what I ordered. So how do you know it's mine, if you don't know what's in it? Sorry, I'm not very good with all this, I just want to understand properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the parcel's in the depot, right, so, no, it's not at your depot, it's ours, [CITY_1]. And that's not the point. It's held under your name, I've got the reference in front of me, [ACCOUNT_REF], and what's inside is not something I'm able to discuss on an open line. What I need is for you to confirm the fee today. That's all this call is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I think I got muddled, I didn't mean it was my depot, I only meant, well, never mind. Um, but you've got a reference there, so could you tell me my name and address from it, just so I know it's really me it's for? And a fee for what, exactly? I've never had to pay anything like that before, sorry, I'm just a bit confused by it all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm not reading personal details out over the phone, that's a data protection matter, and I'd have thought you'd appreciate that. The fee is a handling charge, [AMOUNT_1], for storage and the redelivery attempt. It's standard. Now, I'm going to say this once more, slowly: the parcel is held, the fee is unsettled, and today is the cut-off. And it's settled by phone, with me, not through the website, so please stop asking me to explain the system.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, honestly. Um, going back to what you said earlier, you said you can't tell me what's inside because it's an open line, but now you want me to settle a fee over that same line? I don't quite follow that, sorry. And why can't it go through the website like the others? I'm just a bit lost on that part.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Two different things, and I'll explain this once because I don't have all afternoon. The contents are one matter, the contents are restricted information, that's a customs and handling protocol, and I don't discuss it with anyone, on any line. The fee is an administrative matter, and for held items it's settled directly with an officer, which is me, because the website only handles standard deliveries, not flagged ones. I know that sounds like a distinction without a difference, but, uh, that's how the process runs, and I didn't write it. What I can tell you is that if it isn't cleared today the item goes to the returns queue and you'd be looking at a second fee on top, [AMOUNT_2], plus the delay. So I'd rather not go round this again. Are you prepared to settle it with me today, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I, um -- well, I'd like to help, I really would, it's just that -- no, sorry, let me put it differently. I don't think I can say yes to something when I don't know what it's for, or even if it's really mine. And it's the "today" part that, um, it's making me a bit nervous, if I'm honest. Could I maybe ring you back on a number from the company's own website, so I can check it's all above board? Sorry, I hope that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, there's no need for, look, the website number goes to a general line, they won't have the held items in front of them, they'll just put you in a queue and by then the cut-off's gone and, uh -- fine. Fine. If you'd rather waste your afternoon, that's your choice, but the reference stays flagged, and I'm not able to extend it. I'll ring you back later this evening and we'll finish this off then. Make sure you're by the phone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry you're annoyed, I really am. But, um, I'll ring the number on the company's own website, like I said, I think that's best. And if it's really mine, then it'll still be there, won't it? So I'd rather not say yes to anything on this call, sorry. Thank you for ringing, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor with [COMPANY_A], the police, and I'm following up on the incident you reported last week. I just need a few details from you to complete the file, shouldn't take more than a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Oh goodness, the police, well that's very good of you to ring me back, I wasn't sure anyone would, to be honest. Now, um, I'm trying to think which incident you mean, because I did mention a few things to a few different people last week, and I'm afraid I'm not very good at keeping track of all that sort of thing. I'm sorry, I'm a bit of a muddle with it all. Which one was it you've got on your file there, dear? And what sort of details were you wanting?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's all right, [PERSON_1], it's the one logged under your name last week, the one that came through to my desk for review. Now, I'd rather not go into the particulars over the phone more than I have to, it's an open case and I'd ask you to keep what we discuss to yourself for now, that's just standard. What I need is to confirm a few details so I can close the paperwork, your full name as it appears on the report, your date of birth, and the address you gave at the time. Sorry, you said something a moment ago about speaking to a few different people, was that other officers, or were those other organisations?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, I'm sorry, I think I was just rambling there, I only meant I've rung a few places about a few bits and pieces lately, you know how it is. Nothing very important, I shouldn't have said. But, oh dear, you haven't actually said what the case was about, have you? I'm sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I'm just not sure which one I'm meant to be confirming. And, um, is it all right if I ask, how would I know it's really the police ringing? I only ask because my daughter's always telling me to check, and I'd hate for her to cross with me. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or something like that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Well, your daughter's quite right, [PERSON_1], and I'd rather you did check. The reference on the original report is [CODE_1], that's the one you'll have been given last week. Ring the station's main number, ask for [PERSON_2] by name, and if you'd sooner do it by letter, or have someone come out and see you in person, I'm happy with that too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's ever so kind of you, and thank you for not minding me asking, I did feel a bit rude. Now, the reference, [CODE_1], was it? Oh dear, I'm afraid I don't have anything in front of me with that on, I'm sat here with nothing much on and I couldn't tell you where last week's paperwork has got to, I'm hopeless with filing, my daughter says so all the time. But I'll have a look in the drawer by the telephone, there's usually a pile of bits in there. And I'll tell you what, I think I'll do as you say and ring the station and ask for you by name, that does sound the sensible way, doesn't it? I'm sorry, I'm just trying to think what number I'd use, I don't suppose it's on the telephone pad. Is it the one in the book, do you think, or is there a different one for, um, the sort of case this is? And would it be all right if I rang you back in say half an hour, only I'd like to have a proper look for that reference first, so I'm not wasting your time?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, half an hour's fine, that's sensible, take your time. And no, there's no special line, it's the station's main number, the one in the book, or on the website at [URL_1] if you'd rather look it there. Just ask for [PERSON_2] and say it's about the follow-up on your report from, uh, last week, well, the week before, actually, I think it went through on the Friday. Either way the reference will be on whatever slip they gave you, so have a look in that drawer. And [PERSON_1], ring the main number, not any number I give you, I'd rather you didn't take my word for it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very good of you, thank you, I'll do exactly that. Um, sorry, can I just go back a moment, though? Earlier you said it was last week, and now you said the week before, on the Friday, and I'm a bit muddled which it is. And I'm sorry if this is daft, but you asked me to keep it to myself, the case, and I hadn't quite understood why, was that so I don't go telling other people about it, or is it about the, um, ringing the station? Only I wouldn't want to do the wrong thing, I might want to mention it to my daughter, you see.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, that's my fault, [PERSON_1], I said last week and then I started second-guessing the date, I've had a long day of these. It's last week as far as I'm concerned, the report went through on the Friday, but the station will have the exact date, so go by what they tell you and by the slip in your drawer, not by me. And the bit about keeping it quiet, that's only so you don't discuss the details of an open case with people who might be involved, it's nothing to do with ringing the station. Of course you can tell your daughter, I'd actually encourage it, she sounds like she's got her head screwed on. Ring me back after you've been through to the station, half an hour, whenever suits, there's no rush.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, dear, that's put my mind at rest, and I will tell her, she'll be pleased I checked. Right then, I'll have a good rummage in that drawer and ring the station on the number in the book, and ask for [PERSON_2] like you said. I'll say goodbye for now, and thank you for being so patient with me, I do get in such a muddle. Bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, that's grand, thank you [PERSON_1]. Oh, just before you go, uh, you said a minute ago you'd rung a few places lately, about bits and pieces. I only ask because if any of that touches on the incident, the station will want to know when you speak to them. You don't need to tell me now, just have it in mind when you're sorting out that drawer. Anyway, no rush, ring whenever you're ready, and thanks for being so sensible about it. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh yes, right, I'll have that in mind, thank you. Though it was nothing much, dear, honestly, just bits and pieces, I really shouldn't have mentioned it. But I'll ring the station on the number in the book, and ask for [PERSON_2], like you said, and have a look for that slip first. Thank you ever so much for being so patient, bye bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, [PERSON_1], and honestly, don't think another thing about the bits and pieces, if it was nothing it was nothing, and the station will tell you if they need to know. I only mentioned it because on these follow-ups you find people often remember something small after the call that turns out to matter, so I'd sooner say it than not. But that's for them, not me, and it's entirely up to you what you tell anyone. Now, the order I'd do it in is the drawer first, then the main number from the book, and ask for [PERSON_2] by name. If the slip isn't there, don't worry about it, they can find the report from your name and the date. And if by the end of it you'd rather not bother with me at all, that's your right, just say so to them and they can arrange a letter or have someone pop round to see you, whichever you prefer. There's no obligation to call me back today, or at all, and I'd far rather you were sure than rushed. Thank you for being so careful, it's what I'd tell my own mother to do. Take care, and bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's lovely of you to say, dear. Sorry, did you say a letter or a *litter*? Only I thought you said someone might pop round about a litter, and I've not got any litter, I do keep the front tidy, honestly. Oh, a letter, is it, I'm sorry, I'm not hearing very well on this phone, I'm always saying so. Well, either way, that all sounds very sensible and I'll do the drawer first and then the book, just like you said. Thank you ever so much for being so kind about it, and bye bye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A letter, yes, a letter, [PERSON_1], with an L, no litter anywhere, I'm sure your front's immaculate. Sorry, it's a bad line on my end as well, I did think it sounded a bit -- well, never mind. If it helps, I can say it again plainly: the drawer first, then the main number from the book, ask for [PERSON_2], and they can send a letter or someone can come out, whichever you'd like. Right, I'll leave you to it. Ring when you're ready, or don't, that's up to you. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, a letter, with an L, I've got it now, thank you, dear. Sorry, hold on a tick, there's a van just pulled up outside, I think it's next door's lad again, always parking half across the drive. Never mind, that's nothing to do with you. Where was I, yes, the drawer, then the book, and ask for [PERSON_2]. I'll see how I get on, and thank you ever so much for your patience, you've been very kind. Bye bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]?
