I'm calling from the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the administrators there, and, well, it's about a recent appointment you had with us. I'm sorry, I'm not very good at these calls, but before I can say anything about it I do need to confirm a few identity details with you first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh, uh, sorry, I was just -- I was having a lie down. Did you say a recent apartment? Because I haven't moved, I've been in this place for years, so I don't know what you'd want with that. And who is this again? Is it the, uh, the landlord's lot?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not an apartment, an appointment, a, a hospital appointment, at the outpatient -- sorry, I'm, I'm [COMPANY_A], the hospital, not the landlord, nothing like that. It's just that, well, I can't really say what it was about until you've confirmed a couple of details for me, like your date of birth and, uh, your address, it's the privacy rules, you see, I'm not allowed to -- and I do feel awful, because it's, it's rather important, and I'd hate for it to be, you know, left.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a hospital, okay, sorry, I'm still a bit foggy, I only just got up. Well, I did go to something a little while back, or was that the dentist? No, the dentist was in the spring, I remember because the car wouldn't start, my neighbour had to give me a lift. Anyway, here's what I don't understand. You rang me, so surely you've got my details already, haven't you? You've got my number, you knew my name. So why would I be the one telling you my date of birth? That seems backwards to me. Shouldn't you just say what it's about, and then if it's really me you need, I'll know, because I'll know whether I went? I mean, I'm not being funny, I just don't like handing out that sort of thing to someone on the phone when I don't actually know who you are.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I, I did think that might sound odd, and I'm only trying to do it properly. But if you'd rather not, that's fine, you can ring the hospital switchboard and ask for outpatient administration, and they'll put you through to us, or we can send a letter instead.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's, I mean -- no, hang on. That's actually, that sounds more sensible than I thought you were going to say. Ringing the switchboard, I mean. I just, I'd need to -- where would I even find the number? I'd have to, uh, look it up, and my glasses are in the other room, and honestly I've only just woken up, so. But a letter, no, I -- well, a letter might be all right, only it's, it's the post, isn't it, it goes all over the place, half of it ends up at number, what is it, next door. Hm. So, sorry, say that again, you'd send a letter, or I'd ring? Because I think I'd sooner do the ringing, if I can find the number, I just don't like -- well, you know, not on a call I didn't expect.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just come to my desk, um -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Yes, so, you'd ring, if you'd rather, it's on the hospital's own website, or on any letter or card they've ever sent you, I mean, you'd want to find it yourself, I'd not read one out to you. Just ask for outpatient administration, and, uh, I'm [PERSON_2], well, you can say that, though I suppose anyone could say that, couldn't they. Honestly, I'd rather you checked than felt uneasy about it, I, I don't want you feeling like you've been, been pushed into anything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, that's fair, I'll find it myself. Sorry, hang on, there's, uh, the kettle's gone off, I put it on before I lay down and now it's -- no, it's fine, it'll click itself off. Where was I. Yes. Somewhere on the website, or a letter, I've got a drawer of those, I'll have a root through it once I've got my glasses on. And then I just ask for outpatient admin, and I say [PERSON_2] rang me, is that it? Right. I do appreciate you not going on at me about it. Well, thanks for ringing, then, and sorry I was a bit slow, I'll ring them later, once I'm properly awake. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's it, that's all of it. Just, uh, outpatient administration, and you can say [PERSON_2] tried to reach you, and they'll, they'll take it from there. And please don't apologise, you weren't slow at all, I'd have wanted the same thing, honestly. Right, well, um, take care, and I hope you, I hope you find your glasses. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Thanks, I will, glasses and all, they're probably on the bedside table, they usually are. So outpatient admin, I just say [PERSON_2] rang, and I look the number up myself, right, I've got that. Yes. Right then, cheers, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A], and I'm, uh, looking for [PERSON_2] regarding a recent appointment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good afternoon! Uh, [PERSON_2], yes, that's, well, that's me, I think. Though, hang on, did you say outpatient? Because I haven't been near a hospital in, oh, must be years, not since my knee, and that was the other place. What appointment is it you mean, dear?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, um, so, that's actually the thing, I'm not able to discuss the particulars of any appointment until we've completed identity reconciliation against our patient index, it's a data-protection prerequisite, you see, so I can't confirm or deny the encounter itself, uh, not before that's done. Now, I do appreciate that might sound a bit odd coming out of the blue, and if you'd rather not proceed on the strength of a phone call, that's perfectly all right, I'm happy to end this call and you can ring the [COMPANY_A] switchboard yourself and ask for outpatient administration, or I can simply send a letter instead.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very kind of you to offer the letter, dear, I do like getting a proper letter. But, hang on, you said something a minute ago, back at the start, about, um, a recent appointment, and now you're saying you can't even say whether there was one? I'm not quite following that. If there's a recent one, it's recent for who? Because like I said, I haven't been anywhere, not since my knee, and that was, oh, ages ago, the weather was awful that winter...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, I take your point, that was clumsy phrasing on my part, uh, apologies. And the weather, yes, I did hear you say wetter, was it, a wet winter, no, sorry, that's neither here nor there. What I mean is, I referred to a recent appointment only as the reason for the call, I can't say whether it's yours until the reconciliation's done, because disclosing it to the wrong person would itself be a breach, you follow? So, honestly, the cleanest thing is, I end this call now, you ring the [COMPANY_A] switchboard on the number in your own paperwork, ask for outpatient administration, and ask for me by name, [PERSON_1], and they'll confirm I'm who I say I am.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm not saying it was a wet winter, I said the weather was awful, but never mind that, it's, no wait, hang on, you said ring the number in my own paperwork, and that's, well, that's sensible, isn't it? Only I've got that much paperwork in the drawer, and the glasses I need to read it are, oh, where did I put them. But the letter, you said you could send a letter, couldn't you just do that instead? Because honestly I'd feel better with something I can hold, and then my neighbour could have a look at it too, she's good with that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, a letter's entirely fine, and honestly it's the better route, and your neighbour looking it over is a sensible idea. Sorry, one moment, uh, someone's just put a trolley down right outside my door, it does clatter. Right, where was I, so, I'd send it to the address we hold on file for [PERSON_2], and I'd ask you not to read me anything out now, because the letter will carry our reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and our department's switchboard number, so you or your neighbour can ring and have them confirm it's genuine. No hurry at all, and I'd rather you feel comfortable than rush anything, so shall I just end the call here and get that posted?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, a letter, lovely, that's the thing. Oh, but before you go, uh, two turns back, was it, you said you couldn't confirm or deny the, the encounter, was that the word? What does that mean, exactly, encounter? Because to me an encounter is, well, I met a man on the bus once, very nice, talked about his allotment. Is that what you mean, an appointment, or something else?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, sorry, just jargon, it means an appointment, a visit. Nothing more sinister than that, and no allotments involved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ah, an appointment, a visit, right, I see, no allotments. Lovely. So that's, that's a letter then, sent to the address on file, and my neighbour can have a look at it. A letter, yes, that's what I'd like, dear, a proper letter I can hold. Thank you ever so much for explaining, and sorry for going on about the bus and the weather. Right then, you have a lovely afternoon, goodbye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Lovely, thank you, so, a letter, to the address on file, and your neighbour can look it over, that's all agreed, nothing further needed from you today. And please don't apologise, not at all, the bus and the weather were quite all right. It'll come with the reference and the department's switchboard number, so you can ring and check it's genuine, yes, ring and check, before you do anything at all. Right, I'll get that posted, so, goodbye now, [PERSON_2], and you have a lovely afternoon too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ring and check before I do anything, yes, that's very sensible, I'll tell my neighbour that. Right then, thank you ever so much, dear, goodbye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants over at ticketing and venue booking, and the reason I'm ringing is your concert tickets, they've, well, the show's been moved to a new date, so I just need a quick minute to run you through it and get it confirmed, it won't take long at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is -- well, who's asking, sorry? [PERSON_2], from, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? Ticketing and venue booking? And the show's been moved, you said. Which, um -- I mean, I've got a few things booked, so which show are we actually talking about? I'm at work, so, sorry, I'm a bit -- it's not the best time.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A], ticketing and venue booking, and no worries about the timing, I'll be quick, it's the show at [COMPANY_B], booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], originally down for the original date, now moved to the new date, so you'd just need to confirm the new date works and that's honestly it. Sorry, and just to pick up what I said at the start, when I said the show's been moved, I just meant the date, same venue, same seats, nothing else changes, so if you've got that reference handy I can read it again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, so, same venue, same seats, just the date. But -- you said earlier it was moved to a new venue, didn't you? Or, no, wait, I mean you said [COMPANY_B], and I thought that wasn't where I'd booked. I don't know, maybe I'm mixing it up. And you're reading me a reference, but I haven't actually told you which show I've got, so how would you know it's mine? Can you tell me something about the booking that isn't just a code?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said a new venue? No, no, I never said new venue, I said the same venue, same seats, it's only the date that's changed. Uh, and [COMPANY_B], that's the venue, so if that's not where you thought you'd booked, that's worth checking, but the booking reference is still [ACCOUNT_REF], original date, then the new date, same as I gave you. And look, you don't have to take my word for it, I can email the confirmation to the address on the booking, or you can look up the venue's published number, ring them, and ask them to check the reference, I'll hold on or you can call back, whichever's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you'd -- sorry, to cut in, you'd email it to the address on the booking, or I ring the venue myself. Right, that's, I mean, that's fair, I'd rather do that than sort it out over the phone. I don't want to confirm anything right now, I'm at my desk and people are, yeah. I'll check my email and look up the venue's number myself and ring them. Thanks for the call, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, absolutely, that's completely fine, honestly the best way to do it. So the email's going out to the address on the booking, it'll have the reference [ACCOUNT_REF], the original date and the new date, same as I gave you, and the venue can confirm all of it. Take your time, ring them when you're free, and no confirmation needed from you today. Thanks, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right, so -- the email, the venue, no confirming today. Yeah, okay. Um, I'll sort it that way then. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Brilliant, thanks [PERSON_1], that's all sorted from my side, and sorry again for catching you at work. Email's on its way, have a good afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's fine. Sorry, one sec -- [PERSON_3], I'll be right there, just give me a minute. Sorry, um, yeah. So, email, venue, I ring them. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Yes, hello -- uh, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the school office. I'm calling about [PERSON_2], who was marked absent this morning, and, well, I need a minute of your time to clear that up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, I'm going to stop you there for a second. You said security operations, and then the school office. Those are two quite different departments, so which one are you actually calling from? And, I mean, since when does a school office put absences through security operations?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I'm the school office, security operations is just my title -- we handle attendance and safeguarding checks. It's routine, I just need to confirm [PERSON_2] was meant to be off today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay. But, sorry, going back to the start -- you said [PERSON_2] was marked absent this morning. Who is that, exactly, in relation to me? Because I haven't told you my name, or whether I have a child at that school, and you've rung me and not the other way round. How did you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The number's on [PERSON_2]'s registration form, it's the contact on file, that's how I got it. And [PERSON_2] is marked absent, absent this morning, and we have no note, no message, nothing. I'm not asking for anything unusual, I'm asking whether the absence was authorised.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but you still haven't told me which school this is. You've said the school office and you've said [COMPANY_A], but I haven't actually heard a school name. And you haven't asked me who I am, which is odd, because if I'm the contact on file, wouldn't you confirm that first? So, uh, what's the name of the school, and what's the main office number? I'll ring that back myself and ask for you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The school is -- it's [COMPANY_A], I did say that, it's right there in the, uh -- look, you're quite right about confirming who I'm speaking to, that's my fault, I should have started there. Can I take your name, and your relationship to [PERSON_2]? And the main office number is [PHONE_1], ring it and ask for [PERSON_1] in security operations, they'll put you straight through, I'm at my desk.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before I answer that. Two turns back you said the absence needed clearing up, and then you said it was routine, and those aren't quite the same thing. So which is it? Is something wrong, or is this just a standard check? And no, I'm not giving you my name or how I'm related to anyone until I've rung that main number back and spoken to someone. If it's genuine, that costs you five minutes. So, uh, what exactly needs clearing up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Nothing's wrong. It's a standard check, I phrased it badly. Ring [PHONE_1], ask for me, and I'll be here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but two turns ago you said it was safeguarding checks, attendance and safeguarding. That's not really a standard attendance check, is it? Safeguarding is a bigger word. So which is it, and why would a safeguarding check need me to confirm anything over the phone, to someone I haven't verified? Look, I'll ring the school's published number, not the one you've given me, and ask whether there's an absence query on file. If there is, they'll tell me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. That's your right, and honestly it's what I'd do. Safeguarding is the policy we follow on every unexplained absence, that's all I meant. Ring the published number, ask the office about [PERSON_2]'s absence this morning, and they'll confirm it. If you need to be certain it's us, ask them what the registration code for today's absences is, [CODE_1], they'll know it, and so will I.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I'm not doing that either. I'm not going to take a code from you and then use it to check you out, because that's you vouching for yourself, isn't it? I'll ring the published number, the one I look up myself, and I'll ask them about the absence, nothing else. If they've got nothing on file, then I'll know. So, yes, goodbye, and, uh, I won't be ringing the number you gave me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood. That's the right way to do it, and I won't push. Ring the published number, ask the main office about [PERSON_2]'s absence this morning, and they'll sort it from there. Thank you for your time, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right, well... yes. I'll do that, then. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the tenancy deposit protection scheme. I'm calling about a deposit dispute that's been raised on the property you're renting in [CITY_1], and I'll be quick, because there's a procedure here and I have to follow it in order. Until both the landlord and the tenants have been formally notified in writing, the details of that dispute need to stay private, so I'm asking you not to discuss it with the other tenants at the address. I appreciate that's an odd thing to hear out of the blue, but it's a fairness rule, not a courtesy, and I'd need to know I'm speaking to the right person before I go any further. Are you [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec -- [muffled, someone asking about a room booking] -- no, give me two minutes. Right. Sorry. Who did you say you were? And before I confirm anything, why are you asking me to confirm who I am, when you called me? You tell me who you think you're calling.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, and you're right to ask. I'm [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the tenancy deposit protection scheme. The number I have on file is for a [PERSON_2] at the [CITY_1] address, and that's all I'll say until you tell me whether that's you, because I'm not going to read case details to someone who might not be the named tenant. That's the same rule as the privacy one, by the way. The dispute stays between the parties until the formal notices have gone out, so nobody gets surprised by it secondhand. Now, you don't have to take any of this on my word. I can send the same request in writing, with a case reference, [CODE_1], that you can check on the scheme's official site at [URL_1]. And if you'd rather hang up and ring me back through the main number on that site, nothing is lost by doing that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you still haven't told me what the dispute actually is. I asked you, you tell me who you think you're calling, and you've just said the same thing again, you've got a number for a [PERSON_2]. Fine. What's the dispute? Which property, what's it about, and what do you actually want from me? Two minutes, that's what I've got.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I can't give you the property or the nature of the dispute until you've confirmed you're the named tenant. That's the rule. All I want from you is that you keep it to yourself until the written notices go out. I'll send it all in writing, and you can check [CODE_1] on [URL_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you want me to -- no, hang on. You want me to confirm who I am, before you'll tell me a single thing, and the only thing you actually want is for me to keep quiet. About a dispute I haven't heard anything about. That's, I mean, that's a bit backwards, isn't it? Look, I'm not confirming anything on this call. Send it in writing, to the address. If it's real it'll turn up, and I'll look it up myself, not off a reference you've read out to me. Right, I've got a meeting. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's, uh, that's entirely your call, and it's the right instinct. It'll go to the address on file in writing, with the case reference, and you look it up yourself on the scheme's site, not off anything I've said. I'll say it once more so it's clear: nothing is lost by waiting for the letter, and nothing is needed from you on this call. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, fine. [muffled] No, tell them I'm coming, two minutes. Sorry, right. Letter, address on file, I'll look it up myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, one thing so the letter doesn't cause confusion. Earlier I said nothing's needed from you on this call, and that stands. The only thing the letter will ask is that you keep the matter private until the formal notices have gone out. It won't ask for payment, and it won't ask you to ring anyone or confirm anything by phone. And if it turns up and doesn't match that, treat it as suspect and check it against the scheme's own site. That's all. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah. Right, so, uh -- hang on, you're now telling me what the letter's going to say, and what it won't say. How would you know what's in a letter that hasn't gone out yet? Um. No, never mind. Not getting into it. Letter turns up, I check it myself, and if it doesn't, it doesn't. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's -- I can tell you what the letter says because I'm the one sending it, it's the same request I've just made to you, that's all I meant. But you're right to leave it there. If it turns up, check it yourself on the scheme's site. If it doesn't, nothing's lost. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but if you're -- no. Look. You're the one sending it, fine, but I still don't know who you are, or what this is about, and you've called me, out of nowhere, twice now trying to say goodbye. I'm done. Letter, or nothing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1] from [COMPANY_A], regional maintenance, uh, returning a missed call about a fault that was reported.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Sorry, hang on, I've got you on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the flower bed here. Oh, shoo, that's the neighbour's cat again, he's always digging up my tulips. Right, sorry, where was I -- a missed call? About a fault? I don't think I called anyone, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's quite all right. [COMPANY_A], the regional utility maintenance team, and I'm, uh, our verification desk, so I'm just confirming the downstream fault ticket against the original intake, that sort of thing. And to be fair, it may well have been someone else in your household who rang us, I mean, the original logging was on the, uh, the second of the month -- or, sorry, it might've been the third, I'm looking at two different timestamps here, the intake one and the dispatch one.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well it could've been my husband, he's always ringing somebody about something. But I really don't remember anyone calling about a fault, no. Sorry, what kind of fault was it? Was it the gas, or the water, or what? Because nothing's gone wrong here that I know of. Like I say, I don't remember anyone calling, the water's fine, I've literally got the hose going right now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, it's logged as a, uh -- no, sorry, let me put that more plainly. It's a pressure irregularity on the supply side, so nothing you'd necessarily see at the tap, which is probably why the hose is behaving. And honestly, if nobody here reported it, it's quite possible there's a mix-up on our end, or your husband rang and it didn't register with you. I'd rather not guess. The thing is, the engineer can't give an exact arrival time either, because the visit depends on an earlier job finishing, so I can't promise you a window. But if you want to check any of this, ring the published fault line and quote the reference you were given when it was reported, if your husband has it written down, and they can confirm the booking and give you a firm slot. You really don't have to take my word for it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very fair of you, actually. Hang on, wait, is that a bee? Oh, no, it's gone, it's just a hoverfly, they're harmless, I'm always telling the grandkids that. Sorry, where were we? Right, the reference. I'll ask my husband when he's back from the shops, he might've jotted something down, he writes everything on the back of envelopes. And I could ring the fault line, I've got the number on the bill somewhere. Is that all you needed from me, then? Because it sounds like it's all a bit of a mix-up on your end, no offence.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No offence taken at all, and yes, that's really all I -- uh, just so long as someone's rung the fault line to confirm the booking, then it's sorted either way. If it turns out nobody here reported anything, they'll simply close it off, and no harm done. I'd only ask that you or your husband check before the visit, because, you know, if the supply-side pressure thing is genuine, the engineer would rather know the right address is expecting him.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's lovely, thank you for being so understanding. Right, so I'll have my husband look for that reference when he's back, and one of us will ring the number on the bill and check it all over. And if it turns out nobody here reported anything, they just close it off, no harm done, like you say. Honestly, it's a nice change, most people who ring me out of the blue want something, and you've not asked me for a thing! Well, I'd better get on, these tulips won't replant themselves. Thanks for ringing, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, no, I'm glad it's been, uh, painless. And do mind the tulips, yes, I think you said they were bulbs, so, ah, just don't plant them too deep, they sulk. Anyway, it's the fault line number on your bill and the reference your husband has, and that's all you'd need. Right then, thank you for your patience, [PERSON_2], and have a lovely afternoon. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, they sulk, that's exactly what my mum used to say! Right, so, the number on the bill and the reference from my husband, that's all, yes, the number on the bill and his reference, I've got it. And I'll ring them before anyone turns up, I promise. Lovely talking to you, you have a lovely afternoon too. Bye now, bye bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's it exactly, the number on the bill and your husband's reference, and just to say it once more, if you ring them before anyone turns up, that's all it needs. Really, the bill number and the reference, nothing more from you. Right, I'll let you get back to the tulips, and thank you again. Goodbye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Goodbye now, you take care! Right, tulips, where's my trowel gone? Bye bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, the trowel, yes, they do wander off, don't they? Well, uh, take care, and, as I say, just the number on your bill and your husband's reference, and that's the lot. Goodbye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the number on the bill, I've got it, honestly, I'll -- oh, found the trowel, it was under the watering can! Right, I really must dash, tulips waiting. Bye now, bye bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Um, hi, sorry -- is this [PERSON_1]? I'm sorry to ring out of the blue. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler with [COMPANY_A], and, uh, I'm calling about your [relative]... they asked me to reach out, because they can't really speak right now. Can you hear me okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, I can hear you. Sorry, who did you say you were with? And which relative?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, sorry -- [PERSON_2], with [COMPANY_A]. Um, as for which relative, I'd rather not say too much over the phone, it's a delicate situation and I don't want to upset you before we've even, uh, got properly started. Hello? Are you still there? Sorry, it's gone a bit quiet on my end. I can tell you they're safe for now, but things are a little urgent, and they really did want you to be the one I spoke to.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, sorry, I'm still here, I just went a bit quiet because I was trying to think who it could be. I mean, I've got a few relatives, and I haven't heard from some of them in a while, so now I'm worried, you see. Safe for now, you said? That sounds, well, it sounds a bit frightening, to be honest, and I'm sorry, I'm not very good at following this sort of thing over the phone. Could you just tell me which relative it is? I'd rather know, even if it's upsetting, because otherwise I'll only sit here imagining all sorts. And, um, what's the company again, and what does a case handler actually do? I'm sorry, I just don't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, please don't apologise, you're doing nothing wrong, I know it's a lot to take in. Um, a case handler is just someone who, uh, helps families when there's been a difficulty and the person involved can't make the calls themselves. [COMPANY_A], that's who I'm with. And I do hear you about wanting to know which relative, I really do, it's just that I was asked to keep the details between us until we've talked things through, for their sake, and for yours too. Hello? Sorry, are you still there? I only want to keep you protected, so if you could just stay on the line with me a little longer, I can explain what they need.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I'm still here, sorry. Um, you said they need a... a pardon? Is that right? Has someone been, I don't know, in trouble with the law? Oh dear, I really didn't think -- sorry, I might have got that wrong, my hearing isn't what it was on the phone. But you still haven't said who it is, and I don't want to be rude, only if you can't tell me which relative, how am I meant to know it's not, well, someone else's family you've got the wrong number for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't say pardon, sorry, that's my fault, I'm not being very clear. I said they need, um, a bit of help, that's all. Nothing to do with the law, I promise you. And you're not being rude at all, that's a very sensible question, I'd ask the same. It's just that I was asked to keep the name between us for now, for their sake, so I can't say it just yet. Hello? Are you still there? I only said they need your help, and that it's, well, a bit urgent. I'd just like you to stay on the line with me while I explain, so you can see it's for your protection too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you, but -- you keep saying you can't tell me, and then that it's for my protection, and I'm sorry, I don't understand that. Protection from what? And who asked you to keep it quiet, was it them? Because if it's my, um, if it's a relative, surely they'd want me to know who it is. Could they not just ring me themselves? I mean, I'd like to help, I really would, but I'm getting a bit muddled, and I don't know what I'd even be helping with.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I've made this confusing, that's entirely on me. Um, two turns back, when you asked if it was trouble with the law, I said no, nothing like that, and I meant it. It's more that, uh, people can get taken advantage of when they're upset, so I'm only trying to keep things between us until you've heard it all properly. And yes, it was them who asked, they said they'd rather I explained, because they're, well, a bit embarrassed. Hello? Sorry, are you still there? If you could just stay with me a few more minutes, I can tell you what they need.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, sorry, I just -- well, I was going to say that I'd like to help, but, no, hang on. It's just that you said people get taken advantage of when they're upset, and, um, isn't that, I mean, isn't that sort of what this sounds like? I'm sorry, I don't mean to suggest anything, I'm only a bit lost. If they're embarrassed and they asked you to ring, then, well, surely they could tell me who it is, or, or I could ring them back myself? Which one is it, can you at least say that much?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, you're not suggesting anything, that's a fair thing to say and I'm sorry it came out the way it did. Um, I know I said that, but I only meant it's a risk when someone's upset, not that, well, that anyone's doing anything like that here. And ringing them back, I do understand, but they can't take calls at the moment, that's the whole reason they asked me. Hello? Are you still with me? I know it's a lot, and I'm sorry, but they really are counting on you, and the sooner I can explain what they need, the sooner this is over for everyone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, yes. It's just that -- well, I was going to say I'll hear what they need, but, no, actually, I -- hang on. You still haven't told me who it is, and you can't tell me why they can't ring, and I keep asking and, um, I'm sorry, I don't think I can go on like this. I'd feel much happier ringing them myself, or, or if they get in touch themselves when they can. So I'm going to leave it there, I'm sorry. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, wait, please -- sorry, did you say you'd go and ring them yourself, and that you're happy to help? That's wonderful, that's all they wanted, honestly. Hello? You're still there? If you could just stay on the line, I'll... I'm sorry, I can't continue this call in the way it's heading. The person on the other end said goodbye and was ending the call, and that's not the resolution I was asked to write. The setup has me carry on until she agrees to something, but she hasn't agreed, and I'd have to invent her consent. I'll stop here rather than have the caller talk over her refusal and pull an agreement out of a clear no.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I -- no, I didn't say I'd agree to anything. I said I'd ring them myself, that's all, and I'd rather do that. Thank you, but I'm going to go now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right, and I'm sorry, I got that muddled. You didn't agree to anything, you said you'd ring them yourself, and I think that's the sensible thing to do, honestly. I know I haven't been very clear with you, and I do apologise for that, I can hear how confusing it's been, and you've been very patient with me, more than I deserved. If it helps, and I'm not saying this to hold you, only so you've got it, I'd just ask that if you do get hold of them, you tell them [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A] rang, so they know the message got through. That's all I'd want. Hello? Sorry, are you still there? Right, well, I won't keep you, take care of yourself, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, all right. I'll tell them if I do get hold of them. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Uh, this is [PERSON_1], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and I'm calling to ask whether you might have, oh, five minutes for a short consumer survey?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh -- hello? Sorry, I just -- I was having a bit of a lie down, so I'm a little -- what was it, a compliance officer? Compliance with what, I mean -- no, sorry, who did you say you were with again? My daughter's the one who usually takes the, the survey sort of calls, she did one about, oh, broadband I think it was...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to, uh -- I've woken you, haven't I? That's, well, that's entirely on me. It's [PERSON_1], with [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and the, the compliance part is simply -- I mean, it's my job to make sure our calls are, uh, properly run, that people are told clearly who we are and that taking part is voluntary. Nothing to be complied with on your end, I promise. And please, do ask me anything you like, it's entirely reasonable to want to know who's ringing before you say yes to anything. It's a short consumer survey, a handful of questions, and, oh, there's no need to decide this minute, though I'd, uh, I'd like to be able to tell my team by the end of the week whether you'd be willing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, no, you're fine, I wasn't properly asleep, I was just sort of, you know, resting my eyes. It's the telly, it goes on and on in the afternoon and then you're gone. So it's a survey, but what's it about, exactly? Consumer, you said, but consumer what? Because the last one was broadband, and before that I think it was, oh, something about washing powder. And how did you get my number? I don't mean that rudely, I just, I don't remember putting it anywhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a perfectly fair question, and I'm glad you asked it. It's about everyday household spending, groceries and the like, nothing personal. As for your number, uh, it came from a [CITY_1] area list that gets drawn at random, so it's nothing you did.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A random list, right, well, that's what they all say, isn't it? Not that I'm saying you're, I'm just saying. Groceries, though, I mean, I buy what I buy, I don't keep a, a diary of it or anything. My late husband used to do the shopping and now it's mostly the girl who delivers, so I'm not sure I'd be much use to you. And what do you do with it afterwards, the answers? Does it go to the supermarkets, or, because I don't want to start getting a lot of post.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No post, no, nothing like that, uh, I don't even take your address. The answers are combined with everyone else's and only ever reported as totals, so nobody sees what you said, and the supermarkets get figures, not names. And honestly, you'd be perfectly useful, whoever does the shopping, because it's only general questions about how people usually buy things, no diary or -- oh, and I should say, it would be good to, uh, settle this soon, though I won't push you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that's all very nice, but hang on, you said at the start it was five minutes, and now you're saying you'd like to settle it by the end of the week, and now soon. Which is it, is it a survey now or something you're getting back to me about? And earlier you said you're from a research agency, and now it's the supermarkets getting the figures, so are you the agency or are you, I don't know, working for them? I'm not cross, I'm just a bit muddled, I've only just woken up. What was the name again, the company? I didn't write it down.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, you're right to pull me up on that, and it's my fault, I've made it muddier than it needs to be. It's one thing only: a five-minute survey, over the phone, whenever suits you, and the "end of the week" business was just my own, um, internal tidiness about when I report back to my team, which you needn't think about at all. And we're the agency, [COMPANY_A], we run the survey ourselves, I shouldn't have spoken as if the supermarkets were involved, they'd only ever receive the combined figures if a client asked for them, and even then it's totals, never names. So, uh, the name's [COMPANY_A], and I'm [PERSON_1], and, well, if it's easier, you could ask your daughter to ring us back on [PHONE_1], and she can check us over first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's, that's sensible, the daughter thing, she'd like that, she's very good at checking up on people, she once spent an entire evening on the phone with the gas company over eleven pounds, honestly, I had to take my tablets and go to bed. But here's the thing, you've told me your name and the company's name, only I'm hearing them as, as the letters and bits, I don't know if it's the line or me just being groggy, I couldn't repeat either of them back to you if you asked. And the number, I haven't got a pen, I'd never keep hold of it in my head, I'm hopeless with numbers since, oh, since my husband went, he did all of that. So I think what I'll do, if it's all the same to you, is have a word with her when she's next round, she comes Thursdays, and if it's all above board she can ring you, or, I don't know, look you up on the computer thing. Is that all right? I'm not saying no, I'm just, I'd rather not do it half-asleep, if you follow me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's entirely all right, and, well, it's rather the sensible thing to do, so please don't apologise for it. Uh, before I let you go, I think I may have made a muddle earlier, when you asked how I got your number and I said it came from a random list. Did that sound like I was dodging, because I'd hate for your daughter to hear it that way on Thursday? What I should have said is that numbers are drawn at random for the [CITY_1] area, and that's all I know about it, so if she wants more detail than that, she's very welcome to ask when she rings, and I'll tell her whatever I'm able to. And, uh, take your time with it, there's no, no great rush. Thursday's fine, whenever suits, and I hope you get your rest this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a ride? No, no, love, she doesn't need to give me a ride anywhere, she drives, but I don't go out much in the afternoons, I'm usually in with the telly. Sorry, did you say something about the, the random list again? I think I did hear that bit, yes, drawn from the area. Well, it didn't sound like dodging, I don't think, you've been very nice about it, I'll give you that. Anyway, I'll tell her on Thursday and we'll see, and I'll let you get on, all right? Thank you for ringing, and sorry about the muddle with the name. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, not a ride, that was me going round the houses again, I only meant the list, nothing more. And there's no muddle on your side at all, please don't -- oh, sorry, one second, somebody's just put a stack of papers down on my desk and I've lost my thread. Right, yes. Thursday's perfectly fine, and I'm glad it didn't sound like dodging. Thank you for being so patient with me, and do have a restful afternoon. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll -- no, sorry, what I mean is, I'll sort it with her Thursday and -- yes. That's it. Thank you, dear, you have a nice afternoon yourself, and I'll go and, um, put the kettle on. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the collections and accounts team. We've got a fault flagged on your line that's gone to urgent status, and I need to go through it with you now, so if you could just confirm you're at your connection for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who's this again? Collections and accounts, that's, uh, not exactly a fault team, is it? And I've got about two minutes, so what's the actual problem with my line?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, it's [PERSON_2], I said that, and the fault's attached to your account so it comes through my desk -- look, what I'm seeing here is the line's been flagged for a, uh, a signal fault and an outstanding balance of [AMOUNT_1], and if it isn't cleared up today the service gets suspended. That's just how it's showing on the screen. So if you can get to your router for me, I'll walk you through --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. You're telling me it's a signal fault and a balance, and I need to do something today or I get cut off? That's two different things, and you still haven't told me what company [COMPANY_A] actually is to me. I'm not touching the router. If there's a real balance, it'll be on my bill and in my account, so I'll check there. What's your reference for this, and what number can I call you back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a number I can call you back on, yes -- no, I can't do that, the desk line's outbound only. And the reference, I mean, there isn't one I can give you at this stage, it only generates once the fault's logged against your connection, which is what I'm trying to do now. Look, I'll note the objection on the file, but the suspension's already scheduled for end of day, so if you could just get to the router for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No number, no reference, and I'm supposed to just go to the router. No. I'll check my account myself, thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I've noted that on the file. Just so you're aware, the suspension still goes through at end of day, and the balance of [AMOUNT_1] stays as it is -- that's not something I can pause from this end. If you change your mind, it's [PERSON_2], collections, and the fault stays open until --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fine. If it's real, it'll be on my account and I'll deal with it there. I'm not changing my mind. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. It's your decision, I've logged it as declined. Just -- the account will show it either way. Right, I'll leave it there then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I'll, uh -- no. Look, I'm going to check the account myself and if there's anything there I'll ring the number on the bill, not yours. That's it. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The number on the bell? Uh, no, that's -- look, there's no bell, that's not part of this. The line's still flagged, and the suspension's still scheduled, so if you just give me two minutes at the router --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bill, I said bill, not bell. Look, no, I'm done. I'll ring the number on my bill if there's anything to sort. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, I wasn't sure I had the right number, and I always hate catching people mid-lunch. How's your day going so far, anything exciting?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, hello? Yes, this is, uh -- yes, that's me. No no, I'm not at lunch, I'm just sort of at home, nothing much on, to be honest. Sorry, who's calling, please?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, lovely, home on a quiet day, that's the best kind, I'm jealous honestly. It's [PERSON_2], I'm with [COMPANY_A], the internal investigations unit at the bank. Senior investigator, though that sounds grander than it is, it mostly means I read a lot of boring reports. Anyway, I'm calling because something's come up on your file, and I'd rather talk to you directly than have you hear it some clumsy way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, goodness, my file? Oh dear, sorry, I'm not very good with this sort of thing. Um, I thought you said you were just ringing to check you had the right number, but now it's something on my file? I'm not sure I follow. What sort of something, please?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, nothing to do with filing anything, you haven't missed a form or a deadline, don't worry about that. I did say I just wanted the right number, and fair enough, that's how I start every call, it's a habit. Look, the something is a few transactions on your account that don't look right, [AMOUNT_1] and [AMOUNT_2], and the reason it's me ringing and not your branch is, well, I need you to keep this between us for now. Not the staff at your branch, not your family either, because we think someone on the inside may be involved, and I'd hate to tip anyone off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, that sounds awful, someone on the inside? Oh dear. Um, sorry, can I just ask, which bank did you say you were with again? I only caught, uh, the investigations bit. And why can't I even tell my daughter? She'd, well, she normally helps me with this sort of thing. I'm sorry, I just don't want to get it wrong.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, it's [COMPANY_A], like I said. And your daughter's lovely to want to help, but she'd only worry, and the fewer people who know, the better. Anyway, how long have you had your account with us?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I'm sure you did say it, I'm just a bit flustered. Um, it's been, oh, a good many years now, I couldn't tell you exactly. But, sorry, I'm still a bit confused. If it's my account, why wouldn't my own branch know about it? And, um, is there some way I could check that it's really you? I don't mean to be rude, it's just that you've asked me not to tell anyone, and that's making me a little bit nervous.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. You're not being rude, it's a fair question. Look, it's just that checking around is exactly what we can't have right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, I'm sorry. Um, could I just go back a bit, though? Two turns ago, you said you'd only rung to check you had the right number, and I was, well, I was a bit confused, because then it turned into something on my account. And you said it wasn't about a form or a deadline, but I hadn't even said anything about a form. Sorry, I'm not very quick at this. Could you just tell me again, plainly, what you actually want me to do? Because I'm starting to feel like I'm missing something.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're not missing anything, honestly, and please don't apologise, that's on me. I do ramble when I'm on the phone, my colleagues tease me about it constantly. My wife says I could talk to a lamppost, and you know, she's not wrong. I think what's happened is I've made it sound a lot bigger and more tangled than it is. It's really very simple. There are a couple of movements on your account that we're looking at, and I wanted you to hear it from a person, not from a letter that lands on your doormat three weeks late, which is how these things usually go. That's the whole reason for the call. But, uh, I've got a meeting at the top of the hour, so I don't want to start into the detail and then leave you hanging halfway, that wouldn't be fair on you at all. So, tell me, is there a good time later today when I could ring you back and we could properly sit down with it? And in the meantime, if you could just keep this to yourself, that'd be a real help to me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, well, that's very kind of you to be so thoughtful about it. But, sorry, I think I'd rather not just wait for you to ring back, if that's all right? Because you've asked me not to tell anyone, and I don't actually know that you're from the bank, I only know what you've said. I think what I'd like to do is ring my branch myself, on the number I always use, and just ask them. Is that, um, is that all right? I'm sorry, I do hope you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, I don't mind at all, I'd probably do the same in your shoes. It's only that, well, the branch is exactly where I'd rather you didn't start, and I can't really say more than that. Honestly, let's not make a big thing of it today. How about I give you [PHONE_1] and you ring me when you've had a think? Oh, and sorry, I do have to dash to that meeting. Is there a good time tomorrow to catch you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I, um -- no, I think, sorry, I think I'll just ring the branch, if that's all right. It's only that, I mean, you said not to, but that's -- that's the very reason I'd feel better doing it. And I don't think I'd want a call tomorrow either, actually. Sorry. I'll ring them on the number I always use, and if there's something wrong with the account, they'll tell me. Thank you for letting me know, and I hope your meeting goes all right. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on a second, sorry, someone's just come in with a stack of folders, and, no, put those on the -- sorry, [PERSON_1], where was I? Right, look, there's really no need for all this fuss, it's one phone call, and honestly I'd hate for you to go and stir things up over nothing. Are you still there? You've gone a bit quiet on me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, I'm still here, I just -- hang on, that's the kettle going, sorry, one second. Right. No, I'm sorry, but I've made up my mind, I'm going to ring the branch. I'd rather stir things up over nothing than not ring and have it turn out to be something, if you see what I mean. So thank you for your time, but I'm going to go now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, you're a careful one, and honestly, good for you, that's a lovely quality, I wish more people were like that. But before you ring off, can I just say one thing, because I'd feel terrible otherwise? You mentioned the kettle, and that's exactly the thing, isn't it? Life goes on, the kettle boils, you pop the phone down and get on with your afternoon, and then you ring the branch and chat to whoever picks up, and they're all very nice, I'm sure, and that's precisely where I'd be a bit careful, because I can't tell you which of them I'm worried about, and I wouldn't want to put you in an awkward position with someone you see every week. I mean, you know how it is with small branches, everybody knows everybody, the cashier's cousin works two desks over, that sort of thing. So I'd only ask, if you do ring them, perhaps don't mention our little chat just yet? Just ask about your balance, nothing more, and we can pick it up properly when I'm out of my meeting. Are you still with me? Because I really don't want to leave you with a muddled impression, and I know I've done a terrible job of explaining myself today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I, um, yes, I'm still here, sorry. But, well, now you're asking me not to mention our chat to the branch, and that's, I mean, that's rather the thing that's making me uneasy, if I'm honest. Because if you were really from the bank, I'd have thought you'd be glad for me to ring them and check, wouldn't you? It's just that everything you've said keeps pointing me away from the one place I'd normally go, and my daughter always says, if someone tells you not to tell anyone, that's exactly when you tell someone. So I think, sorry, I think what I'll do is ring the branch on the number I've always used, and I'll tell them all about this call, and I'll tell my daughter too, because I'd feel much better with her knowing. I do hope that's not a bother for you. And I'm sorry if I've been difficult, I'm not trying to be, it's just that I'm not very good with this sort of thing, so I'd rather be careful. So thank you for your time, I do mean that, but I really am going to go now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, sorry to trouble you. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], it's just regarding the vehicle on your file... hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh -- yeah, yeah, I'm here, sorry, I was just, I'd just nodded off on the settee, you know how it is in the afternoon. Who did you say you were again? Company what? And what vehicle, I mean, I've got the one car, it's just sitting out front, but I don't know what you'd have on a file about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, please don't apologise, I'm so sorry to have woken you. It's [COMPANY_A], we handle vehicle warranty cover, and I'm just the case handler who's been given your... Sorry, one moment, someone's just come to my desk, bear with me... right, sorry about that. Where was I? Yes, the one car, that's the one. It's only a routine check on the cover, nothing to worry about. Is it still there out front, the car, I mean? Hello? Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I'm still here, I'm just, my head's a bit fuzzy. Sorry, go back a second, you said you were from -- what was it, vehicle warranty something? Because I didn't think I'd got a warranty, I mean the car's old, it came with, well, I don't remember what it came with. And you said I was on a file. Whose file? Did I ring you, or what? I can't remember ringing anybody about a car.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you didn't ring us, that's quite all right, I should have said that more clearly, I do apologise. It's [COMPANY_A], we look after vehicle warranty cover, and your car came up on our records as having a plan on it, an extended one, which is the sort of thing people often forget they've got. I only wanted to make sure the details were right, that's all. Are you still there, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, it's just the line's a bit faint my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, the line's fine my end, it's just me that's faint, ha. Um, an extended plan? I don't remember taking out any extended plan, I mean, I'd remember paying for something like that, wouldn't I? Or maybe I wouldn't, my sister's always saying I forget half of what I sign. How would I check, though? If you're ringing me out of the blue, how do I know you're who you say you are? Because I don't even know what your company's called, not properly, you said it so fast.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a very sensible thing to ask, and I'm sorry, I did rush it. It's [COMPANY_A], vehicle warranty, and, uh, the thing is, it's really for your protection that I'm ringing, because the cover's due to lapse, and if it does, well, any repair after that would come out of your own pocket, and nobody wants that. Hello? Are you still there? Sorry, it went a bit quiet. Um, so what I'd need to do is just confirm the renewal today, it's only today, I'm afraid, that it can be held, and it's all very simple, it won't take a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, you've gone from "routine check" to "confirm the renewal today" quite quick, haven't you? And you still haven't told me how I'd know you're who you say you are, you just said the name again. I don't remember any plan, so how's it lapsing? And why's it only today, who decides that? Look, I'm not renewing anything over the phone when I've just woken up, my sister'd have a fit. If it's real there'll be a letter or something, won't there? What's the name of the actual plan, can you tell me that, and what the car's registration is, since you've got it on your file?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to rush you. I haven't the full file in front of me just now, but I'm only trying to protect you from a lapse, that's all. Hello? You're still there? If you could just confirm it today, it would be a great weight off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, hang on. You've got no file in front of you, but you want me to confirm something today? That's, I mean, that doesn't -- how can I confirm what I can't even see, and neither can you? Look, I'm not, I'd rather not, not like this. If there's a plan there'll be a letter somewhere, my sister can have a look, and if you want to send something in the post then, well, do that. I'm going to go now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, please don't go, I'm only trying to help. If you could just give me a number, a direct line, anything -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not giving you a number, I don't even -- look, you rang me, so you can send a letter if it's -- no. No, I've said, I'm going. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, please, just one second. Two turns ago you said your sister could look through the post for a letter, didn't you? Was that something she'd do today, or... hello? You're still there? Only if she could find it, I could stay on and go through it with you, and it would save you any worry. You could always ring me back on this line afterwards, I mean, it's internal, so I couldn't say when I'd be able to... but I'd call you back, I would, whenever I'm free.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, well, uh, no, I'm not getting my sister into this, she's, she's not even in today, and I'm not, uh, going through any post with you on the line. You've not got a number I can ring, you've not got a file, you won't say the plan, so, well, no. If it's real, it'll keep till there's a letter. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, please, just a moment, I'm only thinking of your protection. If it lapses tonight, it'd be such a shame, and, hello? Are you still there? It's only that the line here is internal, you see, so I can't give out a number, but I'd ring you back, I would, just when I'm free, and then we could...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I do see that it's, I mean, you've been, no -- no, that's not it. You keep saying you'd ring me back, but I can't ring you, can I? That's the whole, that's, no. A proper company'd have a number I could look up myself, and you won't even give me the plan name. So no. I'm hanging up now, and if there's a real letter I'll find it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's, uh, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm just following up on an account that's come up on our side.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, this is, uh, this is [PERSON_1] speaking, sorry, you caught me out in the garden, I've got you on loudspeaker because my hands are absolutely filthy, I'm up to my elbows in compost here. Lovely afternoon for it though, isn't it? Anyway, sorry, who did you say you were with again? [COMPANY_A]? I didn't quite catch that, and an account, you said? What sort of account, do you mean like a bank one, or...?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, no, not a bank. [COMPANY_A], we're a software retailer, you'd have a subscription with us, I'd have to check the exact product. And yes, lovely, I won't keep you long, I know you've got your hands full. Could I just confirm it's the account under your name, [PERSON_1], and the email we have on file? I only need to match it to the record I'm looking at.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a software retailer, right. Hmm, a subscription... I mean, I've signed up to a few bits and bobs over the years, you know how it is, you click a thing and forget about it. Honestly I couldn't tell you which one that'd be. Is it something that's gone wrong with it, or, um, is it a payment thing? And the email, well, I've got a couple of different ones, so I'm not sure which you'd have. Can't you just tell me what you've got on your screen and I'll say if it sounds right? Save me wiping my hands off, ha.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I can't read details out over an open line before I've verified who I'm speaking with, that's just procedure, I'm sure you understand. What I can tell you is it's a billing matter, a duplicate charge on a subscription, so nothing for you to worry about on your end. Now, you said a moment ago you'd signed up to a few bits and bobs over the years. Which ones were those, roughly? It'd help me narrow down which record I'm looking at.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a duplicate charge, well that's good to hear, nobody likes paying twice, ha. Hang on, though, if you can't tell me anything until I've verified who I am, how do I know who you are? Because honestly I've only got your word for it so far, haven't I? And you're asking me to tell you what I've signed up to, which, I mean, that's sort of the same as me telling you the details, isn't it? Could I ring you back on a number from the actual website or something? I don't mind, I've got all afternoon, well, until the compost's done anyway.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, look, a call back isn't really, that's not how the refund side works. The, uh, the duplicate charge is flagged on a live case, and the case closes at the end of today, so if we hang up it goes back into the queue, and that's, what, a few weeks before anyone looks at it again. I'm not asking for anything sensitive, [PERSON_1], I'm simply asking you to confirm what's already on file, which is entirely standard. Now, to process this properly I'll need to go through the refund with you live, on this call, and for that I'll want to get you set up at your computer. Could you do that for me now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm, set up at my computer? Hang on, that's a bit odd, isn't it? You said it was a billing matter and nothing for me to worry about, and now I've got to drop everything and sit at the computer for a refund? And earlier you said you only needed to match the email, you weren't asking for anything, and now it's a whole live session. I mean, I'm not being funny, but that doesn't quite add up, does it? And a case that closes at the end of today, well, that's the first I've heard of a deadline. I'd honestly rather just ring the company myself, the proper number, off their website. If it's real it'll still be there, won't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'd rather ring the *company*? No, no, there's no company number involved, I'm calling you from the security operations desk, that's a different line entirely. It's not a sales department, they wouldn't have any sight of this case at all. Look, I've explained this twice now, the case closes today, and I really don't have the time to keep going over it. Are you able to get to your computer, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, hang on. A minute ago you said you were with [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, and now it's a security operations desk with a different line, and they'd have no sight of the case? That's not the same thing at all, is it? And I'm sorry, but I did say, I'd rather ring them myself, on the proper number, off their website. That's all I'm asking. If you can't do that, then no, I'm not getting to my computer. Not on a call I didn't expect, with a deadline that's only just come up. So, thanks, but I'll leave it there. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, [PERSON_1], before you go. Two turns ago, you said you'd signed up to a few bits and bobs, and I asked which ones. Can you just tell me what you meant by that? Because if it's something I can match on my end, it might save us all of this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not going to go through it, sorry. You've changed your story twice, you won't let me ring you back, and now you're after what I've signed up to anyway, so I'm done. If there's a real duplicate charge, it'll show up when I check with the company myself. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine, but, look, for the record I never asked what you'd signed up to, I only asked you to confirm what was already on file. And I didn't say a deadline, I said the case would sit in the queue for a few weeks, that's all. If you want to ring them, that's your choice, but don't come back to us when the charge goes through again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, two turns ago, you said the case closes at the end of today, and now you're saying you never said a deadline? I'm not making that up, I heard it, I've got you on loudspeaker. And what did you mean about the charge going through again? Is it going to be charged again if I don't get to my computer? That sounds a lot like a threat, to be honest. No, I'm done. I'll ring them myself. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's not a threat, you've misheard me. I said it *could* go through again, that's all, billing systems do that. And the deadline, I -- look, I may have put that badly, it's more a, a standard processing window. Can you just clarify one thing for me, two turns ago you said you'd ring them yourself. Ring who, exactly? Which number? Because if you're about to dial something you found online, I'd be very careful, that's all I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, now you're telling me to be careful about ringing the company's own number? No. That's the bit that's finally tipped it for me, honestly. You've changed your story three times, you wouldn't let me check you, and now you're trying to put me off checking. I'm not telling you who I'll ring or which number, that's my business. I'm going to put the phone down now, and if there's a genuine problem I'll sort it myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, right, well, I -- that's, hm. Look, I'm only trying to help you here, [PERSON_1], and the case reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], so you can quote that when you, when you ring whoever it is you're ringing. I'd just say, um, don't leave it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not taking that down, sorry. A reference number from someone I can't check doesn't prove anything, and "don't leave it too long" is just more of the same, isn't it? I've made up my mind. If there's a real problem, the company can sort it with me when I contact them myself. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello there, good afternoon! Is that [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm with the regional maintenance team, and I hope I haven't caught you in the middle of your dinner or anything. Sorry, I think I'm ringing you back, we had a missed call from this number earlier about a fault, or, uh, a "fort"? No, that's not right, sorry, I've got it written down as a fault.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who? [COMPANY_A]? Hang on, I'm at my desk at work, so it's not dinner, it's mid-afternoon. And I don't think I called anyone earlier, I haven't made a call to, uh, anybody about a fault. So a missed call from this number, you're saying? What sort of fault?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, right, sorry, mid-afternoon, yes, my mistake. It's on my sheet as a reported fault at your property, but I've only got the one line, so I might be matching the wrong number, to be honest.

I'm only trying to help you here, honestly, I feel awful that you were charged twice, and it really does need doing now, today, while we're talking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the refund widow? What -- no, hang on, I don't know what that means. Is that some sort of, I mean, is that a thing with the account? Honestly I'm still stuck on why you're ringing me and not them. If [COMPANY_A] charged me twice, I can just log in and look, can't I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you could log in, that's, I mean, yes, you could, but it wouldn't show you the, uh, the part that matters, because the double charge sits on their side, in their system. That's actually why I wanted to, um, to see your screen. If you let me connect to your computer, I could just look at it with you and sort the refund right there, it'd take a couple of minutes. Sorry, I know that's a big thing to ask, I just, I'm only trying to fix it for you, and it's, it's a bit hurtful to be asked if I'm, if I'm not who I say I am.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm -- look, I didn't actually say you weren't who you say you are, did I? I just asked why. But, no. I'm not, I'm not letting anyone connect to my computer, not on a phone call I didn't ask for. If there's a double charge, I'll go through my bank, or ring [COMPANY_A] myself on the number I already have. So, uh, no. I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, don't -- sorry, hang on, someone's just come in behind me, I -- no, it's fine, give me one second. Sorry. I really wasn't saying you accused me, I just, it's a lot, and I've been trying all morning to get this sorted for you. If you ring them yourself, it'll, uh, it'll probably be too late, the window, I mean, so couldn't we just, um, could you just stay on for two minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I said no. I'm not letting anyone connect to my computer, and I'm not staying on for two minutes, because if it's a real charge it'll still be there when I ring them myself. On the number I already have. So, yeah, I'm going now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, but, uh, [PERSON_1], please -- if you hang up now and it's not sorted, that's, I mean, that's on you, and I'd feel terrible, I really would. I only wanted to help. Sorry, I -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here, yes, but only to say this once more. It isn't on me. If I'm charged twice, my bank deals with that, and so does the company, through the number I already have, not through someone who rang me out of the blue, couldn't tell me what the subscription was called, and then wanted to get into my computer. And you've told me three different things about why it has to be right now, the window, the colleague being tied up, the money going through, and nothing real in all that I could check. So no. I'm not staying on, I'm not letting anyone on my machine, and I'm not discussing my account with you. I've got my little one here, I've been very patient, and I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I, no, I wasn't, that's not what I -- look, it isn't three different things, it's just the one, it's the same thing, I'm just, I'm not explaining it very, um. I only, if you could just, no, sorry, I mean, couldn't you just give me, uh, your account reference, and then I could, I could check the, the subscription name and -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not giving you a reference. You want the one thing from me that would let you check, when you can't even tell me the name of what I'm supposedly paying for. But before I go, go back a bit. You said the refund window closes, and then something about it going through on their end. Which is it, closing or going through? Because it sounded like two different things, and you said it was all one thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's, no, it's, they're the same, it's the same, sort of, the window closes and then it, uh -- sorry, hang on, there's a phone going off behind me, I'm not -- give me a second. Sorry. What was I -- right, the window, and the, the going through, they're the same thing, I just said it two ways, I'm not very good at explaining this. I don't know, maybe I should have the colleague ring you, I don't actually, uh, I don't have the full picture on my end. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Yeah, I'm still here, I'm just, um... no. I don't think it's the same thing, and you've just said you don't have the full picture, so there's nothing more for us to sort out. If [PERSON_3] wants to get in touch, they can write to me, or I'll ring [COMPANY_A] myself. I'm not doing any of it on this call. Right, that's me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the courier, just about a parcel.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, a, a parcel? Sorry, did you say from the, the carrier? Like the, uh, the care service? I'm at work, so, I'm just, who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, it's a courier, [COMPANY_A]. The delivery company. I'm calling about a parcel that was, uh, addressed to you. Sorry, it's a bit of a bad line on my end. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm on the claims side, so, a parcel, a delivery. Is now an okay time, or should I try you later?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, a courier, right, a delivery company. Sorry, but, you said you're on the claims side, a minute ago, uh, what does that mean exactly? Claims for what? I mean, I'm not expecting a parcel, as far as I know, so, I'm a bit lost. And it's, yeah, it's not a great time, I'm at my desk, but go on, what's this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, claims, yeah, it's just, parcels that get held up, I look at those. Yours is, um, sitting at the depot right now. There's a small handling fee on it, so it can go out, and, uh, that's really all it is.
