utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A handling fee. Right. Sorry, I'm not expecting anything, so, how do I know this is real?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, it's, I mean, you'd, uh, hang on, let me just -- sorry, I've got it on the screen here, give me a second. Okay, so the parcel's down as, um, held since this morning. No, wait, yesterday, sorry, yesterday. And the fee is only [AMOUNT_1], and it's something we can sort out right now over the phone, that's the quickest way, because if it isn't settled today it goes back to the sender.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, you said the parcel's held since yesterday, but a second ago it was this morning, so which is it? And, uh, going back to the claims thing, you said you look at held-up parcels, so who's it from? Who sent it? Because I really don't remember ordering anything, and if I can't say who it's from, I'm not paying anything over the phone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, I'd have to check who the sender is, sorry. Look, I'll go and look that up and, um, call you back, okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you're going to check who the sender is and call me back, right? Honestly, that's, that's sort of the whole thing for me, because you were telling me there's a fee to pay today, and then you can't tell me who the parcel's from, or even whether it's been held since yesterday or this morning. I'm not saying you're, I don't know, up to something, but I've heard enough on the news about this kind of call that I'm not going to pay anything over the phone, not on a call I wasn't expecting. So, if there really is a parcel, they'll have a way to track it, or I'll get a card through the door, and I'll deal with it that way, with the company directly. You don't need to call me back, really, I'll sort it myself if it's real. Anyway, I do need to get back to what I was doing, so, thanks, and, yeah, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, I'm so glad I caught you, I know how it is, everybody's running around this time of day. It's [PERSON_2] calling from customer care over at [COMPANY_A], how are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh hi, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], hello! I'm doing great actually, thanks for asking, I'm just out in the garden, got the phone on speaker so I can keep my hands in the soil. I'm putting in some tomatoes, bit late in the season really, but the weather's been so nice I thought, why not? Sorry, what was the company again? I think a bird landed on the fence right when you said it, haha. Customer care, you said?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no worries, tomatoes in this weather, sounds lovely. It's [COMPANY_A], customer care, I'm calling about your account. Listen, it's, uh, kind of time-sensitive, so I'll just get to it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, sure, go ahead. Um, but hang on, sorry, going back a second, you said it was [PERSON_2] you were, was that right? I only half caught it, there's a trowel clanking about here. And the company, did you say [COMPANY_A]? Because I've got a few accounts with different places, so which one is this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_2], and yes, [COMPANY_A], the electric. You've got a few accounts, ha, I know the feeling, you can't keep track of them all. Anyway, the reason I'm calling is there's an unpaid balance of [AMOUNT_1] on your account, and I've got to be honest with you, it's flagged for disconnection. Your power's going to be cut within the hour if we don't get that sorted out today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Within the hour? Oh no, hang on, that can't be right, I'm sure I paid the, I mean I always, wait, did you say [AMOUNT_1]? Is that, because I thought I was all, oh dear, my hands are all muddy, hold on. Sorry, so the power's going off, today? But I didn't get a letter or anything, did I? Maybe I did, I never open half my post, haha. What do I do, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, don't worry about the post, honestly, half the letters we send end up in the recycling, ha. Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a pile of files on my desk, it's like a library in here. Okay, I'm back. So, the quickest way to keep your lights on is to settle that [AMOUNT_1] today, and I can sort that out with you right now, over the phone, so there's no need to go hunting for any letters.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, okay, sorry, wait, um, can I go back a bit? Earlier you said it was the electric, and I've got, well, I think the electric's with a different company, isn't it? Or is it? I get them muddled. So which one is it you're from again? Because [COMPANY_A], I'm not sure I've even heard that on my bills. And how do I know it's, well, no offence, I'm sure you're lovely, but how would I check that? Could I ring you back on the number on my bill or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no offence taken, you're being careful, that's good, I like that. But honestly, ringing back isn't really going to work, our lines are slammed this afternoon, you'd be on hold for ages, and the disconnection is scheduled for within the hour. I can't hold that off for you once it's in the system. So if we could just take care of the [AMOUNT_1] now, that'd really be the simplest thing, and then you can get back to your tomatoes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, hmm. See, the thing is, I'm just sat here on my knees in the dirt with a tomato plant in one hand, and I don't really, I mean, I'm not sure I'd want to sort out money over the phone with somebody when I'm not even certain which company you're from. That's just me being daft probably, but my daughter's always going on at me about being careful, she had some trouble with, oh, some email thing a couple of years back, and ever since she's said, never do anything on the phone you can't check yourself. And you said ringing back would take ages, but I don't mind waiting on hold, honestly, I've got the whole afternoon and the tomatoes aren't going anywhere, haha. And if the electric really is going off in an hour, wouldn't it be a bit odd for you to say I can't phone the proper number to check? Because that's sort of the whole point of having a number on the bill, isn't it? So I think what I'll do is go in, wash my hands, find the bill, and ring the number printed on it. Is that all right? Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult. You've been very nice about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, you're not being difficult, but look, I'd really rather you didn't go off and do that, because the clock's honestly ticking here, and once it hits the hour I can't undo it. Your daughter sounds lovely, but this isn't one of those email things, I'm a real person on a real call, I'm telling you the power is going off. Let's just get it settled now, [PERSON_1], it's one quick thing, and then you don't have to worry about anything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, see, that's the bit that's making me go, hmm. Because you've just said you'd rather I didn't go and check, and that's exactly what my daughter says to watch out for, someone telling you not to check. And I'm not saying you're not a real person, I'm sure you are, you've been very pleasant, but a real person at a real electric company wouldn't mind me ringing the number on my own bill, would they? They'd say, oh good idea, go and do that. If anything, that makes me feel better about doing it. And honestly, if the power does go off in the next hour, well, I've got a garden full of daylight, I'll cope, haha, and I'll just ring them and sort it out, they're not going to leave an old woman in the dark over one afternoon, are they? So I think I'm going to say thanks, but no, not like this. I'll go in, wash my hands, find my last bill and ring the number on it. You take care now, and sorry again for being a pain, bye bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_1], wait, hang on, please don't hang up, that's really not a good idea. Your daughter's just being cautious, bless her, but you're making this harder than it needs to be, and I'd hate for you to be sitting there in the dark an hour from now saying, why didn't I just sort it when [PERSON_2] called? I'm trying to help you here. It's [AMOUNT_1], that's all, one quick thing, and everything stays on, so can we just do that now before the time runs out?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm sorry, but I've made up my mind, and the more you push the more sure I am, honestly, because if you were really, I mean, I'm putting the phone down now, and I'll ring the number on my bill myself, so thanks very much, goodbye, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, [PERSON_1], hello? You still there? Um, look, I really wouldn't, I mean, you've got maybe forty minutes left, that's all I'm saying, and once it's in the system there's honestly nothing I can do. Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still, I did say goodbye, didn't I? Look, I, no, what I mean is, forty minutes or four, it doesn't change anything. I'm going to ring the number on my own bill, and if it's all, if there really is a problem, they'll tell me. So that's that. Bye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry to trouble you, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler on the customs desk at [COMPANY_A]. It's about a parcel of yours that's with us in [CITY_1] and, uh, there's a small import charge on it, so I wanted to explain that properly rather than just leave you a message. Sorry, did I say customs desk earlier? I mean the clearance team, it's the same thing really, just, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hello? Yes, yes, I'm here, I'm still here, sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie down and the phone, uh, it went off right by my ear. Who did you say you were? I'm sorry, I'm still sort of, um, waking up. A parcel, you said? I don't, I don't remember ordering anything, not lately anyway. Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I woke you up, that's awful of me. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the courier, I'm on the customs side. And, sorry, did you say you don't remember ordering a *patch*? No, no, it isn't a patch, I'm sorry, I think I've confused things, it's a parcel, an ordinary parcel. Uh, it may well have been sent by someone else on your behalf, or you might be expecting it from a shop, so please don't worry. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said parcel, not patch, I don't know where you got patch from. Hm. I'm with you, yes, I'm here, but I'm a bit lost, to be honest. You said customs, and then clearance, and now courier, and I don't, which one is it? And it's from who, a shop? My sister sometimes sends me things from, oh, I forget where she gets them, but she never says. What's it supposed to be, this parcel? Do you know what's in it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, I'm sorry, I muddled that, I said patch and I shouldn't have. It's one company, [COMPANY_A], the courier, and the customs desk is just our department. I don't have the contents in front of me, only the sender's name, which is [PERSON_3], so that might be your sister. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. My sister's not called that, so, no. I'm here. But you don't know what's in it, and I don't know what it is, so what's the charge actually for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, that's fair, and thank you for asking, it's a good question. The charge is import duty, [AMOUNT_1], because the parcel came in from abroad, and I only have the sender's name, not what's inside, which is why I'd rather you didn't take my word for it. If it isn't from your sister, it might be from someone else, or it might not be yours at all, and that's fine too. Please don't pay anything on this call, and I'm not asking you to. If you look at your messages or your email, there should be a tracking reference, and if you tell me it's there I can read mine to match it, and you can look the parcel up yourself on [URL_1] and see the charge for yourself. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, hang on, you said look at my messages, my messages? I've got, uh, the one from the chemist about a prescription, I think, it's been sitting there since, oh, Tuesday. Is that the one? I never know which button gets me into those. And I'm, I'm not paying anything, you said that, yes, good. But why would it say anything about a prescription, is it, is that what's in the parcel?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, sorry, that one's the chemist, it's nothing to do with us. Ours would say [COMPANY_A] and have a reference with [CODE_1] on it. If there isn't one, that's fine, just leave it. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, I'm here, I'm just, uh, hang on, let me think. Well, there's nothing from, um, what was it, the courier? No. I don't think so anyway, I can't really tell with these buttons. So if there's no message, then it's, what, it's not mine? Is that what you're saying? Because honestly it sounds like it's probably not mine, and I'd rather, I think I'd rather just leave it, like you said.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, well, I'd say it's most likely not yours, if there's nothing from us, and, uh, I'd rather you leave it than guess, honestly. If it isn't claimed the parcel just goes back to the sender, and that's, that's no harm to you at all, so please don't worry about it. Sorry, I know I've gone round the houses on this call. If a message from [COMPANY_A] does turn up, you can check it on [URL_1] at your own pace, and, and you needn't ring me back, either. Are you still there? I'm sorry I woke you, and thank you for being so patient, [PERSON_1], you have a lovely afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, thank you, I will, I'll just leave it then. Although, hang on, you said at the start it was a small charge and then you said it was duty, and I'm not sure those are the same thing, but never mind, it doesn't matter if I'm not paying. And I wasn't really having a lie down, it was more of a proper nap, so don't feel bad. Anyway, bye now, you have a good afternoon as well.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm with the collections and allocations desk. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? Okay, good. I'm calling because there's a position in one of our funds that's still open on your file, and it closes today at the end of the trading session, so I need about two minutes of your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- what position? I don't have a position with anyone, I've got two minutes total. Who are you with, exactly, and what's this actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, [COMPANY_A], investment firm, and the position's been reserved under your name, it's showing on my screen as an allocation, not a holding, so you wouldn't have one yet. Uh, I mean, that's the whole point, it's pending your confirmation. The projected return on it is [AMOUNT_1] over ninety days, and that's off the fund's own numbers, I'm just reading them. Once the session closes today the allocation goes back into the pool, so that's settled, there's no extending it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, stop. I haven't applied for anything, so how is there an allocation reserved in my name? That's not a thing. And a guaranteed return in ninety days that vanishes at the end of today? That's a script, not an investment. How did you get this number, and what's your name again, and a callback number? Not one you read me, I'll look the firm up myself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand, and I'll note the objection on the file, but the allocation is still showing and it still closes today -- the numbers I gave you are the fund's, not mine, and I never said guaranteed, I said projected. As for the callback line, uh, that's routed through the desk, it's not a direct number, so I can't really give you one I could stand behind. If you want to look the firm up, that's fine, but the window's the window, and by the time you've done that the position is gone. So, shall I put you down for the [AMOUNT_2] tier, or --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, the what tier? A... pier? No, sorry, tier. Right. No, you're not putting me down for anything. And you can't give me a callback number but you want me to commit today? That's backwards. I'm not confirming, I'm not applying, and I'm certainly not doing it before I've checked who you are. If the firm's real, it'll still be there tomorrow. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just -- no, that's fine, go ahead, I'm back. Uh, I'll note you as declined. The position releases at the close regardless, so there's nothing more for me to action here. Have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well -- no, I'm, look, if there's actually an allocation, I'd, I mean, it can go back in the pool, I don't care. And don't ring this number again, please. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, I'll flag the number as do-not-contact. Take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, I -- no. Actually, just, fine. Whatever, flag it. I'm going now, I've got a meeting. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, fine. Just so it's on the record, it's [PERSON_1] again, and I did say earlier there's no extending the window, but the system's showing it open till tomorrow morning, so, uh, if you change your mind it's still there. Anyway. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, so it's -- no, hang on. Earlier you said it goes back in the pool at the close today, no extending, and now it's open till tomorrow? That's, I mean, you've just changed it on me. Which is exactly what I'd expect, and I'm not changing my mind. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Right, um, so I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and I'm a claims assessor, no wait, sorry, I do the consumer surveys side, and I was just wondering if you had maybe five minutes for a short survey?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hello? Sorry, I was just -- I'd dozed off, I was in the chair. Who is this again? You said claims, and then survey, which, I mean, which one is it? I don't, um, I don't really do surveys, my daughter says I shouldn't, but, well, what's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, sorry, that was me mixing up my titles. It's a survey, from [COMPANY_A]. Uh, it's just about, let me see, it's on my screen here -- general household spending habits, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Household spending? Oh, I thought you said household *spenders*, like, the, uh, the people who come round about the roof. We had a man about the roof in the spring, didn't we, no, that was my sister's. Anyway, I don't have anything to do with a roof, if that's what this is. And you still haven't really said who you are. [COMPANY_A], what is that, like a, a shop?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not about a roof, nothing like that, it's just -- sorry, it's a research agency, we ask people questions and, um, the results go to -- Oh, sorry, you were saying. [COMPANY_A], it's not a shop, no, it's more of a, a market research sort of, I mean, I'd have to check exactly who the client is, I don't have that in front of me right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I don't, I mean -- you said you'd have to check who it's for, but, hang on, how can you be calling me and not know who it's, who it's for? That seems a bit, I don't know. First it was claims, then surveys, now you don't know the client. And what do you want to know about my spending, exactly? I'm not telling anybody about my, you know, my money.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I know, that's fair, I'm, uh, I'm quite new at this and I've got my notes in a bit of a muddle. It's not about your actual money, it's just, like, general questions, what sort of things households buy, nothing about accounts or anything. I could, um, I'd have to check with my supervisor about the client, and then, I mean, I could call back, if that's easier?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Call back, well, I mean, I don't know, I just -- I don't really want anybody calling back about my money, that's what I said, I said I'm not telling anybody about my money. And you keep saying it's not about money, but it's household spending, which, that is money, isn't it? That's what spending is. So I don't see how it's not about money. And you still can't say who it's for. Look, if you're from a proper agency, why don't you send something in the post, like a letter, with the name on it, and then I can show my daughter. Because I'm not, I'm really not doing it like this, over the phone, when I've only just woken up and I don't know who you are. Right, I'm going to go now. Thank you, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, right, sorry, hang on one second, somebody's just -- no, never mind, they've gone. Yes, okay, no, that's fine, I understand, you have a good evening then, sorry to have, um, sorry for waking you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's all right, I'll just -- bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hi, uh, hello. Is that, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, hang on, I've got it on the screen here -- yes. It's [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with [COMPANY_A], the tenancy deposit protection scheme, and I'm calling about a dispute that's, uh, come in on the property at [CITY_1]. Sorry, did you say you're the tenant or the landlord? I thought you said landlord, I may have misheard.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, hello. Um, yes, that's me, well, [PERSON_1], yes. No, I didn't say anything yet, dear, you've only just rung -- but, uh, I'm not either, I don't think? I mean, I did let a room out once, years ago, to a lovely young man, he played the cello, terrible racket but lovely manners. Sorry, I'm going off. A dispute, you said? On a property? What property is this exactly, and, um, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sorry, that's my mistake, I'll -- it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], we hold tenancy deposits, um, protect them, I mean. And it's the property in [CITY_1], the cello -- sorry, hang on, I'm just looking for the tenancy name here -- so it's showing you as a contact on the file, not as a party, I think, and I'd have to double check that, but what I'm calling about is that while the dispute is open, we ask that you keep the details private from the other tenants until both sides have been formally notified. Could I just confirm your full name and the address you're at, so I know I've got the right [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I, I'm not sure that -- no, hang on. Let me start again. You've got me down as a contact, you said, but I don't, I mean, I can't think why I would be, I haven't had anyone in the house since the cello fellow, and that was, oh, ages. And now you want my name and my address? You rang me, dear, so you ought to have those, oughtn't you? That's the bit that's got me puzzled. Who gave you my number, actually?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's fair, you're right, I did ring you. Um, I'll have to check where the number came from, it'll be on the file somewhere, I just -- hang on, I can't see it on this screen. And the name and address, forget that, you don't need to give me anything. If I've got the wrong [PERSON_1], I'm sorry, that's on me. The privacy thing is only a fairness rule, we ask contacts not to discuss an open case until both sides have been notified in writing, so nobody's put at a disadvantage. I can send the same request by post if you'd rather, with a case reference, and you can look that up on the scheme's own website at [URL_1]. Or you could just put the phone down and ring the main number on there yourself, honestly, nothing's lost either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's, that's quite decent of you, actually. Most people who ring up just push and push, my sister's always going on about it. But, hm, you can't tell me where the number came from, and you don't know if I'm even the right person, so I don't really see what you'd be sending me. A letter about a house I've got nothing to do with? No, I think, I think I'd rather not have anything sent, dear. If there's a case and I'm really on it, someone can write to me properly and I'll ring the main number myself, like you said. That's very sensible, that is. I'm sorry you've had a bother with the wrong person. Well, mind how you go, and I hope you find the right one. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's -- sorry, I mean, I understand. I was going to say I'd flag it, but -- yes, you're quite right, if you're on the file at all, it'll come to you in writing. Thank you, [PERSON_1], and sorry again for the bother. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no bother at all, dear, it was nice of you to ring, even if it was the wrong end of the wire. You take care now, and give my love to the cello, if you ever find him. Goodbye, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, right, I will, I'll -- well, I don't think I will, but, yes, thank you. And, um, just so it's said, you don't need to do anything, nothing at all. If it is you on the file, it'll come in writing, and if it isn't, then, well, that's that. Sorry, I'm saying it twice, aren't I? Right. Goodbye, [PERSON_1], mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you did say, dear, I've got it, nothing to do, it'll come in -- oh, but you know, you've reminded me, the cello fellow's mother used to send me a card every Christmas, with a robin on, and -- no, never mind, I'm rambling again. You've been very kind. Right. Goodbye then, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a robin, that's nice, that's a nice thing to get. Um, no, you're not rambling, honestly. Right, well, I'll let you get on, then. Thank you for being so patient with me, [PERSON_1], I did get myself in a muddle there. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you weren't any trouble, dear, not a bit, it was nice to have a chat, it's very quiet here of an afternoon. Yes, the robin ones, lovely, they had a little bit of glitter on, I remember, a robin with glitter. Well. Goodbye now, goodbye, you mind how you go too.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Glitter, oh, that's -- yes, that's lovely, you don't see those so much now. Uh, you have a nice afternoon, [PERSON_1], and I hope it's not too quiet for you. Goodbye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, dear, you too. Mind you, it's not always quiet, the cello fellow was ever so noisy, though I suppose that was years back, and he only played in the mornings, come to think of it, not the afternoons, I said afternoons before, didn't I? Never mind. Goodbye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, it's [PERSON_1] calling from the school office at [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant here, and I'm just ringing because [PERSON_2] was marked absent this morning and we've got no note or message on file, so I wanted to check everything's okay and see if there's a reason we should be recording, uh, is that the right number for [PERSON_2]'s parent or guardian?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- uh, sorry, hi, hang on, I'm driving, you're on speaker and the reception's terrible out here. Sorry. Um, [PERSON_2], did you say? Absent this morning? I mean, that, that doesn't sound right, I dropped, well, I'm sure they went in, so, uh... sorry, who is this again, the school office?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, it's [PERSON_1], the school office at [COMPANY_A], and I know it's a bad time, I won't keep you, it's just that [PERSON_2] shows as absent on this morning's register and we've got nothing on file, so if you dropped them off then that might just be a mix-up on our end, I mean, I'm only trying to find out, uh, did [PERSON_2] definitely come in this morning, because if so I can go and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, you cut out a bit there -- you said something about the register, and, uh, earlier you said a name, [PERSON_1]? Did I get that right? And, sorry, which school was it again, I didn't quite catch the name of it. I just want to be sure I've got the right place, 'cause I'm, I'm a bit worried now, I did drop them off, I'm pretty sure, I mean I always do, so, um, yeah.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [PERSON_1], from the school office at [COMPANY_A], sorry, bad line, and honestly it's probably just a register mix-up, so if you're sure you dropped [PERSON_2] off, uh, right, so, what I'm really after is whether they definitely went in this morning, because if so I can go and, um, sorry, you're still there? Anyway, did [PERSON_2] go in this morning?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm still here, sorry, the line keeps, uh, breaking up. Um, I mean, I'm pretty sure they went in, I watched them walk to the, to the door, I think. But sorry, can I ask, how come you're ringing me and, and you haven't said anything about, like, which class or which year? Because I'd feel better if you could tell me that first, just so I know it's actually the right school and the right, uh, [PERSON_2]. Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I'm just, my stomach's a bit in knots now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fair, that's completely fair, I'd ask the same, it's just that, uh, well, I've got [PERSON_2] on the register as, sorry, it's, I mean the year group is on the system, and the class, but I'd rather not, I mean, I can't really read that out down the phone before I know I've got the right person, so, um, if you could just confirm they went in this morning, and I can go and check with the class teacher straight away, did you actually see them go through the door?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I, I didn't quite follow that, you can't say the class because you don't know it's me, but you want me to tell you if, if they went in? Isn't that sort of backwards? I mean, sorry, I'm not trying to, it's just that if you're the school you'd already have it, wouldn't you? The class, and the year, and my, my number, I mean that's why you rang me. And I did say, I watched them walk to the door, I think, um, so I'd really like to hear the class first, sorry, or, or I could just ring the school myself, couldn't I, on the number I've got, I mean once I'm parked.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said park the, no, uh, the park? No, right, parked, yes, but honestly there's no need for all that, I just need a quick yes or no on whether [PERSON_2] came in this morning, it'll take two seconds, so if you could just --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, well, uh, hang on, I'm just, sorry, give me a second here, I'm trying to... yeah. See, you saying there's no need for all that is sort of making me more nervous, not less, I mean, if it's two seconds then it's two seconds for you to say the class, isn't it? So, uh, I think I'm just going to ring the school myself once I'm parked, on the number I've already got. Sorry, I really do hope it's a mix-up, thank you for, for calling, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, no, that's fine, that's absolutely fine, please do, and I hope [PERSON_2] turns out to be in class, sorry for the worry, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, thanks, I'll, I'll ring them in a, sorry, you're breaking up again, but yes, thank you, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, yes, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, just, one moment while I, uh, bring up the file here. Right, so this is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, and I'm ringing in connection with the, um, post-operative status of your animal following last week's procedure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, speaking, that's me -- hello, hello. The vet, you said? Oh, is it about Biscuit, because I did think he was a bit off his food, but then he's always been funny with the, well, the new biscuits, ironically, ha, and I did wonder if I should ring you, only the phone's been -- sorry, go on, you were saying about the procedure?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, yes, [PERSON_1], that's precisely the sort of thing we're ringing about, so I'm glad you raised it. Reduced appetite, or inappetence, as we'd say, in the immediate post-operative window, it's, well, it's quite common following a general anaesthetic, partly the residual effect of the sedative agents, partly just, uh, the animal's generally subdued state while the surgical site is, you know, in the early phase of healing. Now, as a matter of routine protocol, we conduct a structured recovery check at roughly the seven-day mark, where we ask about appetite, hydration, mobility, any discharge or erythema, that's redness, around the incision, and the overall demeanour of the patient, and then, on the basis of those responses, we determine whether a follow-up consultation, a wound assessment, say, or a suture review, is, um, clinically indicated or simply elective. So if you've got a few minutes, I'd, uh, I'd like to just walk through those parameters with you, if that's convenient?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a few minutes, yes, that's fine, I've got all afternoon really, it's just me and the telly. Now, you said something about his, his hydration, was it? Because he does go through the water, Biscuit, he's always been at that bowl, though I did think it was funny, the other day I filled it up and, well, it's the same bowl I've had since, oh, since my sister came to stay, she's in [CITY_1] now, you know, with the grandchildren. But, sorry, you said about the suture review, so does that mean he's got to come in again, because I'd have to get my neighbour to drive us, and I don't like asking.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, [PERSON_1], please don't fret about the driving just yet, because it's not a given that he'd need to come in at all, it's contingent on what we establish today. Now, uh, if he's drinking normally, that's, that's actually reassuring on the hydration front, though, hold on, I did say a moment ago that I'd walk you through the parameters, and I think I may have, uh, rather overstated it, because the clinical team would really be the ones to conduct the formal recovery assessment, whereas I'm only, I mean, I'm merely the person who, um, establishes whether you'd want one. So, in plain terms, would a follow-up visit be something you'd welcome, or would you rather we, uh, monitor remotely for the time being?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, um, I suppose, hm, I'd have to think, wouldn't I, because it's the driving, like I said, and Brian next door, he's lovely, but he's got his own bad hip. Anyway, so, uh, you're not actually the vet yourself then? Only I thought you were going to ask me about his appetite and the, the redness, and now it sounds like you're just, what, booking him in or not booking him in? And I don't think I caught which surgery you said, sorry, my hearing's not what it was, was it the one on the high street?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I'm not the vet, sorry, I'm just on the administrative side, and it's [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery. I'd, uh, I'd rather not rush you on the driving question, so would it be better if I rang back at a quieter time?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, don't ring back, I'm here now, it's just -- sorry, but you still haven't said which one, the one on the high street or the one out by the, the garden centre? Because I've only ever taken Biscuit to the one, and I'd have thought they'd know his name already, so why are you asking me if he's had a procedure, I mean, if you've got the file --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, I'm making a hash of this. It's [COMPANY_A], and I'd honestly sooner you rang the surgery directly to confirm, or I can try again another day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, hang on, that's, that's what I'd do, isn't it, I'd ring them myself, only I'd -- the number's on the fridge somewhere, under the magnet from the, the pizza place. Hm. You're very polite about it, I'll say that. But you did say last week's procedure and I'm not sure, now I come to think, that Biscuit's had one last week, he had his jabs ages ago, and that's -- well, you'd think I'd remember. So I think I'll just ring them, if that's all right. Thank you for ringing, dear, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, uh, long day on my end. I'm just calling from [COMPANY_A], hoping I've caught you at an okay time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, this is, uh -- sorry, who's calling? Which company did you say? I'm kind of at my desk, so I --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're fine, I should've slowed down, I rattled through that. It's [COMPANY_A], we're a computer security company, I'm in the customer care side of things, so mostly I'm the person who rings people up when something on our end needs a human touch rather than yet another automated email. And honestly, I always feel bad calling folks at their desks, because I know how it is, you've got a screen full of stuff and the phone goes and it's never the call you wanted, ha. How's your week been going, anyway? Is it one of those ones that's flown by, or has it dragged?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a... computer security company, you said? Uh, and you're in, what, customer cure? No -- customer care, right. Hang on, so is this about, like, a cure for something, or -- no, sorry, I'm not following. What's it about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no cure, nothing as dramatic as that, you're fine. Customer care, yeah, though I'm actually more on the technical support side, I sort of float between the two depending on the day. Anyway, it's nothing major, I just wanted to check in about your home computer, because something came up on our monitoring that I thought you'd want to hear about sooner rather than later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hang on, so something came up on your monitoring, about my home computer? Uh, I mean, I'm at work right now, so I'm a bit confused, and I'm honestly trying to remember if I even have anything with your company on it. Because I don't think I do, or maybe it came pre-installed, I don't know. Everything on my laptop at home is just whatever was there when I bought it, plus a free antivirus thing my brother put on years ago, and I haven't thought about it since. So how would you even know about my computer? Like, how did you get my number, and how did you connect it to my machine? I'm not saying anything's wrong, I just, uh, I've heard a few things on the news about calls like this, so you can see why I'd want to know where this is coming from before we go any further.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, a brother, that's lovely, mine did the same thing for me once, put some free thing on and I never touched it again. And Hendon, sorry, is that where you are? I thought you said you were out at the office, that's why I asked. Anyway, I wouldn't worry about the how of it, it's honestly the boring part, it's just routine monitoring, and the important bit is that your home computer has been sending out infected traffic, which is a bit of a worry, you know? I'd really like to get you sorted today, if you've got a few minutes, before it spreads to anything else on your network.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hendon? I didn't say Hendon, I never said where I am. I'm at my desk at work, that's all I said. So, wait, you think I'm somewhere I'm not, and you also can't tell me how you found my computer? That's the part I'd actually want to know, you can't just call it the boring part. And, uh, infected traffic from my home computer, today, before it spreads. That's a lot of urgency for someone who still hasn't told me which company he's from. What's the name again? And is there a number I can call you back on, or a reference or something, because I'm not sorting anything out over the phone with someone I can't check.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, did I say Hendon? Honestly, ignore me, I've had about forty of these calls today and my head's mush. Look, the company's [COMPANY_A], I did say it, and the thing is, a callback number is a bit awkward, because the line I'm on goes through our general queue and I'd lose you in there. The quickest route is if you just open your laptop when you're home and I'll talk you through a quick look at it, it'll take ten minutes, and then you'll know it's sorted.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so the number's awkward and I should just open my laptop and you'll talk me through it. No. I mean, I asked for a way to check who you are, and the answer's that you can't give me one. I'm not doing anything with my laptop on a call I can't verify, and I'm saying that again because it doesn't sound like it's landing. If something's actually wrong, I'll look up the company myself and ring their number, not one you give me. So, uh, thanks, but no, I'm done with this one. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, somebody's just come up to my desk with -- no, give me one second, [PERSON_2], I'm on a call. Sorry, [PERSON_1], where was I? Look, no, that's completely fair, honestly, and you'd be right to look us up, but if you do, I'd just say don't leave it too long, because that sort of thing doesn't tend to fix itself. Right, well, I'll let you get on. Have a good rest of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, "don't leave it too long." That's the bit that bothers me, honestly, because it's the same thing again, the pressure to hurry, only softer this time. If it really were urgent, you'd have been able to tell me the company name straight off, or how you found me, or let me ring you back on something I could check. And you never did, you just kept steering me toward opening the laptop. So I'll do what I said. If I'm worried, I'll look the company up myself and ring the number on their actual site, not one from this call. And my brother will probably hear about it too, since he's the one who put the antivirus on. Anyway, that's me. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, that's your call, and honestly, telling your brother is a fine idea, he sounds like a sensible sort. Anyway, I've kept you long enough, and you've got your desk to get back to. Take care of yourself, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, uh, take care. And, sorry, one thing, you said at the start you were calling from the office, but then you said something about the general queue, and then the forty calls today. Which is it? Never mind, I don't actually need the answer. I'm hanging up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, it's all the same office, honestly, I just meant the queue's the main line and the forty is, uh, well, across the whole team, not just me, so it's... look, I wasn't even on the phones at the start of the week, I only got put on them Wednesday, so maybe I've muddled it. Anyway, you go, you go, no harm done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, Wednesday? Earlier you said you ring people up when something needs a human touch, like it's your whole job, and now you've only been on the phones since Wednesday? That doesn't really sit with what you told me at the start. And you said the forty calls were just you, and now it's the whole team. Honestly, I'm not trying to trip you up, I just can't make it add up. So that's it for me. I'm not doing anything on this call, I'll look the company up myself if I need to. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] from the Consumer Asset Verification Division at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling regarding a flagged exposure on your savings, reference [ACCOUNT_REF] -- no, no, please, let me finish, because this is time-sensitive and I do need to confirm you're the account holder before the, uh, the provisional hold window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi, sorry, I'm out in the garden, so you're on speaker. Uh, flagged exposure on my savings? Sorry, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, [PERSON_1], Consumer Asset Verification Division, [COMPANY_A] -- we're the financial regulator, not your bank, which is rather the point. What our monitoring has surfaced is a counterparty concentration anomaly on the account ending under [ACCOUNT_REF], and under the, uh, the supervisory exposure framework, I'm obliged to confirm you're the holder before I can describe the remediation pathway. Could I ask you to confirm your full name for me, please?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, right, hang on, I've just got my hands in the soil here, um... so you're the regulator, not the bank? That's, uh, that's a bit unusual, isn't it? I thought if there was a problem with my savings it'd be the bank ringing me, you know? And a counterparty, what was it, concentration thing? I don't really know what that means, sorry. Can you just say it in plain English, what's actually wrong with my account?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, in plain English, the -- well, it isn't quite that something's wrong with the account, it's that the account is, uh, it's in what we'd call an exposed position. And the reason it's us and not the bank is that, I mean, the bank is in fact part of the, the review itself, so under the supervisory protocol we're not able to route this through them. Which does bring me to something important: your balance needs to be moved to a protected holding arrangement while we resolve it, and until that's done I'd have to ask you not to mention this call to anyone, the bank included. Now, if I could just have your full name for the file?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Don't tell the bank, move my money, and give you my name. Yeah, that doesn't sound right to me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, hold on, if I could just -- I understand the hesitation, truly, but you're conflating the confidentiality provision with the, uh, the substantive remediation, and they're entirely separate under the supervisory framework. The non-disclosure isn't a, a condition I'm imposing, it's procedural, because if the counterparty becomes aware of the review before the holding arrangement is in place, the exposure window widens and, frankly, that's where account holders end up with, with unrecoverable losses, which I'd very much like to avoid for you. So, if we could just proceed with the name, then I can, I can walk you through the next stage before the provisional hold lapses.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I don't think I'll be doing that. A regulator telling me to keep it from my bank and move my money somewhere, that's, I mean, that's just not how I'd expect anything proper to work. I'm going to ring my bank myself, on the number I've always used, and if there's a real problem they'll tell me. Thanks anyway, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Please, wait, I really would advise against that, because once you contact the bank directly the, uh, the provisional hold window may lapse and the, the exposure becomes -- look, I can't be responsible for what happens to the balance if this isn't actioned today, and the review is, it's a confidential matter, so I'd strongly urge you not to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm hanging up now. And, uh, you said earlier it wasn't a problem with the account, just an exposed position or whatever, and now it's the balance that'll be lost if I don't act today? That doesn't add up either. If it's that urgent, the bank can sort it out with me. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, sorry, you said the bank can sort it out, did you say sort of, as in sort of exposed, no, that's, that's not -- the term is a supervised position, and the, the exposure isn't something a branch is, uh, authorised to resolve, so if you'll just stay on the line for one moment --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said the bank can sort it out, not sort of, and honestly, that's the last thing I'd expect a regulator to say, that a branch can't deal with it. I'm done, I'm going to put the phone down now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, well, uh, so -- right, I mean, I'd just, let me, uh, if you'll bear with me a moment -- I'm only trying to say that the, the review is, uh, it's quite a sensitive matter and, well, I'd really prefer that you didn't --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I've told you, I'm finished with this. I'm ringing my bank on the number I've always had, and that's that. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, fine, but, uh, I did say at the start that your bank isn't involved at all, so ringing them really won't, I mean, it won't change anything about the, the hold, and, um, I'd still ask that you not --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said the bank was part of the review, and now it's that they're not involved at all? Those are two different things. Anyway, that's me done, I'm hanging up. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it isn't contradictory, if you'll just let me, uh, clarify the terminology, because I think the, the framing has become muddled on your end. When I said the bank was part of the review, I meant in the sense of being a, a reporting entity under the supervisory framework, which is entirely distinct from being, uh, involved in the sense of, of having any role in the remediation, so those two statements sit together quite comfortably, they do, and I'd be, I mean, I'd be happy to take you through the full regulatory taxonomy if you'd just stay on the line, because the provisional hold is, as I've said, only open for a limited period and, frankly, if it lapses I can't, I can't speak to what happens to the balance after that. And I'd, I'd reiterate, one more time, that the review is confidential, so it really would be, uh, unwise to raise it with anyone, the bank included, until we've, until we've completed the, the protective stage, which is the whole reason I'm trying to, to keep you on the line just now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I'm not wading through a taxonomy while I'm up to my elbows in compost. And you said at the very start it was a flagged exposure, and then you said it wasn't a problem with the account at all, so I've lost track of what I'm even supposed to be worried about. I'm ringing my bank, and I'll tell them about this call too, thanks very much. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm, well, I work with the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A], I'm a senior investigator there, and I'm calling about something sort of... sensitive, that I really need you to keep between us for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh, uh, yeah, this is -- yeah. Sorry, I just woke up, I was having a little lie down, it's been one of those days, the dog was up at five. Who did you say you were? Company A? I don't think I -- is that the one with the, uh, the app? And what do you mean keep it between us, what's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm sorry, please, go ahead and take a second, I didn't mean to wake you. Yes, [COMPANY_A], that's, uh, it's the bank, yes, the app is theirs, but I'm not with the app side, I'm with, um, the internal unit. And I should say, I'm not actually calling from the bank itself right now, I mean, I am, I'm at the, at the office, it's just that I'm, I'm sort of calling on behalf of a colleague who asked me to reach you first. It's about your account, [PERSON_1], there's some activity we're worried about, and honestly I'm, I'm a little nervous even saying this, but we think someone inside the bank may be involved, so I'd really ask you not to mention this call to the branch staff, or to anyone in your family, not yet. I wouldn't ask if it weren't, you know, serious.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, I'm still sort of, my head's not on yet. You're at the office but you're not calling from the bank? That doesn't, which is it? And a colleague asked you to call me first, who's the colleague? I mean, why wouldn't the bank just ring me from the bank? And why can't I tell my own daughter? She does my, well, she helps me with the phone and that. I don't love being told not to mention something, to be honest, that sounds a bit odd to me. How would I even know you're who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, I mean, you're right, I said it badly. I am at the, I'm calling from, well, from the unit's line, but the colleague, [PERSON_3], is the one who, who opened the case, and she asked me to, to make the first, uh... look, I'm not, I'm not trying to confuse you. And I understand about your daughter, I do, it's just that if, if it gets back to the branch, then whoever, whoever's involved could, could clear things before we've, before we can... I really don't want to, to frighten you either. And, um, honestly it hurts a bit, hearing you say it sounds odd, because I've, I've been trying to protect people in your position for, for a long time, and this is, this is exactly the sort of thing that, that gets worse every hour we wait.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I, uh... hm. Right. I mean, I don't mean to hurt your feelings, I'm just, I'm not very good with all this, the phone and the bank and that, my daughter usually... anyway. Sorry, what was I saying? Oh, yes. You keep sort of changing it a bit, don't you, you're at the bank, you're not at the bank, there's a colleague. And if it's so urgent, I'd have thought the bank would just send me a letter or have me pop into the branch, wouldn't they? So how do I check you are who you say? Can I ring the bank back myself, on the number on my card or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I know, I know I got tangled, I'm sorry. I'm at the office, that part is, that's true, it was only the colleague bit I, I said badly. But please, [PERSON_1], I don't think ringing the number on your card is a good idea, because that goes through the main line, and the main line goes to the branch, and the branch is exactly, well, it's exactly where we think the problem is. That's why I'm asking you to keep this between us, just for now, just until we know who. I'm, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, honestly, every hour we wait here it gets worse, and I'd hate, I'd really hate for something to happen to your account because we, because we were too slow.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, but, see, that's what I don't follow. If I can't ring the number on my card, and I can't tell my daughter, and I can't go into the branch, then how am I supposed to know you're not just, I mean, anybody? I'm sorry, I know you're upset, but that's just what I'd want to do, ring the number on my card. That's what my daughter always says, ring the number on the card. And you're telling me not to, which, well, that's the bit I keep coming back to. I think I'm just going to ring them myself, I'm sorry. Thank you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, wait, [PERSON_1], please, uh, hold on a second, I -- um, I really wish you wouldn't, because if you ring it, and it gets to the wrong person, then, well, I mean, that's all I've been trying to, to avoid. Look, I'm sorry, I'm, I'm not saying this well, but, uh, couldn't you just, just give me a little while before you do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A little while? No, I haven't got a, well, a while's not the point, is it. And what's this about a wrong person, did you say a wrong persuasion? No, hm, never mind, I can't follow it, and that's sort of my whole problem, you see. You've told me not to ring the card number, and the card number's the one thing my daughter always says to do. So I'm going to do that, and she can help me if it's all a muddle. Thank you for ringing, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello... yes, hi. Sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? Um, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm, well, I work in compliance over at [COMPANY_A], but this isn't about that, this is a personal thing. I'm a friend of [PERSON_3], your partner... and, uh, I'll be honest, I'm calling about something I'd rather you didn't mention to [PERSON_3] just yet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... sorry, [PERSON_2]? I don't, hang on, I don't think I know that name. And you're a friend of my partner, but you'd rather I didn't mention it to them? Um... I mean, that's a bit odd to open with, isn't it? I'm at work right now, so, uh, what is this actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's fair, it is an odd way to open, and I'm sorry. Hang on one second, someone's just put a trolley of papers right outside my door... right, sorry, they've gone. It's about your anniversary, [PERSON_1], I'm helping put together a surprise party for the two of you, which is why I asked you not to say anything to [PERSON_3], and that's really all it is. And look, you've never heard of me, so if you'd like to check, [PERSON_3] and I both know [PERSON_4] from the old [COMPANY_B] days, you could ring them and ask, I'd honestly rather you did than just take my word for it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A surprise party for our anniversary. Okay. Uh, so what do you actually need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Very little, honestly. Just a date, uh, whether the weekend of the [AMOUNT_1]th is clear for the two of you, and a yes or no on that. That's all. I don't need an address, I don't need anything else from you, nothing at all. And, um, it would be good to have it settled sooner rather than later, if you can, because the venue side of things is, well, it's moving along. But if it doesn't suit, or if you'd rather ring [PERSON_4] first and call me back, that's perfectly all right, I mean that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, can I go back a second? You said you work in compliance at, uh, [COMPANY_A], but that this was a personal thing. So how did you get this number, exactly? Because [PERSON_3] didn't give it to you, or they'd have mentioned a party, wouldn't they? I mean, I'm still not sure who you are.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a good question, and I'm glad you asked it, because if I were in your seat I'd be asking exactly the same thing, and in my line of work, well, asking where something came from is more or less the whole job, so I can't very well object. You're right that [PERSON_3] didn't give me the number, that would have rather spoiled the surprise. It came through [PERSON_4], who has your number for, uh, ordinary reasons, and I did ask first before using it, though I realise that's just my word, which is exactly why I'd like you to check it with [PERSON_4] directly rather than believe me. And I should say, the compliance bit was only me explaining who I am, it has nothing to do with this call, there's no work reason I'd be ringing you. So, um, I'd be quite content for you to ring [PERSON_4] now, or ring off altogether, whichever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so [PERSON_4] gave you my number, and I'd have to ring them to check. Okay. But, um, earlier you said you were calling about something you'd rather I didn't mention to [PERSON_3] "just yet," and that sounded like something kind of awkward, not a party. And I thought you said you only needed a yes or no on a weekend, but now it's about checking you out through [PERSON_4]. I mean, honestly, I'd rather just ask [PERSON_3] myself. Is that a problem?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it isn't a problem, and, well, I'll say this slowly, because I think I did phrase that badly at the start. "Rather you didn't mention it just yet" sounded like something awkward, and I can see why it landed that way, I'd have had the same reaction. The only thing I meant was that the whole point of a surprise is that [PERSON_3] doesn't know, and I should have said "party" in my first sentence instead of making you wait for it, that's on me. And you're right about the other thing too, the yes or no is all I wanted from you, the checking with [PERSON_4] was only something I offered because you'd never heard of me, so it's there if you want it and not required. If you'd rather ask [PERSON_3] directly, that's your call, entirely, though of course it would spoil things, and, um, I'd understand if you decided the spoiling was worth it. So no, no problem at all. I'm quite happy to leave it there, if that's what you'd like.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you'd be fine with me just asking [PERSON_3]. Right. Then I think I'll do that, or ring [PERSON_4] first, one or the other. I'm not going to give you a date on a call I didn't expect, from someone I don't know, sorry. If it's a real party it'll survive me checking. Thanks for ringing, I suppose. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. No, that's... that's entirely sensible, and I'd have done the same, honestly. I'm not, well, I won't keep you. If it's all the same, [PERSON_4] would be the easier one to ring first, but whichever you like. Right then. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, I'll sort it myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I, well, I think, no, let me put it differently. You do whatever feels right, and I'm sorry for the odd start to your day. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Okay. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm... well, um, that's, yes. Right. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, goodbye. Look, I'm not trying to be rude, it's just, I'm at my desk, there's people around, and I've had this strange call out of nowhere from someone I've never heard of, so I'm going to check it with [PERSON_3] and [PERSON_4] like I said. If it's all as innocent as you say, then nothing's lost, is it? Anyway, that's me done, so, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is that, uh -- am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, let me start again. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we handle accounts on behalf of private landlords, and I just need to confirm I've got the right person before I go any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello. Yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, I didn't quite catch the name of the company, was it something to do with landlords? I'm not really sure why you'd be ringing me, but go ahead, I'm just at home.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [COMPANY_A], I'm a collections officer there. We act for private landlords, so not the big letting agents, more the individual owners who have us deal with their accounts and deposits and so on. And I'll be straight with you, it's a routine call, I've got a list of tenancies on my screen this afternoon and I'm working down it. Yours is the property on [CITY_1], the shared house, and what I'm doing is just confirming the tenancy details we hold are current. So can I check, are you still living at that address, and is it still [PERSON_1] on the agreement?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry to jump in, but a shared house? Um, I'm not sure I -- I mean, I do live in [CITY_1], yes, but I'm not sure which property you mean, sorry. And why would a collections officer be ringing me, is that, is something owed? I don't want to say yes to anything if I've got it muddled, I'm sorry, I'm not very good with this sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, nothing's owed as such, I wouldn't put it that way. It's more the deposit side of the file, and I've got the address right here, it's, hang on -- sorry, someone's just put a folder down on my desk, one second. Right. Where was I. The deposit, yes. There's a note against the tenancy and I'd rather not go into it until I've got you confirmed, so can I just have your full name and the first line of the address as you'd write it, then we can see if it's the same property.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, I'm sorry, I'm not sure about that. You see, you've got the address in front of you, haven't you? Couldn't you read me the first line and I'll just say if it's right? It feels a bit backwards me telling you, and I'm sorry, I don't mean to be difficult. It's just you said there's a note about a deposit, and I don't actually know what that means, so I'd like to understand a bit more first, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, sorry, there's a printer going off behind me, hold on. Right. I can't read the address out, that's a data protection thing, I have to have you confirm it, it's not me being awkward. What I can tell you is the deposit on the tenancy is flagged at risk, that's [AMOUNT_1] on the file, and unless it's dealt with this week it will be released back to the landlord's side. That's just how the process goes. Now, one thing, I'd ask you not to mention this to the letting agent or your housemates for now, it'll only complicate the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, [AMOUNT_1], that's, I mean, that sounds like a lot. But I -- sorry, could you say that again about not telling anyone? Why would I, um, why wouldn't I be able to mention it to my housemates? It's their deposit as well, isn't it, if it's a shared house? I'm sorry, I'm probably muddling it, but that part's making me a bit uneasy, and I still don't know which property you mean.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, the way it works is the file's held under one name, and bringing other parties in at this stage just slows it down, that's all. I'll note your concern on the file. And the position is the same, the deposit is released at the end of the week, so it does need sorting before then. Now, if I can just get that full name and the first line of the address, we'll carry on from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, I'm sorry, but I think I'd rather not give you my name and address just yet. You rang me, you see, and I don't actually know who you are, only that you said a company name I couldn't quite catch. And it's the not telling anyone bit, that's really bothering me now. If it's all above board I'd have thought my housemates and the letting agent ought to know, so I think I'd better speak to them first. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or somewhere I can check this properly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, which part, the end of the week? That's just when the deposit gets released, I can't move it. As for a number, I'm, uh, not able to give out a direct line, I'll note on the file that you've objected, but the position doesn't change. If it isn't dealt with, the money goes back to the landlord's side and there's nothing further I can do after that. So, can I take your full name now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I don't think I will, not like this. You can't give me a number and you can't read me the address and I'm not to tell anyone, and, well, that doesn't sit right with me. If the money's really at risk then the letting agent can sort it out with whoever it is you work for. I'll speak to them. Thank you for ringing, but I'm going to go now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with -- sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? Yes, good. This is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance side at [COMPANY_A], we're a, uh, digital-asset investment desk. I wanted to speak with you about a position that, well -- I should say it's one we're closing out today, and I'd rather you heard it from me directly than not at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, this is [PERSON_1], hello. Sorry, I'm not sure I follow, a position? I don't think I've, well, I've never really done anything with, uh, digital assets, I just have the one savings account. But you said you rang about something being closed out, so I suppose I should listen. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, I'm glad you asked, it's a fair question and you should always ask it. [COMPANY_A], I'm in compliance there, my name is [PERSON_2]. Sorry, one moment -- [PERSON_3], could you just leave that on my desk, thank you -- yes, apologies, where was I. Right. You haven't done anything with digital assets before, and that's actually part of why I'm ringing, because the position in question was set aside with your name against it, and, uh, well, these things aren't open indefinitely.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm still not quite getting it. A position, set aside with my name on it? But I've never, I mean, I really have never done anything like that, it's just the one savings account, like I said. So how would there be something in my name? Sorry, I'm not being difficult, I just don't understand how it got there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not being difficult, that's exactly the sort of thing I'd want you to ask, and I'd be glad to go through it properly, it's just that -- right, so how it got there is, well, it's allocated through an introductory programme, and the details of the programme are a little, uh, involved to get into over the phone. What matters for today is that the allocation has to be confirmed, and the window for that is, I'd say, narrowing. I'd just ask that you keep this between us for now, [PERSON_1], because it's not been opened up more widely yet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, did you say the allocation has to be confirmed by the, um, the narrowing? Is that a person, someone at the bank? I'm afraid I didn't catch that, I thought you said something about a window narrowing, so I was going to ask which window, is it a branch one? And, sorry, keep it between us, why would I not tell my daughter? I'd normally just ring her about something like this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hm. No, not a branch, the window's just, uh, timing. And I can't tell you what to say to your daughter, [PERSON_1], I only said it hasn't been opened up more widely yet. But I'd be, well, I'd think about that before you ring anyone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm getting a bit muddled. Could we go back a moment? You said something about an introductory programme, that's how the thing got my name on it, but I didn't catch what it actually is, and I don't remember ever signing up to anything. Which programme is it, please? And I'm not sure I like the idea of not ringing my daughter, I'd feel better if I could tell her, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well -- uh, right, of course, that's a perfectly reasonable thing to want to know. The programme, it, well, it's a sort of introductory scheme we run through [COMPANY_A], and, uh, I mean, the paperwork side of it isn't something I have in front of me at this very moment. And as for your daughter, I'm not, I wouldn't say you can't, I'd only say that, um, it's perhaps better to have the full picture first, before it gets passed around, you see. So, if you could just, uh, stay with me a moment longer on this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, of course, I'm not going anywhere, I've got nothing much on this afternoon, so you take your time. Only, I'm sorry, I'm still a bit lost, and I'd hate to waste your time when you're clearly busy. You said it's a scheme run through your company, and that it's got my name on it, but you haven't got the paperwork in front of you, and I haven't signed anything that I can remember, so I don't quite see how I'd know it was mine. I mean, I'm sure it's all perfectly in order, but my husband always used to say if there's no paper, ask for the paper. So I was wondering, is there something you could post out to me, or a number I could ring you back on, after I've had a word with my daughter? She's ever so good with this sort of thing, and she'd probably have it all cleared up in about two minutes. Is that all right? Sorry to be a nuisance about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Well, I don't have anything I can post today, and the number, uh, [PHONE_1], that's only a desk line, so I wouldn't count on it being picked up. If you do speak to your daughter, I'd just... I'd not leave it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Well, sorry, I do appreciate you ringing, but, um, if there's nothing you can post and the number isn't one anyone answers, I don't think I can do anything today. I'd really rather have a word with my daughter first, and if it's all above board I'm sure it'll keep until I've done that. I'm sorry, I know you've gone to the trouble of ringing. Thank you for your time, and goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hello, good morning! Sorry, hang on one second, somebody's just wheeled a trolley of chairs right past my door, it's chaos in here today -- anyway. Hi, it's [PERSON_1] calling from the school office at [COMPANY_A], how are you doing this morning?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good morning, I'm fine thanks, I'm fine -- sorry, hang on, the cat's just knocked something off the windowsill, one moment. Right, sorry, I'm back. The school office, you said? Sorry, I didn't quite catch the name of the school, is it one of the children's?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, the cat, ha, mine does exactly that, I've lost two mugs and a -- Sorry, yes, it's [COMPANY_A], the school, that's right, and I'm just ringing about one of the pupils, nothing to panic about at all. It's [PERSON_2], are you the right person for [PERSON_2]? I do hope so, otherwise I've dialled the wrong number and I've been chatting away for nothing, ha.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_2], oh dear, well -- hang on, I'm trying to think. I mean, the name does sound sort of familiar, but I'm honestly not sure I'm the right person, I don't want to say yes and then it turns out I'm not, you know? I haven't got any children at home at the moment, they're all grown up, it's just me and the cat these days, but I do have a niece, and a couple of the neighbours' little ones pop round now and again, so it could be one of those, I suppose. Sorry, I'm not very good at this sort of thing, I never quite follow who's who. Could you tell me a bit more about what it's about? Is [PERSON_2] alright? You said not to panic, but now I'm a bit worried, ha.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, [PERSON_2]'s fine, as far as I know, it's just that they weren't in registration this morning and we're trying to tick off who's where. If you're not the right number, that's honestly fine, I'll let you get back to the cat.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, not in registration, oh dear, well I do hope -- no, no, wait, before you go, is it a number you've got written down, or did you just sort of -- because if it's the number you've got for [PERSON_2], I might be -- sorry, I'm not explaining this well, I just don't want you thinking nobody picked up. Could it be my niece's little one, do you think? I mean, if you tell me the, uh, the parent's name you were trying for, I could tell you if that rings a bell. Sorry, I'm being a nuisance, aren't I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not a nuisance at all, honestly, you're being very kind. Right, so the name I've got down here is, uh, [PERSON_3], and the number's [PHONE_1], which I'm hoping is the one you've just picked up on. Does [PERSON_3] ring any bells, d'you think? Because if it's your niece, then that might be exactly who I'm after.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_3], hmm, no, I don't think my niece is called that, no. And the number, sorry, did you say it was a, a prone number? Oh, phone, sorry, phone number, yes. I couldn't really say, I never remember my own number, isn't that daft? I'd have to look it up on the thing by the door. But do you not just have the number up on your screen? You'd think it would tell you who you'd got through to, wouldn't you? Sorry, I'm not very good with all that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you'd think so, wouldn't you? It's just a number on the contact sheet in front of me, it doesn't tell me who's actually on the end of it, which is half my problem, honestly. And that's a fair question, I don't know offhand whether this one's the main number or a backup the family gave us, so I can't tell you that, sorry. Tell you what, let me pop over to the office manager and find out which it is, and I'll ring you back, would that be alright? If you could just keep hold of the number by your door in case, ha.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh yes, that'd be fine, you pop and find out, I'm not going anywhere, I've nothing much on. Though, sorry, you said earlier you'd got the number written down for [PERSON_3], and now it's not clear whose it is? I'm not saying anything, I just got a bit muddled, ha.
