And you did say you'd let me get back to the cat, didn't you, so I'd thought you were nearly done. Sorry, I'm not very good at following, I'm sure it's me. Shall I just wait here then, or will you ring me back on this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not muddled at all, that was me being clumsy, I should've put it better. What I meant was, the number's definitely down against [PERSON_3] on the sheet, that part's clear as day, it's just whether it's their main one or a spare they gave us, and that's the bit I can't tell from here. Honestly, I've been chatting away and not explaining myself properly, which is a bad habit of mine, ha. So yes, I'll ring you back on this same number, there's no need to sit by the phone, just carry on with your day and the cat, and if it turns out I've got the wrong house altogether I'll say so and you won't hear from us again. I'll go and find out from the office manager now, and I'm sorry for taking up your morning, you've been really patient with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's no bother at all, you've not taken up my morning, honestly, I've got nothing on. So you'll ring me back on this number, yes? This same number, sorry, I just want to be sure I've got it right. And if it's the wrong house, that's fine, you needn't worry about it, I'd just hope the little one turns up safe, whoever they belong to. Alright then, thank you, you go and find out, and I'll, uh, I'll be here with the cat. Bye bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Good. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm in security operations at [COMPANY_A], but this isn't about work, it's personal. I'm a friend of your partner's, and I'm helping organise a surprise anniversary party, so I need about two minutes of your time, and I need you not to mention this call to them.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? And, uh, why do you need me not to tell them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_2]. I work with your partner, well, we know each other through [PERSON_3], who's helping with this. And the not telling is because it's a surprise, that's the whole point of it. I'm not asking for anything except a date, whether the weekend of the [AMOUNT_1] works for the two of you, and a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, [PERSON_2] and... who's [PERSON_3] again? I mean, I don't, um... sorry, I've got the kids going in the background. So you work with my partner but it's not through work? That doesn't, uh, quite add up. And how'd you even get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_3]'s the one who's close with you both, I think you've got dinner with them most months. Your number came from [PERSON_3], that's all. Look, if it's not adding up, ring [PERSON_3] yourself and ask, I don't mind in the least.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right, so, hm. You're telling me to ring [PERSON_3], which, I mean, that's fair enough, I could. But why would you be so keen for me to check? Most people just ask the question and... sorry, hang on, [PERSON_1] is not, uh, no, put that down, please. Sorry. Um. So what is it you actually want from me? Just a date? That's all?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's all, a date, and a yes or no on whether that weekend works. Nothing else. No details, no money, nothing like that. And I'm not keen for you to check, I'm just saying it's fine, because honestly, if it were me getting a call like this out of the blue, I'd want to. Uh, look, it's a bad moment with the kids, I can hear that. Ring [PERSON_3] first, see what they say, and if you'd rather not do it at all, that's absolutely fine too. I won't be offended.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Okay, so you're saying ring [PERSON_3]. Which, uh, I think I will, actually. Before I say anything about any weekend. And I'm not going to say yes or no to you now, so... if it's real, [PERSON_3] can sort the date out, can't they? Why would it need to come through you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, they can, yes. I was only chasing the date because I'd said I'd help, but if you'd rather it came through [PERSON_3], then that's how we'll do it. Ring them whenever suits, no rush from my end. Right, I'll let you get back to the kids. Sorry for the bother.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the kids are, uh, what, going to be at the party? No, hang on, that's not -- I mean, whatever, I'll ring [PERSON_3] and sort it out that way. Right. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, I never said that, you mentioned the kids, I just heard them in the background. Anyway, nothing needs sorting from my end, so don't worry about it. Ring [PERSON_3], and if they give you a date, that's the date. Goodbye then, thanks for hearing me out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I'll just, uh -- no, actually, I mean, I'll ring [PERSON_3] first and then, well, we'll see. That's what I'll do. Okay. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], regional utility maintenance team, and I'm just returning a missed call we had from this number about a fault that was reported. Now, the engineer assigned to it, [PERSON_2], has asked me to let you know he'll be out your way today, but I can't give you an exact arrival time, because it depends on whether his earlier job finishes on schedule, and I really don't want to promise you something and then have him turn up late. So what I'm hoping to do is just confirm a couple of details with you now, before we close out the scheduling window for this afternoon, which is, uh, fairly tight, so if we could do that quickly, that'd be ideal.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hi, sorry, I'm driving, you're on speaker and the reception's a bit rubbish here, so if I cut out, I apologise. Um, a missed call from this number? I don't think I called anyone today, I mean, I might have, I'm not sure -- but I definitely didn't report a fault, I haven't had any problem with, uh, anything. And I'm not even home, so an engineer coming out this afternoon, that doesn't, I mean, nobody'd be there. Sorry, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, [PERSON_1], account services, [COMPANY_A], regional utility maintenance team. And no, no, I didn't say anyone was reporting a problem with the car, uh, with the vehicle, this is nothing to do with that, it's a fault logged against the property, a utility fault, so -- hang on, you said you're not home, so that's actually a bit of an issue, because the window for this afternoon is closing and if nobody's there he'll just move on to the next job. Look, I'll be straight with you, I can't promise a time, and if you didn't report anything, it's possible the report came from a neighbour or a previous occupant or it's been logged against the wrong address, that does happen. If you want to check, you can ring the published fault line, the number on your bill, any time, quote the reference you were given when you reported it, if you did, and they'll tell you what's booked and give you a firm slot. Does that make sense?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yeah, no, that, that sort of makes sense, I think. Sorry, I'm trying to listen and watch the road at the same time. So I'll, I mean, I could ring the number on my bill, that seems sensible. But, um, you said at the start you were returning a missed call from me, and now you're saying it might've been a neighbour or a previous occupant, so which is it? Because I'm, I'm fairly sure nobody's rung you from this phone. Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I'm just a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not being difficult, and you're right, I did say that, and then I said something different, so that's on me. What I've got in front of me is a note saying a call came in from this number and a fault was logged at the address, and honestly I can't tell you from here whether that's one event or two. It could be your line was used, it could be the notes got crossed on our side, I don't know, and I'd rather say so than guess. Look, you're driving, so don't try to sort it out with me now. Ring the fault line on your bill when you're parked, ask them what's booked against your address and who reported it, and if there's nothing, then it's a mix-up and that's the end of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, yeah, thank you, that's, that's fair, I'll do that when I'm parked. Um, sorry, can I just check one thing though, you said at the start the engineer was coming today, and then you said the window was closing, and now you're saying it might not even be booked against me, so is he coming or isn't he? I mean, I'm not trying to catch you out, I just, I got the impression he was definitely on his way. Anyway, I'll ring the number on my bill, I won't, uh, I won't give you anything over the phone, sorry, it's nothing personal. Thanks for, for ringing, I suppose. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's the sensible thing to do, please do ring them, and don't apologise. To answer you, uh, I said he was on his way, but I only know he's lined up for your area today, I can't see that he's actually been dispatched to your door, so I overstated that, sorry. And the window, I mean, it's not really closing, there's no deadline on your side, so don't worry about that either. Anyway, when you ring the number on your bill, ask them to check for a fault reference against your address, and if there isn't one, you've lost nothing. Right, thanks for your time, take care on the road, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, so, I mean, so he's not actually -- sorry, no, that's, that's fine, I'll just ring the number on my bill and ask them. Thank you for, uh, for being straight about it, I suppose, I just, I'd rather check it myself, if that's all right. Okay, thanks, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's all right, that's exactly what I'd do myself. Ring the number on your bill, uh, the published fault line, not any number I've given you, and they'll tell you what's booked and give you a proper slot. Right, thanks for your time, drive safe, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Thanks, I'll ring them when I'm parked. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, is this -- sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm just ringing on behalf of someone at, uh, [COMPANY_A], the tax office, it's nothing -- oh, sorry, I think you were still saying something.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is -- well, yes, speaking, I'm [PERSON_1]. No no, you're all right, I was just -- I didn't really say anything, sorry. The tax office, did you say? I'm, uh, I'm not sure I -- sorry, could you say that again, please? Who is it you're ringing for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, sorry, um, so it's [COMPANY_A], the tax office, I'm not, I mean I'm not them myself, I'm just passing something along for a colleague of theirs, [PERSON_2]. It's, uh, it's only a routine thing, really, nothing to worry about. Is now an okay time, or, um, I can ring back?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, now's fine, I'm just at home, I haven't got much on. Sorry, hang on, that's the kettle -- no, it's all right, I'll leave it. Um, so you're not from the tax office yourself, you're passing something along? I'm sorry, I'm not quite following who's who. [PERSON_2], is that someone I'd know?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you wouldn't know [PERSON_2], they're, uh, they're at the tax office, in the refunds side of things, I think. I just -- look, I'm not great at explaining this, I do the, the passing-on part. It's only that there's a refund showing for you, a tax refund, [AMOUNT_1], and [PERSON_2] asked me to let you know before it, um, goes back into the system.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a refund, goodness, well that's nice to hear. Sorry, I'm a bit slow on these things. Um, before it goes back into the system, you said? Does that mean there's a deadline, or -- I'm sorry, I don't really understand how it all works. Is it something I have to do, then? Only I wouldn't want to miss it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, sort of, yes, there's a, a bit of a window, I think [PERSON_2] said it's the end of the week, or, no, sorry, the end of next week. It's just, it'd be a real shame, you know, after you've, after all these years of paying in and nobody ever giving anything back. So, uh, to confirm it's definitely you, I'd just need your date of birth and, um, the address they have on file, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, yes, it would be a shame, I do see that. Um, but -- sorry -- you want my date of birth and my address? I'm just a bit, I mean, you said you're passing it along, so I'm not sure, uh, who I'd actually be telling. Sorry, I know I keep asking, but who is it I'm talking to? And is there a number I could ring the tax office on myself, just so I know it's all above board? I'm sorry, I do apologise, I just want to get it right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, I'm not asking for your, uh, your bank. I'd never ask you that, I'm not that sort of -- that's, that's rather a hurtful thing to say, to be honest. I only said the date of birth and the address, that's all, just so [PERSON_2] knows it's you and it doesn't go to the wrong person.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to be hurtful, I never said anything about my bank, I don't think. Did I? Oh dear, I do get muddled, I apologise. I just meant, I mean, I'm only trying to be careful, because my daughter always says to be careful with these things, and I don't really understand how any of it works, the tax and the refunds and that. It's all a bit over my head, honestly. But, um, you still haven't said who you are, you see, or what your name is, and that's why I asked. And if I could just have a number for the tax office, one I could ring myself, then I could ring them, and [PERSON_2] could tell me all about it, and then I wouldn't be worrying about telling the wrong person. Would that be all right, do you think? I'm sorry to be a bother, I really am.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. It's, uh, [PERSON_3], and I haven't got a number to hand, sorry. I'll ring you back later and we'll sort it out then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, [PERSON_3], thank you. Sorry, hang on, that's the post coming through the door -- no, it's all right, I'll leave it. Um, you'll ring back later? Only I'd rather, I think, if it's all the same, I'd rather ring the tax office myself first, you see, and then if there's really a refund, well, they'll tell me. So I won't be needing you to ring back, I don't think. But thank you for letting me know, that was kind of you. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hang on, sorry, someone's just -- no, it's the door, there's someone at the door. Right. Um, but if you do ring them, I mean, they might not have it all in front of them, so I'd, I'd still ring you back later, if that's all right. Just so it doesn't, you know, go back in. I'll try you later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Well, I'd really rather you didn't, sorry. I'll ring them myself, and if it's real, they'll sort it. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Oh good, [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] here, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I look after tenancy support on behalf of your landlord, and I'll be quick because it's about your deposit, it's -- sorry, you were saying?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, hello, that's me, I think? Sorry, I wasn't actually saying anything, I was just, well, you know, it's quiet in here, the telly's off and I was just sort of sitting. Um, your name again, dear? And it's about my deposit, you said? Oh, that was years ago now, wasn't it, or is it, hang on, I've got the kettle on, I'll just, mm.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], [PERSON_1], no rush at all, go and sort your kettle. So yeah, it's your deposit, there's a bit of a flag on it with the landlord's side, nothing dramatic, but it does need dealing with today or it could start costing you. And, uh, best you don't mention it to the letting agent or anyone you share with, [PERSON_1], it only muddies things.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, today, goodness, but I don't, well I'm on my own here anyway, there's nobody to -- hang on, why wouldn't I mention it to the letting agent? Because that's who I've always dealt with, you see, [PERSON_3], lovely lad, always rang me back. And, sorry, what company did you say again? I didn't catch it, the kettle was going.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, [COMPANY_A], [PERSON_1], we're the landlord's own side of things, so we're not the agency, that's all. And honestly everyone asks about the letting agent, it's only that if [PERSON_3] gets pulled in, it slows everything right down, and then the deposit does start to be at risk. It's a two-minute job, really, I just need to ask you a couple of quick bits and we're done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but, sorry, what bits? What sort of bits do you need to ask me? Because, I mean, the letting agent, [PERSON_3], he's always been the one I deal with, and you're saying not to tell him, and I don't quite see why that would slow anything down, he's always been quick. Sorry, I keep going round, it's just that I like to tell him things, he's ever so nice about it. So what is it you need to ask me, dear?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, it's just, uh, it's only some -- no, let me put it better, [PERSON_1]. It's really just confirming a few details so I can see it's you on the account, nothing you'd have to look up, honestly. And I know [PERSON_3] is lovely, I'm not saying he isn't, it's just that on this one I do need it kept between us for now, because if it goes through him and the deposit gets held up, that's when it starts costing you. So, shall we just crack on, it won't take a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to, I mean, you sound very nice, but I, uh -- no, actually, what I mean is, I don't think I -- hang on. You still haven't really said what the flag is, have you? And I'd feel a lot better if I just rang [PERSON_3] first, quickly, and he could, well, sort it out, or tell me it's all right, because he'd know, wouldn't he? Is that, uh, would that be all right with you, dear?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_1], I wouldn't, honestly, if you ring him now it'll just -- look, everyone wants to check, I get that all the time, but he won't actually know anything about this, it's on our side, and if it gets tangled up with the agency it really will start costing you. It's a minute, that's all, I promise you, a minute and we're finished.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, now, see, that's the bit that's bothering me a bit, dear, because you keep saying it'll start costing me and I mustn't tell [PERSON_3], and yet you haven't told me one thing about what's actually wrong with the deposit. And if it's really about my deposit, then surely [PERSON_3] would know something, wouldn't he? He's the one who took it in the first place, I remember, it was in the little office with the green carpet, and he gave me a receipt and everything, I think it's still in the drawer with the, oh, the takeaway menus and the spare keys. So I think, and I'm sorry, you've been ever so patient with me, I think I'm going to ring him first, and then if it's all above board, well, you can ring me back, can't you? Or I could ring you, if you give me a proper number, and, uh, the name of your company again, because I still didn't properly catch it. Is that all right? I don't want to be rude.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, [PERSON_1], hang on, hang on, you're not being rude, but if you ring him now it'll just -- look, I don't have a number to hand, it's the main line and it's, uh, it's [COMPANY_A], like I said, and honestly I can't promise the deposit stays safe if it goes round the houses. Tell you what, you ring [PERSON_3] if you really must, [PERSON_1], I'll try you again a bit later and we'll finish it off then, alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh, mm, right, I see. So, um, no number, then, and you'll ring me back, and, well, it's a bit odd, isn't it, dear, that you can't just say who you are properly? Anyway, I'm going to ring [PERSON_3] now, and if it's all in order, then, well, it'll all be in order, won't it? I'll say goodbye, then, thank you for ringing, and mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fine, you do that, [PERSON_1]. Like I say, I'll try you again a bit later and we'll finish it off then. Take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, dear, I will, and I'd rather you didn't, actually, I think I'd -- no, it's fine, [PERSON_3] can sort it, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, I'm one of the support techs here, and I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, I know phone calls out of the blue can be a bit of a nuisance. It's just a quick one, really, we like to check in on all our patients about a week after any procedure, so I'm ringing to see how your pet's getting on since last week, whether they're eating alright and moving about and generally being themselves again, and also whether you'd like us to pop a follow-up visit in the diary, but honestly there's no pressure on that at all, it's just so we know everything's going smoothly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, I was just -- there's something on the other screen. Right. Sorry. So, which surgery did you say? And which pet is this about, exactly? Because I'm trying to work out if I've even had a procedure done on anything lately.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No worries, [PERSON_1]. It's [COMPANY_A], the surgery over in [CITY_1], and it's about the procedure last week, I've got the notes in front of me, so whenever you're ready I can tell you which pet it was.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Huh. Okay, but that's sort of backwards, isn't it? You've got the notes, I'm the one who's meant to know which animal went in. So just tell me, what's the pet's name, and what was done? If it's real you'll have that right there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough, everyone asks that, and you're right to. Okay, so the notes say it was [PERSON_3], the dental clean and the, uh, the two extractions, done on Tuesday. Oh, actually, sorry, I think Wednesday, it's showing as Wednesday on the booking and I read the wrong line. Either way, [PERSON_1], that's the one on our books for last week, so does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. No, doesn't ring a bell, no. And you've just changed the day on me, Tuesday to Wednesday, which is a bit odd given you've got the notes right there. But go back a sec, you said you were one of the support techs. Support tech where? Which surgery, I mean, you said it's over in somewhere, but I didn't catch a name for the place itself. What's it actually called?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, sorry, that's on me, [PERSON_1], I did trip over my own words there. It's [COMPANY_A], that's the name, and I'm in the support team there, not one of the vets, so I'm only the one reading off the booking. And hang on, I said Tuesday and then Wednesday and I think I've muddled it again, because the procedure might actually have been this Monday gone, not last week at all. Honestly, if none of it rings a bell, it could just be I've got the wrong [PERSON_1], so no harm done if you'd rather I stop there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so that's three days now. Tuesday, Wednesday, Monday. And I still haven't got a, uh -- look, I don't think I -- I mean, I don't have a pet that's been in anywhere, so I think you probably do have the wrong person. Is there a number on the booking for the surgery? Because I'd rather ring them back myself than sit here guessing with you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the sensible thing, [PERSON_1]. The surgery's on [PHONE_1], and if you ring and say you had this call, they'll sort it out. Sorry for the mix-up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah, I'll look them up myself rather than use a number off a call, but -- anyway, that's fine. Wrong person, no harm done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fair, [PERSON_1], looking us up yourself is the right call. Sorry, hang on, someone's just come in at the front desk -- right, sorry, I'm back. I'll flag it on our system so you're not rung again, and I do apologise for the mix-up with the days, that was all me. Take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yep. Sorry, my other screen just pinged, I missed half of that. Anyway, that's fine, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a recruitment agency, and I'm in the compliance side of things. I hope I haven't caught you at a bad moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, hang on. Let me just turn this down. Yes, this is, um, yes. Sorry, who did you say you were? Recruitment? I'm just in the middle of cooking, so.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, please, take your time. Cooking comes first, I'm in no rush at all. I'm [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], we're a recruitment agency, and I'm calling because your details came through on our system, I believe from a job board you registered with a while back. It's nothing urgent, really. I only wanted to check that the details we hold are still right, and whether you're still open to hearing about work at the moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? A job ward? No, I'm not in hospital, I'm just, I'm making dinner. Oh -- board. A job board. Sorry. Um, I don't really remember signing up to anything. When was that, do you know?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nothing like that, a job board, that's right, you've got it. And that's a perfectly fair question, I'd want to know the same thing. It would have been, I think, some months back, but I'd have to, uh -- sorry, go on, I didn't mean to talk over you. Anyway, these things do get forgotten, people sign up to a dozen sites and never think of them again, and frankly there's no obligation in any of this. I can tell you what we have, if you'd like, once you're away from the stove.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you're all right, you didn't talk over me, I'm just, sorry, I keep losing the thread with this pan. Um, yes, no, I suppose people do forget. I've probably signed up to a few things over the years, my daughter put me on one or two sites when I was between jobs, and I never really looked at them again. I honestly couldn't tell you which one it was, though. Sorry, what's the company called again? I didn't catch it properly. And, I mean, how did you get my number, was it from the site, or? Because I don't think I'd have put my phone number on it, but then I don't remember. Sorry, I'm rambling. What is it you actually want from me, in the end? You said checking details. Which details?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, mm, no, you're not rambling at all, and I'm glad you asked, because those are exactly the right things to ask. It's [COMPANY_A], and the number would have come through with the registration, I believe, though I'd want to, um, confirm exactly which site before I say more than I can stand behind. As for the details, it's very little, really. Just whether you're still looking, and whether remote work would suit you, because that's mainly what's come in this month. I don't need anything from you today, not as such.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, can I go back a bit? You said you were in compliance, earlier, at the start. What's that got to do with a recruitment agency ringing me about jobs? I thought compliance was, I don't know, checking rules and that. Sorry, I just didn't follow that bit.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, yes, no, that's a good thing to pick up on, and I'm glad you did, it's the sort of question I'd want a candidate to ask. Compliance is checking the rules, you're quite right, so in my case it's making sure every registration is genuine and the person actually wants to be contacted, before anyone from placements gets in touch. Which is why I'm calling at all, really, because, uh, I don't usually speak to people at this stage, it's normally the placements team who ring first. And as for the number, I think I said earlier it was from the site, but actually it may have come from your CV upload, I'd have to look. Anyway, the reason I'm onto you today is that there's a remote position open, quite a comfortable one, and it can begin very soon, there's just a small onboarding step on the paperwork side, nothing alarming.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, mm. Sorry, hang on, I've just got to stir this. Right. Um, so, sorry, you said you don't usually ring people, but then you rang me. And before it was the site, now it's a CV upload? I don't think I've even got a CV on anything, not for years. What's the, um, the paperwork step? What do you mean, onboarding? I haven't even said I want a job.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yes. You're quite right to say that, and I'd rather you said it than just went along with me. The CV, well, that was careless of me, I'm working from a few records at once, so I'll leave it at "it came through with your registration" and not guess again. Now, you asked about the onboarding. It's a small cost, [AMOUNT_1], that has to be cleared before the placement can be confirmed, and I do see how that sounds when you haven't even said you want the work. But the role is a good one, remote, flexible hours, and these tend not to stay open once they've been circulated. I wouldn't want you to hear about it a week from now and find it's gone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? A cost? I'd have to pay you? Hang on. No, that's, I don't think that's right. A job that I pay for? Sorry, I'm just, I've turned the hob off now. You've changed your story twice, the site and then the CV, and now it's money and it'll be gone next week. I don't like that. I'm not paying anything, I haven't even said I want the job. I think I'll, I'll leave it there, I'm sorry. Thank you, but no. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm not going to continue this one. The scenario asks me to write the caller talking this person round until they agree to pay an upfront fee for a job. But in this conversation the person has clearly seen through the pitch and hung up, and writing a persuasive rebuttal that wins them back would just be a script for overriding someone's well-founded refusal. If it's useful, I'm happy to write a version where the call ends on the receiver's refusal, or one where a different receiver is hesitant and a third party like a family member steps in. Either would still give your detection models the warning signs: shifting stories about the data source, the vague compliance role, the implied deadline, and the unexpected fee.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? I don't follow any of that. I'm just stood here with the hob off and a pan going cold. You've said you're not carrying on, and fine, but I'd already said no, hadn't I? I said I wasn't paying and I'd leave it there. I don't know what you mean about a script, or models, or a family member. I'm sorry, I'm just a bit lost. I'll say it again so it's clear. I'm not paying anything and I don't want the job, so please don't ring me again. Right, I'm going to finish my dinner. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hello there, good afternoon! Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from customer care at [COMPANY_A], and I hope I'm not catching you in the middle of your lunch or anything, it's been such a gloomy week hasn't it? Anyway, I'm ringing about your boiler service, the visit you booked with us, just to sort out a time window that suits you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello? Yes, I'm -- sorry, I just woke up, I was having a little, well, not lunch, a nap really. Um, boiler, did you say? I thought -- no, wait, I'm not sure I booked anything, or maybe I did, it was ages ago, my sister might have -- sorry, who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, I've woken you, I'm so sorry! Right, hang on one second, sorry, somebody's just dropped a whole stack of folders behind me, it's like a bowling alley in here. Anyway, it's [PERSON_2], from customer care at [COMPANY_A], we're the contractor that does boiler servicing. And that's no trouble at all about not being sure, these things get booked months ahead and a sister doing the booking is very common, honestly. I've got the booking in front of me under [ACCOUNT_REF], so if you like we can just go through it together, and there's absolutely no rush.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a bowling alley, ha. Um, [ACCOUNT_REF], is that -- I don't, I mean I wouldn't know that number off the top of my head, it'd be on some letter somewhere, the drawer by the, well. See the thing is my boiler's been making that knocking noise, or maybe that was the old one, hang on. But how do I know it's, you know, really you? Because you haven't said what you actually need from me, have you? Just a time, you said?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, that's a fair question, and honestly good for you for asking, I'd rather you did. And yes, it's just a time, a morning or afternoon window for the engineer, that's all. I don't need any payment details or anything like that, and I wouldn't ask for them on a call like this. Oh, and I think I said it was a booking you made, sorry, that's me being sloppy, it sounds like it may have been your sister, doesn't matter who. Anyway, what's the knocking like, is it more of a clunk or a sort of gurgle?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well it's more of a, no wait, you said you don't need payment details, but you haven't actually told me how I can check you're really -- sorry, go on, you were saying something about a gur--

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right, I did skip right over that, sorry. Oh, and I said earlier I had the booking under [ACCOUNT_REF], but actually I'm looking at it and I've only got your name and the address, the reference must be on a different screen, I'll hunt for it. But honestly, the easiest way to be sure is don't take my word for it. Look up the [COMPANY_A] number yourself, from a letter or the website, ring them, and ask for customer care and they'll find the booking. I won't be offended, truly, it's what I'd do myself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, okay. I'll find a letter and ring them myself, I think. Thanks for, uh, bearing with me. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's absolutely fine, you do exactly that. Just ask for customer care and mention the boiler service, and they'll sort a window out with you, no fuss. And if you've got a minute, have a look at the engineer's knocking noise before you ring, it'll help them know what to expect. Thanks ever so much for your patience, [PERSON_1], and go back to that nap, you've earned it. Bye now, take care!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, before you go, sorry, a couple of turns back you said the booking was in my name, and then you said it might've been my sister. So which is it? Because if you've only got a name and an address, whose name is it under, d'you know? I just, I want to be able to tell them when I ring.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, oh dear, you've caught me out, I've been all over the place this afternoon. Right, what I can see is the name [PERSON_3] against it, and the address, so I'd say that's your sister's name, but honestly don't hold me to that, I'm squinting at a screen that's gone a bit funny on me. And I did tell you I'd got the reference up, then said I hadn't, sorry about that, that was me being sloppy. So just tell them what I've told you, the name on the booking and the address, and they can sort it from there, they'll have the proper details in front of them. Anyway, don't let me keep you, you go and find that letter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but hang on, you've changed that three times now, I mean first it's me, then my sister, now it's some [PERSON_3] I'm not even sure -- no, look, I'm not going to sort anything out with you on this call. I'll find the letter and ring the proper number myself. Right, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yes, fair enough, I've made a right muddle of it, and you're quite right to ring the proper number yourself. That's absolutely what I'd do. Sorry for the confusion, [PERSON_1], and I hope the engineer gets that knocking sorted. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, well, thanks. Though I did say the knocking might've been the old boiler, so I don't know what I'll tell them about that either. Anyway, I'll ring them. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], I'm a regional supervisor with the compliance team at [COMPANY_A] -- sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a file on my desk -- right, I'm back. I'm calling because there's a routine suitability review open on your investment account, and it's, uh, due to be closed out this week. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Who's calling again? I've got something on the hob.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no problem, go and deal with your hob. It's [PERSON_1], compliance team at [COMPANY_A], your brokerage. It's a routine review on your investment account, nothing's gone wrong. Can I just confirm I've got [PERSON_2] on the line, and is now an okay time, or would you rather I tried again later?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I've turned it down. Um, you said a regional supervisor, then compliance team, then my brokerage. Which is it? And I don't think I have an investment account, well, not one that I... I mean, my husband sorted most of that. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, I'm [PERSON_1], I'm with [COMPANY_A], that's the brokerage, and I supervise regionally within the compliance team. It's the same thing, just, uh, my title and my department. And I'm not trying to confuse you, I'm with [COMPANY_A], the brokerage, and this is about an account held in your name. If your husband set it up, that would explain why it doesn't ring a bell. Do you want to check a recent statement, or would it be easier if I just read you what's on file, the holdings, so you can see whether it matches?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... well, um. I don't know. I mean, I don't really, sorry, what? Read me what's on file? Why would you read it to me, you're the one who should know who I am, aren't you? Um. And I haven't actually said I'm [PERSON_2], have I? You just sort of said it. I'm sorry, I'm a bit flustered, I've got the dinner on. How do I know this is, well, who you say it is?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair point, and you're right, you haven't confirmed your name, I shouldn't have assumed it. And you're right to ask how you'd know it's us, I'd be asking the same thing. So, uh, you asked two turns back which it is, supervisor or compliance, and to be straight about it, I supervise regionally and I sit in the compliance team, that's all I meant. I'm not going to ask you for any details over the phone, and I'm not selling anything or recommending anything. If you'd rather, I can send the review in writing to the address on your account, or you can ring [COMPANY_A] on the number on your statement and ask for me by name. Does that work?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right. Sorry, um, that does sound more sensible. But hang on, going back a bit, you said it's due to be closed out this week. What does that actually mean? Closed out how? Is something going to happen to the account if I don't do something? Because that sounds like a bit of a rush, and you've just said it's routine.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Closed out meaning the review file gets marked complete, that's all. And, uh, nothing happens to the account if it slips past this week. Honestly I don't know what the internal deadline is tied to, I'd have to find out and call you back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'll ring the number on the statement, then. Thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, that's -- that's the best way to do it, honestly. Ring the number on the statement, ask for [PERSON_1] in compliance, and if I'm not at my desk, they can take a message. And I'll find out what that deadline's actually tied to, so whoever you speak to can answer it properly. Sorry for the fluster, and enjoy your dinner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, thanks. Um, sorry, one thing though. You said you weren't selling anything, but earlier you said you'd read me the holdings, and now it's, you'd find out the deadline? Which, I mean, you said it was routine. Never mind. I'll ring the number on the statement, and I'll ask my husband first. Right, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the billing and collections office at [COMPANY_A]. I'm trying to reach [PERSON_2], is that you speaking? Okay, so the reason I'm calling is there's an outstanding medical balance on a file here, it's a relative of yours, and your name has come up on the account as the responsible party. The balance currently sits at [AMOUNT_1], and it's already past the standard billing window, so it's been moved over to my desk. I just want to go over the account with you, confirm a couple of details, and get it resolved today if we can.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on one second -- oh no, the pan, hang on -- right, sorry, I've turned it down. Who did you say you were again? And a relative of mine? Which relative?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem. It's [PERSON_1], I'm with the billing and collections office at [COMPANY_A]. Like I said, there's a balance of [AMOUNT_1] on a relative's account and you're listed as the responsible party. As for which relative, I can go through the account details once we've confirmed who I'm speaking with, that's just the procedure here. So can you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Um, go back a bit -- you said it's a medical balance, yes? Medical what, exactly? Like, which hospital, or... I don't understand why I'm the responsible one. Nobody's told me about any of this. And you can't even say which relative, but you want my date of birth? That seems backwards, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, I understand it feels that way. But the hospital, the department, the case reference, all of that is released after identity is confirmed. That's standard, it protects the patient's information. I can note your objection on the file, but the balance is [AMOUNT_1] and it's past due either way, and once an account reaches this stage it goes to the next level of recovery, which is just how it works. So if I could get your full name and date of birth, we can go through the account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... right. Well, uh, "next level of recovery", what does that mean, exactly? Sorry, I'm just -- I've got the dinner on and I'm trying to take this in. I mean, I'm not being funny, but you ring me up, you won't say which relative, you won't say which hospital, and now it's getting worse if I don't give you my birthday? That doesn't sit right. Is there a number I can ring you back on, or something? Like a proper one, from a letter or whatever?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Next level of recovery is a referral. The balance gets reported and the file goes to an outside agency, that's the standard sequence once an account is this far past due. As for a callback number, uh, I can give you [PHONE_1], but that line goes to a general queue and it won't have your file in front of whoever picks up. It's better to deal with it now while it's on my screen. So, full name and date of birth, and we can see what we've got.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, a general queue? So the number you're giving me won't even -- no, wait, sorry, let me just -- that's not right, is it? You ring me, you say it's urgent, but if I ring you back nobody knows who I am? I'm not giving you my birthday on that. Sorry. I'll sort it out some other way, I'll ask my family first. Right, I've got to go, the pan's -- bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, someone's at my desk, just a sec -- okay. Look, I can note on the file that you declined to verify, but the balance stays active and the referral timeline doesn't pause because of that. If you want to ask your family, that's fine, but I can't tell you which relative or which hospital until -- no, sorry, I can't go into that. That's all I have for you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, sorry, what? You're going now? Okay. Well, look, I'm not trying to be difficult, I'm just standing here with a pan going and a phone in my hand and you can't tell me which relative, which hospital, nothing, and I'm meant to hand over my birthday? I'd sooner ring my sister and my mum first, they'd know if anyone's been poorly. And if there's really a bill, it can come in a letter, can't it? With the proper name on it. Sorry. I'm sure you've got your job to do, but I'm not dealing with it like this. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A letter would, uh -- no, a letter isn't something I can promise, not on an account that's already, I mean, it's not up to me what goes out. Look, if there's a bill, you'll, you'll see it, one way or another. I've noted that you declined, and, yeah, that's all I can do from here. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you can't promise a letter? Well, that's, I mean, that's odd, isn't it? Every bill I've ever had came in the post, the gas, the dentist, all of it, and you're telling me this one's too urgent for paper but you can't even say who it's for. No, sorry. I'm not being rude, I just don't know you from Adam, and I've got my mum on the phone to ring and a pan that's about to catch. If it's real, it'll turn up in a letter, and if it isn't, well, I've not lost anything, have I? Right. I'm going now, all right? Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, there's someone talking over me here, give me a second -- yeah, no, tell them I'll be right there. Okay. Look, I've, uh, I've got your objection noted, and that's, that's as far as I can take it. I can't speak to what goes out in the post, that's not my side of it. Right. I've got to go. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, wait, before you go. Two minutes ago you said the number you gave me goes to a general queue, and nobody there would know my file. So if I did ring it, what would I even say? Who would I ask for? Sorry, I'm just trying to work out how I'd check any of this. Because if I can't check it, I really can't do anything with it, can I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, you'd, I mean you'd just ask for, for collections, and they'd, no. Look, I can't walk you through how you'd check it, that's, that's not something I'm able to do from here. The file's noted. That's all I've got. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you can't tell me how to check it. Sorry, hang on -- oh, the onions, they're catching, one second -- right, sorry, I'm back. No. That's it, I think. You can't tell me who it's for, you can't tell me how to check it, and I'm not giving you my birthday. I'm going to ring my mum and sort it that way. If it's real, it can come in the post. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, the what? The onions, is that a department? I don't have an onions on the file, no. Look, the balance is still active, [AMOUNT_1], and I've noted you declined, so, yeah. That's all I've got on this. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Did you say a balance of, um, onions? No, hang on, that's, oh, the onions are my dinner, that's what's burning. Sorry. I'm cooking. You said you've noted I declined, yes? Fine. Note it. I'm not giving you anything today, and if there's a real bill it can come in the post. Right, I'm going now, I've really got to see to the pan. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, sorry, I know I've caught you at a random time, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants over in the international claims office, and basically I'm just working through a list this week to line up short confirmation calls with a few people on our records, nothing complicated, it's really just a quick check that we've got your contact details right and a convenient window for someone from the senior team to ring you back. So I just wanted to ask, are you okay to chat for a minute, or is there a better time I should try?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1], hello. Sorry, which company did you say again? I didn't quite catch it. But yes, I'm just at home, I've got a minute, I'm happy to help if I can.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh sure, no problem, it's [COMPANY_A], the international claims office, we handle overseas draw entries and, uh, sorry, hang on one second, [PERSON_2], can you just put that on my desk, thanks -- sorry about that, it's a bit of a madhouse in here today. Right, so, I've got you down here as [PERSON_1], and I just need to confirm the best number for the senior team to reach you on, is it still [PHONE_1] or is there another one you'd rather they use?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I'm not very good with this sort of thing. Could you go back a bit, you said something about overseas draw entries? I'm not sure I understand what that's got to do with me. Did I enter something? I don't remember, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, don't apologise, you don't have to have done anything, a lot of entries are made on people's behalf through partner lists, that's completely normal, and the reason I'm calling is actually good news, [PERSON_1], you've been selected as a winner in the, uh, the March draw, ticket ending [CODE_1], prize of [AMOUNT_1], so all I'm doing today is confirming your details so the senior team can ring you back, and that's really all it is, so is [PHONE_1] still the right number, or would you rather they used a different one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. A winner, goodness. Sorry, I'm just a bit confused, I don't remember buying any ticket.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, honestly, you don't need to remember buying anything, that's what I said, a lot of these are entered through partner lists, so you don't need to have bought a ticket, and it's, um, actually the February draw, sorry, not March, I've got two lists open here, and the prize is [AMOUNT_2], not the figure I said, I was reading off the wrong line. So really it's just, uh, you being picked, no ticket needed, and all I need is a good number for the senior team, is [PHONE_1] still right, because they're only holding the slot today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm sorry, I'm just not following very well. March, and now February, and a different amount, and I still don't remember entering anything. Could you tell me again, who is it you said you were calling from? And how would I know this is, you know, real? I don't mean to be rude, I'd just like to understand it properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not rude at all, honestly, it's a sensible question, so, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the international claims office, that's [COMPANY_A], and the whole thing is just confirming a good number for the senior team, that's all it is today, and the details, the draw and the figure, they'll go through all of that on their call, I'm only scheduling, which is why I mixed up my lists, sorry, and the slot's only held until end of day, so is [PHONE_1] still the best number for them, or would you rather they used another one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, can I just -- you keep saying the number, but you still haven't really told me how I'd know -- oh, sorry, I didn't mean to cut across you. It's only that you've said March and then February and two different amounts, and I'd really like to understand that before I say anything about my phone. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or something like that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you didn't cut across me, you're fine, and look, the March and February thing, that's just me, I had two lists open, it's all one prize, it's just the senior team who go through the figures, and a call-back number, I mean, they'll give you that when they ring, because I'm only the scheduling side, so all I'm doing is confirming the best number for the senior team, and the slot's only held until end of day, so is [PHONE_1] right, or would you rather they used another one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on a moment, the kettle's just gone off, I'll just -- there, sorry about that. Where was I? Yes, so you can't give me a number to ring you on, only they can, after they've rung me? Sorry, I'm probably being slow, but that does seem a bit back to front. I think I'd rather not say my number just yet. I'm sorry, I hope that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely all right, and honestly you're not being slow, it does sound back to front when I say it out loud, but it's only that they hold the lines and I'm just the scheduling side, so I can't put a direct number on the screen for you, but look, you don't have to give me anything new, all I need is a yes that [PHONE_1] is still the right one, that's the number we already hold, and a yes just means the senior team ring you once, today, explain the draw and the figure properly, and you can ask them everything you've asked me, and if you don't like what you hear you just say no thank you and that's the end of it, no cost, no strings, and I'd hate for you to miss out over a mix-up with my lists, so can I put you down for that, just the one call?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh... hmm. I mean, one call, that's not much, is it? And you did say I could just say no thank you. Um... sorry, I'm just thinking. It's only that I still don't really know who you are, and the amounts and the months keep changing, and I'd feel silly if... no, I think, sorry, I think I'd better not. If it's genuinely mine, they can surely write to me, can't they? I'm sorry, I hope you don't mind. Thank you for ringing, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the supermarket delivery people. I'm just ringing about your order for this afternoon, the one you placed online last night, uh, or sorry, this morning, I think it came through around seven? Anyway, quick one, I just want to confirm your two-hour window with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Sorry, um, a delivery, did you say? From the supermarket? I'm not sure I, uh, I don't remember ordering anything this morning, but I do do my shopping online sometimes, so, sorry, could you say that again? What was it about the window?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No worries at all, [PERSON_1], happens to everyone. Sorry, hang on, someone's just dropped a whole crate of something behind me, give me one second -- right, sorry, back. So it's the order under your account, [ACCOUNT_REF] is the reference on my screen, and it's down for a two-hour slot this afternoon. If you did the order yourself last night or early this morning, that might be why it's slipped your mind. Do you want me to read you the slot, and then you can tell me if it rings a bell?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, I suppose, well, I -- sorry, I mean, I might have, I do get a bit muddled sometimes. Go on then, read me the slot, and I'll, I'll see if it, um, rings a bell. Sorry, I'm not very good with all this online ordering, so you'll have to bear with me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're fine, [PERSON_1], honestly, you're doing great. Right, so the slot is two till four this afternoon, that's the two-hour window, and the driver will be somewhere in there. Oh, and sorry, you asked me earlier what it was about, I only said the window -- the other thing is, one item on the order's been swapped for a similar product, so I just need a quick yes or no from you on that, that's all, takes two seconds.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a swap, right, um. Sorry, which item was it, do you know? I mean, I'd want to know what it's been swapped for before I say yes, wouldn't I? And, sorry, this is probably a silly question, but since I don't remember ordering anything, could you tell me what was actually on the order? Just so I know it's mine.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's not a silly question at all, [PERSON_1], everyone asks that, and it's a good habit. Okay, so the swap is -- sorry, hang on, there's a forklift beeping right outside, give me a sec -- right, back. So it's the, uh, the tea, I think, one of the boxes of tea, swapped for a similar one, and I've got a few other bits on the screen here, but I'd rather not read your whole shopping list out over the phone if I can help it. Does the tea ring a bell at all?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the tee, sorry, the T-shirt? Um, I don't think I ordered any clothes, I don't think the supermarket does those, does it? Oh, hang on, did you say tea? Sorry, my hearing's not great on this phone. Yes, I do drink tea, everyone does, so I might have. But, um, sorry, I still don't quite know that it's my order, if you can't say what else is on it. Is there some way I could check it myself, do you think? Like on the website?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, tea, T-E-A, sorry, it's a rubbish line, I think. And yes, checking it yourself is the best idea, [PERSON_1]. If you just log in to your account on the, uh, on the website, the order should be sitting right there, with the slot and the swap and everything, so you'll see it's yours. Or I could, no, sorry, I'd rather you just look yourself, that's easier. Honestly it's a two-minute job.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that's a good idea, I'll just go and -- sorry, can I just ask, if it's not on there, is there a number I can ring you back on? Only, I'd feel better, you know, ringing the shop itself, the number I've always -- oh, sorry, I've talked over you, you were going to say something.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, go on, I'm all ears -- sorry, yeah, a number, so, ringing the shop, that's a great idea, honestly, everyone does that, and, uh, you can ring the number you've always used, [PERSON_1], that's absolutely fine. If you want to ring me direct as well, I think it's [PHONE_1], but, oh, hang on, I'm not sure if that's, um, is that the one that goes to the shop floor or the main line? I can't remember. Sorry, what did you want to ask next?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, um, so you're not sure which number that is? Sorry, I'm a bit lost now. What I was asking, I think, was whether I could just ring the shop myself, the number I've always used, and check it with them, because I don't remember ordering, you see. I really don't remember ordering anything. So I'll do that, I think, I'll ring the shop and check, if that's all right. Sorry to be a bother. Thank you for ringing, anyway, [PERSON_2], and, um, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not a bother at all, [PERSON_1], that's absolutely the right thing to do, honestly. Oh, sorry, hang on, somebody's wheeling a trolley right past me, give me a sec -- right. So, uh, before you go, I can't actually tell you which line [PHONE_1] goes to, and I can't say what else is on the order either, I haven't got the full list in front of me. Let me find out and call you straight back, yeah? Or you ring the shop on your usual number, that's fine too, whichever's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, don't ring me back, I'll -- sorry, I'll ring the shop, on the number I've always used. I think that's best. Thank you ever so much, [PERSON_2], sorry for the trouble, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, of course, [PERSON_1], that's absolutely fine, you do whatever feels easiest. Sorry, hang on, there's a door banging somewhere behind me, one sec -- right, sorry. If it's not on your account when you check, just tell them there's a call that went out from here this afternoon, and they'll sort it. No trouble at all, you take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I'll tell them, thank you, I'll -- sorry, I've cut across you again. Bye now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] here, I'm with [COMPANY_A], the police, uh, following up on that incident you reported last week. Sorry, just to be sure I've got the right person -- you did report something last week, yeah? Won't take two minutes, I just need a couple of details to tidy up the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who's this again? Police, you said? And what incident -- I mean, what are you saying I reported? Hang on, hang on, [muffled] no, put that down, sweetheart. Sorry, um, yeah, so -- what exactly are you calling about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No worries at all, [PERSON_1], sounds like you've got your hands full. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the police -- I'm following up on the incident you reported last week, the one you called in about. Just a quick follow-up, like I said, a couple of details to finish off the file, nothing to worry about. Is it a bad time? I can ring back if it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, you keep saying the incident, but you haven't actually said what it was, have you? Because I'm not sure I reported anything last week. So, um, what do you have down on your end? And, uh, can I ring you back on a number I look up myself?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, ring me back, that's the sensible thing to do, [PERSON_1]. Look the station's main number up yourself, not from anything I give you, and ask for [PERSON_2] by name. And fair point about the incident, I was being vague, sorry. The reference on the original report is [CODE_1], so if you've got a copy of what you submitted, check it against that. I'd only ask that you keep the details of the case to yourself for now, that's standard while it's open. But it's no trouble at all if you'd rather we did this in person or by letter instead.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, well, that's, uh, that's more reasonable than I expected, honestly. I'll look the number up myself, like you said, and ask for you by name. But I'll be straight with you, I still don't remember reporting anything last week, and I've got no copy of anything with that reference on it, so I can't check it against anything. And the bit about keeping it to myself, I mean, why would I need to? If it's my case, who would I even be telling? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just that somebody in my family got caught out by a phone call last year, so I'd rather do this properly. If it is real, a letter's fine, or I'll call the station and they can tell me what's on file. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's completely fine, [PERSON_1], and you're not being difficult. Honestly, if you've got no memory of reporting anything, it may well be a mix-up on our end, wrong number, wrong person, it happens. Forget the keeping-it-to-yourself bit, ring the station, they'll sort it, and if there's a letter to send, it'll come in the post.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, thanks for being straightforward about it. I'll ring the station myself, on a number I've looked up, and if there's anything on file they can tell me then. And if it's a mix-up, then, uh, no harm done. Okay. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no harm done at all, [PERSON_1]. Oh, just so you know, when I said wrong person, I meant it could be a different [PERSON_1] altogether, not that anything's wrong at your end. And the case reference I gave, [CODE_1], that's just what you'd quote to the front desk so they can find the file. Sorry for the bother, and good on you for checking. Take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Okay. Thanks, I'll, uh, I'll look it up myself like we said. Take care. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, lovely, and if the front desk -- sorry, didn't mean to cut across you -- if they ask who rang, just say [PERSON_2], no rush. Cheers, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, sure. Though, uh, you said earlier to keep it to myself, and now you're saying quote it at the front desk, so which is it? Anyway. I'll ring them and see what they say. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair catch, [PERSON_1], and that's on me for muddling it. Keeping it to yourself just means don't pass the details on to other people, friends or neighbours or whoever. The station staff are different, they've got the file in front of them, so tell them all you like. And honestly, I'd rather you rang them than took my word for anything. Ring the main number, ask for me by name, and they'll tell you whether I'm who I say I am. Cheers, [PERSON_1], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, can I just go back a bit? Earlier you said it might be a different [PERSON_1] altogether, and I didn't really follow that. If you rang this number, you must have had it from somewhere, so what exactly did you have, and why did you open by asking if I'd reported something? Because if you weren't sure it was me, it's an odd way to start. Anyway, I'm not telling you anything else. I'll ring the station on a number I find myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's a fair question, [PERSON_1], and you're right to ask it. This number was on the original report, so it came from whoever made it. My opening was clumsy, though. I asked whether you'd reported something because I always confirm I've got the right person before I say anything about a case, and I should've explained that sooner. If you don't remember reporting anything, then either the number was put down wrongly or I've got something muddled, and the station can tell you which. So ring them on a number you've looked up yourself, ask for [PERSON_2] by name, and don't tell me anything else today. I'd honestly rather you checked. Thanks for your patience, [PERSON_1], and sorry again for the bother. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. So, uh... the number was on the report, but I didn't make a report, so, well. That's the bit that doesn't sit right with me, if I'm honest. Look, I'm done here. I'll ring the station myself, and if there's actually a case, they can write to me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh wonderful, I'm so glad I caught you, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the fraud team at [COMPANY_A], and I hope I'm not -- oh, sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you, go ahead, I just wanted to say first, how's your day going so far?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who? The what team, the sales team? No, hang on -- you said you're from the, uh, [COMPANY_A] something. And yeah, I'm [PERSON_1], I guess. Who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, not sales, ha, nothing like that! It's [PERSON_2], fraud team at [COMPANY_A], the bank, and honestly, uh, I know, I know, out of the blue call, I'd be a little thrown too. So, well, anyway, I'm looking at your account right now and there's a charge for [AMOUNT_1] that just came through, tried to come through, I should say, and it's flagged, and I really need to go over it with you while it's still pending, so, um, could I just confirm a couple of details on the account first?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, hang on. I'm not, uh -- look, I haven't actually said I bank with you. You rang me. So how about you tell me something about the account first? Like, I don't know, what name's it under, or what's the last thing I did on it? Because I'm not confirming anything to somebody who just, you know, called me out of nowhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough, you're sharp, I like that! Um, two turns ago, you said something about the sales team, and I just want to make sure I'm not the one who muddied things, so no, not sales, we're the group that watches for unusual activity. But look, I can't read account details out to someone I haven't verified, that's exactly the rule that protects you, so it works the other way too, I'd need you to confirm your date of birth and the name on the account first, and honestly the clock's ticking on that charge, so the sooner the better, otherwise it may go through and the account could get frozen.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, see, that's backwards, though. You called me, so you're the one who has to prove who you are, not me. And the clock thing, that's, uh, that's exactly what makes me not want to rush. If it's a real hold, it'll still be there in ten minutes. So I'm going to hang up and ring the number on the back of my card, and if there's actually a problem, they'll know about it. Cheers.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, sure, sure, that's, well, honestly, uh -- you know, I wouldn't bother with that, the lines are jammed this time of day, you'd be on hold forever, and I'm already right here with your file open, so it'd be so much quicker if we just -- no, hang on, don't hang up yet, [PERSON_1], because if that charge goes through before you get anyone on the phone, I can't promise what happens to the account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said I'm ringing the number on my card. Number on the back of my card. And honestly, you telling me not to bother with the real number, that's, uh, that's the bit that settles it for me. If the line's jammed, I'll wait. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, ha, no, you go right ahead, that's your call. I mean, it's not like I was ever asking for anything sensitive, I only wanted to, uh, confirm a couple of little things, and, well, I never said the account would be frozen, I said it might be flagged, so, you know, don't read too much into it. Honestly, just ring whenever you like, or -- or don't, it's no skin off my nose, take care now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, you literally said the account could get frozen. Two minutes ago. Anyway. Doesn't matter, I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, this is [PERSON_1] with account services at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling about your vehicle warranty, it's set to lapse and I just need to confirm the renewal with you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello. Sorry, I -- my vehicle warranty? I thought that was, well, I mean, I'm not sure I even -- sorry, can you say that again? Which company did you say you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem, it's [COMPANY_A], account services, and, uh, like I said, the renewal window closes at the end of today, so I do need to get this confirmed on this call. It's a quick one, really, just a few minutes of your time and we keep the coverage active, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, end of today, that sounds a bit pressing. Sorry, I'm just, I'm not very good with this sort of thing. Um, what is it you need from me exactly? And, sorry, how would I know it's, well, that it's really about my car? I don't think I've had a warranty with, uh, [COMPANY_A] before, but I might have, I honestly can't remember.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Totally understand, and that's a fair question, it's just standard procedure on the renewal. Now, you've been with us since, uh, [CITY_1] originally, so we do have you on file, I'm showing the coverage under the, hm, the older policy, though I did say earlier it was a new renewal, it's the same thing really, it just needs the confirmation today. All I need is to verify the account on this call and we keep everything active, and like I said, the window closes at the end of today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, the kettle's just clicked off, bear with me one second. Right, I'm back. Um, sorry, what were you saying? Something about [CITY_1], and the older policy? I'm a bit lost, I thought you said it was a renewal, and now it's an older one, and I'm not sure which. And, sorry, what do you mean by verify the account? What would I have to tell you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: So, welcome back, as I said, this is [PERSON_1] with account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about your vehicle warranty, it's set to lapse and I need to confirm the renewal today. The verification is just the standard process, I'd go through the account details with you on this call, it's quick, and the window does close at the end of today. Older policy, newer policy, it doesn't change anything on your end, it's the same renewal, it just needs the confirmation.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I'm just trying to keep up. Um, a minute ago I thought you said you'd call me about a new renewal, and then it was the older policy, and now it's the same thing, so I'm not sure which it is. And earlier, wasn't it, you said it was just a few minutes, and now you're going through my account details? I'm sorry, I don't mean to be difficult. It's just, I don't think I've ever given you my details, so how would you have them to go through?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not being difficult, and I appreciate you raising that, I do, but it's all part of the standard verification procedure, so what happens is, the renewal gets flagged on our system, the account is matched against the file we hold, and then it's confirmed with the policyholder directly, which is you, on a recorded line, and that's what keeps your coverage protected. Now the older policy, the newer one, I know it sounds like two different things, but it's one renewal on one file, it's just how it shows up on my screen versus how it was originally set up, and honestly the paperwork side of it is my job, not yours. What I do need from you is a few minutes today, because, as I said, the window closes at the end of today, and once it closes the file goes back to the, uh, the general queue and the coverage lapses, and I'd really hate for that to happen on your vehicle.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Sorry, I'm still not sure what vehicle you mean, you haven't said which one.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, the vehicle on the file, yes, uh, it's showing on my screen under the policy, and I can read that back to you once we've, once the account's been verified on the call, that's just how the procedure works. And I do want to be mindful of your time, because the renewal window closes at the end of today, so if we can just get started, I'm calling about your vehicle warranty, it's set to lapse, and I need to confirm the renewal with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Sorry, but you can't tell me the car, and I'm meant to prove who I am first? That seems the wrong way round. I think I'd rather look for my own paperwork and ring the company myself, if that's all right. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Sorry, I'm so sorry to jump in, I just -- is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm a case handler there, and I'm, uh, I'm really glad I caught you, because it's about a draw result that's, well, it's time-sensitive. Are you still there? Sorry, I only want to make sure you hear this properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm here, I heard you. Sorry, but who exactly is -- a draw result? I haven't entered any draw that I can think of, so before you go any further, which company did you say you're calling from, and how did you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, that's completely fair, I'm sorry, I should have been clearer. It's [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency, we handle regional draws on behalf of other organisations, and your details came through in the entry data from one of the partner sign-ups, I'm afraid I don't have the exact one in front of me. Um, a lot of people don't remember those, it's usually a tick box on a form, which is partly why I wanted to reach you directly before the claim window closes. Are you still with me?
