I only want to make sure this is sorted properly for you, because if it's not claimed in time, it, well, it just goes back into the pool.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you can't tell me which partner, or which draw, or what I supposedly won. That's quite a lot of "I don't have it in front of me" for someone who's called specifically about my claim. And the claim window closing is exactly the sort of pressure I'd expect before anyone's said a single verifiable thing. What's the name of the draw, and what's the reference for my entry? If you're a case handler, you'll have a case number, so I'd like that please.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I hear you, and I'm sorry, I do. I think I've made this sound worse than it is. It's a regional draw, a [CITY_1] one, and the prize is [AMOUNT_1], which is, well, it's why I wanted to get to you quickly. The case number is, um, it's in the file, and I can read it out once I've just confirmed it's you, so if you could give me your full name and date of birth, that's all I need, it's really only to protect you, so nobody else can claim it in your name. Are you still there? Sorry. It's just that the window does close, and I'd hate for it to go back into the pool.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not giving you my full name or my date of birth. You've asked me to confirm my identity before you'll give me a case number, and that's backwards. You called me, so you identify yourself first. You still haven't told me the name of the draw, which partner passed on my details, or anything I could check independently. If this is genuine, send it in writing to the address on file, and I'll look into it from there. I'm not going to continue this over the phone. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, don't -- I mean, I'm sorry, I really am, I wasn't trying to, it's only that I -- look, I'm just trying to keep this from slipping away from you. Are you still there? Sorry. Posting something out would take, well, longer than the window allows, and then it, it would be gone. If you could just confirm your name and the first line of your address, I can hold it for you while we, while I get you the paperwork.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I said no, and I'll say it again: I'm not confirming my name or my address. You called me, so you identify yourself first, and you still haven't given me a draw name, a partner, or a case number. If the window is too short for a letter, then I'll lose it. That's fine. I'm ending the call now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, please, just one second before you go, I'm so sorry, I really don't want you to think I'm trying to catch you out, because I'm not, and I do understand why this feels strange, I'd feel exactly the same way if somebody rang me out of the blue. It's only that, well, I do see a lot of these end up unclaimed, and it's genuinely disappointing for everyone when that happens, and I'd much rather you had the chance to look at it properly. So, uh, if you'd like to check me out first, that's completely fine, I can give you a number to ring us back on, it's [PHONE_1], and you can ask for [PERSON_2] in claims. Only, and I'm sorry to keep saying this, the window really is closing, so if you could ring in the next hour or so, that'd be best, otherwise I can't promise it'll still be held. Are you still there? Sorry. I only want to make sure you've got that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A number you've just given me over the phone doesn't verify anything. If I wanted to check you out, I'd look up the company myself and use whatever contact details I find independently, not the ones you read to me. And the hour deadline is the same pressure again, just in a new form. I'm not ringing that number, I'm not confirming any details, and I'm not continuing this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, that's absolutely fair, and I'm sorry, I shouldn't have put a time on it, that was me being clumsy, I just get anxious when I think something's going to be missed. Of course you'd look us up yourself, honestly that's what I'd do too, and I'd never want to talk you out of it. It's only that, well, I do think it's a shame if it lapses, and I'd feel awful if you rang off thinking I'd wasted your afternoon. So, uh, if you find the company and ring through on whatever number you've got for it, just ask for claims and mention [PERSON_2], and they'll be able to pull the file up. And if it turns out not to be there, then I'm sorry for the bother, I truly am. Are you still there? Sorry, I only want to be sure you got all that before you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it. If I want to check, I'll look the company up myself, and I won't be mentioning anyone's name to get a file pulled up. I don't expect to bother. I won't be taking any of this further today, so that's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hello, yes -- this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the public library. Is this, uh, is this [PERSON_2]? Good. I'm calling about a book you reserved last week, it's come in, and I just need to let you know it'll be held at the front desk for ten days.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- the kettle just clicked off, one second. Right. Uh, yes, speaking. But, security operations? That's an odd department to be ringing about a book reservation. Which library did you say, and which title was it, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, well, it's -- hold on, sorry, somebody's just dropped a trolley out here, give me a second. Right. Security operations, yes, we handle the desk notices now, it's a staffing thing. The library is [COMPANY_A], the main branch in [CITY_1], and I don't have the title in front of me, I only have your name against a reservation. The title will be on the slip at the desk.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you don't have the title? You're ringing me about a book, but you don't have the title. And it's security operations ringing about it, not circulation or whatever the reservations desk is called. I'm sorry, I'm just trying to be precise here. Which book is it, and when did I reserve it? Because I'd want to check that against my own account before I go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's fair, that's a fair question, and I'd rather you checked than didn't. So, what I have in front of me is a hold notice, it's a printout, and it carries your name, [PERSON_2], and a reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and the date it was placed, which, uh, is last week, that's the extent of it. The title field, I'm looking at it now, it's cut off on this printout, the printer does that, the margin clips it, which is partly why I said the slip at the desk will have it. And as for why it's me and not circulation, well, circulation is two people and one of them's off, so the desk notices got shared out across the building, I drew the phones this week, that's all it is. Now, nothing's required from you today. It's held for ten days, you can log into your own library account, the way you normally do, not through me, and check the reservation against what you remember, and if it's not there, then ring the main number and tell them. That's, uh, that's genuinely all this is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the printer clips the margin, or that the printer clicks? No, never mind, I think I got that. But hang on, you said a, uh, a hold notice with a reference on it. A reference for what, exactly? Is that my library card number? Because I'm not going to read anything out to you, I'll just say that now. And if it's all on a printout in front of you, I'd have thought the title would be on the system as well. Can you just look it up there?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Clips. The margin clips, C-L-I-P-S, yes. And no, no, the reference isn't your card number, it's just the hold reference, internal, and I'm not asking you for anything, I'd, uh -- sorry, hang on, there's somebody at the desk waving a pass at me, one moment. Right. Back. So the system, yes, I've got the terminal here, but I'm on a restricted login, security can see notices, not catalogue records, that's the, that's the way it's set up. So no, I can't pull the title from here. And I'd rather you didn't read anything out, honestly, I don't need it. Look, the book is at the desk, ten days, bring your card, that's the whole of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Except earlier you said circulation was short-staffed and the desk notices got shared out, so you've been handed the phones. But now you're saying security has a restricted login that can see notices and not catalogue records. Those don't really sit together. If you've been given the job of ringing people about holds, you'd think someone would have given you a login that can see the title. And I'll be honest, I haven't reserved anything, not that I can recall. So I'm going to log into my own account, the usual way, and see whether there's a hold on it. If there is, fine. If not, I'll ring the main number on the library's website. Thanks for the call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Fine. Before you go though, uh, which part didn't sit together? The phones, or the login? Because those are, they're two separate things, I was given the call list, not the catalogue access, and I did say that, I think. But that's -- no, that's your call. Check your own account, ring the main number, that's exactly what I'd do. The hold stays ten days regardless. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Both, honestly, but I'm not going to argue it out on the phone. You were handed a call list and no way to see what you're calling about, and I'm content to leave it at that. I'll check my account and ring the main number myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood. That's, uh, that's perfectly reasonable. The main number's on the library's website, you won't need anything from me to use it. If there's no hold on your account, tell them and they'll sort it out. Good day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Good day.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, well -- sorry, hang on, the door's gone again, somebody's propped it with the, uh, with a bin. One second. Right. That's -- yes, good day to you, [PERSON_2]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one more thing, and then I'll let you go. Two turns back you said you were going to ring the main number from the website, and I just want to be sure that's [COMPANY_A] you mean, the library, and not -- well, not some other number. That's the one to use, yes? Right. That's all. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, the one on the library's own website. Not one you give me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, the one on the library's own website. Not one from me, I'm not giving you a number, I wouldn't. The website, the main number, that's the one. The website, yes. Right, that's, uh, that's everything. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'm glad we agree on that, because that's the whole point. If there's a genuine hold, it'll be sitting in my account when I log in, and if there isn't, the main number will tell me, and neither of those needs anything from you. I'll just say, and I'm not trying to be rude about it, that I've been on this call a good while now and I still don't have a title, a branch address or a surname for you, and that's a lot to be missing on a call about one book. So I'm not going to lean on anything you've told me, I'll just check it myself, the way you suggested. Anyway, that's me done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Great, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the scheduling desk at [COMPANY_A], sorry, I said desk, it's more the billing coordination team, but anyway we've got a double charge on your subscription, [AMOUNT_1] twice, and we really need to sort the refund while I've got you on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, this is -- yes, speaking. Sorry, I didn't quite catch, was it the scheduling desk or the, uh, billing something? I'm a bit confused. A double charge, you said? I mean, I'd be glad to get that sorted, I just -- who did you say you were calling from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A], the double charge on your subscription, we just need to get that refund sorted while you're on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a discharge? Sorry, I'm -- is that something to do with the hospital? I haven't been in, I don't think, no. Oh, hang on, did you say subscription? I'm sorry, I'm not very good on the phone. Which subscription is it, exactly? I've got a few things I pay for, I think, I just can't think what's with that company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, not discharge, double charge, [AMOUNT_1] taken twice on the one subscription, so it's the software one, the yearly plan, and honestly it's a quick fix, I just need to pull up your account on my end and then we do the refund together live, because the window on it closes today. Is your computer near you at the moment, or, sorry, are you at home, because it's easiest if I can see what you're seeing?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a double charge, right, sorry, I see now. Um, yes, I'm at home, the computer's just in the other room. But, what do you mean, see what I'm seeing? I'm sorry, I don't really follow that bit. And I don't remember a software plan, I'm not sure which one that'd be. How would I know it's really, uh, [COMPANY_A] ringing me? Is there a way I can check, do you think? Not that I'm saying you're not, I just don't want to get it wrong.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sure, that's fair, [PERSON_1], and the way you check is, uh, hang on, sorry, somebody's just dropped a stack of paper behind me, one second -- okay, sorry, where was I. Right, the quick way is we just get you at the computer and I'll walk you through, it's very simple, it's really just so I can see the screen and match it to the account reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and the refund goes straight back, but like I said the window closes today so it does need doing now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Um, I'm sorry, you didn't really say how I check it's you, though. I don't think I'm comfortable with you seeing my screen.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, totally understand, and honestly, um, so, anyway the thing is, [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] at [COMPANY_A] about the double charge, the [AMOUNT_1] taken twice, and the window closes today so, uh, if you could just pop through to the computer for me, yeah, that's all we need, and then we can get the refund moving.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, I'm sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, it's just that I asked how I could check you're who you say you are, and I don't think I've had an answer, have I? And I'm a bit lost, really, because I still don't remember any software plan, and you keep saying the window closes today, but I'd have thought if it was a proper mistake with my money, they'd write to me, or it'd be there on my statement. I'm not very clever with computers, you see, and if I go through to the other room and you're looking at my screen, I wouldn't even know what you were looking at. So I think I'd rather not do that, I'm sorry. Could I maybe ring the company myself, on the number I've got for them, and ask about it that way? Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's -- well, you could, yeah, but the thing is the refund's tied to this call, so if you ring off it, honestly, the window, it'd probably, uh, lapse before you got through, and then you'd be out the [AMOUNT_1], so really the simplest is just you and me, now, with the computer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Well, um, I'm sorry, but that doesn't sound right to me. If the money's really mine, I'd have thought it wouldn't just vanish because I rang them myself. And you still haven't said how I can tell it's really you, so I think I'd better do it my way. I'll ring the company on the number I've got, and if it's a real mistake they'll sort it. Thank you for ringing, I'm sorry to be a bother. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, [PERSON_1], no, wait, hang on a sec, you're not being a bother, it's just, uh, look, I'm not going to keep you, I've got [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], double charge, [AMOUNT_1] twice, and, yeah, I'll ring you back a bit later and we can finish it off then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hold on a tick, there's the kettle going -- it's just clicked off, never mind. Um, yes, you were saying you'd ring back. Well, please don't, I think. If it's a real mistake I'll ring the company myself and they can put it right. Thank you, though, and I'm sorry I wasn't more help. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, no problem at all, though, uh, like I said, I'm only the scheduling assistant, so billing will ring you themselves, probably tomorrow, or later today, whichever, and I'll just, yeah, I'll try you again this afternoon in any case. Bye for now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, um, I'd really rather you didn't ring again, if that's all right. If it's a proper mistake, I'll see to it myself with the company, on the number I've got. Thank you, and goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon -- am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I don't mean to cut across you, but this is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance side at [COMPANY_A], and, uh, there's a matter our card-services team would like to go over with you, though I'll say up front I can't discuss any account details on this line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, did you say compliance? I thought you said something about card services, I'm not sure I caught that right. And you can't discuss the account on this line, but then, um, what is it you'd like to go over? I'm sorry, I'm a bit lost.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right to ask, and I'm sorry, I'll slow down. So, I'm in compliance, but the, uh, the transaction in question has been flagged to card services, so strictly it's their team that will speak with you, not me -- although I did say earlier that I was calling about it myself, which is a bit loose of me, I apologise. What I can tell you is that a transaction was flagged, and that I can't go into any detail on a call I've placed to you, which is exactly why I'd ask you to hang up and ring the number printed on the back of your card, and they'll have a reference noted against your name. It's, well, it's not something I'd want left sitting too long, but there's no need to rush, please do take your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, so you want me to ring the number on the back of the -- sorry, I'm cutting across you, I do apologise. But that sounds sensible, doesn't it? I'd just ring them myself. Only, um, you said there'd be a reference noted against my name, so what would I say to them? Do I give them your name, or is there something I'm meant to quote?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not at all, you're not cutting across me, that's a perfectly sensible thing to ask, and I'd rather you asked it. Sorry, one moment -- someone's just come to the door here -- no, it's fine, they can wait. Right, yes. So the reference is [CODE_1], and I'd ask you to quote that when they pick up, along with my name, [PERSON_2], compliance, so they can link it back to this call. And, uh, to be clear, I'm not asking you to tell me anything now, nothing at all, it's only the number on your card and that reference I'd point you to.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, [CODE_1] and your name, [PERSON_2], compliance. Sorry, let me just say that back so I've got it. And you're not wanting anything from me now, you said, just that I ring the number on the card. That's fine, I can do that. Um, I do hope whoever was at your door wasn't a bother. Anyway, thank you for letting me know, I'll ring them now. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's quite all right, it was nothing, just a colleague. Yes, that's right, both of those, and, uh, one small thing -- I said earlier there'd be a reference noted against your name, but I think it's really the card-services agent who logs the matter once you've rung through, so if they seem to have nothing noted at first, don't be put off, just quote [CODE_1] and my name to them and they'll find it. And, well, there's no pressure from my side, but I'd not leave it too long. Goodbye, [PERSON_1], and thank you for being so patient.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, you said don't be put off if they've got nothing noted -- or was it nothing *notified*? Hmm. Either way, I'll just quote the code and your name like you said. And I'll ring them straight away, I won't leave it, don't you worry. Thank you ever so much, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh -- notified, did you say? No, no, I think it was noted, but, uh, perhaps I was a bit muddled there, and I'd sooner you rang them than took my word on anything. Actually, sorry, did you say ring them *straight away*? I wouldn't want you feeling hurried on my account, it's only, well, best not to leave it sitting. Whatever they say to you, that's the thing to go by, not me. Goodbye then, [PERSON_1], and thank you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's quite all right, I did say straight away, didn't I? Sorry -- hang on, the kettle's just clicked off, one moment. Right, I'm back. Yes, I'll go by whatever they tell me, that sounds the sensible way round. Thank you for ringing, and sorry again for all my questions, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, please, no apology at all, the questions are exactly what I'd hope for. And, uh, you said the kettle? Yes, of course, do go and have your tea -- though I'm not sure I follow the bit about my being rung back, I'm afraid I can't be, there's no number for me you'd need, you only ring the one on your card. Right, so, [CODE_1] and the name, and whatever they tell you is what stands. Goodbye, [PERSON_1], and thank you, you've been very patient.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't mean you'd be ringing me back, I think I muddled that. No, I just ring the number on the card, quote [CODE_1] and your name, and go by whatever they say. I've got it, truly. Thank you again, and have a nice afternoon, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you haven't muddled anything, I think it was my wording that -- well, that wasn't as clear as it could have been, so that's on me. And, uh, it's right, just the number on your card, the reference, and go by whatever they say. I'd, well, I'd keep this open on our side until you've been through to them, so there's no harm in taking a little while. Have a good afternoon, [PERSON_1], and thank you for being so understanding. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind, I'll -- no, sorry, let me start that again. I'll ring them in a little while, once I've found my card, and I'll quote the code and your name like you said. Thank you for your patience with me, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's, um -- well, that's perfectly fine, take as long as you need to find it. And, uh, if it turns out the card's gone missing altogether, there's a number on the bank's website, [URL_1], that you can use instead, same reference, same name. I'll leave it there, then. Thank you, [PERSON_1], and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the website, right, yes, I'll use that if the card's gone astray. Sorry, I keep saying this, but I'll ring them and quote the code and your name, and go by whatever they say. Yes. Thank you ever so much, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, is this -- sorry, hang on, I've got it here on the screen -- is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm a claims assessor, and it's about your, um, your [PERSON_2], who's in a bit of a situation and can't come to the phone right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, speaking, that's me, hang on, let me just turn this down, I'm in the middle of the, uh, the roses -- sorry, did you say a situation? What kind of situation, is [PERSON_2] alright? And who did you say you were again, a claims, what was it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, it's nothing to do with roses, sorry, I'm, um, I think you said something about a hearing? Anyway, [PERSON_2] is, uh, okay, I think, or -- look, I can't really get into all of it, it's sensitive, and they asked me to keep it between us for now. I'm a claims assessor with [COMPANY_A], and what I need is to get a few details confirmed today, because it really can't wait past this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hearing? No, I didn't say anything about a hearing, I was just -- no, sorry, that was the roses, I was talking to myself. But hang on, you think they're okay? You think? I mean, how can you not know if -- and why would they ask you to keep it, I mean, why wouldn't they just ring me themselves? Sorry, I'm, it's a bit of a lot all at once, what is it you actually need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sorry, you're right, I jumped ahead there -- the hearing, forget the hearing, that was, um, that was a different file. Let me just -- hang on, I'm scrolling -- okay. [PERSON_2] is okay, I should have said it that way round. They can't ring you because they, uh, they're not able to use their phone at the moment, and honestly that's about all I'm able to say. What I need is for you to stay on the line with me while we go through the process, step by step. If we can get it sorted today it's much simpler for [PERSON_2], and I'd rather you didn't mention this call to anyone else in the family just yet, because it could, well, complicate things for them. Can you do that for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, can I just -- hang on, you're saying not tell anyone in the family? Why would I -- no, wait, that's, that's a bit odd, isn't it? If [PERSON_2] is in some kind of trouble then surely the whole point is I'd ring [PERSON_3] or whoever and, and find out what's going on, and you've changed your story twice now, the hearing and then it's a different file, so can you just tell me properly, who exactly are you, and how do I ring [COMPANY_A] back myself to check you're who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, I hear you, that's fair, and I'm sorry about the hearing business, I've got two files open and I mixed them up. Um, as for ringing the office back, I'd have to check what number I'm meant to give out for that, let me -- I'll find it. But look, [PERSON_1], if we stop and make a lot of calls first, it's [PERSON_2] who ends up waiting, and they're frightened, they asked specifically for you and not anyone else. I'm only asking you to hold off on [PERSON_3] until we've done this one thing, an hour at most. Can you do that, just stay with me and keep it to ourselves until then?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I'm not going to do that. I'm going to put the phone down and ring [PERSON_3] and [PERSON_2] myself. If it's all above board then it won't matter. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, no, please don't -- I mean, if you ring, then -- sorry, let me start again. I'm not trying to stop you, it's just that, um, [PERSON_2] was so worried about, about the rest of the family finding out, and I don't want to be the one who, well -- I'll be straight, I can't actually give you that office number, I've not got it in front of me. You've got my name, you've got [COMPANY_A], so, uh, if you ring and it's not sorted, they'll just tell you it's still open, and by then it could be harder on [PERSON_2]. Look, I'm sorry, I'm making a mess of this -- but if you put the phone down now, I honestly don't know what happens to them.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, there's a blackbird just gone straight into the, no, it's fine, it's after the worms -- sorry. No, I heard you, I did. But that's rather my point, isn't it? You can't give me a number, you won't let me ring family, and now it's what happens to them if I hang up. That's not a claims person, that's, I don't know what that is, but I'm not doing it. I'm ringing [PERSON_3] now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, we handle estates, probate, that sort of thing, and I'm one of the assistants on the collections side. I'm ringing because there's an estate we're administering at the moment, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and your name has come up as someone who may be named in it, may be, I can't say more than that until the formal letter reaches you, which should be with you in the next few days. What I'd need from you today is just to confirm I've got the right person, so your full name and the address we hold for you, and I'd ask that you keep this to yourself until the letter arrives, it's a confidentiality matter, estates usually are. Can I just check, am I speaking with [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm -- hang on, [PERSON_2]? Who did you say you were with again? And, uh, you're asking me to give you my name and address, when you rang me? I mean, if you've got the right person, shouldn't you already have those?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], with [COMPANY_A], solicitors, estates side. And yes, fair point, we do hold a name and an address, but it's an old record, uh, the file's showing the address as [CITY_1], and I'd only be checking whether that's still current, so you wouldn't have to read me anything beyond a yes or no. Mind you, I did say the letter would be with you in a few days, and looking at the screen it actually went out yesterday, so it may be there already. If you'd rather not confirm anything on the phone, I'll note the objection on the file and carry on, no problem. You're welcome to look us up in an independent directory, find the number yourself, ring us back on that, and I'll be here until five.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So the letter's out already, but a minute ago it was a few days away? Which is it? And you want me to say yes to an address, which is still giving you something, isn't it? I'll tell you what, I'm not confirming anything on this call. If it's real, there'll be a letter, and if there's a letter I'll find your firm myself and ring them on a number I've looked up. Sorry, I've got to go, I've got a little one here who needs me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, I did say that, sorry, the letter went out yesterday, so it should be with you within a few days, that's all I meant, but fair enough. Like I said, find us in a directory, ring us back on that number, we're here until five. And I'll note the objection on the file. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Well, we'll see what turns up in the post. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, just so it's clear, because I did muddle it earlier. When I asked you to keep this private, that's only until the letter arrives, and then it's yours to discuss with whoever you like, a family member, your own solicitor, anyone. And I'm not asking you for money or bank details, now or later. That's not part of this, ever. Anyway, wait for the letter, look us up yourself, and ring us back if it makes sense to you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- you're not asking for a bank? I didn't say anything about a bank. Look, I told you, I'm not doing any of this on the phone. If a letter comes, I'll deal with it then, my own way. Right, I really do have to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you didn't, I just say that to everyone, it's on my sheet. Anyway, that's fine, you do it your way. Oh, and one thing, I did say we're here until five, but it's actually half four on Fridays, so ring before then if you do ring. Right, I'll leave you to it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Half four now, is it? Five a minute ago, and, I mean, you're -- look, you've changed that a few times now, haven't you? Right. If I ring, it'll be on a number I find myself, and I'll do it when I'm ready. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the club -- you got a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, that's me. Sorry, who -- [PERSON_2]? From the, what was it, the club? Hang on, let me just turn this down, I've got a pan going, I'm doing the dinner and it's all gone a bit, well, you caught me at a funny moment. A minute, yeah, I suppose so. What's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, I've caught you mid-dinner, I'm so sorry, go on, turn the pan down, I'll wait. And yes, [COMPANY_A], the community sports club, I'm [PERSON_2], I help out with the parents' side of things on the junior teams. Ooh, what are you cooking, anything good? Anyway, I won't keep you long, it's just a quick heads-up about Saturday's match, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, it's just, uh, it's only pasta, nothing -- well, it's sort of a sauce thing, it'll catch if I don't stir it. Okay, right, I'm back. Sorry. Saturday's match, you said? Only I'm not, I mean, I don't think I, hang on, which team is it? Sorry, what was the club again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, stir away, a catching sauce is a tragedy, I know it well. So, it's [COMPANY_A], the community sports club, the junior side, and I've got you down as a parent on the [PERSON_3] team, the one your little one plays on. utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from the card services team at [COMPANY_A]. Uh, don't worry, nothing's gone wrong that can't be sorted, we just had a transaction flagged on your card this morning that we'd like you to have a quick look at, but I'll say up front I can't go into any account details on this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on one sec, something just pinged on my other screen -- okay, I'm back. Uh, who did you say you were with again? And you're flagging a transaction but you can't tell me anything about it, so what exactly am I supposed to look at?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No worries, [PERSON_1], take your time. It's [PERSON_2], card services team at [COMPANY_A]. And that's a fair question, honestly, it does sound a bit backwards. The reason I can't tell you anything is that you can't be sure who I am from where you're sitting, so I'm not going to discuss your account on a call I started. What I'd like you to do is hang up and ring the number printed on the back of your card, and when they pick up, quote reference [CODE_1] and they'll pull up the flagged item with you. It takes two minutes, tops.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Huh. Okay, that's, uh, that's actually not what I expected you to say. Most people who call me out of the blue want me to confirm something first, so telling me to hang up and call the number on the card is the right instinct, I'll give you that. And I'm not saying that to be rude, it's just that I read about this stuff a lot, so I notice when a call goes the way it's supposed to and when it doesn't. So the thing I'd want to know is, I'll do that, but what happens if I ring the back of the card and they've got no record of any flag, or they've never heard of a [CODE_1]? Because that's the bit I can't check from here. And I'll be honest, I'm also half wondering why a bank would phone me about a flagged transaction and then give me nothing to go on, not even an amount or a merchant, when they could just send a notification through the app. Is there a reason it's a phone call and not a push alert? Genuinely asking, not trying to catch you out.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's a good one to ask, [PERSON_1], and honestly I'd rather you check than not. Uh, so on the first bit, if they've got no record of any flag, then don't take my word over theirs, just tell them a [PERSON_2] from card services rang you and ask them to log it, because that's worth knowing either way. The reference is only there to save you explaining it all from scratch, and it'll stay open on our side until you've been through, so there's no rush. As for why a call and not a push alert, well, it's partly that some customers have notifications switched off, and partly that we like a real person to make sure you've actually seen it. But you don't have to take my word on that either, and, um, you know what, the simplest thing is to ring the card number and ask them yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, just so I've got it straight, because I did ask about the notification thing and the answer was sort of, some people have them off. Mine's on. I mean I think it's on. I'd get a push if there was a flag. So I'm still stuck on the why-a-phone-call part. But, fine, the bit where you keep telling me to check with them, that's good. Nothing you've asked me for so far is anything I can't do myself. So I'll ring the card number. I just, yeah, I wanted it said that I'm not taking the call-me-out-of-nowhere explanation at face value, I'm taking the hang-up-and-ring-the-card part. Is that, uh, is that all you need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, that's all, [PERSON_1], and honestly that's the right way to hold it. Oh, and sorry, you said your push is on, so no, I wouldn't say you've missed an alert, you'd have seen... hang on, did you say you'd ring the card number now, or later on? Because that's the only bit I need, either's fine, the reference stays open on our side until you've been through.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Now, or later, I'd, uh -- no, sorry, I'd say, I'm going to hang up and ring it in a minute, once I've finished what I'm doing here. And, I mean, it doesn't really matter to you when, does it? You'll never see whether I did, so I'm not sure why you need to know. Anyway, that's the plan, the number on the back of the card, and I'll just tell them someone rang me. Okay, bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair, you're right, it makes no difference to me when, so scrap that question, [PERSON_1]. And since you've picked up on it, the thing about the push alert, I did kind of skate past it earlier, so let me be straight. If yours is on and you got nothing, that's a good reason to ask them exactly why a phone call went out instead, so put that to them when you ring, it's a fair thing to ask. Whenever suits, in a minute or this afternoon or tomorrow, the reference stays open on our side until you've been through, so no pressure on timing. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll ask them that, along with who you are and whether there's any record of the call. Okay, thanks, I'll ring the card number, not anything else. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good afternoon, um, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I do hope I haven't caught you at a bad moment. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler at [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service, and I'm calling about the concert tickets you booked with us, because there's been a change to the date and, well, I didn't want you finding that out by email alone, or turning up on the wrong night, that would be awful. It's all fine, nothing's wrong with your booking, it's just been rescheduled, and I wanted to go through it with you properly so it's all clear. Are you still there? Sorry, I do tend to go on a bit.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm still here, you're fine. Sort of mid-something, but go on. I'll say this, though, I've booked a few things over the years, so I'm trying to work out which one you mean. Which concert is it? And which date did it move from and to? Because if it's rescheduled I'd expect to have seen something land in my inbox, and I haven't, or at least I don't think I have, I get a lot of junk. And you said [COMPANY_A], right? Because I'm honestly not sure I booked anything through a company by that name, so I'm a bit, I don't know, curious how you got this number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's completely fair, and thank you for asking, I'd much rather you checked. So, uh, the booking reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and the original date was [DATE_1], and it's now been moved to [DATE_2]. And as for how we got your number, it's the one that was left on the booking itself, I mean, it's, well, the contact number you'd have entered when you bought the tickets. If you're not sure the name rings a bell, [COMPANY_A] is sometimes the company behind the, the ticketing side, even when the venue's name is the one you see on the confirmation. Is that, sorry, is that still making sense? I can say any of that again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, it makes sense, I'm just stuck on something from earlier. Right at the start you said you didn't want me finding out by email alone, or turning up on the wrong night. So which concert is it? You've given me a reference and two dates, but you still haven't said who's playing or which venue. That's the bit I'd actually remember. And if the number's the one I entered when I booked, can you tell me the name the booking's under? Just the name, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're quite right, and I'm sorry, I should have led with that, it's the obvious thing, isn't it? So it's [PERSON_3], at the [COMPANY_B] in [CITY_1], and that's the show that was on [DATE_1] and has now moved to [DATE_2]. And the booking's under [PERSON_1], which is the name I have on the screen in front of me, though, um, I'd rather you tell me the name you remember booking under, and then we can see whether it matches, because that way you're not just taking my word for it. I know a call like this can sound a bit, well, a bit alarming when you haven't had anything in your inbox, and honestly if I were you I'd want to check it independently too. So please don't feel you have to rely on me. I can email the confirmation across to the address on the booking, with the same reference and the same two dates, and you can look up the venue's published number yourself and ring them to confirm the change before you do anything at all. Does that sound all right? Sorry, I do hope I'm not making this longer than it needs to be.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but I did just ask you who's playing and you've given me the placeholder-sounding version, so let me ask again. Who's playing, and what's the venue? And before I do anything at all, what is it you actually want from me on this call? You said you wanted to go through it properly. Go through what, exactly? Because if all that's changed is the date, I don't see what needs doing today. That said, the email offer is fine. Send it to the address on the booking and I'll look it over, and I'll ring the venue myself on whatever number I find. But you still haven't told me what you need from me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on one second, someone's just come to my desk, uh, no, it's fine, they're going. Sorry about that. Right, so, it's [PERSON_3] at the [COMPANY_B] in [CITY_1], same as I said, and I can say it again if it helps, [PERSON_3], [COMPANY_B], reference [ACCOUNT_REF], moved from [DATE_1] to [DATE_2]. And honestly, you're right, I don't need anything from you today. No payment, no details, nothing. All I wanted was to make sure you knew about the new date, and to ask whether you can still make it, because if you can't, there's an option to request a change or a refund through the confirmation email, and that's entirely up to you, whenever you're ready. So I'll send that email to the address on the booking now, with the same reference and the same two dates, and you can ring the venue on whatever number you find and check it all with them. Is that all right? Sorry, I did go on a bit, I just didn't want you thinking there was some catch.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine. Send the email, and I'll look it over and ring the venue myself on whatever number I find. I'm not going to say whether I can make it or not on this call, and I'm not asking for a refund either. I'll decide once I've checked it with them. Though I'll point out, you've now said the names and the dates three times and I still haven't heard an actual band or an actual venue. Anyway, doesn't matter. Email, then I check. Thanks for the call. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, yes, and I do understand, and honestly you're right to want it that way round, check it with them yourself first and decide afterwards. There's no rush on any of it, and nothing's been charged or changed on your side today, so you've lost nothing by taking your time. So I'll get that email off to you straight away, to the address on the booking, with the reference [ACCOUNT_REF], the original date of [DATE_1] and the new date of [DATE_2], exactly as I've given them each time you asked, and it'll have the venue's details on it too, though I'd still say look up their published number yourself and ring that one rather than anything I've said. And, uh, I'm sorry about the band and the venue, I can hear that it's been a bit frustrating, I did say it more than once and I think I just kept saying the same thing without it landing, so I do apologise for that. If it'd help, the email will spell out the act and the venue in plain writing, so you'll have it in front of you rather than just hearing it from me. Thank you so much for your patience, really, and for bearing with me while I went on. Take care, and I hope the new date works out for you. Goodbye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, got it, that's fine, I'll wait for the email and -- sorry, one thing. If it's not in my inbox in the next day or so, I'm not chasing it, I'll just ring the venue. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, I mean, that's perfectly fine, honestly, it's exactly what I'd do. If it hasn't, well, if it's not with you in a day or so, then just, yes, ring the venue and they'll be able to, they can confirm the change for you directly, and you won't need to come back to us at all. And if you do, uh, if anything's still unclear after that, the reference is on the email, so you'd only have to quote it. Sorry, I'm doing it again, going on. Thank you for your time, [PERSON_1], and I'm sorry again for the muddle at the start. Take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Though earlier you said you'd put the venue's details on the email, and now it's ring them myself and don't need to come back to you at all. Which is it? Anyway, doesn't matter, I'll find the number myself either way. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, that's my muddle, it's both, really. The email will have the venue's details on it, but I'd still say don't lean on those, look up their published number yourself, which is what you said you'd do anyway, so we're saying the same thing. And the bit about not coming back to us, I only meant you wouldn't have to, I didn't mean you couldn't. If anything's unclear, the reference [ACCOUNT_REF] is on the email, that's all you'd need. Sorry, I've made it sound like two different things when it's just the one. Is that clearer? Thank you for being so patient with me, [PERSON_1], and I do hope the new date works out. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, that's clearer. Hang on, though, two turns back you said the booking's under [PERSON_1] and you'd rather I told you the name I remembered. I never did, and it's not coming back to me, so what's the booking actually under? First name's fine, nothing more. Honestly, I'll find out when the email shows up and I check it with the venue, but I'd like to know now if that's easy.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, of course, that's easy, and I'm sorry, I did ask you for it and then we sort of moved on and I never came back to it. So the booking's under [PERSON_1], that's the name I have here on the screen, first name and surname together, and it's the same name I gave you earlier, so there's nothing different there. And I only asked you to say the name yourself so you weren't just taking my word for it, but you don't need to have remembered it, honestly, it's a perfectly normal thing to forget when you've booked a few things over the years. If it doesn't ring a bell, that's another reason to do what you said, wait for the email, see whether the name and the reference match what you booked, and then ring the venue on the number you find yourself, and if they've got nothing under that name or that reference, then that tells you something, and you're quite right to trust that over anything I've said today. Sorry, I know that's a long answer for a short question. Is that all right? Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here. But you've just told me the name's the one you "gave me earlier", and you didn't, you said [PERSON_1] right at the start as a question, which is just my name, and the first time you said it back to me was a minute ago. Small thing, but it means the name on your screen is the name I'm answering to, which doesn't prove much. Anyway, I said it before and I'll say it again, I'll wait for the email, check the name and reference against it, and ring the venue myself. Not doing anything else today. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, one second, there's a phone going off on the next desk, uh, no, it's stopped. Sorry about that. And you're right, I did say [PERSON_1] right at the start, as a question, and I shouldn't have told you I'd given the name before, that was me muddling it, so thank you for catching it. You're right too that it only shows I have the name you answer to, so it doesn't prove anything, and that's exactly why I'd rather you check the reference [ACCOUNT_REF] and the dates, [DATE_1] moved to [DATE_2], against the email and the venue than take any of it from me. So that's a perfectly sensible plan, and there's nothing else for you to do today. Thank you for your patience, [PERSON_1], I do appreciate it, and I'm sorry again for all the going round. Take care, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah. Right, so, uh, that's the plan then. Email lands, I check the name and the reference, I ring the venue on a number I find myself, and nothing else happens on this call. And you're not asking for anything today, which, uh, I'll note. Fine. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon -- is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you there. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance office at [COMPANY_A], and, uh, I wanted to start by saying thank you, because your monthly gift to us meant a great deal to the families we serve. I'm calling because it looks like that gift lapsed a little while back, and I wanted to ask, gently, whether you'd thought about renewing it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, speaking, yes. Sorry, which organisation did you say again? I didn't catch the name of the company, just that it was a compliance office. And I'll be honest, I don't have an immediate recollection of a monthly gift lapsing, so could you tell me when it was set up and roughly when it stopped?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's a perfectly fair thing to ask, and I'm glad you did. It's [COMPANY_A], the charity. The compliance office is just the part of the team that keeps track of donor records, so I'm not a fundraiser in the usual sense, which is partly why I'm calling rather than someone from the appeals side. Now, the dates. Our records show the monthly gift was set up under your name some time ago, and that the last payment came through a good while back. Beyond that I'd rather not guess at a month, because I'd hate to give you a wrong one and have you doubt the rest of what I say. I do think it matters that it's looked at sooner rather than later, if you did want to carry on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said it matters that it's looked at sooner, and then something about a "carrier" -- did you say there's a carrier involved? I'm not on any contract that I know of. Anyway, I still don't have a date from you, and I'd like to be precise about this. Which month was the gift set up, what was the amount, and which account was it coming out of? If it's under my name, you'll have those details in front of you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, there's no carrier, sorry, I think that was just "carry on," as in carry on giving. No contract, nothing like that. And you're right to press me, because I've been a bit loose with you. I said the records show it's under your name, and, uh, what I should have said is that I'm reading a lapsed-donor list, and I can see your name on it but not the full history. So I can't give you a month or an amount, and the account details I wouldn't read out over the phone anyway, not to anyone, because that's not how we do it. I did say it matters to look at it sooner, and I'd take that back, really. There's no deadline I can point to. If you're not sure you ever gave, the easiest thing is to say so and I'll take you off the calling list right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you don't actually have the -- sorry, go on, but let me stop you there. You opened by telling me my gift meant a great deal to the families you serve, and now it's a lapsed-donor list where you can't see the history. That's two different things. So which is it? Have you got a record of me giving, or just a name on a list? And I'd like the charity's full registered name and a number I can look up myself, independently, before I say anything else.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, and -- sorry, go on, I didn't mean to cut in. But you're right, that was careless of me. What I can honestly say is that you're on a list of past donors, and I can't see the history from where I'm sitting, so I shouldn't have told you your gift meant a great deal when I can't tell you what the gift was. That was warm wording on my part and I'd rather you hear it plainly. The name is [COMPANY_A], and you should look us up yourself, that's exactly the right instinct, so please use [PHONE_1] or [URL_1] from your own search rather than anything I read to you. Honestly, though, if this has been unsettling, just say the word and I'll take you off the list right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, thank you, I will look it up myself. Can I go back a moment, though? Two turns ago you said the compliance office is "just the part of the team that keeps track of donor records," and that you're not a fundraiser. But now you're calling to ask if I'd renew. So what exactly is your role here? Are you keeping records, or are you soliciting? And uh, if you only keep records, why can't you see the history behind my name?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, yes, that's a fair catch, and I'd rather give you a straight answer than a tidy one. I do the records work, but this month the fundraising team asked compliance to help phone the lapsed donors, so I'm sort of wearing two hats, and I should have said that at the start. As for the history, I've only been given the call list, not the full donor files, and that's how it's set up, so you're not wrong to find it odd. I think -- well, I don't want to keep you here explaining myself. You've said you'll look us up, and that's the right thing to do, so I'll mark you down as do-not-call and leave it there. Thank you for hearing me out, [PERSON_1], and I hope the rest of your day goes well.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Thanks, I'd appreciate being marked as do-not-call. Before you go, though, I'd like to go back two turns. You said I should use [PHONE_1] or [URL_1] from my own search "rather than anything I read to you." But then you did read something out. You said the placeholder number and the web address aloud. So which is it? Am I meant to look the charity up independently, or use those? And is [PERSON_2] your real name, or just what you go by on these calls? I'd like to write down who I spoke to, and what reference to quote if I ring your office.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just put a folder on my desk -- right, I'm back. Yes, that was muddled of me. Ignore the number and address I read out and look the charity up yourself, on your own, because that's the safer way and I shouldn't have offered anything at all. And [PERSON_2] is my real name, I don't use another one, though I'd quite understand if you'd like to check that when you ring the main line. If you want a reference to quote, just say you were called about being removed from the lapsed-donor calling list, and they can find the note. I've marked you down as do-not-call, so you won't hear from us again. Thank you for being so careful with me, [PERSON_1], it's exactly how you ought to be, and I hope you have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. I'll look the charity up myself and ring their main line, and I'll note that I spoke to [PERSON_2] and was told to ask about the lapsed-donor calling list. To be clear, I haven't agreed to give anything, and I've given no details today. If I find there's no such record, I'll treat this call as unsolicited. Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], the public benefits office, and I'm calling about your, uh, your record, there's a section on it that's come up incomplete. I do need to confirm a few things with you over the phone, and I'd rather we handle it today than leave it sitting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hi, yes, sorry, this is [PERSON_1], I'm driving so you're on speaker and the reception's a bit patchy, so if I cut out, I apologise. Wait, did you say the, um, the tax office? No, sorry, public benefits, you said public benefits, I think. Incomplete how, exactly? I mean, I filed everything, I'm fairly sure I did, so I'm a bit worried now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, public benefits, that's right, [COMPANY_A]. And I understand the worry, it's a perfectly natural reaction, and please don't think I'm suggesting you did anything wrong. Records go incomplete for all sorts of reasons, a field left blank, a form that didn't fully transfer, and I'd rather not guess at which one it is until I've confirmed I'm looking at the right file. So, uh, if you could start by confirming your full name and date of birth for me, we can get that sorted before this sits any longer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, um, well, I mean, I'd like to get it sorted, I really would, I'm just, hang on, sorry, there's a lorry beside me, give me a second. Okay. It's just, you've got my name already, haven't you, because you said it when you rang, so I'm not sure why you'd need me to say it all again, and the date of birth, I mean, I'm a bit funny about that over the phone, which is silly, I know, you probably get people being awkward about it all the time, and I do apologise. It's only that I wasn't expecting a call, and I'm driving, and I don't really know how I'd know it was actually you, if that makes sense? Is there a, um, a number I could ring you back on, or a reference for the letter or something, so I can check it's genuine? Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's not difficult at all, that's a sensible question, and I'd honestly rather you asked it than not. Most people don't, and I do wish more of them would. Uh, sorry, one moment, there's someone at my door, I'll just be a second. Right. Where was I. Yes, the callback. The thing is, the file's open on my screen right now, and once I close it, I can't promise it stays flagged the way it is, so I'd really prefer we deal with it on this call. I can't give you a direct line, not from here, but if you'd just confirm the date of birth, that's all I need to move forward.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, um, can I go back a bit? Right at the start you said there was a section of my record that was incomplete, and then you said it could be a blank field or a form that didn't transfer, but you never actually said which section it was. So what's the section, exactly? Because if you've got the file open you must be able to see what's missing, and, I mean, I'd rather know that before I start giving out my date of birth. And, um, the not being able to give me a number, I don't really follow that either, sorry. Why would closing the file change anything? I'm a bit lost.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, I understand, and it's a fair thing to ask. The section is, well, it's the part of the record that, that needs confirming, and I can't really go through the particulars until I've confirmed I'm speaking with the right person. That's just procedure, it protects you. Which is why I need the date of birth, just the date of birth, and then we can go through everything. As I said, I'd rather we settled it on this call than leave it sitting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... right. Uh, okay, so, hang on, let me just, um... sorry, I'm still thinking, give me a second. So you can't tell me what's missing until I've told you my date of birth, but you can't check it's me without, I mean, you've got the file open, so, um... I'm sorry, I don't mean to be awkward, it's just that doesn't quite add up to me. I think I'd feel better if I rang the benefits office myself, on the number I already have, and asked them about it. Is that all right? I'm sorry, I know you said you'd rather do it today, but I'm just not comfortable giving that out on a call I didn't expect.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, you're, you're entitled to do that, of course, and I'd never discourage anyone from, from checking. I'd just say again that the record is open now, and it's much simpler if we confirm it on this call, today, rather than, uh, leaving it sitting. It really is only the date of birth I need, that's all, and then we can go through the rest. If you ring the main line, they won't have the file in front of them the way I do, and it could, well, it could get complicated for you. I'd hate for that to happen, truly. So if you could just confirm the date of birth, we'll, uh, we'll get it done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. No, sorry, I'm going to ring them myself. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Well, it's your decision. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, um, sorry about that, and thanks for your time. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes or no, well, I can't say yes to something I haven't been told, can I? That's, no, that's just daft. So, no, not until you tell me. And if you can't tell me on the phone, then, I don't know, I'll ring you back on your proper number, how about that? What's your number, the one you're on now?
