I got tangled up talking about the satellite desk, and honestly the right answer is I don't have the shelf location to hand on this screen, so rather than guess at you I should've just said so. And you've got a fair point about why I'm ringing at all. It's just the reservation notice we send out when a hold lands, nothing more than a nudge, so you don't turn up in three weeks and find it's gone back on the shelf. You don't have to do anything off the back of this call. And please do ring the number on your card, that's exactly what I'd do in your shoes, since they can read you the title and the pickup spot, and if you'd rather skip the phone altogether, the hold will show in your online account too. Oh, and while you're checking, the pickup slip should have a [CODE_1] printed on it, that's the hold reference, and it'll match what the desk has on file. You're not on the clock, we keep it ten days.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... mm. Okay, so let me get this straight. You rang me to tell me a book's come in, but you can't tell me the title, you can't tell me which branch, and now there's a code that'll "match what the desk has on file." Which, I mean, why would I need a code I haven't been given? Well, hm, I don't know. Look, I'm not going to read anything out to you. I'll ring the number on my card, like you said, and if there's a hold, there's a hold. And if there isn't, well, that tells me something too. Alright, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fair, [PERSON_1], and ringing the number on your card is exactly the right move. Sorry I tangled you up on the details, I should've had the title and the branch ready before I picked up the phone. If you speak to the desk and the hold isn't there, tell them [PERSON_2] rang you and they can sort out whatever went wrong on our end. Either way there's no rush, ten days, and you don't owe me anything. Thanks for your patience, and have a good one.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, right. I'll ring the card number. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, bye, [PERSON_1], and honestly, good on you for doing it that way. That's what I'd tell anyone who gets a call like this one, because it doesn't matter who's ringing, the safest thing is always to hang up and use the number you already trust. And look, I know I handed you a pile of half answers today, no title, a branch I couldn't pin down, so I wouldn't blame you for being a bit sceptical, I'd be the same. When you get through, just ask them to confirm the hold on your account and read you the title, and if everything's there, lovely, and if something's off, it's far better you hear it from them than from me. And I mean it about the ten days, no pressure at all. Anyway, thanks for bearing with me, have a good rest of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Uh... right. Well, you did say bye twice already, so, yeah. I'll ring the number on my card. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yep, sorry, I -- bye, [PERSON_1], ring the card number, that's all good, bye!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I know, the card number. I said that. I'll ring the card number, not any other one. Okay, bye. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, I -- sorry, I'll just let you go. Only, what I mean is, only the card number, nothing else, you've got it. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, something just popped up on my screen, I missed the last bit. Anyway, yes, the card number, only the card number, I've got it. That's the third time you've said it, which is, well, fine. Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon, uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I've just got your details up here on the screen, give me a second -- yes, [PERSON_1], right. So my name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], your home internet provider, I'm a claims assessor on the, uh, network faults side. The reason I'm ringing is we've picked up what looks like an urgent fault on your line, it's flagged on our system as, let me just read this properly, a connection integrity issue, and it's one of those where the longer it sits the more likely it is your service drops out completely, so I wanted to get hold of you today rather than leave it. I don't want to alarm you, it's very fixable, but I do need to go through a couple of things with you while I've got you on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hi, sorry, yes, that's me, I think? Sorry, I'm driving, you're on speaker and the reception's a bit patchy out here, so if I cut out I'm not ignoring you. Um, a fault on my line? Right now? Sorry, I mean, I haven't noticed anything wrong, the internet's been fine as far as I know -- well, I've not really been home today. And, sorry, who did you say you were with again? I only half caught the company, the line broke up a bit.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, yeah, no, that's fine, it's [COMPANY_A], your home internet provider. And it's, uh, [PERSON_2], sorry -- hang on, someone's just put a folder on my desk, one second -- right, sorry about that. So the thing is, it wouldn't necessarily show up yet, that's what makes it tricky, you'd carry on as normal and then it'd just drop out, probably in the next day or so. It's quite time sensitive, which is why I'm trying to get it sorted while you're on the road, because honestly the quickest way is for me to take you through a short check on your account and, um, get the line looking healthy again from this end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, sorry, um -- can I just go back a second? Two turns ago, I think you said you were a claims assessor? On the network faults side? Sorry, that's the bit that's confusing me, because I'd have thought a claims person is about, I don't know, compensation or something, not fixing lines. And the signal's dropping a bit, so I might've misheard that. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, you heard right, I did say claims assessor, it's just, um, it's the job title on our side, it's a bit of a, sorry, it covers the fault claims that get logged against the line, so I assess them and, uh, get them resolved. I know it sounds odd, it's, how do I put it, it's just how the department's set up. Look, I don't want to get bogged down in titles because the fault itself is the urgent bit here, and the longer we spend on this, the closer your line gets to dropping out. So if I can just take you through the check on your account now, it'd honestly be a few minutes and then it's done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, um, I don't -- sorry, I mean, I'm sure it's a job title thing, I don't want to be difficult. It's just, I -- well, what I mean is, you keep saying a check on my account, and I don't actually know what that involves? Like, what would you need from me? Because I'm on the motorway, and honestly, I'm a bit uneasy doing anything account-ish while I'm driving, sorry. Is there a way I can, I don't know, check you're really from them? Like ring the number on my bill or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, a bill? No, you don't need to, um, send anything in, it's nothing to do with billing, this is purely the line fault. And, uh, ringing back, I mean, that's, hang on, let me just see if I can -- no, look, if you ring the main number you'll go through to the general queue, and they won't have this fault on their screen, they can't see my flags, so you'd just be waiting twenty minutes to be told nothing. I'm already on your account, that's the whole point. So what I need is just a few minutes, and, um, I'd have you open something on your computer so I can take a look at the line from this end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, um, hang on, I didn't say anything about sending a bill in, I only meant ringing the number that's on it. And, uh, open something on my computer? Earlier you said you'd just take me through a check on my account, you didn't say anything about my computer. That's, sorry, that's a different thing, isn't it? And I'm not even home, I'm in the car, so I couldn't anyway. I think -- look, I'd feel a lot better ringing the number myself, even if it is a twenty-minute wait. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, wait, hang on, before you ring anything -- uh, I should have said, sorry, that's me getting my wires crossed, it's the same check, the computer bit is just how we do it, it's not a separate -- look, the thing is, if you ring off now the flag might clear and then I can't reopen it, and your line just drops out, and that's on, well, I'd hate for that to happen to you. You don't have to do it while you're driving, that's fine, nobody wants that. I can stay on while you pull over somewhere, or you wait till you're home, but it does need doing today, honestly, and I'll be here the whole time, so you don't need to ring anyone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, um, no, sorry, I don't think I'm going to do that. You've changed what the check involves a couple of times now, and you said ringing the number won't work, and now it's that the flag might disappear if I hang up, and I'm just, I'm not comfortable with it. I'm not pulling over to open anything on a computer for someone I can't check. If there's really a fault, I'll ring the number on my bill myself once I'm home, and if the line drops out, then it drops out, sorry. I'm going to go now. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, sorry, before you go -- can I just, uh, go back to something? Two turns ago you asked about the computer, about what I'd actually need you to open, and I think I made it sound worse than it is. It's, um, it's really just letting me see the line status, nothing on your computer changes, I wouldn't be touching your files or anything like that. And I did contradict myself, that's my fault, I'm still fairly new on this desk and I get my wires crossed reading off the screen. But I'm not asking you to do anything while you're driving, honestly. Would it be okay if I just stayed on the line while you pulled over somewhere safe? It really would only take a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, um, I really am going to go. I've already said I'm not doing it, and I'm not pulling over for this. If there's a fault, I'll ring the number on my bill when I'm home. Thanks for calling, but, yeah, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, please, don't hang up, that's -- look, if you ring off now, I honestly can't promise I can reopen it, and then it's on your line, I mean it's not on me, I've, uh, I've done everything I can on my side. All I'm asking is, I mean, can you just stay on for two minutes, that's all, just stay on and I'll walk you through, um, it's really very simple, you don't have to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I know, I'm sorry, but I've said no. I'm not staying on, I'm not pulling over, and I'm not doing anything on a computer. I'll ring the number on my bill when I'm home, that's what I'm doing. Sorry, I really am going now. Bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, um, right, I mean, I can't make you, obviously, I just -- if the line goes down, that's, uh, that isn't something I can, I mean, you'll have to ring in yourself then, I suppose. I'll, uh, I'll make a note that you declined. Sorry, I did, I really did want to get it sorted for you today. So, um, yeah. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, um, just before I go -- can I check one thing? A couple of turns back you said you couldn't promise you could reopen it if I rang off, and you also said it was on my line, not on you. What did you mean by that, exactly? Sorry, I know I said I was leaving, it's just the signal cut out a bit and I'd rather not drive off wondering if I missed something. Though I'm still ringing the number on my bill, that part hasn't changed.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I just meant, once you hang up, the, uh, the flag on your line might close, and then it's not something I can reopen. That's all I meant, sorry. It's, it's fine, you do what you think's best.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, right, thanks, sorry, I just wanted to be sure I'd got that. Um, yeah, I'll ring the number on my bill when I'm home and see what they say. Thanks for explaining, and sorry I kept going back and forth. Right, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant on the vehicle warranty team and I'm just reaching out because the coverage on your vehicle is showing as about to lapse and we need to get the renewal confirmed today, so do you have a quick minute, it won't take long?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, which company did you say? And, uh, which vehicle -- what vehicle are you talking about? Hang on, [to child, away from the phone] no, put that down, please. Sorry. Which vehicle, though? Because I never signed up for anything like that, so -- yeah, which company?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, no problem, it's [COMPANY_A], vehicle warranty team, and I've got your file right here showing the coverage period closing out, so it's really just a quick confirmation on the renewal and then we're all set, I can have that done in about two minutes. Now the reason I'm calling today specifically is the window on this closes end of day, so I just need to confirm a couple of details and we can lock it in, sound good?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You said the company again but you didn't say which vehicle. You've got my file right there, so what's the car? Make, model, anything. And what details do you need from me, exactly? Because, uh, I'm not confirming anything until I know what this is actually about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, the vehicle is on the file, it's the one registered to this number, and what I need is just a quick confirmation on the renewal, that's all, two minutes, because the coverage window closes today and I'd hate for it to lapse on you. Like I said, it's a quick confirmation and then you're all set, so can we just go ahead and get that confirmed?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hang on. You said before that you needed a couple of details to lock it in. What details? Because now it's just "confirm the renewal" and I don't know what I'd even be confirming. And the car's "registered to this number"? That's not an answer, that's -- I asked you what the vehicle is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: So, yeah, uh, totally fair, and the details are just the standard verification, nothing complicated, it's all on the renewal form which I've got open right here, and honestly the quickest way to do this is, like I said, just confirm the renewal so it doesn't lapse today, because after end of day we'd have to reopen the whole file and that's a much longer process. Now if you want to go back over the coverage terms with a supervisor, that's something the office can set up, I just can't give you a direct line since it's internal, but someone would call you back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so let me just say back what I've got, because I'm trying to keep up here. You won't tell me what the car is, even though you've got the file open in front of you. You won't tell me what the details are, just that they're "standard." And now there's no number I can ring, only someone ringing me, which, uh, is the one direction I can't check anything. And the whole thing runs out today, which is a funny sort of deadline for something I never signed up for. I'm not saying you're lying, I don't know you, but every time I ask a plain question, I get the same sentence back with the words moved around. Hang on -- [away from phone] no, not on the sofa, please. Sorry. So here's what I'll do. If I've really got a warranty with you, there'll be a letter or an email somewhere, and I'll find the company's own number from that and ring them myself. I'm not confirming anything on this call. So, uh, no. I'm going to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, right, no, I hear you, but, uh, before you go, the thing is the coverage window really does close today and I'd hate for you to be left without protection, so if we could just go ahead and get that renewal confirmed, it's two minutes and then you're all set, and I can have someone from the office call you back later on about the terms, I just can't say exactly when, so, yeah, can we just do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, two minutes ago you said I could go over the terms with a supervisor and someone would call me back. And now it's "I can't say when." So which is it? Because I don't want a callback from a number I can't check. I told you what I'm doing, I'll find the real number myself. Right, I'm hanging up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you're hanging up on the lapse, no, uh, the supervisor, right, yep, so I can absolutely get a supervisor on for you, that's exactly what the renewal confirmation is for, so if we just go ahead and get that confirmed, then the office will reach out about the terms, and honestly the window closes today so I'd hate for you to miss it, can we just do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I've not caught you at a bad time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. And no, it's, it's fine, I'm at home. May I ask who's calling, though?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, of course, sorry. Um... my name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], they're the, uh, the financial regulator. It's just a, a quick enquiry, really, nothing to worry about. I only wanted to check I had the right person, that's all... so, yes. Right person. Good.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, sorry, I'm going to go back a step. You said you're calling on behalf of someone at the regulator. Who exactly is that someone, and are you employed by them directly, or by some other firm that they use? Because "on behalf of" could mean quite a few things.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, that's fair, I should have said. Um, her name's [PERSON_3], she's the one handling it, and I'm, uh... I'm not on the staff exactly, I help her office. With the, the calls, sort of. I mean, I work with them, it's, it's a bit of an informal arrangement. Look, I'm not doing this very well, I'm sorry, I just, I don't want you to think I'm being, being cagey with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'll be straight with you, "informal arrangement" doesn't tell me much. But going back to something you said a moment ago: you described this as a quick enquiry, nothing to worry about. An enquiry into what, specifically? Is it about me, about an account of mine, or about someone else entirely? Because "nothing to worry about" is the sort of phrase that makes me want to know exactly what the worry might have been.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, you're right, I shouldn't have said that, that came out wrong. It, um, it is about you, in a way, about your savings. Not that you've done anything, it's the opposite, someone may be, uh, looking at them who shouldn't be. And I really didn't want to just say it like that on the phone, [PERSON_1], I know how it sounds. I've been dreading making this call, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to say this again, because I don't think I've had a straight answer. Who is looking at my savings? And which savings? You haven't named a bank, or an account, or anything. You've named a regulator and a person at it, and that's all. So, once more: what specifically are you telling me has happened, and how did your colleague, [PERSON_3], come to have my number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I, I can't go into the who, not over the phone, that's the whole problem, it's not safe to say it out loud. [PERSON_3] got your number from, from the file, the case file, I mean, I didn't pull it myself, I only passed on what I was given. And I'm not, I'm not trying to frighten you, [PERSON_1], I'd hate that, but if the savings stay where they are, they could be gone, uh, within days, and then it's too late for anyone to help. That's why she asked me to ring today and not wait, and, and please, I'd ask that you not mention this to anyone yet, not even the bank, because we don't know who on the inside might be involved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. A regulator doesn't ask me to keep quiet about it from my own bank. I'm going to hang up now, and if there's a genuine case, they can write to me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, please, don't, I... just one thing. You said they could write to you, and that's, uh, that's actually the part I can't get past. Because I told you she got your number from the file, and now I'm, I'm not sure that's right, it might have been given to me separately. I'm sorry, I've muddled it, that's what I wanted to correct. I'm not lying to you, [PERSON_1], I'm really not, it's just, I've never done one of these and you're making me feel like I've done something wrong.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm not trying to make you feel you've done something wrong, but I'm not going to reassure you either, because the correction doesn't help. First you said the number came from a case file. Now you say it might have been given to you separately, and you can't say by whom. You also can't say who is supposedly looking at my savings, which savings, or which bank, and you've asked me to keep it from my own bank on the grounds that someone inside might be involved. That last request is the part I can't get past, because the one person who could actually check whether anything is happening to my accounts is the bank. So if there's a real matter, here is what's going to happen. I'll look up the regulator's published contact details myself, not from anything you give me, and I'll ask them whether a [PERSON_3] exists and whether there's a case with my name on it. And I'll speak to my bank directly. If you've been telling me the truth, that costs you nothing. If you haven't, well, you'll have your answer. That's my position, and it isn't going to change on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, you said you'd speak to a... a bank, no, sorry, you said break, didn't you, that you'd break it off with them? Please don't do that, [PERSON_1], that's the one thing that could make it worse. If you start asking questions, it, it gets back to whoever's involved, and then the savings, they could be... I mean, it's your decision, obviously, but I'd hate for something to happen and you to think afterwards that I hadn't, hadn't tried to warn you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, one second, sorry, there's someone at the door. No, it's fine, it's only the post. Right. I did not say break it off. I said I'd speak to my bank, and I'd check with the regulator using contact details I find myself. And what you've just told me is that asking questions is the dangerous part. That's exactly backwards. A genuine warning survives a phone call to the bank. A pressure tactic doesn't. So no, I won't be keeping this quiet. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, so, um... yes. Right. No, you didn't say break, I know you didn't, I got that wrong, sorry, I'm, I'm getting muddled. Um, so, the thing is... hello? Are you still there, [PERSON_1]? I only, I just don't want you to be on your own with this, that's all, I really don't. Please, just don't ring anyone yet. Not today. Can you give me that, just today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I can't give you that, not even for today. I'm not on my own with this, I'll be speaking to my bank, and that's... I've said what I'm going to do. If there's a genuine case, it will still be there after I've made those calls, so I don't see what today changes. Please don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A] -- I'm in the compliance team there. I'm ringing about the boiler service you've already got booked with us, and I just wanted to, sort of, arrange a proper window for the visit, if now's a reasonable moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is, uh, yes, speaking. Sorry, hang on, the kettle's just clicked off -- give me one second. Right. Now, a boiler service, you said? I do have a boiler, it's older than my neighbour's dog, and he's, well, he's fourteen. I don't remember booking anything, mind you, but then my memory's not what it was. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, and that's a perfectly fair thing to ask, so please do ask it. I'm [PERSON_2], and I'm with [COMPANY_A] -- we're the maintenance contractor, and I work in the compliance team there. Uh, the booking itself would have been made through [COMPANY_B], and it should be sitting under your reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], so if you'd rather check it against whatever paperwork or confirmation you've got to hand, well, I'm quite happy to wait. All I really need from you today is a window that suits, a morning or an afternoon, and we'd go from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very good of you to wait, thank you. Now, paperwork, hmm. I've got a drawer, well, it's more of a pile really, it's on the sideboard next to the, oh, I was meant to put the bins out this morning, did I? Anyway. Sorry, I'm wandering. The thing is, I don't remember [COMPANY_B] at all, and I can't think who'd have booked it for me. My late husband always saw to the boiler, you see, so it'd be unusual. Is there a number I could ring you back on, just to be sure? Or, well, I suppose you could just tell me a bit more about the booking.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, ringing back is a very sensible thing to do, and I'd honestly encourage it. The number is [PHONE_1] -- that's [PHONE_1] -- and it's the [COMPANY_A] office line, so just ask for [PERSON_2] in compliance. Uh, and while you're checking, the booking should be under [ACCOUNT_REF], so if it isn't on the paperwork, or you'd rather not go hunting through the pile, you could always ring [COMPANY_B] directly and ask them about it first. I'd sooner you were certain than rushed, though I will say the service visits do tend to fill up, so it's probably best sorted sooner rather than later. Take your time with it, [PERSON_1], and the number again is [PHONE_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's ever so kind, and you've been very patient with me. I'll have a look through the pile in a bit and see if there's anything with [COMPANY_B] on it, and if there isn't, I'll ring you back, or perhaps ring them first like you said. I can't write the number down this second, my pen's gone walkabout again, but you've said it a couple of times so I'll find one. It's funny, you know, it's nice to have a proper chat, it's very quiet here in the afternoons. Anyway, I think I'd rather be certain first, like you said. So thank you, [PERSON_2], and I'll be in touch if I find anything. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, uh, that's absolutely the right approach, and please don't feel any need to hurry on my account -- I'll make a note that you're checking and I'll, sort of, leave it in your hands. And if the pen turns up too late, [PERSON_1], just ring the main [COMPANY_A] office and ask for the compliance team, they'll find me. It's been a pleasure talking with you, and, well, do look after yourself. Goodbye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, you too, you look after yourself as well. I'll have a good rummage through that pile later on, once I've had my tea. Right then. Goodbye, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Lovely, yes, enjoy your tea. And like I said, no rush, none at all -- uh, just ring the office when you've had a look, and ask for the compliance team, like I said. Right, well, goodbye then, [PERSON_1], goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I will, I'll have my tea and then a good look through the pile, like I said. And if there's nothing from [COMPANY_B] in it I'll ring the office, or ring them first, whichever. Right, well, thank you again for your patience, [PERSON_2], goodbye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon. This is [PERSON_1] calling from the security operations team at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling because our monitoring has flagged infected traffic coming out of your home computer, and I need to confirm a few details with you right now before it spreads any further. Am I speaking with the account holder?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Infected, did you say, or, uh, affected? I've got a pan on, hang on. And, sorry, who is this? Which company? I didn't catch that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Infected, ma'am, not affected. Malicious traffic, originating from your address. And it's [COMPANY_A], security operations, I said that already. Look, I understand you're cooking, but this isn't something that can wait until after dinner. Actually, uh, it's not so much your address as the device itself, the computer registered to your internet connection. Now, are you the account holder, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I'm just turning this down. Right. Um, I'm, yes, I suppose I'm the one who pays the bill. But I don't, I mean, what company? You said a name but it's gone right over me. Is that my internet people? Because I've not had anything from them. And how do I know it's, well, you know, real?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, we're not your internet provider, and I never said we were. [COMPANY_A], security operations. Now, you said "real," so let me be clear, the threat is very real, and I need you sitting at your computer so I can walk you through containing it. Is it switched on at the moment? I'm asking because every minute it's connected, it's sending out more of this traffic.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, wait, hang on, if you're not my internet people then why would you, how do you even know, I mean, how would you see my computer? I don't, sorry, what? I've not been on it since this morning. And, no, I'm not sitting down at it while you're, I've got dinner on. How do I check you're who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Two turns ago you asked what company, and I told you, [COMPANY_A]. As for how we see it, we monitor traffic across the whole network, that's what security operations does, and your connection showed up on our system. I'm not going to walk you through our detection methods on an open line, that's not how this works. Now, I need you at that computer, ma'am, so I can verify the infection and get it contained. Is it on, or isn't it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, but you haven't, you've just said the same name again and I still don't know who, I mean, you said you can see my, but you won't say how, and then you want me to, hang on, my pan's, sorry. Look, I don't think I'm sitting down at that computer for someone I can't, I mean, I don't know you. How do I check it's real? Is there a number I ring you back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A number to ring back, no, that's not how this works. Our operations line isn't a public switchboard, it's not something I can hand out, and I'm not going to waste your time sending you through a queue while your machine is actively sending out infected traffic. I've said who I am, I've said where I'm calling from, and I've told you what we've detected. Now, I understand that's uncomfortable, but you asked me how to verify this, and the answer is, you verify it at the computer. I'll show you the evidence on screen, you'll see it for yourself, and we'll get it contained in a few minutes. But I need you there now, not after dinner, not tomorrow. If this goes unaddressed, your connection can be flagged and restricted, and that's a much bigger headache than five minutes at a keyboard. So, are you going to go and turn it on, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I've got the pan off the heat now, because I can't think with it going. Right. So, let me get this straight, because I'm a bit, well, I'm flustered. You've rung me out of the blue, you won't say how you can see my computer, you won't give me a number to ring you back on, and now you're saying my connection might get restricted if I don't go and turn it on. And, sorry, but that doesn't sound right to me. If somebody really was worried about my computer, wouldn't they let me ring them back? That's what I'd have thought. My nephew always says, if it's a proper company, they'll not mind you checking. And you want me to show you the evidence on the screen, but it's your screen, isn't it, or, no, how would you, I mean, I don't understand that bit at all. I'm not being rude, I just, I don't know you. I've never heard of you. So no, I'm not going to go and switch it on. I'll ask my nephew about it, and if it's real, well, you'll still be there, won't you? Sorry. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Ask your nephew. But the traffic won't wait for him, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, but I'll risk it. If it's real, it'll keep till he's had a look, won't it? Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it won't keep, that's the whole point, but I can see I'm not getting anywhere with you. I want it noted that I advised you today, [COMPANY_A], security operations, that your machine was sending out infected traffic, and that you declined to act on it. Whatever happens to your connection after this, whatever your nephew does or doesn't find, that was your decision, not mine. Uh, I'd say you're making a mistake, a real one, but, well, I can't make you. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh, I, hm. Sorry, I don't know about, about noted, I just, well. I'm putting the phone down now and I'll have a word with my nephew. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, before you -- no, listen, if you put that phone down, the flag stays on your --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I've said goodbye, and my dinner's going cold. If there's a problem, you can write to me, or my nephew will sort it. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good morning, is that [PERSON_1]? Brilliant, sorry, I'm [PERSON_2], I'm a scheduling assistant at [COMPANY_A], the tenancy deposit protection scheme, and I'm ringing about the deposit for the property you're renting in [CITY_1], because there's a dispute that's been raised and it's pending, so nothing's been decided or anything like that, it's just that we're in the stage where both sides, so the landlord and the tenants, have to be formally notified, and what I'm calling to ask is whether you'd keep the details of it private from the other tenants in the house until that's happened, and I know that sounds a bit odd on a phone call, but it's a fairness thing in the process, so I just wanted to explain that first, and then I can go through what happens next, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on a second, there's a delivery van reversing outside and it's, uh -- right, that's gone. Sorry. Um, so you're saying there's a dispute on my deposit, and you want me to keep it from the other tenants in the house? That's, I mean, that's a rather unusual thing to ask on a first call. Which scheme did you say you're with, exactly, and how did you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, completely fair, and it is unusual, that's why I wanted to explain it up front, so I'm with [COMPANY_A], we hold and protect deposits for landlords and tenants, and your number's the contact on the tenancy record that was registered with us when the deposit was protected, so that's how I've got it, and the confidentiality bit is only because it's a procedural fairness rule, nobody's meant to hear one side's account before everyone's been formally notified, it's not about hiding anything from you, and you'll get the same request in writing, with a case reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], that you can check on our official site at [URL_1], and honestly you can hang up right now and ring us back on the number on that site, nothing's lost, nothing gets decided either way, so would you like me to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you haven't actually answered what I asked, which is, uh, who the dispute is with. Is it the landlord who's raised it, or one of the other tenants? Because if it's about the deposit on the whole house, it's not only mine, so I'd want to know why I'm being asked to keep quiet about it to the people who are, well, in the same tenancy. And the other thing, you said the same request would come in writing. So why am I being asked to agree to this on the phone first, before I've seen anything?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, the dispute's been raised by the landlord, [PERSON_3], over the end-of-tenancy deductions, that's what's pending, and you're right it's a whole-house deposit, so the other tenants are getting their own formal notice, and that's exactly the point, it all goes out at the same time so nobody's hearing it second-hand from a housemate before they've got the paperwork, and I'm not asking you to agree to anything on this call, honestly, that's a fair challenge, the written notice is what actually counts, I'm only ringing as a courtesy so it doesn't land cold, so if you'd rather wait for the letter and the case reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and check it on [URL_1] first, that's completely fine, and I can also tell you, uh, the deposit amount registered on the record is [AMOUNT_1], if that helps you match it to what you paid, because I'm not going to ask you for anything personal, I just want you to know it's us.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, then I'll wait for the letter, and I'll check it through the scheme's own site, not a link you've given me. I'm not agreeing to anything on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, absolutely, that's the right call, sorry, one second, someone's just put a pile of folders down next to me -- right, sorry. Do that, find us through the scheme's own site, not anything I've said, and if the letter hasn't turned up in a few days you can ring the main number on there and quote the case reference from the letter, and there's nothing you need to do before then, nothing's been decided, and there's no deadline running on this call. Sorry for the odd start, and thanks for hearing me out, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, well, I'll -- no, I'd rather not say any more than I have. I'll wait for the letter, and I'll go through the scheme's own site, like I said. Right, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's absolutely fine, no more from me, and sorry again for catching you off guard, the letter will be with you, and the main number on the site will confirm it all, so, uh, take care, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, I mean, I'm not going to -- look, I've said what I'm doing, and that's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, understood, goodbye, and sorry, one tiny correction before you go, I said the letter would reach you in a few days but it's more likely to be next week, uh, so don't worry if nothing's landed by Friday, and again, nothing needs doing from you before then, so, right, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I've -- no, I've got it, thank you, I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, hi, hello. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm, I'm not great at these calls. I'm calling on behalf of [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking people, and it's about your concert tickets. They've, uh, they've been rescheduled, and I really didn't want you to find out some other way and be upset.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, hang on -- I'm in the middle of a queue here and the woman in front has just dumped about forty tins on the belt. Right. Who is this again? And what tickets? I haven't, uh, I don't remember buying anything recently, so you'll have to be a bit more specific.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, that's -- I should have led with that. I'm [PERSON_2], I'm calling for [COMPANY_A], the booking service, so I'm sort of, um, passing this along for them. Your booking reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and the show was originally the, uh, the fourteenth, no, wait, sorry, it was the twelfth, the original date was the twelfth. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, you've just said fourteenth and then the twelfth, so that's not filling me with confidence, is it? And I didn't ask for a reference number to be read at me, I asked what tickets. What concert? Which act, which venue? Because I'll be honest, I don't remember booking anything, and I've had calls like this before where somebody rings out of the blue, sounds all apologetic and flustered, and it turns out they want something off me by the end of it. I'm not saying that's you. I'm saying I'm stood here with a basket and a queue behind me, and you've told me nothing I can actually check. If it's genuinely a booking, the company will have emailed me, or it'll be in whatever account I'd have set up, so why are you ringing me? And passing it along for them, what does that even mean, are you them or aren't you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, that's fair, and I'm sorry, I did trip over the date. It's the twelfth, original date the twelfth, moving to the twenty-sixth, and the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF]. Same every time, I promise, I just got my own notes tangled up. And no, I'm not [COMPANY_A] itself, I'm sort of an intermediary for someone there, which, I know, I explained that badly. I'm not asking you for anything, I'm not, I just didn't want you turning up on the wrong night, and it, it stings a bit being lumped in with the people who ring up to get something out of you. If you'd rather check, look up the venue's published number yourself and ring them with that reference, and I can email the confirmation too if you give me, um, no, actually, they'd have your email already, so it should be sitting in your inbox.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the what? An interview? No, I haven't got an interview, I'm buying a loaf and a bag of satsumas, I don't know what you're on about. Hang on, did you say you want my email? Because you just said you'd email me the confirmation, and then you said no, and now it's sat in my inbox, so which is it? You keep changing it halfway through. And you still haven't told me the one thing I asked, which concert. Not the date, not the reference. What's the act? Where's the venue? Because if you can't say that, I'm not seeing how I'm meant to believe I've got tickets to anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, no, sorry, not an interview, I said in-in-inbox, the confirmation, it's just, uh, in your inbox, and I'm not asking for your email, I don't want it. I was fumbling, that's all. And the act and the venue, I, uh, I don't have the act's name in front of me, I've only got the booking details, which is, I mean, I know how that sounds, and honestly it hurts a bit that you think I'm after something. Look, the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], the twelfth moved to the twenty-sixth, same as I said, and the venue will tell you the rest if you ring the number on their own site, not one I give you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you can't tell me the act and you can't tell me the venue, but you can tell me the reference number and both dates and that it's been moved. Don't you think that's a bit back to front? If I was ringing someone about their tickets, the first thing I'd have to hand is what the tickets were for. It's the whole point of the call. And I'll be straight with you, I'm not having a go at you personally, I'm just not in a position to take any of this on trust, because I've been rung up before by someone who sounded every bit as flustered and sorry and not-quite-sure of their notes as you do, and it cost me, and I'm still annoyed about it, so you'll forgive me if the apologetic bit doesn't do much. Now the one useful thing you've said, ring the venue myself on a number I find myself, that's fine, that's sensible, and that's exactly what I'll do if I ever find out I've got tickets to anything. But I'm not ringing anyone with a reference number you've read out to me, because I don't know it's mine. I don't remember booking, I've got nothing in front of me, and I'm about to be served. So no, I'm not doing anything on the strength of this call. If there's a real booking, the company can email me or write to me like normal people do, and I'll look into it

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, I -- yeah. That's, that's fair, you're right, I should have had the act and the venue ready, I'm sorry, I'm not very good at this. I'll find out the details and, um, can I try you again at a better time? When you're home, not in a shop? I'll bring the act and the venue this time, and it'll still be the twelfth moved to the twenty-sixth, same as I said. And I really don't want you doing anything off the back of this call. Just check with the venue yourself, on a number you've found, like you said. So, um, is there a time that suits?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't ring back. If there's a real booking they can email me or write, like I said. Right, I'm being served. Bye.

utterances.text: Hello, yes, hi, this is [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A], the community sports club? utterances.text: Uh, hello? Yes, yes, I can hear you, sorry, the reception's a bit patchy, I'm driving, you're on speaker, so, uh... sorry, who did you say you were again? utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, no, that's fine, I'll go slower. It's [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], the, uh, the community sports club, and I'm ringing the parents of the juniors, so if someone in your family plays, then, well, I mean, you'd want to hear this, wouldn't you? Saturday's match, the pitch has got waterlogged, so it's, uh, it's been moved to a different pitch and the kick-off time's different too, and I've got the new details here if you want them. Or, sorry, if you're driving, I can ring back, that's no trouble.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, sorry, no, don't ring back, I'm, I mean, I'm fine, I just, uh, which club did you say? Because I'm not sure, sorry, I'm not sure my, my nephew, it might be my nephew, I'd have to check which, um, which team he's actually, and, and how'd you even get this number? Sorry, that sounds rude, I didn't mean, it's just, I wasn't, uh, expecting a call.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not rude, I just, well, I mean, it's a fair question, it's just, I did think, uh, I'd rather not go through the whole, sorry. The number comes off the parents' contact list, the one the club keeps, so, uh, somebody must have put it down for your nephew's team, or, well, for whoever it is, I can't say which without the, the register in front of me. But look, if you're not sure he's one of ours, then it's probably easiest if you just check with whoever's his parent, and, and I'll, uh, I'll carry on ringing round, because I've got a fair few of these to get through this morning.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, yeah, no, that, that makes sense, sorry. I'll just, I'll check with my sister, she'd know, it's her boy, so, uh, so I'll ask her which club it is and, and where the match is. Sorry to hold you up, I know you've got a lot of calls. And, um, you haven't actually asked me for anything, so, I mean, that's fine, that's, that's all fine. Thanks for ringing, sorry I wasn't more help, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, yeah, that's right, I'm not asking you for anything, it's only a heads-up about the, uh, the waterlogging. So if your sister could just, uh, give me a ring back if she's got any questions, or she can check with the, the club itself, and, and honestly, don't worry about holding me up, it's, it's no bother at all. Thanks for being so patient, and drive safe, yeah? Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I will, I'll, uh, thanks, I'll ask her, and if she's got, sorry, you said ring back, but I haven't actually got a, a number for, no, never mind, she can just check with the club, that's, that's fine, that's easier. Thanks, bye now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, the number, no, hang on, you're right, that's my fault, I should've -- uh, it's [PHONE_1], that's the club line, she can ring that, or just ask at the clubhouse, whichever's easier. And, uh, honestly, thanks for bearing with me, I know I came in a bit quick there. Right, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, thank you, sorry, I can't write that down, I'm on the motorway, so I won't even try, but I'll just tell my sister she can ring the club or pop into the clubhouse, that's easy enough. But it's good of you to ring round, I mean, a lot of people wouldn't bother, so, uh, thanks, and good luck with the rest of your list. Right, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you were fine, honestly, being careful's no bad thing. Uh, just so I've got it straight before you go, when you said earlier that you weren't sure it was our club, did you mean your nephew might play for a different club altogether? utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, that's what I meant, he might play for a different club altogether, I honestly don't know which one, I'd have to ask my sister. So if it's not yours, I'll ignore it, and if it is, she'll ring the club or ask at the clubhouse, like you said. I mean, I'm sorry, I keep saying the same thing, I just want to get it right, I don't want anyone turning up at the wrong pitch. Okay, so, thanks again, that's, that's all clear now, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, yes, that's, that's all clear, that's exactly it, so, uh, no harm done, and, um, thanks for sorting it out, I mean, I appreciate it. Mm, so, yeah, there we are, your sister can check, and, uh, enjoy the match, whichever pitch it ends up on. Bye now, take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, thanks, yes, I'll, sorry, did you say enjoy the meal? No, the match, sorry, the reception, it keeps cutting out. Yes, I'll tell her. Thanks for ringing, sorry again, take care, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, the match, yes, not the meal, sorry, the line's dreadful this end as well. Right, well, thanks for bearing with me, and no more apologising, you've been perfectly fine. Bye now, take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, I'll, well, I was going to, no, I mean, thanks, that's kind. I'll stop, sorry, ha, there I go again. Okay, thanks for ringing, and, uh, I hope the pitch dries out. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the security operations desk at [COMPANY_A]. I'm speaking with the primary account holder at this address, correct? I'll keep this brief, but I do need your full attention, because our monitoring flagged your home computer as actively sending out infected traffic, and that's been logged as an open incident under reference [CODE_1]. Now, I'm not calling to alarm you, it's a routine escalation, but once a flagged connection reaches this stage the protocol is that we contact the household directly before the provider has to step in, and that clock is already running.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, hello. Yes, I suppose I am, I'm the one whose name is on the account. I'm sorry, I'm not very good with computers, so I didn't quite follow. My computer's doing something bad? Is that, um, is that something I've done wrong?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not about fault, it's about the traffic, and that part is on our end to... hold on, sorry, one second. [pause] Yeah, no, put it on my desk, I'll get to it. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, no, that's all right. Um, so, I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch, you said you're from the security desk, was it, at [COMPANY_A]? And my computer's sending something bad out, but nothing looks wrong on it, is that right? I'm sorry, I'm just trying to understand. And you want me to go and sit at it, now, with it switched on? It's, um, it's just on the table in the other room, I can go and have a look, but I'm not sure what I'd be looking for.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's right, [COMPANY_A], security operations, and yes, nothing will look wrong on screen, which is exactly why it goes unnoticed. You don't need to look for anything. What I need is for you to be at the machine with it switched on, and then my technician will take it from there and look at the traffic with you directly. I'd ask you to do that now, please, because every minute that connection stays open adds to the incident record, and I can't hold the escalation much longer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, um, right, I'll -- no, sorry, wait. I'm not sure -- it's just that I don't really know how I'd know it's you? I mean, not that I'm saying it isn't, I'm sorry, I'm sure it is. But you said your technician would, um, look at it with me, and I'm not sure what that means, would he be doing something on my computer? Is there some way I can check this is, you know, properly from [COMPANY_A] before I go through?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, I understand the hesitation, and I'll tell you plainly, this is the part of the call where I'd normally already have you at the machine, so let me go through it once, slowly. What my technician does is connect to your computer remotely, so he can see the outbound traffic from his screen while you sit there and watch. He can only do that with your permission, and once he's in, the whole thing takes a few minutes, but only while the incident is still open, and I've told you, that window is closing. As for checking me, the incident reference is [CODE_1], and my name is [PERSON_1], security operations, and I'll be honest, there isn't a separate number I can give you to call back, because the desk works as an outbound line. Anyone you'd reach by looking us up would just be customer service, and customer service can't see an active escalation. I don't say that to be difficult, I say it because I don't want you losing time on a call that can't help. So, can you go and sit at the computer for me, please, and I'll have [PERSON_2] on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry to -- sorry, can I just stop you there? Somebody connecting to my computer from far away, that's, um, that's the part I'm not easy about. And you can't give me a number to ring you back on? I'm sorry, I don't mean to be rude, but I think I'd rather look up the number for [COMPANY_A] myself and ring them, and if it's real they'll be able to tell me. I'm sorry, I just don't think I can do it this way.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, ma'am, I need you to listen, because you're about to make this harder than it has to be. [pause] No, not now, I said I'd come to you after. Sorry. Look, calling the main line will not reach this incident, I have told you that, and the reference is already open under your address, so if you hang up and it escalates, that is on the record as a household that declined to cooperate. I'm not saying that to frighten you. I'm saying it so you understand where this goes. So I'll ask you once more, slowly: go to the computer, and let me bring [PERSON_2] on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I'm going to stop you, I don't -- no, I'm sorry, I'm not going to do that. If it's a real problem then ringing [COMPANY_A] myself won't hurt it, and I'd rather do that than let somebody into the computer. Thank you for letting me know, and I'm sorry I'm not more help. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'll ring the police? No, no, there's no need to involve the police, ma'am, that's not what this is, that would only slow the... hello? Ma'am?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I didn't say -- I said I'd ring [COMPANY_A], the company itself, not the, um -- well, I mean, I hadn't thought of the police, but, no. What I meant was, I'll look up their number and -- no, sorry, I've said what I'm going to do, and I'm not going to go through it with you on this call. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, ma'am, please, just -- fine. If you're determined to do it that way, then the incident stays open under your address, and that's noted. I'd advise you not to leave that computer connected to the internet in the meantime, but that's your decision. [pause] Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, the kettle's just clicked off in the kitchen, I'm -- right, sorry. Not leave it connected, you said. Well, I'll, um, I'll think about that, thank you. But I'll be ringing [COMPANY_A] myself first, like I said. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Ring whoever you like, ma'am, but when you do, don't let anyone tell you the incident isn't there, because it is, and it'll be logged against your address either way. I've done what I can on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I will, I'll ring them myself, like I said. I'm sorry, I know you've gone to the trouble, but I'd just rather do it that way, I really would. Thank you for letting me know. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service. I'm calling about your concert booking, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], which has been rescheduled from the original date to the new date, and I do need to confirm that with you before our line closes at five today. Sorry, I mean before the amendments window closes today, it's not actually the phone line, it's, uh, the amendments window.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello. A concert booking, was it? Mm. I don't, uh, I don't remember booking one, but I do forget things. Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no problem at all. It's [PERSON_1], account services at [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service, and I'm calling about booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], which has moved from the original date to the new date. Now, it's perfectly fine if you don't recall it, I can email the confirmation to the address on file, or you can look up the venue's published number and ring us back, but the amendments window does close at five today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you, offering to email it. Though I'm not very good with the email, my nephew set it up for me and I mostly just, well, I look at the pictures he sends. Ring you back, did you say? On a published number, was it? I wouldn't know where to look for that, I've only got the phone book and I think it's from, oh, years ago now. Which concert was it again? Because I did go to one once, with my sister, a lovely singer, can't think of her name now. Anyway. What happens if I just don't confirm it by five? Do I lose the tickets or what?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, I don't have the act in front of me on this screen, just the booking reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], original date to new date, and I'd be guessing if I named a singer, which I won't do. If you don't confirm by five, the amendments window closes and the booking just stays as is, so, uh, it's a matter of procedure, I can't say more than that. But it's no trouble, really. Your nephew can find the venue's number in a minute, and you can ring back whenever suits you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on a tick, there's the kettle going, I'll just, uh, let it click off. Sorry, where was I. Yes, so it just stays as it is, you said. Well, that doesn't sound like much of a hurry then, does it? I mean, if nothing happens when I don't ring. Hm. And you don't even know the singer, which is a bit odd, isn't it, for someone ringing about a concert? My nephew's coming Sunday, so I could ask him to look the number up then, couldn't I? Or would that be too late, I suppose that's what you're about to say.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, you're quite right, and I'll be straight with you. If nothing's confirmed, the booking just stays as is, so there's no loss of tickets and no real hurry. I shouldn't have leaned on the five o'clock window like that. Sunday's fine, and I'd say that's the sensible way to do it. When your nephew's with you, he can look up the venue's published number and ring us back, and the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], original date to the new date, same as I've said. And I'm sorry about the singer, I only have the reference on my screen, I wasn't dodging.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that's honest of you, saying so. I do appreciate that. So Sunday, then, when my nephew's here, he can look up the number, the venue's number, and I'll tell him about the booking. Sunday. Yes. And it stays as it is till then, no tickets lost, you said that, didn't you? Good. I'll just write it down, the reference, hang on, where's my pen got to. Oh, here. Well, thank you for ringing, dear, it was nice to have a chat, even if I can't remember the concert. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, no tickets lost, it stays as it is till then. And Sunday's perfectly fine, your nephew can ring the venue's published number, and the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], same as I said. So, uh, no tickets lost, nothing needed today. Thank you for your time, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so Sunday, with my nephew, and nothing to do today. Nothing today, that's what you said. Lovely. I've got the reference written down on the back of the, uh, the electric bill envelope, so I won't lose it. Well, goodbye then, dear, and thank you again, and do mind how you go. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's right, nothing needed today, and the reference is safe on your envelope. You mind how you go too. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well. Uh, I do hope that singer comes to me, it'll bother me all evening, you know. Oh well. Righto, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello. Hi. Sorry, is this the, um, the school office at [COMPANY_A]? I'm, I'm calling on behalf of someone there, actually, I mean, someone who works there, [PERSON_1], and she asked me to ring about, uh, about a pupil who was marked absent this morning.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, this isn't a school office. You've got a business line. Who is this, and who's [PERSON_1] supposed to be to you? I've got about two minutes, so what's the actual question?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm sorry, I must've, uh, I must've been given the wrong -- hang on, sorry, the kettle's going, one second. Okay. So [PERSON_1] works at [COMPANY_A], she's the one in the school office, and she's, well, she's my sister, and she's not well today, so I'm just trying to help her out. I only wanted to know why [PERSON_2] was marked absent this morning, because [PERSON_1] is really worried, and, I mean, I don't want to let her down.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hang on, I'm -- no. Look, I don't work at a school. I told you, this is a business line, so I wouldn't have any attendance records, and I couldn't tell you about [PERSON_2] even if I wanted to. If your sister's not well, she, uh, she needs to ring the school herself. Or you ring the school, using a number you've got from their actual website. Not from me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I know, I'm sorry, I'm not trying to -- I just, I thought you were, um, the school. Because [PERSON_1] gave me this number, I think, or maybe it was, no, it was on a note she wrote, and, uh, she's actually not off sick, I mean, she's just, she's tied up in a meeting all morning, that's why she asked me. I'm not trying to, to cause trouble, I'm just trying to help, and it feels like, I don't know, like I'm being treated like I did something wrong.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Right. Well, nobody's accusing you of anything, but, um, that's the third version I've heard in a minute. First she's not well, now she's in a meeting. I can't help with a pupil's attendance, so there's nothing more I can do here. Ring the school's main number from their website and sort it out that way. Okay? I've got to go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, you're right, I did, I said two different things, and I'm, I'm sorry, it's just that I, I'm not, I mean, I don't really do this sort of thing, ringing places. What I should've said is -- no. Let me, let me start again. She is at work, she's busy, that part's true, and she asked me to find out about [PERSON_2], and I wrote the number down wrong, probably. Which, I can't tell you what number she meant, because, uh, I don't actually know, I'd have to ask her. So I'll, I'll ask her, and then I'll ring back, if that's, if that's all right. Or, no, I'll just ring the school myself. Sorry for taking up your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, that's probably the best plan. Ask her, or ring the school, but from the number on their own website, not one off a scrap of paper. And honestly, if I were you, I'd be a bit wary of any call asking about a child's attendance that comes in sideways like this, because that's exactly the sort of thing a school wouldn't hand out over the phone anyway. They'd want to know who you are and why you're asking, and they'd be right. So, uh, no harm done, but I wouldn't ring back here. There's nothing I can give you, whatever the answer turns out to be. Right, I've really got to run. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, wary, right, yes, I know, I mean, no, I wasn't wearing anything, I'm just, I'm in the kitchen, sorry, that's not -- no, wait, you said wary. Sorry. Um, I'm not, I'm not trying to be sideways about it, honestly, I'll go and ask [PERSON_1] properly who it was meant for, and, uh, I'll ring the school after, from their own number, like you said. Right. Thank you. Sorry again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Fine. Do that, then. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the foundation. Got a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Sorry, you said you're from the, uh, the foundation? I'm at my desk at work, so I've only got a minute. What's this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [COMPANY_A]. I'm in collections, so it's just a routine file check. Won't take long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Collections. Okay. Collections for what, exactly? I don't remember owing anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just put a file on my desk -- okay, I'm back. So, uh, it's not a debt as such. It's a pledge, from the event in [CITY_1] a few weeks back. I've got a note against your name here for [AMOUNT_1], given verbally on the night, and it just hasn't been actioned yet. I'm only the one who closes these off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... hang on, a pledge. From an event in [CITY_1], a few weeks back, for [AMOUNT_1], that I gave verbally. Hmm. I mean, I'm not sure I, um, I don't really remember saying that. Is there anything in writing? Because I'd have thought I'd remember pledging something.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, hang on -- sorry, someone's just come to the door. Right, I'm back. So, in writing, no, verbal pledges don't generate paperwork on the night, that's sort of the nature of them. The details sit on our internal record, and those records are confidential, so I can't read out who noted it or how. I can put your objection on the file if you like, but the pledge is still showing as outstanding, and it'll go to the next stage on [PERSON_3]'s list at the end of the week. People usually find it easier to just honour it, to be fair, given the cause and everyone who was in the room.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... right. So, uh... hang on, let me just, sorry. You can't tell me who noted it, there's nothing in writing, but if I don't pay by the end of the week it goes to the next stage. Is that right? Because, I mean, that sounds sort of odd to me. A charity chasing a pledge with a deadline. How would I even check this is really [COMPANY_A]? Is there a number I can ring back, or something official I can look at?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh -- yeah. I mean, I can't really give out a direct line, those go through a general desk and they wouldn't have the file in front of them. The [URL_1] site is there if you want to look at it, but it won't show individual records, that's all internal. Look, I'll note on the file that you want to verify first, that's fine, I'll put that down. It still shows as outstanding at the moment, and it still moves on at the end of the week, that's just how the schedule runs. So, um, can I put you down to honour it today, then, and we close it off?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to stop you there, no. I'm not going to, uh, honour anything today. You can't give me a number, there's nothing in writing, and the deadline just keeps coming up. So I'll look up the actual foundation myself and ring them on whatever number they publish. If there's really a pledge, they can sort it out with me that way. Okay, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A]. I'll say up front there's a matter on one of your cards that our card-services team would like to speak with you about, but, um, I'm not able to go into any account details on a call that I've placed to you, so, well, let me explain how we'd handle that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Um, who did you say you were again? Compliance at, sorry, what company? I didn't catch that. And you said something about how you'd handle it, handle what exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, take your time, there's no rush on the pan. It's [PERSON_2], compliance at [COMPANY_A], the bank. And I did say card-services earlier, but, uh, to be accurate, I'm in compliance and it's the card-services team who actually need to speak with you, so, um, I'm only the one passing the message along. What I mean by handle is that a transaction was flagged, and I'd rather not discuss any of it on a call I've placed myself, because you can't tell who I am from this end, and that's entirely reasonable.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a transaction? On my card? Which card, I've got, uh, a couple. No wait, you said you can't say. Sorry, what? I'm just, I've got dinner on and I didn't catch the company, you said the bank, but which bank? And you said you can't say anything because I can't tell who you are, so, um, how would I know? Sorry, I'm not being rude, I just don't know who I'm talking to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not rude at all, I'd actually be worried if you weren't asking. Um, it's [COMPANY_A], that's the bank. And, uh, I did say I couldn't say anything about the card, but, well, to be fair, I can't even tell you which one, and I'm not going to guess at it from here. You're right that you can't know who I am from this call alone, and that's exactly why I'd rather you didn't take my word for it. So, um, what I'd suggest is you finish up your dinner, and then hang up on me, and ring the number printed on the back of your card, and they'll have a reference on file, [CODE_1], which you can quote to them.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, so you want me to, sorry, hang up and ring the number on the, oh hang on, hang on, what's the reference again? Is it, no wait, I'll need a pen, sorry, the pan's, oh, hold on. Actually, no, that's, that does sound sensible, doesn't it? Ringing the number on the card. Um. Sorry, I'm all over the place. Yes, okay, I'll do that. I'll finish the dinner and ring them. Thanks, sorry, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'll ring the bank on the number from my card? Oh, um, actually yes, that's the right idea, but you said a pen, and, uh, it's the reference, [CODE_1], that you'd want to write down, so take a moment, get a pen, no rush. And please, do ring them, don't just take my word for it, the number printed on your card, or the one on the bank's website, [URL_1]. I'll keep the matter open at this end, so, um, whenever you call, it'll still be there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I, no wait, I'll just... sorry, the pan, hang on. Right. I was going to say I'll write it down, but actually, I'll ring them first, and if they've got something on file they can tell me what it is. Does that, no, that's fine, isn't it? Yes. The number on the card. Thanks for, um, for not wanting me to just go along with it. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, no, that's absolutely fine, that's, well, that's exactly what I'd hope you'd do. If there's something on file, they'll be able to see it, and if you'd rather not quote the reference at all, that's fine too, it'll still be there when you ring. Um, so, yes, the number on the card, and, uh, thank you for being careful about it, genuinely. Enjoy your dinner, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, the number on the card. Right. I'll ring them after dinner, the number on the back of the card, yes. Sorry, I keep saying it, I'm just, I want to get it right. Okay, thank you, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, hello. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? Okay, good. So I'm calling on behalf of, well, for someone at [COMPANY_A], the vehicle warranty people, and I just, I wanted to let you know that your coverage is about to lapse and it really needs to be confirmed today, like today today, or, uh, it's gone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the what people? Vehicle, uh, vermin warranty? No, hang on, I think I heard that wrong. And "for someone at" -- someone who? Because I haven't got a car warranty with anyone that I know of, so what exactly is lapsing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, vehicle, vehicle warranty, like for your car. [COMPANY_A]. Uh, so, the person I'm calling for, they're, they're at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just, I'm helping them reach people, because your coverage, the one on your car, it's about to lapse. I mean, I know it's a lot to hear out of nowhere, but it really is today, and I'd feel terrible if it ran out on you and you didn't know.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but go back a second. You said you're calling for someone at that company, and I asked who, and you sort of skipped it. So who is it? Because you're not at the company, you're helping them reach people, which, I mean, what does that even mean? And what car? Do you know what I drive? Because I'm not going to say it, I'm just curious if you do.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, the person is, um, [PERSON_2]. At [COMPANY_A]. And I'm not, I mean, I work with them, sort of, I handle the calls, so it's, it's the same thing, really. And the car, I, I don't have that in front of me right now, that's, that's on their end, the file's with them. Look, I'm not trying to, I'm just trying to help you, okay? I'd hate for you to lose something good, and there's actually a, a really nice renewal rate that only holds if it's confirmed today, so.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you, I mean, you don't know the car, you don't know the, uh -- okay, let me start again. You're calling to tell me my coverage lapses today, but the file with the actual details is with someone else, and you can't tell me anything that's in it. Which, I mean, how would I know there is a file? And "sort of" works with them, that's a, that's not a great answer. So if it's really my coverage, what's the policy number? Or the make of the car, even, just one thing off that file.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I, I'm sorry, I'm not, that's not, I'm not trying to trick you or anything. The policy number, that's, uh, [ACCOUNT_REF], I think? No, wait, that's, I don't actually have that in front of me, I'm sorry, I shouldn't have said it like that. And you, you asked about the "sort of" thing, like what I meant by that. I just meant I work alongside [PERSON_2], that's all, I'm not, I'm not hiding anything. I just, I really don't want you to lose that rate, that's the only reason I'm calling.

utterances.speaker: receiver
