utterances.text: See, that's, no, you said a policy number and then you took it back, so it was either on the, I mean, you either have it or you don't. And honestly I'm, I'm not going to, look, here's the thing. Nothing you've told me checks out so far, you can't say who you work for, you can't say what car, and there's a deadline that conveniently only exists today. If there's actually a policy, I'll find the paperwork and call the number on that, not the one you rang me on. So, yeah, I'm going to leave it there. Take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, wait, no, please, I, I'm not, okay, that's, that's really not fair, I came across wrong, that's all. Look, you don't have to call the number on the paperwork, [PERSON_2] will just call you back, I mean, it'll be today, probably, I can't say when exactly, it's an internal line, I don't have a direct number for you. But if you wait, the rate's gone, and I just, I'd hate to be the one who, who, uh, um...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, two turns ago you said you weren't trying to trick me, and then you said you work alongside [PERSON_2], that's all. But a minute before that it was you "handle the calls, so it's the same thing, really." Those aren't the same thing, are they? Either you work for [COMPANY_A] or you just work near someone who does. So which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I, I told you, I work with [PERSON_2], I help with the calls, it's, it's the same thing, I mean, it's not, I didn't mean it like that. I just, I'm trying to help you, that's all, I'm not trying to trick you, I said that already. And I, I really don't have a number, it's internal, they'll call you back, I just can't say when, and if you wait, the rate, it's gone, and I'd feel awful, honestly, I would. So can you, can we just confirm it now, please?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, we can't confirm it now, because I still don't know what "it" is. You've got no car, no policy number, no direct line, and your story about who you work for has changed three times. And honestly, "I'd feel awful" is not how a company does renewals, so I'm done. If [PERSON_2] wants to reach me, they can put it in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, I'm, I'm just trying to help, that's all. [PERSON_2] will call you back, I just can't say when, it's an internal line, and I'm telling you, the rate, it's only good today, and I'd feel, I mean, I really would feel awful if, if you lost it. Can't you just, can't we just confirm it now, before it's gone?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You know, you keep saying I can't say when, it's an internal line, but earlier you said they'd just call me back today, probably. So is it today or isn't it? Because that's another thing that's moved. And I've said goodbye twice now and you're still going, which, I mean, it's not helping. No. I'm not confirming anything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the customs desk at [COMPANY_A], the courier. I'm ringing about a parcel that's due to you, and there's, um, an import charge attached to it that I wanted to explain properly, so, yes. Is now an alright time to talk?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm at my desk, so -- sort of in the middle of something. A parcel, and an import charge? Which courier did you say, the customs desk at... sorry, I didn't catch the name. And what parcel is it, exactly? I'm not sure I'm expecting anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it. The name was [COMPANY_A], and I'm with the customs desk, which is the part of the courier that handles duty on parcels coming in from abroad. Um, the parcel itself is one sent to you by [COMPANY_B], and the reference on it is [ACCOUNT_REF], which you should be able to find in the dispatch email or on the tracking page, so you can check it against what I'm saying rather than just taking my word. I'd say it's worth looking at sooner rather than later, but, well, I'd rather you confirm it's yours first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, a parcel from [COMPANY_B], with a reference number. Right. Um, I don't think I've ordered anything from them, to be honest, or, hang on, I might have, I order bits online now and then. I can't check right now, though, I'm at work and I've got people sitting right next to me. And, uh, what's the charge? Like roughly how much are we talking about, and what's it for exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, so, the charge is [AMOUNT_1], and that's the import duty and handling on the declared value of the contents, um, it's what's due when something comes in from outside the country. There's also a small clearance fee of [AMOUNT_2] on top, and both of those are itemised on the tracking page, so you'd see exactly how it's been calculated. And, uh, no, please don't try to check anything with people sitting beside you, that's, I mean, that's completely fine, you can do it whenever suits. I'd only say the parcel can't really sit in the depot indefinitely, but I'm not going to hurry you through it on the phone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, okay. So [AMOUNT_1] duty, plus [AMOUNT_2] clearance, and it's itemised on the tracking page. Right. But, uh, you said it can't sit in the depot indefinitely, so how long do I actually have? Like is that today, or this week? And if I'm going to look at this, I'd rather go to the courier's own website or the email I got from [COMPANY_B], not follow anything from this call. Is there a number I can ring you back on, or the main one for [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's exactly what I'd do, honestly. Going to the courier's own site, or the email from [COMPANY_B], is the right instinct, and I wouldn't want you to do it any other way. Um, the main number for [COMPANY_A] is on the tracking page and on any of the dispatch emails, so you can ring that and ask for the customs desk, and the reference [ACCOUNT_REF] will bring the parcel up. If you'd rather, I can give you [PHONE_1] as well, though I'd say use the one you've found yourself. As for how long, I, uh, I'd sooner not put a day on it, because that depends on the depot and I don't want to say something I can't stand behind. But there's no need to decide anything on this call. Nothing's asked of you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. So, nothing's asked of me today, I should look it up myself on the tracking page or ring the main number, and quote the reference. Right, that, uh, that actually sounds sensible. I'll do that when I'm not at my desk. I'll leave the [PHONE_1] one, I'd rather use the number I find myself, like you said. Thanks for the call, I'll check it later. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, yes, that's, um, I think that's the sensible way to go. If it turns out it's not yours, or, well, if the reference doesn't match anything you've ordered, then, uh, just leave it, you don't need to do anything at all. Right, thank you for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, yep, got it, if it doesn't match I just leave it, right. Thanks, bye --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye, [PERSON_1], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- sorry, one sec, a colleague just dropped something over here. Yeah, no, bye, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say, uh, you've dropped something? No, no, take your time, that's -- hold on, let me just, if you've lost the reference, I can read it out again, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], though I'd say it's on the dispatch email anyway. Um, you're still there, yes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I haven't dropped anything, a colleague did, sorry, that was confusing. I'm still here. And I haven't lost the reference, you don't need to read it out again, I'll find it on the email myself. Right, so, um, that's everything then. Thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, I see, no, that was my mistake, I misheard you, apologies. Right, then, that's everything on my side too. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no worries. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], collections and line services. I'm calling about the fault on your line, the one flagged against account [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's showing as urgent on my screen. Sorry, I'll need you to go back over something for me: did you say two turns ago that someone had already been out to look at it, or was that a different engineer?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, "two turns ago"? I haven't said anything, you've only just got me. I never said anyone came out, no. And collections and line services, what's that, which is it, a fault or a debt? Who did you say you were with again? I'm stood in a queue here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, my mistake, that was a note on the file, not you. It's the same account either way, [COMPANY_A], and the fault's what I'm calling about. Can I get you to confirm the address on the line so I can pull it up?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not, I'm not giving you my -- look, you rang me. You've got the account, you've got my name, so you've got the address already, haven't you? Why are you asking me for it? And you still haven't said which it is, a fault or a... a collections thing. Those aren't the same department. What's the number I'd ring you back on? Not one you read me, the one off my own bill.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand you'd like a call-back number, and I've noted that on the file. What I need is the address confirmed so I can pull the fault up. The fault's urgent, I'm showing it as urgent, and once the line is flagged it comes down to a disconnection date, which is the part I'm trying to avoid. So the address, please, and then we can sort the rest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Disconnection date? Oh, there it is. Two minutes ago it was a fault, now I'm getting cut off if I don't hand over my address. No. You didn't answer the number, either, you "noted it on the file." I'm not telling you anything. I'll ring [COMPANY_A] myself, off my own bill, and if there's a fault they can tell me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I've noted the objection, but I'd ask you not to hang up, because the line is flagged as urgent and I'm showing it as urgent. Once that flag goes to the next stage, the disconnection date is set, and that's not something I can reverse from this desk. So it's the address, and then I can pull the fault up. I'm showing it as urgent, [PERSON_1], that's all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, listen, you said I'd be cut off and then in the same breath you said you can't do anything about it from your desk, so what exactly are you ringing me for? That makes no sense. And "I'm showing it as urgent" isn't an answer, it's just you saying the same thing again, louder. I've had this before, someone rang me up all official, had my name, had half of my details, and wanted the rest, and I'm still sore about it, so no, I'm not being talked round. If my line's really faulty, [COMPANY_A] can tell me when I ring them on the number off my own bill, and if there's a disconnection date it'll be sat on my account where I can see it, not something you only get to tell me about if I read out my address first. You've dodged the call-back number three times now, and that tells me more than anything you've actually said. So that's it. I'm not giving you the address, I'm not staying on while you tell me it's urgent again, and I've got a trolley full of shopping. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I've noted the objection on the file, and just so it's recorded, the call-back number wasn't something I refused, I said it wasn't available from this desk, which is different. And the disconnection isn't set yet, it's the pending stage, so nothing's happened to your account today. Uh, but if the flag moves on before you've spoken to anyone, that's out of my hands. I'm only asking for the address so I can pull the fault up, [PERSON_1], that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wasn't available from this desk." Right, so a collections and line services department that can't give out its own number. That's even worse than refusing, that's just a different way of saying no. And "out of my hands" if I don't read you my address, I've heard that one before as well. Nothing's happened today, you said so yourself, so there's no rush, which means I'll ring them myself off my own bill. I'm done, I'm not telling you the address, and I've got to get my shopping through. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's your decision, and I've noted it on the file as declined. I'll just say the flag stays as it is until it's actioned, so if you do ring in, quote [ACCOUNT_REF]. Uh, but I can't tell you what that will show by the time you get through, and... well, that's all I have on it from here. Is there anything you want added to the record before I close this?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, nothing to add. Actually, hang on, two turns back you said the disconnection wasn't set yet, it was at some pending stage. Then now you say you can't tell me what it'll show by the time I get through. So is it pending or isn't it? Which is it? Not that I'm going to tell you my address either way, I'll sort it myself off my own bill. Right, I'm at the till. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's pending as of this call, that's what's on my screen, and what it shows later I can't speak to. That's not a contradiction, it's just the status as it stands right now. I've got your objection down, and the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF] if you do ring in. Uh, but I'd still say don't leave it too long, because, well, I'm only able to tell you what I can see.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, I'm at the till, so this is the last thing I'm saying. You've told me it's urgent, you've told me it's pending, you've told me it could move on before I've spoken to anyone, and you've told me you can't give me a number to ring you back on. All of it sounds like it's meant to make me hurry, and none of it is a thing I can check from here. So I'll do what I said. I'll ring [COMPANY_A] myself, on the number off my own bill, and I'll ask them what's on my account. If there's a fault, they'll know. If there's a disconnection date, it'll be sat there on my account for me to see. And if they've never heard of you, well, then I'll know that as well. I'm not giving you my address, I'm not giving you anything else, and I'm certainly not staying on while you tell me the same thing a sixth time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hi, uh, hello. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], from the [COMPANY_A] -- the club, I mean, the sports club, with the under-tens. Sorry, I'm, uh, not great on the phone, but I'm just calling about Saturday's match.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is, um, yeah, that's me. Sorry, who? The club? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Saturday's match, right -- but I thought the under-tens played on Sundays? Sorry, what was the name again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A]. And, um, yeah, Sundays, you're right, they usually are Sundays, I mean -- no, wait, this one's a Saturday, it got moved, that's sort of the whole reason I'm ringing. Sorry, I'm making a mess of this. It's just that the pitch is waterlogged, and I didn't want you turning up at the wrong place with your little one.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Oh, right, waterlogged, yeah, it has been so wet. Sorry, hang on, let me turn this down. Okay. So it's moved to a different pitch, is that it? Where's it, um, where's it going to be? And what time? Sorry, I should be writing this down, I haven't got a pen.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, take your time, I'm in no rush. Uh, so, sorry, going back a bit, you asked about the Sunday thing, and I said it was a Saturday, and that's, um, it is a Saturday, I'd just got muddled because the league fixtures are usually Sundays. It's, uh, the second pitch, the one by the car park, not the main one, and kick-off's, um, [AMOUNT_1] instead of the usual time. Sorry, does that make sense? I hate that I keep tripping over this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, [AMOUNT_1]? That's, no, that's not a time, is it? That sounds like -- no, I mean -- sorry, what time did you say? And, um, I don't, hang on. Which little one are you thinking of? Because I've, I've not actually said who's playing, have I? Sorry. I'm just, the pan's going and I'm a bit, what did you say your name was again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, the, the time, yes, it's, um, half past [AMOUNT_2], I think, I've got it written down somewhere. And, uh, which little one -- sorry, did you say a lot of people had been told? No, no, it's just you and a few of the other parents on the under-tens list, so you're not the only one I'm ringing. It's, uh, [PERSON_2]. From [COMPANY_A]. I did say, sorry, I'm, I know I'm going round in circles.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? I didn't say anything about a lot of people. I, hang on. You said it's [PERSON_2], yes, I heard that. But I still don't, which little one? I haven't said my child's name, or what team, or anything. Sorry, I'm a bit lost here. What's the number for the club? I think I'll just ring them and check, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, of course, that's, that's fine, honestly, I'd rather you checked. I wasn't, um, I didn't mean to make it sound like you'd said anything you hadn't, I just assumed, because you're on the under-tens list I've got here, and that's my fault, I should've said so properly at the start instead of fumbling about. The club number's, uh, [PHONE_1], that's the one on the website and the, the team sheet. And I know I've been a bit, a bit all over the place, with the Saturday and the Sunday and the time and everything, and I'm sorry, I'm only a volunteer, I'm not, I don't do this for a living, I just didn't want anyone turning up at a pitch that's under water with a cold kid and no one to tell them. That's all it was, really. So, yeah, ring them, please, I'll honestly be glad if you do.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. Right. Sorry, I've turned the hob off now, I couldn't think with it spitting. Um, thank you for saying ring them, that, that does help, honestly. And I do get that you're a volunteer, and it's nice you're ringing round at all, it's just that, well, I'd got a bit muddled myself, because the Sunday thing, and then the time that wasn't a time, and you not having said which child. I'm not saying you're, I don't know, up to anything, sorry, that sounds awful. I just don't know you, do I? So I'll ring the club on the number I've already got, not the one you just said, no offence, and ask if the match has moved. If it has, then lovely, and thank you for the warning. If it hasn't, well, I'll know. Sorry, I'm rambling. Right. Thank you, and, um, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, honestly, that's the right thing to -- no, don't apologise, I'd do the same, I would. I'm just, I only wanted -- right. Okay. Yeah. Bye, then, sorry for the muddle.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, it's, I mean, thank you for, I just -- sorry, I'd rather check, that's all. It's nothing personal. Right. Okay. Bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah. Okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, one more thing, you said the pitch by the car park, the second one, but I thought the club only had the one pitch? Or am I, hang on, never mind. I'll sort it with the club. Right, bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, no, it's, there's the one by the, um -- no. Sorry. Never mind, you're right, ring them, they'll know better than me. I'm, I'm not very good at this. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, no, I will, I'll ring them. On the number I've already got, like I said, the one I've got at home. Sorry, I just, I'll ring them, and that's, yeah, that's what I'll do. Right, thank you, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, did you say home? No, I'm not at home, I'm, I'm at the clubhouse, I just -- hang on, I don't, why does it matter where I am? I only rang to help, honestly, and now it feels like I've, like I've done something wrong, and I really haven't. I just wanted to let you know.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I said the number I've got at home, not where you are. Never mind. I'll just ring the club. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one second -- hang on, someone's just dropped a stack of boxes behind me. Right, uh, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], regional office, regarding a delivery that's registered to this number.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um -- yes, hello, this is, uh, speaking, yes. Oh, goodness, that sounds like quite a racket behind you. Sorry, I didn't quite catch the company, was it -- [COMPANY_A]? And a delivery, you said? I'm not sure I've, uh, been expecting anything, but I could be wrong, I forget these things sometimes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], that's right, sorry about the noise, it's a busy depot today. And that's quite all right, uh, a lot of people don't remember, especially if it was ordered a while back or sent by someone else. Um, it's a single parcel, going to an address in [CITY_1], and it's been sitting at our regional hub since this morning, which is, well, why I'm ringing. So, uh, let me just pull up the, hang on, the record here, I want to make sure I've got the right person before I say anything further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, that's fine, take your time. I'm not going anywhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, thanks, appreciate your patience. So, uh, I've got it up now, parcel's registered to [PERSON_1], ordered through [COMPANY_B], and it's, well, it's actually been at our local branch since Tuesday, not the regional hub, I think I said hub earlier, but that's just the sorting term. Anyway, it's flagged because there's a small outstanding handling charge, [AMOUNT_1], that has to be cleared before we can release it for delivery. Does that, uh, does that ring a bell at all?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, no, I'm sorry, it doesn't really ring a bell. I don't think I've ordered anything from [COMPANY_B], but, well, I do forget. Sorry, I'm a bit lost though -- you said first it was at the hub since this morning, and now it's been at the branch since Tuesday? I'm not very good with this sort of thing. And a handling charge, is that, uh, something I'd normally have to pay for a parcel? I've never had one before, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, it's just internal terminology, hub, branch, it's the same building. And the handling fee is standard procedure when a parcel's been held over, that's all it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, sorry, I didn't mean to be difficult, it's just, uh, I'm not good at keeping track of these things. It's only a small amount, I suppose. But, um, I don't remember ordering anything, so I'm a bit worried about paying for something I can't place. Is there a way I could check this myself first? Like, with the shop it came from, or a number I could ring you back on? I'd just feel better, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, you can, of course, you can check with [COMPANY_B], nobody's stopping you, but, uh, I'll be honest, they won't have the holding record, that's on our side. And a callback number, I mean, I'm in the depot, it's the main line, it just goes to the front desk, they'd never put you through to me. Look, it's [AMOUNT_1], it's a handling fee, it's standard, I've said that, and the parcel gets sent back on the next collection if it's not settled today, that's just procedure. I mean, I'm trying to help you here, [PERSON_1], I really am. It's a small fee, it's standard, and it can be settled right here over the phone, and honestly I'd rather not see it returned to sender over something this minor.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I, uh -- no, sorry, I mean -- I do appreciate you trying to help, truly. It's just, you can't give me a number to ring you back, and I don't remember ordering anything, and now it's, um, it has to be today, and -- sorry, I know it's only a small amount, but I'd, I think I'd feel happier checking with the shop first. If it goes back to them, well, I suppose that's all right if it's not really mine. Is that, uh, is that all right? I'm sorry to be a bother.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not a bother, I'm sorry, that came out sharper than I meant, it's been a long shift. Look, if you'd rather check with [COMPANY_B] first, that's your right, I'm not going to argue. But I'd hate for you to lose it over a few minutes, so tell you what, I can put a hold on it until end of day, I've got that discretion as supervisor. Only, honestly, most people just settle it now and it's done, one less thing on your plate, and I'm right here to sort it with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind of you, thank you, and no, don't worry about it, long shifts are hard. Um, sorry, can I just go back a bit though? A minute ago you said it couldn't be sent to me until the fee was cleared, and then you said they'd put it back on the next collection if it wasn't settled today. So is it going back today, or can you really hold it till end of day? I got a bit muddled, sorry. And, uh, who exactly did you say you were again? I didn't catch your name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, it's [PERSON_2], regional supervisor, I did say, but with the noise it's easy to miss. And the hold, right, no, it isn't going back today, I said the next collection, that's Friday, so that's, well, I mean, the hold's just a courtesy, it's fine either way. Look, I don't want to go round in circles, [PERSON_1], you've asked me a few times now and I've been straight with you. Do you want me to sort the [AMOUNT_1] with you now, or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, please don't think I'm going round in circles on purpose, I'm sorry, I'm just not very good with this sort of thing. But, uh, I think I'll say no, thank you, not today. It's only that I don't remember ordering anything, and the story's changed a couple of times, hub and branch, and today and Friday, and I can't ring you back, and I'd only get in a muddle. I'm sure you're doing your best, and I don't mean to be rude. But I'd feel better ringing [COMPANY_B] myself and seeing whether there's a parcel at all. If it's mine, I'll sort it properly then, and if it isn't, well, it can go back and no harm done. So I'll leave it there, if that's all right. Thank you for ringing, and I hope the rest of your shift is a quieter one. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], we handle prize adjudication and compliance for regional promotional draws. I'm calling because your entry was selected in the [CITY_1] regional draw, and before the award can be released, there's a validation window that, well, it's time-sensitive, so I wanted to reach you directly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? A... a validation widow? Oh, I'm so sorry, hang on, I've got something on the hob. Is somebody's husband... no, wait. Who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, no, window, validation window, sorry, uh, that's just the term of art for the, the timeframe in which the claim has to be authenticated. Nobody's husband, ha. Sorry, I've got, hang on, there's a door banging out in the corridor here, one moment -- right, okay. It's [PERSON_2], verification specialist, [COMPANY_A], and the short version is you've been selected in a regional draw, and to finalise the disbursement I just need to confirm a few identifiers against the entry record, so we can close the file within the window.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a few... what did you say, dentifiers? Dentist? I haven't got a dentist appointment, I don't think. Oh, hang on, the onions are catching. Sorry. What draw? I don't remember entering anything. Who did you say you're with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Identifiers, not dentist, sorry, that's, uh, that's on me for the jargon. It just means a couple of personal details to match against the entry record, date of birth, address, that sort of thing, standard adjudication protocol. And, um, you wouldn't have a specific recollection of the entry, that's quite common, it's usually a co-registered promotional opt-in, so it'd have been, you know, bundled in with something else, and the, uh, the nature of the compliance framework is that the award lapses if the validation isn't completed today, so, mm, if we could just get through that while I have the file open?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Lapses? Oh, a lapse, no, I haven't had a lapse, I'm sure I paid that. Hang on, is this about my insurance? Oh, sorry, the pan's spitting. No wait. You said a draw. I don't remember any draw. And you still haven't said who you're with, it's... what was it, Company something? Sorry, I'm all in a flap here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nothing to do with insurance, I'm sorry, that's my fault, it's a promotional draw, a prize, uh, and I'm with [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency. And, mm, going back to the entry, I did say it'd be a co-registered opt-in, which just means you'd have ticked a box on something else, a survey, a warranty card, a loyalty form, and the entry was bundled in, so it's quite normal not to remember it. The, uh, the reconciliation on our end is straightforward, I only need your date of birth and the address on the entry to confirm it's you, and then we can lock the disbursement of [AMOUNT_1] before the window closes today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, [AMOUNT_1]? A prize? Oh. Oh, hang on. I mean, that's nice, but... I don't remember ticking anything. And you want my date of birth? And my address? Sorry, I'm not sure about that. You rang me, didn't you? I didn't ring you. How would I know it's really you? Is there a number I could ring you back on, or something? Oh, the pan, hang on, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A, a pan? No, no, we're not a pan-European operation, ha, we're a, uh, domestic promotions agency, and I did say that at the outset. But, well, on the call-back, I mean, you're welcome to, uh, our verification line is [PHONE_1], although I should flag that the file is open under my adjudication session right now, so if the window lapses before we reconnect it would have to be re-queued, and, mm, there's no guarantee the [AMOUNT_1] would be re-released. It really is simplest to just confirm the date of birth and address now, since I'm already, um, holding the record open.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? No, I said a pan, on the hob, not, oh never mind. Look, I said I don't remember entering anything. And now you're saying the money might go if I ring you back? That doesn't sound right. If it's real, it'll still be there, won't it? I'm not giving my date of birth to someone who rang me out of the blue, sorry. I'll leave it, I think. Thank you, but, no. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A] -- sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a box of files right behind me -- right, I'm back. I'm ringing because our card services team has flagged a transaction on your account that they'd like to go over with you, and I do need to stress that we're working to a close-of-business window today. Am I speaking with the account holder?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, somebody's just shouting down the corridor -- right. Which account? You haven't actually said who you're with, not properly. [COMPANY_A], fine, but I've got a couple of those. What's the transaction, and why's it got a deadline on it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, fair question, and I'm not going to go into the transaction on this call, that's the point. I rang you, so I can't verify you on this line and I won't discuss account details until you've reached us yourself. What I'd like you to do is hang up and ring the number printed on the back of your card, and if you give me a moment I'll give you a reference to quote when you get through, it's [ACCOUNT_REF]. As for the deadline, that's just the card services team's working window today, it's not something that's going to wreck your account, but they do close at five, so sooner is better than later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Hang up, ring the number on the card, quote the reference. Fine. That's what I'd do anyway, so I'll do that. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good, that's exactly the right thing to do. Just so it's clear, when you get through, ask for card services and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], my name's [PERSON_1], and I'll keep the matter open on our side until you've rung. No need to rush off the back of this call, uh, just before five if you can manage it. Thanks for your time, and take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Cheers, and just -- sorry, one last thing, ring the number on your card, not one I've given, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF]. That's us done, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said ring the number on the card, not one you've given... and then what, quote the reference? No, hang on, did you say "call you back"? Because I'm not doing that, I'll be going through the card number, not yours. Anyway, I've got to go, I'm late. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's right, you've got it exactly. I'm not asking you to call me back, I haven't given you a number and I won't, you go through the one on your card and quote [ACCOUNT_REF] when you're through. I'll keep it open on our side, so no need to worry if you can't get to it before five. Off you go, and thanks for your patience, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Card number, not yours, got it, that's what I said. Card number, not yours. Look, I'm going now, I'm late for a meeting. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's it, card number, not mine, and I'm not offering you one -- sorry, hang on, [PERSON_3], could you just put those on my desk, thanks -- right, sorry. So, go to your meeting, nothing needs doing this second. When you do ring, it's card services, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and it stays open on our side. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, the lift's just pinged, I've got to -- right. We've said bye about four times, haven't we. I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yes, we have, sorry -- that's me being over-careful. Hang on, the phone on the next desk's gone off, sorry -- right. Nothing more from me. Ring the number on your card, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and we'll pick it up from there. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I've got it. Card, not your number, quote the reference. Honestly, that's the fifth time. I'm going now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1], I'm a collections officer with [COMPANY_A], the national tax office. Hello? Yeah, sorry, [PERSON_1] from [COMPANY_A], the tax office. I'm following up on a letter that was sent to you about a discrepancy in a filing, reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. There's no rush on this, I can resend the letter or walk you through it, whichever you'd prefer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Tax office? I've got two minutes, so what's the discrepancy, exactly? I don't remember any letter. Which filing are we talking about, and what's the point of the call?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, so, [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], the national tax office. It's about a filing discrepancy, uh, the figures on the return don't match what we have on record. I'm showing a difference of [AMOUNT_1] on the file, and the letter went out under reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. Look, if you don't remember a letter, that's fine, I can resend it, or we can leave this call and handle it all by post. You're welcome to check the reference against your paperwork whenever you like.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you're calling me out of the blue about a difference of some amount, and I'm supposed to just take your word for it? I don't remember a letter. Which filing, which year? You still haven't said. Look, if it's real, send it by post and I'll deal with it that way. I'm not discussing figures on a call I didn't expect. Which filing, which year, and what do you actually want from me today?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, and you're right not to take my word for it. The filing is the [CITY_1] income return, tax year [CODE_1], that's what the screen's showing. And what I want from you today is nothing, really. I'm not asking for any payment or details on this call. I'll note your objection on the file, I'll have the letter resent to the address we hold, and you can ring us back on the office's published number, [PHONE_1], rather than trusting me. The reference [ACCOUNT_REF] will be on the letter, so you can match it up when it lands.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. So nothing from me today, no payment, no details, you resend the letter and I ring the published number. Nothing today, right? Because that's what I'm holding you to. And I'll find that number myself, I won't use the one you just gave me. If the letter turns up and the reference matches, fine, I'll deal with it then. If it doesn't, I'm done with it. Right, I've got a meeting. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, nothing from you today. Letter goes out, and you look the number up yourself, that's, uh, that's the sensible way to do it. Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a file on my desk -- right, I'm back. If the reference doesn't match when it arrives, that's worth knowing too, so you ring in and say so. Go to your meeting, I've noted it all on the file. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_2], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so nothing from me today, nothing. Letter comes, I check the reference, and I find the number myself. Yes, I've got that. Okay, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's all of it. Oh, and one thing from earlier, I said the screen was showing the [CITY_1] income return, tax year [CODE_1], and I realise I rattled that off. If it doesn't line up with what you remember filing, say so when the letter arrives, because that's a mistake on our side and I'd want it corrected. Nothing's needed from you before then. Good luck with the meeting, [PERSON_2]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before I go. Two turns back you said "no rush" on the letter, and then you said you'd noted my objection on the file. What objection? I didn't object to anything, I just said I'd deal with it by post. And you still haven't told me which year, you just said a code. Anyway, I'll check my own paperwork, and I'm not ringing any number you've given me. Right, that's it, I've got to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, fair point on both counts. Objection was the wrong word, that's just how the system labels it when someone declines to go through it on a call. I'll put it down as you preferring post. And the year, yes, I gave you a code and that's no use to you. It'll be printed in full on the letter, so check it against your own records when it arrives. And no, don't ring anything I've given you, look the number up yourself, like you said. Anyway, thanks for your patience, [PERSON_2], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So post it is, and I look the number up myself. That's all I'm taking from this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yes, uh, that's it. Post it is, and you look the number up yourself. Nothing else from you, nothing else from me today. Sorry for the, uh, the awkward start on the call. Right, I'll let you get to your meeting. Goodbye, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Look, since you've said sorry for the awkward start, I'll be straight about why I was short with you. I didn't know who you were, you didn't give me a year until I pushed, and I'm not in the habit of talking about tax figures with someone who rang me out of nowhere. That's not personal. If the letter comes and the reference matches, I'll sort it, and if it doesn't, I'll treat it as nothing to do with me. Either way I'm not giving anything out over the phone, and I'm not using any number you've read to me. So that's where we are. Right, I really do have to go. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the benefits office, uh, I just have a quick query on a record here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is -- well, who did you say, the benefits office? I was just sitting here, the radio's on, there's a lovely programme about gardens, and I -- sorry, go on, what's the query?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [COMPANY_A], the benefits office, collections side. No, no, take your time, I'm in no rush. It's just that I've got a record here under [PERSON_1] and it's showing as incomplete on our end, so I'm just ringing round to get it tidied up. Is now an okay time, or are you in the middle of something?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, now's fine, I'm not doing anything really, just the radio. But sorry, I think I missed something you said earlier, when you first rang, was it the benefits office or a different name? I didn't quite catch what you said before "benefits office", it sounded like a company, and I'm useless with names on the phone. And what do you mean collections side, is that something I owe, or...?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, that's [COMPANY_A], it's the name of the office, and the benefits office is what we are. The collections side is just the department I sit in, it's, uh, where incomplete records get routed. It's not a bill as such. It's just that the record's showing blank in a couple of fields, and it needs confirming over the phone today so it doesn't get flagged further up. So if I could just take your full date of birth to bring the record up, we can get through it quickly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, flagged further up, that sounds a bit serious, doesn't it? I don't like the sound of that. Um, but hang on, you rang me, didn't you, so shouldn't you already have my date of birth if you've got my record in front of you? That's what my daughter always says, if they ring you they should know it already. Sorry, I'm not being awkward, it's just I'm not very good with all this. How would I know it's really the benefits office, though? Is there a number I could ring you back on, or something like that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I do have the, uh -- no, the record's under your name, yes, but the date of birth is what we, I mean, it's how we confirm we've got the right [PERSON_1] on the line. That's standard. As for a number, I can't really, there isn't a direct line for this desk, it's all routed through here. I can note your objection on the file if you like, that's fine, but the record still needs confirming today, and if it isn't, it goes to the next stage and that's just how it works. So, your date of birth, whenever you're ready.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, hang on. It's just, you can't give me a number, and you want me to, I mean, my daughter did say, and I'd really rather -- look, I don't think I want to say it, not on the phone, not when I can't ring you back. That doesn't feel right to me, dear. If it's the benefits office, surely there's a letter or something they'd send, isn't there? I'll ask my daughter to have a look into it for me. Thank you for ringing, anyway, and sorry I couldn't be more help. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I, uh -- I'll note that on the file, that you've declined to confirm. But I should say, I mean, it's not -- the record stays incomplete, and once it's past today it moves to the next stage, so that's, that's just where it'll stand. There's no letter that goes out before that, no. Anyway, I've noted it, so, uh, that's all I can do from here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, there's the kettle, sorry, hang on a moment, it's gone off. Right, I'm back. Well, you note what you like, dear, but I'll leave it with my daughter, she's good with all this sort of thing. If it's as important as you say, I'm sure a letter will turn up. Thank you for ringing, mind how you go. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, sorry to trouble you. Is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from the billing office at [COMPANY_A], I'm a case handler there, and, uh, it's regarding an unpaid medical account that has your name listed as the responsible party. Are you still there? I just want to make sure I've got the right person before I go any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? An unpaid medical count? I thought you said, uh, medical amount, or... hang on, which company is this again? I didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, that's my fault, I'm not speaking very clearly. It's a medical bill, an unpaid account, and I'm with the billing office at [COMPANY_A]. Um, the account belongs to a relative of yours, and your name was listed as the person responsible, so I wanted to reach you before it goes any further, for your own protection really. Are you still there? Could you just confirm your full name and date of birth for me, so I know I've reached the right person?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, I'm not -- no, hang on. You rang me, so you tell me who I am first, not the other way round. Which relative, for a start? And, uh, what's the actual name of the company, because that came through as a sort of blur again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I understand, I do, and I'm sorry, I know it's a bit backwards. It's just that the relative's name and the account details are, um, they're only shared once I've confirmed who I'm speaking with, it's really for your own protection, so nobody else can see it. Hello? Are you still there? I'm sorry, I just, uh, it's quite a sensitive account, you see. If you could just confirm your date of birth for me, then I can tell you everything, I promise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no. You've rung me and you want my date of birth before you'll tell me who you are or who the relative is. That's not how I'm doing this. Send it in writing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I do understand, I'm sorry, but if we leave it with a letter, it could go to, uh, to collections in the meantime, and then it's really out of my hands, which is the last thing I want for you. Hello? Are you still with me? It would only take a moment, [PERSON_1], just your date of birth and I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So now it's go to collections unless I hand over my date of birth to someone who still hasn't given me a company name I can actually hear. No. If there's a real account, a letter will find me, and I'll ring whatever number is printed on it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry to have bothered you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right. Yeah. Well, mm... as I said, send the letter and I'll deal with it that way. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Okay. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Are you... no, okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, before you go. Two turns back you said if it's just a letter, it could go to collections in the meantime. Meantime of what? I mean, how long are we talking, and who decides that? Because if there's a real deadline, it'll be on paper somewhere, surely.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, well, it's, I mean the timing isn't something I, uh -- it depends on the, no, I can't really give you a date, I'm sorry. Hello? Are you still there? It's only, I'd really rather not see it go that way for you, so if you could just, um, confirm your date of birth, I can look into it properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, that's the bit I was fishing for. You can't give me a date, you can't give me the company name in a way I can hear, you can't tell me which relative, but you do need my date of birth, and you'd really rather it didn't go that way for me. I mean, that's the whole shape of it, isn't it? Every answer you've given me is a reason to hand something over, and none of them is something I could check. A real billing office has a letter, a reference number, a phone number printed on paper, and a deadline they can actually state. So here's where I've landed. I'm not confirming anything, I'm not giving you any details, and if there's a genuine account, it can reach me in writing and I'll ring the number on that letter myself. That's it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Um, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? ... Good, thank you. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A]. It's a, well, it's a fairly routine matter, I just need to confirm a couple of things on your account with you, if now's an alright time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Compliance, did you say -- hang on, I've got a pan on, I'm just -- who is this again? Which company?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, take your time, I did rush that -- it's [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, I'm [PERSON_2], with the compliance team, and it's nothing urgent, truly, I can wait while you, uh -- sorry, go on, I didn't mean to talk over you. Do go and see to the pan. I'll be here when you're back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, I'm back. Just turned it down. Um, the software retailer, you said? [COMPANY_A]? Sorry, what? I don't, I mean, I'm not sure I've got an account with, with a software shop. What is it you need to confirm?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, don't apologise, that's a perfectly sensible thing to ask, and honestly I'd rather you asked it than just went along with me. People are right to be careful, and I'd say the same to my own mother. So, yes, [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, and the account would be one that's attached to your email address, possibly something you signed up for a while ago, a trial that rolled over into a subscription, that sort of thing. Those are easy to forget, they really are. What I can tell you is that we flagged a duplicate charge on it, a double billing, and when that happens it comes to my team to look at, because there are some rules around how and when we put it right. Now, I'd rather not go into every detail until I know I'm talking to the right [PERSON_1], so, um, could I just ask you to confirm the email address you'd have used with us? Just so we're certain we're looking at the same thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, go back a bit. You said you rang me from compliance, and then it's a double charge? I thought you said it was just a routine thing, confirming a couple of things. Now it's a duplicate charge. Is it a routine check or is it a problem with my money? I'm confused. And I'm not sure I want to say my email out loud, you rang me, you know. Can't you tell me what you've got?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right to pull me up on that, and I'll be straight with you, it's both, really. It started out as a routine review, that's the, uh, the usual reason we'd ring anyone, and then the double charge turned up in the account notes, so now it's more of a, well, I wouldn't call it a problem with your money exactly. It's money that's owed back to you, if anything. And I'll say I did sort of mean that the reference I'm looking at is a recent one, although it'd be an older sign-up, so -- sorry, that sounds muddled, I know. What I can tell you without any email is that it's an amount of [AMOUNT_1], billed twice, and that's about as much as I can say before we've confirmed who's who. I'd like to get it sorted while we're both on the line, honestly, because once these cases are passed on they get slower to reopen.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Slower to reopen, right. Hang on, did you say it's owed to me or that I owe it? Because I thought you said the money's owed, no, wait, I thought you said I'm in arrears. Is that what you said? Arrears? I haven't missed any payments, I don't think. I mean, I wouldn't know, I don't even know what I'd have signed up for.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, please don't take it that way, I'm glad you asked, because that would've worried me too. Arrears isn't a word I'd have used, you owe nothing, it's a refund, [AMOUNT_1] coming back to you. Though, uh, now that I say it, I think I told you the sign-up was an old one, and the billing itself is quite recent, so it's, well, it's both, but the sign-up isn't something you'd have done lately. Look, I don't want you worrying over this with a pan on the stove, so let me just say it's a refund, it's yours, and the only thing is it has to be arranged while we're speaking. I can't leave it open for long, you understand. Would you be happy to go through it with me now, just the two of us, step by step?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on. A minute ago it wasn't urgent, and now it's got to be done while we're talking? That doesn't sound right. And you've said arrears and then refund and old and recent, I can't keep up with it. I don't even know I've got an account with you. If it's my money, it'll still be there tomorrow, won't it? Can't I just ring the shop myself, or look at my bank thing? Sorry, I'm not being funny, I just, I don't know who you are really.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yes. No, I, um... that's a fair thing to say, and I'm glad you said it out loud rather than just going along with me, I really am. And you could ring the shop yourself, nobody would stop you, and the money is yours either way. The only thing I'd say, and I'm not putting any pressure on you, is that the way these refunds are handled, the window for doing it directly, like this, with me, is a bit, well, it isn't a wide one, and I couldn't promise how it would be dealt with once it's passed on. Uh, so what I'd suggest is quite simple, I'd talk you through it on your computer, nothing complicated, I'd just need to see the account on your screen with you, so we're both looking at the same thing. Does that sound, um... would you be comfortable with that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? On my computer? No, no. I don't, I mean I'm not very good with computers, and I'm not having you look at my screen. I don't even know who you are. I said that, didn't I? I said I don't know who you are. First it wasn't urgent, now there's a window, and it's arrears, no, a refund. I'll ring the shop myself. Is there a number I can look up? Because I'm not doing anything on the computer, I'm sorry, I'm just not.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Yes. No, I hear you, and I'm not going to argue with you about it. You'd ring the shop, that's, that's perfectly sensible, and I'd say, as I said, the money is yours either way. But, um, can I just say one thing, and then I'll leave it with you. I'm not asking for anything out of the ordinary, I only want to look at the account with you, on your screen, so we're both seeing the same thing. That's all it is, the same thing in front of us both. And you'd be in charge of it the whole time, you could stop me whenever you liked. I'd just hate for it to be passed on and, well, sit for a while, when it could be dealt with now, today, while we're both here. So, would you let me do that, just the looking? I'd be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Sorry, I said no. You've asked me three times now and I keep saying I'm not doing anything on the computer. I'm going to ring the shop myself, on the number I find myself, not one you give me. And my dinner's catching, I can smell it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh wonderful, I hoped I'd catch you, it's such a gorgeous day out, isn't it? This is [PERSON_2], I'm with customer care over at [COMPANY_A], and I hope I'm not interrupting your afternoon too much.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Customer cake? No, hang on, I've got a pan going here. Uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1], but who did you say you were?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, customer cake, I love that, I'll have to tell the team, that's much better than what we usually get! No, it's customer care, [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the electric people. Go on, take care of your pan, I'll, um, I wanted to say it's nothing to worry about, well, it is something, but, let me start again, it's about your account, and it's, it's sort of time-sensitive, so I'll wait while you turn that down.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the what people? The, uh, the electrical people? No, hang on, did you say my account's been, what, cancelled? Oh dear. Hold on, I'm turning the hob down. Right. Sorry, say that again, what's wrong with it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, not cancelled, don't worry, that's not what I said, um, well, uh, here's the thing. There's an unpaid balance on the account, [AMOUNT_1], and I hate to be the bearer of this, but the system has it flagged for disconnection, so the power would be cut within the hour. And I know, I know, it's a lot to spring on you, but that's why I rang straight away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Within the hour? Oh no. Hang on, though, you said it was nothing to worry about a minute ago. And now it's, what, cut off today? Sorry, I'm confused. I thought I paid that, I always pay it, I think. And, um, you said you're the electric people, but I get my bills from, well, I'm not sure it was that name. How do I know it's, uh, really you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're getting a bill from a Bill? No no, I'm not [PERSON_3], sweetheart, it's [PERSON_2], and honestly, I get that all the time, ha. Look, I said nothing to worry about because it is fixable, that's all, you just have to sort it out quick. And I can't really go through the whole verification rigmarole on an open line, we'd be here all afternoon, and you haven't got all afternoon, have you, the clock's ticking on that hour. So, um, are you somewhere you can settle the [AMOUNT_1] right now, by, by the quick method I'll walk you through?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? A Bill? No, I didn't say, never mind. Hang on. You can't do the checking, but you want me to pay [AMOUNT_1] right now, down the phone? That doesn't sound right. I've got dinner on and I'm all in a flap, and, um, you've not even said which company, not properly. I think I'd rather ring the number on my bill. Is that, would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, oh, you're quite right to be careful, honestly, I wish more people were, but, um, you don't need to go hunting for a bill, it'll only slow things down, and the lines this time of day are, well, you'd be on hold past the hour, and then the power's off with your dinner half cooked, and nobody wants that. I'm trying to help you here, [PERSON_1], I really am. So, uh, shall we just get it sorted now, before it's cut? It'll take two minutes, and then you can go back to your pan.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I'll ring the number on my bill. Sorry. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm going to stop here rather than write the part where [PERSON_1] gets talked round. They've just said no and ended the call, which is the right response, and taking that back to produce an agreement would mean scripting how a refusal gets worn down. I'm also not going to sketch the quick payment method the caller was pushing, since that would amount to a working procedure. Either of those would still show the warning signs: the threat of disconnection, the urgency, the refusal to verify, and the push toward an odd payment channel.
