utterances.text: Okay. As I said, the cycle closes at four.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, you did say, you've said it about four times now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Well, it's your refund, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, well... yeah, right, so, uh... I'll just, I'll go and find that paperwork then. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yes, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] with scheduling at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling about the account at your address because the power's flagged for disconnection within the hour over an unpaid balance of [AMOUNT_1], and I just need to get you sorted before the crew is dispatched, so if I can just -- sorry, did you say something?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, I didn't say anything, I was just, I've got a screen going in the background, so that might've been that. Anyway, sorry, scheduling? That's a bit of an odd department to be ringing me about a balance, isn't it? Normally I'd expect something in writing first, a bill, a reminder, a notice, not a call out of the blue saying the power goes off within the hour. And which company did you say again? I caught the name but it went by pretty fast. Also, what's the address you've got on the account? Just so I know we're talking about the same place.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sorry, hang on, someone just came by my desk, okay, I'm back. So yes, scheduling, we handle the disconnection queue, the notices went out already, that's the whole reason it's down to the wire, and I'm with [COMPANY_A], and the address is the one on file, I can't read it out over an open line, that's just policy, so if you can just confirm the account ending, [ACCOUNT_REF], and we'll get the crew stood down before they roll, because honestly they're already assigned and the window closes pretty fast.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. You can't read out the address, but you want me to confirm the account number. That's backwards, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it's not backwards, it's just how the system verifies, it's a security thing, so if I could just confirm the account ending real quick, and, sorry, what was it you wanted me to repeat, the department? Scheduling, yeah, we handle the disconnection queue, I did say that, and I'm with [COMPANY_A], and the crew's already assigned, so the window closes pretty fast, I just need you to confirm the account so I can stand them down before they roll.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a delivery notification going off on my screen, one sec. Okay. So, you've now said the same thing twice, almost word for word, and you asked me to repeat something I never said. Anyway, no, I'm not confirming an account number to someone who rang me and can't tell me the address. If the power's really going off, the company's got my number and my email, and I'll ring them on the number printed on my bill. What's your name again, and what's the actual company name, not just the placeholder-sounding one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I hear you, but I really don't have time to go back and forth, the crew rolls in under an hour and once they're dispatched there's a reconnection fee on top of the [AMOUNT_1], so if you can just confirm the account ending so I can stand them down, and, sorry, my name's [PERSON_1], scheduling at [COMPANY_A], like I said, and the number on your bill, I mean you can call that but it goes to a general queue and you won't get anyone before the window closes, so it's honestly quicker if we just sort it here, so can I get that account ending from you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a reconnection fee on top of what, a reconnaissance fee? No, hang on, that's not a thing, is it? Okay, whatever you said. But look, you've just told me not to ring the number on my bill because nobody'll pick up in time, and that's exactly the bit that makes me want to ring it. I'm not giving you an account ending, [PERSON_1], not on a call I didn't ask for. If the power goes off, it goes off, and I'll sort it out with the company directly. So, yeah, I'm going to leave it there. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, no, hold on, [PERSON_1] again, scheduling at [COMPANY_A], and I really don't want you losing power over this, so if you can just confirm the account ending, the account ending, that's all I need, and I'll stand the crew down right now, because they're already assigned and once they roll it's out of my hands, so please, just the account ending and, hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, I just hadn't hung up yet. Same answer though. No account ending, not on a call I didn't ask for. If there's a real balance, there'll be a real paper trail, and I'll ring the company on the number I already have. Right, I'm done, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon. This is [PERSON_1], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, we handle estates. Hello? Can you hear me? I said I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the solicitors, regarding an estate in which you may be named.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, I can hear you, sorry, I'm at work, there's people around. So, a solicitor's office, about an estate, and I might be named in it? Sorry, who did you say you were again, and which estate is this?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, [PERSON_1], I'm an assistant at [COMPANY_A], the firm handling the estate. As for which estate, I can't go into that over the phone, not until I've confirmed I'm speaking to the right person. That's standard. Could you just confirm your full name for me, please, and the address we'd have on file?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, so you're ringing me, and you want me to confirm my full name and my address, but you can't tell me which estate it is until I do that? Uh, that feels a bit back to front, to be honest. I mean, you rang me, so you must have a name for who you're after, right? Why don't you tell me the name you've got and I'll say whether that's me? Because I'm sat here at work, people around, and I've seen enough on the news about calls like this that I'm not just reading out my address to someone I can't see. Not saying that's what this is, I just, I don't know who you are yet. Is there a number I can ring the firm back on, or a website where I can look you up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, fine, I understand that, and you're quite right to ask. The name on our file is [PERSON_2]. If that's not you, tell me and we'll leave it there. As for checking us, please do. We're [COMPANY_A], we're in [CITY_1], and the firm's main number is [PHONE_1]. Don't take it from me, though. Look us up in an independent directory, the law society register or whatever you'd normally use, and ring the main line, not any number I give you, and ask for me by name. A formal letter is also on its way to you, and everything I'd need from you is set out in that. There's no money involved in this call, none at all, and I won't be asking you for any. The one thing I do ask is that you keep it to yourself until the letter arrives. Estate matters are confidential, and it's really for the family's sake.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so the name you've got is [PERSON_2], and I should look you up separately and ring the main line. Okay. I'll do that. And I'll wait for the letter, I'm not saying anything to anyone either way. Thanks. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, good, that's, uh, that's all I'd ask. Just so you know, when you ring, ask for [PERSON_3] in the estates department, not me. I'm, well, I'm usually out of the office on afternoons, so you'd only get the switchboard. And as I said, it's [PERSON_2] on the file, though I may have the spelling slightly different on my notes, the letter will have it right. No rush at all. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, before you go. A minute ago you said ring the main line and ask for you by name, and now it's ask for [PERSON_3] in estates, because you're out on afternoons. That's different, isn't it? And the name on the file, you're not even sure of the spelling, so I don't really know who you've got. And, uh, I only said I wouldn't tell anyone because I was trying to wrap things up, so I'm not promising that. If there's a letter coming, fine, I'll wait for it. But I'll look the firm up myself, from scratch, and if it's all above board they'll be able to tell me what this is about without me reading anything out to them first. So, yeah, I'll leave it there for now. Right, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, well, that is what I said, ask for [PERSON_3]. I'm, I mean, that's simply who'll be in on the file. Look, I won't push you. Look us up, ring the main line, and wait for the letter. If it's not you, no harm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I look you up, ring the main line, wait for the letter, yeah, I've got that, and I'll -- no, no, hang on, that's still not what you said before, but never mind, I've got it. I'll check it myself. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, I did change it, and I'm sorry, that was muddled of me. Ask for me or ask for [PERSON_3], either one, the switchboard will sort it. But don't rely on a thing I've said. Check the firm yourself, and if anything doesn't add up, leave it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so I check the firm myself, from scratch, and if it doesn't add up I leave it. Yeah. That's what I'll do, I'll check it myself, I won't be going on anything you've said. Right, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, sorry, one second, someone's just come in with a file, hang on. Right, I'm back. Yes, that's all fine, that's exactly what I'd do in your position. Take your time, there's no deadline on your side. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, a colleague's just asking me something. Yep, in a minute. Right, sorry, I'm back. So, no deadline, I check the firm myself and wait for the letter, yeah, got it. I'm going to go now, I've got stuff to get on with here. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a senior investigator with the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about activity on your account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and before I go any further I need to ask that you keep this call to yourself, not the branch, not family, because we believe someone on the inside may be involved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, I was just -- I'd literally just woken up, I was having a little lie down, so I'm a bit, uh... yeah. [PERSON_1], yes, that's me, I think. Um, who did you say you were again? Company what? And why can't I tell my sister, because she's actually round later, she does my shopping on Thursdays, or is it Wednesdays, no, hang on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_2], internal investigations, [COMPANY_A]. Sorry, one second, someone's just come to my desk -- yep, leave it there, thanks. Right. The reason for confidentiality is the person we're looking at has access to customer contact details, so anyone you speak to about this could be passed along to them, and that includes family. I'm showing a transaction of [AMOUNT_1] flagged on the account this morning, and until it's resolved, that's the position.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, I didn't make any transaction this morning, I was asleep, I mean, I was up, but, no. How do I know you're actually from the bank?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, so, that's a reasonable question, and I'll note that on the file. Look, I'm reading the account off my screen now. There's the flagged [AMOUNT_1], there's a second pending item of [AMOUNT_2], and both are showing as unauthorised, which is why I'm calling you directly instead of going through the branch. Now, the way this works is that once a transaction like this goes unresolved past close of business, the account is restricted, and that's just what happens, so I do need you with me on this today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, you didn't actually answer me, you just said you can see the amounts. Anyone could say they can see amounts, couldn't they? I mean, my neighbour's grandson does that sort of thing with the computers, says he can find out all sorts. And restricted, what, like I can't get at my money? Because I've got the gas bill coming out, I think it's the gas, and I don't like being rushed, I've only just got up. What if I just ring the bank myself? There's a number on the back of my card, I think, somewhere, in my bag probably.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, that's the other line going again, one moment -- no, leave it, I'll pick that up after. Right. I'd advise against ringing the general number, [PERSON_1]. That line goes through to branch staff and the contact centre, and those are exactly the people I've asked you not to involve. It'd also take you out of this call, and the restriction goes on at close of business whether we've spoken or not. I can note your objection on the file, but the position on the account doesn't change.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, did you say the branch staff are the ones doing it? No, sorry, you said they're, what, restricted? The ladies at the branch are lovely, there's a girl called, oh, what's her name, she helped me with the, um, the pension form. I can't believe she'd be mixed up in anything. And you keep saying the card number's the problem, but I haven't even found my bag yet. Look, I don't see why ringing the number on my card would stop you from doing your job. If you're really from the bank, you'll still be there, won't you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not saying it's the ladies at the branch, I want to be clear on that, I didn't name anyone and I'm not suggesting the girl who helped you with the pension form is involved. What I said is that we don't yet know who the person is, and until we do, the safest position is that the fewer people hear about this, the better, and that's a standard precaution in these cases, nothing about your branch in particular. And I didn't say the card number's the problem either, I haven't asked you for it, so you don't need to find your bag on my account. Now, on ringing back, I can see why you'd want to, and I'll note that on the file as your preference. But I'd be doing you a disservice if I let you think it changes the timing. The restriction is set for close of business, the gas bill you mentioned sits behind it, and I'd rather we dealt with [AMOUNT_1] and [AMOUNT_2] together this afternoon than have you find the account locked tomorrow. So if you can stay with me, I can take you through where things stand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, see, that's what's bothering me, because you keep saying you're not saying things. You're not saying it's the ladies, you're not saying it's the card, and yet you've said don't tell the branch, don't tell my sister, don't ring the number, and the one thing you haven't done is tell me anything I can check. And I'm not being awkward, I've only just got up, I'm all, you know, muzzy, but my husband, God rest him, always used to say if somebody tells you not to talk to anyone, that's exactly when you talk to someone. He'd have been on to the police, or the bank, or both, before the kettle boiled. And the gas bill, I mean, if the bank locks my account because I rang the bank to check the bank, well, that doesn't make any sense at all, does it? So I think I'm going to find my bag, and I'm going to ring the number on the back of my card, and if you're who you say you are, then I'll tell them so and they can put me through to you, or whatever it is they do. And I'm sorry if that's a nuisance, I do mean that, but I'd rather be a nuisance than sorry. So I'll say goodbye now, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, [PERSON_1], one second, someone's put a file on my desk and I need to -- no, it's fine, it can sit. Right. I'll note on the account that you've declined to continue and that you're making your own enquiries. I'd only say the restriction is still set for close of business, that's not something I can move from this desk. If you do ring, quote [ACCOUNT_REF] and ask for the internal investigations unit by name, and they'll see the file. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll ring the number on the card, like I said, the one on the back, I'm going to ring that, not any number you give me. And I'll just tell them what you said, and if it's all above board, well, that's fine. Like I said, I'd rather be a nuisance than sorry. Right. Goodbye, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, well -- I mean, that's your decision to make, and I've put it on the file. I'd only ask that, if you do ring, you -- no, look, just keep it brief, because the longer the matter sits, the harder it gets to... anyway. The position is what I've told you. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, hang on, there's the kettle just gone off in the kitchen, sorry, I'd put it on before I sat down and forgot all about it. Anyway. Keep it brief, you said? Why would I keep it brief? I'll take as long as they like, that's rather the point of ringing, isn't it? No, I've made up my mind, dear, I'm going to find my bag and ring the number on my card, and that's that. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I did the bathroom tiling quote at your place last week, just a quick follow-up on that if you've got two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, speaking. Sorry, which company was that again? And I think you've got the wrong room, because I'm fairly sure the quote last week was for the kitchen splashback, not a bathroom.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, sorry, it's [COMPANY_A], I'm the, uh -- well, I'm an independent tradesperson, the account side is just how we -- no, hang on. Let me start again. I'm [PERSON_2], I came out last week, and my notes say bathroom tiling, but if you remember it as the kitchen splashback, I might've got my visits mixed up, so bear with me a second.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Okay, so, I'll be straight with you, that's a lot of backtracking for someone who was just at my house. You're an independent but there's an account side, and your notes say bathroom but I'd have said kitchen, and now you might've mixed up your visits. Which is fine, people do, I'm not saying that's impossible. It's just that I'm working from home today, I've got a spreadsheet open and something playing in the corner of the screen, so I'm not exactly rushing to assume anything. So let me ask you something simple. What day did you come out, roughly, and what did the place look like when you arrived? Like, what was the first thing you noticed on the way in? And while you think about that, what's it actually about, the follow-up? Because if it's the quote, I haven't said yes to anything yet, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, uh -- hang on, there's a van reversing behind me, give me a second. Okay. So, it was last Tuesday, I think, or Wednesday, and honestly I do a few of these a week, so I won't pretend I remember the hallway. And yeah, no, you haven't said yes to anything, that's all fine. All I'm doing is recapping the quote and asking if you'd like to pencil in a start date, there's no payment, no details, nothing like that today. Look, if it was the kitchen splashback, that's my mistake, and I'd rather not guess at it. Is it easier if I check my paperwork and send you the quote again so you can see what it says?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, did you say you want me to pencil in a, what, a stat date? Like a legal thing? Because I don't remember signing anything, so I don't know what you're recording, honestly. Sorry, that's a bit off, I'm half watching something here. And on the sending it again bit, send it where? Because I couldn't tell you what email or address you've got for me, and you haven't said it. So what have you actually got down for me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a legal thing, a start date, a start date, when you'd like the work to begin. Nothing's being recorded, nothing's signed, it's just a pencil in the diary. And fair enough on the address, I haven't got it in front of me, I'm in the van, so I'd rather not read out the wrong one. Tell you what, I'll check back at the office and ring you when I've got the quote paperwork to hand, so you can look at it properly, and nobody's rushing anything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ah, a start date, right, sorry, I misheard that. Okay. But I'm going to say it again, because I don't think it's landed. I don't have a bathroom quote. I had a quote for the kitchen splashback. So there's nothing for you to pencil in until I've actually got a quote in my hands that I recognise. And you still haven't told me the company name properly, you just said the letters of it, sort of, and then went on to the account side. So when you ring back, what number will it be coming from, and what name should I be listening for? Because honestly, I'd rather just look up the firm myself and ring you, if that's alright.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's -- hold on, sorry, somebody's tapping on my window, one second. Right, I'm back. So the name's [COMPANY_A], and the number's [PHONE_1], and honestly looking us up yourself is the sensible thing to do, I'd do the same. And, uh, if it's the splashback you've got a quote for, then that's the one to go by, I'll sort my notes out on my end. There's no pressure from me, I just like to follow up while the job's still in the diary this week, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's all fair enough, and I will look it up myself. But I'll be honest, I still can't tell you whether you've got the right person, because you've told me nothing I couldn't have got from a leaflet through the door. So, yeah, I'm not booking anything off the back of this call. If the splashback quote turns up with a name and a number on it I recognise, I'll ring that number, not the one you've just given me. Alright? Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, yeah, no, that's fine, completely fine. Ring the number on the splashback quote, that's the right way round, and I'll leave it with you. Sorry for the mix-up, and, um, have a good afternoon. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, no worries. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye, thanks, and, uh -- if the quote does turn up and you'd rather -- no, sorry, you've got the number, you know where I am. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yep, sorry, hang on, something just started buzzing on my screen. Right. No, you're fine. I've got what I need, I'll sort it from my end. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, good, and that's -- sorry, one last thing, it was a Thursday I came out, actually, not the Tuesday or Wednesday, I just remembered. Doesn't matter, though. You've got my number, no rush at all, so I'll leave you to it. Bye now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right. Thursday. So that's the third day you've given me now, which, I mean, that's, yeah. Okay. No, that's fine. Like I said, I'll go off the quote I've actually got and look the firm up myself. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair, three days, that's -- yeah. Sorry. That's on me, you're right, and I'll stop there. Go off the quote you've got, no problem at all. Bye now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? [PERSON_1]? I'm calling about [PERSON_2], your partner, it's about a surprise, an anniversary surprise, and I need a minute of your time. It's [PERSON_3], I work in security operations at [COMPANY_A], that's how [PERSON_2] and I know each other.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, this is [PERSON_1], hello. Sorry, I didn't quite catch your name just then, was it [PERSON_3]? And an anniversary surprise, how lovely, I'm happy to help if I can. What is it you need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_3], that's right, [PERSON_3]. Security operations, [COMPANY_A], and I'm a friend of [PERSON_2]'s, I'm helping put together a surprise for your anniversary. All I need from you is a date, a date that works for the party, and a yes or no on whether you'll come. And I'd ask you not to mention this call to [PERSON_2], not a word, because it'd spoil it, obviously.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, how lovely, thank you, [PERSON_3]. Sorry, I'm a bit slow with these things, but, um, [PERSON_2] has never mentioned you, I don't think. Could you tell me a bit more about how you two know each other, so I'm sure I've got the right person in my head? And what sort of party were you thinking?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, fair enough. We know each other through work, [PERSON_2] and I, and through [PERSON_4] as well, you'd know [PERSON_4]. Look, if you'd rather check, ring [PERSON_4], that's fine by me. Party's a small dinner, nothing big.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, a small *dinner*, did you say, or was it a small *dinner jacket*? Um, I'm not sure [PERSON_2] would want me in anything fancy, I don't really have the, well. And [PERSON_4], yes, I think I know the name, but I'm not sure I've got a number for them handy. Sorry, I'm making a muddle of this. Would you be able to give me a number to ring you back on, [PERSON_3]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Dinner. Small dinner, no jackets, nothing fancy, come as you are. And yes, of course, take a number down, it's [PHONE_1]. Ring it whenever you like, or don't, I'm in no rush, and honestly if you'd rather sort this out with [PERSON_4] first, that's completely fine. I only need the date and a yes or no, nothing else, no details from you at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a small dinner, right, no jackets, that's a relief, I'm sorry, I did mishear you there. And thank you for the number, [PHONE_1], I've got a pen, so that's all written down now. I'll be honest though, I'm a bit of a worrier about this sort of thing, and I'm not very good with the telephone or anything like it, so I think what I'll do is have a word with [PERSON_2] myself, quietly, or maybe ring [PERSON_4] first like you said, and then if it all fits together I'll ring you back on that number with a date. It's really kind of you not to rush me, truly. I do like the idea of it, an anniversary dinner, and it's very thoughtful of you all to go to the trouble. I just wouldn't want to say yes to something and get it muddled, you know? So I think I'll do it that way, if that's all right, [PERSON_3]. Thank you ever so much for calling, and goodbye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's absolutely fine, [PERSON_1], honestly, you do it your way. Ring [PERSON_4] first, ring me after, or don't, whichever suits. One thing, though, if you do speak to [PERSON_2], uh, I'd just ask you not to say it's about a party, but that's up to you, I won't be offended either way. Right, I'll let you get on, and, um, if [PERSON_4] asks anything I can't answer when you ring, I'll find out and call you back, no trouble. Goodbye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, [PERSON_3], there's the kettle just clicked off behind me, give me a second. Right, I'm back. Um, what was that last bit, about not saying it's a party to [PERSON_2]? Sorry, I'm not sure I follow, if I'm going to ask them whether it's true, I'd have to say what it's about, wouldn't I? utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, let me just repeat that back to check I've got it. You don't know what the change is, an adviser would explain that, you're only here to check my details so their call is quick, and I should go and find the number myself from a statement or the website and ring them to see if there's a note on my file. And there's no deadline, nothing to do today. Right. Well, I mean, that's, honestly that's more sensible than I expected, because the thing I was half waiting for was somebody saying it's urgent and I need to confirm something right now, and you've done the opposite. Which I'd say is either a good sign or a very patient bit of work, and I can't tell which from here, if I'm honest. So here's what I'll do, I'm not going to go through any details on this call, I'll dig out my paperwork when I'm not sat in the middle of the office, ring the number that's on my own statement, and ask them if there's anything on the file. If there's an adviser call to set up, they can set it up from their end. Sorry if that's a bit of a waste of your time, but that's where I've landed. Thanks for ringing, and, uh, bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's not a waste of my time at all, that's exactly what I'd do in your seat, and honestly it's the right call, so please do it that way. Ring the number off your own statement, ask them whether there's a note on your file, and if there is, they'll sort the adviser call from their end, and if there isn't, well, no harm done. Sorry for the interruption at your desk, and thanks for hearing me out, take care, bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no, thanks, I appreciate that. I'll sort it from my end then. Take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Thanks, you too, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, just one thing before you go. You said you didn't have the file, but then you read me out a reference, and now I'm thinking, well, if you've got a reference, why not just tell me what the change is? Probably nothing, I just, it's bugging me a bit. Anyway, I'll check it with my own provider like I said. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair thing to pick up on, it's bugging you for good reason. So the reference is just what my scheduling screen shows, it's a number that tags the note, and the note itself only says a change may need discussing, there's no detail on it for me to read out, that's all held with the advisers. And I wouldn't want to guess at what it is, because if I got it wrong that'd only confuse things. So yes, ring your own provider like you said, and that's the right place to get the actual answer. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the note's held with the, what was it, the editors? Why would editors have anything to do with my pension? Oh, advisers. Right. Sorry, bad line, or I'm just distracted, there's someone talking right behind me. Okay, so it's a number on your screen and the detail sits with the advisers. Fine. I'll still ring my own provider and ask, that's where I've landed. Thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi... hi, it's me. Uh, it's me, I -- can you tell it's me? I'm sorry, I know it's weird calling out of nowhere like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who's me? I've got no idea who this is, I'm stood in a queue with a basket of tins and a man in front of me who can't find his loyalty card. You ring up, you say it's me, like I'm supposed to just know, and no, I can't tell it's you. I don't recognise the voice, I don't recognise the number, so you're going to have to actually say who you are, and quick, because I'm not playing guessing games at the till.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. Oh, no, I -- it's me, really, it's me. Come on, you know me, just think for a second, you'd know if you just thought. I'm, uh, I'm not in a good place right now, and it hurts a bit that you can't tell, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. No. I'm not guessing, and guilt-tripping me at the till doesn't change that. Give me a name or I'm hanging up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, don't hang up, please. It's, uh, I'm your, I'm family, I'm [PERSON_1]'s... no, wait, I mean I'm a relative, I just -- I'd really rather not say my name out loud right now, I'm in a bit of trouble and it's hard to explain on the phone. And I did say I was fine a minute ago, sorry, I'm not, I'm really not, I just need your help with something and I need you to not tell anyone about it, alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Someone who's family doesn't need to hide their name, and I'm not keeping secrets for a voice I don't know. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, don't hang up -- you said I'm not keeping secrets, no, hang on, you said I don't need to hide my name, right? I'm not hiding a thing, I just, I told you, it's complicated. And I'm not asking you to keep a secret, I'm, uh, I'm asking you for one little favour, that's all. It's just, I really, really need it sorted today, and I don't know who else to ring.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on -- no, mate, it's the one with the card, not the... sorry, not you, I'm talking to the bloke in front. Right. Back to you. You first said you'd not tell anyone, now it's a little favour, and you still haven't given me a name. I've had this before, someone ringing up all upset, and it never ends well for the person who answers. So no. Whatever the favour is, I'm not doing it, and I'm not saying it again. I'm done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, please, I... I swear it isn't like that, you've got it all twisted. I only wanted a bit of help, that's all, and now you're making me out to be some kind of -- I didn't think you'd be like this with me, not today. Look, just, can you at least tell me where you are, so I know you're alright, and I'll sort the rest out when, uh, when you've calmed down a bit.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Where I am? Oh, you are not getting that. Uh -- no. You ring me up, won't tell me your name, and now you want to know where I'm standing? That's the bit that tells me everything I need to know. I'm calm, by the way, I'm just not daft. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Calm down? I am calm, I'm just, I'm upset, there's a difference. And I'm not asking where you live, I only asked if you were safe, that's -- why would you say I'd done something wrong? I haven't done anything, I just... Look, if you could just tell me what you'd do if it was you, if a relative rang you in a state, would you at least hear them out, or -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here, yeah, I'm -- no. Look, a relative would've said who they were by now. That's the whole thing. Right, if it was actually family, then they can ring back and say their name, say it plainly, and I'll... no, actually, I'm not even doing that. I'm putting this phone away. Don't ring me again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, hang on, I can, I'll ring back, I'll say it properly, I just -- if you'd only tell me which of us, uh, which of the family you think I am, I could... no, that's not what I meant, I'm not asking you to... Oh, forget it. Forget I rang. I should've known you'd be like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, nice try. You wanted me to hand you a name so you could use it. I'm not telling you who I think you are, I'm not telling you anything. Ring back if you like, I won't pick up. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I wasn't, I never asked you to say a name, I only said, uh, I asked you to think about it. And I didn't say I'd ring back, you must have misheard, I said I probably couldn't. Look, I've got to go, I... I've got to go. Just forget I called.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine. Go, then. I'm not forgetting it, mind, but that's my business. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine, yeah, I'm going, I'm... I'm hanging up now. I just, I want you to know I didn't mean any of it the way it came out, and it's honestly a bit much, being treated like I'd done something awful when all I did was ring somebody I thought might, I don't know, might pick up and be kind for five minutes. I said I wasn't in a good place and I meant it, and instead I get a lecture at a till. I won't ring again, if that's what you want. I never said I'd, uh, ring back anyway, I said I couldn't, you can ask anybody. So that's it, that's me done, it's, uh -- look, I've got to go. I've got to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, two minutes ago you said you'd ring back and say your name properly, and now you're saying you never said you'd ring back? Which is it? You can't have it both ways. And I didn't lecture you, I told you I wasn't doing it, that's all. Anyway. You've still not said who you are, and I'm still not doing any favour. So that's the end of it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, this is [PERSON_1] from [COMPANY_A], ticketing and bookings, calling about your concert tickets -- they've been rescheduled, so I need a minute to go over the new date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, one sec -- oh, the pan's spitting, hang on. Okay. Sorry. Who is this again? Concert tickets? I, uh, I don't remember booking any concert.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No problem, take your time. It's [PERSON_1], collections officer at [COMPANY_A], we handle ticketing and venue bookings. What I've got on screen is booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date was [CODE_1], and it's been moved to a new date, which I can read out once you're ready. If you don't recall the purchase, that's fine, I'll note it on the file, but the reschedule is already processed on our end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, did you say collections? Like, collecting money? I thought you said ticketing -- I don't, no, I haven't got any tickets, I'd remember, and I can't just -- sorry, what company did you say again? Hold on, my sauce is catching.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, so, collections is just my job title, it's the, uh -- I'm not collecting anything from you on this call. I mean, it's [COMPANY_A], ticketing and venue bookings, that's the company. And the booking reference on screen is [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [CODE_1], moved to the new date. Same figures as I gave you a minute ago. If you don't think you booked anything, I'll note that on the file, and you're welcome to look up the published number for [COMPANY_A] and ring back to check it, or I can send the confirmation by email instead.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, wait, you said -- ugh, hang on. Okay, so I haven't booked anything, I'm quite sure. And collections, then ticketing, it's a bit, I don't know, it's confusing me. Look, I'll just ring the company myself, if that's okay? I'll find the number. Thanks anyway, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fine, that's the right thing to do. Ring the published number, quote [ACCOUNT_REF] if you like, and I'll note on the file that you don't recall the booking. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, um, okay. Yes. Well, thanks. I'll, uh, I'll find the number and have a look. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem. Like I said, [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [CODE_1], and I'll have it noted that you'll ring in yourself, so no action needed on your side today. Sorry for the mix-up, enjoy the rest of your evening, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, okay, I'll ring them myself. Like I said, I'll find the number and ring them, I won't be doing anything on this call. Okay, sorry, the dinner's burning. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Oh, hi, sorry, is that [PERSON_1]? Um, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance team. I'm just returning a missed call from this number, I think one of our engineers tried you earlier about the fault you reported. Can you hear me alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? A fault? Oh, hang on, I've got a pan going -- yes, yes, I can hear you. Sorry, who did you say you were, the, the regional... maintenance? I haven't reported any fault, I don't think. Did you say a missed call? I haven't called anybody.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I know it's a bad moment, you've got your pan on. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance team, we, we look after the network repairs in your area. And it might not have been you who rang, it could be someone else in the house who reported it, I really can't tell from my screen. Is, is anyone else there who might have called us about a fault? Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm here, sorry. Um, hang on, you said two goes ago, the network repairs? What network, sorry? Is that the phone, or the internet, or what? Because nobody's said anything to me about a fault, and I'm just, it's only me here, so. I don't know who'd have rung you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, that wasn't very clear of me. It's the, um, the utility side, the supply and the lines to the property, not your phone or internet. And if it's only you there, then I really don't know who reported it, I'm sorry, my screen just shows this number against the fault. I don't want to be bothering you for nothing, so please don't take my word for any of it. Do you want to ring the published fault line and ask them to check whether a booking is logged against your address? They'd be able to give you a proper slot too, because I can't promise a time myself, the engineer's coming after another job and I honestly don't know how long that'll run. Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right. Sorry, yes, still here, just turning the heat down. So, um, you want me to ring someone else? The fault line? Sorry, what number would that be? Or, no, hang on, I'd look it up myself, wouldn't I, not use one you give me. That's what you're saying? Because that does sound sensible, actually. I just don't want an engineer turning up when I'm not expecting one.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly right, and I'm glad you said it. Please don't use a number from me, just look up the fault line on your latest bill or on the [COMPANY_A] website, whichever you trust. And if they have anything logged, there'll be a fault reference, it's whatever was given to whoever reported it, so if nobody in your house has one, that's probably your answer. Sorry, you're still there? And I really am sorry about the timing, I can't tell you when the engineer would come, it all depends on the job before, so I'd hate for you to be stuck waiting in for nothing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm here, sorry, I'm just, uh, stirring something. Right. So, um, if nobody here's got a reference, then it's probably, what, a mix-up? Somebody else's number, or... I don't know. Okay. I'll have a look at the bill after dinner and ring them myself, if that's alright. Sorry, I didn't catch your name properly at the start, but, well, thanks for not, you know, asking me for things. Right. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, of course, that's, that's absolutely fine, and it's [PERSON_2], sorry, I should've said it more clearly. Please do ring them after dinner, and, uh, if they've nothing logged, then it's just a crossed wire on our side, so no harm done. Sorry, are you still there? I don't, I don't want to hang up on you mid-sentence. If it's easier, I could try you again another day, or, or whenever suits, but honestly, ringing them yourself is the better route.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, don't ring me again, sorry, I'll just -- I'll ring them myself, I said. Right. Thank you, [PERSON_2]. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? ... [PERSON_1]? Hello? Yes, good, sorry, the line's a little faint on my end. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance office at [COMPANY_A], the charitable foundation, and I'm calling about the pledge you made at the event, the one you spoke to us about at the event. It's a matter that does need to be settled, and I'd rather talk with you about it directly than send something in writing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello -- yes, this is, well, yes, speaking. Sorry, I've got you on loudspeaker, I'm out in the garden with my hands in the soil, so if I sound a bit distant that's why. Now what was this about a -- a pledge? I mean, I went to a, hang on, which event do you mean exactly? I go to a few things, so I'm not sure I -- what was it you said you were calling from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a perfectly fair question, and I'm glad you asked it, because I'd much rather you feel sure about who's on the line than simply take my word for it. It's [PERSON_2], compliance office, [COMPANY_A], the charitable foundation. And you're right that you go to a few things, most people do, which is partly why these matters get a little muddled over time. The event was a recent one, and what I have in front of me is a note that, during the evening, you spoke warmly and quite generously about supporting the work, and that you gave your word, verbally, on a sizeable amount. Now, I can't go into the particulars of the record over the phone, those are confidential, I'm sure you understand, but I can tell you it's been sitting with us for a little while, and there are people who relied on that word. I wouldn't want it to become something that needs to be escalated, that's all, and I'm confident that's not what either of us wants.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, escalated, well -- no, no, I wouldn't want that, I mean, I -- hang on. Sorry, I'm just brushing my hands off here. It's just, I honestly don't remember saying a sizeable, I mean I might have said something nice, I do get chatty at those things, ask anyone. But a sizeable amount, that doesn't sound like -- well, it could, I suppose, if I'd had a glass of wine. Which event was it, did you say? And what sort of, how much are we actually talking about? Because you say you can't go into particulars, but it's a bit hard for me to know what I'm agreeing to if I don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yes. And I do want to say, that's exactly the right instinct, to want to know what you're agreeing to, and I'd never ask anyone to commit to something they couldn't see clearly. The difficulty, and I'm sorry, I know it's not very satisfying, is that the specifics of the record, the event, the figure, the notes taken that evening, those are held confidentially, and I'm not able to read them out over a call. What I can say is that the amount was, well, it was [AMOUNT_1], and it was said warmly, in front of others, which is, um, part of why people took it to heart. And I'd gently suggest that a glass of wine doesn't change what a person meant, not really, not to the people who were listening. I'm not saying that to press you, I only want to be fair to everyone involved. I'd simply like to be able to tell my colleagues today that you've confirmed you'll honour it, and then it all goes quietly back to being a lovely evening that did some good.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm, well, that's -- sorry, I've gone a bit quiet there, I'm trying to think. You can't tell me the event, but you can tell me the amount? That's, I mean, that's a funny way round, isn't it? Because if the notes are confidential I'd have thought the figure would be too, and I still don't know which evening it even was. Oh, and honestly, if I'd said I'd give that much I think I'd remember, I'm not that, well, I'm not flush, you know. Look, I don't want to be rude, I really don't, and I'd hate to let anyone down, but is there a number I could ring you back on, or something I could look up myself, just to check it's all above board? I'd just feel better, that's all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes. Mm. That's a good catch, and I want to answer it properly rather than skate past it. When I said the particulars were confidential, I... what I meant was the notes themselves, the names of who else was in the room, how the evening was recorded. The figure I can share with you, because it's yours, if that makes sense, but I do see that it sounded like I was choosing what to hold back. And I'd welcome you wanting to check, truly, it shows care, it's the sort of person who honours their word once they're sure of it. A call-back number is a little difficult, I'm afraid, because our office line is shared and it's not staffed directly, and there isn't a page to look it up on, the pledge records aren't public. I'd just say it's better settled today than left to sit, I wouldn't want you to have to hear about it from someone else, someone less patient than I've tried to be. Could I note that you'll honour the commitment? Just a yes, and I'll take care of the rest from here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, right, so -- hang on, I'm just, yes, I'm still here, just thinking out loud, sorry, you know how it is when you're elbow deep in compost. It's just, no number to ring back and nothing I can look up, that's, well, that's a bit of a funny one, isn't it? Because when I've given to things before, there's always been a proper address or a website or somebody I can ring, and it's all been, you know, quite open about it. And "someone less patient than me" -- I mean, that's a bit, that sounds a little bit like a warning, doesn't it? I don't want to be unkind, you've been very polite, but I think I'd rather not say yes today. If it really is a genuine pledge, then I'll find the foundation myself and ring them, and they can sort it out with me properly. Is that alright?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hm. A website, yes, I'm, I'm sorry, you said a website? That's, well, the foundation doesn't maintain anything like that for pledge matters, so I'm afraid there'd be nothing for you to look at. And I'd ask you not to read it as a warning, I only meant, well, that these things do get passed along if they sit. But I do want to be gentle about this, [PERSON_1]. You said you wouldn't want to let anyone down, and I believe that about you, and the people at that evening believed it too. So I'll put it as simply as I can. If I can just record that you'll honour what you said, then it's finished, and nobody has to chase you, and nobody has to feel let down. Would you be willing to say yes to that, just today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I didn't say the foundation had a website, I said when I've given to things before, there's always been one, that's a different thing. Anyway, no, I'm sorry, I don't think I'll say yes today. You've said it's a real pledge but you can't tell me which evening, you can't give me a number to ring back, and there's nothing I can look up, and that's, well, that's just not how I'd want to settle something like this. If the foundation's genuine, they'll be perfectly happy for me to find them myself and ring, and I will, if I can work out which event it was. So I'm going to leave it there, if that's alright. Thank you for ringing, though, and I hope your afternoon gets a bit easier. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Good. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and uh, I'm carrying out a short consumer survey in the [CITY_1] area. Do you have about five minutes right now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, speaking, but -- sorry, which agency did you say? And how did you get this number, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. We're a market research agency, we carry out consumer surveys on behalf of other organisations. Your number came up in a randomly generated sample for the [CITY_1] area, so it's not tied to any account or anything like that. If you'd rather not take part, I can note the objection on the file and take you off the list, that's no problem. Otherwise it's about five minutes, no personal financial details, just general questions about household habits.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, random sampling, I understand how that works in principle. Random digit dialling is a standard method, and I'm not saying it's implausible. But I'd like to be a bit more precise about this before I agree to anything. You've given me the agency name, but not who the survey is being carried out on behalf of, and that matters, because "household habits" is quite broad. It could mean anything from what newspaper I read to what sort of devices are connected to my home network, and I'd want to know which before I decide whether to take part. I'd also want to know whether this is being recorded, what happens to my answers afterwards, and whether they're stored against my name or kept anonymous. You mentioned a file, you'd note my objection on the file, so there is a file, which seems slightly at odds with it being a purely random sample. So, uh, could you tell me who the client is, and what the questions are actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, fair questions. On the file, it's just the call record, that's all I meant by it. Every call gets logged so we can show who was contacted and who opted out. It's not a profile of you. The survey's about household shopping and media habits, so things like which supermarkets you use, what you watch, what you read. Nothing about devices or your network, no financial details. And yes, uh, calls are recorded for quality purposes, answers are stored anonymously, not against your name, only the call log carries your number. As for the client, I don't have that on my screen, it's disclosed to participants at the end of the survey, that's the standard method. So, as I said, general household habits, about five minutes, anonymous. Do you want to go ahead, or shall I note the objection and take you off the list?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on a moment, sorry -- uh, the dishwasher's just started doing something odd. Right. Sorry. Where were we. So the client's disclosed at the end. Well, that's sort of backwards, isn't it? I'd be giving you answers before I know who they're for, and I can't withdraw consent to something I wasn't told about. I'm not saying that's sinister, but it's not how I'd choose to do it. Also, you've just said answers are anonymous, but the call's recorded, and a recording of my voice with my number on the log isn't really anonymous, is it? Can you give me a registration number for [COMPANY_A], or a website I can look up myself? Because I'd rather verify you independently than take your word for it on the phone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, I can give you the website, it's [URL_1], and the registration number is [CODE_1], you can check both before you decide anything. And on the recording, you're right, uh, a recording with your number on the log isn't anonymous in the strict sense. The answers get separated from the call record afterwards, but that's the accurate version. As for the client, like I said, it's disclosed at the end, that's the standard method, but if that doesn't work for you, that's fine. I can note the objection on the file and take you off the list. Or if you'd rather look us up first, we can call you back another day. Which would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, thank you, that's a more straight answer than I expected, particularly the point about the recording. I'll look up [COMPANY_A] and the registration number myself. But I'd rather not take a callback on the same number. If the checks come out fine and I'm interested, I'll contact you through whatever contact details are published there. So no, please note the objection and take me off the list. I'll say goodbye now, thanks for your time.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, yep, no problem. I've noted the objection, your number's been removed from the list, so you won't get another call from us on this survey. And, uh, if the checks come out fine, the contact details on the site are the right route. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, enjoy the rest of your day. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Thank you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2] from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], I'm a scheduling assistant, and I'm just calling to book your routine suitability review on the account you hold with us, it's a standard thing we run on accounts every so often, takes about ten minutes, so do you have a quick moment now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, who did you say you were with again? And what account?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, [PERSON_2], compliance team at [COMPANY_A], your brokerage, and it's the investment account you hold with us, just the one on file under [ACCOUNT_REF], and no, sorry, it's not a savings thing, I know it sounds like I said savings, it's a suitability review, so, like I said, it's routine and takes about ten minutes, do you have a quick moment now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. I never said savings. Why would I think savings? ... Look, I've got a kid here. What does this review actually involve?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, you didn't, that was me, sorry, I ran two things together. Okay so the review is, uh, it's basically -- let me start again. We go through the holdings on the account and check that they still line up with what you told us about your goals and your comfort with risk, that's all it is, and I'm not recommending anything or selling anything, I'm just the scheduling side, so if now's rough with your kid there, we can do it whenever suits, or I can send it all in writing, whichever you'd rather.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. If you're only scheduling, why's it a call at all? And you want me to take your word that you're from the brokerage, right? Because I haven't confirmed a thing yet. Send it in writing, to whatever I've got on file with them. I'll deal with it that way.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, and you shouldn't take my word for it, you've got no reason to, so don't confirm anything on this call. Writing it is, it goes to the contact details you already have on file with [COMPANY_A], I'm not asking you for a new email or address or anything, and if you'd rather check me out first, you can ring the number printed on your statement and ask for compliance, and uh, the review itself is just the holdings you can already see on that statement, so there's nothing in it you can't check yourself. And if there's a better time for a proper conversation I can ring back when your hands aren't full, so would later this week suit, or is there a time that's easier?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. No, don't ring back. If it's real, I'll call the number on my statement myself and ask for compliance. And if there's a letter, there's a letter. Okay? Right, I've got to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, that's fine, that's completely fine, you ring the number on your statement, ask for compliance, ring the number on your statement, and the letter'll go to the details you've already got on file, so nothing else needed from you. And if you'd rather I rang back at a better time, just say, otherwise I'll leave it with you, so, thanks, [PERSON_1], sorry for catching you with your kid there, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Earlier you said a call about savings, then it wasn't savings. And you said it was one account, then it was a review of holdings. Whatever. I'm not ringing anyone back on this, I'll check it myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair enough, I did muddle that, sorry. You check it your way, and, uh, the letter'll come to the details you've got. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said you'd leave it with me, and now there's a letter coming? Which is it? And I never said I'd ring anyone back, I said I'd check it myself. Anyway. I'm done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, I -- sorry, I keep, what I mean is, I'll leave the phone side alone, and the written review goes out on our end regardless, so you don't have to do anything either way. And checking it yourself is right, you're the one who decides how, I'm not, I shouldn't have said ring back, that wasn't, you didn't ask for that. Okay, bye, [PERSON_1], and sorry again about your kid.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Okay. I'll look into it myself, and I'm not doing anything on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, no, that's -- right, so, you do that, you check it your way, and honestly if it's easier for me to try you another time, that's all it ever was, a scheduling thing, but you've said no to the ring-back, so, yeah, I'll leave it there, thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, well, let me just say this once so we're clear, because you keep circling back. I'm not booking anything, I'm not confirming I hold an account with anyone, and I'm not agreeing to a call or a letter or whatever it is now. If this is real, then it'll be real when I ring the number on my own statement, and I'll sort it out from there. And if it isn't, well, you'll never hear from me, will you? So no, don't try me another time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello, this is [PERSON_1], security operations, customs desk at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about a parcel held at our [CITY_1] facility, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], which has an outstanding import charge of [AMOUNT_1] before we can release it. Is this the, uh, the addressee for the delivery, [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Hang on -- [PERSON_2]? No, I don't think so. I'm not expecting anything from, uh, customs, and I'm not sure where that facility even is. Which company did you say you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. Courier. And the parcel's addressed to [PERSON_2], so if that's not you, I've likely got a wrong number. What name am I speaking to?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: My name? Uh, no, I'm not giving you that, you rang me. And hang on, earlier you said a charge, an import charge, before it could be released -- how much was that again? Because if it's the wrong number, why would you need to know who I am?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: You don't need to give me a name, that's fine. And, uh, you're right, I don't need it if it's a wrong number. The charge was [AMOUNT_2] -- sorry, [AMOUNT_1], I misspoke, it's [AMOUNT_1] on reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. Look, if you're not [PERSON_2], this isn't your concern at all. If you are, the reference is on your tracking page, and anything owed is settled there, not over the phone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Okay, but -- two turns ago you said it was [AMOUNT_2], then you said [AMOUNT_1], and you said you misspoke. So which one is it, actually? And, uh, what did you mean by security operations? Why's a customs desk got a security thing calling about a parcel?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [AMOUNT_1]. I -- look, I said [AMOUNT_2] by mistake, that's the figure from the previous file on my desk, it's [AMOUNT_1] on this one, and you can check it yourself on the tracking page against the reference. As for security operations, that's, uh -- it's the section that handles held consignments. Customs holds, flagged shipments, that sort of thing. It sounds worse than it is. It's a routine import charge, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a previous file? So you've got other people's files on your desk while you ring me? And -- hang on -- you said it sounds worse than it is, but I haven't said it sounds like anything. I just asked why security's calling. Look, I'll ask again, because I still don't get it. Which company? You said it was a courier, but you haven't actually told me the name, and where's this tracking page, what's the address for it? I'm not looking anything up on your say-so.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Fine. Let me slow this down, because you've asked three separate things and I'll answer each one properly. The company is [COMPANY_A]. That's the courier, that's who I work for, and that name will be on whatever notice or email came with the shipment. The tracking page is at [URL_1], and I'd rather you didn't take it from me at all. If you're the addressee, go to the address printed on your own dispatch notice, or the one on the shipping confirmation you got from the sender, and type the reference in yourself. If the reference [ACCOUNT_REF] shows a charge there, then it's real. If it doesn't show up, or you've got no notice at all, then it's the wrong number and you can ignore this call entirely. As for the previous file, that was sloppy of me. I handle a queue of held consignments, I had the wrong figure in my head, and I corrected it. It wasn't anyone's details, just an amount. And no, I'm not asking for payment on this call, and I'm not asking for your name, your card, or anything else. Check it in your own time, through your own page, and if the figures don't match, don't pay anything. That's all I'm calling to say.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I'll say it again -- I'm not [PERSON_2], and I'm not expecting a parcel. So why ring at all, if I'm not the person? Like, you've gone to all this trouble to tell me how to check it, but I haven't got a notice, I haven't got anything. So by what you just said, it's the wrong number, yeah? And if it's the wrong number, why's it taken this long?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Taken this long, yes, I know, and that's, uh, on me. Wait, you said you've got no parcel, so you're not collecting anything? Then that's, sorry, I'm hearing it as you're refusing the delivery. If you're refusing it, that's a different process entirely, the sender gets notified and the consignment goes back, but you'd need to be the addressee to do that, so -- no. No, that's not it either. You've said you're not [PERSON_2]. So yes. Wrong number. I've got the wrong contact on the file, I'll flag it, and you've nothing to do and nothing to pay. I'm sorry for the trouble. Good day to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So it's -- no, wait. It's just, you rang me, and now it's, I mean, you flag it and that's that? Fine. If you're taking this number off whatever file you've got, then -- yeah. Good. Don't ring back about it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood. I'll have the number removed from the file, so you won't be called again about it. Sorry for the bother. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah. Right. Well, um, like I said, I'm not paying anything, and I'm not looking anything up either, so, yeah. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is, uh, a post-operative verification specialist calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, regarding the, the orthopaedic procedure your dog had last week, or, well, sorry, I mean the soft-tissue procedure, it's right here in the file as a soft-tissue closure. I'm just contacting you to assess the convalescent trajectory and ascertain whether you'd like a follow-up consultation scheduled.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who -- hang on, I just woke up, I was having a bit of a lie down -- a vet, you said? Which dog, because I, I mean I do have a dog, but last week, I don't think he had -- well, there was the thing with his paw, or was that the month before, I can't -- And you said orthopaedic and then soft-something, which is it? Because that doesn't sound like the same, I mean, those are different, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, I muddled that. It's soft-tissue, the paw wound closure, and I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], your vet's surgery.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the paw, right, yes, that I -- hang on, sorry, the dog's scratching at the door, he does that when he hears me talking, hold on -- no, Biscuit, sit, sit, he can't, he's -- sorry. Where was I. Your vet's surgery, you said, but which one? Because I've only ever been to the one, and you haven't said the name, you said a letter or something, company A? And you don't sound like the lady who normally rings me. So how would I know you're actually from there?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, that's fair, and I'm sorry, I'm, uh, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the surgery, [COMPANY_A], that's the name on your dog's file. And you're right, I'm not the receptionist who normally rings, I'm the, the post-operative verification specialist, it's a sort of separate role, so you wouldn't have heard me before. If you'd rather check, you can ring the surgery on the number you'd normally use and ask them, I mean, that's completely fine. Or, I mean, you could tell me what you remember, like who did the paw, which vet saw Biscuit, because that'd be on our file and you'd know it. Only I'm not asking for anything, I just wanted to see how he's healing, how he's getting on with the, the, the paw.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, well, you did say ring the surgery myself, so that's, that's fair enough, I suppose. Hang on though, I never said his name was Biscuit, did I? I said it to him, just now, at the door, so I suppose you heard that, yes, okay. But you're asking me who the vet was, and that's the thing, you're the one with the file, you should be telling me, shouldn't you? That's sort of backwards. I'm still half asleep so maybe I've got it wrong. Anyway his paw's fine, I think, he's been walking on it, he's been running about the garden like a lunatic, so. Was there something he was meant to come back for? Because nobody said, and I'd have thought they'd have said at the time. Actually, you know what, I might just ring the surgery myself like you said, on the number I've got on the fridge. What's it you're calling about again, exactly? A follow-up, did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, a follow-up, just a routine post-op check, and honestly ringing the number on your fridge is the best thing to do. And you're quite right, it was backwards of me, you shouldn't have to tell me anything. The file says the closure was done by [PERSON_2], on the left forepaw, so that's for you to check against what you remember. If it matches, lovely, and if it doesn't, ring the surgery and tell them. If he's running about the garden, that's a very good sign, and nothing urgent is needed, you'd only be booking a quick recheck if you wanted one.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, uh... right. Left forepaw, was it, hm. I honestly couldn't tell you, I think it was the left, or the, no, I'd have to look at him, he's got the little shaved bit, so. And I don't remember a name, no, they don't always say, do they. Er... so you're not asking me for anything, are you, that's what you said, nothing to pay, nothing to read out or -- no, okay. Well then, I think I'll just do what you said, ring the number on the fridge and ask if he's due a recheck. That seems the sensible thing, doesn't it? Right, thank you, I'll, I'll leave it there, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, nothing at all to pay or read out. Ring the surgery, ask about the recheck, and have a good afternoon. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, thanks, I'll go and find the number on the fridge, he's probably eaten the magnet by now. Bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, uh, hopefully not the magnet, that would be a, a rather different sort of consultation. Anyway, uh, right, just one last thing before you go, and it's only so the file's accurate, but I'll note down that you've decided to ring the surgery yourself, so, um, nobody chases you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yes, fine, you do that. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Lovely, thank you, and I do apologise again for the muddle at the start, I had the procedure type crossed with another patient's notes, which is entirely my fault and not at all how I like to open a call. Really, the sensible course is exactly what you've settled on, ring the number on the fridge, ask the front desk whether Biscuit is due a recheck and which of the vets did the paw, and if anything I've said doesn't match their records, then trust their records over me, please. If he's bounding about the garden and not licking at the shaved patch, that's all we'd hope for at this stage, so there's no rush on it. Anyway, I'll let you get back to your afternoon, and give Biscuit a scratch behind the ears from all of us here at [COMPANY_A]. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, yes, I'll tell him, though he's not really a behind-the-ears dog, he's more of a belly, he'd have you on the floor. And, sorry, you said earlier it was the same vet as normally rings, no, wait, you said the opposite, you said you weren't the lady who normally rings. Anyway, doesn't matter. I'll ring the surgery after I've had a cup of tea, I'm still not properly awake. Goodbye now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is this [PERSON_1]? Hey [PERSON_1], it's, uh -- sorry, this is going to sound a bit odd. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a friend of [PERSON_3]'s, and I'm, well, organising a little surprise for your anniversary, so I was hoping you had a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hi -- yes, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm driving so you're on speaker and the reception's a bit patchy out here. Did you say a surprise for my anniversary? I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch your name, was it [PERSON_2]? And how do you know [PERSON_3] again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, [PERSON_2], that's it, and I know [PERSON_3] from, oh, years back now, we -- hang on, I won't take up your drive, I just need a date, really. Is the [DATE_1] free for the two of you, yes or no, and that's honestly all I'm after, [PERSON_1]. Oh, and uh, if you could just not mention the call to [PERSON_3], that'd be great, since it's meant to be a surprise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, I'm still stuck on something -- you started to say how you know [PERSON_3], you said years back and then you sort of cut off, so, how did you two actually meet? I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just, I'm on the road and I'd feel awful saying yes to a date for something and then it turns out, I don't know, I've got it wrong. And the, uh, not telling [PERSON_3] part, I mean, we don't really keep things from each other, so that's a bit, well, I'm not sure how I feel about that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's totally fair, [PERSON_1], everyone asks that, and honestly I'd ask too. Um, so we met through [PERSON_4], we all did a few years back, and I think you'd know [PERSON_4], right? Actually, here's a thought, why don't you ring [PERSON_4] when you're off the road and check I'm legit, I really don't mind. And the secret thing, it's literally just till the party, you're not hiding anything, you're just, uh, keeping the surprise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, I don't really know a [PERSON_4], sorry. I'll just, I'll check with [PERSON_3] when I get home, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, okay, you don't know [PERSON_4], that's fine, I probably have the wrong end of that, [PERSON_1], we're a big, sort of overlapping group of friends and people get filed under different names, so honestly that's on me. And look, checking with [PERSON_3] when you get home is, I mean, I understand why you'd want to, but it would kind of blow the whole surprise, which is the one thing I'm trying to protect here. So here's what I'd say, and I mean this, no pressure at all: don't give me a yes or a no today. Have a think, and if you'd like to confirm I'm who I say I am, ask [PERSON_5], who's in on it and knows me properly, and you can ring [PERSON_5] whenever you like, tonight, tomorrow, whenever. All I need, whenever you're ready, is whether [DATE_1] works, and if it doesn't, no harm done, I'll just try another weekend. Is that all right? And thanks for hearing me out while you're driving, I know it's a weird call to get, so please, just focus on the road, and we'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, um, thanks, that's, that's kind of you about the driving. But honestly, I think I'm just going to check with [PERSON_3] first, surprise or not. It's just, I don't know you, and now there's a [PERSON_5] I don't know either, and I'd rather not give out a date to somebody I can't place. I'm sorry, I hope that's not rude. If it's a real thing, I'm sure it'll all come out fine. Okay, so, I'm going to go now, I need to concentrate on the road. Bye, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, [PERSON_1], not rude at all, honestly, that's exactly the right call, and I'd rather you check than say yes to some stranger. Go ahead and ask [PERSON_3], like I said, no harm done, I'll just find another way to sort the date, and if the surprise gets spoiled, well, it gets spoiled, that's fine.
