I'm sorry for dropping that on you while you're driving, I mean it. Okay, drive safe, [PERSON_1], and take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, thanks, I really do appreciate you being so understanding, I know it's awkward. Sorry again, and, uh, sorry for the muddle with the names. Right, I'll talk to [PERSON_3] later, so, yeah. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I did your bathroom tiling quote last week. Just a quick follow-up to recap what we agreed and see if you'd like to pick a start date, and I should say I'm holding a couple of slots open till end of day tomorrow, so, uh, it's a good time to have a look at the diary.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hi, yes, sorry, this is [PERSON_1], um, I'm driving, you're on speaker, so the reception's a bit, uh... sorry. Did you say a bathroom quote? I mean, I think someone came round last week, or was that, uh -- sorry, can you say the name of the company again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [COMPANY_A], that's me, [PERSON_2], the tiler, I came round last week and measured up the bathroom. And you said the name was, uh, [COMPANY_B]? No, no, it's [COMPANY_A], sorry, just so we're clear on the record. Anyway, the slots I'm holding are only open till end of day tomorrow, so if you could just let me know a date, that'd be great.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, right, okay, sorry, so, uh... yes, someone did come round, I think, and measure, I'm fairly sure about that. It's just, you said a different name there for a second and then corrected it, and I'm, uh, a bit lost, sorry. Hang on, let me just, um... I'm on the road, I can't really look at the diary right now, and I don't want to just say a date when I'm not sure -- can you tell me what the quote actually was, like the price, so I know we're talking about the same thing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, no, fair enough, and sorry about the name mix-up, that was me tripping over my own words. So the quote, it was [AMOUNT_1] for the bathroom, floor and walls, labour and materials, same as on the written quote I left with you. And like I said, I'm holding those slots till end of day tomorrow, so if you could just let me know a date, that'd be great. Or, I mean, if now's not good, we can sort it later, I just need to know by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, [AMOUNT_1], that, I mean -- sorry, I can't actually picture the figure on the paper right now, I'd have to, well, find it when I'm home. And I'd rather, um, I think I'd like to look at that written quote first before I say yes to anything, if that's all right? Is there, like, a number I could ring you back on, or an email, so I can check it's actually yours, sorry, that sounds rude, I don't mean it to...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that doesn't sound rude at all, that's exactly the sensible thing to do, and honestly I'd rather you check it than say yes to a stranger on a bad line. So the number to ring me back on is [PHONE_1], that's the one on the quote and on the card I left in your hall, and if you'd rather do it by email, the address is on the quote as well, so you can match it up against the paperwork when you're home. The scope on the quote is the floor and walls, labour and materials, like I said, and there's nothing to pay or sign today, I only wanted to see whether you fancied pencilling in a start date. Uh, the only thing is the two slots I'm holding, they do close end of day tomorrow, so if you could give me a shout before then, that'd be ideal, but if you'd rather call when you're parked up or at home with the paper in front of you, that's absolutely fine, whenever suits you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, that's, uh, that's really good of you, thank you, sorry for being so fussy. So I'll ring you when I'm home and I've got the paper, and I'll match the number against the card, which, um, you said you left in the hall? Hang on, I thought I had it in my head that you posted the quote through, sorry, that someone sent it by email, I mean -- I'm honestly not sure now. Anyway, I'll check all that and call you back, so, uh, no date today, if that's okay, thanks very much, bye, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, no date today, that's absolutely fine. And about the quote, I, uh -- I left a paper copy and I, well, I may have emailed one as well, I'd have to look, so whichever one you find, just match it up when you're home. The [PHONE_1] number's on both, so ring me whenever suits, and if it's after tomorrow I'll sort something out with the slots, don't worry about that. Speak soon, then, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, right, thank you, sorry again for all the questions. So I'll look for it when I'm home, and, uh, I'll ring that number if it all matches up. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, no problem. Ring when you're ready, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say, uh, bring it when I'm ready? Bring the quote somewhere? Hang on, I'm, the line's gone all crackly again -- I'm not going to bring anything anywhere, I'll just, I'll ring you, from home, when I've found the paper. Okay? Sorry, right, bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, sorry, I said ring, ring me, not bring, you don't need to bring anything anywhere, just ring from home when you've got the paper. Hang on one sec, my van's beeping at me, uh -- sorry, reversing sensor, ignore that. So yeah, ring me whenever's good for you, no rush on my side, and, uh, I'll leave it with you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, ring, yes, sorry, that's the line, not you. Hang on, there's a lorry right up behind me, I think he wants me to, uh -- sorry, I need to watch the road a sec. Okay, he's gone past. So, yes, I'll ring from home, once I've found the paper and matched the number. Thanks, and sorry for all the fuss, bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you concentrate on the road, that's far more important than any quote. Ring me from home when you've found the paper and matched up the number, and there's no rush, honestly. Take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I will, thanks, I'll just -- sorry, I'll let you go, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, bye now, uh -- sorry, hang on, someone's just shouting something at me from the next door, one sec. No, it's fine, he can wait. Anyway, ring me when you're home and you've got the paper in front of you, and we'll go from there. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, yes, I will, I've got it, home, paper, ring you. Right, thanks again, sorry, I really do need to concentrate now, so, bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, um, sorry to bother you. My name's [PERSON_1], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery? I just wanted to see how your little one's getting on after last week's procedure -- are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, yeah, I'm here. Sorry, um, who is this again? Your name came through, but what surgery? And, uh, what procedure? I haven't got a... I mean, I'm between meetings, so what's the actual point of the call?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, sorry, that's -- I should've said it properly. It's [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], we're the veterinary surgery in [CITY_1], and I'm just -- well, I'm one of the case handlers there. It's about the, um, the procedure your pet had last week, and really I only wanted to check they're recovering well, and ask whether you'd like a follow-up visit booked. Is that all right, are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you still haven't told me which pet, or which procedure. You just keep saying "the procedure." If my animal had something done last week, I'd know what it was, so tell me. What's the pet's name, what was it in for? And honestly, I don't recall getting a call from a case handler before. Normally it's the vet or the front desk. So what's this really about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm sorry, that's fair, I don't blame you at all. Um, I'd rather not go through the pet's details out loud until I'm sure I've got the right person, I'd hate to say something about the wrong animal to the wrong owner -- that's just to protect your privacy, really. And you're right, it's usually the vet or the front desk, I'm on the follow-up side, so it's a bit unusual, sorry. Is that all right? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, that doesn't add up. You rang me, so you've got my number and you've got a file in front of you. Shouldn't you be the one confirming it's me, not me guessing what's in your notes? And a minute ago you said you only wanted to check how they're recovering. Now it's a follow-up visit, and you won't tell me the pet's name? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, sorry. It's both, really, but I take your point.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Both, really." That's not an answer. I asked which pet and which procedure, and you still haven't told me. You won't say the name, you won't say what was done, and now it's both. So I'll ask once more: which pet, and what was it in for? If you can't tell me that, I'm going to ring the surgery myself on the number I've got on file, and you can have them pass on whatever you wanted. Fair?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that's completely fair, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to be vague. Please do ring the surgery yourself, on the number you've already got, not one I give you, that's much the safest way. Just ask for the follow-up team, or the front desk will pass it on, and they'll go through everything properly with you. Sorry again for the bother, and, um, I hope your little one's doing well.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I'll ring them on the number I've got. Not asking for any "follow-up team" though, just the front desk, and I'll see what they say about it. Good...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, the front desk is perfect, that's fine, that's absolutely fine. Just the front desk, and ring them on the number you've already got. Sorry again, I really didn't mean to put you on the spot, and, um, I do hope your little one's doing well. Thanks for your patience, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, I'll ring them, and if they've never heard of you I'll want to know why you had my... Anyway, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please do, that's completely reasonable. Um, just so you know, the front desk might not have my name down, I'm really more on the, uh, the vet side of the follow-ups -- sorry, I did say case handler earlier, didn't I? Either way, they'll sort you out. Bye now, and sorry again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, two turns ago you said the front desk wouldn't need to know about you, or rather you said they'd pass it on. Now you're saying they might not have your name at all. So if the front desk doesn't know you, who's meant to be passing what on? And you've changed your job twice now, case handler, then the vet side. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I -- no, you're right, that's, I'm sorry, I wasn't being clear at all. I meant -- what I should've said is, it's -- look, I'm a case handler, that's the job, and the front desk just might not know my name, that's all I -- sorry. So please ring them yourself on the number you've got, ask them directly, and if they can't tell you anything, well, that's fine, then just leave it. I won't ring you again about it. Are you, um, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still... look, I'm not going to, no. Here's where I've landed. You haven't told me a pet's name, a procedure, or even a straight answer on what your job is, so I'm not carrying on with this. I'll ring the surgery on my own number if I want to, and if you ring again, I'll... well, I'd rather you didn't. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is Officer [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about your benefits record, it's showing incomplete on our end and it needs to be confirmed by phone today. Is this the, uh, the account holder? Sorry, you said "speaking," I thought you said "Stephen" -- no, never mind, I just need to confirm a few details and we'll be done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, sorry, I was just -- I just woke up, I was having a little lie down. Who did you say you were again? Officer who? And what company, I didn't catch that. And benefits, what benefits? I get a few things, there's the, um, the pension thing, and my sister says I should be checking the mail more. Is this about the mail?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Officer [PERSON_1], security operations, [COMPANY_A]. It's not about the mail. Um, the record on file shows incomplete, and incomplete records get flagged, so I need you to confirm a few details with me today, over the phone. Just your full name and date of birth to start, and we'll pull up the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I'm still, my head's a bit fuzzy. Officer who, from what company? I didn't catch the company name, and I still don't know what record. You said benefits, and I said benefits, what benefits? Because I get a couple of things and I don't know which one you mean. And you want my name and my birthday, but you rang me, so shouldn't you already have those? That's what I'd think, anyway. How do I know you're really from where you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I've already stated my name and my department, [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], and I don't have time to repeat it a third time, so please listen this time. As for which benefit, that's exactly what the verification is for, because the system won't show me the specifics until the account holder is confirmed. And no, I don't hold your date of birth on the screen in front of me, that's by design, it's a security protocol, the caller is never given the personal details, the account holder provides them. I understand it's been a long day for you, I do, but an incomplete record doesn't stay incomplete without consequences. Payments get suspended, and a suspended file takes weeks to reinstate. Now, I can keep this brief if you cooperate, your full name and date of birth, that's all I need to proceed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I'm not giving you my birthday on a call I didn't ask for. If it's a real thing, I'll ring whoever sends me my payments, on the number I've already got.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, hold on, that's not how this works. You can't just ring "whoever sends your payments," that's, uh, that's not a single office, and the file is open on my screen right now, today. I'm going to say this slower. The record is incomplete, it must be confirmed today, and if it isn't, the suspension goes through. Which brings me back to what I said earlier, you asked which benefit, and I told you the system won't show me until you're verified. So, your full name and date of birth. That's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, go back a bit. Two goes ago you said something about it being, um, a security protocol, that you're not allowed to have my details on the screen and I have to say them. But if you can't see who I am, how do you know you've even got the right person? And how do you have a file open on your screen that's got my name on it, if you can't see my name? That doesn't add up to me. I'm half asleep but even I can tell that's odd. Anyway, I'm not telling you my birthday. I'm going to ring the pension people on the number I already have, and if there's a problem they can tell me. Thank you for calling, but I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, don't hang up, that's a mistake. I never said the file has your name on it, I said the file is open, and the name, uh, the name is masked on my end, that's different. And I didn't say I couldn't see anything, I said I couldn't see the personal details. Look, ringing the pension office won't help, they can't see this flag, it sits with us, with security operations. So if you put the phone down now, the suspension goes through and that's on you, not me. Last time, full name and date of birth, and I'll close this out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A mask? You want me to put a mask on? I'm sorry, I'm not wearing a mask, I'm in my own house, I was lying down. And what's a, a suspension got to do with it, I'm not suspended from anything, I've never been suspended, not even at school. No, look, you've changed what you're saying three times now and it's not adding up. I'm not telling you my name or my birthday, and I'm going to ring the number I've got. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good morning, this is the scheduling assistant over at [COMPANY_A], the events venue, and I'm calling because I'm putting together a private retirement dinner for [PERSON_1], who I believe works with you, and it's a surprise so I'm hoping you can help me keep it quiet, uh, from [PERSON_1] I mean, and I just need a couple of minutes of your time to run through the date and the guest numbers before the room gets released.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a retirement dinner, how lovely! Um, sorry, it's actually afternoon here though, I've only just had my lunch, but never mind that. And I'm not sure I work with, uh, [PERSON_1] exactly, I think you might have the wrong person? But I'd be glad to help if I can, I just, I'm sorry, who did you say you were calling from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, afternoon, sorry, yes, I've had back to back calls since eight, so, uh, the days run together. I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're an events venue, and, well, I -- sorry, let me start that again, I got your name from the organiser's list of colleagues, so it's very possible I've got the wrong person, and if so that's completely fine, I'd rather you tell me than have me guess. And just so you know, I'm not asking for any payment or personal details or anything like that, it's only the date and numbers, and you're welcome to ring the venue yourself on [PHONE_1] and ask for the booking contact, [PERSON_3], to check I am who I say I am.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very kind of you to say I can ring and check, I appreciate that. I'm just, well, I don't, I mean, I wouldn't know what to tell you about the date, because I'm, uh, I honestly don't think I know [PERSON_1] at all. Sorry, I'm probably not much use to you. Is there someone else on your list who'd be better to ask, or, I mean, shall I just have a think and, um, ring back on that number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you're not -- sorry, go on, I didn't mean to cut across you, but honestly that's really helpful, it just means my list has you down wrong, so please don't worry about it, and if you do want to ring back that's absolutely fine, I'd rather you check with [PERSON_3] first anyway, and I'll make a note to take you off, uh, off the list so nobody bothers you again, and I'm so sorry, I really am, for catching you just after lunch.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very good of you, thank you, and honestly don't be sorry, I'd only just sat down anyway. Um, I'll maybe ring that number, though I think I'd need you to say it again, I didn't catch it, sorry. And, oh, I said I didn't know [PERSON_1] at all, didn't I, but actually I think there might be a [PERSON_1] two doors down, so, uh, I don't know, perhaps that is who you want? But no, I don't work with anybody, I'm just at home, so I'm not sure why you'd have me on a colleagues list. Sorry, I'm not much help, am I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, you've been a big help, honestly, and the number's [PHONE_1], ask for [PERSON_3] on the booking desk. And look, since you're at home and it sounds like I've got the wrong end of this entirely, I'd rather not take up any more of your afternoon, so, uh, would it be easier if I rang you back another time, or -- actually no, maybe best I just sort out my list first and not ring at all, sorry, I'm running on, I'll let you get back to your lunch.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's all right, you're very kind. And I'm not at lunch now, I finished that ages ago, I'm just sitting here with the telly on, so you haven't interrupted anything, honestly. Um, thank you for the number, I've got it, and I'll leave the ringing back, I think, since I can't help you anyway. Good luck with the dinner, it sounds like a nice thing to do. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Thank you, that's really kind of you, and I'm sorry again for the mix-up, uh, hang on, sorry, somebody's just dropped a tray of glasses in the hall behind me, it's chaos here, anyway, where was I -- yes, you take care, enjoy the telly, and if you ever do want to check anything, [PERSON_3] on the booking desk is the one to ask. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, I hope nobody's cut themselves on the glass! Right, well, thank you ever so much, and good luck with the dinner. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, sorry, I should say up front I'm not calling about an account or anything of that sort. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist over at [COMPANY_A], but that's just my day job, this is a personal call. It's about [PERSON_3], your partner -- there's a, let's say, a coordinated social initiative in the works, and I'd rather confirm your availability parameters before I say more.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A coordinated... did you say a social, uh, an inflation? No wait -- hang on. My partner? Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, sorry, that was me being ridiculous, I do that when I've been at work all day. Social, as in a party. I'm [PERSON_2], I'm a friend of [PERSON_3]'s, and the reason I'm calling is, well, I'm helping put together a surprise for your anniversary. Uh, so, yes, a surprise party, that's all it is, and the one thing I'd ask is that you don't mention the call to [PERSON_3], for obvious reasons.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A friend of [PERSON_3]'s. Okay. Funny, I don't think I've ever heard [PERSON_3] mention a [PERSON_2]. And you rang me, not them? How'd you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, and I'd be a bit wary too. I got the number from [PERSON_4], who's helping me with the guest list, and I'm guessing [PERSON_3] mentions [PERSON_4] a lot more than me. Honestly, please ring [PERSON_4] and check before you tell me anything, I won't mind a bit. And you asked me to clarify something earlier, was it the secrecy part? I only mean don't mention the call, since it'd spoil the surprise. I'm not asking for anything except a date, whether you're free, and a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, I didn't ask you to clarify anything. You said that, about the party. And a minute ago you said you weren't after anything, and now it's a date and a yes or no? Which is it? Sorry, I've got the little one pulling at my sleeve here. Why does it need to be a secret from [PERSON_3] that you rang me, if all you want is whether I'm free?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, you're right, I did say that, my mistake. Uh, it's just a date, whether you're free that evening, nothing else. And the secret's only so [PERSON_3] doesn't find out about the party. Look, ring [PERSON_4], and if it's a bad time, I'm happy to leave it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right. Well. Hm. I mean, I'm not going to give you a date, sorry, not to someone I've never heard of, on a call I didn't expect. And you started out saying it wasn't about an account, and then it was verification parameters, and now it's a party. That's, um... that's a few different stories in about two minutes. I'll ring [PERSON_4] myself, and I'll talk to [PERSON_3] while I'm at it. I'm not keeping secrets off a phone call from a stranger. Okay? Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fair, and honestly the best thing you can do. Uh, the one thing I'd say, if you don't mind me clarifying what I said two turns back, the account bit, that was only me saying this isn't a work call, and I made a dog's dinner of explaining it. It's just a party. Ring [PERSON_4], and if you'd rather tell [PERSON_3] everything, well, the surprise is lost, but that's far better than you feeling uneasy. Sorry for the muddle, and I hope the little one settles down. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Like I said, I'll ring [PERSON_4] myself, and I'll tell [PERSON_3]. That's what I'm doing. I'm not giving out a date, and I'm not keeping anything quiet, so... yeah. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Perfectly all right, and thank you for being straight with me. Do ring [PERSON_4], and tell [PERSON_3] whatever you like, that's your call, I'd much rather lose the surprise than have you feel pushed. Uh, sorry again for the jargon at the start, that was daft of me. Take care, and enjoy the rest of your afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, well. I'll be honest, it's not that I think you're a terrible person, it's just, you've rung a number you got secondhand, you opened with verification specialist and parameters, and then you moved the story around a couple of times, and there's a kid hanging off my arm and I haven't got the patience to untangle which version is true. A friend of the family would've just said party in the first breath, wouldn't they? So no hard feelings, but I'm going to ring [PERSON_4] and I'm going to tell [PERSON_3], and if it turns out you're exactly who you say, then you can have your surprise some other way, one that doesn't involve me keeping quiet. Right. Okay. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, this is [PERSON_1] from the fraud team at [COMPANY_A]. Uh, we flagged a charge on your account just now, and I need to go over it with you before the window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi! Sorry, bear with me, I've got you on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the tomato beds here. Um, who did you say you were with again? [COMPANY_A]? And a charge on my account, what sort of charge, I haven't bought anything today, I don't think -- well, unless the seed order went through, I did order a few things last week.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [COMPANY_A], the fraud team. And no, ma'am, this isn't the seed order, this one's a pending charge of [AMOUNT_1] that came through just now and it doesn't match your usual pattern. I do need to verify a few details to pull it up, and uh, I can only hold the charge for the next few minutes, so if we could step away from the tomatoes for a moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, [AMOUNT_1], that's a lot, hang on, let me put the trowel down. Um, sorry, can I just go back a second? You said [COMPANY_A], and I thought that's, hm, is that my bank or my card? I've got a few things and I honestly lose track of which one is which. Which account are you actually calling about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, I understand, a lot of customers hold more than one product with us, it's very common, and it's no trouble. The account in question is the one ending in [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the reference showing on my screen, and the flag is against that one specifically. Now, what I can tell you is the charge is pending, it hasn't posted, which is why timing matters, because once the window closes it moves from pending to completed and then we're into a longer dispute process, paperwork, a few weeks, nobody wants that. What I'll need to do, as part of our standard verification procedure, is confirm a few personal details with you before I can release any further information on the charge. So if you could start by confirming your full name and date of birth, and then we can get this sorted well inside the window. Ma'am, I do want to help you with this, I just can't discuss the account until the verification is complete, that's policy.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, so, um -- well, I was going to just give you my, no, hang on. It's just, you rang me, didn't you? And now you're asking me for my name and my birthday, and that feels a bit, I don't know, back to front. I mean, if you're really from the bank, surely you'd already have all that on your screen? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, uh -- is there a number I could ring you back on? Or I could just ring the number on the back of my card, that might be easier.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I, uh -- no, see, the thing is, what's on my screen is the flag, not the, the -- look, ma'am, this is a standard verification procedure, I do have to confirm the account holder before I can disclose anything, that's for your protection. As for a number, I, uh, I'm not able to give out a direct line, the lines are routed through the fraud queue, and if you hang up now, the pending charge will most likely complete while you're waiting on hold, and then it's out of my hands. So if we could just get your name confirmed, we're well inside the window, but I can't keep it open much longer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the lines are what, rerouted? Oh, so you're not even at the bank, you're, like, somewhere else? Hang on, hold on, I've got dirt in my ear, hello? No, wait, I mean, that sounds a bit odd, doesn't it, if the phone number is going somewhere different. Can you just say that bit again, because now I'm not sure who I'm even talking to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, let me go back to the start, because I think that's where we got tangled. I'm [PERSON_1], I'm with the fraud team at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling today regarding a pending charge of [AMOUNT_1] against the account ending in [ACCOUNT_REF]. When I said routed, all I meant is that fraud calls don't come in through the general branch line, they go through a dedicated queue, which is standard, and I wasn't saying I'm somewhere else, ma'am, I'm with the bank. Now, what I can offer, and I do want to be clear on this, is that the fastest way to protect your account is to complete the verification now, while the charge is still pending, because once the window closes it posts, and then we're into the dispute process I mentioned, which is paperwork and weeks of waiting, and I'd really rather spare you that. So, if we could just start with your full name and date of birth, then we can pull up the charge together and I can walk you through what's happening on it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a dedicated cue, like a queue at the shops, okay. No, sorry, I'm with you now, so you're saying the charge is already, what was it, posted? And then there's a pile of paperwork, oh, that sounds like a nightmare, I've still got the paperwork from when the shed got broken into and that was ages ago. Hang on though, I'm still a bit stuck on the name and birthday bit. I think I'd honestly feel better ringing the number on the back of my card and asking for the fraud people myself. Would that be all right? Or is that going to make it worse?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, no, not posted, ma'am, it's still pending, that's the whole point, it's still pending, but the window is closing, and I can't hold it open much longer. Uh, if you ring off and go through the main line, I can't promise the charge won't complete in the meantime, I just can't, and then we're into the paperwork I mentioned. But, I mean, I do hear you, you want to be careful, and that's, that's fine. Let me do this, I'll try you again a little later on, once I've checked where the charge is sitting, and we can finish the verification then. Okay? So, uh, I'll ring back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I -- no, actually, hang on. If it's, if you can just ring back later, then it can't be all that urgent, can it? Or, I mean, I thought it was going to, um -- anyway. I think I'll just ring the number on my card myself, and if there's something wrong they'll tell me. Thanks for letting me know, though, that's kind of you. Bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, if I could just -- no, no, I'll still ring you back, uh, later on, once I've checked where the charge is sitting, and we'll finish up then. Okay? Right. I'll, I'll ring back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a blackbird going absolutely mad at my seedlings, shoo, go on, get off! Sorry, what was that? You'll ring back? Oh, no, honestly, don't worry, don't ring me, I'll ring my bank myself, on the number on the card. Right, that's decided. Thanks anyway, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, if I could just -- uh, I'm [PERSON_1], with the fraud team at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about the pending charge of [AMOUNT_1], that's all I want to say, but I do have to be clear that if you ring off and go through the main line, I can't say what the charge will be doing by the time you're through, and I wouldn't want you to be out of pocket, because once the window closes it's the paperwork and the weeks, which, uh, nobody wants. That said, it's your account, and I can't make you do anything, that's, that's not how this works. So I'll leave it with you, and I'll ring back later on, once I've checked where it's sitting, and we'll finish it off then. Okay? Right. Speak soon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you're still there! Sorry, I thought we'd finished. Honestly, I'm fine, I'll sort it myself with the bank, so you needn't ring back. I've got a whole tray of seedlings that need watering before the sun gets round, so I'm going to go. Thanks for your time, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, well, um... okay, so, I'll, I'll still ring back later on, once I've checked where it's sitting, and we'll finish it off then. Okay? Right. Speak soon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you'll ring back about the, what was it, the sitting? Oh, the sitting hen, no, I haven't got any hens, just the one very fat cat, and he's no use at all, he's asleep in the greenhouse. No, listen, honestly, there's no need to ring back, I'm going to ring the bank myself on the card number. Right, I'm hanging up now, bye bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Is this -- is this [PERSON_1]? Okay, good. So, I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the, uh, computer security company, and I'm sorry to just spring this on you, but your home computer has been sending out infected traffic. I mean, we think it has, and it's sort of urgent, because if it keeps going, it could hurt other people, you know?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who's this again? You said you're calling on behalf of someone at the security company, so, which someone? And I'm, uh, I'm at my work laptop right now, not a home computer, so I'm not sure what you'd even be seeing on your end. How would you know it's mine?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, right, no, I -- the person is [PERSON_2], on the, the technical team at [COMPANY_A]. I'm just passing it along, I'm not the technical one. And, okay, it wouldn't be the work laptop, it's the one at your house, the, uh, the traffic comes back to your home connection. That's how they, they traced it to you. I mean, I'm only trying to help here. It's not an easy call to make, and I'd feel terrible if this kept going and people got hurt because nobody picked up the phone. Could you just, uh, get to your computer at home? [PERSON_2] said they could look at it directly if you let them, and it would only take a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said they could look at it directly if I let them? Wait, "look at it directly," like, in person? Someone's coming to the house? Because that's not, no, I don't think so. And I'm still stuck on the tracing thing. You said it comes back to my home connection, but my home connection is just an address and a router. That's not "me." How did they get from a bunch of traffic to [PERSON_1] picking up this phone? And who gave you my number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not in person, I'm sorry, I said that badly. It's more like, uh, they connect to the computer from their end, remotely. It'd just be a few minutes. And the number, I, uh -- it came from [PERSON_2], I think, or maybe it was off the account, I'm not sure which. I'm just the one who was asked to call, so I don't have all of that in front of me. And, okay, I did say it was the home computer earlier, but it might be the work one too, I mean, they're both on your name, so it's, it's kind of the same thing. Look, I'm really not trying to upset you, I just don't want to be the person who knew and didn't say anything. Could you, uh, just get to the computer now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, wait, back up. Two turns ago you said, and I wrote this down, that it's the home computer, the traffic comes back to my home connection. Now it's "might be the work one too." Which is it? Because those aren't the same thing at all. And you also said "off the account," what account? You haven't told me one thing I'd have to have with that company for them to know my name. So I'm still waiting on a straight answer: who's [PERSON_2], what's the actual name of the company, and why am I the one getting a call instead of my internet provider?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, I -- you're right, I did say home, and I shouldn't have said the work one, that was me mixing things up. It's the home computer. That's, that's what I was told. And the account, I, uh, I don't actually have that in front of me, I'm sorry. I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, I get nervous on these calls, and this is, honestly, it hurts a little that you think I'm trying to trick you. The company is [COMPANY_A], I did say that, and [PERSON_2] is on the technical side, that's all I was given. I don't know about your internet provider, maybe they were called too, I can't say. But it's, it's really time-sensitive, and if you could just let [PERSON_2] connect to your computer so they can check, it would clear this up quick. Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not letting anyone connect to my computer, not on a phone call I didn't ask for. And you still haven't answered what I asked, you've just told me you don't have it in front of you. Twice now. Who is [PERSON_2], what's the account, and why isn't my provider the one calling? I'm not saying you're a bad person, but "it's urgent, let a stranger in" is not a good enough reason. If [COMPANY_A] really thinks there's a problem, they can send it in writing to an address I can check. I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. Okay. I, uh, I really was just trying to help... but okay.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, my screen just did something. Never mind. Look, I said I'm going. If it's real, put it in writing and I'll deal with it that way. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm with the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is -- sorry, who? [PERSON_2], from the compliance team at, uh -- my energy supplier, you said? I'm at work right now, so, what's this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_2], compliance team at [COMPANY_A], and I do apologise for catching you at work, I'll try to be brief. The reason for the call is, uh, a fairly small thing really, though it sounds more serious than it is: we've found two meter readings on your account that don't match each other, and that's an inconsistency in our own records, not anything you've done. I want to be clear about that at the start, because a call from compliance can sound alarming, and it isn't meant to be. What I'd like, when you have a moment, is the current figure on your meter, so we can correct the bill, but please, take your time deciding whether that's something you want to do on this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, two readings that don't match, and you want the current figure off the meter. Right. Uh, I mean, I'm not at home, so I can't read it anyway, I'm at my desk. But, how do I know you're actually from [COMPANY_A]? Because I've heard about people ringing up and, you know, saying they're from the supplier. No offence.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No offence taken at all, and I'd honestly rather you asked, so thank you. Now, you said, uh, something two turns back that I want to pick up properly: you asked who I was, and I gave you my name and the team, but I never explained why compliance is the one ringing. It's because a mismatch between two readings gets flagged to us before it goes back to billing. That's all it is. As for how you'd know it's us, well, you don't have to take my word, and I'd rather you didn't. Log in to your account on the [URL_1] site, or use the number printed on your bill, and ask them about the reading query on [ACCOUNT_REF]. If they confirm it, ring me back, and if you'd rather not give me the figure at all, that's fine, the bill simply stays as it is for now. There's, uh, a point where the records do have to be settled, of course, but I'm not going to rush you through it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, uh -- hang on, let me just, um... so you're saying log in myself, or ring the number on the bill, and ask them about a reading query on [ACCOUNT_REF]. And if they say yes, ring you back. Hm. That's, I mean, that's actually what I'd do anyway. It's just -- why's it come through a phone call at all, if it's only a small thing? Couldn't you have just sent a letter or an email?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's a fair question, and, well, the honest answer is, uh -- we did write, actually, or rather, no, let me put that properly. A letter does go out as the standard step, but a reading that's out of line with our records is the sort of thing we try to settle by phone as well, because a figure read out today is quicker to correct than one posted back in a week, and I'd, I'd rather not leave your bill sitting wrong while we wait on the post. But the letter route is still open to you, if you prefer it. Whichever you choose, nothing on the account changes until you've had the chance to check this with [COMPANY_A] yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, okay. Sorry, you said "we did write, or rather, no" -- so did a letter go out or not? Because I don't remember getting anything. Anyway, look, I think I'll just ring the number on my bill and ask them about it. If they say there's a query, fine, I'll deal with it that way. So, yeah, I'll do that, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's a fair catch, and I did tangle myself there, so let me say it plainly before you go. I can't tell you for certain that a letter reached you. The standard process is that one goes out, but I'm looking at the account notes as we speak, and I can't see a confirmed send date, so I'd be guessing if I said it had gone. That gap is in our own records, and it's one more reason I'd rather you checked with [COMPANY_A] directly than relied on anything I say. So ringing the number on your bill is exactly the right thing to do. When you get through, quote [ACCOUNT_REF] and ask whether there's a reading query open, and if it turns out there isn't, then I'd want to know that too, because it would mean something has gone wrong on our side. And, uh, I'd sooner not have you leave a desk job half-distracted anyway, so if it's easier, I can ring you back at a better time, say this evening or tomorrow, once you've had a chance to check. You wouldn't need to do anything on this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a, a better *time*? No, no, you don't need to ring me this evening, I'm, uh, I'm not going to be in. Wait, you said if there isn't a query open, you'd want to know. Why would you need to know? Surely I just ring the number on my bill, they say yes or no, and that's the end of it. Anyway, I'm going to go and do that. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's right, you've got it, uh, hang on, sorry, someone's just come to my desk, one moment -- yes, that's fine, I'll be there shortly -- sorry about that. What I was getting at is only that if the number on your bill says there's no query, that's a fault in our records, so I'd want it reported, but that's my job to chase, not yours. Your part really is just what you said: ring them, ask, and that's the end of it. And of course, no evening call then, I won't ring unless you ask me to. Goodbye, [PERSON_1], and thank you for checking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, uh, my colleague just dropped something over here, I missed the last bit. But I think I got the gist, ring the number on my bill, quote the reference, ask if there's a query open. And you won't ring me back unless I ask. Right. Okay, I'll do that. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this... [PERSON_1]? Good. Uh, my name's [PERSON_2], and I should say straight away, I'm a friend of [PERSON_3]'s. We've met a couple of times, through [COMPANY_A], actually. I'm calling about something rather, well, sensitive, and I'd just like to know if now is an alright moment to talk, or whether I've caught you at a bad time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm driving, so you're on speaker and the reception's a bit patchy. Um, [PERSON_3]... hang on, I don't think I've met you through [COMPANY_A], I mean, I don't actually think I know anyone from [COMPANY_A], sorry, that might just be me not remembering. But go on, it's, uh, it's fine, I'm just on the motorway, what's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, sorry, hang on one second, there's a delivery person at my door and I -- right, never mind, they've gone. Sorry about that. Um, and please, don't apologise, it may well be that you and I have never been introduced. [PERSON_3] and I have mostly crossed paths at work things, so that's probably my fault for putting it that way. Look, since you're driving, I'll keep this very short and I really don't want you taking this call while you're on the motorway, so, the gist is, I'm helping put together a little surprise for your anniversary, and I'd, uh, I'd just need a date from you, and for you not to say anything to [PERSON_3] about my ringing. That's honestly all of it. But if now isn't good, I'd much rather you called it a day and we picked this up later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, a surprise for our anniversary? Hang on, I'm a bit lost, sorry. Two turns ago you said you were a friend of [PERSON_3]'s, and then you said we mostly crossed paths at work things, and I don't, I mean, I'm not sure whose work, or who you actually are. Sorry, it's the reception too, I might've missed a bit. And, uh, which anniversary, exactly? I'm just, I'd like to understand who this is before I say anything about dates.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're right to ask, and I'd rather you did. I was, uh, I was clumsy with how I put it, so let me try again, properly. I'm [PERSON_2]. I know [PERSON_3] through the [COMPANY_A] side of things, work, yes, but we also get on as friends, and I think that's where I tangled myself up. And as for which anniversary, I'd honestly rather not guess at that, because that's exactly the sort of thing I'd be asking you, not telling you. But look, here's what I'd suggest, if it helps: [PERSON_3] and I both know [PERSON_4], and if you rang [PERSON_4] and asked whether a [PERSON_2] is organising something, I think that would settle it. And if you'd sooner end the call here, truly, that's fine. I'd only ask that, well, you don't mention it to [PERSON_3] in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Sorry, I'm just, I'm not really comfortable with this. You don't know which anniversary, you want me to keep it from [PERSON_3], and I can't ring anyone while I'm driving anyway. I think I'll just ask [PERSON_3] myself. Sorry, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, of course, that's completely fair, and I'm sorry, I've handled this badly. Um, just one thing before you go, and I may have said it wrong earlier, I'm not actually with [COMPANY_A] at all, I just know [PERSON_3] socially, so, uh, ignore the work part. And I do know the anniversary, it's the one coming up, I only meant I wouldn't presume to say the date out loud. But you're driving, so please, don't think about any of this now. Would it be easier if I rang you back some other time, when you're parked up and can check with [PERSON_4] first?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, please don't ring back, sorry, I -- look, that's the third version of who you are, and I'm just, I'm going to talk to [PERSON_3] myself, that's all. Sorry. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, understood, and I won't ring back, you have my word on that. Honestly, you're perfectly right to go and ask [PERSON_3] yourself, I'd have said the same thing in your position, and I'm sorry I made a hash of explaining myself while you were trying to concentrate on the road. The only thing I'd ask, and it's a request, not a condition, is that if [PERSON_3] does know who I am, you needn't make anything of it, and if they don't, well, then you've lost nothing and I'll have to sort out my own mess. Please drive safely, and, uh, sorry again for the trouble. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, thanks, sorry. Um, just so you know, I never actually said I'd keep it quiet, I'm definitely going to mention it to [PERSON_3], I just, I didn't want to leave you thinking I'd agreed to that. Sorry, I know that sounds a bit blunt. Anyway, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's not blunt at all, and honestly I'm glad you said it, because it's the sensible thing to do. Please do mention it to [PERSON_3], I won't hold it against you, and it was never a promise I had any right to ask for in the first place. If anything, I'd rather you told them, because then it's [PERSON_3] who can say whether I'm who I said I was, and that's a far better check than anything I could offer you down a patchy line. And, uh, I know I've muddled the story a couple of times, and I'm sorry for that. I got flustered when you pushed back, which, in fairness, you were right to do, and I'd sooner leave it there than keep talking and make it worse. So go and ask them, no hurry, and keep your eyes on the road. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, thanks, that's, hang on, sorry, there's a lorry coming up on my left and it's, right, he's gone past. Sorry. Yes, no, I'll ask [PERSON_3], that's the plan, so thank you for being, well, for understanding. Right, bye now, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], I'm the regional supervisor, I came out to the house last week about the bathroom tiling. I'm just ringing to run back over the quote with you, uh, the [AMOUNT_1] we talked about for the floor and the two walls, and then see if you want to lock in a start date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, this is, uh, yes, that's me. Sorry, who did you say you were again? Somebody came about the bathroom, I think, I mean, I've had a few people round this year, the boiler man, and the fella about the gutters... lovely chap, the gutter one, talked for an hour about his dog. But the tiling, hmm. Was that last week? What did you say your name was?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], [PERSON_2]. I'm the supervisor for the region, I came out last Tuesday, uh, last week anyway, and we went through the bathroom together. Floor and the two walls, the tiling job, I measured up and everything, I'm fairly sure you made me a cup of tea. So I'm just ringing to go back over the quote, and I'd have thought that'd ring a bell, but never mind.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a cup of tea, well, I make plenty of those, I couldn't tell you which -- no, hang on, you said last Tuesday, and I had my sister's -- oh, but it was somebody about the bathroom, wasn't it, I do remember the tape measure, or maybe that was the gutter man, he had one too. Sorry, love, I don't mean to be difficult, it's just I don't have a note of any quote, and I'm sure I'd have written it down, I write everything on the calendar. Which company did you say again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [COMPANY_A], I'm an independent tradesperson, I work under that name. Look, there's no need to be sorry, I just thought it would be on your calendar, that's all. We're not talking about anything complicated, uh, floor and two walls, [AMOUNT_1], and I'd had it down that you were happy with it. But if you've no note of it, that's fine, I'm not asking you to commit to anything on the phone today. Would it help if I dropped the quote through the door, so you've got it in writing and can look it over with your sister or whoever?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you, dropping it through the door, a bit of paper is always easier, I can't be doing with numbers over the phone. Hang on, sorry, there's a pigeon on the windowsill, big fat thing, it does that every afternoon, thinks I'm going to feed it, and I'm not allowed because of the, well, never mind. Where was I? The quote, yes. Only, you said regional supervisor at first and now you're saying independent tradesperson, so which is it, love? I'm not being funny, it just sounds like two different things to me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A different person? No, no, it's the same fella, it's me, [PERSON_2], I've only ever been the one person on this job. Look, I don't see why that's an issue, I wasn't trying to catch you out, I'm just ringing to be helpful. I mean, if you'd rather I didn't bother, just say so, but I did take the time to come out and measure up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, no, I didn't say a different person, I said two different jobs, the supervisor and the, the... oh hang on, that's the kettle, it's gone off, it does that click thing and I always think it's the doorbell. Right. Sorry. Where was I? Yes, I don't want you to think I'm being rude, you've been very nice about it. But I'll be honest with you, I don't actually remember you coming, and if somebody had measured up my bathroom I think I'd know. So I'd rather not go on about it over the phone, if it's all the same. If you want to post something through, I'll have a look at it with my sister, and if it's right, it's right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Posh? No, no, I'm not posh, love, I'm just a bloke with a tape measure, ha. Anyway, that's fine, I'm not offended, honestly. I'll pop the quote through the door in the next day or two, with my number on it, and you can look it over with your sister. And if it turns out I've got the wrong house, well, no harm done, you just give me a ring and say so. I'd just check the address on it when it lands, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, not posh, I said post, love, put it through the post, or the door, either's fine. Mm. Well, uh... right then. Hmm, it's gone a bit quiet, hasn't it? Sorry, I always go and fill the gaps, my sister says I'd talk to a lamppost. Anyway, yes, you do that, and I'll have a look at it with her, and if the address is wrong, I'll ring the number. Thank you for being so nice about it, I do get a bit muddled. Goodbye now, love, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, post, right, sorry, I heard that wrong, my fault. And you're not muddled, honestly, it's a perfectly fair thing to say when you've no note of it. I'll get it in the post, then, with my number on it, and if it's the wrong house, just ring and tell me and we'll say no more about it. Thanks for being so patient with me, [PERSON_1]. You take care now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye bye, love, you take care too, and, oh, mind the pigeons if you're ever round this way, they're terrors. Cheerio now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, I will, though I'd have sworn there were no pigeons the day I came round, just that cat on the wall by the gate. Anyway, I'll leave you to your kettle, [PERSON_1]. Cheerio, cheerio.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A cat on the wall? Hang on, I haven't got a cat on my wall, love, there's never been one, there's a, well, it's a fence, not a wall, and it's got that blue gate. Hmm. No, I really don't think you've been here at all, you know. Not to be rude about it, but I think you've got the wrong house, and I'd rather you didn't post anything through. Right, I'm going to go and have my tea now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, a fence, not a wall, and a blue gate, no, that's not the one I'm thinking of, that was a black gate, I remember now. Well, there you go, then, I've clearly got my addresses crossed, and that's my mistake, not yours, so I won't post anything. I'm sorry for taking up your afternoon, [PERSON_1]. Enjoy your tea, and I'll sort it out at my end. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sort it out at your end, yes, oh, you said a black *cat* before, didn't you, on the wall? Because the little black one two doors down is Mr Pettigrew's, he's called Biscuit, he's ever so greedy, sits on everybody's wall. But anyway, that's not you, is it, you've got the wrong street. Right, well, no hard feelings, love. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, a black cat on a wall, no, I said a cat, never mind which, I'm clearly mixing up two streets in my head. Biscuit, that's a good name for a greedy one though. No hard feelings at all, [PERSON_1], and I'm sorry about the muddle. Cheerio now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, don't be sorry, love, it's an easy thing to do, I once went to the wrong house myself, years ago, with a casserole for my sister's neighbour, and it turned out she'd moved to Harrogate, so I stood on the step looking daft with a hot dish. Anyway, that's me, I get things crossed too. But I'll tell you what's nagging at me now, and I don't mean it unkindly. You knew my name, didn't you, [PERSON_1], right at the start, and you said the quote, and the amount, and the floor and the two walls, which is an awful lot of detail to have for the wrong house. So if you've got the wrong street, how come you had all of that? Hm. It's probably nothing, I'm probably just being a silly old thing, but I'd feel better if I had a proper company name and a number written down before you go, and then my sister can have a look at it, because I'd rather not leave it like this, with it all sort of hanging.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's, no, that's a fair thing to ask, and you're not being silly. The detail, well, I had the job sheet in front of me when I rang, so the name and the, uh, the floor and two walls were all on it, and that's what's wrong, I think, I've been given the wrong sheet, or I've got the wrong address against the right sheet. It happens when you're juggling a few quotes. Right, so I'll give you the number, it's [PHONE_1], that's [PHONE_1], and the name's [COMPANY_A], and I'm [PERSON_2]. Have your sister look it over, and if there's anything that doesn't sit right, you ring and ask for me, and I'll go through it with her. Is that better? Thanks for being so decent about it, [PERSON_1]. You enjoy that tea now, bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, [PHONE_1], and [COMPANY_A], and [PERSON_2], I've got it written on the back of my electric bill, it's the only paper I could find. Hmm. Well, I'll show it to my sister on Sunday, she's good with this sort of thing, and if it doesn't sit right, I'll leave it, I won't be ringing. I do think you've got the wrong sheet, love, but thank you for being so patient with an old woman and her pigeon. Right, my tea's stewing now. Goodbye, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi... it's me. Um, sorry, I know it's, I know it's out of the blue. Are you there? Can you hear me okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hello? Yeah, yeah, I can hear you, sorry, you're a bit, uh, crackly, I'm in the car and the signal's, hang on, sorry, there's a lorry right on my tail, give me a second -- okay. Um, who is this? Sorry, I don't think I caught your name, or I did and it just cut out, I'm really sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you didn't miss it, I didn't say. It's me. Come on, you know my voice... can you not tell? I really don't want to say it over the phone, I'm sorry. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, still here, sorry, it's just the line, it keeps sort of dipping in and out. Um, I mean, I'm really sorry, I do feel like I should know, and it's awful that I don't, but honestly the speaker in this car is rubbish and everything sounds sort of tinny and flattened, so, I mean, it could be anyone, it could be somebody I talk to every week and I wouldn't, I wouldn't be able to tell right now. And you sound, I don't know, a bit upset maybe? Or is that just the signal? Sorry, I'm rambling, I'm a bit on edge anyway, I'm trying to watch the road and there's roadworks coming up. But, okay, I don't really get why you can't just say your name. Is something wrong? Like, is someone hurt, or, or is it something I should be worried about? Because if it is I think I'd rather just pull over, but I can't really do that for a bit, so, uh, can you at least tell me who you are, or give me a hint or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nobody's hurt, I promise, please don't worry about that. It's just... it's a bit of a situation, and I'd really rather not say it all on the phone, in case, I mean, I just don't want it going any further than you. Can you guess? Just try, please, I'd feel so much better if you could just say it. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, okay, that's, that's a relief, sorry, nobody's hurt, good. Um, but I don't want to guess, if that's alright? Because I honestly don't know who it is, and if I just throw a name out, I could get it wrong, and then that's awkward for both of us, or, I don't know, I'd be sort of handing you the answer, and that feels a bit, uh, backwards? Sorry, that sounds rude, I don't mean it to be, I'm just, I'm quite anxious today anyway and this is sort of making it worse, because I keep thinking, why wouldn't you just tell me who you are? If it's someone I know, then I'm going to be nothing but sympathetic, you know? I'd want to help. But I can't really help when I don't even know who I'm helping, and I'm doing about forty in a, a thirty, I should slow down, sorry. And the "don't let it go any further than you" thing, that makes me a bit uneasy, honestly, because what does that mean, what is it, that I'm meant to keep a secret from, from who? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult. Could you maybe just say your name, or say how we know each other, or something small, and then we can go from there? Because I'm happy to listen, I

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, please, you're not being rude, I'm sorry, I'm making this harder than it needs to be. It's just, I can't say it, not yet, and it's honestly for your own protection that I'm keeping it light, I just need to know I can trust you with it first. Are you still there? I just need a bit of help with something that's come up, that's all, it's nothing awful, and then I'll explain everything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, I'm, sorry. Um, so, help with something, I mean, I'd, no, wait. What I mean is, I'd like to help, honestly, I would, if it's someone I know, but I can't say yes to something when I don't know what it is or who's asking, and, and "for my own protection" is, I don't know, that's just making me more nervous, sorry. Can you just, um, tell me what the help is? Or, no, actually, maybe, if you really can't say your name, maybe I should just ring you back, on, on whatever number I have for you? Would that, I mean, would that be okay?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um... no, don't, please don't ring back, I'm, uh, I'm not on that number, it's sort of a, a borrowed phone, and it won't, it won't work for that. Sorry, I know how that sounds. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here, sorry, I'm, um, I'm trying to concentrate, it's, hang on. Okay. So, a borrowed phone, and you can't say who you are, and I can't ring back, and it's, it's something I'd have to keep quiet, and you need help, and, I mean, I'm sorry, but when I put it all together out loud it sounds, I don't know, a bit off? And I really don't like saying that, because if you are someone I know, then I feel awful, but I think, I think I'm going to have to stop here. If it's genuinely someone I know, they can message me, or, or call from their own number once they've got it sorted, and I'll, I'll absolutely listen then. I'm sorry, I really am, I just can't help with something when I don't know who's asking or what it is. Take care, okay? Bye, bye.

utterances.text: No, wait, please, don't hang up, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to... hello? Are you still there? It's just, I can't do it from my own number, I really can't, and I don't have anyone else I can, I just... please, I only needed a minute, I'm not trying to...

utterances.speaker: receiver

Because that's the bit that's really stuck with me, and you didn't, I mean, you sort of skipped past it, and if I'm meant to be in some kind of, I don't know, danger, or it's something that could land on me, then I'd honestly like to understand that before I do anything, sorry. Is that, is that a fair thing to ask?

utterances.speaker: caller

It's just that the less you know right now, the safer it is for you, that's all I mean, honestly. I just need you to trust me for a minute and not ask me to say it all out loud, and then I can explain. Are you still there? Please, I just need you to stay on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I'm sorry, but that's, that's the opposite of what I'd want to hear, because, um, "the less you know the safer it is" is, I mean, that's not a thing a friend says to someone they're asking a favour of, is it? And, sorry, earlier I think you said nobody was hurt and it was nothing awful, and now it's about me being safe, and, I don't know, I can't make those two go together. So I'm going to stop here, I really am, and I'm sorry if I've got it wrong. If you really are someone I know, then, then message me from your own number when you can, or tell someone else to, and I'll, I'll talk properly then. I'm going to hang up now, okay? Take care. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] over at [COMPANY_A], we ran that little prize draw at the, uh -- sorry, don't want to cut you off, but I think you won something, and it's nothing scary, I promise!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, that's me, uh -- sorry, hang on a second, the kettle's just clicked off, I'll, um... right, sorry about that. A prize draw, you said? I'm so sorry, I don't remember entering anything, but I do fill in those little slips sometimes. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're fine, [PERSON_1], take your time, it's -- oh, sorry, I'm [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the shop on the high street, and I'm sure you did, it was the draw we ran at the [CITY_1] spring market, uh, back on the weekend of the [CODE_1]th, you'd have filled in a little slip at our stall, it only takes a second. Anyway, good news is you've won a hamper, nothing huge, and you don't have to pay anything or do anything complicated, you just pop into the shop and pick it up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a hamper, well that's, I mean -- that's lovely, isn't it. I think I did go to the, um, the spring market, I'm sure I -- no, wait, was that this year or last? Sorry, I do lose track. And I'd just pop in and pick it up, you said, so there's nothing I'd need to, uh -- nothing I'd have to send you or anything first? I'm sorry, I'm not very good at these things, I just want to be sure I've understood.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, it was this year, [PERSON_1], just a few weeks back. And no, nothing to send, nothing at all, everyone asks that, and it's completely fair. You just walk in, say your name, and we hand it over, that's it. The only thing I'd need to do on my end is, uh, pop your address down, so I can send the little confirmation slip, takes two seconds, so if you could just -- oh, hang on, did you say you wanted it sent? No, no, no postage, it's all collected in person, don't worry about that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I'm getting a bit muddled. Could we go back a moment, you said earlier that it was the weekend of the, um, [CODE_1]th at the spring market? I just didn't quite catch which weekend that was, and I want to be sure I'm thinking of the right one. And then the address, if I'm just collecting it in person, what's that for, exactly? Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I'm just a bit lost.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're not being difficult at all, [PERSON_1], honestly. So, the spring market, it was the weekend of the [CODE_1]th, yeah, the [CODE_1]th, that's the one, we had the stall by the, uh, by the entrance. And the address, I mean, you know what, you don't actually need to give me that if you're just popping in, it was just for the little confirmation slip, but it's really nothing, forget I said it. Just come by the shop, say your name at the counter, and we'll have the hamper ready, easy as that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, thank you, that's very kind. Um, sorry, can I just go back to something? A minute ago you said the thing about "everyone asks that" when I asked if I had to send anything, and then you said you'd need my address, and I wasn't sure if I'd said something wrong. And, I mean, I'd like to pop in, but what's the shop called again, and which bit of the high street? I'm so sorry, I didn't catch it properly at the start.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you didn't say anything wrong, [PERSON_1], that was me being clumsy, sorry. It's [COMPANY_A], on the high street, uh -- hang on a sec, sorry, somebody's just come in at the counter, bear with me. Right, sorry, back. So it's [COMPANY_A], and the exact spot on the high street, I mean, you'll see it, it's -- hmm, actually, I'm not sure I've got the number to hand, I'm only covering the phones today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you're only covering the phones, I see. Sorry, did you say the shop's got a, um, a phone number I could ring? Because you said "hamper" and I thought you said "camper" for a second, and I thought, goodness, that's a very big prize! No, no, a hamper, of course. But if you're not sure where the shop is, maybe I could just ring the shop itself and ask for the right person, if that's all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fair, [PERSON_1]. Honestly I can't give you the shop's direct number off the top of my head, so let me find out and call you right back, all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, um, well, I mean, that's very kind of you to offer, but, sorry, it's just that I'd rather look the shop up myself, if that's all right. Sorry, I hope that doesn't sound rude, I'm just not very good with these things, you see. So, um, thank you for letting me know, and I'll see what they say. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's not rude at all, [PERSON_1], you do that, honestly. Just, uh, if you do ring them, they might say the draw was in the autumn, I think, sorry, I might've said the spring market earlier, I get my events mixed up. Anyway, they'll sort you out. Bye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the autumn? Right, sorry, I'm a bit lost now, but never mind, I'll just ask them when I ring. Thank you ever so much for calling, and for being so patient with me. Bye now, take care, bye bye.

utterances.text: Good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2] calling from the collections office at [COMPANY_A], hospital billing. I'm contacting you about an outstanding balance of [AMOUNT_1] on an account where you're listed as the responsible party.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um... yes, that's me, I think. Hospital billing, you said? I don't, uh... I'm not sure I know what that's about.

utterances.text: Right, so it's a relative's account, it shows unpaid since the last statement cycle, and you're named as responsible on the file, so -- I do need to confirm a few details with you before I can go further. Can you just confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a relative's, hm. A, uh, a retired account, did you say? Well, that'd be my husband's old pension, I suppose, he's been gone a few years now -- lovely man, he used to do all the post and the paperwork, I never really, uh... Sorry, dear, what was it you wanted me to confirm?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not a pension, ma'am, it's a medical account, an outstanding hospital balance of [AMOUNT_1]. And I'm sorry to hear about your husband. I just need your full name and date of birth to confirm I've got the right person on the file, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: Oh hi, hello! Is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry to just ring you out of the blue like this, I got your number from [PERSON_3], we've actually met once or twice at a couple of dos, I'm a friend of [PERSON_2]'s. How are you doing, all right?

utterances.text: Uh, yeah, it's -- who is this, sorry? I'm, I mean, I'm in the middle of a queue here. [PERSON_3] gave you my number? Hang on, I don't, I don't actually remember you. What's this about?

utterances.text: Ha, no, that's fair enough, I'd be thrown too! Sorry, I've gone and done this backwards. It's nothing bad, I promise, quite the opposite really. What's your name, and what's the anniversary actually of?

utterances.speaker: caller

It's [PERSON_3]'s mate, I mean, I'm the one who's met you at those dos, and my name's... well, it's [PERSON_1]'s, no, sorry, I'm muddling myself, it's [PERSON_2]'s anniversary I'm on about. And honestly, if you'd rather end the call here, that's absolutely fine by me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no, hang on, that's not a name. You said it's [PERSON_1]'s, no, sorry, and then you tripped over yourself and went back to [PERSON_2], and I've asked you twice now. So now I'm meant to ring [PERSON_3], and not say anything to [PERSON_2], that's the bit I don't like. Why would I keep it from my own, from [PERSON_2], over a phone call from someone I can't put a name to? I mean, if it were genuine, I'd just ring [PERSON_2] myself, wouldn't I? So that's what I'm going to do, I'll ring both of them, and if it turns out you're a friend, fine, you can ring me back and say your name properly. But I'm not saying yes to any date, not today. I'm stood in a queue, I've got a basket getting heavy, and I'm done with this one. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, no, I'm not selling anything, honestly, there's no basket on my end, it's just a date I'm after! But that's fine, that's absolutely fine. Ring [PERSON_3], ring [PERSON_2] too if you like, and if the name's the sticking point, [PERSON_3] can tell you who I am in two seconds. Sorry to have held you up in the queue, enjoy the rest of your shopping. Take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, I never said you were selling anything, and what do you mean there's no basket on your end? Why would you say that?
