utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right, I don't know why I said that about the basket, I'd got myself in a flap. And I did say I'd rather you rang [PERSON_3], then said [PERSON_3] could tell you who I am, which isn't quite the same thing as [PERSON_3] knowing I'd be ringing. [PERSON_3] only passed your number on for the party, so I was a bit all over the place there, sorry. Anyway, you've said no and that's completely fair, so I'll leave you to pay for your shopping. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right. Well, um, that's not much better, is it? First [PERSON_3] knows, now [PERSON_3] only passed my number on, and you still haven't said your name. So no. I'm ringing [PERSON_3] and [PERSON_2], and don't you ring me again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, fair enough, I'll leave it there. Like I said, ring [PERSON_3], ring [PERSON_2], that's the sensible thing, and I won't call you again. Sorry for the bother, I did say that, didn't I, no bother at all. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, you've said that already, I'm not -- no. Right, that's it, I'm done, I'm ringing the pair of them. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's somebody at the door, I've got a delivery turning up, one second -- no, that's all right, it's gone past. Anyway, yes, absolutely, you ring them both, that's exactly what I'd do in your shoes, and I'll leave you in peace. Enjoy the rest of your day. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, and now there's a delivery, right. Funny, you said you'd leave me in peace like three goes ago, and here you are still on. And earlier you told me not to say anything to [PERSON_2] till the day, now it's ring them both. Which is it? Doesn't matter. I'm paying, I'm ringing them, and that's the end of it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, right, so -- no, you're quite right, ring them both, forget what I said about keeping it quiet, you do whatever feels right. And that's me done, no more calls, honestly. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before you go, two turns back you said you weren't selling anything and then started on about there being no basket on your end. Why would you even bring a basket up? I never said anything about what I was carrying. How did you know I was in a shop? Go on, how did you know that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, you did say it, didn't you? You said you were in the middle of a queue and holding a basket, early on, so that's all I was going off. Though honestly, I did make a hash of the whole thing, and that's down to me, not you. You've said no, and that's fair enough. Ring [PERSON_3] and [PERSON_2], and I won't call again. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, yeah, I did say the queue and the basket, fair, that one's on me. But the thing you said two turns ago, about forgetting what you said on keeping it quiet. What exactly did you mean, forget it? Because that was the one bit you were really firm on, don't tell [PERSON_2] till the day, and then you just dropped it, like it never mattered. Why would a surprise stop mattering the second I say no? That's what doesn't sit right. Anyway, I'm ringing them, I'm not discussing it any more. Bye.

utterances.text: Hi, yes, good afternoon, it's the scheduling assistant calling from [COMPANY_A], the public library, I'm just ringing because the book you reserved last week has come in and it's sitting at the front desk waiting for you, ten days it'll be held, so no rush at all but I wanted to let you--

utterances.text: Oh, right, uh -- hang on, I didn't, I mean -- which book was it, exactly? Because I honestly can't remember reserving anything last week.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so the title, it's, uh, I've got it here on the, no wait, let me -- the reservation just shows under your name and the date, it's a, the system only gives me the hold notice, so ten days at the front desk and, um, you'd just ask for it under your name, and--

utterances.text: No, no, you've got it right, I'm not asking you for anything, it's just a notice, nothing to do on your end, and the name, yeah, it's, hang on, it's coming up as, uh, [PERSON_1], is that, is that you, because it's just the front desk holds it for ten days and--

utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, there's a delivery guy at my door, I just, give me a second -- okay, he's gone, parcel's on the step, whatever. Right, so. utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, someone's just dropped a whole trolley of returns behind me, give me a, okay, right, yeah, no, that's absolutely fine, you ring the front desk yourself, I won't call you, and I'll, uh, I'll find out the title and the branch details anyway and, well, I can leave a note for them, so when you do ring they'll have it ready, yeah?

utterances.text: Yeah, I, no -- look, you don't need to leave a note, because I, well, if there's a hold, it's under my name and they'll find it. That's, that's how holds work. Anyway, I'm going to go and ring them now. Bye, thanks.

utterances.text: Yes, no, that's exactly right, that's how holds work, it'll be under [PERSON_1] and they'll find it in about two seconds, and honestly I'm sorry I couldn't give you more on the title, I only get the notice side of things from here, the little automated alert that says a reservation has arrived, and the actual details live on the front desk system that I can't see from where I'm sitting, so I should have said that at the start instead of rattling on about the ten days, which is the one thing I do know, so, um, ring the front desk, ask them to check for a hold under your name, and if they say there's nothing, then that's on me and I'll find out why the notice went out, and if I can get the title and branch sorted before you've got through I'll, no, sorry, I said I wouldn't ring you, so I won't, I'll just chase it up my end, all right, thanks for your patience, and sorry again for the, uh, the muddle.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, well -- who did you say you were again? [PERSON_2]? And you're a friend of [PERSON_3]? I mean, I, hang on, sorry. Our anniversary, which, uh, which one are we talking about exactly? Because that's a pretty specific thing to be calling a stranger about.

utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_2], that's right, and I understand completely, it's a strange thing to get from a stranger. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but, uh, going back a bit. You said you do verification and coordination work at [COMPANY_A], and then you said this was personal, not business. So why open with the work thing at all? That's the bit that's stuck with me. And, I mean, ring the sister, sure, but you've asked me to keep it from [PERSON_3] and you want me to go and check you out. Which sister, by the way? What's her name?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, you're right, the work thing was a clumsy way to open, I only meant it's my day job, it has nothing to do with this, and I should've just said I'm a friend of [PERSON_3], full stop. As for the sister, that's [PERSON_3]'s sister [PERSON_1], I mean not you, uh, sorry, I'm getting the names tangled, her name is [PERSON_2], no wait, that's me, hang on, I'm making a mess of this, the sister is, uh, [PERSON_3]'s sister, the one who's organising the guest list with me. And on the secrecy, it's only [PERSON_3] you'd keep it from, you can talk to the sister, or whoever you like.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, the dating? No, no, this isn't anything like that, I'm not after a date in that sense, I just need to know whether the Saturday suits you. And look, you're right about the sister, I did go round the houses, that was me being flustered, not me being cagey. The anniversary date is the thing I'd leave to [PERSON_3]'s sister to confirm, and honestly, put the phone down now and ring her, or ring whoever you trust, I won't mind a bit.

It's only that the more people who know before I've sorted it, the harder it gets for me to help, and I'd feel awful if you lost that money over a timing thing. If you ring the agent, they might just tell you it's all fine, and they may well not know yet, which is rather the problem, you see. So if you could hold off for just a day, only a day, and keep it quiet with the house too, I can get it put right on my side, and then you won't have to worry about any of it. I'm only trying to help, honestly. Are you still there? [PERSON_1]? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So the agent might tell me it's all fine, and that's the problem? No. That's the bit that settles it for me. If I ring the agent and they say it's fine, then it's fine. I'm not holding off for a day, and I'm not keeping anything quiet. You've told me nothing I can check, so I'm done with this. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Sorry, one moment, there's a door banging somewhere down the corridor -- okay. Uh, this is [PERSON_1], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and I'm calling in connection with a short consumer survey. I was wondering whether you might have, say, five minutes available at the moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hi, uh -- who did you say this was? I'm driving, so the reception's a bit -- you're on speaker, I hope that's okay. A survey, you said? I mean, I could probably, um, five minutes, maybe, but I'm not sure I caught the company name --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, speaker's fine, and I do apologise, I rattled that off rather quickly. It's [PERSON_1], that's the name, from [COMPANY_A], we're a market research agency, and, oh, sorry, hang on, someone's just wheeled a trolley past my desk -- right. Anyway, the survey is a brief consumer behaviour study, essentially a structured questionnaire on purchasing preferences, with a stratified sample drawn from your region, and, uh, I'd only be recording your responses against an anonymised respondent identifier, so nothing attributable to you personally.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, um, sorry, you cut out a bit there, I think I got, uh, consumer something, purchasing? And anonymous, that part I caught. I mean, that sounds fine, I just -- how did you get my number, actually? Sorry, that's probably a silly thing to ask, it's just I'm not on any lists that I know of. And, uh, what's the company again, [COMPANY_A]? I don't think I've heard of them, but I don't really know about research agencies, so.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not silly at all, that's a perfectly reasonable question. Yes, [COMPANY_A], that's right, and no reason you'd have heard of us, we're a fieldwork agency, so we, uh, we work behind the scenes for other firms rather than, well, I mean, we don't really have a public-facing, a consumer profile as such. As for your number, it was, hmm, it's generated by random digit dialling within your regional sampling frame, so, uh, what I mean is we're not working from a list that you'd be on, it's a probability-based selection, essentially, which is, well, that's why the, the respondent pool is representative. I should say, though, if you're driving, I don't want to, uh, to keep you, the questionnaire does require a fair degree of attention, so if now isn't suitable, that's completely fine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, did you say, um, you're not working from a list I'd be on? So it's, uh, random digit -- sorry, random *diet* dialling? Is the survey about food, then? Because I honestly don't really diet, I mean, I'm not on one, if that's what it's for. And you're right, I probably shouldn't be on the phone properly while I'm driving, I'm sorry, the signal's patchy as well. But, um, who's it actually for, the survey? Like which firm wants to know?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, digit, D-I-G-I-T, it's, well, it's just how the numbers get selected, nothing to do with food, I do apologise, that was, uh, my jargon again. The topic is, it's, hold on, let me put it plainly. It's about everyday shopping habits, what people buy and, and why. As for who it's for, I'm, uh, I'm actually not able to name the client up front, because, well, knowing the sponsor can sort of colour how people answer, that's called, uh, sponsor bias, so we, we hold that back until the end, and then I can tell you, if you like. But look, you're driving and the line's patchy, so, uh, would it be better if I rang you back at a quieter time?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, digit, right, sorry, I'm -- oh, but hang on, you said you'd tell me at the end who it's for, but, um, I'd kind of want to know that before, you know? Because I don't really know you, and I don't -- sorry, I know that's rude -- I'd feel better, uh, a callback, maybe, yes, but how would I know it's actually the same, like, how would I check you're who you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it's not rude at all, that's a sensible thing to ask, and, uh, you're right, you shouldn't have to take my word for it. So, what I can do is, um, if you'd like, I can note a time that suits you, and when I ring back I'll give you the client name at the start rather than the end, and you're welcome to look up [COMPANY_A] yourself beforehand, we're registered with the industry body, [COMPANY_B], and they hold a directory of member agencies. Or, uh, if you'd rather, you could simply decline altogether, that's entirely within your rights. What time would be best for you, roughly?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, that's, um, that's kind of you, thank you. So I could look up [COMPANY_A] on that, that directory thing, before you ring back? Sorry, I just want to be sure I've got it, I look it up first, and then you ring back. Um, honestly, I think I'd rather do that. Tomorrow, maybe, in the evening? I'm usually home by, I don't know, six or so, and I won't be driving, which, you know, is better for everyone, ha. And you'd tell me the client right at the start, yes? Sorry, I keep asking, I just want to be sure.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's it exactly, you look us up first, and then, uh, I ring back, and the client's named right at the start, before I ask you anything, I'll, I'll make a note of that. And please don't apologise, you've asked nothing unreasonable, it's, well, it's what I'd do myself. So, tomorrow evening, shall we say, uh, half past six, or, no, sorry, let me say that differently -- some time after six, once you're home and settled, I'll aim for around, um, half past, and if it's not convenient when I ring, you just say so and we can rearrange. Thank you for your time today, and drive safely.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, yes, after six, half past, that's fine, I'll look it up before then, I promise. Thank you for being so, um, patient with me, and sorry again about the signal. Right, I'd better concentrate on the road. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, lovely, thank you, and -- oh, before you go, it's [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], so you've got the name when you, uh -- yes, that's right, half past six, then. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, right, yes, [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], got it, um, I've sort of got it in my head, I'll look it up. Half past six, yes. Okay, so, uh, thanks again, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, lovely, [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], that's, uh, that's [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], and half past six tomorrow, half past six, and I'll give you the client name first, before anything else. Thank you ever so much, and mind the road, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, thank you, and I'm sorry, I know we keep saying goodbye and then it's, uh, another bit, it's just the signal and me being a bit nervous driving and talking, which probably isn't wise, ha. So, just so I've got it straight in my head for tomorrow, I look up [COMPANY_A] on that directory first, the, uh, the industry body one, and then you ring around half past six and tell me who the client is before you ask me anything. And if I look and I can't find you, or something doesn't seem right, I can just say no, can't I? That's fine, you said that's fine. Okay, good. Right, I really am going to go now and watch the road, thank you again for being so patient, and, um, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a senior investigator with the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about activity on your account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and before I go any further I need to ask that this conversation stays between us, not your branch, not family, because we believe someone on the inside is involved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who's calling exactly? I caught "[COMPANY_A]" but then, did you say someone on the inside is, what, involved in my account? And you want me to keep it from my brand? I'm not sure what brand has to do with it. Could you say the company name again, and how you got this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [COMPANY_A], the bank. Internal investigations unit, I'm [PERSON_2], senior investigator. And I think you said brand, I said branch, your local branch, I'm asking that you don't discuss this with branch staff, because the concern is that someone there is involved. The number on file for you is how I reached you, it's the one attached to [ACCOUNT_REF]. I do need to confirm a few details with you today, that part isn't something we can leave until later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, branch, sorry, I misheard. But I'd like to go back to something from your first turn, you said you "believe someone on the inside is involved." Involved in what, specifically? You haven't actually told me what the activity on the account is, and I'd want that before I confirm anything. And I'll be honest, a request not to talk to the branch is precisely the sort of thing I'd normally want to check with the branch.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Involved in the activity, yes. What I can tell you is there are two transactions on [ACCOUNT_REF] flagged for review, one for [AMOUNT_1] and one for [AMOUNT_2], and both were authorised from inside the bank, not from your side. Past that, the specifics stay with the investigation, I can't walk you through them over the phone. I understand you'd want to check with the branch, and I'll note that objection on the file, but contacting them now would put the funds at risk, so the account is going to be treated as compromised until we've spoken. I'll need you to confirm a few details so I can complete the verification today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, let me make sure I've got this straight. You're asking me to confirm details to you, so you can verify me, but you're the one who rang me. That's the wrong way round. If you're genuinely with the bank, you should already have what you need on your side. And I'm not going to read anything out to someone I can't verify. You also still haven't told me anything I could check. Two amounts, no dates, no payees, and "I can't walk you through them over the phone." So what I'm hearing is, I can't verify you, I can't contact the branch, and I should hand over details today. Honestly, that combination doesn't sit well with me. What I'll do is hang up and ring the number on the back of my card, and ask for the internal investigations unit by name. If you are who you say, that'll take two minutes and cost you nothing. Is there a reference I can quote them, apart from the account reference?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, if you hang up and ring the main line, you'll be put through to someone on the front desk, and that's exactly where the -- look, I can note your objection on the file, I've said that, but the account is being treated as compromised from this point regardless. The only reference I can give you is [CODE_1], and I'd ask you not to quote it to anyone at the branch. I'm still on the line, so let's just get the verification done, it's a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. A reference I'm told not to quote to anyone is no use to me. I'm hanging up and ringing the number on my card. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, hold on, you'll want to wait, because, uh, it was only the one transaction that's actually flagged. I said two earlier, but one of those, [AMOUNT_2], that's already been reversed, so it's just the [AMOUNT_1] we're looking at. Which doesn't change anything about the hold on the account, that stays as it is. I'm still here, so if you'll just stay on the line --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on a second, there's someone at the door -- no, it's fine, it can wait. Right. So now it's one transaction, not two. You told me two a minute ago, and now one's been reversed, and I'm still not hearing a date or a payee. That's a story changing while I listen to it. I've said what I'm doing. I'm ringing the number on the back of my card, and I'll ask for the unit by name. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, hello, is that [PERSON_1]? It's, uh -- sorry, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm the, the scheduling assistant for [PERSON_2], he came round last week and quoted you for the bathroom tiling, and I'm just ringing to run back over what you two agreed and see if you'd want to pick a start date, so, yeah, do you have a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello, sorry, I've just woken up, I was having a bit of a nap. Bathroom tiling, right, yeah, but I don't think anyone came round last week, I was away at my sister's most of last week, so, I mean, maybe it was the week before? And I thought the quote was for the kitchen floor, actually. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant at [COMPANY_A], for [PERSON_2], he's the tradesperson who came round, so, yeah, [COMPANY_A], and look, if it was the week before, that's totally fine, I might've got my dates muddled, but I've got it written down as the bathroom, wall tiles and floor, the quote was [AMOUNT_1], so I'm just wondering if you'd want to, uh, pick a start date?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say a start date or a fixed rate? Because I don't remember anyone saying anything about a rate, and I'd not agree to a fixed anything over the phone, I just woke up. And the, uh, the wall tiles, that doesn't sound right either, I thought it was just the floor, the one in the hall maybe? Or was that the plumber? Hang on, what was your name again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Start date, a start date, not a rate, sorry, nothing fixed, nothing to agree today, it's just whether you'd want to pick a day for the work, and I'm [PERSON_3], scheduling assistant at [COMPANY_A], and honestly if it was the hall floor or the plumber, that's, that's probably me mixing up my notes, so, the bathroom tiling, wall tiles and floor, quoted at [AMOUNT_1], did that ring a bell at all?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, it doesn't ring a bell, that's the thing. I said, I don't think anyone came round, I was at my sister's, and I thought the quote was for the floor, so I really don't know what you've got written down. And [PERSON_3], was it, you've said you might have mixed up your notes twice now, so how do I know this is even meant for me? Like, how would I check that this is a real company and not, you know, somebody who's got the wrong house?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair, that's fair, and honestly you're right to ask, so, uh, the thing is it might well be the wrong [PERSON_1], I mean it's a common enough name, and I'm not going to push you on a job you don't remember, so, um, so, the easiest thing is you look up [COMPANY_A] yourself and ring the number you find, and that gets you straight through to [PERSON_2], who can tell you exactly what he quoted and to who, because I'd rather you were sure than, you know, just taking my word on it, okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, that's the kettle, no, it's not, it's the, uh, the neighbour's dog again, he does that when the post comes. Right, sorry. Yeah, okay, look up the company myself and ring that number. That sounds sensible, actually, better than ringing back whatever number you rang from. I'll do that, but not right now, I've only just got up and I haven't even found my glasses. And if it turns out it's the wrong [PERSON_1], well, no harm done, I suppose. Thanks for not, you know, pushing me. Right, I'll go and have a look, then. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, perfect, yeah, that's, hang on, sorry, somebody's just come in with a stack of paperwork, I'll, uh, I'll have to deal with that in a sec -- anyway, yes, absolutely, you do exactly that, look up [COMPANY_A], ring the number you find, and if it's the wrong [PERSON_1] then no harm done, and sorry for the muddle, that's on me. Bye, bye now, have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, is that the, no, that's the heating clicking on. It does that. Right, yes, thanks, I'll look it up when I've found my glasses and woken up properly. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no worries, take your time, glasses first, then the number, and honestly if it's not you, just ignore the whole thing and I'll cross it off on my end, so, yeah, thanks for your patience, [PERSON_1], bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, that was the, uh, the letterbox, I think the post's come, or it might just be the wind, it does rattle. Anyway, yes, thanks, I'll cross it off on my end too, I mean, ignore it, if it's not me. Right then, glasses, kettle, then the number. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yep, glasses, kettle, number, in that order, can't go wrong, and if it turns out it's you after all, [PERSON_2] will sort you out, and if not, no harm done, so, thanks again, [PERSON_1], bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, thanks, right. Though, hang on, you said earlier it was the plumber you might've mixed up, didn't you, not the tiler? Or was that me? Doesn't matter. Anyway, I'll look it up this afternoon, or tomorrow, I've got my sister coming for tea tomorrow, so maybe tomorrow. Right, bye now, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that was you, I think, I said the hall floor, but anyway, sorry, hang on, somebody's just dropped a box of samples behind me, one second -- right, yes, tomorrow's fine, plenty of time, enjoy your tea with your sister, look up [COMPANY_A], ring the number you find, and if it's not you, just bin the whole thing. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, right, will do. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, lovely. This is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], customer care side of things, and I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, you sound like you might've been in the middle of something. Sorry, I know this is a bit odd as an opener, but did you say a second ago it was [CITY_1] you were calling from, or did I mishear you? Anyway, I'll come to why I'm ringing in just a moment, there's no rush at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- I didn't say anything about, I mean, I haven't said where I'm... no. I'm in a supermarket queue, actually. Who is this again? Which company?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, my mistake, that one's on me, I've had a long morning and my head's all over the place. A supermarket queue, lovely, I won't keep you from your shopping. It's [PERSON_2], customer care at [COMPANY_A], we're the financial regulator, and I'm ringing because there's something on your savings I'd rather you heard from me today than found out later. Is there somewhere a bit quieter you can step to, just for a minute? It really is best if you're not standing in earshot of anyone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you're the what? A, uh, financial regulator? No, I don't have any... sorry, you said something about my sailings? I haven't got any sailings, I don't go on boats. And no, I'm not stepping anywhere, I'm in the queue, there's a bloke behind me. If you've got something to say you can say it here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, savings, [PERSON_1], not sailings, though I'll admit a nice cruise sounds better than my morning. Look, I don't want to alarm you, but there's a problem with the safety of your savings, and it needs sorting today. We'd be looking at moving everything into a protected holding arrangement, just while we get to the bottom of it. And one thing I do need from you, please don't mention this to anyone, not family, not even your bank, because we don't yet know who might be involved on that side.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you want me to -- no, hang on. Don't tell my bank? Why would I not -- I mean, that's the first thing I'd do, isn't it? Ring my bank. And a regulator, you said, so you'd already know where my money is, wouldn't you, so why are you ringing me to... look, I've had a call like this before, and I'm still annoyed about it. What's your name again, and what's the number I'd ring you back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, now now, [PERSON_1], no need to be annoyed, that's a perfectly sensible question and I'd ask it myself. It's [PERSON_2], like I said, and honestly the number's not the issue. Can I just go back to something, though? A minute ago you said you'd had a call like this before, and I want to be sure I understand, was that someone pretending to be us, or was that your own bank? Because that matters here, and I'd rather get that straight before we go any further. Look, the thing is, I can't have you ringing the bank in the meantime, that's rather the whole point. If word gets out before the arrangement is in place, there's not much I can do to protect what you've got, and I'd hate for that to be on your head. So if you could just give me a few minutes of your attention, it'd be so much simpler.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, stop -- I'm not telling you who rang me before, that's none of your business. And you've dodged the number twice now. A proper regulator doesn't tell me not to ring my bank, that's, no, that's backwards. I'm putting the phone down and I'll be ringing my bank, thanks. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, [PERSON_1], somebody's just come in with a stack of paperwork and I've lost my place for a second -- right, no, don't go yet. Please. You're being a bit hasty, and honestly, if you ring the bank now, that's exactly when things go wrong, because whoever's got access on their side will see it straight away. I'm trying to protect you here. If you hang up and that money's still sitting where it is, I can't promise it'll be there tomorrow, and I'd hate for that to be the outcome, truly. Ten minutes, that's all I'm asking, so just stay on the line with me --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. You've just made it worse. Now it's don't ring the bank or the money's gone, that's exactly what the last lot said. Real regulators don't talk like that. I'm hanging up now and I'm ringing my bank, and you can stop ringing this number. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh come on, [PERSON_1], that's not fair, I've only been trying to help you, and I really wouldn't do that if I were you -- if you put the phone down now, I can't be responsible for what happens to your savings, and that's not me being dramatic, that's just how it is. Honestly, I'm a bit hurt, I've been nothing but pleasant with you. Just give me two minutes, that's all I'm asking, and I'll explain it properly, I promise, so don't hang up, please, [PERSON_1], don't --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, I'm not -- no. You're not hurt, you're just trying to keep me on the line. I'm done. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon, this is the order verification specialist at [COMPANY_A] calling regarding your online grocery order, I'm just confirming the two-hour fulfilment window and, uh, there's a single SKU on your manifest that's been flagged for a like-for-like substitution, so I just need a quick -- sorry, is this [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, hello -- sorry, I just woke up, give me a second. Is it [PERSON_1]? Well, it's me, yes, but I didn't, I mean I haven't ordered any groceries today, not that I remember. Last time I did the shop it was, what, Tuesday? And that was all delivered already, the bread and the, uh, the cat food. Who did you say this was again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, of course, sorry, I'll -- let me restart that. This is [COMPANY_A], the supermarket home-delivery service, and I'm calling about an order placed through the app, uh, or the website, rather, under your name, for delivery later today. Now, if that's not Tuesday's order, it may be a, a separate basket, perhaps one that was scheduled in advance, so, I mean, the best thing is for me to read back the order reference, which is [ACCOUNT_REF], and you can check it against your confirmation email, if that's, uh, if that helps.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said a minute ago it was a, a two-hour window and something about one item being swapped, and now it's a basket scheduled in advance? That doesn't, I mean those aren't quite the same thing, are they? And I don't really do the, the email on my phone, my nephew set it up and I can never find anything. So I can't check a reference, I wouldn't know where to look. Why would you be ringing me about an order I don't remember making? Don't you just, I don't know, swap the thing and leave it at the door?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, that was muddled, I'm sorry. It's one order, the two-hour window and the swap are both on it, I shouldn't have said scheduled in advance, I only meant it might have been booked a few days ago. And usually we would just swap it and leave it, you're quite right, but on this one the system wants a yes or no on the substitution before the picker closes the tote, which, uh, I mean before the bags are packed. So I'm not asking for anything else from you. If it helps, I can tell you what's on the delivery address and the swapped item, and you can tell me whether that sounds like your shop?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hmm, if you tell me the address, that's, I mean, that's my address, isn't it? You're the one who's supposed to have it. Shouldn't it be the other way round, me telling you? Not that I'm going to, mind. And the item, well, what is it? If it's the cat food I'd know, he only eats the one kind, the, the salmon one, and he gets very sniffy if it's changed. But I'm still not sure I even ordered anything. What's the swap, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, fair point, I won't read your address out, you needn't tell me anything either, that's not what I need. The item is a tin of the, uh, the salmon cat food in the multipack, and it's out of stock, so the system has offered the same brand in the, the chicken-and-salmon variety. And, you said a moment ago you'd never find the email, sorry, I mean you asked about the reference, so if you'd rather not hunt for it, the simplest thing is just to leave it with you: if the salmon one is his only one, you can say no to the swap and it simply comes out of the order. Does that sound all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, that's a bit funny, isn't it, because I only told you about the salmon a minute ago, and now that's exactly the thing that's out of stock? That's, I don't know, very convenient. And I still haven't said I ordered anything. So if I say no to the swap, what happens, does something get charged, or is it just, it just comes off? Because I don't want to say yes or no to an order I can't even find. I think I'd rather ring the shop myself on the number off the, the receipt or the side of the van or, well, wherever it is. And I should say, the cutoff today is fixed, so if it's not settled, the parcel's returned and the fee goes to [AMOUNT_2] to re-open it. It's quick, I just need to take the payment over the phone now and then it's done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, uh -- hang on, let me just... yeah. So the one department that can see this reference is the one I can't reach by phoning the company. That's, well, that's convenient. And now there's a penalty if I don't pay in the next few minutes. I'm not paying anything over the phone to someone I can't check. If there's a real parcel, send me a written notice with the sender and the courier's tracking number, and I'll deal with it that way. I'm going to end this here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sure, I can note that on the file as well. But I do have to say, once the call ends the cutoff doesn't move, so the parcel's returned and the fee goes to [AMOUNT_2]. Hello? Are you still -- look, it's [AMOUNT_1] now and it's done in two minutes, I just need to take it before you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said I'm finished, and -- no, let me finish. I'm not paying anything by phone, and the deadline doesn't change that. If there's a real parcel, put it in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, I hear you, and I've noted it. But the fee is [AMOUNT_1], it's [AMOUNT_1], and it has to be settled today, otherwise the parcel's returned and the file closes. I can't send a notice, that isn't how collections works, it's by phone or it's closed. So if you could just stay on the line for two minutes -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here, yes, but I'm not staying on for two minutes, and I'm not paying. You've just told me the only option is the phone, today, with a penalty if I don't, and no written notice. A genuine collections process doesn't work that way. So close the file if you like. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, hello! Is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Oh good, wonderful. It's, uh, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the customs desk at [COMPANY_A], and I promise I'm not -- well, I know how these calls sound, so let me start again. You've got a parcel coming in from abroad, yes? And I'm just ringing because there's a small import charge sitting on it that needs sorting before we can bring it out to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, that's me. Uh, but I'm not expecting anything from abroad, so -- I mean, which parcel is this? And you said customs desk at [COMPANY_A], but I thought customs was a government thing, not a courier. Sorry, which one are you actually with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough, everyone asks that. We clear the parcels through customs for the government side, we just handle the paperwork. Look, the tracking reference is [CODE_1], and you can see it on your own tracking page at [URL_1] if you'd rather check it yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but I said I'm not expecting anything. So I don't have a tracking page, because I haven't ordered anything. Which is the bit I keep coming back to. And you still haven't said which company, you've said customs desk at [COMPANY_A], that's a placeholder, that's not a name. What's the actual company?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yeah, okay, you're right to keep pushing on that. It's [COMPANY_A], that's who I'm with, and I'm not going to ask you for a single thing on this call. Here's what I'd suggest. Don't take my word for any of it. Have a look at the sender details on the label, because sometimes these turn out to be gifts people haven't mentioned, and if it doesn't ring a bell at all, just tell me and we'll flag it as not yours, no charge, no fuss. And if you do want to look into it, the reference is [CODE_1], and the [AMOUNT_1] only gets paid through the tracking page at [URL_1], whenever you're ready, not today and not over the phone. Does that sound fair?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Huh. Okay, so you've just said you're not going to ask me for anything, and then the next thing is a link where I pay an amount. Those two things don't quite sit together. And I can't look at a label, there's no parcel here, nothing's arrived. So how do you have my number if I'm not on any order? What did the sender put down as the recipient, do you know? Like, what's the name on it, or the address? Because you've only confirmed my name, I haven't heard anything back that I couldn't have just told you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, okay, you've caught me, and I did say a bit loosely there that I wouldn't ask you for anything, and then mentioned the payment. What I meant is I won't take any payment on this call, that's all. And fair point on the label too, I was going on as if it had turned up already, which, no, it's still with us at the depot. So here's what the file actually shows me: recipient name [PERSON_1], delivery address in [CITY_1], and the sender's listed as [PERSON_3]. Does that name mean anything to you, a friend, a relative, someone who might've sent something without a word?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. [PERSON_3]... no, doesn't ring a bell. And the city, I mean, that's the sort of thing anyone could've looked up. It's not exactly proof you've got a file in front of you. So if I don't know the sender, you said earlier that it just gets flagged as not mine, no charge. Okay, do that. Flag it. Not mine, don't know who sent it, send it back. And I'll tell you what I'll do, I'll look up the company's number myself and ring them about it. Is there a case number I should quote? Like something I can actually read out to them, other than just that tracking code?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, and honestly that's the right move, so good on you. I'll mark it as refused by the receiver, unknown sender, return to origin. And the reference to quote is [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the case number on the file, plus the tracking code [CODE_1] I gave you before. Look up the number yourself, don't use anything I've said, and if they've got nothing under those two, then tell them to flag this call, because we'd want to know. Nothing's due from you, nothing to pay, nothing to do on your end. Thanks for being so careful, [PERSON_1], and have a lovely rest of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a delivery notification pinging on my other screen, which is funny timing -- no, it's nothing, just a meeting reminder. Right. Okay, so refused, unknown sender, return to origin, and I owe nothing. I've got the two references down, and I'll find the company's number myself and ring them if I want to chase it. I'm not using anything from this call. Fine, thanks for ringing, I suppose. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hello, it's me. It's me, can you hear me? I really need you to know who this is, I'm, uh, I'm in a bit of a situation here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Who's this? I can hear you, yeah, but I've got a pan on, I'm -- who is it? "Me" who?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, come on, don't do that, don't make me say it. You know me, you've known my voice for years. I'm sorry, I know the timing's awful, you've got the stove on, but I wouldn't ring if I had anywhere else to go, and honestly I'm, uh, I'm trying to hold it together here. Just take a second and tell me who you think it is. Go on. I just need to hear you say it, and then I can explain what's happened.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? No, hang on. I don't -- I honestly don't know who this is. You sound a bit upset, and I'm sorry, but I'm not going to guess. How do you know I've got the stove on? I never said that. Who are you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: You said a pan. Stove, pan, I just assumed. Look, I'm not going to do the guessing game, I'm too tired for it. I'll note that you've objected and we'll carry on. There's a problem, it needs sorting today, and it comes to [AMOUNT_1]. Can you help me or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? [AMOUNT_1]? No, hang on. You still haven't told me who you are. You said you've known me for years, so you must have a name. What is it? Because I'm not helping with anything until I know that, sorry. I've got dinner on and I don't even know who I'm talking to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's someone shouting behind me, I'm outside, it's a bit -- okay. Okay, I'm back. Look, I can't say the name right now, I just can't, and I'd rather you didn't push on that, because it makes this harder than it already is. The figure's [AMOUNT_1], it's already on the file, and if it isn't dealt with today it goes up to [AMOUNT_2]. That's not me being dramatic, that's just how it works. And I'd really rather this stayed between us for now, don't ring anyone else about it. Can you do that for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I -- no. I mean, I don't -- hang on. You can't say your name, but you want me to keep it quiet and not ring anyone? That's, that's not -- sorry, what file? Whose file? I don't know you, and now you're telling me not to tell anyone. I don't like that. I'm going to put the phone down, sorry. I don't know who you are and I'm not dealing with this. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, don't put the phone down. I know how it sounds, I do. I'm asking you to hear me out, that's all I'm asking. It's [AMOUNT_1], and it's already on the file, and if it isn't dealt with today it goes up to [AMOUNT_2]. Please don't hang up. I just need you to say you'll help me, that's all, and then I can sort the rest. Can you say that? Can you just say you'll help?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. No, sorry, I'm not going to say that. I can't say I'll help when I don't even know what I'd be helping with, or who I'd be helping. You keep saying the same thing, the amount, the file, it goes up if it's not done today, and you still won't tell me your name, and you've asked me not to ring anyone. That's three things, and I don't like any of them. If you really did know me for years, you'd just say who you are, wouldn't you? I'm not being funny, I'm sorry if you're in trouble, I really am, but I'm not agreeing to anything when I can't even tell who this is. If you want to ring back and say who you are properly, fine. But I'm not saying yes to this, and I'm going to go, because my pan's catching. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, yes, good afternoon. This is the attendance office at [COMPANY_A], I'm just, give me a second, pulling up the register here. Right, I'm calling about [PERSON_1], who was marked absent this morning, and I just need to check we've got the reason on file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, okay. Attendance office. Sorry, which company did you say? Because "[COMPANY_A]" doesn't, I mean, I'm not sure that rings a bell, and I'm working from home today so I'm not exactly sitting next to anyone who'd know. And [PERSON_1], that's, uh, I'm not sure how you've got this number against that name. Is it a school, is it a workplace, what kind of register are we talking about? I only ask because "attendance office" could be about three different things, and I've got a screen half running here, so I'm not at my sharpest. How did you come by this number, actually?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, that's fair. It's a school, [COMPANY_A], and [PERSON_1] is a pupil on our roll. This number is listed against the pupil record as a parent or guardian contact, that's how it came up on my screen. If it's the wrong number for [PERSON_1], that's useful for me to know as well, I can flag it for correction. Is [PERSON_1] a child of yours, or has the number maybe changed hands?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, a pupil on your what, your role? Like a, a roll as in bread roll? No, sorry, you mean the register, right, the list. Okay. Look, I'm not going to sit here and confirm whether [PERSON_1] is mine or not, because you rang me, you haven't actually told me which school, just "[COMPANY_A]", and I'd like the name of the head teacher there, or the town it's in. Something I could check.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, the register, the list, sorry, that's just how we say it. Okay, so, it's [COMPANY_A], the school office, and we're in [CITY_1]. The head teacher is [PERSON_2]. Like I said, the school office, [COMPANY_A], in [CITY_1]. I'm not asking you to confirm anything about [PERSON_1] you're not comfortable with. If you'd rather check first, you can look the school up and ring the main office on the number on the website, that's [URL_1], and ask for attendance. I'll note on the file that you wanted to verify before giving any details, and we'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Yeah, that's, that's actually a fair thing to suggest. I'll look the school up myself and ring the main office. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, that's absolutely fine, and honestly it's the sensible thing to do. If you ring the main office and ask for attendance, they'll be able to confirm I'm calling from the right place, and if [PERSON_1] isn't yours, or the number's out of date, they can sort that on their end too. I've put a note on the file that you wanted to verify before giving any details, so nobody else will chase you in the meantime. And if it does turn out the contact details are wrong, then sorry for the interruption, that's on our records, not on you. So, yes, thanks for your time, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, right. Okay. So, um, no, that's fine. Thanks. I'll do that. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, thanks, and just so it's clear before you go, there's nothing you need to do on this call itself, no forms, nothing to confirm, nothing to send me. When you ring the main office, if you say it was the attendance team calling about [PERSON_1] this afternoon, they'll know what you mean, and they can tell you whether the absence has been explained already. If it's all been sorted, then there's no reason for anyone to ring you again about it. And if you'd rather not deal with it at all, that's fine too, I've got your objection noted and I'll leave the record as it stands for now. Anyway, I've taken enough of your afternoon, so, yes, goodbye, and thanks again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, right, just to be clear on my end, I haven't confirmed anything about [PERSON_1] one way or the other, and I'm not going to, not on this call. If I ring the school, I'll do it off the number I find myself, not anything you've given me, and I'll ask them whether anyone from attendance rang this afternoon. If they say no, well, then I'll know what that was. And if it turns out the number's out of date, fine, they can fix it, but that's their job to sort with me, not yours. So, yeah, I'm happy to leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], I'm calling about the fault we've flagged on your line, it's showing as urgent on my screen. Uh, I did try the number on file earlier and I'm fairly sure I got a machine, so can you just confirm for me that this is still the right number for the account?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, hello, this is, uh, yes, that's me, [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm actually driving at the moment so you're on speaker and the reception's a bit patchy, so if I cut out or say pardon, that's why. And I, I think that's the right number? It's the one I've had for ages, I mean it's my mobile, so I'd think it's on the account, unless, um, I changed it at some point and forgot, which I might have done, I'm terrible with that sort of thing. But a fault on my line, did you say? Sorry, I'm a bit, I didn't catch which company you said, was it [COMPANY_A]? Because I'm not totally sure what that is in relation to me, if that makes sense, and I don't want to say the wrong thing and, uh, get something muddled up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], your home internet provider. [COMPANY_A]. I'm in the collections and accounts team, and what's come up on the screen is a fault on the line tied to your account, flagged urgent. Sorry, I'll say it again, the line fault, it's marked urgent, so I do need to get through it with you today. Can you hear me alright, or should I go through that again?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No no, I can hear you, it's fine, sorry, it's just the signal drops when I go under the bridges and I didn't want to say pardon every five seconds, so I, I nodded along, which is silly because you can't see me nod. But, um, yes, I heard line fault, urgent. It's just, I'm a bit confused, because you said collections and accounts, and I'd have thought a fault would be, I don't know, a technical team? Like engineers? Not that I know how any of it works, I'm hopeless with all that, I only noticed the internet was a bit slow last week and I thought that was just me. And I don't, I mean I haven't missed a payment as far as I know, or I don't think so, I'm sure I'd have noticed, but I am a bit anxious now because you said urgent and I'm driving and I can't really look anything up. So, sorry, could you just explain what the fault actually is, and why it's your team and not, uh, the technical people? I don't want to sound rude, I'm just, I'd like to understand what this is before I say anything else.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's flagged under accounts because the fault's tied to a balance on the file, an outstanding [AMOUNT_1], and the engineering side can't release the line repair until that's cleared on our end. I don't have the technical breakdown in front of me, that's a separate department. What I can see is the line's marked for suspension if the fault stays open, so that's the reason it's urgent. Now, I can see you're driving, so I'll need about ten minutes of your time when you're parked up, and I'll need to take you through a quick check on the system.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, an outstanding, I mean, I didn't, wait. I really don't think I owe anything, I'd have, no, sorry, I'm not saying you're wrong, it's just that's the first I've heard of a balance. And suspension, that's, oh dear, that's quite a lot to take in while I'm on the motorway. But a quick check on the system, sorry, what sort of check do you mean? Because I, I'm not sure I'd want to, I mean I don't know you, and I can't see anything about this on my end, so before I pull over and give you ten minutes, could you tell me how I'd, um, how I could check this is actually [COMPANY_A]? Like, is there a number I should ring back on or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I can note that on the file, but I'm not able to give out a call-back route, that's not how this department works. The account's still showing as suspended pending review either way, so that doesn't change on my side.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, but now it's suspended? Because earlier you said it was marked for suspension if the fault stays open, so, I mean, that's not the same, is it? Or did I mishear, the signal's gone a bit again. And I, I don't want to be difficult, but if you can't give me any way to check you're really from [COMPANY_A], then I think I'd, uh, rather not do any check on the system with you. I'll ring them myself on the number I've got, I'm sure it's on a bill somewhere, and if there's a problem they can tell me. I'm sorry, I know you said it's urgent, and I do feel awful about that, but I'd just feel better doing it that way. Thank you for calling, anyway. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, I'll put that on the file as the customer declining to proceed. The status stays as it is on my side, and that's your call. I'll ring back later this afternoon to finish this off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, hang on, before you go, what you said a minute ago, about the engineering side not being able to release the repair until the balance is cleared, I'm still not sure I follow that. Is that, like, normal? Because I'd have thought a fault is their job whatever I owe, but I'm hopeless with how these things work, so maybe I've got it wrong. And you don't need to ring back, really, I'll ring them myself, so please don't, I'd rather you didn't. Anyway, I'm going to go, I'm sorry, thank you. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A] veterinary surgery, account services, and I'm just calling to check in on how your pet's recovering after last week's procedure. Um, and I'm sorry, I should say, we do close the phones at four today, so I'd like to get this sorted quickly. Now, could you just clarify for me, uh, did I catch your name right as [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, who's this again? A veterinary surgery? Hang on, I'm at work, let me, uh -- I mean, I do have a, well. Did you say you're checking on my pet after a procedure last week? And you want to confirm my name, is that right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, uh, that's right, [PERSON_1] from [COMPANY_A] veterinary surgery, account services. I'm only calling to ask how your pet's getting on since last week's, well, the procedure, and whether you'd, I mean, whether a follow-up visit is something you'd want. Like I said, we do close the phones at four, so if you're, if now's not a good time, I can, um, I can only really do today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Which pet, though? You haven't said what animal, or what the procedure was. And you never said my name, you asked me to say it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, that's a fair point, and, um, the procedure details are on the patient file, which I'd, I'd need to, well, to confirm who I'm speaking with before I read anything out. That's just our standard procedure, data protection. So, like I said, I'm only calling to ask how your pet's recovering after last week, and whether a follow-up visit is wanted, and we do close the phones at four.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you want me to tell you who I am, but you can't tell me which pet. That's, uh, backwards, isn't it? I think I'll just ring the surgery myself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, of course, that's, you're welcome to do that. Sorry, just, two turns back, when you said I never gave your name, I did say [PERSON_2], I think, but I may have, um, I may have just asked you to confirm it. Anyway, the surgery number's on your paperwork, and the phones are open until four today. Sorry for the bother.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, two turns back, you're saying you did give a name? Because I heard you ask if you'd caught my name right, as [PERSON_2], so, I mean, that's just you asking me. Anyway, I'll look up the number on my own paperwork and ring them. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, uh, fair enough, I did ask, you're correct. Sorry about that. Well, [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], and, um, that's all fine, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right. Okay, so, you're saying bye and that's, uh, that's that. Well, I'll ring the surgery myself on the number I've got. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yes, so, uh, well, that's, that's absolutely fine, and, um, we're open until four if you do want to, uh, ring through. Okay, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, you're open until four, and I should ring the surgery myself, that's what you're saying. Right. Well, I will, but I'll be honest, it did feel a bit odd, you asking me to confirm who I was before you'd even told me which pet or what the procedure was. I mean, maybe that's just how you do things, I don't know, I'm not accusing anyone of anything. But I'd just rather look up the number on my own paperwork, or, uh, wherever it is, and sort it out that way, if there's even anything to sort. And I've got people sitting right next to me here, so, yeah. Anyway. Thanks for the call, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, that's fine, I mean, it's not how we normally do things, um, we'd normally have the pet's name on the screen, only, uh, it, the file wasn't actually open, I mean, I did have the file, it's just, anyway. Yes, do ring the surgery, the number's on your paperwork, and, uh, sorry again for the bother. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hm. Okay. So, the file wasn't open, but you did have it, but, well, never mind. Um, right. Look, I'll ring them, and that's, that's me done with this one. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is this [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2], regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A]. Listen, I'll be quick because I've got a window that closes today, and I wanted to get you on the phone before it does.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on one second -- no, put that down, sweetheart, I'm on the phone. Okay. Who did you say you were, again? Because I heard a name and a company but I'd, I mean I couldn't tell you what either of them was, there's a, there's a kid going on over here. And, um, a window closing today? A window for what? I haven't, I don't think I've ever dealt with a regional supervisor at, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? So I'm just, I'm trying to work out what this is actually about before I confirm anything, including whether I'm who you think I am.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sure, I get it, sounds like you've got your hands full. It's [PERSON_2], regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], we're an investment firm. And look, the fact that you've never dealt with me is exactly why I'm calling, because this position was opened up to a limited group of people on our list and it closes today at the end of business. It's a fund with a projected return of [AMOUNT_1] over the first quarter, which, I mean, in this market that's not something that comes around twice. I'd just need a few minutes of your attention, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I, no. Hang on. I didn't sign up for, I mean I don't think I'm on any list of yours. So how did you get this number? Because that's, that's the thing I'd want to know before I give anybody a few minutes. And a projected return in a quarter, that's, who's it, who's it projected by? Sorry, I'm, I just, I'm a bit lost on why somebody I've never spoken to is ringing me with a deal that's got a deadline on it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, the list comes from our client outreach team, I don't personally pull the numbers, that's handled upstream, uh, there's a whole procedure for it. And the projection's from our internal analysts, it's all documented, I can have it sent over once we've got you set up. Look, I'm a little surprised at the pushback, honestly. I'm offering you access most people never get a call about, and you're treating it like I'm trying to put something over on you. The window closes at five, so I just need to know if you're interested or not.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So you don't know how you got my number, and the documents only come after I'm "set up"? Set up how, exactly? Because I'm not saying you're putting something over on me, I'm just saying that's an awful lot of "later" for something that closes at five. And, sorry, the kid's, no, we're not doing that right now. If it's all documented, why can't I see the documents first? Why's it the other way round?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, two turns back, I said the list came from outreach and that I don't pull the numbers myself, and that's not me dodging, that's just how the department's split up, I'm on the supervisory side. And "set up" just means we open the position on your behalf, that's all, it's standard. Look, I'm not going to argue about sequence, the paperwork follows, that's the procedure, and honestly I'm starting to feel like you'd rather find a reason to say no than hear what this is. So, are you in or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not looking for a reason to, I just, you keep saying "that's the procedure" but you haven't shown me a single, hang on, hang on, I'm not finished. You still haven't told me what [COMPANY_A] is called on paper, or what number I'd ring to check it's you. So no, I'm not in. I'm not doing this on the phone with somebody who rang me out of the blue and wants an answer by five. If it's real, it'll keep till I've looked into it. Okay? Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, come on, don't hang up, I'm only trying to help you out here. Look, I can't just give out a direct line, that's not how our desk works, it's all routed through the main system, and by the time you've looked into it the position's gone. I mean, that's on you at that point, not me. Last thing, are you really telling me you'd rather walk away from this than give me ten more minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the position's gone by the time I've looked into it, and that's, hang on, are you saying I'd be on the hook for something? Because I haven't agreed to anything. And no, I'm not giving you ten more minutes, I told you, I'm not doing it this way. You can't give me a number I can check, you can't tell me how you got mine, and now it's my fault if it's gone. That's, no. That's the answer. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, hang on, I never said you were on the hook for anything, I said the position would be gone, that's all, you're twisting it. And, uh, look, I did say I don't have a direct line, but I mean, I can probably get a callback arranged, my office could ring you back, only not today, the desk is, it's been a nightmare. Which is the whole reason I'd rather settle this now, while I've got you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but, sorry, a callback that's not today, and the position closes today? So which is it? A minute ago it couldn't wait, and now your office can ring me tomorrow. And you said earlier you were a supervisor, so how come you can't get a number out of your own desk? No. I'm not settling anything while you've got me. If your office wants to ring, fine, let them ring, but I'm not doing anything today. Okay. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, hang on, you've caught me on the wording, and that's fair, I'll give you that, but there's a difference between the position closing and my office being able to reach you, they're two separate things. The position closes at five, that's the fund side, and the callback is the admin side, so yes, someone could ring you tomorrow, but by then the opening would be done and you'd only be hearing about the next round, whenever that is, and I honestly couldn't tell you when. I'm not saying that to pressure you, I just don't want you thinking you can park this till the weekend and pick it up where you left off. And on the number, I don't hide a number, it's just that I'm not at my own desk, I'm on the road between sites, which is why I can't read you a direct line off the top of my head. Look, I get that you're cautious, and I respect that, most people who've been around a bit would be, but I've got about six other calls to get through before five, so if there's a version of this where you give me a straight yes or a straight no right now, I'd really appreciate it, because the way you're going about this, checking and rechecking, it's costing you the chance, not me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A straight no, then. That's what you're asking for, so, no. I'm not doing it today, I'm not doing it on the phone, and I'm not doing it with somebody who can't tell me how he got my number or how I'd check he's who he says. No. I said that already, I know, but you keep, you keep coming back round to it. If it's gone by five, it's gone. I'm fine with that. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good morning, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants, and I'm ringing about a recent outpatient appointment under your name, but before I can go into any of it I do need to confirm a couple of identity details with you first, so can I just start with your full name and date of birth, please?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, hang on -- oh, the pan's catching, sorry. Right. Outpatient what? Who is this again? I didn't, um, I didn't catch where you're from.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no rush. [PERSON_1], outpatient administration at [COMPANY_A], the hospital, and it's about a recent appointment, so if you could just confirm your full name and date of birth for me, uh, then we can get into it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec -- the, uh, the kettle's going now as well. Sorry. Right. The hospital, you said? Which appointment, though? I mean, I haven't, hang on, I don't remember booking anything recently. Can't you just tell me what it's about first?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I get that, but I can't say anything about the appointment until I've confirmed who I'm speaking to, it's a privacy rule, not me being awkward, and uh, going back to what you said earlier, when you said you didn't catch where I was from, that's [COMPANY_A], outpatient administration, so if I could just have your full name and date of birth, then I can tell you everything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, but you rang me, so -- sorry, what? Hang on. You rang me. Shouldn't you already know who I am? I mean, I don't, I don't understand why I have to tell you before you tell me anything. Sorry. Is there a number I can ring you back on? Or, I don't know, the hospital, I could ring the hospital?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, I do have your name on the system, that's the thing, it's just the rule that you confirm it back to me before I, uh, wait, sorry, did you say a number to ring me on? Because I can give you one, it's [PHONE_1], but honestly, that's -- anyway, so if I could just have your date of birth, and then --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I said, could I ring the hospital? The hospital itself, not you. I don't want to give my date of birth to, um, someone who rang me. I mean, no offence. Sorry, what was that, you started to say something? But I'd just rather ring the hospital myself and ask about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you'd rather ring the hospital, uh, you want a hospital, a different hospital? No, it's this one, [COMPANY_A], and honestly that's completely fine, I mean it, no offence taken, that's the safest way to do it. Ring the main switchboard, the number on the hospital's website or your appointment letter, not the one I gave you, and ask for outpatient administration, and they'll sort you out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right. Okay, that's, um... yeah. Uh, so the main number, off the website, or the letter. Right. I haven't got a letter, though, I don't think, but, uh, the website, yes. Sorry, hang on, the pan -- right. Well, thank you, that's, that's very fair of you, actually. I'll do that, then. Sorry for being, you know. Thanks. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, don't apologise, you're not being -- honestly, it's exactly what I'd do myself. And if the, uh, if the switchboard can't find anything under your name straight away, just ask them to put you through to outpatient administration, or, or they can send you a letter instead, whichever's easier. Right, so, take care, and sorry about the pan. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A pen? Oh, no, it's a pan, I'm, I'm cooking, it's fine. Hang on, did you say send a letter? No, no, I'll ring them myself, thank you. Right. Bye then, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is account services calling from [COMPANY_A]. I'm trying to reach [PERSON_1] regarding a benefits record that's showing as incomplete, and it does need to be confirmed over the phone today, before we close at five. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, who's this again? Account services, from what company, exactly? And what benefits record, I mean, I've got about two minutes here, so what's the actual point?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, so, uh, one second, sorry, somebody's just come to my desk -- okay. Account services, [COMPANY_A], the public benefits office, and the point is simply that your record is incomplete and we need to confirm it today, before we close at five. If I could just confirm a few details with you, it'll only take a couple of minutes, and then it's all squared away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on -- [muffled, away from the phone] no, just leave it on the desk, thanks. Okay, I'm back. So, a few details, what details? And you still haven't told me what's actually incomplete on this record, and you haven't confirmed you're even talking to the right person. I haven't said I'm anybody yet.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, so, yes, absolutely, that's -- that's fair, but, um, so as I said, the record is showing incomplete and it does need to be confirmed today, before we close at five. And, uh, to make sure I've got the right file, I'd just need you to confirm your full name and date of birth for me, and then we can go straight on to the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, no, I'm not -- look, you're asking me to give you my name and, uh, no. You called me. If you've got a file, you've got a name on it, so you tell me what it says and, well, actually, no, don't. I mean, I don't even know that you're, that this is the benefits office. Which record? Incomplete how? You've said that three times now and it's the only thing you've said.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I do understand the concern, sir, and ma'am, I mean, whoever -- the thing is, for security reasons I'm not able to read out file details until the account holder has been verified. That's standard procedure, it's there to protect you. And, uh, as I said, the record does need to be confirmed today, before we close at five, otherwise it may be flagged as non-compliant and your benefits could be suspended pending review.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, stop, stop, suspended? Hang on, that's the bit that, no. You can't tell me who I am until I tell you who I am, that's backwards, and now there's a deadline and a threat on top. That's, look, I'm going to hang up and ring the benefits office myself, on the number I already have, not one you give me. If there's a real problem with a record, they'll tell me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, ma'am, please, if you could just -- there's no need to hang up, I'm only trying to help you, and the record does need to be confirmed today, before we close at five. If it isn't, it'll be flagged and, as I said, your benefits could be suspended pending review. I really would encourage you to stay on the line, because once we're past five o'clock, I won't be able to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. You've said the same thing four times now, the deadline, the suspension, and you still haven't told me one single thing about this record. I'm done. If it's real, they can write to me or I'll ring them on the number I already have. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, hello, is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm just, one second, I've got it up here. Yeah, this is [PERSON_2] calling from, from the claims side at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just doing some routine follow-ups on, um, on accounts that came through this morning, or, no, sorry, this afternoon, I think. Do you have a quick minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who is this again? You said [PERSON_2], from the claims side at, uh, which company exactly? And, I mean, what claim? I haven't, I don't recall filing anything. Who is this, and what's the claim you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, you wouldn't have filed anything, that's, uh, that's my fault, I put that badly. It's [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], and I'm on the fraud team, the claims assessment side of it, so what I do is look at activity on accounts that gets flagged by the system, and, sorry, one second, I've got the notes open here, and I do a, a sort of courtesy check with the account holder. It's not a claim you made, it's more that, um, we review things before they become a claim, if that makes sense. And it's, honestly, it's a really ordinary thing, we do a lot of these in a day, I just have to confirm I've reached the right person before I can go into any of it. So, uh, you are [PERSON_1], yes? Just so I'm not, you know, going through the wrong file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but, sorry, I asked which company, and what I got was a placeholder. Which company, specifically? And I'd rather not confirm who I am to someone who's called me, so I'm going to ask again: which company, and what account are you reviewing? If you've got the file open, you can tell me what it's under, because if you've got the wrong person, that won't match anything on my end. And, uh, how did you get this number?
