utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, uh, sure, that's fair. It's [COMPANY_A], the fraud team there, like I said, and the file is, um, hang on, let me scroll, it's under [ACCOUNT_REF]. Does that, does that ring a bell at all? And the number, it's, it's on the account as the contact number, that's how it comes up on my screen, I didn't, I wouldn't have dialled it otherwise. So, look, the reason I'm calling is a charge was just attempted on the account, for [AMOUNT_1], it was, um, it was held, it didn't go through, but the system flagged it, and I do need to go through a couple of things with you before it clears or, or gets declined for good. So if you could just confirm your full name and, uh, the date of birth on the account, then we can get into it properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, it doesn't ring a bell, and I'll be honest, nothing you've said so far is something I can check. You've given me a company name that's still a placeholder to my ears, an account reference that means nothing to me, and an amount you haven't actually stated. And the order of this is backwards, isn't it? You rang me, so you're the one who needs to establish who you are, and then you're asking for my full name and date of birth, which is precisely what someone would need to impersonate me. If you really were calling from the fraud team of a company I do business with, I'd expect you to be able to tell me something that isn't on a screen in front of you, like which product the account is for, or how long it's been open. And I'd expect that if I hang up and ring the number printed on the back of the card, or on a statement, I'd get straight through to the same team and they'd know about the held charge. So that's what I'd prefer to do. Is there a reference I can quote when I call back, and which department I should ask for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, no, I hear you, and a reference, yeah, I'd have to check what I can give out there, I'll have to look into that. Sorry, can I just, can I go back to something, when you said I hadn't actually stated the amount, I did, didn't I? It was [AMOUNT_1], or, hang on, no, I think it might be [AMOUNT_2], I've got two things up here and I'm not, sorry, I'll sort that out. The thing is, if you do hang up and ring around, the hold on that charge doesn't stay open very long, so it'd be, it'd be better to deal with it now while it's still pending, because once it lapses it's, it goes through as authorised and, uh, that's much harder to dispute afterwards. So if you could just confirm the name and date of birth, that's all I need to move it along.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you've just given me two different amounts, you can't tell me which is right, and you can't give me a reference I could quote. That's about where I'm going to stop. And the bit about the hold lapsing, that's the part that worries me most, because a real hold doesn't turn into an authorised charge because I took five minutes to ring the bank back. It's just a pressure line to get me to answer now rather than check. So no, I'm not confirming my name or date of birth to someone who rang me and can't verify a single thing. If there's genuinely a held charge, I'll find out when I ring the number on the back of my card, and if it's gone through in the meantime, I'll dispute it through them. Thanks for your time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, uh, no, hang on, please don't, I mean, you're, you're free to ring whoever you like, I can't stop you, but I'd say that if it does go through while you're, while you're sorting that out, then, um, that's on, that's more or less on the account holder at that point, because we did try to deal with it today. And the reference, I'll, I'll have to check about that, I'll look into it and, uh, someone could ring you back with it, probably.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well, uh, that's the second time you've told me it's on me if I check, and no, that isn't how it works. If a charge goes through, I dispute it with the bank, and the bank will want to know it was a card transaction, not me turning down a phone call. I won't be ringing anyone back on a number you give me, either. I'll use the one on my card. So, no, I won't be confirming anything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, sorry, I'm just, I'm only saying the hold is on the account right now, it's still pending, it's pending today, that's all I'm, that's all I'm trying to get across. And I did say someone would ring you back with the reference, I said that, I just don't have it in front of me, I'd have to check. So, uh, you're sure you don't want to just confirm the name, just the name, and then I can see what's, what I can... hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here, yes. Right, so, you said the hold's pending today, but earlier you told me the charge had already been held and it didn't go through, and that it'd lapse and clear as authorised. Which is it, pending or already held? And you also said you'd have to check whether you could even give me a reference, and now it's a thing someone will ring me back with. So no, I'm not giving you my name, not even just the name. I'll ring the number on my card. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi, sorry -- is that [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from the IT helpdesk at [COMPANY_A], and, um, I hope this isn't a bad moment. It's just a quick follow-up on the ticket you opened this morning, if that's alright...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... hello? Yeah, sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie-down, so I'm a bit -- what ticket? I don't think I opened a ticket. I mean, my laptop's been doing that thing where it goes really slow, but I thought that was just, you know, Tuesdays. Who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I've woken you -- that's completely my fault, I should have checked the time. It's [PERSON_2], from the IT helpdesk at [COMPANY_A]. Um, the ticket's number [ACCOUNT_REF], it was logged this morning about the laptop running slowly, and I think [PERSON_3] on your team escalated it up to us, so I'm only calling because it's flagged as something we ought to look at sooner rather than later, for your own protection really. Are you still there? Sorry, I just want to be sure I haven't lost you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I'm still, I'm here. It's just, I didn't, well [PERSON_3] might have, I mean she does sometimes do things without, no wait, that's not fair, she's actually quite good about telling me. Um. So the laptop thing, you're saying it's, what, flagged as urgent? For my protection? Protection from what, exactly? Sorry, I'm still sort of, my brain's not quite switched on yet.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a fair question, and I'm sorry, I made it sound more dramatic than it is. It's probably nothing serious. The slowness got picked up by our monitoring as the sort of pattern we like to look at early, in case it's, um, something that could spread, so we'd just like to have a look at the machine. And that would mean me connecting to your laptop remotely, just for a short while, while you watch, and I'd only do it with your say-so. Are you still there? Sorry, I keep checking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm here, you keep asking that. Connecting to it remotely, hm. Look, I'm not very good with that sort of thing, I never really know what I'm clicking on. And hang on, you said earlier it was something I opened this morning, but now you're saying your monitoring picked it up, so which is it? Did I ask for this or did your system just decide? Because I honestly don't remember opening anything, and I'd want to ask [PERSON_3] first anyway, if she's even in today.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, that's, uh, I should have been clearer, I'm sorry. The ticket came in through [PERSON_3], so it wasn't you who typed it up, and then the monitoring flag was, well, what made it urgent, so it's sort of both, which I realise makes it sound muddled. And honestly, asking her first is a perfectly sensible thing to do, I'd rather you did. If you'd feel better, I can put it back through the internal portal, so you can see it there, in your own name, and we can pick it up whenever you're comfortable. Are you still with me? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, still here. Okay, so, going back a bit, you said something about it spreading? Like the slowness could spread, to what, other people's computers? Because that's a bit different from just, my laptop's slow, isn't it? I mean if it's something that goes round the whole office, wouldn't someone have said something to everyone, or is it just me they're worried about? Sorry, I'm probably not making sense, I just, that's the bit that's stuck in my head.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're making perfect sense, that's a, sorry, hang on one second, someone's just put a delivery down on my desk -- okay, sorry, I'm back. Um, what was I, right, spreading. So, honestly, I used that word a bit loosely, and I'm sorry, because it made it sound bigger than I know it to be. I don't actually have the detail on whether anyone else's machine has flagged, or whether there's been a wider notice going round, I only have your ticket in front of me. And I don't want to guess and get it wrong. Would it be alright if I found out properly and rang you back? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm, no wait, you don't need to ring me, because actually I'd rather, I mean I'm going to ask [PERSON_3] myself, and if it's real I'll just put it through the portal like you said, myself, and then, I mean, you don't even have a, hang on, you rang me, so how do I know you're actually, no, I'm just going to, I'll check it with her. Is that, yeah. That's what I'll do. Thanks. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, really, that's the right thing to do, and I'm sorry for the muddle. Check with [PERSON_3] first, and if it's real, the portal will have the ticket under [ACCOUNT_REF], so you'll see it there in your own name. Sorry again for waking you. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah, no, that's, I'll do that. I'll go and find her, she's usually over by the window, or if she's not in I'll message her, and I'll look at the portal too, though I'll probably have to find the thing to log in first, because I never, it always wants a new password, which is a whole other business. And honestly it's probably just Tuesdays, like I said, it does this every week, or at least it feels like it does. Anyway. Thanks for not, you know, pushing. Okay. Bye now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? ... Sorry, one moment, there's someone at my door -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Right. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, and I'm calling about a refund that's been flagged against your name. It's a fairly sizeable amount, I'll say that, and I'd rather we dealt with it properly than leave it sitting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- uh, [colleague's name]? No, no, I'm fine, just put it on my desk, thanks. Sorry. Right, so, you're from the tax office, and there's a refund flagged against my name? A sizeable one? Uh, I wasn't expecting anything, to be honest. Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, and I appreciate you asking, it's exactly what I'd want you to do. [PERSON_2], compliance, at [COMPANY_A], the national tax office. Now, you said you weren't expecting anything, and that's quite common, these usually do come as a surprise... the amount I have in front of me is [AMOUNT_1], though I'd want to confirm that against your file before you rely on it. Before we go further, could you confirm your full name and date of birth for me, just so I know I've got the right [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, so [AMOUNT_1], right, that's -- yeah, that's not nothing. But, um, I mean, it's funny, I've honestly been sat here thinking about this because there was a story on the news not that long ago, about people getting calls like this, tax refunds out of the blue, and I'm not saying that's what this is, I'm really not, it's just, it's in my head now, you know? And I'm at work, I've got people sort of milling around, so I'm not keen on reading out my full name and date of birth over the phone to someone I can't, I mean, I don't actually know who you are yet. You said you'd got a file in front of you, so if you've got my file, surely you've got my name already? Like, what name have you got on it? And is there a reference number or something, or a number I could ring the tax office back on myself? Because I'd feel a lot better about that, honestly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a very sensible instinct, and I'd rather you were careful than not. Please, never feel you're being rude by asking. The file has a name on it, yes, but it's one of those cases where I confirm it with you rather than read it out, that's simply how we handle disclosure. The reference is... [ACCOUNT_REF], that's for the 2021 tax year, and, uh, the figure I gave you, [AMOUNT_2], yes. As for a number to ring back, I'd hold off on that for the moment, because the lines are very busy this time of year and I'd hate for this to lapse while you're waiting in a queue. If we could just confirm those details now, we can keep it moving.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, um, hang on, so, [AMOUNT_2]? Because a minute ago you said [AMOUNT_1], I'm sure of that, and now it's -- sorry, I'm probably, I don't know, I might've misheard, there's a bit of noise here. But, uh, so you're telling me you can't give me a number to ring back, because it'd lapse? That's, I mean, that's a bit, hmm. Because a refund doesn't just lapse in the time it takes me to ring the tax office, does it? And you've got a reference there, which, okay, but I can't check a reference with you, can I, it's your reference. So, uh, yeah, I think I'd rather look up the tax office number myself and ring them, if that's all right. Is that going to be a problem?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's not a problem, no, and I'd never discourage you from checking. I welcome it, genuinely... and on the figure, I think the noise has played tricks, I'd have said it the same way both times, though it may be worth my re-reading the file in case I've transposed something. Look, I'll say this much, a file in this state doesn't stay open indefinitely, and I can't promise what the position will be once you've rung round and come back to it. But by all means, do what you feel is right. I just wouldn't want you to lose it over a few days' delay.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, you're saying it might -- no, I mean, you said the figure was, you'd have said it the same way both times, but it wasn't, was it, it was two different amounts, I'm fairly sure of that. And, hmm, the thing about it not staying open, I mean, if it's a real refund then it, it doesn't just vanish because I rang the tax office first, surely? That's, that doesn't sound right to me. So, yeah, I'm going to look up the number myself and ring them, I think. If it's genuine, it'll be there when I do. Right, so, thanks for the call, and, uh, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well... that's your decision, of course. I did say it may not be as it stands. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- [colleague's name], yes, the blue folder, it's on the left, thanks. Sorry, right. So, uh, you're saying it may not be there, okay, but I'll take my chances, I think. If it's real, it'll keep. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yes. Well, I won't keep you. I'd only say, and I'm not putting it any more strongly than that, that these things do tend to close once they've been flagged for a while, and I'd hate you to... but no. You've made up your mind, and that's entirely your right. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, uh, no, I have, yeah, I've made up my mind, and I don't want to sound rude about it, I'm really not trying to be. It's just, you know, you gave me two different amounts, and you wouldn't give me a way to check you, and then it's a bit of, well, it might not be there if you wait, and that last bit, that's the bit that sits wrong with me, because a real refund doesn't, I mean, it doesn't tick down like that, does it? And I'm at work, I've got people about, I can't be doing this on the hoof anyway. So I'll look up the number myself and ring them, and if there's something there, there's something there. If not, well, I haven't lost anything, have I? So, uh, thanks, I suppose, for ringing, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, uh... I'd, I mean, I'm not sure that's quite how I'd put it, the, the amounts, I think we may be at cross purposes there, and I did try to... no. No, I won't argue it with you. I'll just, uh, I'll note on the file that you wanted to look into it yourself, and... well. I can't say what that does to the position, but that's what I'll do. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you'll, uh, no, I mean, you note down whatever you like, that's -- that's fine, but I'm not, I don't think it, hang on, what I mean is, I've said what I'm going to do, and that's ring the tax office myself on a number I've looked up. So, yeah. That's me done. Thanks, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Well, as I say, I did mention at the start that it was a fairly modest sum, so I wouldn't want you thinking I'd oversold it... but, uh, no, you've decided. I'll leave it there. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, modest? You said it was sizeable at the start, you said "fairly sizeable", I'm, no, I'm sure of that. So that's, that's yet another thing that doesn't add up, and I'm not, I'm not going to go round it again. I'm going to look up the number myself and ring the tax office. That's what I'm doing. I'll look it up myself and ring them. So, yeah, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, sorry to -- is this [PERSON_1]? Oh, good, I'm so sorry to catch you like this, it's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler at [COMPANY_A], the promotions agency, and I'm calling because, um, you've actually been selected as a winner in the regional draw, and I just wanted to make sure I reached you before the claim window closes today. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, sorry, I'm still here, I've just got a pan going, one second -- um. Sorry, what? A winner? Of what, exactly? I don't, I don't remember entering anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's completely fine, take your time, I'm, uh, I'm still here. So, it's the regional draw, the one run through [COMPANY_A], and honestly a lot of people don't remember entering, it's often through a sort of, um, a partner sign-up or a form somewhere, and I know that sounds odd, I do. The prize is [AMOUNT_1], and it's, well, I just want to make sure it's protected and goes to the right person, so I only need to confirm a few details with you before today's deadline. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm still here, sorry, I've just turned the heat down, it was starting to catch. Right, so, um, [AMOUNT_1]? That's, that's quite a lot, isn't it? I mean, I'm sorry, but I really don't remember filling in anything, and I do get a lot of bits through the door and emails and things, and I never really read them properly, so maybe, I don't know, maybe I did. But, um, what details? Because I'm not sure I like the sound of that, "confirm details", sorry. And you said the deadline's today? Why is it today? Sorry, what did you say the company was called again? I didn't catch it, I was stirring.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, don't apologise, you're quite right to ask, I'd -- sorry, it's [COMPANY_A], the promotions agency. And the deadline, it's, well, it's just that the claim window, um, it closes today, and after that the prize goes back into the pool, which I'd really hate to see happen to you, I'm only trying to protect your entry. It's just your full name and date of birth, and, uh, the bank details where you'd want it paid, so it goes to the right place and nobody else can claim it. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Bank details? Um, no, I don't, I don't think I want to give that out, not over the phone, not to someone I don't know. I mean, you rang me, I didn't ring you. And you've said it's the promotions agency, but you haven't really said which one, it's just a, a name, and I can't, I can't check it, can I? Sorry. Is there, I don't know, a number I can ring you back on, or a letter, something I can look at? Because if it's really mine, surely it'll still be mine tomorrow, won't it? Sorry, I've got something catching on the hob again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, that's -- hang on, sorry, someone's just come into the office, one moment. Right, I'm back, sorry about that. No, no, I do understand, truly, and I'm not trying to rush you, it's only that I'd hate for you to miss out, and the callback line is, um, it's busy at the moment, so it's, it'd be quicker if we just sorted the details now, just so everything's protected. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I've got the pan off now. Right. Um, sorry, can I go back a bit? You said before that the prize goes "back into the pool" if I don't claim today, but then you said you're protecting my entry, so which is it? And, sorry, what did you mean by "so nobody else can claim it"? How would anyone else claim it? I thought it was mine if I'd won. And the callback line being busy, that's, um, well that doesn't really help me, does it? I'd rather ring back later, honestly. Sorry, I just, I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, no, I've, I've muddled that, haven't I, I didn't mean it to sound -- it's not really about anyone else claiming it, it's more that, well, I said the deadline was today, but, um, I suppose it might be, I mean it could run to the end of the week, I'd have to check, and, sorry, I did say the line was busy, but it's not that it's always busy, it's just, um -- look, I only need the details so it's, so you're protected. Are you still there? [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Did you say I'm, I'm "projected"? Projected for what? No, sorry, I don't, hang on. You've changed it, haven't you? First it was today, now it's the end of the week, and the line's busy, and then it isn't. I'm sorry, I just, I'm not giving anybody my bank details on a call I didn't ask for. If it's really mine, I'll, I'll wait for a letter. Thank you, but no. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? I'm ringing from the office at [COMPANY_A], about the course place you applied for.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, who is this? I'm in a queue, I can't, uh -- what course? I haven't applied for anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm, uh, I'm not very good at these calls. I'm ringing on behalf of the admissions team at [COMPANY_A], the adult training place, and it was about a place on one of their courses, um, under your name, [PERSON_1]. If you didn't apply, then, well, maybe I've got the wrong person, I don't want to waste your time. It's just, I'd feel awful if somebody missed out on a place because of a mix-up on my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I didn't apply, so yeah, wrong person. Or, hang on, how'd you get this number? Where's it from, who gave it you? Because I've had this sort of thing before and I'm not, I'm not in the mood.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I understand, honestly. The number's just on the application they've got on file, that's all I was given, I don't know where it came from before that. And I'm not, um, I'm not trying to sell you anything, it's just a message I was asked to pass on. I'm ringing from the office switchboard, so it won't show a number, and, well, the line only goes out, so you can't ring it back. But I could email you the same details right now, if you'd rather read it than hear it from me. Or, actually, you don't have to take my word for it at all, [COMPANY_A] has a main number on their website, and you could ask for [PERSON_2] in admissions and check.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Uh, right, well -- no, don't email me anything, I'm not giving you an address, no. And hang on, no number showing and I can't ring you back? That's, I mean, that's convenient, isn't it? Look, I didn't apply, so there's nothing to check, is there? Just take me off your list, whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fair, I'm sorry, I won't send anything. And, uh, I didn't say email you, I mean, I did, but it doesn't matter, forget the email. It's just, I'm not on any list, I was only passed this one name this morning, or, no, yesterday, I think. I really don't mean it to sound convenient. It's just how the line is, I can't do anything about that. I'll let them know it's the wrong person, and you don't have to do anything at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, good, you do that. But I'll tell you, this morning, yesterday, I think, that's, that's not very convincing, is it? You don't even know when somebody gave you my name. And you rang me up, you used my name, you said you were from some office, and now it's I can't be rung back, and I've not applied for anything, and you're sorry, and you feel awful. I mean, who feels awful about a course place? I got stung once, properly stung, by somebody who was ever so polite and ever so sorry, so I'm not, uh, I'm not being rude, I'm just not buying it. If that office exists, fine, they can write to me, on paper, to the address they've supposedly got. Anyway, I'm nearly at the front here, so, yeah. Wrong person. Please don't ring again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, hang on, somebody's just dropped a whole stack of files right next to me, sorry. No, you're right, honestly. If they've got an address for you they can write, and that's, that's the better way anyway. I'm sorry about the muddle over yesterday and this morning, I'm just not good at this. I won't ring again. And I'm sorry you got stung before. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Fine. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say fine? Oh, right, sorry, I thought you said five, like five minutes, I was about to say I'll leave you to it. No, fine, that's, uh, that's fine. Thank you for not hanging up on me straight away. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? No, hang on, I'm at the till, she's, uh -- yes, card, thanks. Right. Whatever you thought I said, I said fine, as in fine, goodbye. Don't ring again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, yes, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the national tax office. I'm following up on a letter we sent you regarding a discrepancy in a filing, and, well, I'll just need a moment to, uh, pull the file up here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Security operations at the what? I'm in the middle of a queue here. And what letter? I didn't get any letter, I'd remember a letter from the tax office. Who is this, again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_2]. Security operations, [COMPANY_A], the national tax office. Look, I understand you're busy, but this is a routine follow-up, and I'd rather you hear it from me than ignore it, because a filing discrepancy that sits unanswered doesn't resolve itself, it goes on your record and it moves along to the next stage. Now, the letter went out by post, so it's entirely possible it's been misplaced, or it's sitting in a pile somewhere, that happens more often than you'd think. It carries a reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and I'd actually encourage you to find it and check that reference against what I tell you, rather than take my word for anything. If you can't find it, I can resend it today, or we can go through the discrepancy together on this call. Either way, there's no deadline today. I'm not asking you for money, and I'm not going to ask you to do anything on this call that you'd be uncomfortable doing. I'd just like it dealt with properly, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you still haven't told me who you are. Security operations. At the tax office. Since when does the tax office have security operations ringing people up? I've heard this one before, mate, and I didn't like it then either. If there's a letter, send me the letter. I'm not going through anything on the phone in a supermarket queue. What's the number I ring you back on, and don't say this one.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Fine. That's, uh, that's a fair thing to ask, and I'll answer it properly. [PERSON_2], security operations, [COMPANY_A]. Yes, we do have a security operations function. It deals with filing integrity and flagged discrepancies, and it does ring people, not often, which is exactly why it catches people off guard. I'm aware how that sounds, believe me, I get this reaction a good deal, and frankly you're right to have it. A lot of people have been burned by calls like this one. So here's what you do. Don't ring back on any number I give you off the cuff. Look up the published number for [COMPANY_A] yourself, the one on the website at [URL_1], or on any letter, statement or form you've ever had from us, and ring that. If you'd rather have my number to cross-check against it, it's [PHONE_1], but I'd put the published one first. Ask for security operations, give them my name, they'll put you through to me or confirm I'm who I say I am. And the letter, yes, I'll have it resent to your address on file, today. You don't need to do a thing on this call. You can deal with the entire matter by post, start to finish, if that's what you prefer, and honestly, in a supermarket queue, I'd prefer

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I heard enough. Look, that's the first sensible thing you've said, ring the published number myself, so that's what I'll do. Not now, I'm at the till. And if there's a letter, it'll turn up and I'll deal with it by post. Don't ring me again about it. Right, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, uh, that's exactly the right call, ring the published number, and the letter will go out in the post today, quote the reference on it when you -- no, hang on, one thing, sorry, before you go, because it would save you a second call. When you ring, they'll ask you to confirm the address the letter was sent to, so have the one on your last return in mind. That's all. I won't ring you again, you have my word. Good luck with the till.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. I'll have it in mind, fine. Doesn't mean I'm saying it to you, though. I'm not reading out an address down a phone in a queue, so don't think that's what that was. I ring the published number, they can ask me whatever they like. Right, I'm at the till. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, understood, and I wasn't asking you to, I'd rather you didn't. Say nothing to me. Uh, one thing though, I said earlier it was a letter we sent you, but strictly it's a notice, the letter's just the cover for it, so if you're ringing the published number, ask about the notice, and the reference on it is the thing to quote. Right, I'll leave you to your till. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Notice, letter, whatever. Hang on -- no, I've got my own bags, thanks, ta. Right. Letter, notice, I don't care what you call it, I'm ringing the published number and asking them, not you. And you said goodbye twice already, so go on, go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you've got your own bags? No, I haven't asked you to bring anything, not a bag, not a document, nothing. Uh, that's, that's not a thing I've said. Hang on, I think the line's cut out on me a bit there. Anyway, you ring the published number and ask them, and if they can't find any notice against your name, then you've lost nothing and neither have I. Right. Goodbye, and thank you for your patience.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, the bags was the lad at the till, not you, I wasn't -- look, I don't care. I'm done. If there's a notice, it'll turn up in the post, and I'm not doing anything else off the back of a phone call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A]. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? Right, I'll be brief, I'm calling about your monthly donation, which, uh, lapsed on our records a while back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, I just woke up from a -- what was that first bit? Security operations? Is that, like, a charity thing, or... I'm not sure I follow. And I don't really remember setting up a monthly donation, I mean, I might have, my daughter does a lot of that stuff on the computer. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. The charity. Security operations is just the department I sit in, it's, uh -- hold on, sorry, somebody's dropped a stack of folders out here, give me a second. Right. Yes, so, I know the title sounds more alarming than the call actually is. Nothing's wrong with anything of yours. Our records show a monthly gift under your name that stopped a while back, and I'm calling to thank you for it and ask if you'd want to start it up again. That's all it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, so a thank you call. But -- sorry, I keep going round this -- I don't remember giving to, uh, [COMPANY_A], I really don't. Like I said, my daughter does a lot of the computer things, so it might've been her, I mean, I honestly don't know. And I still don't get why it's the security people ringing me about a donation. That's the bit that's got me. Why wouldn't it be, I don't know, the fundraising people or whoever?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and honestly, you're right to ask it. The fundraising team's stretched thin, so the supporter lines get shared out, and, uh, I've been on this list for a few weeks. It's not usual, I'll give you that. As for the gift, I can only tell you what's on my screen, and that's a monthly donation under your name that stopped. If it was your daughter who set it up, that'd explain why you don't remember it. I'm not asking you for anything today, nothing at all. If you'd rather not go any further, just say so and I'll take you off our calling list, no fuss.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah, I think I'd rather just ask my daughter first, if that's alright. She'd know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's sensible, you check with her first. And, uh, I'll take you off the calling list as well, so you won't hear from us again unless you get in touch yourself. Sorry, one correction, I said earlier I'd been on this list a few weeks, but it's more like a couple of days, I only picked up the supporter calls this week. Anyway, if your daughter does recognise it and wants to sort it out, she can reach the supporter line directly. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_2], and have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, okay, I'll ask her, like I said. I'll have a word with my daughter first, she'd know, she does all that. Thanks for ringing, I suppose, and sorry, I'm a bit muddled, I only just woke up. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no need to be sorry. And, uh, sorry, did you say you'd be back in touch with the supporter line yourself? No -- right, that was you saying you'd ask your daughter, I misheard. Fine. That's all sorted either way, you're off the list. Take care of yourself, [PERSON_2], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yes, thank you. Though, uh, you said earlier it was a few weeks you'd had me on your list and then it was a couple of days, so I don't know, one of those. Anyway, daughter first. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that, uh -- no, that's fair, I did say two different things. It's -- I mean, it was a couple of days that I've had the calls, and the list itself has been around a few weeks, and I ran the two together. My mistake, not yours. You've noticed it, so good. Ask your daughter, and if it isn't anything she recognises, you can just leave it. Goodbye, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, right, yes, fine, if she doesn't know it I'll just leave it. Oh -- sorry, hang on, there's the kettle going, I put it on before I dozed off, I'd forgotten all about it. Where was I? Yes. Daughter first, then leave it if it's nothing. Alright, goodbye then, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, well, no, go and see to your kettle, that's the main thing. Um, and, uh, daughter first, then leave it if it's nothing, that's exactly right, and you won't hear from us again either way. Thanks for putting up with the call, [PERSON_2]. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, uh... yes. Right. Thanks, then. I'll, um, go and see to that kettle. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Go on, the kettle. And, uh, just so it's said once more, you're off the list, so no more calls from us, and nothing needed from you today, nothing at all. If your daughter recognises the donation, she knows where to find us, and if she doesn't, just leave it. Thanks again, [PERSON_2], and sorry for catching you half asleep. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, that's alright. Oh, hang on, the cat's gone and knocked something off the sideboard again, honestly, every time I sit down. Sorry, what was I saying? Right, yes, nothing needed, daughter first, leave it if she doesn't know. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], collections on vehicle warranty accounts. I'm showing the coverage on your file lapsing, uh, and the renewal has to be confirmed today. Sorry, before I go further, can you just confirm for me whether you're still the registered keeper on the vehicle? I want to be sure I'm reading the right record.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, who? Collections? I haven't got a warranty with anyone, I'm stood in a queue at the shop. And no, I'm not confirming a thing to you, you rang me. What company did you say again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], vehicle warranty. And I understand you're in a queue, but the file shows a, uh, a renewal pending at [AMOUNT_1], and when you say you haven't got a warranty, that's not what I'm reading. Coverage lapses at close of business, so it's a today matter. I'll note the objection on the file, but I do need to know whether you want it renewed or whether we let it go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh, let it go, then. I told you, I haven't got one, so there's nothing to renew. And "note the objection," what's that supposed to mean? Look, you still haven't told me how I'm meant to know you are who you say you are, so, um, no. I'm not doing this in a supermarket queue.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, I'll note that you've declined. Just so you're aware, once it lapses today, any repair costs on the vehicle are yours, so that's settled on our side. If you want to verify, I can have someone ring you back. It's an internal line here, so I couldn't say when, but you'd get a call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, no, don't ring me back, I don't want a call from anyone. And hang on, you said it was a collections thing at the start, now it's a renewal, now it's me paying for repairs. Which is it? Doesn't matter, I'm not interested, I'm hanging up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Collections is the department, the renewal is the matter, the repairs are the consequence. I'll note that on the file. If you change your mind before close of business, you'd want to -- Right. I'm going to leave it there. Have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, whatever, I won't be changing my mind. Oh, for -- no, hang on, mate, I'm in the queue, there's a till free, I'm coming! Sorry, not you. Anyway, don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, two turns ago, you said there was nothing to renew. Just so I record it correctly, is that because you've never held a warranty, or because you cancelled one with [COMPANY_B]? Because the file says -- hang on, it's not showing which. If you could just tell me which vehicle you mean, I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Not telling you anything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, noted. Just so the file's accurate, you said earlier you'd never had a warranty, but, uh, then it was [COMPANY_B] you'd cancelled, and the system's showing the vehicle registered in [CITY_1], which, I mean, isn't what you told me -- no, sorry, that's not right either. Look, I can't pull the keeper details up without you, so that's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. I never said anything about cancelling with anyone, and I never said a city either. You came up with that. And two turns back you said it was a today matter and the file showed a renewal, now you can't even pull it up? Make your mind up. That's it, I'm done, don't ring me again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Yes, hello -- uh, right, good, I've got someone. This is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, we handle estates. I'm going to need to confirm I've reached the right person before I say anything further, so, uh, could you state your full name for me, please?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- [muffled] no, put that down, please. Uh, right. You've phoned me, so, why do you need my name before you tell me anything? Who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and I'll answer it, but I did say it, so, uh, once more: [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], solicitor's office, estates. I work in the security side of the firm, we're very careful about who we speak to, that's all that is. It concerns an estate where you may be named, may, I can't say more until I know I've got the right person, so, name, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'm not -- sorry, that's backwards, isn't it? You ring me, and I'm the one who has to prove who I am? If I'm named in something, then surely you've got a name already, so, what name have you got written down there?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Written down, yes, I've got a name, and no, I'm not reading it out to a stranger, that's the whole point of -- sorry, did you say you want to reverse the charges? No, no, nothing like that, there's no charge to you, none at all. Look, I'm only asking you to confirm your name and the address we'd have on file, because the formal letter will carry those same details, and, uh, I'd ask you to keep this between us until it arrives.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, I never said anything about reversing charges, so, where did that come from? And you said before that you needed my name first, now it's name and address, and keep it quiet until a letter turns up? If there's a formal letter coming, why not just wait for the letter? Sorry, I've got a little one here, so I'm only half -- what's the firm called again, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, you didn't, that was -- I was, uh, thinking of another call, I've had a few this morning. My mistake, strike it. [COMPANY_A] is the name, solicitor's office, [CITY_1], and look, you're quite right, if the letter's coming, then, well -- actually, here's what I'd suggest. Don't take my word for it. Look the firm up yourself, in a directory, not from anything I give you, find the main number, and ring us back. And I won't ask for anything beyond your name and address, nothing about money, no fees, no bank details. Not today, not ever.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. [muffled] No, sweetheart, not the -- put the lid back on, please. Sorry. Right. So, "not today, not ever" -- that's a funny thing to promise on a first call, isn't it? Why would you say that? And the look-it-up bit, that's, well, that's what I'd do anyway, so I'll do it. But I'm not giving you a name or an address now, whatever I find. If there's a letter, I'll wait for the letter.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, because people hear estate and they think -- right, yes, that's exactly why I said it, so you'd -- no, listen, that's sensible, that's absolutely what I'd want you to do, look us up and -- Sorry, go on, you were saying. No, you've said it. Fine. You don't give me anything today, that's your right, I'm not going to push you on it. When the letter arrives it will have the firm's name, the address, the reference, all of it, and you can check it all against the directory. The only thing I'd ask, and I do mean ask, is that you keep it to yourself until then, estates can get, uh, awkward, with families. You've got your hands full, I can hear that. Is there a better time for me to ring you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, there isn't a better time. I'm not giving you a name or an address today, I said that, so there's nothing for you to ring about. If there's a letter, I'll wait for the letter. And the keeping it to myself bit, why would I? If it's all above board, why shouldn't I mention it to anyone? Sorry, [muffled] no, I'm on the phone, give me a minute, love. Right. I'm going to look the firm up and I'll ring them if I want to, so, yeah, I'm finishing this now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's fine, that's your right. Look the firm up, ring the main number if you like. And on the keeping it to yourself, you're not bound by it, it was only a request, mention it to whoever you want. I won't ring again, uh, you'll have the letter in due course. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. [muffled] No, not the sofa, we don't -- sorry, hang on. Right. Okay. Well, I'll see if a letter turns up, and I'll look the firm up myself like I said. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, yes, that's all in order then. The letter will, um, it'll come in the post, and the firm's easy enough to find, [COMPANY_A] in [CITY_1]. Sorry, I'm, uh, still here, I just -- yes. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one thing before you go. Two turns back you said that thing about reversing the charges, and then it was another call you were thinking of. What call was that, exactly? And the "security side of the firm", what's that when it's at home? Never mind, I'm done, I'll look you up. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Which call, uh -- it was just a call, one of several this morning, nothing to do with you, I misspoke, that's all it was. And the security side, it's just, it's the part of the firm that checks we're speaking to the right person, the right person, before anything's said. I did misspeak, I said so. Look, you're right to look us up, [COMPANY_A], [CITY_1], find the main number yourself and ring them. That's all I'd ask. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah, I've got it, you misspoke, and I'm -- no, stop, I've heard enough. I'm looking the firm up myself and that's all I'm doing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hello there, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the tenancy deposit protection scheme. How are you doing today, not caught you in the middle of your tea or anything, have I?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, the what scheme? Tea, no, no, I'm at my desk at work, I've got people sort of around me. And you said it's about a, a tenant deposit, was it? I don't, I'm not a landlord, so I'm not sure what you'd want with me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, right, sorry, that's on me, I jumped straight in. We hold deposits for people renting, and your name's down as a tenant on a property in [CITY_1] where there's a dispute open. Nothing for you to do today, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A dispute open, on a property in [CITY_1]? Hang on, I, I'm not sure which property you mean. I mean, I've rented a couple of places over the years. And you said nothing for me to do today, but then why are you ringing me? Sorry, can you tell me again who you're with? I didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, fair question, and don't apologise, I'd be asking the same. It's [COMPANY_A], we're a tenancy deposit protection scheme, and I'm [PERSON_2] in customer care. The reason I'm ringing rather than just writing is, well, I'm actually sending you the same thing in writing today as well, so you'll have it all on paper. It's about the deposit at the [CITY_1] property you shared with the other tenants, and the thing I wanted to ask is that you keep the details of the dispute to yourself for now, not mention it to the others in the house, just until both sides have been formally notified. That's all it is, it's a fairness rule on our end, so nobody gets a head start.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, hang on, you're ringing me about a deposit dispute, but you can't say which property, and you want me not to tell the other people in the house? Uh, I never said I shared that place, did I? I said I'd rented a couple of places. And earlier you said nothing for me to do today, but now there's something I'm supposed to do, which is keep quiet. That's, I mean, that's a bit odd. How would I check you are who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're right, that's a fair catch, and I'm not going to wriggle round it, the confidentiality's a procedural rule, it's so neither side is influenced before they've both been notified, and that's all it's -- sorry, go on, you were saying how you'd check, and honestly, please do. I'll give you the case reference, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], and you can look it up on our official site, [URL_1], or find our number yourself and ring us back. Nothing's lost by hanging up, I promise. And look, if you don't want to keep it quiet, I can't stop you, but I'd rather you saw it in writing first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you'll give me a case reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and I look you up myself, or ring back on a number I find myself. Okay, that, that does sound fair, I'll give you that. But hang on, a minute ago you said it's a fairness rule so nobody gets a head start, and now you're saying I can't be stopped from telling people if I want to? Which is it? And you said you're sending something in writing today, but earlier you said you were ringing because it was easier than writing. Uh, no, sorry, I think that's wrong, you said you were ringing rather than just writing. I'm not sure it adds up, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you've got me, that came out muddled, and I did say it two different ways. It's a request, not a legal gag, so you're free to tell whoever you like, I'd just ask you not to until both sides have been notified. And the letter's going out regardless, it's not instead of the call, I rang as a courtesy so it didn't land cold. But you know what, I did get the property wrong earlier, I said "you shared with the other tenants" and I don't actually know that, so forget I said it. Honestly, the best thing is you look us up yourself on [URL_1], find the number on there, and ring back quoting [ACCOUNT_REF]. I'm not offended in the slightest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so let me get this straight. It's a request, not a rule, I can tell who I like, and the letter's coming either way. And you're taking back the bit about the other tenants. Right. Well, I appreciate you saying that, but honestly, it's still a lot of wobbling for one call, and you still haven't told me which property this is. So no, I'm going to do what you said. I'll look up the scheme myself, find a number on my own, and ring them if I think there's anything to ring about. And if a letter turns up, fine, I'll read it then. Thanks for the call, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yes, that's exactly right, and honestly, good for you. Find the number yourself, don't use anything I've given you, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF] if you do ring. If the letter turns up and none of it rings true, bin it, no harm done. Sorry about the wobbling, that's on me, not you. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say bring the letter in? Because, no, I'm not bringing anything in anywhere. Hang on, no, bin it, you said bin it. Right. Yeah, okay, I'll sort it my own way. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, nothing to bring in anywhere, you've got it right, I did say bin it, if it doesn't ring true to you. Sort it your own way, that's absolutely the right call. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, before you go, one thing from a minute ago, I said bin the letter if it doesn't ring true, and I don't want that coming across wrong. If it does look right to you once you've checked us out, please do read it properly, because there are dates in it that matter. That's all I meant. Right, bye now, [PERSON_1], and thanks for being so careful with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, two turns ago, you said the bit about the other tenants, and you said forget it. But I'm still not sure what that was about. Did you actually have the names of the people in the house, or was that just a guess? And dates that matter, dates for what, exactly? You keep adding things on the end.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough, you're right, I do keep tacking things on. The other tenants bit was a guess, a bad one, I don't have names in front of me and I shouldn't have put it to you like I did. As for the dates, there'll be a response window set out in the letter, and that's the lot, but you're better off reading that in the letter than taking my word for it. I'll stop adding bits now. Look us up yourself, ring on a number you find, and I'm quite happy for you to do just that. Bye now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. So the tenants thing was a guess, you've got no names, and the dates are in the letter, if there is a letter. Right. I think that's enough for me for one call, honestly. If something turns up in the post I'll deal with it then, and I'll look up the scheme myself first. Bye now.

utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? I'd just want to make sure I have the right address first, and, I mean, there are a couple of things on the application that ought to be dealt with fairly soon, so, uh, I'd rather not leave it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a couple of things on the application that ought to be dealt with fairly soon? Hang on, did you say a *course* place, or a *cost* place? Because I don't remember paying for anything. And uh, which company was that again, I didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Course, c-o-u-r-s-e, a course place. Not a cost, no, nobody's asking you to pay anything on this call, and I'd be rather concerned if you'd thought that. utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, I mean, that's a fair thing to ask, and, well, you'd be right to expect me to have it to hand. Um, and I'd say that if, once you've seen it, it doesn't ring a bell at all, that's worth knowing too, and you should tell [PERSON_3] in admissions when you ring the main number, because then we'd want to look at how your details came to be on our system. Now, I haven't gone on about it, but the sooner that's sorted, the easier it is all round. So, uh, may I take the email address you'd like it sent to?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no. You're a compliance officer reading a record, and you can't tell me the course title or the date. I'm not giving you an email address. If I've got an application on file, I'll ring the main number myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, and I'd rather you did it that way, honestly. Uh, before you go, one thing, just so there's no confusion. Earlier you asked whether I'd said a course place or a cost place, and I answered the word but not the real worry, which was whether anyone's asking you for money. They aren't. Nothing's owed, nothing's being asked of you on this call. So, ring the published number at [URL_1], ask for [PERSON_3] in admissions, and if there's no application under your name, that's an answer in itself. I won't send anything to you, since you haven't given me an address. Right, thank you for your time, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. I'll look it up myself, if I look it up at all. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, one moment, someone's just come in behind me -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Yes, of course, that's entirely your decision, and I'd say, if you do look it up, the number's on the website at [URL_1], under contact, nothing to dial back to me. And if there's no application in your name, then, well, no harm done, and you've lost nothing by checking. Right. Thank you for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll -- look, if there's an application, it'll be on file, and if there isn't, well -- no. I'm not doing any of it on your say-so, that's all. Goodbye.

utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the fraud team at [COMPANY_A]. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_1], fraud team, [COMPANY_A]. And yes, [AMOUNT_1], that's what's on my screen. Merchant shows as [COMPANY_B], attempted from a device in [CITY_1], so if that isn't you, it's exactly why I'm calling. When you're back, I'll need to confirm your full name and date of birth against the account before I can release any more detail.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? A device in, did you say [CITY_1]? No, no, I haven't been anywhere, I'm in my kitchen. And the, the merchant, did you say it was a... a bakery? Sorry, I just, I don't know who you are properly. How do I know it's really the bank?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I didn't say a bakery, I said the merchant shows as [COMPANY_B], so I can't tell you what they sell. And I said ten minutes ago, well, call it twenty, so it's actually only just come through, about five minutes back, if that. Anyway, I understand the concern, I'll note on the file that you've queried my identity. It doesn't change the position, though: the hold is still live and the charge releases if it isn't confirmed as fraudulent. So, [PERSON_2], if I could have your full name and date of birth to verify the account, that's the next step.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? You said something about a file, did you say you'd put me on a, a fine? Oh no, I haven't done anything, I've never had a fine in my life. No, hang on, the, the hold, you said the hold. Right. But you've just said different things, haven't you? Twenty minutes, then five minutes, I don't know. I'm getting muddled. And you still haven't said how I can check you're really the bank. Can't I just ring them myself? The number's on the back of my card, I think. Let me go and find it, my bag's just through there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not a fine, a file. I'm noting your query on the account record, that's all, you haven't done anything wrong. As for the times, that's the system timestamp against the hold, I wouldn't read anything into it. Now, you can ring the number on your card, that's your call, but I'd advise against waiting, because once the hold lapses the charge posts and recovering it afterwards takes weeks, if it can be done at all. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, sorry, a file, not a fine. Okay. But, um, you said they wouldn't have the case in front of them? If it's really on my account, then surely they would, wouldn't they? That's what the bank's for. And you said ring the number on the card, so I'm going to ring the number on the card. I'm going to go and get my bag and ring the number on the back of my card. Yes. So, um, don't ring me back, please, because I'll be, I'll be on the phone to them. Thank you for, for letting me know, I suppose. Right. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that's your decision, I can't stop you. I'll note it on the file that you declined to verify. Just so you know, I'll still be trying you again later, because the case stays open on my side until it's closed out. Mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Declined to verify? I didn't, I mean I haven't declined anything, I've just said I'm going to ring the bank myself, that's all. That's not the same thing, is it? And you said you'd try me again, but I did say please don't, because if it's a real thing on my account then the proper people will tell me when I ring, won't they? And if it isn't, well, then there's nothing for you to close, is there? Oh, I'm flustered now, I've got pasta going and my bag's through there and I just want to do it properly. My daughter always says if somebody rings you out of the blue, you ring them back on the number you already have, not the one they give you. I think that's what she says. So that's what I'm doing. Right. Thank you. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Declined, queried, it's the same entry on my side, I'm only noting what's been said. Your daughter's advice is fine as a general rule. This is a live case though, so the file stays open and I'll ring back later to finish it off. That's all I have for now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, but -- sorry, I'm going, I'm going to ring the bank, and I'd rather you didn't ring back, thank you. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, I'll leave it on the file. The case is still open at this end, so I'll ring back later to finish it off. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? No, I said I'd rather you didn't ring back. I'm going to ring the bank, the number on the card, and that's, that's all I'm doing. So please don't ring back. Right, I've got to see to my pasta now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, um, is this -- sorry, am I speaking to [PERSON_1]? It's, uh, my name's [PERSON_2], and I'm ringing on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the pension people. I'm not, I mean, I don't actually work there myself, I'm just passing something on for them, and it's about, well, a change to your plan that they need to talk through with you first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, that's me. Pension, did you say? Sorry, I'm a bit slow today, who is it you're ringing for again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you're not slow, it's me, I'm -- sorry. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, hang on a minute. You're not from the pension, you're ringing for someone who is, and they're not your colleague exactly? I'm not sure I follow, dear. And it's funny, I was only thinking this morning I ought to sort out all my papers, they're in a shoebox somewhere, my late husband always did all that. Anyway, it's a bit odd to be asked my date of birth by someone I don't know, isn't it? Why can't the person at the pension ring me themselves? I wouldn't mind a chat with them.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're right, it is odd, I -- sorry, I shouldn't have asked you for that, not like that. I'm just, I only meant -- it was only ever to help, I didn't want to, I mean I'd feel dreadful if you thought I was, um, well. Look, I won't ask you anything else. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's, I mean, that's very kind of you to say, and no, I don't think you're, I wasn't thinking you were -- well, I didn't quite know what to think, to be honest.
