Or I could ring them myself, you're right, the number's on the statements somewhere, in the shoebox probably, with my husband's old, oh, never mind, I'll find it. Thank you for not pushing, dear, it's nice of you. Is that, um, is that all you needed then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's all. Sorry again for the bother, and I hope the shoebox turns it up. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, no bother at all, dear, it's been nice having a chat. I'll have a look for that number, in the shoebox, like I said, and I'll ring them myself. Yes, the shoebox. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, a, a shovel? No, sorry, shoebox, yes, I heard you right, I just -- it's the line, it's a bit crackly here. Anyway, yes, do ring them yourself, that's the best thing. Bye now, [PERSON_1], mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a mind? No, no, I haven't lost my mind yet, dear, not quite, ha! Though I do put things down and forget where, that's the shoebox again. Anyway, you mind how you go too, and thank you for ringing, it's been lovely. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is the collections desk at [COMPANY_A], the public library. I'm calling for [PERSON_1], about a book you reserved last week. Hello? Yeah, the reserved book has arrived, it's at the front desk now, and we'll hold it for ten days.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on -- hang on, the pan's spitting. Sorry. Library, you said? A book I reserved? Um, I did put one in last week, I think. Sorry, who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No worries, take your time. It's [PERSON_2], collections desk at [COMPANY_A], the public library. Uh, like I said, the book's come in and it's on the hold shelf at the front desk, and it'll sit there for a fortnight -- sorry, ten days, ten days, I misspoke. That's all it is, there's nothing you need to do on this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Oh, right, okay. So it's just -- it's come in. Ten days. Sorry, I'm just turning this down, one second. Which book was it? Only I can't quite remember what I put in for. Was it the, um, the gardening one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Let me pull it up. Uh, I've got the reservation here on the screen, placed last week under your name. The title on it is [BOOK_1]. I don't have a subject listed, just the title and the author, so I can't tell you whether that's the gardening one. If it doesn't ring a bell, the staff at the front desk can check it against your reservation when you come in. Either way it's held for ten days, and after that it goes back on the shelf for the next person.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right. Hm, [BOOK_1]. Sorry, what? No, it doesn't ring a bell, not really. But I put in a few things, so, I mean, it might be. I don't know. Okay, so I just go in and, what, ask at the front desk? And they'll sort it out? I don't have to bring anything, do I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, so, you just ask at the front desk and they'll find it under your name. Bring your library card if you've got it with you, but if you don't, they can look you up. Um, nothing else. No payment, nothing like that, it's just a reserved item. And, uh, if you'd rather check it's genuine first, that's fine, the main library number's on the website.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, that's fine then. Library card, yes, I think it's in my purse somewhere. Sorry, you said a fortnight, didn't you, at first? Two weeks? And then ten days. So which is it? Not that it matters much, I'm only asking because I'm away on, um, the weekend after next, so I'd want to know. And you said the website, but I don't really do the website. Sorry, what was it you said your name was?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ten days, it's ten days, that's what's on the screen, the fortnight was me misspeaking. And the name's [PERSON_2], collections desk, [COMPANY_A] -- so if you're away the weekend after next, I'd just get in before that, it'd still be -- sorry, go on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, ten days, okay. So before the weekend, then, yes, I can do that. Oh -- sorry, hang on, that's the smoke thing, no, it's fine, it's only the onions catching. Sorry. Where was I? Yes. Front desk, library card, ten days. That's all, is it? You didn't want anything else off me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's all, nothing else needed from you. And if you'd feel better ringing the library yourself first, look the number up your own way and call the main desk, that's perfectly fine by me. Just ask for the collections desk or the front desk and they'll confirm the hold is there. I'll note on the file that you may call in, so no one's surprised. Anyway, that's everything from my end, so, uh, enjoy your dinner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, lovely, thank you. Right, so I'll pop in tomorrow, then, or, um, no, Thursday, I'm out tomorrow. And I'll bring the card, and I won't need to pay anything, you said it was two pounds or something -- no, sorry, you said no payment. Sorry, I'm getting muddled, it's the onions. Anyway, it's the gardening one, I think, whatever it's called. Right. Thank you, [PERSON_2]. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, hello, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor here, and um, I'm following up on a letter we sent you, about a, a discrepancy in a filing. Hello? Can you hear me okay? It's [COMPANY_A], about the letter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you, sorry, I was just -- hang on, the dog's got something in his mouth, that he shouldn't. Okay, no, it's fine. Right. So which letter is this? I don't remember getting anything from a tax office, and you said a discrepancy in a filing, what filing, which year?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, so, the letter would've gone out, uh, a few weeks ago, I think, and it's about, hang on, let me just pull it up -- it's your return for, um, the most recent filing year, I believe, but I'd have to -- Sorry, to be honest I don't want to guess at the year and get it wrong. The letter has a reference on it, [ACCOUNT_REF], so if you've got it somewhere you can check it against that, or I can just send you another copy, no problem at all. Or if it's easier, I can talk you through it now, whichever you'd rather, there's no rush on this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I don't actually, I mean, I haven't got a letter in front of me, and, no, wait, let me start again. You're the one who rang me about it, so I'd have thought you'd know which year. That's sort of the first thing on the file, isn't it? And, uh, you said you'd send another copy, to where? Because what address have you got for me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair, you'd think I'd have the year, I do, it's, uh, it's on the file, I just, I've got a few screens open and I'm not looking at the right one. Sorry. So the address, um, that's the part I'd need you to confirm, actually, so if you could just give me the address you've got for yourself, and your date of birth, I can match it against the file and then, uh, then I'd know where to send it. And like I said, the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], if that helps, it's on the letter, and there's really no rush, I can resend it, or we can go through it now, whichever you'd rather.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, my date of birth and, what was that, the address you've got for me? No, hang on, you said you've got it on file. Hm. So you want me to tell you the address, and that's how you'd know where to send the letter? That's, I mean, that's sort of backwards. If you've got my file open you'd just read it out to me, and I'd say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, you're right, that is backwards, sorry. I'm, uh, I'm still fairly new on this, I should've read it out to you, I'll have to check the file for that. Look, you don't need to give me anything on this call. Honestly. If you'd rather, I can just post the letter out again, or you can ring [COMPANY_A] back on the number that's published on the website, [URL_1], and ask for the claims team, and just quote the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF]. That's, that's probably cleaner anyway. And, like I said, there's no rush on it, none at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, okay. That's, uh, a fairly sensible thing to say, I'll give you that. Calling back on the published number is what I'd do anyway. But I'd also have to say it's a bit odd. You rang me about a discrepancy, you don't know the year, you don't have my address, and now you're telling me not to bother with the call. So what's the discrepancy, actually? Give me one concrete thing from the file. Not the year, I'll let you off that. Just what's supposedly wrong with it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so the, uh, hang on, someone's just put a trolley down right behind me, sorry, it's a bit of a, one second. Right. So the actual discrepancy, I'd, uh, I'd have to check the notes, because I've only got the summary open and it just says, it says something about a mismatch, between what was declared and what we've got from, um, a third party, but not what the, the actual figure is. I'm sorry, I know that's not what you want to hear. I'd rather not guess and be wrong about it. If you like, I can ring you back when I've got the right screen up, or you can ring us, whichever suits you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, the dog's dragging something across the floor again. Oh, it's a sock. Fine. Right. Where were we? Mismatch with a third party, no figure, no year, no address. So that's, uh, that's not much of a file. I'm not going to wait for a ring back either. I'll look up the number myself, on the actual website, not the one you read out, and if there's a letter it'll be on my record. Thanks for your time, I suppose. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, yes, that's fine, honestly. Look it up yourself, that's, I mean, that's what I'd do. And if it's easier, if you'd rather I -- no, sorry, let me put that differently. I can do the letter again by post, so it's all in writing, and then you can ring us when it suits you, whenever's better, there's no deadline on this. Or if you'd like me to try you at a better time, just say when, and, and I'll, uh, I'll make a note of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't ring me, and don't bother with the post. I'll sort it myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant over here, and I'm just reaching out because we've got one position left in the fund that's closing today, so I wanted to get you booked in with an advisor before the window shuts. Sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm just calling about the position that's closing today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, a position in a fund? Closing today? I'm at work, I -- who did you say you're calling from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [COMPANY_A], we're an investment firm, I'm the scheduling assistant, so I'm not the one who'd go through the fund itself, that's the advisor, I just get you the slot. And it's not so much a position you'd have asked about, it's more that you were on a list from your enquiry last spring, uh, well, not an enquiry exactly, more like a general interest list. Anyway it closes at five today so I've got the advisor free in about ten minutes, so I just need to confirm you're [PERSON_1] and we can lock that in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, wait, a general interest list from last spring. You said enquiry, then not an enquiry, so which is it? I don't remember signing up for anything like that. And an advisor in ten minutes, today, closing at five -- I mean, I'm at my desk, I can't just. Who gave you my number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, it's just a list we work from, I don't have the source in front of me. Like I said, the window shuts at five and the advisor's free in ten, so can I just confirm you're [PERSON_1] and get you in?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you don't know where you got my number, but you want me to confirm my name so you can book me in for something that closes at five. Yeah, no, I'm not confirming anything until I know who you actually are. Is there a website or a main number I can look up for [COMPANY_A] and call you back on? Because honestly this is sounding a bit off to me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I totally get that, it's a fair thing to ask, and honestly most people do ask, but the thing is the advisor's slot is only held for a few minutes and if I have to release it, it goes to the next person on the list, and the position goes with it, so, uh, it'd really be easier if we just got you confirmed now and then everything else, the website, the numbers, all of that, the advisor can walk you through on the call, because I'm only scheduling, I don't have the compliance side in front of me and I wouldn't want to give you the wrong thing. And I mean, I could give you my direct line, it's [PHONE_1], but that just comes back to me and I'm about to be in back-to-back bookings, so you'd probably end up in voicemail, which is why I'm calling now rather than leaving it. So if I can just get a quick yes that you're [PERSON_1], I can hold the slot and we're, we're good, so is that you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so let me get this straight. You can't tell me where you got my number, you can't point me to a website, and the only way I can check you out is a line that goes to voicemail. Yeah, that's not a yes from me. If the slot goes to the next person, fine, let it go. If [COMPANY_A] is real, they'll still be there tomorrow, and I'll find them myself. I'm not confirming my name on a call I didn't ask for. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you'll find me tomorrow? Oh, that's, uh, that's actually not going to work, the position's gone by tomorrow, that's the whole, that's why I'm ringing today, so if you could just give me a quick yes on the name and we'll, we'll get you sorted before five, so, [PERSON_1], is that you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I said I'd find them, not you. I'm done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you're done with the fund? No no, you haven't even been in it yet, there's nothing to be done with, it's just a quick slot with the advisor and then it's...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said I'm done with this call. I'm not confirming my name, I'm not booking anything, and I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, okay, fine. I'll note it down as a no, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, you do that. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, well, before you go, and I'm not trying to hold you, I just want to say, you've got the wrong end of it a bit, because there's nothing for you to sign or pay on this call, it's literally a calendar booking, that's all I do, I put people in the diary, and, uh, the reason it sounds rushed is only because the advisor's calendar is tight today and the fund does close at five, that's not me, that's just how the fund works. But look, if you really want to check us out, that's absolutely your call, you do your own homework, and I'd only say that if you do decide to look into it later and the position's gone, that's, well, that's just the timing, so if you change your mind in the next hour or so, just ring the direct line back, it's [PHONE_1], and if it goes to voicemail leave your name and I'll slot you in before the window shuts. Okay? So, yeah, take care, and, uh, sorry again for catching you at work.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. So if I want to check you out I just do my own homework, and if the position's gone, it's gone. Fine by me. I won't be ringing that number, but thanks. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yes, hello, is this -- sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm just calling from, uh, [COMPANY_A], it's about your account, I won't keep you long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who's asking? I mean, which account are we talking about? Sorry, hang on -- [muffled, away from the phone] no, put that down, please -- sorry, go on. Who did you say you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, take your time. It's [COMPANY_A], I'm with the, uh, the fraud team there, I'm a claims assessor. Sorry, I said [COMPANY_A], the bank, and it's just a routine thing about your account, nothing to worry about. Is this [PERSON_1], did I get that right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... I haven't said who I am yet, have I? You rang me. So, uh, what account is it? Because I've got a few things, and, well, "routine" and "fraud team" don't really go together, do they?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sorry, you're right, I did ring you. Um, and the, the lunch account, did you say? No -- sorry, no, I've got it here on the screen, it's the current account, ending, uh, hang on, I'll just -- anyway, the thing is, there was a charge attempted on it just now, for [AMOUNT_1], and I do need to confirm a couple of details with you before it goes through. It's quite time sensitive, so if we could just do that quickly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the lunch account? I never said anything about a lunch account. And you've lost the number on your screen, so... what, you don't actually know which account it is? Look, if there's a charge you're worried about, why are you asking me for details? Shouldn't you already have them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. It's just how the process works, I need you to confirm your details first, for security.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: For security? No, no, hang on, you rang me, so you should be proving who you are to me, not the other way round. And you still haven't said the bank's actual name, you just keep saying [COMPANY_A] -- so what's a number I can ring back on? One that's, I don't know, on the back of my card, not one you give me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, someone's just -- [PERSON_3], I'll be with you in a minute -- sorry, uh, what was that? A number, right, yes, I'd have to check on that, I'd need to see if I'm allowed to give out the direct line. Look, I really don't think we've got time for that, because the charge is pending right now, and if it isn't confirmed in the next few minutes the account gets frozen, and then you're without access to it altogether.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, no, that's -- see, that's the bit I don't like. You can't tell me which account it is, you can't give me a number I can check, you're not sure if you're even allowed to, and now it's a few minutes or I lose access to everything? A real bank doesn't work like that, does it? If something was pending, it'd just sit there, or they'd block the card, and I'd get a letter, or a text, or I'd ring them myself. Nobody gives you a countdown over the phone. And honestly, if my account does get frozen, fine, I'll deal with that, I'll walk into a branch and sort it out, that's a lot better than reading out my details to someone who rang me out of the blue and can't even say what bank they're from. So, no, I'm not confirming anything. I'm going to hang up and ring the number on the back of my card myself. Okay? Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, wait, please, before you -- sorry, you said something two turns back, about them just blocking the card, and, uh, I didn't catch that properly. Can you say that again? Because that's actually what I need to avoid here, and if you hang up now, I can't stop it, and then it's on you, honestly, the account will be frozen and that's, that's not something I can reverse once it's flagged. So if you could just confirm your date of birth and the, uh, the postcode, that's all I need, then I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Now it's on me? That's -- no, I'm not giving you my date of birth or my postcode. You've asked me for details three times now and you still can't tell me which bank you're with. If the account gets frozen, I'll sort it out myself, in person. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, don't -- look, if you just let me finish, it's only the two things, the date of birth and, uh, and the postcode, and then I can stop it before it -- please, [PERSON_1], I'm trying to help you here, and if you put the phone down it's going to go through and I, I really can't --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said goodbye. I'm not telling you anything, and I'm not discussing this any more. I'll ring the number on my card myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: But if you hang up, then it, uh -- hello? [PERSON_1]? Hello? ...Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: [away from the phone] No, sweetheart, not on the sofa, take it to the table -- thank you. [back to the phone] Sorry, what? I'm still here, I hadn't put it down yet. But I meant it, I'm not giving you anything. If there's really a problem, the bank can write to me or I'll ring them on the number I already have. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, yes, hi, is this -- am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm, um, I'm calling on behalf of the landlord, [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], about your deposit, and I'm afraid it's, well, it's sort of urgent.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, who's this, sorry? I didn't catch the, um -- which landlord? And what about my deposit?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I'm -- hang on, one second, someone's just come in with, uh, with a delivery, sorry. Right. So, I'm [PERSON_3], I'm just, I work for [PERSON_2], the landlord's, um, representative, and the thing is, your deposit's at risk, [PERSON_1], it really is, and I'd hate for it to come to that. I'd just ask, please, that you keep this between us for now, not the letting agent, not your housemates, because it'll only make things, well, harder for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said the landlord's, uh, [PERSON_2], and now you're the landlord's representative? Which is it? And why would I not tell the letting agent -- they're the ones who hold the deposit, aren't they? I mean, that's -- sorry, [name], hang on, no, put that down, sweetheart -- why keep it between us?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I said -- look, I work for [PERSON_2], I'm not the landlord, I never said I was, I'm just the, the person who, uh -- please, [PERSON_1], I'm trying to help you here, and it's, it honestly hurts a bit that you'd think I'd -- the agent can't know, not yet, because if they find out before you've spoken to me it'll go badly for you, and the deposit's the very first thing to go. I just need you to hold off telling anyone today. Can you do that for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not agreeing to that. Why can't the agent know? They hold the deposit, that's what I keep saying. Why can't they know? If something's wrong with my deposit, they're the ones I'd ring, and you haven't told me a single thing that's actually wrong. What's the problem, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I can't go into the details on the phone, I'm sorry. It's just easier if you don't ring them yet. Please, [PERSON_1], I'm only trying to stop it getting worse for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you can't say what's wrong, and I'm not to ring the people who hold it. No. I'll be ringing the agent, and that's all I've got to say. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, please, don't -- um, [PERSON_1], I really wouldn't do that, not today, because if you ring them it's going to, well, it'll count against you and I can't undo that once it's, uh, once it's said. I'm only trying to help and honestly it's a bit hurtful to be, to be hung up on like -- hello? Are you still there? Please, just give me two minutes before you ring anyone, that's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here. No, I'm not giving you two minutes. You've said it'll count against me if I ring them, but you won't say what the problem is, and that's the part that worries me. I'm ringing the agent, and I'll check with them whether anyone's been in touch about my deposit. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, please, [PERSON_1], please, just don't -- I'm asking you, I'm only asking you to wait, that's all, just wait before you ring them. It'll go worse for you if you ring them today, I promise you it will, and I'd hate to see that, I really would. Please, just two minutes, just -- hello? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm here, I just -- hang on. Look, you keep telling me it'll go worse, but you still won't say what's wrong, and nobody who's actually trying to help tells you not to ring the people who hold the money. So no. I'm ringing the agent now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I -- no, that's not fair, that's really not fair, I've been nothing but, uh, nothing but kind to you and you're making me sound like I'm, like I'm some kind of -- look, I'm telling you, if you ring them, it's out of my hands. I can't protect you after that, I just can't, and that'll be on you, [PERSON_1], not me. Please, just wait until tomorrow, that's all, give me until tomorrow before you say a word to anyone, and I can still sort it, I'm sure I can sort it, but only if you -- hello? [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm not -- look, I'm not trying to make you sound like anything. I just -- no. Actually, you've still not told me one thing that's wrong, and now it's until tomorrow, it was two minutes a second ago. If it can wait a day, it can wait while I ring the agent. I'm not waiting, and I'm not agreeing to say nothing to anyone. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a, uh, meter data verification specialist at [COMPANY_A], your electricity and gas supplier. I'm calling because there's a, well, an inconsistency between two readings we hold against your account, and, I mean, it's on our side of the records as much as yours, so there's nothing alarming, but I'd like to reconcile it if you've got a moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm driving, I'm on speaker so the reception's a bit, it keeps cutting out. Did you say there's a... a leak? On my account? Oh no, I don't, I mean I haven't noticed anything, is it the gas? Should I be pulling over?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a leak, sorry, I can see how that came across -- it's a records matter, nothing to do with safety, so please don't pull over on my account, and honestly if you're driving we can do this another -- well, what I mean is, it's two meter readings that don't agree in our own system, the estimated one and the submitted one, and, uh, that's a discrepancy on our end, in the reconciliation layer, so no urgency whatsoever. If it's easier I'll just leave it with you and you can ring us back once you're parked up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, phew. Yeah, I'll ring back once I'm parked, sorry. Is there a number I should use, or, I'd just ring the one on my bill?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, please, the number on your bill is exactly the one to use, or the one on our website if you'd rather look that up yourself. I'd honestly prefer that to anything I read out to you now. When you get through, just say there's a meter reading query on your account and they'll pull up the notes. And there's no rush, nothing changes on your bill until you've spoken to them, so you're completely fine to take your time, and do check your online account first if you like, the readings we hold are listed there. Safe driving, and thanks for being so patient, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, that's, yeah, that's really kind, thank you. Sorry for being all flustered, it's just the word gas and I'm, well. I'll ring the one on my bill once I'm parked and have a look at the online account first. Thanks for calling, and sorry again for the, uh, the bad line. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, no apology needed at all, honestly, I should have, I mean, I should have led with the fact it was only a records query rather than, uh, anything to do with the supply itself. So that's on me. Do ring the number on your bill, check the online account first, and, well, take care on the road, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, wait, sorry, one quick thing before you go, and it's probably me being slow. Two turns back, you said there was an estimated reading and a submitted one that don't agree? Um, which one is the wrong one, do you know? Because I'm not sure I ever sent one in, so I'm a bit confused now. Sorry, the line's still cutting out.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a fair question, and honestly I can't tell you which one's wrong, because that's the very thing the -- right, so what I can see is that the estimated figure and a submitted one disagree, but I don't know where the submitted one came from, whether it was you, a smart meter, or somebody keying it in on our side, and, uh, if you never sent one in, well, that's worth mentioning when you ring, because it may point to an error at our end, and I'd much rather you heard that from the team with the full account history in front of them than from me guessing. So check the readings listed in your online account, ring the number on your bill, and ask them to look at the notes. And I won't need anything from you today, [PERSON_1], so please, mind the road. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, yeah. I'll check the account and ring the number on my bill. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from the, uh, the claims office at [COMPANY_A], we're the international lottery claims, and I just need a moment to confirm a couple of things on a file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hello? Sorry, yeah, I'm, I'm driving, you're on speaker and the reception's kind of terrible right now. Um, did you say lottery? Sorry, I only caught like half of that. Who is this exactly, and, uh, what was the name of the place again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, lottery, [COMPANY_A], international claims office. I'm a security operations officer there, [PERSON_2]. It's a routine file confirmation, nothing you need to do while you're driving, so just tell me, are you [PERSON_1], yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, I mean, I, I'm [PERSON_1], yeah, sorry. But, um, I don't think I've entered any lottery? Like, I really don't remember buying a ticket or anything, so I'm, I'm confused why there'd be a file on me. And why is a security officer calling about it? Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, it's just, the signal keeps cutting out and I'm a bit nervous, so, uh, can you say again what this is actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, right, I understand, but -- [PERSON_1], listen, the entry was registered under your name, that's why there's a file. Security handles it because any prize over a certain threshold goes through verification before release, standard procedure. Your ticket, number [CODE_1], was drawn on the, uh, the fourteenth, and the sum attached to it is [AMOUNT_1], so we do need to confirm your claim details today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, okay, so, uh... hang on, sorry, let me, I'm just, I'm sort of merging lanes here, so, um... right. Sorry. So, a ticket, drawn on the fourteenth, but I really, I really didn't buy one, so how would it even be in my name? And, uh, why does it have to be today? That sounds, I don't know, kind of rushed? Sorry, I'm not accusing you of anything, I just, um, how would I even check that this is, you know, real?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and I'll answer it properly, because I do have to run through this with every claimant. The entries were registered in bulk through partner promotions, so a lot of winners never remember a purchase, that's actually quite common with the overseas draws. As for today, unclaimed prizes at this tier get released back to the pool after the deadline, which is why my office makes the calls rather than sending letters, and I'm not in a position to hold the file open past today. And as for checking, you're welcome to look us up, but the verification window is narrow, so I'd rather we confirm now and you do your due diligence on the back end. Now, where did I -- yes, your ticket, number [CODE_1], drawn on the, uh, the twenty-first, and the sum is [AMOUNT_2], so if you could just confirm you're willing to proceed with the claim, we can get this finalized before the close of business.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, okay, so, sorry, hang on, I think the road's about to split here, so bear with me if I go quiet for a sec. Right. Okay. It's just, I'm a little stuck on a couple of things, and I'm sorry if I'm going on, I do that when I'm nervous. You said the draw was on the fourteenth, and now you're saying the twenty-first, and the amount's different too, [AMOUNT_1] before and now [AMOUNT_2]? Or maybe I misheard, the signal's been cutting in and out, so I really might have, but I don't think I did. And the other thing is, you said I can check you out, but only after I confirm I'm willing to proceed, and that feels backwards to me? Like, I'm not saying you're doing anything wrong, I really don't know you at all, but if it's a real thing, wouldn't it still be real if I called back later, or looked up the number myself? I mean, I'd feel a lot better doing it that way. Sorry, is that, um, is that okay?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you didn't misspeak, I did, the signal's been dropping on my end too, so the fourteenth, the twenty-first, those are both on the file, it's a clerical thing, the amount as well. I'm telling you the claim is valid. The claim is valid, [PERSON_1]. And I'm not asking you to skip checking, I'm saying the window closes today, so calling back later is, well, it isn't something my office can guarantee. Look, you've been very reasonable, and I appreciate that, truly, so let's just keep this simple. You're willing to proceed with the claim, yes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... uh... so, hmm, yeah, sorry, I'm just, I'm thinking, give me a second. Um. Okay, so, I really appreciate you saying that, and I'm sorry, I know you've been patient with me, but the dates and the amounts both changing, that, that's making me, I don't know, more nervous, not less? And you can't hold it open, but you also can't tell me how to check it myself, so, um, I think I'd rather, I'd rather not say yes to anything while I'm driving. Is there, like, a number I could look up on my own and call? Or, I guess, if it's real, it'll still be there, right? Sorry, I don't want to be rude.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so -- uh, look, you're not being rude, nobody's saying that. And I know the figures sounded different, I've explained that, the file's been updated twice, which is why you've heard two versions, but it's one claim, one valid claim. A number you could look up, yes, of course, the claims desk has a line, but honestly that just puts you in a queue behind everyone else, and the close of business doesn't move for a queue. So, um, you've been careful, I respect that, and I'd say you've done your due diligence just by asking. Can I note that you're willing to proceed, [PERSON_1]? Just a yes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, no, sorry, I, I don't think I can say yes. I know you've been patient and I feel bad about it, but, uh, the dates and amounts kept changing, and I never bought a ticket, and now there's a deadline I can't check on my own. I'm going to say no for now, and if it's real, I'll find the claims office myself and call them. Sorry, I really am, but that's, that's my answer. Okay, so, bye now, I need to concentrate on the road.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that's your decision, [PERSON_1], though I should say I never told you to skip checking, I said the window was narrow, that's all. And I did say the claims desk had a line, I just didn't say it was a queue, that was, uh, never what I said. Anyway, the file stays open until close of business, and after that, it's out of my hands. Drive safe.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, sorry, before you go, can I just, one thing? Two turns back, you said the claims desk has a line, and that it'd put me in a queue behind everyone else. And now you're saying you never said it was a queue? I'm, I'm confused, because I'm pretty sure that's what I heard, but, uh, the signal's been bad, so maybe I'm wrong. Sorry. It just makes me even more sure I should look it up myself. Okay. Thanks, I guess. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, one moment -- sorry, someone's at my door, I've got a courier standing here. Yes, no, put it on the desk, thanks. Right. Back. What I said, [PERSON_1], is that it's a line, and lines have waits, I wasn't going to argue about the word. It's not a trick, it's just how the desk works, and you're free to hang up and call whoever you like. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, okay. Yeah. I'm going to hang up now and look it up myself. Sorry, and, uh, thanks for your time, I guess. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2] from the collections desk at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about a parcel on hold under your name, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and there's a handling balance of [AMOUNT_1] outstanding that needs settling today. Sorry, uh, before I go on -- can you just confirm for me that the delivery address on the file is still the one in [CITY_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Um, you said a parcel -- a parcel from who, exactly? And, sorry, what was the company again, I didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem. It's [COMPANY_A], the courier, I'm on the collections desk. The parcel came in from an overseas sender, I don't have the sender name on my screen, just the reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. And, uh, it's been sitting at our depot in [CITY_1] since, I think, Tuesday, so the balance is [AMOUNT_2] now, not the [AMOUNT_1] I said, that's just the fee that's been added on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a fee? For, what, a deposit? I haven't put down any deposit on anything. Hang on, let me turn this down. Um, and the sender, you don't know who sent it? That's a bit odd, isn't it? How do you not know who it's from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not a deposit, a handling fee, it's -- right, I understand it's odd, I'll note that objection on the file. The sender field just isn't populated on my screen, that's the overseas intake, it happens. What I can see is the parcel is held, the balance is [AMOUNT_2], and if it isn't settled today it goes back to the depot for return processing, and that's, well, that's just how it works after the hold period. So it's simplest to take care of it now, over the phone, with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, wait. Two minutes ago you said the fee was the first amount, and then it was the second one? I didn't follow that. Which is it, what do I actually owe? And, sorry, why does it have to be today, over the phone, with you? Can't I just ring the courier myself?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, [AMOUNT_1] is the handling fee, and the [AMOUNT_2] is that plus the storage charge since Tuesday. The [AMOUNT_2] is what's owing today, I should've said it that way. You can ring the main line, sure, but they'll only send you back to this desk, and the parcel goes to return processing at close of day regardless. I'll note that you asked to verify it, but it's simplest if we settle this now, while the hold is still active. So, can I take it that we're going ahead?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, hang on, I'm not saying yes to anything yet. I've got the pan going and I can't think straight. Um, so you're telling me I owe money for a parcel I don't know anything about, from a sender you can't even name, and I've got until close of day or it all goes back? That's, I mean, that's an awful lot of hurry, isn't it? And you said if I ring the main line they'll just send me back to you, but how would you know that? You don't work on the main line. Sorry, I'm not being rude, I just, I've never had a call like this before, and I don't really know what you'd even want me to do. I'm not going to do anything down the phone, not today, not like this. If there's really a parcel, I'd sooner look up the number myself and ring them, and if it goes back, it goes back. I'm sorry. I think I'll leave it there. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, I -- no, I understand, I'll note that on the file. But I should say, if it goes back, it goes back with the storage charge attached, that's just how the, uh, how the account stands once the hold lapses. It's not a threat, it's just the figure. I'm not able to take this where you're agreeing to settle it, though. You've said no and you're going to look up the number and ring them yourself. That's your call to make, and I'm going to leave it there too. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, if there's a charge, they can send me a letter about it. Sorry. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], we're the financial regulator, I'm on the support side there. Nothing to panic about, but we've picked up some activity on your savings that we need to sort out today, and it's honestly a quick one, couple of minutes, tops.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh... yeah, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, who did you say you were again? Activity on my savings, you said?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, [PERSON_1], everyone asks that, happens all the time. So it's [PERSON_2], I'm a support technician with [COMPANY_A], we're the financial regulator, we sit above the banks basically, we keep an eye on accounts that look like they might be exposed. And what's happened is, uh, a flag came up on your savings, there's been some movement that doesn't match your normal pattern, and when that happens we step in to get the funds into a protected holding arrangement while we look into it. It's really just a short process, [PERSON_1], nothing complicated, I'd walk you through the whole thing myself. The one thing I do need from you, and I say this to everyone so don't take it the wrong way, is that you keep this between us for now, so no mentioning it to the bank or anyone else, because if the wrong people get wind of it while it's open, well, that's how savings end up gone. So, have you got a few minutes right now, [PERSON_1]? Sooner we start, the sooner your money's safe.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I... I mean, I've got time, I'm just here at home, it's only me and the radio, really. But, uh, why wouldn't I -- no, wait. Why can't I tell the bank? That seems a bit odd to me, I always tell my bank everything, well, not everything, but... sorry, I'm rambling. Who is it you're with again, the regulator? I didn't know there was one that rang people up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not rambling at all, [PERSON_1], that's a really sensible question, and honestly, uh, we do ring people, it's not unusual, we only do it when it's urgent like this. Now, the bank thing, it's not that the bank's done anything wrong, it's just that, well, the movement we flagged, we're, um, we're still working out where it started, so it's better kept quiet for now, that's all. And I did say couple of minutes, but I should be straight with you, it might run a little longer, say twenty minutes or so, but it's all very simple, I'll do the heavy lifting. So, you're at home, good, nice and quiet, so shall we get started on moving that money across to the holding arrangement, [PERSON_1]? I'd hate for anything to go missing before we've got it covered.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Twenty minutes? Well, that's, uh... that's a bit more than a couple, isn't it? You did say a couple. And moving my money across, I don't, hmm. I don't think I understand that part. Why would the money have to go anywhere? It's safe where it is, isn't it, it's in the savings, that's what savings are for. And you still haven't quite told me, sorry, I know you said, but who are you with, and how would I know that, you know, you are? I'm not very good with all this phone business, my nephew usually does the, the computer side of things, he's in [CITY_1] now though. Oh, and I still don't see why I can't just ring my bank, they've always been very nice to me there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, [PERSON_1], that's the thing, it's not safe where it is, not right now, that's exactly why we're ringing, and every minute we -- no, no, don't ring your bank, [PERSON_1], please, not yet, that's the one thing that could really upset this, and honestly it's only a bit longer than I said, I'm not trying to trick you. I'm with [COMPANY_A], the regulator, I've told you, and I can't have you hanging up and waiting around, because if that money's still sitting there tonight, well, I can't promise it'll be there tomorrow. So let's just move it across now, [PERSON_1], all right? It's really nothing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm. No, I don't think so. I'm sorry, dear, you seem nice enough, but a minute ago it was a couple of minutes and now it's twenty, and I mustn't ring my own bank, and I'm to move my money somewhere tonight, and you can't tell me how I'd know you are who you say. That doesn't sit right with me. If it's really that urgent, the bank will know all about it, won't they, so I'll just ring them, on the number on my card, thank you very much. I'm not moving anything today. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_1], hang on, hang on, sorry, one second, someone's just come to my desk, uh -- no, go on, I'm here. Look, everyone gets a bit wobbly at this stage, that's normal, but please don't ring the bank, [PERSON_1], that's the one thing that'll mess it all up, and I really can't say what'll happen to that money if it's sitting there tonight. Just stay with me two more minutes, that's all I'm asking, [PERSON_1]? [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, dear, I said goodbye. I'm going to ring my bank, on the number on my card, that's what I'm doing. And you keep telling me not to, which is exactly why I'm going to. So, no, I'm not staying on, and I'm not moving anything, not today. Goodbye now, I mean it, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm just, I've got your details up here on the screen. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with [COMPANY_A], the recruitment agency, and I'm calling about the remote position you registered interest in. Um, you may have had an email from us earlier, I think it was, hang on, yesterday? Or the day before, sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, speaking, yes. Sorry, I'm -- who did you say you were with again? A claims assessor? That's, I mean, that's an odd title for a recruitment agency. And I don't, um, I don't actually recall registering interest in anything remote, so I'd like to know which email you mean.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, no, fair question. [PERSON_2], claims assessor, [COMPANY_A], it's, uh, it's just the title on my screen, I think it's what they call the people who assess applications, sort of. And the email, hang on, it'd have come from, um, I don't have the sender in front of me, but it was about the remote role, the one that starts as soon as the onboarding cost is cleared. You'd have seen that, I'd think? The remote role, starting as soon as that's cleared.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on. Onboarding cost? A recruiter asking a candidate to clear a cost before a job starts, that's, well, that's not something I've ever come across. Employers pay agencies, not the other way round. And you don't have the sender in front of you, but you do have my details on your screen. So what details exactly, and where did they come from? Because I'd like to know what I supposedly registered on, and which site. I can check my inbox while we talk, but I'm not going to confirm anything about myself until I know that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, so, the details. I've got your name, a contact number, and, um, sort of a general profile, I think, hang on. It would've come from one of the job boards we, uh, we partner with. I'd have to check which one, I don't have that in front of me right now. And on the cost, I mean, it's a fairly standard step for us, it's [AMOUNT_1], and the role is, um, well it's paid quite well for remote, [AMOUNT_2] a week to start, so it more than covers itself. Honestly the main thing is just getting the process moving today, because the placement slot, I think it's held until end of day, or, sorry, end of tomorrow, I'll need to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, I'm going to stop you there, because you've now told me you can't name the sender, the job board, or the deadline, and -- Sorry, go on, but no, I've heard enough of the shape of this. A fee up front, a good weekly rate, a slot that expires. And you don't know which day. I'm not paying anything, and I'm not confirming a single detail of mine. If [COMPANY_A] is real, I'll find their number myself and ring the main line. Not this one. So, what's the vacancy reference, please? Actually, no, don't. I'm done with this. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, hang on, please. That's, uh, that's completely fine, you can ring the main line, I'd say go ahead. I'll, I'll have to check what the reference is, so, um, no, honestly it's not really a fee, it's more of a deposit, sorry, I did say cost earlier. And it's not today, the slot, I meant the end of the week, I think? So there's no rush, but if you could just, um, stay on a moment while I find it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say a deposit? No, hang on, you said it's not a fee, it's a deposit, and then it's the end of the week, so no rush, but earlier it was end of day. I'm sorry, you're going to have to pick one. And, uh, did you say stay on while you find a reference? I can't tell, you keep changing what the thing is called. Fee, cost, deposit. It's the same money leaving my pocket whatever the word is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, you're right, I keep, um, sorry, that's on me, I've got a couple of these open at once and I'm mixing the wording. It's the same thing, the cost, I should've just stuck with that. And the slot, I think it's the end of the week, but I'd have to, um, I'd have to check with someone on that. Look, the reference, I don't have it to hand, but I can have it sent over, and then you can, I mean, you can look into it however you like. I just, I don't want you to lose the placement over, over wording.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I -- look, it isn't the wording. It's that, well, you've changed the deadline twice, you can't tell me the sender or the job board, and you want money before any work, which is, I mean, that's the whole pattern. I won't lose anything by not paying, because there's nothing here to lose. If there's a real vacancy, I'll find it myself through the agency's own website. Don't send me anything. I'm ending the call now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, I, I understand, and I'm not, I don't want you to feel pushed into anything, that's, that's not what this is. Um, look, I'll say this, and I know it's, it's gone a bit round in circles, I'm sorry, I'm still fairly new on this desk and I think I've, I've muddled the details, the timing and what we call it and so on. So what I'll do is I'll, I'll have to check with my supervisor about the reference and the, the actual deadline, and, and then someone can, um, ring you back, or I can, or I'll send something over, I'm not sure which yet. And, honestly, if you do want to go through the main line, that's, that's your call, I just, I'd hate for you to miss out, because the role really is, it's quite a good one, for remote, and the weekly rate is, is genuinely higher than most of what's out there, so, um, if you could just, I mean, would you at least let me note down that you're still interested, in case it, in case it turns out to be, to be all in order?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I won't have you note me down as interested, because I'm not. And I'd rather be exact about why, so there's no ambiguity on your end. I've told you I never registered for anything, and you've never been able to tell me which board or which email, which is the one thing that would have settled it. You've also described the same payment as a fee, a cost and a deposit, and you've given me three different deadlines, one of which was today. Muddling the wording I could put down to nerves. A confident ask for money ahead of any work is a different matter, because that part of the story never changed once. So here's how I'll handle it. If a genuine agency exists and wants me, they can tell me what I registered on and when, in writing, and I'll check it against the main line I look up myself. I don't want a callback, I don't want anything sent over, and please remove this number from whatever list it's on. I won't be giving you any details at all. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just, uh, someone's put a file on my desk, hang on. Right, sorry. Okay, so, um, I'll take the number off, I'll flag that, I'm, yeah, I'm not meant to ring after a, after a request like that. I'll, I'll mention it to my supervisor too, about the reference and the, the timing, and, um, I suppose if anything's, if anything's in order, it'd come to you in writing like you said. Sorry for, for the muddle, I hope you, yeah. Right. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Please do take it off. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, will do, I'll take it off, um, today, I mean, or, well, it might be tomorrow, it depends when my supervisor's in. Oh, and just so you know, nobody from here would ring you back, I think I said someone might earlier, but that's not how we do it, so, um, you won't hear anything. Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Noted. And that's now a fourth thing that's changed, the callback. Anyway, I'll leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, sorry, that's, um, that's fair, I did say that, didn't I. I'll, I'll check that with my supervisor too, I mean, about the callback, and, uh, whether it's one or, or not. Right. Sorry about the, yeah. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine. No more calls, please. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm, um, calling from the tenancy deposit protection scheme, about a thing at your building.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, um, speaking, yeah. Sorry, the tenancy deposit... scheme? About a thing at my building? I mean, I own my place, I don't, uh, I'm not renting or anything, so -- sorry, who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, right, sorry, I should've said. I'm not calling about your deposit, you don't have one, I know that. It's, um, a landlord and tenant at the building are in a dispute, and I'm sort of the go-between for [COMPANY_A], that's the scheme, and I'm ringing because you're, uh, you're listed as the contact for the building. I'm really not good at these calls, sorry. What I'm meant to ask is, um, could you keep it to yourself for now? The dispute, I mean. Not tell the other tenants until both sides have been formally notified. It's just that it wouldn't be fair on either of them if it got around first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, let me just make sure I've got this. You're from a deposit scheme, a landlord and a tenant in my building are in some kind of dispute, and I'm listed as the contact for the building, and you want me to not tell the other tenants. Right. Please do tell her, and ring the office together if anything in the letter puzzles you. I won't take any more of your afternoon, [PERSON_1], and thank you for being so patient with me. Goodbye now.
