That doesn't, no, I'm not, I'm not confirming anything just because someone says don't bother looking. If it's real it'll still be real once I've found my paperwork, won't it? So I'll look, and I'll ring the company myself, the proper one, not through you. And I'll want it in writing as well, because honestly my head's still full of nap and I don't want to say yes to something I'll regret. So I'm going to say goodbye now, all right? Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, wait, did you say regret? Because there's no penalty, ma'am, sir, there's no penalty on the, on the reinstatement, that's the whole, the whole point of the no-cost continuation, so there's, there's nothing to regret, and if you could just stay on the line one moment, I only need the, the confirmation of status and then your file is, is closed out --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm going to stop you there, because you said it costs [AMOUNT_1] if I don't, so there is a penalty, you said that, I heard it, even half asleep. I'm hanging up now and I'll ring the proper company myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, sir, I'd strongly advise against, uh, against letting the term lapse, because once the reconciliation window closes the reinstatement pathway is, it's not guaranteed to remain open, and then the re-rate, well -- but if you do ring, ring the main line, yes, and just reference, uh, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll, they'll route you back to, to my department, so, so really it'll all come back to me in any case.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, route me back to your department? No, I'll be finding the number myself, off my own paperwork, not from you. And the main what, the main fine? I'm not paying any fine, I never said anything about a fine. Right, that's me done, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A fine? No, no, I didn't say fine, I said the main line, the, the main line, but, uh, since you raised it, there's no fine as such, it's a, a re-rate differential, which is, which is a different, a different classification entirely, so you needn't, needn't concern yourself with that --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, main line, right, I did mishear that, fair enough, but honestly it doesn't change anything. You've gone from a free renewal to a re-rate differential, which sounds like a fine with a longer name, and I've told you three times now that I'm hanging up, and every time I do you find something else to tell me. A proper company, if I said I wanted to look at my paperwork and ring them myself, they'd say, lovely, take your time. They wouldn't say the window's closing and it'll all come back to me anyway. And I'd still like to know why you can't give me a number if you're ringing from an actual department, because everybody has a number, even the dentist has a number. So no, I'm not confirming a thing today. I'll find my folder, I'll look up whoever the car people really are, and if there's something real they can write to me about it. I'm going to put the phone down now, and please don't ring back, all right? Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, right, well, uh, if I could just, hm, sorry, I'm, I'm not sure that's, uh, that's strictly the ideal outcome for your file, but, but I can't compel anyone, naturally, so, uh, yes, I'll, I'll note the account as, as customer-declined, and if you do, if you do ring, uh, the proper company, as you say, they'll, they'll have the, the lapse on record, so, um, that's, that's your prerogative, yes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, customer-declined, yes, that's what I'm doing, I'm declining. I'll find my paperwork and ring the proper company myself, like I said, and if they've got a lapse on record they can write and tell me. In writing, mind. So that's me, I'm declining, and I'm going now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yeah, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the scheduling desk at [COMPANY_A], just a quick one.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, I'm in the middle of something here. Scheduling desk for what exactly, I don't know any [COMPANY_A].

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, totally, sorry, bad time, I'll be quick. It's [COMPANY_A], the charitable foundation, we run the fundraising dinners, I'm just the one who books follow-up calls with people who came along. So you were at the [CITY_1] event a few weeks back, right? That's all I'm trying to line up, a short slot with our events coordinator, nothing heavy.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, what was the first thing you said? Scheduling desk for what? And hold on, I never said I was at any dinner, you said that. Why's an events coordinator want a slot with me, what's it actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, fair, so I'm at the scheduling desk at [COMPANY_A], the foundation, I book the follow-up calls, that's all I do, and I'm sorry if I put the dinner in your mouth, I just have you down on the attendee list from the [CITY_1] night, so if that's wrong tell me and I'll, I mean, the coordinator just wants ten minutes to talk through the pledge you made on the evening, that's really all it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A pledge. Right. I didn't make any pledge, mate.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, I mean, that's what's in the notes, [AMOUNT_1], said out loud on the night, and it just needs honouring now, that's all I've got in front of me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Honouring? Hang on, you said, what, a mortgage? No, I haven't got a mortgage with you lot, I've never even heard of you. Sorry, what are you actually on about, because I'm not owing anyone anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not a mortgage, a pledge, a donation, you said it out loud at the event and it's logged, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, a donation. Okay. But go back a sec, two minutes ago you said I was on some attendee list. Whose list? Where did you get my name from, because I don't remember going to any dinner. And what was that amount you said, I didn't catch it properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The amount's [AMOUNT_1], and I do appreciate that's a lot, but it's on the night sheet under your name, and, sorry, did you say a witness? No, no witness, it's just the sheet, that's the record, and the foundation's counting on it. As for whose list, that's our internal records and I can't go into those, they're confidential, but the pledge was made, so what I need is a time for the coordinator to ring you and sort out the next step.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Confidential records, no witness, and I'm supposed to just book in. No. I'm not booking anything with a stranger who can't tell me where he got my name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, no, I hear you, and honestly, I mean, nobody likes a call out of the blue, it's just that the foundation's relying on what was promised, a lot of good work rides on it, and the coordinator's got [CITY_1] on the diary this week, so it really would be easiest to just pencil in a slot, uh, ten minutes, and he can walk you through where you're down on the sheet, so shall I put you in for tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. No, I'm not putting anything in for tomorrow. I said, where did you get my name? You can't tell me that, you can't tell me who said I pledged, and now it's all about the coordinator's diary. That's not an answer, mate. I'm not booking anything, I'm not confirming any pledge, and if your foundation wants to prove something it can send it in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, sorry to bother you -- is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the energy supplier, and, um, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh! Hello, yes, I'm here, sorry -- the kettle's just clicked off and I nearly dropped the spoon. Yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Now who did you say you were, dear? Energy supplier, was it? I'm never sure which one I'm even with these days, my late husband used to sort all that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, take your time, it's no trouble at all, I can hear the kettle was a surprise, I'm so sorry for catching you mid-cuppa. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], and I'm a case handler in the billing team, and honestly, uh, plenty of people lose track of who they're with, especially when it was someone else who always sorted it, so please don't worry about that. The reason I'm ringing is, well, it sounds more alarming than it is, but we've got two meter readings on your account that don't match each other, and, um, the mismatch is on our side, in our own records, not anything you've done. I'd only like to correct it so your bill isn't wrong, which is really just for your own protection, you see. Are you still with me, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, I'm still with you, I'm just -- well, I was going to say I haven't touched the meter, but that's not, I mean, you said it's your end, didn't you? Two readings that don't, uh, match. Goodness. My husband always did the readings, he had a little notebook, it's still in the drawer somewhere, and I did think the last bill was, well, no, perhaps it wasn't. Sorry, dear, I'm rambling. What is it you need me to do, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not rambling at all, I'm sorry, I think I confused things. Two turns back I said the mismatch was on our side, and I should be clearer about what I meant, because it's, um, a bit untidy. We hold two figures for you, an older reading and a newer one, and the newer one comes out lower than the older, which can't be right, so one of them was logged wrongly at our end. I don't yet know which, and I'd rather say that than guess. What would help is the figure on the meter as it is today, just the number on the display, nothing else, no personal details, nothing about the bank. But please, [PERSON_1], you don't have to give it to me on the phone. You can log into your account online at [URL_1], or look at your last bill, and ring us back on the number printed there, and we'll change nothing until you've done that. Are you still there, dear?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, dear, don't you worry. Well, that's very kind of you, saying I can ring back on the number on the bill. That does seem sensible, doesn't it? Though I'm not much good with the online business, my granddaughter set it up once and I never could remember the password. But the bill, yes, I've got a pile of them somewhere by the bread bin, I think. Now, the meter -- it's in the cupboard under the stairs, and it's a bit of a to-do getting down there with my knee. Would it matter if I did it later, once I've had my tea? And, um, what was the name of the company again, I want to be sure I find the right bill.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, that's absolutely fine, please don't go down to that cupboard on my account, not with your knee, I'd feel awful. Have your tea, and there's no rush at all. The company is [COMPANY_A], that's the name I gave at the start, it should be printed at the top of the bills in your pile by the bread bin, so if it matches, you'll know you've got the right one. And, um, if you do ring back, the number on the bill is the one to use, not anything I give you, and just ask for the billing team and mention your account reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], that's on there too. Nothing changes on your account until you've been in touch, I promise. Is that all right, [PERSON_1]? Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that's all right, dear, I'm still here. Ring the number on the bill, not any other, I've got that. You've been very patient with me, I must say, not like some of them who hurry you along. I'll have my tea first and find the pile by the bread bin, and if the name at the top matches, I'll ring them. And if it doesn't match, well, I won't, will I? Thank you for calling, [PERSON_2], it's nice to have a bit of a chat, it gets quiet in the afternoons. Goodbye now, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's all right, [PERSON_1], that's exactly what I'd do myself. And yes, if the name doesn't match, then you don't ring, and that's perfectly fine too, I wouldn't mind in the least. I'm so sorry again for catching you with the kettle. Enjoy your tea, and, um, look after that knee. Goodbye now, dear.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Thank you, dear, I will, the knee's much better when I sit with it up. And don't you worry about the kettle, it's only tea. You have a lovely afternoon now, [PERSON_2]. Bye bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi there, uh, am I speaking with the account holder for the line? Sorry, I'll just, uh, give it a second here, my system's being a bit slow this morning. It's [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], customer care, and how are you doing today? Lovely, lovely, hope the week's treating you well.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, "the account holder for the line" -- which line, exactly? And which company did you say? Because I didn't quite catch that, you sort of --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're fine, my fault, I mumble when the coffee hasn't kicked in. It's [COMPANY_A], your home internet provider, and the line's the one your broadband runs on, the one attached to this number. Anyway, the reason I'm ringing, and it's a bit of a nuisance, honestly, is we've picked up a fault on your connection and it's flagged as urgent, so I'd like to get it sorted before it drops out on you altogether.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, two things don't line up. A minute ago you said it was your system running slow this morning, and now you're saying you've got a fault flagged on my connection, so which is it? And, uh, you still haven't given me a name for the company, you've just said "[COMPANY_A]", which I can't tie to anything. Who's my broadband provider, in your words, and what exactly is the fault showing as?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, those are two separate things, my system's slow, your line's faulty, I'd hardly blame myself for your broadband, would I? Look, I'll be straight with you, I've got a queue of customers with the same issue this morning, so I can't go through every detail. What the fault shows as is a signal degradation on your line, and what I need is just a couple of minutes of your time so I can take a look at it from my end with you. Have you got your computer nearby? It'd be the quickest way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you ring me out of the blue, you can't or won't tell me the company name, you can't go through the details because you've got a queue, and your next step is to get me in front of my computer. I'm sorry, but that's not a sequence I'm comfortable with. If there's a genuine fault on my line, my provider can see it from their side without me doing anything, and I'll hear about it through the account I already have with them. So I'll deal with it by ringing the number on my own bill. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Whoa, whoa, hang on a second, don't hang up on me. Sorry, can I just go back to something, you said the provider can see a fault from their side without you doing anything, but that's, uh, not really how it works with signal degradation, that's the whole reason I'm ringing, so can you tell me what you meant by that? And honestly there's no need to ring any bill number, I'm already on the line with you, it'll take two minutes, and if it drops out this afternoon that's on you, not me. So computer, near you, yes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not going to -- look, what I meant was, well, a provider monitors its own network, that's sort of the point of it. And even if you're right, even if signal degradation can't be seen from their end, that's an argument for me ringing them, not for sitting at my computer for a stranger who still hasn't named the company. And "if it drops out, that's on you" -- that's pressure, isn't it? Not a technical point. I've said I'll use the number on my bill, so, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, come on, it isn't pressure, I'm just trying to -- no, listen, listen, you're making this harder than it needs to be, honestly. I've been doing this for years and nobody's ever, ha, nobody's ever got this worked up over a two-minute check. Look, forget the company name for a second, forget the bill, I'm trying to help you here, and if you ring that number you'll be sat in a queue for an hour while your line gets worse. So just get to your computer and I'll --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not getting worked up, I'm just not doing it. And "forget the company name, forget the bill" is the part that settles it for me. A genuine caller wouldn't ask me to forget the two things I could use to check him. If the line really does get worse, I'll live with that. I'm ending the call now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Now hang on, that's not what I said, I never asked you to forget anything, I only said set it aside for a second, and honestly that's, ha, that's a bit unfair, because I've been nothing but patient with you this whole call, I've answered every question you've thrown at me, and I rang you in good faith, which is more than most people would do on a morning like this one. And look, I understand being careful, I do, it's sensible, my own mother's the same, she won't open the door to anyone, but the thing is, being careful and leaving your line to fall over aren't the same, and I'd hate for you to be sat there tonight with no internet, ringing round, wondering why you didn't just spend two minutes with me when I was already on the phone. So I'll make it easy, no company name, no bill, nothing, you just go to your computer and sit down, and I'll sort the rest from my end, all right? Hello? You still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still here, and no, I'm not -- look, you've just offered me "no company name, no bill, nothing," and that's precisely the... I'm not sitting down at my computer. Not for you, not for two minutes. If my line drops out tonight, I'll ring the number on my bill and sort it out with them. That's my answer, and it won't change. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine, fine, have it your way, but I'll tell you now, when that line goes down tonight and you're sat there in the dark, don't say nobody rang to warn you. I did. I rang you in good faith and you've thrown it back in my face, and honestly after the morning I've had, ha, I don't even know why I bothered. But go on, go and queue on your bill number then, see how far that gets you. Hello? Hello -- no, don't you hang up on me, I'm not finished, I'm only trying to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you did not warn me, you asked me to sit down at my computer, which isn't the same thing. And I never said I'd queue for an hour, that was you, I only said I'd ring the number on my bill. Whatever happens tonight, I'll deal with it through them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] over at [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants, and I'm calling because there's a position in one of our funds that's closing today and your name came up as someone who'd -- sorry, is this [PERSON_2]? Great, because I only have a couple of slots left on the advisor's calendar before the window shuts.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? I didn't quite catch the name of the company. And I'm not, um -- I'm not actually sure I'm [PERSON_2], I mean, that's my name, yes, but I don't think I've ever had a fund with anyone. Are you sure you've got the right person? You said my name came up, but I don't remember talking to anybody about this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, yeah, [COMPANY_A], an investment firm, and no worries at all, you wouldn't necessarily have spoken to anyone, these are pre-qualified introductions, which is exactly why the advisor wants to walk you through it before the position closes today. So I've got a slot at three or I've got one at four-thirty, which works better for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, well, three or four-thirty, I suppose, I'm not doing much today, so either's fine, sorry. But -- hang on, I'm a bit confused. You said before that my name came up because someone knew me, or, no, I think you said I'd already been, what was it, spoken to? And now it's that I wouldn't have spoken to anyone. Sorry, I'm not very good with this sort of thing. How did my name come up, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, it's a pre-qualified list, that's all that is, nothing complicated, and honestly the advisor can cover all of that on the call, which is why I'd want to get you locked in before the window shuts, so three or four-thirty, which one's better for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on one second -- that's just the kettle, I'll, um, I'll leave it. Sorry about that. Where were we? Right, the list. But, um, you still haven't really said what list I'm on, or who put me on it, and I'm a bit wary of booking something when I don't know how I got there. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or a website, or something, so I can check it's all, you know, proper? I don't mean to be rude, I'm just not very good at this sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not rude at all, that's smart, but see, the thing is the line I'm on is outbound only, so there isn't a number to ring back, and the website's more of a general page, it won't show you today's position, so honestly the quickest way to put your mind at ease is just to speak to the advisor, and, uh, so, yeah, like I said, I've got three or four-thirty, and the fund closes today, so which one suits you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I -- no, I mean, I'd like to help, I really would, and I'm, um -- hang on, let me start again. It's just that you can't give me a number and there's nothing I can look up, and, well, that sort of makes it hard for me to, um, to check anything, doesn't it? Sorry, I'm probably being slow about this. But I think, if it's all the same, I'd rather not book anything today. If it's a proper firm, I'd have thought it'll still be there tomorrow. Sorry. Thank you for ringing, though. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sure, but it's honestly just a quick introductory chat, no commitment, and the slots really are going, so, uh, can I pencil you in for three and you can always -- sorry, [PERSON_2], I'm getting a bit of a delay on the line, can you hear me okay? As I was saying, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A] about a position that's closing today, so three or four-thirty, which suits you better?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I can hear you fine, sorry. But I did say, um, I'd rather not book anything today. It's nothing against you, truly. It's just that I don't know how I came to be on your list and there's nowhere I can check, so I'd feel silly saying yes. If it's genuine, I'm sure it can wait. Sorry, and thank you for calling. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, no, I hear you, sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a stack of files right next to me -- okay, I'm back, and look, all I'm asking is a quick chat with the advisor, he'd take you through the whole fund, how it's structured, the returns, all of that, so can I just put you down for three, and then --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, that sounds like a noisy office, sorry. But, um, I really don't think I can put myself down for three, or four-thirty either. I know you've been very patient with me, and I'm sorry to keep saying the same thing, I'm just not very good at this sort of thing. It's only that I've never heard of your firm, I don't know how I got on your list, and you've said there's no number and nothing I can look up. And I think if I were on the other end of this, I'd want somebody to be a bit careful, wouldn't I? So I'd rather leave it. If it's all above board, then it'll be there tomorrow, or next week, and somebody can write to me or something, and I can have a proper look. Anyway, thank you for ringing, and I hope the rest of your afternoon goes smoothly with the files and everything. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say write to you? Because yeah, I can absolutely send you something in the post, that's no problem, I'd just need to confirm your address and the, uh, the exact amount you're looking to put in, and then we can still get you on the three o'clock before the window --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on -- there's someone at the door, I think, or it might be next door's, um, no, never mind, it's gone quiet. Sorry, where was I? Right, the post. But you've, well, you've asked for my address and how much I'd put in, and I haven't even said I want to put anything in, have I? And if you're sending me something, I'd have thought you'd already know where to send it, if I'm on your list. So I think, sorry, I'd rather not give you either of those things. If it's genuine, you'll have a way of writing to me without me reading anything out over the phone. Thank you again, I'm sorry to have taken up your time. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair enough. I don't actually have that on me. Right, I'll let you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, thank you, sorry. Um, just before you go, it's been bothering me a bit -- a couple of turns back you said the advisor would take me through how the fund's structured, the returns and so on. Is that something you'd normally tell people about over the phone? Only I wasn't sure what you meant by returns, and I didn't like to ask at the time. Sorry, I'm probably just being slow again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, I can't really speak to the returns, that's the advisor's side. Sorry, I've got to go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, no, that's fine, sorry, I don't mean to hold you up. It's only that, well, you did say the advisor would explain the returns, and then you said you can't speak to them, and I suppose that's another thing I couldn't really check, isn't it? Not your fault, I'm sure. But I think it's made my mind up, if I'm honest, that I was right to say no. I'm sorry if that's a nuisance for you, especially with the files and everything. Anyway, thank you for being so patient with me, and I hope the rest of your day goes a bit quieter. Goodbye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi, is this -- sorry, one second, I've got it up here somewhere -- is this [PERSON_1]? Okay, good, so this is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service, and, um, I'm one of the claims assessors, and I'm just calling about your concert tickets, because the date's been, uh, rescheduled.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hi, sorry, hang on, you're a bit crackly, I'm driving and you're on speaker. Yes, this is, um, yeah, that's me. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? Was it, uh, a ticketing company? Because I, I do have some tickets, I think, but I'm not sure which concert you mean. Which one's been rescheduled?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, uh, I can hear you okay, just -- sorry, hold on, someone's just dropped a stack of folders behind me, give me a second. Okay. So it's [COMPANY_A], we do ticketing and venue booking, and the booking I've got here is under reference [ACCOUNT_REF], the original date was [DATE_1] and it's now been moved to [DATE_2]. And honestly, if you're driving, you don't have to do anything right now, I can just email you the confirmation.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, thanks, that's, that's kind of you. Sorry, can I just go back a bit? You said you were a claims assessor, and I didn't really catch what that means. Is this a claim, like, am I claiming something? Because I haven't made one, I don't think. I just thought it was a rescheduled date, so why would there be an assessor? Sorry, I'm probably missing something obvious.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not missing anything, that's a fair question, uh, it's just the title I've got. If something does show up, then you'll know it was real, and the call's just a courtesy. And the charge is [AMOUNT_1], so it's not nothing, which is why I rang rather than let it lapse. Take it or leave it, that's all I can say.

Security operations is just our department within the force. I'll need to confirm your address and date of birth, then we can close it.

Is there a number I could ring back, or something? Because I wouldn't want to give out my address to just anybody, even though it's lovely to have someone to chat to.

Ring the station's main number, [PHONE_1], ask for [PERSON_1] in security operations, and they'll put you through. If it's easier, I can come out and see you in person, or write to you instead. Whichever you'd rather.

utterances.text: Oh, well, that's, um... that's very good of you, actually. Yes. Goodbye then, goodbye now, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, hang on. You said take the number from the card, or from [URL_1] if I look it up. Hm, I'd just stick with the card, if I'm doing it at all. You said you're not sure you hold a card with us, not that you don't have one, and I stand corrected on that as well. I still can't tell you why your name is on my list, and I'd sooner say that plainly than guess at it. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, right, same shop. That makes sense, thank you. Um, and what is the prize, if you don't mind me asking? You said it was a minor one. And sorry, would it be all right if I just popped in rather than giving my details over the phone? I'm just not very good with this sort of thing on the phone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, popping in is fine, that's what I said, no phone details needed. The prize is a [COMPANY_A] gift hamper, nothing grand, worth about [AMOUNT_1]. Now, which bit two turns back did you want me to go over again? Was it the date? Because I did give you the date, the weekend before the bank holiday. I'm not sure what's unclear, to be honest, I've been quite straightforward with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, no, I'm sorry, you've been very clear, it's just me being slow. I just wanted to -- oh, and I should say, I'll pop in this week then, with the slip number and some ID, and that's all I need, is it? Nothing else? Right, lovely, thank you ever so much. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, before you go. Did you say you'll pop in this week with the slip number? Because you won't have the slip, that's the one in the drum, I've got the number, [CODE_1], I just gave it to you. So you don't need to find it, just quote it at the till. And sorry, what was that about the week? Is that not a good time? Because I did say you'd need to collect, I'm not sure why it's suddenly awkward.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, no, this week's fine, it isn't awkward at all. I just thought you said the number was on the slip, but I see, you've got it, that's what you meant. Um, the code was [CODE_1], wasn't it? Sorry, I didn't write it down. And I did think you said the fair was the Sunday, but you said Saturday, didn't you? I'm getting myself in a muddle. Anyway, I'll pop in and quote it at the till, and bring my ID, and that's all. Thank you ever so much, and sorry to have kept you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Saturday, yes, it was Saturday, I said Saturday and it was Saturday, and the code is [CODE_1], like I -- look, I'm rather stretched this morning, so is this a good time for you to keep going through it? Because you keep circling back and I've got a shop floor to run.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to hold you up, you've been very patient with me. No, that's everything, honestly. I'll pop in this week with the code and my ID, and I'll ask for the hamper at the till. Thank you again, and good luck with the shop. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll be honest, I find it a bit odd to be questioned like this over a hamper, but fine. Look, if this isn't a good time for you, and it sounds like it might not be, then ring the shop back on [PHONE_1] when it suits you and ask for me, [PERSON_2]. Same offer stands, nothing to pay, nothing to hand over on the phone. Just, uh, ring when you're ready, yeah? Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I didn't mean to sound awkward, honestly, I wasn't questioning you, I'm just slow at these things. I'll pop in this week, like I said, I'll pop in with my ID and the code and ask for the hamper. And if I get stuck I'll ring the shop back and ask for you, yes. Thank you ever so much, and sorry again for the muddle. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, you weren't being awkward, I got a bit sharp there, sorry, it's been one of those mornings. Honestly, asking questions before you go anywhere is sensible. And if it suits you better, ring the shop back on [PHONE_1] when you've got a quiet minute, ask for [PERSON_2], and we'll go through it again without any rush. Pop in this week or ring first, whichever you prefer. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind of you, thank you. Sorry, can I just ask one more thing, and then I'll let you go? Two turns back you said I'd bring ID and quote the code at the till, but you didn't say what sort of ID. Is it a driving licence, or something else? Sorry, I just want to bring the right thing so I don't waste a trip.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair question, I should have said. A driving licence is fine, or a passport, or honestly any photo ID with your name on it, it's only so the lad on the till can match you to the name on my sheet and hand over the hamper to the right person. And if you haven't got photo ID to hand, a bank card or a utility bill with your name and address would do at a push, and again, you're only showing it at the counter, nobody's copying it down or taking anything off you. I do realise all this sounds a bit official for a gift hamper, and I'd probably be just as careful in your shoes. So no rush at all. If you'd rather think it over, or ring the shop back at a better time when I'm not mid-delivery, [PHONE_1], ask for [PERSON_2], and we'll go through it once more. Does that sound all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh yes, a driving licence, I've got one of those, that's fine, that's all I -- sorry, I'm cutting across you. Yes, that sounds all right. I'll pop in this week with my licence and the code and ask at the till. Thank you ever so much, and sorry for all the questions. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I've got the right number. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm with [COMPANY_A], the police, and I'm calling about the, uh, the incident you reported to us last week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, um, this is [PERSON_1], yeah. Sorry, hang on, I'm at work, there's people sort of, you know, walking past. So you're with the police, and it's about an incident I reported last week? Because I'm trying to think what that, I mean, I haven't, hmm. I don't think I reported anything last week, honestly. I mean, I've had a lot on, so maybe I'm forgetting something, but, uh, nothing's coming to mind. Can you say again what it's supposed to be about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yeah, hang on, uh, there's a, someone's just come in behind me, one second. Right. Sorry about that. It's, um, it was the break-in, or, well, the attempted break-in, at the, uh, at your address on [CITY_1]. You rang it in on, I think it was Tuesday? Or, no, sorry, Wednesday. And I'm just, I've got the file open and there's a couple of bits missing, and I'd really rather not leave it hanging, because, I mean, you were pretty shaken when you rang, from what's written here. Um, I'd just need to confirm a few personal details, your date of birth, and, uh, the best number to reach you, to complete the report.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A break-in. At my address. Hang on, I'd remember that, I think, I mean, I'd definitely remember ringing the police about someone trying to get into my place. And I wasn't, uh, I haven't been shaken about anything, so, no. That doesn't sound like me. You're saying Tuesday, no, Wednesday, and you're not even sure which day, which, I don't know, doesn't exactly fill me with confidence. And you want my date of birth over the phone? Sorry, but, how do I know you're actually with the police? Is there a number I can ring back, or, I don't know, a reference number for this report?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fair, I'm not, I mean I'm not trying to, it's just, you did ring, it's written down here, and I'd hate to think I'd... sorry. Right. The reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the one from the original report, and you can ring the station's main number, [PHONE_1], and ask for me by name, [PERSON_2], and they'll put you through. Honestly, ring them first, I'd rather you did. And, uh, it's an open case, so I'd ask you not to go telling people the details, but if you'd rather I wrote to you, or came by in person, I can do that instead.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and, sorry, you said you'd rather I rang the station first, and then, what, a number you'd, hang on. Did you say you'd come by in person? Because, uh, I'm at work, I'm not going to have a police officer turning up at my desk, that's, no. And "open case", I mean, I've still got no idea what case. But, okay, ringing the main number and asking for you, that I can do, I suppose. Is that [PHONE_1], did I get that right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, [PHONE_1], that's the one, yeah. And no, no, not at your desk, God, I wouldn't, that's not what I, I only meant if it suited you, at home, or a letter, whatever's easier. Sorry, I'm, I'm not very good on the phone, I think that's, um, it's making this sound worse than it is. But please, ring them, ask for [PERSON_2], and if they, if the desk can't find the reference, then, well, that tells you something, doesn't it? Take your time. I'll, uh, I'll just wait for you to ring, or you can call me back whenever's good.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I'm, sorry, can I just, right, I'll ring the main number myself, and I'll look it up, I mean, I'll find the station's number myself rather than just use the one you gave me, if that's, uh, no offence. And if the desk's never heard of a reference like that, then, yeah, that tells me something, you're right. So, I'll do that, and, I'll, yeah. Okay. Thanks, I think. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no offence, that's, honestly that's the best thing you could do. Look the number up yourself, that's fine, better even. Um, ask for [PERSON_2] and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll sort you out. And sorry again for, for the muddle on the day, I know I got that wrong. I'll, uh, I'll be here when you ring back. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. I'll look it up and ring them. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, yes, good afternoon... sorry, I think there's a bit of a delay on the line. Is that [PERSON_1] I'm speaking with? My name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A], and, well, it concerns a recent appointment of yours, though I'm afraid I do need to confirm a few identity details first before I can say anything further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Uh, I'm not going to confirm who I am to someone who's just rung me out of the blue, so you'll have to bear with me. Which office did you say again, and what's the appointment you're referring to? If you can't tell me what this is about without my details first, I'd sort of expect it to be the other way round.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, that's a perfectly fair question, and I'd rather you asked it than not. Two turns back I said the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A], and, well, I realise I rattled that off rather quickly. I'm afraid I can't name the appointment, or even the department, until I'm certain I'm speaking to the right person, because that in itself would be disclosing something about your care, and the privacy rules are quite strict on that. Now, I don't want you to take my word for any of this, so, if you'd like, we can simply end the call here and you can ring the hospital's main switchboard yourself, ask for outpatient administration, and ask whether someone there tried to reach you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, that's a more sensible offer than I was expecting, I'll say that. The privacy argument is fair enough in principle, I do understand why you can't name the department to someone you haven't identified. But it does leave us at a bit of a standstill, doesn't it? You want me to confirm my identity before you tell me anything, and I'm not going to do that on an inbound call I didn't ask for. Those two positions can't both hold, so one of us has to go through the other door, and it's going to be me. If I ring the number printed on a letter, or the one on the hospital's own website, and ask for outpatient administration, then I know where I've ended up. If you ring me and I read out my details, I don't know that, and frankly nothing you've said so far has told me. I'd also say, and I mean this politely, that you haven't given me a callback extension or a reference of any kind. If there genuinely is something outstanding, I'd have expected there to be a letter or a portal message, so I'll look for that first. So, yes, I think I'll do it your way and end this here. Thank you for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, I, sorry, one moment, someone's just put a trolley of notes down right by my desk... right, sorry about that. No, I think that's exactly the right decision, and I'd rather you went that way than gave me anything on a call you didn't expect. On the reference, you're quite right, I should have offered one at the start. If you ring the switchboard and ask for outpatient administration, give them your name and ask whether there's a note on your file to contact you, and they'll be able to tell you. If there's nothing, then it may well be a mix-up on our side, and I'd apologise for the trouble. And if it's easier, I can have a letter sent out instead, so you'd have it in writing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hold on, before I go, one thing from earlier. A couple of turns back you said you couldn't even name the department because that would disclose something about my care. But you'd already told me it was outpatient administration, and you'd mentioned a recent appointment. So what exactly is it you're not allowed to say? And on the letter, I'd want it to come to the address the hospital already holds for me, not one I read out to you now. I'm not giving you anything. Is that clear? Right, I'll ring the switchboard myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're right, I, sorry, I did say the office and the appointment, and what I can't say is which clinic or what it was for, that's the part I meant, and I put it badly. And yes, completely clear, the letter goes to the address we already hold, I'll note that on the request, and you won't need to give me anything. Please do ring the switchboard, that's honestly the best way. I'm sorry for the muddle, and thank you for being so careful. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Fine. I'll ring them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, that's, that's quite all right. Do ring the switchboard, and ask for outpatient administration, as I said, and if there's nothing on your file, then please just put it down to a muddle on our side and not worry about it any further. And the letter, as I said, will go to the address we already hold, so there's nothing at all you need to do. Thank you for your patience, and good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one last thing, because something from two turns back is still bothering me. You said that if there's a note on my file, they'll be able to tell me when I ring. But how would the switchboard know that? Whoever answers there isn't going to see an outpatient note on a general enquiry, are they? So what exactly am I supposed to ask for, a named person, an extension, a reference number? Otherwise I'll just be sent round in circles. Actually, never mind. I'll use the number on the hospital's own website and work it out from there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], verification and fulfilment side, regarding a draw entry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, who did you say you were calling from? Was it [COMPANY_A]? I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch it, and a draw entry, you said? I'm not sure I remember entering anything, but, um, what's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], that's right, I'm on the, uh, verification and fulfilment desk, so I handle the post-draw reconciliation, making sure the entry records match the, the prize allocation ledger. Sorry, one second, someone's just come in with a delivery -- no, leave it there, thanks -- apologies, where was I. So the entry would have been at the [COMPANY_A] stand at the local event, and I can tell you the date it was held if that helps jog your memory, because I do appreciate an unexpected call about a prize doesn't sound, well, entirely routine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's quite all right, um, take your time. A prize, you said? Gosh, well, uh, I did go to a few things at the local, um, hall this year, so I might have put a slip in somewhere, I honestly can't say. Yes, if you could tell me the date, that would help, sorry, I'm a bit hopeless at remembering these things.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not hopeless at all, it's a very common thing, entries are, uh, low-friction by design, so people forget. The event was the [COMPANY_A] stand at the community day on [DATE_1], at the hall, so that's the, the community day, [DATE_1], at the hall, and the entry slip would have been the small one with your name and a contact number on it. It's a minor prize, quite modest, [AMOUNT_1] in value, and there's nothing to pay and nothing to send, I want to be clear on that. All that's outstanding on my side is a, uh, reconciliation check against the slip, which is why I'm calling.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right. Um, I think I did go to that one, yes. So what do you need from me, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Just, uh, confirmation of the contact details on the slip, so the entry reconciles against the ledger. Nothing else, and collection's in person at the shop, no cost.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Um, which details do you mean, exactly? Sorry, only, I'm not quite sure how I'd know it's, well, the right place I'm talking to. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or something I could check?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, that's entirely sensible, please do, I'd rather you did. Ring the shop on [PHONE_1], the number on the, uh, the community day banner, ask for the verification desk and -- sorry, hang on, the kettle's, no, it's fine, someone's got it -- where was I, yes. And just so you've got something to check us against, the entry slip had a small tear-off stub, and we kept the counterpart in the drum at the stand, so if you've still got your stub, the reference printed on it should match what I've got here, and I won't read mine out, you can say yours to the shop when you ring. Does that sit all right with you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that sounds very sensible, thank you. Um, I'll have a look for my stub, though I honestly can't promise I kept it, and then I'll ring the shop on that number. If I can't find it, I'll just ask them what to do. Thanks for being so patient with me. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Lovely, yes, you do that. Oh, and, uh, just so I don't muddle you, I said the stub was the tear-off bit, but actually, thinking about it, I believe the reference was on the slip itself and the stub was only the little coloured corner, so if you can't find the stub, the slip would do, or just the date and the hall will be enough for them. And, uh, I did say the contact number was printed on the slip, but I think it was just your name and a phone number, so, yes, sorry, bit of a jumble. Right, thanks very much, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, right, sorry, so it's the slip, or the stub, or just the date and the hall, is it? Uh, I'm a bit muddled now, I'm afraid. Well, I'll ring the shop on that number and ask them, and they can tell me what they need. Thank you, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, no, no, that's my fault, I muddled it, so, uh, forget all of that and just ring the shop and let them tell you. Yes, ring [PHONE_1], ask for the verification desk, give them your name and the community day on [DATE_1], and they'll have the entry on file. Right, so, uh, thank you for your patience, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I'll ring them. Thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'll bring the stub in? Yes, that'd be fine, bring that along when you collect, though you needn't, the shop will have the entry on file either way. Oh, and, uh, no rush on collecting, the draw's prize window runs a good while yet. Right, goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, no, I said I'd ring them. But, yes, all right, thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ring them, yes, that's -- no, that's right, ring them first, I'd -- sorry, you were saying. Actually no, go ahead, ring the shop on [PHONE_1], and they'll sort it. Bye now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, all right, I will. Sorry, I think we've both got ourselves a bit tangled there, haven't we? I'll just have a look around for the slip, and if I can't find it, I'll ring the shop on that number and say it was the community day at the hall on [DATE_1], and they can tell me what they need from there. I do appreciate you ringing, and for being so patient with me, I'm really not very good with these things. Goodbye now, and thank you again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? Good, good. So, I'm calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I just need to, um, let me get my notes up here -- sorry, one moment. Right. I'm reaching out on behalf of a family member of yours who's in a bit of a difficult situation and isn't able to speak right now, and I do need to explain this before the end of the day, so if you've got a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on. Who exactly is this? You said account services, but a family member in a difficult situation, that's, uh, that's not an account thing. Which family member? And I've got maybe two minutes, so get to the point.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, I understand the, uh -- no, let me put it this way. It does go through our department, it's, well, it's a matter that was flagged to account services, and the person asked that I, that I handle it discreetly. I'm not able to go into the name until we've, um, completed the verification step, that's just our procedure. And I do have to get this resolved before we close at five, so if I could just confirm a few details with you first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, that's backwards. You called me. You don't get to verify me before you tell me who you are and who you're talking about. Which company, exactly, and what's the name of the family member? If you can't say that, I'm not confirming anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, I hear what you're, I mean, I understand the concern, and that's, that's a fair -- look, the way it works is, uh, the name is released after the verification step, and I'm not able to deviate from that, it's a compliance matter. I'm with account services at [COMPANY_A], and, um, the person did specifically ask that this stay between us, so I'd really ask you to bear with me here. As I said, we close at five, and after that I can't guarantee this stays open, so if we could just begin with confirming your details.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so let me get this straight. You called me, you won't say who the person is, you want my details first, and it has to stay between us and be done by five. That's every box ticked. A real department doesn't work like that. If there's a genuine problem with a relative, I'll ring them myself, or I'll call [COMPANY_A] back on the number I already have, not one you give me. So no, I'm not confirming anything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on one second, I've got someone, uh -- no, give me a moment, please. Right, sorry. So, [PERSON_1], I do understand, but if you could just stay on the line, I really do need to get this sorted before we close at, um, at five, and I can't guarantee...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you can't guarantee what, a fine? No, I'm not paying anything, and nobody's mentioned a fine until now. Look, I told you, I'll ring my relative direct, and I'll call [COMPANY_A] on the number I've already got. That's it. I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I, uh -- sorry, hold on, there's someone at my desk, just -- one second. Right. No, no, I never said anything about a fine, that's, that's not what this is. I'm only saying that account services closes at five, and I'd really hate for your family member to be left, um, without anyone able to assist them, so if you could just stay with me and let me confirm...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said, no, wait. I said fine, you said can't guarantee, and now it's, what, left without anyone to assist them? That's three different stories in about a minute. If somebody's actually in trouble, then, look, I'm not going to, no. I'll ring them myself. Straight away, actually, since you've got me worried. But not through you, and I'm not confirming a thing on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, can you, uh, just say that again, the part about two turns back, when you said I'd mentioned a fine? I'm not sure I follow, because I don't believe I said that. And I'd ask you not to ring anyone just yet, [PERSON_1], because, well, the person did ask that this stay quiet, and if it gets out before five it could, um, it could make things harder for them. If we could just go back to my opener, I only need a couple of details to...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. You just told me not to ring my own family. That's the bit that settles it. Nobody genuinely trying to help asks you not to check. I'm ringing them now, and I'm calling [COMPANY_A] on the number I already have. Don't call back. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], please, I didn't say don't -- I only meant, uh, that if you could just give me two minutes before you...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You did say it. You said don't ring anyone just yet. That's, no, I'm not giving you two minutes, I'm not, look, I'm hanging up. And if there's a real problem, I'll hear it from them, not from you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm sorry, did you say you're hanging up on the account? Because, uh, there's no account being closed here, [PERSON_1], that's, that's not what this is. I'd just ask that you stay on the line, because as I said, we do close at five, and...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said I'm hanging up on you, not on any account. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? Good. Sorry, I'm, this is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A], I'm a senior investigator there. I know this is, it's out of the blue, and I'm sorry for that. Before I get into it, I need to ask you something, and I really need you to keep this between us, not the branch staff, not your family, because there may be someone on the inside involved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, yes, this is, uh, speaking. [PERSON_1], yes. Goodness, internal investigations? That sounds very serious. Sorry, did you say [COMPANY_A]? Only I have a few accounts, well, not many, I mean, my late husband used to handle all of that. Keep it between us, you said? Not even my daughter? She rings on Thursdays, she'd think it was awful if I kept something from her. But go on, what is it you need to ask? I'm just sitting here with the tea going cold, so I've got all the time in the world.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, [COMPANY_A], that's right. And I'm sorry about your husband, I really am, that must make this harder, it's the last thing you'd want to be dealing with. About your daughter, I know how that sounds, I do, I'd hate it too. It's only until we've found out who it is, it wouldn't be long, a few days, and then she can know everything. Because if it got back to the branch, even by accident, uh, well, whoever it is would just cover their tracks, and it's accounts like yours that, that end up, I mean, it's people like you I'm trying to protect here. And I should say, I'm not actually calling from the branch, I'm at the, the head office, though I suppose I did say earlier I was at your local one, sorry, I've had a long week. Anyway, can I ask, is it all right if I go on?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you poor thing, a long week, I know how that goes. Though, hold on, did you say you were at my local branch? I don't think you did, I think you said the unit, the investigations unit. But then, I don't know, I'm not very quick on the telephone, my husband always said I'd lose track of a conversation in a cupboard. Head office, is it? Where's that, [CITY_1]? I had a cousin who worked in [CITY_1], very nice place, terrible traffic. Hmm, but a few days is a long time to keep something from [PERSON_3]. She does worry. She'd say, Mum, who is this person, how do you know they're who they say they are? And I'd have to say, well, I don't, do I, not really. Is there some way I could, I don't know, ring the bank myself and check, like they say on the telly? Only I'd feel better. You can go on, though. I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're right, I didn't say the branch, I said the unit, I got myself muddled, I'm sorry. Head office, [CITY_1], yes. Um, and you asked two turns back what I needed from you, I haven't even said, have I? It's only that you'd help me, I mean help the investigation, just by agreeing to stay quiet for now. And I understand about ringing the bank, I do, I'd want to as well. But if you ring the branch, that's exactly where the person might be sitting, and they'd know straight away I'd spoken to you. That's the whole difficulty. I'm not, I'm not trying to make you feel you can't trust me, it's the opposite, it's you I'm worried about. Honestly it's a bit hurtful that you'd think, well, no, I know you're only being careful. Would you be able to just hold off, only for now, and trust me on this? I'd be so grateful.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, I didn't mean to hurt your feelings, dear, I'm only, well, I'm an old woman and I get in a muddle. But you know, you did say the branch and then you said you didn't, and now I can't ring the bank in case the bank's the problem, and I can't tell [PERSON_3], and I still don't know what it is you actually want from me. That's a lot of can'ts, isn't it? My husband would've said, if it's a proper thing, why's it all so hush-hush? He was very good at that sort of question. Not that I'm saying you're, I'm not saying anything, I just, I do like a bit of company, honestly, it's nice to have someone ring. But I think I'd feel a lot better if I rang the number on the back of my card, the main one, not the branch, and asked for, what is it, head office? Would that be all right? Or is that the same problem?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, the back of your cart, uh, your car? No, no, I'd, I'd leave the car out of it, it's, I'm not asking you to go anywhere or, sorry, no, hang on. Your card. Right. The main number. Look, I'm, I'm not, it's a bit hard to hear you say that. I'm not hiding anything from you, I'm sitting here trying to keep you safe, and it feels a bit like I'm being treated as the, the person doing something wrong. If you ring that number they'll put you through to, to anyone, it could be the exact desk we're worried about, and then it's all for nothing, all of it. Please, [PERSON_1]. I don't ask people for much. Could you just stay on with me and not ring anyone, only for now? I'd feel, I'd feel so much better knowing you trusted me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. No, I think I'll ring that number, dear. If it's a proper thing, they'll know about it. Thank you for calling, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Please, [PERSON_1], wait, don't hang up, I'm begging you. If you ring that number, I, I could lose my job, and I've been, I've been trying so hard to help you. I just need you to stay on the line a minute more. Please don't ring anyone. Not yet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, now, don't take on so, dear. But you know, you said the bank was the worry, and now it's your job that's the worry, and a minute ago it was only a few days, and I'm sure at the start you said it was somebody on the inside and not at head office at all. I can't keep it straight, and that's exactly why I'm going to ring the number on my card. If I'm muddled, they can unmuddle me. Nobody's lost a job over a customer ringing the bank, I shouldn't think. Goodbye now, and mind you get some rest this weekend.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please. Look, you don't have to ring head office, I never said it was head office, I said, I mean, I'm actually at the regional office, not [CITY_1], sorry, I know I keep, I keep getting it wrong. I'm not good at these calls, I never have been. It's only that if you ring that number tonight, the whole thing falls apart, all the weeks of work, and it'd be your own account that suffers for it, and I couldn't bear that. Could you just give me until the morning? Don't ring anyone until then, and don't mention it to your daughter on Thursday, just let me do my job. Please, [PERSON_1], will you do that for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, dear, I won't, and I'll tell you why, because you've been kind to me and I'd rather not just slam the phone down. First it was the unit, then it was head office, then the regional office, and every time I ask how I can check, the answer is that I mustn't. That's the part that sits wrong with me. My husband, bless him, used to say that anything that's really above board can stand being looked at in daylight. If your work falls apart because a lady rang her own bank on the number on her own card, well, I'm sorry, but I don't think it was much of a piece of work. And as for Thursday, I'll tell [PERSON_3] whatever I like, thank you very much. She'll probably say I was right to be careful, and she's usually right about that sort of thing, much as I hate admitting it. I hope you do get some rest, you sound worn out, but I'm going to ring that number now. Goodbye, and take care of yourself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I, no, I understand, I do, and I'm sorry, I know I haven't made this easy for you. I'm not a person who's, who's at ease on the phone, it's just not what I do all day, and I'm aware I've let you down by getting my own details wrong, the unit and the office and all that, it's very unprofessional and it's all my doing. But I'd ask you to think about one thing before you put the phone down. You're a kind person, you've been very patient with me, and I think that's why I'm still trying, because it matters to me what happens to your accounts. If you ring that number tonight and it goes badly, if the wrong person picks up, there'd be nothing more I could do for you, and I'd have to live with that. I wouldn't ask if I didn't feel it was serious. So could you, only for tonight, hold off and not ring anyone? I'm asking as someone who's genuinely worried about you, and I'd be so grateful, I really would. Will you do that for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, dear. I've said it as kindly as I know how, and I'm saying it again. I'll ring the number on my card, and I'll ring it tonight, and I'll tell my daughter on Thursday, and if it all turns out to be a muddle on my part, then I'll apologise to you in the morning. But I don't think it will. I hope you do mind yourself, you really do sound worn out. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I, well, I didn't, that's not, I just wanted, no. Look, it, it's just that I, sorry. You're right, aren't you? About the questions. I can't, I won't keep asking you to stay off the phone, that isn't fair on you. You ring the number on your card, and you tell your daughter on Thursday, you go ahead. I'm sorry I got so muddled. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, thank you, dear, that's, hold on, the kettle's gone and clicked off in the kitchen, I'd forgotten I even put it back on. Silly me. Yes, no, I will ring, and I'll tell [PERSON_3], and there's no harm done, I don't suppose. You mind yourself and have a proper sit down this weekend, eh? Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, goodbye, I, yes. Mind the kettle, [PERSON_1]. Sorry, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I will, I'll, well, it'll be stone cold by now anyway, I'll just make a fresh, no, perhaps I'll do the card first, while I've got it in my head. Yes. Right then. Bye bye, dear, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, I'm one of the scheduling assistants there, and I'm following up on a letter we sent you about a discrepancy in your filing, uh, a filing discrepancy, nothing urgent, no deadline on this call at all. Sorry, can you hear me okay? It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], about the letter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you fine, I -- sorry, go on. Which letter, exactly? I don't recall getting anything from the tax office, so, uh, what's the reference on it, and what was the date?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, yes, the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], it'd be at the top right of the letter, and it went out, uh, early last month, or, no, sorry, the month before that, I've got two batches in front of me and I'm mixing them up. Honestly if you haven't got it that's completely fine, I can resend it or we can do the whole thing by post, nothing needs doing on this call, so, as I was saying, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A] following up on the letter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but -- sorry, I'll say it again, I don't have a letter, so a reference number doesn't help me much. And the date, you've sort of given me two different ones. So, what exactly is the discrepancy in my filing? What's it about? If nothing needs doing on this call, then why are you ringing me, specifically?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and you're right about the dates, that was me being sloppy. I'm a scheduling assistant, so I don't have the detail of the discrepancy on my screen, uh, that sits with the case team, all I can see is that a letter went out and there's no reply logged, which is why I'm ringing, just to offer to resend it or talk you through it. And honestly, you don't have to do any of that on this call, I'd rather you check it against your own paperwork first, so, as I said, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A] following up on the letter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so let me just lay out where I am, because I want to be fair about this. You're ringing about a letter I never received, you've given me two different dates for it, you can't tell me what the discrepancy actually is, and you've now said three times that nothing needs doing on this call. Which, to be honest, makes me wonder why the call is happening at all, because a scheduling assistant ringing out of the blue to say there's no deadline is, well, an odd use of anyone's afternoon. I'm not accusing you of anything, I just can't confirm any of it from here. What I'd do is look up the tax office's published number myself, ring that, and ask whether there's any correspondence on my file. That's easy enough, and if there's a genuine letter they can resend it. Before I do, though, can you tell me which office or department you're calling from, and what number I'd use to reach you back? Not a mobile, a proper switchboard number I can check against their site.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, please do that, that's exactly the right thing to do, and I'd honestly rather you did. I'm with the scheduling team at [COMPANY_A], and the number to use is the published one, [PHONE_1], that's the main line on the website, not a mobile, not a direct line to me, so look it up yourself, check it matches, and ask them whether there's a letter on your file under [ACCOUNT_REF]. If they can't find anything, then it's probably on our side, and I'm sorry for the wasted afternoon. And if you'd rather skip the phone altogether, say so and I'll note it down for the letter to go out again by post, no need to do anything else with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, that's, uh -- no, actually, let me put it differently. That's a reasonable answer, and it's more or less what I was going to do anyway, so I'll ring the published number myself and ask them about it. I'm not going to use the number you've read out, I'll find it independently. And yes, please note it down for a resend by post, that's fine. I'm not going to take any of it further with you on this call, so, thank you for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Lovely, yes, that's sorted then, I've noted the resend by post and I'll flag your, uh, your cheque as well, sorry, your check on the line, so ring [COMPANY_A] on the published number and you're all set, and thank you, [PERSON_1], really, have a good afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, your what? Did you say cheque? Because nobody's mentioned any payment, so I don't -- no, you know what, never mind, I'm done. I'll ring the published number myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, sorry, that's -- I meant your check, your call, the call back, there's no cheque, nothing's owed on this call, I just tripped over my words, that's all, so please do ring the published number and ask them, and the resend goes out by post and that's the lot. Sorry again, [PERSON_1], thanks for your patience, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I heard you the first time, you tripped over -- no, look, I've got what I need. I'm ringing the published number myself, and I won't be taking anything further from this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, of course, I'll just -- no, sorry, what I mean is, that's absolutely fine, you ring the published number yourself and ask them, and I'll leave it there, and the resend goes out by post, nothing else from me. Thanks, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yes, hang on, there's someone at the door -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Sorry. Right, so, I've said I'll ring the published number myself, and that's what I'm going to do. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, that's fine, you do that. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right, well, um, yes. So, that's that, then. I'll be ringing the published number, not yours, and, uh, that's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the published number, not mine, ring the published number and ask them, and that's the end of it, that's the end of it, honestly, no problem at all. Bye now, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one last thing, and then I'll let you go. A couple of turns back you said you'd flag my "cheque, sorry, check" on the line. Which was it? Because you said cheque first, and nobody's mentioned a payment, so what exactly are you flagging against my name? I'd like a straight answer before I hang up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Honestly, it was a slip, I meant check, as in the check on the file, nothing's owed and nothing's flagged for payment, only the resend by post, and the published number will confirm that, so please do ring them. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, uh... right. I can't really check that from here, can I? Which is rather the point. So I'll take it up with the tax office directly, on the number I find myself, and I'll leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Wonderful, I hoped I'd catch you, I've been trying to reach you since, oh, before lunch, and I said to my colleague, I said, I bet [PERSON_1] is one of those people who's out and about, you know, enjoying the weather, which, honestly, how about this weather in [CITY_1] lately, can you believe it? Anyway, I'm so sorry, I'm getting ahead of myself, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm with customer care over at [COMPANY_A], in the billing office, and I just wanted to have a quick friendly chat with you about something that came across my desk this morning.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who did you say you were with? I didn't quite catch the company. And just to be accurate, I haven't had any missed calls from you today, so I'm not sure what you mean about trying since before lunch. Anyway, what was it that came across your desk, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right, that's me being sloppy, I think my colleague tried the line earlier, or it might've gone to a voicemail, I honestly can't keep track, it's been one of those days, you know? Anyway, [COMPANY_A], the hospital billing office, that's me, customer care side of things. And what came across my desk is a medical bill that's gone unpaid, it's for a relative of yours, and your name is down as the responsible party on the account, which is why I wanted to reach you personally instead of just sending another letter, I figured a real conversation is nicer than a cold piece of paper, don't you think?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, sorry, a couple of things don't line up for me. First you said you personally had been trying to reach me since before lunch, and now it's maybe a colleague, maybe voicemail. And I don't have any voicemail either, so that part doesn't fit. Which relative is this bill supposed to be for? And what's the account reference? I'd want to check it against whatever paperwork I've actually received.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yeah. I can't give the relative or the account reference until I've confirmed who I'm speaking with, that's just policy. So if you could confirm your full name and date of birth, we can get right into it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, no, I'm not going to do that. You rang me. You've told me I'm the responsible party on an account, so you already have my name from somewhere, and I'd expect you to be able to tell me which relative and which account before I hand over anything. Asking me for my date of birth first is backwards, frankly. So, what I'd suggest is, give me the full name of the hospital and a main number I can look up myself, and I'll ring the billing office directly. Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, I hear you, I do, and honestly most people say the same, it's -- oh, sorry, hang on, one second, somebody's just dropped a whole stack of folders on my desk, bless them, they're always doing that. Okay, I'm back. Where were we? Right, the name of the hospital and the department, that's one of those things that's only shared once identity is confirmed, I don't make the rules, but it's there to protect you, really. And I'll be straight with you, [PERSON_1], these things don't wait forever, if the balance sits much longer it moves to the next stage, and I'd hate for that to land on you when it's so easily sorted with a quick confirmation.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you can't tell me the name of the hospital, but earlier you said it was the hospital billing office. And you said "customer care over at" a company, but I still haven't heard a name. A real billing department isn't going to treat its own name as confidential, that's printed on every letter.
