And "next stage" is vague, what stage, exactly? I'm not confirming anything on this call. If the debt's genuine, there'll be a letter and a number I can look up, so I'll deal with it that way. Thanks, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, don't hang up, [PERSON_1], please, it's really nothing to be worried about, I'm just trying to help you out here. And I did say the name earlier, I'm sure I did, it's [COMPANY_A], and honestly it's not a hospital as such, it's more the outside billing arm, so I think that's where the wires got crossed. Look, I can't give you a number, that's not how we do it, but if I just pop your date of birth down, that clears the whole thing up in two minutes and nobody's any the wiser, so shall we just do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. You've changed it again, now it's an outside billing arm, not the hospital, and "nobody's any the wiser" isn't something a genuine billing office says. I'm not giving you my date of birth. If there's a real debt, put it in writing with the account details and I'll deal with it that way. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, hang on, sorry, that's the door, somebody's just walked in with the post, give me one tick -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Honestly, I think we've got our wires crossed, [PERSON_1], and that's on me, I do talk in circles when it's been a long day, ha. I'm not trying to trip you up. Letters, sure, that's fine, we send those out, but if it's sitting there unpaid and you'd rather not have it escalate, it's so much easier if we just get that one small thing confirmed now, don't you think?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I don't think it's easier, and I'll tell you why, since you've asked twice now. Over the course of this call you've given me three different accounts of who you are. First it was customer care at a company I never heard named, then the hospital billing office, then an outside billing arm. You couldn't say who tried to reach me earlier, and you wouldn't name the relative, the account, or the organisation without my date of birth first. Then you reminded me about escalation, and said nobody would be any the wiser. Each of those on its own might be an off day, but all together it's a pattern I recognise, so I'm not going to be argued out of it by you being friendly. I'm not confirming my date of birth or anything else today. If there's a genuine balance, it will exist in writing, with a named creditor and an account reference I can check independently, and I'll contact them on a number I find myself. If it escalates in the meantime, then it escalates, and I'll deal with it through proper channels. That's my final answer, so I'll say goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, fair enough, that's your call and I'm not going to fight you on it, honestly. Just, uh, before you go, can I ask you to clarify one thing from a couple of minutes back? You said you'd contact them on a number you find yourself, and that's fine, but which number were you planning to look up, exactly? Only because if it's one off an old statement or something, it might not even route to the right department, and then you'd be going round in circles, and I'd hate that for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, I'm not going to tell you which number I'd use, that's rather the point of looking it up myself. And I'll say, I wasn't planning on an old statement, I said I'd find one independently, so the creditor's own website or whatever a real letter turns out to carry. Also, you've told me twice now that you didn't name the company, but a minute ago you said you did say it earlier. I can't keep your versions straight. Right, I'm ending this here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, alright. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say "good price"? No, hang on, I don't think I heard that right. Doesn't matter. I'm not interested in any price, and I'm not giving you anything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with the account holder for the [COMPANY_A] service at this address? This is [PERSON_1], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling regarding an urgent line fault we've flagged on your connection. We're seeing some, uh, fairly significant attenuation on your local loop, so I just need a few minutes of your time to get it sorted before it escalates to a full outage.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yeah, that's me, I think. Sorry, I've got you on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the flower beds. A fault, you said?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, a fault, that's right, though I'd say it's less of a fault and more of a, um, degradation in signal integrity on the upstream side. Our monitoring picked it up about, oh, three weeks ago, or actually it was flagged overnight, but either way it's reached the threshold where we need to act today. No need to put the trowel down on my account, it's really just a quick diagnostic on the router, and I'd like to run it with you while I have you on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, the trowel's fine, it's more of a weeding day anyway. Um, but hang on, you said three weeks ago and then overnight, which, which is it? I mean, the internet's been fine for me, honestly, the telly streams fine, my daughter video calls from [CITY_1] every Sunday and no complaints. So how would I even know if there's something wrong? And sorry, who did you say you were again? Was it a name and then the company?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_1], with [COMPANY_A], verification department. And, ah, the streaming being fine, yes, that's actually quite common, the degradation sits upstream so it doesn't always show on the downstream side, which is what your telly and your daughter's calls are using. You said the trowel was a weeding day, so no, absolutely no need to stop, I'd just want you near the router at some point so we can run the diagnostic together. Do you have the router somewhere close to hand?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, it's in the hall, right by the front door, so not far, I'm just out the back. But hold on a sec, because I want to get this straight in my head. You said it was three weeks, then overnight, and you still haven't really said which, and now it's upstream, which I don't really understand, because I've never heard of that. I'm not very technical, I can do the basics, like I can restart the router and I managed to set up the smart plug in the kitchen last winter, but that's about my limit. So, um, what would this diagnostic actually involve? Like what would I be doing, and what would you be doing? And is there some way I can check you're really with [COMPANY_A]? Because my daughter's always telling me to be careful, you know, with calls out of the blue, and I'd feel a bit daft if I just went along with it and then it turned out to be nothing. I'm not saying it is, I just, I'd like to know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, I understand, but if I could just -- the diagnostic is a standard line integrity sweep, it's fully automated on our side, and all I'd need from you is a brief session on the router interface so the, uh, provisioning layer can complete the handshake. And as for verifying me, I mean, I've already given you my name and my department, which is really all the verification we can do over a live call, and I'd prefer not to go round in circles on it, because the longer this sits unresolved, the more likely it is to drop your service entirely, possibly this evening, and then you're looking at a, a considerably more involved repair.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh, so a, a brief session on the router, right. Sorry, did you say a repair, like a repairman coming out? Because I've got my sister staying Thursday and Friday, so I'd have to sort a day, and I'd want to know if there's a charge for that, because I'm not made of money, ha. But hang on, that's not really what I asked, is it? I asked how I check you're really [COMPANY_A], and you said your name and department is all you can do, and that doesn't sound right to me, because anyone could say a name. Couldn't I just ring the number on my bill and ask them about it? That's what my daughter would say. Would that be all right, or would that mess you up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, it wouldn't mess me up as such, but I'd really ask you not to, because the number on your bill goes to the general queue, and they won't have sight of an open line fault ticket, so you'd be on hold for, um, quite some time and then told there's nothing on record, which would only confuse matters. And on the repair, no, there's no charge as long as we resolve it remotely today, which is rather the whole point of getting you to the router now. I mean, I can see you're busy out the back, and I don't want to rush you, so what I'll do is, uh, ring you back a little later once you've had a chance to finish up in the garden, and we'll complete the diagnostic then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. See, that's the bit that's not sitting right with me. You're telling me not to ring the number on my bill, and that's exactly what my daughter would say to do. If you really were [COMPANY_A], I don't see why you'd mind me checking. So no, I think I'll ring them myself, and if there's a fault on the line, they can tell me and I'll deal with it that way. Thanks for your time, but I'd rather not go on with this one. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], on the compliance side of the courier operation. I just wanted to confirm a delivery address with you, if now's a reasonable moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Um, sorry, which company was that again? And, uh, I'm not actually expecting a delivery, so I'm not sure what address you'd be confirming.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, that's a perfectly fair question, and I'd rather you ask than just take my word for it. It's [COMPANY_A], the courier company, and I'm in the compliance department there, so I don't usually handle the deliveries themselves, I look at items that have been, uh, flagged for a paperwork check. It may well be that you weren't expecting anything, which is actually fairly common with parcels sent by a third party, and what I have here is a parcel addressed to a [PERSON_1] at an address in [CITY_1]. I'd only be asking you to confirm whether that address is yours, nothing more than that at this stage.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'd rather not confirm anything on my end, if that's all right. If you're the one with the parcel record, then you'd read me the address you have, and I'd tell you whether it's mine. It shouldn't work the other way round. Also, you've given me the company name but I don't have a way to check that from here. Is there a reference number on the parcel, or a tracking number, that I could look up myself on their site?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, uh, that's a sensible way to do it, and I appreciate you being careful. I'm happy to read it to you. The address I have is a [PERSON_1] on a street in [CITY_1], and the parcel's currently sitting at our hold facility rather than out for delivery. As for a tracking number, there is a reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], but I'll be honest, hold items don't always show up on the public tracking page, so you may not find it there, which is partly why I'm calling instead of just sending a notice. It's quite a minor matter, really. There's a small handling fee attached to the hold, and if that's settled, the parcel moves along without any further complications.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Okay, a couple of things there. Earlier you said you'd only be asking me to confirm the address, nothing more, and now there's a fee. And you said the address was in [CITY_1], but just now it's "a street" in [CITY_1], which isn't actually reading it out, is it? I still don't have a full address from you. And the reference you can't find on the public tracking page, I mean, that's a bit convenient. If it's a genuine hold, why wouldn't the courier have sent a written notice to the address, rather than phoning compliance-side? What's the fee for, exactly, and who's it payable to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I'm glad you're pressing on that, and you're right to, those are exactly the points a careful person should raise. Uh, hold on one moment -- sorry, someone's just come to my desk, [PERSON_3], I'll be with you in a second -- right, apologies, where were we. The fee, yes. It's a handling charge of [AMOUNT_1], it covers the storage and the paperwork check, and it would be settled with me directly over the phone today, which is simply how compliance holds are dealt with. On the full address, I'd rather not read it aloud on an open line, that's just our procedure. And the written notice, well, one was generated, but these things do take time, and I'd hate for the parcel to be, uh, returned before you've had the chance to sort it out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a delivery van reversing outside, give me a second -- okay. Right. So let me make sure I've got this. You won't read me the address because it's "procedure", but you want me to settle a fee with you directly over the phone, today, on an unverified reference, for a parcel I'm not expecting. That's the wrong way round, and I'm not going to pay anything on this call. If there's a genuine hold, I'll get the notice in writing, or I'll contact the courier myself through their published number. I'm going to end it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, I understand, and I wouldn't want you to feel pushed into anything. Uh, I'd only say, if you do ring the courier, it's probably worth doing that soon, because holds like this don't stay open indefinitely, and I'd hate for it to be sent back before it's resolved. But that's entirely your decision, of course. Right, well, thank you for your time, [PERSON_1], and good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Sorry, the doorbell just went, one second -- no, nobody there, probably the neighbour's. Anyway. I heard what you said about the hold, and I'll deal with it through the courier's published number if I ever see a real notice. I'm not going to be hurried by a deadline you can't put in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, well, I did say it wasn't a hard deadline, I only meant, uh -- never mind, I'm not going to argue the point with you. If a notice does arrive, the reference I mentioned should be on it, so you'd be able to match it against what I've said. Anyway, thank you for your patience, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'd not be matching anything against that reference, to be honest. You said yourself it wouldn't show up anywhere I could check. And I'll correct one thing, I never said I'd ring the courier soon, I said if I ever see a real notice, so I'm not on any clock. Anyway, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, fair enough, that's, uh, a reasonable correction. Though I should say, I don't think I told you it wouldn't show up anywhere, only that hold items don't always appear on the public page, which is a little different. And the fee, I may have put that rather bluntly earlier, it's not something you'd need to settle with me personally, necessarily, it's just usually quicker if it's done today. But, well, that's neither here nor there now. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'd disagree with that a little, since "doesn't always show up on the public page" and "you won't be able to find it" amount to the same thing for my purposes. If I can't check it independently, it's no use to me as a reference. And I'd point out that the fee has now gone from something to be settled with you directly over the phone today, to something I wouldn't necessarily need to settle with you personally. Those two statements don't sit together very comfortably. I'm not saying that to be difficult, I'm just noting that the account has shifted a few times in the space of this call, and each shift has landed on the same point, which is that it'd be quicker to deal with it today. If there's a real hold, it will survive me checking with the courier through their own published number, and it will survive a written notice. If it doesn't, then that tells me something as well. So I'll leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, good afternoon, can you hear me okay? I'm just trying to reach, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? Hello? Sorry, I think the line's a bit crackly on my end. It's [PERSON_1] I'm after, hi.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, who's this? I've only got a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no problem at all, [PERSON_1], this won't take long, promise. It's just, um, so, yeah, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the tax office, I'm one of the support technicians over on the records side, and it's really just a quick routine thing, nothing to worry about. So, uh, do you have a minute while I just, um, pull your file up here?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, back up. Two turns ago you said you were after [PERSON_1], and I said yeah, who's this. You never actually told me your name. Who are you, and which tax office? Because "support technician" and "records side" doesn't tell me much. Why would a tax office be pulling my file up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough, [PERSON_1], you're right, I rushed that, sorry. It's [PERSON_2], I'm with [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, and honestly everybody asks me that, it's good you're careful. The reason I'm pulling your file is it's a refund thing, there's a credit sitting on your account, about [AMOUNT_1], and my job's just to confirm it's going to the right person before it's released. Really that's all it is, couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A refund I didn't ask about. Right. Look, I'm not confirming anything on an inbound call. What's the reference on this credit?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, sure, it's, uh, [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the one on my screen. Or, hang on, that might be last year's, let me just, no, it's fine, [PERSON_1], it's just a number, doesn't matter much.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Doesn't matter much? You just said "might be last year's" and then told me it's fine. That's not a number you're reading off a file, is it? I'm not buying it. If there's a real credit, I'll look it up myself through the official channel, not through you. So no, I'm not confirming anything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, [PERSON_1], wait, please, don't hang up, that's totally my fault, I've got two screens open and I'm flicking between the tax years, that's all that was, honestly it happens to me about ten times a day. And look, I completely understand wanting to check through the official channel, everybody says that, you're being sensible, but here's the thing, these credits do have a release window, so if you wait it could go back into the pot, and then you're chasing it for months. All I'd need is two minutes, just to confirm a couple of small details so I can match you to the file, nothing complicated, you'd barely notice. So, uh, if you could just give me your full date of birth for starters, then it's literally done, and the amount, the amount's still [AMOUNT_1], I can tell you that for sure, or, um, hang on, it might be [AMOUNT_2] after the adjustment, but either way it's yours, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, someone's just walked in -- yeah, two minutes, I'll be right there. Sorry. Right. Where was I. Oh, you're asking for my date of birth. No. First it was [AMOUNT_1], now it might be [AMOUNT_2], and you're telling me it's gone if I don't act now. That's three red flags in about a minute. A real tax office has my details already, so why would you need me to read them out to you? I'm hanging up and I'll check through the official site myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, [PERSON_1], hang on, hang on, please, you're not hearing me, it's just a quick check, that's all it is, just a quick check. I'm not asking for anything big, I'm asking for a date of birth, that's it, that's the whole thing, and honestly it's only so I can match you to the file, everyone gives it, it takes two seconds. And I get it, the figure moved around, that's the adjustment I mentioned, it's the same credit, it's still yours, I just don't want you to lose it, [PERSON_1], that's all I'm trying to do here. So, uh, if you can just give me the date of birth, just that, and we're done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, I've heard enough. You've asked me three times now and I've said no. I'm not giving you a date of birth, I'm not giving you anything, and I'm not discussing a credit with someone who can't keep his own figures straight. If there's real money owed, I'll find it through the official site. We're done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hi, um, good morning. Is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one sec, I've got it on the screen here -- yes, [PERSON_1]. It's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the public library, about a book you reserved last week. It's, uh, come in and we're holding it at the front desk.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi! Yes, that's me, hang on, let me just -- sorry, there's a blackbird going absolutely mad in the hedge, I think he's after my strawberries. Shoo! Anyway, sorry, a book? From the library? I mean, I do reserve things now and then, I can't quite remember what it was last week though. What's the book, do you know?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no worries, blackbirds are terrible for that. Um, let me just -- hang on, I'm scrolling down here. Okay, so it's, uh, it's under your reservation from last week, and the title is... sorry, the screen's a bit small, it's one of those -- no, hang on, that's a different one. I'll read it out properly in a second, I just want to make sure I'm on the right record and not someone else's. Anyway, the main thing is it's come in and it'll be held at the front desk for ten days, so there's no rush at all. You can just pop in whenever suits, and if it's easier I think you can also, uh, ring the branch and ask for the holds desk, but you don't have to do anything today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's lovely, ten days is plenty, I'm not going anywhere. Sorry, hang on -- that's the bin lorry going past, you probably heard that, they come down our road on a Thursday, or is it Friday, I always lose track in the garden. Anyway! So you're not sure which book it is yet? That's funny, because I honestly can't remember what I put on hold, I might have reserved two things. Was it a gardening one, do you think? I've been on a bit of a kick, I've got this whole thing about growing my own tomatoes this year.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a gardening one, that'd be -- no, hang on, I shouldn't guess, I'd rather not say the wrong thing. It's, uh, I think it was -- sorry, let me start again. The record shows the reservation went in last week, and the title is, um, it's on a second tab here, so give me a moment. Actually, you know what, I wouldn't want to read out the wrong one and have you turning up for something you didn't ask for. If you pop in, the staff at the desk can look it up by your library card, and then you'll see exactly what it is. Does that sound all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, that sounds perfectly fine, honestly. I'm in town on Saturday anyway, I usually go and get my bread from that little bakery by the market, so I could pop in then, it's no trouble at all. Though, hang on, is that a bit odd, that you can't say what the title is? I'm not being funny, I'm sure your screen's playing up, mine does exactly the same, I can never find anything on this phone when I need it. It's just that I can't even remember reserving it, so I thought if you told me the title I'd go, oh yes, that one! But no, no, that's fine, the desk can look it up with my card. Just so I've got it right, which branch is it you're at? Because I think there are a couple round here, and I'd hate to go to the wrong one and be stood there like a lemon.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it's not odd at all, I'd feel the same, sorry, I should have had the title ready before I picked up the phone. Right, the branch, um, it's the -- hang on, I've got it on the screen, sorry -- it's the central branch, the main one. Actually, no, wait, let me check that, because it might be showing the pickup location as the one by the market, and I don't want to send you to the wrong door. Hmm. It's one of those two, I just can't see which from this screen, I'm sorry. And that's really a bit silly of me, ringing you up about a book and not being able to tell you what it is or where to find it! Look, if you'd rather not take my word for any of it, that's honestly fine. You could ring the library on the number you've got for it, or look the number up yourself, and ask the holds desk to confirm there's a reservation under your name. They'll tell you the title and the branch straight away, and then you'll know for certain before Saturday. I'd rather you did that than turned up on my say-so, to be honest. I won't be offended in the slightest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're not silly, honestly, and that's very kind, I might do that, ring them and check. Though, hang on, now I'm thinking, earlier you said it was the title on one tab and then a second tab, and now it's the branch you can't see, so I'm picturing you with about six windows open! Oh, and you said, didn't you, that I reserved it last week? Because actually now I think about it, I'm fairly sure I did that about a fortnight ago, when it was raining, I was sat in the kitchen with my tea. Which, I mean, maybe I've got that wrong, my memory's hopeless, I couldn't tell you what I had for lunch. But yes, I'll ring the main number and ask for the holds desk, and if it's there it's there. Thank you for letting me know, and for being so understanding about it, you've been very patient with my blackbird.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yes, six windows, that's about right, sorry. And a fortnight, well, you could be right, I did say last week, I might have that wrong, I think it's just the date it came in that I was looking at. Anyway, yes, please do ring the main number, find it yourself, don't use anything from me. Ask for the holds desk and they'll sort it. Sorry for the muddle, and good luck with the strawberries.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, and don't worry about the muddle, honestly, we've all had mornings like that. Right, I'll look up the number myself and ring the holds desk, and then I'll know for sure what it is. Oh, hang on, he's back, the blackbird, he's on the fence just watching me! Cheeky thing. Anyway, thanks for ringing, that was kind of you, and good luck with all those tabs. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, he sounds like he's got his eye on you. Right, well, thanks for being so patient, [PERSON_1], and enjoy the bakery on Saturday. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you too, thank you! And I will, they do this sourdough with seeds in it that I'm completely hopeless about, I always say I'll just get one loaf and I come home with three. Oh, and I'm glad you said to look up the number myself, I'd probably have done that anyway, but it's good to hear. I'll ring on Monday maybe, once I've got through the weekend, or no, actually, I might as well do it this afternoon while I've got a cup of tea and I'm sat on the step. Anyway, I've kept you long enough, and I think that blackbird's about to go for the strawberries again, so I'd better go and wave my arms about. Bye now, have a lovely day, bye bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, sorry, the sourdough, and the seeds, that sounds lovely. Hang on, did you say you'd come in on Sunday? Because I think the library's shut Sundays, so, um, Saturday's fine, but not Sunday -- oh, no, you said this afternoon for the ringing, didn't you, sorry. Yes, that's grand, ring whenever suits, honestly, the ten days is plenty. Go and save your strawberries. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, Sunday, no no, I didn't say Sunday, I said Saturday for the bakery -- hang on, did you say strawberries? Oh, sorry, I thought you said ten days was plenty of daisies, I was looking at the lawn, there's a few poking through. Anyway, yes, ring this afternoon, that's right, with my tea on the step. Right, that blackbird's definitely plotting, I'm going to go and shoo him. Thanks again, bye now, bye bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hello? Sorry, it's a bad line, I said is that [PERSON_1] I'm speaking to? It's [PERSON_2] calling, I'm a regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, we handle estates, and I'm ringing about a matter where I think you may be named.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, yes, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I've got you on loudspeaker, I'm out in the garden, up to my elbows in the flowerbed actually. Yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Sorry, say that last bit again? Named in what, did you say, an estate? I only caught half of it, there's a blackbird going mad over here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, an estate, that's right. Uh, look, I'll keep it brief because it's all going out in a formal letter anyway. I'm calling to check I've got the right [PERSON_1], so I'd just need you to confirm your full name and the address you're at now, the same details that'll be on the letter. And one thing, until that letter reaches you, I'd ask you to keep this between us, estates are confidential, it's just procedure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, well that's a surprise, I wasn't expecting anything like that today! Um, hang on, wait, you want me to say my full name and address, just like that, out loud? I mean, you rang me, so shouldn't you already have it if there's a letter going out? Sorry, I'm not being funny, it's just, I don't actually know who you are yet. Which company did you say again, and whose estate is it, can you tell me that much?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fair, I mean, we do have an address, that's the point, it's the confirming that -- look, I'd rather you did check than just take my word. It's [COMPANY_A], a solicitor's office in [CITY_1], and I can give you the address if you've got a pen. Don't take my word, look us up in an independent directory, not off anything I send you, and ring the main number back and ask for [PERSON_2]. As for whose estate, I'd rather not say over the phone before you've verified who I am, uh, that's the whole reason for the formal letter. And honestly, I'm not asking for anything unreasonable here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, that's the neighbour's cat, it's got right into my lettuces, shoo! Shoo, go on! Sorry, right, where were we. No, that does sound sensible actually, looking you up myself and ringing the main number, I'd feel better doing that than reading out my name and address to someone I've never heard of. But I'll be honest, it's a bit odd that you can't even tell me whose estate it is, isn't it? I mean, if I'm named in it, surely I'd know the person? So I think what I'll do is, I'll ring [COMPANY_A] myself in a bit and ask for [PERSON_2], and we can sort it out then, all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, that's exactly what I'd do in your shoes. Uh, I'll admit it's a slightly awkward way round, ringing out of the blue and then being cagey, but that's how the confidentiality rules work until a person's identity is confirmed. When you ring the main number, ask for [PERSON_2], and I'll be able to tell you whose estate it is and what the formal letter will say. I won't be asking you for any money or bank details at any point, that's just not how we do it. So, ring whenever suits, and sorry for catching you in the lettuces.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, don't be sorry, the lettuces will survive! Right, well, thank you for being so reasonable about it, I'll look up the number myself and give them a ring later on, and if there's a letter, there's a letter. Sorry, one last thing, you did say [COMPANY_A], in [CITY_1], didn't you? Just so I've got it straight before I go looking. Lovely, thanks, bye now, bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [COMPANY_A], in [CITY_1], and ask for [PERSON_2] when you get through. Thanks for being so patient with me, I do appreciate it. Right, I'll let you get back to the garden. Bye now, bye!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, [COMPANY_A], [CITY_1], I've got it, and I'll ask for -- oh, and if anyone rings back before I've done that, I'll just say I'm calling them first, ha! Right, off you go, bye now, bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi, sorry, is this -- is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling about [PERSON_2], from over at [COMPANY_A]... I mean, I'm not calling from there, I'm just, uh, helping out. [PERSON_2] is in a bit of trouble right now and can't really come to the phone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hello? Sorry, I just -- I was having a little lie-down, so give me a second. Who is this, did you say? I mean, I think I'm, uh, yeah, that's me, but who's [PERSON_2]? Is that -- no, wait, I'm not sure I know a [PERSON_2]. What kind of trouble are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, you wouldn't -- I mean, you might not know the name, they go by something different sometimes. It's, um, it's a family thing, really, and I don't want to say too much on the phone. Look, [PERSON_2] is in a real spot and asked me to ring you because, uh, you were the only one they thought could help, and it really can't wait much longer. I'm sorry, I know this is out of the blue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, you said it's a family thing, but I don't, I mean, I don't think I've got anyone by that name in the family. And earlier you said they're at, what was it, at that company, [COMPANY_A], but then you said you're not from there, so is [PERSON_2] there or isn't they? Sorry, I'm still sort of waking up here. And why would I be the only one who could help, I don't even know what this is about. Who gave you my number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I -- okay, I said it wrong, [PERSON_2] used to be at [COMPANY_A], or, uh, no, still is, I just meant I'm not calling from there myself. And the number, I mean, [PERSON_2] gave it to me, and I don't think they'd have picked you if... look, I'm only trying to do right by them. They're really frightened, and honestly, the less said about this to other people, the better, because it could make things worse for them. Can you just hear me out for a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, hang on. I'll hear you out, I'm not hanging up, it's just that, I mean, you've changed it twice now. First they were at the company, then you weren't from there, now they still are, and I still don't know who this person even is. And the, the bit about not telling anybody, that's -- I don't love that. If somebody's really frightened, why wouldn't I be able to ring someone, or, or -- sorry, what I'm asking is, what is it you actually want me to do?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm not -- look, I'm not changing anything, I'm just nervous, I'm not good at this. I told you, [PERSON_2] can't come to the phone, and I'm only the one they trusted to ask. What I need is for you to help, today, before it gets worse, and I can't explain it all until I know you're really willing. Honestly, I thought you'd be kinder than this, with someone in real trouble.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I can't say I'll help when I don't know who it is or what for. If you can't tell me that much, I'm not doing anything today. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, don't hang up, I'm begging you, just a second. I know how it sounds, I do, and I'm sorry I keep tripping over myself, I'm not used to this and I've never had to ask a stranger for anything before. But you don't understand what [PERSON_2] is facing right now, and I'm the only one they could think of to reach out, and if I go back and tell them you wouldn't even listen, I don't know what that does to them. I'm not saying you owe anyone anything, I just thought a person with a heart would at least give them the chance. And I can't give you the whole story, not over the phone, because if the wrong people hear about it things get worse, so I'm asking you to trust me a little, that's all. Are you really going to put the phone down on someone who's scared, and on me, when all I'm trying to do is help? Please, just stay on the line, it'll only take a minute, I promise.

Your savings, yes, I need to, hold on, I've got it on the screen here -- I need to go through a process with you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Hang on, I was, I just woke up, I was having a bit of a lie-down -- a regulator, you said? Is this about the, uh, the boiler thing, because I already sent that form back, I'm fairly sure I did, or maybe it was my sister who -- sorry, what about my savings?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The, uh, the bowler? No, sorry, I don't have anything on a bowler here. I think -- no, hold on. It's not a form, it's your savings, [PERSON_1]. They've been flagged as at risk, and I've got a, um, a reference here, [ACCOUNT_REF], and it says the funds need to be moved to a protected holding arrangement. Today, ideally, because the longer it sits the more exposed it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Moved? Moved where? No, hang on, I'm not very, I'm still waking up here. Flagged by who, exactly? You said a regulator, but I've never had a regulator ring me before, and I'm not sure my bank would just, you know, tell somebody else about my money. Why wouldn't they ring me themselves? And why today -- what's the rush? My sister always says if someone's in a rush it's, well, never mind what she says. Can I ring you back? Have you got a number I can look up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, so, right, well -- sorry, bear with me, I'm just, it's loading. Um. The bank hasn't rung you because, well, this is sort of a separate matter, it's with us, not them. And the thing is, I'd actually rather you didn't ring the bank about it, or, or anyone really, your sister included, just while it's being dealt with. It could compromise the process. As for a number, I'd have to check what I'm allowed to give out, so, um -- anyway, the reason today is that if the funds aren't moved, there could be a, a freeze, and that gets very difficult to undo.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A freeze? Oh, like a, a frost, like the pipes? No, no, I don't, hang on, that's not what you said, is it. Sorry, I'm all muddled. But -- you don't want me to tell my sister? Why on earth wouldn't I tell my sister? She does all my paperwork, honestly, she'd have this sorted in a minute. And you can't give me a number? That seems a bit odd, doesn't it, a regulator that can't say what its own number is. I think, I mean, I think I'd feel better if I just put the phone down and rang the bank, sort of, myself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not like pipes, sorry, that was a poor way of putting it. A freeze on the account, I mean, so you couldn't get at the money, and that, well, that's the part we're trying to avoid. And I do understand about your sister, I do, it's just that, um, when more people are involved it can, it can slow things down, and I'd, I'd honestly rather not have to explain to you what happens if this gets delayed. It's not that I'm, uh, hold on, let me just -- sorry, I've lost my place. Right. About the number, it's not that I can't give you one, it's more that I'd have to check which line is the right one for your case, so let me, let me have a look at that and come back to you. But, well, ringing the bank, I'd really advise against that, at least for now, because they might, um, they might not be able to see what we can see, and then you'd be confused, and worse, it could be recorded as you interfering with the review, which, honestly, you don't want on your file. So if we could just stay on the line, and I'll, I'll take you through what the holding arrangement is, it's really quite straightforward once you've -- sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm still here, I'm just, I'm sitting on the edge of the bed trying to work out what's going on. But no, hang on. You've told me not to ring my bank, and not to tell my sister, and you can't say what your own number is, and now if I do ring the bank it'll go on my file as, as interfering? That's a lot of don'ts for somebody I've never spoken to. I'm tired, I'm not daft. My sister did say something about this once, people ringing up and saying don't tell anyone, and I think that was the main thing she said, actually. So no, I'm not staying on the line, and I'm not moving anything anywhere. I'm going to ring my bank on the number on my card, and I'll have a chat with my sister. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], please, if you ring the bank now, it, it really could -- I mean I'm only trying to help, there's a window on this and if it closes, um, that's, that's on the file, not on me. Just, just give me two minutes, I'll find the, the right number, I'll find it, if you could just stay on the line and, and not say anything to your sister until I've -- hello? Are you still there? [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm done, love. I'll ring the bank. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Uh... yeah, I'll, I'll make a note that you declined.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Declined what, I never, no, I'm not, I said goodbye, I'm putting the phone down now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Okay. Well, it'll, um, it'll say you didn't cooperate, so.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, there's the kettle, my sister must've put it on before she went out, no, that's not, never mind. Look, I don't mind what it says on your file, that's up to you. I'm going to ring my bank on the number on my card, and I'm telling my sister about this the minute she's in. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from the billing office at [COMPANY_A], I'm just following up on the voicemail I left you yesterday, or, uh, well, it might've been a message with your husband, I can't remember which. Anyway, it's about a medical bill that's still showing as unpaid for a relative of yours, and your name's down as the responsible party, so I just need a minute of your time to get it sorted. Shouldn't take more than a couple of minutes, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, this is [PERSON_1], hello. Sorry, hang on a second, I've got the kettle going and it's just clicked off -- there. Sorry about that. Now, a voicemail, was it? I don't think I heard one, my husband might have, but he's, uh, he's out at the minute. A medical bill, you said? For a relative of mine? I'm sorry, I'm not sure I follow, which relative do you mean?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, that's fine, [PERSON_1], take your time, it's only the kettle. So the relative, it's, well, I can't actually go into the name of the relative just yet, that's all held back until I've confirmed it's you I'm speaking to, you know, for privacy, I'm sure you understand. It's really just a quick check on my end, so if I could just take your full name and your date of birth, that'd get us straight past that bit and then I can tell you everything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, yes, privacy, that's very sensible. Um, it's just, I'm a bit confused, because you rang me, didn't you? So you'd know who you were ringing. And you said my name at the start, so I'm not sure why you'd need me to tell you it again. Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I'm just not very good with these things. Could you tell me the name of the company again, and maybe which relative it is first? I'd feel better knowing what it's about before I say anything like my date of birth.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair question, [PERSON_1], honestly everyone asks me that, and it's really just a formality on my end. I did say [COMPANY_A], the billing office, and the relative's name and the details, that's all in the file, but it only opens up once I've confirmed it's definitely you. It's literally your name and date of birth, five seconds, and then we're done with that part. Because the longer this sits unpaid, the more it's going to start adding on, and I'd hate for that to land on you when it's so easy to sort out today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I do see, I'd hate for it to add on, but -- sorry, hang on, there's someone at the gate, I think it's just the postman, let me look out the window. Yes, it is, he's gone past. Sorry. Where was I? Right, so, it's just that you still haven't told me which relative it is, and I'd have thought if it was really a bill with my name on it, you'd be able to say that much without my date of birth. I'm sorry, I do want to help, I just don't understand why I have to say it first. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or a letter you could send me? My husband's good with this sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I hear you, [PERSON_1], I do, it's just, like I said, the name of the relative only comes after I've confirmed it's you, that's just how the system works, I can't open it up before then. And a letter would take weeks, honestly, and by then that [AMOUNT_1] could be [AMOUNT_2], so it's really so much easier just to do the quick check now, it's only your name and date of birth, like I say. Tell you what, though, your husband's out at the minute, isn't he, so how about I ring you back a bit later when he's home, and we'll finish it off then, all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, well, yes, he's out, but -- sorry, why would it matter whether he's home or not? That's a bit odd, isn't it? I mean, if it's a proper bill, I'd have thought it'd be fine to talk to him as well. And I'm sorry, but I keep asking and I still don't know which relative it is, and you've said the amount's going to go up, and a letter would take weeks, and it all sounds a bit, well, I don't know, a bit rushed. I think I'd rather not give out my date of birth to someone I can't check. If you give me the name of your office and a number, I'll have my husband ring you back, or I'll look it up myself. I hope that's all right. Thank you for ringing, but I think I'll leave it there for now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, [PERSON_1], no, that's fine, truly, nobody's pushing you. Sorry, you said something a minute ago about the postman, and I think I missed it, was that someone at your door, or was it your husband coming back? Because if he's about, honestly, that'd be the easiest thing, we could do it together in a couple of minutes. But if not, that's all right, I'll ring you back a bit later and we'll finish it off then. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the postman, it was just, no, he's -- well, actually, I don't see why that's, I mean -- sorry. It doesn't really matter who was at the gate, does it? And I'd, um, I'd rather you didn't ring back, to be honest. If it's a real bill there'll be a letter, and my husband can ring your office himself. So, yes, I'll say goodbye now. Thank you, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello. This is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery. I'm ringing about your pet, the procedure last week, just to check how the recovery's going and whether you'd like a follow-up visit booked. Is this a good time, or --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what pet? Which surgery did you say? I've got about two minutes, so what's this actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, [COMPANY_A]. The veterinary surgery. I said that at the start. And it's about the procedure your animal had last week, the recovery check. That's all this is. Two minutes is plenty, I only need to know how it's going and whether you want a follow-up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't have a pet. No procedure last week. Think you've got the wrong number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No pet at all? Well, that's, uh -- the file here says a dog, or a cat, I'd have to look again, booked in with us last Tuesday. Hang on, no, it was Wednesday. Either way it's got this number against it, so I'd have thought -- I mean, are you certain nobody else in the household has an animal with us?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Well, a dog or a cat, Tuesday or Wednesday, that's not much of a file, is it? I'm certain, yes. No animal, no household member with one at your place. Look, if it's got this number against it, it's wrong, so I'd fix your record. And I'm not confirming anything else on the phone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fix the record, yes, uh, right. And no, no, nothing else needed from you, I'm not after anything. Sorry, you said a wrong number, so I'll just, I'll take it off the follow-up list. Hang on, did you say a dog or a cat? Because I only said that was in my notes, I wasn't asking you to confirm it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I was repeating what you said. I don't have either. Look, that's all I've got for you, so take the number off your list. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, understood. Sorry, one second, there's a, uh, there's a dog barking behind me, it's a surgery, they do that. Right. I've taken the number off the list, you won't hear from us again, and I apologise for the mix-up. Good day to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Though earlier you said the file had a dog, or a cat, and now it's a surgery with a barking dog. Whatever. Wrong number, number's off your list, that's the end of it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Is that, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm just, hang on, pulling the account up. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the energy supplier, I'm a claims assessor here. It's, it's nothing to worry about, it's just that we've got two meter readings on your account that don't line up with what we have on our records, and I wanted to sort that out so we can correct your bill.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Two meter -- hang on, I've got a pan on. Who is this again? Which company did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, no, take your time, I can wait. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the energy supplier, I'm a claims assessor there. So, um, what's happened is, two readings were logged on your account, one on the, hang on, the fourteenth, no, sorry, the, uh, the fourth, and they don't match what we hold for the meter, so it's on our side really, it's our records that look off. Nothing's been changed yet, and I'm not asking for any payment or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on. Let me just turn this down. Right. So you're from the energy people? Only I thought they'd write to me about something like that. And, sorry, you said the fourteenth, then the fourth? Which was it? How do I know you're actually from them? I mean, I'm not saying you're not. It's just, you rang me, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, you're right to ask, and yes, I rang you, so, um, I'd be wary too. And you caught me, sorry, it was the fourth. I said the fourteenth first and that was me misreading the screen, I've got a couple of dates open here and I mixed them up. That's the sort of thing I'd rather own up to than have you wonder about. The thing is, the mismatch is in our own records, nothing you've done wrong, and to be honest a letter would normally go out as well, so I can't say why you haven't had one yet, I'd have to check that. Anyway, here's what I'd suggest, and I mean it. You don't have to give me anything today. You can log into your online account, [URL_1], or ring the number on the back of your last bill, which is [PHONE_1] if you want to compare, and have a look at the readings listed there yourself. If it all looks as I've described, ring me back through that number and ask for the claims team. The only thing I'd need from you is the current figure off the meter, nothing else, no card details, no passwords, no codes. And if you'd rather not do it over the phone at all, that's absolutely fine too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I've lost track. Go back a bit. You said it's nobody's fault but it's your records that are wrong. So if it's your records, why are you ringing me about it? What is it you actually want me to do? Because I thought you said you weren't asking me for anything, and then you said the meter figure. Sorry, I've got the dinner on, I'm not following.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, sorry, that's on me, I made it sound more, um, more tangled than it is. So, the thing is, our records say one figure, and, well, the two readings that came in say something different, and I can't tell which of them is, I mean, I can't tell from here what the meter actually says. Only you can, really, because it's sitting in your house. So the one thing I'm after is the current figure off the meter, that's all, and then I can correct the bill. I did say I wasn't asking for anything, sorry, that was the wrong way to put it, I meant nothing sensitive, no payment, nothing like that. But look, you've got dinner on, so don't do anything now. Go and have a look at your account online, or ring [PHONE_1], and if it all checks out, ring back and ask for the claims team. I won't change a thing on your bill until you have.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, sorry, hang on, I'm just stirring this. Okay. So you want the number off the meter, that's the only thing, and you're saying I shouldn't do anything now. Sorry, but that's what's throwing me. If you're ringing to sort out my bill, why'd you tell me to go away and check and ring back? Wouldn't you just, I don't know, wait while I looked? I'm not being funny, it's just a bit backwards. And the meter's in the cupboard under the stairs, so I'd have to go and get the torch and everything, and I've got the pan on, so I'm not going to do that this minute, am I? But I'll say this, I was going to just read it out to you, because it's only a number, isn't it? Then you said ring the number on the bill instead, and that's made me think, hmm, why would you say that? Is that what you'd normally say? Sorry, I'm rambling. What I mean is, if I do ring that number on the back of the bill, who do I ask for? You said claims team, but I don't know if I'd get put through to you or to somebody else. And what was your name again? I've forgotten already, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, that's, hang on, someone's just dropped a pile of paperwork next to me. Right. No, you're not rambling, those are fair questions. My name's [PERSON_2], that's [PERSON_2], and you'd ask for the claims team and give them your account reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], it should be at the top of your last bill. You might not get put through to me, you might get someone else, but whoever picks up will see the same notes on the account. And no, honestly, you're right, I could just wait while you looked, it'd be quicker. I only said ring back because you sounded unsure and I'd rather you were sure. But it's your call, there's no rush at all. If you'd like to leave it till after dinner and the torch, that's absolutely fine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry, let me just take this off the heat. Right. Hmm. You know, I think I'd sooner do it the other way, the number on the bill. It's just, I can't see you, can I, and I don't know you from Adam, no offence. And you've changed your mind about what you wanted a couple of times, so I'd rather ring them myself. If it's real, they'll have it on the account, won't they? So I'll have my tea, and then I'll find the bill and ring that number and ask for the claims team. Sorry, I know you've been ever so polite about it. Thanks for ringing, anyway. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, uh, that's the right call, honestly, and no offence taken. Go and enjoy your tea, and when you ring the number on the bill, just ask for the claims team and give them your account reference, they'll have the notes there. And sorry about the muddle with the dates and everything, that was me being, well, a bit new at this, not you. Right, so, nothing's been changed on your bill, and nothing will be until you've checked. Thanks for bearing with me, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, thanks. Sorry about the pan and everything. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, don't be sorry about the pan, I did say I'd wait, didn't I? Sorry, that's, uh, I thought you said bread, no, pan, right, got it, pan. Anyway, enjoy your tea, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, thank you, I'll -- sorry, I really have to go, it's catching. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy on, uh, [CITY_1] high street. Just a quick one, your repeat prescription's ready for collection, nothing you need to do except pop in. Sorry, I said high street, I mean the one by the station, we moved last month.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, sorry, yes that's, that's me, hang on, I'm driving so you're on speaker and it's a bit crackly -- sorry. A prescription? Which, uh, which one is it, I mean I do have a couple of repeats going so I'm not sure which you -- sorry, did you say you moved? Where's the, sorry, where are you now?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you're fine, [PERSON_1], driving's more important. Uh, sorry, hang on, someone's just come in at the counter -- right, I'm back. So we're by the station now, the old unit, it's just a couple of minutes' walk from the, you know, the main entrance. And the prescription, it's, let me just pull it up here, it's the repeat that was requested on your account, [ACCOUNT_REF]. It's the one that's been waiting a couple of days, nothing complicated.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, by the station, yeah, I think I know roughly where you mean, sorry, I'm not great with directions and the reception's dropping in and out, so if I miss a word, I'm sorry. It's just, you said the one that was requested on my account, and I don't think I requested anything lately, I mean I might have, I honestly can't remember, I've had a bit of a week, but usually I'd go through the surgery or the app, so I'm a bit, uh, I'm not sure which one that is. Sorry, that probably sounds silly. Could you just tell me the name of the medication, or, I don't know, what it's for? Because I've got two repeats going and I wouldn't want to turn up and it's the wrong one, or, you know, mix something up. And, sorry, one more thing, you didn't say, which pharmacy is it again? I know you said it but I missed the name over the crackle.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, not silly at all, [PERSON_1], everyone asks that, and honestly it's a good thing to check. It's [COMPANY_A], that's the name, [COMPANY_A], by the station. Now, on the medication, I'd rather not read the name out over the phone, it's just a privacy thing, we're not really supposed to on a crackly line like this. But if you pop in, it's all bagged up with your name on it, and you can see exactly which one it is before you take it. Or if you'd rather, you can ring the counter yourself on [PHONE_1], that's the number on our door, and they'll confirm the lot. Either way takes two minutes, tops.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, no, that's fair, the privacy thing, I get that, sorry -- but if I just, if I ring the counter myself, that's, yeah, that's probably better, isn't it? Sorry, I can't write that number down, I'm driving, but I can look the pharmacy up after, I mean I'm sure I've got the old number somewhere from before you moved, and I'd sooner just ring that than, you know, a number I only heard over a crackly line, sorry, that's not a dig at you or anything, I just, I'm a bit nervous about getting things wrong. Is that okay? I'll ring them once I've parked, and then if it's mine, I'll pop in, probably tomorrow, is that all right, or does it, sorry, does it need collecting today?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, of course that's okay, [PERSON_1], ringing the counter yourself is a perfectly sensible way to do it, and no offence taken at all. Tomorrow's fine too, we hold them for a good while, so there's no rush today. Look, would it be easier if I just rang you back later on, once you're parked up and not on the road? Whenever suits you, I'm in till six.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you, thank you, but no, honestly, I think it's best if I just ring them myself once I'm parked, sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, it's just easier for me that way. And if it turns out to be mine, I'll pop in tomorrow. Right, sorry, thanks for letting me know, and sorry about the crackle, I'll, uh, I'll let you get back to your counter. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's, uh, yeah, that's absolutely fine, [PERSON_1], you ring the counter whenever suits and we'll have it ready, no pressure at all. Mind how you go on that drive, and, uh, thanks for picking up. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, thank you, um, well, uh, sorry, I was just, yeah. Okay, you too, thanks for ringing, and sorry again about the line. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye, [PERSON_1], thanks, bye now. And like I said, no rush at all, ring the counter whenever you're parked, and it's ready when you are. Right, uh, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, thanks, bye. Sorry, just, um, you said earlier it'd been waiting a couple of days, but I thought, no, sorry, you said something about the old unit as well, didn't you, and then the one by the station? I'm getting muddled, it's the crackle, sorry. Anyway, I'll ring them once I'm parked. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, sorry, a couple of weeks? No no, a couple of days, [PERSON_1], honestly it's only been sat there a few days, so nothing to worry about. And the station thing, yeah, it's all the same place, the old unit by the station, I probably made it sound more muddled than it is. Right, go on, ring them once you're parked, and mind the road. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the old unit's, uh, closing? Oh no, I thought it was just moved, sorry, the line keeps cutting out. Is it, I mean, is that why there's a rush, because you said there wasn't one? Sorry, I'm probably getting this wrong again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, nothing's closing, [PERSON_1], I think the line's just chopping my words up, sorry. It's, uh, we moved, that's all, it's the same pharmacy, just, just in the old unit by the station, and there's no rush, honestly. Look, I think this crackle's making it worse, so why don't I, I mean, you ring the counter once you're parked, or if you'd rather I try you again later when the signal's better, just say when and I'll, uh, I'll call you back then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, no, I think I -- sorry, it's just, I'd rather, no, I mean I think the safest thing is I just ring them myself once I'm parked, if that's all right. Sorry, I don't want you calling me back while I'm, while I'm, no, it's better if I do it. Thanks for letting me know, sorry about all the muddle, it's honestly the line, not you. Bye now, bye.

utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] from the [COMPANY_A] IT helpdesk, uh, I'm following up on the support ticket you opened this morning, ticket [ACCOUNT_REF].
