utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. So, uh... let me just get this straight. A regulator is ringing me out of the blue to say my savings are at risk, they need me to move the money somewhere, and I'm not to mention it to my bank. Which is, I mean, pretty much the one thing I'd expect a regulator to tell me to do first. Ring the bank. So why the secrecy? And what's the name of the protected holding arrangement, exactly? Who runs it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I hear the concern, and I'll note that on the file, but the secrecy is -- sorry, let me finish -- it's there because the exposure is internal. Part of the risk sits with the bank's own processing, so if the branch is told before the funds are secured, the flag clears on their side and the balance stays where it is, exposed. That's simply how the sequence works. As for the arrangement, it's a holding account under [COMPANY_B], administered through our unit. I'm reading the reference here as [CODE_1]. And I should say, the exposure window closes at the end of today, so the balance would be treated as unprotected after that. That's not a warning, it's just the position on the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, let me say this back to you, because I want to be sure I've got it. The risk is inside the bank, so I can't ask the bank. The money has to go into an account run by your own unit, and the deadline's today, conveniently. And the one person I'd normally check this with is the one person I'm not allowed to talk to. Honestly, that's a bit of a closed loop. Every single check I could do is the thing you've told me not to do. And I'll be straight with you, I don't have any particular reason to think you're lying. But I also can't see anything from where I'm sitting that tells me you're not. A regulator doesn't usually ring people up and ask them to move their savings into an account the regulator administers. That's not really what regulators are for, as far as I know. They write the rules, they investigate firms, they don't hold my money for me. So here's what I'd do. You give me the main switchboard number for [COMPANY_A], the one that's published, not one you read out to me now, and I'll look it up myself and ring in. If you're who you say you are, they can put me through to you or confirm the flag exists. Does that work? Because if it doesn't, uh, I'd like to know why not.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll note the request on the file. I can't give you a switchboard number to ring, though, because the main line doesn't hold this case. The flag sits with our unit only, so a general operator would see nothing against your name, and then you'd have a clear record of nobody confirming it, and the exposure window would still close at the end of today. I'm not saying that to push you. It's just where the file is. What I can do is send you a reference, [CODE_1], and a direct line, [PHONE_1], so you'd be speaking to this unit and not a switchboard. And, uh, I'd ask again that nothing is raised with the bank until the funds are secured. If it's raised first, the protection can't be applied. So, are you in a position to proceed with the transfer to the holding arrangement now, yes or no? I have another file I need to open at the top of the hour.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No -- hang on, no, I'm going to stop you there. A direct line that you give me is just you again, isn't it? That's not a check, that's the same call with a different number. And the other file at the top of the hour doesn't make this my problem. So, no. I'm not moving anything, and I'm going to ring my bank on the number I already have. If this is real, it'll still be real in twenty minutes. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll note the refusal on the file, but I'd advise against that, because it won't still be there in twenty minutes. The window closes at the end of the day, and, uh, I did say the exposure comes from outside the bank, so ringing them won't show you anything either way. And it's no use going through the line I gave you, I'd rather you didn't contact us again today, the file will have been passed on by then. Look, the balance is still showing [AMOUNT_1] this morning, I mean, [AMOUNT_2], sorry, that's the updated figure. That's the position as it stands.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I said no. And you just changed the balance on me, it was one figure and now it's another, and you said sorry and carried on like that was fine. It isn't. I'm ringing my bank, on the number I already have, and I'm not moving anything. That's the answer. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The figure was a screen refresh, nothing more. I'll note that you've declined, and the file will show it was your decision and not ours. Once the window closes, any loss to the balance is outside what our unit can reverse. That's just how it stands. I won't ring again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, and the "I won't ring again" bit is a nice touch, but I'm -- no, I'm done, I've said it three times now. Nothing's moving, I'm calling my bank, and you can note whatever you like on your file. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood. Noted as declined.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, something just pinged on my other screen -- no, never mind, it's nothing. Right. Yeah. You've got your note, I've got my answer, and nobody's moving anything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Then the file closes on your decision. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the file closes on my... what, decision to collect? No, I'm not collecting anything, you said that yourself, that was the whole bit at the start. Anyway. Doesn't matter. I'm hanging up and ringing my bank. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Right, it's [PERSON_2], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the sports club. I'm ringing about Saturday's junior match, there's been a change, pitch and kick-off both, and I need to know you've got that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, that's me, uh -- sorry, hang on, the kettle's just clicked off, one second. Right, sorry. Security operations, did you say? I thought the sports club was, well, you know, the committee lot. But a change to Saturday, oh dear, no, I haven't heard anything. What's changed, the pitch and the time?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, security operations, I did say that. It's just my title, I handle the grounds and the pitches, the committee lot do the paperwork. Now, the pitch and the kick-off, that's the change. The main pitch is waterlogged, so Saturday's match is moving to the back pitch, and kick-off is now [CODE_1] instead of the usual time. Did you get that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, waterlogged, right, sorry -- did you say the back *patch*? Is that the bit round the side by the car park, the, uh, the vegetable patch? I didn't know they'd put a pitch there, I thought that was where the allotment lot had their sheds. And I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch the time, it sort of went funny. What time is it now?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Pitch, not patch. The back pitch, behind the pavilion. Not the allotments, nothing to do with the allotments. And the time, I said it was [CODE_1], I'm not going to keep repeating it. If you don't have it written down, that's your lookout, because the match goes ahead at [CODE_1] whether you've heard it or not.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, sorry, I'm not very good on the phone. Behind the pavilion, right, got it. But the time, it came out as a sort of, uh, a code, like a car number or something? I honestly didn't hear a time. And I'm sorry, did you say your lookout? I'm not sure what lookout you mean, is that a person, someone who's watching the pitch for us?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, lookout isn't a person, it's just an expression, it means it's your responsibility. Nobody's watching anything. And fine, the time, if it came through garbled, then it's half past [CODE_1], sorry, no, I mean, hang on, it's on my sheet here, kick-off is [CODE_1], that's the revised time. Look, I've got a list of parents to get through before this evening, the pitch has been condemned for Saturday, the referee's been told, the other side's been told, and all I need from you is a yes that you've got the new pitch and the new time, because if the child turns up at the wrong end of the grounds at the wrong hour, that's a forfeited match, and I'd rather not be the one explaining that to the committee. So, behind the pavilion, [CODE_1], can I put you down as informed?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm being awful, I know you've got a whole list. Could I just go back a bit, though? Two minutes ago you said the committee do the paperwork and you do the grounds, and I've never heard of security operations at the club, so I'm not quite sure who you are. And honestly, the time still came through as a sort of code to me, so I can't say I've got it. Could you just say it slowly, like a normal time, and, uh, say your name again too, I missed that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I've said it twice, and the name's [PERSON_2]. If you're not satisfied, ring the clubhouse and ask them, I haven't got time for this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, I didn't mean to -- but I can't put myself down as informed when I haven't actually heard the time, can I? And ring the clubhouse, yes, I will, that's -- hang on, you said ring the clubhouse, so is there a number for -- no, sorry, I'll find it myself. I'll just ring them and check, and then I'll know, won't I? Sorry to be a bother, thank you for letting me know, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine, ring them, but it won't change a -- right. Behind the pavilion, [CODE_1], that's all it is. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'll ring them, sorry -- I'll find the number myself, don't you worry. Thank you, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Whatever suits.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I didn't mean to be difficult, I just like to be sure. Right then, I'll ring the clubhouse and they can tell me about Saturday. Thank you for calling, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, well, do that. Oh, hang on, [PERSON_3], not that gate, the other one, it's chained for -- sorry. Right, yes, ring the clubhouse. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I will, I'll ring them straight -- oh, you're busy with the gate, sorry, I'll let you get on. Goodbye then, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm? Sorry, there's a mower started up behind me, I can hardly hear myself. Yes, fine, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's all right, don't you worry, I'll, um, I'll just -- yes. Well. Right. I'll ring the clubhouse, like I said, and, uh, goodbye then, take care with the mower. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Right, this is [PERSON_2] calling from the collections office at [COMPANY_A], the charitable foundation, I'm on the pledge fulfilment desk, and I'm ringing about a verbal pledge of [AMOUNT_1] that was made at our recent event in [CITY_1], which, uh, is now showing as outstanding on the file under [ACCOUNT_REF]. I do need to get that closed out today, so I just need a few minutes of your time to confirm it and arrange how it's going to be honoured.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, that's me, sorry, hang on, you're on loudspeaker, I've got my hands in the soil here -- oh, get out of it, you daft bird, that's my compost, not yours. Sorry, where was I? A pledge? At an event? I mean, I go to a few things, I'm not sure I remember promising anything, but, uh, what was the event again? And did you say you're from a charity, or a collections office? I got a bit lost there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a printer going off behind me, give me a second. Right. So, charity, it's the foundation, the collections office is just the department that follows up on pledges, so both, really. The event was the one in [CITY_1], I've got it here on screen, and the pledge is logged at [AMOUNT_1], verbal, taken on the night. As for who took it and the detail of the record, that's confidential, I can't share that over the phone, but I can note on the file that you don't recall it, and the pledge stays outstanding either way. So what I need from you today is to confirm you'll honour it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ooh, hang on, sorry, I'm still stuck on something from before. You said the collections office is part of the foundation, fine, but then you said you can't tell me who took the pledge because it's confidential? I mean, it's my pledge, isn't it, so how's it confidential from me? And you said it stays outstanding even if I don't remember it, which, I don't know, that sounds a bit odd to me. Sorry, I'm probably being slow, but can you go over that bit again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair question, and I'll note the objection on the file. So, the way it works is the pledge sheets from the night are held under the foundation's donor records policy, and that covers who took it and the exact wording, so I'm not able to read any of that out on a call, it's only released through the formal request route. That's standard, it isn't aimed at you. What I can see on screen is the pledge, [AMOUNT_1], verbal, recorded at the event, and under the foundation's terms a recorded pledge is treated as a commitment whether or not the donor remembers making it. It's not a threat, that's just how it's been classed, and the account will carry as outstanding until it's settled. Now, I know a lot of people say they don't recall, it was a busy evening, there was a lot going on, and the foundation does understand that. But the work that pledge was meant to fund is already planned around it, and there are people relying on it. So I'm not asking you to hand over the full amount today, I'm asking you to confirm you'll honour it, and we'll go from there. Can I put that down?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the work is already *planted*? Planted around it? Oh, that's funny, I'm literally planting things right now, I've got a whole tray of lettuces here. Is the foundation a gardening one, then? Because that would be a nice coincidence, I do love a bit of gardening. But hang on, you still haven't said what it actually does, the foundation, I mean. And, uh, I'm still not sure I'd want to say yes to something I can't remember, so, no, don't put anything down just yet.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Planted, uh, well, I'm not sure about that, I wouldn't say it's a gardening charity as such. Anyway, I'll note you're not prepared to confirm at this stage, that's on the file now. But I should say the account still shows outstanding, and once it moves to the next stage of the process, the pledge will be passed to the recovery team and it's recorded against your name from that point. I really don't want it to go that way, [PERSON_1], especially with the people who are counting on it. So if you could just say you'll honour it, that keeps everything simple and I can close this off on my side today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the recovery team? Oh, the *recovery* team, no wait, I thought you said recovery tea. Like, a tea thing, a cuppa to recover from the event? Ha, that's lovely, I could murder one actually. No, hang on, I'm being daft. You mean like debt people, don't you? That's a bit of a leap for something I don't even remember saying. And you still haven't told me what the foundation actually does, you keep sliding past that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just put a folder on my desk, it's, right, never mind. Yes, recovery as in the recovery team, but that's only if it goes unresolved, and I'd honestly rather it didn't, so I'll note that the foundation's aims weren't covered and that you've raised it. The detail on that is in the donor pack, and I can't go through it on this call. Look, [PERSON_1], nobody's sending anyone round, it's just a record on the file, and if you can simply tell me you'll honour the pledge, I can mark it as agreed today and that's all it needs.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. No, I think I'll leave it there. You can't tell me what the foundation does, or who took the pledge, and I don't remember making it, so I'm not saying yes to anything today. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm, I'm calling on behalf of [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier, and I, um -- I don't really enjoy making these calls, but there's an overdue balance on your account and I wanted you to hear it from a person before anything, you know, happens to your supply.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- overdue? Hang on, I was just, I've literally just woken up, I was having a little lie down and -- who is this again? Because I pay the, uh, the thing, the direct debit, my daughter sorted that out years ago, so I don't see how, I mean --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I know, I'm sorry to wake you, I do, it's just that -- look, I'm [PERSON_2], I'm calling for [COMPANY_A], and the direct debit, that's, uh, that's actually part of it, it seems like a few payments didn't go through, and I'd hate for your power to be switched off, especially, you know, with the weather. I mean, it's [AMOUNT_1] outstanding, and if it isn't sorted by, um, by the end of next week, supply would be interrupted, and I really don't want that for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Switched off? Next week? Oh, that's, no, I don't like the sound of that, it's been cold as anything, I had the heating on all morning. But, um, how do I know you're from the, the energy people? Because you've not said my name properly, you said it like you weren't sure, and my daughter always says, she always says don't, well, I can't remember exactly what she says, something about people ringing up. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or, I don't know, can I look at my bill? It's in the, it's in one of those drawers somewhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, that's a good thing your daughter says, honestly, she's right. Sorry, one second, someone's just put a trolley right by my desk -- right, sorry. Yes, please, get the bill, I'd really rather you did. Your account reference on it should be [ACCOUNT_REF], and the last bill should say [AMOUNT_2] on it, and I'm not asking you for anything on this call, I don't take payments or card details or anything like that. If you want to, you can log in to your own account at [URL_1] and see the balance and the missed payments yourself, and if the lump sum is too much, we can look at a payment plan, spread it out. And I did say your name wrong, I'm sorry, I'm, I'm just not very good at these calls, it's [PERSON_1], isn't it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, I haven't gone and got the bill yet, you've only just said, and I've just woken up. And you did say my name a bit wrong, didn't you, but you're asking me if it's right, so, I mean, how would you not know? That's what's bothering me. The log in thing, I don't really do the computer, my daughter does all of that, so I can't just go and look at a, a website. Could I ring you back instead? Is there a number? Because I'd rather ring the number on my bill, if I can find the bill, in the drawer. You said you're not asking for anything, which is, well, that's good, I suppose, but then why ring me up about it? Why not just send a letter?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's fair, that's all fair, and I'm sorry, I'm making a mess of this. The name thing, I've got it written down here but the handwriting on my sheet is a bit, uh, scrappy, and I second-guessed myself, which is silly, I know, it sounds worse than it is. And there have been letters, that's the thing, a couple of them, and when there's no reply, we're meant to try a call before anything gets, you know, switched off, because it feels wrong to just cut someone off without ever speaking to them, especially someone who's been with the company a long time and been, um, well, a good customer, I mean it's not like you've been ignoring anyone on purpose, it's probably just post getting lost or the direct debit changing at the bank or something. So, no, you shouldn't take my word for any of it, and you don't need the computer either, just ring the number on your bill, the one printed right on it, not one I give you, and ask them about [ACCOUNT_REF], and if your daughter's about she can look at the account with you and sort out the payment plan. I'm only, I just didn't want it to be a shock if the power went off on you, that's all. I'm sorry I woke you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay. Well, I'll find the bill, and I'll ring the number that's on it, and maybe ring my daughter as well. Thanks for, um, letting me know, I suppose. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, that's the right thing to do, honestly. And please don't worry, nothing's going to happen today, it's, uh, it's the end of next week, so you've got time to go through it properly with your daughter. I'm sorry again for the muddle, and for waking you. Thank you for being so patient with me. You take care, [PERSON_1], and, um, keep warm. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I will, I'll go and look in the -- right, bye now, bye, thank you, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with -- sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from, well, it's [COMPANY_A], we're a computer security firm, and I just -- let me start that again. I'm hoping to ask you a couple of quick questions about the internet setup at your home, if now's an alright time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um -- hello? Yes, I'm, well, I think so, who -- sorry, I just woke up, I was having a bit of a lie-down. Computer security, did you say? I mean, I've got the, the thing, the router, but my nephew set it all up, so I don't really -- what was it you wanted to know?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to wake you. That's -- no, please, take your time. Computer security, yes, [COMPANY_A]. And that's quite alright about the nephew, that's very common, it's usually a family member who sets these things up. I'd just like to ask, if I may, whether you're the person who looks after the computer at the house, or is it your nephew who looks after it? Sorry, I know I'm asking twice, I just want to be sure I'm speaking to the right person.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, nobody really looks after it, I suppose. I just use it for the, you know, the emails and the pictures of the grandchildren. My nephew comes round now and then if it goes funny. Um -- but hang on, how did you get my number? I don't think I've ever, I mean, did I ring you about something? Because I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you didn't ring us, that's, I'm glad you asked, actually. It's a very fair question, and I'd rather you ask it than not. The number comes from, well, it's -- let me put it this way. We work with the broadband providers on a certain type of flagged activity, and your line came up on a list we're, uh, required to follow up on. I can't really go into the particulars of the list, you understand. But the thing I wanted to ask, and it's nothing to worry about at this stage, is whether you've noticed the computer running slowly at all, or doing anything odd in the last week or so?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A list? What sort of list, sorry, I don't -- I mean, you said that, but you didn't really say who gave you my number. Was it the broadband people? Because I'm with, well, I can't think of the name just now. Anyway, the computer, no, it's been the same as ever, a bit slow, but it's always a bit slow. But what list is it? Who's on it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. I did hear you, and I'll say it plainly -- I can't tell you who else is on it. That's rather the point of it being a list. What I can say is that your connection was sending something out that it shouldn't have been, and, well, these things don't tend to wait forever.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sending something out, um -- well, hang on, I'm just, give me a second, I'm trying to think what -- sending what out, exactly? Because I haven't done anything, I just do the emails and, uh, the pictures. And you still haven't said which broadband people, so how do I know you're not just, you know, anybody?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm glad you said that, I really am. You're right to ask, and honestly more people should. It's the sort of care that stops trouble, so please don't apologise for it. I did say I couldn't go into the particulars, and I'm afraid that holds for the provider's name as well, it's part of how we're asked to handle these. As for what was being sent out, it's traffic, infected traffic, which usually means something got onto the computer without anyone doing anything wrong. You wouldn't have seen it. That's rather how it works. Now, the way this normally goes, someone on our side takes a look at the machine directly, and, well, the sooner that happens the better. I'd rather not say more than that just yet. Do you have the computer near you at the moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, it's in the back room, I'm not near it, I'm on the settee. But hang on, you said at the start it was just a couple of quick questions about the internet, and now somebody's got to look at the machine directly? That's not quite, I mean -- and you said it was nothing to worry about, and now it's infected. Which is it? And you still won't say who gave you my number, so I don't really see why I'd let anybody look at anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I do see why that sounds like a change, and I'd be uneasy in your place too, so thank you for saying it. I wouldn't call it two different things, though. It was nothing to worry about at that stage, and the stage has moved on a little now that we've spoken. I'm, uh, not able to say more than that. What I'd suggest is that you go and sit in front of the machine, just so it's there, and we can think about the next step together. I'd rather we didn't leave it too long, you understand, but there's no need to rush yourself either. Could you do that for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hang on, hang on, there's the kettle, no, that's not the kettle, that's next door's dog again, he's been at it all afternoon. Sorry. Where was I -- the machine, yes. Well, no, I don't think I'll go and sit in front of it just now, if I'm honest. You've told me it's fine and then it's not fine, and you won't tell me who you are working for, and now I'm meant to go and, what, sit there while you tell me what to do with it? I'd rather ring my nephew first and have him have a look. Is there a number I can ring you back on, a proper one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ringing your nephew, well, that's a sensible instinct, and I wouldn't want to talk you out of it. It's just that, uh, the longer a machine in that state is left connected, the more it tends to, well, I won't go into it. A number to ring me back on, I'm not able to give you one from this desk, I'm afraid. The lines here are all outbound, you see, it's a matter of how the department is set up. Perhaps what we could do is, if you ring him now, I could stay on, and then we could all, hm, no, that's probably more than you'd want. Let me think. Sorry, I've lost my place. Could you just tell me whether the machine is switched on at the moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not going to tell you whether it's switched on or not, that's -- I don't know why you'd need to know that. You've gone round in circles a bit, haven't you? Nothing to worry about, then infected, then no name, then no number to ring back. I'm sorry, but I'm going to ring my nephew and let him sort it out, and if you're genuinely from a proper firm then I expect you'll manage without me. Right, well, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'd ring your nephew's firm? No, no, I wouldn't do that, he won't have the, well, it's not a thing a firm of his sort could -- hello? Are you still there? I only meant that we'd rather -- hold on, I think I've lost you. Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, yes, I'm still here, I was just, hang on. No, I didn't say his firm, I said my nephew, he's not got a firm, he's just, he does something with, I don't know, something in an office. Anyway. And now you're telling me not to ring him? That's a bit odd, isn't it, a minute ago you said it was a sensible instinct. No, I think I've had enough of this. I'm going to ring him, and you can sort out your list on your own. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. No, I wasn't telling you not to, I only -- well, you've put it differently to how I meant it. I can hear you've made up your mind, and I don't want to be the sort of firm that, uh, keeps someone on the line. So I'll leave it with you. I would only say that these matters do have a way of, well, I can't give you a date, but they don't stay where they are. Perhaps, hm, perhaps I'll try the line again later in the week, once you've had a chance to -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still here, I've said goodbye twice now, haven't I? No, don't ring again later in the week, please. If it's something real, my nephew will deal with it, and if it's not, well, then it's not. Right, I'm putting the phone down now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello... yes, good afternoon. This is [PERSON_1], compliance, at [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, and I'm calling about a refund that's, uh, been sitting on file in your name.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hello? Sorry, I'm in the car, the reception's awful out here -- did you say tax office? A refund? Sorry, can you say that again, I'm on speaker and I only caught, uh, something about a refund on file.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, no trouble at all. I said this is [PERSON_1], from compliance, at [COMPANY_A], the national tax office... and there's a refund on file in your name, a, uh, rather sizeable one, [AMOUNT_1]. It's, well, it's best we settle it sooner rather than later, you understand. Now, is this a safe moment to talk, or are you driving?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, I am driving, yeah, sorry. A refund... for what, though? I didn't think I was owed anything. Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, well... that's a perfectly fair question, and I'm glad you asked it. Most people are surprised, you see, uh, it's an overpayment, the kind that builds up quietly over, over several years, and then the system flags it for release. I'm [PERSON_1], compliance, [COMPANY_A]. Now, to match the file to you, I'd just need to confirm a few personal details, your date of birth, to begin with... and, um, it would be good to have this finished before the window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, okay, an overpayment, right, I mean that does make sense, I suppose, I've been in the same job a while and I never really check those things, my partner always says I should, sorry, I'm rambling. It's just, I'm on the motorway right now and the signal keeps cutting out, and I'd honestly feel a bit better if I could, uh, check this properly first? Like, how would I know you're actually from the tax office? I'm not saying you're not, I really don't mean to be rude, it's just that it's a lot of money, and, um, you said a window closing, which, what window? Nobody's ever mentioned a deadline to me before, so I'm a bit confused about that part. Could I maybe just call the tax office back myself, on the number I already have? Or would that, I don't know, mess up the file or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a very sensible question, and I'd never want you to feel rushed or uneasy about it. Checking is exactly what a careful person does. Now, the window, I may have put that more strongly than I should, it isn't a fixed date as such, more that files like this don't stay open indefinitely, you understand. And calling back, well, you could, but I'd gently say the main switchboard won't have this file in front of them, it's held in my section... and, uh, as I said earlier, the amount is [AMOUNT_2], for the, the most recent year. So if you could simply confirm your date of birth, we can keep this moving.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, can I just -- you said it was [AMOUNT_1] before, and now it's [AMOUNT_2]? Is that, are those different amounts? And, uh, hang on, if the main number can't see my file, then how does anyone check you're who you say you are? I mean, that's sort of the whole point of calling them, isn't it? I'm really not trying to be difficult, I just, I'd feel much better ringing the number I already have, and I'm not giving out my date of birth while I'm driving anyway, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, yes, the, uh, motorway, I did catch that part, and no, I'd never ask anyone to, to tackle a... a tax return while driving. But I should say, it isn't a return, it's a refund, and the figure is the figure, [AMOUNT_1], or, well, [AMOUNT_2], these things get adjusted for interest, you see, depending on the year. I do appreciate you raising it, truly, it shows real care with your affairs. If we could just confirm your date of birth, once you're parked, that would, um, keep the file from lapsing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, but, uh, you've said the file might lapse now, and before it wasn't a fixed date, and the amounts keep changing, and I'm just, I'm getting a bit lost, honestly. And you still haven't really said how I'd know it's you, you just keep asking for my date of birth. I'm sorry, I know that sounds rude, but I think I'm going to ring the tax office myself on the number I already have, once I'm parked. If there's a refund, they'll be able to tell me, won't they? So, uh, thank you, and sorry for the trouble, but I'm going to do that. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I do understand, and I'm glad you raised all of it... but if I could just say once more, it's a refund, a genuine refund, held on file in your name, and the file, uh, it won't stay open for very long, you see. Before you ring off, if you could simply confirm your date of birth, once you're parked, we can keep it from lapsing... hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, sorry, I'm still here, the signal keeps going. But no, I'm sorry, I'm not going to give that out, not to someone I can't check, and you've said the file might lapse three different ways now. If it's real, the tax office will tell me when I ring them myself. So, thank you, sorry again, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I, uh, I wouldn't say three ways, I don't think I said it would lapse at all, only that these things don't stay open indefinitely... and, as I mentioned at the start, that's really why I rang you directly rather than writing, though I believe I said earlier that it would be a letter that went out. If you do speak to the main line, I'd, um, I'd gently suggest they may not be able to see it, and then you'd have lost the, the opportunity, quite unnecessarily.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, wait, two minutes ago you said it was a refund that was on file, and now you're saying it would be a letter that went out? Which is it, did you send me a letter or not? Because I haven't got one, and, uh, you said the main line might not see it, which is the bit that really worries me, honestly. If it's my money, surely they can see it. I'm sorry, I'm going to ring them myself, I really am. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], about the course place you applied for. Uh, sorry, before I go on, did you say earlier that you'd already had something from us by post, or was that a different provider? Only I've got a closing time on the place today, so I'd like to get that straight first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hello? Sorry, I've just, I was having a bit of a lie down, it's been one of those days, so give me a second. Yes, that's me, I think, [PERSON_1], yes. But I didn't say anything earlier, did I? I don't think we've spoken before, unless you mean someone else rang me, because honestly the phone goes and I'm half asleep and I couldn't tell you who's who. And post, well, I get a lot of post, the hall table's just covered in it, the council, the bins, something about the boiler, so I couldn't say if there was one from you or not. What was it you said it was, a course place? I don't remember applying for anything, but then I don't remember a lot of things at the moment. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you didn't say anything earlier, that was me getting ahead of myself, sorry. It's [PERSON_2], account services at [COMPANY_A], we're an adult training provider, [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about a course place linked to an application in your name. Now, I know it's out of the blue, and if you don't remember applying, that's fine, that's exactly why I'd rather send you the details in writing, so you can look at them when you're properly awake. I can email them across right now, it'll take a minute, but I do have a closing time on the place today, so it'd be good to get that moving. Is the email address on your application still the right one to use?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, you said I didn't say anything earlier and then you said that was you getting ahead of yourself, I'm not sure I followed that, I'm still a bit foggy. But the thing is, if I don't remember applying, how would you have my email? That's what I'd like to know. I mean, you're asking me if it's still the right one, but you've not said what it is, so you must have it written down somewhere, so why don't you just read me what you've got and I'll tell you. Because I'm not going to just give it out to someone I've never spoken to, sorry, it's not that I don't believe you, I just, I don't know who you are, really. And what do you mean a closing time today? Closing for what? I've not paid for anything, have I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're right to ask, and you've not paid for anything, nothing's been taken, nothing's due on this call. Uh, the thing is, I, I can't read the address out over the phone, it's, well, it's just not something we do, so I'll leave that alone, and you're quite right not to give it to me either. What I can say is the place is held in your name, and the closing time is just when the place is released to the waiting list, that's all it is, so, so really it's, it's the details I'd like you to have in writing, which is the whole reason for the call. Now, this is an outbound-only line, so I can't take calls on it, which I know sounds awkward, but the main number for [COMPANY_A] is on our website, [URL_1], and you can ask for the admissions team and speak to [PERSON_3] directly, and look that up yourself, not from me. Would that suit you better than me emailing anything today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh... hm. Right. So, let me think, I'm still, sorry, I'm still a bit, you know, waking up. So you're saying look it up myself and ring them, not you, and that's, well, that's actually, hm, that's not what I expected you to say, I thought you'd be pushing a bit more. Um, but I still don't remember applying for anything, that's what's nagging at me, and if there's no application then there's no place, is there, so what would I even be ringing about? And the website, I'd have to find the thing, and write it down, and I've not got a pen, it's all in the kitchen drawer somewhere, or maybe the hall table, under the boiler letter...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, well, no rush, take your time, I'm, I'm not going anywhere. And that's a fair point, if there's no application on their system, then there's no place, and that's exactly the thing the admissions team can check for you, so you'd be ringing just to ask whether an application exists in your name, that's all. You don't need a pen, either, just search for [COMPANY_A] and the main number's on the front page, so, so there's nothing to write down. And honestly, if you don't recognise it, you can leave it altogether, there's no obligation, nothing happens if you don't ring. The closing time I mentioned, forget I pushed that, it's not a reason to rush, not at all. Would you like me to send a short note by email anyway, uh, to the address we hold, so it's in writing, or would you rather just leave it with the admissions team?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a short note by e-mail, right. Hang on, did you say a short note or a short *quote*? Because I've not asked anyone for a quote, I had a man round about the boiler, and he said he'd send one, and I never got it, so is that what this is? No, no, you said course, sorry, I'm all over the place. But look, you've been quite straight with me, I'll give you that, you've not been pushy. I think I'll just leave it, if that's all right, and if I do remember applying for something I'll look the number up myself. I don't think I want anything sent to an address you won't even tell me, to be honest. Right, well, thanks for ringing, I suppose, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, a note, not a quote, nothing to do with your boiler, sorry, I should've, no. That's, that's absolutely fine, and I'd rather you were comfortable than, well, sent something you weren't sure about. So I'll leave it there, nothing goes out, nothing's due, and if the application does ring a bell, search for [COMPANY_A], ask for admissions, and mention [PERSON_3], and they can check it for you. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, go and get that lie down. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I might do that, ta. Though if I lie down now I'll never get up again, ha. Anyway, thank you, bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, and sorry, did you say the boiler's in for a service? Because we don't do anything with boilers, that'd be a different company entirely. Uh, anyway, I'll let you go, [PERSON_1], thanks again, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, I never said it was in for a service, I only said there's a letter about it on the hall table. Anyway, doesn't matter, I know you don't do boilers, you said, it's a course thing. Right, I really will go now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, my mistake, you said a letter, not a service, sorry, I've got, uh, hang on, someone's just dropped a pile of folders behind me, give me a second -- right, sorry about that. Yes, a course thing, that's all it ever was, and nothing needed from you. Bye now, [PERSON_1], take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, well, uh, right, so, yes, that's... you take care too, I suppose, and, um, I hope the folders are all right, ha. Anyway, I'll look it up myself if it comes to me, so, yes, bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, they're fine, thanks, just a bit of a, uh -- right, and that's all it needs, you look it up if it comes back to you, [COMPANY_A], admissions, ask for [PERSON_3], that's the, that's the whole of it. Thanks again, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, right, yes. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon! Is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? Lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the customs desk at [COMPANY_A], and I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, how's your week been so far? I'm ringing about a parcel that's due to come to you, there's a small import charge sitting on it that needs sorting before we can deliver, and, oh, sorry, did you say you're not expecting anything?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, one sec -- [muffled to a colleague] yeah, just leave it on my desk, thanks. Uh, sorry. So, a parcel, and there's an import charge on it? And no, I didn't actually say anything yet, but, no, I'm not really expecting anything. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're fine, no apology needed, I always catch people mid-task! So it's [PERSON_2], P-E-R, well, [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the courier, I'm on the customs desk there. And I'm ringing about a parcel with an import charge on it, [AMOUNT_1], that's all it is, a small one. I hear you though, if you're not expecting anything that's a bit odd, isn't it? Anyway, the tracking reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and you can look that up yourself on our site at [URL_1], no need to take my word for it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you're [PERSON_2] from the courier, [COMPANY_A], and the charge is [AMOUNT_1]. And I can look the reference up on your site, right. Uh, but I'm at work, I've got people around, so I'm not really going to be typing in a tracking number off a phone call. If I'm not expecting anything, who's it even from? Like, who's the sender?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, completely fair, honestly I'd be the same, I wouldn't type anything in off a cold call either. The sender on our system is listed as [COMPANY_B], it's from overseas, and I can't see much more than that on my screen, I'm afraid. Now, the only thing is the parcel only stays in our depot here in [CITY_1] for a few more days before it goes back, but that's, I mean, it's your call entirely, so, oh, sorry, were you going to say something?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, no, I was just -- thinking. So, [COMPANY_B], from overseas, and you can't see anything else, that's... sort of odd, isn't it? Like, if it's my name on it you'd think there'd be more on your screen. And a few days, then it goes back. Right. Hmm. Look, I'm not ordering anything from anywhere that I know of, so, um, how do I check this with someone other than you? Is there a number I can ring myself, or...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yes, good question, and I'll be honest, you're right that it does sound a bit thin from my end. Sorry, which bit did you want me to go back over, the few days thing? Because I should be clearer, I didn't mean it's a countdown or anything, it's just how long the depot holds parcels before they go back, and there's no rush from me at all. And yes, please do check it with someone other than me. Ring the number on the [COMPANY_A] website, or pop the reference [ACCOUNT_REF] into the tracking page at [URL_1] whenever you're somewhere private, and if the charge is real it'll be sitting there on the page. You don't need to pay anything or tell me anything on this call, I'm only ringing so you've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so I don't need to pay or tell you anything now, and I can ring the number on the [COMPANY_A] website myself, or look up the reference later when I'm somewhere private. Right. That's, uh, fair enough, actually. I'll do that. If it's real, it'll show up, and if it's not, well, then it won't. Thanks for being straight about it, I appreciate that. I've got to get back to what I was doing, so, yeah. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, not at all, and thank you for hearing me out, I know a call like this lands a bit out of the blue. That's exactly the right way to go about it, honestly. Ring the number on the website, or look the reference up on the tracking page when you've got a quiet minute, and if there's nothing there, or it doesn't match anything you're expecting, then just leave it be, you won't hear any more pressure from me. I'll make a note on my side that you're going to check it yourself, so nobody rings you back in a flap. And, oh, the weather's turning here in [CITY_1], so I hope you've got a nicer afternoon than the one I'm having! Anyway, you get back to your desk, [PERSON_1], and take care now. Bye for now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, you too. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I know it's a bit late in the day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, well, it depends who's asking, doesn't it? I mean, I just woke up, I was having a bit of a lie down, you know how it is, the afternoon gets to you and then the telly's on and you're gone. And it's not that late, is it? Or maybe it is, I haven't looked at the clock. Who is this, sorry?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, you're fine, nothing wrong with a good lie down, I'm the same, honestly. Oh, sorry, hang on one second, [PERSON_2], can you grab that for me? Thanks. Sorry about that, it's a bit of a zoo in here today. My name's [PERSON_3], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], customer care side of things, and I just wanted to check I had the right household before I say anything else.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a zoo, yeah, I can hear it a bit, sounds busy. Uh, [COMPANY_A], is that, hang on, is that the one with the, no, that's a different one, I think. Right household for what, though? I mean, you've rung me, so you must have a number written down somewhere, haven't you? You'd think you'd know who you were ringing. What's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, right, a lizard? No, no, no lizards here, though honestly it sometimes feels like it, we've got the heating cranked right up. Anyway, you're quite right, I do have a number in front of me, I just like to confirm with people first, it's good manners. So, tell me, how long have you been in the house there, [PERSON_1]? Lovely area, I'd imagine, [CITY_1] is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A lizard? No, I said a zoo, I think, or you did, whatever. Oh, hang on, the kettle's, no, that's the fridge, it does that clicking thing, drives me mad. Sorry. How long have I been here? Why do you want to know that? Years, anyway, ages. But you still haven't said what it's actually about, and now you're asking me about my house, and I haven't even said it's [CITY_1], have I? Did I say that? I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you're right, you didn't, and that's on me, it's just on the file in front of me, that's all, nothing sinister, I promise. Honestly, I do run on a bit, my manager's always telling me to get to the point, and my wife says the same, I can talk the hind leg off a donkey, so let me stop waffling and just say it. What it's about is, uh, our monitoring picked up some unusual traffic coming from your home computer, quite a lot of it actually, and it looks like it's infected. Now, it's nothing to panic about, we see it all the time, but it does need dealing with fairly quickly, because the longer it runs the worse it gets, and what I'd like to do is just get you to switch the computer on so I can have a quick look at it with you while we're on the phone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Infected? Oh no, hang on, is this about the flu, because I did have a jab, I'm fairly sure, or was that last year? Though what the flu's got to do with a computer I don't know, that's the telly's fault, they go on about it all the time. And you're from, what was it, [COMPANY_A], and you want me to switch something on? Look, I'm still half asleep. How would you even know what's going on with my computer? I never gave anyone permission to look at it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, not the flu, though fair enough, it's the time of year for it. Look, we don't need your permission to see the traffic, that's all just on our side, it's the same way the water board knows if you've a leak, you follow? And listen, I did say I was ringing from the security side of [COMPANY_A], didn't I, not customer care, sorry, I get my departments mixed up, it's the same building anyway. The thing is, if we leave it till tomorrow it could spread to everything else on your network, so if you could just pop the computer on for me now, it'll only take a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, you said customer care before, I'm sure you did, and now it's security, and, uh, mm, the water board, that's not quite the same, is it? A leak's a leak, you can see it on the meter. Hmm. Er, I don't know. You keep saying it's nothing to panic about and then in the same breath it'll spread and I've got to do it now. That's a bit, well, which is it? And I haven't really got the computer on, it's in the back room, it's under a pile of, oh, never mind what. How do I know you are who you say you are, anyway?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, you know, I'd say you can just ring us back, except, uh, hang on, the switchboard's down today, it was only ever the one line I had open, so that's no good, is it? And I'm sure I said it was a light bit of traffic earlier, not a big thing, though honestly it's quite a lot, I mean, it's not much, but it's enough that we can't leave it. Look, forget the back room, the pile of whatever it is can stay where it is, you only need to go in and press the one button, and then I can show you everything from here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I don't know about that. See, you've just told me the switchboard's down, which is exactly the thing that'd make me want to ring you back, and now I can't, so that's rather convenient, isn't it? And you said it's a lot of traffic and then you said it's not much, and I'm tired, I'm not daft, I did hear that. It's a bit like my sister, she rang once about some prize, and it turned out, well, never mind what it turned out, she lost her good coat over it, don't ask me how. Anyway, I'm not going into the back room and pressing anything while you're on the line telling me what to do and you can't even tell me who you are properly. If you're really from [COMPANY_A], there'll be a number on a bill somewhere, or on the back of something, and I'll ring that myself when I've had a cup of tea and woken up properly. So no, not today, I don't think. Thank you, but no. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm, I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], they're a promotions agency, and, well, I've been asked to reach you because you've, uh, you've won something. A regional draw, in [CITY_1]. And I know that probably sounds strange, but it's sort of time-sensitive, so I wanted to get hold of you today if I could.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, well -- who's asking, exactly? Sorry, I just, I don't recall entering any draw. Like, I mean, I don't think I've -- what was the name of the, the agency again? And which draw?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I understand, I do. It's [COMPANY_A]. They're a promotions agency, I said that, I think? And it's the regional draw, the one in [CITY_1], the, uh, the one you were entered into. I'm not the one who runs it, I'm just, I'm passing along the message for [PERSON_2], who asked me to call. And honestly, it's a good prize, it's [AMOUNT_1], and I'd hate for you to miss out on it, because they can only hold it for a short while, so, so that's really why I'm calling today and not, you know, next week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said I won it, but now I was "entered into" it. Which is it? Because I still don't remember entering anything. And you keep saying "the draw," but you haven't actually told me what it's called. So what's it called, and when did it supposedly happen?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, you're right, that's, I wasn't clear, I'm sorry. You won it, that's the, that's the main thing. When I said entered, I just meant, um, that your name was in it, you know, put in by someone, or through a form, or, I mean, I don't have the whole paperwork in front of me, that's [PERSON_2]'s side of it, not mine. utterances.text: Well, hang on, hang on, before you ring anybody, that file is going to, uh, move to the next stage on my end, and I can't speak for what happens after that. So, once more, just confirm the name on the file, and we can, uh, sort this right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a warning, what, a warrant? Is this about a warrant now? Nobody said anything about the police, I thought it was a bill, and now I'm hearing it's, I don't know, court or something, and that's even more reason I'm not giving you my name over the phone, honestly. If it's a real warrant I'd think a person would turn up at the door, wouldn't they? Right, I'm going to look up the real number and ring them myself, so, thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the claims verification office at [COMPANY_A]. It's just a routine enquiry regarding a contact record we have on file, do you have a moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, hi, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, bear with me, I've got the phone on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the tomato beds. Claims verification, you said? From, hang on, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? I don't think I've got any claims going, but, I mean, I'm happy to chat, it's a lovely afternoon. You said it was a moment ago a, what, a contact record? Whose, mine?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yours, precisely, and no need to apologise, the tomatoes sound far more important, I'll be brief. It's a, well, it's an entry in our overseas draw registry, and the contact field is currently flagged for re-validation, which is purely a housekeeping matter on our side, you wouldn't have needed to do anything, but I do just need to confirm a few particulars with you before the, uh, before the record can be reconciled.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, an overseas draw registry. Don't remember entering any draw, to be honest. What particulars, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, that's quite common actually, a good many entries originate through third-party aggregator enrolments, so the individual wouldn't necessarily recall, you know, opting in. The particulars are only the standard reconciliation set, namely your full name as registered, the correspondence address, and, uh, the confirmation of the entry itself, which is where the ticket reference [CODE_1] comes in, and, hm, yes, the draw dated, let me see, the fourteenth, which carries a tier-one disbursement of [AMOUNT_1], pending your validation.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, shoo, get out of it, sorry, that's the neighbour's cat, it keeps digging up my seedlings, honestly. Right, sorry, where were we. A disbursement, did you say? Of [AMOUNT_1]? That's, well, that's quite something, isn't it. But hang on, I never bought a ticket, so how would I have won anything? And you're asking for my address and a reference, but how do I know you are who you say you are? What did you say the company was again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one moment, uh, a colleague just put a file on my desk, and, yes, I'm back. So, [COMPANY_A], the international claims office, and that's a perfectly sensible question, I'd expect it from anyone. As for the ticket, the entry would have been auto-generated at the aggregator tier, so no purchase on your part, that's the standard enrolment protocol. Now, on the draw date, I did say the fourteenth, but, hm, I'm looking at the amended schedule and it may be the twenty-first, and the sum has been re-tiered to [AMOUNT_2] following the, uh, the quarterly actuarial adjustment. The important thing is that the validation window closes this afternoon, so if I could just have the address you have on file, we can lock the record before the lapse.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, hang on, hang on, now it's the twenty-first, not the fourteenth, and the amount's gone and changed as well? Uh, [AMOUNT_1] to [AMOUNT_2], that's, well, that's a bit odd, isn't it? I mean, I'm no expert, but if you can't quite keep the date straight, I'm not sure I'd want to hand over my address. And closing this afternoon, why's it all got to be this afternoon? Sorry, the trowel's slipped, one sec. So, um, can I ring you back on a number from the [COMPANY_A] website, or something like that? Because that seems like the sensible thing to do.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, I wouldn't characterise it as an inconsistency, it's a reconciliation of the schedule against the amended tier structure, but I do understand the, the hesitation. The difficulty with a callback is that our verification lines are, hm, routed through a regional queue, so you'd be placed in the general holding pool and the validation window would very likely lapse before we could reconnect. If you could simply confirm the correspondence address now, we can secure the record, and you can authenticate us at your leisure afterwards, which is entirely, uh, standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, no, I think I'll leave it there, if that's all right. You said earlier it'd be no bother and I wouldn't have to do anything, and now it's got to be done this very minute, and I can only check you out afterwards? That's backwards, isn't it? I'd want to check first. So I'll find the number myself and ring them, and if there's really a record, it'll still be there tomorrow. Thanks for your time, and mind how you go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Hello? Sorry, I said, is this [PERSON_1] I'm speaking to? It's [PERSON_2], calling from [COMPANY_A], just a routine enquiry about your file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, hang on, I was half in something else here. Who did you say you were calling from? Because I heard a name and a company but it came through a bit garbled, and I didn't catch what "your file" is supposed to be. I mean, I've got a few files with a few different outfits, so that doesn't exactly narrow it down. And I'm not trying to be difficult, I just don't confirm who I am to someone who rang me out of the blue. You rang me, so how about you tell me what [COMPANY_A] is, and what this routine enquiry is about, and then we'll see.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, uh, fair enough, that's reasonable. It's [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A], we're the public benefits office, I'm in the collections section. It's about your benefits record, there's a field showing incomplete on our system, so it's just a routine tidy-up, nothing to worry about. Um, so if you could just confirm your full name and date of birth for me, I'll pull it up and we can get it closed out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I'm not, I mean -- hang on. Collections section of a benefits office, that's, uh, that's a funny pairing, isn't it? Collections is the bit that wants money back, as far as I know, not the bit that tidies up fields. And you want me to give you my name and date of birth when you're the one who rang me, which is sort of backwards, you've got a file open in front of you, so you tell me what name is on it. Or, no, actually, better question. What's the incomplete field? Which one is it, specifically?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, [PERSON_3], I said leave that with me, I'll sign it after. Sorry, go on. Right, the field. It just shows as incomplete on the screen, it doesn't give me a lot more than that, which is why I need you to confirm the details so I can match the record. And I'll be straight with you, if it's not confirmed today, the record gets flagged and your payments are suspended, that's just how the system processes it. If you object to giving details over the phone, I can note that on the file, but I do still need the confirmation.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, hang on. A minute ago it was a routine tidy-up, nothing to worry about, and now my payments get suspended today if I don't read out my details. That's, uh, those two don't really sit together. And you said you're in collections, but now you're a records person who can't see what the field is, so which is it? I mean, you can see it says incomplete but not which bit, that's an odd screen. Tell you what, give me the name of the office and a number, and I'll ring them back on whatever I find myself, not what you read me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I did say it was routine, and it is, I've got forty of these on my list this afternoon. And I'm not a records person, I'm collections, I just, uh, I don't get the screen detail on every field, that's a different team. As for a number, I can't give out a direct line, the callback goes through the same system and it'll just show as unverified, which is the flag I'm trying to avoid. I'll note your objection on the file, but the record still shows incomplete, and after today the suspension goes through. So, full name and date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm, I'm not going to -- look, I was going to say maybe, but, no. You can't give me a number, the callback shows as unverified, so what you're telling me is the only way to sort this out is to trust the person who rang me. That's, uh, that's exactly backwards. A real office doesn't mind me ringing the published number, it's the whole point of having one. So I'll find it myself, and if there's a genuine flag on my record, it'll still be there when I get through. Not giving you my name or date of birth. Cheers.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I'll note that you've declined, but it won't change the status, the suspension still goes through at close of business. And I mean, it's not me ringing you for money, this isn't a collections matter, it's just the record. So if you could just confirm the name and date of birth, we can -- hello? Hello, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, I just said no. And you said it's not a collections matter, but you opened with collections, so -- anyway, I'm done. I'll ring the published number myself, and if there's a real flag it'll still be there. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. It's [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], the tiling, I came out last week to look at your bathroom. Sorry, can you hear me all right? It's [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], I just wanted to go back over the quote with you, if now's an alright time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello? Yes, I can hear you, sorry, I've literally just come round, I was having a bit of a lie-down, you know how it is in the afternoon, the telly was on and then it wasn't. Now, tiling, tiling... somebody did come, I think, or was that the man about the boiler? No, no, the boiler man was before that, he had the van with the ladder on top. Hang on, which bathroom, I've only got the one, mind you, there's the little toilet downstairs too, but that's not really a bathroom, is it? Sorry, I'm rambling. Who did you say you were again, and was that last week or the week before? Because I'm not sure I remember anyone measuring up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, take your time. I'm, uh, [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], I do tiling, bathrooms mostly. And it was last week, I think, so, ah, let me think, the Thursday, mid-morning. I had a tape measure and a little notebook, and I looked at the upstairs bathroom, the main one, not the little toilet downstairs. I was in there about, oh, twenty minutes, I'd say, and we had a cup of tea in the kitchen after. It's quite possible it's gone clean out of your head, though, it's no trouble at all, and honestly I'm glad you asked, because I'd much rather you were sure who you're talking to than just go along with it. If you'd rather, I can ring back another time, when you've had a chance to think it over.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, a tape measure and a, no, hang on, a cup of tea in the kitchen, I'd, I mean I'd remember that, wouldn't I? Or, no, maybe not, I do put the kettle on for anybody, the post lady gets one. Thursday, was it? I think Thursday was, uh, no, that was the chiropodist, or, honestly I couldn't swear to it either way. It's very good of you to say you'll ring back, that's, that's decent, but I'm just wondering, what is it you actually want to go over? Because I don't, I'm not sure I ever said yes to a quote, so I don't know what there is to go back over.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's a fair thing to ask, and I'm glad you did. So, uh, to be clear, you haven't said yes to anything. The quote's just a price I wrote up for the tiling in the upstairs bathroom, the walls round the bath and the floor, and I only wanted to read it back to you, so you could see whether it matches what we talked about. There's nothing to sign, nothing to pay, I'm not asking you for anything today. And if it turns out I've got the wrong house, or the wrong week, well, that's an honest mistake, and I'd sooner find out now. Could I ask, is that [CITY_1] address on, uh, on the road with the, the green postbox at the end?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Green postbox, well, no, ours is, I think it's a red one, they're mostly red, aren't they? Although, hang on, there was one painted for the, what was it, the Olympics, a gold one, that was somewhere else though. Oh, I don't know, I'm not going to say yes to that, am I, because you could say anything and I'd go "oh yes, that's right." I mean, you haven't said my name, have you? You've said a lot about the bathroom and the tea, but not who I am, and I've no idea what you've got written down in that notebook. So what name did you put on this quote, and what's the house number, if you've got it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, you're right, and that was a poor question on my part, the green postbox. I shouldn't have put words in your mouth like that, you'd have been quite right to just say yes to it. So, uh, the name on the quote is [PERSON_2], and the house is number [CODE_1], on the road I came to last week. Now, I did say earlier I was in there twenty minutes or so, and then you mentioned the chiropodist, so, can I just ask, when you said it was probably Thursday, did you mean Thursday you had the chiropodist, or Thursday someone measured up? Only if the chiropodist was Thursday, then I've either got my days muddled or I've got the wrong house, and either way I'd sooner sort that out before we go any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_2]? No, no, that's not me, that's not my name at all, I don't, no. And that number, no, that's not ours, we're nothing like that, I'd know my own door. So it sounds like you've got the wrong house, doesn't it? Which, you know, these things happen, and I'm not cross about it. The chiropodist, he does come Thursdays, yes, but he's been twice this month and I'd have noticed a second man in the bathroom with a tape measure. Anyway, I think you want to look at your notebook again, love, and ring whoever it was that's actually expecting you. I'll say goodbye, then, and good luck with it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, I think you're right, that does sound like a wrong number, or the wrong house, one or the other. I'm sorry to have taken up your afternoon, and especially to have woken you from your lie-down. I'll go back through my notebook and sort out who it is I'm meant to be ringing. Thank you for being so patient with me, I do appreciate it. You take care now, and enjoy the rest of your afternoon, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's all right, no harm done, I was only going to be dozing anyway, you know, and then I'd have woken up with a crick in my neck and... well, anyway. Hmm. Yes, so, you take care too, and I hope you find the right house, and the kettle's on for whoever it is, ha. Right then, goodbye, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, uh, let's hope they've got biscuits as well. Anyway, right, I'll, uh, I'll let you get on, and thank you again. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, oh, I should hope so, a tea without a biscuit, whatever next. Right, well, bye then, bye bye, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye, bye, yes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], the recruitment agency. I'm calling regarding your candidate profile, which has cleared our preliminary screening for a fully remote position, and I just need to run through the onboarding validation protocol with you before the placement window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, speaking, yeah, that's me. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? Because I've honestly got a few recruiter things floating around in my inbox from over the last few months, so I'm not sure which agency this is. And I don't actually remember applying for anything recently, or at least nothing that would've gone through screening, so I'm a bit lost on what profile you mean. Also "onboarding validation protocol" is a mouthful, what does that actually involve? Like, what are you going to ask me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, of course, [COMPANY_A], that's the agency, and uh, to your point about the profile, it would've been aggregated from, well, several of the job-board syndication feeds, so you wouldn't necessarily have applied to us directly, that's, that's sort of standard under the passive-candidate sourcing model. As for the protocol, it's really just a credential-alignment step, where we reconcile your profile against the employer's compliance matrix and, uh, clear the one-time onboarding cost so the provisioning of your remote-access tier can be released. It's [AMOUNT_1], fully reimbursable on your first payroll cycle, and the position itself is, I mean, quite generous for the hours, so the window really is time-sensitive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a minute ago you said my profile had cleared your screening, and now you're saying I never applied to you and you pulled me off some feeds. So which is it, did I get screened or did you just find me? And, sorry, you want me to pay [AMOUNT_1] before I've got a job? Because in my experience the employer pays the recruiter, not the other way round. What's the actual company, the one doing the hiring? And what's the position called?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, so, uh, the screening was an automated pass against the aggregated data, so both statements hold, the algorithmic triage precedes any direct application, that's just, that's how the pipeline architecture sequences it. And it isn't a fee in the conventional sense, it's a cost-clearance against the provisioning layer, which is why the employer's, uh, [COMPANY_B]'s, disbursement structure doesn't cover it upstream. The role is, I mean, it's categorised under remote operations coordination, though the exact title is finalised after the credential-alignment step, so I'd rather not misstate it. Now the clearance has to be settled through the, the designated settlement channel by end of day, otherwise the placement reverts to the next candidate in the queue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so let me get this straight. You can't tell me the job title, but you need money from me by end of day to unlock it. A "cost-clearance against the provisioning layer" is a fee, I'm sorry, whatever you call it. And real employers don't make candidates pay to be considered. Quick question, what's the agency's registered address? Or a company number I could look up while we're talking? Because I'm going to look you up, and I'd rather it matched what you tell me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sure, uh, the registered address is, it's the, the [CITY_1] operations office, and the company number is, well, I'd have to pull the filing reference, it sits under the parent entity rather than [COMPANY_A] directly, so it wouldn't, I mean, it may not surface the way you'd expect. But if I could just, uh, circle back to something, when you said you don't remember applying, could you clarify what you meant by that? Because if your profile isn't linked to an active application, then the credential-alignment would need to be re-initiated from scratch, and that's, that's a different timeline entirely, so before we go further I'd want to confirm which of those two situations we're actually in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, stop, I'm going to cut in there. You've now dodged the address, the company number, the employer's job title, and you're trying to flip it round onto me about my application. That's four things I asked for and none of them answered. So no, I'm not going to pay [AMOUNT_1], and I'm not going to confirm anything about my profile to you. If [COMPANY_A] is real, they can email me from their actual domain with the job spec, and I'll read it. Otherwise, we're done here. Take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, hang on, [PERSON_1], if I could just, sorry, one second, someone's at my desk -- no, not now, I'm on a call -- right, sorry about that.
