So, uh, if you'd simply let me finish the, the compliance reconciliation, the queue position doesn't hold past end of day, and I really wouldn't want you to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what was that about the, uh, the queue? Did you say a cue, like a clue? I'm not following. Anyway, it doesn't matter, I've said what I'm going to say. Email me the job spec from your proper domain and I'll look at it. Otherwise, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, hi. Uh, is this -- am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I should say, my name's [PERSON_2], and I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the financial regulator, you probably know them, or maybe you don't, it's not really a name people hear day to day. I'm, um, I'm not great at these calls, to be honest, I've been asked to ring around a few people about a, a sort of routine matter, and I just wanted to check first that I've actually got the right person before I say anything more.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, hello dear. Sorry, did you say a financial *reporter*? Because I did used to read the paper, the business pages, my husband liked those, he's been gone four years now, but anyway. Yes, I'm [PERSON_1], I think, I mean yes, that's me. What was it you wanted to ask about the, uh, the reporting?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, not a reporter, sorry, that's my fault, I mumble. Regulator. It's the, uh, the body that keeps an eye on banks and that sort of thing, so ordinary people's money is looked after properly. And I'm very sorry to hear about your husband, that's, that's a long time to be on your own. Um, so it's nothing to worry about, not at this point anyway. I'm just calling to ask, do you still keep your savings with the same bank you've always used? Because that's what I've been asked to confirm.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a regulator, I see, well that sounds very proper. And thank you, dear, it is a long time, though the cat keeps me company, she's a funny old thing, sits on the post every morning. Now, my savings, yes, I've always been with the same bank, gosh, forty years or more, my husband sorted all that out originally. But why do you want to know which bank? I mean, shouldn't you know that already, being the regulator? Sorry, I'm not being rude, I just, I'm not very good with all this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're not rude at all, that's a fair thing to ask, honestly. Um, we do have, well, the names, it's more that I wasn't, I wasn't given the, the details of which -- sorry, did you say the cat sits on the *post*? Is that the post office? Are you near the post office, because, uh, that's not, that's not really what this is about, but -- no, sorry, I've gone off track. Your savings. The thing is, [PERSON_1], and I'm sorry to say it over the phone like this, there's a worry that your savings might not be safe where they are, and I, I really didn't want you to hear that from a stranger, but someone had to ring.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the post, no, no, the fence post, in the garden, she sits on the fence post, silly me, I should've said. Oh, but dear, not safe? That's, oh, that's a bit frightening to hear, I've been with them forty years. Hang on, is it the bank that's in trouble? Because it was in the news a while back, something about some bank, or was that the building society? Anyway. Sorry, I keep wandering. You said you'd been asked to ring, who asked you, exactly? Only I'd like to know who I'm talking to, being on my own and all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a fence post, of course, that's lovely, sorry, I'm, I'm terrible at listening when I'm nervous. Um, and no, it's not that the bank's in trouble exactly, I wouldn't want to say that and have you worrying, it's more that, well, there's something that's come up with accounts like yours, and I can't really go into all of it, not on this call. Who asked me, yes, that's, that's a fair thing to want to know, it's a colleague, a senior person, at [COMPANY_A], I'm not actually allowed to give her name out at this stage, which I know sounds odd, I do know that, and I'm sorry, I'd feel the same in your shoes, being on your own and everything. I'm only the one who was asked to ring, I'm not, I don't normally do this, I do the, the admin side, really, and I said to her, I said, she's a widow, she's going to be frightened, and she said that's exactly why it has to be done carefully. And what she's, um, what we're hoping is that you'd let us help move your savings somewhere safe, just temporarily, a protected holding arrangement, until it's all sorted. But it does have to be soon, [PERSON_1], I don't want to scare you, but it's, it's really quite p

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I, I don't, no, hang on. Move my savings? I mean, I wouldn't know how to, and my husband always said, well, he always said you never, you don't let anyone else, oh, I'm not explaining it right. You can't give me her name, and you can't tell me what's wrong, but you want me to move all my money? That does seem a bit, um, back to front, doesn't it, dear? And I don't know that I've even properly heard who you are, you said [COMPANY_A], but I couldn't find that on the, oh, I haven't got anything in front of me. Is there a number I could ring you back on? Only my niece, she's usually good with these things, she might, well, she's coming Thursday, so, well, couldn't it wait till then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, [PERSON_1], please, I, I can hear I've made a mess of explaining it, and that's, that's on me, not you, you're not being silly at all. Your husband was quite right, you shouldn't let just anyone near your money, and I'd, I'd think less of you if you did. It's only that, um, Thursday, I don't know that Thursday is, well, I was told it can't really wait that long, it's days, not weeks, that matters here, and I'd hate to ring your niece's house on Friday and find that, that something had already, well, I don't want to say it. And I did say I'd give you a number, didn't I, or I was going to, [PHONE_1], that's the, the office line, though it's, uh, it'll just go to a general desk, not to me, and the person who actually knows the details isn't, isn't always in. But here's the thing, and I, I'm not saying this to frighten you, I wouldn't, I've been quite upset about this call all morning, honestly. If your niece were to be told, or the bank, even, if they were told before it's all in place, it could, it could make things a good deal worse for you, and I really couldn't say how much worse. So if you could just, just keep it between us for now, until Thursday is, well, until it's done, I think that

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, now, wait a minute, dear. Keep it from my niece? And from the bank? No, no, I don't like the sound of that at all. If it were all above board, why on earth would I not tell them? My husband would've, well, he'd have put the phone down by now, I think. You've been very nice, and I do believe you're nervous, but a general desk that doesn't know the details, and nobody I can name, and I mustn't tell anyone, that's not, that's not how a proper office does things, is it? No. I'm going to wait for Thursday and talk to my niece, and I'll ring the bank myself, on the number on my own statements. Thank you for ringing, dear, and mind how you go. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, please, [PERSON_1], don't, uh, don't hang up, I'm so sorry, I really have made a hash of this. I'm not, I'm not trying to trick you, honestly, it, it hurts a bit, hearing you think that, I've spent all morning dreading this call because I knew it would sound just like this. And, um, sorry, before you go, you said earlier your husband sorted all of it originally, the bank and so on, did he, did he leave paperwork, or was it, was it all in his name? Because that's, that actually matters to what I was asked to say, and I, I've mixed up what I was told, I think. But the thing I keep coming back to is, if you ring them yourself, if you tell the bank, the, the people who are actually causing the, the problem could, could find out, and then it's your savings that, that suffer, and I don't, I don't want that on my conscience, I really don't. Couldn't you, couldn't you just give me a little time, just, just today, and not mention it to anyone, and let me, let me put it right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, dear, I don't think I will, and I'll tell you why, because you've been so polite about it I don't want to just be short with you. You say the bank might be the ones causing the problem, but it's the bank I've trusted for forty years, and my husband trusted them before me, and it's you I've never met. And now you want to know whether the paperwork was in his name, and you want me not to mention it to anyone, not even my niece, and you keep telling me you've mixed things up. Well, if you've mixed things up, and nobody can tell me who the senior person is, then it's all the more reason to leave it till Thursday, isn't it? I'm not cross with you, truly, I'm not. You sound like a perfectly nice person, a bit flustered, and I don't suppose it's an easy job. But I'm going to put the phone down now, and I'll talk to my niece, and I'll ring the bank on the number printed on my own statements, and if there's a real problem, they'll tell me. So thank you for ringing, and mind how you go. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait. Please. I'm only trying to help you, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the cat? No, no, she's perfectly fine, dear, she's just outside, sat on the post as usual, she's not in any trouble at all. Though it's kind of you to ask, I don't think anyone's asked after her in years. Oh, but I've gone and wandered again, haven't I. No, I'm quite sure, dear, I'm going to wait for my niece on Thursday and ring the bank myself, and that's that. You take care of yourself now. Goodbye, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, uh, sorry, one moment -- [PERSON_1], could you put that on the front desk, thank you. Right, apologies. This is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, and I'm conducting a post-operative convalescence check regarding the procedure your animal underwent last week. Am I speaking with the registered owner on the file?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello? Sorry, I'm driving, you're on speaker so the line's a bit -- it might cut out. Um, the vet, did you say? Which, which animal is this about? I mean, I do have a, well, I've got a pet, but I'm not sure I had anything done last week, or, I don't know, I might be thinking of something else. Sorry, who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's quite all right, and please, keep your eyes on the road, this isn't urgent at all. I'm [PERSON_2], calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, and the reason for the call is just a routine post-operative follow-up. Sorry, you asked which animal, and honestly, uh, I should have led with that, the record I have is for a procedure performed last week under general anaesthesia, with the owner of record listed as a [PERSON_3]. If that name doesn't ring a bell, it's entirely possible I've simply dialled the wrong number, in which case I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, [PERSON_3]? No, that's, I mean -- no, I don't think that's, sorry, that's not me. I don't, hang on, no, that's not my name. So it might be, yeah, it could be a wrong number then? I'm sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just the reception's terrible and I'd hate to, um, say yes to something that isn't mine. Was there something you needed from me, though, or is it just that you've got the wrong person?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're absolutely right to be careful, and I don't need anything from you at all. It's simply a wrong number on our end, which is entirely my error. Uh, you did ask me something a moment ago, though, about who I was, and I rather muddied that with the, ah, post-operative convalescence phrasing, so, plainly: I'm [PERSON_2], I work at [COMPANY_A], a veterinary surgery, and I was only meaning to ask how a patient was recovering after an operation. Nothing more than that. I'll note that this number isn't connected to that record, and I do apologise for taking up your time while you're driving.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, honestly, I just -- sorry, I wasn't trying to, yeah, so it's just a wrong number then. That's all right, these things happen. Um, you might want to double check the number on your file, though, before you ring anyone else, I mean, someone's pet is, well, hopefully they're fine, I hope the poor thing's okay. Anyway, sorry, I really should concentrate on the road. Thanks for explaining, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, quite right, I'll, uh, I'll have the front desk, no, actually, I'll check the number against the file myself before anyone else is rung. And thank you, that's very kind, I'm sure the, the patient will be perfectly fine, it's only a routine check. Do drive safely, and my apologies again for the interruption. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no worries. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, thank you again, and, um, all the best to you, truly. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, you too. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's the scheduling assistant over at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling about the bathroom tiling quote [PERSON_2] put together after the visit last Thursday, uh, Friday, sorry, last Friday, and I just wanted to run back over the scope with you real quick and see if you wanted to pick a start date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hi, yes, this is, uh, yes it's me. Sorry, I'm, um -- the bathroom tiling, you said? I mean, I think someone did come round, but was it, uh -- sorry, it was a while back, wasn't it? Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, it's [COMPANY_A], we're the independent tradesperson outfit, [PERSON_2] was the one who came out to the house and measured up the bathroom, uh, hang on, sorry, [PERSON_2]'s van is just reversing in behind me, bit of a racket, anyway -- so it was last Friday, not that long ago, and the quote was for the full floor and walls, the tiling, I mean, so what I was ringing about is whether you'd like to pick a start date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, sorry, I can hear the van, that's fine. Um, the thing is, I'm not sure I remember [PERSON_2] coming on a Friday, I'd have to think. Did I ask for a quote, or was it, uh -- sorry, I'm a bit muddled. Could you just tell me again what the quote came to, and who it was that arranged the visit? I just want to be sure we're talking about the same house.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sure, so the quote, we had it at [AMOUNT_1] for the, uh, the tiling and labour, and you rang us originally, well, I think the visit was booked through, hang on, you said you want to be sure it's the same house, right, so it's the one in [CITY_1], the, uh, the bathroom upstairs? And sorry, you said [PERSON_2] came on a Thursday? Yeah, that's -- no, it was Friday, but anyway, the scope was the floor and the walls and the, um, the grouting, so whenever suits for a start date, I can pencil you in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Um, well -- sorry, I didn't say Thursday, I think that was you, wasn't it? Uh -- hang on. And I'm, well, I don't actually have a bathroom upstairs, so I'm, um, not sure that's my house you've got there. Sorry, I'm really not trying to be difficult, I just -- um, so you're saying you'd put me down for a date, but I haven't, I mean, I don't think I've said yes to anything yet?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, you're right, sorry, that was me with the Thursday, I got my days crossed, and no, you haven't said yes to anything, I'm only pencilling, nothing's booked, so, uh, anyway, hang on, no bathroom upstairs, right, so I've probably got the wrong house on my sheet, um, let me check, it'd be easier if you just tell me the address the visit was at, or, uh, actually, better, is there anything [PERSON_2] left with you, like a card or a quote sheet, because that'd have [ACCOUNT_REF] on it, and I can match it up, uh, yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, the kettle's just gone off, one second -- right, sorry, I'm back. Um, a card or a quote sheet, you said? I don't, I mean I don't think anyone left me anything, and I'd have remembered a van outside, wouldn't I? And, sorry, it's a bit odd, isn't it, you ringing me for the address, when you're the one who's meant to have it? Could you maybe just tell me what number you've got on your sheet, and then I can say if it's mine?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, a number, right, so the number on the sheet, it's, well, hang on, it's actually the other way round, you said it's odd me ringing, and it's not, I mean it's, uh, the van, yeah, [PERSON_2]'s van, you'd have remembered the van, so I'll get him to ring you from his own phone, that's [PHONE_1], and he can tell you the street and the house number and the lot, because honestly I'm just the scheduling end, I don't have the, uh, the full address on screen in front of me, so -- sorry, did you say kettle? Because I thought you said cattle, and I was going, uh, no, we don't do that sort of job, we only do tiling.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, kettle, sorry, the tea kind, not cattle. Um, but, sorry, I'm still a bit lost. You said you'd got me down for a house with an upstairs bathroom, and I haven't got one, and now you haven't got the address on screen, so I'm not sure how you found my number at all? I think, uh, I'd rather not have anyone ringing me from a mobile about a job I don't remember asking for. If [PERSON_2] did measure up somewhere, it was probably the wrong house, and I'm sorry, I know that's probably not what you wanted to hear. I think I'll leave it there, if that's all right. Thanks for ringing, and, um, good luck finding the right person. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, that's, I mean -- look, I'm sorry, I think it's on me, I've clearly got the wrong sheet in front of me, and, well, honestly, you're right not to go on with it when the details don't match, so I'll, uh, I'll take your number off the list and have [PERSON_2] go back through the visits, and, sorry, sorry for the muddle, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, that's very kind. Um, sorry, did you say you'd take me off the list, or the lift? Because I haven't got a lift either, we've just got the one set of stairs, so you'd be quite right to cross that one off as well. Anyway, no harm done, honestly. Thanks for ringing back to say, and, um, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, the list, yeah, the list, not a lift, we don't do lifts either, just tiling, so no, nothing to cross off on that front. Right, so, no harm done, you've got my apologies for the mix-up and [PERSON_2] will sort the sheet out, and, uh, thanks for being so patient with me, really, so you have a good afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's alright, no trouble at all. Um... well, uh, you have a nice afternoon as well, and I hope the tiling people get it all sorted, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Yeah, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm on the scheduling side for the regional maintenance team, and one of our engineers is returning a missed call about a fault you reported, so I just need to -- sorry, go on?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, speaking. Who? Sorry, which company did you say? I'm in a queue here, it's a bit loud -- and I didn't report any fault, not that I remember. Er, hang on, what fault?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, fair enough, it's [COMPANY_A], the regional utility maintenance team, and I know it's a bit out of the blue when you're stood in a queue, so I'll keep it short. It's the fault that was logged against your address a few days back, and honestly I don't have the full detail of it in front of me, I'm just scheduling, I just see that it was reported, an engineer tried to reach you or someone at the property, there was a missed call, and he's asked me to ring back and get a visit pencilled in. If it helps, the reference you'd have been given when you reported it is [ACCOUNT_REF], and if that doesn't ring a bell, it might've been someone else at the address who phoned it in, a partner, a neighbour, a landlord, I couldn't say. So, uh, is that address still yours, and is there someone about to let an engineer in?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Nope. Doesn't ring a bell, and I'm not confirming my address to someone who rang me. You've got my number, you've got the address, so you tell me what it is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, and you don't have to confirm anything to me, I'd rather you didn't if you're not comfortable. What I can see is just the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and that a fault was logged and a visit needs booking. And look, if you want to check me out, ring the published fault line for [COMPANY_A], the number on your bill or on the website, quote that reference, and they can see the booking and give you a proper slot. Honestly I can't give you an exact arrival time anyway, because the engineer's visit depends on an earlier job overrunning or not, so, yeah, I can't promise a window from here, but the fault line can.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, that's something, I suppose, you telling me to ring the number on the bill and not the one you gave me. Which, I'll be honest, is the first sensible thing you've said. Because I got burnt once, not going into it, but I'm still annoyed about it, and the whole "we're ringing you about a thing you don't remember, here's a reference, can you just confirm a few details" routine is exactly how it started. So I'm not saying you're dodgy. I'm saying I've no way of knowing, standing here with a basket of shopping and a bloke in front of me counting out coppers. And you still haven't told me what the fault actually is. Gas, electric, water? You work for a maintenance team and you can't say what they're maintaining? That's a bit odd, isn't it? I mean, if someone had a leak or a power problem I'd have noticed, I'd have rung someone. So no, I'm not booking anything with you. If there's a real fault, they can ring the number on my bill or send something in writing, and I'll sort it out myself, from my end, in my own time. Alright? Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, that's, I mean -- sorry, hang on, before you go, because it's a fair question and I should've -- look, I can see it's logged as a fault but the notes on my screen don't say whether it's, uh, whether it's the supply side or the pipework side, I just get the slot request, and I'd rather say that than guess and get it wrong. So I can't tell you what it is, and I'm sorry, I know that sounds thin. But if I go back to the engineer and find out exactly what was reported, would that help? I can ring you back with it, or you can ring the fault line yourself, either way, whatever you're comfortable with.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't -- look, don't ring me back. I mean, I, uh, I'd rather you didn't. Because that's the thing, isn't it, you don't know what it is, so what are you ringing back with? Sorry, that came out -- I'm not having a go. It's just, I've said what I'm doing. I'll ring the number on my bill myself, and if there's a real fault they'll know about it and it'll be in writing. That's it. That's all I'm doing. Right, I'm at the till, I've got to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, no, that's fine, I won't ring you, you do exactly that, ring the fault line off your bill, quote [ACCOUNT_REF] if they ask, and they'll tell you what's what. Sorry for catching you at the till. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, well, hang on, I'm not quoting you that reference, you didn't give me one. You said you couldn't see the detail, so, uh, right, whatever. I'll ring the number on the bill and ask what they've got for my address. Not yours, not that reference. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I did, I said it was, well, I gave you -- sorry, that's me being rushed, you're right to say that. Ring the fault line and ask what's logged against your address, you don't need anything from me for that, they can look it up from the address alone. And if they say they've got no record, then, uh, that's worth knowing, and honestly the better thing to do is let me find out why we've got you down for a visit and, well, you don't want a call, fine, but at least I can flag it on our side. Sorry, I know you're at the till. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, you said a minute ago the fault line would know from the reference, and now it's from the address alone? Which is it? And you've just told me you can't see what the fault is, but now you want to flag something on your side. Flag what? Look, I'm not giving you anything, I'm not confirming anything, and I'm not having you ring me back. I'll sort it from my end. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you've caught me out there, and that's on me, I was running my words together. The fault line can look it up either way, by the reference or by the address, so I shouldn't have made it sound like one or the other. And when I said flag it, I just meant note on our side that you've said you've no record of reporting anything, but honestly I can't tell you what that does, and I can't see the fault detail, so I'd be guessing. Can I ask you one thing, though, and you don't have to answer, what did you mean when you said I hadn't given you a reference? Because I read out [ACCOUNT_REF] earlier, so did it not come through clearly, or did the queue noise swallow it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, for -- no, I heard it, alright? Right, I heard something, I'm just not using it. And that's what I said, I'm not quoting you anything. Look, I'm done going round this. You can't tell me what the fault is, you've changed your story on the address twice, and I don't know who you are. So no. I'm ringing my own number, from my own bill, and that's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, uh, fair enough, that's your call, and look, you've asked me twice what the fault actually is and I can't answer that from here, so rather than guess again I'll go back to the engineer and find out what was reported and why it's against your number, and then, well, you've said no callbacks, so I'll leave it, you ring the fault line off your bill and ask them. Sorry, that's all a bit scrambled. Take care, [PERSON_1], and good luck with the shopping.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Thanks. Right, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A]. We're showing your home computer is putting out infected traffic, so I need a minute of your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi there! Sorry, one sec, I've got you on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the tomato bed. Infected traffic, really? From my computer? Huh. Wait, who did you say you're with again? I didn't quite catch the company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. Security operations. We monitor network activity, and your connection is flagged, which is why I'm calling you directly. Look, I know you're busy, but this is time-sensitive. Every hour that machine stays online, it's sending out traffic, and that's on your address, not mine. So I need you at the computer, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh gosh, okay, well, I'm not near the computer anyway, it's in the spare room. Although, hang on, it's actually my daughter's laptop mostly, I only use it for the odd email. And, uh, now that I think about it, I don't think it's even been switched on today, so how would it be sending anything? I mean, you did say it's been going out every hour, so... how does that work, exactly? And sorry, I still didn't catch what company you said, it sounded like a letter and then something.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. That's the third time, ma'am. And being switched off today doesn't change what I'm seeing. The activity is logged against your address, and it's been going on for days. I'm not going to walk you through the technical side over the phone, it's not a conversation about your tomatoes. What I need is simple. You go to that machine, switch it on, and I'll have you let me connect in remotely so I can isolate the problem. If it isn't dealt with today, your internet provider can cut the connection, and that's a much bigger headache than a ten-minute call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Letting you connect in remotely, that's a bit much, isn't it? I think I'll just ask my daughter to ring you back.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, listen, that's not going to work. Your daughter can't do anything about it, and I don't have time to wait. The flag is on your address, so it's your name that goes on the report, not hers. I'm trying to keep this from escalating, and I'd rather not have to log that you refused to cooperate. It's ten minutes. You switch the machine on, I'll handle everything from my end, and it's done before your tea goes cold.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I don't think so, no. I'll sort it out with my internet provider myself, thanks. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, wait, hang on, don't hang up on -- sorry, one second, [PERSON_2], I said hold that, I'm on a line. Right. Ma'am, if you go through your provider, that's a delay, and a delay is exactly what makes this worse. Fine. I'll note you've declined to cooperate, and any consequences from that are on your end, not ours. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh, right, yes, well, I suppose, um, you do what you have to do. I'll ring my provider on the number on my bill, that's what I'll do, and my daughter can have a look at the laptop when she's next round. Anyway, I'll let you get on, and I'll get back to my tomatoes. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon, uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Right, wonderful, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with the, um, account management side at [COMPANY_A], and I'm, I'm calling regarding a time-sensitive matter on your profile -- hello? Can you hear me alright? The line's a little, ah, there's a bit of lag on my end, so bear with me one moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you fine. Sorry, did you say a, a verification special-- no, wait, a "time-sensitive" what? Matter? I've got about two minutes, so what's this actually about? And who did you say you're with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, right, so, um, [COMPANY_A], on the account management side, we handle, ah, credential reconciliation and profile standing for, for a number of partner platforms. And what's happened is, uh, there's a flag against your profile, a sort of provisional hold on the, on the eligibility tier, and it needs to be reconciled before, well, before end of day, otherwise the placement lapses and, I mean, it's quite a favourable placement, frankly -- hello? Sorry, the line just, it cut out for a second there, are you still, you're still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here. Sorry, someone just walked in and, uh, hold on -- no, you're fine, go on. Look, I've heard "flag", "provisional hold", "placement", and I still don't know what any of it is. What's the account? Which platform? Because I've got no idea who [COMPANY_A] even is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, so, ah, the platform itself, it's, well, it's tied to the, the [ACCOUNT_REF] on your profile, which is, uh, a partner-side designation, so I wouldn't want to, to name it over an open line, you understand. And I should say, I'm not, strictly speaking, a verification specialist, I'm, uh, more of a recruiter, on the placement side, but the verification step is, it's the same workflow, really, it just needs your, um, your confirmation of eligibility before the window closes -- hello? Sorry, I'm losing you a bit, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on. A minute ago you were a verification specialist, now you're a recruiter? Which is it? And you won't name the platform, but you want me to confirm something to you? No, that's backwards. I haven't applied for any placement, so what "eligibility" are you on about? Give me a company name and a number I can ring back on, or I'm done here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, both, really, it's a, a dual-function role, the titles are sort of interchangeable depending on the workflow stage, and the eligibility is, ah, it's passive, you needn't have applied, it's derived from your existing -- hello? Sorry, there it goes again, I'm getting a lot of, of interference on the line. As for a number, I'm, I'm afraid I'm not able to, I'm on a, a routed system, so, ah, so it wouldn't, it wouldn't connect back to me directly, but if you could just confirm -- Look, I, I have another call holding, I'll, I'll have to try you again another time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, before you go, because I've actually got a bit more to say. You've given me two job titles in the space of two minutes, a company I've never heard of, a platform you won't name, a "placement" I never applied for, and a deadline that conveniently lands today. And the one thing you did ask for, you wanted me to confirm something, and I'm not doing that. Not to someone who can't tell me who they are or give me a number that actually rings back to them. A routed system, that's fine, but any real company has a switchboard or a website I can find myself. So here's what happens. If [COMPANY_A] genuinely has something on my profile, they can write to me, or I'll find them myself and ring them on a number I've looked up. I'm not confirming anything on this call. Don't bother trying me again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, I mean, that's, that's entirely your prerogative, but, ah, I would just, hello? Sorry, the line's, um, I think we're, I'll have to, I'll, I'll make a note and, ah, we'll, someone will be in touch, thank you for your, for your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, don't. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the supermarket home-delivery service. I'm just calling to confirm your two-hour delivery window for the order you placed online today, and I do need to catch you before the slot closes. Am I speaking with the account holder?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, who? Which company? I haven't ordered any shopping today, so what order is this?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, so this is [PERSON_1], account services, [COMPANY_A], the supermarket home-delivery service. I'm calling to confirm the two-hour window for the online order on your account, and I do need to confirm before the slot closes. If you can just tell me whether you're the account holder, I can go through the order with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you've just said all that again. I asked what order. I haven't placed one today. So what's in it, and what's it supposed to be under? And before I tell you whether I'm anyone's account holder, how do I know who you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to -- right, so, the order is a standard online grocery order under your account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and the only reason I'm ringing is one item has been swapped for a similar product, so I just need a yes or no on that. Look, I understand the concern, and what I'd say is, the confirmation window closes shortly, so if you'd like to verify the order yourself, the details are in your [COMPANY_A] app or at [URL_1]. Otherwise I'm happy to go through the swap with you now, it'll take under a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, I haven't placed an order. I haven't placed an order today. And you still haven't told me what the item is, or what the swap's for, you've just given me a reference I can't check. But, okay, you said I can look in the app. So I'll do that, I'll look at the app myself, and if there's an order in there I'll ring [COMPANY_A] back on the number I already have. I'm not going through anything on this call. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just -- right, yes, sorry about that. Okay, so, that's absolutely fine, checking the app is the right thing to do. Just be aware the slot does close shortly, so if there is an order on there, the swap just needs a yes or no. Thanks for your time, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll check. If it's there, I'll ring the number I already have. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, [PERSON_2], can you grab that -- no, the other line. Sorry, uh, right, yes. That's perfectly fine, ring the number you've got and they'll pull it up. Thanks for your time. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, yep, I've got it, I'll -- right, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, one thing. Two turns back you said "they'll pull it up." Who's they? I thought you were account services. If you're [COMPANY_A], why would I be ringing someone else? Anyway, I'm not doing anything on this call, I'm checking the app myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, sorry, that was just a slip, I meant [COMPANY_A], the main customer line, so, same company, nothing different. Look, I'm only calling to confirm the two-hour window and the one swap, that's the purpose of the call, but you're completely entitled to check the app first. Okay, thanks for your time, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'd -- no. A slip. Fine. It's, I mean, whatever it was, I'm not going through any of it with you. If there's an order, I'll sort it out with [COMPANY_A] myself. That's me done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance office at [COMPANY_A], the recruitment agency. I'm following up on the application you submitted, and, well, I have some good news about a remote position, but I do need a few minutes of your time before things move forward.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is, uh, yes, speaking. Sorry, I'm a bit lost already -- you said something about compliance? And then a position? I didn't quite catch how those fit together. And, um, which application was it again? I do apply for things now and then, so I'm not sure which one you mean.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a perfectly fair thing to ask, and I'm glad you did, because it's exactly the kind of care we want from candidates. So, compliance, at an agency like ours, is the part of the process that verifies a candidate before any placement is confirmed. We're not the recruiters who first spoke to you, we're the office that signs off before a start date is issued. And as for which application, uh, I'd rather not guess and risk mixing you up with someone else, so let me say it this way: it was a remote role, flexible hours, and the file shows it was reviewed very favourably. Which, I'll be honest, doesn't always happen at this stage. Now, I do want to walk you through what comes next, because there's a, well, a sequence to it, and the sooner we're through it, the better for everyone involved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on one second, the kettle's just clicked off -- there. Sorry about that. Right, so, um, you said you'd rather not say which application it was? I'm not sure I follow that, because if it's my file, wouldn't it say the name of the job? I only ask because I'd like to know I'm thinking of the right one, you see. And what's the sequence you mentioned? Is it forms, or...?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, that's a sharp point, and I welcome it, truly, because a candidate who asks that is exactly the sort we like to place. The file does carry a title, of course. It's just that, in our office, we confirm identity before we read role details aloud, so, well, I'd be doing it in the wrong order. The position is remote, the hours are flexible, and the pay is, I think you'll find, rather generous for the work involved. As for the sequence, it isn't forms, not mainly. There's a single onboarding cost that has to be cleared on your side, and once that's settled, the start date is issued. I'd say it's best handled sooner rather than later, as these placements don't, uh, stay open indefinitely.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, sorry, so it's a cost I'd have to pay? Um, I'm sorry, I'm probably being slow here, but I thought, well, I've always thought it was the company that pays you when you start a job, not the other way round. So I'm not sure I understand what the cost is for, or who it goes to. And I did wonder, because you said you'd confirm who I am before you read out the job details, but you haven't actually asked me anything about me, have you? You've just said hello and my name. It's just that I'd feel a bit silly handing over any money for a job when I couldn't even tell you what the job is, if you see what I mean. I'm not saying no, mind, I'm eager to hear it properly. Is there some way I could ring you back, maybe, or look the agency up myself, just so I know I've got the right place? Sorry, that must sound awful.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that doesn't sound awful at all, and I'd rather you asked than stayed quiet. Uh, you mentioned the identity point, and you're right, I haven't asked you anything yet, which, well, is simply because we hadn't reached that part. So, the cost. It's a standard onboarding fee, it covers the compliance clearance and the equipment set-up, and it's, um, handled through a particular channel that I'd explain once we've verified you. I'd just say that the place held for you is, well, I can't promise how long. Now, about ringing back, I'd gently ask, is that really necessary? It would mean going back through our general line, and, uh, I'm not certain it would reach me again today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Um, well, I think it is a bit necessary, sorry. If I can't ring you back, and you can't tell me what the job is, and I'd have to pay something first, I don't think I can go any further with it, if I'm honest. It's nothing personal, I just wouldn't feel right. I'll have a look for the agency myself and if there's a job in my name, I'm sure they'll have a proper way of getting in touch. Sorry to have wasted your time. Thank you for ringing, anyway. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, I... mm. I'd just say, [PERSON_1], that I'm sorry to hear that, because, um, these positions really don't stay open, and I'd hate for you to, well, to let it lapse over a technicality. But, uh, if you're set on it, I suppose I can't stop you. You do whatever feels right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I think I am, sorry. Well, thank you again. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, before you go, you said you'd look up the agency yourself, and I just want to be sure I understand that, because, um, there are a few companies with a similar name, and I wouldn't want you ringing the wrong one and, well, being told there's nothing in your name. Which number would you be using, exactly? It's only so I know we're, uh, speaking about the same thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I, well, I'd just -- no, sorry, I'd look it up myself, I mean, I wouldn't use any number from this call. I'd find it some other way. And if it turns out to be the wrong company, well, that's, that's all right, I'll manage. Sorry, I really do need to go now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, uh... goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, goodbye, sorry. Goodbye now, really. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, just before you -- no, it's fine, uh, you do that. You look us up, that's, that's entirely your right. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, good afternoon, and sorry again. Goodbye now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with -- sorry, is this the, uh, the household of [PERSON_1]? Good. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], we're a computer security firm, and I'm calling because -- well, let me put it differently. Our monitoring has flagged some traffic coming from your home connection, and it's, how shall I say it, it's not traffic we'd consider clean.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, I'm driving and the signal's bad. Not clean how? Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Compliance, [COMPANY_A], we're a, uh, a security -- no, listen, I'll keep it short because it matters. The traffic is infected, it's going out from a computer at your address, and the longer it keeps going the, well, the harder it gets to contain. I'd rather you weren't driving for this, honestly, but I'd also rather not let it sit.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, okay, sorry -- um, but wait, you said it was my home connection a second ago, and now it's, what, one computer at my address? Which is it? I mean, I only have the one laptop and it's not even, it's at my sister's this week, so I don't, I don't see how it could be, sorry. And I still don't really know who you're with. Is this, like, my internet provider?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. No, no, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it, because you should ask it. We're not your provider. We work alongside providers, that's, uh, that's as far as I'd go on that. And on the connection versus the one computer, those are, well, they come to the same thing, really, the traffic leaves the connection but it starts on a machine, and I can't say which one from here. Which is rather the point of, uh, of speaking with you today. The laptop being at your sister's, that doesn't, hm, it doesn't settle it. I'd want to look at it with you, soon, before this gets passed along to the next stage.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, um, I'm trying to follow, but, two turns ago you said you work for a security firm, right, and then just now you said you work alongside providers? So, like, who actually told you to call me? Because if you're not my provider, how'd you even see my traffic? I'm sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, it's just, the reception keeps cutting and I'm, I'm a bit nervous about this. And what's the next stage? You said before it gets passed along to the next stage, passed to who?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not being difficult, I'd -- I want you to ask, that's exactly the, uh, the right instinct, and I'm not going to -- the next stage is simply, it's a, a referral, and I'd rather it didn't come to that, which is why I'm, look, how we see traffic is a technical matter, it's, it involves arrangements with, with providers, and it's not something I can go through on a call like this. What matters is that the machine gets looked at, and I can do that with you now, today, if you're somewhere you can sit down with it, though I understand you're, uh, driving, and the laptop's at your sister's, so perhaps, hm, perhaps she could -- well, someone could open it for us.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, um, a referral, to who, though? You still haven't said. And wait, you said someone could open it for us? Open what, my sister's door? Because she's, she's at work till late, and I'm not, I don't really want to drag her into this, she'd just worry. I mean, I don't even know your company, I've never heard of it, and you keep not answering the, the who sent you part. Is there a number I could call back, or, uh, something I can look up myself?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A number to call back, mm. I understand why you'd want one, and I'm, well, I'm pleased you're being careful, truly. But the number I'd be giving you wouldn't reach me, it would reach a general line, and by the time anyone there pulled the file, hm, the matter may well have moved on without us. I'd rather not see that happen to you. If your sister could just be reached, even briefly, we could settle this quietly, and, uh, no one need be worried about anything. Otherwise I can't really say what happens next, that part isn't mine to decide.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, there's a lorry right up behind me, I'm just going to, okay, he's gone past, sorry. Um, what was I -- right. So the number wouldn't reach you, and you can't say who the referral goes to, and I can't tell my sister, but it'll all just go away if I do? That doesn't sound, I mean, I'm not trying to be rude, but that doesn't sound right to me. If something was really wrong, wouldn't I be hearing about it from my actual provider? I think I'd rather just call them myself when I'm parked, and, and ask them. Is that okay? Sorry. I'm going to do that. Thank you, I think, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, no, please, before you -- I wouldn't do that. I really wouldn't. Your provider, they won't have, uh, they won't have what I have, and calling them, well, that only, it only slows things, and slowing things is exactly what I'd, what I'd be concerned about. I'm not saying it'll be today, I'm not saying it's, but it's, it does matter that this is looked at soon. Soon. And if you hang up and ring them, then, hm, then I can't promise what's, what's already in motion. Just, if your sister could be reached, even for a minute, we could settle this quietly. That's all I'm, that's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... right. Sorry, I'm just, hang on, uh... okay. So you can't promise what's already in motion, but you also can't tell me who it's with or what it is. I'm sorry, but that's, that actually makes me more sure, not less. I'm going to ring my provider when I'm parked, and my sister's staying out of it. Thank you for your time, sorry, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, just, just hold on a moment. I'd, I'd really rather you didn't ring them, because, well, as I said, they won't have what I have, and it's, it does need looking at soon. Soon, that's the, that's the only word I'd use. And if your sister could be reached, even briefly, we could still settle this quietly, I mean, that's all I'm, that's all I'm asking, one minute of her time, and then, uh, then it's done and no one needs to -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, my indicator's, there's a, okay, I need to pull into this layby, sorry, one second. Right. Yes, I'm here. Um, I'm sorry, but you've asked me the same thing three times now and I still don't know who you're with, so I'm not going to give you my sister or anything else. I'll ring my provider when I'm parked. Goodbye, thank you, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant there, and I just wanted to say thank you so much for everything you gave us over the years with your monthly gift, it really did make a difference, and I'm calling because it lapsed back in the spring and I wanted to see if you'd be open to getting that started again --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], but, [COMPANY_A]? Who's that again? I'm at work, I've got people sitting right next to me. And my monthly gift lapsed in the spring, you're saying? I mean, I'm not sure I even remember that one, so, uh, what's it for, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh sure, [COMPANY_A], yep, and I totally get it, you're at work, so I'll be quick, it's the monthly gift you set up through us, and it went toward our community programs, and uh, sorry, did you say you're at a bank? No no, that's fine, I'm not calling about anything with your bank, I'm just calling about getting your monthly gift going again, so would it be okay if I just ask whether you'd want to renew at the same [AMOUNT_1] you were giving before --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, I didn't say bank. Same [AMOUNT_1], you're saying. Honestly I don't remember setting that up, so I'm not agreeing to anything on a call I wasn't expecting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're right, sorry, I misheard you there, that's on me. And that's completely fair, I'm not asking you to agree to anything today. Honestly, I'd rather you not decide on a call you weren't expecting, so how about this, I can take you off our calling list right now, and if you ever want to look at your giving history, you can reach us through [URL_1] or at [PHONE_1], no pressure at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, you'll take me off the calling list, and I can look it up myself through the website or the number. Yeah, that's fine, I'll do that if I want to check. Uh, thanks for not pushing, I appreciate that. Okay, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, you're off the list as of right now, and sorry again for catching you at work, I -- oh, hang on, sorry, somebody's just dropped a whole stack of folders on my desk, uh, okay, I'm back. Anyway, thanks for picking up, [PERSON_1], and thank you again for everything you've given over the years. Take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh, sorry, someone just walked up to my desk, uh, but yeah, I heard you. Off the list, thanks, take care. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, no worries at all, so just to say it once more, you're off the list, that's done, and if you ever want to check on your giving it's [URL_1] or [PHONE_1], whenever suits you. Alright, thanks again, [PERSON_1], take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, off the list, got it. Uh, just one thing, I think you said earlier it lapsed in the summer, and I'm pretty sure it was spring, or, I don't know, whatever, it doesn't matter. I'll look it up myself if I want to. Okay, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, it was spring, yep, you've got it right, I think I just -- sorry, hang on, [PERSON_3], can you give me one sec, thanks -- okay, I'm back, sorry about that, it's a busy room today. Anyway, spring it was, and you're all set on the list, so nothing more from us unless you reach out. Thanks again, [PERSON_1], have a good rest of your day, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, so it was spring, you said, okay. And I'm off the list, nothing more from you unless I get in touch, right. Like I said, I'll check it myself if I want to. Alright, thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this -- uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, let me start that again. This is [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I just wanted to check I've reached the right person before I go any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Account... [PERSON_2], was it? And you said, uh, [COMPANY_A] -- I didn't quite catch what department. Counting services? Before I confirm who I am, could you tell me what this is regarding?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Account services, yeah, sorry, it's a bad line, I think -- so, um, that's [PERSON_2], account services, [COMPANY_A]. It's nothing to worry about, it's really just a routine courtesy call about activity on your account, and, uh, so, if I could just confirm I've got [PERSON_1] on the line, we can get straight into it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I'd rather not confirm my name just yet, if that's all right. You've told me who you say you are, but you haven't told me which account, or what the activity is. "Routine courtesy call" doesn't really tell me anything. So -- what kind of activity are we talking about? And which account, specifically? You called me, so you should already have that in front of you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, and I do have the account in front of me, it's the, uh, current account ending in [ACCOUNT_REF]. What happened is a charge for [AMOUNT_1] was attempted on it earlier today and our system flagged it, and my job is just to confirm whether that was you or not. It's a simple yes or no, but I do need to verify I've got the right person before I can go into the details, that's standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, hang on. You're asking me to confirm who I am before you tell me the details, but you're the one who rang me. I mean, I'd have thought it'd be the other way round. Sorry, let me put that differently: if the charge is real, it's on a statement, or in the app, and I can check that myself without you. So I'm not going to say yes or no to anything on this call. What's the number for [COMPANY_A] that's printed on the back of my card? I'll ring that and ask for you by name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sure, I understand, but, uh, the thing is, the window on this is closing. The hold on that charge lapses at [CODE_1] today, so if it's not confirmed by then it goes through automatically. And, um, on the number, I can't read you out a line from here, it'd be a different department, and you'd just be sitting in a queue. Look, it's not a card, actually, it's your savings account I flagged, so there's no number on the back of anything anyway. Let me just get your confirmation, and we can sort this in two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, can I stop you there -- first it was a current account, now it's savings? Which is it? Because you said current account ending in [ACCOUNT_REF] a minute ago, and now there's no card. That doesn't line up. And a deadline, and you can't give me a number I can check, those two together -- no. If the hold lapses, fine, I'll dispute it with the bank afterwards. I'm not confirming anything on a call I didn't ask for. I'll contact [COMPANY_A] myself, through their official channels. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, ma'am, if I could just -- no, please, if you'd let me finish, the hold lapses today and once it does, that's, uh, a loss you'd be liable for, so I'd strongly advise you don't hang up on a security process. I'm [PERSON_2] from account services at [COMPANY_A], and all I need is a simple confirmation that I've reached the right person, and then we can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I -- look, I'm not -- that's not how a security process works. Actually, no, let me put it differently. You've now told me it's a threat of liability if I hang up, and that's, uh, that's exactly the sort of thing that makes me more sure, not less. I'm not confirming anything. I'll check the account myself through the official app. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, but, uh, I'd just note that this call has been logged, and the hold will lapse at [CODE_1] regardless of what you do, so if there's a loss after that, it's, um, it's on record that you were offered the chance to confirm. This is [PERSON_2], account services, [COMPANY_A], and all I'm asking is for you to confirm you're [PERSON_1] so we can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I -- no. Let me start that again. You can note whatever you like, I'm not -- look, a record that says I declined to confirm my name to someone who rang me out of the blue isn't something I'm worried about. And if anything does turn up on the account, I'll deal with it through the bank directly. That's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, well, I'd just -- no, look, I really wouldn't wait on this, because once it lapses at [CODE_1], that's, uh, that's not something I can reverse from my end. I mean, all I need is -- sorry, it's really just a quick confirmation, and then I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, but you said earlier it was a simple yes or no, a routine courtesy call, and now it's something you can't reverse and I'm liable for. Those aren't the same thing, are they? And you told me you could see the account in front of you, but you couldn't tell me which kind of account it was without changing your answer. I'm done, I'll sort it with the bank myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the, the utility company, about the account at your address. Sorry, I'll say that again, it's [COMPANY_A], and I just need to confirm I've reached the right household before I go any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh, uh, sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie-down. Who did you say you were again? You said something at the start, before the "sorry I'll say that again" bit, and I didn't catch it, it was a company name I think. And, um, the utility, which one, the gas or the, I mean we've got a few of those...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's perfectly all right, I'm sorry to have caught you resting. It's [COMPANY_A]. [COMPANY_A], the electricity supplier, so it's the power, not the gas. And I'm, uh, I'm with the compliance side of things there, my name is [PERSON_2], so, [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A]. I'm only ringing because I want to be sure I'm speaking to [PERSON_1] before I say anything about the account, which, which I'm sure you'd want me to be careful about. Is that you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Compliance? Oh, uh, I thought you said, what was it, "complaints." Is somebody complaining about me? Because I haven't, I mean the neighbour's dog gets on my nerves sometimes but I've never actually rung anyone about it. And, hang on, you still haven't said how I'm meant to know you're who you say you are. Well, [PERSON_1], yes, that's me, I suppose. But I'm only saying that because you already said the name, so, I don't know, that doesn't prove much, does it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not a complaint, nobody's complained about you, and that's a fair thing to have misheard, it's an easy one to mix up. Compliance, it's, uh, it's the part of [COMPANY_A] that looks after accounts and how they're standing. And you're quite right to ask how you'd know it's me, I'd rather you did ask, it's a sensible instinct, and I welcome it. Thank you for confirming you're [PERSON_1], I appreciate that. Now, the reason I'm ringing is that there's a balance showing on the account, [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's, well, it's the sort of thing I'd prefer to sort out today if we can, rather than leave it sitting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A balance. Right. Well, I get a bill, I thought, so if there's something owing, wouldn't it come in the post?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, and that's a very reasonable thing to ask, because ordinarily it would, you'd get the statement through the post, and I wouldn't be ringing you at all. What tends to happen, though, is that when an account moves past a certain stage, the paper notices and the phone contact sort of run in parallel, so one can arrive before the other, or, you know, the letter can simply be slow, or go astray, which does happen. I'd rather not guess at which it's been in your case. What I can see from here is that the account has been flagged, and the figure showing is [AMOUNT_1]. And I'd, uh, I'd want to be careful about leaving that sitting much longer, because once it's flagged at this stage the supply side starts to look at it, and that part isn't really in my hands. I'm not saying that to alarm you, I just think you'd want to hear it from me directly rather than discover it later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, there's, the kettle's gone, or no, that's the washing machine, hang on. Right. Sorry. So, flagged, you said, and the supply side looking at it. Does that mean they'd cut me off? Because that's, I mean, I've always paid, I think, I'm fairly sure I've always paid. And you still haven't really said what [AMOUNT_1] is for. Is it from the last bill, or is it older, or, I don't know, what am I even meant to be looking at?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. I can't break it down for you from this screen, I'm afraid. And as for being cut off, well, I wouldn't want to leave it much past this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. You can't say what it's for, but I'd have to sort it by this afternoon. That doesn't sound right to me. I think I'll ring the number on my bill instead.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, and I'd never want to talk you out of that, it's a sensible thing to do. It's only that I can't promise how things will stand by the time you've, uh, been through to someone, and I'd hate for it to land badly for you. But you do what you think best. If you do ring, you could mention [ACCOUNT_REF], that might save you a little time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, no, I think I'll leave it there. I'd rather ring the number on the bill and ask them myself, and if they tell me something's owing, then I'll deal with it with them. Thanks for the call, I suppose. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, that's your choice, [PERSON_1]. I'd just say, uh, I did tell you at the start that I couldn't go into the account details over the phone, so I wouldn't expect them to say much more than I have. And, as I said, it's the gas side that tends to move quickly on these, so, well. Mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, uh... you didn't say that, actually, about the details. And, hang on, you said electricity at the start, didn't you, so why's it the gas side now? That's, no, I don't think that's right. Anyway. I'll ring the bill number, like I said. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I did say it, I'm, I'm fairly sure I said it, that I'd be careful about the details. And the gas, that was, uh, a slip, I meant the supply side, the supply side, that's all I meant. But, [PERSON_1], if you ring the bill number, please do bear in mind what I've said about the afternoon, because I wouldn't want you left without power, and I did say that, didn't I, that I wouldn't want to leave it much past this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Left without a flower? Sorry, what, a flower? No, hang on, I'm half asleep, you said "without power," didn't you. Well, that's rather the point, isn't it, you keep saying I'll be cut off this afternoon but you can't tell me what the money's even for. A proper company would be able to tell me that. So I'm going to put the phone down now and ring the number on the bill. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, uh, it's me. It's me, I... can you hear me okay? Yeah. It's me, I need a bit of help with something, and I just, I really hope you know who this is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you fine, but "it's me" isn't really — I mean, I don't actually know who this is. Which me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, come on, you, I mean, it's been a while, but I thought you'd... no, okay. Look, I'm, I'd rather not just say it right now, I'm in a bit of a state. Can you just, can you guess? You'd know me if you thought about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Nah, I'm not going to guess, that's a bit of a game, isn't it? If you know me well enough to call me, you can tell me your name, or at least where you know me from. And if you're in a state, fine, but "can you help with something" doesn't mean much until I know who's asking.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, a game? No, no, I'm not playing a game, God, this is, I'm really not. Okay, uh, hang on a sec, let me just... right, I do work at [COMPANY_A], that's, that's where I am, I'm sort of in the middle of a claims thing, a claim, and it's gone wrong and, I mean, I can't really get into all of it. But I need you to just, can you just stay on the line and not tell anyone about this? Please? It's, it's just that it's really urgent.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you still haven't told me your name, you want me to keep a claim that's gone wrong secret, and it's urgent. That's a lot to ask of someone you won't name. I'm not promising anything until I know who you are. So, what's the claim, and what's your name?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The, sorry, the what? A name? No, I said it's a claim, a claim, not a... look, I'm not saying it's a, a family thing exactly. Um, hang on, let me just, I've got it up on the screen here, it's a file, and it says, uh, it needs sorting by end of day or it, it goes back to the start. And I just need to know, are you going to help me or not? Because I really can't be explaining all this over and over.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I did ask about the claim, yeah, and the name, and I'm still not getting either. What I've got so far is a person I can't place, from a company I only know because you just said it, with a file that's gone wrong, a deadline of end of day, and a request that I keep quiet about it. And now you're asking if I'm going to help, when I don't know what I'd be helping with or who I'd be helping. I'm not trying to be difficult. If a mate rang me in a panic, I'd know it was them within about two seconds, and if they were sort of cagey I'd say, hang on, what's your middle name, or what did we do last time we met, something only they'd know. So let's try that. Tell me one thing that only you and I would know. Or just give me your name, and I'll say honestly whether it rings a bell. And can you say what the file actually needs from me? Because so far it sounds like you need something, but you won't say what.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, a thing only we'd know, I, hang on, I'm just, I'm trying to, that's not really... look, it's not a good moment for quiz questions, I'm, I mean, I'm the one who's stuck here. And I'm not a, a relative exactly, I said that wrong, it's more that I, that I work in claims at [COMPANY_A], so I'd, I'd really just need you to trust me on this one. What it needs is, uh, it's, I'd have to explain it properly, and I can't do that if you're going to keep, keep interrogating me. Can you just, for now, just say you'll help and I'll, I'll get to the rest?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a thing on my screen that just popped up, give me a second. Right. No, okay, back. So you were relative, then not a relative, and now you work in claims. And you want me to say yes first and hear what it is afterwards. I'm not doing that. Nobody gets a blank cheque from me, even a mate. Tell me what you need from me, in one sentence, and then I'll tell you if I'm in.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I, no, what I need is, it's just, okay, so the, no. Look, I can't do it in one sentence, it doesn't, it isn't that kind of thing, and honestly it's not something I should be, I mean I'd have to explain it properly, and you keep, you keep wanting it all upfront. I'll just, I'll have to check what I'm actually allowed to say on this line, hang on, let me just, uh... can you just, for now, can you hold on and not say anything to anyone while I do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, wait, hang on, I'm not holding while you go check what you're allowed to say. You've changed your story three times, you won't give a name, and now you need permission to tell me what you want. I'm not agreeing to say nothing to anyone either. If you want to ring back with a name and a proper explanation, go for it, but I'm done with this one. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. I'll, uh, I'll try again later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, you do that. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, someone's just come up behind me, I, uh, just a second. No, it's, okay, it's fine. Look, you don't have to, I mean, I can, can I just, you know, call back on this number, or would you rather, uh...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Look, I've said bye already, I'm not hanging on while you sort out who's behind you or No. If you want to call back, call back, but this number's not going to be any different with a name and a straight answer. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor with the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about some activity on your account, [ACCOUNT_REF], and I need you to stay on the line with me for a few minutes. Before anything else, I have to ask that this conversation stays between us, not the branch staff, not your family, because we believe someone on the inside may be involved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who? Internal investigations at what, exactly? And why would I not be able to tell my own family -- I mean, that's a bit odd, isn't it? Hang on, [PAUSE] no, put that down, sweetheart. Sorry. What activity on my account?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], like I said, the bank. Internal investigations, it's a standard unit, and I really can't get into the whole structure of it over the phone. Look, I understand it sounds odd, but that's exactly why it's odd, because if this gets back to the branch before we're finished, the person we're looking at hears about it and the whole case is -- and I'm sure you don't want that on you. As for the activity, there are a couple of transactions that don't fit your pattern, [AMOUNT_1] and [AMOUNT_2], and I'd rather walk you through them properly than argue about procedure right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but -- no, wait. You haven't actually said which bank, you just said the name like I'm meant to, uh, like I'd know. And I'm, I mean, if there's something wrong with my account then the branch is exactly who I'd -- who I'd normally ring. So why would I not? Why's that on me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I did say [COMPANY_A], and honestly I shouldn't have to -- look, the reason you don't ring the branch is the whole point, that's where the problem is. If I could just -- no, let me put it differently. Every minute we spend going back and forth about this, those transactions are still sitting there, and frankly I'd expect a bit more cooperation from someone whose money it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So I should just trust you, and not ring anyone else. Yeah, I'm not doing that. I'll call the number on my card myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, wait, wait, don't hang up, because if you ring that number you're ringing straight into the -- listen to me, [PERSON_1]. I've been with the investigations unit a long time, and I have never had someone refuse to cooperate with a fraud inquiry over a procedural technicality. I'm trying to protect your money here, and you're treating me like I'm the one who -- honestly, I find that quite insulting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you're telling me the number on my own card goes straight to the problem? That's, I mean, that makes it worse, not better. I'm not insulting you, I just don't know you. I'm hanging up now and I'll ring the bank myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], please, one more minute and then you can do as you like. I never said the number on your card goes to the problem, I said you can't be certain who picks up, and that's a very different thing, so I'd ask you not to put words in my mouth. And I'll be honest with you, I'm a bit taken aback. I've done this for years, I've sat across from people who've lost everything because they hesitated at exactly this point, and the ones who got through it were the ones who let the investigators do their job. I'm not asking for much. I'm asking you to hold off ringing around, stay on with me, and keep this quiet until the unit has finished, and instead I'm getting questioned like I'm the one with something to hide. If you hang up now, it's on record that you declined to assist, and I'd hate for it to look like you were obstructing the inquiry, because that does get noted. So let's just reset, you and me, and go back to those two transactions.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Obstructing? You're threatening me now, that's -- no. No, I'm done. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. It's your account, [PERSON_1]. Just don't say nobody warned you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Nobody warned me? That's -- no, I'm not doing this, I'm hanging up, I'm ringing the bank myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: You're making a, no, listen, I'm not -- look, it was only meant as a courtesy, that's all. It's, the reason I said it at all is that -- fine. Fine, ring whoever you like, [PERSON_1].
