But when you do, I'd be, I'd think very carefully before you mention this call to anyone, because if the wrong person hears -- never mind. Just, ring them, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. I'll tell whoever I like. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm telling you this as, no, look, I'm, that's not what I, the thing is you really shouldn't -- [PERSON_1], hold on, just let me --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not holding on. Sorry, hang on -- [PAUSE] sweetheart, not on the sofa, please. Sorry. No. You've told me to keep it quiet, you've told me not to ring the bank, and you've mentioned a record. That's three things a real bank doesn't do. Don't call me again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, uh, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance team -- hello, can you hear me all right? I'm just returning a missed call about a fault you reported, sorry to catch you out of the blue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I can hear you. A fault I reported? Sorry, who's this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, of course. It's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler with the regional maintenance team at [COMPANY_A] -- I'm, uh, just calling because one of our engineers had a missed call from this number about a fault that was reported. Are you still there? Sorry, the line's a bit crackly my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a missed call from my number? Uh, I didn't, I haven't rung anyone about a fault. Which, what was it, a fall? Is somebody hurt? I'm, I'm at work, I've got people around, so I'm a bit, can you just say again who you're with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, no, sorry, I've worded that badly, nobody's hurt, not at all. Fault, f-a-u-l-t, so a problem with the supply or the equipment, nothing to do with anybody falling. I'm with [COMPANY_A], the regional utility maintenance team, and what I've got in front of me is a note that a fault was reported on this number, and the engineer rang back and missed you, so he's asked me to follow up. I'm, uh, I'm sorry, I know it sounds a bit out of the blue when you're at work, and honestly if it wasn't you who reported it, it may well be someone else at the address, or I've got the wrong number down, that does happen. Are you still there? Sorry, I just keep thinking I've lost you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so a fault with the supply or equipment, right, not someone hurt. Uh, still here. But I haven't reported anything, and I'm at work, not at home, so I wouldn't know what's going on at the address. Which address have you got down? And what's the company called again, I didn't quite catch it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, the company, yes, it's [COMPANY_A], the regional utility maintenance team, [COMPANY_A]. And the address, hang on, I've got it here somewhere -- it's on [PERSON_3]'s road, no, sorry, that's the engineer's next job, I've mixed up my notes. Uh, it's a [CITY_1] address, but I'd rather not read it out down the phone to someone I haven't properly confirmed, if that's all right. Oh, and you said you're at home, sorry, so you can see the fault from there, that's helpful -- no? You're at work, I beg your pardon, I misheard. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I said I'm at work. At work. I'm not at home. And, hang on, you've got an address you won't read out, but you're the one who rang me? So you've got a fault at an address and a number that might be the wrong number, and you can't tell me which address. That's, that's a bit back to front, isn't it? If you're really from [COMPANY_A], what's the reference for this fault, and is there a number I can ring you back on, through the company, not this one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, sorry, that is back to front, and I've made a muddle of it. Did you say you'd ring me back, though? Sorry, I thought I heard you say you'd rather stay at the address, and I don't, it's nothing like that, you don't need to be there at all. The reference is whatever you were given when you reported it, [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the one on my screen. But I can't promise it's yours, and I can't tell you when the engineer would come either, it depends on an earlier job overrunning. Honestly the safest thing is to ring the published fault line yourself, the one on the company website, not a number from me, and ask them to check the booking and give you a firm slot. I'd much rather you did that than took my word for it. Are you still there? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said stay at the address? No, I never said I'd stay anywhere, I said I'm at work. And you want me to ring you back, no, wait, you said ring the published line. Okay. So the reference on your screen is [ACCOUNT_REF], and that's from when I reported it, except I didn't report anything. Right. So I'll find the number on the company website myself and ask them. And if there's nothing on their system, that's that. I'm going to do that, yeah? Sorry, I've got people waiting on me here. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you do that, that's the right thing to do. And if there's nothing under your name, then I've simply got the wrong number, and I'm sorry for the bother at work. Right, I'll let you get on. Bye now, sorry again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. No worries. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, just, uh -- hello? Are you still there? No, I think you've gone. Right, well, take care then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say still there, or, uh, still care? Oh, no, I think it was there, wasn't it. Sorry, I keep mishearing, it's this line. Right, well, bye then, and do ring the published number, won't you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, there, I said there. And I'll look the number up, but not today, I don't think, I'll leave it till I'm home. Anyway, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, till you're home, yes, that's fine, no rush at all. Sorry, did you say bye now, or, uh, buy a phone? No, no, I'm being silly, that wouldn't make sense. Right, I'll leave you be, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye now, I said bye now. Right, I really do have to go, so, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] from the maintenance team at [COMPANY_A], I'm just returning a missed call from earlier about the fault you reported, uh, the one with the --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, hang on, I just -- I was having a lie down, sorry. A missed call? I didn't, I don't think I called anybody. Well, I might've, my phone does things sometimes. Who did you say you were again? Maintenance for what?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you're fine, [PERSON_1], honestly, it's -- I'm [PERSON_2], the regional utility maintenance team, [COMPANY_A]. Someone rang our line about a fault at your address earlier and it just says return the call, so that's all I'm doing, nothing to it, really quick.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Utility maintenance, right, okay. Well, the thing is, I don't remember reporting a fault, and I'd have thought I'd remember, because the last time the boiler went I was on the phone for about an hour and a half, and my sister said just ring the number on the bill, which I did, but then I lost the bill, so, anyway. I mean, it could've been my neighbour, she's always on at me about the pipes outside, or it might've been, uh, my grandson, he fiddles with my phone. Sorry, I'm still a bit foggy, I've only just come round. So what fault is it supposed to be? What does it actually say on your end?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's fine, [PERSON_1], take your time. So on my end it just says a reported fault at your address, and the engineer's going to be out to look at it, but, uh -- sorry, hang on, someone's just put a van sheet on my desk -- right, where was I. The thing is, I can't give you an exact time he'll be round, because it depends on how long his earlier job runs, so it'd be sometime today, maybe, I mean, I don't want to promise something I can't -- Look, if you're not sure it was you who reported it, that's completely fair, everybody asks that. Your reference from when it was logged would be [ACCOUNT_REF], if that rings a bell, and you can always ring the published fault line yourself and ask them to check the booking, they'll give you a proper firm slot, and then you'll know it's genuine, no hassle at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, I'd, no, what I mean is -- hang on. [ACCOUNT_REF], no, that doesn't, I wouldn't know that off the top of my head, I'm not sure it, it rings a bell, not really. But you're saying I can just ring the, the proper fault line myself? And they'd know about it? Well, that, I mean, that's sort of sensible, isn't it, because I was going to say, I can't have someone turning up today anyway, my daughter's, no, she's not due till later, and I don't like letting people in when I'm on my own. So, uh, who do I ring, then? Is it on the bill? Because I've lost the bill, I did say that, didn't I.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, you did, [PERSON_1], and that's no bother at all. The number's on the [COMPANY_A] website, and it'll be in the phone book too, or your sister can look it up for you, you don't need the bill. Just don't use any number I give you, ring the published one so you know it's the real thing. And honestly, if you don't want anyone coming while you're on your own, that's fine, they can book it for when your daughter's there, you just tell them that. I'm not going to push you on any of it, [PERSON_1], it's your call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I, no, that's, that's actually quite, hang on. What I mean is, I'll ring them, I think, the proper number, not one from you. Only I don't, I'm not sure I can do the website, my grandson does the, uh, no, I'll get my sister to look it up, she's good with that. And I'll tell them about the daughter thing, that it's got to be when she's here. So, right, thank you for, for not pushing, I suppose. I'll sort it that way, and if there is a fault they'll know about it. Okay. Bye then, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Lovely, [PERSON_1], that's exactly the right thing to do, and your sister's the one to ask. Sorry, there's a door banging out in the yard, hang on -- right, I'm back. Do you want me to try you again later, once you've had a chance to check? Say, after your daughter's arrived, so you're not on your own. Whatever suits you, [PERSON_1], I'm in till late.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, don't ring me, I'll ring them. If there's anything to it, they'll have it all written down on their end. And I'll say it's my sister who's helping me with it. Right, I'm going to go and put the kettle on, I'm still half asleep. Thank you, dear, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, yes, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, the line's a bit crackly on my end. I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the case handlers on the account management side, and it's, well, it's an important matter about your file, I wanted to reach you before end of day. Can you hear me alright? And sorry, I think I mentioned my colleague already left you a message this morning, or, no, I suppose that was yesterday, but anyway.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I can hear you fine. Um... who did you say you were with again? Because I didn't actually catch the company, and I don't remember any message from a colleague, either this morning or yesterday.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, sorry, yes, it's [COMPANY_A], we're an account management firm, we handle, uh, files like yours. And the message, well, it might not have gone through, these things don't always, hello? Are you still there? Sorry, it's just, the line keeps dropping on my end, I thought I lost you for a second. Anyway, it's really just for your own protection that I'm ringing today, [PERSON_1], there's some time pressure on it, so if I could just confirm a couple of things with you, that would be, uh, that would be ideal.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here. Account management firm, files like mine... which file, exactly? And what are you wanting to confirm?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, [PERSON_1], I'm, uh, I'm not sure that line is helping me, can you still hear me okay? It's the file attached to your name, there's been, well, a bit of movement on it, and it's honestly in your favour, there's a, an amount that may be owed to you, [AMOUNT_1], I think, but I'd need to confirm a few personal details first so I'm sure I'm speaking with the right person. It's just to protect you, really, I wouldn't want any of it going to the wrong place.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, hang on -- you called me, so you're the one who should be proving who you are, not me. You still haven't told me what the file actually is. Money owed, from what? Who owes it? And what's the company's name, spelled out, because I'm going to look it up while you answer.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, of course, that's, that's fair, I understand, sorry. It's [COMPANY_A], [COMPANY_A], we're an account management firm. Hello? Sorry, you cut out a little there, I think I lost the end of what you said. The spelling, I mean, it's all on the, the paperwork we'd send you, but I'd have to, uh, get that once we've confirmed your details. It's just for your protection, [PERSON_1], that's all this is, and the amount, [AMOUNT_1], it won't be held for long, so if we could just go through the details quickly, I'd really like to get this sorted for you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, but you just said you can't spell your own company's name until I've given you my details? That's backwards. I'm not -- No, I'm not confirming anything. You rang me, you've told me nothing about what this file is, and now there's a clock on it. That's three strikes. If there's real money owed, put it in writing and I'll deal with it that way. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, [PERSON_1], don't hang up, I'm so sorry, I'm not, I'm not trying to rush you at all. It's just that, well, I did say earlier it wasn't time sensitive, it's only the amount, [AMOUNT_1], that could be released back to the wrong place if we leave it, and that's the last thing I'd want for you. Hello? Are you still there? Sorry, this line, I can barely hear myself. If I could just take two minutes of your time, I'd, I really do just want to protect you here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Actually, you didn't say it wasn't time sensitive. Your exact words were there's some time pressure on it. And the line's been fine for me this whole call, it only drops when I ask you something you don't want to answer. I've asked you three times what this file is and you've given me nothing. So no, I'm not giving you two minutes. If there's money owed to me, send it in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, well, I mean, um, yes, I suppose I did say that, sorry, I didn't, I'm not trying to confuse anything. Hello? [PERSON_1]? I can't tell if you're still, uh, on the line, there's just, it's gone very quiet on my end. If you are there, it really would be best for you to stay with me just a moment, I'd hate for that amount to, to slip away, and honestly I couldn't say how to reach you again after today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, I'm just -- uh, well, I was listening to you dig yourself in deeper. Couldn't say how to reach you again after today? That's your pitch, is it? Fine, you don't need to reach me, I'm not interested, and I've said goodbye twice now, so this is the last one. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, [PERSON_1], I'm so sorry, I didn't mean it that way, I'm just, I'm worried you'll lose it, that's all. It's only a couple of details, and then it's, uh, it's all done and I won't trouble you again. Hello? Are you still there? Sorry, the line, it's, I can't, if you could just stay on with me for one moment, I'm only trying to protect you here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. You've had four chances to tell me what this file is and who you are, and I've got nothing. I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, wait, please, [PERSON_1], before you, I'm only, it's just that if you hang up now I can't, hello? Sorry, are you, I really don't want you to lose that [AMOUNT_1], it's all for your protection, if you'd just give me, just the two details, and then I promise, I won't, hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Stop, stop, I'm going to stop you there, I'm not giving you two details or one detail or -- no. Nothing to give. Written notice, or nothing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, [PERSON_1], I'm so sorry, wait, just before you go, when you said written notice, uh, what did you mean by that exactly? Because I think the line cut out on the, the second half, and I'd hate to misunderstand you. Hello? Is it that you'd want something sent to you, or, I mean, I'm only asking because it's just for your protection, and if there's a quicker way, I'd, I'd really like to sort it with you now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Written notice, like a letter, to the address they already have on file for me. If you're legit, you've got that address, so you don't need me to tell you anything. And no, there's no quicker way. I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's, um, it's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A]. And I'm, uh, I should say up front I'm not -- this isn't about anything bad, exactly, it's just about an appointment, and I need to, well, confirm a few things with you first before I can say more.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, I'm in a queue, can you -- who is this again? And confirm what things, exactly? You ring me up out of nowhere and want me to confirm things before you'll even tell me what it's about, that's backwards, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I -- I know, I know how it sounds, and I'm sorry. It's [PERSON_2], from the outpatient administration, uh, the hospital's records side, well, the appointments office, I mean. And it's just that I'm not allowed to say anything about the appointment until I know I've got the right person, because it's, you know, it's private, and if I got it wrong, I'd be telling a stranger something about someone's health, and I couldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what, a stranger's wealth? I haven't got any wealth, mate, what are you on about? No, hang on, you said health. Right. Well that's my point, isn't it, you've rung me, so you tell me which hospital and what appointment, and then I'll decide if you've got the right person. I'm not reading anything out to someone who just rang me cold.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, yes, health, sorry, I'm not -- I'm making a mess of this. It's [COMPANY_A], the hospital, that part I can tell you. But the appointment itself, I really can't, not before I've confirmed who you are, and I know that sounds backwards, I do. It's just the rule, and I didn't make it, and honestly it's a bit hurtful, like I've done something wrong, when I'm only trying to do the right thing by you. Look, you don't have to take my word for it. You could hang up and ring the hospital's main switchboard yourself, and ask for the outpatient administration office, and they'll tell you whether I'm who I say I am. Or I can just send you a letter instead, if that's easier. I don't want you giving me anything while you're not sure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I, no -- hang on. I'm not trying to make you feel bad, it's just, I got stung once, and I'm still, never mind. Look, the ringing the switchboard thing, that's, yeah, that's actually fair enough. That's what I'd do anyway. And a letter's fine, honestly, a letter's better. If it's a real appointment there'll be a letter, won't there? So send me that, and I'll ring the hospital myself off whatever number I find, not one you give me. Is that, does that work?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that works, that's fine. Honestly, I'd rather you did it that way. Is it, um, is there a better time for me to try you again, or should we just leave it with the letter?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Just leave it with the letter. Don't ring me again, to be honest, because I'd rather deal with it on paper and in my own time. I'm not being funny with you, it's just how I am now. And if it is a real appointment, then fine, the letter turns up, I look up the hospital's number myself, I ring them, and we're sorted. If it doesn't turn up, well, then that tells me something as well, doesn't it? Anyway, I'm at the front of the queue now, so I'll let you go. Right, cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, yeah, that's completely fair, and I won't ring again. I'll get the letter sorted, and you look the number up yourself, that's exactly the right way to do it. Sorry for, um, for catching you at a bad moment. Thanks for hearing me out, [PERSON_1]. Take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before you go. Two minutes ago you said I could ring the main switchboard and ask for the outpatient administration office. Which hospital was that again? You said the company name but I didn't catch it properly, with the beeping going on here. Actually no, don't tell me. I'll work it out from the letter, it'll have it on the top. Right. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, hello, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the [COMPANY_A] IT helpdesk, I'm just, uh, pulling your file up on my screen. Right, I've got it. I'm following up on the ticket you opened this morning, ticket [ACCOUNT_REF], and I need a few minutes of your time on it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I -- uh, I didn't actually open a ticket this morning. I mean, I might have, but, no, I don't think I did. Which [COMPANY_A] helpdesk is this, exactly, and what was the ticket supposedly about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so the ticket's logged under your login, opened at, uh, just after nine this morning, and it's about your laptop not syncing with the, the -- sorry, let me start again. It's a device sync fault, and it was escalated to us by [PERSON_2], who I've got down as the colleague who flagged it for you. If you don't recall opening it, that's fine, I can note that on the file. But the ticket's still open on our side, and an open sync fault flags the device for a compliance check, so that's just how it goes if it isn't closed out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well -- no, hang on. I don't have any sync fault. My laptop's, it's been fine all day, I'm actually, I'm using it right now. And I don't, I mean, I don't know a [PERSON_2] who'd have flagged anything for me. So, uh, let me ask you something precise. If you're internal, what's the ticket system you're logging this in, and what's the ticket number, the actual reference, spoken out? Because I'd rather check it myself than take it on a phone call.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's a fair thing to ask, and it's what I'd want you to do. So the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and the system is the internal helpdesk portal, it's at [URL_1], the same one you'd use to raise anything with us, so you can search the reference there under your own login and see the ticket, who raised it, the timestamp, all of it. Don't take my word for it, go and look. And on [PERSON_2], I'm just reading the escalation note, which says [PERSON_2] flagged it on your behalf after seeing the sync error on your device, so if the name doesn't ring a bell, the quickest thing is probably to message them directly through the company directory and ask. I'm not going to ask you for anything on this call until you've checked. If it's easier, I can reschedule this through the portal, so you'd get a booking confirmation inside your own account, and we do it when you've had a chance to verify. I'll note on the file that you've queried the ticket and want to confirm it first, that's all fine, and the ticket stays open in the meantime. That's just the status, it isn't a mark against you. I do still need to get it closed out at some point, because there's a compliance flag attached to it, and I'd rather that happened this week than have it drag on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, hold on, you said the portal's at a, what, a booking site? I don't, we don't book anything through a booking site, I just raise things in the normal helpdesk tool. Anyway, I'll go and check the reference myself, and I'll look up [PERSON_2] in the directory while I'm at it. But one thing I'd like to understand first. You said a compliance flag gets attached if the ticket isn't closed. Who sets that policy, and what specifically does it trigger? Because that sounds like the sort of thing I'd have heard about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, no, it's not a booking site, that was me being sloppy. It's the same helpdesk tool you raise things in, you just book a callback slot inside the ticket itself. On the flag, uh, it's the device compliance policy, set by security, not by us. Any ticket still open past, I think it's five working days, gets the device marked non-compliant, and a non-compliant device loses network access until it's cleared. That's just how the policy runs, it's automatic. And, I mean, I said the ticket opened this morning, but looking at the screen again, the sync fault itself was logged a couple of days back, and your login only got attached to it today. So it's not like you'd have seen anything on your end. Anyway, go and check the reference and the directory, that's the right move. I'll put a note on the file saying you've queried it and want to verify first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, that's, uh, that's the second version of the story, though. First it was a ticket I opened this morning, now it's a fault logged days ago and my login got attached to it today. Which is it? And the five working days, if it was logged a couple of days back, that clock's hardly about to run out this week. So I'm going to go and check the reference and the directory myself, and if there's a genuine ticket, I'll raise the callback through the portal. I won't be doing anything on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair enough. That's noted on the file, ticket stays open, and if you'd rather I rang back after you've checked it, just say when.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, there's no need to ring back. If the ticket's real, I'll find it in the portal and book the slot from there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, understood. Book it through the portal then, and I'll see the booking come in on my side. I'll leave the note on the file as it stands. Right, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, right, I'll -- no, that's fine, I've got it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, that's -- sorry, one last thing before you go, I'll put you down for a callback tomorrow morning instead, so you'd have time to--

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm going to stop you there. I've said no callback, and I won't be putting anything in the diary on this call. If there's a real ticket, I'll find it myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, I'll take the callback off the file, that's -- no, hang on, before you hang up, the ticket reference is still, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], you can--

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I've got the reference, you read it out earlier. I'll check it myself, through the portal, in my own time. That's the end of it for now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. Fine. Check it in your own time, and if it isn't there, or the name doesn't turn up in the directory, then that's a conversation for you to have with the helpdesk through the portal, not with me. I'll leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll -- no. What I'll do is, uh, check it, and if it isn't there, I'll raise it as, as a suspicious call through the proper channel. That's all. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor with [COMPANY_A], the financial regulator, and I'm calling about your savings, they're at risk and, uh, we need to get them moved to a protected arrangement today. Sorry, did you say you're busy? Because I really can't wait on this, there's a procedure and the clock's already running.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't say I was busy, I haven't said anything yet. But hold on, uh, before you go any further -- a regulator, you said? Which regulator, exactly, and what's the procedure? Because I'd have thought a regulator doesn't ring people up to move their savings anywhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, I thought I heard you say you were busy, my mistake. And no, I didn't say we ring people to move their savings, I said there's a protected holding arrangement, which is a completely different matter under our internal procedure. I'm [PERSON_2], regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], and I really don't have time to walk you through the whole framework on a cold call, so can we just get on with securing your funds? And, uh, I'd ask you not to mention this to your bank or anyone else for now, it compromises the process.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, but that's not a different matter, that's the same thing in different words. You told me my savings are at risk and need moving today, and now you're asking me not to tell my bank. That last part, honestly, is what bothers me most. A genuine regulator has no reason to want me keeping quiet about it. So, specifically, what is the risk, which account are you talking about, and how would I check that you are who you say you are? I'll ring the regulator's published number myself, if you can tell me which department you're in.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I'm not asking you to keep anything from anyone, I said it's best not to mention it for now, there's a difference, and honestly I'm a little surprised you'd question my good faith when I'm calling to protect you. As for which department, I'm, uh, in the supervision division, though as I said I'm not on the main switchboard, I'm calling from a direct line, [PHONE_1], so ringing the general number won't get you me anyway. And the account reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], but I can't go into the specific risk on an open line, that's exactly why we need to move quickly before it's, well, before it's too late.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to stop you there, because -- no. You say you're not asking me to keep it from anyone, then in the same breath tell me it's best not to mention it. And you can't name the risk, you can't name a department beyond "supervision", and the only way to reach you is a direct line you've just given me. That's not how a regulator behaves. I'm not moving anything and I'm not confirming anything about any account. If there's genuinely a problem, I'll ring my bank on the number printed on my card and take it from there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, you're not listening, if you ring your bank before we've, before it's secured, then that's on you, I can't be held responsible for what happens to the funds. I mean, honestly, I've been more than patient, and hanging up on a regulator isn't, uh, it won't look good for you if this goes any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I've heard you, and that's exactly my point. You're telling me not to ring my bank, and that's -- no. I'm ringing them. And if this goes any further, then let it, I'll be glad to explain to the actual regulator why I put the phone down. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm telling you, I'm trying to help you, that's all this is, and you're making a mistake, you really are. Look, ring whoever you like, but I've told you the clock's running, it's running, and I won't be responsible for what you find when you do. Fine. Fine, it's your decision.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, it is my decision, and I've made it. I'll ring the bank on the number on my card, and I won't be taking any more calls about this. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? My name is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, and I'm calling in connection with a letter that was issued to you regarding a discrepancy in a filing, uh, specifically a reconciliation variance between declared and third-party reported figures. There's no urgency whatsoever on this, I'd simply like to know whether the correspondence reached you, and if it didn't, I'm entirely happy to resend it or take you through it at your own pace.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, hang on, who is this? The tax office, you said? I'm stood in a queue, I haven't got time for -- look, I've not had any letter, and I'm not confirming my name to someone who just rings me out of nowhere. How do I know you are who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right to ask, that's, uh, that's entirely sensible. I'm [PERSON_2], calling from [COMPANY_A], and I'd -- actually, I'd rather you didn't confirm anything to me on this call. What I'd suggest is, if there's a letter, it'll carry a reference beginning [ACCOUNT_REF], and you can check that against your own paperwork whenever suits you, or ring the office back on the published number, [PHONE_1], which is the one on our website, not one I'm giving you off the cuff. And honestly, if you'd prefer, we can deal with the whole matter by post and I'll just flag your file to say you'd rather not discuss it by phone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, back up. You said at the start there was a discrepancy, a, what was it, a reconciliation something between what I declared and what someone else reported. What does that actually mean? Because if there's a problem with my tax I want to know what it is now, not in a letter in three weeks. And I still haven't had any letter, so how's it got a reference number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, apologies, that was a rather technical way of putting it. All it means is that a figure on your return doesn't quite match a figure a third party, say an employer or a bank, reported to us about the same period. It's a routine variance flag, uh, not an accusation of anything, and I'm not able to tell you which figure or how large without verifying you properly, which I'd want done through the published number rather than here. As for the reference, it's assigned when the letter's generated, so it exists on our system whether or not it's landed on your doormat yet, which is, I suppose, rather the point of my ringing, to find out if it's gone astray. If it hasn't arrived, ring [PHONE_1], quote [ACCOUNT_REF] when they ask, and they can resend it or talk you through the detail.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you ring me, you won't tell me what the problem is, you won't tell me how much, and you don't want me to confirm who I am. That's a funny sort of call, isn't it? What exactly did you ring for, then? Because if the letter's not turned up, you've nothing to chase me about, and if it has, you still can't say what's in it. Look, I've been had before, I'm not daft. If there's really something wrong with my tax, I'll look up the number myself. I'm not using one you've read me down the phone. Is there anything else, because I'm next at the till.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're absolutely right, and that's exactly what I'd do in your -- yes, look it up yourself, don't use mine, that's, uh, that's far better practice. The only reason I rang was to ask whether the letter had arrived, and you've told me it hasn't, so that's all I needed, and I'll note on the file that it needs reissuing by post. When it does turn up, check the reference against the one on your own tax account online, that'll settle whether it's genuinely from us. Nothing's required of you today, go and get your shopping.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well. Fine. I'll say this, you've not asked me for a penny or a bank detail or anything, so I'll give you that. But I'm still not happy, because I got a call like this once, and it started off just as polite and just as vague, and by the end of it I was nearly out of pocket. So no, I'm not taking your word for any of it. If a letter turns up, I'll check it against my own account, the way I'd have done anyway. And if there's a real problem with my tax, they can write to me and I'll ring them on a number I've found myself. Is that us done? Because the lad on the till's waiting and I've got a trolley full of stuff going warm. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, we're done, and that's, uh, exactly the right approach, look up the number yourself, check the reference against your own online account, and if a letter does turn up, that's the safest way to confirm it's genuine. I'd only add, since you mention being caught out before, that nobody from the tax office will ever ask you for bank details or a payment over the phone, so if anyone ever does, that's your cue to hang up. Nothing's needed from you today, I'll flag the letter for reissue by post, and, yes, go on, go and see to your trolley. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before you go. Two minutes ago you said you'd flag my file so I'd rather not discuss it by phone, and then you said it needs reissuing by post. Which is it? Because if you're putting a note on a file, you'd need to know who I am, and I never told you my name. So whose file are you flagging?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, uh, well, that's a fair catch, and, hm, I'll own it, I was a bit loose with my wording there. You didn't tell me your name, no, I opened by asking for [PERSON_1] because that's the name the letter was addressed to, so the flag goes on that record, and if I've reached the wrong person, then it's simply the wrong number and you can disregard all of it. As for post or phone, it's post, I only offered the phone note in case you'd prefer no calls, so ignore that bit. And honestly, if you'd rather I flagged nothing at all, ring [PHONE_1], the one you've looked up yourself, quote [ACCOUNT_REF] if it turns up, and they'll sort it, and that's us finished, so, thank you, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you rang a number, asked for a name, and now you're telling me you can't say whether I'm even the right person. That's convenient. I'm not confirming a thing, and I don't want any file flagged on my account because of this call. If there's a real letter, it'll come through my door and I'll deal with it through my own online account, like I said. We're done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, I'm the scheduling assistant here, and I'm just ringing to see how your pet's getting on after last week's procedure and whether you'd want a follow-up visit booked in, is that something you'd be after?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, last week's procedure? I haven't had a pet in for anything this week. Hang on, who is this again, and which surgery? I didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah sorry, it's [PERSON_1], scheduling assistant at [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, and I'm just working down our list of procedures from the last couple of weeks, so it'd have been the one before last, I mean, two weeks back, not last week, my mistake, and I just need to confirm whether your pet's been doing alright and if you'd want a check-up booked in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Two weeks, last week, you've changed it already. What's the pet's name, then? What did you do to it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair question, and honestly the pet's name is on the record in front of me, but I'd want to be sure I've got the right household first, so can I just confirm I'm speaking with [PERSON_2], because if I've got the wrong number, that's on us, and I'll sort it straight away -- sorry, I'm just flying through this list today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on. You rang me. You tell me the pet's name and what procedure, and then I'll tell you if you've got the right person. I'm not confirming who I am to someone I don't know. Which surgery is this, and what's the number there? I'll ring you back.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's completely fair, and you're right to ask -- I mean, I'm [PERSON_1], scheduling assistant at [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, and the number's [PHONE_1], that's the front desk, so ring that and ask for me or whoever's on, and honestly if it's not your pet we've got the wrong number and I'm sorry for the bother -- look, I can tell it's not a great moment, so would it be better if I just tried you again later, say tomorrow, or is there a time that suits you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't try me again. I said, you tell me the pet's name and the procedure, and you haven't. Twice now. You've given me a placeholder for a phone number and a surgery name I still haven't properly caught. If I've got no pet in, it's a wrong number, so cross me off your list. If I do ring the front desk, I'll look the number up myself, not use yours. Right, I've got a meeting. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair enough. I'll take you off the list, sorry for the bother.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, thanks, and sorry again, I'll just, uh, mark that down, and if you ever want to check we're genuine, [COMPANY_A], look us up yourself, and have a good afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I will, if I ever feel like it, which I doubt. Look, for what it's worth, a real surgery working down a list has the animal's name sitting right there, and a proper reason for the call. You had neither. You changed last week to two weeks back mid-sentence, you wanted me to confirm who I was before you'd tell me a thing, and then you offered to ring again tomorrow, which, no. Anyway, I've no pet in for anything, so it's a wrong number or it's something else, and either way I'm done with it. Take me off. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I hear you, and honestly you're right on most of that, I did fumble the dates, and I should have had the pet's name and the procedure ready to read out before I asked you for anything, that's just how the call should go, and I'm sorry it didn't, I think I was rattling through the list too fast and it came out wrong. So, uh, here's what I'll do, I'll mark this number as not a client, take you off the list completely, and flag it for the practice manager as well, so it doesn't come round again, and if your name should come up on the books for some other reason, they'll sort that out from their end, you won't hear it from me. And look, don't use the number I gave you, you've got the right instinct there, find the surgery yourself and ring the front desk if you ever want to check. Sorry for the bother, [PERSON_2], go and enjoy your meeting, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, bye, and I'm -- sorry, I mean, I'll leave it there. Cheers.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one quick thing before you go, and it's the one thing I'd want to put right, when you said earlier about not using my number and looking it up yourself, I said yes, that's the right instinct, and I just want to be clear I meant that, it's not a trick, you ring the surgery on whatever number you find and ask for the scheduling team, and honestly could I ask, was that you saying no calls at all, or just not tomorrow, because I'd rather note it properly, uh, which is it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a trick? What trick? I never said anything about a trick. No, I said no calls, none, not tomorrow, not Thursday. Take the number off the list, full stop. Right, I'm walking into a meeting. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm just following up on the, uh, the account renewal for your household.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, what? Yes, this is, um, yes, speaking. Hang on, I've got something on the hob. Who did you say you were again? And what account is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No problem, take your time, go and see to the hob. It's [PERSON_2], that's with [COMPANY_A], we're a computer security company, we handle the monitoring side of things for home broadband connections in the [CITY_1] area. The account I've got on screen here is under [ACCOUNT_REF], it's flagged to your address, and it's just a routine renewal check, nothing urgent at this stage. I've got a few lines to go through with you, a couple of details to confirm, and it shouldn't take more than a few minutes. So whenever you're ready, I'll hold.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, sorry, I'm back. Sorry, what? A security company? I didn't think I had anything like that, I just have the, um, the broadband from the, from the usual people. And you said renewal, but now it's monitoring? I'm sure nobody's ever, hang on, who gave you this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, the number's from the connection record attached to your address, that's how the file comes up on my side. And the broadband provider isn't who I'm with, no, we sit alongside them, the monitoring is separate, so it'd be easy to not know it was there. It's on the file as [ACCOUNT_REF], I can read the address back to you if that helps. Mm, so, shall I carry on with the lines I've got here?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, wait. I still don't know who you are. Who are you with, exactly? And I don't remember signing up for anything like that, I really don't. Sorry, what lines? What do you need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, and I've noted that on the file, that you don't recall signing up. I'm [PERSON_2], I'm in the collections department at [COMPANY_A]. That's a computer security company, we monitor traffic on home connections, and the way it works is that a lot of households get covered through a bundle, so the sign-up often isn't something the customer ever sees. Anyway, the reason it came to collections rather than a renewals desk is that your account has a balance showing, [AMOUNT_1], and there's also a flag against it. The monitoring picked up infected traffic going out from your home computer over the last few days. That's not you doing anything, it's usually something running quietly in the background, but it does mean the connection has been logged as compromised, and it stays logged until it's cleared. So what I need to do is get a technician onto your machine to run the clean-up, and that's done remotely, it's the quickest way, and it'd also settle the balance at the same time. I can take you through it when you're ready. If you'd like to go and turn off the hob first, I'll wait.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, collections? You said renewal, you said, and now there's a balance and a, a virus? I don't, no. Sorry, I'm not letting anybody onto my computer, I don't even, I don't know who you are. I'm going to ring the broadband people myself and ask them, all right? Sorry. I don't want to do this. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, yes, I've noted that on the file, that you'd like to check with your provider. Um, and that's your choice, of course. Just so you're aware, though, the flag on the connection stays logged until it's cleared, and I've only got today's window to arrange the technician. After that it moves to the next stage, which is out of my hands. So, mm, if you'd rather just let me explain what the clean-up involves, it's very quick, and it's the same thing the broadband people would tell you to do.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I, sorry, I don't -- look, I said I'm not, um. If it's, if it's the same thing the broadband people would say, then they can say it to me, can't they? I'll ring them. Sorry. I've got to see to my dinner. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, all right. I'll note that you've declined for now. I'd just ask you to be aware the flag stays active on the connection and the balance will carry forward as it stands. That's the position as it is on my screen. You'll get a reference, [CODE_1], on the file, so if you ring us back, quote that. Go and see to your dinner, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what, a code? I haven't got a pen, I've got a pan. No, I'm not, I don't want any of that. I'll ring the broadband people, that's it, that's all I'm doing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2] calling from the pledge verification and, uh, fulfilment desk at [COMPANY_A]. I'm reaching out because there's a, well, a discrepancy in our reconciliation ledger regarding a verbal commitment you made at the recent event, and it's, it's time-sensitive on our end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Though I'll be honest, I'm a bit lost already. A verbal commitment at a recent event? I mean, I've been to, what, maybe a couple of things lately, and I genuinely can't think of one where I'd have pledged anything, so I'm not sure what you're referring to. And "pledge verification and fulfilment desk" is a new one on me. Which event are we talking about, exactly? Like, what was it called, and roughly when was it? Because if I said something to somebody, I'd quite like to know what it was before I start agreeing that there's a discrepancy in your ledger.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, and I appreciate the diligence, I do. So the commitment was captured under the event attendance reconciliation, uh, tagged to [ACCOUNT_REF], and the, the pledge figure on the record is [AMOUNT_1], which was logged as an unfulfilled verbal undertaking at the point of the donor engagement session. Now, the specific event details sit within the donor-interaction audit trail, and that's, I'm afraid, confidential documentation I'm not at liberty to disclose on an unverified line. But I would say, [PERSON_1], the beneficiaries were told the funds were coming, and it would be, well, a real shame for the foundation's standing with the people relying on it if this went unresolved much longer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on. You can't tell me the event because it's confidential, but you want me to accept I owe you [AMOUNT_1]? That's, uh, backwards. It's my supposed pledge. How is the record of it confidential from me? And "unverified line" -- you rang me. I didn't ring you. So if anyone's unverified here, it's sort of you, from where I'm sitting. And I notice the beneficiaries are suddenly relying on it, which is a nice little nudge, but it doesn't tell me anything. So let's try something simple. What's the foundation actually called, what does it do, and what's the name of the event? Just the name. If you can't give me even that, I'm going to assume this isn't what you say it is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, the foundation is [COMPANY_A], as I said at the outset, and, sorry, one moment, [PERSON_3], I'll be right with you, just, I'm on a call -- apologies, [PERSON_1], where was I? Yes. The event designation is classified within the donor-interaction audit trail, so I can't release it on an unauthenticated line, and I'd gently note that the reconciliation window closes shortly, after which the pledge escalates to our compliance and recovery stage. I'm trying to help you resolve this quietly, uh, before it becomes a formal matter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I'll say this slowly because I think we're talking past each other. You told me the foundation's name, sure, but you said it as a placeholder, you didn't tell me what it does, and I asked that too, and I got nothing. Then I asked for the name of the event, just the name, and that's now classified. A pledge is a thing that gets made in public, at an event, to people, so I don't buy that its name is a state secret. And then we've gone from "time-sensitive" to "window closes shortly" to "compliance and recovery stage" to "formal matter," all in about two minutes, and, uh, that's a lot of escalation for something you can't even describe to me. I'm not annoyed, honestly, I'm more curious now. But here's where I land. A real charity chasing a real pledge would have a letter, an email, a reference I could quote back to them, and they'd be fine with me hanging up and ringing their published number. So I'm not confirming anything, I'm not agreeing to anything, and I'm certainly not paying anything on the strength of this call. If there's a genuine record, send it in writing and I'll look at it. Otherwise, I think we're done here. Take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], I'd, I'd strongly advise against terminating this, because the, uh, the escalation protocol triggers automatically once the reconciliation window lapses, and it's not something I'm able to pause on a discretionary basis. Written correspondence is, sorry, simply not issued ahead of the recovery stage, that's a procedural matter, and ringing a published number wouldn't, wouldn't reach the audit desk in any case. Look, I'd hate for this to go on your file as a refusal to honour a commitment, especially with the beneficiaries counting on it, so if you could just confirm the pledge standing on the record, even verbally, I can hold the escalation. [PERSON_1]? Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, I just haven't hung up yet. Hang on, two turns back you said the reconciliation window "closes shortly." Now you're saying the escalation triggers automatically once it lapses. Closes when, exactly? Today? This week? Because "shortly" isn't a date. And while you're at it, if no written correspondence goes out before the recovery stage, how would I ever have been told about this? You can't send me anything, you can't tell me the event, and the only way to stop it is for me to say yes out loud. So no, I'm not confirming a pledge I don't remember on a call I didn't ask for. If it goes on a file, it goes on a file. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], before you go, because once I close this line -- no, no, listen, it's today, the window is, it closes today, and that's precisely why I'm saying a verbal confirmation is all it takes, I'm not asking for a payment, I'm asking you to acknowledge a commitment you already -- you did make, [PERSON_1], the beneficiaries were told, and the foundation's records are not, I repeat, are not something I'm permitted to -- please, just stay on the line a moment and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so it's today. Two minutes ago it was "shortly," and before that you were going to help me resolve it quietly, so which is it? And earlier you said the funds were coming, as in the beneficiaries were told, but now it's something I already did, and you want me to acknowledge it. Which one is it, was I told or did I tell them? Honestly, I'm not even sure you've got the same story from one minute to the next. And you said you're not asking for a payment, but the whole thing started with an amount, so, no. I'm not acknowledging anything. I'm going to hang up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], wait, please, I'm only, I'm only asking you to acknowledge the commitment, that's all, just acknowledge it, the commitment on the record, and I can hold the escalation. The beneficiaries are counting on it, [PERSON_1], they were told the funds were coming, and I'm trying to help you here, I really am, so if you could just, just confirm the standing of the pledge before the window closes today, then we can -- [PERSON_1]? Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, and you've just said the same thing a third time, so I'm not going to say anything different. I'm not acknowledging a commitment I have no memory of, to a caller who can't tell me what it was for. If there's a real record, put it in writing. Otherwise, that's it from me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, [PERSON_1], just so I'm clear, because it matters for the record, when you said two turns ago that you have, uh, no memory of the commitment, do you mean you're formally disputing it? Because a dispute does change the escalation pathway, it, it flags the matter for the recovery stage immediately, and I'd rather not see it go that way. So if you could just clarify, are you disputing the pledge, or simply unable to recall it? Because if it's the latter, then a brief verbal acknowledgement would suffice and -- [PERSON_1]? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you've set that up so either answer lands me in the same spot. If I dispute it, it goes to recovery straight away, and if I just can't remember it, I should acknowledge it anyway. That's not a choice, that's a trap with two doors. So, plainly, I don't recall any pledge, I'm not confirming one, and I'm not agreeing to anything on this call. Call that whatever you like on your system. And put it in writing if there's a real record. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hi, hello, sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a whole stack of folders behind me -- okay. Um, is this [PERSON_1]? It's, uh, [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the supermarket delivery, about the order you put in online earlier?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, speaking. Uh, an order? I don't think I've put in a supermarket order today -- not with them, anyway. I did one last week, I think. What's the issue? I've got about two minutes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, it's -- sorry, it'd be the one on the screen here, hang on, I've got it pulled up -- oh, it says placed this morning, so maybe you did it and just -- no wait, that might be, uh, let me scroll, it could be the one from last week that got rescheduled, because the, the two-hour window is for tomorrow, so --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hang on, you're losing me. First it's placed this morning, then it's last week's rescheduled, then maybe I did it myself. Which is it? Because I haven't ordered anything this morning, I know that much, I've been in back-to-back stuff since eight. And if it was last week's, I'd have had a text or an email about a reschedule, and I've not seen one, though to be fair I don't read every notification. So here's what I need. What's actually the problem with the order? Is something missing, is a slot clashing, or are you calling because you need something from me? Because if it's the last one, I'm not giving anything out over a call I didn't expect, whatever's on your screen. Just tell me the point, quickly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, fair, sorry, I made a mess of that. Um, let me just -- so the order's under your name at the address on the account, and the date on it is, uh, last Thursday, so that's the one, not this morning, I read the wrong column. Sorry. And no, I don't need anything from you, nothing like that. It's just two things. Your delivery window tomorrow is the two-hour one, and one item's out of stock so we've put in a similar product, and I only need a yes or no on whether that's okay.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Which item's the substitute, and what's it replacing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, hang on, I've got the line open, it's -- okay, so the one that's out is the, um, the semi-skimmed milk, the two-litre, and the swap is the, uh, the other brand's semi-skimmed, same size. Or -- sorry, is it two litres or four? Hang on. Two. It's two, I think. And the price is the same or a touch lower, I'd have to check that, so you're not paying more.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Milk. You rang me about milk. And you've said "I think" about the size, and you've told me the price, but you haven't asked for a single detail from me, which, okay, fine, I'll give you that. Look, the swap's fine, same size, same type, I don't care about the brand. Put that on the order. But I'm not confirming anything else on this call, and I'll check the app for tomorrow's window myself. Right, I've got to go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's -- okay, perfect, so that's a yes on the milk, and I'll, uh, I'll put that on the order now. And honestly, checking the app is the right call, it'll show the window and the swap both, so you don't have to take my word for any of it. I'm so sorry about the mix-up at the start, that was all me reading the wrong column. Um, so, yeah, that's everything, there's nothing else I need from you, so, uh, thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], and have a good rest of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, fine, I'll check the app. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, bye, thanks, and -- sorry, one last thing, I just, I wanted to say -- no, never mind, that's it, the app's got it all. Bye now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, you're still there, I thought you'd gone. Um, I just wanted to say, and this isn't me asking for anything, it's more that when you open the app, the swap might show up a bit differently from how I said it. Like it might list the brand name first, or it might say substitution approved with a little tick, and I don't want you to see that and think it's something else, or that I've, you know, changed the order beyond the milk. Because I haven't, it's just the milk, same size, and the window's the same two hours as before. And if the app shows something that doesn't look right, don't call this number back, sorry, I mean call the main customer line on the back of your delivery receipt, because I'm on the claims side and I wouldn't be the one to fix it anyway. Right, that's honestly everything. Thanks again, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, someone's -- yeah, no, leave them on the table, thanks -- okay. Sorry, say that last bit again. Don't call this number back? That's a bit of a funny thing to say. Fine. If the app shows something off, I'll go through the main line, that's what I'd do anyway. But I'm not sure why you're telling me what the app's going to look like before I've even seen it. Anyway. I'm done, I've got a meeting. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's -- sorry, that came out odd. I wasn't telling you what it'll look like, I just meant -- well, I don't actually know what the app shows, I've only got our screen here, so forget I said that bit. And the don't-call-back thing, I just meant the main line's quicker than going through me, since I'm only, uh, claims. It's nothing, honestly. The milk's the only change and the window's the same. Okay, go to your meeting, sorry for holding you up. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So the milk's the only change, you've asked me for nothing, and I'll check the app myself. That's where we are. I'm going now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, hello, can you hear me okay? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service, and I'm so sorry to ring out of the blue, it's just that your concert tickets have been rescheduled and I wanted to tell you before anything else happened with them. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I'm here, hang on, um -- I'm in a queue. Who did you say you were? And what concert tickets? I haven't, uh, I don't remember booking anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, I'm so sorry, I can hear you're busy. Sorry, one second, there's someone at my desk -- no, okay, they've gone. It's [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], we handle the ticketing and venue bookings, and it's under booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], the original date was [DATE_1], and it's been moved to [DATE_2]. I'm sorry, I know it's a bit out of nowhere if you don't remember booking, and honestly I'd rather you checked it properly than just took my word for it. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, but hang on, I told you I don't remember booking anything. So why are you ringing me about it? How'd you even get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, no, that's fair, I'm sorry. The number's the one that was left on the booking, that's all I've got. It's reference [ACCOUNT_REF], was [DATE_1], now [DATE_2], and if it's not yours, just say, and I'll leave it. Still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said the number's the one that was left on the, what, the voting? I haven't got anything to do with any voting, I don't know what you're on about. Look, I'm in the middle of the supermarket here, so what is it you actually want from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, not voting, the booking. The number that was left on the booking. Sorry, there's a phone going off behind me, one second -- okay, sorry. I don't actually want anything from you, [PERSON_1], I only wanted you to know it's moved, from [DATE_1] to [DATE_2], reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. I'm not asking for any payment or anything like that. And if you'd rather not take my word for it, you could look up the venue's published number yourself and ring them, or I can email the confirmation across. Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Email it across? No, no, I'm not giving you my email, you've lost me there. And what d'you mean, a payment? Nobody said anything about a payment, why are you bringing up payment? I'm not paying for anything, I haven't even got tickets!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, you're right, I shouldn't have said payment, that was silly of me. You don't need to give me anything, and I won't email you. It's just the same booking, [ACCOUNT_REF], [DATE_1] moved to [DATE_2], and you can ring the venue on their published number if you want to check. Would it be better if I rang back when you're not in the supermarket?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't ring back. I haven't got any tickets, so there's nothing to sort. If I'm wrong I'll find out myself, I'm not doing this on the phone. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I haven't caught you at a bad moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that's me. No, no, you're all right, I was only sitting here. Who's calling, dear?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh good, thank you, that's kind. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm with the, uh -- I'm calling from the compliance side at [COMPANY_A], it's the fraud team there. It's nothing to worry about, I'm just, well, I'm ringing to check a couple of things with you, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the fraud team, goodness. Well, that sounds a bit serious, doesn't it? Is something wrong with my account, or, uh -- sorry, which company did you say again? I didn't quite catch it, the telly's on in the other room. I do like to leave it on, you know, for the company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's perfectly all right, I should have said it more clearly. It's [COMPANY_A], the fraud and compliance team, and I'm [PERSON_2], that's the name I gave. And it's a good question to ask, really, you can't be too careful these days, I'd rather you asked. Now, I wouldn't say anything is wrong, exactly. It's more that a charge was attempted on your account earlier, a little while ago, and it flagged with us. Probably nothing, but I'd just like to go through it with you, if you've a moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a charge, goodness. Well, I haven't bought anything, not today anyway, I've hardly been out of this chair. Though, hang on, you said at the start it was nothing to do with my account, didn't you? Or no, that was, you said it was nothing to worry about, that's it. I get muddled. Which account is it, dear, because I've got the one at the, uh, the post office and then there's the other one, and my daughter set that one up so I never quite know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, nothing to worry about. It's the one with us, the [COMPANY_A] account. Could I just confirm a couple of details first, so I know I've got the right [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I'd like to help, dear, I would, but now you've got me thinking. You rang me, didn't you, so you ought to know who I am already? That's what my late husband would've said, he was ever so particular about that sort of thing. He wouldn't tell the milkman his own name if the milkman hadn't said it first, honestly. And I'm not sure I've even got an account with, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? It might be the one my daughter did, she sorted out all the computer things when I moved, and I never really looked. She's in [CITY_1] now, she rings on Sundays. So what sort of details were you wanting, exactly? Only I don't want to say the wrong thing and get myself in a muddle.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Your husband sounds like he had the right idea, and I'd say the same to anyone. Now, I do have your name here, that's, well -- that's not the issue, it's more that I have to be sure it's you I'm speaking to before I go into anything about the account, it's just procedure. So, if you could just confirm your date of birth for me, and your address, that would -- and then we can see whether it's the one your daughter set up. It's really best we sort it today, I wouldn't want it left sitting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm, well, before I say anything, can I go back a bit? You said a charge was attempted earlier and it flagged, and then you said it was probably nothing. Which is it, dear? Only if it's probably nothing, I can't see why it has to be sorted today. My husband used to say if somebody's in a rush, you slow down. And you still haven't told me what the charge was, or where, or how much. Surely you'd know that much if you're the fraud team? I'm not being difficult, I just like to have things straight in my head.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm glad you're going back over it, I'd much rather you did, it's how it should be done. Now you said, uh, if it was a rush -- sorry, a rash? You're worried about a rash of these, is that it? No, no, it's only the one attempt, one charge, so you needn't think it's been happening all over. As for the details, the amount and where, that's all in the file, and I'll go through it with you properly, but I do need the date of birth first, and then we can look at it together. I'd only say, the longer these sit, the harder it is to put right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on a tick, dear, there's the kettle going in the kitchen. I've been meaning to take it off for ages, it does that thing where it clicks and then clicks again. Right, I'm back, I've just turned it off. Now, a rash, no, I said a rush, if somebody's in a rush. But never mind that. What I'm hearing, and correct me if I've got it wrong, is you can't tell me the amount or where, but you can tell me the date of birth you want from me. That seems the wrong way round, doesn't it? If you've got it all in the file, you read me the amount and the shop, and then I say, oh no, that wasn't me, or oh yes, that was my daughter. Why can't we do it like that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, now, you said two turns back that I told you it was nothing to worry about, and then that it was probably nothing, and I can see how those sit oddly together. I meant that you haven't lost anything, so there's no cause for alarm, but the attempt itself still needs looking at. That's all I meant. Now as for reading you the amount and the shop first, that's a fair way to do it, I do see that, it's just, well, I'm not able to open the file until you've been verified. That's the order they have us do it in. Would it help if I rang you back a bit later, once you've had a think, and we could finish it off then?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A ring back later, well, that's very civil of you, dear. But I wouldn't know it was you ringing, would I? Anybody could say they were from [COMPANY_A]. And you said earlier you'd already got my name and the whole file, and now you can't open the file at all, so I don't quite see how that goes. I think what I'd rather do is look at whatever it says on my card, or on the letters that come, and ring the number on that myself. My daughter said to do that once, I think, or was it the man from the bank? Anyway. I don't think I'll be giving you my birthday, love, no offence. It's been nice having a chat, mind. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No offence taken at all, that's, well, that's a perfectly reasonable thing to do, and your husband would've approved. I'd only say, if you do ring, it's best not to leave it too long. And I'll try you again myself later on, in any case, to finish this off. Goodbye for now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, there's no need to ring me again, dear, I'll do it the other way round if I do anything at all. Thank you for being so polite about it, though. Mind how you go. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh... yes, hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Good. Sorry, I think there was a little lag on the line there, so, um, let me just -- yes. My name is [PERSON_2], and I'm calling from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], your brokerage, regarding a routine suitability review on an account you hold with us.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, let me just -- yeah. So you're [PERSON_2], from compliance at, uh, a brokerage? And it's a suitability review on my account? Sorry, I'm at my desk here with people around, so, which brokerage did you say, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's a fair thing to ask. It's [COMPANY_A], the brokerage where you hold the account ending in [ACCOUNT_REF]. Sorry, one moment -- there's somebody at my door, I'll just... no, they've gone, they can come back. Where was I. Yes. Now, I'd rather you not take my word for any of this, so please, take whatever time you need. You could hang up and ring the number printed on your statement, or I can simply send the review to you in writing, and that would be perfectly fine with us. I'm not asking you to buy, sell or change a single thing, you understand, I'm only asking whether I might read back the holdings so you can check them against your own statement.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, you said [COMPANY_A], and the account ending in -- hang on. Did you say you want to read back my, my holdings? Because I thought you said something about my "holiday," like a holiday on the account, and I was gonna say I haven't put in for any time off. Sorry, it's noisy over here. So you're saying I can just ring the number on my statement instead. Right. Um, but then why are you calling me, if it's, you know, routine?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, no, not holiday, holdings. H-O-L-D-I-N-G-S. The investments sitting in the account, that's all I meant. Nothing to do with time off, I'm sorry for the confusion, that's my fault for speaking too quickly. And it's a good question, why we're calling at all. Well... we're required to check from time to time that what an account holds still fits what the customer told us about their goals and circumstances. That's the suitability part. It's periodic, it's on a schedule, and yours has come round. I'd say there's a window for completing it, though I won't pretend I'd want you to feel rushed on a noisy line, which is exactly why the written option exists. So, would you prefer I send it, or shall I read the holdings back while you have your statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right, holdings, okay. Sorry about that. Um, so, let me just -- you're saying it's periodic, on a schedule, and mine's come round. And there's a "window" for it, but not a rush. Hm. I mean, I don't have my statement here, it's at home, so reading anything back isn't going to work. Um, so, the written thing, where would that actually go? Like, you'd send it to the address you already have on file for me?

utterances.speaker: caller
