utterances.text: Yes, to the address already on file, nothing new, and I wouldn't want you giving me another one over the phone anyway. Uh, though I should correct myself, because I said a moment ago that it's all on a schedule, and, well, it's a bit more that yours was flagged at this cycle's review, which is routine, it just isn't quite the same as a calendar date. I'm sorry, I'd rather be exact with you. And no statement at hand is perfectly all right, so let's leave the holdings alone entirely. If you'd like, you can also check me from your end, the review will be on your online account under your documents, or you can ring the number on the back of your statement, and ask whether [PERSON_2] in compliance has a review open for you. I'll wait, or I'll send it. Whichever you'd like.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, hang on, you said "flagged." Two turns back, you said it was periodic, on a schedule, and mine had just come round. Now it's "flagged at this cycle's review." Which is it? Because those aren't quite the same thing, are they? Flagged sounds like somebody noticed something.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, they aren't the same, and I phrased that badly. Nothing's been noticed, nothing's wrong with the account. "Flagged" is just the word our system uses when a review comes due, so, same thing as periodic really, and I should have kept to one word. Ring the number on your statement and ask them, I'd welcome it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, you said "the word our system uses when a review is due," right, and then you said ring the number and ask them... did you say ask them about a "refund"? Because I haven't asked for any refund, I'm not owed anything as far as I know. Sorry, one of my colleagues just walked past and I caught half of that. Is this about money coming back to me, or...?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no refund, nothing like that. I said ring and ask them whether a review is open for you, that's all. There's no money coming back and nothing owed in either direction, and I'm not asking you to pay or transfer anything. Sorry, the line's been poor on both sides, I think. Now, one thing you could do that doesn't rely on my word... ask whoever you reach at the number on your statement to confirm that compliance has a review open on your account, and, uh, they'd be able to tell you the review reference, which is [CODE_1]. If it matches, you'll know it's us. And if you'd rather, I'll simply send it in writing and you can look it over at home, with your statement beside you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, let me just repeat that back. No refund, nothing owed, and I ring the number on my statement, ask if there's a review open, and they can match it against [CODE_1]. Right. Um, and honestly, that's what I'll do, because you did say I should and the written thing sounds fine too. I'm not going to go through anything on this call. So send it to the address you've got, or don't, and I'll check it myself from home tonight. Okay? Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly right, and thank you, [PERSON_1], for being so careful about it. I'd much rather you check than simply take my word. So, to be clear about what happens next: nothing further is needed from you on this call. I'll have the review sent in writing to the address we already hold, and when you ring the number on your statement this evening, you can ask whether compliance has a review open for you under [CODE_1]. If they confirm it, good. If for any reason they can't, then please don't act on anything from me, and tell them that you had a call. I'd want to know that too. And, um, one small thing, since you mentioned the noise at your desk. If you do reply to the written review, do it at home, where you can have your statement beside you and take your time over it. Nobody ought to be hurrying you. Thanks again, and good evening.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, ring the number on my statement tonight, ask about [CODE_1], and if they can't confirm it, I don't act on anything and I tell them about the call. Yeah. I'll do that, I'll ring tonight, from home. Right, so, thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hey, hey, it's me. Uh... yeah, it's me, don't you recognise my voice? Come on, I know it's been a little while, but guess who it is, you'll get it straight away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Me who? ... Sorry, I've got a kid running around here, you'll have to just say your name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, sorry, I know, bad timing, I can hear the little one in the background. It's just, uh, okay, so, um... look, I don't really want to get into names right now, it's been a really rough morning and I'm kind of, you know, hanging by a thread here. Just try, one guess, I promise you'll get it, and then I can ask you something real quick, it'll take two seconds.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not guessing. You said it's been a while, and now you're saying you're hanging by a thread, so which is it, we talk all the time or I haven't heard from you in ages? And you asked for a favour before you've even told me who you are. Just say your name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, you're right, that's, I mean, I did say both things, I'm just, I'm a mess right now, I'm not thinking straight. Everybody asks me that, honestly, it's not a big deal, we can sort out the name part in a minute. Look, I just need a hand with something small, really small, it's one quick thing and then I'll explain everything, and, um, could you maybe not mention this call to anyone? I just don't want it getting around yet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Don't mention it to -- no. I mean, why would I... okay, wait. You still haven't told me who you are, and now it's a secret? Who asks for a favour and for silence from someone they won't even name? I'm not doing anything until I know who this is. So, name. Or I'm hanging up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, don't hang up, please, I'm not asking you to keep secrets, I never said that, I just said not to spread it around, that's different. And honestly, I'm not even a, uh, I'm just calling from the road, I'm in the car, it's, I mean, I'm at home actually, it's just a lot going on, you know? Look, it's me, you know me, just trust me on this one, it's two minutes, I swear.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You said you were in the car, and then you're at home, and a minute ago you said you didn't want it mentioned and now you're saying you never asked that. So I don't know what to believe. And I don't hand out trust to someone who won't say their own name. I'm sorry, but if you can't tell me who you are, there's no favour, and I'm done with this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, wait, don't, okay, I'm not, that's not what I meant, I just, ugh. Listen, you're getting the wrong idea, I'm not trying to trick you, I'm just, uh, I can't really get into it on the phone right now, that's all. Please, just stay on a second, I'm literally just asking you to listen, it's not a big thing, honestly, you're making it sound way bigger than it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm not -- look, I'm not trying to make it sound bigger than it is, I just -- okay, listen. I'm still here, aren't I? But "I can't get into it on the phone," that's the part I don't get, because you called me. On the phone. So what is it you can't say, your name? If it's really nothing, then say it. One word. Then we'll see.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, the thing is, it's not that I can't, it's, uh -- no, wait, that's not it either. I mean, it's [PERSON_1], obviously, you know it's, um -- ugh, the line keeps cutting out on my end, can you hear me okay? Look, just, can you stay right there, don't go anywhere, and I'll explain the whole thing in a second, I promise, it's honestly nothing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Obviously? You said obviously and then you said um, that's not a name, that's -- no, hang on, don't tell me to stay right there, I'm not waiting for a, I can hear you fine, the line's fine, so what's the -- okay, no. No. You've had five goes at one word and you can't say it. I'm not doing this. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, don't, I swear it's, uh -- hello? You still there? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on -- no, sweetheart, put that down, we don't throw that. Sorry, what? ... Yeah, I'm still here, I just -- no. I already said goodbye and I meant it. If you can't say who you are, I'm not helping, and I'm not staying on. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yes, sorry, is that [PERSON_1]? It's just [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants over here, and I'm only ringing to see if you've got a few minutes later this week for a quick, uh, a quick chat with one of our technicians, it won't take long at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Who is this -- [COMPANY_A], is that, I don't, hang on, I've got a pan going here. A technician for what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you're fine, take your time with the pan, I'll, uh, I'll hold on, and honestly it's nothing to worry about, it's really just a routine chat, we're a computer security company, [COMPANY_A], and I'm only the scheduling side so I just need to find a time that suits you, so would sometime Thursday work or is that, is mornings better for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Computer security? Sorry, I don't, I haven't asked for anything like that. What's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, you haven't asked, that's, well it's, so what happened is our monitoring picked up some, uh, some traffic coming from your home computer that's, well it looks like it's infected, sending stuff out without you knowing, which is why the technician wants a quick word, and it's really better sooner than, so would Thursday morning suit, or is today easier?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Infected? Sorry, my computer's, what do you mean sending stuff out, I don't, hang on, how would you even know that? You're, I mean how did you get my number, and how do I know you're actually from -- from where you said?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, so, I'm only on the scheduling side so the technical side is really for the technician to explain, but the traffic's tied to your address, that's how we, we've got your details on the alert, and it's honestly quicker if you just talk to him, he can walk you through it, so is Thursday morning okay, or would today be easier because the longer it's, uh, the longer it's sending, the worse it, so shall I say today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, go back a bit. You said before, it's picking up stuff coming from my computer, and now it's tied to my address? Which is it? Is that my computer or my, my address, I don't -- and you still haven't said how you got my details. And don't say today, I've got a dinner on, I can't just, sorry, what's your name again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say dinner, no that's fine, I'm not, we don't need to do it over dinner, uh, anytime that suits, and it's [PERSON_2], like I said, [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], and the technician will go through all the, the address and the computer side when he rings, so what I'll do is I'll ring you back a bit later on, once you've, once you've finished your pan and your dinner, and we'll get it all finished off then, yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, hang on. You still haven't told me how you've got my details, and I don't want somebody ringing me about my computer when I don't know who you are. If there's something wrong, I'll ring [COMPANY_A] myself, on the number I already have, not one you give me. So, no, don't ring back. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Um, am I speaking with the registered keeper of the vehicle on file with [COMPANY_A]? I only ask because, uh, my notes show two names on the record and I just want to be sure I've got the right one before I go on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, hello. Sorry, I'm not sure I follow, the registered keeper of the, which vehicle did you mean? I do have a car, yes, but I didn't catch who you said you were calling from. Who is this, sorry?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, that's a fair -- sorry, it's [COMPANY_A], I'm in compliance there, the vehicle warranty side. And it's really just a routine check on the file, nothing to worry about, I only need to confirm which car we're, uh, talking about, so if you could just tell me the make and, well, whichever one you drive most --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, the warranty side. Um, I'm sorry, I don't really recall hearing from [COMPANY_A] before, so I'm a bit lost. Is it something to do with the car I bought, or, I mean, did I miss a letter or something? I'd hate to have done something wrong. How would I, um, how do I know it's definitely you who's calling, if you don't mind me asking?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, please don't apologise, that's a, that's a very sensible thing to ask, and honestly I wish more people did ask it. It's, uh -- sorry, one second, somebody's just come to my desk -- yes, I'll be right with you, just leave it there -- sorry about that. Where was I. Right, so, you haven't done anything wrong, nothing like that, it's only that the warranty on your file is coming up for renewal and it does need confirming today, and I'd rather we got it sorted while I have your record open in front of me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's all right, no need to say sorry, I've got nothing much on this afternoon. Um, but I'm afraid I still don't quite understand, because you said I haven't done anything wrong, which is a relief, but then you said it needs confirming today, and I'm not sure why it would be so urgent. I mean, I don't really remember a warranty that was about to run out, I'd have to go and look in the drawer where I keep all the car papers, and I'm not very good with that sort of thing, my paperwork's a bit of a muddle, honestly. And you still haven't quite answered what I asked, sorry, about how I'd know it's really you. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or something like that? I don't want to be difficult, I'd just feel a bit better knowing for certain.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so glad you asked that, truly, and, uh, I'd never think of it as difficult, it's exactly the sort of care we'd hope every customer takes. Now, you said the drawer where you keep the car papers, and I'd actually, um, leave the drawer for now, because I wouldn't want you to go to any trouble with the paperwork when I already have the whole file here. As for a number, the line I'm on is an internal one, so it isn't something I can give out, but one of our team will certainly ring you back, I just couldn't tell you exactly when. What I'd say is the renewal really shouldn't be left to sit, it would be a shame for it to lapse over something so small, and, well, if we could just get it confirmed now, it's all very straightforward.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, sorry. But, um, I did ask about a number, and you said it's an internal line, so I can't ring you, and someone will ring me, but you can't say when. So I'm sorry, I still don't see how I'd know it's really you, that's all I'm asking. And you said leave the drawer, but then I don't know what I'd be confirming, do I? I haven't even told you which car yet, and you've got the whole file. Why would you need me to confirm anything, if you've got it all there?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, and that's, uh, that's a very good question, and I'm glad you put it so plainly, because it deserves a proper answer. The file has the details, yes, but the renewal itself needs a, a spoken confirmation from the keeper, that's just how the process is set up, it can't be done on my side alone. And I understand the callback business sounds a little odd, I do, but it's simply how the office is arranged, and I wouldn't want you to read anything into it. What I'd say is, the, the cover on the car is quite generous at the moment, much better than most people have, and it would be a real pity to let it slip over a few minutes' hesitation. So if you could just say yes to the renewal, I can close it off for you right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, I'm sorry, I'm still a bit muddled, but, um, say yes to what exactly? You haven't told me what it costs, or which car, or even what the cover is, so I wouldn't know what I was agreeing to, would I? And, I mean, you keep saying it's a pity if I hesitate, but I'd feel awful saying yes to something I don't understand. I think, uh, I think I'd rather you sent me something in the post, and then I can have a proper look at it with my papers. Would that be all right? I'm sorry to be a bother.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Well, I'd, I'd gently say that waiting for the post rather defeats the purpose, because, uh, the window on this is, well, it isn't one I'd like to see you miss, and I couldn't promise a letter would reach you in time. And please, you're not a bother, I'd never say that, but I do think a few minutes now is a lot easier than the, the difficulty of reinstating it afterwards. As for the details, the cost and so on, that's all included in what I'd be confirming for you, it's, it's very reasonable, I promise you that. So if you'd just, um, give me your yes, I can close the file, and then you needn't think about it again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm. Well, um... right, I see. Sorry, I'm just thinking, give me a second. Uh, it's just that you said the cost is included in what I'd be confirming, but you haven't told me what the cost is, and that does seem a bit backwards, doesn't it? I'm sorry, I don't mean to be rude, you've been very patient. But I really don't think I can say yes to something when I don't know the price, or even which car it's for. I'd much sooner it came in writing, and if it lapses, well, I suppose it lapses. So I'm going to say no thank you for now, and I'll wait for the letter. Thank you for ringing, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Now, wait, hold on a moment, please, before you put the phone down, because I don't think that's quite the right decision, and I'd be doing you a disservice if I let you make it without saying so. You've asked sensible questions all the way through, and I've welcomed every one of them, truly, and I'd say it's the price that's put you off, which, uh, is entirely understandable, but the price is very small, I mean genuinely small, set against what the cover protects, and once it lapses, well, it isn't a simple matter to put it back, you'd likely be starting again from the beginning, with less generous terms, if you could get them at all. And a letter, I'm afraid, would only reach you after the point where it matters, so that route really isn't open to you. I'd much rather you didn't lose the cover over what is, I think, a small hesitation, so if you could just give me your yes now, I can hold everything exactly as it is, and then, um, nobody needs to worry about any of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, hold on, did you say the cover is, what was it, the, the cuff? No, I'm sorry, I think I've got that wrong. Starting again from the beginning, you said, with less generous terms? Oh dear. But, um, I'm not sure I want to be starting anything today, you see, I only really wanted to be sent a letter. And you've said twice now that I'd lose it, but you still haven't told me the price, even though I asked. I'm sorry, I think I'll stick with what I said. If it's real, it'll keep until the post comes. Thank you ever so much for your time, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Right, so, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with the card-services team at [COMPANY_A], and, um, I'm calling regarding a transaction that was flagged on your card ending, well, I won't go into the account particulars on this line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Um, yes, this is, yeah. Hang on, I've got a pan on. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? And what was that about my card, you said something about a flag, and then you said you wouldn't go into the particulars, so, what's actually happened?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, [PERSON_1], go ahead, no, I'll -- right, so, [COMPANY_A], card services, and what's occurred is an anomaly was flagged by our transaction-monitoring layer, a velocity pattern that, uh, deviated from your baseline, and I'd rather not elaborate on an inbound-initiated line, which, well, this technically is, from a compliance standpoint. So what I'd ask is that you take the pan off the heat, hang up, and ring the number printed on the back of your card, and I'll give you a reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], to quote so they can route you to the right team.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Um, sorry, hang on, let me just turn this down. Right. So you want me to hang up and ring the number on the back of my card? And quote that reference, the, what was it, ACCOUNT_REF? Sorry, I didn't catch where that came from, did you say it or did I miss it? I mean, that sounds sensible, doesn't it? Better than giving you anything over the phone. But you still haven't really said what the transaction was. Is my money all right? Should I be worried?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right, it is sensible, and, uh, you didn't miss it, I only named the reference rather than reading it out, so let me do that properly: it's [ACCOUNT_REF], and I'll say it once more at the end.
