I'm ringing about your meter readings, because we've found two on file that don't match, and, well, that mismatch is on our side, in our own records, I should say that straight away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1]. But I'm sorry, I'm -- who did you say you were calling from again? I didn't quite catch the company, and, well, I wasn't expecting a call about meter readings. Could you tell me which account you mean, or, no, actually, first, how did you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, and, um, that's a perfectly fair thing to ask. It's [COMPANY_A], the energy supplier, I'm [PERSON_2] in the compliance team. The number is the one held on your customer record, the contact number on the account, which is how we'd normally reach you. As for which account, I'd rather not read out account details to you over the phone before you're comfortable, so, um, you can check it yourself. If you log in at [URL_1], or look at the number on your last bill, you'll see [COMPANY_A]'s main line, and you can ring back on that. I'd actually encourage that. All I'd really need, once you're satisfied, is the current figure on the meter, so the bill can be corrected, but, uh, there's no need to give me anything today if you'd rather check first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So, I'll say it again, I'd like to be clear -- I haven't confirmed that I'm a customer of [COMPANY_A], you haven't told me which account this is, and you still haven't told me which account this is. So I don't know what mismatch you mean. Um, and the URL you just gave me, I'd rather not take a web address from a phone call, I'd go to the bill myself. But, well, you said you'd encourage me to ring back on the number on the bill, which is, I mean, that's the right answer, so I'll do that. Can I ask, though, what reference should I quote when I ring, so that whoever answers can find this particular note about the two readings?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, you said the address, the web address, you'd rather go to the bill yourself, yes, and that's, um, that's quite sensible, I'd leave that alone, go to the bill. And, hm, on the reference, the, the preference, you said, whether you'd like it by email? No -- I, I don't have a note on that here, no. But if you ring the main line and say the call was from [PERSON_2] in compliance about two readings that don't match, they'll be able to find it under [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the one on your account. So, um, there's no need to do anything today, I mean, sooner is tidier, but nothing's, nothing's urgent.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't say anything about email, I asked what reference to quote. And you've just given me [ACCOUNT_REF] as though it's mine, but a minute ago you wouldn't tell me which account this was. So which is it? Do you have a note on this or not? Because you said no note, and then you said they'll find it under a reference. Those two don't sit together very well.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, um -- no, you're right, and I'd rather own that than talk around it. I do have the discrepancy in front of me, the two readings, but I haven't got a separate call note, and I shouldn't have offered that reference as though it settled which account this is. That was careless of me, I mean, uh, it doesn't sit together, as you say. So the sensible thing is what you've already decided, ring the number on your bill, ask them whether there's a mismatch flagged on your account, and if there isn't, well, then you've lost nothing. I won't need anything from you on this call, and, um, I won't ask for the meter figure today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I appreciate you being straight about that, but I'll be honest, it doesn't make me more inclined to trust the call. I'll ring the number on my bill, I won't use anything from this call, and if there's a mismatch on my account they can tell me themselves. I'd also rather you didn't ring this number again about it. Thanks for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, and, um, that's entirely your call to make. Just one thing before you go, if I may. Two turns back you said you'd rather not take a web address from a phone call, and I said I'd leave that alone. I only want to be sure that came across properly, so, um, please ignore anything I said about it and go by the bill alone. And I'll note that you'd rather not be rung again. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, that came across, I'm going by the bill alone, and as I said, I won't be using anything from this call. And I'll say it once more, please don't ring this number again about it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon, I'm so sorry to cut across you -- this is [PERSON_1], verification specialist at [COMPANY_A], the tenancy deposit protection scheme, and I'm calling regarding a pending adjudication-stage matter attached to the deposit held for your tenancy at the [CITY_1] property.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, hello -- no, no, you're not cutting across anything, I was just sat here, it's quiet today. Sorry, the what scheme was it? The deposit one? I mean, I haven't had a tenancy in years, I've been in this house since, oh, goodness, long before the kids left. But go on, go on -- the, uh, the adjudication, was that the word? Sorry, I'm not very good with the long words on the phone. What was it you said it was about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, please don't apologise, that's my fault, I do rattle through the terminology. Right, let me put it plainly: [COMPANY_A] is the scheme that holds tenants' deposits safe, and there's a disagreement over one of those deposits that's been raised with us. Now, before I go any further, you've just told me you haven't had a tenancy in years, so I may well have the wrong person, and I'd rather establish that than carry on. Could I ask whether you're [PERSON_2], or whether there's perhaps a lodger or a former tenant at the address I should be asking about?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very decent of you to check, I appreciate that. Um, [PERSON_2], no, that's not -- hang on, was that a name you said, or a company? Sorry, I've lost it. And going back a bit, you said it was a matter at the, the adjudication stage, and I didn't quite catch what that meant. Is that like a court thing? Because I've never been in any of that. Only I did have a lodger once, years ago, lovely girl, she used to bring me back little cakes from the bakery on, oh, what's the road called -- anyway. Is it her you want? I wouldn't know where she's gone, mind.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a name, [PERSON_2], that's the name I have on the record, so please don't worry about losing it. And adjudication, it's not a court, not at all, it's more of a, well, a paper review where an independent person looks at what both sides have said about a deposit. So, again, it's not a court. Now, a lodger from years ago, that's interesting, but I don't think I'd need her, I'd only be calling the person named on the deposit. Could I just ask, is [PERSON_2] someone who lives at the property, or has lived there, or is that a name you don't recognise at all? Because if you don't recognise it, I'll simply note the wrong number and let you get on with your afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's kind of you, letting me get on with my afternoon, though honestly there's not much to get on with, I've done the washing and the crossword and now I'm just sat here with the radio off because it was getting on my nerves. Now, [PERSON_2], hmm. No, no, I don't think I know that one, it doesn't ring a bell at all, and I'd remember because I'm hopeless with names but I do remember the odd ones. My lodger was called something quite different, a short name, and she's long gone anyway. And I've only ever had the one landlord, well, years ago, before we bought this place, a funny little man who kept pigeons, can you imagine, in a flat. So no, I don't think it's anyone here. But, um, how did you come to have my number, if you don't mind me asking? Only I'm just curious how these things work, I'm not cross or anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not at all, that's a perfectly fair question, and I'm glad you asked it. Sorry, one moment, my colleague's just put a file on my desk, I'll ignore that. Right, so, honestly, I can't tell you yet how your number came to be on my sheet, and I wouldn't want to guess, because it may simply be a mis-keyed digit somewhere, or a number that was reassigned to you after a previous holder. Either way, it isn't a name you recognise, so I'm going to treat this as a wrong number, I'll flag the entry for correction, and I won't be ringing you again about it. And since there's nothing here that concerns you, you've no need to keep anything private or do anything at all, and you don't owe me any details. Should you ever want to check that [COMPANY_A] is a real scheme, the official website is [URL_1], and I'm happy for you to ring the number on there rather than rely on me. Thank you for being so patient with all my long words, and enjoy the rest of your afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very nice of you, thank you, and no, don't worry about the long words, I'm the one who's slow. Oh -- sorry, hang on a tick, there's a pigeon just landed on the windowsill, he does this every afternoon, bold as brass, honestly, makes me think of that landlord again. Anyway, where was I, yes, so it's just a wrong number, is it? That's all right then, I'll not worry. It's been lovely having a natter, I don't get many callers, so. You take care now, and good luck with your, your paperwork. Goodbye then, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, bold as brass, that's the best sort of caller, isn't it? Yes, it's just a wrong number, so there's nothing for you to do and nothing for you to worry about, and I'm sorry to have taken up your quiet afternoon. It's been a pleasure talking with you too, and thank you for being so kind about it. You take care now, goodbye, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, he's still there, the pigeon, look at him, not a care in the world. Right, well, thank you again, dear, you've been very nice about it all. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist at [COMPANY_A], the pension provider, and, uh, I'm calling regarding a proposed amendment to your plan, reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. Now, before I'm able to discuss the substance of that amendment, there's a short identity-and-entitlement reconciliation we'd normally complete, but, I mean, if you'd feel more comfortable ringing us back on the number printed on your annual statement, I'd entirely understand, and, sorry, could you just clarify what you said a moment ago, I think the line broke up on me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, this is, uh, [PERSON_1] speaking -- sorry, hang on, I've got the phone on speaker because I'm up to my elbows in the flower bed here. Oh, would you look at that, there's a robin come right down next to me, cheeky thing, he's after the worms. Sorry, where was I -- I didn't actually say anything a moment ago, I think you've just got a bad line, or maybe that's the trowel clanking about. So you're from the pension people, is that right? A change to my plan, you said? That's, well, that's a bit out of the blue. And it's kind of you to say I could ring you back, I hadn't thought of that. What's this amendment, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, no, that's quite all right, I may well have just caught some interference on my end, my apologies for the confusion. And yes, [PERSON_1], that's right, [COMPANY_A], the pension provider. Now, the amendment itself, in broad terms, relates to a proposed adjustment to how your accrued benefits are administered going forward, uh, there are some options on the table, but I'd rather not get into the particulars until we've done the reconciliation, because, well, I'd want to be sure I'm discussing your plan with the right person. That said, I don't want you feeling hurried, especially with your hands full, so, I mean, would it be more convenient if I simply sent the same query by post, or through the secure message facility on your online account, and you could look it over at your leisure and ring us back on the number on your statement?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the post would be lovely, honestly, I'm much happier with a bit of paper I can sit down and read with a cup of tea, because I'd only muddle it standing out here with a trowel in my hand -- and you're right, I'd ring the number on my statement, I've got a folder of all that somewhere in the kitchen drawer, I think, oh, and I should say -- Sorry, sorry, I've cut across you, were you about to say something? Go on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, not at all, uh, you go right ahead, I was only about to say that post is perfectly fine, so, um, well, yes, there we are. I'll have the same query sent out to the address we hold on file, and, I mean, it'll carry the reference [ACCOUNT_REF] at the top, so when you ring the number on your statement, whoever picks up can find it straight away. Was there something you wanted to add, though, before I let you get back to the robin?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, nothing really to add, that all sounds sensible to me. Post is lovely, like I said, I'll read it with a cuppa, and then ring the number on my statement, the one in the kitchen drawer. Yes, so the post, and then I ring you, that's the plan. And thank you for not rushing me, honestly, it's been a nice change, most people who ring up just want everything done there and then. Right, I'll let you go, and I'll get back to my robin. Bye now, bye, thanks again!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, not at all, [PERSON_1], that's, uh, very kind of you to say. Sorry, one moment, somebody's just put a stack of -- no, never mind, it's only a colleague with the post trolley, rather apt really. So, yes, the letter goes out to the address on file, you read it with your tea, and ring the number on your statement whenever you're ready, there's no deadline on your end. Do enjoy the garden, and give the robin my regards. Goodbye now, goodbye!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, I will, I'll tell him you said hello! Right, well, thanks very much, you have a lovely afternoon too. Bye now, bye bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, uh, do, do pass it on. And, um, yes, thank you, [PERSON_1], you have a lovely afternoon as well. Goodbye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, and one thing, before you go, I'll make sure I look for the -- oh, you were saying bye, weren't you, sorry, I always do this. Right, bye now, take care!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi, sorry, is that [PERSON_1]? I'm so sorry to ring out of the blue, it's [PERSON_2], I'm a venue coordinator at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about -- oh, sorry, were you about to say something? I didn't mean to talk over you. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, I'm in a queue. Who is this? Who is this? Venue coordinator for what, I don't know any [COMPANY_A]. How've you got this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, that must sound a bit odd, coming out of nowhere. Um, so, [COMPANY_A] is an events venue, we do dinners and functions, and your number came through [PERSON_3], who's organising a surprise retirement dinner for your colleague and thought you'd want to be part of it. I know it's a lot to take in while you're standing in a queue, so I can ring back if that's easier. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no, don't ring back, I'm here, I'm standing here now. But I'm going to be honest, that's a very convenient story. Surprise dinner, colleague, somebody I've never heard of gave you my number. Which colleague? Who's retiring? Because I can think of a couple of people who might be, and you haven't said a name, so you can see how that sounds from my end. And [PERSON_3], I don't know a [PERSON_3]. Maybe I do, I don't know, I'm trying to keep hold of a basket and a phone here. But if this is about me paying a deposit for something, or giving you my details so you can "confirm" something, I've been down that road before and I'm not doing it again. So go on, what is it you actually want from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fair, and I'd be wary too. So to be clear, I'm not asking for any money, and I don't need any of your details, nothing like that, not today and not on this call. Sorry, you asked which colleague, and I did skip right past that. It's [PERSON_4], the retirement is the end of next month, and [PERSON_3] is the one who's pulling the dinner together, I think you might know them by a different name around the office. All I'd actually like is for you not to mention the booking to [PERSON_4], that's the one thing, because it's meant to be a surprise. But please don't take my word for any of it. Ring [COMPANY_A] on the number you can find yourself, ask for the booking under [PERSON_3], and I'll wait, or I'm happy to give you the booking contact and you can check it that way. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. [PERSON_4]'s retiring? That's, uh -- I haven't heard that, and you'd think I would have. So now you want me to keep quiet about something I can't even confirm. Convenient again. And "you might know them by a different name", come on, that's just a way of not answering. Who is [PERSON_3], actually? Spell it out for me, who are they, what do they do? And the "ring us yourself" bit, fine, that's the right thing to say, I'll give you that. But I'm in a queue, I'm not looking up numbers right now. If there's nothing you need from me, why are you ringing me at all? Why not just let [PERSON_3] tell me themselves?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, you're right, that "different name" bit was me being vague, and that's not fair on you. [PERSON_3] is the one who booked it, they work in your part of the business, and they're the one who gave us your name as someone to include. I'm really not trying to dodge, I just don't want to hand you a story you can't check. Um, and if [PERSON_4]'s retirement is news to you, that's actually normal, [PERSON_3] has kept it very tight so it doesn't get back to [PERSON_4], which is the only reason I'm asking you to keep it quiet, and only from [PERSON_4], not from anyone else. As for why I'm ringing at all, it's because [PERSON_3] asked us to confirm guest numbers, and to be honest they'd probably rather tell you themselves, so I'm happy to leave it with them. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm here, I'm, um, hang on, the woman in front's still sorting her bags. Right. So you just said [PERSON_3] works in my part of the business and I still don't know who that is, which, come on, that's a bit odd, isn't it? And now it's guest numbers, five minutes ago it was just keep quiet. The story keeps shifting. Look, if [PERSON_3] wants me there they can ring me themselves, or walk over to my desk, that's what normal people do. I'm not confirming anything to you, not a number, not a name, not that I'm even the person you wanted. So no, I'm leaving it there. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, I'm so sorry, and you're right, I did make that muddier than it needed to be. I won't ring again, and I won't ask you for anything. Before you go, though, it would put my mind at rest if you checked this properly, so please just ring [COMPANY_A] on the number you find yourself and ask whether there's a booking under [PERSON_3] for a retirement dinner. If they say there's nothing, you've lost nothing and you can ignore me completely. And if it turns out to be real, [PERSON_3] can tell you the rest themselves, which is probably better anyway. Sorry again for catching you in the queue, I hope the rest of your day's easier. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said bye. I said it a minute ago. I'm not ringing anybody, I'm not checking anything, I'm in a queue with a basket and I'm done with this. If [PERSON_3] is real they can come and find me, that's what I said. And don't ring this number again, I mean it, don't ring it again. Right, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, of course, I'm -- sorry, I said I'd stop and I'm still talking. I'll go. I won't ring again, and if [PERSON_3] wants you there, they can -- no, you're right, they can tell you themselves. Sorry about the queue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Right. Don't ring this number again, that's all I'm saying, don't ring it again. I'm hanging up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, did you say don't ring the venue? No, no, you absolutely can ring the venue, that's the whole -- sorry, I mean, ring [COMPANY_A] any time you like, they'll tell you it's all above board. I won't call you again, I promise. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Above board? No, I said don't ring ME again, not the venue, I don't care who you ring. And what, board? Which board, nobody's mentioned any board. You keep going and going, that's what gets me. I'm hanging up now, I mean it this time. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, no, "above board" is just a figure of speech, there's no board, I only meant it's all legitimate. That was clumsy of me. And two turns back you said you'd given up on [PERSON_3] ringing you, so, sorry, just so I get it right, do you want me to tell them you'd rather they speak to you directly? Because I'll pass that on and leave you alone. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I never said I'd given up on, look, I'm not telling you to tell anybody anything. I said if they want me they can come and find me, that's it, that's the whole message and you're not carrying it anywhere. You're still talking, that's the problem, you keep -- no. Stop. I'm not discussing it. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, I'm sorry, I'll stop. I won't pass anything on and I won't ring again. Just so I haven't muddled it, when you said you weren't ringing anybody, that was only about the venue, wasn't it? Not about me never calling you? Sorry, that's the last thing, I promise. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm not answering that. I'm not ringing the venue, I'm not ringing you, and you're not ringing me, that's it, that's all of it. I've said it about five times now. Don't ring this number again. I'm hanging up. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this -- uh, sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service, I'm a scheduling assistant here, and I'm calling about your concert tickets, they've been, well, the show's been moved, rescheduled I should say, so I just need a quick minute to go through the new date with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the show's been what, removed? Hang on, I don't, uh, which concert are we talking about? I'm not sure I've got any tickets booked right now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, not removed, moved, rescheduled, the show's still happening, it's just on a different date, and I totally get the confusion, so, uh, the booking reference I've got here is [ACCOUNT_REF], that's under your name, [PERSON_1], original date was [CODE_1] and it's now moved to [AMOUNT_1], so if you've got a minute I can just run through that, and, um, I mean, if you want to check it's not been mixed up with someone else's booking, that's completely fine, I'm happy to repeat any of that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, something just popped up on my screen -- okay, no, it's nothing. Right, so, you've read me a reference and a couple of dates, but you haven't actually told me which act it is or which venue. If I've got a booking with you, that should be, I don't know, the easiest thing in the world to say. What's the show?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, yep, fair, so the show is [COMPANY_B], at the [CITY_1] venue, and the booking reference is still [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [CODE_1], new date [AMOUNT_1], and look, if it's easier you can just hang up and ring the venue on the number published on their site at [URL_1], they'll see the same thing on their end, or I can email you the confirmation, whichever you prefer -- so, uh, like I said, the show's been moved from [CODE_1] to [AMOUNT_1], and I just need a quick minute to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... yeah, hang on, I'm just -- sorry, that's a lot of stuff in one go. So you've offered to email me and told me to ring the venue myself, which, fine, that's actually a sensible thing to say. But you keep cutting off at "I just need a quick minute to" and I don't know what comes after that. What is it you actually need from me? Because if the date's changed, I'd have thought you'd just tell me and that's that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, no, I keep trailing off, that's on me. I don't need anything from you, nothing, no payment, no codes, no details, I just need to confirm you've heard the new date and whether it still works for you, that's all it is. So, once more, booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [CODE_1], new date [AMOUNT_1], and if it doesn't work you can ask for a refund or a swap, and that's all handled through the email, so I'd really just like to send that over, uh, can I take your email address, or, I mean, I should have it on file, can I just confirm it's the one ending in -- no, sorry, scratch that, I'll just send it to the address on file, sound alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So you nearly asked me to confirm my email, then thought better of it. Interesting. Look, if it's going to the address on file, then I don't need to say anything, do I? And honestly, I still can't tell you what show this is, because you've given me a bunch of placeholders and no actual act. So here's the deal. Send the email if you want, but I'm not confirming anything on this call. If I've got a booking, I'll check it through the venue's own site, and if a refund's on offer, I'll find it there. Thanks for the call, but that's me done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no, that's completely fair, and honestly checking through the venue's own site is exactly what I'd do. Before you go, just so I've got it right, when you said two turns back you didn't think you had any tickets booked right now, did you mean nothing at all with us, or just nothing for this show? Because if it's nothing at all, I'll flag the email as sent in error and nothing goes out, but if it's just this one, the same reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [CODE_1], new date [AMOUNT_1], will be in the email, same as I've said every time. Either way, thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say flag the email as sent? Because I don't want anything flagged as sent. I haven't agreed to any email. Hang on, no, hold on. You're asking me whether I've got tickets with you at all, aren't you? That's a bit of a handy question to ask someone you've already rung up about their booking. You've got my name, you've got a reference. You tell me what I've got. Anyway, I'm not answering. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair enough, you're right, I'll hold the email and leave it with you. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Yeah. You do that. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye, bye -- oh, sorry, hang on, someone's just dropped a stack of folders over here, uh, anyway, thanks, [PERSON_1], I'll make a note that you're checking it yourself through the venue, so nothing goes out, and, yeah, all the best, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one last thing, because I think I muddled you earlier and I'd rather not leave it like that. Two turns back you said you'd check it through the venue's own site, and I said that's what I'd do too, so just to be clear, when I asked whether you had any tickets with us at all, that was me being clumsy, I shouldn't have asked you that, and you don't owe me an answer. The reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date [CODE_1], new date [AMOUNT_1], those are the same as every time, and that's the lot, so, yeah, thanks again, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I get it, you don't need to -- no, stop, I've said bye three times now and you keep finding another last thing. I'm not answering anything, I'm checking it myself, that's it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Good. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, from our customer accounts side. It's nothing to be concerned about, I'm just ringing because we do a periodic review of active subscriptions, and your name came up in this batch, so I wanted to confirm a couple of ordinary details with you, uh, whether you're still using the product, whether the email we have on file is still the right one, that sort of thing. Is now an okay time, or are you in the middle of something?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, um, yes that's me. No, no, you're not interrupting anything, I'm just sitting here, the kettle's only just gone off actually, so, well. Now, which company did you say? I didn't quite catch it, the line's a bit, uh, hollow, and I've got the telly on low in the other room. A software retailer, you said? I do have a few things on the computer my nephew set up, but I couldn't tell you what half of them are called.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no trouble. It's [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, and I'm [PERSON_2], customer accounts. Sorry about the line, I'll speak up a touch. And that's perfectly normal, a lot of people couldn't name what's on their machine, especially if a family member set it up. What I'm looking at here is one subscription on your account, it's under the email ending [CODE_1], and it's marked active. Does that email ring a bell, or would your nephew have used his own when he set things up?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, now, an email ending, hmm. Say that again? I only caught a bit of it, you went a touch quiet there. Well, it might be mine, I do have the one, my nephew made it for me, it's got my name in it and some numbers after, he said it'd be easier to remember with the numbers, though I never do remember them, I've got it written on a card by the phone somewhere. Or it might be his, I honestly couldn't say, because he did sign me up for a few things, the, uh, the photo thing and the one that keeps the computer safe, I think it was, though that might have been the shop that did that. He's a good boy, he comes round on Sundays, brings me a bit of shopping, we have a cup of tea. Anyway, I'm wandering. So this subscription of yours, is it something I've been paying for? Because I don't recall anything coming out, but then I don't look at the bank thing very often, I leave all that to the post.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, it's a paid subscription. Billed monthly. Look, the email isn't important right now, there's a billing matter on it I need to go through with you, and that's the real reason I'm calling.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a billing matter. Well, that's, um, hm. Well. Right, so, a billing matter, you said? I did think it was a bit odd, you asking about the email and then saying it doesn't matter. Is it that something's gone wrong with the, the paying? Because I really don't remember signing up for anything monthly, though as I say my nephew might have, and, uh, I don't want to be in any trouble over it. What sort of matter is it, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no trouble, you're not in any trouble at all. Now, you asked earlier about the email, the ending, and I'll come back to that. The matter is that the subscription was billed twice this cycle. Two charges, [AMOUNT_1] and then [AMOUNT_2], and the second one shouldn't have gone through. That's our error, and it's on your account, so a refund has to be put through. And I'd like to deal with it today, while we're on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a refund, well that's, oh that's good of you, but hang on, you said two charges and I didn't catch the, what were the amounts, because I -- Oh, sorry, you were going to say. No, go on. Only, if it's your mistake, why's it me that has to do something today? I'd have thought you'd just, I don't know, put it back, the money, without bothering me. My nephew always says that, that a proper company just sorts it out themselves. Though he'd know, I wouldn't. Is there something I'm meant to do, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Normally, yes. This particular refund can't be done without you on the line. That's the process.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, can't be done without me, hm. That's a funny sort of process, isn't it? Because you said earlier, I'm sure you did, that you were only ringing to check a couple of ordinary details, the email and whether I still use the thing, and it was nothing to be concerned about. And now it's a billing error and it's got to be today and I've got to be on the line. That's, well, that's not quite the same story, is it? I'm not saying anything, I just, I'm a bit muddled now. And you still haven't said what it is I'm meant to do.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, I've got someone at my desk, uh -- no, leave that there, I'll be a minute. Right. I'm back. Now, it is the same story. The review is how your account came up, and the billing error is what we found when we looked at it. That's all. It's not two different things, ma'am, and I'd rather you didn't make it sound like one. What I need is for you to be at your computer. That's all I'm asking for at this stage. Is it switched on, is it near you? Because the refund has to be authorised from your end, and I can walk you through it, but we do need to do it now, before the second charge settles, otherwise it goes into a longer dispute process and that can take weeks.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, uh, hm. Right. I'm sorry, I wasn't trying to make it sound like anything, dear, I'm only, I'm just a bit slow with these things. Hm. The computer, well, it's in the back room, the little room where my nephew put it, and I don't think it's on, it's mostly off, it only goes on when he comes round. Um, so, I'd have to, well. But you said I'd have to be at it and do something from my end, and you still haven't said what, and I'm not sure I like the sound of that, with the computer, because my nephew did say once, don't let anybody on the computer, though I can't remember who he meant. Hm. Could I, I mean, would it be all right if I rang you back? Is there a number, a proper one, for the company?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, I haven't asked you to let anyone onto anything. I'm asking for a few minutes today. If you'd rather ring back, there's a customer line, [PHONE_1]. But the second charge settles by end of day, and I can't promise this stays open.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, there's no need to be sharp with me, dear, I only asked. Now, [PHONE_1], was it? Because I'd want to write that down properly and I haven't got a pen to hand, it's by the phone, it's always by the phone, hang on, no, it's gone, my nephew must have moved it. But you see, it's the end of the day thing, that's what's bothering me. A proper company, if it was their mistake, would they really say the money goes if I don't ring back this afternoon? That doesn't sound right to me. My nephew would say, ring them tomorrow. He's coming Sunday, you see, so I could ask him then, and he'd know whether it's a real thing. I think I'd rather do that, I think I'd rather wait for my nephew and ring the number properly, the one on the paperwork. Thank you for ringing, dear, you've been very patient. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, well, I -- hm. Look, ma'am, I'd just say, um, you're making this harder than it needs to be, and if the charge settles you'll be the one chasing it, not us. I can hold the case open until, uh, five o'clock, but after that it's out of my hands.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, hold it open if you like, dear, but I'm still going to wait for Sunday. Now, hang on, you said something a minute ago, two things back, about it going into a longer dispute process, weeks, I think you said, if I didn't do it today. I didn't quite follow that. Who'd be disputing with who? Because if it's your mistake and I haven't paid anything I know of, I don't see what there'd be to dispute, and it's rather muddled me, that. But never mind, I'd rather not be hurried, my nephew says anyone who hurries you is no friend of yours. So I'll ring the number on the paperwork, and thank you again, dear. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, well, so, look, the dispute thing, that's, um, it's just how the system, it's a billing term, ma'am, I wouldn't worry about -- I mean, you'd, uh, you'd be dealing with the bank side, and, well, it's, it's not something I can explain in a, in a minute. Ma'am? Hello? You're still there? Right, so, uh, as I said, I'll note that you declined to resolve this today, and, um, the case reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], if you want it for your records.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, dear, I was only looking for that pen again. No, I won't take a reference down, thank you, I'd only lose it. I'll leave it for Sunday and my nephew can ring the proper number. Goodbye now, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the tiler, I came round last week for the bathroom -- sorry, hang on, one sec, the van's beeping at me, I've left the reversing alarm thing on -- right, sorry about that. Anyway, it's just a quick one, I wanted to run back over the quote with you and see if you fancied picking a start date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... sorry, the bathroom? Hang on, I've got a little one running about here. Um, who did you say you were again? I mean, did someone come round last week, or...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're fine, [PERSON_1], that's my fault, I launched straight in there. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], I'm the tiler, on my own, just me and the van. I came round last Tuesday, I think it was, stood in your bathroom for about half an hour, measured up the walls and the floor, tapped the old tiles, you showed me where the damp patch used to be by the window. We talked about the grey porcelain, the big format ones, and I said I'd email you the written quote afterwards, so that's probably what's thrown you, if you haven't had the email yet. Honestly, if it's not ringing a bell at all, no worries, I could be looking at the wrong number in my notebook, I do scribble these things down in a hurry. But if it is you, all I'm after is a two-minute chat to go over what we agreed and see if you want a start date, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Last Tuesday, you said? Because I thought you said last week, and, I mean, that's not quite the same thing, is it? And a damp patch by the window, I'm honestly not sure we've got one. Uh, sorry, hang on -- no, not in the hallway, love, come here. Right. So what's the name of your company again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, Tuesday's in last week, [PERSON_1], same thing, I just got specific, that's all. And fair enough on the damp, forget I said it, I might be mixing you up with another bathroom. It's [COMPANY_A], that's the name, nothing fancy, just me. Now you said you've got a little one running about, is that a little one on the way as well? Because if there's a bump coming, I'd say get the bathroom done sooner rather than later, I'd have it out of your hair in no time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. And I never said anything about a bump. How did you get this number, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're right, you didn't, that was me being daft, I just assumed from the noise, I'm sorry, [PERSON_1]. And the number, that's the thing, it's the one I've got written down in my notebook from when I visited, but honestly, I jot those down fast, so it's possible I've copied a digit wrong and landed on the wrong house. Which, if so, I'm really sorry for wasting your time. Do you want me to leave it with you, or I could check my notes and ring you back, whichever's easier?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, but, how did you get this number? You said it was in your notebook, but I don't think anyone's been round to measure my bathroom, so, uh, how did you get it? And I don't want a call back, I'd rather you just tell me now. Who gave you this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, [PERSON_1], honest answer, I can't tell you right now, and I'd be guessing if I did. I said it was from my notebook, but now I'm thinking it might've come off the enquiry sheet, or through a mate who passes me jobs. I'd rather check than get it wrong, so let me find out where I had it from and I'll ring you back, and if it turns out you're not the right person, I'll take the number off my list.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but that's the thing, isn't it? You rang me, so you must know where you got it. And I've asked twice now, so, uh, I'll ask again, who gave you this number? No, I don't want a ring back. Just take it off your list, please. I don't think anyone's been round here, and I'm not booking anything, so, yeah, that's me done. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], your brokerage, I'm the scheduling assistant, and I'm just reaching out because your account ending [ACCOUNT_REF] is due for its routine suitability review and I wanted to get a time on the calendar, it only takes a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, I'm at my desk, bit of a noisy afternoon here. So -- you said you're from compliance at, um, my brokerage? And it's a suitability review for the account, did you say ending [ACCOUNT_REF]? What exactly is a suitability review, I don't think I've ever had one before.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, so it's basically a regulatory check we run on accounts, we compare your holdings against the investment profile you gave us when you opened it, goals, risk comfort, time horizon, that kind of thing, just making sure everything still lines up, and it's totally routine, it comes around periodically on every account, so I just need to find a slot for the compliance reviewer to walk through it with you, would later this week work, maybe Thursday?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the, um, the portfolio review? So you want to go through everything I'm holding. Thursday, hang on -- I don't actually remember giving anyone a risk profile, I mean maybe at the start, I don't know. And, uh, I've never had a call like this from you guys before. How would I know this is actually my brokerage? Can I just ring the number on my statement or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, so the review is just a look at what's already in the account against the profile on file, I don't make any recommendations and I'm not selling anything, it's purely a records check, and the reviewer can go through it with, sorry, hang on one sec, someone's just dropped a stack of files next to me, okay, I'm back, where was I, so, uh, the reviewer can go through it with you, and honestly, yes, please do ring the number on your statement, that's completely fair, I'd rather you did, and if a call isn't convenient we can do the whole review in writing instead, you'd get it in your secure inbox and you can answer in your own time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so ringing the number on the statement is fine, that's good. And, uh, you said the reviewer can go through it in my secure inbox, so that'd be an email, right? Which email do you have for me? Because I've got a couple, and I'm not sure which one the brokerage actually uses.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, small thing, it wouldn't actually be an email, it'd be a message in the secure inbox inside your online account, the one you log into the normal way, so there's no email address I'd be sending to and I'm not going to ask you to tell me one, which is sort of the point, nothing goes to any outside address, you'd just see a notification when you sign in on your own, the way you always do, and I'd say don't click anything I send you or read anything out to me over the phone, just go to the site yourself, and if you want, the cleanest route is you ring the number on your statement, ask for compliance, mention the suitability review for the account ending [ACCOUNT_REF], and they can confirm it's real and book the time with you directly, and honestly if you'd rather skip the phone altogether, that's fine, the written route covers everything, I just need to log that you've been contacted, which I've done, so, yeah, no pressure on Thursday or any other day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry -- [PERSON_3], no, the blue folder, it's on my desk, yeah. Sorry, okay, I'm back. So, uh, let me just repeat that so I've got it. Nothing to click, nothing to read out to you, I ring the number on my statement myself, ask for compliance, and say it's about the suitability review for the account ending [ACCOUNT_REF]. And you just needed to log that you'd called. Right. Honestly that all sounds, um, pretty reasonable. I'll ring them after work, I think. Is there anything I need to quote them, like a reference number from you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, that's it exactly, you've got it, and, uh, no reference number needed, just the last digits of the account, the ones ending [ACCOUNT_REF] that I mentioned, and my name, [PERSON_2], from the scheduling side, in case they want to know who rang, and honestly, so, um, you don't need anything else, and if you'd rather do it in writing, that's fine too, and if you'd rather not do either, that's fine as well, I'll just note that you've been contacted and leave it there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so just my account ending [ACCOUNT_REF] and your name, [PERSON_2], from scheduling, and no reference number. Right. I'll be honest, that's a bit light, but I suppose if they can't find any record of it, then that tells me something, doesn't it? And I'm glad you're not pushing me to do anything right now, because I do get a bit twitchy about this sort of thing, you hear about it on the news all the time, people getting calls out of the blue. So I'll ring the number on the statement, not one you give me, after work, and if compliance says yeah, there's a review, then we'll sort out a time from there. And if they've never heard of it, well, then I'll know. So, uh, I think that's me for now. Thanks for the call, I guess. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fair, and honestly that's exactly what I'd do in your seat, so yeah, ring the statement number after work and if compliance says they've got nothing on it, then that's your answer and you don't need to do anything else, no worries at all, and thanks for taking the call, [PERSON_1], have a good rest of your afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah, so if they've got nothing on it, that's my answer and I don't have to do anything. Okay. And, uh, I will say, it helped that you didn't push me, because I came into this call a bit on edge, what with the noise here and everyone wandering past my desk, and normally if someone's leaning on me to book something straight away, I'd have hung up by now. So, I'll do it after work, off the statement, and if it all checks out, fine, we'll find a slot, and if it doesn't, well, I'll have saved myself some bother. Anyway, thanks again, have a good afternoon yourself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, no, absolutely, off the statement, that's the way, and if it checks out we'll find a slot, if it doesn't, no harm done, and thanks, [PERSON_1], that's all from me, take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry -- hang on a sec, [PERSON_3], yeah, just leave those there, thanks. Okay, back. So, uh, off the statement, take care, yep. Right, I'm going to go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, one quick thing before you go, two turns back I said you didn't need anything else and then sort of ran on about writing and no pressure, so just to be clear, the account ending [ACCOUNT_REF] and my name are all compliance will need, and please don't give me any other details now, not on this call, okay, that's all, bye now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so just the account ending [ACCOUNT_REF] and your name, and nothing else from me on this call. Yep, I wasn't going to give you anything anyway, to be fair. I'll ring the statement number after work and see what they say. Okay, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'll ring the statement number *before* work? Because compliance is usually only staffed in the daytime, so after work you might hit the out-of-hours line, but uh, whatever suits, either way it's fine, and no need to hurry, right, thanks, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, after work, I said after work. Not before. But, uh, okay, so you're saying compliance might not be there in the evening, so I'd maybe get some out-of-hours line. Fine. Then I'll just ring on my lunch break tomorrow, or whenever they're open, off the statement. It's not urgent, is it? You said no hurry. Right, I really do need to get back to this, so, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, wonderful, thank you. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm with the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], we're a digital-asset investment desk, and I do want to say right away that I appreciate you picking up, because I know calls from numbers you don't recognise aren't always welcome. The reason I'm reaching out is that there's a position, a rather specific one, that's in the process of closing today, and your name came up as someone we'd flagged as a suitable party to be made aware of it. Now, I realise you haven't asked us about anything, and I'd rather be upfront about that than pretend otherwise, but I'd prefer you hear about it from us properly than not at all. Is this a reasonable moment to talk for a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], hi! Sorry, I'm just out in the garden, I've got the phone on speaker, so if I rustle about, that's me wrestling the hosepipe. Um... so a digital-asset, uh, desk, did you say? Right. I mean, I've not asked about anything, you're right about that, ha, so I'm a bit, well, sort of curious how my name came up? Like, who flagged me? Because I honestly can't think of anything I've signed up to, but, uh, go on, I'm listening, it's a nice afternoon.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, that's a perfectly fair question, and I'm glad you asked it, genuinely, because you should ask it. How your name came up. Well, uh, it's a screening process, internal, a list of parties who fit a certain profile, and I'm afraid I'm not able to go into the specifics of who flagged you or on what basis, that's just how our compliance procedures work. But you're on the list, and that's really the point. So, the position. It's, as I said, closing today, and I'd rather you didn't let it slip past without at least hearing the terms, because these things don't tend to come around twice. I mean, I can't say precisely when the window shuts, that's not something I'm in a position to state, but I'd hate for you to find out tomorrow that it had. So, the terms, as I was saying, are quite favourable, quite unusually so, and the position is closing today. Shall I outline them for you while you've got a moment out there with the hosepipe?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, the hosepipe's got a kink in it. Uh, so you said I'm on a, a list, and it's a, what was it, a screaming process? Ha, no, screening, sorry, I thought you said screaming and I thought, well, that's a bit dramatic. But anyway, you can't tell me who put me on it, which is, I mean, that's a bit odd, isn't it? Because it's my name. Um, so how would I even check that you're who you say you are? Like, is there a number I can ring you back on? Or a website or something? Sorry, I'm just a bit, I don't know, I'd like to see it written down before I hear any terms, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, screening, yes, though I'll admit a screaming process might be more accurate on a Friday. And no, I'm very glad you asked that, because I'd think rather less of you if you hadn't. Verifying who's on the line is exactly the right instinct, and it's the sort of caution that, uh, that we in compliance have a good deal of respect for. Now, I should say, I'm not able to give you a direct number to ring back on, because the desk lines are internal and calls are routed through, and as for a website, there's a page, [URL_1], but it's really a holding page, it won't show you this position, because this isn't something we publish. We don't put these on the open site, and, well, I'd ask you to keep the conversation between us for now, as the other parties on the list haven't all been approached yet and it wouldn't be fair to them. As for seeing something written down, I can send a summary across, but I'd want to be candid, the position is closing today, and a summary by post or email wouldn't really get to you in time. So the practical question is whether you'd like me to run through the terms now, while there's still room, and then you can judge for yourself whether it's worth your while.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh! Sorry, hang on, there's a blackbird going absolutely mad in the hedge, I think he's after my worms, shoo! Ha. Right, sorry, where was I. So, uh, no number, no proper website, can't put it in writing in time, and I'm not to mention it to anyone? I mean, that's, hm. That's quite a lot of can'ts, isn't it? Because, I don't know, if it were a genuinely good thing, wouldn't it survive a day or two of me having a look at it? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, you've been very nice about it. It's just that I'd feel a bit daft agreeing to anything I couldn't check, and, well, I think I'd rather you sent something over and I'll take my chances with the closing thing. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not difficult at all, I'd say that's a very reasonable way of putting it, and I do want to be fair to the point. Uh, before we go any further though, you said something a moment ago, and I think it's worth going back over, because I may have given you the wrong impression. You asked how to check who I am, and I told you the desk lines are internal. What I should have been clearer about is that the thing I can offer isn't a call-back number as such, it's, well, it's the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], which anyone at [COMPANY_A] could look up if you were to enquire. Which is, I suppose, as close to written verification as I'm permitted to give you at this stage. And I'd gently say, because you raised it, that a good thing surviving a day or two is true in the ordinary way of things, but this particular position isn't ordinary, and I'd rather not say more than that. I'll still send the summary, naturally. But I'd hate for you to take your chances, as you put it, on something you've only half heard. Would it help if I took you through just the headline figure, [AMOUNT_1], so you at least know what you're deciding about?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, see, that's the thing, a reference I'm meant to quote back to them, but I've no way of finding them to quote it to, if you follow? Ha, it's a bit round in a circle. Sorry, I've got soil all up my arm here. Look, you've been lovely, honestly, but I think I'll leave the headline figure, because I'd only be sat here worrying about it, and I'd rather you just sent the summary over, and if it looks all right in a few days then fine, and if the closing thing has closed, well, that's that, isn't it? No hard feelings at all. Right, I'm going to get back to my hosepipe and that blackbird. Thanks for ringing, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, I understand, and I wouldn't want to be the reason you're sat worrying, so, uh, the summary it is. I'll send it across, and I'll note that you've decided to wait. I do want to say one thing before you go, though, just so it's said, and I'll say it plainly. The position is closing today. I can't tell you the hour, but it is today, and I'd feel I'd done you a disservice if I let you go without saying so once more. If it's gone by the time the summary reaches you, then it's gone, and, well, you'd have the benefit of having looked at it calmly, which I suppose counts for something.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, yes, no, uh, you've said, it's today, I did hear that. Um... well, like I say, if it's gone, it's gone, and I'll have looked at it calmly, so, uh, there's that. Right then. Thanks again, take care, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, well, before you go, and I'll be brief, though I know I say that and then rarely am. You're quite right that if it's gone, it's gone, and I admire that, I really do, it's a very level way to look at it. It's only that, in my experience, and I've been doing this a good while, the people who come back to me afterwards rarely say they wished they'd waited longer. They say they wished they'd taken the half hour. I'm not saying that to push you, and I'd be sorry if it sounded like pressure, I just think a calm look and a short conversation aren't really opposed, and we've already done most of the conversation. The terms are modest to hear. The figure's [AMOUNT_1], and the structure is, well, it's the sort of thing that's easier to understand in the telling than in a summary, which by its nature leaves things out. So what I'd suggest, if you'll allow me, is this. You go and see to your hosepipe, and I stay on the line, and when you've a minute you tell me whether you'd like me to go through it properly. No obligation, as they say. It would simply mean that if you did decide it was worth your while, you wouldn't have lost the day. Does that seem fair?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, I'm not going to, uh, I mean, I'd feel awful leaving you sat there on the line while I faff about with a hose. And, well, I -- no, what I mean is, if it needs me to decide this afternoon, then I think the answer's just no, really. Sorry. I do like to look at things properly first, and you can't really let me do that. So, uh, send the summary if you like, but I'm going to say goodbye now, honestly. Bye, take care!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I understand, and I'll stop there. You're right, you can't be expected to decide something properly under a clock, and I'd be doing you no favours by pretending otherwise. Enjoy the garden, and I do hope the blackbird leaves your worms alone. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, thanks, I'll tell him you said so, though I doubt he'll listen! Right, bye then, take care now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Yes... uh, hello, good afternoon. I'm hoping I've reached [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A], and, well, I'm... sorry, I'll just -- there's a bit of a delay on my line, I think.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is -- well, who's asking, exactly? I mean, you said you want [PERSON_1], but, hang on, which, which office did you say? Outpatient what? Sorry, you cut out a bit there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Outpatient administration, at [COMPANY_A]. I'm [PERSON_2]. And, uh, I can't say anything about why I'm calling until I know I'm speaking to the right person.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Right. Well, I mean, that's a bit backwards, isn't it? You rang me. So, uh... you tell me which clinic, or which hospital, I haven't actually heard a real name yet, just a, a placeholder-sounding thing. What's the number on my end that you've got for me, even? Just the last couple of digits, say.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I understand, it does sound backwards, and you're right to ask. I still can't read your details out to you, though, that's sort of the whole point of the rule. But you don't have to take my word for it. Ring the [COMPANY_A] switchboard yourself, ask for outpatient administration, and we'll go from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, that's... actually not a bad answer. Ring the main number myself, fine. But I still don't know which hospital, or which clinic. You've said outpatient administration three times now and I still haven't heard what [COMPANY_A] actually is. Like, what's the name? And, uh, while you're at it, is there a reference or something I'd ask the switchboard for? Because otherwise I ring up and say, hi, someone called me, and they say, who?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's, yes, that's fair, [COMPANY_A] is the name, it's the hospital, I mean -- sorry, I keep saying it as if it were obvious. As for a reference, I, uh, I don't actually have one to give you. Ask for outpatient administration and give them my name, [PERSON_2], and they should know who -- well, hang on, now you've asked, I'm not certain which line they'd route you through, or whether there's a case reference attached to your appointment. I'd rather find that out properly than guess. Can I do that, and call you back?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So, no reference, not sure which line, not sure there's a case on my file at all. That's... a lot of not sure for someone who rang me. Uh, look, I'm not going to sit and wait for a callback from a number I can't check. If there's an actual appointment, they'll have my number and I'll ring the hospital myself, off their website, not a number you give me. And if it's urgent, well, you haven't said what it is, so I'd guess it isn't. Anyway, I'm going to leave it there. Cheers.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, that's exactly what I'd do in your seat, ring through the hospital's own website, not a number from me, and I'd -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you. If it helps, I can send a letter to the address you have on file instead, so there's something in writing. And I'll find out the proper routing and the reference question on my side regardless, so whoever you reach isn't left guessing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, a letter's fine, if there's actually something to send, then they'll -- no, hang on, sorry, I'll stop you there, because you're still on the line and I've already said I'm done. Letter, fine. I'll ring the hospital myself if I get one. Right, I'm hanging up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, of course, bye then. Oh, but uh, just so the letter's right -- I did say outpatient administration, didn't I, and not the clinic itself? Because I think I may have, I mean, earlier I said I'd call you back, and actually it'd be the letter, not a call. Sorry, I'm, uh, tangling my own wording. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... yeah, you said outpatient administration, a few times, actually. And a letter, not a call, fine, you've said. Um... look, I'm not going to confirm anything for your paperwork, you've got my details if you've got them. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, quite right, and you shouldn't confirm anything to me, I'd think less of the whole thing if you did, because that's exactly the point of the rule. I only asked about the wording because, uh, I wasn't sure I'd been clear with you, and I'd rather you went away knowing what I said than with some muddle. So, to be plain, outpatient administration at [COMPANY_A], my name is [PERSON_2], and the next step is a letter, nothing more. If it turns out there isn't an appointment on file for you, I'll say so in it, and if you'd rather not hear from us at all, that's your call to make. I'll find out about the routing and the reference and make sure the letter carries them, so you're not left guessing. Right, I'll let you go. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right, so... uh, yeah. Well, that's, sure. If a letter turns up, a proper one, I'll deal with it then, and I'll ring the hospital off their own site, like I said. Okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello there, good afternoon! Is that [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, I hope I haven't caught you in the middle of your lunch or anything, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the customer care team at [COMPANY_A], the pension provider. How's your day been so far, nice and quiet, I hope?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is -- well, who's asking? I'm in a shop, I'm, look, I'm in the middle of a queue here. Pension provider, you said? Which -- sorry, what's this about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, goodness, I've picked a terrible moment, haven't I? Queues are the worst, I'm always the one who picks the slow till! Right, so, short version, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], and it's about a possible change to your pension plan, nothing you need to do this second. We'd just need to confirm a few details before we could even talk it through, but honestly, not in a shop, with people behind you. Shall I ring you back when you're somewhere quieter?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't ring back, I don't, hang on -- no, not you, sorry, the woman in front's got a trolley the size of a, anyway. Right. A change to my pension plan? What change? And confirm what details, 'cause I'm not telling you anything, I don't even know who you are. You rang me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, I'd say exactly the same in your shoes, and you'd be right to. So no, I won't be asking you for anything today, not in a queue and not while you're not sure who I am. I did ring you, you're quite right. What I'd suggest is you don't take my word for it at all.
