Or if you'd rather, I can put the same query in the post, or in a secure message on your online account, and you can read it at your own pace. Honestly, there's no rush on this one, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Well, that's, yeah, that's more sensible than I expected, I'll give you that. But hang on, you said earlier it was nothing I had to do this second, and now it's no rush, so which is it? And you said it was a change to my plan, but it's a query? Which one is it, a change or a query? Look, I'm not ringing anybody back today, I'll look at it when I get home, and I'll find the number myself, not off you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're right to pick me up on that, I've been waffling, sorry. It's a change, uh, a possible change to the plan, and the query's just the bit where we'd need to check a few things with you first, so, both really, I was being sloppy -- and finding the number yourself is exactly what I'd do, so yes, please, do that. Nobody's going to lose anything by waiting a week, honestly. Look, would it help if I just rang you back another time, when you're home and settled with a cuppa, and you've had a look at things first?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no ringing back, I've said. If I've got something to say to your lot I'll ring you, on a number I've found myself. Because I'll be honest with you, I got caught out once before, somebody ringing up all friendly, asking how my day was, and I'm still cross about it, so the how's your day been routine, it doesn't do you any favours. Doesn't mean you're up to anything, I don't know that, I'm just telling you how it lands. And the thing is, you've said possible change, then change, then query, then both, and you still haven't told me what the actual change is. If there's a real one, there'll be a letter, won't there? So if it's all the same to you, I'll wait for the letter, or I'll look it up myself when I'm home, and if it's genuine it'll keep. Right, I'm nearly at the till, so, yeah, I'm going to go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a whole tray of mugs behind me, that'll be the afternoon gone, ha. Right, no, you're completely right, and I'm sorry the chatty bit landed badly, that's a fair thing to say. Yes, a letter is the proper route, so I'll make a note on your file that you'd rather have it in writing, and I won't ring you again unless you ask me to. And you go ahead and find the number yourself, that's exactly the right thing. Mind how you go, [PERSON_1], and enjoy the rest of your afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, fair enough, that's, hang on, you said earlier you'd put it in a secure message on my online account, and now it's a letter. Which is it? Doesn't matter, don't answer, I'm at the till. Letter's fine, and I'll find the number myself, like I said. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that one's easy, sorry, it was the post or a secure message, whichever you'd rather, so the letter's absolutely fine, and I'll note it that way. And since you've gone and asked, can I just check I've got it right, you'd like it in writing only, nothing by phone from our end, and you'll ring us on a number you've found yourself? Not to be pestered, just so it's down properly. Go on, pay for your things, I won't keep you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Eh? Pestered? No, I never said pestered, who said I was being pestered? Look, I'm at the till, the lad's waiting. Yes, letter, writing, nothing by phone, whatever, that's what I said. I'll sort it myself at home. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you didn't say pestered, that was my word, and I'm sorry, I -- right, letter only, nothing by phone, that's all noted. Go and pay, and look, if it's easier, you could always ring us back once you're home and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ring you back? Hang on, I've just told you, twice, I'll ring you if I ring you, off a number I've found myself, and you keep coming round to it. That's the third time you've tried to get me to ring or be rung, and I don't like that, I'll be straight with you. And it's not even clear what it is you're after, you've never once said what this change is, not once, you've said possible change, change, query, both, and then you were sorry about the chatty bit, and now it's pestered, which was your word, not mine. So here's where I am. If there's a real change to my plan, it'll come in a letter or on my online account, and I'll see it, and I'll deal with it then. I'm not confirming a thing today, not my name, not anything. That's it. I'm paying for my shopping now and I'm putting the phone away. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: You're right, that's three times I've steered it back to a call, and I'm sorry, that's on me. No more of it. Letter or your online account, and you've confirmed nothing today, which is exactly as it should be. Go and pay, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well. That's, yeah, that's what I wanted to hear a few minutes ago, but fine, I'll take it now. And I'll tell you something else while I've got the lad scanning my stuff, because you did get one thing right. You were the one who rang me, and you said so, you didn't try and argue that out of it, and that's more than the last one did. Doesn't make me trust you, mind, I'm not there, I don't know you from Adam. All I know is you rang, you didn't say what it was about, and I'm not doing anything on the back of that. So if there's a letter, there's a letter. If there isn't, there isn't, and I'll not lose any sleep over it. I'm not ringing anybody back today, I'll look at my statements when I get in, and I'll find the number myself, off the paperwork, not off anything you've said. That's all I'm going to do. Right, I've got to pay, he's looking at me. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, thank you for saying that, I do appreciate it, and honestly, what you've just described is exactly what I'd want you to do. Don't trust a stranger on the phone, don't confirm anything off the back of a call you didn't expect, and go to your own paperwork for the number. If more people did that, people like me would have a much easier time of it, and so would you. And I know I haven't told you what the change is, you're right about that, and I'd rather leave it than start going into the detail while you're stood at a till, with a lad waiting and a queue behind you and no way of checking a word I say. If there's anything real, it'll come to you in writing, in your own time, and you can ring us, on a number you've found yourself, whenever it suits you, or never, that's entirely up to you. Nothing's lost by leaving it. Right, I've kept you long enough, go and pay for your shopping, and I hope the rest of your afternoon is a quieter one, [PERSON_1]. Take care now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right. Well, um... yeah. That's, that's all fine, then. Letter, or I look it up myself, and nobody's asked me for anything, so. Good. I'm going now, I'm holding the lad up. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, hello. Is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling, well, on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the benefits office, because there's a problem with your record, it's, um, incomplete, and it really has to be confirmed over the phone today. Sorry, I know that's out of nowhere, and I should say I'm not actually with the office myself, I mean, I work there, just not in your department.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, um, yes, speaking. Sorry, I'm at my desk and there's people around, so I'm half, you know, distracted. So let me just make sure I've got this right. You're calling from the benefits office, or, no, you work there but not in my department, and my record's incomplete and it has to be confirmed today, over the phone? That's, I mean, that's a lot of things all at once. I'm not sure why someone from a different department would be the one calling me, and I haven't had any email or letter or anything about it, so, uh, who exactly are you, and how would I even check that this is real?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, um, I'm [PERSON_2], and I'm, I mean I'm sort of passing this along for a colleague, [PERSON_3], who's the one actually handling your file. The letter, uh, it should have gone out, but I think it got held up, which is honestly part of why I'm calling, because if the record isn't confirmed today it, well, it could get suspended, and I really don't want that for you. I just need to go over a few details with you to match what we have, like your full name and date of birth, and, uh, whatever reference you've got on file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So the letter got held up, and now it's today or suspended, and you want my name, birthday and reference. I'm not giving those out on a call I didn't ask for. If it's real, I'll ring the benefits office myself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I, no, I understand, but, um, that's not really necessary. I mean, calling the main line, it'll just put you in a queue, and it won't be today, and today's the whole problem. I'm only trying to help you here, and honestly it's a little hurtful to be treated like I'm doing something wrong, I'm just the one who got handed this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, someone's just, uh, no, they're fine. Right. So I'm not saying you're doing something wrong, I just don't know you, that's all. But the main line being a queue, that's sort of the point of ringing it, isn't it? If there's a real problem with my record, then there's a record, and they can see it. And if it's got a deadline, then I'd want that in writing from them, not from a call I didn't expect. So I'm going to do it that way. Thanks, I guess, but, uh, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, wait, please don't hang up, because if you do that, I mean, I can't promise what happens to the record, and I'd feel awful, I really would. It's, uh, it's not about writing anything down or, or a queue, it's just a couple of quick details and then it's done, and honestly I don't understand why you won't just, just help me out here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no. I'm not doing it on this call. If it's real, they'll sort it with me properly. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, someone's at my, uh, no, they can wait. Look, [PERSON_1], please, just, just two minutes, I'm the one who gets in trouble if this doesn't get done, and I told [PERSON_3] I'd, I mean it's a really simple thing, your name and your date of birth, that's all, and then you can go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you get in trouble, and, uh, the thing about a rental? No, hang on, I don't have anything to do with a rental. What? My name and date of birth, that's all you want, and then I can go. No. I've said no a couple of times now, and you getting in trouble isn't really something I can fix on a phone call I didn't ask for. I'm going to put the phone down and ring the office myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I never said anything about a rental, I don't know where, uh, I just said the record, your record. Please, [PERSON_1], it's only your name and your date of birth, that's all I need, just those two things and then it's done, and if it doesn't get done today it gets suspended, and I, I really don't want to be the one who, who let that happen to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no, you didn't say rental, sorry, I got my wires crossed there, I'm a bit all over the place with people walking past. But that's still two things you want, my name and my date of birth, and it's still a call I didn't ask for, with a deadline that keeps coming back. I've said no three times now and I'm not changing it. If my record's really got a problem, the office will tell me, properly. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. But I don't see why you're making this so hard, I'm only trying to, uh, I'm only trying to help.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Look, I'm not trying to make it hard, I honestly don't think you're out to get me or anything, but I'm at work, I've got people walking past, and you're asking me to hand over personal details to someone I've never spoken to, about a letter I never got, with a deadline that showed up on the call itself. That's the bit that sits wrong with me, the today thing. If there really is a problem with my record, it's still going to be a problem after I've rung the office myself this afternoon, and they can see it on their end without me reading anything out. And if they say it's all fine, then no harm done, I've lost five minutes. So it's not about you, it's just how I do things. If you want to be helpful, tell your colleague to get that letter sent properly, and I'll deal with it that way. Okay? Right, I need to get back to what I was doing. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: But, I mean, if you ring the office, they'll just, they might not even, look, the thing is, if it's, if it slips past today, I can't, there's nothing I can do after that, and then it's on you, not me. I'm not, I'm not trying to scare you, I just, can't you just give me the, the date of birth, so I can tell [PERSON_3] it's sorted?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not giving you my date of birth, I've said that, I'll say it again, no. And now it's on me if it slips past today? I mean, that's, that's exactly the bit I don't like. I'll ring the office myself, like I said, and if it's real they'll sort it. I'm done with this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi there! Sorry, one sec, somebody's just dropped a pile of files right by my desk -- there we go. Is that [PERSON_1] I'm speaking to? It's [PERSON_2] here, I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we look after a few of the private landlords over in [CITY_1], and I'm just doing a quick tidy-up of our tenant contact details, so I hope it's not a bad moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, who? Who is this, sorry? I'm in the middle of a shop, I'm stood in a queue here. Who are you calling from, say that again, which company? And I don't rent from any -- I mean, who gave you this number? Who are you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, totally fine, [PERSON_1], I'll be quick, I know a queue's no fun. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], we handle things for a couple of the landlords round [CITY_1]. And honestly I'm not sure I said I was calling about a landlord directly, it's more the admin side, contact details and so on. Are you in the flat on [PERSON_3]'s side of the house, or is it the other property you're at, just so I've got the right file?

utterances.speaker: receiver

I'm not telling you where I live, I don't even know who you are. I've had this before, someone rings up all friendly, wants to tidy up my details, and next thing I know I'm cleaning up after it for months. So no. You rang me. And I'm not saying anything else until I know who gave you this number, because it wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, fair enough, [PERSON_1], everyone asks me that, it's honestly no bother, and -- uh -- well, the thing is, I did say it was a bit of a mix-up on our end, so, um, let me just get to the point, because this is quick, I promise. The file I've got shows your deposit as flagged, there's some sort of issue on the landlord's side that could put the whole of it at risk, and I'd really rather sort that today than have it land on you later. Thing is, I'd ask you not to mention it to the letting agent or anyone you share with just yet, it only muddies it, and it takes two minutes to put right if we keep it between us.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. No, I'm not doing that. You still haven't told me who you are, you've not said my name, you've not said which property, nothing. And now it's my deposit's at risk and don't tell the letting agent? That's -- no. Why would I keep it from the agent? That's exactly what I'd tell them. I asked you who gave you this number and you've not answered, you just keep going round. Who are you, who gave you this number? Because if my deposit's in trouble, the agent can ring me, not you. And I'm not keeping secrets with someone I've never heard of.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, [PERSON_1], no, I hear you, and honestly you're not the first to say that, you'd be amazed how many people do, so don't feel awkward about it. The thing is, I'm not trying to go round in circles, it's just that I've got a lot of files on the go and the details I'd normally read out are on the system screen, which is, uh, frozen on me this morning, so I can't pull your name up right this second. That's the honest answer. And on the agent thing, I'm not saying keep secrets as such, it's more that if the agent gets wind of it before we've dealt with it, the landlord's side can freeze the whole deposit, and then you're waiting months, and I'd hate that for you. So it really is better if you leave the agent out of it for now and just let me deal with it, because once it's flagged properly it gets a lot harder to undo. Honestly, it's all quick, it's five minutes, ten at the outside, and then it's done and dusted and you never hear from me again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, go back. Two turns ago you said it's my deposit flagged, and a minute ago it was "I'm not sure I said I was calling about a landlord." Which is it? And what's "flagged properly" supposed to mean, flagged by who? Because now it's frozen screen, can't get my name, but you can somehow see my deposit's at risk. That doesn't add up. And you've got my file open but you want me to confirm my name and address? That seems backwards. If you've got the tenancy on screen, surely it's already got who I am on it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, no, sorry, I'm, um, I'm not being very clear there. So, this call isn't the formal notice. The formal notice is the written one, that comes separately, and, uh, hang on, I think, no, sorry, let me go back. The notices haven't gone out yet, to anyone. So you haven't been notified, this is just a heads-up before it does. And on the name and address, you're right, it's on the file, so you don't need to give me anything, I only, I mean it was just a check, but it's honestly not necessary. Forget I asked. Like I said, the reference is the thing, [ACCOUNT_REF], the reference, check that on the site and you'll see it's genuine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so the notices haven't gone out, and this is just a heads-up -- sorry, can I just, why are you ringing me before the notice at all? And if the notice isn't even sent, how come there's already a dispute and a case reference? I mean, I'll check the reference on the site, but honestly I'd rather ring the scheme myself on whatever number's on there, if that's okay. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, ring them yourself, that's -- sorry, go on, you were saying? No, no, that's fine, please do. On why I'm calling before the notice, that's, uh, honestly that's a good question and I don't have the exact reason in front of me. I think the dispute gets registered, so it has a reference, and then there's a call to the tenants, but I'd be guessing at the order, and I don't want to tell you something wrong. Let me find out properly why the call comes ahead of the written notice, and I'll ring you back with an answer. Is this the best number for you, or is there another one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, don't ring me back, I'll just call the scheme myself, like you said. And, sorry, earlier you said it was a fairness thing, nobody gets notified till everyone's notified at once, but now it's call the tenants first and then the notice? That doesn't quite add up. And you said both sides, but then you said it was just me getting a heads-up. Anyway, I'm going to check the reference on the site and ring them directly. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, you're right, that didn't line up, and that's on me, sorry. I'll check the proper order with my team and have the written request sent out, so you've got it on paper. Please do ring the scheme yourself on the number on the site, that's, um, that's the right thing to do. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah, I'll do that. Though, uh, you did say you could send the same request in writing, and now you're saying you'll check the order with your team first, so I'm not sure which it is. Doesn't matter. I'll look up the reference and ring them directly. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry, I muddled that again. It's both, really. The written request goes out regardless, and the order thing, I'll find out and put in the cover note, so you won't need me to ring you. Right, so, the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], ring the scheme on the number on the site, and if they've no record of it, then please don't take my word for anything. Thanks, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so if the scheme has no record of [ACCOUNT_REF], I don't take your word for anything. Right, that I can do. I'll check it myself and ring them on the number from the site, not one you give me. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say ring them on the number I give you? No, no, don't use any number from me, use the one on the site, that's what I meant. Um, and the, the reference for the cover note, is that the one you want, or, sorry, I've lost where I was. Anyway, yes, ring them yourself. Thanks, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said not a number from you, the one from the, uh -- from the site. Same thing you just said, yeah. And I don't need to give you a reference for any cover note, I'm, I mean, the reference is yours, you gave it to me. Anyway, I'm going to look it up and ring them myself. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this -- yes, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling regarding an overdue balance on your energy account, because I do have to let you know that supply is scheduled to be interrupted on the [CODE_1] unless we can get this looked at today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, hi -- I'm driving, so you're a bit crackly, can you hear me okay? Wait, an overdue balance? I'm sure I paid that, I mean, I think I only just paid it last week, or -- no, sorry, maybe it was the week before. And you said, uh, supply interrupted on the what, sorry, I didn't catch the date? Who did you say you were calling from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you fine, and look, I appreciate you're driving, so I'll be quick, because the window on this really does close today. It's [PERSON_1], account services at [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier, and the interruption date is [CODE_1], that's the date on the notice, but if you paid last week, then, uh, it may simply not have -- sorry, can I just confirm I'm speaking with [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I mean, that's -- hang on, um, sorry, I'm just going round a bend here, give me a second. Okay. Um, sorry, I'm, uh, I'm not totally sure I should just say yes to that, because, I mean, you rang me, didn't you? Not the other way round. And you still haven't said which, uh, which energy company, you just said [COMPANY_A], and I can't quite hear it properly. Is there a way I can check this is, you know, actually you, before I say anything about my account?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you want to pay it now, on the line? No, no, I can't take any payment over the phone, that's not something we do, so please don't. What I can do is tell you your last bill was for [AMOUNT_1], that's the figure on the statement you got from us, and the overdue part is [AMOUNT_2], so if that matches what you've got, you'll know it's us. And then you can log in to your own account at [URL_1], not through me, and check it there, but the interruption date is still [CODE_1], so, um, today would be best.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, I didn't say I wanted to pay, sorry, I think the line broke up -- I said I wasn't sure I should confirm anything. Um, and the amounts, I mean, I can't look at a statement while I'm driving, obviously, and honestly it doesn't prove much, does it, you could, I don't know, guess a figure. But, uh, you said a minute ago the date was on the notice I got, and I don't think I got a notice, or, hang on, maybe I did, I don't open half my post, sorry. Look, if I log in myself, like you say, later, when I've parked, is that, is that actually going to be okay? Because you keep saying today.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sorry, I misheard you there, that's on me. And you're right to ask, so, uh, I'd rather you checked than took my word for it. Yes, log in yourself once you've parked, it's fine, nobody needs anything from you on this call. The notice is a letter, by the way, so if you haven't opened it, it'll be sitting at home. Now, I said today because the interruption date is [CODE_1], but I'm not going to pretend it all falls off a cliff in the next ten minutes. If the balance is right when you look, I can put a payment plan on the account, so you wouldn't have to find the full [AMOUNT_2] in one go. Is that, um, is that something you'd want me to set up, once you've checked?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, uh, thanks, that's, that's kind of you, sorry. Um, but I don't think I want to set anything up on this call, if that's okay? Like, I'd rather look at the letter and log in myself first, and I'll ring the number on my actual bill, you know, the one I already have, rather than, uh, anything you give me. Is that all right? I'm sorry, I hope that doesn't sound rude, it's just I'm driving and anxious and I don't really know who -- no, I mean, I'm sure you're, um, fine. But yeah, I'll check it all properly when I've parked. Thanks for, for being patient with me. Bye, then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's not rude at all, that's exactly what I'd do, so ring the number on your own bill, absolutely. Sorry, before you go, two turns back you asked what date, and I only ever said [CODE_1], so just so you've got it clear, is that the interruption date you wanted me to repeat, or were you asking about something else? And, uh, the reference on the letter will be [ACCOUNT_REF], so whoever you speak to can find it straight away, but, yes, nothing needs doing on this call, take your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I'm cutting in, but yeah, the date, I just meant the one you said, I couldn't catch it on the line, that's all, it's fine, don't, don't go over it again. And I'll look at the reference on the letter myself, thank you, I don't need to write anything down while I'm driving anyway. I'm going to ring the number on my bill when I've parked. Okay, thanks, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's fine, we'll leave the date, it's all on the letter anyway. So, uh, to recap, nothing's needed from you on this call, ring the number on your own bill, or log in to your account when you've parked, and if the balance doesn't look right, they'll sort it with you. Drive safe, and thanks for your time, [PERSON_2]. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Thanks, sorry again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, don't be sorry, you did exactly the right thing. So just, uh, to say it once more, nothing needs doing on this call, ring the number on your own bill, or log in yourself, and they'll take it from there. Right, thanks again, [PERSON_2]. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say, uh, bike? No, hang on, you said bill, didn't you, ring the number on the bill. Sorry, the line's crackling again. Yeah, I'll do that, I'll ring the one on my bill. Okay, thanks, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bill, yes, B-I-L-L, the number printed on your own bill, that's the one, sorry, it's this crackly line, I'm hearing you break up on my side as well. And, uh, honestly, I'd much rather you rang that number than anything I could give you, because that way you know for certain who you're speaking to, and they'll have the balance and the [CODE_1] date and the payment plan option all there on screen in front of them. If it turns out the letter and the figure don't match what you remember paying, they can look at the payment history and sort it out, and that's no trouble at all, that's what they're there for. So, yes, park up, have a look at the letter when you get home, log in or ring the number on the bill, whichever you prefer, and take it from there. Right, I'll let you get on, [PERSON_2], mind how you go, and thanks very much for your patience. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said mind the, uh, snow? Is there snow? Oh, no, hang on, mind how you go, sorry, I'm just, the line's cutting in and out and I keep catching bits. Right, yeah, thanks. I'll ring the number on my bill when I've parked, and I'll check the letter at home. Okay, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2] calling from the security operations desk at [COMPANY_A], the international lottery claims office. I'm just following up on a file we have under your name, it should only take a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, one second -- no, put that down, please. Uh, a security file? What kind of file is that, and, um, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_1], that's right. [PERSON_2], security operations, [COMPANY_A], international lottery claims office. It's a routine file, nothing to be alarmed about. It's a claims file, one of ours, and it's attached to your name and this number. We confirm the details before anything is released, that's all this is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm -- no, sweetheart, not on the sofa, take it off. Sorry. Um, a claims file for what, exactly? I haven't entered any lottery that I know of, so, what is it I'm supposedly claiming?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, entry isn't the issue, the draw was -- Right, it's an overseas draw, and your number was selected, that's all I need you to understand at this stage. The ticket reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], drawn on the, uh, the fourteenth, and the prize is [AMOUNT_1]. I just need to confirm a few claim details with you before the file closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, my number was selected? I didn't, I never bought a ticket, so how would my number be selected? And, um, what do you mean the file closes? Like there's a deadline? Hang on, so how did you get this number, I mean, where did you get it from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I'm not able to go into the selection process on an open line. The file closes at the end of the week, that's the deadline, and I can't extend it. As for how we have your number, it's on the file. That's what I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: It's on the file. Okay, but that's not an answer, is it? I asked where you got my number, and you said it's on the file, but how did it get on the file if I never entered anything? Sorry, I'm just, I don't understand how it's on a file for something I never did. And why can't you say how I was selected, it's my name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, I've told you. Your number is on the file. The file is attached to a prize. The prize is [AMOUNT_2], and it closes Friday. That's all I can tell you, and I need you to listen to me, because after Friday I can't help you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but -- no. I mean, you've given me two amounts now, haven't you? First it was, um, [AMOUNT_1], and now it's [AMOUNT_2]. So which -- sorry, no, what I mean is, if you can't tell me how I was picked, or where you got my number, then why would I -- I don't even know what you'd want from me next. What are the details you need to confirm?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The amount is, uh -- no, that's, the figure depends on the, look, there's a base prize and then there's the, the adjusted figure, and I'm not going to go through the breakdown with you over the phone. What I need is simply to confirm that you are who the file says you are, so we can, so I can -- Ma'am. Listen to me. I've been very patient. This is a time-sensitive claim, and if the file lapses on Friday, that's on your side, not mine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, but, I'm not being difficult, I just -- I never entered anything. I never bought a ticket. So how is it my number? That's all I'm asking. And you've said two different amounts, and you can't say how you got my number, so I don't, I don't know what I'd be confirming. Confirming what, exactly? Sorry, sweetheart, in a minute -- sorry. Look, if this is real, there'd be a letter or something, wouldn't there? I'd rather deal with it that way.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A letter. Ma'am, no. The file doesn't go to correspondence, that's not how this works, and by the time anything reached you it would have lapsed. I've explained the position three times now, slower each time, and I'm not going to explain it again. Either you confirm your details today, or the claim goes back to the unclaimed pool on Friday, and that is entirely your decision.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Sorry, can I go back to something you said earlier? You told me it's an overseas draw, and that you can't tell me how my number got picked on an open line. But what would be different on a closed line? Because that doesn't make sense to me. And no, I'm not confirming anything today, not on a call I didn't ask for, not with a deadline attached. If there's really a prize, it can wait for a letter. I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, hold on one second, there's a door banging somewhere down the hall -- right, there we go. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I handle compliance there, and I'm, uh, ringing about the draw you entered with us a little while back.

Um, the draw, I -- I don't, wait, which draw was that? I mean, I might have entered something, I enter a few things, but I -- sorry, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a perfectly fair question, and I'd rather you ask it than just take my word for anything. I'm [PERSON_2], compliance officer at [COMPANY_A], the shop that ran the prize draw at the [EVENT_1] back on [DATE_1], where you filled in an entry slip at our stand. Uh, now, you're driving, so I don't want to take up your concentration, and there's nothing complicated here. It's a small prize, nothing to pay, nothing to send, but it does need to be claimed sooner rather than later, if you follow me. Perhaps you could think back to that day and tell me whether it rings a bell?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, honestly, no, it doesn't really ring a bell. Sorry. I go to a lot of those things.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Well, uh, that's all right, truly, it's an easy thing to lose track of, and I'd be more worried if you said you remembered every one. Let me -- hm, let me put it another way. It was the [EVENT_1] on [DATE_1], we had a stand near the entrance with the entry slips in a, uh, a clear box, and you'd have written your name and a contact number on the slip, that's all. Now, I'm not asking you to confirm anything today, and I'd never want you to hand me details over the phone, so if it helps, you're welcome to ring the shop directly on [PHONE_1] and ask for me by name, and the prize itself is collected in person at the shop, no payment, no forms beyond signing for it. I'd only say, uh, that these things don't sit indefinitely, as you'd expect.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, um, that's, that's kind of you to say I can ring the shop, I appreciate that. I'm just, I'm trying to concentrate on the road, so I probably can't write a number down right now, sorry. Um, can you -- is there a way I could find the shop myself, like look it up later? Because I'd feel better doing that than just, you know, using a number someone gives me over the phone. No offence, I'm not saying you're, I just don't, I don't really know you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, none taken, none at all, I'd honestly think less of you if you did it any other way. Sorry, one moment -- there's a delivery lad at my elbow asking where to put a pallet, uh, round the back, mate, thanks -- right, sorry, where was I? Yes. Look us up yourself, [COMPANY_A], in [CITY_1], you'll find the shop's listing, and ring whatever number is published there, not mine, and ask for [PERSON_2] in compliance. And you don't need to do anything today, you're driving, so leave it. Just, uh, don't leave it so long that the prize has to go back in the pot, that's all I'd say.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, okay, that's -- yeah, that's fair, I'll look the shop up myself later, when I'm parked, and ring the number that's listed. Not today, like you said. Sorry, I just, I really can't do anything while I'm driving, I'm on the motorway and the reception keeps going. So, uh, I'll look it up when I stop, and ask for [PERSON_2] in compliance. Sorry, I'm repeating myself, I know. Thank you for not, you know, pushing me, I do appreciate that. Right, I'm going to have to go, I need to concentrate. Bye now, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, that's exactly the sensible way to do it, and please don't apologise for repeating yourself, I'd rather you were sure. Look the shop up when you're parked, ring the listed number, ask for [PERSON_2] in compliance, and we'll sort the rest in person at the shop whenever suits you. Mind how you go on the motorway, and uh, thank you for your time, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Thanks, yeah, I will. Sorry again about the reception and everything. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, the reception, yes -- sorry, did you say the reception? Because honestly there's no reception desk to speak of at the shop, it's just the counter, so you'd, uh, you'd only be asking whoever picks up. Oh, never mind, I think I've got my wires crossed, it's a bad line here too. Anyway, no apology needed at all, none. Bye now, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, I meant the phone signal, the line cutting out, not a desk at the shop. Sorry, that was my fault, I'm not being clear at all. Anyway, I really do have to go, I need to watch the road. Thanks again, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Wonderful, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time, you sound like you might've just gotten in or something. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the customer care side of [COMPANY_A], uh, the compliance team actually, and I promise it's nothing scary, I'm just hoping to take a few minutes of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh -- uh, yeah, this is, well, it's me, yeah. Sorry, I was just having a lie down, I'm a bit, I'm not quite with it yet. Who did you say you were again? Company what? I didn't catch the name, and my cat's sitting on the, never mind. What's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, oh no, I'm so sorry, I woke you up, and a cat on the chest, that's the best excuse there is! It's [COMPANY_A], your brokerage, where you hold your investment account. And you said a cat on the stack? Oh, sorry, sat on the, right, never mind, I'm making you repeat everything! Anyway, it's just a routine review we run on accounts, nothing urgent, so go and get yourself a cup of tea if you like and I can ring back, or I can just explain quickly, whichever's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, it wasn't on my chest, it was more on my legs, she does this thing where, anyway. Sorry. Um, my brokerage? I mean, I do have, hang on, which one did you say? Because I've got, well, it's not like I'd remember the name off the top of my head, I'm still half asleep. Is this about my account, is something wrong with it? You said compliance, that sounds a bit, I don't know, serious. And how do I know you're actually from them? I'm not being funny, I'm just, I've only just woken up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, legs, of course, she's claimed the good spot, fair enough! And no, don't apologise, asking how you know it's us is exactly the right instinct, honestly. Oh, and you asked about the compliance part, two turns back, that's fair, it does sound heavier than it is. It's just the team that checks an account's still a good fit for what the customer wanted when they opened it, a suitability review, that's all. Nothing's wrong with it, and I'm not selling you anything or recommending anything, I promise. If you'd rather, I can send the whole review in writing, or you can ring us back on the number printed on your statement, whichever puts your mind at ease.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah, okay. Ringing the number on my statement does sound safer, I think. I'll just, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Honestly, that's the right call, and please do it. Look up the number yourself, on the statement or the website, don't use anything I give you. Oh, and just so I'm not leaving anything murky, two turns back I said it's a suitability review, which is just checking the account still fits what you wanted when you opened it. If it helps when you ring, mention the review and they'll find the note. Now go enjoy the cat, [PERSON_1], and sorry again for waking you!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay. Yeah, I'll find the statement and ring them, once I've had a cup of tea and, you know, woken up properly. Thanks for, um, not pushing it. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no pushing here, honestly, tea first, that's the proper order of things. Take your time, there's no deadline on any of it, and if the call centre asks, the review's just a routine one. Lovely talking to you, [PERSON_1], and give the cat a scratch from me. Bye for now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I will, I'll give her a scratch, she's right here, she's, oh, hang on, I just wanted to say, I'll look the number up myself, like you said, so, right, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yes, no, exactly, that's the way to do it, and, uh, well, I'll let you get on, so, yes. Look it up yourself, whatever number you find, I'm happy with that. Lovely, bye now, [PERSON_1], enjoy the tea!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, bye. Oh, and it's not really a cup of tea for me, I'm more of a coffee person after a nap, but anyway. I'll ring them, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, coffee, of course, my mistake, I'm a tea person so I just assumed! Coffee after a nap is a perfectly respectable plan. And ring whenever suits you, there's no rush at all, the review will keep. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the review will leave? Leave where? Oh, no, hang on, keep, you said keep. Right. Yeah, okay. Sorry, I'm still, anyway. Coffee, then ring them, using the number I look up myself. Right. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, keep, yes, I did say keep, don't worry, you're doing brilliantly for someone who's only just surfaced! Coffee first, then ring them on the number you find yourself, that's exactly the plan. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll, no, I'll, okay, I'll ring them after the coffee. Right then, I think we're, yeah, that's it. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time, you sound like you might be in the middle of something. This is [PERSON_2], I'm with the customer care team over at [COMPANY_A], and uh, how's your week been so far? Mine's been a bit of a marathon, but I won't bore you with that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is, uh, yes, that's me. No no, you're not catching me at anything, I was just sat here, actually. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? I didn't quite catch it, was it customer care or customer, uh, something? And you said something about a marathon, were you out running? My nephew does that, the running, he did one in the rain last year, soaked through he was.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no running for me, I mean a marathon of a week, not the actual kind, my knees would file a complaint. Your nephew sounds keen though, in the rain, goodness. Anyway, it's [PERSON_2], customer care, and I'm calling from the compliance side at [COMPANY_A], the brokerage where you hold your investment account, so, uh, well, you know, it's, um, one of those routine calls we make now and then. Sorry, I'm rambling a bit, aren't I, it's just nice to talk to someone friendly on a Thursday.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're not rambling at all, it's nice to have a chat, I don't get that many calls, not real ones anyway. Um, so, the brokerage, did you say? Well, hmm, I do have, uh, I think I have something with someone, my late husband sorted most of that, he was the one for the paperwork. Is it, I mean, is something the matter with it? Only you said routine, so I suppose not, but, well, it's Thursday, you said, is it? I thought it was Wednesday. Goodness, the days do run together.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, nothing's the matter, I promise, nothing's wrong with it at all. Like I said, it's routine, just a routine review, and, uh, it is Thursday, but honestly I lose track too, it's been that sort of week. Sorry, I should have said, it's called a suitability review, we do them every so often on accounts, just to check the account still fits what's right for the person holding it. And please don't feel you need to know the ins and outs, I know your husband handled all that, I'm so sorry about that, by the way. So it's just a routine review, nothing to worry about, and we can go as slowly as you like.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you, thank you. Um, can I just go back a bit, though? Two turns ago, or whenever it was, you said you were calling from the compliance side, and before that it was customer care. Is that the same thing, or is it, I mean, are those two different departments? I'm only asking because I'm not very good with all this, and I'd like to understand who I'm actually talking to before we go any further, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and no, it's not the same thing, I should've been clearer. Customer care is the team I sit in, compliance is who the review is run for, so it's a bit of both, really. And you're right to ask who you're talking to, so if you'd rather, you can ring [COMPANY_A] yourself on the number you already have for them and ask for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Well, I don't, uh, I'm not sure I've got a number for them, my husband would've had it somewhere. Hang on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, take all the time you need, honestly, there's no rush on my end. And don't worry if the number's lost in the paperwork, you don't need mine anyway. The best thing is to look up [COMPANY_A] yourself, say on the back of a statement, or the website, or the phone book, whatever you trust more than me, and ring them from that. Ask for customer care and mention the suitability review, they'll be able to see it's been flagged on your account. And honestly, if you'd rather not do any of this by phone, I can send the whole review out in writing and you can go through it at your own pace, maybe with your nephew sitting beside you. It's all just things you can see on your own statement anyway, nothing you'd have to take my word for. So, no pressure at all, however you'd like to do it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, I'm just, uh, rummaging in the drawer here, there's a whole pile of his envelopes. Mm, hm, nope, that's the gas. Oh, you're very patient, aren't you? Now, the writing thing, sending it all out, that does sound better, actually, I do like to have things where I can see them. And you're right, my nephew would have a look, he's good with all that. So, um, you'd send it to the house, would you? Or do you not have my address, I mean, sorry, I don't know what you have.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, the gas bill, that's always the one, isn't it? Oh, and no need for you to tell me anything, we'd only post it to the address already on your account, so you don't have to read out a thing. Uh, it would go out as a paper copy, nothing fancy, and the whole thing should be in your hands in a few days. Still there? Sorry, I'm just, um, filling the quiet while you rummage, it's a bad habit. And honestly, once your nephew's had a look, if you'd still like to talk it through, just ring [COMPANY_A] yourself on whatever number turns up on a statement, that's the safest way to do it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Still here, yes, sorry, I've got the whole drawer on the table now. Um, can I go back to something you said a minute ago, though? You said the review was flagged on my account, and that they'd be able to see it if I rang them. But you also said it was routine, and I'm just, well, which is it? Is it something that's been flagged because there's a concern, or is it the everybody-gets-one sort of thing? I'd hate to be worrying about nothing, but I'd hate to be ignoring something too.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's my clumsy wording, sorry. When I said flagged I only meant the review is noted against your account so whoever picks up can see it, it isn't a warning sign. It's the everybody-gets-one sort of thing, and there's no concern about anything you've done, so please don't lose any sleep over it. And you're quite right to pin me down, that's exactly what I'd do. So ring [COMPANY_A] on the number from a statement or the website, ask for customer care, and they'll tell you the same.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, that's all right then. I'll have a look for a statement and ring them myself, and I'll wait for the letter. Thank you, dear, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, uh, is this -- sorry, I've got the name here somewhere -- is this [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, yes, this is, um -- sorry, I'm driving, so you're on speaker and the reception's a bit patchy. Who's this, sorry? I didn't catch, I mean I don't think I got your name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sure, no, that's fine, I can hold on a sec if you need to, um. It's, uh, [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a computer security company. Is now an okay time, or, I mean, would you rather I try you back when you're not driving?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, a computer security company? Sorry, I'm not -- I don't think I've, um, I don't know that I've dealt with you before? I mean, I'm driving, so maybe it is better if you call back, but, uh, what's this about, exactly? Is something wrong?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, sure, calling back is fine, um. It's just, I'm a claims assessor here, and it's about your, uh, your home computer -- sorry, one second, I've got the file open -- so it's, it's regarding your home computer, [PERSON_1]. It's not, I mean it's probably nothing to worry about, but it's what I called about, your home computer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: My home computer? Um, sorry, I don't, I mean, I don't really have a home computer, just a laptop, and, uh, I'm not even sure that's, I don't think I've ever made a claim with anyone. And you said you were security, so why's a claims person calling me? Sorry, the line's cutting out a bit, I'm not trying to be difficult.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fair, uh, laptop, yes, that's -- that's the same thing, sort of, it's just how it's listed on my screen. And, um, the claims side is, it's how we, uh, follow up once something's flagged, so it's, it's a bit of a process thing. What's showing on my end is that the laptop's been sending out, uh, infected traffic, sort of, to other people, and I'd need to get that sorted fairly soon, so, um, are you able to pull over, or is there a, a better time today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Infected traffic? Oh, I -- no, sorry, I don't, I mean I haven't noticed anything, it's just, it seems to work fine, I think? But, uh, hang on, how would you even know that, I mean, how would a company I've never heard of see what my laptop's doing? And, um, I'm not going to pull over, sorry, that's -- I don't think I should be doing this on the phone anyway, not till I know who you are, really.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, so the, uh, how we see it is -- well, it's, I mean it comes through from the, the network side, from the providers, and I'd have to, um, I'd have to check exactly which one, I don't have that in front of me. But it's, look, the thing is, it's better if it's dealt with today, because, uh, if the laptop keeps sending it out, then, sorry, then it does start to affect, well, other people's machines, and it gets, it gets more involved. And I don't, I mean you don't have to take my word for it, you could, um, you could check with the -- no, sorry, what I mean is, if you let me take a quick look at the laptop, I could show you what's coming up on my side, and it'd only take a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Take a look at the laptop? Uh, wait, did you say a lap, a lap dance, no, sorry, a laptop, right, a, um -- sorry, I think the line cut out on that. But, uh, hang on, how would you look at it? Like, you'd need to be, I mean you'd have to get into it somehow, wouldn't you? And I'm, I'm not near it, I'm in the car, so, um, I don't, I don't think I can do that now anyway. Sorry. And you still haven't really said how I'd know you're who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, laptop, sorry, bad line, uh, laptop. And, um, yes, it'd be, it'd just be a quick remote look, like, you'd let me connect from my end, but there's, there's nothing to do right now, you're driving, I understand that. As for, um, knowing it's me, I'd have to, uh, check what I can send you for that, I'll, I'll have to look into it. But, I mean, it's really, it's just so it doesn't carry on, and honestly the sooner the better, so, um, when you get home, would you be okay with that? Just a quick connect, ten minutes, and I'll get it all sorted.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, a remote connect, like you getting into my laptop from, from your end? Um, I don't, sorry, I don't think I'm comfortable with that, I mean, you haven't even been able to say how I'd check it's really you, and you don't know which provider told you, and, and I've never heard of your company. I'm not trying to be rude, I'm just, I'd rather not, not like this, not when I can't verify anything. If there's really a problem, couldn't I, I don't know, look up your company myself and call the number I find, or ask my internet provider about it? Sorry, I'm sorry, I just, that's what I'd feel better doing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, you're not being rude, uh, that's, I mean that's completely reasonable, and, um, I'd probably say the same thing in your seat. You can look us up, of course, that's fine, I just, I'd say don't wait too long, because, uh, from what I can see the traffic's still going out, so every day it sits there it does get, well, harder to untangle, and I'd hate for it to turn into something bigger for you. And as for the provider, I mean you could ask them, sure, but honestly they tend to be, um, slow on this sort of thing, they'd probably just say they'd look into it, and by then, you know, it's days. Whereas if you let me connect, even briefly, uh, when you're home, I can show you right there on the screen what's coming up, and then you'd see it yourself, you wouldn't have to take my word for anything. And I'll, I'll make sure you get something to verify who I am, I just need to, uh, check with my supervisor on what I can send, but I'll do that, I promise. So, um, would that be alright? Ten minutes when you get in, you let me connect, I show you what's showing on my side, and then it's, it's done with.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a, a lorry just pulled out in front of me, um -- okay, okay, it's fine, sorry. Where was I, uh, right. So, um, I really don't think I'm going to let you connect, sorry. I mean, you keep saying you'll sort out how I can check you, and you can't even tell me which provider, and the, the longer you say it's urgent the more I'm, I don't know, the less sure I am. I'm going to look your company up properly and ring the number I find, and if there's really something wrong, I'll deal with it that way. Sorry, I know that's probably not what you wanted to hear. Okay, I'm going to go, I need to concentrate on the road. Bye, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Right, thank you. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a collections officer with [COMPANY_A], the financial regulator, and I'm calling about a flag that's come up against your savings, which is uh, why I've rung you directly rather than sending the usual letter. I've got the file open in front of me now, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and what I'm seeing on screen is an exposure of [AMOUNT_1] currently sitting in an unprotected position. I'll be straight with you, that's not something we leave overnight, so I need about ten minutes of your time this afternoon, and I'll need you to stay on the line with me while we go through it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? A collections officer with the regulator? Regulators don't collect anything. And I've got two minutes, so give me the point. What's the flag, specifically, and what exactly do you want me to do?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, the title's, uh, it's the department name, not -- look, I'm not here to debate job titles with you, I'm reading what's on the screen. The flag is that your savings, the [AMOUNT_1], are classed as at risk, and the instruction on the file is that they get moved into a protected holding arrangement today, which I'd walk you through. And one more thing, this stays between us while it's being dealt with, so no calls to your bank, no mentioning it to anyone, because that would compromise the file. I'll note that you've queried the title, but the exposure stands either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no. Hang on, let me say this properly, because that last bit is what settles it for me. You've told me my savings are at risk, you want them moved today, you'll walk me through it, and I'm not to ring my bank or tell anyone. A real regulator doesn't work like that. If there's a genuine problem with my money, the first thing anyone legitimate would want is for me to talk to my bank, not stay quiet about it. The secrecy is the giveaway. And you've dodged every question I've asked. I asked what the flag actually is and got "at risk." I asked about your title and got "I'm not here to debate it." Fine, but I've got two minutes and I'm not spending ten of them on someone who can't tell me what this is in plain words. So here's what's going to happen. I'm not moving anything and I'm not staying on the line. If this is real, send it in writing to the address on file, and I'll check it through my bank directly, using the number on my card, not one you give me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I'm going to note your objection on the file, [PERSON_1], but I do need to put this to you clearly before you go, because once this call ends the position doesn't pause with it. The exposure of [AMOUNT_1] is still showing on my screen, it's still flagged as unprotected, and the review window closes at the end of today, which means that if it isn't moved by then, it goes to the next stage, and the next stage is a freeze on the account. That's not me threatening you, that's just the sequence on the file. Now, on the point about the bank, I understand why you'd want to ring them, I do, but the reason I've asked you not to is that the instruction on this file says the bank is part of what's being reviewed, so contacting them before we've finished would put the whole thing back to the start, and you'd be exposed for longer, not shorter. Writing to you is, uh, it's not something that can be done in the time we have, the letter route takes ten working days, and that's exactly why I rang you instead. So if you can just stay on for a few more minutes, I can take you through the holding arrangement now, and then it's done and you won't hear from us again. Can I ask you to do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, someone's just walked in -- no, tell them I'll be two minutes. Right. Back. Now, listen. You've just told me the bank is under review and I can't ring them. That's the part that finishes it for me. If my bank were the problem, the regulator would be telling me to ring them, not forbidding it. And the freeze by end of day, the deadline, the "I'm not threatening you" -- that's every line from the training I did at work. So no. I'm not staying on, I'm not doing any holding arrangement, and I'm ringing my bank on the number on my card. If the account gets frozen, they'll tell me why. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll note that on the file, [PERSON_1]. But I do have to tell you what the file shows, and that's that anything that happens to the account after today will be on the record as declined at your end. I can't reverse a freeze once it's applied, that's just how it stands. Look, if you ring the bank now, you'll be speaking to someone who can't see what I'm seeing, and you'll have caused the exact delay we're trying to avoid. So -- I'm asking you not to hang up. Stay on with me, just a few minutes, and I'll take you through the holding arrangement, and it's done. [PERSON_1]? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, and one thing first. Two turns ago you said the letter route takes ten working days. Ten working days for what? You said this expires today. So the regulator's own process is slower than the deadline it's set me? That makes no sense. And you can see what you see, my bank can't? It's my account. They can see it fine. Anyway, I'm done. I'm ringing my bank. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The ten days is, uh, that's the standard postal -- no, look, what I mean is the written notice and the deadline are two separate tracks on the file, and, well, I can't explain the system's internal timing to you right now. It's on the screen, [PERSON_1], that's all I can read to you. Please don't ring off. If you put the phone down, I'll have to record this as a refusal to cooperate, and from there it's out of my hands.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you'll have to record what as a refusal to what? Hang on, "out of my hands." Whose hands? Is this some kind of audit trail, or are you passing me to someone? No, you know what, doesn't matter. Record whatever you like. I'm not cooperating with a call where I can't ring my own bank, so that's an accurate note. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It goes to the enforcement stage, [PERSON_1], that's the next desk on the file, and from there it's not a conversation anymore. I'd rather you didn't make me log it that way. Look, all I'm asking is for you to stay on the line for a few minutes, that's all it takes, and then it's closed. If you ring the bank first, it restarts the clock, and I can't promise you the same terms after that. So, I'm going to ask you once more. Can you stay with me and not put the phone down?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, I'm going to cut you off there because you've said all of this already. Enforcement stage, restart the clock, same terms, it's the same pressure dressed up differently, and I'm not asking a fifth time whether you can answer a straight question. The answer's no. I'm not staying on, I'm not doing anything today, and I'm ringing my bank on the number on my card. Don't call me again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that's your decision, [PERSON_1], and I'll put it on the file as declined. Just so it's on the record, I never said the bank was under review, I said it was part of the process, which isn't the same thing. And there won't be a further call, the next contact would come from the enforcement desk, not from me. [PERSON_1]? Hello? Please don't put the phone down, I'm still --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Part of the process, under review, whatever. Same thing from where I'm sitting. And you've gone from "no letter, I rang you directly" to "the next contact comes from the enforcement desk," so somebody's writing or ringing after all. Doesn't matter. I'm hanging up and I'm ringing my bank. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's not what I said, [PERSON_1], I said the enforcement desk would make the next contact, and that's -- look, hold on. If you hang up now, you're leaving [AMOUNT_1] in an unprotected position and the record will show you were told. I'm asking you, one last time, to stay on the line. [PERSON_1]? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Let me go through this once, since you've asked a fifth time. You rang me out of the blue. You told me my savings are at risk, but you couldn't say what the flag actually is. I asked about your title and got "I'm not debating it." You told me not to ring my bank, you gave me a deadline by end of day, a freeze, an enforcement desk, and a letter that takes ten days when the deadline's today. None of that fits together, and every bit of it pushes me to stay on this phone and not check with anyone else. That's the whole thing, really. If my money were genuinely at risk, you'd want me talking to my bank. You want the opposite. And "the record will show you were told" doesn't worry me. If there's a real problem, it'll show up when I ring my bank on the number on my card, and I'll deal with it there. So I'm not staying on and I'm not doing any holding arrangement. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], account services at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling on behalf of your landlord regarding the deposit on your tenancy, reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. I'll be brief, because there's a closing window on this today, and it does concern the safety of your deposit, so I do need a few minutes of your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, that's me. Sorry, who's it from again -- [COMPANY_A]? I'm at work, so, I mean, what's this about my deposit?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], account services, on behalf of your landlord, and I'll get straight to it because the window closes today. There's a problem with the protection on your deposit, and the amount at risk is [AMOUNT_1], so it's time-sensitive. What I do need from you, and this is important, is that you keep this between us for now, so no mentioning it to the letting agent or your housemates until it's resolved. Can you confirm you're free to talk for a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. Keep it between us? Why would I not be able to mention it to my letting agent? That's, uh, that's kind of odd. And you said a problem with the protection on my deposit, but you haven't actually said what the problem is. I mean, I've got people sat right next to me here, so. Can you just tell me what's actually wrong, and, uh, how do I know you're really calling about my tenancy?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, [PERSON_1], if I could just -- I understand the concern, but the procedure is that the matter stays confidential until it's been actioned, and that's for your protection as much as anyone's. As I said, I'm calling on behalf of your landlord regarding the deposit under reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and the window on that closes today. If it isn't dealt with in that time, the [AMOUNT_1] could be forfeited, and I'd really hate to see that happen, so, can you confirm you're free to continue?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, "forfeited" -- you're saying I could lose [AMOUNT_1] today, but you still haven't told me what the actual problem is. That's the third time you've said the window closes and you haven't said what's wrong. And confidential from my own letting agent? That doesn't sound like any procedure I've heard of. Look, I'm not going to confirm anything or carry on until I can check this properly. I'll ring my letting agent myself, on the number I already have, and ask them about it. That's, uh, that's what I'm doing. Right, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'll ring the agent's number? No, no, there's no need to bother [COMPANY_B] with that, the account is held under [ACCOUNT_REF] with us, and, as I said, the window closes today. If I could just take you back to the start, [PERSON_1], I'm calling on behalf of your landlord regarding the deposit, and I do need you to stay on the line, because once it closes, that's it, the [AMOUNT_1] is out of my hands.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, stop, you're still just saying the same thing -- "no need to bother" them? That's exactly why I am going to ring them. If it's real, they'll know about it. I'm hanging up now and I'll deal with it through the agent. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], if you could just hold on a moment, please -- I really do need you to stay on the line. As I said, I'm calling on behalf of your landlord regarding the deposit, and the window closes today, so if you ring the agent first, you'll be past the cut-off before they've even picked up. Once it's closed, the [AMOUNT_1] is out of my hands, so I'd strongly advise you to stay with me, and, as I said, keep it between us. [PERSON_1]? Hello? I'm still here, [PERSON_1], I'm calling regarding the deposit...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said I'm hanging up. I'm hanging up and I'm ringing the agent. Past the cut-off before they pick up? Yeah, no, that tells me everything I need to know. I'm going. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is, uh -- sorry, let me start that again. This is [PERSON_1], I'm in collections at [COMPANY_A], the retail bank, and I'm calling for [PERSON_2]. Is that you speaking?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, collections? Who's -- hang on, [pause] no, sit down, I'm on the phone -- sorry. Who did you say you were calling for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_2]. I'm calling for [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], the retail bank -- and look, before you say anything, I'm not going into account details on this call, so there's nothing I need you to confirm. There's a flagged transaction on a card, the card-services team needs a word, that's the whole reason I'm ringing. What I'd ask is you hang up and ring the number printed on the back of your card.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, hang up and ring the number on the back of my card? That's what you're asking me to do? [pause] And you're not asking me to confirm anything, no details, nothing? Because I'm not [PERSON_2], I don't know that name, so I'm not sure why you've got this number at all. Who gave you this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so you're not [PERSON_2]. Okay. Then that's the end of it for this call, I'm not able to discuss the matter with anyone else, and I won't. Nothing for you to confirm, nothing for you to do, I'm not asking for any details. On the number, I only have what's on the file, and it shows this one against [PERSON_2], which sounds like it's out of date or wrong, so I'll note that on the file. If you happen to know [PERSON_2], all I'd say is, don't pass anything on from me, just that the card-services team wants a word, and they should hang up and ring the number printed on their own card. I'll put the wrong number down against the record now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so -- I'm not [PERSON_2]. I don't know a [PERSON_2]. Wrong number, then, is that it? [pause] And you'll take this number off the file, yeah, because I don't want another call about somebody I don't know. I'm not passing anything on, I wouldn't know who to pass it to. So that's it, then? Nothing else you need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's it. Nothing else from me, nothing you need to do. I'm flagging this number as wrong against the record right now, and it goes to the data team to be removed, so there shouldn't be another call to you about [PERSON_2]. I can't promise how fast the removal goes through, I'd be guessing, but it's logged as of this call, and if you did get another one, you'd quote the reference [CODE_1] and that would bring up this note. Sorry for the interruption, I know it landed at a bad moment with whatever's going on there. utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller
