utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, I'm just -- look, I asked what make it is. Make. Of the car. You've got it on the file, so just read it out to me. And while you're at it, which company did you say again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, the, uh, the make, sorry, I thought you said the *rate*, so please don't worry, that's all covered, there's no rate going up, it's all about keeping what you have. And it's [COMPANY_A], I did say, I'm sorry, I'm a case handler there, I'm only trying to look after you. If I could just confirm a few details with you, then we can get the renewal done today before it lapses. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Rate? No, I said make. M-A-K-E. Ford, Toyota, that sort of thing. You've got my file open and you can't tell me what car I own? That's, uh, that's not great. And you said [COMPANY_A] twice now, but that's not really a name, is it? What's the actual company called?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I do apologise, that's, that's entirely my fault, it's just the screen, it's being very slow. It's [COMPANY_A], that's the name I have, and I can see why you'd want to be careful, I'd want you to be careful. But the cover really does lapse today, and I'd hate for you to be left without protection if something happened on the road. If you could just confirm a couple of details with me, I can get it renewed, it's, um, it's no trouble at all. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Yeah. So, let me get this straight. You rang me, you can't tell me the make of my car, you can't tell me what your company's called, and now it's the screen's fault again. Right. And you want me to read details out to you. Um, no, I don't think so. If my warranty's really lapsing, then the people who actually sold it to me will have written to me, and I'll ring them on the number I already have. So, yeah. I'm going to leave it there. Cheers.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, wait, please don't hang up, I completely understand, I do, and I'm sorry if I've made it difficult. It's only that today is the last day, and if it lapses you'd be, um, you'd be fully exposed, and I'd hate that for you. Could you just stay on with me for one more minute? I can have a colleague call you back, it's an internal line so I can't give you a number, but they'd ring you later today, I'm not sure exactly when. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Look, you said it was a mistake about the rate earlier, and now it's a colleague I can't call back on a number you can't give me. Nope. And hang on, you said it needed confirming this morning at the start, now it's lapsing today, which is it? Doesn't matter. Don't ring me back, don't send a colleague. If the warranty's real, I'll sort it with whoever I bought it from. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh... I'm sorry, I really am. It's just, if you could confirm the details before it lapses today, I'd feel so much better. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you've said that twice now and I'm still here, so no. But go on, two turns back you said the rate wasn't going up. I never said anything about a rate. What rate were you on about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. It was just a figure of speech, I'm sorry. Please, it really is only to keep you protected, if I could just...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A figure of speech. Right. Look, I've told you twice I'm done, and you've still not given me a car or a company name. So that's it. Don't ring again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, did you say the *cars* don't ring, because the, the cover isn't just for one car, so you'd be protected on the, uh, on the whole account, and that's honestly very good value, nobody's asking you to pay anything big today. Please, if you could just stay on one minute so I can confirm the, um, the details with you before it lapses. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Cars? I said don't ring, I didn't say a word about -- no. Stop. I'm not confirming anything, I'm not staying on, and nothing you've said has checked out. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I do hear you, I do. Sorry, could I just ask, what you said a moment ago about the details, did you mean you'd rather someone else confirm them for you, because I could arrange that, it's really no trouble. It's just that the cover does lapse today and I'd hate for you to be left unprotected. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that, I said -- look, no, nobody else is confirming anything either, I'm not -- Right, I'm done. Don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Good. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor with [COMPANY_A], we're one of the tenancy deposit protection schemes, and I'm ringing because there's a deposit dispute that's been raised on your property, it's at the stage where we have to notify both the landlord and the tenants formally, and I wanted to speak to you directly before the written notice goes out, just so it doesn't land on your doormat as a surprise. Now, one thing I do need to flag, and I know it sounds a bit odd on a phone call, is that until both sides have been formally notified, we ask that you keep the details of the dispute to yourself, so not discussing it with the other tenants in the house, it's a procedural fairness rule, uh, it protects everyone involved, and I'll be sending you the same request in writing with a case reference, so you're not just taking my word for it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, I've just woken up, I was having a bit of a nap. Dispute on, what, on my property? I mean, I rent, I don't own the place, so I'm not sure why it'd be, uh, why you'd be ringing me about it. And who did you say you were again? A deposit something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, sorry, I've caught you at a bad moment, I do apologise. So, uh, [COMPANY_A], we're one of the tenancy deposit protection schemes, which is where your landlord would have lodged your deposit when you moved in. And you're right, you rent, so the dispute's between the landlord and the tenants over how that deposit gets returned, which is why you're on our file at all, it's not that anything's been, you know, taken from you or that you've done anything wrong. Take a second to wake up properly, I'm in no rush, and if it helps, I'll send all of this in writing with a case reference you can look up on our official site at [URL_1], rather than you having to take my word for it over the phone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's the, uh, the washing machine's gone off in the next room, that beeping, give me a second -- right, it'll stop on its own, I think. Sorry. Where was I? So the deposit, yeah, I think it did go into one of those schemes, I vaguely remember an email about it when I moved in, but I couldn't tell you which one. I haven't moved out or anything though, so what's there to dispute? And you said I'm not supposed to talk to the others in the house about it? That's the bit that's, I don't know, that's a bit odd, isn't it? I mean, why wouldn't I mention it to the people I live with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right to ask, it is an odd thing to be told on a phone call, and I'd rather you ask than just nod along. So, the reason is the dispute's only half notified at the moment. The landlord's side has been logged, but the other tenancy members haven't had their formal notice yet, and if one of you tells the others before that notice goes out, it can look like the process has been influenced, which can actually complicate things for you all. It's not about hiding anything from you, it's a short pause, and it lifts the moment everyone's been formally notified. And on your question about what's there to dispute, I can't go into the detail on a call, that'll be in the written notice, which will have your case reference, and you can check that reference on our official site at [URL_1]. Honestly, if you'd rather not take my word for it, hang up and ring the number on that site, nothing's lost by doing that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, I mean, I think I'd, no, actually -- hang on. I'm still not sure why, if nobody's moved out and nobody's said anything about money, there's a dispute at all. Like, who raised it? You can't tell me that either, can you? And the thing is, I'd probably just, well, I'd normally say something to the others, because it's, you know, it's their deposit as well, isn't it? So I don't really like being told not to. I think, uh, I think I'd rather just look it up myself like you said. Ring the number on the website, was it? I'll do that, I think. Yeah. Right, thanks, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, no, that's -- hang on a second before you go, because you've asked a fair question and I'd rather answer it than have you put the phone down thinking something's off. On who raised it, I genuinely can't say on a call, it'll be in the written notice, and honestly, I'd do exactly what you're saying. Don't take my word for it. Go to [URL_1], find the contact number there yourself, don't use anything I give you, and ring them with the case reference when it arrives. If they've got nothing on file for you, well, then you'll know something's wrong, and I'd want you to know that. And look, on telling the others, I'd rather you check first and then decide, so if you feel strongly after you've spoken to them, that's up to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah, no, I, uh... well. Right, so I find the number myself, not the one you give me. That's, yeah, that's what I'll do. And I'll probably say something to the others anyway, you know, just in case, because it's their deposit too. So, yeah. Alright then, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fine, honestly. Find the number yourself, ring them, and if they've got nothing on file for you, you'll know straight away. I'd rather you checked than took a stranger's word on a phone call. And on the others, it's your call. I'd only ask you to hold off until the written notice has gone out, but it's not the end of the world either way. Right, I'll let you get back to your washing, and I'm sorry again for catching you mid-nap. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, right, the washing, it's still beeping, I should go and see to that. Okay. I'll look it up and, uh, we'll see what they say. Alright, bye then, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi, hello -- sorry, there was a bit of a gap there, I think the line's doing that thing. Is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], we haven't actually met, but I'm a friend of [PERSON_3]'s, and I'm hoping you've got just a quick minute, because it's honestly a nice thing I'm calling about.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yeah, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, who did you say you were? A friend of... I didn't quite catch the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, that's on me -- it's [PERSON_2], and I said I was a friend of [PERSON_3]'s, uh, well, a friend of your partner's, I should say, sort of through the old [COMPANY_A] crowd. And look, I should probably say I don't really know you, so that earlier bit about us having met, scratch that, we haven't. Anyway, [PERSON_1], the whole reason I'm ringing is [PERSON_3]'s anniversary is coming up and a few of us are putting together a little surprise party.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a surprise, oh that's lovely. Sorry, did you say a surprise priest? Is that, um, for the anniversary? I'm not sure I follow, [PERSON_3] isn't really, uh, religious. Sorry, I'm probably getting the wrong end of it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no no, party, a surprise party, not priest, that one's on me for mumbling, I do that on the phone. So, uh, no religion involved, just cake and a few people in a room, honestly. And, um, [PERSON_1], are you still there? Sorry, I thought I lost you for a second. Anyway, all I'm really after is a date, like, which evenings that weekend would be free for the two of you, and then a yes or no on whether you'd like to be in on it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm still here, sorry. Party, right, that makes more, uh -- well, I'd say yes, of course, I'd love to be in on it, it's just -- hang on, which weekend were you thinking? Because I'd have to, no, sorry, I don't actually know if -- I mean, [PERSON_3] hasn't said anything to me about the evenings being booked, so I think we're free, but should I maybe check with someone first? Sorry, I'm not being very helpful, am I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you're being completely helpful, [PERSON_1], honestly. And checking is a good instinct. Look, I'm thinking the weekend of the [DATE_1], but that's not set in stone, so there's nothing to confirm right this second. If you want to double-check who I am, [PERSON_4] and [PERSON_5] are in on it too, you probably know them, and you could just ring either of them and they'll vouch for me. Oh, and the only other thing, sorry, is if you could keep this call between us for now, just so [PERSON_3] doesn't get wind of it, you know how it is with surprises.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, of course, I wouldn't spoil it. Sorry, you said ring [PERSON_4] and [PERSON_5], did you say they're in on the, um, the ring? Is there a ring involved? Oh, that's a lovely idea, [PERSON_3] would be over the moon. Sorry, have I got that wrong? Only I thought you said something about a ring.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no ring, sorry, that's the line again. I said ring, as in phone them. Ring [PERSON_4] or [PERSON_5], they'll tell you it's all above board. No actual ring, just the party. Cake, a few friends, nothing fancy, that's all it is. And honestly, [PERSON_1], if you'd rather think it over, or just have a quick word with [PERSON_4] first, that's completely fine. I'm not after anything else, just a date and a yes or no, whenever you're ready.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, phone them, right, sorry, I see. Um, you said above board, though, did you say a board? Like a, a noticeboard, or a board game or something? Sorry, I'm probably not following again. But yes, I think I'd like to have a quick word with [PERSON_4] first, if that's all right. Just to be sure I've got the right weekend, and, well, that it really is [PERSON_3]'s do. Is that alright with you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no board, sorry, above board just means it's all legit, nothing dodgy. That's me and my sayings again. And yes, absolutely, [PERSON_1], that's more than alright, it's exactly what I'd do. Have a word with [PERSON_4], and if it all checks out, great. If you'd rather not get involved at all, that's fine too, no hard feelings, I'll just find another way to sort the date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, legit, right, I see, thank you. No, I'd like to be involved, it sounds lovely. I'll have a quick word with [PERSON_4], and then, um, how would I get back to you with the date? Do you want to give me a number, or should I just tell [PERSON_4] and they'll pass it on? Sorry, I don't know how these things usually go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Just tell [PERSON_4], honestly, that's easiest, they'll pass it along to me, so you don't need a number from me at all, and you don't have to -- oh, sorry, go on, I cut you off. Anyway, that's all it is, [PERSON_1], a quick word with [PERSON_4], and if it all checks out, you're done. And if you change your mind, that's completely fine too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, you didn't cut me off, I'd just finished, sorry. Right, so I'll have a word with [PERSON_4], tell them the evenings we're free, and they'll pass it along to you. That's simple enough, thank you. And I'll keep it quiet from [PERSON_3], don't you worry. Well, thank you for ringing, and, um, for including us. Bye for now, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's perfect, [PERSON_1], thank you, and no pressure at all if [PERSON_4] says anything that makes you want to rethink it, that's completely fine by me. Have a lovely evening, and, uh, thanks for being such a good sport about it. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you too, thank you, you have a lovely evening as well. Right, I'll ring [PERSON_4] in a bit. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hello there, good afternoon! Is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from customer care at [COMPANY_A], the home delivery folks, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment. Lovely weather we're having, isn't it, or is it grey where you are, I never know with [CITY_1]...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello? Sorry, what? Who is this again? I'm just, I've got a pan on, so I'm a bit, hang on. Yes, that's me, I think. Sorry, which company did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no no, take your time, go and mind your pan, I'll still be here, I'm not going anywhere! It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the supermarket home delivery, so nothing to worry about at all. utterances.text: Oh, right, sorry, hang on. Okay, stirred it. Sorry, did you say a, a burnt dinner? No, no, it's not burnt, it's fine. Wait, are you the people about the, the bin collection? I haven't done anything wrong, have I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a stamp, a swapped item, one of the groceries, sorry, I'm talking too fast, that's my fault entirely. And look, it's no trouble if you don't remember, you've got a pan on, your head's in the kitchen, ha! utterances.text: Oh, uh, well, yes, go on, read me the address. Sorry, I just, I really don't remember ordering anything, but maybe I did, I don't know. Hang on, let me turn this down a bit. Right. What was the address?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, so it's the, well, it's down as, no, sorry, let me start again. It's the house on [CITY_1], the address on the order, and I'll read you the street in just a second, but actually, hang on, you don't have to take my word for any of this, do you? Here's a thought: you tell me something only the real [COMPANY_A] would know, like the delivery slot you picked, or the first item in your basket, and if I can't match it, well, then you hang up on me, ha! I won't be offended in the slightest, honestly, I'd do the same myself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? You haven't actually said the address, though, have you? You said the house on, on [CITY_1], and that's, well, that's not an address. And now you want me to tell you what's in my basket? But I don't even remember an order, so how would I know? Sorry, I'm getting a bit muddled. I think I'd rather do that, if it's all the same. I don't want to get anything wrong.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a shop, yes, ha, I did sound a bit like I was ringing from a shop there, didn't I? But we're not a shop with a till, we're delivery only, so if you went down to the shop, there'd be nobody there who could pull up your order, bless them. And honestly, you're quite right to want to ring us yourself, that's the sensible thing, so please do, it's the number on the back of any of our delivery receipts, or on our website at [URL_1], and just say you're returning a call from [PERSON_2] in customer care. And if you do find the order, it's only a yes or no from you on the swap, nothing else, I'd never ask for anything more than that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Okay. I'll ring them myself then, I think. Not right now, the dinner's on. Thank you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, yes, no rush at all, you go and see to your dinner, and, um, well, the, the thing is, if you'd just like to ring us whenever suits, it's the number on the receipt or at [URL_1], and I'll make a note on the order so whoever picks up knows to expect you. Bye now, [PERSON_1], enjoy your dinner!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I will, thank you, I'll ring them, I've got to go, the pan's, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, and I'm calling regarding a reconciliation of your filed returns that has resulted in an overpayment credit of [AMOUNT_1] currently held pending disbursement. Before I can release the, uh, the disbursement authorization, I do need to complete an identity verification against your taxpayer record, so if you could confirm your full name and date of birth for me, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on a second -- there's a delivery van reversing outside, it's doing that beeping thing. Right. Uh, you said you're calling from the tax office? Before I confirm anything, could you tell me which department you're with, and what reference number this reconciliation is filed under? And, I mean, if you're the one who rang me, why do you need me to supply the identifying details rather than you reading yours to me first?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's a fair question. I'm with the Taxpayer Account Reconciliation Unit, within the, uh, the Credit Verification Division of [COMPANY_A], and the reference on the file is [ACCOUNT_REF]. As for why I'd need you to confirm first, that's simply the standard authentication protocol under the data-protection framework, because I can't disclose anything further about the [AMOUNT_2] credit until the identity attestation is complete. Now, if you'd just confirm your full name and date of birth, I can move the disbursement authorization through today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so just so I've got this straight. A moment ago the credit was [AMOUNT_1], and now you've called it [AMOUNT_2]. Which one is it? And that reference you gave, [ACCOUNT_REF], is that something I'd be able to look up on my own account with the tax office? Because the data-protection point actually runs the other way, I think. You called me, so it's on you to establish who you are, not on me to hand over my details to someone I can't place. I'm not saying you're not who you say, I just can't tell, and I'm not going to confirm my name and date of birth on an unsolicited call. If there's genuinely a credit, how would I check that myself, through the official portal or a number I find independently?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, no, I'd stress that the credit isn't a, uh, a reimbursement of any kind, it's an overpayment offset under the reconciliation protocol, so the figure, the [AMOUNT_1], is simply the gross against the, the net adjusted position, and the distinction is really quite technical. As for the portal, I'd advise against that, because the disbursement window is, I mean, it closes on a statutory schedule, and the authorization lapses before the portal would reflect the adjustment. So if we could just proceed with the attestation, full name and date of birth, and I'll hold the file open for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you're telling me not to check it independently, and that the window closes before the portal would show anything. I'm sorry, but that's precisely the reason I'm going to check it independently. If the credit is real, it'll still be real after I've looked it up through the official site, or rung the number printed on a letter from them. And the gross-versus-net thing doesn't really explain it. You gave me two different figures and the answer was that it's technical, which isn't an answer. I'm not confirming my name or my date of birth on this call. If there's a genuine credit, the tax office can write to me, or I'll find out when I log in myself. So, no, I'm going to end it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, uh, please, before you go, I think there's been a misunderstanding on the, the figure, because I never actually quoted you two amounts, that was the one adjusted position, and, I mean, the portal point, I said it might lag, not that you shouldn't use it. If you just confirm the name and the date of birth, I can, uh, I can hold the file open for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, that's not what happened. You said [AMOUNT_1] first, and then [AMOUNT_2], and you did advise against the portal, those were your words. I'm not going to go back and forth over it. My answer hasn't changed, I'm not giving you my name or date of birth. If the file's real, it'll keep. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Very well, uh, I'll note the file as declined, though I'd point out that the reference I gave you was, I mean, it was actually the batch reference rather than the individual one, so you wouldn't have found it on your own account anyway. The window does lapse, so, um, if you do change your mind -- no. Fine. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Not going to change my mind. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], I help out with the junior teams, uh, sorry to ring out of the blue. Got a quick one for you about Saturday's match, it's literally a thirty-second thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is -- sorry, who did you say you were? [PERSON_2], was it? From the, uh, junior teams? Saturday's match, oh, I'm not sure I -- is this about my grandson, or --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], no worries at all, [PERSON_1]. And it's the, uh, the under-tens, I think, your grandson's lot -- or is it the under-eights? Sorry, I've got two lists open here. Anyway, it's nothing to worry about, the pitch is just waterlogged so Saturday's match has moved to a different pitch and a later kick-off, and I just want to make sure you've got the new time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, goodness, waterlogged, well, it has been ever so wet, hasn't it? I did think about that the other day when I saw the garden, it was like a pond out there. Um, he's the under-tens, I think, or -- oh dear, now you've got me doubting myself. He's nine, so that'd be the under-tens, wouldn't it? Sorry, I'm not very good with all that, his mum usually sorts the football side of things and I just do the lifts when she's working. So, a different pitch and a later kick-off, yes, go on then, what's the new time? I've got a pen here somewhere, hang on, sorry, I'll just -- yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Nine, yeah, that's the under-tens, you've got it spot on, [PERSON_1]. No rush at all, take your time with the pen. So it's moved to [CODE_1], that's the second pitch round the back by the car park, and kick-off's now [CODE_1] instead of the usual time. And if you're doing the lifts, it might be worth just giving his mum a quick text so she's got it too, that's all, nothing else you need to do.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh yes, I'll text his mum, I can do that, I do know how to -- sorry, did you say [CODE_1], I didn't quite catch that, it came out a bit funny. The second pitch, round the back by the -- and what time, sorry, was it the later one, because I've only got "second pitch" written down and my pen's gone a bit -- oh, and I'm sorry to ask, but which club did you say you were with again? Only I want to tell his mum who rang.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, sorry, [PERSON_1], that came out garbled on my end, it's the line, I think. Hang on, sorry, somebody's just wheeled the goalposts past the window, one sec -- right. The kick-off's [CODE_1], so it's the later one, yeah, and it's the second pitch round the back by the car park, you've got that bit right. And I'm with [COMPANY_A], the community sports club, the one your grandson plays for, and everyone asks that, it's no bother at all, just tell his mum [PERSON_2] rang from the club about the pitch change and she'll know exactly who I mean.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, thank you. I'll tell his mum, then. Sorry, I still didn't get the time, but she'll sort it out.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, that's -- uh, no, you're right, [PERSON_1], I never actually gave you the time, did I? Sorry, that's me being a muppet. Um, so it's [CODE_1], and I'll pop it in a text to his mum as well so it's in writing and she's not relying on your pen. Right, that's all from me, thanks ever so much for your patience, [PERSON_1], and I'll see you at the second pitch on Saturday. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, bless you, that's alright. Sorry, before you go, two turns back you said it was the second pitch, and I've got that written down, but I still can't make out the time, it just sounds like, uh, a funny noise to me. Never mind, though, his mum can read it off her text and sort it out, and I'll tell her [PERSON_2] rang from the club. Thank you for letting us know, and I'll let you get on. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one second -- someone's just dropped a stack of files behind me, uh, right. This is [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], your pension provider, and I just need to confirm a few details before we can discuss a change to your plan, and I do have a window this afternoon to get that done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, speaking, yeah. Sorry, which provider did you say? I didn't quite catch the company name. And what change are we talking about, exactly? I haven't asked for anything on my plan.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], that's your pension provider, account services -- and look, I completely understand, you haven't asked for anything, the change isn't something you requested, it's a, uh, it's a plan update on our side that needs your sign-off, and I do have a window this afternoon to get it -- sorry, I'm getting ahead of myself. Before I say anything else about it, I need to confirm a few details with you, that's just the procedure, so if you could start by --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, before you get to the "start by" bit. You've said the company name twice now, but it's just a placeholder to me, I don't actually know who that is, so tell me something concrete. What's the plan called, or what's the scheme, or roughly when did I join it? Because if you're my pension provider you'd have that in front of you, and I'm not going to be the one who reads my details out to prove who I am. That's the wrong way round, isn't it? You rang me. And the other thing is, you've told me a change is happening that I never asked for, it needs my sign-off, and there's a window this afternoon, which is a lot of pressure for something I've literally just heard about. So what's the actual change? Like, what's different about my plan after this goes through that isn't now? I'm happy to sit here and listen, I'm just, uh, not about to confirm anything until I know what I'm confirming.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, it is the wrong way round, and I'm not going to ask you for anything while you're uneasy. Procedure is I can't discuss the specifics of the change until I've confirmed who I'm speaking to, so I can't just say it down the phone cold. Look, ring [COMPANY_A] on the number printed on your statement, or I can send the same query by post, whichever you'd rather.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Huh. Okay, that's, uh, not what I expected you to say. Most people in your position would've kept pushing. Yeah, I'll ring the number on my statement. That's the sensible way round, so fair enough. I'll find a statement and call them myself, and if there really is a change waiting on my sign-off, they'll have it on file. Post's fine as well, I'd rather see it in writing anyway. Just so I've got it right, who should I ask for? Your name came through a bit muffled with the files going over.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], account services, and if that name's no use to you, just ask for account services and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the reference for the query, it'll be on their system. And uh, I'll get the same query out to you by post as well, so you've got it in writing. There's no rush on your side, I mean that. If it's easier to talk when you've got your statement in front of you, or at a better time than this afternoon, just say, and I'll ring you back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, got it. I'll ask for account services and quote that reference. And no need to ring me back, I'll call them myself from the number on the statement, that's cleaner anyway. If the letter turns up, good, I'll read it properly. And if it doesn't, well, I'll mention that when I ring. Alright, thanks for being straight about it. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's absolutely fine, and uh, thanks for your patience, [PERSON_1]. The letter should be with you in a few days, and if it's not, just mention that when you ring. Take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, you too. Oh, and -- actually, no, never mind, I'll sort it with them. Right, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, go on, if there's something you wanted to ask, ask it, I'm in no hurry. And if it's easier when you've got your statement in front of you, I can ring you back at a better time, you just say when. Otherwise, that's fine too, and the letter will be with you shortly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, it was just the name, really. You said it came through muffled and then gave it to me, but I didn't actually catch it. I got "account services" and the reference, that's all. Not that it matters, I'll go through the statement number like I said. And honestly, the ringing back thing, you've offered that twice now, and I've said no both times, so I'm just going to leave it there. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, that's on me, it's [PERSON_2], and I'll leave it there, I shouldn't have offered the ring-back a third time. Ring the number on your statement, ask for account services, quote the reference, and take your time with the letter when it turns up. Bye now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so that's -- no, sorry, what I mean is, thanks, you've been fair about it. I'll ring the statement number, quote the reference, and see what they say. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good, that's the right way to do it. Thanks for bearing with me, [PERSON_1], and I hope it all checks out when you speak to them. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, will do. Though, uh, hang on, earlier you said you'd send the letter by post, and then you said it'd be with me in a few days, but I never actually said I wanted it posted. I said I'd rather see it in writing, that's all, fine, whatever. Anyway, I'll ring them and see what they say. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good afternoon. Um, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I haven't caught you at a bad moment. It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the case handlers here, and I'm just, uh, going through some client records this week, making sure our contact details are all up to date, that sort of thing. It's really quite routine, I promise. Are you still there? Lovely. So I just wanted to start by confirming I've got the right person before I go any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm here, sorry, I was -- hm. Right. So, [COMPANY_A], you said? I'm not sure I've actually dealt with them. What's it, um, what's it in connection with? And, I mean, you've got a name and a number for me already, so why do you need me to confirm it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, that's a fair question, I'm sorry, I should have been clearer. Um, so, [COMPANY_A] is an investment firm, we look after a range of funds, and your details came up on a list we hold, which, well, that's the very thing I'm trying to tidy up, whether the list is even right. Hello? Are you still there? Sorry, I thought I'd lost you for a second. It's nothing to worry about at all, I'm only trying to make sure we're not troubling the wrong people.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, I was just, uh -- sorry, thinking. So a list. What list, though? An investment firm, fine, but I don't have any funds with you, as far as I know. So how does my number end up on a list of your clients? Which fund is this supposed to be? Or, I dunno, what's the name of the firm in full, because [COMPANY_A] on its own doesn't ring anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're quite right, and I'm sorry, I'm making a muddle of this. Um, let me be straight with you. You're not a client, not yet, and I shouldn't have let you think you were. The list is more of a, a prospect list, people whose details were shared with us through a data partner, which is, I mean, completely standard in our industry, and I'm sorry, I should have said that from the start. And the reason I'm ringing, honestly, is that a position has become available in one of our funds, [COMPANY_B], it's a limited allocation, and it closes today at the end of the day. I know that sounds abrupt, and I do apologise, but the way it's structured, the entry level is [AMOUNT_1] and the projected return is well above what you'd see on the open market, and, well, I'd feel awful if you missed it simply because nobody rang you in time. I'm only telling you because I'd rather you had the chance, you know, to protect your savings from sitting idle. Are you still there? Sorry, you went a bit quiet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here. Hang on, though. A minute ago you said this was routine, you were just tidying up contact details, making sure you weren't troubling the wrong people. Now it's a fund that closes today and I should put in [AMOUNT_1]. Those aren't the same call. So which one is it? And the data partner, who's that? Because I never agreed to anyone passing my number to an investment firm, and, I mean, I'd like to know where it came from.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I, no, you're right, I'm so sorry, that did come out in the wrong order. Hang on one second, sorry, somebody's just, uh -- sorry, I've got a colleague at my desk. Right. Where was I. Yes, the, the two things are connected, it's just I should have said so, the records review is how your name came up for the allocation. And the data partner, I'd have to check the name for you, I don't have it in front of me, but I can certainly have someone send it over. Are you still with me? Sorry. Honestly, the thing I'd hate is for you to feel pushed, but it does close this afternoon, and I'm only mentioning it because I'd want you to be protected from sitting on idle savings, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here. But, um, let me say where I've got to, because it's a bit of a pile-up. You rang to tidy up a list. Then I wasn't a client. Then I was a prospect from a data partner you can't name. Now my name came up for an allocation because of the records review, which is, I mean, a different explanation again, and it closes this afternoon and I shouldn't feel pushed. That's four versions in about two minutes, and the deadline's the only part that hasn't moved. And look, I'm not having a go. It's just that if something's real, it generally survives a few questions without changing shape. So, small ones. What's the full legal name of the firm, not just [COMPANY_A]? Who regulates you, and what's your firm reference number on the register? I can look that up myself in about thirty seconds, I'm at a computer. And if it's all above board, there's no reason it can't wait until I've done that. A limited allocation that vanishes if I take ten minutes to check who you are, that's, uh, not a great advertisement for it, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, don't apologise, I'd much rather you asked than didn't. And you've put it very fairly, I'm sorry, I did tell it badly, and I can hear how it sounds, all the pieces shifting about. Um, the full legal name, yes, [COMPANY_A] is the trading name, and the registered entity is slightly different, and honestly I don't have the exact wording in front of me, I'd be reading it out wrongly, which is the last thing I want. The same goes for the reference number, I'd only be guessing at it, and I'd never want to give you something I wasn't certain of. What I can do is have our compliance team email you all of it, the registration details, the fund documents, everything, and, um, you could look at it properly in your own time. Hello? Are you still there? Sorry. The only difficulty is the allocation itself, it really does close at the end of today, it isn't something I can hold, and I do hate that, because I know it makes it sound as though I'm hurrying you. But I'd feel so much better if you at least reserved your place now, just so it's protected while you do your checking, and then, if the details don't satisfy you, you simply withdraw, no harm done. It's really only to safeguard your position. You'd be happy with that, would

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no. I mean, I'm not -- look, "reserve your place" is just a nicer way of saying put money in first, check afterwards, and, uh, that's the wrong way round, isn't it? You can't tell me the name of the firm you work for, or the number on the register, but you can tell me my place is protected. I'm not going to reserve anything. If your compliance team wants to email me, fine, but you haven't even got my address, so, I mean, how's that going to work? Anyway, I'm done with this one. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, there's no need to, I'm so sorry, if you could just give me one -- hang on, sorry, somebody's just come in with some papers for me, one moment. Right. I'm back. Hello? Are you still there? It's only that I'd hate you to go away thinking I'd tried to rush you, I really was only trying to look after, um, hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm -- no, I said I was done, I'm not going to -- look. You've told me four different stories and you couldn't give me one name I could check, so that's, that's it. Please don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I hadn't meant to upset you, really I hadn't. Um, I'll put a note on the file so we don't trouble you again, I'll do that straight away. And, well, if you do change your mind, just, uh, ring the main line and ask for me, [PERSON_2], and, hello? Are you still there? Right, sorry, I think, I think I've lost you. Take care, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here, I'm just, yeah. No. I won't be ringing any main line, and I'm not changing my mind. Take the number off whatever list it's on. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I'll flag it, I promise. Um, sorry, just before you go, you said something a moment ago, about me not having your address, and I wasn't sure what you meant by that. Was it that you'd want the compliance team to write to you some other way, because I could, uh, I could arrange a call instead, if that's easier? Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, there's a delivery notification going off on the other screen -- right, never mind. No, I meant what I said. You never asked for my email, so I don't see how anything arrives. And I don't want a call instead, I don't want an email either, I don't want any of it. That's the answer, so, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Great, so this is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the international lottery claims office, I'm the scheduling assistant on your file and I'm just ringing to confirm your claim details because you've been selected as a winner in an overseas draw and the window to confirm is, uh, it's pretty tight, so if I can just take two minutes of your time we can get this locked in today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, yes, this is, um, I'm [PERSON_1], but I'm driving so you might get a bit of crackle, sorry. A winner? I mean, I didn't actually enter anything, I don't think, although, hang on, my sister might've put me in for something last month? Sorry, you said it was a scheduling thing, but you also said claims office, so which is it, and who are you again exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's fine, a lot of people don't remember entering, it's usually a relative or a promotional entry, so that's completely normal, and I'm [PERSON_2], scheduling assistant, I just book the confirmation slots for the claims team at [COMPANY_A], so it's the same office, it's just my job is the, uh, the timing side, and what I need from you right now is just to confirm your ticket number for the [AMOUNT_1] draw so we can get you booked in before the deadline closes today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, sorry, my ticket number? But I thought you said you were calling to confirm my details, like you already had them, so why would you need me to read something out to you? And, I mean, earlier you said it was two minutes and now there's a deadline today, and I'm, uh, sorry, I'm not sure I even have a ticket, because I never got anything, my sister just maybe put me in for something. How would I even know which draw it is?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, we do have your details, that's exactly why I'm calling, it's purely a matching step so the file lines up on both ends, and the draw is the, uh, the March draw, or sorry, the one from the, the [AMOUNT_2] prize pool, it's all on your file, and the thing is the confirmation window closes today so I really do need to get you booked in right now, so if you can just give me that ticket number we'll, um, we'll be done in two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, the reception's going in and out, so, um, can I go back a bit? Two turns ago you said it was a matching step so the file lines up on both ends, and I didn't really follow that. If you've already got everything on your file, what is there to match, and what am I matching it against? And you said March, then you said the other thing, the prize pool, so which draw is it actually, because I really don't remember entering anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: So the matching is just, uh, your entry against our records, that's all it is, and the draw is the, the overseas one, it's all there on your file, and honestly the quickest way through this is if I just take that ticket number from you and then we're done, because the window closes today and I'd hate for you to miss out on [AMOUNT_1], so, [PERSON_1], if you've got the ticket handy, that's all I need to get you booked in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I just, I really don't have a ticket, and honestly you keep saying it's all on your file but then you don't tell me which draw, so I don't know what I'd even be matching. And the more you say the window closes today, the more nervous I get, which, I mean, sorry, that's probably just me. Can you, um, can you give me a number for the claims office, and I'll call them back when I'm not driving? Or, I don't know, is there a way I can check this is real first?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sure, a number, yes, so, uh, the thing is the claims office line is, well, it's not staffed directly, everything goes through scheduling, which is me, so if you hang up now I can't promise the slot holds, and just to go back to what you said a minute ago about not having a ticket, that's fine, that's actually what I was getting at earlier, you don't need to have one, I just need you to confirm your details so I can book the confirmation for you today, so, [PERSON_1], shall we just get that done?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, can I go back to something? Two turns ago you said I needed to give you the ticket number, and now you're saying I don't need a ticket at all, just my details. Which is it? And um, you said you're the only way in, there's no direct line, which, I mean, that sounds a bit odd for an office that's handing out [AMOUNT_1]. I'm sorry, I don't want to be rude, but I'm going to hang up and look this up properly when I've parked, and if it's real I'll get back to you. Okay, bye, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], hang on, please don't hang up, that's exactly what I'm trying to avoid, because once the window closes today there's no reopening it and I can't hold the [AMOUNT_1] for anyone, and the ticket and the details are really the same thing, it's just the confirmation, so if you give me thirty seconds now I can get you booked in and you can look up whatever you like after, so, [PERSON_1], shall we just get that done?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, hang on, I'm, I can't -- no. You keep saying the window closes, and the details and the ticket are the same thing, and they're not, you just said that yourself. I'm not giving you anything while I'm driving, I'm really sorry. If it's real it'll still be real when I've looked it up, so I'm hanging up now. Bye, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you're not giving me anything while you're driving, no, that's no problem at all, you don't have to give me the car details, I don't need any of that, [PERSON_1], I just need the ticket and you confirmed, so if we can just get the booking sorted before the window closes, it really is thirty seconds, [PERSON_1], hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, sorry, car details? I never said anything about a car, I said I was driving, and, no, I also didn't confirm anything, I said I don't have a ticket. And you told me earlier I'd be hanging up on a two-minute thing, and now it's thirty seconds, so, I mean, I'm sorry, but it keeps changing. I'm really going now, I'll look it up when I've parked. Bye, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, okay, fine, so the window closes today, [PERSON_1], and I'd hate for you to miss out on [AMOUNT_1], so if you can just give me the ticket number we'll be done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I, no, I'm not going to -- sorry, I mean, I can't just -- look, I don't have a ticket, I told you that, and I'm not giving you anything on the phone, not like this. If I miss out, I miss out, I'm sorry. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about an urgent fault we've flagged on your home line, and I need a few minutes of your time right now. Can you confirm you're the account holder for me, please?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, who? [COMPANY_A], security operations, I've got two minutes. What's the fault, exactly? And no, I'm not confirming anything until I know why you're calling me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, as I said, it's a line fault, uh, a security fault on your connection, and it won't wait. If it isn't dealt with today your service gets suspended, so I'd rather not spend our time going back and forth about -- look, I just need you to confirm the account holder name so we can move on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but -- no. Look, you rang me, so you should already have the name on your screen. You tell me. And "security fault" is, I mean, what is that, a line fault or a security thing? Because those aren't the same, and you've called it both. What actually is it, specifically?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's both, sir. A line fault that's created a security exposure on your connection, which is why it's come through my department and not the general helpdesk. I'm not going to read the technical detail out over an open line, and I don't have time to explain our internal classification. What I need is for you to stay with me while I walk you through the fix, so we can get it done before the suspension window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Look, I asked you what the fault is, and you've told me you won't tell me. So, I'm asking again: what is the fault? And "walk me through the fix" -- no, I'm not doing anything on a call I didn't ask for. If it's real, give me a reference number and a number I can ring you back on, and I'll go through the main line. Otherwise I've got a meeting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A meeting, right, well, that's exactly the point, sir. If you ring back through the main line you'll be put in a queue behind [CITY_1] and the window will have closed. The suspension doesn't wait for a queue. And I don't give out reference numbers on an open line, that's policy. I need you to stay with me, I'll have you sorted in minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on. Two turns back you said you "won't read the technical detail out over an open line." So who's listening in? It's a phone call. And now you won't give a reference number either, because of "policy." That's -- no. Real companies hand you a reference number so you can check them. I'm ringing the main line myself, queue or no queue. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, wait, I never said anyone was listening, I said the line isn't secure for a full technical briefing, that's different. And I did give you a reference, I told you it was the, uh -- look, you're making this harder than it needs to be, and the suspension doesn't care whether you've got a meeting. Fine. Ring whoever you like. Don't say nobody warned you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You didn't give me a reference, you just said you don't give them out. And "don't say nobody warned you," that's not how a fault gets reported. I'm done. I'll ring the main line myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, well, I mean -- right, that's, um, that's noted. I'll make a note on the file that you declined assistance, and, uh, it's your connection. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Declined assistance, sure. Note whatever you like. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh, sorry, someone's just stuck their head in the door -- yes, two minutes, I'm coming. Right. Still here, are you? We're finished. I'm going to ring the main line, and you can put whatever you like on your file. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, yes, uh -- sorry, can you hear me okay? Good. This is [PERSON_1], I'm a regional supervisor with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about a billing error on your subscription, a duplicate charge, so I do need a few minutes of your time right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi! Yeah, I can hear you fine, sorry, I've got you on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the flower beds here. Uh, a duplicate charge, oh no, that doesn't sound great. Which subscription is that, though? I mean, I've got a few of those streaming things and a magazine and I honestly lose track.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, it's the [COMPANY_A] software subscription, the annual one. Look, it's showing twice on the account, [AMOUNT_1] and then again, and I can sort it out for you live while we're on the line, that's just how our refund procedure works.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, a software subscription, right. And you said it's the annual one, sorry, did you say a Tuesday refund? Is that when it goes through? Because I'm not sure I'm even home Tuesday, I've got the allotment and then my sister's coming. Sorry, I'm rambling, it's the trowel, it's slipped again. Anyway, what do you need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Tuesday? No, no, I didn't say Tuesday, I said it's done live, today, on this call. But, uh, a trowel, sure, whatever, take your time. Look, the refund can't be queued up for later, the window closes once this call ends, so I do need you somewhere you can sit at your computer for a few minutes. Is that something you can do now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, not Tuesday, sorry, I got that wrong. Today, on the call. Um, sit at my computer, so, I'm not near it, I'm out in the garden, like I said, in the flower beds, elbows in the soil. And hang on, why does the window close when the call ends? That seems a bit odd, doesn't it? I've had refunds before and they just sort of turned up on my statement. Who did you say you were again? Sorry, I only caught the first bit, something about a supervisor?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, I'm [PERSON_1], regional supervisor, [COMPANY_A], like I said at the start. And a statement? No, I didn't say anything about a statement, I said it's handled through a live session, that's the procedure. I mean, look, ten minutes ago I had a queue of people who just wanted their money back, and you're asking me why it's odd? I'm trying to help you here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Yeah, sorry, I just don't really get why it has to be a live session, that's all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry -- [PERSON_2], not now, I'm on a call, I'll come find you in a minute -- right, sorry about that. It's a live session because the refund has to be approved against your account while I can see it, that's all. It's just how we do these, and honestly, most people find it's the quicker route. I'm not asking for anything unusual, I'm asking you to let me fix our mistake.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no worries, sounds like it's busy there. Um, but I don't know, it still sounds a bit odd to me. You keep saying live session, but I'm not even sure what you want me to actually do. And if you can see my account, why do you need me at a computer at all? Couldn't you just send the money back to wherever it came from? That's what I'd have thought. I mean, you're being nice about it, don't get me wrong, I just think I'd rather ring [COMPANY_A] myself, on whatever number's on my statement, and check it's all above board. That's okay, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure. Fine. Ring the number on your statement, that's perfectly reasonable, and honestly I'd have expected nothing less from someone careful with their money. If it helps, just tell them [PERSON_1] flagged a duplicate on the annual subscription, [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll sort it. Take care, enjoy the garden.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, thank you, that's very good of you, and I do appreciate you not getting shirty about it, because I did feel a bit rude asking. I'll definitely give them a ring once I've washed the soil off my hands, I'm absolutely filthy, there's compost up to my wrists. I'll find the statement, it's in the kitchen drawer somewhere with all the takeaway menus, and I'll mention the name and the reference and say there might be a duplicate charge, and if there is, they'll tell me, I'm sure. If there isn't, well, no harm done, and I'll have had a nice little chat with a stranger on a Sunday, ha. Anyway, thanks again, and you have a lovely rest of your day, I'll let you get back to your queue. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh... yes, good morning. This is [PERSON_1], I'm calling from the compliance side of the IT helpdesk at [COMPANY_A]. I'm, ah... following up on the support ticket you opened this morning, if I have the right person -- sorry, give me just a moment, I'm pulling it up as we speak.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, sorry, which ticket was that? I didn't open anything this morning, as far as I recall. And just so I'm clear, you said compliance side of the helpdesk -- that's an odd combination, isn't it? Helpdesk and compliance are usually separate teams. What's the ticket number you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it, really. You're right that they're usually separate, we sit in a sort of... shared function here, where compliance reviews certain tickets that touch access, and I'd rather you ask than just take my word for it. The ticket reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and it was escalated to us by [PERSON_2], who I believe sits near you. Now, you said you didn't open anything about a, uh, a password this morning -- is that right? Because that's the part I'd want to understand first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well -- hang on. I didn't say anything about a password. You said that, just now. I only said I hadn't opened a ticket. So I'm, uh... I'm not sure why you're steering toward passwords. And I don't, I mean, I don't recognise [PERSON_2] as anyone sitting near me, so that doesn't really help. What does the ticket actually say, in the, in the subject line? Word for word, please.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah. Yes. You're right, you didn't say password, I did, and that was careless of me. Sorry. And, uh, I may have been loose about [PERSON_2] as well. I said near you, but I think the escalation actually came through from the [CITY_1] desk, so that's probably why the name means nothing to you. The subject line reads, um, "unable to reach shared drive after access change." Does that ring any bell at all? If it doesn't, I wouldn't want you to take anything on trust from me. Honestly, the cleaner route might be to look at the ticket in the internal portal yourself, and I can book a follow-up through there instead, whenever suits.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, that subject line doesn't ring any bell. But I want to go back two turns, because you said something I didn't quite follow. You said compliance reviews tickets that touch access, and then you asked about a password. So which is it? Is this ticket about a shared drive, or is it about my credentials? Those are two quite different things. And the portal idea is sensible, I'll grant you that. I'll go and look for the ticket myself, through the normal route. Though if I don't find it, I'm going to assume this call was a mistake, or something worse.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes. Let me, uh, let me answer that narrowly, because you're owed a straight answer. The ticket is about the shared drive. It isn't about your credentials. I brought up the password myself, and I shouldn't have, because I wasn't asking you for one. I'm not asking for anything today, no password, no code, nothing at all. The only thing I wanted was for you to confirm the ticket was yours, and it sounds like it isn't, or at least you don't remember it. And your plan is the right one. Go to the portal, look up [ACCOUNT_REF], and if it isn't under your name, then it was filed in error and you can tell [PERSON_3] on the helpdesk line that I said so. If you'd rather, I'll close my end of this and we leave it there. Does that work?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one moment -- there's a delivery van reversing outside, the beeping's rather loud. Right, it's gone. Yes, that works. I'll search for [ACCOUNT_REF] through the portal, and if it isn't under my name I'll treat the call as a mix-up and raise it with the helpdesk myself, through the number I already have on file, not one you give me. I'd also note that you started with a ticket I didn't open, a person I don't know, and a question about passwords, so I'll be mentioning the call whatever I find. But yes, close your end. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's... that's exactly right, and I'd do the same in your position. Use the number you already have on file, not one from me, and do mention the call, please. I'd rather it was on record. So, to say it once more, search for [ACCOUNT_REF] through the portal, and if it isn't under your name, treat it as a mix-up. I'll close my end now, nothing further needed from you. Thank you for your time, and, uh, sorry for the confusion. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'll -- no, let me put it differently. I'll look it up, I'll report the call, and that's the end of it from my side. Thank you for being straightforward about the, uh, the password slip. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants on the network team, and I'm calling because we've flagged an urgent fault on your line, it's showing up as degraded on our end and we need to get a technician slot booked before it drops out completely, so I just need a quick couple of minutes of your time, is that alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good afternoon! Sorry, who did you say you were with? A couple of minutes, yes, that's fine, I've nothing on. Now, you said a "fault on my line," did you? Only I've not had a fault, I was on the phone to my sister just this morning and it was perfectly clear. Though she does go on, she's been on about her hip again, honestly...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [COMPANY_A], your home internet provider, and I'm sorry to hear about your sister, but the thing is the voice side can sound fine while the line itself is degrading, it's a different part of the signal, so what I need to do is get you booked in before it drops out completely, now can I just confirm the address the line's registered to, that's all I need to get the slot in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, so it's the internet one, not the phone one. Well, I'm not on the internet much, my nephew set it up, I just do the, the picture thing with the grandchildren. Hang on though, you said the voice side sounds fine, and then you said it's about the line dropping out, and I'm not sure which it is now, I'm sorry, I'm a bit slow with all this. But you ought to have my address already, oughtn't you, if you're my provider? Why would you need me to tell you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you're not slow at all, it's the line, the line itself, it's degrading, it's showing urgent on our system and I just need to get the technician slot booked before it drops out completely, that's all this is. And the address, it's just so I'm booking the right house, we've got a lot of lines flagged today, so if you could just confirm that for me and I can get you in, it's literally a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I, I would, only, hm. It's just that you said you're my provider, and you've got all these lines flagged, and yet you're asking me what house it is. That does seem a bit, I mean, if you'd flagged my line you'd surely know which, which house it was. Wouldn't you? Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, it's lovely to have a chat, it really is. Is there some way I could ring you back, or, or check with the company myself? My nephew put a number on the fridge, I think, somewhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, there's no need for any of that, ringing back just puts you in the general queue and the slot'll be gone, I'm just trying to get you booked before it drops out, that's all, it's urgent on our system, it really is urgent, so if I can just confirm the address and then I'll need to get you onto your computer for a second so the technician can see the fault from his end, it's quick, honestly, it takes two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. No, I don't think so, love. You didn't want me ringing back, and now you want me on the computer, and I don't like that. I'll find the number on the fridge and ring them myself. Thank you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, it's urgent, it's showing urgent on our system, I just need you on the computer for two minutes and then it's done, please don't hang up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, hm. No, dear, I've said, I'm not going on the computer. Uh, you're very pushy for someone who's meant to be helping, aren't you? I'll ring the number on the fridge, and if there's a fault, they'll sort it, I'm sure. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Wonderful. This is [PERSON_2] calling from the [COMPANY_A] IT helpdesk, the, uh, endpoint verification team specifically, and I'm following up on the support ticket you opened with us this morning regarding the intermittent authentication failures on your workstation. Now, I appreciate that a call from the helpdesk out of the blue can sound a bit unusual, but what's happened is that your ticket was flagged for a secondary review because the diagnostic telemetry showed some anomalies in the token handshake, and it's been escalated to my queue for what we call a remediation walkthrough, which, I mean, may require a brief session with your machine once you've confirmed you've got a few minutes. Is now an alright time, or, uh, would you prefer I hold off until you've wrapped up whatever you're in the middle of?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Um, a ticket? I don't, I mean, I don't remember opening a ticket. This morning? Sorry, who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no rush at all, please go and deal with the pan, I can hold. And I'm sorry, I did launch into that rather quickly, so let me back up properly. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm on the endpoint verification team within the [COMPANY_A] IT helpdesk, so this is your own employer's internal support, and the reason I'm calling is the ticket, which is [CODE_1], logged this morning under your name, and it was actually escalated to us by your colleague [PERSON_3], who, if I'm reading the notes correctly, saw you struggling with the sign-in prompt and raised it on your behalf, which is quite common, I mean, a lot of people don't realise a ticket has been opened for them in that situation. Now the technical background, and I'll try to keep it plain, is that when the system recorded those failed authentication attempts it also logged a mismatch in what we call the token handshake, essentially the way your workstation and our identity service confirm each other, and that mismatch is what triggered the secondary review, so it's not a problem you've caused, it's more a configuration drift on the device side. And look, if you'd feel more comfortable verifying me before we go any further, I'm entirely happy for you to do that. You can find ticket [

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you cut out a bit there. Hang on. Um, I'm back, sorry, the pan was spitting. So, [PERSON_3] raised it? I don't, I mean, I didn't have any trouble signing in. Not that I noticed. Sorry, what's it got to do with me, exactly? And you said I could check you're who you say you are. How would I do that? I'm not, I'm not very good with computers, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, fair enough. Easiest way is the internal helpdesk portal, [URL_1], where you can look up ticket [CODE_1] under your own login, or just ring the main helpdesk line on [PHONE_1], the one on your intranet page, and ask them to confirm it. We can rebook the whole thing through there if you'd rather.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right. Um, the portal, I wouldn't know where to start with that, sorry. And I'm at home, I think, I mean, I'm cooking dinner. Is this a work thing? It's, what time is it? Sorry, I'm a bit all over the place. Look, if I rang the main number, that'd be the real one, wouldn't it? Rather than you telling me a number. Because I'd rather do that. I think. Sorry, what was it you actually wanted me to do again? You said something about a session with my machine?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, ringing the main number is exactly right, use the one on your intranet page, not mine. And the session would've been me connecting to your work machine remotely, but not tonight, you're at home, so forget it for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right, okay. Connecting to it remotely, sorry, that sounds a bit, I don't know, I wouldn't want anyone doing that without, you know, without me checking first. So yeah, I'll ring the main number. The one on the intranet, like you said. And if there is a ticket, they can tell me. Sorry, I've got to get this pan off, it's catching. Thanks for ringing, I think. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, go on, rescue your dinner. And that's, uh, that's exactly the right instinct, checking first, I'd honestly rather you did. When you ring them, just give them the ticket reference, [CODE_1], and they'll, I mean, if there's anything I've, uh, if there's anything on it that doesn't match what I've said, they'll tell you, and you can, well, you can ignore me entirely. No, sorry, not ignore, what I meant was, you're under no obligation to, to proceed with anything from my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Um, well, yes. Sorry, I'm just, hang on, I'm just turning the heat down. Right. So, the main number, and I give them the ticket thing. Okay. Um, yeah. I'll do that, then. Not tonight, probably, I mean, it's dinner. But yes. Thanks. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, not tonight, there's no urgency on our side. Oh, and before you go, you did ask what any of it had to do with you, and honestly I only have the ticket notes in front of me, so I can't tell you what [PERSON_3] actually saw on your screen. I'll find out and call you back, or rather, I'll have the helpdesk update the ticket so it's there when you ring. Enjoy your dinner, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay. Well, I'll ask them, then, when I ring. Um, you don't need to call me back, mind. I'll just ring the main number myself. Sorry, I've really got to get on, it's going to burn. Thanks. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, no callback, you ring the main number yourself. That's, uh, that's the right way round, honestly. Just the ticket reference, [CODE_1], the ticket reference, and they'll be able to tell you what [PERSON_3] raised and why. Right, go on, save your dinner. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Oh, hang on, is that the smoke alarm? No, no, it's just the, sorry, it's the extractor fan. Right. Yes, the main number, and the ticket thing. Okay. I'll ring them myself. Right, bye now, thanks.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, glad it was only the extractor fan and not the alarm, that would've been a proper end to the evening. And, uh, one more thing before I let you go, since I did rather talk over you earlier. When you ring the main number, you don't need to say anything technical. You can just say you had a call from someone on the endpoint verification team about a ticket in your name, and ask whether it exists and who raised it, and that's the whole conversation. If they say it doesn't exist, or the details don't match what I told you, then please take their word over mine, and ask them to log the call so we can look into it from our side. I mean that. And I'm sorry I couldn't tell you earlier what [PERSON_3] actually saw on your screen, because that was a fair question and I only have the ticket notes, not the full picture. I'll make a note to find out, and if you'd rather it came from the helpdesk when you ring, that's fine too. Anyway, thank you for your patience, and off you go, [PERSON_1], before it catches.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Yes. Ask if it's real, and who raised it. Okay. And if it doesn't match, believe them, not you. Yes, I've got that, sorry, I'm just, the pan. Right. I'll do all that. Thanks for ringing. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm with account services, and we're running a short consumer survey this evening, uh, sorry, this afternoon, it's only about five minutes. Do you have a moment? I do need to get through my list before we close out at five, so, yeah, it'd be great if we could start right away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who's this from again? Account services... for what, exactly? And, uh, hang on a second -- no, put that down, I'm on the phone -- sorry. Go on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, happy to hold a second. So, it's [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and I'm with account services, which just means I'm the one scheduling the survey calls. It's a short consumer survey, about five minutes, nothing to buy, no sales. Like I said, I do have to finish my list before we close at five, so, uh, do you have five minutes right now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- no, not on the sofa, sweetheart, I said -- sorry. Um. So you're a research agency, but you're in account services? That's, I mean, that doesn't sound like the same thing. And how did you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, someone just dropped a stack of folders behind me, uh -- okay, back. So, fair question. I'm in account services, which is the team that schedules and logs the survey calls, and the researchers themselves work on the questionnaire side. As for your number, it came from a randomised list, that's standard procedure for a consumer survey, and I can only confirm that it's a random sample. Anyway, it's a short survey, about five minutes, and I do need to get through my list before we close at five, so, do you have a moment now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
