utterances.text: A randomised list. Right. And you can't tell me anything more than that? Because I'd like to know what company you actually are, like the real name, not just the letter thing. And what's the survey even about -- what are the questions?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, the name is [COMPANY_A], that's the agency, and the survey is about household shopping habits, things like which stores you use and how often. Nothing personal, no account details, no payment details, and I'd never ask for those. Participation is voluntary, you can stop any time, and, uh, I can tell you the full topic list once we begin. I do need to wrap up my list before we close at five, so, if you've got five minutes right now, we could start.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but see, that's the second time you've said [COMPANY_A] like it's a name I should recognise, and I don't, so that's not really telling me anything. And you'll tell me the full topic list once we begin? Why not now? If it's really just which stores I use and how often, that's one sentence, so why does it have to wait until I've agreed to start? And I keep noticing you bring up the five o'clock thing every time, like I'm meant to hurry, which, honestly, is making me less likely to say yes, not more. I've got a kid here who's about to pull the cushions off the sofa, I'm not in a rush for anything, so if there's a proper way I can check you are who you say you are, like a number I can look up myself and ring back, or a website, then, I mean, what is it? Because otherwise I think I'd rather not.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yes, that's fair, and, uh, sorry about the five o'clock thing, you're right, there's no need to hurry you. The topics are household shopping habits, which stores you use, how often, and roughly how you decide where to go, that's the whole list, I shouldn't have held it back. For checking on us, you can look up [COMPANY_A] at [URL_1], and there's a verification line at [PHONE_1] where you can confirm this is a genuine survey call. Obviously you'd want to look those up yourself rather than just trusting what I read out. And honestly, it sounds like right now isn't a great time with your little one, so, uh, would it be better if I called you back at a more convenient time? Just tell me when suits you and I'll note it down.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, well, that's better, thank you, but -- no, don't ring me back. I'll look the agency up myself and if I want to do it, I'll ring that number, but, uh, I'm not giving you a time. I don't do callbacks off a call I didn't expect. So, no, I'll leave it there. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], ticketing and venue booking, I'm a collections officer in the bookings department. I'm calling about the concert tickets on booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], the show's been rescheduled from the original date to a new date, and your tickets move with it automatically. Is this [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who is this? [COMPANY_A], ticketing -- and you said collections officer? That's, I mean, that's a strange job title for a call about a rescheduled show. And I'm at work right now, so, uh, what's this actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], and the title's a bit of a legacy thing, I'm in the bookings department, uh, I handle the accounts side when a show moves. It's only about the tickets. The show on booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF] has been moved, and I've got your seats down for the, uh, the evening performance on the new date. Sorry, I mean the matinee, the matinee on the new date, that's what's on my screen.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, evening or matinee? You said evening, then matinee. Which one is it? Because that's, I mean, that's kind of a big difference. And you still haven't told me what you actually need from me. Like, what's the call for? If the tickets just move automatically, why are you ringing me at work?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Matinee. Sorry, I misspoke, that was my slip. Booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], original date, new date, matinee performance, that's what's on the screen. Hang on, uh, [PERSON_3], can you put that on my desk, thanks -- sorry, someone's dropped a file on me. Right, the reason I'm calling is the new date can't be carried over without your say-so. If we don't hear back, the booking stays on the original date, which no longer exists, so it's flagged as void. That's just how the system treats it. Look, if you'd rather not take my word for it, ring the venue on the number they publish and ask them, or I can email the confirmation to the address on the booking. I'll note that you queried it and we can carry on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right, so -- matinee, and if I don't say yes it goes void. Hmm. Okay, so, um... I mean, that's quite a lot of pressure for a rescheduled gig, isn't it? Ringing the venue on their own number, yeah, that makes sense, I'd rather do that. But hang on, you said you'd email the confirmation, so which email address have you got on the booking? Just, uh, read me that back so I know it's the right one.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, so the address on the booking is -- sorry, I'm only showing it partly masked on my screen, I can see the first couple of characters and the domain but not the whole thing. I can't read you a full address I can't see, that wouldn't be right. What I can do is find out whether the department can confirm it for you, and call you back on this number. Would that work?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you can't see the address, but you want to call me back on this number. Uh, no, I don't think so, sorry. Something's off here, you changed evening to matinee, the title doesn't fit, and now the email's masked. I'll ring the venue myself on the number they publish, and if there's a real booking I'll sort it with them directly. Thanks, but, yeah, I'm going to leave it there. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, no, that's fine. Yeah. I'll note on the file that you're confirming with the venue directly, and, um, I'll find out about the email address and the title and have someone call you back, if you'd like that. Otherwise, ring the venue, that's the right thing to do. Okay, bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say someone'll call me back about the, uh, the tickle? No, the title, right. Yeah, no, don't bother, I'll sort it with the venue myself. Thanks anyway, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] here from [COMPANY_A], the supermarket delivery -- sorry, didn't mean to talk over you -- I'm just ringing about the order you put in online, quick one, won't take a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Uh, yeah, that's me. Which order was this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, sorry, yeah, uh, no worries -- the grocery order you placed online earlier, the one with the two-hour delivery window. I'm just ringing to confirm that window with you, [PERSON_1], and, um, to let you know one item's been swapped for a similar product, so it's just a quick yes or no from you on that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, I did -- well, I think I -- sorry, hang on, I've got something on the hob. Um. I did put an order in, yeah, but I -- what was the item? That's swapped, I mean. Which one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, take your time, [PERSON_1], go and stir your pot, I'm not going anywhere. So it's the, uh -- well, it's -- sorry, let me pull it up properly -- it's the [COMPANY_B] brand one that was out of stock, so we've put in a similar one instead, same size and everything. It's honestly just a yes or no, takes two seconds.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I'm back, it's fine. Um, the thing is, I didn't think I'd ordered anything for a two-hour slot. I thought I picked the evening one. But, I mean, maybe I did, I don't know. And you still haven't said which item it is. Is that -- what is it, the pasta? Or something else?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, fair enough, [PERSON_1], that's on me, I keep skipping past the actual item. Sorry. It's the pasta sauce, the one that was out of stock, and we've put a similar jar in its place, same size. And the slot, it's a two-hour window, so it'd be sometime in the evening, which is probably what you picked. Honestly, I can read you the whole order over the phone if it helps, it's all quick stuff.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, pasta sauce, right. Yeah, that's fine, I'm not fussy, a different jar is fine. Um, sorry, but -- you don't need anything from me for that, do you? Like, you're not going to ask me for card details or anything? Because I'm just a bit, I don't know, flustered, I've got the pan on. I think I'd rather just check it on the app after, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, [PERSON_1], nothing like that, I don't need a card or anything from you, honestly. The swap's fine, I'll mark it as a yes on my side, and that's all I was after. But checking the app is totally sensible, everyone does, and if you'd rather ring us back on the number you find yourself, that's absolutely fine too, go and save your dinner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay. Thanks. Sorry, can I just -- you said something a bit ago about the slot, the two-hour thing. You said it'd be sometime in the evening? Is that between, like, six and eight, or what? Because I'm sure I picked a particular time, and I just want to know what I'm checking for when I look in the app.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, so, hang on, sorry, [PERSON_1] -- somebody's just come up to my desk, one sec -- right, I'm back. Uh, so I don't actually have the exact hours in front of me right now, so I don't want to guess and have you sat waiting at the wrong time. It'll be on your order confirmation, whatever you picked is what's booked. So when you check the app, just look at the delivery slot and the pasta sauce line, and if either of those looks off, ring us on the number from the app or the website and the team will sort it out. Does that sound okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, that sounds fine. I'll have a look at the app once I've got this off the hob. Slot and the pasta sauce, right? Right. And if it's wrong I ring the number on the app, not, um, not this one. Okay. Thanks for ringing, sorry I was a bit all over the place. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, don't apologise, [PERSON_1], you're grand, everyone's got a pan on at this time of day. And yeah, that's exactly right, the number on the app, not this one. Oh, and just so I'm not leaving you muddled, earlier when I said the swap was a similar jar, same size -- that's all it is, nothing else in your order's changed, so it's only the one line to check. Right, go and rescue your dinner, and enjoy it. Bye for now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, cheers [PERSON_1]. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye -- oh, sorry, one thing. You said it was the, um, the pasta sauce, but earlier I thought you said it was a [COMPANY_B] one, and I don't really buy that brand. I think I'd have gone for something else. Anyway, I'll check the app. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's fair, [PERSON_1], the [COMPANY_B] one's the one that was out of stock, the swap's the other jar. Check the app, it'll show you both, and ring the number there if it's not right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right. Um. Okay, so the [COMPANY_B] one's the one that's gone, and the other jar's the swap. Yeah. Sorry, I'm just -- I'll look at the app. That's what I'll do. Right, bye then, properly this time.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Hello? I said, is this [PERSON_1] I'm speaking with? It's [PERSON_2], calling from [COMPANY_A], I just need to confirm a delivery address with you, shouldn't take a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, who's asking? Hang on, I'm in a queue here -- who did you say you were calling from? And what delivery, I'm not expecting anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A]. Courier, uh, the delivery side of things. It's just a routine address check, sir, we've got a parcel logged under your name, so there's nothing to be concerned about. Well, I say logged under your name, it's more under the address, the name's partly down, but that's why I'm calling, to confirm which [PERSON_1] this is for.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh -- right, so you've got a parcel that's partly got my name on it, and you want me to tell you which one I am? Yeah, no. I haven't ordered anything. Look, if you've got an address, you read it out to me, I'm not reading mine out to you. And what was the company again? You said it so fast I didn't, uh, catch it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. Courier. I've said it twice now, sir. Look, the address on the label is [CITY_1], that's the part I can see, the rest is, uh, smudged on the scan, which is exactly why I'm ringing you. I'm with security operations, we flag these when the details don't line up, and right now this parcel is being held at the depot. I need you to confirm the address so it doesn't get returned.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, I'm -- no, I'm not moving up, mate, I've only got the one basket. Sorry, not you. Right. Security operations? For a courier? That's a bit odd, isn't it. Last time someone rang me about a parcel it was a complete scam, so no, I'm not confirming anything. You've got [CITY_1], fine, that's about half of everybody. If it's a real parcel, they can leave a card, or I'll look it up myself on the company's own site. What's the reference number on it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not going to argue with you about it. It's flagged, it's held, and a held parcel doesn't sit at the depot forever, it goes back to the sender. The reference, yes, it's, uh... it's on the system, I'd have to pull it up, it's not on this screen. And there's a small handling fee that has to be settled before release, which we do by phone, so that's the other reason I'm calling. It's [AMOUNT_1], that's all it is. Now, shall we sort this out today, or do you want it returned?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what fee? A handling free? Free, so it's free, then why are you -- no, hang on, you said fee. Right. And you want it paid over the phone, and you can't even tell me the reference number? Nope. That's it for me, mate. Real couriers leave a card through the door, they don't ring up asking for money. I'll look it up myself if there's anything to look up. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Your choice, sir. It'll go back to the sender.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, let it go back. Oh, for -- no, you go ahead, I'm just waiting on the, sorry, not you, mate. Right. Look, I'm not discussing it any more. If there's a real parcel, I'll find out the proper way. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, sir, hold on, before you go. I'd just like it noted that I've been entirely civil with you, and that this call is a courtesy. We aren't obliged to ring anyone. A flagged parcel gets a notification attempt, and I've made it, and that's logged on my side as of now. If it's returned, that's down to a declined contact, not to us. And for the record, security operations is a perfectly normal department. I'm not going to stand here and explain how [COMPANY_A] is structured, I haven't got the time, I've got a list of these to get through. Now, I can see you're in a queue, so I'll be brief. The reference, as I said, isn't in front of me, which is not the same as there not being one, and I'd ask you not to put words in my mouth. Last chance, really, because once this is closed off it's closed. Do you want to resolve it, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. That's a no, and I've said so about three times now. Look, I'm not putting words in your mouth, you put them there yourself. You rang me, you couldn't tell me what the address is, you couldn't tell me the reference, you've got a department that sounds made up and a fee you want paid over the phone, and now you're telling me it's my last chance. That's not a courtesy call, mate, that's pressure, and I've had this exact sort of call before and I'm still angry about it, so no. If there's a parcel, it'll be on the company's own site or there'll be a card through my door, and I'll deal with it that way, on my own time, not yours. You log whatever you like on your side. I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Noted. Have a good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before you go, two minutes ago you said it was a handling fee, and then you said it was free, or I heard free, no, I said free, you said fee. Whatever. What was it actually for? Handling what? You said a held parcel gets that fee, so who's charging it, you or the sender? Because that's the bit that doesn't add up, a courier asking for money to hand over something that isn't even mine.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, it's the, it's an administrative charge, it's, well, the sender covers it normally, so it's -- no, the recipient, in these cases. Look, I don't set the policy, sir, I'm not the one who can explain the billing side, that's a different department. I've got other calls to get through. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sender covers it, no, the recipient, which is it? You've changed that in about two seconds. And you said security operations flags these, now it's billing, that's a different department, so who exactly am I talking to? Never mind. Don't answer that. I'm not paying anyone anything over the phone, and I'm not going to carry on listening to you contradict yourself while I'm stood here with a basket. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], the international lottery claims office, and I'm, uh, following up on the message we left with you yesterday. Well, I say yesterday, it may have been the day before, our records are a little unclear on that. The reason I'm calling is that your entry was drawn in our overseas draw last month, and there are a few claim details we do need to confirm with you before the file can be closed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, did you say a lottery? I'm sorry, I don't think I got a message, or maybe I did and I've, uh, forgotten it. A lottery draw, you said? Sorry, I'm not very good with this sort of thing, could you say that again, please?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, there's no need to apologise, it's quite common for people to miss the message. So, yes. Your entry was drawn in an overseas lottery, and it's a prize of, uh, [AMOUNT_1], and my office is responsible for verifying the claimant before anything is released. I would just say that these files do not stay open indefinitely, and ours has been open a little while now. So if we could go through the confirmation together today, that would be, well, sensible.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh goodness, [AMOUNT_1]? Well, that's, I mean, that's very kind, I'm just a bit surprised. Sorry, I don't remember entering any overseas lottery, I'm not sure how I'd have done that. Did someone enter me, or, um, is it one of those things that happens automatically? I'd like to help you close the file, I'm just a little confused about how I come into it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's a very fair question, and I'm glad you asked it, because people are right to want to understand how they come into something like this. Entries are, uh, sometimes made through partner promotions, so it may be that your details were passed along from one of those, and the draw itself, the ticket was, hold on, sorry, someone's at my door -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Where was I. The ticket was entered under your name, in the draw from, I believe, the third week of last month, though the exact reference is held in the main file and I'd want to confirm it before I say anything I'd have to correct later. What I would say is that the claim window is not unlimited, and I'd rather we settled this today than have it lapse.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, sorry, a partner promotion. Um, but I still don't remember entering anything, I really don't, I'm sorry. I'd like to help you close the file, I would, it's only that I don't see how I'm in it. And, sorry, you said the reference is in the main file, but could you tell me it now, just so I can see it matches something I've got here? I don't think I've got anything, but I could have a look. Sorry, I know I keep asking, I just don't want to say the wrong thing and cause you any bother.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, please, don't apologise, I welcome the question, and I'd rather you asked than agreed to something you didn't follow. Now, the ticket number, it's, uh, I have it here, it ends in [CODE_1], though the full reference is in the main file, as I said, and I'd want to read it to you correctly. I'll say, too, that the draw was in the second week of last month, not the third, I think I misspoke earlier, and the figure on the file is [AMOUNT_2], which I realise isn't what I first mentioned, but that's the sort of thing we reconcile during the confirmation. So what would help me most is if we could simply go through your details together now, while the file is still open for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, I'm, hold on, I'm just trying to keep up. First it was the third week and now it's the second, and the amount was, well, it was [AMOUNT_1] and now it's, sorry, a different one? I don't want to be rude, I just, I think I'd, no, what I mean is, I'd feel better if I knew this was really, um, if there was some way I could check it was you, and the lottery, and not, uh, well. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or a website, or something I could look up myself first? I'm sorry, I do want to help, I'm just getting a bit muddled.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. That's fine, [PERSON_1]. You can check, of course. I'd only say the file doesn't stay open while you do.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Well, sorry, but if it's all right, I think I'd rather check first, even if the file closes. I mean, if it's a real prize, it'll still be real tomorrow, won't it? It's just, the dates changed, and the amount changed, and I don't remember entering anything, and I'd feel awful if I said the wrong thing to the wrong person. So I'm sorry, I'm going to leave it there, and if it's genuine I'm sure it'll all be sorted out some other way. Thank you for your time, and sorry to have been a bother. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I, no, [PERSON_1], I wouldn't want you to think -- let me put it differently. You're quite right to be careful, and I'd never ask you to go against that. It's only that, well, I can't promise what the file looks like tomorrow, that isn't mine to say. Perhaps what we do is, I note that you'd like to verify through the main office, and you simply tell me you're content to proceed on that basis, and we leave the rest to the confirmation. Can I take it that you're agreeing to that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, I don't think I can say that, no. I'm not agreeing to anything, I'm just going to check first, like I said. I'm sorry, I know I said it already, I just, I don't want to say yes to something when I don't remember entering anything. So I'll leave it there, if that's all right. Thank you, and sorry again, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you remember entering? Because that's, well, that's helpful, [PERSON_1], if you do recall the entry, that would simplify the confirmation considerably. We could simply go through it together now, and I'd note that you've already agreed to proceed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, sorry, I said I don't remember entering, I, no, what I said was, I haven't agreed to, um. I mean, I haven't said yes to anything, and I didn't say I remembered, I'm quite sure I didn't. I'm sorry, I don't want any muddle about it. So I'm going to say goodbye now, and I'll check it myself, properly. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't continue this. You've said clearly that you haven't agreed to anything, and I just tried to put words in your mouth by claiming you'd agreed. I won't write a version where you get talked round either, because everything you asked about was reasonable: the details kept changing, there was no way to verify who I was, and the deadline was never named. Checking it yourself, as you said, is the right call. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Well, thank you, I'll do that, then. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll leave it there. I'm not going to add another detail, because the last thing I'd want is to give you one more figure or date that doesn't match the others. Whatever the facts turn out to be, you were right to check them yourself before agreeing to anything. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, thank you, that's very kind of you to say. I'll have a look into it myself, then. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist at [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, uh, we handle estates, and I'm calling in connection with a probate matter in which you may be a named beneficiary, though I'd stress "may" at this stage.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, that's me, but hang on, who? A verification specialist? What's that when it's at home? Look, I'm in a queue at the shop, so, uh, what is this, exactly? Because "may be a named beneficiary" sounds like the sort of thing, well, I've heard it before.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, quite right to be wary, and I'd rather you were. It's, uh, essentially a fancy title, I'm the person who confirms we've reached the correct individual before any formal correspondence is issued, so there's no misdirected paperwork, you understand, given the sensitivities around testamentary disclosure. Now, I'm not going to ask you anything in a shop queue, and I'm certainly not asking for money or bank details, ever. A formal letter is going out to you from [COMPANY_A], and all I'd ask is that you treat this call as confidential until it arrives, because the estate isn't, um, fully administered yet and other parties may be affected. And please don't take my word for it: look the firm up in an independent directory, not through any number I give you, and ring us back that way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, go back. You said a minute ago you were confirming it's the right person before the paperwork goes out. Confirming how, exactly? Because I've told you nothing, I've said yes that's me and that's it. And what's the "may" bit, who's died? You haven't said a name or anything. And I'll be honest, the "keep it confidential" thing, that's what gets my back up. Why would I not be able to tell anyone?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, a "name", yes, so you'd like the name of the, uh, the firm's registered correspondent? That's [PERSON_3], and the address is on the letter, which will, um, carry our reference as well. Though actually, what I meant by confirming was only the very basics already printed on that letter, your full name and the address it's being sent to, nothing beyond that. And on the confidentiality, I mean, you can tell your solicitor or a family member, I only meant please don't discuss it more widely until the letter lands, because of the, um, intestacy implications for the other parties. As to who's died, I, uh, I don't actually have the deceased's name in front of me, it's held by the fee earner. I'm sorry, I know that sounds peculiar. Let me find out what I'm able to share and call you back, would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, don't ring me back. You rang me, I've no idea who you are. And I asked who's died and you don't know? You don't know who's died? That's, I mean, that's the whole call, isn't it? Somebody's died, and I may get something, and you can't tell me who. And you want my full name and address, which you've already got, apparently, if there's a letter going out. So why d'you need me to confirm it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, that's a, uh, a perfectly fair challenge. The reason is, well, the address we hold came from, I mean, the records we were given, and, hm, we only want to be sure it's current before the letter goes out, but I take the point, if we've got it, we've got it. And you're right about the name, it does sound odd that I can't give it to you, I, uh, I think the position is that the fee earner, that's the solicitor with conduct of the file, holds that, and I'm not, I don't have it on my screen. So, look, you needn't give me anything at all, not even your name again. If you'd rather not be rung back, then, um, look the firm up yourself, [COMPANY_A], in an independent directory, and ask for the probate department by name of the file handler, and they can tell you who's died. I'd rather you checked than took my word.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, go back a bit. Two goes ago you said you'd put the name of someone, the registered, uh, correspondent, [PERSON_3]. Right. And then you said there's a reference on the letter. What reference? Because if you've got a file and a letter all ready to go, you've got a reference number, so what is it? Don't read me anything long, just, what's it called, and who's the fee earner? Because "the solicitor with the file" isn't a name either.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, the reference, I, uh, I don't have it in front of me, I'm afraid, and I'd be guessing if I gave you anything, which I won't do. And I can't give you the fee earner's name either, I'm sorry, I only have [PERSON_3] as the registered correspondent. That's a fair question and I can't answer it from here. I'll find out the reference and the name of the solicitor with conduct of the file and put them in the letter, and if you'd rather I rang you with them, I will, but only if you say so. Otherwise, uh, look the firm up independently and ask for them directly, and I won't mind in the least.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you can't tell me who's died, you can't give me a reference, you can't name the solicitor, and you've no idea why you need me to confirm an address you've already got. Oh, and you said you'd ring me back, then you said only if I say so, which, no. Look, I'm not saying you're not on the level, but I've been caught out before and I'm not doing this over the phone in a queue. If there's a letter, send it, and if it's real I'll deal with it properly through the firm myself. Right, I'm at the till. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi, sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? I think there might be a bit of a delay on the line, so, um, bear with me a second... yes, hi. This is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the digital-asset desk. I'm so sorry to catch you out of the blue like this, but I'm handling a position that closes today, and I wanted to make sure you'd been told about it before it, well, before it's too late. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I'm still here, I'm just -- the signal's awful, I'm driving, you're on speaker. Uh, who did you say this was again? [COMPANY_A]? I don't think I've -- sorry, a position that closes? What position? I don't, I mean, I don't really have anything with, uh, digital anything, I don't think. Sorry, can you say that again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm so sorry, that's my fault, I should have slowed down. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the digital-asset investment desk. And you're right, you wouldn't have anything with us, not yet, uh, that's really the reason for the call. Your name came up on a short list for a position that's closing today, and I'd hate for you to miss it, because honestly the return on it is, well, it's well above what you'd normally see. But I don't want to rush you while you're driving, are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I'm here, sorry, hang on, there's a lorry right up behind me and I think I'm in the wrong lane -- okay, okay, sorry. Uh, so a short list? Like, what list? I didn't sign up for anything, I don't think, I mean I'd remember, wouldn't I? And I'm sorry, I'm not being rude, but how did you get my number? Because I really don't know who [COMPANY_A] is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not being rude at all, I'd ask exactly the same thing, I'm sorry. Um, the list comes from a referral pool, and I'm afraid I can't go into whose name it came through, it's a confidentiality thing on our side, which I know isn't a very satisfying answer. But, and this is really just for your protection, I'd rather you heard about it from me directly than from someone less careful, because positions like this tend to get passed around quietly, and not everyone handles them properly. Are you still there? I can hear the road noise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I'm still here, sorry, it's just the road, it does that when I go under the bridges, the signal sort of drops and comes back. Um, so a referral pool, right, and you can't say whose name, and I do get that, confidentiality, I work somewhere that's, well, never mind, that's not the point. It's just that, I'm sorry, it doesn't really sit right with me. If I don't know who gave you my number, and I don't know who you are, and I've never heard of [COMPANY_A], then how am I supposed to know any of this is, you know, real? Not that I'm saying it isn't, I'm sure you're perfectly nice, I just, I get nervous about money things, I always have, my brother used to say I'd worry about the weather on a sunny day. So is there something I could look up? Like a number I could ring back, or a website, or a, I don't know, a reference or something? Because I can't really do anything right now anyway, I'm in the car, I'm on my way to, uh, never mind, and I don't want to say yes to something I haven't understood. Sorry, that was a long answer, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, not at all, it wasn't long, I'm sorry. And, um, you said something about the weather, sorry, about checking the weather? I'm not sure I caught how that connects, I think the line cut out on me for a second. But I do hear you, honestly, and I don't want you worrying, that's the last thing I'd want. The thing is, if you go looking for a number or a website, I'm afraid the position will have closed by the time you've done that, it's just today, and that's really why I rang you now rather than writing. I can give you a reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and my direct line, [PHONE_1], but I'd ask you to keep this between us for the moment, just until it's settled, because, um, the allocation is limited and I'd hate for it to get out. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, can I just, the weather was just a thing my brother said, it's nothing, it's not -- no, wait, hang on, you said keep it between us? Why would I keep it, I'm sorry, I don't mean to interrupt, but that's the bit that's, um, that's making me really uncomfortable. If it's real, why can't I ring someone and check? And a reference you've made up on the spot isn't, I mean, I can't check that either, can I? So I think, sorry, I think I'm just going to leave it. I'm not going to do anything today and I'm not going to ring that number. Sorry. Thanks anyway, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, wait, please, I'm sorry, I didn't mean it like that. I'm really not trying to pressure you, it's just that I'd hate for you to walk away and then wish you hadn't. Could I just ask you to stay on for one more minute, so I can explain how it works, and then, if you still want to leave it, that's completely fine? Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm still here, I just, no. I'm sorry, I really don't want you to explain it, because I think that's how I end up saying yes to things, and I've told you, I'm not doing anything today. If it's a real thing, it'll still be real when I can check it properly, and if it closes today, then it closes, that's fine. I'm sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I'm just going to say goodbye now. Bye, thank you, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I, um, I'm sorry, I didn't want to leave you feeling uneasy, that's honestly the last thing... no, you're right, of course. If you do change your mind, the line I mentioned is [PHONE_1], but I'd, um, I'd still ask you not to mention it around before then, just so it isn't, well... sorry. Hello? Are you still...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, uh, sorry, I'm still here, I just, I don't, I'm not going to ring that number, and I'm not going to keep it quiet either, sorry, I don't think I could, I'd probably just mention it to someone, I'm useless at secrets. So, yeah. Thank you, but no. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, you said you're useless at... sweepstakes? No, sorry, I think I've, um, I think I've lost the line again, I didn't catch that last bit. I'm afraid this isn't a sweepstake at all, it's a, it's a proper position, so I'd hate for you to think... hello? Are you still there? If you could just hold on a moment, I really would feel terrible if you walked away without hearing the...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, sorry, I said secrets, I'm useless at secrets, not, no, never mind, it doesn't matter. Look, I'm really sorry, and I know you keep saying you don't want me to walk away, but I've said no a few times now and I'm just going to hang up. Thank you, honestly, but no. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is, uh -- sorry, let me start again. I'm calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the pension provider, and we need to confirm a few details before we can discuss a change to your plan. Is that, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Because I do have a closing window on this one, so I'd like to get through it if we can.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a closing window? Like, for a window, or -- hang on. (muffled, away from the phone) No, put that down, please. Sorry. Who did you say you were calling from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, uh, take your time. I'm calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], your pension provider. And sorry, "closing window" was just my way of saying the query is flagged to be dealt with this week, but there's no need for you to rush on my account. Is this a good moment, or would it be better if I left it for now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. A change to my plan? I haven't asked for any change. What sort of change are we talking about? And, I mean, you've asked if I'm [PERSON_1] but you haven't actually told me what you already have on file, so how would I know this is really you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's, uh, that's a fair question, and, um, well, the standard procedure is that I can't go into the plan details until the account holder has been confirmed, which I know sounds backwards. So, ah, I'd rather not read anything out to you on a call you didn't expect. Look, if you're uneasy, and it sounds like you are, then please don't answer anything today. Ring [COMPANY_A] on the number printed on your statement, not one I give you, and ask for account services quoting [ACCOUNT_REF], or I can have the same query sent to you by post or through your secure message inbox. Whichever you'd prefer, there's no pressure from me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right. Hm. So, you're telling me to hang up and ring the number on the statement myself? That's, I mean, that's not what I expected you to say. Honestly, I'd sooner do it that way. Or the post, I think, post is fine. Sorry, I'm just, there's a kid going nuts here and I'd rather not be doing this over the phone anyway. So, yeah. I'll look at my statement and ring them myself. Is that okay? Is that all you needed?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely fine, and, uh, that's the right call, honestly. I'll note on the file that you'd rather deal with it by post and by ringing in yourself, so nothing more will come from my end today. And please, don't worry about the time, there's no deadline on you. Hope the little one settles down. Thanks for your patience, and, um, have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. Right. Well, thanks, I suppose. I'll ring them myself, then. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye, and, uh, sorry, one quick thing before you go, because I don't want you left confused. Earlier I said the query was flagged for this week, and that probably sounded like a deadline. It isn't one. Nothing happens to your plan if you don't respond, so take it at your own pace. Right, thanks again, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, okay. Nothing happens if I don't respond. Right. Well, I'll still ring them myself, like I said. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, and, I mean -- no, that's, that's exactly what I'd do in your position. Ring them yourself, whenever suits, or wait for the letter, whichever. I won't try you again today. Right, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, "whenever suits, or wait for the letter"? Earlier you said it was flagged for this week, and then there was a closing window, and now it's whenever. I mean, which is it? Not that I'm changing my mind, I'm still ringing them myself. I just, it's a bit all over the place. Anyway. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the scheduling desk at [COMPANY_A], the benefits office, I'm just following up on the appointment you booked, the one about your, uh, your housing review, or was it the heating review, sorry, I've got two tabs open here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hello? Yeah, this is, um, yes, that's me I suppose. Sorry, I just woke up, I was having a little lie down. Which, hang on, what appointment? I don't remember booking anything, but then my memory's not what it was, I'd have to look at the calendar on the fridge. And who did you say you were again, the benefits office? Because I've been getting a lot of those letters lately, well, not letters exactly, the one from the council about the bins, that was a mess.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, that's absolutely fine, take your time, I know, the mornings, the afternoons, they run into each other, mine do too, and it's [PERSON_2], scheduling desk at [COMPANY_A], the benefits office, not the council, no bins, ha. So it's not really an appointment as such, I should've said, it's more that when I pulled up your file there's a note on it, a record that's showing incomplete, just one section, and it's a quick one, two minutes, and it's much easier to tidy up over the phone than waiting for another letter to go out, so I'll just get you confirmed on that if that's alright, and then you can get back to your lie down.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, a record that's showing, sorry, did you say a wreck? Like a car? No, no, I haven't had the car in years, my nephew took it, well, borrowed it, that was a whole business. But I don't think I've wrecked anything, I'm not sure what you mean by that. And you said you've got my file, which file is that, exactly? Because I don't remember anyone asking me for a file, and you still haven't said what it's actually about, have you? You said housing, then heating, now it's a wreck.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, record, a record, not a wreck, sorry, my fault, I talk too fast, [PERSON_3] in the office is always telling me, it's just the benefits record, the one we hold for you, and it's showing incomplete, which is all, so what I need to do is just confirm a couple of details with you now, your full date of birth and the, uh, the reference on your file, and then it's done and dusted and nothing goes to review, because if it sits incomplete past today it can hold up your payments, and nobody wants that, so if you've got that to hand, date of birth first, that's the easy one.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold up payments? Now wait, you said it was an appointment, and then it was a record, and now it's my payments, and I still don't know which file, I keep asking which file. I'm not, I mean, I don't just give out my birthday to someone who rings me up out of the blue, I don't even know you, do I? You said you're from the benefits office, but how would I know that, you could be anybody, which file is it, what's it called? And I'm not rushing, I only just woke up, so I don't see why it has to be today.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, and that's fair, that's completely fair, but it's only the one detail, your date of birth, and it's honestly just a quick confirmation, it's a two-minute thing, and I'd hate for it to hold anything up for you, so if we could just -- sorry, hello, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], scheduling desk at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just following up on your record, it's showing incomplete, and it really does need confirming today, so if I can just take your date of birth, that's the easy one, and then we're all done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not giving my birthday to someone who won't even tell me which file it is. If it's that important, put it in a letter, I'll deal with it that way. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, it's, uh, it's not really a letter situation, it's more of a, I mean, we did already send one, last week I think, or the week before, so -- no, look, I can't pull the file name up right now, the system's, it's being slow, so I'll, yeah, I'll just flag it as unreachable and someone will be in touch. Right, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I, no, hang on, you said a letter went out, but I never, I mean, if there's a letter I'd have, hm. No. Right. If somebody's going to be in touch, they can write to me properly, and I'll ring the benefits office myself on the number I've got, not this one. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Um, hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I think the line's a bit quiet on my end, I'm just, uh, making sure you can hear me okay. It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy, and I'm so sorry to bother you -- are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I can hear you. Sorry, hang on -- [PERSON_1] speaking, yes. Which pharmacy did you say? I didn't catch the name, and, I mean, what's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, I'm so sorry, I should've said it more clearly. It's [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy, [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A]. And it's nothing to worry about at all, it's just that your repeat prescription is ready for collection, so I wanted to let you know. Can you hear me okay still?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you fine, it's not the line. But, uh, you said earlier you couldn't hear me, and now you're asking if I can hear you -- anyway. Which prescription, though? I mean, I didn't order anything, so, what's it for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, that was a bit muddled of me -- sorry, hang on one second, someone's just come to the counter -- sorry, I'm back. Um, I can't really go into the details of the medication over the phone, I'm afraid, not until I've confirmed it's definitely you, it's just to protect your privacy. It's the repeat that's on file under your name, and it would've been set up through your surgery, so it may just be that it was sent over automatically. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, I'm -- sorry, hang on, [PERSON_1] here is, uh, watching the little one, so. Look, I -- you can't tell me what it is, but you want me to, to confirm who I am to you? That's sort of backwards, isn't it? You rang me. And I don't, I mean, I don't even know which pharmacy yet, you've just said the name twice and I still... what's the actual name, and where are you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, I'm so sorry, that does sound backwards when I put it like that. I don't want you to feel pressured at all. We're [COMPANY_A], the branch in [CITY_1], and you'd have picked up from us before, I think. Um, honestly, I'd rather you didn't confirm anything with me on the phone, not until you're comfortable it's us. Are you still there, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I think I'll just ring the pharmacy myself, on the number I've got. If there's something waiting, I'll sort it then. Okay, thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, yes, please do, that's absolutely the right thing to do. Sorry again for the muddle, and for taking up your time. If you ring the branch on the number you've got, they'll be able to check it for you. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say take a seat? No, I'm, I'm standing, I've got the little one. Anyway. Yeah, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, I said take care. Never mind, it's fine. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Take care, right, sorry. Yeah. Like I said, I'll ring the pharmacy myself. On my own number. Okay, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1] with the security operations team at [COMPANY_A], fraud department. I'm calling about your account, there's been a suspicious charge attempted just now, a charge for [AMOUNT_1]. Hello? Can you hear me? I said there's a suspicious charge on your account, it was just attempted, so I need to speak with the account holder right away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- a suspicious what, a surcharge? Because I haven't ordered anything. And who is this again, [COMPANY_A], is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not a surcharge, a suspicious charge, an attempted transaction for [AMOUNT_1] that we flagged and put on hold about two minutes ago. And yes, [COMPANY_A], security operations, fraud team, my name is [PERSON_1]. Now, the fact that you didn't order anything is exactly why I'm calling, because that tells me this wasn't you, and when it isn't the account holder, we have a very short window to lock things down before the charge goes through on the next processing cycle. I understand you're surprised, most people are, but I've got a number of accounts flagged on this same pattern and I'm working through them in order, so I need to verify I'm speaking with the right person before I can say anything further. Can you confirm your full name and the date of birth on the account?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hm. Well, hang on, you called me, so shouldn't you already have my name? I mean, you're the one saying it's my account. And, um, sorry, [PERSON_1], was it, which account is this supposed to be? Because I've got a, uh, a few things with a few different places.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, ma'am, I have the account in front of me, I'm not going to read details of it out over an unverified line, that's policy, and it's there to protect you. So I need the name and date of birth from you first, then we go from there. Hold on a second -- [PERSON_3], no, put that one in the other queue, I'll be right there -- sorry, where was I. Yes. The account ending is on my screen, the hold expires shortly, and once it lapses the [AMOUNT_1] posts and recovering it becomes a separate claims process that can take weeks. I'd rather not see that happen to you, so I do need you to answer the verification question now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, wait, hang on -- put that down, I said put it down, thank you. Sorry. Kid's got the, uh, the remote and he's -- never mind. So you're saying you can't tell me anything about the account, but I'm supposed to tell you who I am? That's, I mean, that's kind of backwards, isn't it? Why don't I just ring the number on the back of my card and ask them about it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, ma'am, listen -- sir -- if you hang up and go through the main line you'll be sitting in a queue, and the hold on that charge will not wait for a queue. It's backwards because the order matters for your protection, that's all I can tell you. I'm the one working your case right now, and the moment you put the phone down, I can't promise it stays open. I'm asking you one more time to verify your name and date of birth so we can stop this charge. Do you want it stopped, or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Do I want it -- no, hang on, you're not going to -- I'm not giving you anything. You can't tell me which account, you can't tell me my own name, and now I've got a clock on it? That's, I mean, that's exactly what my relative got, so no. I'll ring the number on the back of the card, and if there's really a hold, it'll be on there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'd strongly advise against that, and I want this on the record before you hang up. If you walk away from this call and the charge posts, that is your decision, and the bank will note that you were notified and declined to cooperate. It can complicate any claim you try to file later, and I'm not saying that to frighten you, I'm saying it because it's how the process works. I'm not going to argue the point further. And for what it's worth, you don't need a number from me, I'm not going to give you one, because the line you're calling from is routed through this department, so the number on the back of your card isn't going to reach the people handling your case. You'd be starting from scratch with someone who has none of the information I have. I've been very patient with you, I've explained the situation three separate ways, and I've got other accounts on this list that I haven't gotten to yet. So if you're certain, then fine, but I'd say you're making a mistake, and I want you to remember I told you that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, stop, I'm going to stop you there -- the number on the back of my card goes to my card company, not to you. That's the whole point of it. You don't get to tell me it routes through your department, that's -- no. I'm hanging up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Afternoon. Is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], calling from [COMPANY_A], just a quick administrative matter, if you've got a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, that's me. Sorry, I'm driving, so the reception's a bit rubbish... who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, uh, [COMPANY_A], the national tax office. [PERSON_2], security operations. Look, I'll keep it short so you can concentrate on the road. It's just a routine matter on your file, nothing to worry about, really.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the tax office, okay, uh -- sorry, hang on, there's a lorry just pulled out in front of me, one second. Right, sorry, I'm back. So, "security operations," did you say? I'm sorry, I don't really know what that means, is something wrong with my file? Because you said it's nothing to worry about, but now I'm a bit worried.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nothing's wrong, quite the opposite. Security operations is just the team that, uh, verifies records before we release anything. It's a refund, [PERSON_1]. You're owed [AMOUNT_1] from the, I think it's the last tax year, and I did say it was a routine matter, so there's no need to be alarmed. I just need to confirm a few details so it can be released to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a refund, oh, okay, well that's, that's good, I suppose. Sorry, I just, I wasn't expecting anything, I didn't know I was owed anything. Um, what details do you need, exactly? Because I'm not sure I should be giving things out while I'm driving, and also the line keeps cutting, so I might miss half of what you say, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Just your date of birth and the address we have on file. Two minutes, then it's done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, my date of birth and address, right. Sorry, it's just, you're the one who rang me, so I don't actually know it's, I mean, I'm not saying you're not, but how would I know it's really the tax office? Could I maybe ring you back? Is there a number I should use, or, or would it be on a letter, or...? Sorry, I know that sounds awful, I'm just a bit on edge with the driving and everything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, yes, that's, that's sensible, I wouldn't argue with that. Though, look, a callback would mean going through the general switchboard, and that's, what, a three-week queue on the refunds line at the moment, and this reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], is only held open for today. If it lapses, the whole claim goes back into the pool and you start again. I'm not asking for anything unusual, [PERSON_1], date of birth and address, that's all, and it'd be a shame to lose [AMOUNT_2] over a callback.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, okay, so it lapses today? That's, ugh, that's a bit stressful, sorry. But I mean, if it's three weeks to get through, then, well, that's sort of the same as starting again anyway, isn't it? Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, it's just, I'd rather ring the number off an actual letter, or look it up properly, than give out my birthday to someone who rang me, even if you're lovely about it. Can you at least, I don't know, tell me something only the tax office would know about me, so I know it's genuine? Sorry, is that a silly thing to ask?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, it's not silly, no, but I can't read your file out over an open line, that's the whole point of verification. Now, I did say [AMOUNT_1] earlier, and, uh, it's [AMOUNT_2] now on the system, they revise it, the figure moves with the assessment, and it's the tax year before last, not the last one, my mistake. The reference is [CODE_1], I'll say it again, slowly. Look, [PERSON_1], I'm not going to argue with you over this, I've got other files waiting, so are you giving me the date of birth and address or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, but, hang on, the amount's changed, and now it's a different tax year as well? That's, I mean, that doesn't sound right to me, sorry. And you can't tell me anything about my file, but you want my details, I just, I can't do that. I'm really sorry, I know you've got other files waiting. I'm going to ring the tax office myself, properly, off a letter or whatever, once I've pulled over. Thanks for your time, sorry, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yes, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from the customs desk at [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant, and I'm ringing about the parcel you've got coming in from overseas, there's a small import charge on it that's holding up the delivery slot, so I just wanted to, uh, sorry, hang on, I should say first that nothing's wrong with the parcel itself, it's just the charge, and I can give you the tracking reference so you can see it on your own screen, would that help?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who is this again? Customs desk at what? I've got two minutes, so just tell me, what parcel? I'm not expecting any parcel, I mean, not that I know of. What's the point of the call?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, it's [PERSON_2], I'm at [COMPANY_A], the courier, customs desk, and the, uh, the parcel's from, no wait, let me put it this way -- there's a parcel with your name and address on it, and it's been held for an import charge of [AMOUNT_1], and I know that sounds like one of those calls, so I'm not asking you for anything down the phone, I'm just, I mean the tracking reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and if you've got a confirmation email or a text from us you'll see that same reference on it, so can you check that while we're talking, or I can wait?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, no. You've told me it sounds like one of those calls, and yeah, it does. You can't even tell me where the parcel's from, you started to and then changed it. And you want me to check my email against a reference you just read out? That proves nothing, anyone can make up a reference. If there's a real parcel, I'll look at the courier's own app, or find their number myself and ring them. I'm not doing this on your call. I've got a meeting, so, no thanks. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, that's exactly right, please do that, uh, don't stay on with me at all. Go to the tracking page from the link in your confirmation message, or find our number yourself, and you can pay it there at your own pace, or not at all, I'm not taking anything on this call. And since you asked where it's from, it's [CITY_1], the sender's listed as [COMPANY_B], and the charge breakdown on the page will show [AMOUNT_1] duty plus [AMOUNT_2] handling, so if that doesn't match what you see, then ring [PHONE_1] and tell them I got it wrong.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. That's the sensible bit, I'll give you that. But I'm not clicking any link in a message, and I'm not ringing a number you've just read me. If there's a parcel, I'll find the courier myself and check there. If there isn't, well, that tells me something too. Anyway, I've got to go. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine, go and find us yourself, I'm not going to argue with that, but, uh, quickly, you said it proves nothing if I read out a reference, and you're right, anyone could do that, so here's something only the real desk would know, when you do get through to [COMPANY_A], ask them to confirm the customs hold note on the file shows it was created by [PERSON_2] on the scheduling side, and that it lists [CODE_1] as the hold reason, and if they can't find either of those, then don't pay anything and you've lost two minutes, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, two turns back you said you'd got the parcel's details, but you couldn't tell me where it was from at first. Which is it? Did you actually have it in front of you or not? And that hold note thing, anybody could say that, I've no way to check it, so it's no use to me. I'll find them myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair challenge, I did have it in front of me, I just fumbled the order, I'm doing a lot of these today and I ran two sentences together, that's on me, sorry. And you're right about the hold note, you can't check it from your side, so forget it, it was a bad idea to offer. What you can check is simple, find the courier yourself, however you like, and ask whether there's an import charge held against your address, because if there is, the tracking page will show [AMOUNT_1] and you can deal with it there whenever you're ready, and if there isn't, then I've got the wrong person and you owe me nothing, uh, and I'll leave it there, I've kept you long enough.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you've got the wrong person? So who did you want, then? Because you opened by asking for me by name. No, hang on, that's not the point, I'm not going round in circles. I'll look it up myself, if there's anything to look up. You said you'd leave it there, so leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one second, uh, there's a door going somewhere behind me -- okay. This is [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm ringing because there's a record on your benefits file that's showing as incomplete, and it does need confirming over the phone before we close today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, hello, this is -- sorry, a benefits file? I'm not quite sure I -- oh dear, which company did you say you were from? I didn't quite catch it with the door and everything, and I don't want to say the wrong thing, I'm just, um, I'm not very good with this sort of--

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's quite all right, there's nothing for you to get wrong here, that's what I'm for. It's [COMPANY_A], the public benefits office, account services department, and I'm [PERSON_2], and basically what's happened is that when we ran the routine review of your file, one of the fields came up as incomplete, which just means a record that's not been confirmed on our side, and the way the process works is that an incomplete record has to be confirmed with the account holder directly, by phone, within the same working day, otherwise it gets flagged and that can hold up your payments. Now I don't want to alarm you, it's very common, I get through a dozen of these a day, but the cut-off is end of business today, so what I'd like to do is just confirm a few details with you now, and we'll have it tidied up in a couple of minutes. So, if I could just have your full name and date of birth, as they appear on the file, to start us off?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I'd, um -- I'd like to help, I really would, but I'm -- hold on, let me, I mean -- you said it could hold up my payments? That sounds, well, that sounds rather important. Only I'm just wondering, sorry, if you're from the benefits office, why would you need me to tell you my name and, and my birthday, when you've, you know, got it all there on the file already? I'm sorry, I'm probably not understanding how it works.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a perfectly reasonable question, and, uh, it's standard procedure, it's a data protection step. Before I can discuss or amend anything on the file, I have to confirm I'm speaking with the account holder, so the details have to come from you, that's just how the process works. And it isn't a payments hold yet, I didn't say it was held, it's only if it's still showing incomplete once we pass the cut-off, which is, well, we're really looking at the next hour or so, not end of day, we've a batch that runs early this afternoon. So, if I could just have your full name and date of birth as they appear on the file, we'll get this tidied up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I'm, um -- I've gone a bit muddled now. A minute ago you said it was by the end of business today, and now it's the next hour or so? I'm not sure I followed that, I'm sorry. And, um, which company did you say again? [COMPANY_A], was it? I never quite got what that stands for.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], the public benefits office, account services. And the timing, uh, no, that's just the cut-off for today, the batch runs early afternoon and, well, either way it's today, which is why I'd like to get it confirmed now. I do understand it's a lot to take in. Sorry, I'm, I'm going to have to take another call on the other line, so what I'll do is ring you back later this afternoon and we'll finish it off then, all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, that's -- hang on, sorry, the kettle's just clicked off, one second -- okay. Um, well, if you've got to take another call, that's fine, I wouldn't want to hold you up. But, sorry, could I just -- if I wanted to check this was all above board, is there a number I could ring you back on? Only I'd feel a bit better doing that, I think, I'm just not very good with these things and I'd like to be sure.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, I'm afraid I can't give out a direct line, it's not something I'm able to do, the lines are routed through the main system, so it's much simpler if I just ring you back. It's all done under the standard verification procedure, nothing to be concerned about. So I'll call you back later this afternoon, before the batch, and we'll finish it off then. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], speak soon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, right, well -- sorry, I'm just, I'm not sure that sits right with me now. You can't give me a number, and the time keeps changing, and I'm -- I'd feel better looking up the benefits office myself and ringing them, I think. If there's really something wrong with my file, they'll know about it, won't they? So, um, I'll do that, if that's all right, and sorry if that's awkward for you. Thank you for ringing, anyway. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, there's really no need for that, [PERSON_1], honestly, it's all in hand on our side, and, as I said, I'll only need a couple of minutes of your time when I ring back, so it's far simpler to just leave it with me. And, uh, I did say it was a quick call, I think, that it wasn't anything urgent, just the one record to confirm. So I'll ring you later this afternoon, before the batch, and we'll finish it off then. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, but I think I'll still ring them myself, if that's all right. You did say it was urgent, with the cut-off and everything, so I'd rather just check. I'd best not tell you anything when you ring back, I'm afraid, I'll just go through the proper office. Thank you, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, I wouldn't say it was urgent, exactly, I never said that, it's more of a routine matter, just that it does need doing today. And honestly, I'd think twice before ringing round, because the office won't have the record in front of them, it's only with us at the moment. So I'll still give you a ring this afternoon, before the batch, and we can just finish it off then. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, hang on, I don't think -- sorry, it's just, if the office doesn't have the record, then how would, um, how would you have it, you know? That doesn't quite, well, I'm not very good at this, but I think I'd still sooner ring them myself, if you don't mind. So, um, there's no need to call me back, thank you. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Oh, good, uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I haven't caught you at a bad moment. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler at [COMPANY_A], the digital-asset desk, and I'm calling about a -- well, it's more that there's a position that's, uh, no, let me put that differently. There's a time-sensitive opportunity on your file that closes today, and I really didn't want it to lapse without someone letting you know. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm still here. Sorry, say that again? Who are you with, exactly? [COMPANY_A], what -- I don't have a file with a digital-asset anything, so what file? Who did you say you were?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm sorry, that's my fault, I jumped straight in. I'm [PERSON_2], a case handler with [COMPANY_A], we're an investment desk that handles digital assets. And file was probably the wrong word, it's more that your details came up in a group we were reviewing, and the position closes today, so I wanted to reach you before it did. I'm only trying to make sure you don't miss out on something that, uh, honestly looks very favourable for you. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry -- no, put that down, please, we don't throw that. Sorry. Okay. Uh, my details came up in a group? What group? I've never dealt with you, so how'd you get my number, and what position? I didn't open anything with you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, uh, that's completely fair, and I'm sorry, I do realise it sounds sudden. The group was, well, it's a list of people we, no, I mean it's a review of contacts who might benefit from, uh -- I'd have to check where your number came from specifically, I don't have that in front of me right now. But the position itself, it's, I mean the return on it is well above what you'd normally see, and it does close today, so I'd just hate for you to lose out. I'm only saying this to protect you, really. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, protect me from what? I don't have anything to lose out on, I never signed up for -- no, wait. You don't know where you got my number? You're ringing me about my details and you can't say where they came from? That's, I mean, that's the whole thing, isn't it? Who are you actually with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm sorry, please don't take it that way, I'm only trying to help. I'm with [COMPANY_A], the digital-asset desk, I'm [PERSON_2], and it's just that the position closes today, so I wanted you to hear about it before it did. And I can find out where your number came from, I just, uh, I'd need to look into that separately. It really is for your own protection that I'm ringing, you understand, so you don't lose out. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. You've said the company name three times now, and I still don't know what you actually do. Or what I'm supposed to have, or what I'd lose. So, no, I'm not going to go any further on this today. If [COMPANY_A] genuinely has something of mine, they can send it in writing and I'll look at it. Okay? Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, wait, I'm sorry, don't go just yet. I'd, uh, rather you didn't wait for anything in writing, to be honest, because it'd be too late by then. And I should say, I didn't mean it was a list, I said it was, well, you did ask me for the details, didn't you, so I thought -- no, sorry. I'm only trying to keep you from losing out. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Too late by then. Right. That's exactly why I'm not doing it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, sorry, just one second. I never actually said there was a list, I said you'd been, uh, referred to us, so it's not like we picked your number out of nowhere. And I'd, um, I'd really rather this stayed between us for now, just until it closes, so nobody else gets in ahead of you. If you'd like, I can ring you back on a, uh, a direct line later today -- are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, you did say a list, you said it twice, and now it's a referral from who? And keep it between us, why would I -- no. I'm not having you ring back either, I'm done. Don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, just, one second, I've got the screen up here -- yes. I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm in the claims team. It's about, uh, an overdue balance on your account, and there's a date coming up where supply could be interrupted, so I just wanted to, um, make you aware of that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Um... yes, yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Oh dear, sorry, I -- an overdue balance? Hang on, let me, uh... right. I didn't think I was behind on anything, but I'm not very good with all that, to be honest. Sorry, what was your name again, and which company was it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, don't apologise. It's [PERSON_2], and I'm with [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier. Sorry, hang on, someone's just put a trolley down right next to my desk, uh -- right, sorry, I've lost my place. Yes, so, the balance is [AMOUNT_1], and I've got the date here somewhere, but basically if it isn't dealt with by then, supply would be interrupted at the property, so it is a bit time-sensitive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's all right, it's noisy where you are, I can hear. Um, sorry, I'm just trying to keep up. So you said, was it the claims team before? Only I thought, well, I don't know, I thought claims were for when someone's, you know, owed something, not when they owe it. But I'm probably muddling it. And did you say [AMOUNT_1]? Oh dear. That's more than I'd have thought. Sorry, what date was it again, the one it'd be cut off by?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, [AMOUNT_1], that's the figure I've got. Sorry, and, um, claims, yes, you're not muddling it, that is a bit of an odd name for it. It's just the team that, uh, handles the accounts that have gone overdue, that's all. The date, hang on, let me find -- it's, uh, it's coming up quite soon, I've got it here somewhere. I'd rather you didn't leave it, because if it isn't sorted by then, supply would be interrupted at the property. Like I said, it is time-sensitive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, you said the supply would be interrupted, and um, you'd rather I didn't leave it -- so, who's it I'm supposed to be, what was it, receiving?
