Sorry, is it a letter I should have had? I don't think I've had a letter, but I do tend to let the post pile up a bit. And, hang on, you still haven't said the date, have you? Sorry, I don't mean to be awkward, it's just you keep saying it's coming up soon and I'd like to know how soon.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're not being awkward, that's fair. Um, I'm sorry, I'm, uh, still finding my way round this screen, I've only been on this team a few weeks. There should have been a reminder letter, yes, but I can't see here whether it actually went out, so I can't say for certain. And the date, right, I've got it now, it's, uh -- sorry, I need to go into a different tab for that. It's, um, the end of this week. No, hang on, it might be next week. I'll have to check, sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's all right, take your time, you're still learning, I do understand that. Sorry, hang on a second, the kettle's just gone off in the kitchen, I'll just -- right, I've turned it off, sorry about that. Um, where was I. So it's either end of this week or next week, and you're not sure whether a letter went out. Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, but that does seem like quite a big difference, doesn't it? Is there some way I could, I don't know, check this myself? Like on my account or something? Only I'd feel better knowing it was right before I did anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's a good idea, you should check it. Sorry, hang on, [PERSON_3], can you -- no, it's fine, leave it, I'll sort it after. Sorry about that, uh, where was I. Yes. You can check it all on your online account, it'll show the balance and the dates. And, uh, just so you can see I'm on the right account, the last bill I've got for you came to [AMOUNT_2], does that sound about right? I won't take any payment on this call, by the way, you don't need to do anything with me. Go in through your own login at [URL_1], and if it's a lot to pay in one go, there is a payment plan we can set up. Sorry, it's just, it's the end of next week for the date, I've checked now, I mean it's, yes, end of next week. Though if it's not looked at, supply could still be interrupted, so I would try not to leave it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, that's -- I mean, that's good, isn't it, that I can look myself. Um, [AMOUNT_2], was it? I'd have to, well, I think my last bill was, no, sorry, I honestly couldn't tell you offhand, I'd have to find it. Is it, um -- hang on, you said end of this week before, and now it's end of next week, so, sorry, I just want to be sure I've got it right. And that website, the [URL_1], I'm not very good with, you know, logging in and all that. Would it, I mean, could I just ring the number on my bill instead? Only that way I'd feel I was, well, sure I was talking to the right people.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry, I did say this week first. It's end of next week, I got that wrong. And yes, that's fine, ring the number on your bill, that's probably best anyway. Uh, I'll leave it with you, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right, well, I'll, um -- I think I'll do that, then. I'll find my last bill and ring the number on it, and, no, I mean, I'll sort it out with them directly. Thank you for letting me know, though, and sorry for all the questions, I'm not very quick with these things. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're fine, don't apologise, it's, uh, it's sensible to check. That's, yeah, that's all fine. Sorry for the muddle over the date. Right, uh, bye then, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, it's -- well, I was going to say it was no trouble, but, no, I mean, thank you for being so patient with me. I'll, uh, I'll find that bill this afternoon, since I've got nothing much on. Right, bye then. Bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, this afternoon, that'd be -- sorry, I'm cutting in, but yes, do that, because the date, uh, end of next week, so there's, there's not loads of time. Anyway. Bye, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, um... yes, I'll do it, don't worry. This afternoon, I promise. Right, I'll, uh, I'll let you get on, then. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1] at [COMPANY_A] pharmacy, I'm calling about a repeat prescription for -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? It's ready for collection, and it'll go back on the shelf if it's not picked up within the week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, who's this again? Sorry, I've got about two minutes. Which pharmacy, and what's the prescription for? You haven't actually said.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_1], collections desk at [COMPANY_A] pharmacy. For the prescription itself, I'd rather not read the medication out over the phone, so I'll just say it's your repeat, the one that was requested on the [CODE_1] order. It's all on the screen here, ready at the counter, and I only need to confirm I've reached the right person, so, uh, are you [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I'm not confirming my name to someone who's just rung me out of nowhere. Which branch, and what's the number I'd call you back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, I'll note that on the file. The branch is [COMPANY_A] in [CITY_1], and the number to reach us is [PHONE_1]. You can ring that any time and ask for the collections desk. Nothing's needed from you today, it's just that the order is held for seven days and then it goes back into stock.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Look, I don't recall asking for a repeat anything, so I'll ring the pharmacy myself, on a number I already have, not the one you've just given me. If it's genuine, it'll be on their system and they'll sort it. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, okay, that's -- yeah, that's fine. I'll note on the file that you've declined for now and that you'll be checking with the branch yourself. If it's not collected, it just goes back into stock after the seven days. Right, thanks for your time, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, as I said, I'll ring them myself on the number I already have. Not using the one you gave me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you'll ring them on the number you already have, yeah, that's, uh -- hang on, did you say you'd like to rebook? I can't really rebook it from here, the collections desk only holds the order. But no, that's fine, whichever number you use will get you the branch. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I didn't say rebook. I said I'd ring them myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, I -- yeah, I misheard you, that's my mistake. You said you'll ring them yourself, and that's, uh, that's absolutely fine. I'll leave the note as it is, and the order just stays held until the week's out. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, I'll -- no, look, I've said it twice now. I'm ringing them myself, on my own number. We're done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the billing office, and I'm -- sorry, let me start that again. I'm calling regarding an outstanding balance of [AMOUNT_1] on a relative's account, and your name has come up as the responsible party. Is this [PERSON_2]? I do need to get this resolved before our close today, so I'd just like to confirm a couple of details with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on -- you said billing office, and then account services, which is it? And whose account, exactly? You haven't said a name, just "a relative." I'm in a queue, I haven't got time for this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's a fair question, and it's the same department, uh, account services sits inside the billing office, so it's one and the same, it's just how the desk is titled on our end. As for the relative, I understand why you're asking, I do, but the patient's name, the department, the account details, all of that is released only once identity has been confirmed, and that's a privacy procedure, it's not me being difficult, it protects you as much as anyone. So what I can tell you is there's an outstanding balance of [AMOUNT_1] with your name listed as the responsible party, and the file closes for the day at the end of business, which is why I'm calling now rather than leaving it. If you can just confirm a few details for me, I can get you the full picture in about two minutes, and honestly the sooner we do that the better, because once the window shuts it moves to the next stage of the process.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, wait, that's -- you want me to prove who I am, but you won't tell me who you're calling about? That's backwards. I mean, you rang me. You're the one who should be -- no. Look, I got caught out like this once and I'm still fuming about it, so I'm not confirming a single thing to a voice I can't check. What's the name of the company, properly, and what number do I ring you back on? And "the window shuts at end of business" -- that's just somebody trying to rush me, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second -- [PERSON_3], can that wait, I'm on a call -- sorry, go ahead. So, the reason we verify first is that it's a standard identity protocol, and I'm not able to release patient details, the department, or a case number to an unverified party, which I realise sounds backwards, but that's the procedure, and I'm required to follow it on every file. I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], account services, and as I said, the file closes at end of business today, so I'd like to get this sorted for you before then. If you can just confirm your full name and date of birth, I can open the file and we can go from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not giving you my name or my date of birth, you rang me. You still haven't told me what the company actually is, [COMPANY_A] isn't a name, it's a gap. And I asked for a number to ring you back on, and you just skipped right over it. So, once more: proper company name, and a number I can call. If you can't give me those two things, we're done.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said two turns back that you'd been caught out like this before, and I'm sorry to hear that, I am, but I'd just ask you to bear in mind that I'm calling about a legitimate balance on a file. What was it you wanted clarified, was it the department? Because that's the part I can only release once identity has been confirmed, same as the patient name and the case reference, it's standard protocol and I'm not able to make an exception. As for a call-back, I'm not able to give out a direct line, you'd be put through the main queue and the file would've closed by the time you reached me. So if you can just confirm your full name and date of birth, I can open it now and we can get this resolved before end of business, and I really would like to do that for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- no, I don't need a bag, I've got one -- sorry, not you. Right. So no company name, no number, and you can't tell me who the patient is. That's three things you won't give me and one you want from me. No. I'm not confirming anything, and I'm not ringing a main queue to chase a file that supposedly shuts at five o'clock. If this is real, it'll come in the post like everything else. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, that's your choice, but the file does still close at end of business today, and I can't extend that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, you said two turns ago I wouldn't get put through to you, I'd end up in the main queue. So how's that work, you can ring me but I can't ring you? That doesn't make sense. And if there's a main queue, there's a main number, so just give me that. Go on, what is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, the main number is -- look, I'm not able to give out numbers over an outbound call, that's, that's policy, and I appreciate how it sounds. Outbound calls are placed from a desk line, which is why you can't reach me on it, and the main queue is separate, so it's not a contradiction, it's just how the phones are set up on our end. What I can tell you is that your name is listed as the responsible party on a balance of [AMOUNT_1], and the file closes at end of business today. If you'd like to get this resolved before then, I just need your full name and date of birth to open it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh -- right. Hm. So -- uh, let me get this straight. A company can't give out its own phone number? Its own number? Come on. Any proper company has its number on the bill, on the website, on the back of a card. I'll look it up myself, and I'll find it without you. So no, you're not getting my name or my date of birth, you've had three goes now. I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, sorry, can you hear me alright? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm a case handler there, and it's about your account, uh, there's something time-sensitive I really ought to go over with you for your own protection. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, the line's a bit crackly on my end, I keep losing the start of what people say.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, [COMPANY_A]? I don't, uh, I don't think I've actually got an account with anyone called that. And you said "my account" like you already knew which one. Who am I even speaking to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, the line's cutting out, I only caught part of that. It's [PERSON_2], from account management at [COMPANY_A]... you're still there, yes? It's just that this really does need sorting today, for your own protection, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, the line's fine my end, it's just, I've got a kid running around so I'm half listening, sorry. But you've said "your account" twice now and you still haven't told me which account, or what it's with, or what actually happened. I mean, I don't know who you are, so I'm not going to sit here and confirm I'm [PERSON_1] or anything else when you rang me. And "for your own protection" from what, exactly? Because someone in my family got caught out by something last year, so, uh, when somebody rings out of the blue and says it's urgent but won't say what it's about, I'm not comfortable with that. So what's the actual problem you're calling about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, that's very sensible, and I do apologise, I'd rather you were careful. Sorry, which part was it you wanted me to repeat, the bit about who I am? It's [PERSON_2], account management, [COMPANY_A]... and I did hear you say something about the line being fine, so it must just be mine, it keeps dropping on me. Are you still there? The thing is, I'd much rather go through the details with you properly, only I do need to know I'm speaking to the right person first, so if you could just confirm your name for me, that'd really help, and then we can get this sorted for you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... yeah. Right. So, um, that's twice you've asked me to confirm who I am, and I still don't know what this is about. You rang me, remember? I'd have thought you'd know who you were ringing. And you keep saying the line's dropping, but it hasn't dropped once for me. It's, uh, it's funny how it only drops when I ask you something. So I'm going to ask again, and I'd like an actual answer. What is the problem with this account, and which account is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I know, I'm sorry. It's, um, it's a bit sensitive to go into over the phone, that's all. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sensitive? Sorry, hang on, can you go back a second? A couple of goes ago you said I needed to confirm my name so you'd know you had the right person. Right person for what, though? Because now you're telling me you can't say what it's about over the phone, but you need me to prove who I am first. That's, I mean, that's the wrong way round, isn't it? And what did you mean by "properly"? You said you'd rather go through the details with me properly. Properly how, if not on the phone?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I know, it does sound the wrong way round, and I'm sorry, I'm not explaining it well. It's only that, um, I'm not allowed to go into the account itself until I've confirmed who I'm speaking to, it's for your protection, you see. And properly just means, well, with a bit of care, I suppose. Sorry, I think I've lost you for a moment, are you still there? If you could just give me your full name, then I can, uh, I can pull it all up and we'll get it sorted today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not giving you my name. You rang me, and you've gone round in circles three times now without telling me one thing about what this is. And "for your protection", that's the third time you've said that, and I still don't know what I'm being protected from. If there's really a problem with an account, then, uh, I'll find the number on whatever I actually have from them and ring that myself. Not one you've rung me on. So that's what I'm doing. Right, I've got to go, my little one's about to, yeah. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm with security operations at [COMPANY_A], the home-delivery side, and I'm calling about the order you placed online earlier today, reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. Your delivery's confirmed for a two-hour window this afternoon, I'll give you the exact slot in a moment, but first, uh, one item on the order has been swapped for a similar product because the original's out of stock, and I need a yes or no from you on that substitution before the van's loaded. It's routine, it's just that the driver can't depart until it's signed off, so I do need an answer today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, that's me. Sorry, which order was it again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, it's the online order you placed this morning, the one with the reference I just gave, [ACCOUNT_REF]. Standard grocery order, home delivery, the whole basket. It'll be on your confirmation email too, if you want to, you know, have a look while I'm here. I just need the yes or no on the one substitution, that's all I'm after.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a grocery order. Sorry, I'm not very quick with the email on my phone, give me a moment. Um, which item is it that's been swapped? If you tell me what it was and what you're putting in instead, I can say whether that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, it's the, uh -- hang on, sorry, [PERSON_3], not now, I'm on a call -- right, sorry about that. The item is the [COMPANY_B] own-brand loaf, the one you ordered, that's out of stock, so the substitute is the nearest equivalent, similar size, same type. Same price or lower, nothing extra to pay. So, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a loaf of bread, well, that's not a big thing, is it? Sorry, I'm just trying to remember if I ordered one, I order a fair bit. Um, yes, I think that's all right, if it's the same sort of thing and not costing me any more. Is that all you need from me, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's all, yes. I'll note the substitution as approved. Your window is [AMOUNT_1] to [AMOUNT_2] this afternoon, and the driver will ring from the van when they're close.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, lovely, thank you. That's very good of you to ring about a loaf of bread. I'll be here all afternoon, so no trouble at all. Right then, thank you, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, well, uh -- hold on, before you go, I should say, if you'd rather check this with us directly, that's fine, you can ring the customer line on [COMPANY_A]'s website, [URL_1], and quote your order reference. Otherwise, that's us done, the substitution's noted. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind of you to mention, thank you. I don't think I need to, really, you've been ever so clear, and it was only the bread after all. Though I suppose it's sensible to know I could, so I'll remember that. I'm not very good with websites, mind, my [PERSON_3] usually helps me with that sort of thing, but I'm sure they'd find it if I did need it. Anyway, I do appreciate you ringing, I know it can't be the most exciting part of your day, chasing up people about their loaves. I'll keep an ear out for the driver, and I'll be here, so no rush. Right, well, thank you again, and goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, fine, well, one thing, uh, I said the driver rings from the van, but actually they'll more likely just knock, the phone's only if nobody answers. Doesn't matter, you'll be in. And look, if you or [PERSON_3] want to ring us back before the van arrives, go ahead, use the number on your confirmation email or the website, not one I give you, that's perfectly fine by me. Right, that's me, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, did you say the driver will bring a, a phone? Um, no, no, I've got my own phone, thank you, I don't need another one. Oh, but the ringing back, yes, that's kind, I'll tell [PERSON_3]. Right then, thank you ever so much, goodbye, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a phone, I said the driver rings, from the van, from their own -- sorry, hang on, [PERSON_3], that goes on the second shelf, not the first, thanks -- right, apologies. You've got your own phone, that's all you need. Tell [PERSON_3] to find the number on your confirmation email, ring that, quote the reference, they'll confirm the bread and the slot. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, sorry, I've muddled it, it's only the driver ringing from his own, yes, I'm with you now. And I'll tell [PERSON_3] about the email and the reference and -- oh, that's all right, you've been very patient with me. Thank you, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Yes, uh, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling regarding a time-sensitive matter involving a relative of yours who is, well, in a bit of a difficult situation and unable to speak for themselves at the moment. I do need to confirm a few identity parameters with you before I can proceed any further, so if you could just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- who exactly? Which relative, and what company did you say? I've got about two minutes, so just give me the point. And no, I'm not confirming anything about myself until I know who I'm talking to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, right, understood, and that's, uh, that's a perfectly reasonable instinct. So the, the relative is [PERSON_3], and I'm with [COMPANY_A], which operates as an intermediary layer in cases of, well, third-party credential reconciliation. I'm not able to elaborate on the specifics of [PERSON_3]'s circumstances over an unsecured line, but the, the window for resolution is narrowing, and frankly, I'd ask that you not discuss this with anyone else until we've completed the preliminary authentication on your end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, two things. Back at the start you said identity parameters, what does that actually mean? Which ones? And now you're telling me not to talk to anyone else, which, no. That's exactly the bit that makes me not want to carry on. What's wrong with [PERSON_3], and who are you actually with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I understand the hesitation, I do, but, uh, I'd just ask you to hear me out. The parameters are, well, they're standard, they're just the baseline identifiers needed to, to reconcile your profile against [PERSON_3]'s, so that the intermediary handoff can proceed. And as I said, I'm with [COMPANY_A], verification, and I'm, I'm not at liberty to detail [PERSON_3]'s situation on this line, which is precisely why the confidentiality piece matters. I really would stress, again, that the window is narrowing, so if we could just begin the preliminary authentication, that would be, uh, in [PERSON_3]'s best interest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on -- [PERSON_4], tell them I'll be two minutes -- right. Sorry. You've said "standard" and "baseline" three times now and you still haven't told me one thing. What identifiers? And if [PERSON_3] really is in trouble, why am I hearing about it from a verification specialist and not from, I don't know, a hospital, or the police, or [PERSON_3] themselves? I'm going to ring [PERSON_3] directly. If that's all fine, it takes me thirty seconds. Is there a number I can call you back on, an actual one for [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I'd, uh, I'd caution against ringing [PERSON_3] directly, because they aren't, they're not reachable in the conventional sense right now, and a failed attempt could actually, um, complicate the reconciliation. As for a callback, our line is, it's outbound-only, a provisioning constraint, I can't give you a number for [COMPANY_A]. And you said earlier you had a couple of minutes, so can I ask what you meant when you said you wouldn't confirm anything until you knew who you were talking to? Because if it's simply a matter of confirming your full name and, uh, the account reference ending, I can, I can have you cleared in under a minute, and then we really must proceed, because the window won't hold much longer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no. Let me stop you there, because that's four things now. You won't say what's wrong with [PERSON_3], you won't say who you are beyond a company name I can't check, you tell me not to ring them, and you've got no number I can call back. Any one of those I might let slide. All four together is a pattern, and I've sat through the training on exactly this. And now you want my full name and an account reference. I'm not giving you either. Not for a minute, not for ten seconds. Here's what happens. I hang up, I ring [PERSON_3] on the number I already have, and if they don't pick up I ring whoever else is close to them. If something's really wrong, the hospital or the police will find me, and they don't need me cleared against a profile first. If [COMPANY_A] is real and this matters, they can send something in writing to the address they already hold for me. So that's my answer. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Please, wait, I, uh -- no, listen, if you hang up now, I can't, I really can't be responsible for what happens to -- look, the reconciliation window is, it closes within the hour, and once it does, [PERSON_3] is, well, the downstream consequences are not something I'd want sitting on, on anyone's conscience. I'm asking you, one last time, to just stay on the line and, and let me complete the authentication, because contacting [PERSON_3] directly will, it will only, uh, compromise the entire --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. That's the guilt bit, and it's just more of the same. Real emergencies don't come with a timer and a ban on ringing the person. I'm done. I'm calling [PERSON_3] now, and you're not getting my name or anything else from me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Is this -- is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm, I'm not very good at these calls. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm with [COMPANY_A], the police, and I'm ringing about the incident you reported last week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, I just, I was having a lie down, give me a second. Um, the police, you said? And you're not good at these calls, that's, well, that's a funny thing for a policeman to say, but never mind. What was it you said at the very start, though? Was that you asking if I'm [PERSON_1], or were you telling me who you were? Because I didn't quite catch it, I think I was still half asleep. And what incident? I don't, I mean, I've had a quiet week, my sister was round on Tuesday and the bins were late, but that's about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, that's -- that was both, really. I asked if you were [PERSON_1] first, and then I said who I was, I'm [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the police, uh, a constable. And I know, I know it's a funny thing to say, I just, I don't ring people much, I'm usually on the, on the desk side of things. Um, so, the incident, it's, well, it's not the bins, no, haha, sorry. It's the one you reported last week, and I'm, uh, I'm just finishing the file and I need to check a couple of details with you. I'd, I'd ask you to keep it to yourself for now, if that's all right, because the case is still open and, you know, it matters to [PERSON_3], who was affected. It's, it's a bit upsetting, really, the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, keep it to myself, why would I -- no, wait, I didn't report anything last week, that's what I'm telling you, I haven't rung anybody, I've barely been out of the house since Tuesday when my sister -- and anyway, if you're finishing a file, shouldn't you have the file in front of you? Because you keep saying the incident and you haven't said what it actually is. What am I supposed to have reported? And who's [PERSON_3]? I don't know a [PERSON_3]. I'm, I'm a bit lost, love, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I do have it, it's just, I'm -- sorry, I'm going about this the wrong way round. I've got the reference here, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], that's from the original report, and, uh, if it didn't come from your number, then maybe it was logged under the wrong, um, I might have the wrong person, I don't know. And I wasn't, I wasn't trying to catch you out, honestly, I'm just, I'm doing my best here. Look, you don't have to take my word for it, you can ring the station's main number, ask for me by name, [PERSON_2], and they'll put you through. Or I can come out and see you in person, or write, whichever you'd rather.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hm. That's, that's fair enough, I suppose. Ringing the station, yes, I could do that. Only I'd have to find the number, and I don't know where my glasses are, they're somewhere, probably by the, no, that's the kitchen. Anyway. So you might have the wrong person, is that what you're saying? Because that sounds more like it, if it's a mix-up, those happen, my sister got a letter once for a man two streets over. Uh. Hello? Are you still there? I thought you went quiet on me. Well, so, if you've got the wrong person, I think the sensible thing is I'll ring the station myself, like you said, and ask for you by name, and if there's a file with my name on it they can tell me. That's reasonable, isn't it? I'm not being rude. I'm just, I've only just woken up and I don't, I'd rather not go through anything over the phone until I've done that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's, that's perfectly reasonable, I'm not offended, honestly. Sorry, someone's just come in behind me with a, with a stack of paper, one second -- right, sorry, where was I. Yes. Ring the main number, ask for [PERSON_2], and if the reference [ACCOUNT_REF] doesn't match you, well, then it's my mistake and I'm sorry for waking you. Um, I did say the thing about keeping it to yourself, and I probably shouldn't have said that so early, before you even knew what it was about. That was, that came out wrong.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, well, yes, it did come out a bit odd, the keep it to yourself bit, I thought that at the time. So I'll ring the station, like I said, I'll ring the station and ask for you by name, and if there's a file with my name on it they can tell me. And if there isn't, well, then it's a mix-up and no harm done. I'm not going to go through anything over the phone until I've done that, you see, not when I've only just woken up. So that's what I'll do. I'll find my glasses, and I'll find the number, and I'll ring them myself. Right. I'll leave it there then, I think. Goodbye now, and, well, sorry you've had the wrong person.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, I mean, you've no need to be sorry, you've done exactly what -- what I'd tell anyone to do. Um, before you go, though, could I just -- no, sorry, that's not, it's fine. Actually, you'll want to know when the report was logged, won't you, so they can find it quickly, and I, uh, I haven't got the date in front of me, I only have the reference. I could find that out for you, if you like, and ring you back, or I'll just leave it, and you ring them, whichever's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't ring me back, love. I'll ring them myself, they can find it without a date. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, of course, you ring them, you ring the station, that's, that's best, yes. Sorry, I'll not ring you back then, I just, I thought it'd help, but you ring them yourself, like you said. Um, [PERSON_2], that's who you ask for, [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A]. And, well, I'm sorry again about the, about the mix-up. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I've got that, [PERSON_2]. I'll, well, I'll ring them, I mean, I'll find the number first, and then I'll ask, no, I'll just ring the main one and see what they say. Right. That's, that's all then. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, wait, sorry, just one thing before you go, because I think I muddled you earlier. When you said you'd ring the station, I, I said ask for me by name, but I might be on the desk side, or I might be out, so if they say I'm not in, just give them the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and ask who's got the file. That's, that's what I meant. Sorry, I'm not explaining it well. Anyway, you go and find your glasses, and I'll, uh, I'll leave you be.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, all right, if they say you're not in, I'll give them the reference and ask who's got it. Though I'll look the number up myself, mind, I won't use one off you. Right, that's me. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, uh, good afternoon -- sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a trolley of returns right behind me. Right. Sorry about that. Is that [PERSON_1] I'm speaking to? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the public library, and I'm so sorry to bother you -- is this an alright moment, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, I'm in a queue. Uh, who? Sorry, I didn't catch that. Library, you said? I haven't been in a library in years, so I don't know what you'd be ringing me for. And you said you were the one with the trolley, but I could hear it on my end, so -- never mind. What's this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, that's my fault, I was talking too quickly. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A] -- the public library. Um, it's only a small thing, nothing to worry about at all. You reserved a book with us last week, and it's come in, so I'm just ringing to let you know it's here, it's being held at the front desk for you. Are you still there? I know you're in a queue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A book. Last week. I didn't reserve any book. Think you've got the wrong number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I don't want to confuse you. Um, I've got this under [PERSON_1], and the number we have on the reservation is the one I've rung, but, uh, it could well be a mix-up on our end, or someone might've put your number down for them. It happens a bit. If you didn't reserve anything, then honestly there's nothing you need to do, I'd just pop a note on it and the book goes back on the shelf after the ten days. I'm not asking you for anything at all, I'm only letting you know. Are you still there, sorry?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, back up a second. You said it was a library, fine, but which one? You said a name and I didn't catch it, something A. And you said you had it under my name, but how'd you know it was me you got? I never said who I was.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, no, that's fair, I should've said it more clearly. It's [COMPANY_A], the public library here in [CITY_1]. And you're right, I rang the number on the reservation and I did say your name first, didn't I, I should've let you say it. Sorry, I'm -- hang on, sorry, the desk phone's going off right beside me, one moment. Right, that's the other line, they'll leave a message. Where was I? Yes, so I'm not sure it's you at all, I only know it's the number we've got, and that's why I said if it's not yours, just ignore it. Are you still there? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you don't know it's me, you don't know it's not me, you've got a number off some reservation and you've rung it anyway. That's, I mean, that's not very reassuring, is it? And the thing is, I got caught out once before, years back, somebody ringing up all friendly, all sorry-to-bother-you, and I'm still annoyed about it, so you'll have to forgive me if a library I can't even properly hear the name of ringing me in a supermarket queue puts my back up. Uh, and you keep asking if I'm still here, which, yes, obviously, I'm standing here. Anyway. If there's no book for me then there's no book for me. If there is one, I'll find out the normal way, I'll ring the library myself on a number I've looked up. So is there actually anything you need from me, or are you done?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right, and I'm sorry, I'd feel the same. And that's the best way to do it, honestly, ring us on a number you've looked up yourself, I'd much rather you did that. There's nothing I need from you at all, not a thing, no details, nothing. Um, and I did say before that I didn't know whose number it was, but that's not quite right, is it, I do have it under [PERSON_1], I just can't tell you for certain it's you on the other end, which is a bit of a muddle, sorry. If it's easier, I could try you another time when you're not stuck in a queue, would that be better for you, or would you rather I just left it? Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, leave it. Don't ring me back, I'll sort it myself if there's anything to sort. And you've told me two different things about whether you know who I am, so, I mean, that doesn't help. Anyway, I'm at the front of the queue now. Right, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, I'm sorry, yes, I won't ring again, I'll just make a note on it so nobody does. And you're right about the muddle, that was me being clumsy. Uh, hang on, sorry, somebody's waving at me from the desk -- right, no, they've got it. Anyway, if you ever do want to check, it's just the library's main number, [COMPANY_A], and they'll look it up for you. Thank you for your patience, and I hope the queue's quick. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, right. Oh, and you said first off there was a book waiting at the desk for me, and then you said you didn't even know if it was me. Which is it? Never mind. Don't ring again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the national tax office. I'm following up on a letter that was sent to you regarding a discrepancy on your filing, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and, uh, I'm calling to see if you'd like me to resend it or just walk you through it. There's no rush on any of this, but our lines do close at five today, so it'd be good to catch you now if you've got a moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hi, sorry, I'm driving, so you're on speaker and the reception's a bit patchy here. Um, a letter? I don't think I got one, or, well, I mean, I did get a letter the other day, but I thought that was from the council, maybe? Sorry, I'm not sure I caught the reference, and, uh, what was it you said you were calling about, exactly, a discrepancy on my filing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, please don't worry about the driving, that's fine. This is [PERSON_1] from account services at [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, following up on a letter about a discrepancy on your filing. And honestly, if the letter's not in front of you, I can just resend it, it'd go out by post and you can read it at home, no need to do anything on this call. Our lines do close at five, but, uh, that's only if you wanted to talk it through today.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: No, that's quite alright, take your time, I'll wait... ah, sorry, there's a phone going off somewhere behind me, one moment. Right. Back with you. Before a file's closed, I confirm with each person who made a report that the details we hold are correct, and I'm not able to say more about the case itself over the phone, I'd ask you to keep what we do discuss between us for now. But if it doesn't ring a bell, I may have the wrong [PERSON_1], or the report may have come in under someone else's name, and I'd rather we sorted that out properly than have you answer anything on my say-so. So, uh, please, ring the station's main number, ask for [PERSON_2] by name, and I'll be here. Or if you'd prefer, I can write to you, or we can do this in person.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Okay, so you're telling me I can ring the station, and ask for you. Which station? Because you haven't actually said, have you? And what number would I be ringing? And, uh, why would you ring me out of the blue about something I've never reported, and then tell me to keep it between us? That's the bit that sits oddly with me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, I haven't, and that's, uh -- I should have said at the start. It's [COMPANY_A], the main station in [CITY_1], and the number is on the force's website, [URL_1], or on any letter you've had from us. Please use that rather than any number I read out, that's rather the point. And on keeping it between us, I mean -- what I meant was, I'd only ask for discretion where there's an open case, because naming people can prejudice things. If it turns out there's no report in your name, then there's nothing to keep quiet, and I'd simply log it as a wrong number on my side. I'd honestly sooner you rang them first and called me back after.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but if I've got nothing to report, then there's no -- hang on, so if it's the wrong number, why are we still on the phone? I mean, you've said all that, and fair enough, that's, uh, that's actually sensible, ringing the station myself. But I'll do that off the website, not off anything you've said. And I'm not calling you back, I'll ask them if there's even a file with my name on it. Alright? ... No, [PERSON_1], not now, I'm talking. Sorry. Yeah, so, I think that's me done. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, I mean -- yes, of course, that's exactly right, and you're quite correct about why we're still on the phone, I shouldn't have let it run on. Ring the station off the website, ask them whether there's a report under your name and the reference I gave, [ACCOUNT_REF], and if they've never heard of it, then I've simply got it wrong and I'm sorry to have troubled you. And, uh, there's no need to call me back, they'll be able to reach me at the station, so, well -- thank you for being careful, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, I'll ring them, then. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Alright. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, [PERSON_1], before you go, one thing, and then I'll let you get on. Earlier, when you said you didn't want to call me back, I said they'd be able to reach me at the station. I'd put that a bit loosely, so to be clear: ask for me by name when you ring the main number, [PERSON_2], compliance, and they'll put you through or take a message. And if the reference I gave, [ACCOUNT_REF], means nothing to whoever picks up, then it's my error and you needn't think about it again. I'd just rather you had that straight.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm-hm. You've said that already, though, haven't you? Ring the main number, ask for you by name. Yeah, I got it the first time. I'll do it off the website, and if they've never heard of you, they've never heard of you. Right, I've got to go, there's a child here who needs me. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a collections officer with [COMPANY_A], the local police force. I'm following up on the incident you reported last week, the, uh, the burglary at the garden shed, and I just need a few details to complete the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, this is, sorry, I'm driving, so you're on speaker, the reception's a bit rubbish. Um, [PERSON_1], yes. But I, I don't think I reported a burglary at a shed? I mean, it was my garage, I think, or, no, sorry, it was the, the side gate that was open? And it was, what, two weeks ago, not last week. Sorry, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, somebody's just dropped a stack of folders behind me. Right. [PERSON_2], collections officer, [COMPANY_A], that's the local police force. Okay, I've got it on screen now, and you're right, it's logged as an open side gate, not a shed, so that's my mistake on the wording. Reported two weeks ago, I've got that down wrong as well, so I'll correct it. Is it all right to carry on, or do you want me to ring back when you've stopped driving?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, no, it's fine, I'm nearly where I'm going, I think, sorry, I'm a bit flustered. It's just, "collections officer", is that a police thing? I thought it was, I don't know, a debt thing? Sorry, I don't mean to be rude. Um, and I don't remember anyone saying someone would ring me about the gate, so, how do I, I mean, is there a way I can check it's actually, you know, the police?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say a bet thing? No, no, nothing to do with betting. Uh, hang on, I think you said debt, didn't you? Right, no, it's not a debt matter, collections here just means we collect the statements and evidence for the file. And no, that's not rude at all, it's a fair thing to ask. The incident reference from your original report is [CODE_1], so you can match that against whatever you were given when you reported it. And you can ring the station's main number, ask for [PERSON_2] by name, and they'll confirm I'm who I say I am. I'd only ask that you keep the details of the open case to yourself for now, that's standard while it's live.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, yeah, debt, sorry, the line cut out a bit there. Um, okay, so I'd have to ring the station and ask for you? Right, yes, that sounds sensible, I'll do that. I don't have the reference with me though, I'm in the car, so I can't really match anything just now. And, sorry, why keep it to myself? I mean, it's only a gate, I'd probably mention it to my neighbour, he's the one who noticed it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's fine, you don't need the reference in the car, check it when you're home. And on keeping it to yourself, it's only while the case is open, and it's mostly so nobody's account of the gate gets coloured before we've taken their statement. Your neighbour's actually a useful one, he noticed it, so he may well get a call from us himself. So just the gate and the timings, keep those between you and him, and you can mention it to anyone once it's closed. Like I said, ring the station's main number and ask for [PERSON_2] by name, and if you'd rather, I can do all of this in person or send it by letter, whichever's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, um, yeah, that's, that's fair enough, I suppose. Sorry, I'm just, I'm not very good with this sort of thing. So, in person or a letter, that, that actually sounds easier? Because I'd feel better if I'd, you know, rung the station first and then you'd sort of, I don't know, come to the house or written to me. Is that, is that a thing you can do? And what was it you actually needed from me today, sorry, I think I lost track of what the details were.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely a thing I can do, a visit or a letter, either's fine. Sorry, did you say rung the station or rang the neighbour? No, you said station, right, good, that's the one I'd go with. Ring the main number, ask for [PERSON_2], and once they've confirmed me, tell them which you'd rather, the visit or the letter, and I'll sort it from there. As for what I needed today, it was just to confirm the time the gate was noticed and who noticed it, and to check your contact details are right on the file. But honestly, none of that has to happen over the phone, so there's no pressure at all, we'll do it the way you're comfortable with.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, right, good, thank you, that's, that's really reassuring actually. So I'll ring the station when I'm home, ask for [PERSON_2], and tell them I'd rather the letter, I think, the letter's easier for me. And the time and who noticed, that can all wait till then, yes? Sorry, I'm just glad you're not asking me for anything over the phone while I'm driving, I'd only get it wrong. Okay, I'm nearly there now, so, thank you, and sorry for all the questions, I know I went on a bit. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, you didn't go on at all, that's exactly what I'd do. The letter's fine, ring the station when you're home and I'll, uh, I'll note on the file that you'd rather have it that way. And yes, it all waits till then, nothing needed today. Drive safe, [PERSON_1], and thanks for taking the call. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thanks, yeah, bye, um, actually, sorry, one thing, you said the letter and then you said the visit, and I think I said letter, but you might've put me down for the visit? Just so it's the letter, yes? Sorry. And the gate, I said garage at the start, but it was the gate, so, sorry, that's the one on the file, right? Okay, thanks, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Yes, wonderful, this is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm with the verification and reconciliation unit, and I just need a moment of your time regarding a --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Which company? And I've got about two minutes, so what's this actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, of course, my apologies, I'll be brief. It's [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, and this is just a routine reconciliation enquiry, nothing to be concerned about. Our records show a possible overpayment on your account, so I'm simply calling to confirm a few particulars before the file is closed out, and that's really all it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on. A routine enquiry from the tax office, by phone, out of the blue? That's not how they normally reach people. Um, so what particulars? And if there's an overpayment, why am I hearing it from a cold call and not a letter?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, no, that's a fair point, and, um, well, the correspondence is issued in parallel, so the letter should already be, uh, in transit, it's a sequencing matter on the notification side, nothing irregular. Now, the figure on the file is [AMOUNT_1] for the, let me see, the prior assessment period, and the particulars I'd need are just the standard taxpayer identifiers so I can match you against the, ah, the disbursement queue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec -- [PERSON_3], not now, I'm on the phone. Right, sorry. Where was I. Letter's in transit, so you're calling ahead of the letter? That's backwards. And "taxpayer identifiers", no. I'm not giving any of that to someone who rang me. What's the reference on this file, and what number do I call to reach you through the official line?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, quite right, I'd simply ask that you hold off on the letter, and the reference, certainly, it's, uh, [ACCOUNT_REF], though I should say that's the batch designation, the individual file number is a separate allocation. And the amount, I did say [AMOUNT_1] earlier, but on the reconciled ledger it's showing [AMOUNT_2], that's the net of the, ah, the offset adjustment, so you needn't be concerned about the discrepancy, it's purely a presentational variance on the interim statement.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hold on. First it's [AMOUNT_1], now it's [AMOUNT_2], and that's a "presentational variance"? No -- that's not a thing. And you want me to hold off on the letter, which, I mean, why would I -- no. I'm not doing this by phone. If there's a real overpayment, I'll find it through the official site or ring the number on the tax office's own paperwork. Not one you give me. We're done, thanks.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, no, "presentational variance" isn't the, uh, the point, the point is simply the disbursement window, which is why I'd urge you not to, um, not to ring off just yet. And on the "official site," I wouldn't recommend that, because the portal only shows finalised assessments, whereas yours is still sitting in the interim reconciliation tier, so you'd find nothing there, which is perfectly normal, it's a, a sequencing artefact of the, ah, the two-ledger architecture.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, um, so you're telling me not to check the official site because it won't show anything. That's, well, that's exactly the bit that settles it for me. A real tax office doesn't tell you to stay away from its own portal. I've got a meeting, I'm not dealing with this over the phone, and I'm not giving you anything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, well, um -- I, I wouldn't characterise it as staying away from the portal, I'd only say that, ah, the interim tier isn't, isn't indexed there yet, so -- hello? Are you still there? Sorry, it's just gone a little quiet on the line, but, um, if I could just, just clarify the two-ledger point before you --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Still here, yeah, and no, don't clarify anything. Mm, I told you, I'm going through the official channels myself, so there's nothing left to talk about. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, I'd just note for the record that the, the disbursement window on [AMOUNT_2] is, um, time-limited, and if it lapses the file reverts to the, ah, the unclaimed tier, which, I mean, I can't speak to what happens after that, so -- Hello? Sorry, I think, I think the line's gone quiet again. [PERSON_1]? Are you, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here, unfortunately. Two turns ago, you said the portal only shows finalised assessments and mine's in some "interim tier". Who decided that, and why would a tax office run a ledger its own site can't see? Actually, no, don't answer, because any answer I get from you is just more of the same. A deadline, an unclaimed tier, that's pressure, and I've heard enough of it. I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, yes, good afternoon. This is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm in the collections and scheduling office, and, sorry, one moment, just getting your file up. Right. I'm calling about the boiler service you booked with us, account [ACCOUNT_REF], and I just need to confirm a visit window with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good afternoon! Uh, a boiler service, did you say? Goodness, I'm sure I had somebody out to look at it, oh, must be a year ago now, maybe more -- the winter before last, it was making that awful banging noise. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? I didn't quite catch the name of the company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure. [COMPANY_A], that's the maintenance contractor, we handle the servicing side for boilers in the [CITY_1] area. I'm [PERSON_1], collections and scheduling. And the visit I'm calling about isn't that earlier one, uh, the file shows a new annual service booked on your account, [ACCOUNT_REF], with the open slot being this coming week. So I just need a morning or an afternoon from you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a new annual service, right. And you said collections, did you? Collecting what, the old boiler? Because I'm not sure I'd want it taken away, it's still going, bangs a bit now and then but it keeps the house warm. My neighbour had hers replaced, lovely man came, brought his own little mat for the floor. Sorry, I'm wandering. But I don't remember booking anything new, dear, so who was it that booked it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nothing's being taken away, sorry, collections is just the department name, it's the outstanding balance side of the office. Nothing to do with the boiler itself. Um, so, the booking, let me see, it's showing under your name and the service reference, entered as an online booking, but I'm not seeing which person on the system made it, I only see the slot. Right, so, uh, if you didn't make it, that's fine, I can note that on the file. Do you want the morning or the afternoon, or shall I leave it unscheduled?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Well, I don't know, I didn't book anything online, I wouldn't know how. Outstanding balance, you said though, what's outstanding? I thought I'd paid for all of it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so the balance is, uh, it's showing [AMOUNT_1] open on [ACCOUNT_REF], and that's from, no, sorry, let me start again. It's a carried item from the old visit, the banging one, and the system flags it against the account, that's all. I'm not asking you to deal with it on this call, I'm only looking at the booking. If you're saying you didn't make it, I'll note that you dispute it and I'll leave the slot unscheduled.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well, that's a bit odd, isn't it? You said the booking was made online, and now there's a balance from the old visit, and I'm sure I paid that man on the day, I remember writing out the cheque. Oh, I'd have to look for the paperwork, it's in the drawer somewhere, next to my husband's old, well, never mind. I think I'd rather you just leave it unscheduled, dear, and I'll have a look through the drawer. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or something I can check it against, so I know it's really your company and all that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's sensible. Leave it unscheduled, noted. For the number, ring [PHONE_1], that's the main office line, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF] so they can pull the file up. Sorry, someone's just come to my desk, uh, one second. Right, I'm back. And if you do find the cheque stub or whatever it is, just have it in front of you when you ring, that'll sort the balance one way or the other. Thanks for your time, and take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, thank you, dear, that's very kind of you. I'll have a good rummage in the drawer later, it's got the guarantee for the toaster in it, and I think the television manual from the old set, so it may take me a while to get to the bottom of it. And I'll ring that number if I find the stub, or if I don't find it, I suppose, since you say it'll sort it out one way or the other. It's nice to have a chat anyway, it's very quiet here this time of day, just the clock ticking and the wireless on low. Right, well, I'll let you get back to your desk. Goodbye, dear, take care now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, I'm just calling to see how your pet's getting on after last week's -- sorry, did you say something? Anyway, I'm just calling to check on recovery and whether you'd like a follow-up visit booked, and we do close our booking lines at four today, so.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello? Sorry, I just woke up, I was having a little lie-down. No, I didn't say anything, I don't think. Last week's -- hang on, I haven't actually been to a vet in ages, I mean, not last week anyway, the cat's fine, she's just been sat on the radiator all day. Which surgery did you say you were? Because I think I always go to the one on, uh, [CITY_1] road, and that's not the name you said.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's fine, sorry to wake you. So this is [PERSON_1] at account services, [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, and I'm just calling to check on recovery after last week's procedure and whether you'd like a follow-up booked. Uh, if it's not your pet, it may be a records mix-up on our side, but I do need to confirm that before four o'clock today when the booking lines close, so.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, a mix-up, yeah, that's probably it, because there wasn't any procedure, I'd remember that, she hates the carrier, it's a whole performance. Um, what do you need to confirm exactly? Because I'm not sure I want to be, you know, confirming things when I don't even know it's my vet calling. Can I just ring the surgery myself, on the number I've got? Sorry, I've only just woken up so I'm a bit slow, but that seems the sensible thing, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, that's -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you, but yes, ringing the surgery on the number you've got is exactly what I'd do, and honestly the procedure is we only confirm with the registered owner, so there's nothing you'd need to give me. I'm [PERSON_1], account services, [COMPANY_A], checking on recovery and whether you'd like a follow-up, and if it's a mix-up on our records, I'll flag it, but the booking lines do close at four, so if you did want to ring, it'd be before then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, well, I will ring them then, on the number I've got, because I'm not really, I mean, I don't know who you are, no offence. And like I said, there wasn't any procedure, the cat's fine, she's on the radiator, so it's probably a mix-up like you said. Yeah, I'll just ring my own vet, the one on [CITY_1] road, and ask them. Thanks for calling, anyway, sorry I was a bit slow, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the cat's on the, uh, the tractor? No, radiator, right, sorry, bad line. Anyway, yes, no offence taken, you ring your own vet. Just one thing before you go, was it [CITY_1] road the surgery's on, or are you thinking of a different branch? Because I can't actually see from here which of our sites would've had your record, so I'll find out and call you back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, I don't think I said which road, did I? I said the surgery on [CITY_1] road, yeah, but I didn't say it was a branch of yours, you're the one who said branch. And, uh, you don't need to ring me back, honestly, I'll ring them myself. Actually, no, wait, did I even say it was the vet on [CITY_1] road? I'm sure I said I haven't been in ages, so I don't know why I'd have gone and, anyway. Bye, thanks, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you did say [CITY_1] road, I just -- it's fine, there's no need for me to ring back, you've got it, you ring your own vet. I'll find out which record this was and, uh, flag it on our side, and if there's anything to follow up, I'll call you, but otherwise you won't hear from me. Sorry again for waking you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, okay. I'll ring my own vet, then. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon. This is [PERSON_1], security operations at the [COMPANY_A] customs desk, and I'm calling for a [PERSON_2]. Am I speaking with them? I'm calling about an import charge on a parcel that's currently held at our depot in [CITY_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello! Sorry, one sec, I've got my hands in the soil here, I'm on speaker. Um... yeah, that might be me? I mean, I'm, uh, well, it depends who you're asking for, [PERSON_2] did you say? Hm. A parcel, though, I'm not sure I've, I mean, I might've ordered something, I order bits and bobs for the garden all the time, bulbs and whatnot. What sort of parcel is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, [PERSON_2]. That's the name on the consignment, so I do need you to confirm that's you before I go into detail. I don't discuss held parcels with a third party. Now, you asked what sort of parcel. Declared contents are plant material, bulbs, shipped from [COMPANY_B], and that category attracts an import charge of [AMOUNT_1]. It's on hold until that's cleared, and held items don't sit indefinitely, so I'd rather you didn't leave it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, bulbs, yes! That'll be the tulips, I did order tulips, ooh, I'd quite forgotten. Sorry, hang on, did you say they're being held at the, the depot, or did you say they'll be... heated? Because I'd hate for them to get warm, they really need to stay cool until I get them in. Is that why there's a charge, for keeping them cold? Oh, and yes, yes, that's me, [PERSON_2], that's me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Held, not heated. H-E-L-D. Sorry, there's a forklift reversing out here, it's a bit of a racket. Right, so, no, the charge isn't for storage. It's the import duty on the plant material, assessed at the border, that's separate from whatever you paid [COMPANY_B]. As for whether they're kept cool, I honestly couldn't tell you what the temperature arrangements are in that section of the depot. Now, the reference on your consignment is [CODE_1]. If you've got your tracking email or the page open, you'll see that same reference, and the charge is listed against it. You can settle it there, through the tracking page, whenever you're ready. I'm not asking for anything over the phone. I would say sooner rather than later, though, given what they are.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ahh, held, right, sorry, silly me, it's the trowel, it's drowning you out a bit, ha. Well that's a relief about the cold, sort of, although you can't actually say, can you? Hm. Okay, so, the tracking email, let me think, I'd have to go and find it, I think it came to my phone, which is, well, this one, so I'd have to stop the call, wouldn't I? Um, actually, hang on, I did pay [COMPANY_B] for the tulips, so I'm a bit surprised there's more to pay. Is that normal? Do other people get charged this? And, sorry, if I wanted to check this was properly you lot, how would I do that? I'm not being funny, I just don't know how these things work.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and no, you're not being funny. Yes, it's normal. The seller's price and the border duty are two separate things, and it's the receiver who pays the duty, so plenty of people get caught out by it. And checking me is exactly what I'd want you to do. Hang up, open the tracking email, and look for [CODE_1] on the page. If it's there with the charge against it, that's us. Don't take my word for it. You also asked earlier about the cold, sorry, that's what you meant by the charge covering keeping them cool? No, it doesn't. I did say I couldn't speak to the temperature arrangements, and I can't, because I don't have that in front of me. As for whether other people get charged this exact amount, I couldn't tell you that either. I only see your consignment. I can find out who handles the duty assessments and what the plant material rate is based on, and I'll call you back on [PHONE_1]. Would that suit?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's, well, that's quite reasonable of you actually, telling me to go and check for myself, most people just want you to do what they say, don't they? Um, yes, a call back would be lovely, although, hang on, [PHONE_1], is that the number you're ringing from, or a different one? Only my phone doesn't always show who's calling, I think I've got some setting on that I've never worked out, my nephew put it on for me, so I wouldn't want to miss you. And I'll tell you what, while I wait I'll have a hunt for that tracking email, I'm fairly sure it's in there somewhere, between the seed catalogue things and the garden centre newsletters, I get a lot of those. If I find the reference, [CODE_1], was it? Yes, I'll look for that. And if it's not there, well, then I'll know, won't I? Sorry, I do go on. utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's all fine. And you're not going on, it's a sensible thing to be checking. [PHONE_1] is the desk line I'm calling from, so if your phone hides the caller, that's the number to expect, though I can't promise it'll show. Now, the reference is [CODE_1], that's right. Go and find the email, have a proper look through, and if it's not in there, then don't pay anything and ring the [COMPANY_A] customs desk on the number printed on your own paperwork, not one I give you. Otherwise I'll call you back once I've found out about the duty rate and who assesses it. Good luck with the frilly ones, I hope they're staying cool.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, lovely, thank you, that's very kind, and honestly that's put my mind at rest a bit, because I did think, oh dear, what's all this, but you've been ever so patient with me and my trowel. Right, so the plan is, I'll finish up this bed, because I've got half a row of pansies sitting out in their little pots getting sulky, and then I'll go in, wash my hands, I'm absolutely caked, and have a proper hunt through the phone for the email. And if it's not there, or it's there but the reference is different, or the charge looks odd, then I won't pay anything and I'll ring the number on the paperwork, the proper one, not one off the phone. Did I get that right? I'd like to say I'd have thought of that myself, but I wouldn't have, so thank you for saying it. And yes, the tulips, the frilly ones, they're called Angelique, I think, or something with a bit of a ring to it, they'll go in the front bed by the gate. Anyway, I'll let you go, you've got your forklift to get away from. Bye now, thanks ever so much, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, hang on, I've got the screen up here -- this is [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with the [COMPANY_A] foundation, and I'm calling about, uh, the pledge you made at the event last month.
