utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, a claims assessor? For a pledge? That's an odd job title for a charity. And what event are we talking about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, so, uh, claims assessor, that's just the, the role that handles pledges once they've been logged, it's, it sounds odd, I know. And the event was, um, the one last month, the recent one, where you gave the verbal pledge -- the, the verbal commitment, for the large donation. It's showing here as [AMOUNT_1], and it's got to be processed, so I just need to confirm it with you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. "The recent one" isn't an event. Which one? Name, date, city, anything. Because I don't remember making a pledge, verbal or otherwise, and [AMOUNT_1] isn't a number I'd say off the cuff at an event. Also, which foundation did you say again? I didn't catch the full name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, the details of the event are, um, they're on the pledge record and that's, that's confidential, I'm not really able to share the specifics over the phone. The foundation is [COMPANY_A], like I said. And, look, I understand it might have slipped your mind, but, uh, the beneficiaries are already counting on that money, so it'd be a real shame if it fell through because of a, a technicality. Can we just confirm the [AMOUNT_1] today so I can close this out?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a technician? Is something wrong with my account, or is this about the pledge? Because you've lost me. And I'm confused about the confidential bit. It's my pledge, supposedly, so how is the date and place of it confidential from me? That doesn't make sense to me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, not a technician, sorry, I said a technicality, uh, it's just the pledge, nothing to do with an account. And, I mean, the record's confidential in the sense that, um, I can't read out the internal file, that's just our, our process, I don't make the policy. Let me, uh, let me check if I can pull more up on that, hang on... okay, so it's showing the pledge as, as logged, and it's just, it needs to be honoured, and the longer it sits the harder it is on the people who were promised that support. So can you just confirm for me that you'll go ahead with the [AMOUNT_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not confirming anything. You've told me you can't say which event, you can't say when, and you can't say where, and I'm supposed to agree to a figure anyway? That's a no from me. And "it needs to be honoured" is a lot of pressure for a pledge I have no memory of. If it's real, there'll be a paper trail. So if the foundation wants to chase it, it can write to me, and I'll look up the charity myself rather than go on your say-so. Right, I'm going to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, [PERSON_1], please, don't hang up, I mean, there's no need for letters, that just slows everything down. It's, uh, it's actually [AMOUNT_2] on the file, sorry, I said [AMOUNT_1] before, I had the wrong line up. Look, it's only a verbal confirmation I need, and if I have to log this as declined, those families are, well, they've already been told it's coming. Can you just stay on with me a minute while I check something?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's the bit that's not helping you. You gave me [AMOUNT_1] a minute ago, and now it's [AMOUNT_2], and the explanation is that you had the wrong line up. A real file doesn't change its number halfway through a phone call. And I notice every time I ask for something I can check, the event, the date, the city, it's confidential, but the one thing you do want is a yes out of me, today, verbally. Letters slow things down, sure, but that's kind of the point. If a pledge is genuine, a few days of paperwork doesn't kill it, and the families aren't going to be any worse off because I took the time to check. So, I'm not going to stay on while you check something, because honestly I don't know what the something is. Log it as declined, log it as whatever you like. If the foundation's real, it knows how to find me in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, someone's just come to my desk, uh -- no, it's fine, one second. Okay, I'm back. Look, [PERSON_1], I really don't think you want this noted as you refusing to honour your word, because that's what it'll say on the file, and that's, well, that's not a good look with the foundation. I'm only asking for a quick yes today, and I can't put anything in writing from my end, that's just not how this works. Can you just stay with me and confirm it, please?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a delivery notification going off on the other screen. Okay. Right. So now it's a black mark on a file if I don't say yes to a pledge you can't describe, and you can't put anything in writing. That's a threat, with a bow on it. If I'd given my word at some event, you'd be able to tell me which one. You can't, so there's no word to honour. Note whatever you like on your file. I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], that's not, I'm not threatening you, I'm just, uh, I'm just telling you what the process is. I mean, I don't set it, I just -- look, I'll have to check on the event details for you, give me a moment, I'll, I'll pull it up. But I do need that yes today, otherwise it goes down as declined and I really don't want to do that to you. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you don't want to do that to the foundation? No, hang on, you said me, didn't you. Doesn't matter. I'm still here, yeah, I just stopped talking because you'd already got my answer. Pull up whatever you like, but it won't change it. Even if you come back with a date and a city, I'm not giving anyone a yes down the phone, not to you, not today. So, put it down as declined. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a collections officer at [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier. I'm calling about an overdue balance on your account, and there's a supply interruption date on the file, so I need a few minutes of your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on a sec -- no, not now, put that down, please. Okay. Who is this again? And, um, which company did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, sounds like you've got your hands full. Uh, I'll give you a second -- there's a phone going off somewhere behind me here, bear with me. Right. It's [PERSON_2], collections officer at [COMPANY_A], the company that supplies your energy. I'm calling about an overdue balance on your account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh huh. So, wait -- before you said there was a supply interruption date, and now it's just an overdue balance? Which is it? And I mean, how do I know you're actually from them? Because I haven't had anything from them about owing money.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Both. The balance is overdue, and if it isn't cleared, supply gets interrupted on [DATE_1]. That's just where the account stands. If you want to check me, your last bill shows the account reference ending [ACCOUNT_REF], and the balance outstanding on it was [AMOUNT_1]. I'll note on the file that you've queried it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Okay, but you're the one reading me the reference, so that's not really me checking you, is it? utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair point on the reference, you're right, it's me reading it out. So don't rely on me. Look at your last bill, or log in to your own account at [URL_1], and compare the balance. It should show [AMOUNT_1] outstanding, same as I said. And no, I didn't say gas. It's the one account, the electric. The balance is overdue, and supply gets interrupted on [DATE_1] if it's not cleared. That's the one account, electric, and that's the date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'm not logging into anything while you're on the phone, so that's not really... I mean, I'll look at my bill myself, later, and I'll ring them on the number that's printed on it. Not one you give me. Is that, um, is that all right with you? Because if it's genuine I can't see why that'd be a problem.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's all right, and honestly that's what I'd do in your position. Ring the number printed on your bill, not one I give you, and not one off a text or an email either. When you get through, ask them to confirm the balance, the [DATE_1] interruption date, and the payment plan options. We can set up instalments on this, so you don't have to find the full [AMOUNT_1] in one go, and that's a conversation you can have with them directly. I'm not taking any payment on this call, so there's nothing you need to do with me. I'll note on the file that you've declined to discuss it today and that you'll be verifying through your own account. If it's still showing overdue when it comes round, the supply gets interrupted, so it's worth doing sooner rather than later. But yeah, go ahead, check it your own way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's, uh, that's more or less what I was going to do anyway, so. I'll find the bill when the little one's settled, it's in the drawer somewhere, and I'll ring the number printed on it. And honestly, if there's a real date on the account, they'll tell me that when I get through, won't they? So I'm not going to rush into anything just because someone rang me on a Tuesday afternoon, you know? My, uh, a relative of mine got caught out last year by something like this, so I'm just, I'd rather be slow and annoying than quick and sorry. Not saying that's you, I just don't know that it isn't. So, right, I'll check it myself, and if it's all above board, then fine, no harm done. Thanks for not pushing me, I suppose. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said a relative got caught out by, uh, a crime like this? I can't speak to that, I'm only calling about your account. But yes, they'll confirm it all when you get through, so no harm done. I'll note the file that you're checking it yourself. Bye for now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah, I didn't say a crime, I said something like this, but, never mind. Anyway, I'm hanging up now, and I'll ring the number on my bill. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, you said something like this, my mistake. Fine, that's noted. Ring the number on your bill, they'll have the balance and the date in front of them. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, yep, I've got it, the number on the bill, I heard you the first time -- okay, bye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, which venue was that again? And, um, which colleague are we talking about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Totally fair question, [PERSON_1], everyone asks that. It's [COMPANY_A], we're the events venue in [CITY_1], and the colleague is [PERSON_3]. utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: Ha, no, nothing legal, sorry, I mumbled that, it's just a dinner, [PERSON_1], a lovely one, and I think the, uh, the -- sorry, go on? I've got [PERSON_2]'s name down as the organiser on our booking sheet, sorry, I mean the booking's under the organiser at [COMPANY_B], and I'm only ringing you because they listed you as someone who'd want to be there. I'm not asking you for anything, no money, no details, nothing like that. If the retirement part feels off, ring the venue on [PHONE_1] and the booking contact will tell you who made the reservation.
