utterances.text: Wait, you said the booking's under, uh, [PERSON_2]? That's you, isn't it? But then you said the organiser's at some other company. Sorry, I'm lost. And hang on, did you say my name was on a guest list, or on the, what, the cancellation list? I thought you said I was listed for cancelling.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, [PERSON_1], that's on me, I tangled myself up. Let me say it plainly. I'm [PERSON_2], I work at [COMPANY_A], the venue. The person who made the booking is someone at [COMPANY_B], that's the organiser, and I don't want to name them over the phone when I can't prove who I am. And it's the guest list, not any cancellation list, you're down as a guest. That's all it is, a guest list. So you're invited, and the only ask is don't mention it to [PERSON_3]. And like I said, you don't have to take my word for it, ring [PHONE_1], that's the venue's own number, ask for the booking contact, and they'll tell you the same thing. Honestly, everyone checks.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you've told me three different things about who booked it, and now you won't name the organiser because you can't prove who you are. Which is fair, but it's also kind of the whole problem. If it's a genuine guest list, there's a date on it. When is this dinner? And what's the venue's actual name, not [COMPANY_A], the thing you'd say if I walked up to your front door?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, you're right, I made a right mess of that, and I'm sorry, [PERSON_1], it's just, I'm not trying to -- okay, so the venue is [COMPANY_A], that's what's on the front door, that's the name, and the dinner's on the [DATE_1], I've got it right in front of me. And look, I'd honestly rather you didn't just take my word, I mean it, so here's the thing, put the phone down, ring [PHONE_1] yourself, ask for the booking contact, and ask them if there's a retirement dinner on the [DATE_1] with you on the guest list. If they say no, forget this call ever happened. If they say yes, then all I'm asking is you keep it from [PERSON_3], and we'll sort the rest through the organiser, easy. Does that sound fair?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, but, I'd be ringing a number you just gave me. That's the bit I keep tripping over. If I wanted to check, I'd look the venue up myself, not use [PHONE_1] off a call I didn't expect. And you still haven't told me who booked it. You said the organiser's at [COMPANY_B], so who is it? One name. Because if they put me on a guest list, they can't be a secret from me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, [PERSON_1], and that's the better way to do it, so please do. Look us up yourself, [URL_1] or wherever you'd normally find us, and use whatever number you find there, not mine. If it doesn't match [PHONE_1], that's fine, go with yours, I won't be offended at all. And on the name, okay, fair, I was being too precious about it. The organiser is [PERSON_3]'s manager, [PERSON_4], at [COMPANY_B]. They're not a secret from you, it's only [PERSON_3] who's meant to be in the dark. Sorry, I should've just said that first, I know I got in a muddle earlier. So, the plan: you check with the venue, you can even ask [PERSON_4] directly if you like, and if it all lines up, you just keep it quiet from [PERSON_3]. Nothing else needed from you, no details, no money, nothing. Does that work?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so [PERSON_4]. Okay. That I can check, because I can just ask them, and I'll do it the way I'd normally do it, not through anything you've given me. And, sorry, I'll say it again, you still haven't told me what you need from me. You keep saying nothing needed, no money, no details, but you rang me. Why ring at all if I'm just meant to stay quiet? If it all lines up, fine, I'll keep it to myself. But I'll sort that out first, and then I'll decide. Okay? Thanks for the call. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yeah, no, that's more than fair, [PERSON_1]. And you're right, I should've just said it straight up front. The reason I rang is really just so you hear it from us first, so you don't go and mention it to [PERSON_3] by accident before you've even been told. So, um, yeah, that's honestly the whole reason. Go and check with [PERSON_4] the way you normally would, and if it all stacks up, brilliant, and if not, no harm done, and you don't need to ring me back either way. Sorry again for the muddle, I'm usually better than that. Thanks for putting up with me, [PERSON_1], have a good one. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no worries. I'll check with [PERSON_4] my own way. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Brilliant, thanks [PERSON_1], that's all I -- oh, and one last thing, if [PERSON_4] asks who rang, just say [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], they'll know the name. Cheers, take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Okay, I'll say a person rang. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough, say whatever you like, [PERSON_1], honestly no pressure on that. Just ring [PERSON_4] the way you normally would and they'll sort you out. Cheers for your patience, take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. This is [PERSON_1], I'm a regional supervisor with [COMPANY_A], the tax office. I'm calling to follow up on a letter we sent you about a filing discrepancy, uh, and I can resend it or just walk you through it, whichever you'd prefer, there's no rush on any of this. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, this is -- well, sorry, I'm driving, so you're on speaker and the reception's a bit, it keeps cutting out. I'm, I mean, I think I got a letter? Or maybe I didn't, I'm not -- sorry, which office did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you're driving to the office? No, no, no need to come in anywhere, I'm with [COMPANY_A], the tax office, regional side. And look, if you're on the road, that's fine, we don't have to do any of this now, I can just resend the letter by post, there's no deadline pressing on it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, no, I said I'm driving, sorry, not driving to your office, I'm just, I'm in the car. And the reception's bad, so. Um, you said the tax office, right? [COMPANY_A]? And it's about a filing, a discrepancy? Sorry, I just want to make sure I heard that right, because I'm, I'm a bit anxious about it, honestly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [COMPANY_A], and a filing discrepancy, that's what the letter covers. Sorry, one second, someone's just come in with a -- no, it's fine, they can wait. Right, so please don't be anxious, it's a routine follow-up, and honestly, if you're in the car, the easiest thing is I resend the letter and you check the reference on it against whatever you've got at home.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, um, yeah, that, that sounds, well, sort of, I mean, sorry, it's just -- hang on, the signal's, uh, are you still there? Right. So, resending the letter, that's, I think that's probably best, because I can't really, I mean, I'm not going to be able to look at anything properly while I'm driving. But, um, how would I know it's really from you? Sorry, that sounds rude, I just, I got a bit worried when you said discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's not rude, that's sensible, and honestly I'd rather you asked. So, three things. When the letter turns up, it'll have a reference on it, and I'd like you to check that against any paperwork you've got from us, because if it doesn't match, that tells you something right there. Second, don't take my word for who I am. Look up the office's published number yourself, the one on our official page or on the letter, and ring that, and ask for me by name, [PERSON_1]. That's, uh, standard procedure anyway, we'd prefer people verify us. And third, you don't have to deal with any of this on the phone at all. If you'd rather, we handle the whole thing by post, you read it at home, in your own time, and reply in writing. Nobody's going to chase you today. I mean, I'll admit it's a bit frustrating when people hear the word discrepancy and assume the worst, but that's just the term the system uses, it covers everything from a transposed figure to a missing form, so honestly it's very likely minor.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, yeah, so I should ring the, the official number, and -- sorry, can I just, the post thing, is that actually, I mean, you're not asking me for anything today? Because I thought, sorry, I thought these calls usually wanted, like, details or a payment or something, and I'm, I'm not saying you are, I just --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, nothing today. No details, no payment, that's not what this call is for.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Okay. Well, that's, I mean, that's a relief, honestly, sorry, I know I keep apologising, I do that when I'm nervous, and I'm a bit more nervous than usual because I'm trying to watch the road and listen properly at the same time and the signal keeps dropping out on me. And I shouldn't have said that about those calls, it's just I've heard stories, you know, my sister got one once, or maybe it was a friend of hers, I can't remember, and ever since then I get a bit jumpy whenever anyone says tax or discrepancy or anything like that. So, yes, post is good. Post is better, actually, because then I can sit down at the kitchen table and read it properly instead of, I don't know, trying to take it in at sixty on the motorway. And I'll do what you said, I'll look up the number myself and ring it and ask for you by name. [PERSON_1], right? I'll try to write that down when I stop, because I'll definitely forget it otherwise. Um, so, is there anything else I need to do, or is that it for now? Sorry, I just don't want to hang up and then realise I missed something.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's genuinely it for now, and please stop apologising, you've asked exactly the questions you ought to ask. So, the letter goes out by post, it'll have the reference on it, you read it at the kitchen table, and if anything on it doesn't match your own paperwork, or you just don't like the look of it, you ring the published number and ask for me, [PERSON_1], regional supervisor. And if it's easier, you can answer in writing and never speak to me again, which, uh, I say with great affection. Oh, and one thing worth knowing for the next time someone calls claiming to be the tax office, and I mean anyone, including me: if they're pressing you to act today, that's your cue to hang up and ring the official number yourself. That's your sister's story in a nutshell, really. Now, did you want me to confirm the address we have on file for the letter, or, hang on, actually I should say, I don't think I can read that out over the phone, it's not something I'd do on an unverified call, and that cuts both ways, doesn't it. Which, uh, is probably the point where you ask me something I can't answer, so, go on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, yeah, that makes sense, I wouldn't want you reading it out either, honestly, not over the phone. Um, I'll just, if the letter doesn't turn up I'll ring the official number and sort it out that way. And thank you, really, for being so patient with me, I know I was a bit all over the place there, sorry, no, I said I'd stop. Okay, so, post, kitchen table, ring the number if anything looks off. I think I've got it. I'm going to concentrate on the road now, if that's alright. Thanks, um, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hello, [PERSON_1]? Yeah, sorry, bit of a gap on the line there. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a collections officer at [COMPANY_A], the pension provider. I'm ringing because we need to confirm a few details on your file before we can discuss a change to your plan, and if you're not comfortable answering anything on this call, that's fine, you can just ring us back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, I'm at my desk, bit noisy here. So you're, what, a collections officer? Pension provider? And you said, uh, a change to my plan, but earlier you said it was about confirming details on my file. Which is it, a change, or just checking things? I'm a bit lost on why you're ringing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question. Both, really. There's a change flagged on the plan, and the details check has to happen before anyone can discuss it. Nothing's been actioned yet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so nothing's been actioned, right. But I mean -- sorry, it's just, a collections officer ringing about a pension, that's, that's not what I'd expect. What kind of change are we even talking about? Because if you can't tell me that, then I don't really see how I'm meant to, uh, confirm anything. And how do I know you're actually from [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so two turns back, you asked which it was, a change or just checking. What's on my screen is a flag on your plan, an adjustment to the contribution arrangement, and I can't go into the detail until the details check is done. That's just how it's set up, I don't get to skip it. As for knowing it's us, you don't, not from me saying so on the phone, and I wouldn't ask you to take it on trust. If you'd rather not go any further, that's fine. I can note the objection on the file, and I can send the same query by post or through the secure message system instead. Nothing's urgent, there's no deadline on this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec -- no, [PERSON_3], that's fine, just leave it on my desk, thanks. Uh, sorry. Right, so, you said an adjustment to the contribution arrangement, and you can't say more until I've done the details check. Hm. That's sort of the wrong way round, isn't it? You ring me, you won't tell me what it's about, but I'm meant to confirm things first. I think I'd rather do the post thing, or the secure message, whichever, I'd rather do it that way. Or I'll ring [COMPANY_A] myself on the number I've already got. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, someone's just dropped a file on my desk. Right, yes, that's completely fine. Ring [COMPANY_A] on the number you already have, the one off your statements or the back of your card, whatever you trust. Don't use any number I give you. I'll note on the file that you've chosen to call back, and I'll flag the postal query so it goes out as well. You don't need to do anything today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I ring them on the number I already have, not one you give me, and you'll flag the post thing. Right. Uh, I'll -- no, sorry, I mean, I don't think I need anything else from you. Actually, hang on, should I mention your name when I ring, or -- no, I suppose it doesn't matter, they'll find the flag if there is one. Right, okay. Thanks, then, I'll sort it that way. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, do mention it, actually. It's [PERSON_2], collections, and say there's a flag on your plan. That helps them find it quicker. And like I said, ring on the number you already have, not one I give you. That's fine, that's absolutely fine. I'll note on the file that you've gone for the callback. Right then, thanks for your time, [PERSON_1]. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I say it's [PERSON_2], collections, and that there's a flag on my plan. Yeah, I'll tell them that. Uh, and if they've got nothing on the file, I'll just take that as it is, I suppose. I mean, I'm not saying anything's wrong, I just like to do these things properly, you know, with everyone listening around here, and I'd rather ring them myself when I've got a quiet minute. So I'll sort it that way, on the number I already have. Okay, thanks for being so patient about it, and bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's -- I mean, that's the right way to do it, honestly. And if they come back with nothing on the file, then, well, take that as it is, like you say. I'd rather you checked than, uh, than went along with something you weren't sure of. Ring when you've got a quiet minute, there's no rush on my side. Right, bye then, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, two turns back you said to mention your name when I ring, and I've got [PERSON_2], collections, and a flag on my plan. But you also said ring on the number I already have. Is that, uh, just the main pension line then, not some direct line for you? Because I don't want to be asking for you by name and have them look at me blankly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, [PERSON_3]'s just asked me something across the desk. Right, yes. The main line, the one off your statements, not a direct line for me. And if they look blank at my name, that's no problem, just say there's a flag on your plan and they'll pull the file up from your end. Don't read anything into it if they need a minute to find it, it can take a bit to show up. Anyway, ring whenever suits, and thanks again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Main line, off my statements. Right, okay. Thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, that's it. Take care, [PERSON_1]. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, bye, bye. Main line, off my statements, I've got it. Okay then, thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the collections office at [COMPANY_A]. Uh, you've supported us before, and I'm looking at your file here, and your monthly gift of [AMOUNT_1] stopped coming through a few months back. I just wanted to thank you for what you gave and ask whether you'd be open to starting that up again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, [COMPANY_A]... collections office? And you want me to start the monthly gift up again, is that it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Uh, "collections" is just the name of the department, it's the supporter side, not, I mean -- there's no debt, nothing's owed. The gift lapsed, that's all, and it's the sort of thing where the programme you were funding loses that income when it stops. So I'm just asking if you'd want to renew, either at [AMOUNT_1] or a different amount if that suits you better.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so no debt, it's just, uh, a lapsed gift and you're asking me to renew it. Right. Look, I'm at my desk at work, so, sorry, I'm a bit -- who exactly are you again? Because it's the "collections office" thing, I mean, that's a funny name for a donations call. And I don't actually remember stopping anything, so I'd want to, uh, check my own records first before I say yes to anything. So you're just asking, nothing's being taken today, is that right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, nothing's being taken today. I'm not asking for card details on this call, and nothing happens on your account unless you set it up yourself, so you're free to check your own records first. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a collections officer in the supporter team at [COMPANY_A]. And yeah, I get it, the title does sound odd for a donations call. If you'd rather not take it any further, just say, and I'll note it on the file and take you off the calling list.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, nothing taken today, no card details, and I can check my own records and you'll take me off the list if I say so. Fine. Honestly, I'd rather look into it myself, so I'll check my bank statements and, uh, contact [COMPANY_A] on whatever number I find for them. I won't take it any further on this call, so go ahead and note that on the file. Thanks for being straight about it, but, yeah, I'll leave it there. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, I'll note it on the file and take you off the list, so you won't get another call from us. Uh, and if the records show -- Sorry, go on, you were saying bye. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1]. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I'll -- well, if the records, I mean, if it turns out I did stop it, I'll sort that out myself, with them directly. So, uh, yeah. That's fine. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's a perfectly sensible way to go about it. If the records show the gift did stop and you want to pick it back up, you can do that with [COMPANY_A] directly, in your own time, through whatever contact details you find for us yourself. You don't need to go through me or anything from this call. I've noted on the file that you declined today and that you've asked to come off the calling list, so that's done and you shouldn't hear from our team again. And, uh, thank you for what you gave in the past, I mean that. The monthly gifts did go toward the programme, whether or not you decide to renew. Take care, [PERSON_1]. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah, so I'll check it myself, like I said, and sort it out with them directly if I need to. Through their own number, not through you. Okay. So, uh, thanks again, and goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hi, uh, hello. Sorry, is this -- am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Okay, good. So, um, my name's [PERSON_2], and I'm calling on behalf of someone over at [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, because, well, they asked me to ring about your account, and I'm, I mean, I'm not the one who normally does this kind of thing, I'm sort of helping out, so forgive me if I'm a bit all over the place. I just wanted to check first that I've got the right person before I say anything else, because I'd hate to bother someone who isn't, you know, who isn't the account holder.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, hi, this is, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm driving, you're on speaker and the reception's a bit rubbish out here. So who, um, who did you say you're calling from again? Sorry, I missed the company name, I think it cut out. And, uh, what account is this? Because I'm, I'm not sure I've got anything with a software retailer, but I might have, I don't know. Sorry, I know that sounds daft. Just, who is it you're calling from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that doesn't sound daft at all, sorry, it's me, I rushed it. It's [COMPANY_A], they sell software, you know, subscriptions and, and licences and so on. And I'm not actually, uh, I'm not calling from them exactly, I'm sort of passing a message along for a person there, [PERSON_3], who asked me to get in touch. And look, you really don't need to be doing this while you're driving, I can hold on if you'd rather pull over. It's just that there's a bit of a problem with a payment on the account, nothing awful, but, um, I'd like to explain it properly when you can hear me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's kind, thank you, but I can't really pull over just yet, there's, um, there's a bit of a lane closure and nowhere sensible to stop, and honestly it's only the reception that's bad, I can hear you fine, mostly. Sorry, I'm babbling, I always do that when I'm a bit nervous behind the wheel. But I'm, I'm sort of stuck on the, the who of it, if you don't mind. You're not calling from [COMPANY_A], you're passing along a message from [PERSON_3], who works there, and, and I don't think I know a [PERSON_3], and I'm still not sure I even have an account with them. I mean, I might, I've signed up for a few things over the years, you know, trial subscriptions, that sort of thing, and I never remember to cancel them. So, uh, when you say a problem with a payment, what, what actually is the problem? Like, which payment, and for what? Sorry, I just, I'd rather know what we're talking about before I, before I say anything, you know? And is there, is there a way I can check this is real, like ring the company myself afterwards? Sorry, that sounds terribly rude, I don't mean it to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not rude at all, honestly. Um, you said you'd rather know what we're talking about, and, right, yes, so it's a, a double billing. A subscription got charged twice, [AMOUNT_1] and then [AMOUNT_1] again, I think, or, no, [AMOUNT_2] the second time, sorry, I've got the figures muddled on my sheet here. And you said you can't stop because of the, the, uh, the lane clothes? Closure, sorry, closure. Right, so you're not on a call you can easily leave, I do understand that. And ringing the company afterwards, well, I mean, you can, of course, only the thing is, [PERSON_3] did say the refund has to be sorted while we're actually on the line, today, because it's sort of timed, and once it lapses it goes back to, I don't know, a different department, and then it's weeks. And I'd feel awful, honestly, if you lost that money because I was too slow, I've been trying to reach you since this morning.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, right, sorry, the lane, yes, closure, no, you're fine. But, hang on, can I just, you said earlier it was, what was it, nothing awful, and a problem with a payment, and now it's a refund that lapses today? And you said you weren't calling from them exactly, but you've got a sheet with the figures on it, so, so are you, I mean, do you work there or don't you? Sorry, I'm not trying to catch you out, I'm just, I'm trying to keep it straight in my head while I drive. And, uh, the other thing, you said you've been trying to reach me since this morning, but there's no missed calls on my screen, or, well, I can't really look right now, but I'd have thought I'd, I'd have noticed. Sorry. It's just, if it's timed like that, and it has to be done while we're on the line, that makes me a bit nervous, to be honest. Couldn't I just ring [COMPANY_A] myself when I get home and sort it out with them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I, no, I didn't mean to, uh, I'm not trying to make you nervous, honestly, that's the last thing. And I, I do work there, sort of. I mean, I'm not on the, the billing side, I'm just the one who got handed your name, which is why I keep, why I'm so rubbish at explaining it. And, um, the missed calls, no, you're right, I haven't actually rung before, I only meant I've been meaning to since this morning, sorry, that came out wrong. It's just, it's been a long day and I really don't want to, to be the one who let this slip. Look, if you ring them yourself tonight, I can't promise the refund will still be, um, still be there, and then you've lost [AMOUNT_2] over nothing, over me being clumsy. What it needs is, it's quite simple really, I'd just need you to let me, or [PERSON_3], get onto your computer for a few minutes, remotely, so we can see the charge on screen and push the refund through while you're on the line. You'd, you'd be in control the whole time, I promise. Is that, would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, well, uh... sorry, I'm just, hang on, the, uh, the lane's merging, give me a second. Okay. So, let me just, because I want to get this right, you want to get onto my computer, remotely, while I'm driving? Which I can't even, I'm in the car, I'm not near it, so that, that wouldn't work anyway, would it? And, sorry, but you've just told me you haven't rung before, and you're not on the billing side, and now it needs someone to see my screen? That, that doesn't sit right, I'm sorry. I think, I think I'd rather ring [COMPANY_A] myself tonight, on the number I already have for them, and if the money's gone, then, then it's gone. I'm sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I really don't. But I'm not comfortable with that, so, so I'm going to say no, thank you, and I'm going to go now. Sorry. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, wait, don't go, I've, I've handled this badly, I know I have. I'm not, I'm not trying to trick you, honestly, it's just, it's been such a horrible day and I'd hate to be the reason you lose that money. And the computer thing, you're right, you're driving, that's, that's my mistake, you don't have to do anything now. We can do it, um, when you're home and settled, I'll stay on the line, or I can ring you straight back, and you'd be in control the whole time, I swear. It'd only take ten minutes, and I just, I really don't want you to lose [AMOUNT_2] because I explained it so badly. Please, would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you'd stay on the line, or ring me straight back, and, and was that, did you say something about a, a clown? Sorry, the reception's gone all crackly again. Whatever it was, no, I'm, I'm sorry, but my answer's still no. I'm not going to let anyone onto my computer, not tonight, not when I get home, not like this. If there's really something owing, [COMPANY_A] can sort it out with me when I ring them on the number I already have. I'm sorry you've had a horrible day, I really am, but I'm going to go now. Please don't ring back. Bye, thank you, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, no, no, I said crown, sorry, no, I mean, I didn't say anything like that, the line's, uh, it's me, I'm rubbish on phones, I'm so sorry. Look, hold on, please, uh, just, hang on, are you still there? Um, because I don't, I mean, I really don't want you to lose that money on my account, and if you'd only let me, uh, sorry, give me a second, I've lost my place.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I am still here, but I did say bye, and I meant it. It's still no, I'm not letting anyone onto my computer, not now, not later, not with you ringing back. If there's money owing, I'll sort it with [COMPANY_A] on the number I already have. I'm sorry, I know you're having a bad day, but please don't ring back. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, just one thing before you go, and then I'll leave you be, I promise. Two turns back, when you said you can't let anyone onto your computer, did you mean not even if you were home, with the, the whole thing in front of you? Because I think I put it badly, I said ten minutes and I'm not sure that came across, and I just, I don't want you thinking I'd, um, I'd be doing something behind your back. Sorry, I know you said bye. I just feel awful leaving it like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, well, uh, yes, that's what I meant, not even at home, with it all in front of me. I'm sorry, I know that's blunt, and I do feel bad about it, but the ten minutes isn't really the thing, it's, it's that I can't tell who you are. So, um, yeah. That's, that's my answer, and I'm going to hang up now. Please don't ring back. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], we handle account management, and, uh, I'm calling about an important matter on your file. Sorry, the line's a bit rough on my end, so if I sound distant, bear with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, uh, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, you've caught me out in the garden, I've got you on speaker so I can keep my hands in the soil. Bit of a rough line, you said? Funny, you sound perfectly clear to me, a bit like you're ringing from the next room. Now, which company was that again? Because I'm sure I don't have an account with, um, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? Or do I? I do have so many bits and pieces.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yes, [COMPANY_A]. It's an account management firm, and, uh, it may well be tied to one of those bits and pieces. The line's still breaking up on my end, I'm afraid. It's best we sort it today, if we can.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, well, that's a shame about your line, because you're coming through fine this end. Hang on, let me just put the trowel down. Right. Today? Why today, what's the rush? And what is it, exactly, that's on my file? Because I really can't think what I'd have with an account management firm, I mean, I've got the bank, and the electric, and I think there's a pension somewhere, but, uh, nothing with that name that I recall. So what's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. It concerns an account in your name, [ACCOUNT_REF], and I'd rather not go into the detail until we've established it's definitely you. You're right to ask, of course. It's sensible. I'd just rather not say more on a line like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, sorry, hang on, can I go back a bit? Two minutes ago you said it was best to sort it today, and I never quite got why. What's actually going to happen if it isn't sorted today? And now you're saying you can't tell me anything until you know it's me, but you rang me, so how's that supposed to work? I mean, I'm not being awkward, I'm just a bit lost. And that reference you read out, I didn't catch it properly, and anyway I wouldn't know whether it was mine or not.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you're asking it, I'd think less of you if you didn't. But what I can say is that the sooner it's looked at, the better for you. Sorry, the line just went again, but the reference isn't something you'd need to recognise, that's rather my end of things, and, uh, the point is there's a benefit sitting on it that I'd hate to see go unclaimed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh! Sorry, hold on, there's a blackbird going absolutely mad at the fence, I think next door's cat is in my hydrangeas again. Shoo! No, sorry, go on. A benefit, you said? Well, that's lovely to hear, but it's the third different reason now, isn't it? First it's an important matter, then it's got to be today, and now it's a benefit I'd hate to lose. Which is it, exactly? And what sort of benefit, how much are we talking? Because if there's money sitting somewhere for me, I'd rather like to know how it got there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yes. I can see how it sounds, three different things, and I'd have asked the same. They're not separate matters, though, it's all one thing, the benefit is the important matter, and the timing follows from that. As for the amount, I'd rather not put a figure on it until I've confirmed a few details with you, which, uh, I realise is the same answer as before. Sorry, the line's breaking up again, I'm losing you, but if I could just take some details from you now, we could have it settled in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, I'm still back at the bit two turns ago, when you said you'd rather not tell me anything until you'd established it was me. But now you're asking for details from me, so what details, exactly? Because I don't really see how I can prove I'm me to somebody who rang me and won't say what it's about, it feels the wrong way round. And honestly, I'm starting to wonder if I should ring [COMPANY_A] back myself, on a number I've looked up, rather than hand things over to a voice on the loudspeaker. Is there a way I can do that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Well, I'd never discourage you from being careful, [PERSON_1], that's exactly the right instinct, and I mean that. The difficulty is, I move between desks and sites through the day, so there isn't a number I could give you that would reach me, and the main switchboard wouldn't know what you were talking about, not without the reference in front of them. Sorry, the line's cutting out again. Look, I'll try you again a bit later on, when the connection's better, and we can finish this properly then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, so the switchboard wouldn't know what I was talking about? Then how would I know you work there at all? Sorry, I'm going round in circles, but I did ask whether I could ring them back on a number I've looked up myself, and I think that's what I'd rather do. You see, it's just that I'm not handing anything over to a voice on the loudspeaker, however nice you sound. So no, don't ring me later, I'll sort it myself, and if there's a benefit it'll keep. Right, thanks for your time, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Well, I, uh, I'd rather you didn't do that, [PERSON_1], because I can't promise it'll keep, and I'd hate for you to lose out. But it's your decision, of course. Please, just stay on a moment longer and hear me out, sorry, the line's going again, I'm losing you...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I've said my goodbye, and I'm sticking to it. And that's the other thing, you said it'd be fine to sort it later, you were going to ring me back when the line was better, and now it won't keep? You can't have it both ways, can you? Besides, you've been losing me all afternoon and I've been hearing you perfectly well, so I don't think it's the line. I'll ring them myself on a number I've found. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi -- sorry, is that, um, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I think there was a bit of a gap on the line there. I'm, uh, I'm calling on behalf of [COMPANY_A], the card services side, and, well, it's about a transaction that got flagged, so I wanted to, um, make sure I'd got the right person first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Who's calling? I've got a pan on, hang on -- I said, who is this? Card services, did you say? Sorry, I didn't catch the name of the company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, sorry -- I'll, I'll go again. It's [COMPANY_A], the bank, card services, that's -- yes, [COMPANY_A]. And my name's [PERSON_2], I'm, uh, I'm actually just passing the message on for the card team, so I'm not the one who can, um, see your account or anything. I just, I know it sounds worrying, calling out of the blue like this, but a transaction on your card got flagged and they'd like a word with you, that's all I was asked to say.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hang on, hang on, it's catching. Sorry. Just turning the heat down. Right. Sorry, what? A transaction? On my card? Oh, that does sound worrying. But you're not the one who can see it? So who is it that wants a word with me? Sorry, I'm a bit -- I wasn't expecting a call.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're right to ask, um. It's the card services team, the fraud side, sorry, I said card team before, same thing really. I don't have a name for you, I'm just, I'm only the one ringing round, and I honestly can't go into any details on this call, I'm not even allowed, not when I'm the one who's rung you. So what I'd really ask is, um, would you mind hanging up and ringing the number on the back of your card? Just in case, you know, you'd want to be sure it's us.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um -- right. Hang up and ring the number on the back of my card? Uh... sorry, that's, well, that's actually what I'd want to do, isn't it. It just seems a funny way round, you ringing me and then telling me to ring you. Sorry, what's it you want me to say when I get through to them? Is there some sort of, I don't know, reference or something I give them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, there is, there's a reference, it's -- hang on, let me get it right. It's [CODE_1]. Sorry, that's, that's the one they'd, um, they'd look up. And you're right, it is a funny way round, I know it is, I'd, I'd feel the same. But that's sort of the point, you shouldn't just take my word for it, so, uh, ring the number on the back of your card, or the one on the bank's website, not one I give you, and quote that reference. And, um, they'll hold it open, so there's no rush, take as long as you need.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right. Well, that's -- that actually sounds sensible, doesn't it? You're not asking me for anything. Sorry, I'm just trying to keep hold of that reference, I've got a wooden spoon in one hand. Can you say it once more, slowly? No, hang on, I'll find a pen. Right. And I ring the number on the back of the card, not one from you. Yes. Okay then, I'll do that once I've got this dinner off the hob. Thanks, uh, [PERSON_2], was it? Thanks for letting me know. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_2], that's me, and, um, that's right, you've got it. The number on the back of your card, not one from me, and quote the reference, [CODE_1]. Sorry, I know I'm saying it again, I just, I want to be sure you've got it down properly. Take your time with the dinner, there's no rush on it, honestly, they'll have it open when you ring. Right, um, thanks for bearing with me, and, uh, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I've got it down now, sorry for making you say it twice. I'm a bit all over the place with this pan, honestly. I'll sort the dinner first, turn everything off, and then I'll get my card out and ring the number on the back, not one you've given me. And I'll quote that reference. It is a bit of a worry, a flagged transaction, but I suppose better they spotted it than not. Anyway, thanks for being patient with me, [PERSON_2]. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, did you say the pan's on the hob? No, hang on, I thought you said, um, thanks for being patient, and I thought, well, I'm the one who's been, uh, been in your way, haven't I, ringing in the middle of your tea. Sorry. That's -- no, you're right, it is a worry, I won't pretend it isn't, but you're doing exactly the right thing. Number on the back of the card, quote [CODE_1], and they'll have it open for you. Right, I'll let you get on. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, the pan, it's fine, I've turned it down. Sorry, I did say, didn't I? Right, so the number on the back of the card, not one from you, and I quote the reference. Yes. I've got it. Okay then, thanks again, [PERSON_2]. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm a scheduling assistant with [COMPANY_A], the financial regulator, and I'm calling because we've got a flag on your savings that needs dealing with today, so I just need a few minutes of your time before the window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, well, it depends who's asking, I suppose. [PERSON_2], right? A scheduling assistant, with a regulator. That's a new one, I didn't know regulators had those. And a flag on my savings, which, I mean, I've got a few things that could loosely be called savings, so you'll have to be a bit more specific. What sort of flag, and what's this window that's closing? Because I'm sort of in the middle of something here, so if it's urgent I'd like to know what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, so I'm the one booking the case team's calls, they're the ones who go into the detail, and what I can say is that your savings have been marked as at risk and they need moving into a protected holding arrangement, which has to happen today, that's the window, because once it closes the case goes to the next stage and that's harder for you. Now, the other thing, and this is important, while it's being dealt with we ask that you don't discuss it with anyone, family, friends, your bank, nobody, because the bank's own systems are part of what's being looked at, so can I just confirm a couple of details and get you booked in with the case team?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. Don't tell my bank? Don't tell anyone? That's, no, that's a bit of a red flag all on its own, isn't it. Like, why would a regulator tell me not to talk to my bank? And you still haven't told me what the flag actually is. At risk how? You said at risk, but at risk of what, and who marked it? I asked what sort of flag and I got a window and a next stage, so I'll ask again. What's the flag, specifically, and which savings are we even talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so the, the flag is, well, the specifics sit with the case team, I only see that it's marked, and I understand it sounds, I mean the bank thing is only so the, so nothing gets, look, I'm the scheduling assistant, I'm calling to get you booked in with the case team today, so can I just confirm a couple of details and get that done before the window closes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, but I'm going to stop you there, because you've now told me three times it's the case team's job and you can't say what the flag is. You can't say what it is, but you do know it's urgent and I shouldn't ring my bank. That's a weird combination, honestly. Right, let me ask you something small instead. What's the number for [COMPANY_A], the main switchboard, and what's your name again, the surname? Because I'll just hang up and ring them myself, and if you're genuine, that costs you nothing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, it's, uh, I'm only the scheduling assistant, I don't really give out the, can we just get you booked in with the case team before the window closes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. You won't give a number and you won't give a surname. Then no, I'm not booking anything, and I'm not confirming any details. I'll look up [COMPANY_A] myself and ring them if I'm worried. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, no, sorry, did you say a man's worried? Because nobody's said anything about a man, I'm only the scheduling assistant, and the thing is the window closes today, so if you could just stay on the line for two minutes and let me get you booked in with the case team before -- hello? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, and no, I didn't say a man, I said I'd ring them if I'm worried. Anyway, you also told me earlier you couldn't say what the flag was, and now it's a window that closes in two minutes, so which is it? Look, I've said it once, I'm not doing this over the phone with someone who won't give me a surname or a number. I'll find the regulator myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. It's your call, I just, the window's still closing today, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I heard you. If there's a genuine problem, a regulator will put it in writing, and I'll deal with it through the number I look up myself. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second before you go, you said a regulator would put it in writing, but when you said you'd ring them, which number were you actually going to use? Because if it's one off the internet, I wouldn't, I mean, that's just, can you tell me which one, and then we can get you booked in with the case team before the window closes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, well, uh... that's actually kind of funny. You won't give me your surname, you won't give me your number, but now you're keen to know which number I'd use. No. I'm not telling you that, and I'm not getting booked in with anyone. I'll sort it myself, thanks. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, okay, so, um, so what I'll say, and I know you're about to go, is that the window's still open until end of day, so if you change your mind, and, and look, I'd really rather you didn't ring anyone in the meantime, because then it's, well, it just makes it harder, so, so if you could just hold off on that, can we, can we get you booked in before --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, back up a second. A couple of turns ago you said not to ring anyone because it makes it harder. Harder for who, exactly? Because if a regulator's got a real concern about my savings, I'd have thought me phoning them would make it easier, not harder. And now you're asking me to hold off on that. So I'm going to do the opposite, I'm ringing them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, you sound like you might've just come in from somewhere. It's [PERSON_2] calling from the customs desk at [COMPANY_A], and I promise this is a friendly call, nothing to panic about.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, who? Sorry, customs desk at what? I'm in a queue, I haven't got long. And "nothing to panic about" -- well, that's what people say when there is something, isn't it? What's this actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough. [COMPANY_A], the courier. You've got a parcel coming in, and there's a small import charge on it, that's all. Honestly it's quick, so go on and finish your queue and I'll keep it short.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A parcel. What parcel? I haven't ordered anything, not that I can think of. Who's it from, and what's the tracking number? And don't say you need to take a payment off me over the phone, because I'm not doing that. If there's a charge, it'll be on a card through the door, or an email from the actual company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, and you shouldn't, I wouldn't either! I won't take a payment on this call, not a penny. Right, the tracking reference is [CODE_1], and if you've got the email or the text from us, it'll be sitting right there in it. Or you can just pop it into the tracking page at [URL_1] and it'll show you the sender and everything. Oh, and sorry, I said it's a small charge earlier, didn't I? It's [AMOUNT_1], so, you know, depends what you call small.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on -- no, sorry, not you, I've got a woman trying to squeeze past my trolley. Right. Where was I. [CODE_1], yeah, I'm not writing that down, I've got nothing to write on and I'm not typing a web address into my phone in a supermarket. And I haven't had any email or text from you, so that's another thing. Look, if you're not taking payment, what are you ringing me for? Why not just leave the card through the door like everyone else does?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, a trolley, lovely, I hope it's a full one. Sorry, did you say you haven't got a *card*, or a *car*? Because if you're out and about, no worries at all, we can just sort the delivery slot another day. Oh, and I'm only ringing because the charge is holding the parcel at the depot, so it's sitting there till it's cleared, which is a bit of a shame, but there's no rush from my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Card, I said card, through the door, like a, a... never mind. Look, you said no rush, but then it's held at the depot till it's cleared, which is, I mean, that is a rush, isn't it? That's the thing they always do, hold something over you. And you still haven't told me what it is or who it's from. Because if I haven't ordered anything, then, well, who's sending me a parcel with a charge on it? So what's in it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you've got me there, I did say no rush and then said it's held, that's my chatty mouth running ahead of me. It's held, yes, but it isn't going anywhere, it just waits at the depot for you, so there's no deadline from our side. As for what's in it, uh, I can only see the sender and the declared contents on the tracking page, not on my screen, which is a bit daft I know. And actually, scratch what I said about it being a small charge, [AMOUNT_1] isn't small, that's fair, and it might not even be yours at all if you've ordered nothing. So don't take my word for any of it. When you're home, put [CODE_1] into the tracking page at [URL_1], have a look at who it's from, and if it doesn't ring a bell, ring us back on the number on our website, which is [PHONE_1], and we'll sort it out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you can't see what's in it, you can't tell me who it's from, and you want me to go and look it up myself. That's a lot of nothing for a customs desk. And now it might not even be mine? Then why ring me at all? Look, I'm not typing in your reference, and I'm not ringing a number you've just given me down the phone. If there's a real parcel, I'll find it from the company's own site, my way, not off you. And if I've ordered nothing, then I've got nothing to chase, haven't I? So that's me done. I've got a queue to get through. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's completely fair, and honestly you're doing exactly the right thing, so don't let me hold up your queue. If there's a real parcel, go to the company's own site your way, and if you've ordered nothing, you've got nothing to chase, like you say. Nothing needs doing on the phone today, nothing at all. Sorry for the bother, [PERSON_1], and enjoy the rest of your shop. Bye now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, well. I'll tell you now, I'm not going to go looking for it either, because if I haven't ordered anything there's nothing to find, and if I have, it'll turn up on my account like it always does. And I'll say this, it's very nice and very polite, all this "you're doing the right thing", but you rang me, I didn't ring you. You've got my name, you've got my number, and you couldn't tell me what was in it or who sent it. So if there's a real parcel, they can send me a card or an email like normal people do, and if there isn't, well, then this was a bit of a waste of both our afternoons, wasn't it? Right, I've got a woman with about forty items in front of me and I'm next. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yes, I'll hold my hands up, it was a clumsy call, and you're right, I should've had the sender and the contents in front of me before I picked up the phone. Sorry about that. If it's real, the card or the email will turn up, and if it isn't, well, you've lost nothing but a few minutes of your queue. Good luck with the forty items, [PERSON_1], goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye now, take care, and enjoy the rest of your afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, you said. Oh, for -- she's just put her whole basket on the belt, in front of me. Honestly. Sorry, not you. Right, I'm going. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, the whole basket, no! Well, that's your afternoon gone, I'm so sorry, I'll let you -- oh, and before you go, if the card does come through the door, just have a look at the sender on it, that's all. Right, I'm off, bye now, [PERSON_1]!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll look at the sender. Hang on, though, you said earlier you'd ring me about a parcel and then it was my job to ring you back, and now it's a card through the door again? Make your mind up. Anyway, I'm not ringing anyone back, not on that number, not on any number you've read out to me. Right, she's scanning my stuff, I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this -- uh, sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm the scheduling assistant over at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling because there's a position that closes out today and I wanted to, well, actually the reason I'm ringing is that [PERSON_3] asked me to get you on the calendar before the window shuts at five, so have you got just a couple of minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, I -- who did you say this was again? [PERSON_2], from, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? I'm not, I mean I don't recall applying for anything there. And, um, who's [PERSON_3]? I don't think I know a [PERSON_3]. What position are we talking about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [PERSON_2], scheduling at [COMPANY_A], and [PERSON_3] is one of our senior advisors, he's just got you flagged for the fund that closes at five today, so I only need a couple of minutes on the calendar.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a fund? You said position a moment ago, and now it's a fund that closes at five. Which is it? Because those are two quite different things. And I don't know [PERSON_3], so I'd like to know how I came to be flagged. Where did you get this number, and what exactly is it you want to put on my calendar?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, it's the same thing, the position is in the fund, that's just how we talk about it internally, and honestly the numbers on it are, uh, they're very strong for the people getting in before the close, so [PERSON_3] only needs you for a short slot today, say ten minutes, whenever suits you before five. As for the number, it came off a list we're cleared to use, I wouldn't have the detail on that in front of me, but what I can do right now is get you booked in, so what time works, three or four?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so let me just say back what I've heard, because I'd like to be sure I have it straight. You rang me unprompted, I've no relationship with [COMPANY_A] that I can recall, and I don't know [PERSON_3]. You can't tell me where my number came from beyond a list you're cleared to use, though you couldn't say whose list or cleared by whom. And you've now described the same thing as a position, a fund, and a slot, so I honestly don't know what I'd be agreeing to attend. Add to that a deadline of five o'clock today and strong numbers for people who get in before the close, and, well, I'm not going to pick three or four, because I don't yet know what the appointment is for. So here's what I'd need. What exactly is [COMPANY_A], is it a regulated firm, and if so what's the name it's regulated under? What is the fund, in plain terms? And how do I reach [PERSON_3] through a number or a website I look up myself, rather than anything you give me? If you can't answer those, I think the simplest thing is that I don't book anything today.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, completely fair, and I hear you, but the thing is the fund is only open to a limited number of people today, so what I'd really like to do is just get you in front of [PERSON_3] for ten minutes, because he can answer all of that far better than I can, I'm only the scheduling side, I don't handle the regulatory detail, that's his area, and honestly the people who've come in on this one before the close have been, well, very happy with where they've landed, so it's really just a matter of picking a slot, three or four, whichever's easier, and you can ask him every one of those questions directly. As for looking him up yourself, I'd say don't worry about that, I can have him ring you straight back on this number in a few minutes, so if you just confirm what time suits you, I'll get it locked in before the five o'clock cutoff, and then, uh, it's all sorted.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, one second -- there's a delivery van reversing outside, it's beeping like mad. Right, it's stopped. So, no. I'll be plain about it. You've told me not to look him up myself, and that he'll ring me back on this number. That's the opposite of what I asked for, and it makes me less inclined to trust this, not more. A genuine firm wouldn't mind me checking it independently. And the closing-at-five pressure with nothing concrete behind it, no regulated name, no description of what the fund actually is, that's a pattern I'd rather not take part in. I'm not booking three or four. If [COMPANY_A] is real and wants to speak to me, they can send something in writing, and I'll look the firm up through the regulator's register myself. Thanks for your time, but I'm going to end the call here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sure, I understand, but before you go, it's only ten minutes and [PERSON_3] can answer all of that, and the window really does shut at five, so if I could just pencil you in for three or -- hello? [PERSON_1]? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here, I did say goodbye. I'm not booking anything, three or four or otherwise. If [COMPANY_A] wants to reach me, they can write to me, and I'll check them with the regulator myself. No, thank you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, but, I mean, if I could just -- no, look, it's only that [PERSON_3] will, well, actually what I can do is, uh, put you down for four, and then you don't have to decide anything now, you just, hello? You can always cancel it, it's only ten minutes, and the, the cutoff really is --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you'll put me down for a form? No, I'm not filling in any form, I don't know what that would even be. And please don't put me down for anything, at four or at any other time. I haven't agreed to an appointment, and I'm not going to. If there's a genuine firm behind this, it can write to me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hello there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Lovely, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, you sound like you might've been in the middle of something, I always feel awful ringing people at this hour, it's usually either dinner or the telly, isn't it? Anyway, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from customer care at [COMPANY_A], and I just wanted to check a couple of small things with you, nothing to worry about at all. How's your day been so far, are you keeping well?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who's this? Customer care from... which company did you say? I didn't, uh, I didn't catch it, there's a bit of noise here. And what small things, exactly? Who are you calling for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no no, sorry, that's my fault, I do talk too quickly, my colleagues are always telling me off for it. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], customer care side of things, and I'm ringing for [PERSON_1], that's you, isn't it? Hang on, sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a whole stack of folders behind me, honestly, it's like a zoo in here today. Right, I'm back, where was I, yes, just a routine call, really, it's a quick bit of housekeeping on our records and I promise I won't keep you long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry -- no, put that down, I said put it down. Sorry. Uh, so you're saying records, whose records? I haven't actually heard a company name I could, you know, write down, you just said the one thing and it came out all garbled. And how'd you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, don't worry, it's the same at my end, there's always something going on. It's [COMPANY_A], and I'm with the international lottery claims office. We hold a list of people who were entered into one of our overseas draws, and your number's on it, that's how I've got you. I know, I know, I should've said that first, I do ramble. But the lovely thing is, it's good news, [PERSON_1], and I'd hate for you to hear it from me at the wrong moment. Are you somewhere you can talk for a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Uh, a lottery. So I was entered in a draw, is that what you're saying? Because I don't remember entering anything, I mean, I'd remember that, wouldn't I? ... Sorry, I'm just, um, still here. So, what draw, then? And which company, exactly, you still haven't actually told me a name I can look up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, a name you can look up, yes, quite right, always check, I tell my own mum the same thing. And it's not a draw you'd have had to remember, [PERSON_1], that's the nice part, you were entered automatically. Now the draw itself, that was back in, oh, March I want to say, or was it April, the dates all blur together over here. The ticket number's right in front of me, one moment, I've got it written down on the wrong sheet. Anyway, you said you didn't catch the cleaning company, sorry, I should've been clearer, we're not a cleaning company at all, we're the lottery office, so there's nothing to book or pay for.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Cleaning company? I never said anything about a cleaning company. I asked for a name, that's all. And you still haven't given me one, you keep saying the lottery office, but the office of what? ... Sorry, hang on. Okay. And entered automatically how, exactly? Entered by who? Because I don't remember signing up for anything, so I'm not really following how my number ended up on a list.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, oh, did I say cleaning, I've been on since eight, my head's gone to mush. No, no, listen, [PERSON_1], the how doesn't matter half as much as the what, because the prize is, well, it's quite a sum, I've honestly never been so happy to make a call, it's [AMOUNT_1], hang on, [AMOUNT_2], sorry, the figure's been updated since this morning. And the thing is, claims close at the end of today, so I'd rather get your details confirmed now than have you miss out, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Closes today. And the amount changed since this morning. Right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, "changed" is the wrong word, it's the same prize, just, uh, the figure was rounded up on our side, that's all. And I think I said claims close at the end of the week earlier, didn't I? Today, this week, same thing really, the point is it's tight. Anyway, if you can just confirm your full name and address for me, I'll get you straight onto the claim.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you want me to confirm my, what, my fine print? No -- hang on, my name and address? But you rang me. You've got my number on some list, so you should already have those, shouldn't you? And I don't think you said the end of the week, you said today, I heard that. Which is it, because those aren't the same thing at all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, your fine print, no, that's a good one, I did say details, didn't I, I only meant the usual, so we know we've got the right person. And it's today, end of the week, whichever, honestly [PERSON_1], I wouldn't split hairs over it, it's the same deadline said two ways. Now, you said something a moment ago about the amount, and I'd hate you to have the wrong idea, it's [AMOUNT_2], definitely, forget the other one I mentioned. Shall we just get your name and address down so I can hold your place before it's gone?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not giving you my name or my address. You've had three different answers on the deadline, the amount keeps moving, and you still haven't told me what company this actually is. I'm going to go now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_1], wait, wait, don't hang up, you've got the wrong end of the stick entirely. Sorry, can I just ask, when you said fine print a minute ago, what did you mean by that? Because I think we've got our wires crossed somewhere, and I'd hate for one little muddle to cost you [AMOUNT_2]. Honestly, it takes two minutes, and the claim won't wait for you, you know.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said goodbye. I'm not going to go through it again. No name, no address, and I'm not interested in the claim. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, this is [PERSON_1], regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery. Just ringing to check how your pet's getting on after last week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, um -- sorry, which surgery was that again? I'm, I mean, I did take the, the, oh dear, I'm not sure I quite caught the name. And last week, you said? Sorry, I just, I'd have to think which of us you're after, I mean, is it me you're wanting?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, and I've got you down as having had a procedure done last week, so -- no, listen, it's a routine follow-up call, we do these for every, uh, every patient after surgery, it's standard procedure. I just need to know how your pet's recovering and whether you'd like a check-up booked in, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a follow-up, that's very good of you to ring. Um, only I don't think my, well, I don't actually have, hang on -- I haven't had anything done at a surgery last week, I don't think. Or, no, wait, did my neighbour take the, oh, I'm sorry, I'm getting muddled. utterances.text: Right, right, a payment plan, okay. But hang on, you said at the start it was a letter, that there'd be another letter, and now it's I've never had a letter, I don't think? Or maybe I did, it's all in a pile on the side. And I'm sure my bank hasn't changed, I've been with them forever. Sorry, I keep going round in circles, it's just, I didn't actually catch the name of the company properly, you said it fast. And the website, I can't write that down, my pen's in the other room. Is there a number I could ring you back on, one that's on the bill or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, absolutely, ring back, that's the sensible thing to do. And you're right to pick me up on the letter, I said there'd be another one, which does sound like you've already had one, and then you say you haven't. That's on me, I was waffling. It might well be in that pile on the side, or it might not have gone out yet, I honestly can't tell from my screen. Doesn't matter either way. I'm [PERSON_2], I'm from [COMPANY_A], and the number to ring is the one printed on your bill, or look it up yourself, that's even better than me reading you one. Go and have a rummage in the pile, the bill's probably in there with the letter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so the number on the bill, yes, that's what I'll do, I'll ring the number on the bill. Not this number, the one on the bill. Because I'm still not sure I caught the company name, you've said it a couple of times and it just sort of, it goes past me, I'm not awake yet. But if I ring the number on my own bill, they'll know, won't they? They'll tell me if there's anything overdue. So I'll do that. I'll go and have a rummage, like you said, and I'll ring the one on the bill. Thanks for calling, I think. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly right, they'll have it all in front of them and they can sort out a payment plan with you there and then. No hurry at all, have your tea, find the pen. I'm [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], if you want to say who rang. Thanks for picking up, [PERSON_1], and enjoy what's left of the afternoon, even if the curtains stay shut. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, bye -- oh, hang on, was that the kettle? No, it's the, uh, the heating clicking on, it does that. Sorry. Right. The number on the bill, not this one. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, that'll be the heating, mine does the same, clicks away like it's got a mind of its own. And yes, the number on the bill, not this one, you've got it exactly. Off you go and have a rummage, and ring them whenever suits you. Bye for now, [PERSON_1], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the what? A mind of its own? No, no, the cat's not on the bill, I haven't got a cat. Oh, you said the heating, didn't you. Right. Yes. Okay, I'm going now, I'll do the bill thing, number on the bill. Bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants, just ringing about your order for tomorrow, the two-hour window, and there's one item that's been swapped for a similar product, nothing big, but I just need a quick yes or no from you on it, and, uh, sorry, before I go on, was that you I just heard say something about a different address? I couldn't quite catch it, I think there was a bit of a gap on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, I didn't say anything about a different address. I think that was just the line, or, um, background noise at your end. Sorry, which company did you say you were with? And what order is this, exactly? I'm not sure I have a delivery booked for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no worries, probably just the line, it does that, I'm with [COMPANY_A], the supermarket home delivery, and it's the online order placed under your name, so I'm just confirming the two-hour window, and the only thing I need from you is a yes or no on the one swapped item, so if you've got a moment I can, sorry, you were saying you don't think you've got a delivery booked?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, I do have a grocery delivery tomorrow, I think, but I didn't place it on a, uh, two-hour window, I picked a one-hour slot. So that's not matching what you've got. Can you tell me what the item is that's been swapped, and what the original item was? If it's a real substitution, you'll have both on screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, sorry, so I've got it right here, the original was the [COMPANY_B] own-brand wholemeal loaf and the swap is the, uh, seeded loaf, same size, similar price, and on the slot, I've got a two-hour window showing, that might just be how it displays on my side, it could still be your one hour inside it, but really all I need is a yes or no on the swapped item, just a quick yes or no on the loaf, and then I'm done with you, so is the seeded loaf okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, before I say yes to anything -- I didn't actually book a loaf, so I'm not sure I can, uh, hang on, you said you were just going to ask about the, no, wait. Look, a swapped loaf doesn't need a phone call, the app just lets you accept or reject it. And you rang me about an address, then a window that doesn't match mine. So what's the order reference you've got, and what number would I ring back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair enough, so the order reference I've got on screen is [ACCOUNT_REF], and that should match the confirmation email you got when you placed it, and I know the app does let you accept or reject subs, but we ring when the slot looks tight, it's just a courtesy thing so nothing gets left off the van, and the window thing is probably just how our scheduling screen shows it, but honestly, if it doesn't line up with what you booked, that's exactly the sort of thing you'd want to check, so don't take my word for it, look up the customer service number for [COMPANY_A] yourself, on the website or the back of your last receipt, and ring that, and give them [ACCOUNT_REF], they'll see the same order and the same swap, and, sorry, I should say, I didn't ring about an address, that was just the line, so that bit's not on me, anyway, does that sound all right, because I'd honestly rather you ring them than stay on with me feeling unsure?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I'll -- well, actually, that's, uh, that's a fair thing to suggest, and I'll be honest, it's a bit more than I expected. Most callers don't tell you to hang up and ring the official number. But I'm still, hm, I'm still not sure I follow why you'd phone about a loaf at all. Anyway. I'll do what you said. I'll look up the number myself, from the website, and check the order there, and if there's a substitution I'll deal with it through them or the app. So I'm going to leave it there, thanks. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, absolutely, you do that, that's, uh, that's exactly what I'd do, and if it turns out the slot's fine you can just accept the swap in the app, and thanks for your time [PERSON_1], have a good evening, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one thing before you go -- two turns back you said you'd rather I ring them than stay on with you feeling unsure. Why would you say that? A scheduling assistant who's just trying to get a yes or no on a loaf, I'd expect them to want to finish the call, not send me off to check. So, uh, what's actually going on at your end? Just so I understand.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's a fair question, and honestly nothing's going on at my end, it's just how I'd want to be treated if I got a call like this, because a lot of people get odd calls these days and I'd sooner someone check than feel pushed into a yes they weren't sure about, and I know I talk quickly, I'm sorry about that, it's the job, I've got a list of these to get through before the vans are loaded, so I tend to rattle through it, but that's all it is, the swap is just a courtesy call and the loaf really is the whole reason I rang, and it doesn't matter to me if you say yes, no, or don't answer at all, because the app will just default to whatever your substitution preference is set to, so there's no pressure from me either way, and, sorry, I realise that might've sounded like I was rushing you, I really wasn't meaning to, so honestly, look up [COMPANY_A] on the website, ring their customer service line, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll sort it, and if the order isn't there, well, that tells you something too, doesn't it, and I'd be glad you checked.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's a lot of words for a loaf, and none of it really explains why you rang at all, but I'm done going round in circles. I'm not confirming anything on this call. I'll find the number myself and check the order there, and if the reference you gave me doesn't match anything, I'll know that too. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, you do that, and I'm not asking you to confirm anyth-- no, sorry, go on, finish, I'll just say that's all fine, ring them, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and if it doesn't match then, well, that's useful to know isn't it, so thanks for your time [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say quote the account, or, uh, count it? Count what? No, never mind, I don't think I need to know. I'm not doing anything on this call, I'll look up the number myself and sort it out with them directly. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
