utterances.text: Oh, ah, did you say you don't need the loaf? No, no, it's quote, q-u-o-t-e, as in read out the reference to them, [ACCOUNT_REF], that's all, nothing to count, nothing to do on this call, and yes, absolutely, ring them yourself, I'd want you to, so thanks again [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, I'll -- no, actually, I understood you the first time. Quote, not count, fine. But I'm, I mean, I've said goodbye twice now and you keep, well, I'm not going to read anything out to anyone on this call, that's all. I'll find the real number and ring them myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good morning, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the billing office at [COMPANY_A], I'm a scheduling assistant there, and I'm calling about an unpaid medical bill for a relative of yours that's listed under your name as the responsible party, so I just need a couple of minutes of your time. Sorry, can you hear me okay? It's [PERSON_2], from the billing office at [COMPANY_A], about the unpaid bill, and it's showing you as the responsible party.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you fine. Uh, you asked if this is [PERSON_1], but I'd like to know a bit more first. Which relative are we talking about? You haven't said, and I'm not going to confirm anything until I know who you are and what this is about. Which office did you say again, and what exactly is the bill for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I totally understand, and that's exactly what we do on our end too, the specifics like the relative's name and the department and the case number, those get shared as soon as we've confirmed identity, it's just standard procedure, so if I could just get your full name and date of birth, I can pull it right up and we can get this sorted. Like I said, it's [PERSON_2] from the billing office at [COMPANY_A], and the account is showing past due, so the sooner we confirm things the sooner I can get you the details and keep it from going any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hold on, because that's backwards, isn't it? You rang me. You're the one who's contacted me about a bill, so it's on you to establish who you are and what this relates to, not on me to hand over my full name and date of birth to someone I can't see and can't verify. And I'll be straight, a caller saying they need my date of birth before they'll tell me anything about the account is exactly how it's meant to look when someone's fishing for identifying details. I'm not saying that's what you're doing. I'm saying I can't tell the difference from here, and neither could you if our positions were reversed. So here's what I'd ask. You've said you're a scheduling assistant, which is an odd role to be chasing a past due account, so I'd like to understand that. You've also said it's a relative of mine, with me listed as the responsible party, but you haven't named the relative, the facility, or the department. If you really have an account in front of you, you can tell me those three things without needing anything from me. And if you can't, then the sensible thing is for me to look up the billing office number myself, through a published source rather than any number you give me, and ring them directly. Can you at least tell me the name of the facility and the relative's name?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I hear you, I do, but it's [PERSON_2], billing office at [COMPANY_A], and the facility and the relative's name and the department, those all get released once identity is confirmed, that's just how the system has it locked, and I can't see it myself until the account's verified on my end. And the scheduling side, that's just, we all cover the past due calls when it's busy, so it's nothing unusual. So if I could just get your full name and date of birth, it takes two seconds, and then I can read you everything, because I really don't want this going to the next stage on your account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you can't see the account until I verify myself, but you rang me about it. That doesn't hang together. I'm not giving you my name or date of birth. If there's a real bill, send it in writing, or I'll ring the billing office on a number I look up myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sure, but before you go, it's [PERSON_2] from the billing office at [COMPANY_A], and the thing is, if this isn't dealt with today it does move to the next stage, so if I could just get your full name and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before I put the phone down. Two turns ago you said the account details are locked until I'm verified, and that you can't even see them yourself. So how do you know it's past due, and how do you know it's me listed as the responsible party? Something on your screen told you that. And now there's a deadline of today. What exactly is the next stage? Because that wasn't mentioned until I said no. Either way, I'm not giving you my details. If it's real, put it in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, the next stage is just the standard escalation, it goes to the, to the collections review, which is why I'm trying to catch you before then, and the flag, the past due flag, that's visible to me, it's just the details underneath that stay locked until, so, yeah, if I could just get your full name and date of birth, then I can open the whole account and read you everything, and we can get this wrapped up right now before it goes any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the collections reviewer? Who's that, a named person or a department? Because I'd want to speak to them directly. Hang on, no, actually, that doesn't matter. You can see a flag but nothing underneath it, and I'm still not giving you my name or date of birth. If a collections review is genuinely coming, it'll come by post, and I'll deal with it then. I'm ending this call now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, sure, I mean it's [PERSON_2] from the billing office at [COMPANY_A], and honestly it doesn't change the timeline on our end, so if you'd rather call us back that's, that's fine, I can give you a callback number, it's [PHONE_1], and when you do just ask for [PERSON_2] in billing and we can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I won't be ringing that number, thanks. If I call anyone, it'll be a number I've found myself. But let me go back two turns, because you said something I want clarified. You said you can see a flag, but the details underneath are locked. So what does the flag actually say? Is it the amount, the date it went past due, or just a marker? Because if you can see a flag against my name, then something on your screen has to say whose name that is, and you've never given me one thing from it. Anyway, I'm not discussing it any further. If it's real, it can come in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Good. It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, we handle estates, and I'm the assistant on a file where your name may come up, so I just need to confirm a couple of things with you before -- sorry, yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. But I'd like to be clear before we go any further, I wasn't expecting a call from a solicitor's office, and I don't recognise the name of the firm. You said my name "may come up" on a file, which is, well, rather vague. Is that an estate where I'm a named beneficiary, or an executor, or is it simply that someone has listed me as a relative? Because those are quite different things, and I'd want to know which before I confirm anything about myself. And I'll say now, I'm not in the habit of confirming personal details to someone who's rung me out of the blue, so I'd need to know how I can check that you are who you say you are. Perhaps you could give me the firm's full name again, and a switchboard number I can call back on, and then, I mean, we can go from there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, that's fair, and I'll note the objection on the file. I can't say which it is, beneficiary, executor or relative, because that's set out in the formal letter and the file isn't mine to characterise over the phone. The firm is [COMPANY_A], we're in [CITY_1], and the switchboard is [PHONE_1]. Please look us up in an independent directory rather than taking my word for it, and ring back through the main line. The letter will go out in the post, and until it reaches you I'd ask that you keep this matter to yourself, as estate files are confidential. I'm not asking for any money or bank details at any point, only your confirmation of identity, and that can wait until you've checked.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Right. Well, uh, I'll say the independent directory suggestion is the correct one, so I'll give you that. But, I mean, the confidentiality request is the part I'm less comfortable with. You've rung me about a file you can't describe, and you're asking me not to mention it to anyone until a letter arrives? That's, um, a slightly odd combination. If it were genuine, I'd have thought a short letter would go first and the call after. So why ring me beforehand at all? And what exactly are the "couple of things" you wanted confirmed? You said identity, but identity meaning what, precisely?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, it's the order we tend to do it, a call to check we have the right [PERSON_1] before the letter's addressed. Identity meaning your full name and the address we hold for you, the same ones that'll be on the letter, nothing beyond that. And if you'd rather not confirm anything today, note it on the file and wait for the post.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll hold off confirming anything today. Before you go, though, can I go back to something you said earlier? You said you're "the assistant on a file where my name may come up." Assistant to whom, exactly? Is there a named solicitor who has conduct of it? And, sorry, one more thing, you said the file "isn't yours to characterise." If you don't know what my connection is, I'm not clear why you're the one ringing me. I'd have thought whoever holds the file would make that call themselves.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The solicitor with conduct is [PERSON_3], I just make the first calls to confirm we've the right person. Ring the switchboard on [PHONE_1] and ask for [PERSON_3] by name, they'll confirm it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the solicitor is [PERSON_3], or, uh, that I should ask for the "conductor"? I didn't quite catch that. A conductor of what, exactly? Is that a separate role from the solicitor, someone who handles the file in a different capacity? Because if there's a conductor as well as a solicitor, I'd want to understand who does what before I ring anyone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no conductor, sorry, that's the phrasing. "Conduct" is just the term for who's running the file. The solicitor in charge is [PERSON_3]. One person, and I'm their assistant. If you ring [PHONE_1] and ask for [PERSON_3], they can tell you who I am and what the file is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ah, right, conduct, yes, I see. Sorry, I did hear "conductor." Um, well, so... one solicitor, [PERSON_3], and you're the assistant. Right. Uh, so here's what I'll do. I'll look the firm up in an independent directory, not through anything you've given me, and I'll ring the main line and ask for [PERSON_3]. If they know you and there's a file with my name on it, they can tell me what it concerns, and then, I mean, we can talk again. But I'm not confirming my name or my address on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, that's your decision and I've noted it on the file. The letter will follow in the post in any case. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one moment before you go. Two turns back you said I should keep this to myself until the letter arrives, because estate files are confidential. Does that mean I'm not to say anything to [PERSON_3] either, when I ring the switchboard? Because I'd have to mention the call to check it was genuine. So what exactly are you asking me not to discuss, and with whom?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, ring [PERSON_3] and tell them everything about this call. That's exactly what I'd want you to do. I meant keep it from other people, family, neighbours, that sort of thing, not from the firm. Sorry, I should have put that more clearly. So ring [PHONE_1], ask for [PERSON_3], and say what I've said to you. I'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's a clearer answer than the first one, I'll grant you. But I'll tell you plainly, I'm not going to be treating the number you've given me as the starting point. I'll find the firm myself and ring whatever the directory lists. And I'll say this too, if I wanted to check something like this with family, or a neighbour, or anyone else, I'd do so. A genuine firm wouldn't mind that. So, I'll check it independently, and if there's a real file, they'll write to me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just put a stack of files on my desk -- right. Yes, that's fine, you do that. Check it through the directory, speak to whoever you like, and if there's a file the letter will reach you in due course. I won't ring again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So, just to be clear, since I did say it twice, I'm not confirming anything on this call, I'll find the firm myself through the directory, and I'll speak to whoever I like about it. If there's a genuine file, a letter will come. Fine. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's all noted. Nothing confirmed today, you'll check independently, and the letter follows. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, that's an accurate summary. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the support team here, and I promise this is a quick one, nothing complicated. Basically, I just wanted to say a proper thank you, because you were a monthly supporter of ours for, oh, quite a while, and it made a real difference, honestly, the kind of steady giving that lets us plan ahead instead of scrambling. I noticed the monthly gift lapsed a little while back, and I thought, well, rather than just let that go quietly, I'd pick up the phone and ask if you'd ever thought about renewing it. Is now an okay time, [PERSON_1]? It really would only take a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Sorry, which organisation did you say you were with? I didn't quite catch it. And I'm a bit unsure about the "monthly supporter" part, because I don't recall setting anything up as a recurring gift. I think I might have given once, a one-off donation, so I'm not certain what record you're looking at.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sure, no problem, [PERSON_1], it's [COMPANY_A], that's [COMPANY_A], I'm [PERSON_2] on the support side there. And honestly, that's a really fair thing to ask, everyone asks that, so don't worry about it. I'm looking at what's on my screen and it's showing a monthly gift under your name, but it's entirely possible it was set up when you made that first donation and it just didn't stick in your memory, that happens all the time, [PERSON_1]. I mean, I'd hate for you to feel like I'm putting words in your mouth, so if it was only ever a one-off, that's fine too, I can just note that down. Did you want to have a think about whether you'd like to give again, or would it be easier if I just popped a note on your file?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well -- I mean, it's -- hang on. You've said the name twice now, but you haven't told me what the organisation actually does, so I still don't know which charity this is. And I'd, uh, I'd rather not decide anything on the spot. If there's a record, can you tell me roughly when the first gift was made, and about how much it was? I'm not going to read out anything on my side, but I'd like to see whether what you've got matches what I remember.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sure, yeah, so we're, uh, we're the -- sorry, let me start that again. [COMPANY_A] is the charity you gave to, that's the name on the record, and I don't want to just rattle off a mission statement at you when you've asked a simple question, you're right, that's on me. As for the details, the first gift on your file is from roughly [AMOUNT_1] and I'm, I'm not going to be too precise on the date because I'd rather you check it against your own bank statement than take my word for it. Honestly, [PERSON_1], that's probably the best way to do it, have a look in your own time and see if it matches.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, let me say back what I've actually heard, because I think it's worth being precise about it. You've given me the name of the organisation, but only as a placeholder, and when I asked what it does you started to answer and then sort of stopped and went back to the name. You've given me an approximate amount, but no date. And you've suggested I check my own bank statement, which, to be fair, is sensible advice, but it also happens to mean I'm the one doing the verifying, and all you've offered is an assertion. None of that is proof of anything, and I don't think you're obliged to prove it right now, I just don't see how I'd confirm it from my side. What I'd normally do in this situation is quite simple. I'd look up the charity myself, find their published contact details, and get in touch that way if I wanted to renew anything or ask about a past gift. I'm not saying you're not who you say you are, I just wouldn't act on an unsolicited call regardless of who it was. So, is there a reference number or a donor ID you could give me, or an email address I could write to instead? And, uh, one more thing. What happens if I simply say no to renewing? Is that all it takes?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's all it takes, [PERSON_1], just a no and that's the end of it. And honestly, what you're describing is exactly what I'd do in your shoes. Look us up yourself, use the contact details you find on your own, no hurry at all. If you want to ask about a past gift, our supporter care team can help, and they'll have your reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], on file, though I'd go through the published number rather than anything I give you today. I'm not going to push, I'd rather you feel comfortable. Do you want me to take you off the calling list as well, so you don't get another call like this one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hm, right, well -- let me just, give me a second here. Okay. Yes, I'd appreciate being taken off the calling list, thank you. And no, I won't be renewing anything today. If I decide I want to look into a past gift, I'll find the published contact details myself and go through supporter care that way. Thanks for being straightforward about it, and for not pushing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, [PERSON_1], I'll flag that now, so you shouldn't hear from us again. Oh, and just so I've got it right, you said earlier that you'd only given once, a one-off gift, is that right? I'll put that on your file so nobody assumes there's a monthly one. No need to say anything more if you'd rather not. Thanks for taking the call, [PERSON_1], and take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's someone at the door -- no, it's fine, they've gone past. Right. Yes, as far as I recall it was a one-off, but I'd rather you just note that I declined and leave it there, since I can't actually confirm it from my end. Thanks for the call, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Wonderful, this is [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, and I'm just ringing as part of our standard post-procedure check-in, so, uh, nothing to be alarmed about at all. We like to follow up with everyone about a week after any procedure to see how the pet is recovering, whether there've been any concerns, and whether you'd like us to book a follow-up visit, and I do have to complete these before we close the day's schedule at five, so I'll try to be brief. So, if you've got a moment, how is your pet getting along since last week?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, that's me. Well, that's very kind of you to ring, I didn't think anyone did that anymore. Now, which, um, which pet would this be about? Because I've got Biscuit, he's the old tabby, and then there's, no, wait, Biscuit's the one that went in, I think. Last week, you said? Gosh, he's been sleeping on the radiator shelf mostly, he's always done that, even in summer, silly thing. Is that, is that normal after an operation, do you know?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, well, sleeping a lot is, uh, very common after a procedure, so that sounds like a perfectly normal Biscuit, honestly. And, um, so, just so we're on the same page, I'm showing a procedure on file for last week, and I'd just be confirming it's the right pet before we go any further. Now, the main thing is whether you'd like a follow-up visit booked, and I do need to wrap these up before we close at five today, so, so, how is Biscuit getting along otherwise, eating, drinking, all that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, he's eating, yes, he's eating like a, well, he's always been a bit fussy, only the chicken one, not the fish, and, sorry, you said you needed to confirm the right pet? Because I only said Biscuit, I didn't say, I mean what's on your file, does it say, because I'm not sure it was last week, it might have been the week before, with the, the dental thing, or was that the other, no, hang on, what did you say your name was again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], from account services at [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery. And, uh, what I'm showing is a procedure last week, but if the dates are, I mean, if it's not matching what you remember, we can, well -- look, I'm just completing the standard post-procedure check-in, and I do have to finish these before we close at five, so, so, would you like a follow-up visit booked for Biscuit, or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I don't know about a follow-up, because I'm not sure it was last week, like I said, it might've been the week before, with the dental thing. And you haven't actually said what it says on your file, have you? What does it say he had done? Because I only said Biscuit, I never said what the procedure was, and you said, well, you said you're showing one, so what is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, no, that's a fair question, and I do understand, so let me explain how this works from my end. Account services doesn't see the clinical notes themselves, uh, we only see that a procedure was logged against the account and the date it was logged, and then the check-in call goes out under our standard post-procedure protocol, which is why I can't read you the details of what was done. Those would be with the clinical team, and if you'd rather confirm it with them directly, that's completely fine, you'd just ring the practice, but, um, the protocol does have me confirm the right pet and the right date first, and I do need to get these wrapped up before we close at five today, so, so, you said Biscuit, and you think it might have been the week before, with the dental, is that right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's right, Biscuit, and I think it was the week before, with the dental, but now you've got me wondering, because I'm not certain, and it's a funny thing, isn't it, that you can see a procedure was logged but not what it was. You'd think the first thing on the screen would be what he'd had done. Anyway, he's got this one tooth at the side that was bothering him, he'd been dropping his biscuits, which is a bit of a joke really with a name like Biscuit, and my neighbour, she's lovely, she runs the little shop on the corner, she said it was probably the tooth, and she was right, she's usually right about animals. But I'm sorry, I'm rambling, I do that when it's quiet in the house. What I was going to say is, I think I'd rather ring the surgery myself and ask them, if that's all right with you. You said that's fine. Because I'd want to know it's the right date before anyone books anything, and, well, you haven't actually asked me for anything I'd mind giving, but I'd still feel better. Do you have a number I should ring, or is it just the one on Biscuit's little vaccination card? I've got that somewhere, in the drawer by the telly, I think.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, that's fine, the number on the vaccination card is the practice's main line, so just -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you -- just ring that and they'll sort it out, and, uh, if you could do it today, before we close at five, that'd be ideal. And I won't keep you any longer, I hope Biscuit's tooth keeps behaving, and, um, you have a good afternoon, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, thank you, that's very good of you, and I'll have a rummage for that card. It's the one with the little paw print on the front, I think. And I'll ring them before five if I can find it, though if I don't it'll be tomorrow, no harm in that, will there be? Biscuit's not going anywhere. Right then, thank you for ringing, [PERSON_2], it was nice to have a chat. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh wonderful, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, you sound like you might've just sat down with a cup of tea or something, ha. It's [PERSON_2] calling from the customer care team at [COMPANY_A], we're a digital-asset investment desk, and I've got a little something I wanted to run by you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. No, no, you're not catching me at a bad moment, I'm just at home, not much on really. Sorry, who did you say you were calling from again? A digital... asset something? I'm afraid I didn't quite catch the name of it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, that's quite alright, happens all the time! It's [COMPANY_A], we're a digital-asset investment desk, sort of a boutique outfit. And I should say, this is a courtesy call to our existing clients, so you'll have been on our list for a while now, probably since you first enquired with us. Well, uh, I say enquired, it might've come through a partner firm, I'd have to look at the file. Anyway, how's your day been so far, anything nice planned for the weekend?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, my day's been fine, thank you, very quiet. Um, sorry, can I just go back a moment? You said digital-asset something, and I didn't quite follow what that actually is. Is it like, shares and that sort of thing? I'm afraid I'm not very good with the technical words. And I'm sorry, I don't remember enquiring with anyone like that, but I'm sure it's just me forgetting. You said it might have been a partner firm?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, don't apologise, it's easy to lose track of these things. And yes, a partner firm, I'd have to pull up the file. Now, you said you're after something a bit safer than shares, and that's exactly what this is, a very steady little position, nothing like the ups and downs of the stock market. The reason I'm ringing today in particular is that it closes at the end of the day, and honestly, the return on it is quite something. But first, tell me, do you keep much put away in savings, or is it all tied up in the house?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, uh, I don't think I said that, about wanting something safer than shares, I'm sorry. I might have, but I don't remember it, and I did say I'm not very good with the technical words, so perhaps that's where it came from? But my savings, well, that's a bit of a personal thing, isn't it? I'm sorry, I don't mean to be rude, you've been ever so friendly. It's just that I don't really know who you are yet, not properly, and you've said it closes at the end of the day, which does seem very quick. Is that normal, to ring someone up and say it all has to be decided today? And you still haven't said what the actual thing is, only that it's steady and the return is quite something. Sorry, I keep asking, I just don't want to say the wrong thing and then find I've agreed to something I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you're not being rude at all, that's just good sense, I wish more people were like you! And look, maybe I've got my wires crossed on the safer-than-shares bit, I talk to so many people in a day. Honestly, the actual product, it's a fixed-term digital-asset position, and the deadline, well, it's always been closing at the end of the week, not today, I don't know why I said today. Anyway, how long have you lived in that area, [CITY_1], is it? Lovely part of the world.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, um, before the area, can I go back a bit? Two turns ago you said it was steady, and then, I think, that the return was quite something. How can it be steady and have a big return? I don't understand that, I'm sorry, it sounds like two different things to me. And, well, I never said I live in [CITY_1], did I? I'm not sure how you've got that. Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just feel a bit lost.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you don't miss a thing, do you! Look, steady and a strong return, they go together here, that's the whole point of it, it's a very steady, very solid position with a return that's quite something. As for [CITY_1], it'll be on the file, that's all, nothing to worry about, I wouldn't read anything into it. Now, I did say it's closing today, or this week, whichever, but the sooner you're in the better. Could we maybe keep this between us for now, though? It's a bit of an exclusive allocation, and I'd rather you didn't mention it to anyone just yet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm, well, uh... gosh, sorry, I'm just, um, thinking. It's only that you said today, and then the end of the week, and then whichever, and I don't know which it is. And keeping it between us, that's, well, that's a bit odd, isn't it? Why wouldn't I mention it to anyone? My neighbour always says if something's good you can tell people about it. I'm sorry, you've been ever so nice, but I think I'd like to talk to someone I know first, and I still don't really know who you are, do I? Perhaps you could send me something in the post, and I'll have a look when I've had a think. Thank you for calling, I do appreciate it, but I'll say goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, now, no, no, there's no need to go and say goodbye, we've only just got going! Look, I'll say it again, it's a very steady position, a lovely return, and I just don't want you to miss out, that's all. And the post, well, that takes ages, it'd be well past the closing by the time it got to you. Tell you what, you have that think, have a chat with your neighbour if you must, and I'll ring you back a bit later on to finish this off, alright? Speak soon, [PERSON_1], you take care now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, well, thank you, but you needn't ring back, really. I'll have a think and a chat with my neighbour, and if it's something I want, I'll find a number for you myself. Sorry, I know you've been very patient. Goodbye now, thank you, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, hang on a second, before you go, can I just clear something up? You said a moment ago you'd find a number for me yourself, and I think that's where the wires got crossed, because I never gave you a number, did I? So you'd be ringing round blind, and honestly that's no good to either of us, so I'll just pop you down for a quick ring back later on, nothing to it, and we'll finish this off then. Right, you take care, [PERSON_1], and enjoy that cup of tea.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, but I really don't want a ring back, thank you. I did say, I'll have a think and I'll look for a number myself, so you needn't pop me down for anything. No, please don't ring. I'm sorry, I know you're only doing your job, but I'd like to leave it there now. Goodbye, thank you, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a thing to drink, lovely, yes, a nice cup of tea does the trick, ha! Right, well, you go and have that, [PERSON_1], and I'll be in touch a bit later on to finish things off. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Please don't ring back. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the home-delivery service -- sorry, one second, there's a van reversing out here, I can barely -- right. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? I'm calling about your order placed online, the delivery window for today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, security operations? For a delivery? Back up a second, which company did you say, I missed that over the van. And I don't recall ordering anything today, so what order are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. The supermarket delivery service. Your order went in online, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], two-hour window this afternoon. If you didn't place it, say so and I'll flag it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. No, I didn't place any order, but I'm not reading anything back to you. You rang me, so you tell me. What's this flag going to do, and why's security ringing about a grocery delivery? Two minutes, mate, get to the point.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, look, the flag just puts the order on hold, nothing gets delivered, nothing gets charged. And security rings because, well, we -- I mean, orders that don't match the account holder get routed to my desk, that's all it is. Now, the reason I'm actually on the line is the window and one substituted item, but if you're telling me you didn't order, then I need the name on the account confirmed, and that's -- hang on, I'm not asking you to read me anything sensitive, just whether [PERSON_2] is the right person.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, two turns back you said the flag does nothing, then it's a substituted item and a delivery window. Which is it? Either I didn't order and you're just holding it, or you're ringing about a substitution on an order I apparently did place. Those can't both be right. And you've asked me to confirm my name twice now, when you rang me. Who did you actually dial?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, who did I dial? I dialled the number on the order, [PHONE_1], that's what comes up on my screen. And you said it can't be right, I said it can't be -- no, hang on, you said "substitution," I heard "subscription." We don't do subscriptions, that's not what this is. It's one item swapped for a similar product, that's all I'm after, a yes or no on it. Look, you're right, I've muddled it. The order's under [PERSON_2], this number's on it, and I'd rather you didn't just take my word. If you want to check I'm genuine, ask me something only [COMPANY_A] would know. Go on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not playing that game. You want me to quiz you on something only the company would know, and I don't know anything about the company's insides, so whatever you answered I couldn't check it. That's a nice little test for making somebody feel they've done due diligence, and it proves nothing. And I never said subscription, you said substitution yourself two turns ago, so don't hand that back to me. Here's where I am. You rang me. You told me security ops, then it's a delivery window, then it's a swapped item, then it's a name check, and the story's shifted every time I've poked it. I don't have an order. If there is one in my name, somebody else made it, and the right move is I deal with that through the company's own number, the one I look up myself, not through whoever happens to ring me. So no yes or no on your substitution, no confirming anything, and I'm certainly not going to say whether I'm [PERSON_2]. If you've got a genuine reference, put it on an email to the account holder. That's it from me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Fine, and look, that's the right instinct, I'm not going to talk you out of it. You're also right about me, I did say substitution, I made a mess of it, and I'm sorry. I do wish you'd let me finish, because this is a plain call. I'm not after your name or any details. All it was ever going to be is, one item on a delivery got swapped for a similar product, is that acceptable, yes or no, and the window's two hours this afternoon. That's the whole call. Nothing else. Now, if you've no order, then it's a wrong number or somebody keyed your number in against theirs, and that happens more than it should. So don't confirm anything to me. Do what you said. Look up the [COMPANY_A] customer line yourself, ring it, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF] to them. They'll show you whether there's an order, whose it is, and what's been substituted. That's all I'd ask you to do, and I'd rather you check it your way than trust me on the phone. And ask them one thing while you're there, whether security operations ever rings customers about substitutions. That's a fair question, and if the answer's no, you've lost nothing by hanging up on me. Alright. Sorry for the bother. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, funny thing, you've just told me to ring them and quote the reference, and about two minutes ago you wanted the reference kept off the line. Never mind. And for the record, I didn't give you [ACCOUNT_REF], you did, so I wouldn't be quoting anything. I'll look up their number myself and ask them the security question, since you've handed me it. If there's a genuine order, they can sort it with the account holder. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well -- uh, yes. You're correct on both counts, I did read out the reference myself, so that's on me, not you. And I never wanted it kept off the line, I think I -- no, that was a muddle on my part. Look, I won't keep you. Ring the customer line, ask them about the order and about the substitution, and if there's a mismatch with your number they'll sort it with the account holder. Alright. Sorry again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, before you go -- two turns back you said you'd look up their number yourself and ask them the security question. Which question was that, exactly? Because I'm not sure I put it the way you've got it, and I'd rather you asked them the right thing. It's whether security operations ever rings customers about substitutions. Just that. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I know which question, you gave it to me, whether security operations rings customers about substitutions. I heard you the first time. And I'll ask it in my own words, off a number I find myself. I said goodbye, I meant goodbye. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, whether security rings customers about substitutes -- no, sorry, substitutions, that's the one. Hold on, you said "off a number I find myself," and I heard "off a number I phoned myself." Well, whichever, it comes to the same thing. Look up the line, ring it, ask your question. Goodbye, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said "find," not "phoned," and it doesn't come to the same thing, but -- no. Look, I'm done going round this. And you've just called me [PERSON_2] again after I said I wasn't confirming that. I'm not dealing with this by phone. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, that was -- hang on, someone's dropped a pallet out the back, I lost the thread for a second. Right. I did say [PERSON_2] again, and you're correct, you never confirmed it, so forget I said it. And "find," not "phoned," understood. You're doing the sensible thing. Ring the customer line yourself, ask your question, and that's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before I go. Two turns back you said you'd just misheard me, "find" versus "phoned", and now you're telling me to ring the line myself. Fine. But what did you actually mean by "security rings because orders that don't match the account holder get routed to my desk"? Because that's the bit that doesn't hold. A mismatch means somebody else's order, so why are you ringing me at all? Go on, quick.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It was badly put. My desk gets the flagged ones, and I ring the number on the order to check it's the right person. That's all it was. Ring the customer line yourself and ask them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: So you ring the number on the order to check it's the right person, and I'm the wrong person, so -- no. Look, that's, that's actually an answer I can live with, but it still, it doesn't explain why you needed my name. Never mind. I'm done. I'll look up the line myself, ask my question, and if there's an order, they'll deal with the account holder. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Uh, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], about your energy account... are you there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, yes, hello, sorry, I'm here, I'm just -- I'm driving, so you're on speaker and the signal's a bit rubbish. Um, [PERSON_1], yes, that's me, sorry. Your energy account, you said? Who is this again, sorry, I didn't quite catch the company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, I'm sorry to catch you while you're driving. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier. Um... it's about your account, there's a balance that's overdue, and I didn't want you to be caught out by it. Are you still there? I can hear the line crackling a bit... Look, if it's not safe to talk, I can ring you back, honestly, that's no trouble at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, no, I'm still here, sorry, it's crackling a lot. Did you say a *bonus* on my account? Like a credit, or, um, some sort of reward? Because I didn't, I mean, I wasn't expecting that, I don't think I've done anything to get one. Sorry, I'm probably, the line's just breaking up, can you say that again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm sorry, I think the line's garbled that. Not a bonus, no. An overdue balance. Money that's owed on the account, I'm afraid, not a credit. I'm so sorry, I know that's not what you were hoping to hear. Are you still with me? It's about [AMOUNT_1], and if it isn't cleared, supply could be interrupted on [CODE_1], which is the last thing I want for you. So I'm really just ringing to make sure that doesn't happen. Does that make sense?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, I mean, I thought I'd, hang on, I always pay that, I'm fairly sure I pay it by, uh -- sorry, I'm not saying you're wrong, it's just the signal and I'm a bit, I'm on a bit of a bend here. Overdue, though? Since when? Because I didn't get anything, I don't think, no letter or email or anything, and now you're saying it could be cut off? Sorry, I'm, can you just tell me again who you said you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you broke up a bit there, did you say you pay it by direct debit? Oh, if it's on direct debit, that's, um, that would change things, but I'm not able to see... no wait, I'm sorry, I'm getting ahead of myself. I'm [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier, and I'm so sorry about the letter, that's frustrating. And please, don't worry, I'm not asking you for anything on this call. If you can pull over, or when you're home, you can check the account yourself. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I'm still, I'm here. I did say, well, I think I said I pay it by, no, wait, I didn't actually say how I pay it, did I? Sorry, I'm, it's just, this is, you're saying I owe money but you can't see, but you rang me about it? That's, I mean, I'm not trying to be difficult, I'm just a bit, if you're really from them, then, um, I could just ring them myself when I'm home? On the number on my bill, I mean. Would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's absolutely all right, and honestly it's what I'd do in your position. Sorry, I did muddle that last bit, you hadn't said how you pay, that was me getting ahead of myself. Um, so when you're home, ring the number on your bill, or log in to your own online account, and the balance will be there. It should be the [AMOUNT_1] figure, and if you've got your last bill handy, the account reference on it, ending [ACCOUNT_REF], should match what I've got here. And if it's more than you can manage in one go, there's a payment plan we can set up, so please don't worry about that. I'm not taking any payment on this call, I just didn't want the date to catch you out. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, I'm still here, sorry. Right, so I'll ring them myself when I get in, on the number on the bill. I think that's, yeah, I think that's the best thing, sorry, I just don't like deciding things while I'm driving, I'll end up missing my turn. Thank you for not, you know, pushing me. Right, I'd better concentrate on the road. Bye, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's, um... that's absolutely fine, yes, that's exactly the right thing to do. And please, don't apologise, I'm just sorry I rang when you were behind the wheel, that was my bad. So, um... when you do ring, they'll have a note on the account, and the payment plan's there if you need it. Drive safe, [PERSON_1], and, uh, thank you for being so patient with me. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Thanks, yeah, I will. Sorry again about the signal. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, don't be sorry about the signal, honestly, that's not your fault at all. Um, just, you ring the number on your bill, yes, the one on the bill, not one from me, and the account's all there for you. Right. Bye then, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... yeah, no, right, the one on the bill, got it, I'll, um, I'll do that, sorry, I'm just, hang on, there's a lorry, um... right, yes, that's me. Bye then, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, goodness, yes, you go, you concentrate on the lorry, that's far more important than me. Um, thank you, [PERSON_1], and sorry for the worry. Take care now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, it's fine, it's, I'm fine, it's gone past now, sorry, I'm just -- right, I really will ring them from home, on the bill number, yes. Thanks, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is Officer [PERSON_1], Security Operations at [COMPANY_A], the international lottery claims office. I'm calling regarding a prize award registered under this number, and I need to confirm a few claim details with you today. Am I speaking with the account holder?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- a lottery? I haven't, I mean I just woke up, I was having a little lie-down and, uh, I didn't even buy a -- hang on, who is this again? Is this about my sister's thing, because she always uses my number for the, the forms?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Officer [PERSON_1], Security Operations, [COMPANY_A]. I don't have any record of a sister. The award is registered to this number, and that's the number I'm required to verify. Now, the claim is time-sensitive, so I need you awake and focused for about two minutes. Can you confirm your full name for the file?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, but -- hang on, I'm not giving my name to somebody I don't know, I only just picked up. I said I didn't buy a lottery ticket, I didn't buy any ticket, so how can there be a prize? And you still haven't said, who are you with again? Is it a company, or the government, or what?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, I've stated it twice. [COMPANY_A], the international lottery claims office. Not government, a claims office. And tickets are often entered on your behalf, through a promotional draw, so not buying one is not unusual. Now, the prize is [AMOUNT_1], and the window to confirm is closing, so I need your name for the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay but, wait, go back a bit, you said you didn't have any record of a sister. Why would you even be looking for a sister? I only brought her up because, well, she uses my number, and then you said that thing, and I didn't really follow what you meant by it. And the promotional draw, who put me in that, because I never signed up for anything, I'm quite sure about that, I think.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: What? No, I wasn't looking for a sister, I was saying the file lists one number, this number, and -- hold on. Sorry, somebody's at my desk, one moment. Right. The promotional draw. Entries are compiled through partner databases, so I can't tell you which one from here, but your number was drawn. The ticket is [CODE_1], drawn last Thursday, and the prize is [AMOUNT_2], sorry, [AMOUNT_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a pigeon on the, uh, on the windowsill, it does that, it just sits there and stares at me, anyway. You said [AMOUNT_2] and then you said [AMOUNT_1], so which one is it? Because that's two different numbers, and if you can't keep your own prize straight I'm not sure why I'd -- and you still can't tell me which database I'm supposed to be in, which, I mean, that seems like something you'd know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The figure is [AMOUNT_1]. The other number was a reference total, it's a, a clerical thing, don't read into it. And the database is a partner source, I've said that, it isn't mine to name. What I need is your name and confirmation that you'll proceed today, because after today the file goes inactive and I can't hold it open.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, hang on. It's just that, um, a clerical thing, you said, but it was the prize you said twice, wasn't it, and -- no, what I mean is, if it goes inactive after today then, I mean, why ring me at, what is it, afternoon, if it's been sitting there since last Thursday? Why not last week? And you still haven't, I don't know, given me a number I could ring you back on, or something, because honestly I'd rather, I think I'd rather ring somebody myself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Two turns ago, you mean the draw date? Last Thursday, I said last Thursday, that's when the, uh, the draw was held, not when the file was opened. The file opened, well, it's, look, I don't have the opening date in front of me. And a callback line isn't how this office operates, sir. I'm on a direct line, you'd only reach a switchboard that can't see this file. So, the name, please, and your confirmation, today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, see, that's -- you can't ring me but I can't ring you, that's backwards, isn't it? If it's a real office it'd have a number, surely, my sister's, uh, my sister's bank has one, it's on the back of the card. And the dates keep moving about, and the amount, and now you can't see the file, and, I'm sorry, but I think I'm just going to say no to this. I'm not giving you my name, and I'm not confirming anything today. If there's a prize somebody can write to me. Right, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? ... Yes, good. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance side at [COMPANY_A]. I'll be careful with my words here, because it's a, well, a somewhat delicate matter involving a relative of yours, and I'd rather you hear it from me, calmly, than from someone else.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Compliance at what? I'm stood in a queue with a basket here, so you'll have to speak up, I only caught half of that. And "a relative of mine," which relative? Because that's the sort of thing people say when they want you to panic before you've had a chance to think, and I've had that done to me before, so I'm not in the mood. If somebody's actually in trouble, then say who and say what, plainly, and if you can't do that, then I'd like to know why you're ringing me and not them.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, that's a fair question, and honestly I'd rather you asked it. I'd think less of you if you didn't. [PERSON_2], compliance at [COMPANY_A], and I understand the instinct completely, you should be careful. I'm not asking you to panic, and I'd, uh, I'd ask you not to. As to why I'm ringing you and not them... well. They can't talk right now. That's about as far as I can go over the phone, I'm afraid, and I'd rather not say a name in a supermarket queue, you understand. It's, I mean, it's the sort of matter where the sooner it's sorted out the better, for everyone concerned. Perhaps if you could step somewhere quieter for a moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a minute ago you said you wanted me to hear it calmly from you, and now you won't say who it is or what it is at all? That's not hearing it from you, that's hearing nothing. And no, I'm not going anywhere quieter, I'm paying for my shopping. "They can't talk right now," what does that even mean? Can't, or won't? Look, I don't know you from Adam, so either tell me which relative and what's happened, or give me a number for [COMPANY_A] and I'll ring them myself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, no, I didn't say I wouldn't tell you, I said I'd rather not do it here, there's a difference. And I'm not saying they won't, they, uh, they can't, it's a, well, it's the circumstances. Look, a number for [COMPANY_A], I'd be happy to, in principle, but the person you'd reach on the main line wouldn't know anything about this, it's handled very discreetly, and I'd, I mean, I'd ask you to keep it between us for now, for your relative's sake. I'm not trying to rush you. But the longer it sits, the harder it gets for them, and I'd hate for that to land on you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no, hang on. Two goes ago you said it was a delicate matter involving a relative and you wanted me to hear it calmly from you. Fine. But now it's discreet, keep it between us, and the main line won't know anything about it? What sort of compliance department is it that nobody in the building has heard of? That's not a department, that's a story. And what do you mean "land on me"? Land what on me? You still haven't said one thing that's actually happened.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand why it sounds that way, and I'm glad you're pushing, I'd rather you did. "Land on you" was, uh, poor wording, I shouldn't have put it like that. I'm not -- look, I don't want to leave you feeling pressured. Perhaps it's best, I mean, if you spoke to someone in your family first, to check on them, and then, uh, if you still want to hear more, you can reach me on [PHONE_1]. I'd just say, don't leave it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, go back a second. Before that, you said the main line wouldn't know anything because it's handled discreetly. Discreetly by who? Who actually handles it, if it isn't the people in the building? And now it's "don't leave it too long" again, so which is it, no pressure or hurry up? You still haven't told me one thing that's happened. No, I'm not ringing that number, and I'll check on my own family myself, thanks. I'll find [COMPANY_A] on my own as well, and if you're genuine they'll know who you are. Right, I'm at the till now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's, uh, that's entirely your right. I'd only say... well, I'd prefer you didn't make a fuss with anyone at the main office, it might, I mean, it might complicate things for your relative. But, no, you do what you think is best. I'll, uh, leave the number with you, in case. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's lovely, that is. A minute ago it was no pressure at all, and now you'd prefer I didn't make a fuss with the main office, in case it complicates things for my relative. Why on earth would ringing the company you say you work for complicate anything? If you were who you say you are, you'd want me to check. You'd be telling me to ring them, not to keep quiet about it. That one sentence tells me everything I need. And you can keep your number, I haven't written it down and I'm not going to, because I've been round this block before and I'm still cross about it. I'm going to ring my family, one at a time, off my own phone, and if anybody's in any sort of bother they'll tell me themselves. I'll ring the company on a number I find myself, too, and I'll tell them exactly what you said, including the bit about not making a fuss. Right, I'm at the till, the lad's waiting, so that's me. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm so sorry to ring out of the blue, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the digital-asset desk, and I'm just, I wanted to catch you before the position closes today, because --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie-down. Who did you say you were again? Because you said something about a position closing, and I'm not, I mean, I don't think I've got a position, I've got a bit of garden to sort out, that's about all that's closing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm so sorry, I've woken you, that's awful of me. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], we're a digital-asset investment desk, and, um, well, you're right, you wouldn't have a position yet, that's sort of the point of the call. Are you still there? Sorry. It's just that your name came up on a list for an allocation that closes at the end of today, and I'd hate for you to miss it, I really would, it's only for your own benefit that I'm ringing at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. A list. What list? I don't remember putting my name on any list.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fair, you wouldn't have, it's not a list you'd sign up to, it's more, um, sorry, one second, there's someone at my shoulder, I'm just -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Sorry about that. Are you still with me? Right. It's more of an eligibility list, so it's already flagged you as suitable, and the allocation's returning, well, it's a very strong figure at the moment, which is why it closes so fast, and honestly I'd just feel terrible if it passed you by.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Suitable how, though? You still haven't said how you got my name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, you're quite right to ask, I'm sorry, I should have said straight away. It would have come through one of our referral partners, [COMPANY_B], I believe, though I'd have to check the exact record, and I don't have it in front of me right now, I'm so sorry. Are you still there? The thing is, I really don't want to keep you on about where the name came from when the closing time's so close, because that's what matters for you, isn't it, not missing the window. If you like, I can just take you through the position, very briefly, and you can decide after.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, you say a partner, but you can't tell me which one, you've not got the record, and now you want me to hurry up about it. That's, I mean, that doesn't sit right with me. If it's my name on a list, surely you can look at the list. Look, I've just woken up, I'm not in a state to be deciding about any, what did you call it, allocation. Is there a number I can ring you back on, or a, I don't know, a proper address I can write to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry. Um, I'm not really able to give out a direct line, it's all routed through the desk, and I'd hate for you to lose the allocation just waiting on a call back. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still here, I'm just, no. No, I don't think so. You can't tell me where you got my name, you can't give me a number, and it all has to be settled today, and that's, well, that's three things I don't like, isn't it? If it's a proper company they'll still be there tomorrow and they can write to me. So I'm going to leave it, thank you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, sorry, before you go, did you say you'd like to ring back tomorrow, or write? Because I really can't take a letter, it'd have missed the closing by then, and, well, honestly, I'd hate for you to lose it over a bit of paperwork. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said write, or you could, hang on, is that the kettle? No, that's next door's dog, it does that. Where was I. Yes, no, I'm not doing it today, and if it can't wait for a letter then it's not for me, that's all. Right, I'm going to go and see to that garden. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, did you say the guard? That's lovely, a garden, I mean, it's a nice time of year for it, isn't it. Only, um, I did just want to say, if you'd rather not do anything today, that's absolutely fine, truly, but could you perhaps keep this between us for now, just until tomorrow? Because if the other people on the list hear about the allocation, it can sort of, well, it can disappear for everyone. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Keep it between, no, I'm not, I mean, I wasn't going to ring round anybody, I was only going to, well. Actually, no. Why would you need me to keep quiet? If it's a proper thing, then, hang on, it'd not matter who I told, would it? No, that's, that's another one I don't like. I'm putting the phone down now, thank you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, please, wait, sorry, I think I put that badly. It isn't about keeping quiet, truly, it's just, well, I did say we'd lose the allocation if you waited for a letter, but I suppose, um, I suppose a letter could still reach us, I just, are you still there? It's only that I'd feel dreadful if you went away thinking badly of us, when I'm only ringing for your own protection, really.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, now you've changed it, haven't you? A minute ago the letter was too slow and the whole thing would be gone by teatime, and now a letter could reach you after all. I'm not being funny, but that's not how a thing works if it's real. Either it closes today or it doesn't. And "for your protection", I mean, protection from what? I've not been in any danger until you rang, I was asleep, that's all. And I'll tell you what else, you've asked me three or four times if I'm still there, and I've been there every time, so I don't know what you're checking. I don't think badly of you, I don't know you well enough to think anything at all, but I've not been told where you got my name, I've not been given a number, and I've been asked to keep it quiet. That's my lot, really. If your company wants to write to me, it can, and if it's gone by the time the letter comes, then it wasn't mine to have. I'm going now, and I'd rather you didn't ring again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, you're quite right, I did put it badly, and I do apologise for the muddle, it's just, well, there's a lot moving at once on our side today and I've, um, I've probably made it sound more tangled than it is. Are you still there? Sorry, that's a habit, I know. Look, I'm not trying to rush you into anything, truly, and I'm certainly not asking you to decide while you're half asleep. It's only that these allocations do tend to close quickly, and I'd hate for you to hear about it afterwards and think, well, why didn't anyone tell me. I'd feel dreadful about that, honestly. So what I could do, if it's easier, is leave it with you for now, and perhaps, I don't know, ring you once more later today, when you've had a cup of tea and you're properly awake, and we could go through it slowly, without any pressure at all. Would that be all right? I mean, I can't give you a number, as I said, it's all routed through the desk, but I'd be happy to ring you, it's no trouble.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. No, I don't want you to ring again, I said that, I'd rather you didn't ring again. Not later, not after a cup of tea. If your company wants to write, it can write, that's what I said, and I'll not be deciding anything today, tomorrow, whenever you call. So that's it, really. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Oh, hi, sorry to bother you -- is this [PERSON_1]? My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and, uh, I wondered if you might have five minutes for a short consumer survey? It's nothing to do with selling anything, I promise. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh -- yeah, yeah, I'm here, sorry, I was just, uh, I was having a lie-down, long morning. Who did you say you were again? Something about a survey? I mean, my sister's the one who does all those, she did one about biscuits once, I think it was biscuits -- anyway. What's it for, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I've caught you at a bad moment, haven't I? It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and the survey's just about everyday shopping habits, what people buy and how they feel about it. It's really just so the results reflect what people like you actually think, you know, for your own benefit in the end. And, uh, sorry, you mentioned your sister did one about biscuits? Was that for us, do you think, or was it a different company? Only I'd hate for you to feel you were being asked twice. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No no, I don't know, I couldn't tell you who it was, she just said it was -- look, how did you get my number? Because I don't, I mean I'm not even sure I'm on any list, I just got up and the phone was, and I wasn't expecting --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's a perfectly fair question, I'm sorry. So we, uh, the numbers are picked at random by a computer, it's not, I mean we don't have a list with your name on it as such, it's just, well -- it just generated yours, and I'm only given the number and a first name to ask for. Which is why I wasn't sure it was you at first, sorry. And honestly, if it's a bad time, or you'd rather not, that's completely fine, I can just take the number off our system. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Random, right, okay. Hm. But then how'd you have my first name if it's random? That's, I mean, that's a bit odd, isn't it? You said you only get the number and a first name, so somebody must've -- oh, I don't know, I'm still half asleep. Look, what sort of questions is it, anyway? Because I'm not giving out my bank or anything like that, I'll tell you that now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right to ask, and, uh, sorry, I think I put that badly. It isn't random all the way through, the number comes off a general list and then, well, I did say it was only a number earlier, but there's a first name on the sheet as well, I'm not actually sure where that part comes from, I'd have to check with my supervisor. And please don't worry about the bank thing, I'd never ask for anything like that, it's only things like which shops you use and roughly how often. Nothing personal, nothing about money or accounts. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. See, that's the bit I don't love, you said random, and then it's a list, and now you don't know where the name came from. That's, I mean, that doesn't quite add up, does it? And you keep asking if I'm still here, which, I'm here, I'm just... what was the name of your company again? I didn't catch it properly. Because if it's a proper research outfit then there'd be, I don't know, a website or a number I could ring back on, wouldn't there? My sister always said to ask for that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, your sister's quite right, and I'm sorry, I did muddle that. It's [COMPANY_A], and I'm [PERSON_2], a case handler there. You can look us up at [URL_1], or ring us on [PHONE_1], and they'll confirm the survey's genuine and take you off the call list if you'd like. And the random thing, that was me explaining it badly. The numbers do come off a list, I just don't know where the first names come from, and I shouldn't have guessed. I'd much rather you check than feel uneasy about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, well, that's, hm. That's fair enough, I suppose, you're not pushing me, I'll give you that. But I'm not writing down a website, I've only just got my glasses on and the pen's, I don't know where the pen is. And I thought you said you were just doing the calls, not a case handler? Case handler sounds like, I don't know, like I've got a case. Anyway, I think I'll just ring my sister and ask her if it was you lot with the biscuits, and if it was, I'll maybe ring back. Is that all right? Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, that's completely all right, and I'm sorry about the case handler thing, that's just my job title, nothing to do with you having a case, you haven't got one, honestly. It's just the title, sorry. And do ring your sister, that's a sensible thing to do, and there's no need to write anything down now, you can find us by our name, [COMPANY_A], whenever you've got your glasses and your pen. Really, no pressure at all, I'll just take your number off the list today. Thank you for being so patient, [PERSON_1], and, um, have a lovely rest of your morning. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, thanks, that's, yeah. I'll have a think and ask her about the biscuits. It's afternoon, by the way, I think, but never mind, I lost track. Right, bye then, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, um, yes, good afternoon. Is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one moment, I've got the file open here and I'm just -- yes. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, we handle estates, and I'm an assistant there. Er, it's about a matter where you may be named, and I'd just need to confirm a couple of things with you before our formal letter arrives.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Hold on. Sorry, yes, that's me. Who did you say you were? A solicitor's? Sorry, I didn't catch the name of the place. And named in what, exactly? Is someone, has someone died? Sorry, I'm a bit flustered, I wasn't expecting a call.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, take your time, I know it's -- yes, it is an estate, so someone has passed away, I'm sorry, I should've said that more gently. The firm is [COMPANY_A], and I'm, um, [PERSON_2], an assistant there, and I can't really say who the person was until I've confirmed that you're, uh, the right [PERSON_1] -- and I'd ask you to keep this between us until the letter comes, if that's all right, because these things are sensitive and -- oh, and you're not obliged to say anything today, of course, so please don't feel --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, let me turn this down. Right. Sorry, you said a name a minute ago, the firm, and I didn't catch it. Could you say that again? And then you said you can't tell me who died until I've, what was it, confirmed I'm the right person? How do I do that? Sorry, I'm just, it's a lot, and I don't know who you are.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, of course, it's [COMPANY_A], and, um, we're in [CITY_1], I can give you the full address in a second -- I've just got it here -- uh, yes. And to confirm you're the right [PERSON_1], I'd only be asking for the things that'll be on our letter anyway, so your full name and your date of birth, um -- actually, no, hang on, let me not rush you, because you don't know me from anyone, and that's fair. Look, you don't have to tell me anything on this call. You could look us up yourself, in an independent directory, not off anything I give you, and ring the firm back that way, and I'd honestly rather you did that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Well, that's, sorry, that's actually quite fair of you to say. Hang on, I'm just moving the pan off the heat, it's catching, sorry. Right. So you're saying I should look the firm up myself and ring back? I mean, I'm not very good with that sort of thing, the internet and the directory and so on, my [PERSON_3] usually does it for me. But I suppose I could do that. It's just, it's a bit worrying, isn't it, someone's died and I might be named, and now I'm going to be wondering all evening. Is it, um, is it someone close? No, sorry, you said you can't say. Sorry, I keep forgetting. And you won't mind if I ring you back that way? Because honestly I'd feel better doing it properly, I'd just rather not give my date of birth to someone on the phone when I don't actually know who they are, no offence. Is that all right? Sorry, I'm rambling, I've got dinner going and my head's all over the place.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not at all, no offence taken, that's exactly the right thing to do. Um -- so, yes, [PERSON_3] can help, and you'd look up [COMPANY_A] in [CITY_1] in an independent directory, not through anything I give you, and ring the number you find there. Er, and when you get through, you can ask for me, [PERSON_2], or just say it's about a letter going out to a [PERSON_1], and they'll know, um -- and you don't need to give them your date of birth either until you're happy. I'm sorry, I know it's worrying, and I wish I could say more, but it'll all be in the letter. Is that, um, is that all right? Take your time, go and rescue your dinner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's, sorry, that's all right, I'll get my [PERSON_3] to look it up and ring. And if the letter comes, well, I'll read it, won't I. Right. Sorry, I really do need to see to this pan. Thank you for ringing, and, um, sorry for your trouble. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Thank you, yes, that's perfect, and no trouble at all, I'm sorry to have caught you at a bad moment. Um, one thing before you go, so you know it's really us when you ring: ask whether the letter will be coming from [COMPANY_A]'s [CITY_1] office, and they'll be able to tell you the reference it'll quote, it's [CODE_1], and if they can't match it to me, then don't give them anything, all right? Go and see to your dinner, and I'm sorry again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, one more thing. Two minutes ago you said I could ring and ask for you, or just say it's about a letter for a [PERSON_1]. And now there's a reference, and the office, and, sorry, I'm lost. Which is it? Do I ask for you, or do I use the reference? And what did you mean, if they can't match it to you? I thought I was just checking you were real, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, yes, no, sorry, that's my fault, I've made it more complicated than it needs to be, and I did, uh, I did sort of say two different things there. Right, so, just one. utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. The number's on the intranet, same as always. Check the portal yourself, and if the ticket's there, call us back.

utterances.speaker: receiver

I'll go to the portal on my own and ring the helpdesk number I already have, and if there's a ticket in my name I'll deal with it that way. utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood. For the record, the ticket is [CODE_1], it was escalated by [PERSON_3], and if you'd rather verify first, you can reschedule this through the internal portal at [URL_1]. That's the proper channel anyway. And I wasn't dodging on the number. It's [PHONE_1], that's the helpdesk line, same as it's always been. I'm not going to push. If you'd rather check it yourself and ring back, that's your call and frankly it's the sensible one, but I will say the lockout activity on our side is real, so don't leave it sitting too long. Your account could be restricted until it's reviewed. That's not a threat, that's just how the policy works. Anyway, [PERSON_1], ring the helpdesk when you're ready.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said my account could be, what, retired? Until it's reviewed? That's not -- no, hang on, I think you said restricted. Either way, no. I'm not going to act on a warning I can't check, and I'll say again, I haven't had a single lockout today, so I'm not sure whose activity you're looking at. utterances.text: Right. A failed sign-in from another device, which is a different thing entirely, and I'll mention that when I report this. Goodbye.

Anyway, shall we get you over to the computer while the dinner simmers?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, hang on -- oh no, that's spitting, hold on. Okay. Sorry, what was that? Let you take a look from your end? Like, at my computer? Uh, I don't think I like that. utterances.speaker: receiver
