I'm not. I said that, didn't I? Not till I know who you are. So if you want to ring back later, that's up to you, but I'll have rung my cousins by then, and I'd rather you told me your name when you do. Right, I'm going now, I've got tomatoes to see to. Bye now.

utterances.text: Okay. Okay, uh... fine. I'll, I'll ring you back later, then. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, a loan? I didn't say anything about a loan, I, uh -- hang on. You said support, now it's investigations? Which is it? And, sorry, why does it matter if there's anyone around me? Why would you need to know that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, right, so, uh, you're quite right, I did say loan, my mistake, let me, I mean, it's both really, support and investigations, same floor, same department, everybody asks that, [PERSON_1], honestly. And the around-you thing, that's just, well, it's sort of, there's a bit of sensitivity on this one, nothing to do with you, but we're asking people to keep it just between us for now, from the branch staff, from family, because, and I shouldn't say too much, there may be somebody on the inside who's, uh, involved. So it's really just a quick chat, you and me, two minutes, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hang on. Two turns ago you said it was just a quick routine thing. Now it's someone on the inside and I'm not supposed to tell family? That's not routine, is it? And you still haven't told me which bank, you just keep saying [COMPANY_A]. So, um, why would a routine call need to be kept secret from the branch?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I mean, it is routine, [PERSON_1], the call itself is, it's just that the, well, the reason, I mean, the way we -- look, it's the sort of thing where the call is simple, but the confidentiality is because of the, uh, the other matter, which I really can't get into on an open line. And the bank, I did say, it's [COMPANY_A], that's who I'm with, that's all I can tell you right now. Honestly, everyone asks me that, and it's fine, it's a very normal question. So, can we just keep going, two minutes, you and me, and then you can get right back to the little one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So I can't tell anyone, you can't tell me why, and you can't tell me which bank. Yeah, no. I'm not doing this over the phone. If there's really something on my account, I'll ring the number on my card. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], your brokerage. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? I'm calling about the suitability review on your account ending [ACCOUNT_REF], it's a routine one, uh, flagged for this quarter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what review? A, uh, stability review? Of my account? I'm not sure I follow. And, ah, who exactly did you say you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Suitability, not stability. Um, so, it's a periodic check that your holdings still match the risk profile we have on file for you. And I'm with the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], that's the brokerage where you hold the account ending [ACCOUNT_REF]. It's required, so it does need to be completed this quarter, but I'm not asking you to buy or sell anything, there's no sales side to this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, suitability, I follow now. But I'll be honest, I haven't had a call like that from a brokerage before. Usually it's a form or a message through the portal. So, um, what exactly would you need from me on this call? And I'd also like to know how I can confirm you're actually who you say you are. I'd rather ring the number printed on my statement, or on the website, than just take your word for it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, that's fair, I'll note your objection on the file. And yeah, calling the number on your statement is fine by me, just ask for compliance and mention the review on the account ending [ACCOUNT_REF]. Uh, sorry, one second, someone's at my desk -- okay, back. So on what I'd need: nothing sensitive. I read you the holdings off my screen, the same ones on your statement, you confirm they look right, and I update your stated risk tolerance and time horizon. If you'd rather not do any of that by phone, I can send the questionnaire in writing and you complete it through the portal instead. Which would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Portal's fine. Send it in writing, and I'll ring the number on my statement if I have questions.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, writing it is. Uh, one thing I should clear up, you asked two turns back what I'd need from you. So, to be exact, nothing today. The questionnaire covers your risk tolerance, time horizon, that sort of thing, and you'd complete it in the portal, no calls needed. It goes to the email we have on file, and I'll note on the account that it was sent at your request. The quarter's review period closes in [CODE_1] days, so if it isn't done by then, the account gets restricted to closing trades only until it's completed. That's just how the policy works. Anything else you'd like me to note before I let you go?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, the dog's going at the door -- [PERSON_1], I'm still here. Right, so, one thing for the note. Restricted to closing trades if it isn't done in [CODE_1] days. I'd like to see that in writing too, in the same message, along with the policy reference. And I'm going to log in to the portal directly, not through any link. If the questionnaire isn't sitting there, I'll ring the number on my statement. Is that fine?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's fine, and I'll add it to the note. The restriction wording and the policy reference will go in the same message as the questionnaire, so you'll have both in writing. And yes, logging in directly is the right way to do it. There's no link you need to click on my end. If it isn't sitting in the portal, then ring the number on your statement, ask for compliance, and quote the account ending [ACCOUNT_REF]. Is there anything else you'd like on the file before I close this out?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I think that covers it. Oh, wait, one thing -- you said there's no *clink* I need to click, so, um, is this a different sort of portal from the one I normally use? Because I only use the one login, the one I've always used.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, same portal, same login you've always used. I said link, no link, and I just meant there's nothing in the email you'd need to click. Everything's behind your normal sign-in, so if you ever see a different address or a different login page, don't use it, and ring the number on your statement. Okay, so I've got the questionnaire going out in writing with the restriction wording and the policy reference, and a note on the file that you did this through the portal at your own request. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, that's everything. Although, uh, one correction for your note. You said it goes to the email you have on file, and I'd said I'd just check the portal. So please don't note that I asked for it by email, because I didn't. I said portal, and I'll log in directly. Right, thanks for the call, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, I'll correct that. Portal, not email, you'll log in directly. I'll put it down as portal, portal only, at your request. The questionnaire will be sitting there with the restriction wording and the policy reference, and if it isn't, you ring the number on your statement. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_2]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yep, so, okay, that's us done then. Sorry, just, um, just finishing the entry here -- right, it's saved. Enjoy the rest of your afternoon, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Thanks, you too. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Goodbye, [PERSON_2] -- and, uh, you'll see the questionnaire in the por--

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I heard. I'll check the portal myself, and if there's nothing there I'll ring the number on my statement. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Oh good, I'm so sorry to ring unannounced, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the tenancy deposit protection scheme, I'm a case handler there. Um, I'm ringing about a dispute that's been raised over the deposit at your address, and I'll try to be quick -- you're still there, yes? Sorry, I did say I'd emailed you about this yesterday, well, no, actually it went out in the post, I'm getting my own notes muddled, apologies.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, I'm still here, sorry. Um, I'm a bit lost, I'm afraid. You said you'd emailed me, and then it was the post instead? Which was it, sorry, because I haven't seen anything either way, and I'm not sure what dispute you mean.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, that's my muddle, it's the post. A letter went out yesterday, so it won't have reached you yet. It's a deposit dispute at your address, and there's a case reference on the letter. Still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hold on, the kettle's just clicked off and I've gone and... right, sorry, I'm back. Yes, still with you. So the letter's not come yet, no, nothing today. Um, a deposit dispute, you said? I'm sorry, I don't quite follow whose it is, I haven't got a landlord or a tenant that I know of, I mean, I'm not renting anything out. Who raised it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, there's someone at my desk -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Right. I'm so sorry, [PERSON_1], I think I should check something first, because if you're not renting and there's no landlord, then it's possible I've got the wrong person, and I'd hate to have worried you for nothing. Could you just confirm for me whether you're a tenant at, or have ever lived at, a shared property? Because the case I'm looking at involves a shared house, and I was asked to ring tenants there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, one second, there's a van reversing outside and it's beeping terribly, I can't quite hear myself. Right, it's stopped. Um, a shared house? Well, I did live in a shared place years ago, when I was younger, but that was ages back, I wouldn't have thought it'd still be, I mean, would a deposit still be going on after all that time? Sorry, I don't really understand how these things work.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a perfectly fair question, and I'm sorry, I should have explained it better from the start. Deposits aren't really "going on" for years, but a dispute can sometimes be raised well after the tenancy ended, and the scheme has to contact everyone who was named on the original tenancy, including people who moved out long ago. So it may be you're simply on the old record, and that's all it is. Um, and the reason I rang rather than just waiting for the letter is that, until both sides have been formally notified, we ask everyone to keep the details to themselves and not discuss it with the other tenants. That's not about hiding anything from you, it's a fairness rule, so nobody's account gets shaped by a conversation before they've seen the paperwork. And please don't just take my word for it, [PERSON_1]. The letter will have the case reference, you can check it on the scheme's official site at [URL_1], and if anything feels off, you can put the phone down and ring the number printed on the letter rather than any number I give you. Nothing's lost by waiting, I promise. Are you still with me? Sorry, I do keep asking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, don't be sorry, I'm still here, I just -- sorry, can I just stop you there, because you said not to talk to the other tenants, and I wouldn't even know how to, I haven't seen any of them in years, I wouldn't know where to start. Um, but the letter, that sounds sensible, I'll wait for that and ring the number on it. Is that all right? Or is there something you needed from me today, sorry?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's absolutely all right, and honestly it's the best thing to do. Nothing's needed from you today, [PERSON_1], I only wanted you to know it was coming. Um, and on the other tenants, sorry, I put that badly. It only means don't go chasing anyone up about it, and if you've lost touch with them all, there's nothing for you to do at all. Now, you asked me a minute ago whether it was email or post, and I gave you a muddle, so let me be clear, it's the letter only, nothing's been emailed, and if anything did turn up by email claiming to be about this, I'd ignore it and use the number on the letter. Is that all right? Sorry, I do hope I haven't made it sound worse than it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, you haven't made it sound worse, honestly, you've been very kind about it, and I'm sorry if I've been a bit slow on the uptake. It's just, I don't get many calls, and I'm not very good with these things, so when someone says dispute and deposit I go a bit, well, hot and cold. But that's all clear now. The letter's the only thing, nothing by email, and if something does turn up by email I'm to ignore it and ring the number printed on the letter. I'll make a note of that, I've got a pen here somewhere. Um, I did wonder, though, since you rang me and I didn't ring you, and I don't want to sound rude, is there something I should look for on the letter itself, so I know it's the right one? Only I'd hate to ring the wrong number by mistake, sorry. And I suppose if it doesn't come, say by the end of the week, I could just ring the scheme myself and ask for you, or would it be somebody else?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look for the case reference, it'll be printed at the top, and the scheme's name, [COMPANY_A]. Check that reference on [URL_1] and ring the number on the letter. If nothing's come by Friday, ring the main line and give them your address, anyone there can pull the case up, doesn't have to be me. Sorry, and thank you for being so patient with me, [PERSON_1], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh lovely, thank you, I've written that down now. Case reference at the top, the scheme's name, check it on the website, and ring the main line on Friday if nothing's come. Sorry for all the questions, and thank you for being so patient with me too. I'll keep an eye out for the post. Right, well, goodbye then, and take care, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? Hi, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the claims department at [COMPANY_A], the courier company. Sorry, one second, I've just got your file up here -- yes, so there's a parcel that's currently being held at our depot, and there's a small handling fee that needs to be settled before we can release it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, this is [PERSON_1], hang on, let me just, uh, put this trowel down. Sorry, I'm in the garden, you're on loudspeaker so if I sound a bit far away that's why. A parcel, oh that's interesting, I think I might be waiting on something actually. My sister said she was sending me, oh, what was it, some bulbs? Or was that last month? Anyway. What sort of parcel is it, do you know? And what's the fee for, exactly? I've never had one held before, I just usually get a card through the door.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, bulbs, uh, I mean I can't see the contents on my screen, it just says, hang on, it says general parcel, so I couldn't tell you what's inside. And the fee, it's a handling fee, [AMOUNT_1], it's because the, um, the label was incomplete when it came into the depot, so it got flagged. Sorry, you were asking about the card through the door, weren't you? That's usually only for a missed delivery, this is a bit different, it's a held item. So what we'd need to do is just settle that fee over the phone today, because after that it goes back into the queue and, well, it may get returned to the sender.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a cue? Sorry, did you say cue, like a queue? Hang on, no, you said it goes back in the queue, didn't you. Sorry, I thought you said it might get returned to the sender's, uh, sister, which would be funny because my sister is the sender, so she'd just get her own bulbs back! But right, so it's an incomplete label, that's a bit odd, because she's usually very careful with that stuff. Settle it over the phone, though, how would that work? I mean, I'm not sure I'm comfortable just paying something over the phone to someone I don't know, no offence. Is there a way I can check this is, you know, actually you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, none taken, that's, uh, that's fair. Um, so, the thing is, I can't really, hang on, I'd have to check what the verification process is for that, I don't have it in front of me. But honestly it's quite straightforward, it's just the one payment and then it's done. I mean, the sooner it's settled the better, because like I said, today's really the cut-off, or, well, it might be tomorrow, I'd have to look. Sorry, where were we, yes, so if you're happy to go ahead, I can just take you through it now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm, see, that's the bit that's bothering me a little. You said today's the cut-off, and then it might be tomorrow, and you can't tell me how I'd check you're really from the courier. It's not that I think you're up to anything, you sound perfectly nice, but I'd feel a lot better if I could ring the courier myself. Is there a number on the website, or, I don't know, on that card they usually put through the door? And do you have a reference number for the parcel, or a tracking number? Because my sister would've given me one, I'd think, and I could just look it up myself. Sorry, I'm probably being daft, I just don't like paying for things I can't see.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not being daft, uh, it's just, the reference number, hang on, I'll have to check where that is on here, it's not showing on this screen. I can, I can get back to you on that. But a number on the website, I mean, that'd just put you through to the general line, and they won't have the held items, that's, that's our department, so you'd be waiting a long time and the parcel might, you know, be gone by then. Sorry, I did say today, didn't I -- or tomorrow, whichever. It's just, it'd be a lot simpler if we sorted it now while I've got your file open.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, uh, hm. Right. Um, sorry, I'm just, I'm thinking out loud here, bear with me. It's just that every time I ask you something, how do I check, what's the reference, you sort of, well, you have to go and find it, and then it's today, or tomorrow, and I'd really rather not rush into this, you know? If it's my sister's parcel she can give me the tracking number, I'll ring her tonight, and if it's real I'll ring the courier on the number from their own website, and if the bulbs go back to her, well, they go back to her, she'll live. So I think I'll leave it there, but thanks ever so much for ringing, and, uh, have a lovely afternoon. Bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, right, okay. Well, I'll, um, I'll make a note on the file that you wanted to check first, I suppose. I will say it might, uh, it might take longer to sort out that way, but, yeah, that's, that's up to you. Sorry, I did, I'll have to check about the reference number and, um, anyway. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, you do that, thanks. And, oh, one thing, I did say my sister's sending bulbs, but actually, now I think about it, she might've said it was a book. Anyway, either way, I'll ring her tonight. Cheerio now, bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a book, right, yeah, that, uh, hang on, someone's just come up to my desk -- sorry -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Yes, so, a book, or bulbs, I mean, like I said, the screen only says general parcel, so it could be either, really. Anyway, ring your sister, that's fine, and, um, thanks for your time. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say someone's come up to your desk, or, no, hang on, I thought you said someone's run off with my sister? Ha, no, that can't be right, I've misheard again. Never mind! Right, I'll ring her tonight, and I'll sort it with the proper courier line. Thanks again, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a collections officer with [COMPANY_A], the local police force. I'm following up on the incident you reported last week, and I just need to confirm a few details to complete the file. Have you got a couple of minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh hello, yes, this is, uh, hang on, let me turn the trowel down -- sorry, I'm out in the garden, phone's on speaker. Wait, did you say a collections officer? Like, for a debt? I haven't got any debts, I don't think, unless it's that library thing from ages ago -- oh, but you said police, didn't you? And an incident I reported last week, hm, I can't think what that'd be, but go on, I've got a couple of minutes, the tomatoes can wait.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, not a debt, sorry, the job title throws people. It's an evidence and property role, nothing to do with money you owe. It was, uh, the report you made about the, the vehicle on [CITY_1] Road, I've got it here on screen, logged on the Monday. Actually, no, sorry, it'd have been the Tuesday you rang it in. Anyway, I just need to confirm your full name and date of birth against the file, and I'd ask you to keep the details of the open case to yourself for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the vehicle, right, hang on, I think I know the one -- except, hm, I don't think I rang anything in on a Tuesday, I'd have said it was more like the weekend? Or maybe I'm muddling it with the thing about the van by the allotments. Sorry, I do ramble. But you said Monday and then Tuesday, so which is it, because now I'm not sure we're talking about the same report at all. And, uh, this might sound daft, but if you've got it all on screen, why do you need me to tell you my name and date of birth? Shouldn't you already have that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and it's not daft. The date, Monday, Tuesday, it's logged one way and you may have rung it in another, so I won't argue it. And I have the name on screen, yes, but I confirm it against what you say to me before I go any further, that's the procedure. Name and date of birth against the file. That's all I need for now. Look, I'll note your objection on the file and carry on, but you're entitled to check me. The incident reference from your original report is [CODE_1], you'll have been given it when you reported. And you can ring the station's main number, ask for [PERSON_2] by name, and they'll put you through. If you'd rather, I can come out and do this in person, or send it by letter. Whichever you're comfortable with.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ooh, right, thank you, that's fair of you to say I can check. Um, can I just go back a bit, though? Earlier you said it was an evidence and property role, nothing to do with money, but you started by saying collections officer. So what is it you're actually collecting? Is it, like, something from me? Because I'm just a bit lost on why a property person is ringing me about a vehicle I reported, and I've still got my gloves on here, so I'm not going to go hunting for any reference number, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I'm not collecting anything from you. It's a title that sounds like something it isn't. It's about logging and tidying up the paperwork on a case so the file can be closed, that's the whole of it. And look, you're lost on why I'm ringing, and you've got gloves on, so let's not force it. Ring the station's main number, ask for [PERSON_2] by name, and check I'm who I say I am. Or I'll put it in a letter and you can reply when it suits you. There's no rush on your side.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's decent of you, a letter would be lovely, actually -- oh, shoo! Sorry, there's a blackbird going at my seedlings, cheeky thing, I've got half a tray of lettuces and he's eyeing them up like it's a buffet. Right, where was I. Yes, ring the station, I can do that, I'll just look the number up myself rather than use one you give me, if that's all right. And I'd rather you didn't take my name and date of birth just now, not till I've done that, no offence meant. So, um, a letter, sure, or I'll ring in, and then we'll see if there even is a report. Does that sound all right? I'll say thanks for your time, then, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's perfectly all right, and looking the number up yourself is the sensible way to do it. I'll note on the file that you'd rather verify first, so there's no -- right, I'll get a letter out to you, and if you ring in, just ask for [PERSON_2]. No offence taken at all. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], and enjoy the lettuces, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thanks, bye -- actually, sorry, one quick thing before you go, because it's just come back to me. Two minutes ago you said you'd put it in a letter, and I never gave you my address. So where would you be sending it? Is that on your screen too, or -- hm, I'm just wondering. Anyway, I'll ring the station like I said, so, thanks again, bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, yes, hello... am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I think there's a bit of a delay on the line, or maybe that's just me. This is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], in the compliance department. Is now an alright moment, or have I caught you at a bad time?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yeah, that's me. Sorry, I'm just out in the garden, you're on speaker... what's this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, that's perfectly fine, the garden, lovely... um, well, you know, it's a, it's a fairly routine enquiry, really. We're just going through some of our records at [COMPANY_A], making sure the contact details we hold are current and that we've, ah, got the right person on file. Would you mind just confirming for me that this is still the best number to reach you on, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the best number to reach me on? Yeah, I mean, this is it, this is the one you've just called, so, yeah. Oh, hang on, sorry, I'm pulling up weeds here, so, this number, you rang this number, it's fine. But what was it again, [COMPANY_A]? Is that the, um, do I have an account with you or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, good, that's, that's all I needed on the number, thank you. And, well, an account, uh, I wouldn't want to say yes or no without being, um... I mean, it's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it, because you should ask it. You're on our contact list, there's an enquiry reference against your name, [ACCOUNT_REF], and some of the people on that list were flagged for, well, for a particular review, which is really why I'm, why I'm ringing. Do you, do you have a moment to hear about it, or is the garden, is the garden calling?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, the garden can wait, it's not going anywhere. Um, but, sorry, flagged for a review? I don't, I mean, what sort of -- hang on. What kind of review? Because I'm still not sure what [COMPANY_A] even is, to me, you know? Is it a bank, or...?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, a bank, no, no, not a bank, and I'm glad you asked, because, um, it's an important distinction. We're an investment firm, [COMPANY_A], we manage funds. And the review, well, it's not a, a problem with you, I'd want to be very clear on that, it's more that, ah, a position has come up in one of our funds, [COMPANY_B], and a small number of people on the list are being offered it before it closes. I'm sorry, you said you weren't sure what we are, is that, did you say you weren't sure whether you had an account with the bank? Because I can, I can certainly go into how we, how we handle that sort of thing, if that's the worry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, I never said anything about a bank account, I asked whether it was a bank, there's a difference, I think? Anyway. Wait, you said compliance department at the start, and now it's, what, a fund you're offering me a position in? That's, um, that's not really a records check, is it? That sounds more like sales. And I'm still not sure why you've got me on a list, I don't, I don't think I've ever invested anything with anybody.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're right, you did ask whether it was a bank, I, I misspoke, and that's a fair catch, and I'm glad you caught it. And yes, I, I take the point about the compliance side, it's... well, it does sit between the two, if I'm honest, the two functions overlap a little in how we, ah, how we reach out. As to why you're on the list, I'd, I'd want to be careful there, I can't really go into how names come to be on it, that's not something I'm able to, to open up over the phone. What I can say is that the position in [COMPANY_B] closes today, and it's, well, the return profile is, is really quite unusual, which is why I'd rather you heard it from me than, than missed it. Would you want me to take you through the figures, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a blackbird going absolutely mad at my compost heap, shoo, go on... sorry. Right, um, no, I don't think I want the figures. It started as a records check, then it was compliance, now it's a fund that closes today and you can't tell me how I got on your list? That doesn't add up for me, and I've never invested in anything, so I'm just not going to do it over the phone, sorry. If [COMPANY_A] wants to write to me, fine, but I'll leave it there. Thanks for calling, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Hello, hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A] over in [CITY_1], I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment. Can you hear me okay? It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, yeah, yeah, I can hear you, I just, I was just having a lie-down, sorry. Who is it? Who did you say you were? I heard, was it a company, [COMPANY_something]? Sorry, who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I've woken you up, haven't I? Honestly, go back to your lie-down if you like, I can ring another time. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the shop over in [CITY_1]. And no, no, it's not a sale, you said something about a sale? Ha, no, nothing like that. It's good news, actually, quite small good news, but it's from the little draw we ran at the event a while back. Is now alright to chat for a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A draw? Uh, I don't remember any draw. I didn't say sale, I don't think. Go on then, what's the good news.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you didn't, that was me getting ahead of myself, sorry. It was the [COMPANY_A] stand at the [CITY_1] community fair, and you'd have popped your name and number on a little raffle slip. Probably a while ago now, so it's no wonder it's slipped your mind. Anyway, your slip came up for one of the smaller prizes, a little hamper, nothing grand, and there's nothing to pay or anything like that, you'd just pop into the shop and collect it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A fair? Hm. I mean, I go to the fair sometimes, there's usually a fella with the tombola and the, the cakes, my sister always does the cakes. But I don't, I can't say I remember a raffle slip. I probably put my name on something, I do that, and then I get the, the leaflets through the door. Why's it taken so long, if it was a while ago? And how'd you get this number, was it on the slip? Sorry, I'm still sort of waking up here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's a fair question, and don't apologise, I'd be asking the same thing. Yes, the number came straight off your slip, that's the only place I've got it. And it's taken a while because we had a bit of a backlog after the fair, a few of the prizes sat in the back room longer than they should have, that's on us. Look, I'd say don't take my word for it, you're half asleep and a stranger's ringing you up, so if you'd rather look the shop up yourself and ring us back, that's absolutely fine by me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's, that's fair enough of you to say. Look it up. Hm. I'm not very good with the, the looking things up, my nephew usually does that, he set up the little, the tablet thing. But I could, I suppose. Is there a number I'd ring? Or would I just, I don't know, go in? Because if it's only a hamper and I just collect it, I'd not need to give you anything now, would I? You're not wanting anything off me on the phone?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nothing at all, you don't need to give me a thing on the phone, that's the whole point. Sorry, one second, [PERSON_3], can you pop that on the shelf, thanks -- sorry, we've had a delivery land right in the middle of the shop. Right, where was I? Oh, yes. So just go in, and it was the stand at the [CITY_1] community fair, so I could tell you the date as well if it helps jog your memory. If you'd sooner ring first, don't use a number from me, get your nephew to look up [COMPANY_A] and use whatever number he finds.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, okay, that's, yeah, that sounds sensible, I'll get my nephew to have a look when he's round. Sorry, you said it was a, a raffle slip earlier, but then now you've called it a draw? Or I think you did. And the date, no, don't bother with the date, it'll only muddle me more, I can't even tell you what day it is today. I'll, I'll see if I can find it. Right, well, thank you for ringing, I'll, I'll have a think. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's just me being loose with my words, same thing really, the raffle slip is what went in the draw. Sorry, I do ramble. And you're right, no rush at all, have a think. When your nephew's round, get him to look up the shop and ring us on whatever number he finds. We're open most days, and whoever picks up can find your name on the winners list. No hurry on the hamper either. Right, I'll leave you to your lie-down. Thanks for putting up with me, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, my nephew, I'll get my nephew to look it up, like you said. He's round on, well, I couldn't tell you, Thursday maybe. And I'll not use a number from you, I'll use the one he finds. Yes. Thanks for ringing, then. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Lovely, that's exactly right, Thursday, whenever he's round, no rush at all. Oh, hang on, sorry, that's the kettle going in the back, one second -- right, I've switched it off, where was I? Yes, the number he finds, that's the one to use. And if it helps, just tell whoever answers the shop that [PERSON_2] rang about the fair draw. Take care of yourself, [PERSON_1], and enjoy the rest of your lie-down. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, [PERSON_2], about the fair, the draw, I'll tell them. And the number from my nephew, not from you, I've got that. Thursday, he's round Thursday. Well, thanks for ringing then, goodbye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yes, that's the one, [PERSON_2] about the fair draw, you've got it all. And uh, well, like I said, no hurry, whenever suits you. Right, I'll let you go then. Bye now, bye, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I'll, no, I'll let the nephew, well, I'll just, yes. Bye now, take care yourself, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh wonderful, it's [PERSON_2] calling from customer care at [COMPANY_A], and how are you doing today? Not catching you at a bad time, am I?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh... hello? Yes, this is, um, yes, speaking. No no, not a bad time at all, I'm just, you know, at home, nothing much on. Sorry, I didn't quite catch that, where did you say you were calling from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah no worries at all, it's a bad line, I get that a lot! Customer care at [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency, [PERSON_2] speaking. And you said you're at home with nothing on, lovely, lovely, because honestly I wish I could say the same, it's been one of those weeks where the phones just haven't stopped. Anyway, I've got some really good news for you, [PERSON_1], I just need to be sure I've got the right person first, are you still living in the [CITY_1] area?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, a promotions agency, right, sorry, I'm not sure I quite follow, but, well, good news, that's nice, isn't it? Um... and yes, yes, I'm still in [CITY_1], sort of, I mean, that's where I am, yes. Sorry, was there something I'd, uh, won, or...? I'm a bit lost, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, don't apologise, you're not lost at all, I'm the one rambling! So yes, you've, well, you've been selected as a winner in our regional draw, the one for [CITY_1] and, uh, the surrounding area. And before you say anything, I know, I know, most people don't remember entering, that's totally normal, it's usually from a form or a survey, something you filled in months ago and, I mean, who keeps track of those? The thing is, the prize has to be claimed by end of day tomorrow or it goes back into the pool, so I just want to get you sorted quickly. Can I just confirm your full name and date of birth for the file?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh my goodness, a winner, well, that's, uh, that's lovely, I never win anything. But, sorry, I honestly don't remember filling in any form, I mean, I might have, I don't know. Um, why do you need my date of birth, though? I'm just a bit, well, you've not said what the prize is yet, and I don't really know who you are, sorry, is there a way I could check this is, you know, properly from [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's a fair question, honestly, you're being sensible, and you'd be amazed how many people just say yes to anything! Anyway, the prize is [AMOUNT_1] in cash, plus a little bonus on top, and look, the date of birth is only so I know I'm talking to the actual winner and not someone else in the house, it's just the one thing, that's all. As for checking, you can look us up any time, but the thing is the clock really is ticking, [PERSON_1], and I'd hate for you to lose it over a bit of paperwork. Now, are you right-handed or left-handed, out of curiosity? No, I'm joking, I'm joking, just, can I take that date of birth and we'll get this wrapped up for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, that one's a funny question, uh, right-handed, I suppose. But, sorry, [AMOUNT_1], that's quite a lot of money, isn't it? And you still haven't really told me how I'd, um, check it's real, you just said I could look you up, and I'm not very good with the computer, I wouldn't know where to start. I'm not trying to be difficult, honestly. Could I maybe ring you back on a number from the, from the company's own website, or... would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, of course, you ring whoever you like, I'd never want you feeling rushed, that's, um, that's not how we do things here. Mm, the only thing is, and I'm just being straight with you, the lines on the main switchboard are all through to the general queue, so you'd be sat on hold forever, and it's end of day tomorrow, remember, so, yeah. Honestly, [PERSON_1], I've done hundreds of these and the people who just tick it off now are always so glad they did, it's really only the date of birth, that's all I need. I can hear you're a lovely, careful person, so, shall we just do that together, right now, and get you your [AMOUNT_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's very kind of you to say, but, um, I think I'd still rather ring the company myself, if that's all right. I did ask, sorry, about ringing back on a number from their own website, and, well, you said the lines are busy, but I don't mind waiting on hold, honestly, I've nothing on. And I'm a bit, I'm not comfortable giving my date of birth to someone I can't check, I'm sorry, I know you've been very nice about it. So I think I'll do that, I'll ring them, and if it's real, it's real. Thank you for calling, anyway, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the club. Sorry, long day, I've been ringing round all afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], hi! Sorry, you caught me out in the garden, I've got you on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in compost here. Um... the club, did you say? Which, uh, which club is that, sorry -- I'm a member of a couple of things, so, yeah, remind me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, that's fair enough, easy to get mixed up. Um, it's [COMPANY_A], the community sports club, your little one's on the junior team, yeah? Anyway, how's the garden going, are you getting any of this rain, because honestly, we've had buckets over here, and, well, that's sort of why I'm ringing, actually.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the junior team, right, yes, okay, that rings a bell, I think. Gosh, the rain, no, we've been lucky, it's been properly lovely here, bit dry actually, I've been out with the watering can every evening, and today I'm finally getting the tomatoes in, which is late, I know, everyone else did theirs weeks ago. Honestly my back's killing me already. So, uh, what's the rain got to do with it, is the pitch flooded or something? Is training off?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, tomatoes in June, you're fine, honestly, mine always go in late and they still come good. Sorry, hang on, [PERSON_3]'s just dropped a whole bag of cones in the corridor, I can hear it all rolling about -- right, where was I? Yes, the pitch. It's not training, it's Saturday's match, the home pitch is properly waterlogged, so it's been moved to a different pitch and the kick-off time's changed as well.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, poor cones, that's a proper racket, I can almost hear it. Right, so Saturday's match, moved pitch, new kick-off, okay. Hang on though, you said at the start I'm a member of the club, but, um, I'm not sure that's quite right, I think it's my sister's lad who plays on the junior team, not mine. Or, hmm, maybe I'm thinking of the other club, I do get them mixed up. Anyway, where's it moved to and what's the new time? I'll need to write it down, well, I'll need to find a pen that's not covered in soil first.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no worries at all, find your pen, I'll wait, there's no rush on my end. And actually, hang on, that's a fair point, I've been working off the parent contact list and I may have just assumed you were the dad, so that's on me. If it's your sister's lad on the team, then the number on my list might be down as yours for some reason, maybe she put you as the backup contact, which loads of people do, because then there's always someone who can get hold of the family if one phone's dead. It's honestly not a problem, it just means we both did the sensible thing, you picked up and I rang round, and the message still needs to get to her either way. Right, so, the details: it's [CITY_1] Park, the second pitch, the one round the back by the pavilion, and kick-off's moved to [CODE_1] instead of the usual time, so a bit later, which gives the ground a bit longer to dry out. Would you be all right passing that on to your sister, or would it be easier if I got her number off you and rang her myself?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, got the pen, sort of, it's a bit muddy but it writes, um... right, so [CITY_1] Park, second pitch, round the back by the pavilion, and kick-off's later, yep. Ha, sorry, I didn't catch the time, it came out a bit garbled, you said something like... I don't know, it sounded like a code or something, so can you say that again? Oh, and yeah, I'm happy to pass it on to her, she'd probably prefer that to a stranger ringing, no offence, but I'm not going to hand out her number, I wouldn't feel right doing that without asking her. Uh, so it's the second pitch, is that right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, sorry, that's on my end, the line's gone a bit crackly, I think [PERSON_3] has the corridor door open again. Yes, second pitch, round the back by the pavilion, you've got it spot on. And the time, it's [CODE_1], so about an hour later than usual, which is what I meant to say, so I'll make sure it goes out properly in the club message tonight as well. And honestly, you're quite right about your sister's number, no offence taken at all, I'd far rather you ask her than hand it over. Just tell her it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], and if she's got any questions she can ring the club on [PHONE_1], right, I'll let you get back to your tomatoes, thanks so much, [PERSON_1], and good luck with the back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, lovely, thanks, um... yeah, so, second pitch round the back, about an hour later than usual, got it, I've written it on the back of my hand actually, which is about as organised as I get out here. Uh, hang on, so, right, I'll pass that on to my sister tonight, and she can ring the club on, uh, that number if she's got any questions. Well, you've been very nice about the whole mix-up, so, yeah, thanks for ringing, and good luck with the cones, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier. Uh, am I speaking with the account holder? I do need to be upfront, we've found two meter readings on file that don't match, and I'd like to get that sorted before our billing run closes today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, depends who's asking, really. You said [COMPANY_A], right? Which meter are we talking about, electricity or gas? And what are the two readings that don't match?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair questions, and, uh, yes, [COMPANY_A], account services. It's the electricity meter. Our records show one reading from the last bill and a second one logged later that's lower than the first, which shouldn't happen, and I'll be honest, that mismatch is on our side, not yours. I'd rather not read figures out over the phone, though, since I haven't confirmed who I'm speaking with. All I'd need from you is the current figure on the meter, nothing else, and, um, we do want that in before today's billing run closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the bill's gone up on the meter? No, hang on, you said lower. Okay. So the reading's lower than before, which can't happen, fine. But you won't tell me what your readings are, and you haven't confirmed who I am either, so you've got me down as the account holder without a name. What name have you got on the account?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, lower, that's right. And no, I can't give you a name either, that's the verification procedure, I'm not permitted to disclose account details before the account holder is confirmed. Look, you don't have to do this now. Log into your account at [URL_1], check the readings there, and ring us back on [PHONE_1], and we won't change anything until you have.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but hang on, you rang me. You're the one who wants a -- Okay, so I'm not logging into anything off a link you've read me down the phone. If I check, I'll go to the site myself, or ring the number that's printed on an actual bill. Not yours. And you've got the billing run closing today, but also nothing changes till I ring back. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's the right instinct, ignore the link, go to the site yourself or use the number on your bill. And you're right about the two things, that was sloppy. Today's run is just when I'd like it in, but nothing gets changed or billed until you've checked and given us the figure. Sorry, hang on, someone's just put a -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Where was I? Right, so there's no deadline on your side, the bill simply stays as it is until you ring.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Right. So no deadline, bill stays as it is. Well, that's, uh... that's a fairly different call from the one I picked up a minute ago, isn't it? I mean, first it's the billing run closing today, now it's nothing happens till I ring. So I'll do what I said. I'll find the number on an actual bill, ring that, and if there's a mismatch they can tell me about it. Okay? Thanks for the call. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, yes, so, as I said, nothing is -- no, hang on. You're quite right, and honestly I'd do exactly the same. That cutoff was an internal target of mine, not a deadline on you, I should have put it better at the start. Ring the number on your bill, quote [ACCOUNT_REF] if you want, and they'll see the two readings on file. Sorry for the muddle, and, um, thanks for bearing with me. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, quote what? A [ACCOUNT_REF], did you say, or was that, uh, a reference number off the bill? Hang on, I haven't got a bill in front of me, so no, I'll just ring the number on it myself and take it from there. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [ACCOUNT_REF] is just the account reference printed at the top of your bill. You don't need it, and you don't need to tell me anything now, they can find you by name and address. Ring the number on the bill, and if you're not happy once they've gone through the readings with you, it's your right to ask for it in writing. Sorry again for the confusion, and thanks for your patience. Have a good afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Will do. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good morning, uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1], the parent or guardian of [PERSON_2]? Sorry, I should say first, my name is [PERSON_3], and I'm the compliance officer at [COMPANY_A], that's the school office, and I'm only calling because the register this morning shows [PERSON_2] as absent, and, well, I wanted to understand how that came to be recorded that way, because it may simply be a misunderstanding on our side, I really don't want to presume anything. It's nothing alarming, but, um, these things do tend to need tidying up reasonably soon, so I thought a quick call would be the kindest way to go about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Good morning. Uh, before I confirm anything, could you tell me which school you're calling from, exactly? You've said [COMPANY_A], but I'd like the actual name. And "compliance officer" is a slightly odd title for someone ringing about a register, so what's your role there, precisely? I'm not saying anything's wrong, I'd just like to know who I'm speaking to before I discuss my child's attendance.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, uh, that's a perfectly sensible thing to ask, and honestly I'd rather you asked it than not, because a parent who doesn't ask is, well, a little worrying in its own way. So, um, the school is [COMPANY_A], that's the name on the front of the building, and the office number you'd find on any of the letters home is [PHONE_1], so you're very welcome to ring that and ask for me by name, I wouldn't mind in the slightest. As for the title, yes, it's a bit grand, I know, it's really that I look after the attendance records and make sure they're accurate, so, uh, I'm not the person who marked the register, I'm the person who checks it afterwards. Does that, um, does that make a bit more sense?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, I've got the kettle going and it's just, uh, there. Right. Yes, that does make a bit more sense, thank you. But you've just said the name on the front of the building and given me a number from the letters, and neither of those tells me anything I couldn't have looked up. So here's what I'd do. I'll ring the school on the number I already have, not the one you've just read out, and ask for you by name. Or, alternatively, tell me what time the register was taken this morning and what the absence was recorded as, and I can check that against what I know about my child's day. Which would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I'd, uh -- no, I'd much rather you rang the number you already have, honestly, that's the sensible way round, and I'd think less of myself if I tried to talk you out of it. If you ask the front desk for [PERSON_3] in the attendance side of things, they'll put you through, or, um, if I'm away from my desk they'll take a message and I'll ring you straight back. As for the register itself, I could tell you what time it was taken and how it was marked, but, I mean -- actually, no, better that you hear it from the office directly, because that's the record you'd want to trust. And, uh, it'd be good to sort it out before the end of the day if that's at all convenient, though please don't feel rushed on my account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, that's, uh, a reasonable answer, thank you. Though, can I go back to something you said two turns ago? You described the title as a bit grand and said you look after the attendance records and check them afterwards. But you opened by saying you wanted to understand how the absence came to be recorded that way. Recorded how, exactly? Was my child marked absent without a reason, or marked as having a particular reason? Because those are quite different things, and I'd like to know what I'm walking into when I ring the office.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, uh, no, you're quite right to pick me up on that, I wasn't clear. Marked, um, marked as absent with no reason against it, that's all, nothing more than that, so it isn't a case of anyone recording a particular excuse. And, uh, I should say I wouldn't call it, what was it, a trauma or anything like that, I do hope it didn't come across that way, it's really just a blank in the box where a reason would normally go. Sorry, that's, I think I've gone off at a tangent, I thought you'd asked how it affected [PERSON_2], but, no, you asked what was written. So, yes. Absent, no reason recorded, and that's the whole of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, that's, uh, a bit of an odd thing to have wandered into, because I never said anything about trauma, and I'm not sure why you'd bring it up. Blank reason, fine, that's simple enough. And no, I'm not going to confirm anything further on this call, including whether I'm [PERSON_1] or what my child's day looks like. If there's a genuine query, the office can ring me on the number they hold, or I'll ring them on the one I've got. I'll take it from there. Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's -- yes, you're right, I did say that, and I can't honestly tell you why. I think I was answering a question you hadn't asked, which is, well, not very tidy of me. And you're entirely right not to confirm anything on a call you didn't expect. I'd far rather you rang the office on the number you hold and asked for me by name. It's just a blank in the register, and I'm sure it will be cleared up in a minute or two once you've spoken to them. Thank you for being so careful, it's what I'd want from any parent. Goodbye, and, uh, I hope the rest of the day goes smoothly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'll -- no, let me put it differently. I'll ring the school myself, on the number I already hold, and if nobody there has heard of you, or of any query, then that, uh, tells me what I need to know. Until then I've nothing more to say on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, did you say nobody's heard of the quiry? Because I'd have thought -- no, it's not that it's urgent, it's just that, well, if you ring and the office says it's already been dealt with, then that's, that's perfectly fine too. And, um, I'd be glad if you did ring, honestly, I'd think better of everyone involved. So, yes, please do. Thank you for your patience, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say quiche? No, uh, hang on, query. Right. I think I heard "already been dealt with" and that's a bit odd, isn't it, because a minute ago it was a blank in the register that needed tidying up, and now it might be dealt with already? utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, I'm still here, I'm just, well, you went a bit fast for me there. Just my name, or more than that?

utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: Uh, yes, I can hear you fine, sorry, I was just -- yes. This is [PERSON_1] speaking. Now, which order is this, exactly? I'm not sure I've placed one with [COMPANY_A] recently, so, um, could you tell me what's on it and when it was placed?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's a perfectly fair thing to ask, and I'd much rather you ask than just take my word for it. Sorry, one second, someone's just come to my desk -- yes, I'll be there in a moment -- sorry about that. So, the order was placed through our website, and what I can see here is that it's a standard grocery order, a two-hour delivery window, and one item on it has been swapped for a similar product. Beyond that, I'd rather not read the full list out over the phone until you've had a chance to think about whether it sounds like yours.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to stop you there, because that's actually the wrong way round. You're the one who's rung me, so it's for you to establish the order, not for me to decide whether it sounds like mine. "A standard grocery order" doesn't tell me anything. What's the order reference, what was the total, and what was the item that got substituted?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, no, that's fair, you're absolutely right to push on that, and I'd rather you did. Sorry, you said the order, uh, the order reference -- and the total, and the substituted item. Yes. So the substitution is, um, it's a like-for-like swap, same kind of product, different brand, which is why I'm ringing, because we ask for a yes or no before it goes out. Now, the reference, I'm afraid, is held on the order system and I've only got the summary in front of me, and the total, I mean, I wouldn't want to quote you a figure I couldn't stand behind.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- sorry, let me just make sure I've got this. You've rung me about an order, you can't give me the reference, you can't give me the total, and, well, you haven't actually named the item that's supposed to be swapped, have you? You said "a similar product", which, I mean, that's not a product. So what I've got so far is, uh, nothing I can check. Can you at least tell me what the original item was, and what the, the replacement is?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, I do see that, and I'm glad you're pressing me on it, because it's a sensible thing to want. Sorry, you said the original item, and what it's been, um, replaced with -- yes. Now, what I've got on my screen is the, uh, the basket summary, not the line-by-line, and I wouldn't want to guess at a product name and have you say yes to the wrong thing. Is it, sorry, is it the delivery window you're worried about? Because that's confirmed, that's the two hours, and, well, I'd rather have an answer on the swap before it goes out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, there's somebody at the door -- no, it's fine, it's just a courier, they're leaving it on the step. Right, where was I. No, the delivery window isn't what I'm worried about. What I'm worried about is that you've now told me you can see the order, but you can't see a single line of it, and you want a yes or no from me on something you can't name. Nobody can ask me to approve a substitution without telling me what's being substituted. So here's what I'll do. I'll look at my own account, and if there's an order there, I'll deal with it through the app or the number on the website. Not this call. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, please, sorry -- before you go, because you're right, and I can't answer that from the summary I've got. I don't have the line-by-line in front of me, and I'd sooner find out properly than keep guessing. So let me go back to the order team, get the reference and the item names, and ring you back with those, and you can check them against your own account at the same time. And if you'd rather not take another call, that's, well, entirely up to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'd rather you didn't ring back, sorry. I'll check my own account, through the app, like I said. If there's an order there, I'll deal with it that way. Not on a call someone else starts. And if there's nothing there, then, well, that tells me something too. So, yes, I'll check it myself, through the app. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], I'm the regional supervisor, I came round last week and went over the bathroom tiling with you. Just ringing to recap the quote before we get you booked in, you got a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, speaking. Sorry, though -- I'm fairly sure nobody came round last week, I think it was a phone conversation, maybe, about the tiling? Which company did you say again, and what's the quote you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, right, well -- visit, call, whichever, I'm the one who did the survey, so I'm not sure why that's -- look, it's [COMPANY_A], [PERSON_2], regional supervisor, and the quote's for the bathroom tiling, the floor and the wall surround, that's [AMOUNT_1] all in, same as it's been on file since the walkthrough. Honestly I'd have thought this was all fresh in your mind by now, it's only been a week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, it isn't fresh, because I don't recall a walkthrough. Can you tell me the reference on the quote, please?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The reference, yeah, sure, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], that's on the paperwork I sent over. Sorry, did you say a refund? No, no, nobody's talking about a refund, this is just the quote, nothing's been paid. Look, I'm not sure why you're being so difficult about this, I've got your job down here as agreed and I'm only asking if you want to pick a start date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say refund, I said -- no. Sorry, let me start again. I haven't received any paperwork, so that reference doesn't, it doesn't mean anything to me. And I'd, uh, I'd rather not pick a start date for a job I can't remember agreeing to. If you're from the company, what address did you visit, or what's the phone number on the paperwork? Because those are things you'd have on file.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the paperwork's gone missing? Well, that's a postal thing, I can't help what the post does, and it's not a reason to hold up the job. Look, the address is on file, the phone number's on file, I don't read that stuff out over the phone, that's internal procedure. I'd have thought if you'd had a surveyor in your bathroom you'd remember it, so I'm honestly not sure what the hesitation is here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I want to go back a bit. Two turns ago you said it's only been a week, and that the quote's been on file since the walkthrough. But if you did a walkthrough, you'd have been in my bathroom, so what exactly did you measure, or look at? And I did not say the paperwork went missing, I said I never received any. That's not quite the same thing. Also, you said nothing's been paid, so is there a deposit involved at some point? Because if so, I'd want that in writing before anything else.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, look, I measured the floor and the wall surround, the usual, it's all in the survey notes. And I keep saying, nobody's asked you for money, I'm only asking if you want a start date, that's all I'm asking. Fine, a deposit would be on the written quote, obviously, nothing's taken over the phone, that's, that's just how we do it. But honestly, if you've got no memory of any of this, maybe the simplest thing is I check my notes and ring you back, because I'm clearly not getting anywhere like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, there's a delivery van reversing outside and I couldn't hear you for a moment. Right. You'd ring me back, is that it? Well, no, I'd rather you didn't. If I haven't agreed to a job, there's nothing to ring me back about. If I did request one, then I'll find the company's contact details myself and call them, and I'll ask for the reference you gave me. Which, by the way, you've still not given me a name I can verify, so, no. I won't be booking a start date on this call. Thanks, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, [PERSON_3], not there, round the side! Sorry, that's one of the lads, we've got a lorry on site. Right, so, look, that's your call, I'm not going to chase you, but I'll say it was a bit much to question my good faith when all I did was ring about your own quote. Fine. You've got my name, [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A], so if you do find the paperwork, ring the office and we'll take it from there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I wasn't questioning your good faith, I was asking for details I couldn't place. If I find any paperwork, I'll contact the company directly through its published number. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, just so I've got it right, two turns back you said you'd find the company's contact details yourself and ask for the reference. That's [ACCOUNT_REF], yes? Because if you do ring the office and they've got nothing under it, that's a different matter and I'd want to know. I'm not trying to be awkward, I just don't like loose ends. Right, well, that's us then. Take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, that's the, no, wait. I'm not confirming a reference with you. You gave it, I haven't verified it, and that's all it is as far as I'm concerned. If I ring, I'll say what I've got and they can tell me whether it exists. Anyway, that's us done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, yes, hi. Is this -- sorry, am I speaking to [PERSON_1]? I'm, um, I'm actually calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the energy supplier, and I -- no, let me start again. It's about your meter readings, there's a, a mismatch, and I was asked to ring you about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, this is -- sorry, the signal's terrible, I'm driving, you're on speaker. A mismatch? Sorry, who did you say you were with again? Because I'm sure I haven't had a meter reading go in this year, I mean I haven't touched it, so I don't see how there'd be a mismatch, unless -- well, I did send one in last week, I think. Or was that the water? Sorry, I'm rambling.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, um. I'm ringing for [COMPANY_A], well, for someone there, I'm just passing it on. They've got two readings that don't match their own records, and, uh, I don't think it's anything you did wrong. Maybe don't talk and drive though, I can call back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, it's fine, I'm just on the ring road, it's only slow. Um, so, uh, hang on, sorry. Who's the someone, though? Like, is it a person there, or, I mean, is it the billing department? Because I don't want to say anything wrong, and you said you're just passing it on, so, um, I'm not sure what you want me to do?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's, um, [PERSON_2], in the billing team at [COMPANY_A]. I'm only the go-between, so I don't know much more than what she wrote down. What she'd like is for you to read me the current figure off the meter, just that number, and then she can correct the bill. And, uh, I should say, I don't need your date of birth or bank details or anything like that. Just the meter figure. Actually, wait, that's not quite right, sorry. She did ask me to confirm your address first, so, um, could you give me that? No, hang on, I think she already has it. I've, I've muddled my notes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Um. Right, so, uh, sorry, give me a second, I'm just -- there's a van. Okay. So you, you don't know if you need my address or not? Because that's, I mean, that's sort of the bit that's making me a bit nervous, sorry, no offence. Um, if she's the one who needs it, couldn't she just ring me herself? Or, or, is there a number I could ring back on, like one that's on my bill? Because I, I'm not at the meter anyway, I'm in the car, so I couldn't read it out even if I, uh, wanted to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, none taken, that's fair, I'd be nervous too. Um, two turns ago, when I said the address thing, that was me getting my notes wrong. She's already got your address, I shouldn't have asked, so please forget I said it. Honestly I feel a bit daft now. I'm only trying to help here. And yes, ring back, please do. Use the number on your bill, or log into your account online and look at the readings it shows, that way you can check the mismatch is real before you change anything. The two readings she's got, one's the figure from your last online submission and the other's from the, uh, estimated read, and they don't line up, that's all it is. And if she's the one you'd rather speak to, ask for [PERSON_2] in billing and quote [ACCOUNT_REF].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay. Okay, that's, uh, that's actually a relief, sorry. So I ring the number on my bill, not one you give me, and I can check the readings online first. That, that sounds sensible. I mean, I'm not saying you're not who you say, I just, I'd rather do it that way, if that's all right? I'll look when I'm home, I'm not going to do it while I'm driving, obviously. Um, thanks for not, you know, pushing me. Right, so I'll, I'll sort it that way. Sorry for being a bother. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, you're not a bother at all, honestly, you did exactly the right thing. I'd much rather you checked than just took my word for it, because, well, there are people who ring up pretending to be from suppliers, and I'd hate you to think I was one of them. So, um, yes, ring the number on your bill, not any number I'd give you, and have a look at the readings online when you're home. And if the figures it shows don't match what I said, then you'll know something's off, and you can tell [PERSON_2] that too. Sorry again for muddling my notes earlier, with the address. I get, I get a bit flustered on the phone, it's not really my sort of thing. I was only asked to pass it on because, uh, [PERSON_2] was tied up. Anyway, there's no hurry, it'll keep till you're home. Drive safe, and, um, thank you for being so patient with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, will do, thank you. Oh, um, sorry, one small thing -- you said the other reading was from the estimated read, but earlier you said both were off her records, so I'm a bit lost on which is which. Not that it matters, I'll just have a look online and ring the number on my bill. Sorry, I'm picky about it, I know. Okay, thanks for ringing, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're not picky, that's, uh, that's a fair catch, and it's my fault, I said it badly. What I meant was, both readings are ones [COMPANY_A] has on file, so I said they're off her records, but they don't agree with each other. One's from your online submission and the other's an estimate they put in themselves. So, um, it's their own two figures that clash, not anything you've done. I should've just said that the first time, sorry. And look, if it helps, [PERSON_2] can tell you the date of your last submission, that's on your account, so if she gets it right when you ring the number on your bill, you'll know she's genuine. Anyway, yes, have a look online, and, um, thank you, really. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, that makes sense. I'll look online when I'm home and ring the number on the bill. Thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good, yes, that's, uh, that's all I wanted. Online first, then the number on your bill, and ask for [PERSON_2] in billing, with [ACCOUNT_REF]. Sorry, I said that already. And she'll tell you your last submission date, that's how you'll know it's really her. Right, um, thank you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, no, I've got it, sorry. Online first, then the number on my bill. Right. Thanks for ringing, then. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2] from account services at [COMPANY_A], your home internet provider. I'm calling about an urgent fault we've detected on your line, and I do need to get this sorted before our technician window closes at four o'clock today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Speaking, yes. Uh, sorry, could you say that company name again? I didn't quite catch which provider you said. And when you say a fault you've detected on my line, what sort of fault, specifically? Because I haven't noticed any problem with the connection.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [COMPANY_A], your home internet provider. And, uh, sorry, hang on one second -- [PERSON_3], I said put that on my desk, not -- sorry about that. Right. So the fault is a signal integrity issue on your line, it won't always show up on your end yet, which is why most customers haven't noticed anything. But it does get flagged on our side as urgent, and the technician window closes at four, so I do need to confirm a few details on the account with you now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you've said the company name again as if I'd heard it, and I'm telling you I haven't caught it. Which company, exactly? Spell it for me, please. And the fault, a signal integrity issue that doesn't show up on my end. How was that detected, then? Because if I'm not seeing anything, I'd like to know what you're seeing, and from where.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, I said [COMPANY_A], I'm not going to spell it out, that's the name on your account, sir, or ma'am, sorry. And the detection comes from our network monitoring, it's automated, I can't walk you through the technical side on this call. What I can tell you is the fault is flagged urgent and the technician window closes at four o'clock. So if I could just confirm a few details on the account, we can get you booked in before that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you won't tell me the company name, and you can't explain how the fault was detected. And in the same breath you're asking me to confirm account details. I'm sorry, but that's the wrong way round. If you're genuinely with my provider, you already have the account, so there's nothing for me to confirm to you. What do you need from me, exactly? And what's a reference number I could quote if I phone the provider myself, on the number printed on my bill?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, I understand, but I'm not able to issue a reference number on an outbound call, that's not how the process works. The fault is logged against your account, and the technician window closes at four, so if you hang up and call in, you'll be starting from scratch with a different department, and I can't guarantee the slot will still be there. All I need is a quick verification so I can get you booked in, and I'd also need to take a brief look at your connection from my end. That's standard procedure for a line fault.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm going to stop you there. Earlier you said this was a signal integrity issue on the line, and now it's something you need to look at on my connection from your end. Those aren't the same thing. And a quick look at my connection, meaning what, exactly? Me letting you onto my machine? Because that's not happening on an inbound call. I'll ring the number on my bill, and if there's a fault logged, they'll find it. If the slot's gone, it's gone. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, wait, I do need to flag that if this isn't resolved before four o'clock, the fault escalates and you may lose service entirely. This is a routine procedure, I'm only asking for a brief verification so I can get you booked in. If you could just stay on the line for two minutes, I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I've heard enough. You won't name the company, you won't give me a reference, and now it's lose your service entirely. I'm ringing the number on my bill. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
