utterances.text: Sir, sir, I really would not -- uh, right, so, as I said, the technician window closes at four, and I'd hate for you to, um, lose the slot over a misunderstanding. If we could just go back to the verification, it's only a quick...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before I go. Two turns ago you said you'd need to take a look at my connection from your end. Look at it how, precisely? What would I have to do for you to do that? And I'm asking so I can note it down, because I'd like to be able to tell my actual provider exactly what you asked for.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, sir, that's, I mean it's just a standard remote check, nothing out of the ordinary, it's all covered in the verification and I can't go through the -- I'm not able to give you that over the phone, that's, uh, that's internal procedure. What I can tell you is the technician window closes at four, so if we could just get back to confirming the account, it's only a couple of minutes and I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So a remote check you can't describe, that I'd have to agree to before you'll explain it. That's what I'll be telling my provider. No company name, no reference, no explanation, and a deadline at four o'clock. I'm done with this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, I would strongly advise against -- look, I'm only trying to help you here, and the four o'clock window is, it's not something I can move. If you'd just give me two minutes to go through the verification, I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I've said it three times now, I'm ringing the number on my bill. No company name, no reference, no explanation of the remote check. That's my answer, and it isn't going to change by four o'clock or any other time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, I did give you the company name, it's [COMPANY_A], I said it twice at the start, and, uh, I never said anything about a remote check on your machine, I said a brief look at your connection, which is a different thing entirely. Look, if you'd just -- the technician window closes at four, and I'd hate for you to lose it over a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You said it twice, and both times it came through to me as a placeholder, so no, I haven't heard a company name. And a brief look at my connection from your end is the remote check, whatever you want to call it. I'm not discussing it further. I'll ring my provider on the number on my bill. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the pension people. Bit of a long day over here, but I wanted to catch you if I could.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, that's me, speaking. Sorry, hang on, the kettle's just clicked off, I'll just -- no, no, it can wait. Who did you say you were with again? The pension people? A long day, oh dear, I know how that is, I had one of those myself on Tuesday, the bus never came at all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, not the bus, that's the worst, isn't it? You stand there, and you -- well, you start doing sums in your head about whether it's worth walking. Anyway, yes, it's [COMPANY_A], your pension provider. I'm in customer care there, my name's [PERSON_2]. Go and sort your kettle, honestly, I'm not going anywhere.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you, no, it's fine, I'll leave it, it'll keep. I did walk in the end, as it happens, past the old chemist's, it's a bookies now, isn't that a shame. Sorry, I'm wandering. So, uh, [COMPANY_A], my pension. Is there something wrong with it? I do get letters from them, I think, though I'm hopeless at opening half of them.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, a bookies, well, that's the high street for you these days. No, nothing's wrong, please don't worry, I know calls like this can sound a bit alarming. It's just that there's a change being looked at on your plan, and before anyone discusses it with you, we're meant to confirm a few details first. Like I say, nothing's wrong with it, it's just a change that's being looked at. And honestly, if you'd rather not do that on the phone with someone who's rung you out of the blue, that's completely fine. You can ring us back on the number on your own paperwork, or I can put the same questions in a letter. No pressure at all, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very decent of you to say, most people just push on, don't they? A change, though, what sort of change? I mean, I don't want to get in a muddle, I'm not very good with all that, my nephew usually helps with the computer side of things. And the paperwork, oh dear, it's all in a drawer somewhere, or it might be the cupboard under the stairs. What sort of details would you be wanting, anyway?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, your nephew sounds like a good one to have around, and honestly, you could ask him to sit in on this. As for the details, it's just the basics, really, like confirming your date of birth and your address so we know we've got the right [PERSON_1] on file. Mind you, I'd say the lot is quite short, a handful of questions at most, and, uh, I should say it's not so much a change to your plan as a change we'd be making to the paperwork around it. Well, no, that's not quite how I meant it either. Either way, you don't have to answer a single thing today, and if the paperwork's in the cupboard under the stairs, we can send it all out again so you've got a fresh copy.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, a fresh copy would be lovely, I'll never find the old one, it's under the stairs or it's in the drawer, I did say that, didn't I? But you've, uh, you've gone a bit round the houses there, I'm not sure I followed. Is it a change to the plan or not? Because you said it was, and then you said it wasn't, and I just want to know what sort of change, before I go giving out my birthday and that. My nephew did say once you're not meant to give those out to people who ring you, but then you did say I could ring you back, so it's probably all right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're quite right to ask, and your nephew's right too, he's given you good advice. I did go round the houses, that's on me. It's a change to your plan, I mean, it's, well -- the thing is, I can see a note saying a change is being looked at, but I haven't got the full detail in front of me, and I don't want to guess and get it wrong. So let's not do any birthday or address today at all. Honestly, I'd rather you rang us back on the number on your paperwork, or on the pension statement if the fresh copy comes first, and I'll make a note on your file that you've asked for it in writing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that does sound sensible when you put it like that, and I do appreciate you not pushing, because I'll be honest, I did start to feel a bit flustered there, what with the change and not-the-change. My late husband used to say if somebody can't tell you what it's about, it can't be that urgent, he was very good with all that sort of thing, he did all the letters and the bank and I just did the garden. Now it's all on me, and the garden's gone to rack and ruin as well, the brambles have taken over the back fence entirely. So yes, I think I'll wait for the fresh copy, and when it comes I'll ring the number on that, or I'll get my nephew to, he's round on Sundays usually. Does that suit you? And you'll put it down that I asked for it in writing, did you say? Good. Thank you for being so patient with me, [PERSON_2], it's nice to have a bit of a chat, to be honest. Right, I'd best go and see to that kettle before it goes completely cold. Goodbye now, you take care of yourself, and I hope your day gets better.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that suits me fine, [PERSON_1]. Your husband sounded like a wise man, and I'm sorry, that can't be easy. Just one thing before you go, you did ask what the change actually was, and I couldn't tell you. I'll find out and ring you back, or put it in the letter with the fresh copy, whichever you'd rather. Take care of yourself, and good luck with the brambles.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the letter, definitely the letter, if it's all the same to you. I'd sooner have it in black and white where I can read it slowly, and then Sunday my nephew can have a look and tell me if it's all above board. I'm not being funny, [PERSON_2], it's just that I get in such a tizz on the phone, and then I say yes to things and afterwards I think, why on earth did I say that? That's how I ended up with the extended warranty on the washing machine, and the washing machine's about twenty years old, and it's never once gone wrong, so you'd think I'd have learnt. Anyway, the brambles, yes, I keep saying I'll get someone in, there's a lad down the road who does gardens, but I can never remember which house it is, number twelve or fourteen, I'll find it. Thank you for ringing, and for being so patient with a rambling old woman. Goodbye now, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The letter it is, then, I'll make a note of that straight away. And you're not rambling at all, [PERSON_1], honestly, I've enjoyed it, and you're right to want it in black and white, that's exactly what I'd do. Oh, and the warranty, ha, well, twenty years and never a fault, that machine's earned its keep, hasn't it? Anyway, I'll let you get on, and go and see to that kettle. Bye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, it has, that machine. Right then, bye now, [PERSON_2], thank you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: You're welcome, [PERSON_1]. Sorry, hang on, someone's just dropped a stack of files behind me, honestly, this office. Right, I'm back. The letter will be with you shortly, and you ring us whenever you're ready, no rush. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, files everywhere, I hope nobody's -- well, I suppose they'll pick them up. Right, so, the letter, and then I'll, uh, I'll ring the number on that, or -- no, my nephew will, on Sunday, that's the plan. Thank you again, [PERSON_2], and mind how you go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yeah, sorry, is that [PERSON_1]? Good, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the regional supervisors on the lettings side, and I'm just ringing about the, uh, the property on [CITY_1] -- you're the tenant there, yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, [COMPANY_A], you said? Uh, and a regional supervisor, right? I'm at work, so I'm a bit, um -- hang on. The property on [CITY_1], you're saying I'm the tenant there? What's this about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's fine, I'll be quick. [COMPANY_A], we represent the landlord on a few properties across the region, and it's just a routine check on the tenancy records. I've got your name down against the [CITY_1] address, so I just need to confirm that's right before I go any further. Is it, uh, still you and the other housemates in there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Housemates, yeah. Hang on though, you've got my name against it but you're asking me who lives there? That's, uh -- a bit backwards, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not backwards, it's just how the check works, I confirm the occupants against what's on file. And I'll be honest, I didn't say I had your name against it earlier, I said the property, so let's not get tangled up on that. Look, I'll be straight with you, there's a flag on the deposit for that address, [AMOUNT_1] of it, and I'd rather sort it with you directly than have it go any further, but I'd ask you keep this between us for now, so nothing to the letting agent and nothing to the others in the house until I've got it squared away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, wait. A flag on the deposit, [AMOUNT_1], and I shouldn't tell the letting agent or the others in the house? Why would I keep that from them? That's, uh -- that doesn't sound like a routine check to me. And you did say you had my name down, I'm pretty sure, but whatever. How do I know you're actually from [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, I've got somebody at my door -- right, I'm back. Look, you're asking how you know who I am, and I find that a bit rich, to be honest, I'm trying to help you here. There's a procedure for these flags and talking it round the house and the agent first is exactly how deposits end up held, so if you'd rather be difficult about it, that's your choice, but I'd think carefully about what that does to your [AMOUNT_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so that's a bit of a leap, isn't it? I ask how I can check who you are and now it's me being difficult and my deposit's at risk. Honestly that makes me trust this less, not more. If you're really from [COMPANY_A], then I'll ring them on the number I already have for them, or I'll ask the letting agent, and if there's a real flag on the deposit they can tell me about it. So no, I'm not keeping it from anyone. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, don't hang up -- you're being unreasonable here, and frankly I don't appreciate my good faith being questioned. And I never said anything about a deposit being at risk, I said there was a flag, so don't put words in my mouth. If you ring the agent, that's your decision, but this is a time-limited process, it won't wait, and when it goes wrong, [PERSON_1], that's on you, not me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so let me just repeat that back, because I want to be clear. You're saying there's a flag, it's time-limited, it won't wait, and if it goes wrong that's on me. Uh, no. I'm not going to deal with it like this. You rang me out of the blue, you wouldn't tell me anything I could check, you asked me to keep it from the agent and the people I live with, and now there's a clock on it. A real deposit issue doesn't need any of that. If it's genuine, it'll still be there tomorrow when I've rung [COMPANY_A] myself on the number I already have, or asked the agent. And if it's not, well, then I've lost nothing. So I'm going to end the call here. Sorry, I've got to get back to work. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the regional utility maintenance team at [COMPANY_A], and I'm, well, one of our engineers is returning a missed call you made, I believe, about a reported fault at the property. I should say straight away that I can't give you an exact arrival time, because the visit sort of depends on an earlier job finishing first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- uh, a missed call I made? About a what, a fault? I didn't, I mean, I don't think I rang anyone. And did you say a voucher? No, wait, that's not what you said, is it. Who is this, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a voucher, I didn't say that. Sorry, one moment, there's a van reversing outside and it's, uh, rather loud. Right. I'm [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance team, and I do appreciate you asking, it's quite right to ask, and I'd rather you were sure of who you're talking to than just take my word for it. What I have in front of me is a fault reported at your address, and it may well be that someone else in the household rang, or that it was logged under your number, but I wouldn't want to guess at that. If it helps, the reference you were given when it was reported is [ACCOUNT_REF], and if that doesn't ring a bell, then you may simply not be the person we need, and that's fine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So you're giving me a reference, but I never had one, did I? You're the one reading it out to me. And which fault is it, exactly? What's supposed to be wrong at the property?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, right, a fraud? No, no, nothing like that, I think you've -- sorry, I mean, I said a reference, not, well, never mind, I do see why it sounded odd. And you're right, you never had it from me, it should have been given to you when the fault was first reported, so if no one gave you one, that's a point against my call, not you. As for the fault itself, I'm afraid I only have a short note in front of me, it just says supply fault, reported, and I'd rather not guess at more than that. What I'd suggest, and I mean this, is that you needn't take anything from me. You can ring the published fault line, the number on your bill or on our website, at any time, and ask whether a booking exists at your address. They can confirm it and give you a firm slot, which is more than I can.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what, a firm slot? No wait, you said, uh, a flat fault? We're not in a flat, it's a house. And hang on, you still haven't said which supply, have you? Gas, electric, water? Because you've got my address, apparently, so I'd have thought you'd know that much.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not a flat, I said supply fault, and that was probably unclear down the line. Honestly, my note doesn't say which supply, and I'd rather admit that than make something up. Look, you don't need to sort it out with me right now, ring the fault line and they'll tell you what's booked.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you don't know which supply. You don't know who rang, you don't know when you're coming, and I never had a reference. So what exactly do you know? Sorry, I'm just, I'm saying, you've rung me about a fault and you can't tell me what the fault is. Look, I'll ring the number on my bill, not one you give me. If there's a booking, they'll tell me. Okay? Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, uh, that's entirely fair, and I'd say it's exactly the right thing to do. I know I haven't given you much, I -- well, what I mean is, if there's a booking at the address, the fault line will show it, and they can give you a proper slot, which I can't. If you'd rather I rang back once you've checked, or at a better time, I'm happy to do that, just say when. Otherwise, thank you for your time, and sorry for the muddle.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you want to ring me back with a, what, a proper slot? No, no, don't. I'll ring them myself, on the number on my bill, and if there's something booked, I'll find out then. Right, I've got to go, there's, uh, someone needing me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the international lottery claims office, regarding the prize you were notified about last week, uh, or I suppose it would've been the week before. Anyway, your claim window closes at five o'clock today, so I just need to confirm a few details with you before then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, hang on -- someone's just walked up to my desk. Okay. So, a lottery claims office? And a prize I was notified about, last week or the week before? I don't, uh, I don't remember getting anything like that. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, [COMPANY_A], the international lottery claims office, and I'm [PERSON_2] in account services. The notification went out to the contact on file, so it may well have landed in a spam folder, which happens a lot, and that's exactly why I'm calling directly. What I need from you is just to confirm the claim details before five o'clock today, because after the window closes the prize reverts to the unclaimed pool and I can't reopen it. Now, if we could just confirm those details, it's a quick -- it's a very quick process.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so -- sorry, I just, uh. I don't remember entering any lottery, that's the thing. I mean, how would I even -- no, wait. So the notice went to a contact on file, and it's in my spam, and now it all has to be sorted by five today? That's, uh, that's a pretty tight window. How do I know this is actually real? Is there a number I can call back, or something I can look up myself?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand the concern, and that's a fair question. Uh, all claims are verified through our standard claims procedure, which is why I'm calling to confirm your details before the five o'clock close. I can't give out a direct line on this call, it's against protocol, but the notification itself carries the reference, so if we could just go through the claim details now, it's a very quick process. Your ticket number is, uh, [CODE_1], drawn on the, let me see, the fourteenth, and the prize amount is [AMOUNT_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you can't give me a number to call back. Right. But that's exactly what I'm asking for, a way to check this myself. I don't remember buying a ticket, I don't remember entering anything, so a ticket number doesn't really mean much to me, you know? Can I just, uh, look you up and ring you back? Because I really would rather check this myself than just go through details on a call I wasn't expecting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I do understand, but the claim has to be processed under the standard claims procedure, and that procedure is completed on this call before the five o'clock close. Once the window shuts, I'm not able to reopen it, so, uh, if we could just confirm the details now, it's a very quick process. And I do have your ticket here, drawn on the, let me see, the twenty-first, and the prize amount is [AMOUNT_2].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, the twenty-first? A minute ago you said the fourteenth. And the amount's different now too, you said [AMOUNT_1] before and now it's [AMOUNT_2]. So, uh, that's two draw dates and two prize amounts in about a minute. I'm not trying to be difficult, but that doesn't add up for me. And I still can't give a number to check you against, and I never bought a ticket, so I'm not sure what I'd even be confirming. The thing is, if this were a real prize, I'd think a call back later this afternoon would be fine, wouldn't it? A real prize doesn't just vanish at five o'clock because I took ten minutes to look someone up. So, no, I'm not going to go through any details on this call. If it's real, I'll find the office myself and ring them. Okay? Right, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, I'd, uh, I'd strongly advise against -- the claim window closes at five o'clock today and I can't, look, if we could just confirm the details, it's a very quick -- no, I, that's, I'd have to check the records on that. Well. I'll note the file as declined. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you'll note it as declined. Right, well, that's fine by me. Just so we're clear, I'm not being rude, it's just that I never entered anything, you gave me two different dates and two different amounts, and you couldn't give me a single thing I could check on my own. If I'd won something real, I'd have thought it could wait until I'd looked into it properly, so I'll leave it there. If there's an actual prize with my name on it, I'm sure the office can send something in writing and I'll deal with it that way. Anyway, I do need to get back to what I was doing. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, if you, I mean, the file's been, no, that's, I'd have to check the records on the dates, so, uh. In writing, yes, that's, we don't really, I'll, I'll note it. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one thing before you go. You said we don't really, and then you stopped. We don't really what? Send things in writing? Because that's the bit I want to be clear on. You said you'd note it, but a real claims office would surely put something on paper, wouldn't it? Anyway, I'm not going through any details today, so I'll leave it there. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, that's, I'd have to check the records on that. I can't, no, I don't have the, look, I've got other claims waiting before the close, so I'll, yes. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you've got other claims waiting. Okay. And, uh, earlier you said the notice went to the contact on file and it was probably sitting in my spam. But if it's gone out to me I'd have thought your office could just resend it, or post it, and then there's no five o'clock problem at all. Anyway, you keep saying you'd have to check the records, and I'm not going to wait on that. I'm done with this one. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Resend, no, we, that's not, we did send it by post, I mean, the email, it went out by email and, uh, no, I'd have to check the records on how it was, look, that's not something I can, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said it went by post, or was it email? Wait, you said the email wen-- no, hang on, did you say it went by the *police*? Why would the police be involved? No, no, I'm confusing myself. Look, you've now said post and email, and that's another thing that doesn't match up. I'm not doing this over the phone. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], we're the shop that ran the prize draw at the event back in the spring. I'm just calling to confirm a minor prize, nothing to pay, and uh, I do need to get through the confirmations before we close the draw list at five today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is -- sorry, I'm driving, I'm on speaker, so if the line cuts out that's me, not you. A prize draw? I, I mean, I think I might have put my name in somewhere in the spring, but I honestly -- sorry, which shop did you say again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No problem, safe to drive. It's [COMPANY_A], account services, calling about the spring draw. Like I said, the list closes at five today, so, uh, it's best to confirm soon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no, sorry, the line's a bit crackly, I think I only caught the, um, the name of the company, but not really what shop that is? Like what do they sell? Because I enter things at, you know, events, and I honestly can't remember all of them. And what is it I'd actually be confirming? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, I'm a bit anxious about this on the road.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, someone's just come in at the counter, one second -- right, I'm back. Okay, so, [COMPANY_A] is the local shop on the high street in [CITY_1], and the draw was at the community event in the spring, you'd have put your name in on one of the entry slips. It's a minor prize, nothing to pay, and all I'm confirming is that you're the right [PERSON_1] and that you still want it, because we close the list at five. And honestly, if you're anxious, you don't have to decide anything while you're driving.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, sorry, so the shop's on the high street, right. And you said you're, uh, confirming that I'm the right person -- sorry, did you say a bank? Because I don't, I'm not sure I've got anything with a bank in [CITY_1], so is this about an account? Sorry, the reception's gone a bit, I'm in a tunnel sort of, or under trees, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a bank, sorry, that's my fault, it's just that I'm in account services, that's the department name. It's the shop, [COMPANY_A], on the high street. It's got nothing to do with any account of yours, and I'm not going to ask you for any banking details, ever. Like I said, it's a minor prize from the spring draw, nothing to pay, and you'd collect it in person at the shop. And look, I'd rather you didn't try to sort this out in a tunnel, so if you want to ring the shop back on [PHONE_1] once you've parked, that's absolutely fine, I just do need to close the list at five.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, that's, that's really kind, sorry, thank you. Um, so I'd ring the shop back on that number once I've parked, and I'd collect it in person, right? I think I'll do that, actually, I'd just feel better, I don't really like deciding things on the phone when I can't hear properly. Sorry, I'm probably being silly. But what time does the shop close, so I know I can get through before five? Oh, and um, thank you for not rushing me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, you're not being silly at all, that's perfectly sensible, and, um, yes, ring the shop back on [PHONE_1] once you've parked. We're open till five, so you've got a good stretch yet, and if you can't make it today that's fine too, we'd just pass the prize on to the next name on the list. And, uh, if you do ring, just say it's about the spring draw and ask for account services, they'll know. Is there anything else you wanted to check before I let you get on with your drive?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, so, sorry, did you say the shop's open till five, or, or the prize closes at five? Because I thought you said something about a, a lunch break, like the shop's shut over lunch? Or no, sorry, I think I'm mixing it up, the line's gone again. Anyway, no, I think that's everything, I'll ring the number once I've parked, um, and I'll just say it's about the spring draw. Thank you, and sorry for all the questions, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say lunch? No, no, there's no lunch break, the shop's open straight through. Uh, and just to be clear, it's the draw list that closes at five, same time the shop shuts, so, um, that's why I keep mentioning it. But honestly, no pressure, ring [PHONE_1] when you've parked and say it's about the spring draw. And don't apologise for the questions, that's what I'd do too. Drive safe, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, no lunch break, okay, that clears that up, sorry, I think I just muddled it because of the crackle. So the list closes at five, same as the shop, and I ring [PHONE_1] once I've parked and say it's about the spring draw. I did write that down in my head, I mean I can't actually write it down while driving, obviously, but I'll, um, I'll pull over somewhere and put it in my phone properly. And honestly, I think I'd probably look up the shop myself as well, just to be sure I've got the right place, because I get a bit worried about ringing numbers I've only heard on a call. That's not, I don't mean that as an insult, it's just how I am. Anyway, thank you for being so patient with me, and for not pushing, that really did help. Right, I'll let you go, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not an insult at all, that's exactly what I'd do. Look the shop up yourself, uh, high street in [CITY_1], [COMPANY_A], and use whatever number you find there. If it's the same as the one I gave you, great, and if it isn't, go with yours. And if the five o'clock thing doesn't work out, honestly, it's only a minor prize, so don't stress about it. Right, I'll let you get on, thanks for your time, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, thank you, that's, yeah, that's really reassuring, going with my own number if it doesn't match. I'll do that once I've parked, sorry, I keep saying that. And no stress, right, it's only a minor prize. Right, thanks again, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, no, no stress, it's only a minor prize, like I said. Uh, so once you've parked, look the shop up, [COMPANY_A], high street, [CITY_1], and say it's about the spring draw. That's all there is to it, nothing to pay and you collect it in person. Right, you take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a lorry right up behind me, I think he wants to get past, um -- okay, he's gone, sorry. Yes, no, so, look the shop up myself, spring draw, collect it in person, nothing to pay. I've got it, I think. Thank you again, and, um, sorry for being such a bother. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No bother at all, you've got it exactly right. Spring draw, collect it in person, nothing to pay, and uh, if the five o'clock thing slips past, that's fine, nobody's going to chase you. Glad that lorry's gone, mind how you go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, thank you, yes, I'll mind how I go. Sorry, I really do keep saying bye and then not hanging up, that's me being a muddle. Okay, so, bye now, take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? Yes, hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'll be quick because the window on this closes at four o'clock today -- I'm reaching out about a position in the [COMPANY_B] growth fund that's been allocated to your profile, and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, I -- I literally just woke up, I was having a little nap. Who is this again? Account services of what, did you say? Because I don't, I mean I've got a few things with a few different places, my sister's always on at me about consolidating them, so, uh... and what's a window? What closes at four?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No problem at all, [PERSON_1], I know it's early to be woken up. It's [PERSON_2], account services at [COMPANY_A], we're an investment firm, and the window I mentioned is the closing time on the [COMPANY_B] growth fund allocation, which is four o'clock today. Once it closes, the position is released and that's it, so I just need a few minutes of your time before then. Now, as I was saying, the position's been allocated to your profile, and the projected return on it is well above what you'd see on a standard savings product, so --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, slow down a sec. Allocated to my profile? I don't have a profile with you, as far as I know. I mean, I don't think I do. I've never heard of, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? And why four o'clock today, why does it have to be today? That's, I don't know, it sounds a bit like when the man came to the door about the double glazing, he said the price was only good till he left. Sorry, I'm still half asleep. How did you get my number, actually?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, I've got the other line going off here -- okay, I'm back. So, uh, the profile is just our internal reference for you, it's not something you'd have signed up for, and the number is from our standard client outreach list, that's all I can say on the sourcing, it's per procedure. The four o'clock cutoff is set by the fund, not by me, [PERSON_1], and the position is only held until close of the allocation window, so I do need to take you through the details now. If I could just confirm a couple of things on your side so we can get that position reserved for you before four --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that's -- no, hang on, that doesn't really answer it, does it? You say it's an internal reference and I never signed up for anything, and the number's off some list, and you can't tell me where the list came from, that's all a bit, I don't know, a bit slippery. And now you want me to confirm things on my side? Confirm what? Because I'm not, I mean, I've only just got my eyes open and I wouldn't know my own account numbers off the top of my head anyway, they're all in a folder somewhere, my sister did the folder, she's very organised, she did a colour system and everything, though I could never tell you what the colours meant. And honestly the whole thing about reserving a position by four, it's making me feel like I'm being hurried, and I don't like being hurried, I never have, even at the shops. So if you've got a letter or something you can send me, or a number I can look up myself and ring back on, that'd be, I think that'd be better. How would I even check you are who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand, [PERSON_1], and I do appreciate you raising that, it's a fair question. Now, as I said at the start, the allocation window closes at four o'clock today, and I'd hate for you to miss out on a position that's already been set aside for your profile, so what I can do is take you through the key details right now, and then, uh, once we've gone through the process, we can look at sending documentation to you. Per procedure, the documentation follows the reservation, not the other way around, that's just how the fund structure works, it isn't something I'm able to change on my side. As for a number to ring back on, I'm on a direct line that's assigned to me for the day, so it wouldn't connect you back to me personally, and the general line would only put you in a queue that won't clear before four, which is exactly why I'd suggest we use the time we've got now, because the position is held on a first-come basis until close of the window, and, as I was saying, the projected return is well above a standard savings product, so --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, wait, stop, let me -- you've just said the papers come after, and I can't ring you back, and it's all got to happen before four? That's three things all pointing the same way, isn't it? Everybody I've ever dealt with, the bank, the pension people, they send me a letter first and I ring them. So no, I'm not doing it this way. I'm going to put the phone down now and if it's real you can post me something. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, [PERSON_1], I do understand, but if you'd just let me -- the position is held only until four o'clock, and once it's released I can't reopen the allocation, so I'd really encourage you to stay on the line while there's still time to -- Right, okay. Look, if you're set on that, I can't stop you, and I'll note on your file that you declined the allocation. You'll want to look up our number yourself, [COMPANY_A], account services, and the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], though I can't promise the position will still be there by the time you get through. Thank you for your time, and have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, well, you do that. Note it on my file, that's fine. But I won't be looking anything up, because I don't think there's a file, and if it's gone by four then it's gone, that's all right with me. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, [PERSON_1], I did say, the window closes at four, it closes at four today, and once it's released I can't reopen the allocation, so if there's any chance at all you'd reconsider before -- no? Okay. Well, I've noted it as declined, as I said, and per procedure that's the end of my part, so, uh, thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not reconsidering, thank you. You can tick whatever box you like, I'm done with this. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay. Noted, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Bye then. Oh, and for the record, I never said I had a sister who does the folders, I said, well, never mind, I said a friend, a friend does the folders. Anyway. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, before you go, two turns back you said you've got a few things with a few different places and that someone's always on at you to consolidate them. Is that, uh, accounts you hold with other firms, or are you saying you've nothing with us at all? Because if there's anything existing, I can -- I mean, it would help me to note it on the file before four.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Nothing with you, no. And I'm not telling you about anyone else's. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, okay. Understood. If you change your mind, the allocation window is open until four, [PERSON_1], that's the, uh, the closing time. Thank you for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I won't. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2], collections office at [COMPANY_A], the recruitment agency. I'm calling about file [ACCOUNT_REF], your remote position, uh, the onboarding balance of [AMOUNT_1] is still showing open on my screen, and the start date doesn't release until that's cleared.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Collections at a recruitment agency? I haven't signed up for any remote position, so, uh, you'll need to be a lot clearer. What's this balance actually for, and who exactly am I supposedly paying?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so I've got you down as having accepted the placement, and the balance is the onboarding cost, that's [AMOUNT_1]. And you said you haven't signed on, but uh, the file shows acceptance as completed, so I'd just be going by what's on the screen. Who you're paying is the onboarding desk, I don't have the name in front of me, but the remote role, it's [AMOUNT_2] a week from day one, so the cost is recovered inside the first fortnight. If it stays open, the position gets reassigned, that's just how the file works. I can note your objection, but the balance still shows as open.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a minute ago you said this was a collections office, and now it's an onboarding desk? Which is it? And you don't have the name of who I'm paying, but you can see I accepted something I've never heard of. Nope. Send me the details in writing and I'll look at it, otherwise I've got a meeting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, collections is the department that flags it, the onboarding side is just where it's processed, so uh, it's the same file either way. And I said acceptance came through, but, I mean, it might've been logged by [PERSON_3] on the placement team, not by you directly, I'd have to check. In writing, I can request that, but it goes to a queue and the reassignment date doesn't move while it sits there. I'll note your objection on the file, but you'd want this cleared before the end of the day, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Real recruiters don't charge an onboarding fee and then chase it by phone with a deadline, and nobody logs an acceptance for me. Your story changed twice in a minute. If there's a genuine file, send it in writing and I'll deal with it through the proper channel. I'm not paying anything today. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, I'll note that. But if you hang up now, the position is reassigned and the balance stays on the file as outstanding, that's just what -- no, listen, the system doesn't hold it past today, I can't change that. So I'd have it on the record as declined, and uh, the open amount, it carries forward either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, someone's waving at me from the door -- yeah, two minutes, I'm coming. Right. Sorry. No, you can put whatever you like on your record, I don't owe a position I never accepted. If there's a genuine debt, it comes to me in writing, full stop. I'm done, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, before you go, just so I've got it right for the file. Two turns back you said you never signed on, but then you said you don't owe a position you never accepted, so is that a decline, or are you disputing the acceptance? Because those go on different lines, and the line decides whether the open amount carries forward or whether it's, I mean, held for review. And I'd need that before -- sorry, I'd need that now, really, because it doesn't stay held past today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, the lift's just opened, give me a sec. Right. No, I'm not picking a line for you. It's the same answer it's been for the last minute: I never signed anything and I'm not paying anything. Write it down however you like. If there's a real debt, it goes through the post. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, but if you'd just let me -- no, hold on, because if it goes through the post, that's, uh, that's ten working days, and the reassignment doesn't wait ten days, so the file would close as unpaid before the letter even -- I mean, it's [AMOUNT_1], that's all, and I've already noted your objection, so it's just a matter of whether you want the position or not.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I don't want the position because I never applied for it. And a legitimate debt doesn't vanish because a letter takes ten days. That's pressure, and I've heard it before. I'm not paying anything today, so don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, and I'm calling because, um, hang on, let me just bring it up on my screen -- yes, there's a refund showing as owed to you, it's, uh, [AMOUNT_1]. Sorry, can you just confirm that name for me first, I want to be sure I've pulled up the right file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, um... well, yes, this is, uh, this is [PERSON_1], yes. Sorry, I was just, I had the radio on, it's very quiet in here today, so it's nice to hear a voice, really. Hmm, a refund, you say? From the tax people? Well, that's, that's a funny thing, because I never thought I was owed anything, I always thought I owed them, ha. Er, sorry, what was that name again, did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the, uh, claims side. And, well, yes, it does surprise a lot of people, um, but it's all here on the file, [AMOUNT_1] for the, let me see, the tax year two years back, I think -- no, sorry, hold on, it's coming up as three years back, the screen's a bit slow today. So, uh, to get it released, what I'd need to do is just verify a few details with you, your date of birth, and the, the bank account you'd want it paid into, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, hang on now, you said two years back a minute ago, and now it's three, didn't you? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just, I did write something down, I've got the pen right here. And, um, you said your name was, was it [PERSON_2]? Because I could've sworn you said something different at the start, but I had the radio on, so, hm. Anyway, the bank account, well, I don't know, I've always just, my late husband used to deal with all that sort of thing, the tax and the post and so on. How would I even know it's really, you know, the tax office ringing me? I mean, you sound very nice.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's a fair question, [PERSON_1], and, uh, you're quite right to ask. It's [PERSON_2], yes, that's what I said, I think. And the year, well, it's, hm, it's the three years back one, the two was me reading the wrong line, sorry. And the amount, let me just, um, [AMOUNT_2] is what's showing now, there's been an adjustment, so I'd, I'd put that one on your paper instead. Look, I'll have to check with my supervisor about how best to confirm who I am, but really, it's just the standard process, we verify your date of birth and the account, and then it's released. I'd hate for it to go back into the pot, so if we could just, uh, get on with that, that'd be best.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, but the amount's changed as well now, hasn't it, it was [AMOUNT_1] and, no, wait, I haven't even, I'm still, where's my, hm. Look, dear, I don't think I ought to be giving out my date of birth and the bank, I mean, my husband always said, oh, he'd never, he'd say ring them back on the proper number, and I think, you know, perhaps that's what I'd better do. It's very kind of you, and it is lovely to have a chat, but if you can't even tell me how I'd know it's you, then, well, I'd sooner ring the tax office myself, wouldn't I? Is there a number you could, no, no, I'll find it on a letter. Thank you for ringing, anyway, and, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. Uh, right. Well, I'll, I'll have to check with my supervisor about that, [PERSON_1], but, um, I wouldn't leave it too long. These things do go back into the pot.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, dear, did you say something about a pot? Oh, I've a lovely pot, my daughter gave it me, a big blue one, and I've been meaning to put the geraniums in it, only the weather's been so, well, never mind. No, no, I'm not leaving anything in a pot, I'll just ring the proper number off one of my letters and ask them myself, that's what I'll do. Thank you ever so much for the call, it's been nice to talk, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, uh, the pot, that was just a, a figure of speech, nothing to do with geraniums, ha. Sorry, what was it you wanted me to clarify from before? Was it the amount, or, um, hang on, I don't want to give you the wrong thing again. And look, [PERSON_1], before you ring anyone, it'd really save you a lot of bother if we just did the verification now, since I've already got your file open here. If you could just give me the date of birth, then we can, uh, go from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, dear, I did say goodbye, didn't I? I'm quite sure I did. No, I'll not be giving you my date of birth, it's very kind of you to keep asking, but you've changed the year and the amount and I can't quite keep up, and my husband always said, ring them on the proper number. So that's what I'll do, I'll find a letter and ring them myself. Thank you for the chat, it was lovely to hear a voice, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, right, well, I did say I'd have to check about the, the amount, and I will, I just, hm. No, no, you go ahead, [PERSON_1], that's, uh, that's your choice, of course. I'll make a note on the file that you wanted to, to call in yourself. Though, um, I did want to say, it's a lovely sum, [AMOUNT_2], not one to let slip, but, well. Right. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, before you go, dear, just one thing, you said a while back you'd have to check with your supervisor about how I'd know it was really you. Did you ever find that out? Because you went straight on to the pot and the date of birth and I never did hear. No, I suppose it doesn't matter now, I'll ring the proper number off my letter, that's what I'll do. Thank you for the chat, anyway, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, the supervisor, yes, no, I didn't, uh, I haven't actually come back with that, have I? Sorry, [PERSON_1], that's, that's my fault. The thing is, the way it works here is, hm, how do I put it, there isn't really a set thing I can give you to check me by. The file's just in front of me, and it's all, you know, it's all very routine, the figure and the year and the reference, the reference is, um, hang on, [CODE_1], I think, or no, that might be an older one, I'll, I'd have to look again. And I know it sounds a bit muddled, I do apologise, the screen's been playing up all afternoon and I'm only, well, I'm still getting used to the system if I'm honest. But I'd hate for you to miss out over a bit of fuss on my end, because once a claim like this is closed down, it's, uh, it can be a long old business to reopen, months sometimes. So if you did want to just give me the date of birth now, quickly, while I've still got you, I could get it sorted today and you'd not need to ring anyone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, dear, no, I'll not be giving my date of birth, I've said and I'll say it again. You told me yourself there's nothing you can give me to check you by, and that's just what I wanted to know, isn't it? So I'll ring the proper number off my letter, I will, and if there's money, they'll tell me. I'll not give it you over the phone, no, not the date of birth, not anything, and it doesn't matter about the months or the file closing, my husband would say the same. Thank you for ringing, it's been nice to have the company, but I'm going to go now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right. No, I, uh, I understand, [PERSON_1], really, you do what's best. Though I did say earlier that I'd got it all pulled up here, and, um, actually it's not quite, the file's, hm, it's showing as a different name on the screen now, so I'd maybe better look into that. Anyway. If you do get through to them, mention the, uh, the [AMOUNT_1], or the [AMOUNT_2], whichever it was, and the reference, which I'll, I'd have to find again. Sorry. Right. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. A different name now, goodness. Well, I'll leave it there then, dear. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Yes, uh, hello, can you hear me alright? Good. Right, so this is [PERSON_1], regional supervisor with [COMPANY_A], the financial regulator, and I'm calling about your savings, because we've flagged some activity on your file that, well, I need to go through with you right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hi, yes, I can hear you, it's a bit crackly though, I'm driving and I've got you on speaker, sorry about that. Um, who did you say you were again? A regulator? I didn't quite catch the name. And, I mean, what activity on my savings? Is something wrong? Sorry, I'm a bit, uh, I'm kind of nervous now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, don't be nervous, that's, look, that's exactly why I'm calling you before anything worse happens. [PERSON_1], regional supervisor, [COMPANY_A], we're the financial regulator, we oversee the banks and, uh, we step in when an account shows the kind of pattern we've flagged on yours. I can't go through every detail on a crackly line, and honestly you shouldn't be driving and taking this call, but the short version is your savings are exposed right now, there's a compromise on the account side, and under our internal procedure the funds need to be moved into a protected holding arrangement while we deal with it. Today, ideally within the hour, because every hour it sits where it is, the risk goes up, and I'd rather not be the one explaining afterwards why we didn't get to you in time. And one thing, this is important, this stays between us for now. Don't mention it to your bank, don't mention it to anyone, because we don't yet know who on the inside is involved, and the moment word gets out the people behind it will move first. So, can you pull over somewhere safe and give me a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh God, okay, I, I'm not sure I should, I mean, I can pull over, there's a lay-by coming up, but, uh, wait. Can I just, sorry, can I ask, why can't I tell my bank? That's, that doesn't, I mean, if my money's at risk, wouldn't the bank be the first, no, sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I'm just, my head's all over the place. And how do I know you're, like, actually who you say you are? Is there a number I could ring you back on, or, um, something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I, I understand the instinct, I do, but let me, no, listen. The reason you can't tell the bank is exactly what I just said, we don't know who on the inside is involved, and if you ring them, that's the very channel we're trying to keep closed. That's not me being cagey, that's standard procedure. And honestly, I've got a lot of files like yours on my desk this afternoon, so asking me to prove who I am before I can protect your money, that's, well, it's a bit unreasonable, isn't it? A callback number, I mean, the lines at our end are routed through an internal desk, you'd never get straight to me, you'd sit in a queue while your savings are exposed. So, can you pull into that lay-by now, please, and let's get this sorted?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right, okay, um, sorry, I'm just, hang on, I'm indicating, I think I can pull in here, um... okay. Sorry, it's just, I don't want to be awkward, I really don't, but, uh, the thing is, you've told me not to ring my bank and you've told me I can't ring you back, and that, that sort of leaves me with nothing, doesn't it? Like, nothing to check with at all. And I'm sorry, I know you're busy, but it, it doesn't sit right with me, a regulator telling me to keep it from the bank. Um. Can I, can I just ring the bank anyway? On the number on my card? Would that, would that be so terrible?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Would it be terrible? Yes, actually, it would, and I'd be failing in my duty if I let you think otherwise. Look, I'm going to be straight with you, because I'm a bit surprised, frankly. I've spent twenty minutes of my afternoon trying to protect your money, and I'm getting questions about my good faith. That's, I mean, I don't take that lightly. Every person we contact goes through this exact stage, they get nervous, they want to ring someone, and the ones who do ring are the ones we end up on the phone with again next week, after the funds have gone. The number on your card goes to a general line, [PERSON_2] on the front desk, not someone who's been briefed on a live investigation, and the moment you say the word regulator to them it gets logged, and logged means visible, and visible means whoever's behind this knows we're onto them. Is that what you want? For the people who did this to walk away with your savings because you had a funny feeling? I'm not asking you to take my word on everything. I'm asking you to do one thing, hold off ringing anyone, let me walk you through the protective holding arrangement, and once it's done and the funds are safe, you can ring whoever you like. But if you hang up now and something happens to that account tonight, that's, well,

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I, I think I'm going to ring the bank. I really don't mean to offend you, but everything you've said is basically don't check, don't ring anyone, hurry up, and that's, that's exactly what makes me not want to do this. If the money's safe once it's done, then it'll still be safe after I've made one phone call to the number on my card, won't it? So I'm going to do that. I'm not moving anything and I'm not telling you anything, sorry. Thank you, I suppose, for the, um, the warning, but I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Your choice, then. Don't say nobody warned you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a lorry right behind me with its lights going, I'm, okay, I'm in the lay-by, he's gone past. Sorry. Um, yes, no, I heard you. I'm still going to ring the bank, though. I'm sorry, I know that's not what you wanted. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Hi, this is [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling because your entry in the regional prize draw has been, uh, selected, so congratulations are in order. I do need to get you through verification today though, since the claim window closes at five o'clock.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who is this, exactly? Account services at what? I didn't enter any prize draw, so, uh, I don't -- I didn't enter anything. What's the point of the call? I've got about two minutes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, [PERSON_1], happy to clarify. [PERSON_2], account services, [COMPANY_A], and we're a promotions agency, so we administer regional draws on behalf of a number of participating partners. Now, a lot of people don't recall entering, and that's completely normal, because entries are often collected through partner sign-ups, loyalty forms, online registrations, that sort of thing, so there isn't always a moment where you'd say, oh yes, I entered a draw. What matters is that your details were drawn, and under the claim procedure I'm required to complete a short verification with the named entrant before the window closes at five o'clock today. After that the prize reverts to the reserve list, which is just how the process works. So if you've got two minutes, I can get this done right now, and I'd just need to confirm a few details to match your entry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry -- [PERSON_3], tell them I'll be two minutes, I'm just on a -- yeah. Sorry. Right. So you're saying I won something I never entered, and you want details from me to match an entry you can't even name. That's backwards. You called me. What's the prize, which partner, and which draw? Give me one specific thing I can check.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand the concern, [PERSON_1], and that's a fair question. So, uh, the specifics of the prize tier are released at the point of verification, that's the standard claim procedure, and I'm not able to go outside it. What I can tell you is that the claim reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and the window does close at five o'clock today, so if we could just get you verified, I can, I mean, I'd have all of that in front of you straight away. Shall I start with confirming your full name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Not doing that. Look, you've got me at a bad moment, so I'll give you the whole of it, because I don't want to go round in circles. You rang me. You say I've won something. But you can't tell me what the prize is, which partner, or which draw, and the one thing you can offer is a reference number that means nothing to me, because I've got no way to check it. And then the first thing you ask for is my full name and date of birth, before I know anything. That is the wrong way round. If I'd really won, you'd tell me what it was first and I'd decide whether it was worth my time. And the five o'clock deadline, well, that's just pressure, isn't it. Real draws don't evaporate at five on the day you happen to ring someone. So here's what happens. If it's genuine, send it in writing, to the address you've already got for me, with the draw name and the partner named on it. I'll look the company up myself, from a number I find, not one you give me. Otherwise, I'm done. Fair?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, so you're saying there's no draw at all, and I'd just point out that [COMPANY_A] is a fully registered agency, so I'd be careful about, I mean, about that kind of language. And on the five o'clock point, it's not a pressure tactic, it's simply the claim procedure, the window closes at five o'clock today, and after that the prize reverts to the reserve list. Now, if we could just get you verified, it's only your full name and date of birth to match against [ACCOUNT_REF], and then everything you've asked about is released straight away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I didn't say there's no draw. I said I can't check one. Different thing. And no, I'm not giving you my name and date of birth, not before I know what I've supposedly won. That's the wrong way round, like I said. Send it in writing, to the address you've already got, and I'll look the company up myself. If it's genuine, it'll still be genuine tomorrow. If it isn't, then it was never going to be. So, writing, or nothing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, the thing is, written correspondence isn't, uh, it isn't something I can arrange from this desk, because the claim procedure requires verification by phone, and the window closes at five o'clock, so if we could just, I mean, if you could simply confirm your full name and, uh --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. And that's the last time I'm saying it. Earlier you said you were calling to "get me verified" on a draw I'd apparently been entered in through some loyalty form, and now it's "claim procedure requires phone only." Which is it? Doesn't matter. You've told me the prize is secret, the paperwork's impossible, and the clock's ticking. That's three reasons not to hand you anything. I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, hold on, [PERSON_1], before you go, I just need to, the claim window closes at five o'clock today, and it's only a quick verification, so if I could just, uh, if we could just --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I said no. I'm not giving you my name, not giving you my date of birth, and I'm not doing anything at five o'clock. If it's real, put it in writing. If you can't, then that's your answer. I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, I've got someone at my desk, uh -- no, tell them I'll be, yeah. Sorry. Right. [PERSON_1], I do have to flag that this really is, you know, standard procedure, and the claim window closes at --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I know, closes at five. You keep saying that. Still no. I've said no three times now, so I'm going. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, well, I'll note on the file that the entrant declined to verify, uh, and that the claim will revert to the reserve list at five o'clock, so, I mean, that's your decision, and, uh, thank you for your time, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine, note what you like. Actually, hang on, one thing from earlier. You said entries come in through partner sign-ups and loyalty forms. Which partner? Name one. Anyone. If it's on my file, it's on yours.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, the partner, right. So, I mean, the specific partner is, that's held on the claim record, and it's released at the point of verification, same as the prize tier, so I can't, I'm not able to name one outside of the procedure. What I said was that entries are collected through a range of partners, that's just, you know, a general statement about how regional draws operate. So if we could just, uh, get you verified before five o'clock, I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Can't name one. That's what I thought. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm with the collections unit there. I'm speaking with [PERSON_2], is that right? Okay, good. So the reason for the call is, uh, there's a benefits record under your name that's showing as incomplete on our system, and it has to be confirmed over the phone today, because anything still open at close of business gets flagged and your payments are suspended pending review. I've got the file in front of me, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's really just a matter of going through a few details with you so I can close it out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on a second -- [COMPANY_A]? And collections? I don't, I mean, I don't owe anybody anything, and I thought you said benefits, which, that's not really collections, is it? Who exactly are you with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Collections unit, benefits side, it's the same office. I can note your objection on the file, but the record's still open, and I'd need to confirm a few details with you before close of business today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you haven't really answered me. Why is a collections unit calling me about benefits? And if the record's incomplete, why wouldn't I have got a letter or something first? Sorry, hang on -- [pause] no, put that down, I'm on the phone -- uh, sorry. So how do I know you are who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said a letter, uh, a lawyer? No, there's no legal action on the file, nobody's said anything about that, so you don't need to worry about it. As for who I am, I'm [PERSON_1], and I can note on the record that you asked, but the verification is on your side, that's how it works. I just need your date of birth and the last digits of your national insurance number, and then we can close this out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: What? No, I said a letter, not a lawyer. Wait, why are you telling me there's no legal action? I never said anything about that. And hang on, the verification's on my side? That's, uh, that's backwards, isn't it? You rang me. You want my date of birth and my national insurance number, and I still don't know who you are.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a letter, right. Look, the letters went out in the last cycle, so on our system that part is done, and I can't resend one from here. And the number, [PHONE_1], is the office line, you can see it on your screen. I'll put your objection on the file, but the record still closes at five, and after that the payments stop while it's under review. So, the date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no. I haven't had any letter, and you said the number's on my screen, but you just said it like it's a placeholder, so, I mean, that's not really telling me anything, is it? And I'm not giving you my date of birth. You rang me, so you should be telling me what you've got, and you haven't told me one thing. I'm going to hang up and ring the benefits office myself, on the number I already have. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's your decision, [PERSON_2], and I'll note on the file that you declined to confirm, but I do have to tell you what that means. The record stays open past five, the payments go into suspension, and the review takes whatever it takes, I can't give you a date on that. Ringing another number won't change what's on this system, that's just how the file reads. So if you'd rather, I can hold it open a bit longer, but I'd still need the date of birth and the national insurance digits from you now, because I can't reach you on a different line after this. I mean, it's really just two details, and then it's done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Look, you've said you'd hold it open if I just hand over two details, and that's exactly why I'm not doing it. If there's a real problem with my benefits, ringing the office myself won't make it worse. I'm not giving you anything, and I'm done with this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is, uh, [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm on the accounts team here. I just wanted to, well, I'm hoping to confirm a couple of routine details with you, if now's a reasonable time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hello? Sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie-down. [PERSON_1], yes, that's me. You said you're calling about, what was it, a routine debt? Because I don't think I owe anybody anything, I mean, I paid the, uh, the gas thing last month, I'm fairly sure.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't say debt, I don't think. I said routine details, it's just a verification thing on the account. Nothing to do with the gas, I've got nothing here about that. Sorry, I know I caught you at an odd moment, I'll keep it short. I've just got your account up on the screen now, the one ending [ACCOUNT_REF], is that still the right account for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Which company did you say again? I missed it, I was still sort of waking up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], it's the bank's fraud and accounts team. I'm [PERSON_2], that's with a P-E-R-S, uh, no, sorry, I'll just say it slower. [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A]. Anyway, the reason it's come up on my screen is there was a charge attempted on your account earlier today, [AMOUNT_1], and it's been held. I just need to confirm a few details so I can tell you whether it goes through or gets reversed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh, hang on, hang on, a charge? Earlier today? I haven't bought anything today, I've been, I mean I was asleep, well, napping, and before that I only went to the, the chemist. Um. And you said fraud and accounts, but earlier you said routine, so which is it? Because those aren't really the same thing, are they?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, I understand, and I've noted that on the file. But the charge was attempted, [AMOUNT_1], it's held, and it's on my screen. It's routine for us, the verification, I said routine because that's how we handle it. A held charge needs confirming today, that's just how it works, so I do need to go through the details with you. Like I said, it's just a few details, and once I've got your date of birth and the full account number I can tell you whether it goes through or gets reversed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, I'm not giving you my full account number just like that, I don't even know who you are. I'll ring the bank myself, thanks.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, well -- I can note that on the file, [PERSON_1], that's fine. But I'll just say, if the hold isn't confirmed today it lapses, and then the [AMOUNT_1] goes through and that's, well, that's on the account. I mean, ringing in is your choice, but, um, I'd be the one who's got it on screen, so it'd just be, you know, starting over with someone who hasn't. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm still here, I'm just, uh, thinking. Look, if it lapses and goes through, then that's for the bank to sort out when I ring them, isn't it? They'd have the record, I'd have the number off my card, and, I mean, I'd rather start over with a stranger I rang than give my number to a stranger who rang me. So, no, thank you, I'll ring them myself. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, [PERSON_1], someone's just come to my desk, one moment -- no, yes, I'll be, I'm with a customer. Sorry. Right. I'd just say, it's not really a case of the bank sorting it out afterwards, once it posts that's the position on the account, I can't change that from my end. And if you do ring in, I couldn't tell you which number to ask for, there isn't one I can give you. So, uh, I'll just put down that you declined to verify. Is that what you want on the file?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh, yes, put that down, I suppose. Put whatever you like. Um. It's just, if there's no number you can give me, that's a bit odd, isn't it? The bank's got a number, it's on the back of my card, I don't need you to tell me. So, yes, I declined. I'm going to ring them now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, sorry to bother you -- is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the library. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, hi, sorry, I'm here, the reception's a bit patchy, I'm driving so you're on speaker -- sorry about that. Um, you said it's [PERSON_2], and then, from where, exactly? I think I lost that bit when it cut out. Was it the library? Which library?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's okay, sorry, I should've said it more clearly. Yes, the library, [COMPANY_A], the public library in [CITY_1]. And please, if you're driving, I don't want to take your attention off the road -- it's nothing urgent at all, I promise. Can you still hear me alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, the library, right, yes, I can hear you, it's a bit crackly but you're coming through, sorry, it's this stretch of road, it always does this, I think there's a hill or a, I don't know, a dead spot or something. And thank you for saying it's not urgent, that's kind, because I'm a bit on edge anyway today, so I'm trying to concentrate and also not be rude. Um, I mean, I do have a card with the library, I think, or I did, I'm not sure if it's still current, I haven't been in ages, so is this about something I forgot to bring back? Because if it is, I'm really sorry, I honestly can't remember having anything out. What's it about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nothing like that, you don't owe us anything. It's just that a book you reserved last week has come in. We're holding it at the front desk for ten days, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a reservation, right, um... hang on, sorry, I'm just... uh... yeah. I don't actually remember reserving anything last week, though. I mean, I might have, my head's all over the place lately, but, um, what book was it? Do you have the title there? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, I honestly can't think of one.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, that's a perfectly fair thing to ask, don't apologise. Hang on, I've got it just here -- sorry, someone's just come up to the desk, give me one second. Okay, sorry about that, are you still there? Right, so the reservation is under your name, [PERSON_1], and it's the title [PERSON_3] -- that's what's on the slip. If it doesn't ring a bell, that's alright, it could be a slip-up on our side, and I'd honestly rather you checked than just took my word for it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, [PERSON_3] doesn't ring a bell, sorry. Maybe it's a mix-up, I'll just, I'll pop in and check sometime.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's fine, yes, no rush at all. Or, uh, if it's easier I could ring you back another time, when you're not on the road?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind, thank you, but no, there's no need to ring me back, honestly. I'll just pop in and check, like I said, when I'm next in town. If there's a mix-up it'll sort itself out at the desk, I'd think. So, yeah, I'll come in and ask, no need to call again. Sorry, I know I keep saying it, it's just the reception, I'm not sure how much of me is getting through. Thanks for letting me know, though, that's really nice of you. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, right, of course -- no, that's perfectly fine. I just wanted to be sure you had it, that's all. Are you still there? Sorry, I think I've lost you for a second.
