Well, uh, the book's at the front desk for ten days, so there's plenty of time, and if it turns out it's not yours, just tell whoever's on the desk and they'll sort it. Take care on the road, won't you? Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I'm, I mean, I can still, sorry, I think you cut out there for a second but I got the, I got most of it. Ten days, front desk, right. I'll, uh, I'll mention it if it's not mine. Thanks again, and sorry, I'm, anyway. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, alright. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what was that, you said, "bye then," or was it, uh, "buy then"? Because I haven't, I'm not buying anything, I don't think I said that, did I? No, sorry, I think it's just the line breaking up again, never mind. Right, well, thanks, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, it's [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], the deposit protection scheme. Is that [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Uh, no -- I mean, that's not, nobody's called that here. Hang on, [COMPANY_A], what's that, a deposit scheme? I haven't got a deposit with anyone, not that I know of. Who gave you this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, okay, so it's [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], the tenancy deposit protection scheme. And I'm, uh, trying to reach [PERSON_2] about a pending matter on a tenancy deposit -- so if that's not you, I do apologise, the number may have been entered wrong on our side. Can I just ask, is there a [PERSON_2] who lives at this address or uses this line, because I do have a window today to get this notification out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on one sec -- no, put that down, sweetheart, I'm on the phone -- sorry. Right. So, no, I'm not going to tell you who does or doesn't live here, I mean, you've rung me, so surely you'd know who you were trying to reach? And if the number's been put in wrong, which, fine, these things happen, then I'd have thought the simplest thing is you just take it off your list and ring whoever's supposed to be on the other end. What's this window, anyway? Why does it have to go out today? Because that's, I don't know, that sounds like the kind of thing where somebody wants me to hurry. And I'm not saying that's you, I'm just, who exactly are you again, and how would I even check that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, and you're right to ask, so let me do this properly. I'm [PERSON_1], account services at [COMPANY_A], the tenancy deposit protection scheme. And you're absolutely right, if the number's wrong, I should take it off the list and I will, no need for you to confirm who does or doesn't live there. I withdraw that question, sorry. On the window, it's a bit of an internal thing, uh, our notification batch closes at the end of today, which is why I was a bit brisk. But it's not your deadline, it's ours, and nothing you do or don't do on this call changes anything for you. If I've reached the wrong household, there's genuinely nothing for you to act on. And checking me is dead simple. Don't take my word for any of it. Look up [COMPANY_A] on the official site, [URL_1], find the main contact number there yourself, and ring that. Quote [CODE_1] and they can tell you whether I work there and whether there's a case with that reference. I'm not asking you for any details, no names, no money, nothing. If it turns out I've got the wrong number, you've lost five minutes. So, is that all right, or is now just a bad time?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I mean, that's, well -- no, hang on. If there's nothing for me to act on, and it's the wrong household, then, uh, why are you still explaining all this to me? Sorry, I'm not, I don't mean that rudely, it's just -- it's a lot of words for a wrong number. Anyway, yeah, it's a bad time, I've got a kid here who's about to tip a whole glass of juice over. And I'll be honest, if I did want to check, I'd look the number up myself, I wouldn't use a website you just read out to me, so, you know, I don't need your [CODE_1] for that. Is that all you needed? Because I think you've got the wrong number and that's, yeah, that's where I'd leave it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fair, and you should look the number up yourself, that's the right instinct. Uh, so yes, that's all, I'll take this number off the list. And actually, to be straight with you, it was a bit more words than a wrong number needs, I should've left it at sorry and goodbye. The thing is, I said earlier I'd only rung to reach a [PERSON_2], but, uh, there is a short written notice that goes out to the contact on file either way, so if one lands with you, that's the paper trail, the same request in writing, and it carries the case reference you can check. It'll ask you to keep the matter to yourselves until both sides have been formally notified, that's just fairness procedure, nothing for you to do. Look, go and rescue the juice. Is there a better time I could try you, or would you rather I just didn't?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, no no, not on the -- hang on, [PERSON_3], leave it, I'll get a cloth in a sec -- sorry. Right. Uh, wait, a notice? To the contact on file? You said it was the wrong number, so how's there a contact on file for me? And keep it to ourselves, why would I need to keep anything to myself if there's nothing for me to do? That's, I don't know, that's a strange thing to ask. And no, don't ring back. Take the number off, like you said. If something actually turns up in the post, I'll look the real number up myself and ask them, not you. Okay? Okay. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, you're right, I -- look, that came out muddled, and the bit about a contact on file, I shouldn't have said it, because it doesn't fit with a wrong number, and I'd rather not leave you with half an answer. What I should've said is, if I've got the wrong household, there's no notice and nothing to keep to yourselves. And if anything ever did arrive, the confidentiality line would only ever be in writing with a reference you check yourself, never something you're asked to take from me on the phone. So, uh, I'll take the number off now, and I won't ring again. Go and get that cloth, and sorry for the bother.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, I'd just say, you told me at the start you were trying to reach somebody about a pending matter, and then it was only a, what, a batch thing, and now it's a notice that may or may not exist. It doesn't sit right, that's all. Anyway, you've said you'll take it off, so I'm holding you to that. And if something does come in the post I'll check it myself, like I said. Right, I really have got to go, he's got juice everywhere. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, I hear you, and I'd feel the same. My account of it did shift as we went, and I'm sorry for that. Number's coming off the list today, and you'll hear nothing further from me. If anything does come in the post, check it the way you said. Go and sort the juice. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the number's coming off the list *today*, or, no, hang on, you said something about a trial? A trial of what? No, never mind, I'm not signing up to anything, I've got a kid and a flood in the kitchen. Just take it off. Okay. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no trial, I didn't say anything about a trial, and there's nothing to sign up to. I said the number's coming off the list today, that's all. Nothing for you to do, nothing coming from me. Go and deal with the kitchen, I'm sorry for the bother. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, fine, no trial, I probably misheard, there's a lot of noise here. But hang on, two goes back, you said if something lands with me it'd be, what was it, in writing, with a case reference? Why would a letter come to me at all if I'm the wrong household? That still doesn't add up. Anyway, I'm not asking you to explain it again, I've heard enough. If a letter turns up I'll ring the proper number myself. Right, I'm putting the phone down now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, this is [PERSON_2], I'm with the customs desk at [COMPANY_A]. It's about a parcel you're expecting, there's an import charge on it that needs, um, attending to.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, this is [PERSON_1], hello. Sorry, I'm not sure I caught that, who did you say you were with again? And a parcel, I, I don't think I'm expecting one, but, um, what's the charge for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, that's, uh, a perfectly fair thing to ask. [PERSON_2], customs desk, [COMPANY_A], the courier. And, well... the parcel would've come from overseas, sent to you by, I believe, [PERSON_3], so it may not have been on your mind. There's an import charge of [AMOUNT_1] that's been assessed on it, and it does need to be cleared before the parcel can move on to you. Um, I'd rather not rush you through any of this, but these things do tend to sit only so long at the depot.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm, I'm not quite following. [PERSON_3]? Um, I do know someone by that name, but I don't, I don't remember them saying they were sending me anything. So, sorry, just to check I've got this right, it's a charge of [AMOUNT_1], and it's, it's for a parcel from overseas, from [PERSON_3]? Oh dear, I do feel I should know about it. How, how would I even go about, um, sorting it out?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, you've got it right, [AMOUNT_1], and that's, uh, the charge on the parcel from [PERSON_3]. Now, two turns back, you asked who I was with, and I only gave you the name quickly, so let me be more careful. It's [COMPANY_A], the customs desk, and I'm not asking you to take that on my word. The parcel has a tracking reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and if [PERSON_3] sent you a confirmation, or you look it up on [URL_1], you should see the same reference and the charge sitting against it. As for settling it, um, I wouldn't do that over the phone at all. The tracking page is where it's handled, and you can do that whenever you're ready, though, well, parcels don't wait at the depot indefinitely.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's, that's very good of you, thank you. Um, sorry, I'm not very good with the computer, but I think I could manage looking up a reference if I had a pen. And, uh, it's reassuring you're not asking me to pay over the phone, I did wonder about that. Could you, um, say that reference again for me, slowly? And the website too, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, please don't apologise, it's, uh, good that you want to be careful. The reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and the page is [URL_1]. I'll say them once more, slowly, so you can check what you've written. Reference, [ACCOUNT_REF]. Website, [URL_1]. Now, um, I'd also gently suggest you don't just take my word for the website either. If you'd rather, you can look up the [COMPANY_A] customs line yourself, from their own official site or from anything [PERSON_3] sent you, and call me back on that number. I'd honestly welcome that. Whatever you decide, though, it's probably best not to leave it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind of you, and, um, thank you for saying it twice, I've got the reference written down now, I think, though I'll read it back to myself once more in a moment just to be sure. And I do appreciate you telling me I needn't just take your word for it. That's, well, it's more than I expected, honestly. I think what I'll do, if that's all right, is ring [PERSON_3] first, because I really would like to know whether they've sent me something, and it's quite possible they did and just forgot to mention it, they're a bit like that. And then, um, if it turns out to be right, I'll have a go at the website, though you'll have to forgive me if it takes me a while, I'm not much good at those things. Is there anything else I ought to have to hand when I do, apart from the reference? Sorry, I just don't want to get halfway through and find I've missed something.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, ringing [PERSON_3] first is, uh, exactly what I'd do. And as for what to have to hand, really just the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], that's all, and the amount you see on the page should read [AMOUNT_1]. If it shows anything different, or if anything on that page asks for more than that, um, stop there and ring the [COMPANY_A] customs line, the one you look up yourself. I'd say that twice if I could, honestly, look it up yourself, not from anything I've given you today. Take your time with it, it's your call, and I'll note on the file that you're checking first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, thank you. So, um, just the reference and, and the amount, that's all. Sorry, did you say I should stop if it asks for my, my pension? Or was it something else? I'm not sure I caught that last bit properly, but I won't put anything like that in, don't worry. Anyway, I'll ring [PERSON_3] first and have a look at the website after, and thank you for being so patient with me, you've been very kind. Goodbye now, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh wonderful, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time. It's [PERSON_2] calling from the customer care team at [COMPANY_A], the foundation, and I just have to say, what a lovely turnout that was at the event in [CITY_1], wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Who is this? Um, yes, this is [PERSON_1], but I'm just in the middle of cooking, I've got a pan on. Sorry, who did you say you were? And what event? I'm not sure I -- sorry, who is this?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, goodness, I'm so sorry, you go and mind that pan, I'll wait, nothing worse than a burnt dinner! Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a stack of folders on the desk behind me, it's like a bomb went off in here. Right, I'm back. It's [PERSON_2], customer care at [COMPANY_A], the foundation, and it's just a quick little chat about the gala evening, the one where you were so generous with everyone in the room.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? The gala? I don't, I don't think I went to a gala. Hang on, I've got the pan. What's this about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yes, take your time, no rush at all, I'm just, uh, sort of shuffling my notes here. So, it's about the pledge, really. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, hang on. Two turns back you said there's a matter I can't discuss with anyone at the branch. So, wait, what matter? You still haven't told me. And now you're saying don't call the branch or the main line, which is, I mean, that's the one way I'd actually check you. If you're legitimate, why would you not want me to verify it? That's the part that's bothering me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I'm just the scheduling assistant, [PERSON_1], I don't have the details, the investigator does, so I just need a yes on two o'clock.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying yes to two o'clock. If the investigator wants me, they can go through the main line and I'll take it from there. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], wait, hang on, I'm [PERSON_2], scheduling assistant, internal investigations at [COMPANY_A], and I'm really just trying to get ten minutes on the calendar, that's all, ten minutes, so if you could just say yes to two o'clock, or even sooner, because the investigator needs to speak with you today and it has to stay between you and us -- [PERSON_1]? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here, but the answer's the same. You can't tell me what it's about, you don't want me checking with anyone, and you keep asking for a yes on a time. That's not something I'm doing over the phone. If the investigator needs me, it goes through the main line, officially. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, but it's not really official channels that are the issue, it's that the main line is where the, uh, where the flag gets raised, and I did say this is the senior investigator's call, not mine, I'm only the scheduler, I mean, I'm actually the investigator's own assistant, so I just need two o'clock, ten minutes, and then you'd hear everything straight from them -- [PERSON_1], are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the security operations side. I just need to confirm I've reached the right household before I go any further, if you could say yes for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who -- hang on, before you go any further, which company did you say? And I'm not going to say yes to anything until I know what this is about. What's the call regarding?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, that's fair. [COMPANY_A], the national tax office, I'm with the security operations team there. It's regarding a refund on your file, a routine matter, nothing to be alarmed about. So, am I speaking with [PERSON_1], yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a... a return? Like something I ordered, a parcel? I haven't sent anything back to anyone. Hold on, you said tax office, though, so which is it? And a tax office doesn't have a security operations team ringing people, as far as I know. What's the actual reference for this, and what's a number I could call you back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not a return, no. A refund. R-E-fund. A tax refund, owed to you, on your file with [COMPANY_A]. I said tax office, I meant tax office. And the security operations team handles refund verification before anything is released, that's standard, that's why I'm the one calling. The reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and the amount is [AMOUNT_1]. As for a callback number, I'm on a direct line that doesn't take incoming, so we'll just do this now. Can you confirm your full name and date of birth so I can match you to the file?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, hang on, I'm not -- I'm not giving you my name or my date of birth. You rang me, you can't tell me who I am before I've told you who you are. And a direct line that doesn't take incoming calls, that's, uh, that's not really a thing. Every office line takes calls. So I'll look up the tax office myself, from their published number, and if there's a refund they can tell me. What's your full name and your staff number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: My name is [PERSON_2]. Staff number is [CODE_1]. I've given you both, that's more than most callers do. Now, I'll go through this once more, slower. The refund is [AMOUNT_2], for the last tax year, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and it is held pending verification. It does not stay held indefinitely. If it isn't verified in the next couple of days, it goes back into the general account and the claim lapses. You're welcome to look up the office. But that takes time, and the verification window doesn't wait. So, your full name and date of birth, please, and we can finish this in two minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no. Look, I appreciate you've given me a name, but [PERSON_2] and a code that I can't check anywhere, that's, that's just words, isn't it? And the, the window closing in a couple of days, that's the bit that, well, a real refund doesn't just evaporate because I took an afternoon to ring the tax office myself. So I'm not giving you my name or my date of birth. I'll look up the published number, I'll ask them about the reference, and if there's a refund they'll sort it out with me directly. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, hang on, don't hang up, because -- look, I'm trying to help you here. Nobody's asking for anything unreasonable. The figure I quoted you, it's the figure on the file, [AMOUNT_1], or [AMOUNT_2], whichever the system is showing me on this screen, and I'd rather you didn't make this harder than it is. If you ring the main number you'll sit in a queue, and by the time you reach anyone the verification window will have closed. I'm telling you this once, slowly. Give me your name and date of birth and we'll finish this properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh... I mean, you've just quoted me two different amounts, [AMOUNT_1] and then [AMOUNT_2], and now it's whichever the screen shows. That isn't a file, that's guessing. And the queue argument, that's the same pressure again, just dressed differently. So no. I'm not giving you my name or my date of birth, not on a call I didn't ask for. If there's a genuine refund, it'll still be there when I've rung the published number. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, don't -- hold on a second. Sorry, [PERSON_3], not now, I'm on a call, just leave it on the desk. Right. Where was I. The amounts, yes, that's a, there's a correction pending on the file, that's all, it happens, it isn't guessing. But look, I can't keep this line open while you go off and ring around. I'll note that you declined verification, and the claim will be treated as unclaimed. Is that what you want me to put down?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Put down -- no, I'm not, I mean, what I want is, uh, put down whatever you like. If it's unclaimed, then it's unclaimed, and the tax office can tell me so when I ring them myself. A correction pending doesn't explain two different figures, and, well, threatening to mark me as having declined, that's the same push again, isn't it? So no, I'm not verifying anything on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. I'll say this and then I'll leave you to it. You've misread this, [PERSON_1]. Nobody has threatened you. I've explained how the process works, and it works the same way for every claimant, and a note on file that someone declined verification is a procedural entry, not a penalty. I've had the figure wrong because I'm working two screens and a correction is pending on one of them, and I'd have thought a person who's actually trying to help you would get some credit for admitting that rather than being accused of guessing. Now, do ring the published number, by all means, nobody's stopping you, but when you do, I'd have the reference ready, [ACCOUNT_REF], and I'd tell them the security operations team already tried to reach you today, because that will save you being asked the same questions twice. And if they've no record of the refund, well, that would be a matter for them, not for me, though I'd still say it's worth you thinking about whether you want to leave it sitting there unclaimed. I'll be noting this call as it stands. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say they've already tried to reach me, as in the, the tax office rang me earlier? Because no one has. There's been nothing today. Or, hang on, are you saying you're the one who tried, because that's, that doesn't match either. Look, I'm not going to quote your reference to anyone, I'll ask them from scratch and see what they actually have on me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], we're an events venue here in [CITY_1]. Um, I'm the venue coordinator on a private dinner booking, and it's for a colleague of yours, so I wanted to just, sort of, have a quick word with you about it, if that's alright? You're still there, yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh -- yes, hello, this is -- sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie down, so I'm still sort of, um. Yeah, I'm here. Who did you say? An events, a venue? I mean, which colleague, because I've got -- well, there's a few, and I wouldn't, I don't think I've heard anything about a dinner.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I've woken you, haven't I? It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the events venue, um, in [CITY_1]. And that's the thing, you wouldn't have heard about the dinner, because it's meant to be a surprise, it's a private retirement dinner for your colleague [PERSON_3]. I just wanted to ask, if you could, sort of, keep it quiet from [PERSON_3] for now, that's all I'm asking, nothing else. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a retirement, right, well -- that's lovely, I suppose, although I'd have thought I'd have heard something, because usually somebody's passed round a card or an envelope or, you know, one of those emails where everyone's meant to chip in a few quid, and nothing's come my way, but then again I have been a bit all over the place this week, and I did sort of nod off just now so I might've missed things. And [PERSON_3], well, I mean I know [PERSON_3], obviously, but I didn't know they were retiring, which is a bit odd, isn't it, that I wouldn't know that? Sorry, I'm rambling, I'm not properly awake. Um, but how did you get my number, actually? That's what I keep thinking. Did somebody give it to you, or, I mean, is that how these things usually work?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's a fair question, sorry, and you're not rambling at all. Um, hang on, sorry, someone's just come in with a delivery here, one moment -- right, sorry, they've gone. So, the number came from the organiser, one of your colleagues, who put you down as someone who'd want to come along, and I'd rather not say who, just because it's meant to stay a surprise, but I do understand that sounds a bit odd. And honestly, I'm not asking you for anything, no money, no details, nothing like that, I just didn't want you mentioning it to [PERSON_3] by accident. You're still with me, yes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say a delivery? What sort of delivery, because I haven't ordered anything, I don't think, although I did have a parcel due, or I might be thinking of last week. No wait, that's not what you were on about, was it, you said someone came in. Right. So a colleague gave you my number, but you won't say which one, which, I mean, it's a surprise, fair enough, but it does make it a bit hard for me, doesn't it, because how would I know it's true? I'm not saying it isn't, I'm just, I'm sort of half asleep and I'd feel daft going along with something when I can't even tell who started it. Is there someone I could check with? Or I could just ask [PERSON_3] straight out whether they're, no, well, I couldn't, could I, that'd spoil it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, the delivery was nothing to do with you, sorry, that was just somebody here, I shouldn't have said. And you're not daft at all, it's exactly right to want to check. So, you can ring the venue directly, it's [COMPANY_A], and the booking contact is [PERSON_2], that's me, on [PHONE_1], or you can look the venue up yourself rather than using any number I give you, whichever feels safer. And you're right, please don't ask [PERSON_3], that's the one person I'd ask you not to mention it to. Everyone else is fine. Are you still there, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm still here, sorry, I keep sort of drifting. Right, so you're saying I can look the venue up myself, which, well, that's a good point, that's what my sister always says, never ring the number they give you, and I did hear something on the radio about that, or maybe it was on the telly, I can't remember which. But I'm not exactly quick with all that, the looking things up on the phone, I'd probably end up on the wrong page and ring a dentist or something. And I don't have a pen anywhere near me, I'm still half under the blanket here. So I suppose what I'm thinking is, you're not actually asking me for anything, you're just asking me to keep it quiet, which is, I mean, that's easy enough, I wasn't going to say anything to [PERSON_3] anyway, I barely speak to them, we're on different floors. But it still seems a bit odd that nobody's told me themselves, if I'm meant to be going along. Is there a date for it, even? Because if there's a date I could at least have a think about whether I'm free.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, no, that's a sensible thing to ask, sorry. Right, so the date, it's, uh -- hang on, sorry, I'm just, I'm not sure I should say the exact date over the phone before the organiser's actually been in touch with you themselves, because then it comes from them, doesn't it, which is how it ought to be. I'm sorry, that probably sounds unhelpful. You're still there, yes? I really don't want to worry you, and you're quite right to be careful, it's only that I thought a quick call would save everyone a bit of bother.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. See, that's a bit funny, because a minute ago you said I was down as someone who'd want to come along, so you must have the date, surely, and now it's, well, it should come from the organiser first? And you did say the dinner was for my colleague, but I thought you said earlier I wouldn't have heard about it because it's a surprise, and now you're saying the organiser's going to be in touch anyway, so which is it, am I invited already or not? Sorry, I'm not trying to catch you out, I'm just, I'm half asleep and it's not adding up in my head. I think what I'll do is, if the organiser does ring me, fine, and if not, well, I'll hear about it eventually, won't I? And I wasn't going to tell [PERSON_3] anything anyway, so that's all right. Is that, um, is that all you needed?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's all, that's all I needed, honestly, and I'm so sorry if I've muddled you, I shouldn't have rung without the organiser having -- well. You're quite right, it's best you wait to hear from them, and I won't keep you any longer. Just, um, the only thing I'd ask is that [PERSON_3] doesn't hear about it, but you've said you wouldn't, so that's lovely. Go back to your rest now, and I'm sorry again for disturbing you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, bye, though, sorry, before you go, two turns back you said I was down as someone who'd want to come along, and then the date thing, I still don't quite follow that, but never mind, it doesn't matter, you've said you're not asking for anything. Right. I'll go back to my blanket then. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the events venue, and I'm calling because I'm coordinating a private dinner booking for a colleague of yours, [PERSON_2], who's retiring, and I need to explain what that involves before anything else, so bear with me. It's a surprise, which is the whole reason I'm ringing you rather than going through the usual office channels, and what I'm asking is that you keep the booking quiet from [PERSON_2] until the evening itself, that's the only person it's to be kept from. Is this a reasonable moment, or, uh, do you have to hear the details first?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- one second, I've got a little one here. Okay. Uh, you said "security operations" at an events venue? Why would security be organising a dinner? And, I mean, who did you say this was for again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, fair question, and it's the second thing people ask, so. At [COMPANY_A], security operations covers access and guest lists for private functions, which is why the booking lands on my desk instead of sales. Anything with a restricted guest list comes through us. I check who's on it, I coordinate with the booking contact, and I make sure nobody turns up who shouldn't. So it sounds odd, but it's actually quite routine, I do these every week. And the dinner is for [PERSON_2], your colleague, the one who's retiring. That's the name I have, and that's the only person this needs to stay quiet from. Everyone else involved knows, that's rather the point. Now, I'm not asking you for anything today beyond that, no money, no personal details, nothing like that. If you'd rather confirm I am who I say I am, ring the venue directly, ask for the booking contact, and they'll tell you the same thing. I can give you the number, but I'd rather finish explaining first, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, put that down, we don't throw that. Sorry. Sorry, uh -- so you're saying nobody's asked me for anything, but you've rung me, out of the blue, to keep a secret from someone I work with? Why me? How did you get my number, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, understood, and I'll answer that properly, because it's a fair thing to ask. The number came from the organiser, a colleague of yours, [PERSON_3], who put together the guest list and gave me the contact details for everyone on it. That's standard. I don't source numbers myself, I work from the list I'm handed, and every person on it gets one call from me, same script, same request. Why you, specifically? Because you're on the list, which means [PERSON_3] thinks you're close enough to [PERSON_2] that you'd be invited, and the risk with a surprise is that someone mentions it in passing, an email, a corridor chat, and the whole thing is spoiled. So I ring each guest and ask for the same thing: say nothing to [PERSON_2] until the night. That's the entire request. I'm not asking you to hide it from your manager, or from anyone else, or to do anything at all except not mention it to the one person. Now, if any of that doesn't sit right, don't take my word for it. Contact [PERSON_3] directly, you'll know them, and ask whether they put you on the list. Then, if you like, ring the venue on the number I'll give you and ask for the booking contact. I'm not offended, I'd rather you checked than didn't.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but, hang on. Why does a surprise dinner need security calling every guest? Wouldn't [PERSON_3] just tell us themselves? And, I mean, you keep saying I can check, which, fine, but you've also said you'd rather finish explaining first. Finish explaining what, exactly? You haven't asked me for anything yet, so what's the catch?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, there's no catch, and I'll say that plainly, there's nothing left to explain beyond what I've already said. I phrased that badly, that's on me. As for why I'm the one ringing, [PERSON_3] did try telling people themselves, and the trouble is guests don't always take it as firm as they should, so the venue likes it confirmed on our side. That's the whole reason, and it's, I mean, it's genuinely not complicated. So the request is simply this: don't mention the dinner to [PERSON_2]. And the number for the booking contact is [PHONE_1], ring them any time and ask them to confirm it. Does that, um, does that answer it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I'll ask [PERSON_3] myself. And I'll keep my own counsel till then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Do that. Honestly, if now's not a good time, I can ring back when it suits you, just say when.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'd rather -- actually, don't ring back. If [PERSON_3] says it's real, I'll deal with it from there. Uh, I mean, I'll get hold of them myself, I don't need you chasing me. Right, I've got to go, the little one's -- yes, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon -- this is, uh, [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery. I'm calling about, well, the -- sorry, let me start again. We're just checking in on how your pet's recovering after last week's procedure, and whether you'd want a follow-up visit booked in. It's standard practice for us, so it won't take a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, good afternoon -- I'm not sure I follow. Which practice did you say this was, and which pet are we talking about? I don't recall having a procedure done last week, so I'd like to understand how you came to have this number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery in [CITY_1], and the number came off the client file from the procedure booking. Your pet's the one that came in last week, the surgery. Look, I'm not trying to be difficult, but this is a routine welfare follow-up, it's literally our procedure after any operation, so I'd have thought checking on an animal's recovery was a reasonable thing to do.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Checking on an animal's recovery is perfectly reasonable, I'm not disputing that. But you still haven't told me which pet, or what it is. You've said "your pet" twice now, and that's all. If it's on a client file, you should be able to tell me the animal's name, what species it is, and whose name the booking is under. And I should say, I don't actually have a pet that went in for surgery last week. So either you've got the wrong number, or something's off with that file. Can you give me the name on the booking?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, fair enough, I'll pull it up -- hang on. I mean, I do this all day, so I'm, uh, not going to be offended, but I'd have thought a quick follow-up call wouldn't get twenty questions. The booking's under [PERSON_2], and it's, let me see, a dog, the animal's name is down as [PERSON_3]. So if that's not you, then I'm guessing we've got the wrong number on the file, which, honestly, happens, and I'd rather sort that than leave a patient without a check-in. Does [PERSON_2] ring a bell, or is that, you know, not you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, that's not my name, and I don't have a dog. So it does sound like the wrong number on the file. I'd suggest you check where that number was recorded, because if it's attached to someone else's booking, that's a data accuracy problem on your end. Before we finish, can you tell me the surgery's main switchboard number? I'd like to ring back through that rather than carry on over this call.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, that's sensible, and I'd rather you rang back than sat there uneasy. The main switchboard is [PHONE_1], and if you ask for the regional supervisor's office, they'll put you through to me or my team. Oh, and sorry, you said two turns back that the file might have a data problem on our end, and I should've said, you're right, I'll flag it with reception so [PERSON_2]'s record gets corrected and your number comes off it. Does that cover it, or is there something else you wanted me to check before you ring through?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the number's coming off the file, or going onto it? Because I'm hearing something about [PERSON_2]'s record being corrected, and I don't want my number sitting on anyone's record at all. And I'll be honest, I'd rather find the surgery's number myself than use [PHONE_1], if that's all right. So can you confirm, clearly, that you'll have my number removed?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Coming off, definitely off. I'll flag it with reception today so your number's removed from [PERSON_2]'s record and doesn't get used again, and that's a yes, clearly. And sure, look the surgery up yourself, that's perfectly fine, I'd do the same. Anything on our side that needs to be confirmed, the main desk can sort it when you ring.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right. Well, thank you, I appreciate that. You haven't asked me for anything, which is, I mean, fair enough. I'll look the surgery up myself, and if I want to be sure the number's come off, I'll ask the main desk. So, yes, I think that's everything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, no problem. Sorry for the bother. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no bother. Sorry, hang on, there's a delivery van reversing outside and I couldn't quite hear you -- but I think we're done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2], I'm the scheduling assistant at [COMPANY_A], I work with [PERSON_3] on the tiling jobs, and I'm just calling about the bathroom quote he put together after he came round last week, you know, the one with the full re-tile, floor and walls, the new waterproofing underneath, and the grouting all included at [AMOUNT_1] like he said at the time, and basically I wanted to run through the scope with you quickly to make sure we've got it all down right and then see if you'd like to pencil in a start date, because we've got a couple of gaps coming up, so, uh, how's that sound?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, sorry, yes, that's me, but hang on, I'm driving, so you're on speaker and it's a bit -- sorry, the reception's awful here. Was that [COMPANY_A]? Because I did have someone come round last week, I think, about the, the bathroom, so that does -- sorry, go on, I just, can you say the name again? I didn't catch who you said you were with.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [COMPANY_A], that's right, it's [PERSON_2] calling, I'm the scheduling assistant there, and [PERSON_3] was the one who came round to you last week about the bathroom, the re-tile, and no worries at all about the line, I'll keep it quick, so we had the floor and the walls, the waterproofing, the grouting, all in at [AMOUNT_1], and I just wanted to see if you fancy picking a start date, because we've got a couple of gaps coming up, so, uh, how's that sound?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, right. Yeah, I think that's the one. Sorry, can I just, can I look at the quote properly first and ring you back? I can't really think about dates while I'm driving.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, course, no, that's absolutely fine, sorry, you're driving, I should've -- hang on, sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a box of something in the office, uh, right, sorry, where was I, yeah, no rush on the date at all, take your time with the quote, it's all in the email [PERSON_3] sent over, I think, or maybe it was a printed copy, I'd have to check which, but if you're ringing back it's [PHONE_1], and, um, did you want me to flag anything on the scope while you're looking, or is it just the dates you'd like to think about?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the, the what? Did you say the scope, or, no, I think you said the soap? Because I don't remember anything about soap, I thought it was just tiles and the, the grout. Sorry, it's the reception, it keeps cutting out. And, um, I'll ring you back, yeah, but is that number the one that's on the quote? I'd rather use that one, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, scope, sorry, S-C-O-P-E, what's covered, not soap, nothing about soap, it's just the tiles and the grout and the, uh, the waterproofing underneath, that's all, nothing extra. And the number, so it's the -- well, it should be the same as the one on the quote, I think, I mean it's the office line, but I'm, sorry, I honestly can't say for certain that's what's printed on yours, so, uh, I'll check that with [PERSON_3] and call you straight back to confirm, would that be okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, scope, right, sorry, that's -- yeah, that makes more sense. Um, no, hang on, I'd rather, I mean, I'll just ring the number that's on the quote, if that's okay? That way I know it's, well, it's not that I think you're, I just, I'm driving and I'd feel better doing it that way. And then I can ask about the dates properly when I've got it in front of me. Sorry. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's -- yeah, honestly, that's completely fine, ring the one on the quote, that's the best way, and I'll still have a word with [PERSON_3] so he knows you'll be in touch, and if there's anything on the quote you're not sure about when you've got it in front of you, uh, just ask, and if I can't answer it I'll find out and ring you back, how's that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thanks, yeah, that's, that's really kind. Sorry, did you say [PERSON_3] will have a word with the, the bank? Because I haven't, I'm not -- no, hang on, it's the reception, sorry. He'll know I'll be in touch, is that what you said? Right. Okay. Well, thank you, and sorry for, for being awkward about it. I'll ring the one on the quote when I'm home, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], just about, um, your benefits file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, that's me... sorry, who? Which company was that again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yeah, it's [COMPANY_A], the, uh, the public benefits office. I'm one of the claims assessors, my name's [PERSON_2]. Well, actually, I should say I'm in the review team, not claims exactly, it's sort of, um, the same department. Anyway, it's just a routine call about your file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh... my file. Sorry, I just woke up, I was having a nap. Which file's that, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, that's fine, sorry to wake you, I'll be quick. It's just your, uh, your main benefits record, the one under, hang on -- let me just pull it up here -- yeah, there's a section that's showing as, um, incomplete, so I just need to go through it with you and get it, you know, confirmed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Incomplete, hm. I mean, I haven't had a letter or anything about that, and I'd have thought they'd send a letter. Uh, my daughter does most of that paperwork anyway, she's usually the one who... sorry, what section? What's it say's missing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, a letter, yeah, that, um, that normally would go out, I'm not sure why it, uh, it might still be in the queue. It's just a, a section of the record, I can't really get into which one until we've done the confirmation, that's sort of how the process works. So if you could just, um, confirm your full name and date of birth for me, we can get it sorted today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, but you've just told me you can't say what's wrong until I tell you things, and that seems the wrong way round, doesn't it? I mean, you rang me. Look, I'm not giving out my birthday to somebody on the phone, I don't even know you. Is there a number I could ring the office back on, or, I don't know, should I just get my daughter to call you? She's better at all this than me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, a callback number, I -- I'd have to check whether I can give that out, I'll, um, have to look into that. And your daughter, well, she can't really speak to the record, it has to be you, it's your file. Look, it's just your name and date of birth, that's all, and it does need doing today, because if the record stays incomplete, uh, it could, it might affect your payments, I mean it could get suspended.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Suspended? Now hang on, you said it was a routine call, and now it's payments getting stopped, that's not routine, is it? And you can't give me a number to ring, which, I mean, that's just odd. Look, I did say earlier I'd never had a letter, but actually I think one did come a while back, I don't know, it'll be in the drawer somewhere. So I'll find that, and I'll ring the number that's on it, and my daughter can sit with me while I do. Right, I'm going to go, I've had enough of this for now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, hang on, someone's just walked past with a trolley, it's a bit loud in here. Right. This is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the assessors on the client side, and I just wanted to check I've got the right person before I go on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hello? Sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie down, give me a second. Who did you say you were? Because yes, that's, that's me, I think, [PERSON_1], but I didn't catch the company, there was a trolley, you said. Is this about the, um, is it about the boiler? Because I've been meaning to ring someone about that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, sorry, it's not the boiler, I'm afraid, I'd, uh, I'd have to leave that one to the plumbers, ha. So, it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], that's the investment firm, we're based out of [CITY_1], and I'm one of the assessors there, which basically means I look over client positions and, um, make sure everything's tidy on our books. And I'm sorry about the lie down, I can ring back if now's not great, it's just, well, it's a fairly routine call, I've got a few of these to get through this afternoon, so, uh, if you've got five minutes, that'd be, that'd be lovely. Hang on, let me just, I've got your name here on the screen, and, yes, [PERSON_1], that's right, so I've definitely got the right person, which is good.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Investment firm. I don't, I mean, I don't think I've got anything with an investment firm, but I've just woken up, so. What's it about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's, that's fine, you don't need to have anything with us as such. It's just, uh, there's a fund coming up, and your name's come through as someone who might, um, be suited to it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, you said before that it was routine, and that you were checking things on your books, tidying up, something like that. But now you're saying I don't have anything with you, so how am I on your books? I'm not, I'm not following. Is it a, are you selling something? Because I'd have thought an assessor wouldn't, I mean, does an assessor ring people up about funds?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, it's not selling, exactly. It's more of an allocation thing, and I've got, sorry, I've got two things open here, so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, uh, that's sort of the same thing, isn't it, an allocation? If you're allocating me something, that's, I mean, that's selling by another name, surely. And you've gone a bit quiet, are you, hello? Are you still there? Sorry, I just, I keep losing my thread, I think the nap's still, anyway. Where did you get my name, actually? Because you said it was on a screen, but I haven't, I don't think I've ever, who gave you my number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, I'm here, I'm here, just, uh, scrolling. Where it came from, right. So it's, well, it's off the, hang on, the referral list, and look, I'm sorry about the, uh, the lie down, that must be, I mean, a nap's a nap, ha. But the actual thing is, the position closes today, and there's a, a really quite strong return on it, much better than you'd see anywhere, and I'd hate for you to miss it just because it's, uh, a Thursday and you've been napping, because, you know, it's gone by five.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Gone by five, today? No, I don't, hang on. You still haven't said what list. A referral list, who referred me? I'm asking who gave you my number, because I didn't give it to anyone, I don't think. And you said routine, and now it closes today, and that's not very routine, is it? Sorry, I'm not being funny, I just, who gave you my number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's, no, look, I can't, the list is, uh, it's just how it's, [PERSON_1], if I could just, the thing is you'd need to, I mean I'd have to check who, and I will, I'll check that, but the position doesn't wait on that, it really doesn't, so if we could just go through the, the next step now, and then, then I'll find out about the list after, that's, that's the usual way, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, that's, that's the wrong way round, isn't it? You find out who gave you my number first, and then, then we talk about steps. I'm not going through any next step with someone who can't tell me where he got my number from, I don't care if it's Thursday or, or what time it closes. If it's gone by five, well, it's gone. Fine. Look, I'm going to go, I'm still half asleep and I'm not doing anything today. If you want to send me something in the post, you can, but I'm not, yeah. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Good. I'm calling from, uh, from [COMPANY_A], I'm a collections officer there, and I'm, well, I'm ringing on behalf of a relative of yours who's, let's say, in a bit of difficulty at the moment and can't come to the phone. There's an outstanding balance on the file, [AMOUNT_1], and it's going to start affecting things for them as of today, so I wanted to reach you before that happens.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, which relative? Because you haven't said who, and, hang on -- [COMPANY_A], what is that exactly? ... No, sorry, put that down, I'm on the phone -- so who is it you're calling about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, I don't have permission to give out the name on this line, that's a privacy matter for them. I can tell you it's someone close to you, and that they asked specifically that this stay between us for now, so, uh, I'd ask you not to go ringing round the family about it. The balance is [AMOUNT_1] against [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's already flagged, so the consequences on their end are, well, they're happening today regardless. I can note that you've queried the company details on the file, but I do need an answer from you this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, go back. You said you're ringing on behalf of a relative, and then you said you can't tell me who because of privacy. So -- how is it private when you're asking me to deal with it? And what did you mean, "it's already flagged"? Flagged where? And the part about not ringing round the family, why would that matter? I mean, if it's real, why can't I just ask them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said "ask them," and I'd stop short of that, because they're not in a position to answer right now, that's partly why I'm the one calling. And "flagged," uh, that's just the status on the file, it's gone to the next stage as of this morning. Look, I can note your objection, that's fine, it's noted, but the balance is [AMOUNT_1] and it doesn't change because the question's been raised. So, can you tell me what you're able to do today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on -- no, put that down, we don't throw it, thank you. ... Sorry. Right. So you won't say who it is, you won't say how I'd check, and they can't be asked. And now you want to know what I can do today? I mean, do about what, exactly? I don't even know whose debt this is. Give me a number for [COMPANY_A], an actual one, and I'll ring the family myself and see.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I can't -- look, the main line goes to a general queue, and it won't have this file on it, so that wouldn't, that isn't going to help you. And I'd, uh, I'd really rather you didn't ring round the family, because it's -- well, it's the sort of thing where once it's out, it can't really be, I mean, it affects them, not me. I've noted you've asked for a number and a name, that's on the file now. The balance is still [AMOUNT_1], and it's still due, so I need to know if you're dealing with it today or not.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not dealing with anything today. You can't tell me who it is, you won't give me a number I can check, and you keep telling me not to talk to my own family. Someone close to me got caught out by something like this last year, so, no. If the company's real, it can write to me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I've noted that. I've noted the objection, and, uh, the file stays open, that's, that part doesn't change. The balance is [AMOUNT_1], it's still due, and the consequences on their end carry on from today regardless, so -- sorry, you're saying you won't deal with it today? Because if you could just, I mean, if you'd stay on the line a moment, I only need to know what you can do, that's all I'm asking, what you're able to do today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said goodbye, I'm not -- no. I'm not staying on. Write to me, and I'll ring my family. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, uh, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the scheduling department at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just, yeah, I'm reaching out because we've got a disconnection order queued for your address within the hour over an unpaid balance, so I wanted to catch you before the crew gets dispatched.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, a disconnection? I'm -- sorry, I didn't, I'm not sure I follow. Disconnection of what, exactly? I thought I'd, well, I thought everything was, um, paid up, but I could be wrong, I'm not very good with all the, the bills and things.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so that's electric service at your address, and I totally understand, it happens, balances slip through, but the order's already in the system under [ACCOUNT_REF] so what I can do right now is get you pointed at clearing the [AMOUNT_1] before the crew rolls out, and I just need to confirm a couple of details first, so if you can just --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, um, sorry, hang on. Which company did you say you were from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, [COMPANY_A], the power company, we're the, well, the billing and scheduling side, so, yeah, anyway, the crew's set to head out within the hour, so about the [AMOUNT_1] -- or, I mean, it might be closer to [AMOUNT_2] once the late fee's added, either way if we can just get that sorted --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh gosh, um, I'm sorry, I'm just, I'm trying to keep up here. So it's the electric, and it's, what was it, [AMOUNT_1], or maybe more now with a late fee? I'm sorry, I'm not very good at this sort of thing, my head's all in a muddle. It's just that I always thought my electric was, well, I thought it was all sorted, I've got it, um, I think it comes out automatically, or my niece set something up once, I can't quite remember. Is there some way I could, I don't know, look at it myself? I mean, I don't want the lights going off, that'd be awful, but I'm also not sure how I'd, I'm sorry, how would I know it's really you? Not that I think it isn't, of course, I'm sure it's, it's only that I'm a bit lost.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you don't need a hotline, I'm already on the line, so, yeah, the, uh, the late fee's separate, that part's just processing, and the crew's set to head out within the hour, so if we could just get that [AMOUNT_1] moving before they roll, I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, I'm still, hang on. Because I thought you said before it might be [AMOUNT_2] once the late fee was added, and now it's separate and it's still processing? I'm sorry, I'm probably getting it muddled. And I didn't, I didn't actually ask for a hotline, I only wondered if there was some way I could look at the bill myself, you know, on my own, or ring the number on it? Is that, would that be all right? I don't want to be any trouble.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so the number on the bill is, well, that goes to the general line, and they'd just, no, listen, the order's already -- look, I'm the scheduling side, I don't see the billing screens, I only see that the crew's queued, so about the [AMOUNT_1] before they roll --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, hang on a moment, there's, um, the kettle's just gone off in the kitchen, I'll only be a second -- right, sorry, I'm back. Where was I? Oh yes. So, you said you're the scheduling side and you don't see the billing screens? But then how do you know about the amount? I'm sorry, that's probably a silly question, it's only that I'm a bit muddled now. I think I'd feel better ringing the number on my bill, if that's all right. I'm sure it won't take long, and then if there is something owing, well, I'll sort it out with them. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, well, the, the figure just comes through with the order, that's, I mean, it's, look, I can't -- okay, so if you'd rather go that way then, uh, that's, that's your call, I've got other accounts in the queue so I'm going to, yeah, I'll let you go, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay. Well, thank you for ringing, and I'm sorry if I was, um, a bother. I'll give them a ring on the number on the bill and see what's what. Bye now, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with -- uh, is this the, the account holder for the parcel registered under [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from the verification desk at [COMPANY_A], my name is [PERSON_2], and, well, I'm calling because there's a consignment currently held at our [CITY_1] sorting node, and it's, it's flagged for a, a customs-adjacent handling reconciliation that needs to be cleared today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, um, a customs-adjacent -- did you say a custody reconciliation? Is this something to do with a custody arrangement? Because I'm, I'm not sure that's, that's me. And who exactly are you with again? I didn't quite catch the company name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not custody, I said customs-adjacent, it's, it's a, a handling classification, nothing to do with, uh, any family matter. And the company is [COMPANY_A], the courier, I'm with their verification desk, which is sort of the, the compliance layer that sits between the depot manifest and the, the final-mile dispatch. So what's happened is, the parcel's carrier-side declaration doesn't reconcile with the, the manifest tier, and it's been held in a, a pending-release status, and I do need to get that cleared before the end of the, the dispatch window today or it's, it gets escalated to, to return-to-sender processing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So that's a lot of terminology, and I'll be honest, none of it's actually told me what the parcel is. What's in it, who's it from, and what's the tracking reference? Because I haven't ordered anything I'm waiting on, as far as I know. And if there's a genuine hold on it, I'd expect that to show up on the courier's own tracking page, so I can just check there. Which, I mean, I'm happy to do -- is there a reference number I should be looking up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, the reference is, uh, [ACCOUNT_REF], though I'd caution you, the public tracking page, it only surfaces the customer-facing status layer, not the, the back-office hold flag, so it may well show, uh, in transit, which is, I mean, that's just the front-end lag. As for the sender and contents, I'm, I'm not authorised to read out the manifest detail over an unverified line, that's, that's data-protection protocol, but what I can say is the hold carries a small handling fee, [AMOUNT_1], and it needs to be settled by phone this afternoon to release the consignment before the window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, no, I'm going to stop you there. You can't tell me who sent it or what's in it, but you can tell me what I owe, and it has to be paid over the phone today. That's backwards. And "the tracking page won't show it" is a convenient thing to say, because it means I can't check anything you've told me. So here's what I'll do. I'll find the courier's customer service number myself, from their official site, and ring them with the reference. If there's really a hold, they'll confirm it. I'm not paying anything on this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, wait, if you ring the general line, the, the frontline agents won't have visibility of the hold flag, they'll just read you the, the customer-facing status, and by then the dispatch window will have, uh, lapsed, and it, it escalates to -- look, I'm not asking you to pay anything this second, I'm simply asking you to, to stay on the line while I, I re-queue the reconciliation, because if you hang up now it, it genuinely cannot be reopened under the same reference, and, uh, that's not me being, being difficult, that's just the, the process architecture.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Every time I say I'll verify it independently, you tell me why that won't work. The general line can't see it, the tracking page can't see it, and the reference dies if I hang up. That's a lot of reasons not to check, and I've heard that pattern before. If the parcel's real, the courier will still be there after I've rung them. I'm ending the call now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, if I could just -- no, no, please, hold on a second, you're, you're mischaracterising the, the escalation pathway, it isn't that the line can't see it, it's that the, the reconciliation token is session-bound, so the moment you, you disconnect, the -- hello? Are you still there? Because I, I really would like to, to walk you through the, the re-queue before it, uh, before it times out, it'll only take, take a moment, I just need you to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's someone at the door -- no, it's fine, just the neighbour's kid retrieving a ball. Anyway. I've already said goodbye once, and "session-bound token" is just one more reason I can't check anything with anyone else. No. I'm going to hang up now and ring the courier myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants over here, and I'm just ringing because you'd registered your CV with us a little while back and I wanted to see if you're still open to hearing about roles, if now's an okay time for a quick chat.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? [COMPANY_A], never heard of them. And I'm in a queue at the moment. Look, what CV? I don't remember registering anything with anyone, so where'd you even get this number from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, totally fair, uh, it's [COMPANY_A], we're a recruitment agency, and I mean, a lot of people sign up through the job boards and forget, it's usually a tick box on the application, so it'd have been, you know, a while back. I won't keep you, I'm only calling to see if you're still looking for work at the moment, yes or no, and then I can tell you a bit about what we've got on, if now's alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, it's not alright, I'm stood here with a basket and the woman in front of me is counting out coppers. And a tick box on a job board isn't me ringing you up, is it? Whatever I ticked, I did not tick "please ring me at four in the afternoon." Honestly, I've had calls like this before, where they start off all friendly with "oh you registered with us," and it turns out they want something off you, so I'm not about to confirm whether I'm looking for work or not looking for work, to you, a stranger. You've not told me where you're based, you've not told me who I'm even supposed to have signed up with, just a name that means nothing. So if you've got a website, or an email, or a proper number, you can send me something and I'll look at it when I'm home. Otherwise I'd rather you took me off whatever list this is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, completely understand, and I'm sorry, I did catch you at a bad moment, I can hear that, uh, but I'll be quick because this one's a bit time-sensitive, it's a remote role, work from home, good pay, no experience needed, and the only thing is the spots for this intake are filling up fast so I wouldn't want you to lose out. And I can absolutely send you something, the thing is the details are sort of on my side to walk you through, so if you could just confirm you're still looking for work, yes or no, then I can get you booked in for the onboarding.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. No, I said send me something, didn't I? An email, a website, a proper number. And now it's "the details are on my side," and spots are filling up, and no experience needed, work from home, good pay. That's every one of them, that is. I'm not confirming anything, yes or no, I'm not getting booked in for anything, and I'm not having a chat about it in a supermarket queue. If you can't put it in writing then I'm not interested, so take me off your list. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, hang on, I'm not trying to -- look, I can send something, of course I can, it's just that the onboarding bit is time-sensitive, there's a small admin cost to clear and then you're started, so if you could just confirm you're still looking for work and I'll get you booked in before the intake closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: An admin cost? You want money off me for a job? No. That's it, we're done. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, no, sorry to have bothered you. Take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, don't hang up yet. Two minutes ago you said you could send me something. What was it you said you'd actually send? And what did you say your company was called again? Because it wasn't a name I'd ever heard.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, I'd send a, uh, no, what I mean is I'd send over the, hang on, it'd be the -- sorry, it's [COMPANY_A], that's the name, [COMPANY_A], and the something would be, well, an info pack, sort of, with the role details and, and the next steps, but the thing is it's easier if I just walk you through it, so if you could just confirm you're still looking, then I can get that moving for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what I thought. You can't even say what you're sending, you're fumbling it, and you're back to "just confirm you're looking" again. That's the third time you've asked me that. No. There's no info pack, there's no walk-through, and I'm not paying any admin cost. Lose this number. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, this is [PERSON_1] from the fraud team at [COMPANY_A]. We've got a, a charge that just came through on your account that doesn't look right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um... oh dear. Sorry, I'm, uh, I'm just not sure I caught that, you said fraud team? From, from which company was it again? Sorry, I'm not very good with this sort of thing, but, um, yes, I'm here, I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no, that's fine. It's [COMPANY_A], the fraud team, I'm a claims assessor here. Um, so what I'm looking at on my screen is, hold on, an attempted charge, it's flagged as, uh, pending review, so we do need to get this sorted fairly quickly before it posts.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, a charge, oh dear. Sorry, I'm a bit muddled, but I thought you said earlier it had already come through, and now it's still pending? Sorry, I'm not very good at following all this. Which, um, which account is it on, do you know?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, sorry, it's, it's attempted, it hasn't actually posted yet. And the account, it's, hang on, the one ending in, no, I'll need you to confirm your details first, just so I know I've got the right person.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: Oh, absolutely, no bother at all, and honestly that's, that's the, the procedurally correct way to do it anyway. If it's a managing agent lodging a statutory servicing request, well, it would've gone onto a, a compliance schedule, so there should be a letter or an email somewhere in your tenancy paperwork, probably mentioning an annual gas safety or, or boiler servicing visit, and a, uh, a contractor reference. If you find it, then ring [PHONE_1], ask for scheduling, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and we can reconcile the two records and, and fix a window that suits you. And if it turns out the agent doesn't recognise it, that's, that's fine too, you just let them know, and we'd close our side without any, any further action. So, yes, take your time, there's no deadline on this call, and I'll, I'll leave it entirely with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, lovely, thank you, that's really kind of you. Um, so, let me just, hang on, I'm writing the number down, I've found a pen, sort of, it's a bit dry, so... mm. Yes. Right. And the, the reference, I'll look for that on the letter and, well, if it's not there I'll just ring the agent instead. Sorry, I'm a bit slow with all this. Thank you for not rushing me, I do appreciate it. Bye for now, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not at all, you're not slow, and, uh, you've been very sensible about it. Just one small thing, I said earlier that the reference wouldn't need reading back, which, well, it won't, but actually it's, it's on the letter itself, so you'd, you'd be matching it on your side, not me asking you for it, if that makes sense. Sorry, I'm, I'm making a hash of explaining that. Anyway, ring the agent first, ring us if it suits, and either way, thank you for your time, [PERSON_1], goodbye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, that's fine, I did understand, you don't need to, I'll just look at the, oh. Sorry, I've cut across you. Yes, goodbye, thank you, and I'll ring the agent first, I think, that'll be easiest. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Uh, my name is [PERSON_1], and I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and I work in the compliance department there. I'm, um, I'm wondering whether you might have about five minutes for a short consumer survey, and, well, I'd rather ask now than have it hang over us later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, a survey? Yeah, I suppose so, sorry, I've got a bit of time. What's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's a perfectly fair thing to ask first. It's a short consumer survey, about everyday household purchasing habits, nothing technical, and, um, it's about five minutes, as I said. I'd just sort of like to get it done while you've got the time, because, well, these things do tend to close out. And, uh, to be clear, it's a short consumer survey, no sales, nothing to buy, and I won't be asking you for any account details or anything of that kind.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, no sales is good. Sorry, hang on, I think that's the kettle -- no, no, it's the neighbour's dog again, sorry. Where was I? Right, yes, household purchases. I'm not very good with the, uh, technical side of things, but if it's just questions, I can try. Go on then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite all right, the dog is, uh, not a problem at all, and it really is just questions, nothing technical, nothing you'd need to look up or -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you there. Before we start, though, I'd welcome it if you wanted to check who I am first, truly, I'd rather you did. You're free to ask me anything about [COMPANY_A] and I'll answer as best I can, and, well, if you'd like to call us back on the number published for the agency, that's entirely your choice. I'd only ask that we, um, that we don't leave it too long, you understand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind of you, but, um, I wouldn't know where to start with checking. Sorry. I'd have to look up a number and I'm not much good at all that. You sound honest enough, though, so, uh, shall we just do the questions? What's the first one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that's, uh, that's very good of you, and I do appreciate the trust, but, hm, I'd actually feel better if you had something to hold me to. So, um, how about this: when you do get a moment, you could ask [COMPANY_A] to confirm that a survey like this one is running, and, er, they'd be able to tell you the, the reference for it, which is [CODE_1], and only the agency itself would have that to give you. No hurry about it, mind, though I'd, well, I'd rather not let it drift. Or, if you'd like, we simply begin with the first question now, which is, um, roughly how many people live in your household?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a reference, I see, I'll maybe do that later, sorry, I'd only lose the bit of paper. Um, so, how many live here, just me really, well, me and my son, he's here most of the time, though he's not home now. Sorry, I said just me, didn't I? It's two of us, then. Is that all right for the first one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Two, yes, that's perfectly all right, thank you. And, um, you said your son's here most of the time, so I'll put that down as two adults, uh, or -- sorry, did you say he's at school? I thought I heard school. No, no, never mind, it doesn't matter much for this one. The next question is, uh, roughly how often do you do the main grocery shop, would you say weekly, or less often than that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I didn't say school, sorry, I don't think I did. He's grown up, he's, um, he works, he's just out at the moment. Sorry, I probably mumbled. And, er, groceries, yes, weekly, usually a Thursday. Although, hang on, I said earlier I wasn't good with numbers and things, didn't I? That wasn't it, I said the technical side, sorry, I get muddled.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, you're not muddled at all, and I'm the one who misheard about school, so that's on me, I do apologise. Weekly, usually a Thursday, that's lovely, I've got that down. And, um, that's really all I needed for this part.
