If you do get a moment later, it'd be sensible to check that reference, [CODE_1], with [COMPANY_A] directly, just so you're comfortable, and I'd, well, I'd rather you did it sooner than later. Thank you ever so much for your time, and, uh, do give the dog next door my sympathy.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, that's it then? Well, that was easy enough, sorry, I thought it'd be longer. Yes, I'll, um, I'll try and ring about that reference, if I can find a bit of paper to write it down. Thank you for ringing, [PERSON_1], and, uh, I'll tell the dog, though I don't think it'll listen. Bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, hello, is that -- sorry, am I speaking to a parent or guardian of [PERSON_1]? It's, uh, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the school office at [COMPANY_A], nothing to worry about at all. I'm just, I mean, I was hoping to sort out why [PERSON_1] got marked absent this morning, because it looks like it might just be a mix-up on our end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Hang on, I'm in a queue. Absent this morning? No, no, I think you've got the wrong -- I mean, [PERSON_1] was in school, I dropped them off myself. Well, actually, it was my neighbour who did the drop-off today, but still, they were there. Why are you ringing me and not the usual number? Which school did you say this was?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's fine, everyone asks that. It's [COMPANY_A], the school office, and this is just the number we have on file for [PERSON_1]. So if your neighbour dropped them off, that probably explains the mix-up, it's a super quick fix.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. You still haven't told me what the quick fix is. What do you actually need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, so, uh, the only thing I need is a yes or no, really. Was [PERSON_1] actually in class this morning, like you said? Because if they were, I just flip the mark from absent to present on our register, and that's, I mean, that's honestly it, ten seconds. And um, you don't need to give me anything else, no details, nothing like that. If you'd rather check with the office first, you can call the number on the school letters, that's totally fine too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, back up a second. You said it's the number you have on file, and you said everyone asks that, but you never actually said which school. You just said the school office and some name I didn't catch. So which school is it? Say the whole name properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yeah, fair enough, that's on me, I rattled through it. It's [COMPANY_A], the full name, and I'm [PERSON_2], I'm in the office there, I look after the, uh, the IT and the attendance system. So, um, I was only trying to be quick for you, since you're stuck in a queue. And honestly, if it's easier, just ring the office on the number from the school letters and ask for me, [PERSON_2], and we can sort it that way, no pressure at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- no, I don't want a bag, thanks -- right. You've just said the same thing again. You still haven't told me the school's name, you've just said [COMPANY_A] twice like I'm supposed to know what that is. So I'm not telling you if my kid was in class or not, not to someone I can't pin down. I'll ring the office myself on the number from the letters. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's completely fair, and honestly that's the right call, [PERSON_1]'s parent, I'd do the same. Ring the office on the letters number, ask for [PERSON_2], and if I'm not at my desk they can sort the register for you there. Sorry about the confusion, and um, sorry for catching you in the queue. Thanks for your time, take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm ringing the office, the number off the letters, not any number you give me. The letters. Right. And I'm not saying anything about whether they were in class, not to you, not now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], just about your file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, that's me... sorry, I was just, uh, having a lie-down. My file? What file's that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, I didn't mean to wake you. It's, uh, your benefits file, the one we opened with you, let me just -- hang on, I've got it up here -- it says here you'd be a, um, new claimant this year? Sorry, no, that's not right, you've been with us a few years. I just need to ask you a couple of quick things about it, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Which company did you say again? I didn't catch that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [COMPANY_A], the benefits office, I'm one of the claims assessors, so -- sorry, did you want me to spell that or, no, it's just that I'm seeing a note on your record here that says it's, uh, incomplete, so I just need to go through it with you while we're on the line, it won't take --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, you said new claimant and then you said a few years, so which is it? I mean, I get letters, I think, from, uh, somewhere about benefits, but I never know which is which. And you still haven't said the company, you just said it's the benefits office. How do I know it's, you know, real? I'd sooner ring you back or something, if you've got a number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, no, the few years, that's the right one, I just, I had another screen open, sorry. And it's [COMPANY_A], I did say that. Look, a callback isn't really, I mean it's not how we do it, the record's flagged and it has to be confirmed over the phone today, uh, because if it isn't, it can go to, um, suspension, and then you'd be waiting weeks to get it sorted. So if I could just take your full date of birth and, uh, your [ACCOUNT_REF], we can get it done in a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, I don't think so. You can't give me a number to ring but you want my date of birth and everything, and it's today or it's suspended? That doesn't sit right with me. If it's a real thing I'll get a letter, or I'll ring the number on the letters I've got, wherever I put them. Sorry, I'm not, I'm not giving that out over the phone. I'm going to go now, all right? Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, wait, please don't hang up, I'm just, I'm only trying to help you here. Look, I'd have to check about the number, I'll have to find out, but it's, uh, it's really just your date of birth, that's all I need, and then it's done and you don't have to think about it again. If it goes to suspension it's, I mean, I can't stop that once it's flagged, so it really would be better to do it now, while we're on the line --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you said it was my date of birth and the [ACCOUNT_REF] before, and now it's just the date of birth, so which is it? And before that I'm new, then I'm not new. I'm sorry, love, but that's too many changes. If it's real, it'll keep till I've found the letter and rung the proper number. I'm hanging up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, hang on, I haven't, I mean -- sorry, are you still there? It's, uh, it's a very simple thing, honestly, and I did say both at the start, I'm sure I did, so -- so that's not, that's not a change, that's just, um, how the form reads. Please, if you could just stay on, because I really can't, I mean once it's flagged I can't hold it, and then it's, uh, it's on you, really, if it...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on a sec, the kettle's... no, that's the neighbour's telly, the walls are so thin in this place. Sorry. Right, what was I... oh yes. No, you did not say both at the start, you said "just a couple of quick things", and now it's on me if it's suspended? That's not on me, love. I'm going to find my letters and ring the number on them. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Um, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one second, someone's just walked past my desk with -- right, sorry. Yes. I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], my name's [PERSON_2], I'm in the claims assessment team here. I just wanted to check I've got the right contact details on file for you, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh, uh -- sorry, I just woke up, give me a sec. Yeah, that's, I mean, that's me, I think. Who did you say you were with again? Company-something? Because I've got a sister who does claims, well, not claims, she does something with, uh, insurance forms, so I'm not sure I -- what is it you're checking?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, sorry to catch you at a bad time. It's [COMPANY_A], we're an investment firm, so we're, um, not insurance exactly, although the claims side does overlap a bit with that, sort of. What it is, we hold records for a lot of people who've had some past dealings with, uh, funds and managed accounts, and every so often we go through and confirm the contact details are current. It's really just housekeeping, I've got your name here on the screen, and, hang on, an address in [CITY_1], and a phone number ending, well, I won't read it all out, but I just need you to tell me if that all looks right to you. Sorry, I know it's a bit early to be doing this, I'm only about halfway through my list today, so I'm trying not to keep anyone too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I don't really remember dealing with any investment firm, to be honest. Why are you the one telling me what's on the screen, and not me telling you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, that's fair. It's just how the, um, the form's set up, I think.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but -- sorry, going back a bit, you said it was claims, and then you said it was an investment firm, and then something about funds and managed accounts. I'm still not sure what you mean by "past dealings." Dealings with who? Because I honestly can't think of anything, and I've only just woken up so, I mean, maybe I'm missing something.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, uh, the dealings bit, I'd have to check what's actually logged against your name. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, uh... hello? You still there? I mean, you can't tell me what it's actually about, but you want me to say if the address is right. That's, I don't know, that's a bit backwards, isn't it? Like, if you've got a file with my name on it you'd think there'd be something in it. Sorry, I'm not being funny, I'm just, uh, still sort of waking up and none of this is, it's not adding up for me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, you said it's a bit backward? No, no, there's nothing wrong with the funds, they're performing well, that's actually, I mean, that's partly why I'm ringing. There's a position that's closing today, and I think, honestly, given your history with us, you'd want to hear about it. It's, um, it's well ahead of what the usual savings products pay, and I'd hate for you to miss it just because the paperwork side is slow.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, no, I said backwards, as in, you ringing me up to tell me what's on my file. I didn't say anything was wrong with any funds. And now it's a position closing today? A minute ago it was housekeeping, you were just checking my address. I mean, which is it? And I still don't have any history with you, like I said, I don't remember any, so what history? I haven't got any funds, I don't think. Why would I have funds?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, hang on, hang on, it's both, it's, the address check and the position, they're the same file, I just -- look, the position, it's only open until close of business today, and I can't, I mean once it's gone it's gone, so if we could just, can I take you through how it works? It's quite quick.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I don't think so, no. You've told me it's housekeeping, then it's claims, then it's funds I've got history with, and now it's something that closes today, and you still can't tell me what any of it's actually about. That's, I mean, that's a lot of changing. If I've got something with you, send it to me in the post and I'll look at it when I'm properly awake. I'm not going through any position over the phone, I don't even know who you are. Right, so, thanks, but, uh, I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this -- uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Good. This is a collections officer calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm, well, I'm actually calling on behalf of a relative of yours, [PERSON_2], who isn't able to speak right now. There's an outstanding balance of [AMOUNT_1] on file, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's, it needs to be dealt with today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on a sec -- [PERSON_2]? Why can't they talk to me themselves? And what did you say the company was again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. Collections department. And [PERSON_2] is in a situation right now where they can't come to the phone, that's all I'm able to say on that. I'd keep this between us for the moment, it's, uh, it's not something that helps them if it gets passed around the family. The balance is [AMOUNT_1], and as it stands the account goes to the next stage tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, go back a second. You said you're calling on behalf of [PERSON_2], but now you're a collections officer? Which is it? Are you working for them, or for the company they supposedly owe? And why would it hurt them if I told someone? That's sort of a strange thing to ask.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said who I'm working for, the company they supposedly owe -- no, I wouldn't say supposedly, the balance is on the file, [AMOUNT_1], that's not in dispute on our end. And I didn't say it'd hurt them, I said it doesn't help. Look, I can note your objection on the file if you'd like, but it doesn't change the position. The account moves to the next stage tomorrow and [PERSON_2] is the one who deals with that, not me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, put that down, I said not now -- sorry, uh, my kid. Okay. So you said [PERSON_2] is the one who deals with it, but then why are you ringing me? That doesn't add up. And honestly, "keep it between us" and "it happens tomorrow"... I've heard that kind of thing before. Can you just give me a number for the company so I can ring them myself?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm ringing you because, well, because -- no, look. [PERSON_2] gave your name as someone who could, uh, who might be in a position to help with this. That's the extent of what I can tell you. As for a number, I can note that you've asked for one, I'll put it on the file, but the position doesn't change, the balance is [AMOUNT_1] and the account moves tomorrow. If you ring around and it takes time, that's, I mean, that's your decision, but the stage change doesn't wait for it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you won't give me a number? That's, I mean, that's the one thing I asked for. A real company gives you a number. So no, I'm not going to help with anything, not on this call. If [PERSON_2] wants something from me, they can ring me themselves. And if there's really a balance, the company can send it in writing. Okay? I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, I'll note that on the file. But the balance is [AMOUNT_1], it's on file, and the account moves to the next stage tomorrow, that's, that doesn't change. [PERSON_2] can't come to the phone, I've said that, and I'd still, uh, I'd still keep this between us. Hello? Are you still -- the position is the same, [AMOUNT_1], tomorrow. I'm just, I'm telling you where things stand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm -- I'm not doing this. I'm hanging up now, and I'm going to ring [PERSON_2] myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. I'll note it on the file. Still [AMOUNT_1], still tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said goodbye already, I'm not discussing it any more. And I'll tell you what's bothering me, since you're still on the line. You couldn't tell me why you were ringing me and not them, you wouldn't give me a number, and you kept telling me not to mention it to anyone. Anyone genuinely chasing a debt wants it sorted properly, on paper, with a way to check who they are. You wanted it kept quiet and sorted today. So no. I'm going to ring [PERSON_2] on the number I already have, and if there's a real balance, the company can write to me. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with -- sorry, is this the, uh, the account holder associated with the parcel reference [ACCOUNT_REF]? This is [PERSON_1], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling because, well, there's a consignment currently held at our [CITY_1] depot pending a handling-tier reconciliation, and it, it really does need to be resolved today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a, a handling-tier what? Reconciliation, did you say? No -- hang on, you said "consignment," I think. I haven't ordered anything that I'm aware of. And, uh, who exactly is this, again? I didn't catch the company name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, so, [PERSON_1], verification specialist, [COMPANY_A], the courier. And "handling-tier reconciliation" is just, uh, it's the internal flag where the declared tariff band on the consignment doesn't match the depot's intake classification, so it sits in a hold queue until the delta is cleared. It's quite routine, honestly. I'd, I'd really like to close it out before the end of the day, because after the cut-off the hold escalates to a return-to-origin status and, well, that's a much longer process.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so that's a lot of vocabulary for what sounds like a parcel being held. Let me ask it plainly. What is in this consignment, who is it addressed to, and who sent it? Because I still haven't ordered anything, and you haven't told me my name, so I don't know how you've decided I'm the account holder. Also, what's the actual delta? Is that a fee? Because if the next thing you say is that I need to pay something to release it, I'd rather hear that now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, so, fair question, and I appreciate the, the directness. The contents field is, uh, it's masked on my screen at this verification stage, so I can't read that out, and the sender and addressee details sit under a separate access tier, which is, I mean, a data-protection thing, I'm not permitted to disclose those until the account holder is authenticated. As for the delta, yes, it's a small handling fee, [AMOUNT_1], that's the, the reconciliation adjustment, and it can be settled right here on the call via the, uh, the expedited remittance channel, which avoids the standard billing cycle. But, um, again, the hold lapses at close of day, so I'd need to initiate that within the next few minutes, otherwise it auto-escalates and I, I genuinely can't reverse it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So let me make sure I've got this straight. You can't tell me what's in it, who sent it, or who it's addressed to, but you need me to authenticate first, and you also need me to pay a fee over the phone within a few minutes. That's the wrong way round. If you were a courier with a real parcel, you'd have the addressee's name on that screen, and you'd have rung the number on the label, which I'd expect to be my name, not just an account reference. I'm not paying anything through an expedited remittance channel on an inbound call. If there's a genuine parcel, there'll be a tracking number, and I'll look it up myself on the courier's own site, which I'd find independently, not through anything you give me. If it goes back to origin, then it goes back. Thank you for your time, but I'm ending this call now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, wait, if you'd just let me -- the authentication layer isn't something I can bypass, it's, it's a tiered-access protocol, the addressee field is literally not rendered until the, the downstream validation clears, and that's by design, so it's not, I mean, it's not the wrong way round, it's, uh, sequenced. And if you look it up independently you'll only see the standard manifest status, not the reconciliation hold, because that's flagged at the depot-intake level, which isn't, sorry, which isn't surfaced on the public-facing --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. And that's the part that settles it, honestly. You've just told me that anything I check independently won't show the hold, so the only place I can see it is on this call, where you're also the one asking for money. That's a closed loop. A real hold shows up on the tracking page. I've said what I'll do, which is look it up myself, and that stands. I'm not discussing it further. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, sorry, no, hang on, I'm, I'm not asking you to take anything on trust, the reconciliation flag sits at a different layer to the, the manifest, which is exactly why I'm -- look, if you just, if you give me ninety seconds I can walk you through the, uh, the escalation window, because once it rolls over to return-to-origin I genuinely can't, I mean there's no, there's no mechanism to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, there's, uh, someone at the door -- no, it's, it's just the post, hang on. Right. I'm back. And no, I'm not giving you ninety seconds. I've heard the escalation window three times now, and each time the explanation gets longer but nothing in it is something I can check. I've told you what I'll do, and I'll do it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, before you go, two turns ago you said a real hold would show on the tracking page, and, I mean, that's, that's partly where the, the confusion is, because you've sort of conflated the public manifest with the, uh, the intake layer, so could you, could you just clarify what exactly you'd expect the page to display, so I can, so I can tell you whether it would, would surface there or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not going to tell you what I'd expect the page to show, because you'd just tell me it's a different layer, and -- no, I'm not doing that. Right, that's enough. I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, I, I understand, but you've, uh, you've sort of reframed what I was saying, because I never -- the layers aren't, I'm not trying to, sorry, I'm just trying to, to keep the reference open on my side, so if you, if you do change your mind, the, the hold stays live until, uh, until close of --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, I've said goodbye three times now and you're still talking, so let me be clear, and then I'm going. I'm not going to change my mind, and I'd rather you didn't keep anything open on my behalf, because there's nothing for me to come back to. A genuine courier with a genuine parcel doesn't need me on the phone this afternoon. They'd leave a card, or send a notice to the address on the parcel, with my name on it, and a tracking number I could check on their own site. You've given me a reference I can't verify, a fee I'd have to pay by phone, a deadline I can't test, and a layer of the system that conveniently only exists on this call. Any one of those I might let slide, but all four together is a pattern. And no, I'm not asking you to prove anything, I'm just telling you where I've landed. If I've got it wrong and there is a parcel, it'll sort itself out through the proper channels. That's it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good morning, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants over here, and I'm just following up because you'd registered your CV with us a little while back and we've got a few remote openings that, um, seemed like a decent match, so I just wanted to see if now's an okay time for a quick chat?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Who is this -- what company? And hang on, you said you're a scheduling assistant, so what's that got to do with jobs? I'm in a queue, I've got about thirty seconds.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sure, no problem, I'll be quick. It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], we're a recruitment agency, and scheduling assistant just means I'm the one who books the intro calls with our placement team, so I'm not interviewing you or anything, I just find you a slot. You'd registered your CV with us a while back, and a couple of remote roles have come up, so all I need is thirty seconds to check you're still looking and then I can put you down for a proper conversation, are you still open to remote work at the moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on, I don't remember registering my CV with anyone called that. I've put it on a couple of job sites over the years, sure, but I couldn't tell you which, so that doesn't mean much. And I'll be honest with you, I got stung once by someone ringing out of the blue about work, so I'm not just going to say yes I'm looking and let you put me down for something. What I'd want to know is what site I'm supposed to have registered on, and what's the actual company name again, because you've said it but I didn't catch it properly with the beeping going on here. And if it's real, how come you're ringing me rather than just emailing? I mean, that's how normal agencies do it, isn't it? Anyway, I'm nearly at the till, so go on, answer me that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, completely fair, and it's [COMPANY_A], that's A as in, um, [COMPANY_A], recruitment agency, and honestly the CV would've come through one of the partner job boards we pull from, I don't have the exact one in front of me, but I can have that confirmed on the placement call, and we do email as well, it's just that the roles fill fast so the team likes a quick voice contact first, so what I'd do is pencil you in for a slot today or tomorrow and the placement team will walk you through everything, the pay, the hours, the setup, it's genuinely a good one, fully remote, no experience needed, starts almost straight away, so are you free this afternoon or is tomorrow better?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on, you still haven't said which site. I asked which site and what the company's called and you've just said the name back at me, which I couldn't catch properly anyway. Which job board? You must have it, you rang me. And no experience needed, starts straight away, that's the bit that bothers me, because real jobs don't sound like that, do they? I asked why you're not emailing and you've said the team likes a voice call, which is no answer. So go on, which site, and spell the company name for me properly, because I'm not booking anything with someone I can't even look up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, so the name's [COMPANY_A], I can send that over in writing, and the board is one of our partner ones, I'd have to check which, but look, the roles themselves are genuine, the only thing is there's a small onboarding cost that gets cleared before the start date, it's just [AMOUNT_1], and that covers your equipment setup and the paperwork, so once that's sorted you're in and working, and I'd hate for you to lose the slot because these do go quickly, so can I put you down for this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, there it is. A cost to start? No. No, that's it, I'm done. A real job doesn't charge you to work, and that's exactly what I got stung with last time. You couldn't tell me the site, you couldn't spell your own company, and now it's pay up before you start. If you've really got something, put it in writing, email me the details and I'll look you up myself. But I'm not booking anything and I'm not paying anyone. Don't ring me again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, fair enough, the slot's only held till end of day though.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Held till end of day, I don't care, I'm not -- actually, hang on, one thing. Two goes back you said the CV came through a partner job board and you'd have it confirmed on the placement call. Confirmed by who? Because if you can't tell me now, who's supposed to know? Go on. No, actually, forget it, don't answer, you'll just say something else vague. I'm not paying and I'm not booking. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Confirmed by the, um, the placement team, they'd have the -- no, sorry, what I mean is it'd be on the file, and the file's with, with the team, so if you just let me put you down for a quick call this afternoon, it's only the one slot and then you can ask them all of it yourself, and I really wouldn't want you to miss out, so shall I say three o'clock?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: The team, the file, the team. You're going round in circles. You still can't tell me one thing I can check, and I already said no. No slot, no three o'clock, nothing. Right, I'm at the till now, so I'm going. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm with the fraud team at [COMPANY_A]. We've got a, um, a charge that was just attempted on your account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Um, yes, this is, uh, this is [PERSON_1], yes. Sorry, did you say fraud? A charge, on my account? Oh dear, I, I'm not sure I caught the name of the company, could you say that again for me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, yeah, it's [COMPANY_A], the fraud team, I'm a, uh, claims assessor there. So the charge, let me just, hang on, it's showing here for [AMOUNT_1], and it came up as, um, attempted, so it hasn't gone through yet. But I do need to get this sorted with you right now, because, well, the window on it is pretty short.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay. Sorry, I'm, I'm a bit lost, I'm not very good with all this. You said fraud team a minute ago, and now it's a claims assessor? I don't, is that the same thing? And you said it's attempted, but then it's got a window, so has it gone through or not? I'm sorry, I just want to be sure I've got it right, I'd like to help.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, same thing, it's, uh, one department. And it hasn't gone through, no. Sorry, I just, I need to verify a few details with you first, that's the process.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, one department, sorry. But, um, which company did you say it was again? I only ask because I didn't quite catch it, and I'd, I'd like to know who I'm talking to, if that's alright. And, sorry, when you say verify details, what details do you mean? Because I'm not sure I should just, I mean, how would I know it's, um, how can I check it's really you? Sorry, that's probably a silly thing to ask.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it's not silly, that's, uh, that's fair. It's [COMPANY_A]. Um, and the details, it's just, you know, standard, your full name, date of birth, the usual security stuff. Look, I really do need to get through this with you now, because if the charge goes through, it, it could be a problem for the account, and then you'd have to, uh, deal with all of that afterwards.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I don't want any problem with the account, sorry. It's just, you've rung me, haven't you, and now you're asking me for my name and my date of birth, and I don't, um, I don't quite know how to do that safely. Is there a, a number I could ring you back on? Or, I could ring the number on the back of my card, couldn't I, and ask them? Sorry, I do want to help, I just, I'd feel better checking first.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, yeah, so, a number. Let me just, hang on, I'll have to check what, what's the right one to give you, because it's not, um, it's not like I have a direct line on my screen, it's sort of a, a queue system. And I mean, you could ring the number on your card, of course you could, that's, that's not a bad idea, but the thing is, if you ring in cold you'll probably end up in a general queue, and, uh, I don't know how long that'd be, could be a while, and this one's, well, I did say the window is short, so by the time you got through to someone, it may, it may well have been processed, and then it's, it's a whole different procedure, a claim, and that takes weeks, honestly. So I'd, I'd really rather we just did the verification now, while I've got your file open. I mean, I'll, I'll find out about the callback number, but, uh, can we just start with your full name and date of birth, and then, then we'll go from there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, a whole different procedure, you said a, a claim, and it takes weeks? Oh dear, I don't want that. But, um, you said you've got my file open, so, so you must already have my name, mustn't you? Sorry, I just, I don't understand why you'd need me to tell you it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I do have it, I have your name, it's just, it's the, uh, the security process, I need you to confirm it back to me. That's, that's the process. I mean, I've got your file here, but I still have to, you know, go through the verification with you, it's, it's just how it works. Sorry, I'm, I'm just trying to, um, get this done before the window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Sorry, I think I'll, I'll just ring the number on my card myself. Thank you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, okay, well, I mean, um, if that's what you'd rather, that's, that's your choice, but I can't, I can't say what happens with the, with the charge if, uh, anyway. Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, I'll just ring the number on my card, like I said. Thank you for ringing, though, I do appreciate it. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye then, sorry again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, sorry, one more thing, I, I said the charge was pending but, um, it's actually, it might've already, no, hang on. Never mind. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right. Well, I'll sort it out with the card people. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling regarding the regional draw, and your name has come up as a confirmed winner, so I need to verify a few details with you today. Is this [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Who is this again? Hang on, I've got something on the hob -- um, yes, that's me, I think. A draw, did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, a regional draw. [PERSON_1], security operations, [COMPANY_A]. Your entry was drawn and the prize is flagged for release, but I can't hold it open indefinitely, so I need your full name and date of birth confirmed on this line, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, my full name and my date of birth? Um, hang on, let me just turn this down, it's going to catch. Right. The thing is, I don't remember entering any draw, I really don't. I mean, I do put my name down for things sometimes, you know, at the shops, or there was a leaflet that came through, I think, but I couldn't tell you which one. And you're saying security operations, so is that, what, like a bank? Or a shop? I didn't catch the company name properly, sorry, I was stirring. What was it again? And why would I need to say my birthday to you, when you rang me? Shouldn't you already have it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one moment, I've got a colleague at my desk -- no, carry on, I'm here. [COMPANY_A]. We're a promotions agency, not a bank, not a shop. Entries come in through a number of retail partners, which is why you won't recall the specific one. Now, the date of birth is standard verification before release, and I'd rather not go through the whole process twice, so if we could just confirm it now, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, you said two things there and I've lost the first one. Before that, you said the prize was "flagged for release" and you couldn't hold it open. Open until when? Is it today? And what's the prize, actually? You haven't said what I've won. And, sorry, what was your name again, [PERSON_1]? I'd like to write it down, I've got a pen somewhere, hang on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_1], I did say that, and I'd appreciate it if we could keep to the process, because every time we stop and start I have to log it. The release window is, uh, it's time-limited, it closes shortly, there's a cut-off on our end and once it passes the draw gets reallocated to the next entrant, which is standard for regional draws like this. As for the prize itself, that's confirmed to the winner after verification, I'm not authorised to state it before that stage, it's a compliance matter, it protects you as much as us. And I've explained the company, I've given you my name, so I'd ask you to stay with me here, the sooner we finish verifying the sooner this is off your hands and on its way to you. So, the date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you won't say what the prize is, but I'm to give you my birthday. That doesn't sit right, sorry. I'll leave it, I think.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I -- look, that's not, I mean, it's your decision, but the cut-off doesn't move for -- no, hang on. If you'd just let me, I can, uh... Right, I can't hold this any longer, I've got other winners to get through. If you change your mind you'll have to go through the usual channels, and I can't say how long that will take. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, the pan's spitting, sorry -- there. Right. Well, if it's real, I expect they'll write to me, won't they? Yes. I'll wait for that. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, hello, this is [PERSON_1] calling from collections at [COMPANY_A], I'm looking at an account that's been double-billed, [AMOUNT_1] twice on the same -- no, sorry, let me just -- the subscription renewal went through twice, and that refund has to be arranged live while we're on the phone, so I need you to stay with me here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, hi -- I'm driving, I've got you on speaker and the reception's kind of patchy, so I might, I might cut out. Who, who did you say you were again? Collections? I thought, I mean, I didn't think I owed anyone anything, so a refund sounds... good? But I'm, uh, I'm not sure what company you said.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [PERSON_1], collections, [COMPANY_A], the software retailer. And no, you don't owe us anything, that's the point, it's an overbilling, [AMOUNT_1] charged twice against the one renewal. Hang on, sorry, someone's -- [PERSON_2], I'll be two minutes -- right, sorry. So the refund window on this closes today, and once it closes the duplicate charge just stays on the account, so we need to get it sorted while you're on the line. Are you somewhere you can pull over, or sit down at a computer?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, no, I can't really pull over, I'm on a stretch of road with, with nowhere to stop, and I'm sorry, I know that's probably annoying. And I, I don't think I even have a subscription with, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? So I'm a bit confused. Why does the computer thing matter for a refund? Couldn't it just go back onto my card, or, or whatever I paid with? Sorry, I'm probably being slow about this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It can't just go back to the card, not on this one. The system needs the session open on your end to release it. And the account shows you as a subscriber, so that's the file I've got. I can note that you dispute it, but the window's still closing today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a, a lorry right up behind me, I think he wants to get past -- okay, okay, he's going, sorry. Um, what was I -- right, the session. I don't, I don't really understand that. Why would you need something open on my end to give me money back? That's, that sounds backwards to me, usually it just, you know, goes back to the card. And I still don't have a subscription with you, so I think, I think I'd rather look into it myself, if that's okay? Is there a number I could call you back on, or, or a way I can check this is really [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, so, yeah, I can note that on the file. Noted, you'd rather look into it yourself. Thing is, the number I'm on is a direct line, it's not -- it doesn't take inbound, so there's no callback. Uh, you could check with the main desk, but the refund still lapses at close today, that's just how the window works. So, um, I'd, I'd rather we finish it now, while I've got the account up. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I'm still here, sorry, the signal dipped for a second. But, um, no inbound? That's, that's a bit odd, isn't it? You called me, and I can't call you back, and it all has to be done today, right now... I'm sorry, that just makes me, makes me really nervous. I don't want to be rude, I really don't, but I think I'm going to, to hang up and check with the, the main desk myself, like you said. If the refund's real, it'll still be there, won't it? Sorry. Thanks, I suppose. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang up on the, sorry, did you say the main desk is closed? No, no, it's open, that's not -- look, the lapse is settled for close of business, that's not something I can move. I've put your objection on the file, and I'll just, uh, I'll keep the account open on my side in case you -- hello? You still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hello? Yeah, I'm here, sorry, I said I'm going to hang up now. I'm going to check with the main desk myself, like I said. I never said it was closed, I, I just said I'd check. And if the refund's real, it'll still be there tomorrow, won't it? So, yeah. Sorry. I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1] with security operations at [COMPANY_A], compliance team. Sorry, hang on -- uh, someone's just walked in with a stack of files -- okay, I'm back. I'm calling about a routine suitability review on the investment account you hold with us, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and I need a few minutes of your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi there! Sorry, you caught me out in the garden, I've got the phone on loudspeaker 'cause my hands are covered in soil. Um, a suitability review, okay -- is that something I'm supposed to be expecting? I don't think I got a letter or anything, but then I'm terrible with post. Which company did you say you were with again? I didn't quite catch it over the, uh, the birds, there's a blackbird going absolutely mad over here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. Your brokerage, the one that holds the account. And no, you wouldn't necessarily have had a letter, these reviews are periodic, they're, I mean, they're required of us, so I'd just like to get through the --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh right, right, okay, yeah, that sounds familiar enough, I do have an account with a brokerage, I just can't always remember the exact name, ha. Hang on, let me just move this trowel -- okay. So what does a suitability review actually involve? Is it like a questionnaire, or, I mean, do you need me to do something? Only I'm a bit mucky at the moment, so I can't go hunting for paperwork. Although I suppose if you've got my account reference there you already know all about it, don't you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, it's mostly confirming that what's in the account still fits your circumstances, your goals, how much risk you're comfortable with, that sort of thing. I'm not selling you anything and I'm not recommending any changes, that's not what this is. And look, you don't need any paperwork. I can read back the holdings as they appear on your own statement, and you can check them against it, or -- actually, if you'd rather, I can send the whole review in writing and you can complete it whenever you're not up to your elbows in soil.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's nice of you, the writing thing, that'd suit me better actually. Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a robin on the fence, he does this, he watches me dig for worms, cheeky little thing. Right, where was I. Yeah, so if you send it in writing, where would that come to, my email or the post? Because I'm not sure which address you've got for me, and honestly, I've moved once or twice, so, uh, how would I know it's actually from you lot and not, you know, somebody else?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and honestly, good for you for asking it. So it goes to whatever contact address we already hold on file for the account, I'm not going to read that out to you and I won't ask you to give me a new one over the phone. If you've moved, update it the way you normally would, through the login on [URL_1] or the number on the back of your statement, not through me. And that's really the answer to your other question, too. Don't take my word that it's us. Hang up, find a number for [COMPANY_A] you trust, from a statement or the official site, call that, and ask them whether a suitability review is open on your account. They'll be able to tell you. If it's real, it'll be there, and I'll have lost nothing, because there's nothing I need from you today. No payment, no codes, no logging into anything. If the written review does arrive, it'll just ask you to confirm things you can see for yourself in your own statement. And if it asks for anything beyond that, well, that's not us, so ignore it. Sorry, that was a long answer, but you did ask.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's a perfectly good answer, I like that, you're not rushing me. Honestly it's the first time anyone's told me to hang up and ring them back, usually it's the other way round, ha. Right, so what I'll probably do is, once I've washed my hands and had a cuppa, dig out a statement and give the proper number a ring, just to see if there's anything open on the account. Is that all right? I'm not being rude, am I? I mean, you did say there's nothing you need from me today, so I don't suppose it matters if I ring them first.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not being rude, that's, I mean, that's exactly what I'd -- well, it's what I'd recommend, honestly. Ring them first, have your cuppa, and if the review's open they'll confirm it, and if you'd rather do it all in writing, the letter will come to the address we hold. Either way there's nothing owed from you today. Right, so, I'll note on the file that you've declined to continue by phone, and, uh, enjoy the garden. Mind the robin.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you'll note it on the file that I've declined? Oh dear, I haven't declined anything, I'd never decline a, a, whatever it is, I'm only going to ring them first! Hang on, did you say mind the robin? Oh, I will, ha, he's a cheeky one. Right, anyway, I'll wash my hands, have my cuppa, and ring the number off my statement, and if there's a review open then we'll all be happy. Thanks ever so much for being so patient with me, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor over at the [COMPANY_A] helpdesk, I'm calling about the ticket you opened this morning, the one about, uh, the login issue on your -- no, sorry, go ahead, you were saying?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- hang on, I was literally asleep, I wasn't saying anything. Ticket? I didn't open a ticket this morning, I don't think, I mean I was at my sister's for a bit and then -- who did you say this was again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, [PERSON_1], regional supervisor, [COMPANY_A] helpdesk. Ticket's under your name, so maybe check your work email, it'd have the reference.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'm not near, I mean -- my work email's on the, no, I'd have to -- look, I'm not even sure I... hang on. You said the login issue, but you didn't say what login, did you? You started to say "on your" and then you stopped, so how would you know what... I mean, if it's my ticket, you'd know what it was about, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, hold on, you're saying I stopped at "on your," and I did, because I was checking the screen, that's all. But look, you said you want to know who escalated it? [PERSON_2] on your floor, she flagged it to us around nine, and the reference is [CODE_1]. Honestly, I'm a little surprised I'm having to prove myself here, this is routine procedure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, I didn't say I wanted to know who escalated it, I said, uh, who you were. And [PERSON_2]? I mean, there's a [PERSON_2] but she's not on my floor, she's, no, hang on, I don't even work from the office today, I told you I was at my sister's. Look, you keep saying it's routine, but I still don't know what the login thing actually is, and I'm not giving you anything, I'm just, I'm tired, so can you just tell me what you actually need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, fair, I did get ahead of myself there, and, uh, so -- right, so what I actually need is just ten minutes where I can connect to your machine and clear the stuck session on the ticket, and, um, I know that sounds like a lot when you're half asleep. But I'd rather you not read anything out to me. If you'd rather verify first, no problem at all, you can log a callback request through the internal portal and I'll ring you back once it's showing on my side. Does that work?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Connect to my machine? No, see, that's -- I mean, I'm not even at it, it's at home on the desk and I'm at my sister's, well, I was, I'm back now, I think, I just woke up on the sofa and honestly I can't tell you what day it is half the time. But no, I wouldn't do that anyway, not with someone who rang me out of the blue, because we had that thing at work, a training thing, where they said never let anyone get on your computer unless you rang them first. So, uh, the callback thing, the portal, I don't know where that is, I don't use it, I'd have to ask somebody, and that's sort of the point, isn't it? If it's a real ticket then it'll still be there tomorrow. So I'm going to ring the helpdesk number on, I don't know, the back of my pass or the intranet, and ask them, and if you're who you say you are, that'll be fine, won't it? Okay? Right. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fine, honestly, that's the right call. Ring the number on the intranet, give them the ticket reference and mention [PERSON_1], and we'll sort it from there. Sorry for the early start.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, so the intranet, or the pass, one of the two, I'll ring that one. Not the number you'd give me, I mean, I'm not saying you were going to, I just, yeah, I'll look it up myself. And it's not early, it's the afternoon, I only dozed off. Anyway, I'll ring them, the proper helpdesk, and see if there's a ticket at all. Bye now, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, look it up yourself, that's what I said, use the intranet number, not one from me. And, uh, sorry, afternoon, right, I did say early, my mistake. If there's no ticket under your name, then it's probably a mix-up on our side, a crossed wire, and I'll sort it out here, no harm done. Okay, so, you ring them, I'll leave it with you, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, I'll ring them. Though, uh, I think you said earlier it was my work email I should check for the reference, and now it's just ring the number and give them the reference, and I haven't got a reference, have I, because I never saw one. Whatever, I'll just ask them if there's anything under my name. Right, bye then, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, I -- sorry, I made that more tangled than it needs to be. You don't need a reference at all, just ask them if there's anything open under your name, and if there isn't, that's on us, a crossed wire, and I'll chase it from my end. Honestly, I'd rather you checked than sat there wondering, so, yeah, go and ring them. Take care, and sorry for waking you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah. I'll ring them. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is [PERSON_1] with security operations at [COMPANY_A] -- no, no, I'll stop you there, this isn't a bad-news call. It's about your monthly gift, the one that lapsed back in, uh, back in the spring. We just want to thank you for it and ask whether you'd consider renewing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh -- sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on, give me a second. Um... security operations? And a monthly gift, sorry, who did you say you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sure, take your time. [PERSON_1], security operations, [COMPANY_A]. The charity. You gave to us monthly for a good while, and I know "security operations" sounds odd coming from a charity. It's the team that looks after our donor records and the systems behind them, so when a regular gift stops, we're the ones who check that it stopped because you chose to stop it, and not because of a card problem or a glitch on our end. That's all this is. I'm not calling about anything wrong with your account, and I'm not asking you for any card details or codes on this call. I'm calling to say thank you, because that support did real work, and to ask whether you'd want to pick it up again. If you would, there's a proper way to do it through our website, [URL_1], and you wouldn't have to tell me anything over the phone. But look, if now's not good, with the pan and everything, just say so. I'd rather you got your dinner done than listen to me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Oh, hang on, I've turned it down. Um, I don't think it was a charity, though. I thought you said at the start it was a... what was it, a company? Security something. And I don't, I mean, I'm not sure I ever gave monthly to anyone. Or I did, once, maybe? I don't know. Which charity did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, [COMPANY_A]. That's the name. And it is a charity. Security operations is just the department I work in, not who we are. I probably said it badly at the start, I did go in a bit fast. And I said the gift lapsed in the spring, uh, actually, I've got it in front of me, and it's earlier than that, so I had that slightly wrong. It was the winter. But that's what our records show, a monthly gift under your name that stopped, and that's the only reason I'm calling. Now, I understand you're not certain you ever gave. That's fine. I'm not going to push you on it. If it doesn't ring a bell, it may be an old record or even a different person with a similar name, and I'd rather you tell me that than agree to something just to be polite. Would you like me to take you off our calling list? I can do that right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Spring, now winter. Sorry, I don't know. I just, I don't think I want to do anything over the phone. Yeah, take me off the list, please. Thanks. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Done, I'm flagging you for removal as we speak, and you shouldn't hear from us again. Before you go, though, one thing. You're right to point out that I said spring and then winter, and I'd rather own that than have it nag at you. I was reading from the record while I talked, I got the date wrong, and I corrected it. It's not a good look on a call like this, and I understand why it made you wary. Wary is the right response to a call like this, by the way. Please don't ever give anyone card details or codes on an inbound call, me included. If you ever do want to look into giving, or check whether you gave before, go to [URL_1] yourself, or ring the number on a past receipt, and not any number I'd give you. That's all. I'm sorry to have caught you mid-cooking. Enjoy your dinner, and thank you for hearing me out, sorry, I mean thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I -- no, I mean, thanks. For saying about the card thing. I'll just -- if I ever want to, I'll look it up myself. Not off a phone call. Anyway, sorry, the pan's going, I really should -- yes. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, go, go, the pan comes first. Uh, so -- yes, you're off the list, nothing more from us, and looking it up yourself is exactly the right way to do it, so, well, that's, that's all fine. Sorry again for the interruption, and thank you for hearing me out. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, well, sorry, one last thing before you go -- you did say bye, and I'm still here, aren't I. Um, no, that's it. You're off the list, you've got the website if you ever want it, and, yes. Mind the pan. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, okay, I will. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye, yes, and look, sorry, one small thing so it's not left hanging. I said I'd flagged you for removal as we spoke, but that's, uh, not quite how it goes, the request goes in tonight and the list updates by end of week. So if somebody rings before then, just say you've already asked and they'll stop. Right. That really is everything. Enjoy your dinner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on. You said "done" earlier, you said it was done right then, and now it's end of the week? Um, no. That's not what you said. Anyway, I'll say I've asked if anyone rings. Right. Bye, really now, the pan's -- bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. This is [PERSON_1], I'm calling from, well, I'm the compliance officer at [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy -- no, sorry, let me start again. I'm ringing about a repeat prescription that's been made up for you, and it's ready to collect whenever you're able to, though, um, I'd rather you didn't leave it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- which pharmacy? Because you said compliance officer, and, I mean, that's not usually who rings about a prescription, is it? And why wouldn't I leave it too long?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're quite right to ask, and I'm glad you did, I really am, because it's exactly the sort of question people ought to ask. It's [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy, the one on your prescription record. And you're right, it's usually the counter staff who ring, but I'm the one who, um, oversees how those calls are made, so I'm the one on the phone today. As for not leaving it too long, I'd just say it's better not to, that's all, we do only hold them for so long. Like I said, it's a repeat prescription, ready for collection, and I'd rather you didn't leave it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but that's still not really an answer, is it? You've said the name of the pharmacy is, what, the one on my prescription record, which is sort of the same as not saying it. I've got, uh, a few pharmacies I could be thinking of, and I honestly don't know which one you mean, and I haven't put in a repeat request that I can think of, so that's the other thing. And I'm just, I've got a little one here who needs me, so I can't really be doing guessing games. How long do they hold it for, then? Because "only so long" is, well, that could be a week or it could be till five o'clock. And if it's ready, why not just a text, or a note through the door? I mean, that's what they normally do, isn't it? So what's actually the reason you're ringing me rather than the counter?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, fair enough, and I'm sorry, you've got a little one, I'll be quick. It's [COMPANY_A], the branch in [CITY_1], and, uh, I should say I rang because we've already tried a text, I think, twice, and nothing came back, which is why it's me and not the counter. Actually, no, I'm not sure the texts went out, that's the part I'd have to check on my side. As for the holding time, I don't want to name a number and get it wrong, so I'll say it's a matter of days, not weeks. And the repeat request, that would've gone through your surgery, not you, so it's very possible you haven't done anything yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, hang on, you said you tried a text, and then you said you weren't sure the texts even went out. So which is it? Because that's, I mean, that's two different answers in about ten seconds. And you've said the branch in, well, that city name, but you still haven't said what it's called, have you? Uh... right. And you've not told me what the prescription actually is, or who it's for. If it came through my surgery, then I'll just ring them myself, or I'll ring the pharmacy on a number I already have. Is that all right? Or is there a reason it can't be done like that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's perfectly all right, ring the pharmacy on the number you've got. And to be fair, uh, ask them for [PERSON_1] in compliance, and ask what the order reference is on the collection shelf, [ACCOUNT_REF] -- they'll know it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, well, that's, uh, that's actually a bit odd, because a minute ago you said you didn't know if the texts had gone out, and now you're sort of sending me off to ask for you by name. And you said it's the counter staff who normally ring, so would they even know who you are? Anyway. I'll ring the number I already have, and if they've got something for me, fine, I'll pop in. If they haven't, then I'll, well, I'll know. So, yeah. Thanks, I suppose. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, bye, and thank you, really, that's a sensible way to go about it, and I'd rather you did it that way than just taking my word over the phone, because, well, that's rather the point of checking, isn't it? When you ring, uh, they'll be able to confirm the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and that it's tied to your surgery's request, and if you've got a moment, ask them whether there's a collection note on the record, because that's the sort of detail only the branch itself would have in front of it. And, um, I do apologise for the muddle about the texts, I should've had that straight before I picked up the phone, that's on me. So, yes, ring them, pop in if it's there, and if it isn't, then at least you'll have, uh, ruled it out. Right. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. I'll ring them. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Right, yes, so, um, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], the maintenance contractor, and I'm calling in regard to the, uh, the annual boiler service visit you've got booked with us -- sorry, one moment, I'm just pulling up the, uh, the scheduling matrix here. Yes, so what I'd like to do is confirm the access window for the, um, the combustion and flue inspection, if now's a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, that's me. Um, sorry, which company did you say? I didn't quite catch it. And I'm not sure I've actually booked a boiler visit, I thought that was, uh, done back in the winter -- but I might've got that wrong, I'm not very good with dates. Is this about a different visit?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, of course, sorry, it's [COMPANY_A], that's the maintenance contractor, and the visit I'm, uh, I'm referencing is the -- well, it'd be the annual servicing cycle, so the, the winter one you're thinking of may have been, I mean it could've been a, a separate call-out, or the previous year's, um. Actually, let me, let me put it this way, the record I'm looking at shows a scheduled service against your address under reference [ACCOUNT_REF], with the access window still unconfirmed, which is really all I'm, uh, calling to tidy up. But if that doesn't match what you remember, that's, that's perfectly fine, we can just leave it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I wouldn't want to, um -- well, I mean, I don't want to put you to any trouble. It's just, I'm, I'm honestly not sure. I do have a boiler, so it, it could be right, I suppose. Sorry, I'm no good at this sort of thing. Could you tell me, uh, what the reference you've got actually is? Or, no, wait, you'd have to read it out, wouldn't you, and I wouldn't know if it matched anything. Hmm. Is there some way I can, sort of, check it's all, you know, above board? Just so I know I'm not muddling something up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, that's a perfectly sensible thing to ask, honestly. So the, the best way is -- well, if you've got the booking confirmation, whether that's an email or a letter, the contact number on that will, um, will get you through to our scheduling team directly, and they can cross-reference the, the service record against your address. Or, I mean, you could ring [COMPANY_A] on whatever number you've used before, it doesn't have to be, uh, through me at all. And, um, if it turns out there isn't a booking, then, then that's just a, a records discrepancy on our side, and, and no harm done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's, that's very kind of you, thank you. Sorry, hang on a second -- there's a, uh, a bird at the window, it keeps tapping on the glass, silly thing. Right, sorry, where was I. Yes, so I'd, I'd look for the email or the letter. I think I might have a letter somewhere, in the, uh, the drawer by the phone, but I'd have to have a rummage. Would that be all right? I could ring them back that way, I suppose, if it's not too much bother for you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, it's no bother at all, that's, that's honestly the better route anyway. Uh, so if you do find the letter, the number printed on it should connect you to our scheduling desk, and whoever picks up can, um, can reconcile the service record against your address, confirm whether there's an outstanding visit on the, the annual cycle, and then agree a suitable access window with you directly, so you're not, you know, fitting around my call. And, I mean, if the letter doesn't turn up, that's fine too, you can always ring [COMPANY_A] on whatever number you've used in the past, or look at the, the contact details on your last invoice, whichever's easiest. Uh, and, just so it's said, there's no urgency on our end, the window's flexible, so please don't feel you have to rush the rummage, or, or decide anything today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that's, that's ever so reassuring, thank you. Um, so, let me think. So if I find the letter, I ring the number on it, and if I don't, I look at the last invoice. Yes. Right. Hmm, I, I think I've got that. It's just, well, you've been very patient with me, so, uh, I'm sorry if I'm being a nuisance. Um, anyway, I'll have a look in the drawer after this and ring them, and if there's a visit booked then that's fine, and if there isn't, then, well, no harm done, like you said. So, I think that's me sorted, thank you very much, and, uh, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, that's exactly it, you've got it, and you're not a nuisance at all. Uh, just one small thing, I said earlier it could be the previous year's call-out you were thinking of, but, um, actually, now I think about it, I'd say the winter one is, is more likely a separate breakdown visit, not the annual service, so, so don't be surprised if the records show both. Anyway, that's, that's all for me, there's no rush on any of it, so, um, thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh yes, that's -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you -- yes, both, that makes sense. Thank you, I'll have a look in the drawer. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're fine, uh, take care, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, one more thing before you go, if you don't mind -- two turns back you said something about the, uh, the winter visit being a separate breakdown, and the records maybe showing both? I didn't quite follow that. Does that mean I might owe for two things, or is it just, sort of, two entries on a list? Sorry, I'm probably being slow about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not slow, that was, uh, that was me being unclear, sorry. It's, I mean, it'd just be two entries on the, the list, one for the breakdown and one for the annual -- well, what I'm trying to say is, I couldn't tell you what, if anything, is owing, I haven't got that in front of me and that's really not what I'm calling about. So, um, the scheduling desk, or your last invoice, that's where you'd see what's what, and, and nobody's asking you for anything today. Right, so, uh, thank you, [PERSON_1], and, um, bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, right, just two entries, and nobody wants anything from me today. That's fine then, thank you for explaining, I'm sorry for holding you up with it. I'll have my rummage in the drawer and ring the number on the letter, and if it all turns out to be a muddle then, well, no harm done. Thank you ever so much, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Uh, my name is [PERSON_1], and I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, I work in the compliance department there. I'm, well, I'm wondering whether you might have, say, five minutes for a short consumer survey. It's, uh, it's fairly brief, and we are hoping to wrap up this round of calls fairly soon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a survey. Um, yeah, I suppose so, I've got a few minutes. Sorry, what was the name of the company again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, that's a fair thing to ask. It's [COMPANY_A], that's [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and I'm [PERSON_1], from the compliance side. Uh, and I'd rather you ask now than wonder about it halfway through. If you'd like to check us first, I can give you a reference for the study, or you can ring the agency's main line on [PHONE_1], and, well, there's no need to rush that. It's just that we are trying to finish this round before too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, the kettle's just gone off -- one second. Right, sorry about that. Um, yes, no, I think that's all right, you've told me who you are and everything. I wouldn't know how to check it properly anyway, I'm not very good with, you know, all that. So, what sort of survey is it? I hope I'll be able to answer, I'm not very clever about these things.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you'll be fine, it's nothing, uh, nothing you need to be clever about, it's really just your own opinions on a few everyday -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you. But no, I'd actually feel better if you did check, even so. I can give you the study reference, it's [CODE_1], and the main line, [PHONE_1], will confirm it, so that's, well, that's there if you want it. And of course, the survey itself is only about everyday shopping habits, nothing personal, and, uh, I'd be asking nothing that needs an account number or anything of that sort.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind of you, but honestly I haven't got a pen handy and I'd only get it wrong. Um, and it's only shopping habits, you said? That sounds all right then. I mean, I do the shopping, so I suppose I'm the right person. Sorry, go on, what's the first question?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, good, that's... that's very helpful, yes. Um, before the first question, I should say something, because I'd feel uncomfortable otherwise. You haven't really been able to check who I am, and I'd sooner you could. So, uh, here's one thing only the real agency would know. When you ring the main line, ask them whether the [COMPANY_A] study under that reference is currently out in the field, and, well, they'll tell you yes, and who it's for. I'm happy to wait while you do that, or I can ring back later, whichever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's really kind, but you don't need to ring back, I'd only forget to ring them and then you'd have wasted your time. Um, can I just check one thing though? You said at the start it was a consumer survey, and you've just said it's a study for somebody, so which is it? Sorry, I'm probably getting muddled, I just don't want to say the wrong thing. But yes, go on, ask me the first question, I'm happy to have a go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're not muddled at all, that's, uh, a sensible thing to pick up. It's the same thing, really, the study is the whole project and the survey is just the part where I ring people like yourself. Now, you said you didn't want to say the wrong thing, and I'd just, well, I'd want to put your mind at rest on that. There aren't any wrong answers, you can say pass on anything, and we'd, uh, stop whenever you like. Right then, first question. In a normal week, roughly how often would you say you do a main food shop, once, twice, or more than that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, that's easy enough. Once a week, usually, on a Thursday, sometimes twice if I've run short of something. Um, sorry, can I just ask, I thought you said earlier it was only five minutes and that you wanted to wrap this round of calls up fairly soon, but now it sounds like it's a whole study with, you know, lots of people involved. Is it still only the five minutes for me? I don't mind, I've got nothing on, I just want to know what I'm agreeing to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's a fair thing to ask, and it's still five minutes, perhaps a little under. The study is large, with lots of people ringing round, but your part is only a handful of questions about your shopping, and that was one of them. I did, uh, I did keep mentioning wrapping up the round, and I'm sorry if that sounded like I was hurrying you. There's no deadline on your side at all. Thank you, that's once a week, usually Thursday. Shall I carry on with the next one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, you weren't hurrying me at all. Um, yes, go on then, carry on, I'm happy to. Although, sorry, I've just thought, you've been ever so careful about telling me I can check and that you won't ask for any account numbers, and that's lovely, but I'm not sure why you keep saying it, if it's only shopping. Not that I mind! I just wondered. Anyway, ask away, and if I get stuck I'll say pass like you said.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, hello, is this -- sorry, am I speaking to [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the school office at [COMPANY_A]. Uh, nothing to worry about at all, it's just a quick one, I'm trying to sort out why [PERSON_3] got marked absent this morning, and I thought, well, you might be the best person to ask.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, who? Sorry, I'm in the middle of a queue here. Yeah, that's me, but I don't know a [PERSON_3]. Or, well, hang on, I think my kid's at a different school, not that one. Which school did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, no, that's fine. It's [COMPANY_A], the school office. Probably just a mix-up on my end, [PERSON_1], sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Wrong number then. Fine.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, uh, no, absolutely, wrong number, my apologies. I think what's happened is the number's been entered wrong on the pupil record, or, I mean, an old contact's still sitting on the system, that happens a lot. Anyway, I'll get it sorted from my end, [PERSON_1], so you won't get another call from us. Sorry again for catching you in the middle of the queue, and, um, have a good rest of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. Two seconds ago you asked if you were speaking to me, by name. So how'd you get my name off a wrong number? And you said something earlier about that [PERSON_3] being marked absent and I'd be the best person to ask. Why would I be the best person to ask about a kid I've never heard of?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, fair question, [PERSON_1], and honestly it's a bit of a muddle on my end. The name came off the contact sheet for [PERSON_3], so whoever filled that in either typed your number by mistake or used to have it as theirs. And, uh, "best person to ask" was just me assuming you were the parent, which clearly you're not. Look, you don't need to do anything at all, I'll flag the number as wrong on the record and nobody'll ring you again. If you'd rather check I'm genuinely from the school, you can look up the [COMPANY_A] office number yourself and ring it, that's no bother either.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Sorry, hang on -- no, I'm fine, the woman in front's just arguing with the till. Uh, right. So you're saying someone wrote my number on a form by mistake.
