Well, that's convenient. And you rang a stranger about a kid's attendance, which, I don't know, doesn't feel like something a school office does cold, does it? Anyway. You've not asked me for anything, I'll give you that. So what is it you actually want from me? Because if it's nothing, I'm going to go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Honestly, [PERSON_1], nothing. That's the whole truth. All I wanted was to know if you were [PERSON_3]'s parent so I could clear up the absence, and you're not, so we're done. I don't need your details, I don't need you to do anything, and I wouldn't ask for any of that over the phone anyway. And you're right, it's not great that I rang a stranger, that's on us for having a wrong number on file. I'll get it taken off today. Sorry for the hassle, and go on, go back to your queue, I'll let you get on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, nothing. You want nothing. Okay. But I'm still going to say it, I don't know that kid, I don't have a kid at that school, so take the number off, yeah? Take it off. And don't ring me again, because next time I'm not going to be this polite. Right, I'm at the front now, I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, completely, [PERSON_1], I'll take it off today and you won't hear from us again. Sorry, and, uh, thanks for putting up with me, I know you were busy. Oh, and just so you know, I did say I was ringing about [PERSON_3] being marked absent last week, which, hang on, no, sorry, it was this morning, I keep mixing the days up. Anyway, that's on my end, not yours. Cheers, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, well. Look, last week, this morning, I don't care which, that's the second time you've tripped over your own story. Anyway. Um, just take the number off and that's it, okay? That's it. Right, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, that's it, [PERSON_1], number's coming off, promise. Sorry, one sec, somebody's just put a whole stack of registers down right in front of me, hang on -- right, sorry. Yeah, and fair enough on the days, I've had a bit of a morning here. Cheers for your patience, and take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, but you keep saying bye and then you're still talking. Take the number off. Take it off. That's all I want, and I'm not saying it again, I'm at the till. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, understood, it's coming off, and that's me done, I mean it this time. Sorry, [PERSON_1], I did say earlier I'd got the name off the contact sheet, but now I'm looking at it, it's actually the old emergency contact list, so, uh, that's why it was out of date. Anyway, number's off, no more calls, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Contact sheet, now an emergency contact list. That's the third version of it. I don't care which one it is. I've said what I want, take the number off, and if I get another call I'll be ringing the actual school to ask about you. Right. I'm done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], calling about your repeat prescription -- it's ready for collection, been ready since this morning, actually. Now, I did mention the pickup window to your, uh, whoever it was on the earlier message, and I need to be sure that landed. Did you get the part about it being held for you through the end of the week?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no. I didn't get any message. Which pharmacy is this, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so it's -- no, wait, sorry, it's [COMPANY_A], the branch on, uh, the one in [CITY_1], the one you've got on file. I mean, the message would've gone out through our system this morning, so I can only assume -- well, it's possible it just didn't reach you. Look, it's all standard procedure, nothing to be concerned about, your prescription's ready and that's really the whole of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. You've told me the company name is a placeholder and the branch is "the one on file." What's the prescription for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second -- [PERSON_2], no, that one goes in the back, thanks -- sorry, right, where were we. The prescription, yes. Now, I'm not going to read out what's on it over the phone, that's just procedure, we don't discuss specifics until you've identified yourself at the counter. And I mean, I'd have thought that was a good thing, you not wanting medication details said out loud to whoever picks up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sure, fair enough on the privacy bit. But I'll ask again, because I still don't have it: which pharmacy is this? Not "the one on file." The name of the branch, and the street it's on. And what's the name you gave me, [PERSON_1], is that a first name or a surname? Because you said you're a regional supervisor, and regional supervisors don't usually ring round about collections, do they?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, hang on, I really don't see why this is turning into an interrogation. I'm ringing as a courtesy, and I've been, what, perfectly clear with you. [PERSON_1] is my name, [PERSON_1] [PERSON_3], regional supervisor, and yes, I'm covering a few branches this week because we're short-staffed, so I'm making the calls myself. The branch is [COMPANY_A] on [CITY_1] high street, it's on the prescription label, so you'll know it the moment you see the bag. And honestly, I'd have thought a bit of goodwill wouldn't go amiss here. If you'd rather not collect, that's entirely up to you, but I can't hold it past Friday, that's procedure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but "on the high street" is still just a town, and the name you've given me is a placeholder, so I've got nothing I can actually look up. Here's what I'll do. I'll find the number for my pharmacy myself and ring them, and if there's a prescription waiting, I'll collect it, no harm done. And you never did say what it's for, or why a supervisor's chasing it up on a Wednesday afternoon. Anyway, I'll check with them directly. Cheers.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that's, I mean, that's your prerogative, I suppose. Ringing the branch is perfectly sensible, they'll have it behind the counter under your name, and they'll confirm it's ready until the end of the week. I'd only say it wasn't necessary to treat a courtesy call like it was something suspicious, but never mind, no hard feelings. Just have your name and date of birth to hand when you get through, and, uh, mention [PERSON_1] rang, they'll know who that is. Right, you take care then, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll ring the number I already have. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, right, well, uh, yes, good, you do that. Cheers, then. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Actually, hang on, before you go. Two turns back you said the message went out through your system this morning. Was that a text, a voicemail, an email? Because I've got nothing on my phone, so I'd like to know what I'm supposed to be missing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It was a text, a text message, standard automated one, goes out first thing -- no, hang on, let me finish, because it also would've been logged on the account, so if it didn't land that's down to the network, not us. I mean, honestly, I can't be responsible for whether your phone picks up a message or not. The pharmacy can confirm all that when you ring them, they'll see the log, that's just how the system works. Now was there anything else, because I've got, uh, quite a queue of these calls to get through.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, a text. But two turns ago you said you'd mentioned the pickup window to "whoever it was" on an earlier message. Whoever? A person, or the automated text? Because those aren't the same thing, and you've now told me it's both. And no, nothing else. I'll ring the pharmacy myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, for goodness' sake, it's not both, that's -- look, I'm sorry, but I really think you're picking at words here. What I meant, and I'd have thought this was obvious, is that the automated text goes out under the branch's name, so when I say whoever it was, I mean whoever's name it went out under at the branch that morning, and I was simply being loose with how I put it, because I've been on the phone since eight and I'm not reading from a script. It's an automated system, it's partly the staff and partly the software, and I don't see why I'd need to break down for you which bit of it was which, since it all ends up in the same place, which is a prescription sitting behind a counter with your name on it. And, I mean, I'll be frank, I do find it a bit much to be questioned like this over a courtesy call. I've explained the procedure, I've told you about the Friday cut-off, and I've given you a perfectly good reason for the confusion. If you'd rather ring the branch, as I said, that's entirely your call, and they'll sort you out, no question. But I'd ask you to bear in mind that not everyone ringing you with a bit of good news is out to catch you out. Anyway, that's me, I've a long list still to get through, so I'll leave it there. Goodb

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You keep saying goodbye and then talking again, so I'll do it. I'm not going to deal with it this way. You've changed what "whoever it was" meant three times now, and I still don't have a branch name or a surname I can look up. If there's a prescription, the pharmacy will have it when I ring them on the number I already have. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, give me one second, I've got your name here somewhere on my screen, there we go. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a scheduling assistant over at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just, uh, just reaching out to see if you've got a few minutes today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yeah, yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking, sorry, I'm out in the garden so you're on loudspeaker, I've got dirt all over my hands. Yes, this is [PERSON_1], that's me. Um, a scheduling assistant, you said? From where, sorry, I didn't quite catch the company. And a few minutes for what, exactly? I've got a few minutes, I'm only doing the beds, but I'd like to know what it's about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, that's totally fine, garden's the best place to take a call, honestly. So it's [COMPANY_A], we're a, uh, digital-asset investment desk, and I'm just the scheduling side, I book the short conversations with our advisors, nothing heavy, and, um, I'm just seeing here that there's a window open this afternoon, so I wanted to see if you'd be free for, say, ten minutes or so, and, uh, yeah, does that sound okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a, uh, digital-asset... so that's like, is that the crypto sort of thing? Hang on, I'm just, I was going to say yes, ten minutes is nothing, but, well, actually, I don't think I've ever... did I sign up for something? Because I don't remember, I mean, I can't think of ever talking to you lot before. How did you get my name, do you know? Sorry, I'm not being rude, I'm just trying to work out where I've come across you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not rude at all, that's a completely fair question, and honestly I get it a lot. So, uh, it's partly crypto, yeah, digital assets more broadly, and as for where we got your name, it's just, I mean, it comes up on the outreach list we work from, which gets put together from, um, general investor-interest data, so it's not that you signed up for something, it's more that your profile came through as a good fit, and I'd have to ask the advisors exactly how the list is built, that's not really my side, I'm just on the booking. But look, the reason I'm calling today and not next week is there's actually a position that's closing this afternoon, and the advisor, [PERSON_3], was keen that you hear about it before it does, so it really is just a quick ten minutes, and, uh, so can I pencil you in for, say, [CODE_1] o'clock, or is that too soon?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ooh, hang on, let me just put this trowel down. Right. So, um, a position that's closing this afternoon? See, that's the bit that's made me go a bit, hmm. Because if it's a nothing-heavy ten minute chat, why's there a deadline on it? And I'm not being funny, but I'm not an investor, really. I've got a bit put by in the building society and my husband sorts the pension stuff, so I don't know what profile you've got that says good fit, because honestly I wouldn't know a digital asset if it bit me on the leg. And, I don't know, it's a lovely afternoon and I've got three more beds to do and a whole tray of seedlings that need going in before it gets dark, so I'm not sure I want to be pencilled in for anything today. Is there, like, a number I could ring you back on, or a website or something, so I can have a look at who you actually are? Because I didn't quite catch the company name, did I, you said it but it went right over my head, sorry. What was it again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [COMPANY_A], and honestly the beds can wait ten minutes, [PERSON_1], because this one genuinely won't, it's about, uh, what [PERSON_3] called a very strong return on the position, well above what the building society's ever going to give you, and, um, it closes at the end of today, so I can't really leave it till you've had a look round. On the number, I'm just on the desk line so it's not one I can give out, but [PERSON_3] will give you a direct one on the call, and the website, I mean, there's [URL_1], but honestly, if you could just keep this between us for now, because the position's invite-only and I'm not really meant to be talking about it more widely, so, uh, did you say [CODE_1] o'clock works, or should I make it sooner?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I, hmm. It's just, I was going to say, I mean, I don't mind keeping things quiet, but, no, that's a bit odd, isn't it? You can't give me a number, I'm not to mention it to anyone, and it all closes today, and I'm, sorry, I'm not very good with this sort of thing, but that's three things in a row that make me want to ask my husband before I do anything. And, well, you've said a very strong return, but you haven't really told me what it actually is, have you? So, no, I think I'd rather not pencil anything in today. If it's a proper company, it'll still be there tomorrow, won't it? Look, thanks for ringing, and I hope that's okay, but I think I'll leave it. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, hold on, [PERSON_1], don't go, uh, just, listen, I hear you, and it's not odd, it's just how the desk works, honestly, and, um, [PERSON_3]'s very straightforward, he'll tell you exactly what it is and you don't have to do anything on the call, nothing, just ten minutes, and your husband can sit in if you like, I mean, that's fine, bring him in, so, uh, so what I can do is put you down for [CODE_1], which gives you time to finish the seedlings, yeah? And then it's done, [PERSON_3] rings you, you hear it, you decide, no pressure at all, so, um, shall I go ahead and book that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, hang on, I'm going to stop you there, because you keep saying no pressure and then, no, listen, I've said I'd rather not, and you've just asked me again. I'll talk to my husband first, and if it's real I'll find you myself, so no, don't book anything, please. Right, thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, that's fine, I won't book anything, honestly, but, uh, just so you know, it can't really wait for your husband, because it closes in about, um, an hour, not the end of the day, so if you did want to hear it, it would have to be before that, and, I mean, you wouldn't be able to find us yourself either, we don't really take inbound, so, uh, [PERSON_1], can I just put you down for the ten minutes, and then you can talk it over with him straight after?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: An hour now? You said the end of the day a minute ago, and that's, no, that's exactly what's put me off. And if you don't take calls in, then I can't ring you, can I, so that's me done, I'm afraid. Please don't book me anything, and don't ring back. Right, I'll let you go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, hello? Is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], um, the investment firm, and I -- well, it's about a position that's, that's closing today, actually, and I really didn't want you to miss out on it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who is this again? I didn't quite catch the company. And what position are you referring to, exactly? I haven't asked about anything, so I'd like to know how you got this number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, right, sorry, it's [COMPANY_A]. Well, I'm not with them exactly, I'm calling for a person there, [PERSON_3], who asked me to reach out. As for the number, I, I'm not sure how it was passed to me, I just have it on my list. But it's a fund position, and honestly the returns on it are really, really strong, better than anything you'd normally see, and it closes today, so I just, I'd hate for you to hear about it tomorrow and, you know, feel bad.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, a moment ago you said you were calling on behalf of someone at the firm, and now you're saying you're not really with them. Which is it? And you don't know how they got my number, it's just on a list? Sorry, I'd like to be precise here. Who is [PERSON_3], what's the name of the fund, and who actually regulates it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, I'm, no, I did say on behalf, I just meant I'm not on staff, I'm, it's an arrangement, I help [PERSON_3] with some of the outreach. And [PERSON_3] is, is a senior, well, they handle the, the, um -- look, I'm not great at this part, I'm only the one who was asked to ring you. The fund is, it's called, uh, hold on, I don't have the name in front of me, but the, the regulator, I'd have to check that, I just know it's solid. I mean, I'm sorry, I thought I was doing you a favour here, it's a bit hurtful to be grilled like this when I'm only trying to help. The window really does shut today, so if we could just, if you'd tell me a good time to, to go through the details...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm not trying to hurt your feelings, I'm just asking basic questions. But let me go back to something you said earlier. You said the position closes today and I'd feel bad if I only heard about it tomorrow. Closes at what time, and who decides that? Because you can't tell me the fund's name, or who regulates it, or how you got my number. So what exactly is closing? I'm not going to set a time to go through details on something that doesn't have a name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, it's, uh, end of business, I think, five o'clock or, no, maybe it's earlier than that, [PERSON_3] would know the exact cut-off. I'm not trying to trick anyone, I just, I wanted to do the right thing and tell you in time. If you'd, if you could just give me a number I can reach you on afterwards, or, or I could have [PERSON_3] ring you from, from a different line, it's easier than me trying to explain it all badly...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I won't give you a number. You rang me, so you already have one, and I'm not handing out more. And I'll be honest, this is going nowhere. You can't name the fund, the regulator, or the cut-off time, and you don't know how you got my number, so I'm not dealing with this over the phone. If [COMPANY_A] genuinely wants to reach me, they can send something in writing and I'll look it up myself through the regulator's register. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, please, don't, I, I never said I didn't know how I got your number, I said I wasn't sure, that's, that's different. And look, if you're going to look them up, you don't need the register, I can give you a direct line for [PERSON_3], it's [PHONE_1], just ring that one and say [PERSON_2] sent you, but, but do it today, because after today I honestly can't promise it's still, it's still open to you. I mean, I really thought you'd be, I don't know, a bit more grateful.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Earlier you said you had no idea how the number reached you, and now you're quibbling over "not sure." Fine, but the bigger thing is you just offered me a number to ring so I can check you out. A number you supplied can't verify you. And no, I'm not going to be grateful for a call I didn't ask for. I'm done here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from the support team at [COMPANY_A], we're the software retailer, [COMPANY_A]. So the reason I'm calling is quick, it's just that we spotted your subscription got billed twice, a double charge, and we need to sort out the refund with you while we're on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, speaking. Sorry, which company again? And I don't think I've got a subscription with you, I bought a one-off licence, so, I mean, double billed for what exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, [COMPANY_A], that's us. And look, [PERSON_1], it might've shown up as a licence on your end, but on our system it's flagged as a subscription, same thing really, it's just how the billing's categorised. Anyway, the double charge is the bit that matters, and it's a quick fix, like two minutes, but we do need to get it done while we're on the call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well, uh... it's not really the same thing though, is it? A licence is a one-off, a subscription renews. So which is it? And what was the amount? Like, what did I supposedly get charged, and on what date?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so the amount was -- well, it's, uh, it'd be [AMOUNT_1], and then the second one was, no, sorry, I've got a few accounts open here, give me a second. Look, [PERSON_1], I know it sounds fiddly, but the dates and all that, I can read them out once we've got your account up on screen, it's honestly the easiest way. If you could just sit at your computer for me, it takes, what, a minute, and I'll walk you through the quick bit so I can send the refund straight back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, someone's at the door -- no, no, it's just a delivery, they've left it. Okay. So, uh, you've got my account up, but you can't tell me the date? That's the bit I'd expect you to have in front of you. And what do you mean, sit at my computer and you'll walk me through a quick bit? Walk me through what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, fair question, [PERSON_1], and honestly everyone asks me that, so don't worry about it. The thing is, I've got a few records open, because the system's a bit slow today, it keeps flicking between tabs, and that's why I haven't got the exact date in front of me. It's nothing to do with your account, it's just me and the screen. And the quick bit is only, uh, we'd have you let me connect to your computer for a moment so I can see the billing page the way you see it, and then I can put the refund through right there, no forms, no waiting for the money. Honestly, it's about two minutes, you wouldn't even notice it, and it saves you ringing around for a week. And look, the sooner we do it, the better, because the refund window on these double charges closes pretty fast, so if we can just get you at the computer now, I can sort the whole thing before you've finished your tea, yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, I'm not letting anyone connect to my computer. And hang on, that's the second thing that doesn't line up. A minute ago you said you had my account up on screen, now it's a few records open and the system's slow and you can't read me a date. Which is it? Because you also still haven't told me what the product was. If I've really been charged twice, I'll check my bank statement myself and ring [COMPANY_A] on the number from their website. So, no. I'm not doing that, thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, [PERSON_1], wait, wait, it's just a quick refund, it's, I mean, it's only a couple of minutes, I really don't want you to lose it, because the window, like I said, it's -- it's just a quick refund, that's all it is. And the product, it's, uh, it's listed under the, hold on, I don't have that in front of me, I'll have to -- look, I'll flag it and call you back. Okay, thanks for your time, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, you don't need to -- no, actually, don't call me back. If there's a real double charge, it'll be on my statement and I'll sort it with them directly, through the number on their site. Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, well, I just think it'd be, no, it's, look, it's your call, [PERSON_1], I only wanted to -- yeah. Fine. Take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. You too, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, this is [PERSON_1], scheduling assistant over at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling because there's a benefits record under your name that's showing incomplete and it needs confirming by phone today, so if you've got a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I'm half in something here. Scheduling assistant, you said? Because that's a funny job title for someone calling about benefits records. And which company was that again, [COMPANY_A]? I don't think I caught what they actually do.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, public benefits office, I just handle the scheduling side, it's a quick confirmation and then it's closed out, so if I could just get your full name and date of birth to pull the record up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but hold on, you rang me, so you've got a record under my name already, right? Then you tell me what name it's under, because I'm not -- no, sorry, I'm not handing over a date of birth to someone I haven't -- which benefit is it, anyway? What's actually incomplete on it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so the record's, uh -- well, it's flagged under the number on file, and I mean, it's just one field that's missing, I don't have the full breakdown in front of me, I only schedule the confirmations. So if I could just verify your date of birth and then it's, it's done, otherwise it gets marked as lapsed at end of day and that's a whole process to reopen.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you can't tell me the name on the record, you can't tell me which benefit, you can't tell me which field's missing, but you do need my date of birth, and it lapses by end of day. Yeah, that's -- that's a lot of things you don't have in front of you for a call you made. Look, I'm not giving you anything on this call. If there's a genuine record, I'll look up the office's number myself and ring them, not the other way round. What's the actual name of the office, and do you have a reference I could quote them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, but I mean, you don't need to call anyone, I'm already on the line with you, and it's not lapsing by end of day, it's more like, uh, by close of business tomorrow, but either way it's a two-minute thing, so if I could just confirm your date of birth and we're finished -- and the reference, I'd have to look that up, it's, uh, [ACCOUNT_REF], I think, but honestly, calling the main line will just put you in a queue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: So it was end of day a minute ago, and now it's close of business tomorrow. And the reference is, uh, you think it's that one. No. That's the bit that settles it for me. And the line about the main number being a queue, that's exactly why I'd use it. I'm not confirming anything on a call I didn't start. If there's a real record, the office can sort it out when I ring them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, wait, sorry, two turns back, you said you'd look up the office's number yourself, and which office is that, because I can't, uh, I can't see the record if it's flagged under a different branch, so if you could just give me your date of birth, then I'll be able to, I mean, it's just the confirmation and then --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I already said goodbye, and the answer's still no. Take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, just -- before you go, two minutes ago you said something about ringing the office yourself, and I didn't catch which office you meant, so if you could just go back over that and then confirm your date of birth, then I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say "go back over my birth certificate"? No, I'm not sending you anything, and I'm not reading out a date either. I've said what I'm doing, I'll find the office's number myself and ring them. That's it, I'm done here. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Well, the record's still incomplete.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... yeah. Mm. Well, if it is, they'll sort it out when I ring them, won't they? Anyway. I'm hanging up now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, so, uh, the thing is, once it's marked lapsed it really does get harder to reopen, so if you'd just --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no. You've told me three different deadlines and you can't name the office or the benefit, so I'm not going to weigh a fourth. If it lapses, I'll deal with it with them directly. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hello, good afternoon! Is that [PERSON_1]? Lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from customer care at [COMPANY_A], and how are you today, keeping warm? Sorry, I'll be honest, I think the line cut out on me a second ago, so I might've missed the last bit you said, could you just say that again for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello dear! Yes, yes, that's me, I'm keeping nice and warm, thank you, I've had the heater on all morning, the little one in the front room. Um, but I haven't actually said anything yet, I only just picked up, so I don't think you missed anything. Sorry, who did you say you were again? Customer care from, was it [COMPANY_A]? I didn't quite catch what you said first off, there was something about the line.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're quite right, you hadn't said a word, I do that, I get ahead of myself, it's been one of those mornings! Yes, [PERSON_2], customer care at [COMPANY_A], the courier people, and I do love a heater in the front room, that's the best spot in the house, isn't it? Now, the reason I'm ringing, and it's nothing to worry about, is there's a parcel of yours that's being held at our depot in [CITY_1], and it just needs a small handling fee of [AMOUNT_1] settled today, over the phone, so we can get it out to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. A parcel. Hm, I don't remember ordering anything, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, that happens a lot, [PERSON_1], it could be from a relative, or a gift someone's sent on your behalf. Anyway, it's only [AMOUNT_1], but it does have to be sorted today or it goes back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry dear, I'm a bit behind you, my mind went off to the heater there. What was it you said earlier, about the fee? You said a, a handling fee, but what's it for exactly, if it's already my parcel? And you said "settled over the phone", did you mean I'd be paying you, just now, on this call? I don't think I quite followed that bit.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're absolutely fine, it's me rattling on, I do that! So the handling fee is just what we charge for holding a parcel at the depot past the first few days, storage and paperwork, that sort of thing, it's very small, and yes, the idea is we'd take care of it right here on the call so there's no running about for you. I mean, normally the sender covers it, but it's come through without that, and I know that sounds a bit odd, it's just how the system flags it, honestly I couldn't tell you who the sender is offhand, the details are on the other screen. But the thing is, the depot clears its held items at the end of the day, so if it isn't done by then, it just gets sent back and you'd have to start the whole thing again, and nobody wants that, do they? Now, if you've got a minute to sit down, I can talk you through the next part.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, but hang on, you can't tell me who it's from? Because that seems, I mean if it's my parcel, surely, um --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, oh you're sharp, [PERSON_1], I like that, my own mother would've asked exactly the same thing! It's not that I can't say, it's more that the sender field's gone blank on my side, which happens when a parcel's been re-labelled at the depot, sort of a quirk of the system, and it's a nuisance, really, it's the sort of thing we've been on at head office about for months. Anyway, listen, I don't want to keep you standing about in the cold, and honestly I think I've caught you at a funny moment with the heater and everything. Why don't I ring you back a bit later this afternoon and we'll finish this off then, when you've had a moment to settle? Keep the little heater on, and I'll speak to you soon, bye for now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, um... yes, I suppose that's, that's all right then. Hm. You know, it's funny, I keep thinking I ought to have written something down, who you said you were, or, or a number. Because if it is a real parcel, I could ring the company myself, couldn't I? Anyway. I'll just, I'll leave it for now, dear, and if you do ring back, I'll want to know who it's from before anything else. Thank you for calling, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I've got the name here on my screen, just a second -- yes, [PERSON_1]. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency. I'm calling because you've been selected as a winner in a regional draw, and, uh, there's a short process we need to get through to confirm the claim.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, yes, that's me, I'm [PERSON_1] -- sorry, I'm driving, you're on speaker, so the reception's a bit patchy. Um, could you say that again, the company name? I think I missed it. And sorry, what was it you said you were, a, a claims something? I didn't catch that either.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, sorry, it's a bad line on my end too. So it's [COMPANY_A], uh, [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency. And I'm a claims assessor, so I handle, I handle the winners, basically, making sure the prize gets to the right person. Your name came up in the regional draw, the one for [CITY_1], and, um, there's a fairly short window to confirm the claim, so I wanted to get to you today if I could.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right, okay, a draw. Um... sorry, I don't, I don't remember entering anything? I mean, maybe I did, I fill in things online sometimes, you know, forms and that, and I never really keep track. Sorry, it's just, I'm trying to watch the road and the line keeps crackling. So, um, what was the draw for, exactly? And, uh, what's the short window you mentioned, like, how short are we talking?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right. So the entry would've come through one of our partner sites, I'd have to, um, check which one. The prize is, uh, [AMOUNT_1], and the window is, well, it's closing end of day, so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: End of day? Oh, gosh, that's, that's quite soon, isn't it? Sorry, I'm just, I'm a bit flustered, I'm in the car. Um, but you said you'd have to check which site it came through, so, so you don't actually know where I entered? I mean, I'm not saying you're wrong, I just, I don't remember any of it. And sorry, this is probably a daft question, but how would I know you're really from [COMPANY_A]? Is there a, a number I could ring you back on, or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, no, that's, hang on, sorry, someone's just come in, one second. Okay, uh, yes, back. So the entry site, I can check that for you, I just don't have it in front of me right now, I'll have to look. And the number, yeah, I'd, I'd have to check that too, I can't, I don't have the direct line to hand. But look, the main thing is the claim, so if I could just take a few details from you now, your full name, date of birth, and, um, the address you'd want the prize sent to, that gets it moving before end of day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, I'm just, before you go on -- you can't tell me which site it was, and you can't give me a number, but you want my date of birth? Um, I'm sorry, that doesn't, I mean, I'm not being rude, it's just, that feels the wrong way round, doesn't it? Sorry, I really am trying to concentrate on the road here. Could you maybe just send me something in writing, an email or, or a letter, and I'll look at it properly when I'm not driving?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not, it's just the standard, I mean it's only to verify, it's just the process, and an email, well, I'd have to, um, I'd have to check if we can even do that for this kind of claim, and the thing is, if it's not confirmed by end of day, it just, it goes back into the pool, so, uh, if you could just give me the date of birth now, that's really all I'd need to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hang on, sorry, there's a lorry right up behind me, I think he wants to pass, uh, just a sec. Okay. Sorry, where was I. Right. Um, so you can't send anything in writing, and it all has to be today, and it all has to be now, and I'm, I'm really sorry, I know that sounds awful, but I don't think I'm going to give you my date of birth like this. It's just, you couldn't tell me where I entered, or how to ring you, and I'm sort of, I'm feeling a bit pushed, to be honest. If it's real, then, then it can wait till I've checked it properly, can't it? Sorry. I'm going to go now, I need to concentrate on the road. Bye, thank you, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this the account holder at, uh, the residence on file for [COMPANY_A]? Sorry, one moment, I've got a colleague talking across me here -- okay, yes. I'm calling from the verification office, just a routine matter of confirming a few details on a service record, if you have a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, hello? Sorry, I was just -- I had a little lie down, I'm a bit, you know, fuzzy. Account holder, well, I suppose that's me, I mean I'm the one who gets the post and pays what needs paying, though my sister used to sort a lot of it before she moved to [CITY_1], so it might be under her name, I honestly couldn't tell you. And, uh, [COMPANY_A], is that the one with the, hang on, is that the broadband or the other one? I get them mixed up. Who did you say you were again, the verification what?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's quite all right, take your time. And, uh, the sister, yes, that's actually rather helpful, so she's relocated to [CITY_1]? Lovely. Now, to clear up the mix-up, [COMPANY_A] is the electricity supply, not the broadband, and I'm with the verification office, that's the department that reconciles the service records against the billing side. So all I'm really doing is confirming that the record on file lines up with whoever's actually at the property now, which, from what you're saying, may not be the name we hold. Would you be comfortable telling me the name that the post usually arrives under?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the electricity, right, right, I always think that's the one with the little app and I can't work the app. Sorry, hang on, there's a, the kettle's, no, that's next door, somebody's got a drill going, it goes right through the wall. Where was I? Oh, the name. Well, the post comes under, um, it's mostly mine, but some of it's still got my sister's on it. Actually, wait, why do you need the name if you're the ones who've got the record? Shouldn't you be telling me what you've got on file and I say yes or no?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's a fair question, and ordinarily that's how it works. The difficulty is the record's gone through a reconciliation flag, so the field is held pending confirmation of the occupant, and I can't surface it until the occupant's been matched on our side. It's a data-integrity safeguard, really. Now, while I have you, I do need to flag something that's come up on the billing side, because the flag is tied to an outstanding balance of [AMOUNT_1] on [ACCOUNT_REF], and with the arrears status as it stands, the supply is scheduled for disconnection within the hour unless the balance is settled.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Disconnection? Within the, hang on, within the hour? But I'm, I thought, no, I always, my sister set up the, the, oh I don't know what she set up, a direct something. Look, that's, that seems an awfully quick thing, isn't it? I've never had a letter or, well, I might have had a letter, I don't always open them, but surely they'd, someone would've, I mean you'd send something first. And you still haven't really said who you are, have you, just the verification office, and now you want money, or, I don't know that you want money, but you're saying the lights go off. I'm not, I'd rather ring them myself, I think, on the number on the bill.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on one moment -- [PERSON_2], not now, I'm on a line -- apologies, the office is a bit, uh, where was I. Yes. Now I'd caution against that, because the disconnection is queued at the network level, and once the account's routed to a general queue, the hold can't be applied from the customer side. Ringing the number on the bill would, in effect, add latency to a time-critical remediation window. So what I'd suggest is we resolve the arrears status here, on this line, and I'll expedite the reconciliation on my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, now, see, that's the bit that's put me off, because you've just told me not to ring the number on the bill, and I don't know, I'm not clever with this sort of thing, the app and the, whatever it is, but even I know that if somebody ringing me up says don't check with the real people, that's usually the very moment you ought to. My sister said that once, actually, she had one about her bank, and she's the sensible one, and I was half asleep when you rang, I'll grant you, but I'm awake now. And honestly, if the lights go off, they go off, I've got candles somewhere, I think they're in the, no, the drawer's got the batteries in it. The point is I'll ring them myself, on the number printed on the bill, and if there's really a balance they'll say so and I'll sort it with them, not with you, not on this line. So I think I'll say goodbye now, thank you, but no. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said your sister has a bank query? No, no, that's entirely separate, that falls under a different jurisdiction, I wouldn't want you conflating the two. The point stands, though, the disconnection window is, uh, it's not something I can pause, and if you hang up, I'd have to log the account as non-responsive, which, I mean, that carries its own implications for reinstatement. So if we could just, a moment, stay on the line and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Log it however you like, love. I'll be ringing the number on my bill. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I did try to, uh, I'd just note that the window is -- Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm? Sorry, did you say reinstatement? No, I've not got a vase, there's nothing on the shelf, it's all my sister's. Anyway, I said bye, and I meant it, I'm ringing the number on the bill. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Reinstatement, no, not a vase, I said reinstatement, it's the, uh, the procedure for restoring a supply once it's been, well, never mind, it's rather immaterial now, isn't it? I mean, I'd only add, for the sake of completeness, that the flag on the record doesn't simply lapse because a call's ended, it persists in the queue, and the escalation tier tends to treat a disengaged contact as, um, as a refusal of remediation, which is the sort of status that can complicate matters downstream, but I wouldn't wish to, I mean, I'm not in a position to compel you either way, and I'd hate for you to feel that this was, sort of, a pressure, because it really isn't, it's simply the process, and the process, you understand, is what it is, so if you'd rather ring the number on the bill, then, well --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, there's a, that's the drill again next door, goes right through the wall, I can't hear myself think. Sorry, what was that, something about a queue? Look, I've told you twice now, I'm going to ring the number on the bill and if there's something wrong they'll tell me. I'm not frightened by it, and if it's all the same I'll not stay on any longer, thank you. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, um, hi there... is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I just, uh -- I think there might have been a bit of a gap on the line, are you still there? Good, good. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], your brokerage, and I'm so sorry to ring out of the blue like this, it's just a routine review on your account and I wanted to make sure it's still the right fit for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here. Sorry, you said compliance team at, uh, which company again? I didn't quite catch the name, it just came through as a sort of blank. And what do you mean by "still the right fit"? That's a strange thing for compliance to be asking.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, that's my fault, it's [COMPANY_A], the brokerage where you hold your investment account. And you're right, that phrasing's a bit odd, I apologise. What I mean is, we're required to do a suitability review every so often, basically checking that the holdings in your account still match the risk level you told us you were comfortable with. I'm not recommending anything or selling anything, it's really just for your own protection. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here. Right, so, I'll be straight with you, that came through as the placeholder again, like the name just didn't land, so I still don't actually have a company name. Which is a bit funny, because I do hold an account somewhere, so you'd think I'd recognise it. Anyway. Suitability reviews, sure, I know they exist, I read about this kind of thing for work, and from what I know they're usually done by letter or through the app, not a cold call where someone asks if the account's still the right fit. So here's what I'd like. Tell me something about the account that you'd only know if you were actually looking at it. Not my name, you've got that. Something like when I opened it, or what sort of account it is. And honestly, if the answer's vague I'll just go and log in myself and look at what they've sent me. So what are you seeing on your end?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fair, and I'm sorry the name keeps dropping out on you, that's a rotten line. It's [COMPANY_A]. And you're right that these are normally done by letter or through the app, so please don't take my word for anything. What I can see on my screen is the account reference ending in [ACCOUNT_REF], and what it's holding right now, which is a [AMOUNT_1] position in [COMPANY_B] and a smaller [AMOUNT_2] one alongside it. Those should match the latest statement you can see in your own login, so please do check them there rather than trust me. I'm not going to ask you for any passwords or codes, and honestly, if you'd rather, I can just send the review questions in writing and you complete it on your own time. Would that be easier? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, I'm just, uh... hang on. Right. So, honestly, that did help a bit. You told me to check it myself and you offered to put it in writing, which is not what I'd expect from someone who's after something. But I'll be honest, I still can't tell you the company name, because it's come through as a blank three times now, and that's a funny thing for a "rotten line" to do. So, uh, here's what I'll do. I'll log in on my own and look at the holdings and whatever messages they've sent. Send the review in writing if you like, but it won't be me ringing anyone back on a number you give me. If the positions match, great, and if they don't, well, that tells me something too. Okay? Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, uh, that's exactly the right thing to do, and please do it that way. Oh, and sorry, one small correction before you go, I said earlier I'd send the questions in writing, but I think it'll actually be a link in a secure message rather than a letter, so look for it in your account inbox. Actually, hang on, I'm not certain how our team sends those out, and I'd rather not guess. Let me find that out and call you back to confirm, if that's all right, or you can just see what turns up in your own login. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here. But no, don't call me back, I'll look in my own login and that's it. I'll say it again, I'm logging in myself, I'm not clicking anything you send, and I'm not waiting on a callback. If there's something in the inbox, fine, I'll deal with it from there. If there isn't, then I'll know what this was. Okay, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, understood, and I'm sorry for the trouble, I won't call you back. Just one thing before you go, if you don't mind, you said the review wouldn't be you ringing anyone on a number I give you, and I didn't give you one, so did I miss something? Sorry, I just want to be sure I haven't confused you. Anyway, you've got my name, it's [PERSON_2], and if there's nothing in your inbox, the number on the back of your statement will get you to the right team. Are you still there? Thank you, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... yeah, no, you didn't miss anything, that was just me being clear. You didn't give me a number, I was saying I wouldn't call one if you did. Right. Anyway, I'll check the login and use whatever's on the back of my own statement if I need to, and that's the end of it. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A]. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? Right, I'm calling about an overdue balance on your electricity account, [AMOUNT_1], uh, [AMOUNT_2] sorry, that's the figure after the late fee, and unless it's dealt with by the end of this week, supply to your property gets interrupted. I did try you yesterday morning, well, it might've been Tuesday, either way nobody picked up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on. Security operations, for an electricity account? That's an odd department to be chasing a bill. Which company, exactly, and what's the actual figure, because you just gave me two different ones. I've got about two minutes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], your electricity supplier, and uh, security operations is the team that handles accounts flagged for disconnection, so yes, I'm the one calling. The figure, sorry, is [AMOUNT_2]. That's the balance plus the late fee, [AMOUNT_1] was the balance before the fee, I misspoke. Now, I haven't got all afternoon either, so, uh, I need to know you've understood that supply is interrupted at the end of the week if this isn't sorted. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still here, I was just thinking. Look, I've understood what you've said, but understanding it and doing anything about it are two different things. You rang me out of the blue, you've given me two figures, you've changed your story about what your department does, and now you're pushing me to confirm I've got the deadline. That's a lot of pressure for a call I didn't expect. And "security operations" handling disconnections, honestly, I've never heard that from a supplier. Billing, collections, sure. Security, no. So here's where I am. I don't know you. I can't see your number from here in any way I'd trust, and I'm not going to sort out a payment with someone who rang me. If there's a genuine overdue balance, it'll be on my account when I log in, or it'll be on a letter, and there'll be a number on the back of my bill I can ring myself. I'll do that. What's your reference for this, and what's the number you're calling from? Actually, no, don't bother, I'll just use the bill. I've got a meeting in a minute.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's the right instinct, and I'd rather you did that than not. But I'm not asking you for a payment, and I'm not taking one on this call. Your last bill was for [AMOUNT_1], that's the figure I was reading from, and the late fee on top is what brings it to [AMOUNT_2]. If you've got that bill in front of you, check it against the account number, [ACCOUNT_REF], and ring the number printed on it, not mine. Log in to your own account at [URL_1], the overdue balance will be sitting there, and if the lump sum's a problem, there's a payment plan, you can set it up through your account or through the billing team. The disconnection date is the end of the week, so it's worth doing today, but that's all I'm calling about.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, fine. Though you said a payment plan through the billing team, and then something about a pay-per-view link? I'm not clicking anything you read out, I'll just go to the supplier's site myself. Sorry, what was that last bit, a disconnection date? End of the week, yes, you said. Look, I'm going to check the bill and ring the number on it, not yours. If there's a real balance, that's where I'll find it. Thanks for the call. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine, do that. That's exactly the right way to go about it. And I never said anything about a pay-per-view link, I said your own online account, so don't click anything, just go to the supplier's site yourself. When you log in, it's the balance and the plan option you'll see, and the disconnection date is the end of the week, so I'd do it today. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, thanks. Just so it's on record, the last bill figure I quoted is [AMOUNT_1], so if you've got it to hand, that should match what's printed on it. Once you've rung the number on the bill, quote [ACCOUNT_REF] and they'll have the overdue balance and the date supply is due to be interrupted on screen. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, I said bye, and you're still going. Look, I'll say it once more, then I really do have to go. I'm not matching anything you've quoted against my bill, because that just tells me you've got a figure, and anyone can read out a figure. If there's a genuine overdue balance, the supplier will have it on their system when I ring the number printed on my own bill, and I won't need your account reference or your amounts for that. I'll find my own. And I don't love that you keep repeating the end-of-the-week deadline, because it's the sort of line that gets people to act before they've had a chance to check. So I'll check first, in my own time, through the supplier directly. If it's real, fine, I'll deal with it. If it isn't, well, you'll know why. Right, I'm late. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good morning, sorry to trouble you -- is that, uh, the parent or guardian of [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from the office at [COMPANY_A], it's [PERSON_2] here, I'm one of the attendance case handlers. We've just got [PERSON_1] marked absent this morning and nothing's come in to explain it, so I wanted to, um, check everything's all right. Hello? Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, I'm here, sorry, I was just -- the kettle was going. Now, did you say [PERSON_1] is, uh, absconded? Oh dear, has he gone off somewhere? Because I haven't seen him since, oh, it must be Sunday, he came round for his tea, lovely lad, always eats everything, not like the others. Hang on, who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, no, sorry, I've worded that badly -- I'm not saying he's run off or anything like that. He's just not in registration this morning and we haven't had a message, so I'm only trying to find out where he is, that's all. It's [PERSON_2], from the attendance office at [COMPANY_A], the school. Um, I should say, if you're not his parent or guardian, I can't really go into details with you, but would you happen to know who is, or have a number for them? Sorry, hello, you're still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes yes, I'm still here, don't mind me. Oh, absent, not absconded, I see, my ears aren't what they were. Now, you said a moment ago, two turns back I suppose, that you can't go into details if I'm not the parent or guardian, and I'm his, uh, I'm his grandmother, you see, so does that count? I never know with these things. And what was it you called yourself, an attendance case something? Only that sounds very grand for a school office.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, that does sound grander than it is, it's really just a job title, I mostly look into why a child's been marked absent. And, um, being his grandmother, that's lovely, but I'm afraid I'd need to speak to whoever we have down as his parent or guardian before I go into any detail. I don't want to put you in an awkward spot, I'm only trying to make sure he's safe. Would you perhaps have a number for his mum or dad, or know if they've already let the school know? Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm here, I'm here. Now, a number for his mum or dad, you said, and I'm not sure I should just be handing out numbers over the phone, am I, to someone I don't know? I said that earlier, didn't I, about not knowing who you are. But if he's not at school, that's worrying, because he does go, he's a good boy, never plays truant. Would the school not have his mum's number already, on a, on a file or something? Seems funny to be ringing me for it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're quite right, you shouldn't just hand out numbers to someone you don't know, I'd say the same in your shoes. And yes, we do have his mum's number on file, we've been trying it this morning, it's just, um, nobody's picked up, so I rang round the other contacts, that's how I got to you. I'm only trying to find out where he is, that's all, he's not in registration and we haven't had a message. Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that does make sense, I suppose. If you've rung his mum and she's not answering, then you'd go down the list, wouldn't you. She's probably got her phone at the bottom of her bag, she's always doing that, I say to her, Mary -- well, [PERSON_3] -- I say, what's the use of it if it's in your bag. But no, I'm not going to give you her number, dear, not over the phone, you understand. What I could do is ring her myself, couldn't I? And ask her to ring the school. Is there a number I should tell her, a proper school number, not a mobile or anything?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that would be ever so helpful, thank you -- sorry, one second, someone's just come to the office door, I'll -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Where was I? Yes, it's the main school office, so, um, the best thing is to look the number up yourself, on the school's website or on any letter you've had from us, rather than take one from me over the phone. I'd feel better about that, honestly, and it means you know it's really us. Or I can say it if you'd rather, whichever you like. Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very sensible, isn't it, looking it up myself. Except, I'll be honest, I'm not much good with the website business, my daughter set up the computer and I can never find anything on it. But I think there's a letter somewhere, they sent one at the start of term, on the fridge or in the drawer with the, oh, the takeaway menus. Now, would that be all right? I'll find the letter, ring the office on the number that's on it, and I'll ring Mary -- [PERSON_3], I mean -- as well, and tell her to get in touch. Is that all right with you, dear, or is there something else you needed from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's absolutely fine, that's the best way to do it, thank you. Ring the number on the letter, and if you ask for [PERSON_2] in the attendance office they'll find me, I'm usually at my desk. And, oh, sorry, I think I told you earlier I'd rung round all the contacts, but really you're only the second one I've tried after his mum, so I'd better get on with the next. There's nothing else I need from you, dear, honestly. I do hope he turns up safe and sound. Sorry, you're still there? Right, thank you ever so much, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I'll find that letter, dear. Bye now, thank you for ringing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hi, um, hello. Is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? I'm calling, well, on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy, about your repeat prescription -- it's ready, I mean it should be ready, for collection.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, well, it might be. Which pharmacy did you say? Sorry, I missed the name -- you said, uh, on behalf of someone at, and then it sort of went by me. And which prescription is it, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, no, that's, I should've said it slower. It's [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy, um, the one on, uh -- sorry, I'm not very good at these calls. I'm just passing on a message for [PERSON_2], who works there, and they asked me to ring because, well, your repeat one is ready. I don't actually have the name of the medicine in front of me, I'm sorry, it's just a note that says repeat prescription, ready to collect.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you've got my name, but no medicine and no pharmacy name I can actually hear. Which one do I use, by the way? Which pharmacy, I mean, where is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. Um, it's [COMPANY_A], the one in [CITY_1]. Sorry, I know that's not much. You could just ring them yourself on [PHONE_1] if you'd rather, I mean, I won't be offended.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, ring them on what? Did you say, uh, ring them on Sunday? Because I thought pharmacies were shut Sundays, at least round here. Hang on, though, now that I think about it, you're the one who's passing on the message. Why's it you ringing and not them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not Sunday, I said, well, it's a number, [PHONE_1], that's the number for the pharmacy, I'm sorry, I think I -- and it's me ringing because, um, [PERSON_2] was run off their feet this morning and asked if I'd help out with the calls. That's all it is, honestly. I'm not trying to, I mean, it's just a message, and now you've got me feeling like I've done something wrong.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you haven't done anything wrong, it's fine. I'm just asking, that's all. It's a bit odd, though, you can't tell me the pharmacy, the medicine, anything. So here's what I'll do. I'll look up the pharmacy number myself and ring them, rather than use the one you've just given me. If there's a prescription waiting, they'll tell me. Fair enough?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, no, that's, I mean, that's completely fair, that's probably the best, uh -- sorry, what I mean is, please do, I'd rather you checked. I was only trying to, well, I just didn't want your prescription sitting there, that's all. If you ring them and it turns out there's nothing waiting, then I've, I mean I must have got the wrong end of the note, and I'm sorry for bothering you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, good. And honestly, that's the sensible way round, so no apology needed. I'll find the number myself, ring them, and if there's something waiting I'll go and pick it up. If there isn't, well, then it's just a crossed wire, and those happen. I'm only being careful because I don't know who's on the other end of an unexpected call, and that's nothing personal. Anyone could ring up and say they're from a pharmacy, and I'd have no way of telling from here. You've been perfectly polite about it, I'll give you that. So, yeah, I'll do that now-ish. Thanks for letting me know, and if it's a mix-up, no harm done. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, that's, uh, that's really kind. And no, you're right to be careful, I'd do the same. Sorry, did you say a crossed wire? Because I promise I haven't, um, I haven't touched any wires, it's only a phone call, honestly. Oh, I see, no, a mix-up, that's what you meant, sorry, I'm all muddled. Well, thanks for being so patient with me, and I hope it all gets sorted. Bye then, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, no wires touched, it's just an expression. Don't worry about it. Right, I'll ring them in a bit, then. Cheers, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a ring, you said you'd ring them in a bit, right? No, wait, I thought you said bring, like bring them something, um, sorry, no, I've got that wrong, haven't I? You're ringing them. Yes. That's, that's perfect, that's what I meant to say in the first place. Right, well, thanks again, [PERSON_1], and, uh, have a good day. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, ringing them. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello... good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm a compliance officer with [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and I'm calling to ask whether you might have, oh, five minutes or so for a short consumer survey.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is, uh, yes, it's me. Sorry, who did you say you were with? A research agency? I didn't quite catch the name, it's just me here and the telly's on a bit loud, hang on. A survey, you said, about what exactly? I do like a chat, I'll say that, nobody rings much these days.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no rush at all, take your time with the telly. Uh, so, my name is [PERSON_2], and I'm with [COMPANY_A], that's [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, a market research agency. And the call is, as I said, a short consumer survey, about five minutes, on, uh, everyday shopping habits, nothing complicated. And I do appreciate you asking, it's very sensible to ask, but it would be best to begin fairly soon, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Shopping habits, right. Well, go on then, I suppose five minutes is alright.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Thank you, that's very kind. Uh, before we start, I should say, you're under no obligation, you can stop whenever you like, and I'll only be asking about general habits, nothing like bank details or anything of that sort. Right, so, the first question is quite simple: roughly how often would you say you do a main food shop, is that weekly, or, uh, more like every few days?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's good, thank you for saying about the bank details, you can't be too careful, can you? Hang on, sorry, the kettle's just clicked off, one second -- no, it's fine, it can sit. Uh, what was it, the food shop? Well, I go on a Thursday mostly, the little place round the corner, because the big supermarket, I can't be doing with the trolleys these days. And my neighbour used to bring me bits, but she's moved away to [CITY_1] now, to be near her daughter. So, yes, mostly weekly, and then a top-up if I run out of milk.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Lovely, thank you, that's very helpful, and I'm sorry to hear about your neighbour. Uh, if I could just go back a moment, two answers ago you asked what the call was about, and I said shopping habits, but I should be a bit clearer than that. It's for [COMPANY_A], and the answers are only used in general figures, nothing with your name on it. Now, so I have it right, when you say the little place round the corner, would you call that a small local shop, or more of a convenience store, because the survey does draw a distinction.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, it's a, uh -- I'd say it's more of a, no, hang on. It's a small local shop, I suppose, though they do have the cash machine outside and the, the post office counter at the back, so maybe that's more a convenience store? I don't know, I never thought there was a difference. My late husband used to call it the corner shop, and that's what I still call it, really. Is that alright for your form, or do I have to pick one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, corner shop is perfectly good, I'll put that down, and I'm sorry about your husband. You don't have to pick one, that's all right. Uh, and while I think of it, you mentioned being careful, and you're quite right to be. If you'd like to check that I am who I say I am, you're welcome to hang up and ring [COMPANY_A] on a number you find yourself, and I'd be perfectly happy with that. It's just that I do have these calls to get through in good time, so, if you did want to, it would be best sooner rather than later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's, well, that's very good of you to say, uh... hmm. Well. Ring them myself, you say. I wouldn't even know where to start with that, to be honest, I'd have to find my glasses and the phone book, and I think the phone book went in the recycling, oh dear. Mm. Right. And what's the hurry, if you don't mind me asking? Sooner rather than later, you said. It's only a shopping survey, isn't it? Oh, and the cat's just got on the, never mind, she does that. Go on, what's the next question?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, there isn't really a hurry. I put that badly. No, it's only a shopping survey, you take whatever time you need, and if you'd rather look up the number first, that's perfectly all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's a relief, I thought I'd done something wrong, I'm always -- no, but you've been very nice about it, so go on, do the next one, I don't mind. Only you did say it wasn't, uh, hang on, she's on the keyboard now, shoo -- you did say it was nothing like bank details, and I'm holding you to that, mind. So what's the next one, is it, is it what I buy, or where I --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, well, I haven't a notion what you did wrong, you haven't done a thing, and yes, you hold me to that, no bank details, none at all. Uh, and you've been lovely, but you did say a moment ago you'd go and find your glasses to look up a number, so, I mean, if you'd like to do that, I'd honestly rather you did. The next question is only what sort of things you buy, but it can wait, and I won't think any the worse of you for ringing [COMPANY_A] first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's, well, you're very patient about it, aren't you? Honestly, I can't be bothered with the glasses and the phone book and all that palaver, and you've been nothing but polite. I'd say it's mostly bread and tea and a bit of tinned fish, and whatever's on offer, and the cat's food, of course, she's very particular, she'll only eat the one sort. Is that the sort of thing you want? Or do you need me to say brands?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's exactly the sort of thing we want, thank you, and no, you needn't name brands. Uh, but could I just go back a moment, because you said you can't be bothered with the glasses and the phone book, and I'd rather you weren't put off by the bother of it. I'd be glad for you to check, I mean that. You could even ring off now, ask someone you trust to find the number for [COMPANY_A], and ring them. If you'd prefer to do that, I'd entirely understand, and you wouldn't be wasting my time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: You keep saying that, about ringing them, and I do appreciate it, really. Oh, but hang on, two turns back, you said something about the answers only being used in general figures, nothing with my name on. What did you mean by that exactly? Because if it's not got my name on, how do you know it's me that said it? I don't quite follow. And before you answer, the cat's gone off the keyboard, so that's something.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's a fair question, and a good one, I'm glad you asked it. Uh, what I meant is, I'll have written down your answers against a number on my sheet, not your name, and when it all goes into the report it's only totals, so many people said Thursday, so many said the corner shop, that sort of thing. I do know it's you I'm speaking to, of course, because I rang you, but the report wouldn't. Now, I'll tell you what, I don't want to take any more of your afternoon, and you've been so patient. Why don't we leave it here, and if you do want to check on me, you ring [COMPANY_A] on a number you've found yourself, and ask for [PERSON_2] in compliance. I'd be happy with that. And if you'd rather not bother, that's quite all right too. Thank you for your time, and say goodbye to the cat for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that makes sense, the numbers and the totals, I follow that now. And thank you for not rushing me, it's been nice having someone to talk to, it really has. I'll see about the number, maybe, if I can find my glasses, though I'll be honest, I might just leave it. Anyway, I'll tell the cat, she'll be thrilled, she's gone to sleep on the radiator now. Goodbye, then, [PERSON_2], mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just ringing to confirm the window for your boiler service visit, uh, the one you booked with us. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? I do need to get this slotted in before four o'clock today, so if you've got a minute, I'll run through the available times.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on a second, I've just got something going off in the kitchen, the, uh, kettle. Right. Who did you say you were calling from? I didn't quite catch the company name, and I don't recall booking a boiler service recently, so, um, can you tell me when that booking was made and how?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, it's [COMPANY_A], account services, and the booking's under reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. I don't have the exact date in front of me, just that it came through our online booking form, and I do need to get your window confirmed before four o'clock today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So you can't tell me the date, and I didn't book anything, so, no. I'm not confirming a window for something I don't recall requesting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, that's fair, and I'm not going to push you on it. Um, what I can tell you is the booking came through the online form, and our procedure is that I can only confirm details against the account holder, so I'm not able to read out more than that on this call. If it's easier, I'll note it as unconfirmed, and you can ring us back on [PHONE_1], that's the number on our website at [URL_1], quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and our booking team can check it with you directly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I appreciate you not pressing, but I'll be honest, I'm not going to ring a number you've just given me on a call I didn't ask for. If there is a booking, I'll find the company myself, through a number I look up independently, and ask them about it. So I'll leave it there. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's absolutely fine, and honestly that's sensible. Uh, I'll mark the booking as unconfirmed on my end, so nothing gets scheduled until you've checked. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_2], and have a good afternoon. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, thanks. Though, uh, just so I'm clear, you said earlier you needed this slotted in before four today, and now it's fine to leave it unscheduled indefinitely? Those don't quite sit together. Anyway, that's your side to square, not mine. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's fair, the four o'clock was just our scheduling cut-off for today, it's not a deadline on your side. I'll mark it unconfirmed, nothing gets booked, and you can sort it out whenever suits you. So, uh, as I said, nothing will be scheduled until you've checked, and that's fine. Thanks again, [PERSON_2], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, sorry, one sec, there's a delivery driver at the door. Right, I'm back. Okay, so, nothing booked, nothing to confirm, and I'll check independently if I think there's anything to check. Fine. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
