utterances.text: Hello, this is the attendance office at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling about -- yes, sorry, I just need to confirm [PERSON_1] was marked absent this morning and we've got no note on the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... sorry, who is this again? Which, uh, which school did you say? Because I didn't quite catch the name, and, I mean, I've got my hands a bit full here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [COMPANY_A], the school office. Attendance desk, I'm [PERSON_3]. Uh, I'm calling about [PERSON_1], registered as absent at the morning roll call, and there's no reason logged against it. If you're the parent or guardian, I just need to know whether that's an illness or something else so I can put it on the record.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a, what, a "reason for the roll call"? No, I haven't, I don't, I mean I haven't asked anyone about a roll call. Who's this about again? And, uh, how did you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. It's the number on the contact sheet for [PERSON_1], that's all I've got in front of me. If it's the wrong number, say so and I'll note it and move on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I'm not saying it's the wrong number, I'm just not going to say it's the right one either, not yet. You've told me a name, but it's only a placeholder, you haven't actually said which child or which school, not really. And I've got a little one right here beside me, so you can understand I'm, uh, careful about who I confirm things to on the phone. If the school genuinely needs to know, wouldn't they have a way for me to ring them back on a number I already have? Because I'd rather do that than sit here telling a stranger where my kid was this morning.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fair, and honestly that's the right instinct. So, you don't have to confirm anything to me. If you'd rather ring back, call the main school office on the number printed on the school letters or the website, [URL_1], not a number I give you. Ask for the attendance desk and give them [PERSON_1]'s name, and they'll pull up the morning register and see the same blank I'm looking at. It's an unexplained absence, that's all it is. We log them every day, so it's nothing out of the ordinary. If it does turn out to be the wrong number, the office updates the contact sheet then. I'll put a note on the file that you'd rather call back, and I'm not asking for anything else on this call. No details, nothing to confirm. And if the child was simply off sick, a quick message to the office whenever it suits you is all it takes to clear it, no rush.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, okay, I heard that, you said ring the main office, so I'll -- no, hang on, sorry, one second. Put that down, please. Sorry. Right, so, I'll ring them on the number I already have, not yours. Fine. And you're not asking me for anything today, you said. Nothing. That's what you said, yeah? Alright then. Thanks, I think. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right, nothing today. And, uh, if you were asking about what I said two turns back, the bit about the website -- it's only there so you can find the office number yourself, you don't need to use anything I've given you. Ring the main office, ask for attendance, and if it's a misunderstanding they'll sort it in a minute. Sorry for the bother, and, uh, thanks for being careful. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. I'll ring them. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, great, sorry, I know I'm catching you mid-day. This is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants on the desk here, and I'm just, uh, I'm just getting a few calls booked in for the week, so, yeah, do you have a quick minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi, yeah, this is, uh, yeah, speaking! Sorry, you've caught me out in the garden, I've got you on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in compost here. A quick minute, sure, yeah, I've got a minute. But sorry, who did you say you were with again? [COMPANY_A]? I didn't quite catch that, I've got the, uh, the wind and a wheelbarrow going. Who did you say you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, sorry, that's on me, yeah, [COMPANY_A], it's a digital-asset investment desk, we're based out of [CITY_1], and honestly I won't keep you from the compost, it's really just a scheduling thing, I'm lining up short calls with a handful of people this week so the senior advisor can walk them through what we're, uh, what we're doing at the moment. So, um, would you be open to a quick chat with [PERSON_3] sometime later today or tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, investment, okay. Um, I mean, I'm not really -- well, I don't actually think I've ever, uh, I wouldn't have signed up for anything like that, I don't think? So I'm a bit confused how, how you got my number, to be honest. Did I fill something in online at some point? Because I do that sometimes, I'll put my name in for a thing and then forget all about it, my daughter's always telling me off for it. Sorry, ha, I'm rambling, it's the compost. But what is it you're actually wanting to talk to me about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not rambling at all, and honestly that's probably it, yeah, a lot of our contacts come off online forms people have forgotten about, so I wouldn't worry, your daughter can go easy on you, ha. So the short version is [PERSON_3] has a digital-asset position that's, uh, that's closing today, and it's got a return profile that's honestly well above what you'd see from anything on the high street, we're talking numbers that people hear and go, wait, is that right, and it is, which is why the desk is only ringing a small group of people rather than putting it out generally. And the thing is, because it closes today, there's only really a window this afternoon, so what I'm trying to do is just get you ten minutes with [PERSON_3] before the end of the day, no commitment, just so you can hear it, because, I mean, if it's not for you it's not for you, but it would be a shame to hear about it tomorrow when it's gone. So, uh, would you be able to do, say, a call later this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that does sound exciting, I'll give you that, ha. Though, hang on, I'm a bit, um, you said a minute ago it was just a scheduling thing, and now it's closing today and there's only a window this afternoon? Which, I mean, I'm not saying anything, I'm just a bit lost, because I'd have thought if something was that good they wouldn't need to ring people like me out of the blue, you know? My late husband always used to say if somebody's in a hurry to get your money, you want to take your time, and I always thought, well, that's a bit grim, but, uh, he was usually right about those things. And I've got, I mean, I've honestly got no idea about digital assets, I wouldn't know a, a coin from a, a, what do you call it, a token, so I don't know why I'd be on anybody's small group. So what's the company called again, sorry, properly, and is there a website I could have a look at, or a number I could ring you back on? Because I'd sooner look into it myself before I talk to anybody's senior advisor.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair point, and your husband sounds like a sensible man, but honestly it's still just a scheduling thing, I'm not asking you for anything, I'm just booking ten minutes, and you don't need to know a coin from a token, that's exactly what [PERSON_3] is for, he walks people through it from scratch. The company's [COMPANY_A], like I said, and the website's [URL_1], but, uh, between us, I'd keep this one quiet for now, it's not publicly listed, and the desk would rather it didn't get passed around before the position closes, so it'd be a shame to, to have it fall through because someone mentioned it. And the thing is, if you go away and look into it yourself, I mean, you're welcome to, but it closes today, so by the time you've done that the window's gone, so, um, can I just pencil you in for this afternoon, and if you hate it, you hate it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, well, I -- no, hang on, I think I'd rather -- sorry, it's just that, you said keep it quiet, and, and that's a bit, I don't know, that's a funny thing to say, isn't it? Because I'd normally ask my daughter about anything like this, I always do, and now you're saying not to mention it? Which, I mean, I'm not trying to be difficult, I'm sure you're perfectly nice, it's just that, well, if it's all above board, why can't I tell her? And it closing today, again, that, that just makes me want to slow down rather than speed up, honestly. So, uh, I think I'll, I think I'm going to leave it, if that's all right. I'll have a look at that website you said, in my own time, and if it's something I want to know more about I'll ring you. Thank you for the call, though, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, hang on, hang on, don't hang up, I'm not saying don't tell her, I just mean, uh, maybe don't make a big thing of it before you've even heard it, and listen, you're right, I'm sorry, I'm being pushy, that's not how I want this to go, so how about this, just ten minutes with [PERSON_3] this afternoon, you can ring your daughter straight after, I mean, tell her all of it, and if it doesn't sit right you say thanks but no thanks and that's the end, and honestly you've got nothing to lose by just listening, so, um, shall I put you down for, say, half past three?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm, sorry, I'm going to stop you there, because you've just said sorry for being pushy and then asked me again, haven't you? Half past three, and ring my daughter after, and, and nothing to lose, I mean, it's the same thing, just, just wrapped up differently. And I'm sorry, but if I've got nothing to lose by listening, I've got nothing to lose by looking at the website first either, so I'll do that. Right, I'm going to go now, thank you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, you're right, I did ask again, I'm sorry, and, uh, to be fair, I said earlier I wasn't asking you for anything, but [PERSON_3] does need a quick yes today to hold the slot, so that's, I mean, that's the only catch, and ringing your daughter first is completely fine, that's sensible, but if you could just say half past three and let him speak to you for ten minutes, you can tell her everything afterwards, so, um, are you all right to go with that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, but now it's, hang on, it's a "catch", and it needs a yes today, and you've just said that's the only catch? Because a minute ago you told me it was just a scheduling thing and you weren't asking me for anything, and now there's a yes I've got to give you before I've even rung my daughter. That doesn't add up, does it? So no, I'm not going with half past three, I'm sorry. I'm going to ring my daughter, and I'll look at the website myself, and if the slot's gone then it's gone. Thanks for your time, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, hi, hello. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], they're an investment firm, and, uh, there's a position in one of their funds that's closing today, and I really wanted to make sure you heard about it before it's gone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1]. I'm sorry, but who exactly am I speaking with, and how did you get this number? You said you're calling on behalf of someone at the firm, so who is that someone, specifically? And I'll say now, I haven't asked about any investment, so I'd like to understand what this is in reference to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, right, sorry, I should've said. It's [PERSON_2], like I said, and I'm, uh, I'm sort of the go-between for the person at [COMPANY_A]. Their name is, um, [PERSON_3]. They asked me to reach out because, well, your name came up as someone who might be, you know, a good fit. I don't, I'm not totally sure how the number came to me, honestly, it was just passed along. I mean, I understand you didn't ask about it, I do. But it's, it's a really good opportunity, the returns on this one are, uh, well above what you'd normally see, and the thing is it closes today, so I'd hate for you to miss out and then, you know, wish you'd heard about it sooner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so a moment ago you said this person asked you to reach out, and now you're saying the number was just passed along and you're not sure how you got it. Those don't quite fit together, do they? Either [PERSON_3] chose me and gave you my details, or my number came from somewhere you can't name. Which is it? And I'd like to know what [COMPANY_A] actually is. Are they registered, and with whom? Because I'm not going to discuss any returns, especially "well above normal" ones, with someone who can't tell me how he found me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I, that's not, I didn't mean it like, okay. [PERSON_3] did, [PERSON_3] gave me the list, I mean the name, your name was on, uh, no, it came through [PERSON_3]'s office, and I just, I wasn't the one who, who pulled the number. That's all I meant. I'm sorry, I'm not, I don't do this a lot, and I'm getting, I feel like you think I'm trying to, to trick you or something, and that's, that really hurts, because I'm just trying to help. As for the registration, I'd, I'd have to check, I don't have that in front of me, but it's a real firm, [PERSON_1], honestly, and the thing is, if we wait on all this, the position's just gone by end of day, and I'd feel terrible if you missed it over, over paperwork.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm not trying to hurt anyone's feelings, I'm just asking precise questions. But go back to something you said earlier, when you first called. You said you were calling "on behalf of someone" at the firm, and then you described yourself as a "go-between." Are you actually employed by [COMPANY_A], or are you an outside party, a broker or a lead-generation outfit, passing along names? Because that makes a real difference to who's responsible for what you're telling me. And "paperwork" isn't a small thing here. A firm that's registered can tell me its registration in about ten seconds. So I'll find the firm myself and call them directly. What's the name of the fund, and a number I can reach [PERSON_3] on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I, no, I'm not, I don't work there, not exactly. I'm, it's more of a, I just help [PERSON_3] out, that's all, I'm not a broker or anything like that. And the fund, um, I'd have to, I don't have the exact name in front of me, which, I know how that sounds. As for a number for [PERSON_3], I, uh, [PERSON_3] is in meetings most of the day, so it'd be better if I just have them call you, or I could, I could call you back later. That's easier, honestly. But it has to be today, [PERSON_1], that's the, that's the part I can't, I really can't stress enough, because after today the position's just gone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. You can't tell me the name of the fund, you can't tell me who employs you, you can't give me a number for [PERSON_3], and you couldn't say how you got mine. That's too many gaps for a deadline that's conveniently today. If [COMPANY_A] is real and the opportunity is genuine, it'll still be there when I've looked the firm up myself and called them on a number I found independently. I won't be taking a callback, and I'd rather [PERSON_3] didn't ring me either. Please take my number off whatever list you're working from. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, okay, I, wait, please, I'm not, I wasn't trying to do anything wrong, I just, that's honestly a little hurtful. Look, you can call [PERSON_3] yourself, sure, but, um, I'd still say it's best if you don't wait on this, because I mean, I don't think they take calls from the public, not really, it's all through, through the office. Which, uh, I said before that [PERSON_3] was in meetings, that's, that's all that is, they're just really busy. I'll take your number off, I will, I'm sorry to, to have bothered you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Just now you said [PERSON_3] doesn't take calls from the public, and a minute ago you offered to have [PERSON_3] call me back. Which is it? Anyway, that settles it for me. If the firm only works through an office, then I'll contact the office, on a number I find myself, and I'll decide after that. Please do remove me from the list. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from the support team at [COMPANY_A], and, uh, I'm calling about a billing thing on your account. Sorry, can you hear me okay? I said it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A] support, it's nothing to worry about, we just spotted a double charge on your subscription and I'd like to get that sorted for you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you fine. Uh, [PERSON_1], yes. Sorry, which company did you say? Because I only just heard "support team" and then a bit of static. And a double charge on what, exactly? I don't actually have a subscription with them, I don't think -- or, well, maybe I do, I'd have to check.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry about that, [PERSON_1], the line's a bit rough on my end too. It's [COMPANY_A], [COMPANY_A] support, I'm [PERSON_2], on the billing side. And honestly, no worries if you're not sure about the subscription, that's really common, it's the one that renews quietly in the background, you know? Anyway, it's [AMOUNT_1] that went out twice, so it's just a quick refund to fix, takes a minute or two, and I can do it with you right now while we're on the phone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right, so, uh... hang on. You've told me the company name twice now, but you still haven't said what the subscription actually is. Like, what's the service? Because "the one that renews quietly in the background" doesn't really narrow it down. And if you're on the billing side, you can just tell me the last four digits of the card it was charged to, or the date it went out. That's the sort of thing you'd have in front of you, right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so the service is, uh -- well, it's the, the annual one, the, hang on, I've got a couple of screens up here. Sorry, [PERSON_1], what I mean is, the card digits aren't something I can read out over the phone, that's just a security thing on our end, everyone asks that, totally normal. The date, it's, it was, uh, recent, within the last few days, I think. But look, you don't need to dig any of that up, honestly, it's a two-minute thing. If you can just get to your computer, I'll take care of the whole refund from my side, you just need to let me connect in for a moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I've got a delivery driver at the door -- no, leave it, it's fine. Uh. Okay, I'm back. So let me get this straight. You can't tell me what the service is, you can't give me a date, and you can't read out a card number, which, fine, I'll give you that last one. But now you want to connect in to my computer? To give me a refund? A refund goes back to the card, you don't need to be on my machine for that. So, no. And you still haven't told me what the subscription is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I hear you, [PERSON_1], and honestly that's a fair thing to ask, you wouldn't believe how many people say the exact same thing. It's just that, uh, with these double charges the refund doesn't always go straight back to the card, sometimes it has to be flagged on the account side first, and that's the bit where I'd need to see your screen for a second, it's really just a quick look, takes no time at all. And the subscription, right, so it's the, it's under the main [COMPANY_A] plan, the standard one, the, hang on, I've got it here somewhere, sorry, it's the annual renewal, the, you know, the software bundle. It's all in the system but the screen's being slow on me today, so if we could just get you to the computer, it'd be so much faster than going back and forth like this, I promise you it's two minutes, three tops, and then you'll have your [AMOUNT_1] back and we can both get on with our afternoons.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but a minute ago you said the charge was within the last few days, and now it's the annual renewal. Annual renewals don't usually go out twice in a week, do they? So which is it? And "the software bundle" is still not a product name. Look, I'm not getting on the computer so you can look at my screen. If there's really a double charge, I'll check my own bank statement and ring the number on the company's own website. That's it. Thanks for calling, but no. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], please, it really is just, it's a quick thing, it's two minutes and it's, it's all sorted, honestly. Okay, uh, look, I've got another call coming through on the line here, so I'm going to have to, uh, let you go, you just, yeah, you take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I -- no, actually, I don't think there's another call, I think you're just -- never mind. Look, if it's real, it'll still be on my statement and I'll deal with it through the company directly. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I, no, that's, look, [PERSON_1], it's, I'm only trying to -- okay, fine. Fine. You go ahead and do that, that's, yeah. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from customer care at [COMPANY_A], the courier people. And how's your day going so far, not too hectic, I hope? Sorry, I should say, I'm just following up on something from, uh, earlier, so bear with me a moment while I pull your details up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, that's me, [PERSON_1]. No, not hectic at all, it's been a very quiet day actually, I was just sat here with the radio on. Um, sorry, you said you're from the courier people, did you say [COMPANY_A]? I didn't quite catch that bit. And what was it you're following up on, from earlier? Because I don't think I've, well, I'm not sure I've had anyone ring me earlier.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, not you ringing, I meant earlier on our side, a note came through on the system, that's all, my wording, sorry! Yes, [COMPANY_A], customer care. A quiet day with the radio on, that's the dream, isn't it, what are you listening to? Anyway, the reason I'm calling is there's a parcel in your name that's being held at our depot, and it's just a small handling fee of [AMOUNT_1] that needs settling today, otherwise it goes back to the sender.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a parcel. Hm. I'm not sure I was expecting one, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, that happens a lot, [PERSON_1], they turn up from relatives, online orders you've forgotten about. Anyway, it's only [AMOUNT_1] and it does need sorting today, or it goes back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sure that's right, it does happen. Sorry, can I just go back a bit, though? Before, you said you were following up on something from earlier, and then you said it was a note on your system, and I didn't quite follow what that was. Was that about my parcel, or something else? I'm a bit slow with all this, I never know how these things work.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're not slow at all, [PERSON_1], honestly, it's me being clumsy with my words! So, it's the parcel, yes, the same thing. The note's just how it shows up on my screen, the depot flags it and it lands in the queue for whoever's on, and today that happens to be me. Though I'll be straight, I'm only looking at a short summary here, so I can't see exactly where it's come from or who sent it, which is probably why it all sounds a bit vague. Anyway, I'm not ringing just to tick a box, it's about the [AMOUNT_1], because that settles the whole thing by phone today and the parcel gets released rather than sent back. Mind you, you did say it's a quiet day, so that works out nicely, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, but hang on, if you can't see who sent it, then how do I know, I mean, sorry to interrupt, but how would I even know it's mine, I --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, don't apologise for interrupting, that's a fair question, and honestly you're being very sensible, [PERSON_1]. It's in your name, it's tied to this phone number, and that's all the depot needs to flag it, so it's definitely meant for you. The sender details, well, they're held on a different screen, which I can't pull up from here, and I can't say why it works like that, it's just how the system's set up. Oh, and the radio, you never said what you were listening to, that's a lovely thing on a quiet afternoon. Anyway, look, I don't want to rush you, but the fee does need to go through today or it gets sent back, and I've still got a few calls in my queue, so do you know what, I'll ring you back a little later this afternoon and we can finish it off then, how does that sound?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the radio, it's just the, um, the afternoon programme, the one with the old songs, I don't even know what it's called. Hm. Well, you know, I've been sitting here thinking about it, and I don't really like paying for a parcel when I don't know who it's from, and you can't tell me who it's from, so, well, uh... I think I'd rather you didn't ring back, if that's all right. If there really is a parcel, I'll ring the courier myself, on whatever number's on the, the website, or the card, or whatever it is. But thank you for ringing, dear, and it was nice to have a chat. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Okay, good. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency, and, um, hang on, let me just pull this up -- yes. I'm calling because your name has come up as a winner in a regional draw, and I just need to take you through the claims process before it, uh, lapses.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, yes, that's me, I think -- sorry, I'm driving, so the reception's a bit patchy, I'm on speaker. Did you say a promotions agency? Sorry, I missed what the, uh, what the company was called, it cut out right when you said it. And, um, a draw -- I don't remember entering anything, I mean, maybe I did, I'm not sure -- what draw is this exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem, it's [COMPANY_A], that's [COMPANY_A], a promotions agency. And the draw is, uh, it's a regional draw, so it's, let me see here -- it's covering [CITY_1] and the surrounding area. Um, as for entering, a lot of people don't remember, it's usually through a, a partner entry, so it's quite common. I mean, the main thing is the claim window is fairly short, so I'd like to get you through the process today if that's alright.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, right, okay, sorry, I'm just, uh -- hang on, there's a lorry beside me, give me a second. Okay. So, a partner entry, I mean, what partner? Because I really don't remember signing up to anything, and, um, I'd feel a bit silly just going along with it today when I don't know how I got in. Is there, like, a way I could check this is, you know, real? Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I just, uh -- I'm a bit nervous about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I understand. Um, the partner, I'd have to check that for you, I don't have it on this screen. But the process is just a quick verification, I'd need your full name and date of birth, and, uh, the claim does lapse if it isn't confirmed today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, but, sorry, you don't have the partner on your screen? That's -- I mean, that's the thing I was asking, so I'm not sure how I'd, uh, how I'd know it's me who won and not, you know, somebody else. And I'm a bit, I'm not really comfortable giving out my name and birth date to someone I can't check, especially while I'm driving, sorry. Is there a number I could ring back, or a website or something, where I could look up [COMPANY_A] myself? Because I'd rather do it that way, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, one second, someone's just come to my desk -- no, it's fine, it's fine. Right. A number to ring back, um, I'd, I'd have to check what the right one is for you, I'll, I'll come back to that. It's just, the thing is, the claim reference is only held open until end of day, so if you did want to go through it now, it really would be easier. I only need the name and date of birth to match you to the entry, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, can I just -- no, I'm sorry, but that's, that's twice now you can't find something I've asked for. The partner, and now a number, and, um, you want my details before I can check any of it? I'm not doing that, sorry. If it's real, it'll still be real when I can look up [COMPANY_A] properly, so I'll, I'll try that when I've stopped driving. Thanks, but, uh, no, I'm going to go now, sorry. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, wait, please, before you -- the reference is only open till, um, five today, so if you hang up now I can't promise it won't, uh, it won't be released to the next name on the list. I can send you the details by -- no, hang on, I'll, I'll have to check what I'm able to send, just, can you stay on a second while I --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a, uh, there's a car right up behind me, they're flashing their lights or something -- okay, okay, they've gone round. Sorry. Right, what was -- no. No, I heard you, and I really am sorry, but if it's going to be given to the next name on the list, then, um, that's fine, honestly, they can have it. I'm not giving my details out, and I'm not staying on while you check things, I'm driving. Goodbye, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and, sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a stack of -- okay, I'm back. I'm calling about your remote position, the one that's ready to start as soon as the onboarding cost is cleared, and I do have to flag that the slot closes at the end of today. Do you have a couple of minutes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? I'm in the middle of a queue here. And what remote position, I didn't apply for anything, I've not even looked at jobs in, what, a year. Onboarding cost? Hang on, you said you were calling from account services, so which is it, accounts or recruitment?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, [COMPANY_A] is a recruitment agency, and account services is the team that handles onboarding on the recruitment side. It's the same, it's the same company. And I understand you may not remember applying, a lot of candidates don't, your details came through on our system under reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and what I can tell you is the position is fully remote, [AMOUNT_1] a week, no experience needed, but the slot closes at the end of today. So, sorry, do you have a couple of minutes to go through the onboarding?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Stop. You're asking me to pay a cost for a job I never applied for? That's the oldest trick going, I've been done by that one before. A real agency doesn't charge you to start work, they pay you. And "your details came through on our system", whose system, how did you get my number? I'm not going through any onboarding. Give me a proper company name and a number I can ring back on, because "[COMPANY_A]" isn't telling me anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I do understand, and, uh, I hear the concern, I do. But the onboarding cost is a one-off, it's [AMOUNT_2], standard procedure for every candidate, and it's refunded in the first pay cycle. As I said, it's a one-off, it's refunded, and the slot closes at the end of today. For callback purposes, I can only give out the number through the verification step, so, sorry, if I could just confirm a couple of minutes of your time to start the process?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, that's it. You can't give me a callback number unless I go through your "verification step"? That's backwards. A real company gives you a number first, no strings. Refunded in the first pay cycle, yeah, I've heard that one. No. I'm not paying anything, I'm not confirming anything, and I'm not giving you a single minute of my time. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, before you go, and I do respect that you're upset, I just want to say this isn't a trick, it's, uh, it's a standard process and I'm only trying to make sure you don't lose out, because once the slot closes at the end of today it goes to the next candidate on the list and I can't reopen it. So what I can do, and this is me making an exception, is note that you declined the verification step, and that's fine, that's your right, but the position, the remote position at [AMOUNT_1] a week, no experience needed, is still showing against reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and I'd hate for you to hang up and then, sorry, find out later it was a genuine opportunity. So, if you could just give me a couple of minutes, and I mean a couple, we can go through the onboarding together, and then, you know, you'll have a proper number for us, because that comes after the verification, that's just the order we do it in. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, and I've already said no. Twice now. You've just said the same thing again with "exception" stuck on the front. If it was genuine I'd lose nothing by you giving me a number and a company name right now, and you still haven't. So no. If there's a real job it can come through the post or on a proper website, not a phone call in a supermarket. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay. Well, uh, the slot closes at the end of today, so, yeah. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm here, and it's the same answer. Enjoy your slot. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, okay, I'll just, uh, make a note of that. And for what it's worth, we're not actually a [CITY_1] office, we're, well, we're partnered with the [CITY_1] team, so that's, sorry, that's probably where the confusion on the name came from. But, um, the slot closes at the end of the week, so if you change your mind, the, the number's on the, hello? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said end of today, now it's end of the week, that's -- no. I'm not, look, I'm not changing my mind and I don't want a number from you now either. Don't ring me again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a stack of folders over here -- okay. I'm calling from the account services team at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just trying to confirm I've reached the right household. Would this be the residence of [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello? Sorry, I was just -- I'd dropped off for a bit, you know how it is in the afternoon, the sofa gets you. Folders, you said? That sounds like a lot of folders. Um, who's [PERSON_1], did you say? I mean, I don't really know who I'm talking to yet. [COMPANY_A], is that, is that the one with the, hang on, is that the one my sister uses? She's always on about some company, I can never keep track. Anyway, what's it about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, sofa, yes, no, perfectly understandable, happens to the best of us. Um, and sorry, I think there's a bit of crackle on the line, I thought you said your sister uses a different provider, [COMPANY_B], was it? I wouldn't be able to speak to anything on that side, that's a separate entity entirely. But to answer you, it's just a routine verification on the service address, nothing to worry about. Could you confirm for me whether you're [PERSON_1], or the, uh, the person who looks after the household account?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, there's a, the kettle's, no, that's the neighbour's telly coming through the wall again. Right. Um, I didn't say anything about [COMPANY_B], I don't think? I said my sister, uh, anyway. You keep saying routine and nothing to worry about, but you still haven't really told me what it's for. And I'm not going to say whether I'm this [PERSON_1] or not when I don't know who you are. Can you just say again who you're with? And is there a number I could ring you back on, or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's fair, and my apologies, I should have led with it. I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], account services, and the reason for the call is a reconciliation flag against the service address, which, uh, basically means there's a discrepancy between the metered-usage ledger and the settled-payment ledger. As for a call-back number, I'd have to check what's permissible, because this goes through a, a queue-routed outbound line, so anything you'd ring would land you at general intake, not at me, and that would only add latency. I mean, the flag does have a time-sensitivity attached to it, so it's really more efficient if we just confirm the address on file right now, and then I can walk you through what the flag actually means.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ledgers, right, I -- no, sorry, that, hang on. I'm not being funny, but I only just woke up and "metered-usage ledger" is, well, it's a lot. And you've said time-sensitive now, and you can't give me a number, and I'm meant to just, I mean, tell you my address so you can explain what's wrong? It's the wrong way round, isn't it? If it's my account then you've already got the address, so why would I be the one telling you? I think I'd, no, what I'll do is look at whatever bill I've got and ring the number printed on that. Is that all right? Because I'm not -- yeah. I'd rather do that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, one moment, there's someone at my desk -- yes, I'll be right with you -- sorry, where was I. Yes, so, the bill. I'd really, uh, I'd advise against that, in this case, because the general line won't have visibility of the flag, it sits in a separate escalation tier, and what I'm required to tell you is that if the reconciliation isn't cleared this afternoon the service address goes into a scheduled disconnection window, and that window opens within the hour. It's not something I'd like to see happen over what is, frankly, a minor ledger discrepancy. So if you could just confirm the address and the account holder's name for me, I can open the case and we can sort the settlement side right away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well now, hang on, because that's gone from routine to disconnection within the hour, hasn't it? And I'm sorry, but that's exactly the bit that makes me want to go and find the bill even more, not less. I mean, I've had this supply for years and I've never once had anyone ring me out of the blue, I've had letters, proper letters, brown envelopes with the window, and if there was a disconnection coming I'd expect one of those, wouldn't I? Not a phone call at, what is it, half past two? And you're saying the number on my bill won't know about it, which, I don't know, doesn't sound right to me either, because surely if it's my account then whoever answers can see it, that's what they're for. My sister always says, sorry, I'm rambling, but she always says if somebody rings you and says do it now, that's when you stop and do it properly. So no, I'm not going to give you the address or the name. I'm going to put the phone down and ring the number on the bill, and if there's really a problem they'll tell me. Thank you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said a brown envelope, did you? No, no, we don't send anything by envelope at this stage, that's a separate paper process entirely, and the flag has already moved past that tier, which is precisely why I'm ringing instead. And look, I'd really rather you not put the phone down, because once that window opens it isn't something I can reverse from my end. If you could just give me the name on the account, I can hold the case open for you while you, uh, while you --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I'm ringing the number on the bill. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'd strongly caution, uh, once the line disconnects the hold on the case lapses, and I can't guarantee --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A lapse? No, I'm not having a lapse, I'm just tired, I told you, I've only just come round off the sofa. And I'm not giving you a name, I've said. I'm going now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, sorry, I think we've crossed wires, I said lapse as in the case hold lapsing, not you, I wasn't suggesting you'd, uh, I wasn't implying anything about yourself. Terminology, that's all, it's the system's term, a hold lapses when the session terminates, which is just how the case-management side is configured, I don't set the parameters. And I do appreciate you've just come round, truly, which is partly why I was trying to keep this brief, a two-minute confirmation and the flag clears, whereas if it's left to run through the standard escalation, and I'm only describing the process here, it tends to be a good deal more involved than anyone wants on a Tuesday afternoon. So if you'd, if you'd like to reconsider, just the account holder's name and we can, uh, we can keep the window from opening. Otherwise, I mean, I can't compel you, obviously, that wouldn't be, it's your decision entirely.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, there's the dog at the door now, he does this, scratches at it like he's been locked out for a week and he's been out there two minutes. No, Biscuit, wait. Right. Sorry. What was I, yes. Look, I know what you said about the lapse, I just heard it wrong, that's fine. But it's still no, love. You've said disconnection, you've said within the hour, you've said I can't ring the number on my bill, and now it's just the name, just the name, and that's every time the same thing, isn't it? The name. So I'm going to ring the number on the bill and if they say there's a problem, I'll sort it with them. That's it, that's my decision. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi, sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? ... Hello, are you still there? Sorry, I think the line went quiet for a second. It's [PERSON_2] calling from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], your brokerage, and, um, I'm sorry to ring out of the blue like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here. Sorry, who did you say you were with? Compliance at... I didn't catch the company name, it came out kind of garbled.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, that's my fault, I'm on a bit of a rubbish line. It's [COMPANY_A], uh, your brokerage, where you hold the investment account. I'm [PERSON_2], on the compliance team, and I'm just ringing about a routine suitability review we run on accounts, it's really there for your own protection. Is that, um, is that all right to go on with, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Okay, so, I'll be honest, I'm working right now, half watching a screen, so you've caught me mid-something. And I do have a brokerage account, but I'm not sure that's the same one you're calling from, because you still haven't actually said the name. You've said "your brokerage" twice now, which is sort of like someone saying "your bank" without telling me which one. That's, uh, I mean, it's not nothing. So, small thing, what's the company actually called? And what number are you calling from, because I'd want to see if it matches anything I've got on file. Then we can talk about this review.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a completely fair thing to pick up on, and I'm sorry, I should have said it plainly the first time. The name is [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling from [PHONE_1]. Please do check that against whatever you've got on file, or just look at the number on the back of your statement or on the website and ring us through that instead, I honestly wouldn't mind at all. And, um, while you're doing that, I'm not asking you to buy anything or move anything, this is only a review of what the account already holds. Are you still with me, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here, just, uh, give me a second, I'm looking at the, hm. Right. So, okay, you said the name this time, which I'll give you, except what you actually said was a placeholder-sounding string, not a name I'd recognise, but fine, let's park that. Here's a small one. If you're my brokerage, what's the account for? Like, which type, is it the general investing one, or something else? And what should I be seeing at the top of a statement from you? Just humour me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, yes, that's a fair thing to ask. Um, so the account I've got flagged is the [ACCOUNT_REF] one, and on the top of your statement you should see the [COMPANY_A] name and that same reference, and below it the holdings, [AMOUNT_1] in total at the last valuation, I think. Actually, hang on, sorry, I said it was a routine review earlier, but looking at the file again, it's tagged as a follow-up, not a first review, so I'm not certain why. As for the account type, I, uh, I'm honestly not sure the file says, and I don't want to guess at it and get it wrong with you. Can I find out and ring you straight back on [PHONE_1], or, if it's easier, we could do the whole review in writing and you can check every line against your own statement? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I'm still here. So, hang on, let me just say that back. You rang me about my account, you can't tell me what type of account it is, and the review went from routine to a follow-up while we were talking? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, I asked what the account's for, and I didn't really get an answer. That's the bit I keep coming back to. If you're my brokerage, that's on the first line of the file, surely. Anyway, you offered writing, and honestly that I'd take. Send it to the address you've got on file for me, not one I read out to you, and I'll check it against my own statement. Or I ring the number on the back of my statement, not yours. Which of those do you want?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not being difficult at all, I'm sorry, you're right to keep coming back to it. And, um, the account type should be right there on the first line of the file, I agree. I can't see why it isn't, and I don't want to bluff you, so I'll find out. Do the writing, please, sent to the address you already have on file, and I won't ask you for anything on this call. Ringing the number on the back of your statement is perfectly fine too, whichever you'd rather. Was there something I said earlier you wanted me to go back over, the follow-up bit, maybe? Sorry, you're still there, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I'm here, just, uh... hm. Okay. No, I don't need you to go back over the follow-up bit. Writing to the address you've already got is fine. If it's real, it'll turn up and I'll check it against my own statement, and if I want to chase it I'll ring the number printed on my statement, not the one you gave me. Right, so that's what happens. I'm not giving you anything on this call, and I'll leave it there. Thanks for being straight about not knowing the account type, I suppose. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], security operations at [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier. I'm calling about an overdue balance of [AMOUNT_1] on account [ACCOUNT_REF], and, uh, supply to your property is scheduled to be interrupted on the nineteenth unless it's dealt with. Sorry, the twentieth, I mean, the notice says the twentieth, but the point stands, so I need a few minutes of your time now, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, security operations at what, exactly? And, uh, the nineteenth, the twentieth, which is it? I've got about two minutes, so what's the actual point?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. Your energy supplier. The twentieth, it's the twentieth, I misspoke, and I'd ask that you not read into that. Uh, well, the point is a balance of [AMOUNT_1] is overdue on your account, and if it isn't resolved, supply is interrupted. I'm giving you notice so it doesn't come as a surprise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, but look, you've told me the company's name and not much else. I'm between meetings, I've got maybe ninety seconds, and I've had no letter, no email, nothing that I'm aware of saying I'm behind on anything. So I'm hearing a stranger on the phone telling me my power's about to be cut off, and that's, I mean, that's exactly the kind of thing I'd expect to hear if somebody was trying it on. And "security operations" is an odd thing for a supplier to be calling about, isn't it? Billing, sure, but security? I'm not saying you're not who you say you are, I just don't know that you are. So what I'll do is I'll look up the number on my own bill, or the app, call that, and ask about the account myself. If there really is a balance, they'll tell me. If not, well. Is there a reference I should quote when I ring them, or a department?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Look, I don't need you to take my word for it, and I'd rather you didn't. Your last bill showed [AMOUNT_2] as the amount due, and the balance since then is what's brought the account to [AMOUNT_1]. Check that figure against the bill in front of you. And that's the point, we don't take payment on this call, none, so don't give anyone card details over the phone, me included. Log into your own online account at [URL_1], or ring the number printed on your bill, and quote [ACCOUNT_REF] to billing and ask for the arrears team. They can also set up a payment plan, so you're not forced to clear it in one go. But the date stands, so please don't leave it. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a payment plan, you said? No, sorry, I've not got a plan, I'm on, uh, whatever the standard tariff is. And I haven't got the bill in front of me, I'm in a corridor. But look, you've said don't give card details and ring the number on the bill, which, fine, that's actually what I was going to do anyway. So I'll do that. I'll check the app later today, ring the number I find myself, and ask about the account. If there's a balance, they'll sort it. Right, I've got to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's the right approach, do exactly that. And, uh, to be clear, I'm not offering you a plan on the tariff, I mean the arrears team can arrange one on the balance, that's all. Check the figure against your last bill when you're back at a desk, quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and ask billing about the twentieth. Don't leave it past today if you can help it. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, will do. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Goodbye. Don't leave it, please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I heard you, I'm not going to leave it. But let me just say this, since you've been quite insistent about today. If there really is a balance, a few hours isn't going to matter, because nobody cuts anyone off on the twentieth without a proper notice landing on the doormat first, and I've had nothing, not a letter, not an email. So here's what happens. I'm out of this meeting by four, I'll open the app, check the account, see if there's any arrears showing, and if there is, I'll ring the number on the actual bill, not one you've given me, and sort it out with them. If there isn't, then I'll want to know why someone rang me about it. Anyway, I really do have to go now. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, it's [PERSON_2] calling from customer care at [COMPANY_A], how are you doing today? Uh, sorry, I don't think you've said anything two turns ago because we've only just connected, so let me back up a little -- I'm ringing about the little prize draw we ran at the [CITY_1] event a while back, and I just wanted to check you've got a minute before I get into it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a prize raid? No, I'm sorry, I think I misheard that. Who did you say you were calling from again, and what event is this?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, draw, not raid, though I can see how that sounds, sorry! I'm [PERSON_2], customer care at [COMPANY_A], the shop that ran the prize draw at the [CITY_1] community fair, the one where you popped your name and number on a little entry slip at our stall. Do you remember that, or has it slipped your mind a bit?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, I don't recall that. I can't say I've ever filled in an entry slip at a fair.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, that's fair enough, it was ages ago and those stalls get busy, so don't worry. It was the [CITY_1] community fair, the Saturday back in [DATE_1], we had the bunting up and a big glass jar for the slips. Honestly, if it doesn't ring a bell, no harm done, I'd rather you tell me than pretend! It was only a small thing anyway, a [AMOUNT_1] voucher for the shop, nothing to pay, nothing to sign up for, you'd just pop in and collect it in person whenever suits.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, um, well. I still don't remember any of it, and I'd have expected to remember putting my number down. So can I ask, how did you come to have this number, exactly? Do you have the slip in front of you, with a name on it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's a good question, and honestly I'm glad you asked. The slips are all kept in a box in the back office, so I've got your name and this number written on the one I pulled out, [PERSON_1] and [PHONE_1], so I'm not guessing. But look, I don't want you taking my word for it, because I'd be wary too. You don't need to tell me anything else, no address, no details, nothing. If it doesn't feel right, just ring the shop on the number you'd find yourself, ask for [PERSON_2], and they can tell you about the draw. Or come in, and I'll show you the slip in person.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well, I'll give you this, you're not asking me for anything, which is, uh, unusual for an unexpected call. And suggesting I look the shop up myself and ring them is a sensible thing to offer. But I should say plainly that I still don't remember any slip, and reading my name and number back to me doesn't really prove anything, because anyone can have a name and number. So I'm not going to confirm anything about myself on this call, and I'd rather not discuss the voucher any further until I've checked it independently. Before I do that, though, I have a couple of precise questions. Which shop is it, by name and by location? What date was the fair, specifically, not roughly? And who ran the draw, was it the shop itself or an organiser at the fair? If you can't answer those, that's fine, but I'd like to know whether you can.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, those are all fair questions, and you're quite right not to confirm anything. The shop is [COMPANY_A], on the high street in [CITY_1], and the fair was on [DATE_1], that Saturday, I can give you the exact date once I've got the paperwork open. And the draw was run by the shop itself, at our own stall, not by the organisers. Oh, and I should correct something, I said earlier it was a [AMOUNT_1] voucher, but now I think about it, I may be mixing it up with a different prize, so I'd rather you hear the right figure when you ring the shop yourself. Anyway, please do check it independently, and honestly there's no rush at all, the voucher isn't going anywhere. Right, I'll let you get on, it's been lovely chatting, thanks for being so patient with me, [PERSON_1], and I hope the rest of your week is a good one.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, thank you for being straightforward about it, I'll say that. But I'll be honest with you, I'm not entirely satisfied. When I asked for specifics, I got the shop's name as a placeholder, a date you'd give me later once you had the paperwork open, and a voucher amount you've now retracted. That's three answers that were all, sort of, deferred. None of it's alarming in itself, and I appreciate you aren't asking me for anything, but it does mean I've got nothing I could actually check right now. So here's what I'll do. If I decide this is worth following up, I'll look the shop up myself through its own website or the local directory, and I won't use any number from this call. If they've got a record of a draw and my name on it, fine. If not, I'll consider it a wrong number or a mistake, and I won't think any more about it. Either way, I won't be confirming anything about myself today, and I'd rather you didn't ring this number again unless I contact you first. That said, I appreciate the call wasn't pushy. So, thanks for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, absolutely, that's -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you, but yes, that's exactly right, you do that, look us up yourself, and I won't ring this number again, that's fine, I'll make a note on the slip. And honestly, if there's no record, put it down to my mistake, no harm done at all. Thanks for hearing me out, [PERSON_1], take care now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, there's a delivery driver at the door, uh -- no, it's fine, he's leaving it on the step. Right. Yes, thank you, I'll hold you to that about not ringing again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, sorry -- is that [PERSON_1]'s parent or guardian? Um, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the office at [COMPANY_A], I'm the case handler for attendance. I'm just ringing because [PERSON_3] was marked absent this morning and we didn't have a message, so I wanted to check everything's all right. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hello, yes, I'm here, sorry, I was just putting the kettle on. Did you say you're ringing about a, um, a tax case? Because I don't think I've got anything like that going on, dear. Who did you say you were again? It's nice to have a call, mind, it's been ever so quiet today.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, sorry, I think I've confused things -- not a tax case at all, no. I'm [PERSON_2], from the school office at [COMPANY_A]. It's about [PERSON_3], who was marked absent this morning, and we just wanted to make sure they're safe and well. Is that, um, is that someone you look after? Sorry, hello, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a school, right, yes, I'm still here, dear, sorry. Now hang on, you said a name a moment ago, [PERSON_3], was it? Could you say that again for me? Only I don't think I caught it properly the first time, what with the kettle going. I did have a nephew once who went missing from school for a whole afternoon, turned out he was at the pictures, can you imagine. But no, I'm not sure that name is anyone I look after, so I might be the wrong number altogether.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, yes, it's [PERSON_3] -- that's the pupil's name, [PERSON_3], from [COMPANY_A]. And you may well be right that it's the wrong number, I'd hate to have bothered you for nothing. I did only want to be sure the child was safe, you see, that's all this is. Um, hello, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm still here, dear, I'm still here. Well, I think it's the wrong number, you see, because I don't look after any children, not now, they've all grown up and gone, I think it is the wrong number. It's just me here, just me and the kettle. But it's very good of you to ring round and check, I will say that, it's nice that somebody bothers. Was there anything else you needed, or did you just want to make sure about the, um, the little one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nothing else, that was all I wanted, just to be sure the little one was safe, that's all. I'm so sorry to have troubled you, it's only that the number's on our file for [PERSON_3], so I thought -- well, I thought I'd check. Hello? Are you still there? It's only that if it is the wrong number, I'd best look at our records again, and I'd hate to leave you worrying.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm not worrying, dear, don't you fret about me. It's just, well, it's funny that my number would be on your file, isn't it? I've had this number donkey's years. Maybe somebody wrote it down wrong, they do that, don't they, a seven looks like a one. Yes, I'd have another look at your records if I were you, and I hope the little one turns up safe. And thank you for ringing, it was nice to hear a voice, it really was. Right, I'll let you get on. Goodbye now, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, thank you, I'll do that, I'll check the number against our records -- sorry, one second, there's someone at my door, I'm just -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Sorry. Um, you've been very kind, and if you'd rather, you can always ring the school office yourself on the number from the school's own website or the phone book, that way you know it's us. I'm quite happy for you to do that. Hello, are you still there? Goodbye then, dear, and sorry again for the bother.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind of you, dear, but I don't think I'll need to ring anyone, since it's only the wrong number, isn't it? Though it's good to know, about the phone book. I haven't looked in mine for years, I wonder where it's got to. Anyway, no bother at all, no bother. You look after yourself, and I do hope the little one's turned up. Goodbye now, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, hello, sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm, um, I'm calling on behalf of [PERSON_2] at [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy, just to let you know your repeat prescription is, uh, ready for collection.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who's calling? Is this [PERSON_1]... yeah, that's me, but who did you say you're with? Which pharmacy, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, right, sorry, that's -- I should've said that first. It's [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy, the one in [CITY_1]. I'm not actually, uh, I don't work the counter myself, I'm just passing a message along for [PERSON_2], who asked me to ring you because they're tied up with customers right now. I mean, I'm only the, the messenger, really. It's just that your repeat's ready, so you can pop in whenever suits.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Which medication is it, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, I don't have that in front of me, sorry. [PERSON_2] just said it's your repeat.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said it's a, what, a rebate? Hang on, I don't have any rebate with a pharmacy. Oh, repeat. Right, repeat. Okay, but I mean, that's the thing, you can't tell me which medication it is, you're just the messenger. And I haven't got a repeat due that I know of. So what's the name on it? What's it actually made out to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's a repeat, not a, uh, I did say repeat, I -- look, I'm only passing on what I was told, I didn't think it'd be, I mean, I'm just trying to help here. It's under [PERSON_1], that's what [PERSON_2] wrote down, or, no, wait, they said it might be under a different spelling, I'm not sure. I just thought you'd want to know, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you don't know the medication, you're not sure of the spelling of the name, and you can't say who's actually ringing. That's a lot of not sure for a collection reminder. Tell you what, give me the pharmacy's actual number, or I'll just look it up myself and ring the counter. If there's a repeat waiting, [PERSON_2] can tell me what it is when I turn up. That alright with you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I, no, that's -- that's completely fine, I'd, I'd rather you did, honestly. I didn't mean to, uh, make it sound like I was, like you had to take my word for it. It's just, I only wanted to, well, I thought I was being helpful, and now it sounds like I've, I've upset you or something. The number's [PHONE_1], that's the counter. And if you ring and it turns out it's not for you, then, um, I'm sorry, I'll tell [PERSON_2] I must've got the wrong name. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you haven't upset me, it's fine. I'm just a bit cautious with calls I wasn't expecting, that's all. It's nothing personal. Honestly, the fact you're happy for me to ring the counter is the most reassuring thing you've said so far. Though I'll look the number up myself rather than use the one you've just read out, if that's all right. Not because I think you've made it up, it's just the sort of habit I've got into. And if there is a repeat waiting under some odd spelling of my name, they can sort it out when I'm standing there. If it's the wrong person, well, no harm done, you've just had a wasted phone call. So, yeah, I'll check it with them directly. Thanks for ringing, I suppose. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, a habit, right, no, I get it, honestly. And a, a cautious, sorry, did you say cautions? Because I haven't, I mean, there's nothing like that on it, no warnings or anything, it's just a normal repeat, as far as I know. Oh, hang on, you said cautious, didn't you? Sorry, I'm, I've got a bit tangled there. Yes, no, that's absolutely fine, you look it up yourself, and I'll tell [PERSON_2] you might ring. Thanks for being, um, so patient with me. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, cautious, no worries. Don't worry about the tangle. Anyway, I'll ring them myself and sort it out there. Right, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, hang on, did you say sort it out, or sword it out? No, no, sorry, that's not a thing, I'm being daft. Sort it out, yes, of course. That's, that's grand, you do that, and, um, thanks for not being cross with me. I know I made a bit of a mess of it. Right, bye then, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sort it out, yeah. Cheers, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Um, my name is [PERSON_1], and I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency. I'm, uh, a compliance officer there, and I was wondering whether you might have five minutes for a short consumer survey.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good afternoon. A survey, you said? Sorry, I had the telly on, I'll just, hang on, there. A survey, from, what was it, a research something? I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch the name, a research agency, was it? Well, I've got a bit of time, I'm just in on my own, but what's it about, dear?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's quite all right, take your time. It's [COMPANY_A], a research agency, that's, um, [COMPANY_A]. And it's a short consumer survey, as I said, a few questions about, well, everyday shopping habits and the sort of products people buy. It's, uh, a survey about consumer habits, nothing complicated, and there are no right or wrong answers. We are, I'll be honest, hoping to finish the current batch fairly soon, so if you did have five minutes now, that would be, um, very helpful.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I suppose so. Shopping, I can talk about shopping, go on then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Thank you, that's very kind. Now, before I begin, I should say, uh, that taking part is entirely voluntary, and you can stop at any point, you only have to say. The first question is quite easy. Roughly how often would you say you do a main food shop, is it weekly, or, um, more or less often than that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's easy enough. Weekly, mostly, usually of a Thursday, because that's when the, oh, hang on, sorry dear, there's a bird at the window, a great fat pigeon, he comes every afternoon. I put a few crumbs out and now he thinks he owns the place. Where was I? Yes, Thursday, the big shop, and then I pop out for bits and bobs in between, a loaf, a bit of milk. It's only me now, you see, so I don't need much.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, every pigeon needs a regular, doesn't he. Thank you, that's, uh, very helpful, a weekly shop on Thursdays with the top-ups in between. Now, can I just go back for a moment to something you said earlier, when I first mentioned the survey? You said, I think, that you hadn't quite caught the name of the agency, and I'd, um, like to be sure you have it properly before we go on. It's [COMPANY_A], and I'm [PERSON_1], and if you'd like to check any of that, you're, uh, quite welcome to.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's, well, that's very nice of you, dear. I did think, I mean, I'll admit I'm not very good with names on the phone, they just sort of, they go in one ear. Check it, you said? How would I, I wouldn't know how to, oh, I'd have to, I suppose I could look it up, but I haven't got the, my glasses are somewhere, and the computer's, well, my nephew set it up and I couldn't tell you how it works. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or, no, that's silly, you've got your questions to get on with. Go on, carry on, I'm sure it's all perfectly proper.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it isn't silly at all, I'd, um, rather you did check, and I'd be glad if you would. There's no need to use a number from me, in fact. If you look up [COMPANY_A] in a phone book, or ask your nephew when he next calls, or find a number on something you already trust, then ring that and ask for [PERSON_1] in compliance, they'll be able to confirm who I am. I should say I've only got a handful of calls left in this batch, so it would be, well, sensible to do it sooner rather than later, but there's no obligation either way. Shall we leave it there for now, and you can ring when you've found the number?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, um, yes, I suppose that, well, hmm. That's very decent of you, I must say, most people just want you to get on with it. Let me think, my nephew rings on Sundays, usually, so I could ask him then, couldn't I? Though I'll have forgotten the name by Sunday, I always do, I'd have to write it down, and where's my pen, there's never a pen when you want one. Anyway. So you don't want to carry on with the questions now, is that it? Only I was quite enjoying it, to be honest, it's nice to have a chat of an afternoon.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's all right. Better to check first, and I'm glad you enjoyed it. When you find a pen, it's [COMPANY_A], and the name is [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh yes, I'll find a pen, I've got one somewhere in the, oh, and thank you for being so patient with me, dear, you've been very -- Sorry, I've talked over you, haven't I. I do that. What was it you were going to say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, not at all, you didn't talk over me. Though I think you said something about a cousin ringing on Sundays? Ah, no, a nephew, forgive me, I'd misheard. Well, either way, he'll be able to help you look up the number, and I'd be happy for you to ring and have [COMPANY_A] confirm who I am, whenever it suits you. Thank you for your time this afternoon, and do mind the pigeon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you're ever so kind, thank you. I'll tell him on Sunday, my nephew, and he'll find it for me, he's very good like that. And I'll mind the pigeon, he's no trouble, just greedy. Right then, well, goodbye, [PERSON_1], thank you for ringing, it was lovely to have a chat. Bye bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Goodbye, and, uh, just one thing before you go, if I may. Two turns back you said you'd tell your nephew on Sunday, and I wasn't sure whether you meant you'd ask him to look up the number, or whether you'd want him to ring [COMPANY_A] himself on your behalf. Either is perfectly fine with me, I'd just like to be clear. Thank you again, and do take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, did I say that, two turns back? Gosh, I'd have to think. I think I meant I'd get him to look the number up, and then I'd ring it myself, though, well, he might just ring it for me, he's always very quick like that, he doesn't like me fussing with the telephone. Either way he'll sort it out on Sunday, I'm sure. Right, well, goodbye again then, dear, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just calling to arrange a window for your boiler service visit, the one you've already got booked in with us. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? Sorry, did you say you're in the middle of dinner? No, no, that's fine, I'll be quick, we're only holding these slots until end of day today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one second -- the dog's just gone off at something in the garden. Right. No, I didn't say I was at dinner, so I'm not sure where that came from. And I'm afraid I haven't got a boiler service booked with, uh, [COMPANY_A], at least not that I can recall. Who exactly did you say you were with, and how did you come by this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's my mistake on the dinner thing, sorry, I've got a different note open. It's [PERSON_1], account services at [COMPANY_A], we're the maintenance contractor, and the number's from the booking record on your account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. If you don't recall booking, that's fine, I can't do anything on it without confirming, so I'll flag it and you can check with whoever arranged it, uh, [COMPANY_B] or the landlord or whoever.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. I own the place, so there's no landlord, and I don't know a [COMPANY_B]. Which is odd, given you've just read me a reference off my own account. What's the address on that booking?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, I can't read an address out to you, sorry, we don't give property details over the phone before the account holder's been verified, that's just procedure. Look, it sounds like something's been crossed on our side, a wrong number or a mismatched record, so I'll take this booking off the slot list and mark the number as not confirmed. If you do want a service visit at any point, ring the main line on your service paperwork or go through [URL_1], and they'll sort it properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you've got a booking on my account, but you can't tell me the address, and you want me to verify myself to you before you'll confirm the thing you phoned me about. I'd say that's backwards, wouldn't you? Anyway, I'm not giving you anything, and I'm not going to chase a [URL_1] on the strength of this call. If I do need a boiler service, I'll find the number myself, from paperwork I already hold. So yes, take the number off your list. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, and honestly, that's fair, it probably is backwards the way it came out. I'll take the number off the list and mark the booking as unconfirmed, so you shouldn't get another call on it. Sorry for the bother, [PERSON_2], and have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, thanks. Just so it's noted, I never actually said I was [PERSON_2] at any point, you rather assumed that, and I'd also say I wasn't at dinner, I was just at home. Anyway, I'll deal with any boiler servicing myself, so no more calls on this number, please. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Noted, yes, no more calls on this number, I'll make sure that's on the record, no more calls. And you're right, I did assume the name, I shouldn't have, that's on me. So, uh, nothing further from us on the boiler, number's off the list, no more calls. Thanks for your time, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, sorry, that's the post just coming through the door, the dog's off again. Right, I'm back. Fine, then, that's understood, number off the list, nothing further on the boiler. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is the attendance office at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling about -- yeah, sorry, is this the parent or guardian of [PERSON_1]? Because [PERSON_1] was marked absent this morning and we've got no note on the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... sorry, who's this again? The attendance office at, um, which school exactly? And, hang on, sorry, the kids are being loud -- you said absent this morning?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Attendance office at [COMPANY_A]. That's the school, [PERSON_1]'s school. And yeah, absent this morning, marked in at registration, nothing on the system since. It's just a routine check, we do it for every pupil who's down as absent without a reason logged. Are you able to tell me where [PERSON_1] is at the moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, sorry, you said [PERSON_1] is missing? Like, you can't find them? Because I mean, I'm looking right now, I'm, um -- hang on, why are you asking where they are? Shouldn't you know where they are, if it's the school?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not missing, sorry, that came out wrong. Just absent, no reason logged. If [PERSON_1]'s there with you, that's fine, I only need to know why they weren't in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so they're not missing, right. Uh, but see, I'm just -- you're asking me where my kid is and why they weren't at school, and I don't actually know who I'm talking to. You've said the attendance office, and you've said the school, but you haven't said which school, you haven't said your name, and you haven't told me who it is you think you're calling. I mean, anyone could ring up and say a name and ask where a child is. So, um, what name do you have on your system for the parent? And what's the school called? Because I'd sooner you told me that than me telling you anything. And hang on, [PERSON_1], put that down, please -- sorry, sorry, go on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, you're right to ask, and I should've led with it. My name's [PERSON_3], I'm in the attendance office at [COMPANY_A], that's the school, and the number you'd ring to check me is on the school website, [URL_1], or you can phone the main office on [PHONE_1] and ask for attendance. On the system, the contact I've got for [PERSON_1] is [PERSON_2], so if that's you, fine, and if it's not, that's useful for me to know too. And honestly, you don't have to tell me anything on this call. If you'd rather hang up and ring the office back to confirm I'm real, that's completely okay, I'll note the objection on the file and we can carry on that way. All I'm after is a reason for this morning so I can close off the register, whether that's illness, an appointment, whatever it was. I just need to log it, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you've got [PERSON_2] down, which -- I mean, hang on, I'm not saying yes or no to that, I just -- and the number, is that, uh, you said ring the main office and ask for -- no, wait, sorry, I'm talking over you. You said I can ring them back. So, why don't I just do that? Because honestly, if it's just a reason for the register, it can wait ten minutes, can't it? Or is there some reason it can't?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, ring them back, it can wait. There's no reason it can't. And just to be clear on what I said two turns ago, when I said I'd close off the register, I only meant the absence gets logged as unauthorised until a reason goes on the file. So a ten-minute wait doesn't change anything, it just stays flagged for now. Ring the main office on [PHONE_1], ask for attendance, and give them [PERSON_1]'s name. They'll put you through to me or someone on the team, and you can tell them the reason then. Sorry for the confusion earlier, I should've given you all that up front.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Okay. I'll ring the school myself, then. Thanks.
